main_caveats: Ap3b1 itself was weakly perturbed, so lack of correlation cannot prove a true AP3B1/AP3B2 functional opposition.

summary: Known AP3B1 loss-of-function disease biology maps to lysosome-related organelle cargo sorting, while this assay shows no robust neuronal steady-state mRNA signature for Ap3b1 loss.
why_it_matters: For HPS2 or pearl-like mechanisms, cargo localization and organelle phenotyping are likely more proximal biomarkers than single-cell RNA changes after this level of Ap3b1 perturbation.
main_caveats: The screen used acute perturbation in mouse brain cell classes, whereas the disease literature includes human germline loss and constitutive mouse alleles in multiple organ systems.

summary: Neither selected AP-3/BLOC-1 or lysosome-neighbor perturbations nor unrestricted same-cell-type signature neighbors formed a credible Ap3b1-centered transcriptomic module.
why_it_matters: The weak Ap3b1 signature should not be forced into a pathway narrative; related vesicle-trafficking or HPS-adjacent genes were also uncorrelated or transcriptionally quiet.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from weak Ap3b1 signatures; the result is mainly a guardrail against over-calling top signature neighbors.

summary: Chrnb4 showed no reliable on-target mRNA engagement in any profiled cell class.
why_it_matters: Without a measurable target knockdown, the Chrnb4 perturbation cannot be interpreted as a clean β4 nicotinic-receptor loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: A negative on-target mRNA result may reflect low baseline expression, sparse expressing cells inside broad bins, or protein-level buffering rather than absence of β4 biology.

summary: The single significant Pcca decrease in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut did not extend to a propionyl-CoA carboxylase module.
why_it_matters: Pcca is the only FDR-supported Chrnb4 downstream gene, but lack of Pccb and propionate-catabolism partner responses prevents a confident mitochondrial-metabolism pathway assignment.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Single FDR hit in one cell type with weak Chrnb4 target engagement; no orthogonal validation.

summary: Chrnb4, Chrna3, Chrna5, and Chrnb3 perturbations failed to produce a convergent α3β4α5 receptor-cluster signature.
why_it_matters: The result warns that the screen did not recover the expected biology of the curated α3β4α5 receptor module, most likely because the whole cluster was poorly expressed or weakly perturbed.
main_caveats: Correlation analysis is transcriptome-wide and restricted to cell types where both perturbations were profiled; no receptor currents were measured.

summary: The broad 145 MH-LH TH Glut class did not recapitulate medial-habenula Chrnb4 biology.
why_it_matters: Prior work localizes β4-dependent nicotine aversion to the medial habenula, so the null effect in this broad class suggests rare habenular cells or nicotine-evoked physiology were diluted in the dataset.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The cell class label is broader than the medial habenula circuit studied in the literature, and the assay was a basal transcriptomic perturbation rather than a nicotine challenge.

summary: Chrnb2 and Ache were detectably depleted in midbrain/thalamic populations while Chrnb4 was not.
why_it_matters: This comparison argues against a universal failure to perturb cholinergic genes and makes the Chrnb4/Chrna3/Chrna5 receptor-cluster silence more target-specific.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Chrnb2-containing receptors are not interchangeable with α3β4α5 receptors, and downstream signatures of Chrnb2 or Ache were not analyzed here.

summary: Chrnb4 did not have a strong positive or negative global signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Weak nearest-neighbor correlations, including safe-target guides among the leaders, prevent over-interpretation of Htr2a, Vps35, Setdb1, or other nominally correlated perturbations as mechanistic Chrnb4 partners.
main_caveats: This is a restricted signature-neighbor diagnostic, not a physical-interaction analysis.

summary: Safe_target_59 produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic phenotype across 21 assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: This is the expected behavior for a safe-targeting negative control and makes the perturbation useful for estimating the null tail of this screen.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA

summary: Safe_target_59 did not measurably induce a DNA-damage, checkpoint, or apoptosis marker response.
why_it_matters: Safe-targeting guides can still create genomic cuts, so the lack of a marker-panel response argues against Safe_target_59 being dominated by Cas9 DNA-damage toxicity in this dataset.
main_caveats: Marker set was selected post hoc; the dataset measures steady-state RNA, not DNA breaks or cell viability.

summary: The two weakest Safe_target_59 cell-type deviations were isolated nominal hits rather than FDR-supported selective phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Tmem33 in hypothalamic GABA cells and Grin2a/Pld3 in NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut cells should not be promoted to pathway or biomarker hypotheses without replication.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Both examined outlier strata had low perturbed-cell counts, 42 and 32 cells, and all adjusted p values were above 0.30.

summary: Safe_target_59 did not converge with or oppose any real perturbation signature at meaningful magnitude.
why_it_matters: The lack of a positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor argues that the Safe_target_59 profile is null noise, not a hidden copy of a biological knockout program.
main_caveats: The correlation used a global score vector and did not test every cell type separately.

summary: Safe_target_59 has no assignable on-target mRNA, protein, disease, or druggability interpretation.
why_it_matters: Nominal downstream genes cannot be interpreted as consequences of inhibiting a known gene product, and no therapeutic direction should be inferred.
main_caveats: The guide sequence and the intended safe genomic coordinate were not available, so locus-specific off-target checks were impossible.

summary: Abcd3 perturbation produced a recurrent but only nominal knockdown-like decrease of the target transcript, with the clearest engagement in midbrain and thalamic neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This identifies the cellular contexts in which the guide behaves most like an on-target Abcd3 loss-of-expression perturbation while keeping all downstream interpretation below FDR-level confidence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript never achieved adjusted p<0.05, and several cell types had fewer than 60 perturbed cells.

summary: Abcd3 transcript reduction was not followed by an FDR-significant peroxisomal or global transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: A peroxisomal lipid transporter can be partially depleted in these neuronal classes without inducing a large same-day mRNA stress program, so metabolite-level or protein-level liabilities could be missed by this assay.
main_caveats: Negative at the assayed FDR threshold only; weak guide engagement and acute transcriptomics cannot rule out changes in peroxisomal flux, lipid species, organelle morphology, or later responses.

summary: Abcd3 did not converge with Acox1, Hsd17b4, Pex1, Pex13, or Pex14 perturbations, even where Pex14 itself was efficiently knocked down.
why_it_matters: The data argue against treating all peroxisomal lipid-transport, beta-oxidation, and matrix-import genes as interchangeable transcriptional perturbations in neurons.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Most related perturbations were themselves weak; the contrast is strongest for Pex14, whose target transcript reached FDR<0.05 in three shared classes.

summary: Genome-wide signature-neighbor searches did not reveal a credible alternative Abcd3 module.
why_it_matters: The nearest positive and negative neighbors were very weak and dominated by a CA3/CA2-FC/DG signature where Abcd3 was not knocked down, making them poor mechanistic anchors.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from restricted score vectors; the result is a quality-control and hypothesis-triage observation, not evidence that those genes regulate ABCD3 biology.

summary: The silent neuronal signature is best interpreted as context restriction of an established liver/peroxisomal metabolic gene rather than as evidence that Abcd3 loss is benign.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse loss-of-function studies link ABCD3 to bile-acid and dicarboxylic-acid metabolism; this brain Perturb-seq panel lacks the hepatic substrate environment where those consequences were demonstrated.
main_caveats: The assay measured acute neuronal mRNA, not liver physiology, bile-acid intermediates, dicarboxylic fatty acids, or long-term organismal phenotypes.

summary: Cspg4 perturbation was transcriptionally silent across the assayed neuronal classes and showed no detectable depletion of the Cspg4 transcript itself.
why_it_matters: The negative result is biologically interpretable rather than merely uninformative: CSPG4/NG2 biology is expected in OPC, vascular mural, or tumor contexts, not in the glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes assayed here.
cell_types: all 22 Cspg4-assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: DE summaries cannot distinguish absent target expression from poor guide activity; no OPC or pericyte group was assayed for Cspg4.

summary: The lack of Cspg4 response persisted in well-sampled neuronal classes with more than 100 perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: Failure to find downstream genes in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut is not explained solely by the lowest-count Cspg4 groups.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Even these classes lack evidence of Cspg4 transcript engagement, so the finding supports neuronal non-responsiveness rather than biochemical buffering after proven Cspg4 loss.

summary: Nominal Cspg4 peaks and genome-wide signature neighbors were too weak and nonrecurrent to define a Cspg4 module.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpretation of isolated nominal genes such as Tmem131, Prkci, Slc25a44, or Agap2 as pathway readouts.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and are exploratory when the query signature itself has no FDR-significant genes.

summary: Cspg4 and related glial or CSPG4-neighborhood perturbations did not co-activate a PDGF/FGF/integrin signaling state in neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Although NG2 can organize growth-factor and integrin signaling in appropriate cells, neuronal perturbation of Cspg4, Sox10, Pdgfrb, and Itga4 was FDR-silent, whereas Fgfr1, Fgfr2, and Mapk1 showed only isolated single-gene hits.
cell_types: all assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: Pdgfra, Fgf2, Olig1, and Olig2 were not assayed as perturbations, and sparse Fgfr/Mapk on-target rows are not equivalent to a CSPG4 pathway response.

summary: The all-neuronal Cspg4 negative result should not be extrapolated to OPC, pericyte, or melanoma settings in which CSPG4 is a cell-surface disease or therapy target.
why_it_matters: CSPG4-directed antibodies and cell therapies target a membrane antigen whose key normal brain expression is non-neuronal; absence of neuronal DE is therefore compatible with, not evidence against, CSPG4 activity in off-panel cells.
cell_types: all 22 Cspg4-assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is mouse neuronal transcriptomics and did not test antigen density, antibodies, CAR constructs, tumor cells, OPCs, or pericytes.

summary: Bcas3 perturbation was nearly silent across the assayed neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: The sparse response prevents treating this experiment as a strong BCAS3 loss-of-function model, even though BCAS3 is a known disease gene and developmental regulator.
main_caveats: The measured transcript was not depleted; CRISPR mutations can act at the protein level without lowering mRNA, and no endothelial or early progenitor population was present.

summary: Trim23 induction in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was the only FDR-significant Bcas3 response.
why_it_matters: Trim23 is itself connected to selective autophagy, so this isolated hit is an autophagy-adjacent marker to prioritize if BCAS3 neuronal autophagy is followed up.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene support only; no other L4-5 IT genes reached FDR<0.05 and the neuronal context differs from the infected-cell TRIM23 study.

summary: 308 CB GABA had the broadest nominal Bcas3 signature, but it remained below FDR and its strongest restricted neighbors were not BCAS3-specific.
why_it_matters: This distinguishes a hypothesis-generating cerebellar GABA response from a reliable cell-type-restricted program.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All top 308 CB GABA genes had FDR>=0.461, and the restricted neighbor set included a safe-target control.

summary: Bcas3 signatures did not consistently match perturbations of assayed autophagy, mitophagy, Notch, or angiogenic receptor neighbors.
why_it_matters: Known BCAS3 biology centers on endothelial migration and PHAF1/WIPI2-linked phagophore assembly; the lack of in-dataset convergence argues that those programs were not engaged in this neuronal assay.
main_caveats: The comparison used only the top 200 Bcas3-ranked genes in each cell type and pathway-neighbor perturbations also varied in strength.

summary: The dataset refines BCAS3 disease biology toward a requirement for stronger or developmental perturbations outside surveyed mature neuronal states.
why_it_matters: Human recessive BCAS3 loss of function causes a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder, whereas mouse global/endothelial knockout is embryonic-vascular; the weak neuronal Perturb-seq phenotype suggests that scRNA in these neuron classes is not sufficient to read out the disease mechanism.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The inference is by absence of a strong signature, not by a developmental or endothelial rescue experiment.

direction: weak target decrease with no FDR-significant downstream response
summary: Atp6v1e1 perturbation produced no 5% adjusted differential-expression calls across 20 measured cell types despite weak, consistently negative target-transcript scores.
why_it_matters: This limits mechanistic interpretation of the perturbation and argues that downstream absences must be read through weak engagement or buffering rather than as definitive biology.
main_caveats: High confidence for the measured DE table; the dataset alone cannot distinguish inefficient guide activity from post-transcriptional or protein-level buffering.

summary: The subthreshold Atp6v1e1 response was concentrated in 308 CB GABA, whereas the only other pvals_adj<0.10 rows were isolated Snrpn and Chp1 calls in low-count hypothalamic classes.
why_it_matters: The strongest Atp6v1e1 readout in this dataset is cell-type restricted and includes several synapse- or axon-associated genes, consistent with neuronal V-ATPase biology but below standard FDR support.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: No gene reached pvals_adj<0.05; the nearest 308 CB GABA signature neighbors were unrelated perturbations, making the module a weak transcriptomic hypothesis.

direction: Atp6v1e1 much weaker than complex members
summary: Atp6v1e1 was far weaker than other V-ATPase complex member perturbations, especially Atp6v0c, Atp6ap1, and Atp6ap2.
why_it_matters: A core V1 subunit would be expected to connect to the same proton-pump machinery as these comparators; the measured divergence warns that Atp6v1e1 guide efficacy or subunit-specific buffering dominates the dataset signal.
main_caveats: The contrast reflects transcriptomic DE strength, not a matched biochemical measurement of V-ATPase activity for each subunit.

summary: In 052 Pvalb Gaba, Atp6v0c and Atp6v1b2 were the top two positive whole-transcriptome neighbors of Atp6v1e1.
why_it_matters: The overall Atp6v1e1 signal was weak, but this restricted convergence recovers the expected V-ATPase complex relationship in a fast-spiking inhibitory cell class.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The correlations were modest, Atp6v1e1 itself had no FDR-significant Pvalb DE genes, and the shared nominal genes should not be treated as a validated pathway.

summary: Atp6v1e1 perturbation did not induce a broad mRNA-level V-ATPase replacement program and did not closely track mTOR or autophagy pathway-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: Canonical V-ATPase activity intersects lysosomal pH and mTORC1 amino-acid sensing; the Perturb-seq response therefore looks uncoupled from a large transcriptional lysosome-stress program.
main_caveats: Because target knockdown was weak, absence of a CLEAR, mTOR, or autophagy response cannot rule out pathway activation after stronger ATP6V1E1 depletion.

direction: avoid inferring benign loss from weak Perturb-seq signal
summary: The weak Atp6v1e1 transcriptomic footprint should not be interpreted as evidence that V1E1 inhibition is safe or selective.
why_it_matters: Human ATP6V1E1 and ATP6V1A variants can destabilize V-ATPase and cause multisystem cellular-trafficking disease, and the same mouse dataset shows that other V-ATPase subunits drive stronger brain-cell transcriptomic responses.
main_caveats: No ATP6V1E1-selective drug was tested, and human cutis-laxa genetics are not equivalent to partial mouse-brain transcript knockdown.

summary: Cd79b showed no measurable RNA-level target engagement in any assayed mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: The perturbation cannot be interpreted as a productive knockdown response in these cells, and the absence of activity is consistent with CD79B being a B-cell receptor component rather than a brain-expressed neuronal gene.
main_caveats: Target editing was not measured at DNA or protein level; silent transcripts can make logFC unstable.

summary: The only cell-type peaks were nominal, sparse, and not FDR-significant; larger Cd79b bins were also null.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-reading BC005537, Klhl3, Crym, or high-count neuronal classes as a reproducible Cd79b program.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The top two classes had 42 and 56 perturbed cells, so the weak outliers could reflect sampling noise.

summary: Cd79a and Cd79b did not form a convergent perturbation pair in the brain dataset despite encoding the Ig-alpha/Ig-beta BCR heterodimer.
why_it_matters: The result argues that the BCR complex was not engaged in these off-lineage cells, and that Cd79a/Cd79b correlations are dominated by null-signature noise rather than complex biology.
main_caveats: Small correlations are computed over nonsignificant signatures, so they should not be interpreted as direct antagonism.

summary: Cd79b perturbation did not recruit measured BCR, PI3K, immune-marker, or NF-kappaB-associated transcripts.
why_it_matters: Canonical CD79 signaling is expected to propagate through BCR-proximal kinases and downstream second messengers in mature B cells; failure to move this readout panel supports an off-lineage null rather than pathway activation or suppression.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundances for measured genes were tested; acute phosphorylation and calcium flux were not measured.

summary: The Cd79b brain null should not be used to discount CD79B as an immunodeficiency, lymphoma, or antibody-drug-conjugate target.
why_it_matters: Human CD79B biology is validated in B-cell development, ABC-DLBCL BCR signaling, and polatuzumab-based lymphoma therapy, while the perturb-seq rows lack the relevant B-cell receptor context.
main_caveats: Clinical evidence is human B-cell lymphoma; the dataset is mouse brain and cannot adjudicate CD79B targeting in malignant B cells.

summary: A genome-wide score-correlation scan did not reveal a strong Cd79b-like neuronal signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: This closes a loophole in which a weak Cd79b effect could otherwise be assigned to a convergent neuronal module through similarity to other perturbations.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlation scans over FDR-null signatures can rank noise; absence of a high correlation is more interpretable than the identity of weak top neighbors.

summary: Fth1 CRISPR depletion produced a nearly self-only transcriptional phenotype: the target transcript fell in every measured class, but no non-self gene survived FDR correction.
why_it_matters: Ferritin H is an iron-storage enzyme, but the acute mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout shows strong transcript knockdown without a coordinated corrected RNA program, so absence of downstream DE should not be mistaken for absence of the targeted ferritin function.
main_caveats: Transcriptomic endpoint only; FDR correction was per target-cell stratum; no direct iron, ferritin protein, or ROS measurements.

summary: The quality of Fth1 target engagement was cell-type graded rather than binary: thalamic, midbrain, and deep cortical classes carried the strongest corrected Fth1 knockdown, whereas hippocampal and LGE-associated classes stayed nominal.
why_it_matters: Downstream negative results are most interpretable in the high-engagement classes, while low-count or shallow knockdown strata should be treated as underpowered for secondary biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The DE summary does not distinguish editing efficiency from baseline Fth1 expression, guide usage, or post-edit survival across classes.

summary: Canonical iron-import, IRP/IRE, ferritinophagy, and ferroptosis marker transcripts were not transcriptionally recruited after Fth1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Fth1 sits in a post-transcriptionally regulated iron circuit; failure to induce Tfrc, Aco1, Ireb2, Ncoa4, or antioxidant ferroptosis genes at corrected RNA level argues that partial Fth1 loss did not create a broad iron-starvation or ferroptotic state in these acute cultures.
main_caveats: Negative at FDR level; several panel genes were only nominal in isolated classes, and IRP regulation can occur through translation or mRNA stability rather than de novo transcription.

summary: Fth1 did not converge with available iron-storage, iron-uptake, NRF2, or ferroptosis-adjacent perturbations, and the missing Ftl1 and Ncoa4 perturbations leave the ferritin complex and ferritinophagy axis only partially testable.
why_it_matters: The strongest biological partners of Fth1 in curated networks are ferritin light chain and NCOA4, so their absence as perturbations plus the weak signatures of Tfrc, Ireb2, Gpx4, Abcb7, and Nfe2l2 prevent a complex-member interpretation from the present screen.
main_caveats: Some comparators had poor self-transcript engagement, and absent Ftl1/Ncoa4 perturbations mean the most direct ferritin comparisons were unavailable.

summary: The Fth1 knockdown phenotype models loss of wild-type transcript, not dominant ferritin aggregate neuroferritinopathy.
why_it_matters: Human FTH1 neuroferritinopathy is caused by C-terminal truncations that escape nonsense-mediated decay and poison ferritin pores; a self-only mouse knockdown signature cautions against reading this Perturb-seq result as a direct model of toxic mutant ferritin or iron-aggregate pathology.
main_caveats: The dataset does not introduce patient FTH1 variants, measure ferritin inclusions, or assay iron accumulation; Ftl1 was absent from the expression table.

direction: Asah1 generally down but no corrected downstream response
summary: Asah1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed neuronal class despite nominal target mRNA reduction in most classes.
why_it_matters: ASAH1 is the lysosomal ceramidase for ceramide catabolism, so the absence of corrected mRNA changes indicates buffering, incomplete engagement at the protein/lipid level, or a lipidomic phenotype that is not captured by acute scRNA-seq.
main_caveats: On-target Asah1 mRNA changes were nominal and many cell types had modest perturbed-cell counts.

summary: The strongest nominal Asah1 engagement was concentrated in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, where Asah1 was the second-ranked absolute-score gene but no transcriptome-wide hit survived FDR.
why_it_matters: These two classes provide engagement-positive, response-negative examples and show that even the best neuronal Asah1 knockdown contexts in this dataset did not recapitulate an overt ASAH1-deficiency stress program.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assayed classes are not spinal lower motor neurons, and the Asah1 on-target rows did not pass FDR correction.

summary: Asah1 perturbation did not induce corrected expression of a 28-gene sphingolipid or lysosomal ceramide panel, including acid/neutral ceramidase, sphingomyelinase, sphingosine kinase, glucosylceramide, and cholesterol-storage genes.
why_it_matters: The pathway around ASAH1 hydrolyzes ceramide in the lysosome, but the dataset shows no obvious transcriptional feedback through adjacent sphingolipid genes after acute Asah1 perturbation.
main_caveats: Panel analysis is transcript-only and does not test ceramide or sphingosine lipid abundance.

summary: Asah1 signatures were nearly uncorrelated with available related perturbations Smpd3, Sphk1, Lamp2, and Atp6v1a, while the top all-library Asah1 signature neighbors were also weak.
why_it_matters: This argues against treating Asah1 as transcriptionally interchangeable with a generic lysosome perturbation or with the tested linear sphingolipid-pathway neighbors in these acute neuronal signatures.
main_caveats: Correlation analysis used weak Asah1 signatures; Smpd3, Sphk1, Lamp2, and Atp6v1a interrogate only part of the sphingolipid and lysosome space.

direction: no acute corrected neuronal response despite disease and inhibitor prior
summary: The lack of acute neuronal FDR hits after Asah1 perturbation should not be interpreted as neuronal safety for ASAH1 inhibition.
why_it_matters: ASAH1 is explored as an oncology target to increase ceramide, but inherited ASAH1 loss causes severe lysosomal and neurologic disease, so chronic enzyme inhibition could be hazardous even when acute guide-based mRNA signatures are muted.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay drug exposure, chronic inhibition, lipid levels, or glial responses.

summary: Cx3cr1 guide assignment produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response across the 23 assayed neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: This establishes the dominant dataset result and prevents over-interpretation of isolated nominal genes.
main_caveats: The target transcript was not measured, so true target knockdown could not be verified.

summary: The apparent strongest Cx3cr1 responses in CB GABA and P MY Pineal Glut were nominal only, and high-count TH and MB glutamatergic contexts remained FDR-null.
why_it_matters: The data do not support a real cell-type-restricted Cx3cr1 response, even though a few groups had lower nominal p values than the rest.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Top genes did not pass multiple-testing correction and should not be treated as Cx3cr1 effectors.

summary: The FDR-null neuronal profile is consistent with CX3CR1 acting mainly through microglia/CNS macrophages rather than by a direct cell-autonomous program in the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Known effects of Cx3cr1 loss on synaptic pruning, connectivity, and inflammatory neurotoxicity should be mapped to microglial perturbation state, not to the neuronal group_names in this panel.
main_caveats: The dataset itself lacks microglia and cannot measure the expected microglial response.

summary: Cx3cr1 resembled multiple weak innate/microglial receptor perturbations, whereas App showed strong self-transcript depletion in most matched neuronal contexts.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates low-engagement microglial receptor guide assignments from an expressed target that the assay clearly detected.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and does not prove all comparator guides failed mechanistically; some comparator transcripts were measured but not necessarily expressed strongly.

summary: No robust positive or negative Cx3cr1 signature neighbor was found; the largest score-vector correlation to another perturbation was |r| = 0.186.
why_it_matters: There is no hidden convergent module that would rescue biological interpretation from the absence of individual FDR-significant genes.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from restricted score signatures in the DE summary table, not from raw single-cell expression profiles.

summary: Cx3cr1 guide assignment did not feed back onto Cx3cl1 ligand expression in any cell type.
why_it_matters: Even the curated receptor-ligand axis was transcriptionally flat in the assayed neuronal classes, reinforcing that the relevant CX3CL1-CX3CR1 circuit is absent or not perturbed here.
main_caveats: Only transcript feedback was tested; receptor activity, ligand shedding, and microglial responses were not assayed.

summary: Neuronal Cx3cr1 silence should not be interpreted as evidence that CX3CR1 antagonism is inert or safe in the CNS.
why_it_matters: CX3CR1 has documented microglial roles in neurotoxicity and synaptic maturation, so CNS-penetrant drugs could have effects in cell populations missing from this dataset.
main_caveats: This is an inference from absent neuronal target engagement plus microglial literature, not a direct drug study.

summary: Irs1 CRISPRi yielded a near-null RNA phenotype across mouse-brain cell types, with no FDR-supported depletion of the target transcript and only isolated Cbx6 and Aagab non-target hits.
why_it_matters: IRS1 is a canonical signaling scaffold, so the low-amplitude response places a strong target-engagement and buffering caveat on any pathway interpretation.
main_caveats: The finding proves a weak RNA phenotype, not true biological dispensability of IRS1 protein.

summary: The only nominal Irs1 self-depletion events were in GABA classes, led by CTX-CGE GABA, Pvalb Gaba, and MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: If the guide pool engaged Irs1 anywhere, the detectable signal was inhibitory-neuron-skewed, but those cell types still lacked FDR-supported downstream targets.

summary: Nefh signatures do not converge with stronger axonal transport or cytoskeletal perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: The absence of correlation with Dctn1, Dync1h1, Kif5a, Mapt, Stmn2, tubulin, and neurofilament perturbations argues that Nefh loss is not an acute proxy for a general axon-transport stress program.
main_caveats: All-gene correlations can miss sparse shared genes, and transcriptome-wide DE may not capture axonal morphology.

summary: The buffered Nefh knockdown state is distinct from extracellular pNFH elevation used as an ALS axonal-injury biomarker.
why_it_matters: It warns against equating NEFH transcript perturbation in surviving cells with fluid neurofilament heavy-chain release during neurodegeneration.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The disease comparison is indirect: human ALS biofluids and mouse single-cell guide perturbations differ in species, compartment, assay, and injury state.

summary: Fars2 did not show statistically detectable self-depletion in the measured target transcript in any of the 22 assayed cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: The primary perturbation quality check failed: without visible Fars2 mRNA reduction, downstream negative results are best interpreted as weak target engagement rather than proof that Fars2 is dispensable.
main_caveats: mRNA readout can miss DNA editing or protein depletion; no guide-level, raw expression, protein, or enzymatic activity measurements were available.

summary: Fars2 perturbation produced an FDR-null transcriptome across mouse-brain cell types rather than a coherent mitochondrial-translation stress program.
why_it_matters: FARS2 is a mitochondrial tRNA-charging enzyme, so the lack of any corrected RNA signature argues that this screen did not capture the expected mitochondrial aminoacylation/OXPHOS consequence of losing mtPheRS.
main_caveats: The inference is a transcriptomic negative result under weak target engagement; mitochondrial translation could be affected at protein or metabolic levels that are not visible here.

summary: The apparent concentration of the lowest nominal Fars2 hits in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 217 P MY Pineal Glut is exploratory, not validated cell-type selectivity.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-interpretation of the two best-looking cell-type contrasts: the best CNU-LGE gene had FDR 0.237 and the P MY Pineal contrast had only 35 perturbed cells.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: No gene survived FDR correction in either cell type; the lower P MY Pineal count increases susceptibility to large nominal logFC values.

summary: Fars2 did not converge with the available mitochondrial aminoacylation or translation neighbors Lars2, Rars2, and Gfm2.
why_it_matters: Reactome groups FARS2, LARS2, and RARS2 with mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation and GFM2 with mitochondrial translation, but the measured perturbations did not expose a shared mitochondrial-translation state; Fars2-to-neighbor score correlations were near zero.
main_caveats: All four perturbations were weak by FDR, and only Lars2 and Rars2 are same-pathway aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases; Gfm2 is a broader mitochondrial-translation neighbor.

summary: A genome-wide perturbation-neighbor scan found no meaningful positive or inverse neighbor for the Fars2 signature.
why_it_matters: The strongest correlation to another perturbation was only r=0.029, so nearest-neighbor analysis cannot rescue a mechanistic interpretation from the Fars2 DE table.
main_caveats: The scan used all measured genes across cell types; because the Fars2 signature is largely null, correlations are expected to be dominated by noise.

summary: The FDR-null Fars2 response should not be used to de-risk FARS2 inhibition or loss of function.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic FARS2 variants cause combined oxidative-phosphorylation disease, fatal infantile encephalopathy, and later spastic paraplegia; this dataset lacks the target engagement needed to argue that neuronal FARS2 loss is tolerated.
main_caveats: This is a safety interpretation from human genetics plus a weak mouse Perturb-seq negative result, not a direct druggability or toxicology assay.

summary: Lmx1b targeting produced neither a measurable Lmx1b transcript decrease nor any FDR-significant downstream transcriptome response across 23 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The main biological interpretation is a null or non-engaged perturbation, not a new Lmx1b effector gene list.
main_caveats: This is high confidence for the DE table but cannot distinguish true biological dispensability from low expression, scRNA-seq dropout, or ineffective guide activity.

summary: The dopaminergic class did not test the expected Lmx1b mDA maintenance program effectively because 215 MB Dopa had only 20 perturbed cells and no changes in Lmx1b, Th, Slc6a3, Ddc, Pitx3, Lmx1a, or Nr4a2.
why_it_matters: The absence of a dopamine signature should not be used to argue against the established roles of Lmx1b/Lmx1a in mDA neuron development, autophagy-lysosome function, mitochondria, and survival.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The dataset lacks proof of target engagement and the relevant adult mDA maintenance program may require longer-term loss than this assay captured.

summary: Lmx1b targeting did not affect the measured serotonergic markers Tph2 or Slc6a4 in this panel.
why_it_matters: The known raphe Lmx1b program was not sampled or not engaged, preventing interpretation of this dataset as a test of Lmx1b-dependent serotonin maintenance.
main_caveats: No group name corresponded to raphe serotonergic neurons, and Slc18a2/Vmat2 was not present among the Lmx1b DE rows.

summary: Lmx1b signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Lmx1a, Pitx3, Nr4a2, Foxa2, En1, En2, Otx2, or Tcf7l2 signatures in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: This fails to recover the expected dopaminergic transcription-factor neighborhood from single-perturbation signatures.
main_caveats: Near-zero correlations are likely dominated by non-engaged or weak signatures and should not be interpreted as antagonism among these transcription factors.

summary: Nominal Lmx1b hits were sparse and non-recurrent, with no p<0.01 gene recurring in four or more cell types.
why_it_matters: The table does not support a reusable Lmx1b biomarker or convergent downstream module.
main_caveats: The recurrence audit used a nominal p<0.01 threshold and is descriptive because no row passed FDR correction.

summary: The null mouse Perturb-seq result is not evidence that LMX1B loss is safe or biologically inert.
why_it_matters: Curated human disease links and mDA/5-HT neuron maintenance studies argue that loss-of-function biology can be deleterious even though this particular assay did not engage the relevant programs.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: This is a target-biology warning rather than evidence about any specific LMX1B-directed drug program.

summary: Htr1a perturbation did not measurably reduce Htr1a mRNA in any represented cell class.
why_it_matters: A downstream null signature cannot be interpreted as Htr1a loss of function unless the receptor transcript is actually depleted.
main_caveats: The dataset measures Htr1a transcript abundance, not receptor protein or guide editing efficiency.

summary: Htr1a perturbation generated no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional program across 371,818 tests.
why_it_matters: The strongest nominal genes were isolated and non-significant after correction, so they should not be promoted to a pathway or biomarker signature.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The apparent buffering may actually reflect absent receptor knockdown or sparse Htr1a capture.

summary: No assayed cortical, hippocampal, GABAergic, thalamic, midbrain, or hindbrain cell label showed a selective Htr1a transcriptomic response, including high-count Htr1a contrasts.
why_it_matters: The null was not confined to underpowered cell classes; even 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with 194 perturbed cells and 155 MB Glut with 187 perturbed cells lacked FDR-supported genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: 215 MB Dopa was not represented for Htr1a, several cell classes had fewer than 60 perturbed cells, and the data do not isolate dorsal-raphe serotonergic neurons.

summary: Htr1a signatures were nearly uncorrelated with serotonin-receptor paralogs and selected Gi/o-cAMP pathway neighbors.
why_it_matters: Reactome, STRING, and IUPHAR all place HTR1A in an inhibitory serotonin GPCR neighborhood, so the absence of transcriptomic convergence argues that this perturbation did not engage a shared 5-HT receptor module.
main_caveats: Similarity was assessed on weak Htr1a signatures; lack of convergence may follow from failed Htr1a target engagement rather than receptor-specific pathway insulation.

summary: The Perturb-seq null should not be read as evidence against 5-HT1A as an anxiety or drug target.
why_it_matters: HTR1A is a druggable Gi/o receptor, mouse Htr1a loss changes anxiety-like behavior, and 5-HT1A autoreceptors have rapid GIRK outputs that would be missed by endpoint scRNA-seq.
main_caveats: The external literature differs in species, developmental timing, circuit localization, and assay modality; the dataset did not validate Htr1a protein loss.

direction: target transcript mostly down; downstream response absent at FDR 0.05
summary: Partial Fktn transcript depletion was directionally detectable but no Fktn perturbation produced an FDR-significant downstream RNA response in the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The canonical FKTN lesion is loss of α-dystroglycan glycosylation, so the dataset suggests that acute partial Fktn transcript reduction is transcriptionally buffered or invisible to this RNA endpoint.
main_caveats: Target knockdown was itself nominal and all downstream claims are negative after FDR correction.

summary: The strongest nominal Fktn-associated signals were concentrated in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, but those signatures did not coincide with strong Fktn transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: These classes are the best follow-up hypotheses, yet the discordance between response magnitude and on-target depletion warns against treating Plxdc2, Fscn1, Bin1, or Pcp4 as robust FKTN biomarkers.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: No gene passed FDR 0.05 and Fktn itself was not reduced in the strongest 008 signature.

summary: Fktn RNA signatures were nearly orthogonal to measured α-dystroglycan pathway, ligand, and disease-family perturbations despite known biochemical coupling of these genes.
why_it_matters: The result argues that perturbing different nodes of the DAG1 glycosylation and matrix-linkage axis is not transcriptomically interchangeable in these mouse-brain Perturb-seq data.
main_caveats: Some comparator perturbations also had weak target-transcript engagement, FKRP was not assayed as a comparator, and the comparison uses RNA signatures rather than matriglycan abundance.

summary: No strong or recurrent genome-wide perturbation neighbor emerged for Fktn.
why_it_matters: The absence of a high-correlation neighbor prevents assigning Fktn to an alternate recurrent transcriptional module outside the α-dystroglycan pathway.
main_caveats: Conclusion is restricted to correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors and can miss convergence at protein or glycan levels.

direction: canonical biochemical pathway not expressed as a strong acute RNA module
summary: The Perturb-seq phenotype does not recapitulate a dystroglycanopathy transcriptional module, refining FKTN disease biology toward post-translational glycan, ECM-binding, and developmental endpoints.
why_it_matters: For follow-up or rescue experiments, glycosylated α-dystroglycan and laminin-binding metrics are likely to be more proximal than the nominal RNA markers in this dataset.
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure α-dystroglycan glycosylation, laminin binding, muscle cells, or embryonic phenotypes.

summary: FDR-confirmed Ndufa11 mRNA reduction was confined to 155 MB Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: These two glutamatergic classes are the only Ndufa11 contexts in which downstream interpretation is strongly anchored to a measured target-transcript decrease.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Most cell types showed only nominal or non-significant target-transcript decreases, and several had fewer than 70 perturbed cells.

direction: Ndufa11 down without a significant secondary transcriptome
summary: Even where Ndufa11 was depleted at FDR level, the response was transcriptionally buffered: no non-target gene passed FDR<0.1.
why_it_matters: NDUFA11 is in Complex I and respiratory electron transport, so the absence of a secondary mRNA program prevents a simple oxidative-phosphorylation stress interpretation from this Perturb-seq readout alone.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The assay measured mRNA rather than Complex I protein, assembly, respiration, ROS, or viability; buffered transcriptomes do not prove normal mitochondrial function.

direction: Ndufa11 weaker target engagement and weak convergence
summary: Ndufa11 was a weaker and less recurrent Complex I perturbation than multiple other assayed Nduf subunits.
why_it_matters: Although these genes sit in the same respiratory-chain neighborhood, Ndufa11 cannot be used as an interchangeable proxy for pan-Complex-I transcriptional perturbation in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: This is a comparison of measured own-transcript engagement and transcriptome signatures, not a protein-level comparison of Complex I loss.

direction: disease gene down with no FDR-level secondary transcriptome
summary: The screen decouples partial adult neuronal Ndufa11 mRNA depletion from the severe Complex I-deficiency phenotypes caused by inherited NDUFA11 loss.
why_it_matters: Human NDUFA11 variants can cause infantile lactic acidemia or encephalocardiomyopathy, but the engaged mouse neuronal classes did not mount a broad mRNA stress response, pointing to non-transcriptional OXPHOS failure, developmental context, stronger loss-of-function, or cell-extrinsic physiology as plausible disease-relevant layers.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The disease evidence is human germline biology, whereas the dataset is a mouse-brain single-cell transcriptomic perturbation with partial knockdown and no respiratory biochemistry.

direction: absence of DE is not evidence of safety
summary: A flat Ndufa11 Perturb-seq signature should not be interpreted as evidence that NDUFA11 or Complex I inhibition is innocuous.
why_it_matters: Complex I is an essential OXPHOS machine linked to primary mitochondrial disease; mRNA buffering after Ndufa11 perturbation could miss loss of electron transport, ATP production, or cell fitness.
main_caveats: No small-molecule inhibition, viability assay, or mitochondrial physiology was measured here.

summary: No strong positive or negative same-cell-type transcriptomic neighbor emerged for Ndufa11 in the two engaged classes.
why_it_matters: The Ndufa11 contrasts are dominated by the target transcript itself rather than by a reusable multi-gene signature shared with another perturbation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The correlation search was restricted to cell types with FDR-level Ndufa11 depletion and weak Ndufa11 signatures limit neighbor detection.

summary: Cdkal1 perturbation produced a broadly buffered brain transcriptome with only two FDR-significant gene changes across 22 cell-type contrasts and no FDR-confirmed decrease of the Cdkal1 transcript itself.
why_it_matters: CDKAL1 is a translational-fidelity enzyme, so the lack of a broad RNA stress signature argues that the assayed mature neuronal classes either experienced weak enzyme loss, buffered the deficit, or expressed consequences mainly outside the poly(A) transcriptome.
main_caveats: Protein loss and tRNA ms2t6A37 were not measured; every target-transcript row failed FDR, so weak perturbation is a plausible explanation.

summary: Eef1a2 upregulation was the most reproducible molecular output of Cdkal1 perturbation and reached FDR significance in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: EEF1A2 acts in aminoacyl-tRNA delivery during elongation, so recurrent induction after perturbing a tRNA(Lys) decoding enzyme is a biologically coherent but still hypothesis-generating compensation signal.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only one cell type passed FDR; the compensation interpretation is based on transcript abundance, not elongation activity or codon-specific translation measurements.

summary: Ggps1 was selectively induced in 145 MH-LH TH Glut without coordinate induction of other measured mevalonate or prenylation genes.
why_it_matters: The dataset links Cdkal1 to a geranylgeranyl-diphosphate synthase readout in one hypothalamic/thalamic glutamatergic class, but the lack of pathway-wide support prevents calling a canonical mevalonate response.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Ggps1 was the only FDR-significant gene in the contrast and was measured in only 44 perturbed cells.

summary: Cdkal1 was not interchangeable with Elp1 or Elp2 tRNA-modification perturbations in hindbrain/thalamic and midbrain neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This separates CDKAL1 tRNA(Lys)-A37 methylthiolation from Elongator-dependent wobble U34 modification at the level of cell-type-resolved transcriptional output.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The compared genes act on different tRNA positions and are not subunits of one complex; the contrast therefore tests related tRNA-modification biology rather than a one-to-one paralog relationship.

summary: Downstream Cdkal1 output was decoupled from measurable Cdkal1 mRNA knockdown across cell types.
why_it_matters: The cell type with the largest nominal target-transcript decrease, 052 Pvalb Gaba, had no FDR-significant genes, whereas the two FDR hits occurred in cell types where the target transcript itself was not nominally depleted.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Cdkal1 mRNA is an imperfect proxy for guide activity and no cell type showed FDR-level target depletion.

summary: Cdkal1 did not converge with the assayed type-2-diabetes disease-family genes Tcf7l2, Kcnq1, or Irs1 in the brain Perturb-seq signatures.
why_it_matters: Although these genes share diabetes genetics or insulin-pathway relevance, the neuronal RNA phenotypes were essentially uncorrelated, cautioning against treating diabetes-associated targets as one interchangeable brain module.
main_caveats: The comparison used brain DE signatures, not pancreatic islets or glucose-stimulated insulin secretion assays.

summary: Ankfy1 perturbation produced a globally buffered transcriptional phenotype under mild target-transcript engagement, with no FDR-significant genes in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: ANKFY1 is a documented Rab5/PI3P early-endosome effector, so the absence of an acute FDR-level mRNA program indicates that its neuronal loss is either incompletely engaged, buffered, or primarily manifested as local trafficking rather than broad transcriptional change.
main_caveats: Target mRNA depletion was only nominal and protein depletion was not measured.

summary: Ankfy1 mRNA itself, not any downstream gene, was the only recurrent same-direction nominal marker of the perturbation.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of isolated nominal hits such as Drg1 and keeps the target transcript as the only plausible proximal readout in this weak signature.
main_caveats: Nominal recurrence is not FDR-corrected and does not establish a production-grade biomarker.

summary: Ankfy1 did not phenocopy Vps35 or high-signal endolysosomal comparator perturbations in the same matrix.
why_it_matters: Rank-5 has documented links to EHD1 and retromer machinery, but the transcriptome places partial Ankfy1 loss far from Vps35 and from broader trafficking/autophagy-adjacent perturbations, arguing against using those perturbations as interchangeable transcriptional proxies.
main_caveats: Only Vps35 is a direct documented Rank-5/retromer comparator here; other comparators sample broader endolysosomal or autophagy-adjacent biology.

summary: The 308 CB GABA stratum lacked an acute Ankfy1 response despite nominal target knockdown, refining mouse Purkinje-cell literature toward a late, cell-identity-specific, or local maintenance mechanism.
why_it_matters: A reported aging Purkinje-cell degeneration phenotype need not imply a large short-term cerebellar GABA transcriptional response after partial Ankfy1 perturbation.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA may not isolate Purkinje cells, and the Perturb-seq endpoint is acute and transcriptomic whereas the mouse phenotype was age dependent.

summary: Signature-neighbor analysis did not identify a robust ANKFY1 module.
why_it_matters: The top Ankfy1 correlations were weak and partly involved safe-target labels, so neighbor-based pathway discovery would be unstable for this perturbation.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on genome-wide Wilcoxon score vectors and is sensitive to weak Ankfy1 signal-to-noise.

summary: Crhr1 perturbation was globally weak: no tested transcript in any of 22 neuronal classes passed FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: CRHR1 is a stress-neuropeptide GPCR linked to cAMP/ERK signaling, so the absence of a corrected basal transcriptional program argues that receptor perturbation was either poorly engaged, buffered, or not captured by steady-state RNA readout in this dataset.
main_caveats: The result is negative at transcript level only; weak corrected on-target transcript effects mean it cannot rule out CRHR1 protein loss or acute signaling effects.

summary: The most nominateable Crhr1 contexts separated into a near-threshold NP-CT-L6b-OB Dnajc13 signal and a CNU-HYa/HY GABA nominal on-target signal rather than one coherent responsive cell type.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-calling one cell class as the CRHR1 effector population: the only FDR<0.1 non-target gene occurred in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, while the strongest Crhr1 transcript decrease occurred in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and still lacked corrected downstream genes.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Dnajc13 was only FDR<0.1 and not FDR<0.05; the CNU-HYa/HY GABA target decrease had FDR=1.0.

summary: Crhr1 perturbation did not induce the expected ligand/receptor-family or cAMP/ERK immediate-early transcriptional outputs.
why_it_matters: CRH-activated CRHR1 is known to signal through adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, and ERK; the lack of Fos/Jun/Egr/Nr4a/Crem/Dusp5/Rgs2 responses, and lack of Crh/Crhr2/urocortin transcript compensation, suggests that basal Crhr1 editing was uncoupled from the canonical ligand-activated pathway at RNA level.
main_caveats: The literature is dominated by ligand-stimulation and phosphorylation assays, whereas the dataset measures steady-state RNA after genetic perturbation.

summary: Downstream cAMP/PKA/CREB-axis perturbations were much more transcriptionally penetrant than the upstream CRH receptor perturbation and were not correlated with it.
why_it_matters: This argues that Crhr1 is not interchangeable with core second-messenger nodes in the assayed cells; perturbing Prkaca, Adcy3, Prkar1a, or Creb1 can be detected, while Crhr1 produces neither corrected hits nor a matching score vector.
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations may have different guide efficiency and direct transcript detectability; the comparison is signature-level, not biochemical cAMP measurement.

summary: A genome-scale signature-neighbor search found no high-correlation positive or negative Crhr1 partner.
why_it_matters: The weak Crhr1 phenotype was not rescued by a hidden convergence with another perturbation class: even the top positive and negative neighbors had |r| near 0.2 or lower, and no curated cAMP neighbor approached that level.
main_caveats: Correlation used Wilcoxon score vectors and can miss nonlinear or sparse-gene relationships.

summary: The basal neuronal Crhr1-targeting signature gives little transcriptomic support for CRFR1 antagonist-like efficacy by itself.
why_it_matters: A completed GSK561679 PTSD trial posted similar six-week CAPS changes versus placebo, and the dataset likewise shows that simply targeting Crhr1 does not create a strong molecular shift across broad mouse brain neuronal classes; CRHR1 pharmacology may need stress state, ligand tone, region, or biomarker stratification to be visible.
main_caveats: The clinical trial involved adult women with PTSD and an acute antagonist, whereas the dataset is mouse brain Perturb-seq; efficacy cannot be inferred directly from transcriptomic weakness.

direction: target transcript down; downstream response absent
summary: Map6 mRNA was partially depleted but the perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional program in any cell type.
why_it_matters: MAP6 loss has strong cytoskeletal, synaptic, and behavioral effects in mouse models, so the Perturb-seq data suggest that acute partial Map6 loss is buffered at the RNA level or that the main phenotype is non-transcriptional.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The strongest target logFC was only -0.499 and Map6 itself did not pass FDR correction; the assay did not measure MAP6 protein, microtubule stability, axonal transport, or synaptic physiology.

summary: Recoverable Map6 target-transcript knockdown was concentrated in a small set of midbrain, thalamic, hypothalamic, and GABAergic signatures and was weak in several other groups.
why_it_matters: This separates cell types in which a missing downstream response is interpretable from cell types where the guide did not measurably lower Map6 mRNA.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Target mRNA is a proxy for perturbation efficiency; baseline Map6 expression and protein depletion were not measured in this parquet.

summary: Map6 signatures were not transcriptionally similar to assayed microtubule, motor/transport, AMPAR, NMDAR, or Dlg4 perturbations.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a simple shared RNA module linking Map6 to tubulin-stabilization or NMDAR-like perturbation, even though MAP6 is connected to microtubule organization and synaptic plasticity in the literature.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on RNA score vectors only; lack of a shared transcriptional signature does not rule out cytoskeletal or electrophysiologic coupling.

summary: The Map6 screen did not nominate a robust recurrent non-target biomarker.
why_it_matters: Nominal genes such as Sco2 or Map7d2 are hypothesis-generating only and should not be treated as a Map6 response module without orthogonal validation.
main_caveats: The recurrence summary uses nominal p<0.05 events after observing no FDR-significant genes; it is suitable only for prioritizing follow-up.

direction: no FDR-supported Map6 RNA response despite rescue literature
summary: The dataset does not supply an acute RNA pharmacodynamic marker for the microtubule-stabilizer rescue axis described in STOP/MAP6-null mice.
why_it_matters: Epothilone D rescue of knockout phenotypes should be followed with morphology, transport, and synaptic assays rather than assuming a MAP6-specific transcriptional reversal signature.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment tested genetic Map6 perturbation, not epothilone D treatment; ChEMBL absence is not proof that MAP6 cannot be modulated indirectly.

summary: Isl1 perturbation produced no FDR-supported target-transcript or downstream transcriptomic response in any of the 23 profiled broad mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A genome-wide null result changes interpretation: other nominal genes should not be treated as an ISL1 regulatory program without independent validation of target engagement.

why_it_matters: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 215 MB Dopa should be regarded as nominal outliers or low-count contrasts rather than definitive ISL1-sensitive states.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Signals are nominal; all listed top genes had FDR >= 0.141 and some came from contrasts with 22-46 perturbed cells.

summary: The LGE/striatal broad GABA class lacked perturbation of Isl1, Lhx8, cholinergic genes, and direct- or indirect-pathway markers after Isl1 targeting.
why_it_matters: Known Isl1 roles in embryonic forebrain cholinergic and striatonigral differentiation did not appear at the broad 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA level, warning that subtype dilution or developmental timing can mask canonical ISL1 biology.

main_caveats: The cell class is broad, the assay is not embryonic, and there was no transcript-level proof of Isl1 depletion.

summary: Isl1 did not show transcriptomic convergence with Lhx3 or a panel of related developmental transcription-factor perturbations.
why_it_matters: The result does not support a shared adult-brain signature for the embryonic Isl1-Lhx3 or Isl1-Lhx8 circuitry, but the interpretation is limited by the weak Isl1 signature.
main_caveats: Restricted to score-vector correlations of weak signatures; Lhx8 was measured as a transcript but was not available as a perturbation comparator.

summary: The experiment did not reveal an actionable adult-brain ISL1 output despite ISL1's curated developmental-pathway and human congenital-heart-disease context.
why_it_matters: A nuclear LIM-homeodomain TF with no ChEMBL target entry and no corrected adult-brain Perturb-seq response is not supported here as a directly druggable brain target or directional pathway node.
main_caveats: Reactome and disease annotations are mostly developmental and non-neuronal; ChEMBL absence is not proof of undruggability.

summary: Grm6 perturbation produced no reliable on-target repression and no FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic response in 22 assayed mouse-brain neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Without target engagement or FDR-significant downstream genes, the Grm6 vectors should be interpreted as a null or non-expressed-target result rather than as a brain mGluR6 loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: Aggregate DE only; cannot distinguish inactive guides from lack of endogenous Grm6 expression, and three cell types lacked a Grm6 target row.

summary: The lowest Grm6 nominal p values are scattered cell-type-specific outliers rather than a reproducible FDR-supported module.
why_it_matters: Mbd2, Prkci, Sik3, Supt16, and Gale should be treated as exploratory biomarkers at most; their adjusted p values and lack of recurrence do not support a mechanistic claim.

summary: Figla perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response across 22 profiled mouse-brain cell types.

summary: The brain-wide null response refines FIGLA disease biology toward ovarian and germ-cell mechanisms rather than neuronal vulnerability.

summary: Nominal Ndufs1 transcript lowering was present only in a subset of neuronal classes.

summary: Respiratory-chain transcripts did not form a coordinated Ndufs1-dependent module.
why_it_matters: The expected Complex I/electron-transport pathway was genetically targeted, but steady-state OXPHOS mRNAs did not respond at FDR level, implying that functional assays are required to detect any mitochondrial defect.
main_caveats: The respiratory-gene panel was evaluated at the mRNA level only and under weak Ndufs1 knockdown.

summary: FDR-negative Ndufs1 scRNA-seq should not be interpreted as safe suppression of a human Complex I disease gene.
why_it_matters: NDUFS1 loss-of-function biology is clinically deleterious, so this dataset mainly warns that acute transcriptomics can miss mitochondrial dysfunction when knockdown is partial.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The disease evidence is human and often biallelic or severe, whereas the dataset is mouse neuronal CRISPR perturbation with partial transcript lowering.

summary: Adar target-mRNA depletion was directionally consistent but FDR-level target engagement was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells.
why_it_matters: Interpretation should focus on the two engaged neuronal classes; the other Adar contrasts mostly test a weak knockdown rather than a clean loss of ADAR RNA-editing function.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: FDR-level self-knockdown was assessed at the transcript level only; the assay did not measure ADAR protein or A-to-I editing activity.

summary: The two FDR-engaged Adar knockdowns were transcriptionally buffered: Adar itself was the only gene crossing FDR in 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: The direct perturbation was detectable, but the acute steady-state mRNA response did not expand into a broad secondary program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

summary: Adar knockdown did not induce a canonical MDA5/MAVS or interferon-stimulated-gene module in the two engaged neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Classical ADAR1 loss unmasks endogenous dsRNA and activates MDA5-MAVS/type-I-interferon signaling in embryos and in ADAR-mutant human disease; this Perturb-seq result argues that partial acute neuronal Adar depletion is not sufficient to reproduce that disease program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The mismatch is indirect because the dataset used incomplete, acute transcript knockdown in named neuronal classes, whereas published effects involve editing-deficient or null ADAR1 alleles, developmental tissues, whole animals, or human genetic disease.

summary: Adar and the paralog Adarb1 were not interchangeable in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells: both target transcripts were depleted, yet their whole-transcriptome signatures were essentially uncorrelated.
why_it_matters: The result preserves an ADAR-family divergence that agrees with specialized ADAR1 versus ADAR2 biology rather than treating both dsRNA deaminases as a single perturbation class.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The Adarb1 signature was heavily Flnb-centered, so guide-specific or off-target contributions cannot be excluded.

summary: Adar did not have a robust positive or negative signature neighbor in either FDR-engaged cell class.
why_it_matters: The closest correlations were below 0.084 and even included a safe-target control in 155 MB Glut, so the sparse Adar profile should not be over-interpreted as converging on any coordinated neighbor pathway.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The analysis uses simple Pearson correlations over Wilcoxon-score vectors and no replicate-level uncertainty for the correlations.

summary: Add2 perturbation caused broad nominal depletion of the Add2 transcript but no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: The dataset points to a target-centered and transcriptionally buffered phenotype, consistent with ADD2 acting through cytoskeletal and synaptic structures rather than a large acute mRNA program.
main_caveats: The Add2 target row was nominal but not FDR-significant, so the buffered downstream result could reflect incomplete knockdown in some cell types.

summary: Nominal Add2 engagement was concentrated in a small set of hypothalamic/midbrain, cortical L5 ET, and brainstem GABA/glutamate classes, while the CA/DG glutamatergic contrasts that most closely echo hippocampal knockout work were weak.
why_it_matters: Prior Add2-null phenotypes are hippocampal and synaptic; the Perturb-seq result refines that literature by showing that this single-cell mRNA assay did not engage or report those hippocampal programs robustly.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut

summary: Add2 did not phenocopy Add1, Add3, Sptan1, Sptb, ankyrin, or Epb41l1 perturbations at the transcriptome level despite their membrane-skeleton proximity.
why_it_matters: The result warns against assuming that physical membership in the spectrin-actin/adducin network will produce interchangeable single-cell RNA signatures.
main_caveats: The contrast is restricted by weak Add2, Add1, and Add3 signatures; absence of correlation is evidence only for this scRNA-seq readout.

summary: Cells with the clearest Add2 mRNA reduction did not show FDR-supported Add1/Add3, dematin, spectrin, ankyrin, or Epb41l1 mRNA compensation.
why_it_matters: Published Add2 knockout compensation involves alpha/gamma adducin protein abundance or phosphorylation; the acute single-cell dataset suggests that these adaptations are not immediate transcript-level replacements.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA

summary: A buffered mRNA phenotype should not be interpreted as Add2 loss-of-function safety because mouse Add2 loss impairs synaptic plasticity, learning, motor coordination, and new-synapse assembly.
why_it_matters: If ADD2 were considered for perturbation pharmacologically or genetically, morphology, synaptic physiology, and longer-term assays would be needed; steady-state scRNA-seq provides no robust safety biomarker here.
main_caveats: No ADD2 drug was evaluated; the warning is inferred from genetic loss-of-function literature plus a negative transcriptomic readout.

summary: Ap4s1 targeting produced no FDR-significant transcriptome-wide response in any tested neuronal cell type.
why_it_matters: The absence of corrected DE prevents a high-confidence claim of an Ap4s1-responsive transcriptional program and makes target engagement the main interpretive bottleneck.
main_caveats: The negative result could reflect inefficient knockdown, low Ap4s1 expression, slow trafficking phenotypes, or limited cells per type rather than true dispensability.

summary: The closest cell-type-specific response was an unvalidated 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut near-miss, not a robust selective hit.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Extl3 and Dvl3 reached only FDR 0.112846 in 43 perturbed cells; all other cell-type minima were farther from significance.

summary: Ap4s1 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce or repress the known AP-4 cargo, accessory, AP-4-subunit, or autophagy genes that are central to AP-4 biology.
why_it_matters: The result argues that acute single-cell RNA effects are uncoupled from the protein-sorting phenotypes by which AP-4 loss mislocalizes ATG9A and related cargo.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an indirect readout for AP-4-dependent cargo localization, and weak Ap4s1 knockdown may further attenuate pathway readout.

summary: Ap4s1 behaved differently from several other vesicle-coat or autophagy perturbations: AP-2 and Cltc perturbations generated corrected signatures, whereas Ap4s1 did not and was essentially uncorrelated with them.
why_it_matters: This indicates that the Ap4s1 dataset is not showing a generic clathrin/adaptor stress state and that AP-4 biology cannot be inferred by borrowing AP-1, AP-2, AP-3, Cltc, or autophagy signatures.
main_caveats: The true AP-4 partners Ap4b1, Ap4e1, and Ap4m1 were not perturbed, so this is a related-pathway rather than same-complex comparison.

summary: Genome-wide signature neighbors did not reveal a reproducible Ap4s1-convergent perturbation.
why_it_matters: The strongest correlations were modest and confined to cerebellar GABA neurons, so they are better treated as exploratory neighbor statistics than as mechanistic rescue or phenocopy relationships.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Neighbor analysis is restricted to weak Ap4s1 signatures; correlations near |0.35| may be dominated by noise or cell-state imbalance.

summary: The dataset supports a warning that AP4S1 rescue screens should not rely on short-term mRNA biomarkers alone.
why_it_matters: Published AP-4 disease assays focus on cargo localization, especially ATG9A, whereas the mRNAs for ATG9A, DAGLB, SERINC cargoes, and autophagy regulators were silent in this Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: This is a readout warning, not evidence that AP4S1 protein trafficking was normal in the perturbed cells.

summary: Il21r perturbation produced no detectable target-transcript knockdown and no FDR-significant downstream response in any profiled neuronal class.
why_it_matters: This prevents assigning the nominal genes to IL21R biology and makes weak target engagement the central interpretation of the perturbation.
main_caveats: High confidence for the measured absence of FDR signal; it does not prove that IL21R protein was knocked out or that IL21R is irrelevant in unprofiled immune or glial cells.

summary: The largest Il21r nominal hits were cell-type isolated and too weak after FDR correction to define a CA3, cortical, or hypothalamic selective program.

summary: The expected IL21R-common-gamma/JAK-STAT axis was not coherently represented in neuronal perturbation signatures.

summary: Inflammatory CNS literature on IL21R does not generalize to a constitutive basal-neuron Il21r dependency in this dataset.
why_it_matters: IL-21R may still be relevant in MS or stroke lesions with infiltrating IL21-producing immune cells, but this Perturb-seq result suggests therapeutic effects of IL-21 blockade should not be assumed to come from direct effects on uninjured glutamatergic or GABAergic neurons.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The disease studies used inflamed human or ischemic mouse contexts, whereas the Perturb-seq assay profiled basal mouse neuronal transcriptomes and did not include immune-cell readouts.

summary: Camkmt perturbation produced no FDR-supported differential expression in any of 22 assayed neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: This prevents pathway or cell-type activation claims from being made from the processed Camkmt RNA table.
main_caveats: A preserved Camkmt transcript does not exclude DNA editing or protein loss; protein and calmodulin methylation were not measured.

summary: Same-dataset Calm1 and Calm3 perturbations showed robust own-transcript repression, whereas Camkmt did not and was transcriptionally uncorrelated with calmodulin/CaM-kinase perturbations.
why_it_matters: The Camkmt null cannot be explained by a universal inability to detect perturbations of the calmodulin axis in these cell types.
main_caveats: The comparison uses transcript-wide score correlations, not shared protein methylation measurements.

summary: Camkmt perturbation did not induce transcriptional compensation in Calm1/2/3 or Camk2a/b/g/4 even though CAMKMT is a post-translational calmodulin methyltransferase.
why_it_matters: The expected primary perturbation is loss of trimethyl-calmodulin, so the RNA null may reflect pathway buffering or a readout mismatch rather than absence of biochemical impact.
main_caveats: No assay of CAMKMT protein or methylated calmodulin was present.

summary: The dataset did not show a supported cell-autonomous RNA counterpart of the reported Camkmt mouse knockout brain and mitochondrial phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Organismal CAMKMT biology may require strong protein-level loss, developmental windows, mitochondrial functional assays, or multicellular physiology beyond this scRNA-seq screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure calmodulin methylation, respiratory-chain activity, behavior, or development.

summary: The strongest nominal genes, including Fbxo6 and Senp7, were high-FDR and nonrecurrent, making them weak biomarker leads.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Recurrence was assessed by score cutoffs in the processed Wilcoxon table and does not rule out small true effects.

summary: The top positive and negative whole-signature neighbors of Camkmt were weak and did not define a stable convergent module.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on processed score vectors; the top neighbors were not mechanistically interpreted.

summary: Aff2 perturbation produced a single transcriptome-wide significant response: Susd4 was downregulated in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: SUSD4/Susd4 is a complement-related synaptic regulator in mouse nervous-system studies, and Fmr2 loss perturbs learning and hippocampal LTP; the dataset therefore nominates Susd4 loss as the clearest measurable Aff2 output rather than a broad elongation signature.
