main_caveats: The Susd4 hit is robust after FDR correction, but the same cells did not show detectable Aff2 mRNA depletion; this could reflect sparse Aff2 detection, isoform effects, or confounding, so Susd4 should be treated as a candidate biomarker rather than a proven direct target.

summary: Measured Aff2 target engagement and downstream gene-level responses were weak across most cell types.
why_it_matters: AFF2 is annotated to RNA binding, splicing, and transcriptional elongation biology, but this Perturb-seq readout found only one FDR<0.05 gene across 371,818 Aff2 tests and no corrected Aff2 mRNA knockdown, arguing that most cell-type signatures are buffered, underpowered, or not captured by gene-level expression.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: A weak target-transcript readout cannot distinguish true biological buffering from low knockdown efficiency, low Aff2 expression, or failure of gene-level single-cell RNA-seq to capture isoform and splicing consequences.

summary: Aff2 signatures were essentially orthogonal to Aff3 and Fmr1 signatures, including in the L4/5 IT cell type where Aff2 downregulated Susd4.
why_it_matters: AFF3 is an AF4/FMR2-family paralog and Fmr1 is a fragile-X disease-family comparator, yet neither reproduced the Susd4 response or produced correlated genome-wide signatures; the dataset therefore refines the prior expectation from shared family membership toward cell-type- and paralog-specific outputs.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The comparison uses genome-wide score correlations, not matched protein depletion, and no direct literature predicts that Aff2 and Aff3 or Fmr1 must regulate Susd4 in mouse L4/5 IT neurons.

direction: weak positive and weak negative neighbors
summary: The all-perturbation signature-neighbor search found no strong recurrent Aff2 mimic or antagonist.
why_it_matters: The best positive and negative correlations to Aff2 were both only about |r|=0.2 and occurred in a single hippocampal/dentate glutamatergic class, so the screen does not support a robust convergent pathway neighbor that could replace the sparse direct DE readout.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: This is a restricted-signature computation from Wilcoxon scores; weak correlations can be driven by noise or generic state shifts and should not be interpreted as direct physical or pathway relationships.

summary: Bmpr1a loss produced a dataset-wide null or buffered transcriptional phenotype across all 22 measured neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: BMPR1A is a core BMP type-I receptor, so absence of any FDR-supported DE changes the interpretation from a pathway perturbation to a weakly engaged or redundant perturbation in mature neuronal states.
main_caveats: The target transcript was not significantly depleted, so the null could reflect poor CRISPRi engagement rather than complete biological buffering.

summary: Canonical BMP-SMAD response and feedback transcripts were not FDR-shifted by Bmpr1a perturbation.
why_it_matters: The lack of Id-family or feedback-gene movement argues against a hidden tonic BMPR1A-SMAD transcriptional state in the assayed neurons.
main_caveats: These are RNA readouts rather than phospho-SMAD measurements, and their baseline expression may be sparse in some neuronal groups.

summary: Bmpr1a did not converge with perturbations of BMP/TGF receptor or SMAD neighbors, despite those genes belonging to a strongly connected BMP receptor-SMAD module.
why_it_matters: A pathway-core target should often resemble at least one adjacent receptor or SMAD perturbation if the pathway is active and the perturbations are engaged; near-zero correlations argue against a coherent Bmpr1a-like module in this dataset.
main_caveats: Most related perturbations were themselves weak; the comparison used transcriptomic score correlations, not direct receptor activity.

summary: The apparent CNU-LGE LSX GABA Bmpr1a signal is the strongest nominal cell-type lead but is not statistically credible after correction.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of Mcu/Cop1 and other nominal hits as a striatal GABA BMP response.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Only 53 perturbed cells were available and the two leading genes had FDR=0.724.

summary: The neuronal null refines known BMPR1A brain biology toward developmental stem/progenitor, astrocytic, and hippocampal-niche contexts that were absent from the screen.
why_it_matters: BMPRIA has clear mouse brain functions, but their literature contexts differ from acute perturbation in mature glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons; this distinction matters for assigning mechanism to a negative Perturb-seq result.
main_caveats: The dataset does not resolve whether Bmpr1a would be active in astrocytes, endothelial cells, choroid plexus, or neural stem-cell populations.

summary: The Bmpr1a neuronal null should not be used as evidence that pharmacologic ALK3/BMPR1A inhibition is brain-inert.
why_it_matters: BMP type-I inhibitors can hit BMPR1A/ALK3, but weak target knockdown and missing glial/progenitor compartments limit safety or efficacy inference from this screen.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic CRISPR dataset, not a small-molecule dose-response experiment; inhibitor selectivity and developmental exposure are not modeled.

summary: Cckar loss produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic phenotype and no measurable Cckar self-depletion in any of the 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is assay-level failure to engage a sparse GPCR transcript, not evidence that CCKAR signaling is biologically irrelevant in brain.
main_caveats: Negative downstream calls are conditioned on absent Cckar knockdown; raw expression and guide-level data were not available.

summary: Cerebellar GABA cells contained the only multi-gene, same-direction Cckar nominal response, led by Efr3b, Sh2d5, Unc5c, Syn2 and Snph up-regulation.
why_it_matters: This gives a concrete follow-up signature for a cell type where the scalar experiment was otherwise formally negative.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All genes were above FDR 0.10 and the Cckar transcript itself was not depleted in this cell type.

summary: The ligand Cck was directly and significantly depleted in three neuronal populations, whereas both receptor perturbations, Cckar and Cckbr, lacked adjusted on-target knockdown.
why_it_matters: The CCK axis in this dataset is ligand-accessible but receptor-limited; ligand expression should not be read as evidence for broad autocrine CCK receptor signaling in the same coarse cell classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: This compares transcript knockdown of ligand and receptors, not secreted CCK peptide release or receptor activity.

summary: Cckar score vectors did not align with perturbations of assayed PLC/IP3 or adenylyl-cyclase signaling neighbors.
why_it_matters: Canonical CCK1R biology predicts second-messenger signaling after receptor activation; the dataset did not activate a detectable transcriptional version of that pathway after Cckar perturbation.
main_caveats: Correlations are calculated from a very weak Cckar signature and the dataset did not include the proximal Gnaq or Gna11 perturbations.

summary: In the only cell class with a reproducible-looking Cckar nominal profile, 308 CB GABA, the top restricted-signature neighbors were Wdr26 in the same direction and Ranbp2 in the opposite direction rather than Cck or Cckbr.
why_it_matters: This keeps a potentially informative off-axis cerebellar-state relationship visible while marking it as exploratory.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is correlation-based over a subthreshold Cckar profile and does not establish a mechanistic Wdr26 or Ranbp2 connection to CCKAR.

summary: The absence of a Cckar brain Perturb-seq phenotype should not be used as a central-safety readout for drugging CCK1R.
why_it_matters: CCKAR is a tractable GPCR with metabolic therapeutic interest, but this experiment did not demonstrate receptor knockdown in human-relevant sparse CCKAR-expressing regions such as hypothalamus or midbrain.
main_caveats: Therapeutic literature is mainly peripheral or vagal-metabolic, whereas the Perturb-seq assay is mouse brain with no Cckar on-target engagement.

summary: Fmn1 guide assignment produced no FDR-supported target-transcript depletion or genome-wide transcriptional response in any assayed brain class.
why_it_matters: This is the primary interpretive result: downstream negatives cannot be read as Fmn1 dispensability because the mRNA data do not validate on-target engagement.
main_caveats: The result is an mRNA endpoint with 25-156 perturbed cells per class; it cannot exclude protein-level editing or morphology-only phenotypes.

summary: Known Fmn1 actin-nucleation, adherens-junction, and focal-adhesion partners were transcriptionally silent after Fmn1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: It separates canonical Fmn1 cytoskeletal biology from the lack of a Perturb-seq mRNA signature and argues that morphology or protein-localization assays are needed for this target.
main_caveats: The analysis tested transcript abundance of selected pathway genes, not actin filament assembly, focal adhesions, dendritic spines, or protein activity.

summary: The best Fmn1 cell-type hints were nominal and mixed: isolated Ccdc107 and Rgs7 rows plus a 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA cluster led by Nell2, Rtn1, and Agbl4.
why_it_matters: These rows are the only places the dataset suggests possible cell-type restriction, but their lack of FDR support makes them replication seeds rather than conclusions.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Every highlighted row has FDR >= 0.199811, and the densest 059 signal used only 40 Fmn1-perturbed cells.

summary: Fmn1 did not share a transcriptome-wide signature with the related formin perturbations Fmn2 or Diaph2.
why_it_matters: The panel contains related cytoskeletal formins, but their signatures do not rescue or validate interpretation of the weak Fmn1 profile.
main_caveats: Fmn1 lacked validated target engagement, and Diaph2 was present in only two low-count classes.

summary: A search for positive and negative signature neighbors found no stable Fmn1-like perturbation module.
why_it_matters: This guards against overinterpreting a weak individual neighbor or a single noisy cell-class correlation as a hidden biological pathway.
main_caveats: Correlations are computed on weak Fmn1 effects, so absence of a neighbor primarily confirms that the Fmn1 signature is not robust.

summary: CA/DG-containing hippocampal glutamatergic classes did not show the Fmn1 engagement or downstream response expected if the published hippocampal dendritogenesis program were active at the mRNA level in this assay.
why_it_matters: The result narrows the Simon-Areces hippocampal phenotype to a context not captured by this broad-class Perturb-seq readout.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The reference used cultured mouse hippocampal neurons and morphological endpoints, whereas these are broad in vivo-like class labels with weak Fmn1 on-target statistics.

summary: Adcy1 targeting produced a globally buffered basal transcriptome: target mRNA decreased in most measured cell classes, but neither Adcy1 nor any downstream gene reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: ADCY1 is a Ca2+/calmodulin-responsive cAMP generator, so absence of a robust resting transcriptional signature indicates that this Perturb-seq assay is capturing weak basal consequences rather than the activity-dependent AC1 physiology described for neurons.
main_caveats: Target silencing was modest and non-significant after FDR correction; perturbation cell counts were small, with a maximum of 88 cells per class.

summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba was the clearest candidate site of Adcy1 engagement, but even there the response stopped at nominal Adcy1 loss.
why_it_matters: The finding narrows follow-up validation to a plausible inhibitory-neuron context while preventing over-interpretation of the Lrrtm4 and other nominal non-self rows as an AC1-regulated module.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only 55 Adcy1-targeted Pvalb cells were available and the on-target row had FDR=0.121, so this is a candidate cell-type restriction, not a confirmed cell-specific program.

summary: Hippocampal-enriched glutamatergic classes did not reproduce the strong Adcy1 physiology expected from LTP and memory studies.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse work ties AC1/AC8 to hippocampal synaptic plasticity; the weak 012 MEA/LA/CA1/DG and 017 CA3/CA2-FC/DG transcriptional signals separate that activity-dependent electrophysiology from basal single-cell RNA abundance after partial Adcy1 perturbation.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The hippocampal classes were broad and underpowered, with 29 and 39 perturbed cells, and the assay did not stimulate synaptic activity or measure cAMP, ERK, or electrophysiology.

summary: Adcy1 lacked a coherent ADCY, calcium/calmodulin, G-protein or PKA signature neighbor despite pathway proximity to several perturbed genes.
why_it_matters: The near-zero correlations argue that Adcy1 should not be treated as interchangeable with Adcy3, Gnas, Calm1/3 or Prkaca for transcriptional-state inference in this dataset.
main_caveats: Most scalar correlations were computed over weak signatures; the result is best read as failure to detect convergence, not proof that these nodes are biologically independent.

summary: The weak normal-brain response does not phenocopy disease or pain settings in which reducing ADCY1 was beneficial.
why_it_matters: Fragile-X and chronic-pain studies support AC1 inhibition in activated disease circuits, whereas this screen suggests that resting wild-type neuronal transcriptomes are largely silent after modest Adcy1 perturbation; therapeutic biomarkers should therefore track cAMP/ERK or disease-state activity rather than expecting a universal steady-state RNA signature.
main_caveats: The dataset contains normal mouse brain cell classes, not Fmr1-deficient neurons, injured anterior cingulate cortex, nociceptive circuits, drug treatments, or direct AC1 inhibitors.

summary: Il2rg perturbation was transcriptomically silent across all 22 assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: A target expected to sit at the center of immune cytokine signaling produced no FDR-significant neuronal gene-expression response; the result is therefore a strong neuronal negative rather than evidence for gamma-chain pathway activation.
main_caveats: The DE table cannot prove genome editing or protein depletion; the Il2rg transcript itself was extremely sparse, so apparent large logFC values are not useful target-engagement measures.

summary: The only near-threshold Il2rg signal was an exploratory Apba2 decrease in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest single-gene result localizes the weak effect to one L2/3 glutamatergic class, but FDR=0.103 makes it a hypothesis rather than a validated Il2rg effector.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Below FDR<0.10, based on 38 perturbed cells, and unsupported by a coherent signature-neighbor program.

summary: Il2rg targeting did not move measured JAK/STAT receptors, STATs, or SOCS/CISH feedback transcripts in neurons.
why_it_matters: Known IL2RG signaling is routed through gamma-chain interleukin receptors and JAK/STAT, PI3K, and MAPK pathways; their absence from the dataset response supports the interpretation that the neuronal perturbations did not engage a functional cytokine-receptor circuit.
main_caveats: Bulk ranked DE cannot exclude phosphorylation-only pathway changes, and microglia or infiltrating lymphocytes were not part of these assayed neuronal groups.

summary: Gamma-chain receptor partners and STAT5B were also silent and did not converge with Il2rg signatures.
why_it_matters: Perturbations of related receptor subunits did not reveal an interchangeable neuronal module for the gamma-chain family, despite those proteins sharing receptor complexes in immune signaling maps.
main_caveats: This is a loss-of-function transcriptomic comparison in neuronal classes; it does not test ligand-stimulated immune cells in which the receptors are normally active.

summary: The dataset should not be used to infer a neuron-autonomous CNS efficacy or safety direction for IL2RG modulation.
why_it_matters: Human brain expression atlases and microglial literature point IL2RG biology toward leukocytes and brain immune cells, whereas the measured perturbations were neuronal and lacked target engagement.
main_caveats: The warning is about context, not proof that IL2RG lacks CNS roles; direct microglia, border-associated macrophage, or infiltrating-T-cell perturbations are needed.

summary: Mt3 transcript loss is FDR-supported in three cell classes but produces no FDR-supported secondary genes in those classes.
why_it_matters: This separates on-target perturbation from broad downstream response and points to a buffered Mt3 loss state in the assayed transcriptomes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation is transcriptomic and does not assay MT3 protein, zinc, copper, seizure response, or injury challenge.

direction: negative Mt3 logFC in all classes; FDR-supported in a minority
summary: Mt3 target engagement is highly uneven across the 22 measured cell classes.
why_it_matters: Only FDR-engaged classes should drive downstream biological interpretation; weakly engaged classes are primarily negative or underpowered perturbation contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell count, basal Mt3 expression, and guide efficacy are confounded in the target-transcript statistic.

summary: No recurrent downstream gene or pathway was detected after Mt3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The strongest nominal genes are single-class, non-FDR events, so they should remain exploratory rather than being promoted to Mt3 effectors or biomarkers.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: A transcriptomic null does not exclude protein-level, metal-flux, extracellular, or stress-evoked MT3 functions.

summary: Mt3 does not converge with the assayed oxidative-stress neighbors.
why_it_matters: Sod2 was more cleanly knocked down than Mt3 in several classes but still lacked a downstream FDR signature and had near-zero genome-wide score correlation with Mt3; Nfe2l2 was present but unengaged.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: No metallothionein paralogs were available; Nfe2l2 was not engaged; Sod2 is an antioxidant comparator rather than a direct Mt3 paralog.

summary: The Perturb-seq response refines Alzheimer-linked Mt3 literature toward conditional vulnerability rather than a sufficient basal disease transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Human disease papers tied MT3/GIF loss to Alzheimer disease, whereas the mouse-brain perturbation shows partial Mt3 loss alone is transcriptionally quiet, matching knockout evidence for subtle baseline phenotypes and stress-sensitive injury.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not model amyloid, aging, seizures, or human Alzheimer disease cell states.

summary: Abat knockdown was most convincingly engaged in 052 Pvalb Gaba; this was the only cell type with an FDR-significant Abat transcript decrease among 23 tested neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: ABAT is broadly brain-expressed, so the dataset points to guide capture or cell-state-specific engagement rather than uniform transcript depletion across all neuronal classes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Several non-Pvalb classes had nominal Abat decreases, but their adjusted p values were 0.831 or 1.0; protein and enzyme activity were not measured.

direction: Abat down with no FDR-significant non-target response
summary: The FDR-significant Pvalb Abat perturbation was transcriptomically buffered: only Abat itself passed FDR<0.05 and the top non-target gene, Ppp6r1, stopped at FDR=0.051.
why_it_matters: The immediate effect of losing a GABA catabolic enzyme is expected to be metabolic; the single-cell mRNA profile did not reveal a broad cell-autonomous stress, fate, or synaptic-remodeling program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Ppp6r1 was just above the 0.05 FDR threshold, so a larger experiment could nominate a small downstream module.

summary: Abat loss did not transcriptionally feed back onto core GABA-shunt, GABA-synthesis, vesicular-transporter, membrane-transporter, or GABA-A-receptor genes.
why_it_matters: ABAT, ALDH5A1, GAD1, GAD2, SLC6A1, SLC32A1, and GABA-A receptor subunits are functionally connected in GABA metabolism and signaling, but this perturbation did not induce a compensatory mRNA program in those nodes.
main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA, not GABA, succinate semialdehyde, succinate, release probability, or receptor currents.

summary: In Pvalb neurons, Abat was not interchangeable with GABA-synthesis, GABA-transporter, or GABA-A-receptor perturbations: Gad1, Gad2, Slc6a1, Gabra1, Gabrb2, and Gabrg2 had stronger self-knockdown than Abat, yet their transcriptome-wide correlations with Abat were near zero.
why_it_matters: Functional proximity in the GABA pathway did not translate into a shared single-cell mRNA state after individual gene knockdown, arguing against collapsing these perturbations into a generic GABAergic-loss signature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Comparison is restricted to Pvalb neurons and to transcriptomic Wilcoxon scores; Gls was weakly engaged and should not be overinterpreted.

direction: no robust convergence or inverse signature
summary: A Pvalb signature-neighbor scan found no robust positive or inverse whole-transcriptome neighbor for Abat.
why_it_matters: The closest non-self correlations were only about +/-0.06, so top-neighbor identities such as Pitx3 and Tspan12 are likely noise-level rather than evidence of a shared pathway.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The scan used whole-score Pearson correlation within Pvalb neurons only and was dominated by a sparse Abat response.

direction: metabolic/circuit interpretation favored over broad mRNA remodeling
summary: The perturbation supports a model in which partial neuronal Abat loss is metabolically and circuit relevant but largely silent at the cell-autonomous mRNA level in the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Human ABAT deficiency and cell-type-specific GABA-T studies implicate GABA metabolism and inhibitory physiology; the mouse Perturb-seq result shows that those mechanisms need not be accompanied by a broad transcriptional feedback loop.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The disease literature concerns biallelic human loss of function, whereas the dataset is partial CRISPR knockdown in mouse neuronal cell types.

direction: transcriptomic attenuation does not equal enzymatic attenuation
summary: A weak ABAT mRNA signature should not be read as weak pharmacology of GABA-T inhibition.
why_it_matters: Vigabatrin irreversibly inhibits GABA transaminase and has seizure efficacy but retinal risk; enzyme activity, metabolites, and electrophysiology are more direct pharmacodynamic readouts than scRNA-seq DE for this target.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The dataset perturbs Abat genetically and cell-autonomously, unlike systemic irreversible enzyme inhibition by vigabatrin.

summary: Dag1 perturbation did not yield a confident transcriptional phenotype in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The target transcript trended downward in most classes, but no Dag1 mRNA row or downstream row survived FDR correction, so these data should be interpreted as weak transcript-level engagement rather than a clean Dag1 loss-of-function signature.
main_caveats: Loss of the DAG1 protein was not measured; CRISPR coding lesions could alter protein function without lowering the mRNA.

summary: The assayed Dag1 signatures were uncoupled from the dystroglycan extracellular-matrix and glycosylation network at the mRNA level.
why_it_matters: DAG1 is central in a matrix-to-cytoskeleton receptor complex and its glycosylation pathway, yet Dag1 perturbation neither induced significant related-gene compensation nor resembled perturbations of Agrn, Dmd, Sgce/Sgcd, Snta1, glycosylation enzymes, integrins, Lrp4, or Musk.
main_caveats: Restricted to whole-transcriptome score correlations and mRNA compensation; pathway proteins, glycosylation state, and adhesion complexes were not assayed.

summary: The largest nominal Dag1-associated genes were isolated cell-class outliers, not a recurring Dag1 response module.
why_it_matters: Ndufb7 in Pvalb GABA, Cd200 in MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic neurons, Pip5k1c in MB/P/MY GABA, and Kalrn/Akirin1 in L5 ET neurons highlight hypotheses for follow-up but do not define a reproducible program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: All highlighted genes are nominal only, have FDR values from 0.306 to 1, and require validation.

summary: The transcriptomic null result is compatible with DAG1 brain phenotypes being driven by adhesion, glycosylation, synaptic architecture, and glial interfaces rather than by a broad acute neuronal RNA program.
why_it_matters: DAG1 is required in neuronal and glial brain contexts, including inhibitory-synapse systems, but the dataset sampled mainly neuronal mRNA after weak transcript engagement and could miss extracellular, post-translational, or circuit-structural phenotypes.
main_caveats: This is an interpretation of a negative Perturb-seq result; direct synapse, basement-membrane, and glial/endothelial measurements were absent.

direction: mostly target-transcript down; no FDR downstream response
summary: Bckdk perturbation produced partial, mostly downward Bckdk mRNA effects but no FDR-resolved transcriptional response in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: A quiet single-cell RNA phenotype means that downstream mRNA genes are poor biomarkers for this perturbation unless protein depletion, BCKDHA phosphorylation, or BCAA flux is verified.
main_caveats: The no-FDR result is direct, but target-transcript depletion was weak, so buffering cannot be separated from incomplete perturbation.

summary: Canonical BCAA-catabolism, Ppm1k, and Acly transcripts did not move as a coordinated module after Bckdk perturbation.
why_it_matters: BCKDK is expected to control BCKDH and ACLY primarily by phosphorylation, so the dataset points to a post-translational and metabolic readout gap rather than to a clear transcriptional feedback circuit.
main_caveats: The panel test is negative and exploratory; lack of mRNA change does not measure BCKDH phosphorylation or flux.

direction: literature loss-of-function pathogenic; dataset RNA mostly null
summary: Known chronic BCKDK-deficiency neurodevelopmental biology was not phenocopied by a robust Bckdk Perturb-seq mRNA signature.
why_it_matters: The disease mechanism may depend on chronic systemic BCAA depletion, brain amino-acid competition, developmental timing, or neuronal BCKDH activity rather than on an acute cell-autonomous transcriptional stress state.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay BCAA levels, BCKDHA phosphorylation, animal behavior, or developmental exposure.

summary: Bckdk showed no meaningful positive or negative signature convergence with measured BCAA-complex, leucine/valine-catabolic, pyruvate-dehydrogenase, or 2-oxoglutarate-dehydrogenase neighbors.
why_it_matters: The lack of convergence prevents treating the weak Bckdk signature as a reliable proxy for BCKDH-complex biology or for adjacent mitochondrial dehydrogenase perturbations.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak Bckdk RNA signatures; near-zero correlations may reflect low signal rather than true biochemical independence.

direction: inhibition expected to activate BCKDH and lower BCAAs
summary: The absence of a Bckdk scRNA-seq stress signature does not de-risk BCKDK inhibition, whose intended biochemical effect is to lower BCAAs, the same metabolite direction associated with BCKDK loss-of-function disease.
why_it_matters: BCKDK inhibitors should be evaluated with BCAA, BCKA, BCKDHA-phosphorylation, and brain-development endpoints even when acute transcriptomic biomarkers are absent.
main_caveats: The dataset tested genetic perturbation in mouse brain single cells rather than pharmacologic systemic dosing, and it contains no direct safety or metabolite endpoint.

summary: Lrfn2 perturbation produced a cell-type-restricted Slc12a5/Kcc2 increase in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: Slc12a5 encodes KCC2, a key chloride extruder for hyperpolarizing GABAergic inhibition, so the only corrected RNA hit nominates a focused inhibitory-state biomarker rather than a broad PSD-95/NMDAR module.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Only one gene reached FDR < 0.05, secondary genes were nominal, and Lrfn2 target-transcript depletion was not detected.

summary: The Lrfn2 signature was uncoupled from Dlg4/PSD-95, NMDA-receptor, neurexin, and related synaptic-adhesion perturbations.
why_it_matters: Membership in the SALM1 synaptic scaffold did not imply transcriptomic phenocopy; acute Lrfn2 perturbation cannot be substituted for direct Dlg4, Grin, or Nrxn perturbation in this dataset.
main_caveats: Whole-transcriptome correlations test transcriptional similarity, not local synaptic assembly or protein trafficking; Lrfn2 itself had weak measured engagement.

summary: No cell type showed significant depletion of the Lrfn2 target transcript.
why_it_matters: This makes all downstream effects conditional on unconfirmed protein-level perturbation and explains why a known synaptic gene could yield a small RNA signature.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance may be an imperfect proxy for protein activity or genome editing at this locus.

summary: Lrfn2 perturbation was broadly buffered, with 21 of 22 assayed cell types having no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The dataset mostly fails to convert Lrfn2 perturbation into detectable transcriptome remodeling, even in cell types with more than 100 perturbed cells.
main_caveats: RNA buffering cannot be separated from weak guide effect without independent editing or protein measurements.

summary: Hippocampal-like glutamatergic classes did not show a corrected Lrfn2 response despite hippocampal NMDAR and plasticity phenotypes in Lrfn2 KO mice.
why_it_matters: This limits direct extrapolation from hippocampal KO physiology to broad single-cell transcriptional effects and suggests that synaptic electrophysiology can be affected without a large mRNA module.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The assayed cell classes are coarse aggregates, not isolated CA1 neurons; the Perturb-seq modality differs from constitutive knockout electrophysiology.

summary: Lrrc3b perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptome-wide response in any measured central brain cell type and did not significantly reduce its own transcript.
why_it_matters: The negative result reframes all nominal Lrrc3b genes as exploratory and shows that a brain-expressed membrane LRR protein can be transcriptionally silent, buffered, or ineffectively knocked down in this assay.
main_caveats: The self-transcript row was weak in every cell type, so the null downstream result cannot separate true dispensability from weak guide efficacy or low transcript detectability.

summary: Ndrg3 up-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut was the nearest Lrrc3b-associated molecular readout.
why_it_matters: It nominates the only near-FDR gene as a concrete validation marker in the cell class with the strongest Lrrc3b-specific signal.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Ndrg3 was FDR=0.056 rather than FDR<0.05, the other nearby genes had FDR>=0.537, and no nominal p<0.001 gene recurred across cell types.

summary: A weak CB GABA Lrrc3b signature aligned with B9d1 and Ranbp2 perturbations and opposed Wdr26, Cckar, and Nr4a1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: The whole-signature view exposes a cell-type-restricted state that would be missed by single-gene FDR thresholds and nominates strong comparator perturbations for follow-up in cerebellar GABAergic cells.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are modest, were computed from a subthreshold Lrrc3b signature, and do not establish direct molecular interaction.

summary: STRING-predicted Lrrc3b neighbors Adgrl1, Adgrl2, and Adgrl3 did not phenocopy Lrrc3b across the measured cell types.
why_it_matters: It prevents overinterpreting database functional associations as interchangeable perturbation biology in central neurons.
main_caveats: STRING edges are predictive functional associations rather than direct LRRC3B complex evidence; Lrrc3b itself was weakly engaged, which can dampen correlations.

summary: Olfactory and epithelial-cancer LRRC3B functions did not translate into a robust central-neuron Perturb-seq program.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues against assigning a tumor-immune or odor-activity direction to Lrrc3b loss in these brain cell classes without matched validation.
main_caveats: The literature contexts differ by tissue, species compartment, perturbation direction, and tumor microenvironment; the dataset also lacks strong target engagement.

summary: The Nin perturbation was assayed broadly but did not produce FDR-level depletion of its own transcript in any cell type.
why_it_matters: A weak direct target readout makes every downstream Nin signature a lower-confidence proxy for loss of Ninein protein function.
main_caveats: The table reports RNA differential expression of Nin itself, not guide cutting efficiency or centrosomal Ninein protein abundance.

summary: Nin perturbation caused no genome-wide significant mature-neuronal transcriptional program, aligning the dataset more with a developmental progenitor requirement than with a broad postmitotic-neuron response.
why_it_matters: Known Ninein biology centers on centrosome inheritance and interkinetic nuclear migration in proliferative cortical progenitors; the mouse-brain neuronal strata tested here cannot be assumed to reproduce that embryonic mechanism.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant RNA changes could reflect poor effective knockdown, pathway buffering, post-developmental context, or a protein phenotype not captured transcriptionally.

summary: The strongest downstream hint was restricted to 053 Sst Gaba and was a single-gene Bex3 increase rather than a recurrent Nin module.
why_it_matters: The lowest adjusted P value in the experiment should be treated as an Sst-specific outlier, not as evidence for a shared Ninein-regulated pathway across neuronal classes.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Bex3 reached only FDR 0.119; the Sst stratum had 57 Nin cells, and neighboring Sst hits were weaker after multiple testing.

summary: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut was the only cell type with Nin itself among the top nominal hits, yet it still lacked any FDR-significant downstream transcript.
why_it_matters: This separates a modest direct depletion signal from a missing cell-state response and is the cleanest example of possible transcriptional buffering in the dataset.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Nin depletion was nominal and FDR=1.0, so the result is consistent with buffering but cannot prove effective loss of Ninein protein.

summary: Nin signatures were nearly orthogonal to the tested centrosome, ciliary, and microtubule perturbations rather than converging on a general ciliogenesis/centrosome-loss state.
why_it_matters: Ninein is a mother-centriole microtubule anchor, but the response measured here did not resemble perturbations of distal-appendage, transition-zone, IFT, BBSome, or tubulin-associated genes available in the same library.
main_caveats: Direct NIN paralog or subdistal-appendage comparators such as Ninl, Cep170, Cep250, and Ccdc120 were absent, and all correlations use RNA signatures rather than centrosome imaging.

summary: An unrestricted same-cell-type signature search found no close positive or negative Nin neighbor.
why_it_matters: The global scan did not reveal a hidden pathway analog or suppressor-like opposite transcriptional state that would rescue an otherwise weak scalar DE result.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The nearest correlations occurred in weak Nin contexts and did not exceed |r|=0.25, so the identity of those neighbors is exploratory.

summary: Gpr12 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic response in 23 assayed cell types, with only weak evidence of Gpr12 self-transcript reduction.
why_it_matters: GPR12 is a brain GPCR, but this dataset does not provide a clean adult brain loss-of-function signature for the receptor.
main_caveats: High confidence for the DE absence; lower confidence that the receptor was fully perturbed because target mRNA depletion was not significant.

summary: The expected Gs-cAMP-PKA/CREB transcriptional output was not detected after Gpr12 perturbation.
why_it_matters: GPR12 is curated as a constitutively active GPCR linked to cAMP signaling, so the absence of CREB/immediate-early transcripts separates this scRNA endpoint from canonical biochemical GPR12 activity.
main_caveats: Exploratory pathway conclusion because cAMP can be acute or post-transcriptional and because Gpr12 transcript engagement was weak.

summary: Large matched adult neuronal strata, including a thalamic class, remained flat after Gpr12 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The negative result is not explained solely by the smallest sampled cell types, and it refines thalamic and broadly neuronal GPR12 literature to say that these adult scRNA cell classes did not show a strong soma transcriptome response.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The same high-count strata lacked strong Gpr12 mRNA knockdown, so the result cannot distinguish biological buffering from poor perturbation efficiency.

summary: Gpr12 did not converge with expected Gs/PKA/CREB pathway neighbors or close paralogs in the perturbation matrix.
why_it_matters: Gnas was a predicted STRING functional partner, but Gpr12 signatures were nearly orthogonal to Gnas, Prkaca, and Creb1; Gpr3 and Gpr6 were unavailable for a direct paralog test.
main_caveats: Top-300 signature-neighbor correlations were restricted and exploratory; the direct Gnas perturbation was also weak.

summary: This dataset did not reveal a robust RNA pharmacodynamic marker for GPR12 modulation.
why_it_matters: Because selective GPR12 agonists and antagonists are not yet established, a perturbation-derived transcriptional marker would be valuable, but neither cAMP-response genes nor unbiased DE genes passed FDR<0.05 here.
main_caveats: Absence of an RNA marker in this Perturb-seq experiment does not exclude acute cAMP, calcium, electrophysiologic, or circuit biomarkers.

summary: Gabra5 perturbation produced no FDR-supported target depletion and no FDR-supported downstream transcriptomic program in any modeled cell type.
why_it_matters: GABRA5 is a ligand-gated chloride-channel subunit, but this Perturb-seq contrast is effectively a transcriptomic null, so mechanistic interpretation should not assume functional alpha5 receptor loss.
main_caveats: A negative Wilcoxon result cannot distinguish failed guide activity, low baseline expression, protein buffering, and an electrophysiological phenotype without a transcriptional correlate.

summary: The corrected null result persisted even in the two Gabra5 classes with the largest numbers of perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: The absence of a call is not confined to the smallest Gabra5 strata; 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had many cells but no on-target shift, and 155 MB Glut had the strongest nominal Gabra5 decrease but no corrected downstream genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: These are still transcript counts from guide-assigned cells rather than protein or current measurements.

summary: Gabra5 was less transcriptionally engaged than several other GABA_A receptor subunit perturbations from the same screen.
why_it_matters: Alpha, beta, gamma, and delta subunits can participate in the same GABA_A receptor family, yet Gabra1, Gabrb2, Gabrb3, Gabrd, and Gabrg2 showed FDR-supported target depletion in at least two cell types whereas Gabra5 showed none.
main_caveats: The contrast is based on differential-expression readouts, not receptor assembly or electrophysiology.

summary: Gabra5 perturbation did not trigger detectable transcriptional remodeling of other GABA_A receptor subunits or core GABA synthesis and transport genes.
why_it_matters: There is no FDR-level evidence for mRNA compensation by alternate GABA_A subunits, Gad1/Gad2, or Slc6a1 in the measured cell classes.
main_caveats: Because target engagement was weak, absence of compensation should not be interpreted as proof that alpha5 function was lost without feedback.

summary: Restricted score-vector analysis found no robust Gabra5-positive or Gabra5-negative transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: The strongest same-cell-type signature neighbors had |r| below 0.20, and related GABA receptor subunits were far weaker, so signature-neighbor biology should be treated as exploratory at best.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from the same FDR-negative signatures and are useful mainly for ruling out a strong module.

summary: The CA1/DG-containing 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut class did not show the hippocampal alpha5 signal that might be expected from prior CA1 physiology.
why_it_matters: Alpha5-GABA_A receptors are strongly linked to hippocampal tonic inhibition and plasticity, but this coarse glutamatergic class had only 43 Gabra5 cells and no corrected target or downstream response.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The dataset class mixes MEA, LA, CA1, and DG glutamatergic neurons and the Gabra5 on-target effect was weak, so this does not argue against known CA1 electrophysiology.

summary: The screen cannot assign a therapeutic direction for alpha5-GABA_A potentiation or inhibition.
why_it_matters: Alpha5-directed negative and positive allosteric modulators both have disease rationales in the literature, but the Perturb-seq data provide no corrected transcriptional readout of Gabra5 loss from which to choose a PAM-like or NAM-like direction.
main_caveats: Therapeutic alpha5 modulation is pharmacologic and electrophysiologic; it is only indirectly approximated by transcript perturbation.

summary: Ddr2 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across all 22 Ddr2-tested neuronal cell-type signatures.
why_it_matters: DDR2 is a collagen receptor tyrosine kinase, so a broad null result in Glut/GABA brain classes is a real biological constraint on where autonomous Ddr2 transcriptional programs were detectable in this screen.
main_caveats: The measured target transcript was not significantly depleted, so the null may combine weak target engagement with true absence of neuronal DDR2 dependence.

summary: Ddr2 remained FDR-null in high-count 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut signatures even though Ntrk2, Map2k1, and Mapk1 produced detectable effects in overlapping neuronal contexts.
why_it_matters: This comparison argues that the Ddr2 result is not simply an inability of the dataset to detect kinase or RTK-pathway phenotypes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparator kinases are not DDR2 paralogs and have different expression and wiring; the contrast is an assay-sensitivity control, not a claim of shared mechanism.

summary: Ddr2 full-transcriptome signatures did not align with available collagen, integrin, Src-family, SOS, MEK, ERK, PDGFRB, MET, or NTRK2 perturbations.
why_it_matters: DDR2 is curated as a collagen/ECM receptor and literature connects it to Src/Shc RTK signaling, so the near-zero same-cell-type correlations indicate that this neuronal dataset did not engage a canonical DDR2 neighborhood.
main_caveats: Ddr1 was not assayed; Col4a1 is not a Reactome-listed fibrillar DDR2 ligand; many ligand or pathway perturbations were themselves weak in this neuronal screen.
