why_it_matters: The low-amplitude contrast is worth tracking because GRIN2A and GRIN2B are both PSD-95-linked NMDAR subunits, yet the cortical IT data do not support simple paralog interchangeability.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Dlg4 target depletion in this class was only FDR 0.0728 and correlations were small, so this is a hypothesis for retesting rather than a firm directional call.

direction: on-target repression without broad mRNA response
summary: The disease-linked Dlg4 perturbation produced synaptic-gene target engagement without transcriptional collapse, refining DLG4-related synaptopathy toward local postsynaptic or developmental mechanisms rather than an acute broad mRNA stress program.
why_it_matters: Human DLG4 loss-of-function variants are neurodevelopmental, but the mouse single-cell data suggest downstream biomarkers may be electrophysiologic, proteomic or structural instead of robust nuclear mRNA markers.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq animals and sampled cell classes are not a human developmental disease model.

direction: mRNA-silent after Dlg4 depletion; chronic loss and transient uncoupling should not be conflated
summary: Therapeutic PSD-95/NMDAR uncoupling is likely to be pharmacodynamically mRNA-silent in the sampled neurons, and chronic DLG4 suppression would be unsafe to equate with transient pathway uncoupling.
why_it_matters: PSD-95 has been deliberately targeted downstream of NMDARs for ischemic neuroprotection, while inherited DLG4 loss of function causes neurodevelopmental disease; this dataset warns that lack of an mRNA response is not evidence of pathway inactivity or safety.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset did not test nerinetide, ischemia, or pharmacologic PSD-95 inhibition; the warning is mechanistic and translational, not a measured drug response.

direction: Ppp2r2b up in Pvalb; Zdhhc21 down in Sst
summary: Adra2a perturbation yielded FDR-significant RNA changes only in Pvalb and Sst GABAergic classes, with Ppp2r2b higher in Pvalb cells and Zdhhc21 lower in Sst cells.
why_it_matters: The interpretable signal is an interneuron-restricted pair of candidate RNA readouts rather than a broad adrenergic pathway signature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: One FDR-supported gene per positive cell type, and Adra2a target-transcript depletion was not detected.

direction: mostly no detectable FDR RNA response
summary: The Adra2a perturbation was globally buffered at the RNA level, with only 2 of 388046 tests passing FDR<0.05, no significant target-transcript depletion, and no FDR signal in a cAMP-HCN sentinel panel.
why_it_matters: For a Gi/o GPCR, canonical biology can be rapid and post-transcriptional; absence of a large RNA program limits pathway reconstruction from this Perturb-seq slice.
main_caveats: RNA buffering cannot be separated from weak or sparse target engagement in cells lacking measurable Adra2a knockdown.

summary: Adra2a was not signature-interchangeable with Adra2b or the broader alpha-adrenergic comparator Adra1a in the two cell classes with Adra2a FDR hits.
why_it_matters: Shared adrenergic receptor family membership and catecholamine recognition did not predict matched steady-state transcriptomes in Pvalb or Sst cells.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: The Adra2a and Adra2b signatures were themselves weak, so near-zero correlations are a restricted-signature result.

summary: Adra2a had no robust recurrent nominal module and no strong positive or inverse whole-signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The Ppp2r2b and Zdhhc21 hits should not be overextended into a hidden multi-gene pathway without additional validation.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak signatures; absence of a neighbor is support for caution, not proof that no biological partner exists.

direction: loss-of-function RNA response uncoupled from agonist cAMP-HCN physiology
summary: The Adra2a CRISPR-RNA signature should not be inverted as a guanfacine-like alpha2A agonist signature because the canonical HCN/cAMP transcripts were not significantly engaged.
why_it_matters: Alpha2A agonist efficacy in prefrontal physiology is directionally tied to rapid cAMP-HCN signaling, whereas this dataset mainly reports a sparse, weak transcriptional loss-of-function phenotype.
main_caveats: The assay measured steady-state RNA in broad mouse cell classes, not acute drug exposure, cAMP, HCN channel state, or prefrontal firing.

summary: Fgf12 loss was coherent across the assay but strongest only at nominal significance in four midbrain, hypothalamic, pons-medulla, or pineal-labeled neuronal strata.
why_it_matters: The perturbation is interpretable as partial target knockdown, and the best-engaged strata should be weighted more heavily than weak self-knockdown strata.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: No individual Fgf12 self row reached adjusted p < 0.05; 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 37 perturbed cells.

summary: The four most engaged Fgf12 cell types had target-mRNA depletion without adjusted-significant downstream transcriptional responses.
why_it_matters: FGF12/FHF1 is expected to regulate neuronal excitability through NaV-channel interactions; the dataset suggests this perturbation did not force a broad steady-state RNA program under the sampled conditions.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Buffered RNA output could reflect incomplete CRISPRi, compensation, or a purely electrophysiologic phenotype that the assay does not measure.

summary: Fgf12 signatures were nearly orthogonal to Fgf13, Fgf14, and sodium-channel perturbation signatures despite their shared FHF/NaV biology.
why_it_matters: The shared excitability pathway should not be collapsed into a single transcriptional signature; Fgf12 loss is distinguishable from stronger Fgf13 and Scn knockdowns in this dataset.
main_caveats: Fgf12 had weak per-cell-type engagement, so absence of signature convergence is stronger evidence against a robust RNA phenocopy than against electrophysiologic convergence.

summary: Nmnat2 was the only adjusted p < 0.10 non-target outlier, but it occurred in 145 MH-LH TH Glut where Fgf12 itself was not detectably depleted.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting the top adjusted hit as an FGF12-controlled axonal or injury module.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Single cell type, adjusted p = 0.075 not < 0.05, and the target transcript changed only logFC -0.162 with p = 0.302.

summary: Human FGF12 epileptic encephalopathy is driven by gain-of-function NaV-channel dysregulation, whereas this dataset measured weak loss of Fgf12 mRNA and no electrophysiology.
why_it_matters: The quiet transcriptome is compatible with reduced liability at the mRNA level, but it is not evidence that FGF12 lowering normalizes NaV1.6 gating or seizure phenotypes.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Species, developmental timing, gain-versus-loss direction, and readout modality all differ between the Perturb-seq assay and FGF12 epileptic encephalopathy.

summary: Clcn5 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed mouse-brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The primary result is absence of a robust perturbation phenotype: even the measured Clcn5 transcript was not reproducibly depleted, so downstream null results should be interpreted as weak target engagement rather than proven dispensability of ClC-5.
main_caveats: Only a differential-expression table was available; raw expression and guide-level efficacy were not available.

summary: Clcn5 was much weaker than Clcn4 in the same neuronal classes despite both genes encoding intracellular CLC chloride/proton exchangers.
why_it_matters: The paralog contrast matches the stronger neurodevelopmental genetics of CLCN4 versus the kidney-dominant genetics of CLCN5, and argues that CLC family membership alone does not predict an equivalent neuronal transcriptional readout.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Clcn4 had more matched perturbed cells than Clcn5 in the compared classes, and most Clcn4 corrected hits were the target transcript itself.

summary: Clcn5 did not converge transcriptome-wide with Clcn3, Clcn4, or selected endosomal acidification genes.
why_it_matters: Prior pathway knowledge groups CLCN5 with endosomal chloride/proton exchange, but the screen did not show a coordinated neuronal CLC or v-ATPase module downstream of Clcn5.
main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted-signature and correlation-based because Clcn5 itself lacked strong knockdown.

summary: The Dent/proximal-tubule endocytosis neighborhood of Ocrl, Lrp2, and Cubn was silent in Clcn5-perturbed brain cell types.
why_it_matters: A renal receptor-mediated endocytosis mechanism is central to ClC-5 disease biology, but this module was neither differentially expressed after Clcn5 perturbation nor reproduced by Ocrl or Lrp2 perturbations in the neuronal screen.
main_caveats: The canonical mechanism is a renal epithelial trafficking phenotype; neurons in this dataset may not express the same ligand-receptor machinery, and weak Clcn5 engagement limits the perturbation test.

summary: Gipr target-transcript depletion was not detected in any assayed neuronal cell type.
why_it_matters: Without measurable self-knockdown, weak downstream signatures cannot be cleanly interpreted as true loss-of-function biology.
main_caveats: Single-cell Gipr RNA may be sparse, so absence of a self effect may reflect measurement limits as well as weak perturbation.

summary: Prkci down-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut was the only FDR-significant downstream Gipr result.
why_it_matters: It localizes the only corrected dataset signal to one corticofugal glutamatergic class and leaves Prkci as a low-breadth candidate readout needing replication.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only one gene passed FDR; Gipr itself was not detectably depleted in this same cell type.

summary: Most assayed broad neuronal classes, including Sst GABAergic and hypothalamic-containing classes, had only nominal or null Gipr responses.
why_it_matters: The data do not support a broad basal neuronal transcriptional program downstream of Gipr and are more consistent with either biological buffering or lack of effective engagement in most classes.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The dataset cell labels are broad and do not isolate the Gipr-positive hypothalamic, AP or NTS neurons studied in the literature; target engagement was weak.

summary: The only corrected cell type did not activate a cAMP/CREB or immediate-early transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: GIPR is a peptide GPCR linked to cAMP biology, so the absence of Fos/Egr/Arc/Bdnf/Nr4a responses shows that the observed basal L5 ET signature is not a simple transcriptional copy of ligand-stimulated GIPR signaling.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The literature context is largely pancreatic β-cell/adipocyte ligand stimulation, whereas the dataset is basal genetic perturbation in neurons.

summary: Gipr did not cluster with Glp1r, Gcgr, Gnas or adenylyl-cyclase perturbations, and no non-self signature neighbor showed |r| greater than 0.109 in L5 ET neurons.
why_it_matters: A matched incretin/cAMP program would have strengthened the Prkci hit; its absence argues that the Gipr signature is sparse and not a generic class-B GPCR or Gs/cAMP signature.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Most related receptor perturbations were themselves weak, and STRING functional links do not imply identical transcriptional effects.

summary: The weak basal neuronal Gipr loss-of-function response should not be used as a surrogate for GIPR/GLP1R agonist pharmacology in obesity or diabetes.
why_it_matters: Human genetics and tirzepatide pharmacology implicate GIPR in metabolic therapy, but the transcriptomic screen mainly says that these broad mouse neuronal contexts did not capture that mechanism.
main_caveats: The screen does not test acute agonism, peptide exposure, peripheral tissues, oligodendroglial or endothelial cells, or molecularly defined Gipr-positive feeding neurons.

summary: Plpbp perturbation produced a transcriptome-scale null result in this assay because target-transcript engagement was weak and no downstream gene reached FDR<0.25 in any cell type.
why_it_matters: The screen therefore cannot be read as evidence that PLPBP is biologically dispensable; it mainly says that this acute single-cell mRNA assay did not strongly deplete Plpbp or reproduce the known vitamin-B6 pathology.
main_caveats: Target mRNA is only a proxy for protein loss, but absence of FDR-supported DE and Plpbp FDR=1.0 in every cell type make mRNA-level interpretation intentionally conservative.

summary: The only detectable Plpbp-centered response was concentrated in 308 CB GABA, where Plpbp was the tenth strongest absolute feature and nominally decreased.
why_it_matters: This nominates cerebellar GABAergic neurons as the only context worth follow-up in this dataset, but it does so from nominal rather than FDR-supported statistics.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Cnnm3, Atp5l, Nova1, and Plpbp had FDR values of 0.275 or 1.0, so this is a restricted, hypothesis-generating cell-type call rather than a validated CB-GABA program.

summary: Measured vitamin-B6-related and GABA-metabolism transcripts did not form a coherent compensatory module after Plpbp perturbation.
why_it_matters: Known PLPBP biology is metabolic and PLP-cofactor based; the dataset suggests that acute Plpbp guide assignment, even in the strongest CB-GABA context, was not converted into a coordinated Pnpo/Pdxk/Pdxp/Aldh7a1 or Gad1/Gad2/Abat mRNA response.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: The targeted neighbors were assayed only as transcripts, all had FDR=1.0 in the highlighted rows, and metabolite or PLP-dependent enzyme activity measurements were unavailable.

summary: The Plpbp signature had no close positive or negative neighbor among 2,045 other perturbations, and key PLP-pathway neighbors were not directly perturbed.
why_it_matters: There is no same-assay perturbation that can be used as a confident phenocopy or rescue-direction comparator for Plpbp; global correlations near zero argue against hidden convergence with another target.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on Wilcoxon-score vectors; very weak Plpbp signatures reduce the power to detect biologically meaningful similarity.

summary: Human genetics make PLPBP loss-of-function an epileptic-encephalopathy liability, but this screen did not yield a robust mRNA biomarker panel for that liability.
why_it_matters: Any future PLPBP-decreasing intervention should be prioritized for PLP/vitamin-B6 metabolite, PLP-dependent neurotransmitter, and electrophysiologic assays rather than relying on the weak acute transcriptomic readout observed here.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse, acute, and mRNA-only with weak target-transcript depletion, whereas PLPBP deficiency in patients is biallelic germline loss with metabolic and electrophysiologic endpoints.

summary: Epor perturbation showed no convincing RNA-level Epor depletion in any profiled neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Without demonstrable target knockdown, the many null downstream tests are more consistent with weak engagement or basal buffering than with a clean EPOR loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: RNA-level Epor may be sparse, and the assay cannot rule out subtle protein-level or phospho-signaling changes.

summary: A Pvalb GABA-restricted Ifitm10 decrease was the only transcriptome-wide significant response to Epor perturbation, accompanied by a nominal down tail of channel and synaptic genes.
why_it_matters: The result elevates 052 Pvalb Gaba as the only cell class with a dataset-supported Epor-associated signal and is biologically plausible in light of published mouse EPO effects on inhibitory interneurons.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only Ifitm10 passed FDR; the channel and synaptic genes were nominal with FDR=1.0, and Epor itself was not detectably depleted in Pvalb cells.

summary: Expected EPOR-JAK/STAT and growth-factor pathway transcripts did not respond, and Epor signatures were not similar to STAT or cytokine-receptor perturbations.
why_it_matters: The canonical erythropoietin receptor cascade is a curated EPOR output, so its absence argues that these neuronal signatures should not be read as a standard JAK2/STAT5 transcriptional program.
main_caveats: The test is steady-state mRNA; acute JAK2/STAT phosphorylation or ligand-dependent signaling could be missed.

summary: No strong Epor signature neighbor, positive or negative, was detected among all target/cell-type score vectors.
why_it_matters: This guards against assigning the weak Epor profile to an unrecognized module or to a phenocopy of another perturbation.
main_caveats: All-gene Pearson score correlation can miss small nonlinear overlap, and a weak Epor signature reduces power to find neighbors.

summary: The dataset does not establish a neuronal EPOR antagonist or agonist transcriptional direction despite clear literature that EPOR is ligand-druggable and active in nervous-system contexts.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb signal is insufficient as a biomarker for EPO-like treatment response or for EPOR blockade because core loss-of-function and canonical pathway evidence were absent.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The screen did not add EPO ligand, did not model hypoxia or injury, and did not assay glia, endothelial cells, erythroid cells, or electrophysiology.

summary: Nfib produced no FDR-supported downstream expression response in any tested cell class.
why_it_matters: The table does not support high-confidence Nfib-responsive genes, pathways, or cell-type-restricted effector programs.
main_caveats: Negative interpretation is limited by variable perturbed-cell counts, absence of Nfib rows in 215 MB Dopa, and failure to validate Nfib transcript knockdown.

summary: RNA-level target engagement for Nfib was not validated in the Wilcoxon rows.
why_it_matters: The flat downstream signature is better read as a non-engaged or underpowered perturbation result than as evidence that NFIB is dispensable in these cells.
main_caveats: The assay measures Nfib RNA, not NFIB protein, DNA binding, or edited alleles; guides outside the mature transcript could perturb function without changing measured Nfib RNA.

summary: The closest NFI paralogs did not reveal a broad latent Nfib-like program; Nfia and Nfix had no FDR 0.05 hits and Nfic had only two isolated hits.
why_it_matters: Despite the known developmental relatedness of NFI transcription factors, the dataset does not expose a shared mouse-brain NFI perturbation module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Comparison was restricted to the NFI paralogs recovered from the same parquet and to RNA-level Wilcoxon signatures.

summary: This perturbation table does not provide a disease-direction NFIB haploinsufficiency signature.
why_it_matters: NFIB dosage is linked to brain development and human neurodevelopmental disease, but the current Nfib data are too weak to nominate biomarkers or therapeutic rescue directions.
main_caveats: Prior evidence is largely developmental or human-genetic, whereas the dataset is a mouse Perturb-seq differential-expression table with weak Nfib target-transcript engagement.

summary: Ift43 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any of the 23 profiled mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: IFT43 is a ciliary IFT-A component, so a genome-wide null across all sampled classes is the central biological outcome and forces any interpretation to emphasize buffering, assay mismatch, or weak perturbation rather than a strong downstream pathway.
main_caveats: The Ift43 transcript itself was not significantly depleted, so the dataset cannot separate biological buffering from incomplete or poorly captured target engagement.

summary: The CA3/CA2-FC/DG and thalamic glutamatergic nominal peaks remained exploratory rather than resolving a cell-type-specific Ift43 module.
why_it_matters: The top rows identify where validation could start, but their failure to pass FDR prevents over-interpreting isolated nominal genes as an Ift43 pathway.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: All cited genes are nominal only; the dopamine stratum had just 23 perturbed cells.

summary: Ift43 lacked a strong shared signature with same-complex or ciliary-disease neighbors, including Ttc21b and B9d1.
why_it_matters: Known IFT-A physical proximity did not translate to interchangeable RNA signatures in this assay, so ciliary perturbations should not be collapsed into a single expected transcriptomic effect.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to genes targeted in the screen and to mRNA signatures; several direct IFT-A partners were not themselves perturbations.

summary: Measured ciliary transport and ciliary signaling transcripts did not show an adjusted compensatory response to Ift43 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This argues that the screen did not detect a canonical IFT or Hedgehog/GPCR feedback program downstream of Ift43, even though IFT43 is annotated to intraflagellar transport.
main_caveats: The selected panel tests transcript abundance only and cannot exclude altered ciliary localization or protein transport.

summary: The brain-cell transcriptomic null should not be interpreted as systemic tolerance of IFT43 loss.
why_it_matters: Human genetics shows that IFT43 disruption is pathogenic in ciliated skeletal, fibroblast, and retinal contexts, so absence of a brain mRNA phenotype is context-specific rather than evidence that IFT43 loss is harmless.
main_caveats: This is a caution about interpretation, not a druggability analysis; no IFT43-targeting therapy was tested.

summary: Aco2 perturbation produced little transcript-level target depletion and only one FDR-significant downstream gene across all assayed neuronal populations.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is weak or buffered engagement, so the dataset should not be read as a full phenocopy of ACO2 enzyme loss.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an indirect engagement readout for a Perturb-seq perturbation; protein activity and guide-level effects were not available.

summary: Sirt7 up-regulation in CTX-CGE GABA cells is the sole FDR-significant Aco2 response and is consistent with, but does not prove, a mitochondrial stress-feedback state.
why_it_matters: SIRT7 is a nuclear regulator of mitochondrial protein-folding stress in stem-cell systems, making it a plausible hypothesis-generating marker for the one Aco2-sensitive neuronal state.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The finding is driven by one gene in 47 perturbed cells; canonical UPRmt regulators were not shown to be coordinately significant.

summary: The CTX-CGE Aco2 signature does not converge with pyruvate/TCA/OXPHOS enzyme perturbations despite ACO2 being a core TCA enzyme.
why_it_matters: This argues that the measured Aco2 perturbation is transcriptionally idiosyncratic or weak rather than a local rendering of citrate-isocitrate blockade in the TCA cycle.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from DE score vectors, not raw single-cell states; Aco2 itself was not detectably depleted.

summary: Large Aco2-tested glutamatergic populations still lacked significant target knockdown or downstream FDR hits.
why_it_matters: The broad negative result is not only a consequence of the smallest 30- to 50-cell Aco2 contrasts; several >100-cell contrasts remained silent.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: These cell classes still only test transcript-level perturbation and do not exclude protein-level editing or slower metabolic phenotypes.

summary: The negative cerebellar GABA result should refine, not overturn, human ACO2 neuro-ophthalmic genetics.
why_it_matters: Human ACO2 loss causes cerebellar-retinal degeneration and optic atrophy, and Open Targets listed no clinical drug candidates; a weak CB GABA Perturb-seq signature therefore gives no evidence for a compensatory neuronal program that would make direct ACO2 inhibition look safe.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset sampled a cerebellar GABA class rather than retina or optic nerve, and it did not show robust Aco2 engagement in that class.

summary: Osbpl2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant mRNA response in any assayed brain cell type.
why_it_matters: Despite ORP2 being a lipid-transfer protein with defined cholesterol and PI(4,5)P2 activity, the Perturb-seq endpoint did not show a high-amplitude cell-state remodeling response.
main_caveats: A negative mRNA result is conditional on weak Osbpl2 target engagement and does not measure lipid-transfer activity directly.

summary: Osbpl2 on-target transcript depletion was heterogeneous, nominally strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and absent at FDR level in all 22 tested cell types.
why_it_matters: The best cell class had a detectable but still modest on-target trend, while several low-count classes were underpowered; target engagement rather than biology probably bounds downstream sensitivity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: Self-depletion was assessed only at the mRNA level and all Osbpl2 self p values failed multiple-testing correction.

summary: In the best nominal Osbpl2 cell type, Osbpl2 did not transcriptionally track available presynaptic exocytosis perturbations Snap25, Stxbp1, and Syn1.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation contrast argues that published ORP2 control of neurotransmitter release is not organized as a broad core-SNARE mRNA module in this assay and may instead be local, lipidic, or electrophysiologic.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Stx1a, the syntaxin isoform highlighted in the ORP2 synapse paper, was not an assayed comparator; the comparison uses related exocytosis genes with strong target knockdown.

summary: A weak central-brain Osbpl2 loss-of-transcript perturbation did not phenocopy the reported DFNA67 mutant-protein autophagy/endolysosomal mechanism.
why_it_matters: DFNA67 interpretation and the reported rapamycin rescue are tied to cochlear frameshift mutant OSBPL2 biology, so this buffered brain signature should not be read as evidence for or against mutant-allele toxicity in hair cells.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks cochlear hair cells, mutant OSBPL2 expression, protein-aggregate assays, and autophagic-flux measurements.

summary: Neither OSBPL paralogs nor strong unbiased signature neighbors supplied an alternative Osbpl2 pathway hypothesis.
why_it_matters: The absence of related-family targets and the very low absolute correlations of the top positive and negative neighbors argue against over-interpreting isolated nominal Osbpl2 genes as a coherent pathway.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlation used full Wilcoxon score vectors and may miss small, sparse, pathway-specific overlaps.

summary: Across the 23 assayed mouse-brain cell groups, Mrtfa perturbation produced no transcriptome-wide FDR<0.05 effects and no FDR-level depletion of the Mrtfa transcript itself.
why_it_matters: MRTFA is a curated actin-regulated SRF coactivator with neurodevelopmental roles, so the primary result is a weak-engagement negative result rather than a robust loss-of-function state for interpreting downstream biology.
main_caveats: The conclusion is about the measured perturbation signatures, not about absence of Mrtfa biology; target mRNA knockdown was not FDR-significant in any cell group.

summary: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut contained the only Mrtfa-associated row below 10% FDR, a Dnajb5 decrease, but this was a single-gene exploratory tail rather than a broad cell-type program.
why_it_matters: It localizes the strongest measured signal to one intratelencephalic glutamatergic group while preventing overinterpretation of Dnajb5 as a validated MRTFA target.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Dnajb5 did not pass 5% FDR, the other top 008 genes had FDR=1.0, and the Mrtfa transcript itself was not depleted in this cell group.

summary: The expected actin/MRTF/SRF and immediate-early output was not coherently activated or repressed by Mrtfa perturbation.
why_it_matters: Prior mechanistic and neuronal literature predicts MRTFA-SRF coupling to actin-associated transcription, but the Perturb-seq result shows only scattered Cfl2, Myh10, and immediate-early nominal rows with no panel member at FDR<0.05.
main_caveats: The result is restricted to transcript rows in the dataset; Actb was not measured as a DE gene, SRF/MRTFB protein activity was not assayed, and weak Mrtfa engagement can mask a true canonical program.

summary: Mrtfa showed essentially no score-vector convergence with actin-family, TGF-beta/BMP-receptor, or global nearest-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues that the weak Mrtfa signature is not a hidden version of an actin-regulatory or receptor-neighbor program in this dataset, despite curated Mrtfa links to Srf, Actb, Rhoa, Diaph1, and Smad3.
main_caveats: SRF and Mrtfb themselves were not perturbation targets; correlations were computed on already-weak signatures and should be interpreted as absence of detectable phenocopy, not as pathway independence in vivo.

summary: Adcy3 mRNA depletion was widespread but strongest in selected midbrain, hypothalamic/thalamic, and corticofugal classes rather than uniformly across all neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The target was engaged in the dataset, so downstream null results in the best-engaged classes are interpretable, while weak classes need caution.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Target transcript reduction is an mRNA proxy and does not prove protein or cAMP reduction in every cell type.

summary: FDR-significant Adcy3 self-depletion did not propagate to any FDR-significant downstream mRNA in the steady-state Wilcoxon results.
why_it_matters: ADCY3 is an enzymatic cAMP node, so a target-only RNA phenotype implies that the relevant response may be post-transcriptional, spatially ciliary, temporally transient, or diluted across broad subclasses.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay measured RNA only; nominal downstream genes could still be real but were not distinguishable from multiple-testing background.

summary: Adcy3 was transcriptionally distinct from the assayed Adcy1 and Adcy5 paralogs.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating all adenylyl cyclase perturbations as fungible in neuronal Perturb-seq and is compatible with ADCY3-specific spatial regulation at cilia.
main_caveats: Adcy1 and Adcy5 had weaker measured self-transcript engagement, so some divergence may reflect perturbation strength rather than pure paralog biology.

summary: Assayed G-protein, PKA, melanocortin, BBSome, and ciliary GPCR pathway neighbors had near-zero similarity to Adcy3.
why_it_matters: Known MC4R→ADCY3 ciliary signaling is not recovered as a broad steady-state transcriptomic module, which narrows how this Perturb-seq readout should be used for obesity biology.
main_caveats: The PVH MC4R neurons highlighted in the literature may be rare within the broad hypothalamic class labels and pathway activity was not measured directly.

summary: Adcy3 showed a weak positive-neighbor relationship with AP2 adaptor and ciliary-assembly perturbations.
why_it_matters: Although modest, the unbiased neighbor list points toward receptor trafficking and cilia, the same subcellular context in which ADCY3 and MC4R are functionally linked.
main_caveats: The largest restricted cosine was only 0.126, so this is a hypothesis for follow-up rather than a definitive pathway activation score.

summary: The apparent lack of Adcy3 response in 308 CB GABA and 215 MB Dopa is best explained by weak measured target engagement.
why_it_matters: These negative cell types should not be used as evidence that cerebellar GABAergic or dopaminergic neurons are biologically resistant to AC3 loss.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The evidence is restricted to the target transcript; low baseline Adcy3 expression, editing without transcript decay, or low cell count could all produce this pattern.

summary: Because human ADCY3 loss-of-function is obesogenic and the dataset lacked a compensatory mRNA rescue after Adcy3 knockdown, chronic ADCY3 inhibition remains directionally risky.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq result gives no transcriptomic evidence that neurons buffer ADCY3 loss by upregulating an alternate cAMP program, which matters for any strategy that would lower ADCY3 activity.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is a directionality warning inferred from human genetics plus mouse-brain transcriptomics, not a drug study and not an assay of appetite circuitry.

summary: Atxn1 perturbation elicited a concentrated transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than a pan-neuronal response.
why_it_matters: The response was not simply proportional to neuronal identity or cell number; it points to a thalamic glutamatergic context in which the ATXN1 network is unusually responsive.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the highest Atxn1 perturbed-cell count; the cerebellar GABA bin is broad and not a purified Purkinje-cell assay; target mRNA depletion was not detected.

summary: Cic was the uniquely strong Atxn1 signature neighbor in responsive thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The top-ranked, directionally concordant Atxn1-Cic overlap links the Perturb-seq signature to the physical ATXN1-CIC transcriptional-repressor complex rather than to a generic stress or ataxia-gene program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset measures RNA after guide perturbation, not ATXN1-CIC protein occupancy; weaker Celf2 and Srrm2 correlations are exploratory and not interpreted as direct ATXN1 partners.

direction: concordant mixed up and down marker set
summary: A shared Atxn1-Cic reporter module containing Ankrd55, Tecr, Aldh1l2, Lrrc7, Trim9, and Grin2c marked the strongest responsive thalamic state.
why_it_matters: These genes give a compact candidate readout for ATXN1-CIC disruption in this cell type, with both induced and repressed markers instead of relying on Atxn1 mRNA itself.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Reporter genes are nominated from one cell type; direct CIC binding or ATXN1-CIC occupancy was not measured.

summary: Atxn1 did not behave interchangeably with the ataxia-family perturbations Atxn2, Atxn7, or Atxn10.
why_it_matters: Ataxia gene labels were a poor predictor of single-cell transcriptomic state: Atxn10 was active but uncorrelated with Atxn1, while Atxn2 and Atxn7 produced weak or no thalamic signatures.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The comparison uses transcriptome correlations within the assayed cell types and does not test protein aggregation, repeat-expansion toxicity, or noncoding-repeat mechanisms.

summary: The large thalamic signature occurred without detectable reduction of the measured Atxn1 transcript.
why_it_matters: Atxn1 mRNA is not a usable scalar target-engagement marker for this perturbation in the dataset; the thalamic response could reflect incomplete capture of the targeted isoform, protein-level effects, delayed network consequences, or guide effects that require follow-up validation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The parquet contains transcript-level differential expression only; guide efficiency, indels, protein abundance, and isoform-specific knockdown were not measured here.

direction: synaptic genes down in the Atxn1 thalamic response
summary: Wild-type Atxn1 perturbation remodeled synaptic and ATXN1-CIC-linked transcripts in thalamic neurons, a tissue-safety context for ATXN1-lowering strategies.
why_it_matters: Lowering toxic ATXN1 is a rational SCA1 strategy, but this dataset suggests that non-disease Atxn1 perturbation is not silent in every neuronal class and should be evaluated outside Purkinje-centered readouts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a guide-perturbation expression signature in wild-type mouse brain cells, not an ASO dose-response or SCA1 disease-rescue experiment.

summary: Cxcr4 perturbation produced a globally sparse or weakly engaged transcriptional phenotype rather than a broad loss-of-CXCR4 program.
why_it_matters: Interpretation should start from weak target-transcript evidence and minimal corrected differential expression, not from the assumption that every cell received a biologically strong CXCR4 knockdown.
main_caveats: DE summaries cannot separate true buffering from ineffective sgRNAs, low endogenous expression, or sparse Cxcr4 detection.

summary: The only FDR<0.05 Cxcr4 effect was Zgpat downregulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, with only subthreshold Pum1 and Flot2 minima in other classes.
why_it_matters: The corrected signal is cell-type restricted but does not map to the curated CXCL12-CXCR4 pathway, so it is best treated as a hypothesis rather than a mechanistic module.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only one gene survived FDR correction; Pum1 and Flot2 were not FDR<0.05; no known CXCR4 mechanism was inferred for Zgpat.

summary: Cxcr4 perturbation did not significantly alter assayed CXCL12, ACKR3/CXCR7, Gi, adenylyl-cyclase, MAPK, PI3K/AKT, Rho-family, or arrestin transcripts.
why_it_matters: Curated CXCR4 biology is dominated by ligand-gated GPCR signaling, so a lack of steady-state RNA changes in these pathway genes argues that the Perturb-seq endpoint did not capture canonical pathway activation or inhibition.
main_caveats: GPCR second messengers and MAPK or AKT phosphorylation can change without altering mRNA abundance.

summary: Pvalb, Sst, and CTX-CGE GABA classes lacked corrected Cxcr4 responses despite strong literature evidence that Cxcl12/Cxcr4/Cxcr7 regulates embryonic cortical interneuron migration.
why_it_matters: The result narrows the assay context: the dataset does not reproduce a migration and lamination phenotype as a multi-gene mRNA response in these surviving GABAergic classes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Literature studies assayed embryonic migration and receptor signaling, whereas this dataset measures RNA in recovered cell classes with weak on-target transcript evidence.

summary: Cxcr4 showed no meaningful convergence with other assayed chemokine receptors or with any full-transcriptome signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The broad chemokine-GPCR family did not define a shared neuronal Perturb-seq module under these conditions, and the Cxcr4 signature has no strong positive or opposing comparator for mechanistic triangulation.
main_caveats: Correlations used all measured genes from a weak Cxcr4 signature; lack of similarity can reflect low signal-to-noise.

summary: The weak neuronal RNA phenotype should not be used as standalone evidence that CXCR4 antagonism is CNS-neutral or biologically unimportant.
why_it_matters: CXCR4 antagonists can be therapeutically beneficial in gain-of-function WHIM syndrome, but mouse loss-of-function literature shows strong neurodevelopmental migration and dentate-gyrus phenotypes that are not assayed by steady-state DE.
main_caveats: Clinical WHIM biology is hematopoietic and gain-of-function; developmental mouse phenotypes and this pooled Perturb-seq endpoint are only indirectly matched.

summary: Atp1a2 produced no 5% FDR-significant transcriptomic response in the assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation should be treated as a dataset null rather than as a pathway-changing Na+/K+-ATPase phenotype; the only sub-10% FDR signal was a solitary Ubr1 increase that remained above the 5% FDR cutoff.
main_caveats: The absence of FDR-significant genes is confounded by weak measured Atp1a2 mRNA engagement.

summary: The Atp1a2 null is best interpreted as a neuronal-environment restriction, not as evidence that ATP1A2 biology is inert in brain.
why_it_matters: Adult ATP1A2/Atp1a2 action is concentrated in astrocytic Na+ and K+ handling and glutamate uptake, whereas this file contains neuronal Glut/GABA/Dopa labels and no astrocyte class.
cell_types: assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: The conclusion uses cell-class labels rather than independent marker-level reconstruction of every sequenced cell.

summary: Atp1a2 was not interchangeable with the Na+/K+-ATPase catalytic paralogs Atp1a1 and Atp1a3 in this screen.
why_it_matters: Atp1a1 and especially Atp1a3 showed detectable on-target depletion and FDR-significant responses under the same analysis settings, while Atp1a2 did not; score correlations of Atp1a2 with either paralog stayed near zero.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and depends on each guide set achieving target knockdown; Atp1a2 itself lacked detectable mRNA depletion.

summary: Curated ATP1A2 membership in plasma-membrane P-type ATPase ion transport did not translate into a detectable neuronal transcriptional ion-homeostasis program.
why_it_matters: The Reactome assignment correctly places ATP1A2 in an ATP1A:ATP1B:FXYD Na+/K+ exchange complex, but this perturbation did not move that module or any downstream module at 5% FDR in the assayed neuronal classes.
cell_types: assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: A null transcriptional readout cannot exclude acute electrophysiologic or metabolic phenotypes, and target engagement was weak.

summary: No positive or negative signature-neighbor module emerged for Atp1a2.
why_it_matters: The strongest Atp1a2 correlations to any other perturbation were very small and included safe-target controls among the extremes, arguing against a reproducible pathway-neighbor or disease-family convergence in these data.
comparators: top positive signature neighbors|top negative signature neighbors|Safe_target_40|Safe_target_56|Safe_target_92
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors and may miss non-linear or protein-level convergence.

summary: The neuronal Atp1a2 null would not predict astrocyte- and timing-dependent liabilities of ATP1A2 reduction.
why_it_matters: Independent astrocyte ASO work in SOD1 mice reduced SOD1 aggregation yet accelerated disease onset and shortened lifespan, so a neuron-only Perturb-seq null should not be read as evidence that Atp1a2 knockdown is broadly neutral or beneficial.
cell_types: assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: The ALS evidence is from a specific mutant-SOD1 astrocyte model and cannot be generalized to all ATP1A2 diseases.

summary: Adnp loss produced its broadest FDR-level signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest response is concentrated in a thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class rather than distributed across all excitatory or inhibitory neurons, refining expectations from ADNP's broad developmental chromatin role.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Target-transcript knockdown was only nominal, and literature studies were not performed in the same mouse thalamic neuron class.

summary: Cacnb3 induction and Plppr3/Atp9a repression form a sparse recurrent Adnp output across midbrain, hindbrain, and Pvalb GABA contexts.
why_it_matters: These genes may be simpler response markers than the full 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature because they recur in cell types with only one to three FDR-level hits.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cacnb3 is single-gene in Pvalb and Plppr3/Atp9a are not FDR-significant in every Cacnb3-positive cell type.

summary: Measured Adnp self-knockdown was weak and did not explain downstream effect size across cell types.
why_it_matters: The cell type with the largest observed Adnp transcript decrease had no FDR-level downstream genes, whereas the strongest downstream class had only nominal Adnp depletion; response strength should therefore not be inferred from the target transcript row alone.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: A null FDR result can reflect low power or sgRNA effects on unmeasured target isoforms rather than true biological buffering.

summary: Chd4 was the nearest non-self Adnp signature neighbor in the two strongest Adnp classes, supporting a ChAHP-like transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: CHD4 is a physical ADNP partner in ChAHP, so the cross-perturbation convergence ties the single-cell perturbation output to a defined chromatin complex rather than only to ADNP disease genetics.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Score correlations were modest, especially in 155 MB Glut, and Chd4 was not a direct rescue of Adnp.

summary: Arid2 diverged from Adnp in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while Chd4 converged.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-generalizing ADNP loss as equivalent to any chromatin-remodeler perturbation and refines the SWI/SNF-related disease label toward a CHD4/ChAHP-biased state in this neuron class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Arid2 was identified by transcriptomic anti-correlation only; the dataset does not prove direct antagonism between ADNP and ARID2 complexes.

summary: A NAP/davunetide-style microtubule intervention would need to rescue the Chd4-like transcriptional program and the Cacnb3/Plppr3 output to claim broad Adnp correction.
why_it_matters: The clinically discussed ADNP peptide branch is mechanistically distinct from the perturb-seq ChAHP-like branch, so transcriptional biomarkers should be included in rescue assays.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: No drug, NAP peptide, end-binding-protein, or rescue perturbation was assayed.

summary: Dlx5 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any of the 23 assayed mouse brain cell types.
why_it_matters: This global null establishes that Dlx5 downstream biology in this run is buffered, weak, or ineffectively engaged and that nominal rows must be treated as exploratory.
main_caveats: The DE table does not measure guide editing or DLX5 protein loss, so a null transcriptome could reflect incomplete perturbation or timing rather than dispensability.

summary: The only nominal Dlx5 target-transcript decreases appeared in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
why_it_matters: The weak target-row pattern points toward the expected GABAergic territory while making clear that the on-target effect did not survive multiple testing.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Both rows had FDR=1.0 and no direct protein-level validation.

summary: Nominal Dlx5 depletion in Pvalb and CNU-LGE GABA cells did not significantly repress Gad1, Gad2, Slc32a1, Slc6a1, or Arx; Lhx6 was only nominally lower in Pvalb cells.
why_it_matters: A canonical inhibitory-neuron differentiation module expected from Dlx-family developmental studies was not coupled to single-gene Dlx5 perturbation in this assay.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The literature is dominated by embryonic or double-gene Dlx perturbations, whereas these are acute, single-Dlx5, transcriptomic contrasts with weak target mRNA evidence.

summary: The linked paralog Dlx6 did not phenocopy Dlx5; Dlx5-Dlx6 signature correlations were approximately zero in all shared Dlx5 cell types.
why_it_matters: Dlx5 and Dlx6 are usually interpreted together in GABAergic development, so their lack of observed convergence is important and argues against hiding the Dlx5 signal under a Dlx6-like transcriptomic state.
main_caveats: Both Dlx5 and Dlx6 perturbations were FDR-null, so the apparent divergence may primarily reflect weak engagement or noise.

summary: Arx, another GABA-associated homeobox perturbation, generated FDR-significant Pvalb and CTX-CGE GABA responses while Dlx5 generated none.
why_it_matters: This internal comparator shows that the dataset can register at least some GABAergic transcription-factor perturbations, making the Dlx5 null a target-specific observation.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Arx was not a measured biochemical positive control for Dlx5 editing; it is a same-dataset biological comparator.

summary: The FDR-null brain Dlx5 signature should not be interpreted as evidence that DLX5/DLX6 loss of function is systemically safe.
why_it_matters: DLX5 is a developmental homeobox factor and the human DLX5/DLX6 locus is sensitive to regulatory loss in congenital limb and craniofacial disease, so acute brain Perturb-seq cannot de-risk systemic inhibition.
main_caveats: No DLX5-targeted therapy was tested; this is a direction-of-interpretation warning, not pharmacology.

summary: Add1 perturbation was detectable at the target transcript but did not generate any FDR-significant gene in 21 assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: The measurable on-target direction without a recurrent downstream mRNA program indicates that alpha-adducin loss is buffered or primarily structural in this Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself did not pass FDR<=0.05; protein depletion and subcellular axonal effects were not measured.

direction: on-target Add1 decrease with buffered downstream response
summary: 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the strongest well-powered Add1 transcript decreases, but both lacked FDR-significant downstream genes; 145 MH-LH TH Glut showed a larger nominal logFC with low cell count.
why_it_matters: These cell types separate target-transcript engagement from a propagated mRNA phenotype and help distinguish true buffering from total guide failure.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: 155 and 151 still had adjusted p values above 0.05 for Add1; 145 had only 29 perturbed cells.

summary: Add1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Add2 and Add3 signatures in shared cell types despite known adducin-family complex membership.
why_it_matters: Physical membership in alpha/beta or alpha/gamma adducin complexes did not translate into interchangeable whole-cell mRNA phenotypes.
main_caveats: All three adducin perturbations had weak FDR-level responses, so correlations test only restricted signatures.

summary: Measured actin, spectrin, ankyrin, and small-GTPase pathway perturbations did not phenocopy the Add1 signature.
why_it_matters: The literature-supported Add1 cytoskeletal neighborhood is not recovered as a broad transcriptional module in this dataset, arguing against simple pathway scoring from scRNA-seq.
main_caveats: Only measured dataset targets could be compared; the test uses score correlations from weak Add1 signatures.

direction: disease-relevant loss of function but mRNA-buffered in this assay
summary: Known ADD1 developmental and axonal disease mechanisms are not mirrored by an acute recurrent mouse-brain mRNA program after Add1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The result warns that ADD1-related corpus-callosum, ventriculomegaly, and axon-caliber biology may require developmental timing or cytoskeletal morphology assays rather than a cell-body transcriptomic biomarker.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is not matched to human developmental malformations or mouse null phenotypes and did not measure hydrocephalus, corpus callosum, or axon diameter.

summary: Lztr1 RNA depletion was FDR-supported in only 2 of 22 tested neuronal classes, led by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: Most downstream interpretation should be restricted to cell types with demonstrable target knockdown; weakly engaged classes are not strong negative tests of LZTR1 biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction may reflect baseline expression, sgRNA sampling, and per-cell-type power as well as biology.

direction: Lztr1 and Nf1 loss up; Braf, Map2k1, Kras, and Shoc2 loss down for the restricted module
summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the nominal Lztr1 module is concordant with Nf1 loss and opposed to Braf, Kras, Map2k1, and Shoc2 loss, matching de-repression of RAS/MAPK signaling.
why_it_matters: This converts otherwise weak Lztr1 downstream DE into a directionally interpretable pathway readout in one neuronal class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Lztr1 genes used for the correlation were nominal only; full-transcriptome correlations were small.

summary: Strong Lztr1 target depletion produced almost no FDR-significant non-target mRNA response.
why_it_matters: The expected biochemical consequence of LZTR1 loss may be largely post-translational or transcriptionally buffered in mature neurons at this sampling point.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Buffered RNA response does not exclude large changes in RAS localization, ubiquitination, GTP loading, or ERK phosphorylation.

summary: Cacna1b is a near-threshold non-target marker of Lztr1 perturbation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: It is the clearest on-target cortical readout and is distinct from the Vgf/Ptpn5 thalamic module, suggesting cell-type-specific outputs downstream of Lztr1 knockdown.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cacna1b was just above FDR 0.05 and lacked an annotated mechanistic connection to LZTR1 in this analysis.

summary: Cul3 perturbation did not phenocopy Lztr1 in the two main Lztr1-engaged cell classes.
why_it_matters: Although LZTR1 is a CUL3 adaptor, the scaffold perturbation is not an interchangeable proxy for the adaptor in this neuronal dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cul3 had weaker target engagement and lower cell counts in the matched cell types; broad CUL3 biology may obscure LZTR1-adaptor-specific effects.

summary: Atp6v0a1 guide-defined perturbation yielded strong target-mRNA depletion in six neuronal classes and near-significant depletion in four more, while many assayed classes had weak engagement.
why_it_matters: Interpretation of non-responsive cell types must be conditioned on target knockdown: the dataset contains a clear Atp6v0a1 loss signal only in a restricted subset of the 22 assayed cell types.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The six-cell-type pattern is based on the target transcript rather than protein depletion; 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 37 perturbed cells.

summary: Even where Atp6v0a1 mRNA was significantly reduced, the downstream single-cell RNA signature was essentially self-limited.
why_it_matters: A partial decrease of a neuronal V-ATPase V0 a-subunit did not trigger a robust lysosomal, stress, synaptic, or homeostatic RNA program in this assay, indicating that RNA readouts can remain buffered despite perturbing an acidification complex.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Buffering is inferred from mRNA differential expression only; residual Atp6v0a1 protein, incomplete knockdown, or post-transcriptional pH changes could mask functional defects.

summary: Atp6v0c and Atp6v0a1, two members of the same V-ATPase V0 sector, were not interchangeable at the transcriptome level: Atp6v0c perturbation was broad, whereas Atp6v0a1 perturbation was largely target-only.

cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA

summary: Perturbing Atp6v0c, Atp6ap1, or Atp6ap2 recurrently reduced Atp6v0a1 mRNA, but direct Atp6v0a1 perturbation did not reciprocally induce or repress other measured V-ATPase subunits at FDR<0.05.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The evidence is transcript-level and does not show whether Atp6v0a1 mRNA falls because of V-ATPase misassembly, altered cell state, or differential guide strength.

summary: The muted Atp6v0a1 knockdown signature contrasts with ATP6V0A1 disease models in which strong missense or biallelic variants impair lysosomal acidification, autophagy, mTORC1 signaling, neuronal integrity, and synaptic function.
why_it_matters: Absence of a large RNA phenotype after partial Atp6v0a1 depletion should not be read as absence of V-ATPase neurotoxicity; pathogenic ATP6V0A1 alleles may act through stronger, developmental, or post-transcriptional endolysosomal mechanisms.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The dataset perturbs mouse Atp6v0a1 transcript rather than human missense proteins, and it lacks direct lysosomal pH, autophagy flux, neuronal survival, and synaptic vesicle acidification assays.

summary: Atp6v0a1 depletion did not elicit detectable transcriptional compensation by paralogous a-subunits, V1-sector subunits, V0-sector subunits, or the ATP6AP accessory genes measured in the dataset.
why_it_matters: V-ATPase robustness in this assay is not explained by induced replacement of other pump transcripts; compensation, if present, must be constitutive, post-transcriptional, or outside the measured genes.

summary: Kcnc2 perturbation produced FDR-significant target-transcript depletion only in 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut among 22 measured cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: The cell-type restriction defines which dataset contexts are interpretable as true Kcnc2 loss, and it separates robust target engagement from nominal or absent guide effects.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Some non-FDR cell types, especially 053 Sst Gaba and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, had sizeable nominal target decreases and could be underpowered.

summary: The three Kcnc2-engaged cell types showed a buffered mRNA response: Kcnc2 itself was the only FDR-significant gene in each signature.
why_it_matters: Kv3.2 is a membrane channel, so a buffered scRNA-seq response means lack of secondary DE should not be interpreted as lack of electrophysiological consequence.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Nominal non-target genes exist but all failed FDR correction; electrophysiology was not measured.

summary: The Pvalb GABA response confirms a canonical Kv3.2 fast-spiking-interneuron context but does not show loss of inhibitory-cell identity transcripts.
why_it_matters: KCNC2 disease models often emphasize PV interneuron firing; these data place target engagement in a Pvalb class while keeping the mechanism at excitability rather than wholesale interneuron-state remodeling.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Pvalb class had 72 perturbed cells; scRNA-seq may miss firing-rate phenotypes and subcellular channel effects.

summary: Kcnc2 was robustly depleted in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic classes, extending the dataset signal beyond inhibitory interneurons.
why_it_matters: Disease and circuit interpretations should include excitatory thalamic/midbrain neurons as plausible Kv3.2-sensitive cells, not only cortical PV interneurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut

summary: MIF receptor and inflammatory pathway genes were transcriptionally silent after Mif knockdown, and Cxcr2/Cxcr4/Tlr4/NF-kB-MAPK neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Mif.
why_it_matters: Known MIF biology centers on CD74 with CXCR2 or CXCR4, but these neuronal signatures showed neither receptor compensation nor shared signatures with available receptor/pathway perturbations, narrowing the dataset-supported action to a weak on-target RNA effect rather than a canonical inflammatory cascade.
main_caveats: Cd74, Cd44, Ackr3, and Ddt were not perturbations in this library; Cxcr2 was measured as a transcript in only 8 Mif cell-type signatures; phospho-ERK, NF-kB localization, secretion, and paracrine recruitment were not assayed.

summary: The dopaminergic-neuron result is underpowered and should not be read as evidence that MIF is irrelevant to Parkinson-related stress biology.
why_it_matters: MIF is discussed as a neurological-disease biomarker and drug target, and MIF inhibitors exist; however, the MB Dopa bin had only 36 Mif-perturbed cells, nominal-only target knockdown, and no FDR-level downstream response, so this Perturb-seq dataset cannot establish protective or harmful consequences of inhibiting MIF in injured dopaminergic neurons.

main_caveats: Low perturbed-cell count; healthy in vivo single-cell transcriptomics is an indirect context for progressive or inflammatory dopaminergic injury.

summary: Top positive and inverse whole-signature neighbors were weak and concentrated in 308 CB GABA, not a robust MIF module.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Trp53inp2 passed FDR<0.05; other genes in the same cell type were nominal, and no direct FBXW7-TP53INP2 regulatory relationship was identified.

summary: The two L2/3 intratelencephalic glutamatergic classes with the strongest Fbxw7 mRNA depletion had no FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from transcriptional responsiveness and suggests buffering, too little power, or protein-level biology not captured by mRNA profiling in these cortical neurons.

main_caveats: The assay measures RNA rather than FBXW7 substrate protein stability, and the primary Fbxw7 signature is sparse.

summary: No assayed perturbation, including assayed F-box/cullin relatives, produced a strong Fbxw7-like or opposite signature.

direction: loss of Fbxw7 without canonical mRNA activation

summary: Pax1 perturbation produced a broad buffered or under-engaged response across the adult mouse-brain panel.

summary: The adult brain response is largely absent despite strong developmental skeletal and thymic PAX1 disease biology.

summary: Direct PAX1 targeting is not supported as an adult-brain therapeutic direction by this dataset or by current tractability databases.
why_it_matters: A Mendelian developmental disease gene can still be a poor direct adult-neuronal drug target; the weak perturbation response and absence of clinical candidates argue for focusing on developmental mechanism or downstream biomarkers instead.
main_caveats: Database tractability is incomplete and does not rule out future nucleic-acid or developmental interventions; the dataset itself lacks direct target-engagement readouts.

summary: Human EDEM3 loss-of-function disease should not be modeled as a broad acute UPR transcriptional state in these mouse neuronal perturbations.
why_it_matters: Biallelic EDEM3 variants cause a congenital disorder of glycosylation with neurodevelopmental involvement, whereas the mouse-brain Edem3 transcriptome is FDR-silent; this points toward glycan processing, cell-biological ER quality control, developmental timing, or unassayed cell types as readouts to prioritize over bulk Xbp1/Hspa5-style mRNA stress markers.
main_caveats: Species, genetic context, developmental stage, cell populations, and perturbation dose differ from recessive human congenital disease.

summary: Edem3 lacked a robust positive or negative whole-signature neighbor in the best-sampled cell types inspected.
why_it_matters: The top nominal genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut are not part of a strong recurrent Perturb-seq program, further supporting a weak or idiosyncratic Edem3 mRNA phenotype.

main_caveats: Transcriptomics does not read out EXT2 protein, Golgi polymerase activity, or heparan-sulfate chain structure.

summary: No recurrent axon-guidance, synaptic, or HS-responsive non-target module was detected; the only non-target FDR<0.1 rows were isolated Epha5 and Slc6a17 decreases in cell types without FDR-confirmed Ext2 depletion.

main_caveats: Both rows are near-FDR rather than FDR<0.05, are single-cell-type events, and one occurs with no measurable Ext2 transcript depletion.

summary: Ext2 did not show a shared transcriptomic state with its EXT1 complex partner or selected HS-related neighbors in the same cell types.
why_it_matters: The canonical EXT1:EXT2 complex would motivate a phenocopy search, but weak Ext1 self-depletion and near-zero correlations with other engaged HS-related perturbations show that the dataset does not support interchangeability at the mRNA-signature level.

main_caveats: Ext1 was not an engaged comparator, and Hs6st2, Agrn, Bmpr2, Fgfr1, and Fgf13 are pathway-neighbor or functional-neighbor comparisons rather than the same enzymatic complex.

summary: The sparse neuronal mRNA response contrasts with severe developmental EXT/HS phenotypes, pointing to developmental timing, glycan biochemistry, and extracellular signaling as likely layers missed here.
why_it_matters: EXT2 disease mechanisms should not be inferred from acute or endpoint mRNA changes alone; HS quantity and structure can shape morphogen and synaptic signaling without a large immediate transcriptomic echo.

main_caveats: The dataset cell types, developmental stage, perturbation strength, and readout differ from germline human disease and embryonic mouse knockouts.

summary: The lack of a large downstream RNA signature should not be interpreted as support for EXT2 inhibition.

main_caveats: No drug perturbation was tested; the warning is directional and genetic rather than based on a measured inhibitor.

summary: Gpr162 transcript depletion was reproducibly strongest in thalamic/midbrain and midbrain/pons/medulla neuronal classes rather than forming a uniform pan-neuronal response.

main_caveats: On-target mRNA depletion is used as the engagement readout; weak classes could reflect low expression, guide performance, or low perturbed-cell counts rather than absence of biological function.

summary: The best-engaged Gpr162 perturbations were transcriptionally buffered: the depleted Gpr162 transcript itself was the only transcriptome-wide significant gene in each of the three FDR-significant cell classes.
why_it_matters: A 7-transmembrane receptor can, in principle, couple to rapid second-messenger pathways without producing a large basal mRNA program; the screen therefore argues against a broad constitutive cell-state switch after partial Gpr162 loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay captures steady-state mRNA, not receptor coupling, second messengers, phosphorylation, synaptic physiology, or challenged states.

summary: Basal neuronal Gpr162 depletion did not activate or repress a STING/TBK1/Cxcl10 transcriptional proxy module, despite cancer-cell literature linking GPR162 to STING-dependent IRF3 and chemokine induction.
why_it_matters: This separates the DNA-damage/radiotherapy role of GPR162 from the unchallenged brain-cell perturbation phenotype and cautions that the GPR162-STING axis may be stimulus- or cell-context dependent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The screen did not include irradiation or cGAS-STING stimulation, and IRF3/CXCL4 activity was not captured as protein phosphorylation or secreted interferon.

summary: Cartpt mRNA did not respond to Gpr162 perturbation in any profiled cell class, so Gpr162 loss did not trigger a detectable transcriptional feedback loop on its proposed CART peptide ligand.
why_it_matters: If CART-GPR162 signaling operates in brain, these data suggest that receptor depletion alone is not sufficient to tune ligand-transcript abundance at steady state.
main_caveats: The CART receptor evidence comes from pancreatic beta cells; Cartpt peptide release, receptor binding, and stimulated neuronal signaling were not measured.

summary: Ppp2r5d induction in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut was the strongest non-target Gpr162-associated row and the only non-target row below FDR 0.2, nominating an exploratory PP2A-B56δ cortical marker.
why_it_matters: PPP2R5D is itself an established neurodevelopmental-disease gene, so even a weak, cell-restricted link could be biologically important if it validates in a better-powered cortical perturbation.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Ppp2r5d did not pass FDR<0.05, and the Gpr162 self row in this same L2/3 class was only nominal; treat as a hypothesis, not a validated pathway.

summary: Gpr162 signatures were nearly orthogonal to every other perturbation in the three best-engaged classes, and the screen did not contain an engaged Gpr153 or orphan-GPCR comparator that could substitute for a true paralog test.
why_it_matters: The absence of a strong positive or negative neighbor argues that the perturbation is not simply recapitulating a common screen-wide transcriptional axis and that Gpr162 biology remains underresolved in this screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from score vectors and do not prove mechanistic independence; most literature-defined receptor relatives were absent from the perturbation panel.

summary: Kcna2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional program across 21 tested neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: This preserves the main result as an interpretable negative: a voltage-gated channel perturbation can be biologically important yet largely invisible to a steady-state RNA screen.
main_caveats: Target transcript depletion itself was weak and never FDR-significant, so buffering and insufficient engagement cannot be separated.

summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba showed the strongest nominal Kcna2 self-depletion, but the response remained an isolated, non-FDR target-row signal.
why_it_matters: This nominates Pvalb GABA as the best engagement context in the file while preventing overinterpretation as a downstream Pvalb state switch.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Kcna2 self row was nominal only; the literature support is an indirect mouse inhibitory-terminal context rather than a matched Perturb-seq Pvalb class.

summary: Available Kv1 pore and beta-subunit perturbations did not share a transcriptomic program: Kcna1/Kcna2/Kcnab1 were FDR-null, Kcnab2 was self-only, and Kcna2 signatures were nearly uncorrelated with all three comparators.

summary: The Kcna2-null RNA signature refines KCNA2 channelopathy toward a post-transcriptional or electrophysiological mechanism rather than a robust cell-state module.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse genetics show that KCNA2/Kcna2 perturbation is pathogenic; the dataset shows that differential expression is a poor proxy for those channel defects under the tested conditions.
main_caveats: The dataset is a perturbation-expression screen, not an electrophysiology assay and not a model of specific human coding variants.

summary: The weak Kcna2 knockdown signature should not be interpreted as allele-agnostic support for suppressing KCNA2, because KCNA2 disorders include both loss- and gain-of-function mechanisms.
why_it_matters: A potassium-channel target may be chemically assayable, but therapeutic direction must be allele-specific; absence of a transcriptional injury marker after partial suppression does not establish safety for LoF disease contexts.
main_caveats: No drug was tested in the dataset, and disease variants alter Kv1.2 gating rather than simply reducing Kcna2 mRNA.

summary: Etfa perturbation was globally buffered at the transcriptional level, with no FDR-significant genes across 21 profiled cell classes despite directional reduction of the target transcript in most classes.
why_it_matters: ETF is a central mitochondrial electron-transfer hub, so the absence of a corrected RNA program reframes the experiment as partial or buffered Etfa loss rather than a full MADD-like block.
main_caveats: The high-confidence observation is statistical quiescence; the biological mechanism of buffering is not directly measured.

summary: The clearest nominal on-target Etfa transcript decreases were concentrated in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: If followed up, these caudal and thalamic/midbrain classes are the only contexts in this dataset with appreciable Etfa RNA depletion, but their downstream signatures were still not FDR-supported.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity is based on nominal Etfa rows with FDR=1, not corrected differential expression.

summary: Canonical ETF partners and respiratory-chain transcripts did not show FDR-level transcriptional compensation after Etfa perturbation.
why_it_matters: The measured response is uncoupled from the expected electron-transfer pathway, cautioning against assigning isolated nominal genes to fatty-acid beta-oxidation or OXPHOS remodeling.
main_caveats: Only mRNA abundance was measured; ETF protein activity, protein turnover, and acylcarnitine accumulation were not assayed.

summary: Etfa's restricted nominal signature was nearly uncorrelated with Bckdhb, Ivd, Dld, Pcca, and Acox1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: The Etfa response is not simply a generic organic-acid or fatty-acid catabolism stress signature, even though Etfa lies in a STRING functional neighborhood with ETF and acyl-CoA dehydrogenase genes.
main_caveats: Correlation used only 90 nominal Etfa p<0.001 features; low similarity may reflect weak target engagement and cell-count differences.

summary: The quiet neuronal RNA phenotype should not be interpreted as support for ETFA inhibition.
why_it_matters: ETFA/ETF loss is linked to MADD, and this ChEMBL query found no curated ETFA mechanism entries; therefore the negative Perturb-seq phenotype most likely reflects assay sensitivity and partial perturbation rather than a benign loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: This is a directionality warning, not a direct pharmacology experiment.

direction: Arid1a down with mixed downstream up and down regulation

main_caveats: Pearson correlations were modest in absolute value, and Smarca4 had weak target engagement.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

direction: loss-of-function response in a thalamic glutamatergic class

why_it_matters: Coffin-Siris and mouse developmental studies establish ARID1A-BAF neural importance, while this dataset nominates a specific mature mouse-brain glutamatergic class where Arid1a loss remains transcriptionally visible.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The screen is transcriptomic and does not measure Coffin-Siris phenotypes, cortical wiring, hippocampal morphology, or cognition.

direction: Arid1a loss is potentially harmful in susceptible neurons
summary: The screen supports caution against neuronal ARID1A suppression even though ARID1A loss creates targetable synthetic-lethal cancer states.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No drug was tested in the Perturb-seq dataset, and EZH2/PARP synthetic-lethality literature comes from cancer systems.
