summary: Foxj3 signatures were not phenocopied by forkhead-family or STRING-nominated neighboring perturbations.
why_it_matters: Related forkhead factors can occupy overlapping chromatin regions, and STRING nominates developmental and regulatory neighbors for Foxj3, yet the actual perturbation signatures were nearly orthogonal; FOXJ3 should therefore not be treated as interchangeable with any assayed neighbor in this dataset.
main_caveats: Restricted to perturbations present in the same cell types; the closest paralog Foxj2 was not available as a targeted comparator, and low Foxj3 signal limits correlation power.

summary: No recurrent cross-cell-type nominal module emerged from Foxj3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The nominal rows are mostly single-cell-type events, so they do not justify a shared pathway or biomarker module downstream of Foxj3.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative convergence statement; it does not exclude cell-type-specific effects below the sensitivity of the assay.

summary: Gns mRNA knockdown was strongest and FDR-significant only in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, with a borderline direct effect in 155 MB Glut and nominal direct decreases in several other classes.
why_it_matters: The primary positive signal is target engagement itself, and it is not uniform enough to justify strong cell-type negatives outside the best-engaged classes.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only one cell type passed FDR; several negative cell types had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Even where target knockdown was detectable, acute Gns perturbation produced no FDR-supported secondary transcriptome response.
why_it_matters: This separates proximal mRNA engagement from the chronic lysosomal storage biology expected after GNS enzyme deficiency.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Buffered transcriptome could reflect residual protein or incomplete knockdown; substrate storage was not measured.

summary: Available lysosomal and glycosaminoglycan-related perturbations did not converge with Gns despite stronger on-target knockdown in several comparators.
why_it_matters: The lack of convergence argues against a common acute lysosomal-stress expression module in this assay and prevents treating indirect lysosomal comparators as interchangeable with GNS.
main_caveats: Closest Sanfilippo genes were not screened, and many comparator perturbations were themselves sparse at the FDR level.

summary: Gns perturbation did not induce the astrocyte, microglial, or lysosomal marker pattern reported in chronic murine Sanfilippo D brain.
why_it_matters: The result refines the disease mechanism by showing that acute neuronal mRNA depletion is insufficient to reproduce chronic storage-associated neuroinflammation.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq cell classes do not include a primary microglia or astrocyte compartment and assayed mRNA rather than histology.

summary: The weak downstream signature should not be interpreted as evidence that GNS inhibition is safe or that GNS restoration is unimportant.
why_it_matters: GNS loss causes an enzyme-deficiency disease and replacement strategies act on stored substrate, so transcriptomic silence in this assay is a false-negative risk for therapeutic prioritization.
main_caveats: Therapeutic studies measure storage correction after constitutive deficiency, not the same acute CRISPRi context as the dataset.

summary: Agtr2 CRISPRi was target-negative: the measured Agtr2 mRNA did not decrease in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: Because AGTR2 is a membrane angiotensin II receptor, absence of transcript engagement means downstream null data should not be interpreted as a clean receptor loss-of-function phenotype.
main_caveats: Only mRNA-level target engagement was available; lack of Agtr2 transcript depletion could reflect low basal Agtr2 expression, guide inefficiency, or both.

summary: No Agtr2 cell type produced an FDR-supported downstream expression program; the strongest nominal signals were isolated hotspots rather than a recurrent module.
why_it_matters: The broad negative result spans cortical, hippocampal, thalamic, midbrain, cerebellar, glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, so no specific neuronal class can be nominated from this screen.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Nominal p values were present, but none survived cell-type-level multiple testing and the Agtr2 transcript itself was not knocked down.

summary: Canonical literature-adjacent AT2R readouts did not move transcriptionally after Agtr2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The dataset gives no FDR-level evidence for the MAPK, immediate-early, MTUS1, nitric-oxide, NF-kappaB, or Ptpn6/SHP-1 transcriptional changes that would have connected Agtr2 perturbation to known AT2R signaling in neurons.
main_caveats: This is a failure to elicit transcriptional readouts in a target-negative CRISPRi screen, not evidence that AT2R signaling cannot affect these pathways after ligand stimulation.

summary: Related renin-angiotensin perturbations separated into receptor/regulator targets with no engagement and Atp6ap2 with strong engagement but no Agtr2-like signature.
why_it_matters: The comparison argues against rescuing Agtr2 interpretation by appealing to Agtr1a, Agtrap, or Atp6ap2 signatures: the closest angiotensin receptor/regulator perturbations were themselves target-negative, while the engaged pathway neighbor was transcriptionally uncorrelated with Agtr2.
main_caveats: Atp6ap2 is also a V-ATPase accessory protein and is not an interchangeable AGTR2 receptor subunit; correlations are bulk all-gene score correlations within broad cell classes.

summary: Top positive and negative Agtr2 signature neighbors were too weak to define a convergent biological module.
why_it_matters: All non-self all-gene correlations were below |r|=0.19 and safe-target controls repeatedly ranked among top neighbors, so signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a robust hidden pathway or disease-family convergence.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from per-cell-type Wilcoxon scores, not from replicate-level signatures; weak neighbors were not interpreted mechanistically.

summary: The screen does not provide support for an AGTR2 neurodevelopmental disease transcriptional mechanism in the assayed mouse brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: Human AGTR2 was proposed as an X-linked intellectual-disability gene but that assignment has been questioned; the target-negative mouse result is therefore best treated as non-informative for the germline-developmental disease model rather than as confirmation or refutation.
main_caveats: The disease evidence is human germline/developmental and partly disputed, whereas the dataset is an mRNA CRISPRi screen in mouse brain cell classes with no measured target knockdown.

summary: The negative screen should not be used to deprioritize or derisk AGTR2 agonism.
why_it_matters: AT2R has solved ligand-bound structures and the agonist buloxibutid/C21 is in clinical testing, but this dataset assayed weak or absent Agtr2 knockdown rather than ligand-biased receptor activation.
main_caveats: The screen lacks agonist exposure, protein-level receptor occupancy, and target engagement, so it cannot predict the direction of AGTR2 agonist or antagonist pharmacology.

summary: Kcnb2 targeting was transcriptomically silent at FDR < 0.05 across 22 mouse brain cell types, and the target transcript was never FDR-significantly depleted.
why_it_matters: Kv2.2 is an excitable-membrane potassium-channel subunit, so the dataset should be interpreted as lacking a robust RNA loss-of-channel state rather than as nominating a downstream transcriptional program.
main_caveats: FDR-level null could reflect weak guide activity, low baseline detectability, low cell counts, or a physiological phenotype not captured by scRNA-seq.

summary: The two cell types with nominal Kcnb2 mRNA decreases still had no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: These cells are the best candidates for partial target engagement, but the data show either buffering or insufficient power rather than a reproducible transcriptional response to Kv2.2 loss.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The Kcnb2 decreases are nominal only, both adjusted p values are 1.0, and the relevant electrophysiologic state was not measured.

summary: Kcnb1, but not Kcnb2, triggered a Bdnf/Vgf/Zbtb16/Scg2/Nptx2 module in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The result separates two related Kv2 α subunits that might otherwise be assumed to be interchangeable because they can contribute to related delayed-rectifier channel complexes.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and Kcnb1 had more perturbed cells than Kcnb2; it does not test Kv2.2 protein localization or gating.

summary: Kcnb2 perturbation did not robustly induce Kcnb1 mRNA, and Kcnb1 perturbation did not robustly induce Kcnb2 mRNA.
why_it_matters: The weak Kcnb2 phenotype is not explained by a simple reciprocal mRNA-compensation loop between Kv2 paralogs.
main_caveats: Only mRNA rows were tested; compensation by protein abundance, tetramer stoichiometry, localization, or phosphorylation remains possible.

summary: The Kcnb2 Perturb-seq result is a poor direct model of human mono-allelic KCNB2 missense channelopathy.
why_it_matters: Human disease variants alter channel inactivation, whereas this screen mainly reveals weak or absent transcriptional consequences of targeting Kcnb2 RNA; therapeutic reasoning should therefore prioritize allele-specific channel physiology over this null RNA signature.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse, cell-type aggregated, and lacks electrophysiology; the human pathogenic variants were not recreated.

summary: Nominal Kcnb2 hits were isolated rather than recurrent across cell types.
why_it_matters: The absence of repeated nominal drivers further argues against a shared Kcnb2-induced transcriptional pathway in the assayed cells.
main_caveats: This recurrence analysis uses nominal p < 0.001 rows only; the appropriate primary conclusion remains the FDR-level null.

summary: Guide-defined D630045J12Rik perturbation produced a single FDR-significant Kcnf1 decrease concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: This identifies a narrow thalamic glutamatergic, potassium-channel-linked output instead of a broad brain-wide D630045J12Rik response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript was not measured, and the Kcnf1 hit was not FDR-significant in other cell types.

summary: D630045J12Rik perturbation was MAPK-neutral and transcriptionally distinct from Braf, Map2k1, and Nf1 perturbations in Vgf-responsive neuronal contexts.
why_it_matters: KIAA1549 is clinically linked to oncogenic KIAA1549::BRAF fusions, but native D630045J12Rik perturbation in mouse brain should not be treated as a proxy for BRAF-fusion activation or suppression.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Comparators are native mouse perturbations, not expression of a human KIAA1549::BRAF fusion; Braf on-target RNA depletion was only nominal in the TH comparison.

summary: The KIAA1549 retinitis-pigmentosa/ciliary prior did not manifest as a shared ciliary-perturbation module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The result narrows the brain dataset signal to a Kcnf1-dominated output and argues against broad interchangeability with other ciliary or retinal-disease-family targets in this cell type.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to a mouse-brain thalamic class; no mature photoreceptors were assayed, and the Kcnf1-to-cilium link was not directly tested.

summary: Outside the single Kcnf1 hit, the D630045J12Rik perturbation generated only nominal, non-recurrent DE outliers.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-calling pathways from genes such as Flot2, Paip2, or Sgtb that had low nominal p values but poor FDR support.
main_caveats: The sparse response cannot be separated from unknown guide efficacy because the target transcript was absent from the DE measurements.

summary: The strongest D630045J12Rik cell-type signature had no high-correlation positive or negative neighbor in the perturbation library.
why_it_matters: The absence of a close neighbor argues that this weak signature should not be assigned to a larger convergent pathway by correlation alone.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed within one cell type, and low correlations could reflect weak target engagement.

summary: Akt3 targeting produced no FDR-significant transcriptional phenotype in any tested mouse-brain cell class.

why_it_matters: The disease association is consistent with ERGIC1 being biologically important, but the Perturb-seq result points away from a ubiquitous acute brain-neuron transcriptional collapse and toward developmental, neurogenic, secretion-cargo, or protein-level vulnerabilities.
main_caveats: Human germline biallelic loss and congenital arthrogryposis are only indirectly modeled by partial Ergic1 transcript perturbation in mouse brain cell classes.

summary: Ergic1 lacked a convincing positive or negative Perturb-seq signature neighbor, including among early-secretory pathway perturbations.

summary: Lmbr1 perturbation produced no FDR-level transcriptomic response and no significant measured knockdown of the Lmbr1 transcript in any assayed neuronal cell type.

summary: Antxr2 guide assignments did not measurably reduce Antxr2 mRNA in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Without target-transcript knockdown, the mostly silent perturbation cannot be interpreted as evidence that ANTXR2 is dispensable in brain cells.
main_caveats: The row tests mRNA abundance, not protein depletion; CRISPRi effects on a low or sparsely expressed transcript may be underestimated.

summary: A single CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic outlier, Mga down-regulation, was the only FDR-significant Antxr2 response.
why_it_matters: The screen points to at most a very narrow neuronal transcriptional effect rather than a broad ANTXR2 program.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Mga was the lone FDR<0.05 row among 388046 tests, the next genes were sub-FDR, and the target transcript itself was not detectably knocked down.

summary: In the neuronal dataset, Antxr2 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Antxr1 and with assayed collagen/integrin or reported entry-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: ANTXR1 and ANTXR2 are paralogous anthrax-toxin receptors linked to extracellular-matrix disorders, so zero transcriptomic convergence argues against a captured common receptor/ECM module in these cell classes.
main_caveats: Correlation of weak signatures can be dominated by noise; the native ANTXR2 ligand complex is not fully represented among perturbations.

summary: Collagen-VI transcripts did not respond to Antxr2 perturbation, matching a post-transcriptional collagen-VI-turnover model more than a collagen-gene-induction model.
why_it_matters: The major ANTXR2 loss-of-function disease mechanism is extracellular collagen VI accumulation; the absence of Col6a mRNA induction keeps the Perturb-seq result compatible with impaired collagen clearance rather than altered collagen transcription.
main_caveats: The assay used neuronal mouse cell classes with weak Antxr2 mRNA engagement and did not measure extracellular collagen VI protein.

summary: The negative neuronal signature should not be used to de-risk chronic systemic ANTXR2 blockade.
why_it_matters: Human ANTXR2 loss causes a collagen/ECM deposition syndrome, while available ANTXR2 ligands are mostly protective-antigen binding inhibitors; this Perturb-seq screen did not test the mesenchymal or barrier cells in which that liability is expected.
main_caveats: This is a mechanistic warning, not evidence that any existing ANTXR2 ligand causes hyaline fibromatosis.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a reproducible Antxr2-like perturbation module.
why_it_matters: A weak target can still be interpretable if it repeatedly matches stronger neighboring perturbations; that rescue did not occur for Antxr2.
main_caveats: The correlations were computed on the top 100 Antxr2 genes in each cell type and are therefore exploratory and selection-biased.

summary: Eno1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any assayed mouse-brain cell class, and the Eno1 mRNA itself was absent from the DE matrix.
why_it_matters: ENO1 is a canonical glycolytic enzyme, so a clean knockdown might be expected to register either direct target reduction or metabolic adaptation; here the dominant result is an unvalidated, globally null RNA phenotype rather than a glycolysis program.
main_caveats: The target transcript was not measured, so the result cannot distinguish biological buffering from failed or weak Eno1 guide activity.

summary: The only hints of Eno1 responsiveness were nominal and concentrated in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This prevents treating isolated genes such as Abhd6, Kif17, Ptpn4, Rere, or Osbpl10 as robust biomarkers while still flagging the two cell classes that should be re-tested if Eno1 targeting is improved.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All adjusted p values were >=0.211 and the genes were not recurrent across many cell classes.

summary: In high-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut signatures, Pgk1, Tpi1, Gpi1, and Hk1 registered strong on-target depletion whereas Eno1 remained FDR-silent.
why_it_matters: The null Eno1 profile is therefore not explained simply by poor recovery of all glycolytic perturbations in the dataset; neighboring metabolic enzymes can be knocked down and detected in the same neuronal contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Comparator evidence mostly reflects direct target-gene depletion rather than large downstream pathway remodeling; Eno1 itself was unmeasured.

summary: Measured enolase paralogs and core glycolysis transcripts did not mount a detectable compensatory response after Eno1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Because ENO1 and neuron-enriched ENO2 can participate in the same dimeric enolase reaction, the weak Eno2 downtrend and lack of Eno3 or glycolytic induction argue against an RNA-level isozyme-replacement program in these data.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The Eno2 decreases were only nominal, Eno2/Eno3/Eno4 were not present as perturbation targets, and the missing Eno1 measurement limits causal interpretation.

summary: Eno1 did not show a reproducible positive or negative perturbation-neighbor signature.
why_it_matters: Top-neighbor convergence is often useful for rescuing weak single-gene DE results, but the Eno1 vectors were nearly orthogonal to the rest of the library and even included a Safe_target guide among top nominal neighbors, consistent with noise rather than a shared mechanism.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from aggregate DE scores, not from replicate-level signature reproducibility.

summary: The dataset should not be used to de-risk neuronal ENO1 inhibition or to infer absence of plasminogen/cancer-relevant moonlighting effects.
why_it_matters: ENO1 is discussed as a glycolytic and cell-surface cancer target, but this neuronal CRISPR screen lacks measurable Eno1 mRNA engagement and contains no proteomic, surface-localization, plasminogen-activation, metabolite, or viability endpoints.
main_caveats: Cancer and plasminogen literature are human or non-neuronal contexts; the Perturb-seq dataset is mouse brain and transcript-only.

summary: Grik1 produced no FDR-supported single-gene transcriptomic phenotype across any of the 21 tested cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: This is the primary dataset result: a curated kainate receptor subunit did not generate a broad cell-autonomous mRNA program in this screen.
main_caveats: The Grik1 target transcript was also not significantly depleted, so the result cannot distinguish failed target engagement from a true buffered biological response.

summary: Grik1 target-transcript engagement was not confirmed: all 21 on-target Grik1 transcript tests had FDR=1.0.
why_it_matters: Without a corrected target effect, the downstream null should not be interpreted as evidence that functional loss of GluK1 is silent.
main_caveats: mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for genome editing or loss of channel protein.

summary: The two largest Grik1 contrasts, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, remained null despite having more than 100 perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: This argues that the all-cell-type null is not explained only by the smallest cell-type sample sizes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Even 110-127 perturbed cells can be underpowered for subtle neuronal responses, and target mRNA still did not pass FDR.

summary: Broad GABAergic classes expected to contain GluK1-relevant inhibitory neurons did not show a corrected Grik1 response.
why_it_matters: The result refines PV/interneuron literature by showing that these coarse Perturb-seq inhibitory classes did not capture the published GluK1 circuit biology.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type labels, species, developmental stage, and assay differ from the HPA and PV-amygdala literature; Grik1 target engagement was weak.

summary: Several ionotropic glutamate receptor perturbations were far more transcriptionally penetrant than Grik1 under the same analysis.
why_it_matters: The Grik1 null is not simply a universal inability of the experiment to detect glutamate-receptor perturbations; it is strongest for GluK1 relative to Grin1, Grin2a, Grin2b, Gria2, and Grik5.
main_caveats: Different genes had different guide performance and were assayed in partly different cell-class sets.

summary: Grik1 had no strong transcriptomic signature neighbor, including among kainate-receptor paralogs, other glutamate receptors, and disease-family perturbations.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of weak nominal Grik1 ranks as a hidden convergent pathway or complex-member module.
main_caveats: Correlation of weak signatures is conservative; absence of correlation is not a functional epistasis test.

summary: The Grik1 scRNA null should not be used as evidence that GluK1 is dispensable for seizure or neuropsychiatric circuit phenotypes.
why_it_matters: GluK1 disease biology can be electrophysiological, acute, and model dependent, so Perturb-seq mRNA is an incomplete efficacy or safety proxy for GluK1-directed therapies.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay seizures, synaptic currents, amygdala PV circuits, or pharmacologic activation, and target engagement was not FDR-supported.

summary: Bap1 perturbation produced corrected transcriptional responses in only two of 21 assayed neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: The response is not pan-neuronal; it is concentrated in Pvalb interneurons and TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons despite many other subclasses being assayed.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cell types without FDR hits still include some low-count contrasts, and the table measures RNA phenotypes rather than editing efficiency.

summary: Scg2 is the single recurrent corrected gene-level output of Bap1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: A one-gene recurrent module is narrow, but a replicated decrease in secretogranin II makes Scg2 the clearest candidate biomarker of the Bap1 neuronal response.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Scg2, not a broad secretory-granule gene set, recurred at FDR<0.05 in both cell types.

summary: Pvalb interneurons and TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons used largely different Bap1 downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The same perturbation reached corrected significance in both subclasses, but Pvalb cells showed a four-gene Macf1/Lrp1b/Scg2/Rab34 signature whereas the TH Prkcd Grin2c response was broader and included Serpine2, Cnot9, Coro6, Cst3, Prkch, Sema5a, Hdac1, and Acly.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

summary: RNA-level Bap1 target engagement was weak and did not track downstream response size.
why_it_matters: The largest downstream signatures occurred without corrected Bap1 mRNA depletion, so the transcript row cannot be used as the sole confirmation of perturbation strength in this assay.
main_caveats: The perturbation modality may disrupt protein sequence without decreasing Bap1 mRNA, and the dataset does not report indel or protein-level engagement.

summary: Measured PR-DUB recruitment partners did not phenocopy Bap1 in the two responsive neuronal subclasses.

summary: Ogt was transcriptionally active but uncoupled from Bap1 in the Bap1-responsive subclasses.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The proteomic literature supports BAP1 neighborhood membership rather than proving that OGT perturbation should phenocopy Bap1.

summary: No unbiased perturbation was a strong positive or negative Bap1 signature neighbor.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

summary: Bicc1 perturbation showed no detectable Bicc1 target-transcript decrease in any measured neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Downstream null results have to be interpreted in light of absent transcript-level target engagement rather than as proof that functional Bicc1 loss is inert in neurons.
main_caveats: A coding perturbation could alter Bicc1 protein without reducing Bicc1 mRNA; no protein or edit validation is present in the parquet.

summary: No Bicc1 cell-type signature reached FDR < 0.05; the only q<0.10 effect was a borderline Rangap1 increase in L5 extratelencephalic glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: There is no robust cell-type-restricted Bicc1 transcriptional program to interpret; the L5 ET near-hit is hypothesis-generating only.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The term buffered does not distinguish active biological buffering from failed target engagement; Rangap1 missed the 0.05 FDR threshold.

summary: Bicc1 perturbation did not significantly alter named Wnt, cAMP, miRNA, or PKD-axis transcripts that are central to published Bicc1 mechanisms.
why_it_matters: The data do not support immediate use of Axin2/Ctnnb1, Adcy6, Pkd genes, Dicer, Ago, or Cnot transcripts as neuronal Bicc1-response biomarkers in this screen.
main_caveats: The expected effects were drawn largely from renal epithelial and embryonic laterality systems, not from the neuronal cell classes profiled here.

summary: A Ctnnb1 perturbation produced hundreds of significant genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Bicc1 was null there and had negligible correlations with curated ciliary, miRNA, and Wnt-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues that the Bicc1 null is not equivalent to a generic β-catenin/Wnt response and that Bicc1 cannot be treated as interchangeable with Ctnnb1, Dicer1, Pkd1, or related ciliary perturbations in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations are restricted to mRNA DE score vectors; weak Bicc1 engagement limits the mechanistic strength of the contrast.

summary: The neuronal Bicc1 null refines renal-cystic and laterality literature toward a context- and assay-dependent Bicc1 mechanism.
why_it_matters: Bicc1 has strong kidney/ciliary/post-transcriptional precedent, but this screen indicates that glutamatergic and GABAergic mRNA DE is not a sensitive surrogate for that disease module.
main_caveats: The dataset contains neuronal classes rather than kidney epithelium or early left-right organizer cells; HPA is human expression context.

summary: The strongest positive and negative Bicc1 signature neighbors were weak and did not define a reproducible convergent module.
why_it_matters: Top-neighbor inspection did not reveal a hidden biologically coherent Bicc1 response that would be missed by looking only at known pathways.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor calls are correlation-based over null-like signatures; r values below 0.16 should not be treated as pathway membership.

summary: Adrb2-targeted cells showed neither significant depletion of the Adrb2 transcript nor any FDR-significant genome-wide mRNA response across 23 neuronal cell groups.
why_it_matters: ADRB2 is a canonical catecholamine GPCR, so an all-cell-type null establishes that this Perturb-seq slice is not a usable basal mRNA readout of β2AR pathway activation or loss.
main_caveats: The null is confounded by weak measured target-transcript depletion and by sparse Adrb2 RNA.

summary: Adrb2 nominal hits were scattered among cell types rather than forming a recurrent Adrb2 response module.
why_it_matters: The strongest genes should be interpreted as nonsignificant rank leaders, not as pathway biomarkers or cell-type-specific β2AR effectors.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is an empirical statement about corrected and nominal RNA ranks; it does not test acute β2AR second-messenger dynamics.

summary: Adrb2 did not phenocopy beta-adrenergic paralogs or intracellular cAMP/PKA/CREB pathway perturbations, even though several downstream perturbations were detectable.
why_it_matters: The result separates receptor-level loss in basal neurons from intracellular PKA/CREB transcriptional competence; canonical Gs signaling exists, but it was not engaged by Adrb2 guide assignment in this assay.
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation correlations are restricted to mRNA score vectors and compare different target genes with different perturbed-cell counts.

summary: The Adrb2 null is restricted to neuron-labeled classes and does not rule out astrocytic or immune-lineage β2AR biology in brain.
why_it_matters: Published hippocampal β2AR memory biology is astrocytic, and human brain single-nucleus ADRB2 enrichment is not neuronal; therefore the missing cell compartments are plausible responsive contexts absent from this screen slice.

summary: The silent neuronal Adrb2 mRNA signature should not be used to deprioritize pharmacologic β2AR biology.
why_it_matters: ADRB2 is a clinically drugged GPCR with approved agonists; this dataset lacks the ligand stimulation and non-neuronal cell types needed to model those mechanisms.
main_caveats: The finding is a translational caution, not a direct drug experiment.

summary: Ep300 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome response in 21 assayed mouse-brain cell types, and measured Ep300 transcript depletion was weak.
why_it_matters: A nominal or absent Ep300 scRNA signature is the primary result: most downstream analyses have to be interpreted as a negative or buffered perturbation rather than a robust loss-of-function map.
main_caveats: The conclusion is about this mRNA Perturb-seq readout; indels, p300 protein, and histone acetylation were not measured.

summary: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut carried the strongest Ep300 nominal gene cluster, but the signal stopped at FDR=0.102 and lacked Ep300 transcript reduction.
why_it_matters: This is the only cell-type-restricted hint worth preserving, but it is an exploratory CA3 and dentate-family hypothesis rather than a validated EP300 program.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: No gene reached FDR<0.10, and Ep300 mRNA was not decreased in this cell type.

summary: Ep300 and Crebbp did not behave as interchangeable KAT3 paralogs in the shared cell types; Crebbp alone produced a corrected 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response and their whole-signature correlations were near zero.
why_it_matters: p300 and CBP are often grouped biochemically, but their perturbation signatures in this brain dataset should not be merged or assumed equivalent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Crebbp response occurred despite weak measured Crebbp transcript depletion, and Ep300 engagement was also weak.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was a chromatin-perturbation-responsive context for Kmt2d, Chd4, and Ankrd11 but not for Ep300, Hdac5, Ncoa3, or Stat3.
why_it_matters: Related or disease-adjacent chromatin regulators can create sharply different neuronal signatures in the same cell type, so pathway membership alone is a poor predictor of the Ep300 phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only one cell type is used for the detailed disease-family contrast, and the cross-gene correlations are transcriptomic rather than biochemical.

summary: The curated breadth of EP300 transcriptional pathways was not recovered as a recurrent Ep300 single-cell expression module.
why_it_matters: Reactome connects EP300/CREBBP to many TF systems, but in this dataset those annotations did not predict corrected or recurrent downstream targets after Ep300 perturbation.
main_caveats: Weak target engagement can mask pathway activity; this is not a biochemical disproof of Reactome pathways.

summary: The quiet Ep300 signature should not be interpreted as a neuronal safety signal for pharmacologic EP300/CBP inhibition.
why_it_matters: Cancer programs inhibit both EP300 and CBP bromodomains and can affect H3K27ac-rich enhancer networks; a weak single-gene mouse-brain CRISPR signature lacks the modality and engagement depth needed for safety inference.
main_caveats: The dataset does not test small-molecule p300/CBP bromodomain inhibition, combined EP300/CREBBP suppression, H3K27ac loss, or chronic exposure.

summary: Kdm5c perturbation produced one FDR-positive downstream signature, concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and dominated by induced genes.
why_it_matters: This turns a weakly engaged chromatin perturbation into a cell-class-specific hypothesis: the detectable transcriptional consequence of Kdm5c lowering in the adult mouse brain screen is not pan-neuronal but thalamic-glutamatergic.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Kdm5c mRNA was only nominally reduced in 151 and not FDR-significant; no protein or H3K4 methylation readout confirms KDM5C loss.

summary: The largest nominal Kdm5c self-decreases, in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, were not accompanied by any FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: These signatures argue against treating nominal target-transcript reduction as sufficient evidence for a full Kdm5c transcriptional phenotype in every cell type.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The target self-decreases were nominal, not FDR-significant, so this is a partial-engagement buffering observation rather than a strong negative genetic result.

summary: Zmynd8 perturbation co-induced 13 of the 17 non-self Kdm5c FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut even though global score-vector correlation to Kdm5c was weak.
why_it_matters: This preserves a restricted signature-neighbor relationship that would be hidden by whole-transcriptome correlation alone and nominates the Ptgds/Capn3/Msra/Spag5/Zfp532 module for follow-up.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Zmynd8 itself increased under Zmynd8 perturbation, so the comparison is a perturbational signature overlap and not a directional Zmynd8 loss-of-function epistasis result.

summary: Kdm5c did not phenocopy Kdm5b or the stronger H3K4/chromatin perturbations in the same 151 cell class.
why_it_matters: The result separates Kdm5c biology from enzyme-family membership: Kdm5b was silent, Sin3a was the top anti-neighbor, and Setd1a/Kmt2d produced far broader signatures than Kdm5c.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast was quantified only in the 151 class, and comparator target engagement was not fully adjudicated from protein or chromatin data.

summary: Zfp532 is an exploratory recurrent positive marker of Kdm5c perturbation, with nominal p<0.01 in six cell classes but FDR support only in 151.
why_it_matters: A recurrent same-direction transcript may help track weak Kdm5c responses across cell classes even when each individual non-151 signature is underpowered after FDR correction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut

why_it_matters: If the Nfe2l2 rows reflected a strong NRF2-axis state, Cul3, Mafg, or antioxidant-gene perturbations might show an opposing or related signature; near-zero correlations argue instead for either weak Nfe2l2 engagement or strong pathway buffering.

summary: The negative neuronal Nfe2l2 result narrows, rather than negates, NRF2 neuroprotection: NRF2 can protect neurons through astrocytic glutathione support, whereas the Nfe2l2 rows here cover glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes and omit glia.
why_it_matters: The in vivo brain dataset should not be read as evidence that the NRF2 pathway is irrelevant to neurodegeneration; it more specifically shows that acute Nfe2l2 perturbation was not sufficient to collapse antioxidant transcripts in the sampled neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The dataset contains cell-class annotations rather than direct astrocyte contrasts for Nfe2l2, so the glial interpretation is an indirect boundary condition.

summary: Pign targeting produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any measured mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: The central dataset result is absence of a robust Perturb-seq signature, so nominal genes such as Nemf or Atp6ap1 should not be read as a PIGN/GPI-anchor response.
main_caveats: Most Pign guide cells were low-count and Pign mRNA itself was not significantly depleted after correction, so the result is best interpreted as no detected response under weak or partial perturbation.

summary: The acute Pign transcriptome appears buffered or subthreshold relative to the severe human biallelic PIGN disease mechanism.
why_it_matters: PIGN is a recessive neurodevelopmental disease gene, but this dataset does not show an adult mouse-brain expression collapse after Pign targeting; the result therefore separates developmental loss-of-function from the partial acute perturbation assayed here.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: No protein, GPI-anchor surface marker, or developmental assay was measured; insufficient knockdown could fully explain the buffered transcriptome.

summary: The only assayed GPI-adjacent comparator, Dpm1, did not phenocopy Pign across cell-type score signatures.
why_it_matters: Even genes that feed the same GPI-anchor pathway need not create a shared acute transcriptional state; the Pign-Dpm1 relationship is therefore unsafe to transfer by pathway membership alone in this dataset.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to transcriptomic Wilcoxon score correlations; Dpm1 also had weak own-transcript engagement and most direct PIG/PGAP genes were absent from the library.

summary: Pign had no recurrent nominal-gene or signature-neighbor biomarker module.
why_it_matters: The strongest scalar values were cell-type idiosyncratic; preserving this negative result prevents post hoc biomarker hypotheses from single nominal p values.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative signature-level inference from weak Pign perturbations, not proof that PIGN lacks all context-specific downstream markers.

summary: Atp2c1 reached FDR-significant self-transcript depletion only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: These two glutamatergic classes define the interpretable on-target window for this Perturb-seq target.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Corrected engagement was limited to two high-powered tests; target logFC was modest and protein depletion was not measured.

direction: target down with no corrected downstream signature

why_it_matters: The main output is a negative stress-response result, not a multi-gene Golgi or UPR module.
main_caveats: The assay may miss Golgi Ca2+, Mn2+, glycosylation, trafficking, neurite, or protein-level phenotypes.

direction: Atp2a2 induces UPR; Atp2c1 does not
summary: Atp2c1 loss did not activate the Atp2a2/SERCA2-like ER-stress and UPR module in the same glutamatergic cell types.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Atp2a2 knockdown was stronger than Atp2c1 knockdown, so the contrast mixes target identity with depletion depth.

summary: Related calcium-handling perturbations diverged strongly in downstream breadth across the Atp2c1-engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: Family or pathway membership alone was insufficient to predict a shared transcriptomic consequence in this screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparators occupy different organelles or signaling positions and were perturbed with different efficiencies.

direction: partial loss with buffered RNA output
summary: Partial Atp2c1 perturbation in mature brain cells did not phenocopy severe ATP2C1 loss states that cause epithelial disease or embryonic Golgi stress.
why_it_matters: The negative RNA response narrows the interpretation to a buffered partial-loss state and warns against treating absence of DE as absence of SPCA1 biology.
main_caveats: Hailey-Hailey disease is epithelial and the mouse-null phenotype is developmental; neither is directly matched to the Perturb-seq cell types or partial transcript depletion.

direction: no strong positive or negative neighbor
summary: Top-gene Atp2c1 signature matching produced only weak correlations and no robust related-target neighbor.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of nominal Atp2c1 genes as a convergent perturbation module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The analysis is restricted to non-FDR Atp2c1 genes and should be treated as quality control rather than mechanism.

summary: Nsd2 perturbation produced no FDR-resolved downstream transcriptome in any of the 22 sampled neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The strongest Nsd2-associated DE rows are nominal rather than pathway-level effects, so the primary dataset result is a transcriptomic non-response rather than a weakly defined Nsd2 effector program.
cell_types: 22 Nsd2-sampled neuronal cell types
main_caveats: This is a negative result in DE space only; it does not measure NSD2 protein, H3K36me2, chromatin accessibility, developmental phenotypes, or viability.

summary: The Nsd2 guide pool showed weak RNA-level target engagement, so the silent signature is best interpreted as under-engaged or transcriptionally buffered rather than proof that NSD2 is dispensable.
why_it_matters: NSD2 is an enzymatic chromatin regulator; a failed or partial transcript-level perturbation can leave enough protein and H3K36 methylation to mask downstream effects.
cell_types: 22 Nsd2-sampled neuronal cell types
main_caveats: Transcript rows cannot distinguish CRISPRi failure, long protein half-life, incomplete catalytic suppression, or true biological buffering.

summary: Nsd2 was uncoupled from related H3K36 methyltransferase perturbations despite shared pathway annotation with Nsd1 and Ash1l/Setd2.
why_it_matters: A same-pathway annotation would predict at least partial convergence, but Nsd2 had no FDR genes and near-zero signature correlations with Nsd1, Ash1l, and Setd2; Nsd1 and Ash1l/Setd2 yielded detectable responses in the TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class.

main_caveats: The divergence could reflect weaker Nsd2 target engagement rather than a validated mechanistic separation among H3K36 enzymes.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells were broadly sensitive to chromatin-regulator perturbation but still did not respond to Nsd2.
why_it_matters: This argues that the Nsd2 null result is not caused solely by this cell class being refractory to epigenetic regulator knockdown; multiple other KMTs and Chd8 produced FDR-level signatures in the same cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The 151-class contrast is strong for this dataset, but it is still transcriptomic and does not prove that NSD2 catalytic activity was abolished.

summary: No recurrent Nsd2-responsive marker emerged from the nominal tail.
why_it_matters: Hdac8 and Gatad2b were the only genes recurring at p<0.001, and Gatad2b changed in opposite directions, so none of the nominal hits is a robust single-gene pharmacodynamic marker for Nsd2 in mouse neurons.
cell_types: 22 Nsd2-sampled neuronal cell types
main_caveats: This is a biomarker-negative finding for this assay; weak target engagement could erase true recurrent markers.

summary: The weak neuronal response should not be used to de-risk NSD2 inhibition in the nervous system.
why_it_matters: NSD2 is chemically and oncologically tractable, but human NSD2 loss-of-function lowers methylation activity and causes a developmental syndrome; a mouse neuronal dataset with no FDR transcriptomic response and poor RNA engagement cannot rule out chromatin or developmental liabilities.
cell_types: 22 Nsd2-sampled neuronal cell types
main_caveats: The dataset does not test small-molecule inhibitors, human cells, development, or brain exposure; the warning derives from combining a negative acute signature with human loss-of-function genetics.

direction: Dhcr24 up in 151; no FDR-significant genes in 20 other assayed cell-type strata
summary: The FDR-level Agps response is concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Dhcr24 is the only genome-wide significant Agps-regulated gene.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The two absent strata were not tested for Agps after filtering, and Agps mRNA itself was not FDR-depleted in any measured stratum.

summary: Agps perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut induces a coherent cholesterol/sterol biosynthetic module led by Dhcr24 and nominal Cyp51, Sqle, Mvd, Stard4, Fdft1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Ldlr, and Insig1.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Dhcr24 passes FDR<0.05 in the Agps contrast; the module call is based on a coherent set of nominal positive effects and external sterol annotation.

summary: The Agps sterol response is directionally opposite to Srebf2 perturbation in the same 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut stratum.
why_it_matters: Srebf2 loss strongly suppresses Dhcr24, Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Cyp51, and Sqle, so the Agps signature is best interpreted as activation of an SREBP2-regulated sterol program rather than nonspecific high expression of the same genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Srebf2 perturbation has a much stronger target and pathway signature than Agps; the Agps side of the contrast is mostly nominal.

summary: Far1, Pex14, and Pex13 perturbations partially converge with Agps on sterol-gene induction in the same 151 neuronal class, and Pex14, Abcd3, Acbd5, and Far1 are among the most positive global Agps signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: This weak convergence ties the Agps phenotype to a broader peroxisome/ether-lipid axis rather than a single-guide idiosyncrasy, while keeping the low whole-signature correlations explicit.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Pex13 target mRNA depletion was weak, most neighbor sterol genes were nominal rather than FDR-significant, and full-transcriptome correlations with Agps were only r=0.050-0.070 for Far1/Pex14.

summary: Outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Agps produced no genome-wide significant downstream transcripts, even in 155 MB Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut where close to or more than 100 Agps-perturbed cells were available.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a large universal acute neuronal stress response to Agps perturbation in this dataset and prevents overgeneralizing the 151 sterol module to all brain cell types.
main_caveats: A negative FDR test is not proof of absent lipid or protein phenotypes; many strata had only 31-72 perturbed cells and Agps editing cannot be read out directly from target mRNA abundance.

direction: sterol genes up after Agps perturbation
summary: The Agps-induced 151 sterol panel is an exploratory CNS biomarker hypothesis for pharmacologic AGPS inhibition.
why_it_matters: AGPS inhibitor scaffolds have been developed for cancer, while inherited AGPS loss causes plasmalogen-deficiency disease; Dhcr24/Cyp51/Sqle/Msmo1/Hmgcs1/Insig1 up-regulation suggests that neuronal cholesterol-homeostasis transcripts should be monitored in AGPS-loss settings.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset used CRISPR perturbation in mouse brain cells, not small-molecule AGPS inhibition; most biomarker genes are nominal and lineage-restricted.

summary: Gcgr perturbation was a broad null in this mouse-brain DE table: the target transcript was not detectably depleted and no downstream gene passed 5% FDR in any measured cell type.

summary: The weak Gcgr signatures did not align with G alpha/adenylyl-cyclase neighbors or with any strong global signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Although GCGR is canonically coupled to G-protein and adenylate-cyclase signaling, this dataset gives no evidence that Gcgr knockdown drove the same transcriptional state as perturbing measured cAMP-pathway neighbors.
main_caveats: The conclusion is based on weak Gcgr signatures and indirect neighbors; direct Gcg, Glp1r, Glp2r, Gipr, Sctr, and Vipr perturbations were absent.

summary: On-target depletion was detectable for several other ligand, receptor, or signaling perturbations in the same Wilcoxon output, separating the Gcgr null from a universal inability to detect target knockdown.
why_it_matters: The most parsimonious dataset interpretation is target-context limitation for Gcgr, such as very low receptor expression in the assayed neurons, rather than a complete failure of the perturbation analysis pipeline.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparator genes are not GCGR paralogs; they serve only as positive controls for detectability of expressed targets in this table.

summary: This brain Perturb-seq result does not nominate basal neuronal biomarkers for direct GCGR agonism or antagonism, despite GCGR being a druggable metabolic receptor.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic interpretation should remain anchored in hepatic, pancreatic, and circuit-level glucagon biology until Gcgr is perturbed in receptor-positive brain cells or under ligand stimulation.
main_caveats: The dataset lacked peripheral liver, kidney, and pancreatic alpha-cell contexts and measured steady-state transcription rather than acute ligand-evoked GPCR signaling.

summary: Amfr on-target depletion was directional in every measured cell type but genome-wide significant only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with 191 MB P MY GABA as a strong FDR-missed candidate.
why_it_matters: It separates true guide engagement from cell types where low counts or weaker knockdown make downstream interpretation unsafe.

main_caveats: The selectivity is measured as transcript knockdown significance, not AMFR protein loss; many cell types had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: Amfr perturbation produced almost no genome-wide significant trans response after multiple-testing correction.
why_it_matters: An ERAD E3 ligase can be partially depleted in these mouse brain cells without triggering a large steady-state RNA program, so phenotype follow-up should not require bulk DE as proof of biological action.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay cannot exclude changes in AMFR protein, ubiquitinated ERAD substrates, ERAD flux, or lipid metabolites.

summary: Assayed ERAD or ER-stress neighbors were not transcriptionally interchangeable with Amfr.
why_it_matters: Physical proximity to AMFR in ERAD does not imply that single-gene knockdown of Vcp, Edem3, Atf6, Hspa5, or Rnf13 will phenocopy Amfr in brain Perturb-seq.

main_caveats: Several core AMFR partners, including Ube2g2, Derl1, Insig1, and Hmgcr, were not available as perturbation targets; guide efficacy also differed across comparator perturbations.

summary: Nominal downregulation of SREBP/cholesterol-biosynthesis transcripts was the clearest pathway-shaped downstream hint after Amfr loss.
why_it_matters: The Srebf2/Cyp51/Dhcr24/Sqle pattern links a weak mouse-brain transcriptional signal to known AMFR-gp78 control of Insig/SREBP lipid homeostasis and to lipid defects in AMFR-loss spastic paraplegia models.

main_caveats: No sterol gene survived FDR correction; the gene set was inspected because of prior AMFR lipid biology rather than by an unbiased significant enrichment test.

main_caveats: UPR activation can be transient, post-transcriptional, substrate-dependent, or missed by partial knockdown and sparse single-cell sampling.

summary: The Hras-targeted population had no FDR-corrected transcriptional phenotype across 22 measured brain cell types.
why_it_matters: HRAS is a canonical Ras-MAPK signal transducer, so a globally silent expression response argues that endogenous Hras loss was either incompletely engaged or strongly buffered in this postmitotic mouse-brain Perturb-seq setting.
main_caveats: No raw editing-efficiency data were available; CRISPR mutation can leave transcript abundance intact; the result is a transcriptomic negative result, not proof that HRAS protein was absent.

summary: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed the clearest nominal Hras transcript depletion but still no corrected downstream program.
why_it_matters: This separates the best RNA-level target engagement in the Hras arm from broad pathway activation or repression, a pattern expected for a buffered perturbation more than for a strongly penetrant MAPK loss phenotype.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The Hras transcript FDR was 1.0; the cell-type claim is based on a nominal target-transcript rank rather than a corrected target or downstream effect.

summary: Hras and Kras paralog perturbations converged on a silent transcriptional outcome rather than producing a shared Ras-pathway signature.
why_it_matters: The negative convergence is consistent with Ras paralog buffering in mouse genetics and argues against treating an Hras guide population as an automatic proxy for pan-Ras pathway shutdown in mature brain cells.
main_caveats: Kras also had low per-cell-type cell counts and weak target-transcript support; no Nras perturbation was present for a complete Ras-paralog comparison.

summary: Hras did not phenocopy downstream RAS/MAPK or mTOR-axis perturbations that were significant in the same neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: RASopathy and Ras-effector genes cannot be collapsed to one expected transcriptomic direction in this screen: Nf1, Braf/Map2k/Mapk and Tsc/Pten perturbations generated corrected signatures in thalamic or midbrain classes where Hras remained silent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Counts of significant genes do not align perturbations by biochemical direction; the compared targets differ in editing efficiency, pathway position and loss-of-function consequence.

summary: Ksr2 induction in 308 CB GABA is an exploratory RAF-MEK-ERK scaffold marker for Hras perturbation.
why_it_matters: KSR2 links directly to Ras-mediated ERK scaffolding, so its nominal up-regulation is the most pathway-proximal single-gene candidate in the otherwise FDR-silent Hras signature.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Ksr2 was nominal only, had FDR=1.0, and appeared in a cell type with no corrected Hras-response genes.

summary: The Hras loss-of-function screen is directionally mismatched to activated-HRAS Costello syndrome and HRAS-mutant cancer biology.
why_it_matters: A weak wild-type Hras perturbation signature should not be interpreted as evidence against activated HRAS as a disease driver or as evidence that HRAS-directed farnesyltransferase inhibition would be transcriptionally inert in mutant tumors.
main_caveats: The dataset used mouse brain loss-of-function guide assignments, whereas the cited disease and oncology systems involve activating HRAS alleles and non-brain contexts.

summary: Ikzf3 perturbation did not produce detectable depletion of the Ikzf3 transcript in any measured neuronal subclass.
why_it_matters: The dataset cannot verify target engagement from target mRNA, so downstream null results must be interpreted as transcriptomic silence or ineffectual RNA depletion rather than as a confirmed knockout with no phenotype.
main_caveats: The table has no editing-rate or raw-count information; CRISPR editing could occur without measurable target RNA depletion if Ikzf3 is not expressed in the assayed neurons.

summary: Ikzf3 loss yielded no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional program across 21 neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: A lymphoid transcription factor with no q<0.10 neuronal hits is best treated as buffered or inactive in these basal neuronal subclasses rather than as a driver of a broad brain-cell program.

summary: The flat neuronal Ikzf3 signature is more compatible with immune-cell IKZF3 disease mechanisms than with a strong neuron-autonomous mechanism in the tested subclasses.
why_it_matters: IKZF3 is linked to B-cell biology, inborn errors of immunity, and a multiple-sclerosis susceptibility locus in peripheral blood; the mouse-brain Perturb-seq result argues that CNS disease hypotheses involving IKZF3 should specify immune or infiltrating leukocyte context unless new neuronal evidence is supplied.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks B cells, T cells, microglia, disease stimulation, and raw target-expression measurements.

summary: CRBN molecular-glue pharmacology should not be inferred from the null single-gene Ikzf3 neuronal signature.
why_it_matters: Lenalidomide efficacy involves ligand-induced CRBN-dependent degradation of IKZF1/IKZF3 in myeloma and T cells; a weak brain-neuron CRISPR response is therefore a context-mismatched readout for degrader efficacy and for likely on-target immune pharmacology.
main_caveats: No lenalidomide or other molecular glue was applied, and Crbn was only compared by restricted transcriptomic similarity.

summary: Available related-target comparisons did not reveal a robust IKZF-family or CRBN-neighborhood convergence with Ikzf3.
why_it_matters: Prior knowledge predicts IKZF-family and CRBN-centered biology, but the dataset lacks Ikzf1/2/4/5 perturbations and the available CRBN comparison was weak and sign-mixed, limiting claims about paralog interchangeability or CRBN phenocopy in neurons.
main_caveats: The comparison used an Ikzf3 top-50 restricted signature because the full Ikzf3 signature was not FDR-supported.

summary: Dll1 guides did not measurably deplete the Dll1 transcript in any of the 23 assayed brain cell groups.
why_it_matters: The primary perturbation is under-engaged at the RNA level, so absence of downstream Notch biology cannot be treated as a clean Dll1 loss-of-function phenotype.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an imperfect proxy for CRISPR editing; raw guide identities, DNA edits, and baseline Dll1 expression were not available.

summary: Cell-autonomous Dll1 perturbation was uncoupled from canonical Notch transcriptional output.
why_it_matters: DLL1 normally functions as a membrane ligand upstream of Notch receptor activation, but the perturbed cells showed no FDR-significant Hes/Hey/Nrarp/Rbpj response and no global DE hit.
main_caveats: Interpretation is limited by weak Dll1 target engagement and by the fact that a ligand knockdown in a sender cell may be read out mainly in adjacent receiver cells.

summary: No neuronal subclass produced a reproducible Dll1 module; the few nominal genes were sparse and private.
why_it_matters: Prior Dll1 functions are strongest in neural stem/progenitor contexts, whereas these neuronal-cell Perturb-seq profiles did not reveal a mature-neuron subclass with a robust autonomous response.
main_caveats: Only transcriptomic DE in cells carrying Dll1 guides was measured; nominal p values were not cross-cell-type FDR controlled.

summary: Mib1, a Notch-ligand trafficking neighbor, produced a strong sterol/cholesterol module that was absent from Dll1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that not every gene acting on Notch ligands is interchangeable in this dataset; Mib1 has a robust neuronally restricted output, whereas Dll1 does not phenocopy it.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Mib1 has substrates and biology beyond DLL1; the sterol module should not be assumed to be canonical Notch output without direct rescue or pathway assays.

summary: Dll1 had no coherent positive or inverse signature neighbor among Notch1-4 receptors or among all assayed perturbations.
why_it_matters: Although DLL1 is placed upstream of multiple Notch receptors, the single-cell RNA signatures do not show receptor-like convergence that would support a shared autonomous state transition.
main_caveats: The Notch receptor perturbations themselves showed weak or absent self-transcript engagement, so lack of correlation cannot be assigned uniquely to pathway divergence.

summary: The Dll1 null result in these brain cell groups does not argue against DLL1 haploinsufficiency as a developmental brain-disease mechanism.
why_it_matters: Human DLL1 disease is a developmental, dosage-sensitive, multisystem condition; this dataset mainly tests acute autonomous RNA effects in neuronal classes and therefore samples a different biological axis.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks developmental progenitors, neighbor-cell readout, and high-confidence Dll1 depletion.

summary: Broad Notch inhibition should not be inferred from, or optimized against, the weak Dll1 Perturb-seq signature.
why_it_matters: Systemic Notch/gamma-secretase blockade can be toxic, and the present Dll1 signature lacks canonical Notch readouts; ligand-selective or receiver-cell assays would be required for therapeutic direction.
main_caveats: No drug treatment was profiled; this is a mechanistic warning based on pathway position and the negative transcriptomic signature.

summary: Ndufv1 perturbation produced a single FDR-supported on-target transcript decrease, concentrated in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: This defines the clearest cell class for follow-up protein or respiration assays of a catalytic Complex-I subunit.
