main_caveats: The finding is transcript-level only; no NDUFV1 protein or Complex-I activity assay confirms biochemical knockdown.

summary: Ndufv1 transcript depletion was largely self-only; no non-Ndufv1 gene reached FDR<0.05 in any Ndufv1 cell-type signature.
why_it_matters: A central Complex-I gene can be measurably reduced without creating a broad steady-state RNA stress program in this assay, so absence of downstream DE should not be mistaken for absence of target engagement.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The strongest downstream statement is specifically about FDR-corrected steady-state RNA; metabolic phenotypes could occur without RNA changes.

summary: High perturbed-cell counts did not guarantee Ndufv1 engagement or a downstream signature in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The negative result separates weak biology or weak guide effect from simple low power, prioritizing additional validation over adding more matched cells alone.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not report guide sequences, target isoform coverage, basal expression, or protein depletion, so the weak signal cannot be assigned to a specific cause.

summary: Selected ETC perturbations, including related Complex-I members, were dominated by self-transcript hits rather than a convergent OXPHOS collapse.
why_it_matters: Ndufv1 should not be expected to phenocopy all neighboring Complex-I subunits at the RNA level, even though these proteins operate in the same respiratory-chain assembly.
main_caveats: The comparator set was targeted rather than genome-wide and used only NDUF/COX/UQCR/SDH-name perturbations.

summary: The screen is most consistent with partial Ndufv1 RNA perturbation, not a full cellular model of biallelic NDUFV1 Complex-I deficiency.
why_it_matters: Human NDUFV1 disease variants damage Complex-I protein function, so therapeutic or disease conclusions from this RNA screen require orthogonal respiratory-chain validation.
main_caveats: Species, developmental context, perturbation modality, and RNA-versus-protein readouts are only indirectly matched to human mitochondrial disease.

summary: Measured Igsf1 knockdown was not achieved in any assayed neuronal cell class.
why_it_matters: The core perturbation is not interpretable as a strong Igsf1 loss-of-function signature; the negative self-transcript result is target-specific rather than a universal property of Ig-superfamily membrane genes in this dataset because Igsf8 was depleted in several cell types.
main_caveats: Self-transcript abundance is an indirect target-engagement metric; the dataset does not contain guide-level or protein-level validation.

summary: CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic neurons contain the sole corrected hit, an increase of Dgcr8, a Microprocessor/miRNA-biogenesis gene.
why_it_matters: Dgcr8 is the only transcript that survives FDR correction after Igsf1 perturbation, making it the cleanest candidate marker of the observed guide-associated state even though it is not a known IGSF1 effector.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Single-cell-type result with only 48 perturbed cells and no significant Igsf1 self-depletion; neighboring CA3 genes were nominal but did not pass FDR.

summary: The canonical pituitary IGSF1-TRH/TSH/FSH axis was uncoupled from the neuronal Igsf1 signature.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse IGSF1 deficiency is centered on pituitary thyrotropes and gonadotropes, whereas Igsf1 perturbation in this brain-cell dataset did not move Trh, Trhr, Tshb, Fshb, or related hormone transcripts, arguing that absence of a neuronal response should not be read as absence of the endocrine disease mechanism.
main_caveats: The assayed cell classes are neural, not anterior-pituitary endocrine cells; several pituitary hormone genes are sparsely detected.

summary: Nominal Igsf1 hits did not recur across cell types and did not define a positive or negative signature-neighbor module.
why_it_matters: The perturbation behaves as sparse, idiosyncratic transcriptomic noise or a highly buffered response rather than a coherent neuronal pathway perturbation, reducing support for pan-neuronal Igsf1 biology in this assay.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from summary DE scores, not jointly modeled single-cell expression; very weak target engagement limits biological conclusions.

summary: Known or candidate endocrine-axis neighbors did not recapitulate Igsf1, and Igsf8 was also essentially uncorrelated with Igsf1 despite stronger Igsf8 on-target depletion.
why_it_matters: STRING and pituitary literature point toward Trhr/Tshb/Trh/Pou1f1/Prop1-type endocrine wiring, but the dataset lacks a matched transcriptomic collapse of Igsf1 with related receptor or membrane IgSF perturbations.
main_caveats: Igsf8 is an Ig-superfamily comparator rather than a validated IGSF1 paralog; Trhr, Tshr, and Gnrhr transcripts also showed weak measured engagement, so the contrast is restricted to summary signatures.

summary: Hic1 perturbation was not detectably engaged at the Hic1 RNA itself and produced no FDR-significant downstream genes in any tested brain cell class.
why_it_matters: HIC1 is a curated nuclear transcriptional repressor with in-vivo developmental phenotypes, so the flat Perturb-seq result is best interpreted as a failed or strongly buffered RNA-level perturbation rather than evidence that Hic1 biology is absent from brain cells.
main_caveats: The parquet contains DE summaries rather than guide sequences, raw Hic1 expression, indel genotypes, or HIC1 protein measurements; ineffective RNA depletion can mask a real protein function.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Hic1 was flat while Ctbp1, Arid1a, Tcf7l2, and Ctnnb1 perturbations were active and largely uncorrelated with the Hic1 vector.
why_it_matters: The most powered Hic1 context was not globally refractory: perturbing a CTBP corepressor and Wnt/β-catenin or chromatin neighbors yielded significant programs in the same thalamic glutamatergic class, whereas Hic1 did not.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Ctbp1, Arid1a, Tcf7l2 and Ctnnb1 are not interchangeable with Hic1; the contrast is also constrained by the missing Hic1 target-mRNA knockdown.

summary: Canonical HIC1-associated axes were not derepressed: Sirt1, Trp53, Ctnnb1, Tcf7l2, Atoh1, Ctbp1/Ctbp2 and Mta-family transcripts all remained FDR-nonsignificant after Hic1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Prior work links HIC1 loss to SIRT1/p53, Wnt/TCF-β-catenin, CtBP, and Atoh1 regulation; none of these expected readouts appeared in the mouse-brain DE summaries.
main_caveats: The assay did not impose DNA damage, Wnt stimulation, or cochlear differentiation cues, and Hic1 RNA depletion was not observed.

summary: The lowest nominal Hic1 FDR values were scattered across L5 ET cortical, pineal, thalamic, and Sst GABA classes rather than forming a reproducible cell-type program.
why_it_matters: Sirt5 in L5 ET cells and Plekhg5/Rap2a in pineal cells are the most visible candidate biomarkers, but their high FDR values make them triage hypotheses only.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: All highlighted genes fail FDR control, and the pineal comparison has only 35 perturbed cells.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor search found no strong Hic1 convergence or anti-convergence with any other perturbation.
why_it_matters: The absence of a close neighbor prevents reassigning the weak Hic1 phenotype to another pathway on the basis of score-vector similarity; several safe-target controls appeared among top local neighbors at comparable correlations.
main_caveats: The comparison used RNA score-vector Pearson correlations within each cell class and does not test protein-level convergence.

summary: Ddhd1 perturbation produced a globally buffered mRNA phenotype in this dataset: the target was never FDR-depleted and no downstream gene reached FDR<0.05 across 22 cell types.
why_it_matters: DDHD1 is a lipid enzyme, so a weak scRNA differential-expression profile should not be mistaken for absence of lipid, organelle, or disease biology.
main_caveats: All target-transcript adjusted p values were 1.0, and most cell-type contrasts contained fewer than 100 perturbed cells.

summary: Mcl1 up-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA was the only near-FDR Ddhd1-associated transcript change.
why_it_matters: This nominates Mcl1 as an exploratory, cell-class-restricted follow-up marker rather than as a validated DDHD1 pathway effector.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Mcl1 missed the standard FDR<0.05 threshold and Ddhd1 itself was not detectably reduced in this same cell type.

summary: 308 CB GABA showed the strongest nominal reduction of the Ddhd1 transcript, yet still had no FDR-supported downstream response.
why_it_matters: The contrast most compatible with target engagement was still molecularly buffered, arguing against a large cerebellar GABA mRNA program after partial Ddhd1 perturbation.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The on-target Ddhd1 p value was nominal, not FDR-significant; the perturbation used only 74 cells.

summary: Ddhd1 and Ddhd2 signatures were nearly orthogonal in every matched cell type despite being DDHD-family, HSP-linked lipid enzymes that Reactome places in the same PA-hydrolysis reaction.
why_it_matters: The paralogs should not be collapsed as interchangeable perturbations in this transcriptomic assay.
main_caveats: Both paralogs had weak scRNA target engagement, so the contrast is about observed transcriptional signatures rather than definitive lipid functions.

summary: Expected phosphatidic-acid/phosphatidylinositol and mitochondrial-dynamics genes did not convert the Ddhd1 perturbation into a coherent mRNA module.
why_it_matters: The dataset is more consistent with DDHD1 acting through lipid remodeling that is invisible or compensated at the assayed mRNA time point than through a canonical transcriptional pathway.
main_caveats: The check covered selected transcripts only and cannot measure PA, PI, lysophospholipids, mitochondrial morphology, or protein activity.

summary: The weak mRNA phenotype should not be interpreted as evidence that reducing DDHD1 is safe in neurons.
why_it_matters: Human DDHD1 loss is linked to SPG28 and Ddhd1 knockout remodels brain PI/LPI lipids, so transcriptomic buffering does not rule out disease-relevant lipid toxicity.
main_caveats: No DDHD1 inhibitor or lipid phenotype was assayed; the dataset shows acute/partial transcript knockdown rather than human biallelic loss of function.

summary: Acute En2 perturbation produced a globally buffered transcriptome in the emitted mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A weak global response prevents treating En2 as a strong acute regulator in these broad classes and makes single nominal hits require empirical-null caution.
main_caveats: The target transcript was not measurably knocked down, so the result distinguishes a weak/buffered Perturb-seq readout from definitive En2 dispensability.

summary: Tmem191 up-regulation in CTX-CGE GABA was the only En2 response passing FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This localizes the strongest corrected En2 signal to a cortical CGE-derived inhibitory class, but as a one-gene response it is best viewed as a provisional reporter rather than a pathway call.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Only Tmem191 reached FDR<0.10; the En2 transcript test was negative and safe-target perturbations sometimes produced isolated corrected hits.

summary: MB/P/MY GABA showed a nominal Calm3-down/Mgrn1-up pair just outside FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The paired opposite-direction genes mark a possible hindbrain inhibitory response, but its adjusted p value of 0.100201 makes it hypothesis-generating only.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Both genes miss the FDR<0.10 cutoff and no broader corrected pathway accompanied them.

summary: En2 did not phenocopy En1 or assayed midbrain-hindbrain pathway neighbors in the same cell classes.
why_it_matters: The absence of En1/Pax/Otx/Zic convergence argues that this dataset is not activating the canonical embryonic En2 module even though those genes are expected developmental partners.
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptomic and same-dataset, but weak guide engagement for En2 and En1 could attenuate true biological similarity.

summary: The final DE panel under-sampled the cell contexts most emphasized by En2 cerebellar and dopaminergic literature.
why_it_matters: Negative En2 results in broad mature classes should not be over-extended to developmental cerebellar excitatory neurons or adult dopaminergic neurons, two contexts with prior Engrailed biology.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Absence of En2 rows for 215 MB Dopa shows lack of a final DE test, not necessarily absence of all En2-edited cells; 308 CB GABA is not the cerebellar excitatory lineage highlighted by developmental studies.

summary: The largest En2 signature-neighbor structure was in 308 CB GABA and involved Wdr26/Ranbp2 rather than the Engrailed developmental network.
why_it_matters: This flags a restricted, aggregate CB GABA signature as an exploratory state effect while preventing it from being mistaken for En1/En2 pathway recovery.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Driven by full-score correlations without any En2 single-gene FDR<0.10 in 308 CB GABA.

summary: Antxr1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome in any assayed neuronal stratum.
why_it_matters: ANTXR1 is an ECM- and actin-linked receptor in vascular/connective-tissue biology; its absence as a neuronal Perturb-seq driver argues that the assayed brain neuronal classes do not engage that canonical program at the RNA level after Antxr1 targeting.
main_caveats: Negative transcriptomic result only; per-cell-type perturbed counts were modest and the dominant vascular/fibroblast contexts of ANTXR1 were absent from the annotated strata.

direction: Antxr1 nominally down; downstream not significant
summary: The best nominal Antxr1 target-RNA decrease occurred in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, yet that same stratum still had no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: A nominal on-target signal without any corrected downstream response is more consistent with a buffered or underpowered neuronal response than with an active ECM/actin remodeling cascade.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: The Antxr1 decrease was nominal only and may not prove protein loss or guide efficacy.

summary: Antxr1 and its paralog Antxr2 were not interchangeable in this screen.
why_it_matters: ANTXR1 and ANTXR2 are related cell-surface anthrax-toxin/collagen receptors, but every matched Antxr1-versus-Antxr2 score-vector correlation was near zero and the lone Antxr2 FDR event had no Antxr1 counterpart.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Both receptor signatures were weak overall; correlation of weak signatures cannot exclude shared protein-level collagen handling outside the RNA endpoint.

summary: Selected ANTXR/adhesion/vascular pathway neighbors in the library did not converge on the Antxr1 signature.
why_it_matters: The lack of correlation to Antxr2, Itgb1, Lrp6, Mapk1, Pdgfrb, Tek, or Arhgap18 supports the interpretation that canonical adhesion, EGFR/ERK, and vascular-stromal ANTXR biology was not transcriptionally activated by Antxr1 perturbation in these classes.
main_caveats: This used a restricted hand-selected neighbor set and transcriptome correlations; many ECM ligands and post-translational readouts were not assayed as perturbations.

summary: The neuronal null result should not be interpreted as systemic ANTXR1-targeting safety evidence.
why_it_matters: The screen mainly sampled neuronal labels and found no Antxr1 FDR response, whereas human atlas and in-vivo CAR-T data point to normal vascular/smooth-muscle/stromal TEM8 exposure as a plausible on-target/off-tumor liability.
main_caveats: This is a context-coverage warning rather than a toxicity measurement in this dataset.

summary: Antxr1 lacked a robust positive or negative signature-neighbor module.
why_it_matters: The top association, Wdr26 in 308 CB GABA, reached only r=0.225 and the most anticorrelated target, Ranbp2, reached r=-0.217; such weak, cell-type-local correlations do not justify assigning Antxr1 to a new transcriptional pathway.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was calculated from an Antxr1 signature with no FDR-significant genes; the neighbor result is useful chiefly as a guard against overinterpreting weak nominal structure.

summary: Chrna1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered or inactive across all 22 sampled mouse-brain cell classes: the endogenous target transcript was measured but never depleted at even nominal strength, and the perturbation produced only one FDR-level gene overall.
why_it_matters: A silent signature strongly indicates that most downstream Chrna1 comparisons should be interpreted as lack of target engagement rather than as a meaningful acetylcholine-receptor program.
main_caveats: The table contains differential-expression statistics rather than raw counts or guide-level efficiency; several classes have fewer than 60 matched perturbed cells.

summary: The lone FDR-significant Chrna1 response was Fgf9 up-regulation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, making it an exploratory, cell-restricted biomarker candidate rather than evidence for a recurring Chrna1 pathway.
why_it_matters: Preserving this isolated positive result prevents the global negative result from hiding the only multiple-testing-significant gene, while its lack of recurrence keeps the interpretation conservative.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Only one gene in one cell class survived FDR; Chrna1 itself was not engaged, and Fgf9 was not significant in the other 21 classes.

summary: Chrna1 and the assayed muscle-type receptor partners Chrnb1, Chrnd, Chrne, and Chrng converge on the same near-null brain phenotype: no partner showed on-target knockdown or any FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: The most relevant protein-complex comparison supports a complex-wide absence of a functional muscle nicotinic receptor module in these cells rather than an idiosyncratic Chrna1 result.
main_caveats: The inference is transcriptomic and does not assay receptor assembly or ion currents directly.

summary: Neuronal acetylcholine-pathway perturbations were engageable in the same atlas while Chrna1 was not: Chrnb2, Chrna4, and Ache showed strong self-depletion in thalamic, midbrain, or posterior GABA/glutamate classes.
why_it_matters: This separates Chrna1 from neuronal nicotinic biology and shows the negative Chrna1 result is not simply a failure to perturb every acetylcholine-related gene.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only transcript knockdown of the pathway neighbors was measured here; downstream physiological acetylcholine signaling was not assayed.

summary: Whole-signature comparison did not reveal any hidden positive or negative Chrna1 neighbor among 2,045 other perturbations; the strongest absolute Pearson correlation was only 0.033.
why_it_matters: A weak target can still become interpretable if it matches another perturbation, but Chrna1 behaved as a signature orphan and offered no pathway-neighbor rescue.
main_caveats: The correlation was computed on Wilcoxon scores and is dominated by near-null signatures; it should be used only to rule out strong similarity.

summary: CHRNA1 disease and pharmacology priors point to peripheral neuromuscular-junction channel dysfunction, so this brain Perturb-seq null should not be read as a negative disease model for congenital myasthenic syndromes or as evidence that CHRNA1-directed drugs would lack muscle liabilities.
why_it_matters: The result is directionally useful: mouse-brain neurons are the wrong primary context for CHRNA1 loss, whereas neuromuscular studies remain necessary for efficacy and safety.
main_caveats: The warning is based on context mismatch; the dataset did not include skeletal muscle, neuromuscular junctions, or drug exposure.

direction: no measurable target-transcript change and no broad downstream DE
summary: Dmbt1 perturbation produced no measurable on-target Dmbt1 mRNA change and almost no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response across the 21 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset result is absence of response, which argues that Dmbt1 is either poorly engaged or not a cell-autonomous regulator in these neuronal populations.
main_caveats: A guide could perturb rare Dmbt1-positive cells without a bulk mRNA signature; weak target-transcript evidence prevents a clean functional knockout interpretation.

summary: Epb41 down-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut was the single FDR-significant Dmbt1-associated gene-level response.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only statistically strong local event while preventing it from being overgeneralized to other Dmbt1-assayed cell types.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene effect detected in 50 perturbed cells; no direct Dmbt1-Epb41 mechanism was identified.

direction: uncoupled; weak positive and negative correlation
summary: The 027 Dmbt1 signature did not converge with the DMBT1 mucosal/surfactant-associated neighborhood or with any strong positive or negative signature neighbor in the broader library.
why_it_matters: Known DMBT1 biology points to secreted pattern-recognition and surfactant networks, but the only FDR-positive neuronal response was not a phenocopy of Hmgb1, Lgals3, Reg1, or any high-correlation perturbation.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Comparator analysis was restricted to the 027 cell class; STRING edges are functional associations and do not prove a physical DMBT1 complex.

summary: This normal mouse-brain Perturb-seq context did not reproduce a DMBT1 malignant-brain-tumor-like transcriptional phenotype.
why_it_matters: Although DMBT1 was discovered as deleted in malignant brain tumours, the present data argue against using weak Dmbt1 neuronal DE as evidence for acute tumor-suppressor biology.
main_caveats: The assay used normal mouse brain cell classes rather than human glioma or medulloblastoma cells, and Dmbt1 target engagement was not demonstrated.

summary: Cckbr perturbation produced weak on-target knockdown and no FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic response in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: A receptor with known GPCR activity looks largely buffered or under-engaged at the mRNA level, so mechanistic interpretation must start from a negative result rather than from the nominal top genes.
main_caveats: Target transcript depletion was only nominal in four cell classes; absence of FDR-significant DE can reflect low receptor expression, low cell counts, incomplete perturbation, or an acute post-transcriptional phenotype.

summary: Nominal receptor mRNA depletion was concentrated in L5 extratelencephalic, L5/6 intratelencephalic, L2/3 cortical intratelencephalic, and Pvalb GABA classes, with L5 ET showing the strongest Cckbr score.
why_it_matters: The pattern points to narrow, low-confidence engagement rather than a uniform brain-wide Cckbr loss-of-function state.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: All four target-transcript rows had FDR = 1.0, and 001 L5-6 IT Glut contained only 39 perturbed cells.

summary: Cck ligand knockdown and perturbation of the Gq/PLC calcium nodes Plcb1 and Itpr1 did not converge on the Cckbr score signature, while Cckar lacked useful target engagement.
why_it_matters: Although CCKBR belongs to the CCK/gastrin GPCR signaling network, the dataset argues against treating ligand loss, receptor loss, and core calcium-signal-node loss as interchangeable cell-autonomous transcriptomic perturbations.
main_caveats: The Cckbr signature itself is weak; Plcb1 and Itpr1 are shared by many receptors, and Cck is a secreted ligand whose cell-autonomous perturbation is not expected to exactly phenocopy receptor perturbation.

summary: The broad Pvalb class showed nominal Cckbr mRNA depletion without corrected DE, consistent with CCK2 receptor biology that can operate through acute, cell-subtype-specific electrophysiological pathways rather than a pooled transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: It prevents overinterpreting the absence of a Pvalb transcriptome as absence of CCK2 receptor function; PV basket-cell signaling can be acute and subtype-restricted.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The literature is from rat hippocampal PV basket cells, whereas the dataset groups mouse Pvalb neurons broadly across brain regions and measures RNA rather than membrane potential or calcium.

summary: All-gene signature-neighbor analysis found no high-correlation positive or negative neighbor for Cckbr.
why_it_matters: The perturbation was not merely weakly linked to the annotated CCK pathway; it also failed to align with any recurrent transcriptional module among more than forty-three thousand matched signatures.
main_caveats: The correlation analysis used all measured genes and signed Wilcoxon scores; a small receptor-specific effect could be diluted below r = 0.2.

summary: The dataset should not be used to choose CCKBR agonism versus antagonism from transcriptomic direction alone.
why_it_matters: CCKBR is druggable and coupled to rapid GPCR signaling, but every Cckbr cell class lacked corrected DE; antagonist mechanism records therefore supply pharmacologic feasibility, not a transcriptomic loss-of-function efficacy direction.
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measures longer-term RNA consequences of genetic perturbation, not acute ligand bias, dose, or receptor occupancy.

summary: Nrcam knockdown was directionally on target in every assayed class but corrected on-target detection was restricted to 11 of 22 neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: The perturbation was not a complete failure; the primary heterogeneity is cell-type-dependent detectability of Nrcam depletion rather than a reversal of guide direction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Target engagement was inferred from mRNA, not protein; some nonsignificant cell types had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Even where Nrcam mRNA was depleted, the downstream single-cell RNA response was almost completely buffered.
why_it_matters: A strong adhesion-receptor perturbation can be visible at its own transcript while failing to trigger a broad cell-autonomous mRNA program, consistent with phenotypes that depend on protein localization, contacts, axons or synapses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Wilcoxon RNA readout cannot score neurite fasciculation, axon routing, dendritic spines, or membrane microdomain localization.

summary: Nrcam did not phenocopy Ank3 or other curated L1/contactin/axon-guidance neighbors in the profiled transcriptomes.
why_it_matters: Physical or pathway proximity to NrCAM is therefore not interchangeable with an Nrcam-like transcriptional signature; the Ankyrin-G partner had a far larger thalamic RNA phenotype than Nrcam.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison used same-cell-type RNA score correlations; it can miss a shared nontranscriptional or subcellular phenotype.

summary: The known NrCAM-Sema3F/Neuropilin-2/Plexin receptor pathway was not transcriptionally mobilized by Nrcam knockdown.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse work places NrCAM in Sema3F-dependent axon guidance and spine pruning, but this dataset narrows the observable acute response to loss of Nrcam mRNA rather than induction of Nrp2, Plexin, SAP or contactin transcripts.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment does not match the embryonic thalamocortical, postnatal visual-cortex, or amygdalar tract assays that established the pathway.

summary: Crebbp repression in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Letm2 induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut are the only non-Nrcam FDR hits and are weak, cell-type-restricted marker candidates.
why_it_matters: These two genes are the only measurable downstream transcripts that pass correction, so they are useful for follow-up but should not be treated as a general Nrcam module.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Each marker appeared in one cell type only and had an FDR just below 0.05.

summary: The muted RNA phenotype of Nrcam knockdown should not be read as loss-of-function safety for the adhesion pathway.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic NRCAM variants and mouse Nrcam-null studies produce neurodevelopmental or circuit defects, indicating that disease-relevant liabilities can be structural and developmental rather than visible as a large acute adult transcriptomic response.
main_caveats: The dataset used partial mRNA knockdown in cell classes rather than organismal germline loss of NRCAM; it is not a drug safety assay.

summary: Across all assayed mouse-brain cell classes, Eda perturbation failed to produce either significant Eda transcript depletion or any FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is not a hidden pathway activation but a strongly caveated negative result; because EDA is a processed TNF-family ligand, a cell-autonomous Perturb-seq assay may miss non-cell-autonomous ligand functions.
main_caveats: The molecular target was weakly engaged at the transcript level, so the absence of downstream DE cannot be read as proof that Eda is dispensable in the brain.

summary: Calb1 down-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA was the strongest single-gene Eda-associated signal.
why_it_matters: If Eda has a rare neuronal effect in this screen, the LGE GABA/Calb1 axis is the clearest candidate to revisit with higher guide efficiency or pooled validation.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Calb1 did not pass FDR correction and the supporting nominal genes were cell-class private rather than recurrent.

summary: A small 217 P MY Pineal Glut group showed a coherent-looking but non-significant positive nominal signature led by Plxna1, Aplp1, Arfrp1, Tmeff1, and Slc46a3.
why_it_matters: This preserves a possible pineal glutamatergic Eda response without elevating it to a pathway call; it is a prioritization hint, not a confirmed module.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only 38 Eda-perturbed cells were available and the best pineal FDR was 0.728810.

summary: Eda did not phenocopy Edar or NF-kappaB-neighborhood perturbations in the same cell classes; Edar had isolated Rptor and Zmym3 FDR hits that were absent from Eda.
why_it_matters: The assayed brain-cell signatures do not reconstruct the canonical EDA-A1/EDAR/EDARADD/NF-kappaB module, warning against treating ligand and receptor perturbations as interchangeable in this dataset.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptomic and restricted to cell-autonomous perturbations; weak Eda target engagement is sufficient to explain failure of ligand-receptor phenocopy.

summary: The Eda Perturb-seq result should not be used to infer that EDA activation or replacement would have strong neuronal transcriptional effects.
why_it_matters: Human EDA loss is a prenatal ectodermal-organ disease, whereas this screen sampled mouse brain cell classes and did not measurably deplete Eda; the therapeutic direction remains anchored in ectodermal development rather than in the nominal neuronal genes reported here.
main_caveats: This is an interpretation safeguard based on lack of signal, not a direct efficacy or safety experiment.

direction: near-null except one Sst Dhtkd1 induction
summary: Ednra perturbation was transcriptionally quiet in the assayed neuronal classes, with no detectable target-transcript knockdown and only one significant gene among 338,323 Ednra DE tests.
why_it_matters: This makes broad mature-neuronal EDNRA activity a poor explanation for the dataset and prevents interpreting most null cell types as confident loss-of-function biology.

summary: Il12rb1 perturbation did not produce a statistically robust target-transcript or downstream RNA response in any tested mouse-brain cell class.

summary: The canonical IL-12/IL-23 receptor-JAK/STAT module was uncoupled from the Il12rb1 perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: IL12RB1 is the shared receptor subunit for IL-12 and IL-23 signaling, but key receptor-family and STAT-output transcripts remained unchanged, indicating that these brain cell classes did not execute a measurable IL-12/IL-23 transcriptional response after Il12rb1 perturbation.
cell_types: Il12rb1-tested neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: Evidence is at mRNA level only; phospho-STAT signaling, secreted cytokines, IL12RB2, IL12A, and IL23A were not all measurable as an induced protein pathway in this table.

summary: Il12rb1 lacked both expected IL-12/IL-23-family convergence and data-driven positive or negative transcriptomic neighbors.
why_it_matters: The near-zero correlations to Il12b, Il23r, Stat3, Stat4, and every other well-covered perturbation argue against a hidden coherent Il12rb1 module that is merely mislabeled by the top single-gene hits.
cell_types: Il12rb1-tested neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: This is a restricted-signature correlation analysis with weak Il12rb1 target engagement; near-zero correlations should be read as no detectable convergence in this assay, not as evidence that the proteins are unrelated in immune cells.

summary: The Perturb-seq negative result confines interpretation away from the known lymphoid IL12RB1 deficiency mechanism rather than challenging it.
why_it_matters: Human IL12RB1 loss causes IL-12/IL-23 signaling failure and infection susceptibility in immune lineages, whereas the measured neuronal classes showed no IFN-gamma, IL-23, or STAT4 transcriptional response; this dataset is therefore poorly matched to therapeutic or Mendelian immune disease mechanism inference for IL12RB1.
cell_types: Il12rb1-tested neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: This is a context warning, not evidence about IL12RB1 function in T cells, NK cells, macrophages, or patients.

summary: Chrm3 yielded no FDR-supported transcriptional response in any of 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes.

main_caveats: The negative result is transcriptomic and coincides with weak target-transcript knockdown, so it cannot exclude acute receptor signaling or CHRM3 activity in unassayed conditions.

summary: Chrm3 target engagement was weak even where the target transcript was measured.
why_it_matters: The broad absence of downstream FDR hits is most parsimoniously interpreted as failed or weak Chrm3 depletion plus possible low RNA detectability, not as proof that M3 signaling is unnecessary in every cell type.

summary: The downstream H2ac8 transcriptome was FDR-null across all 23 mouse-brain cell classes.

why_it_matters: Negative brain-cell RNA results should not be used to de-prioritize DYNC2I1 disease biology; the relevant mechanisms may require early development, stronger allelic loss, or direct ciliary transport phenotyping.
main_caveats: This refinement is inferred from absence of a robust RNA signature in profiled mouse-brain classes; the assay did not test embryonic skeletal or neural-tube tissues.

summary: Alx3 perturbation did not measurably shift the Alx3 transcript in any of 23 tested cell classes.
why_it_matters: The main Alx3 phenotype must be interpreted under weak transcript-level engagement or low endogenous expression rather than as a clean target-depletion signature.
main_caveats: Target mRNA abundance is not the same as DNA editing or protein loss, and raw guide-level editing information was unavailable.

summary: Serinc3 downregulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut was the only FDR-significant Alx3 downstream response.
why_it_matters: This preserves the single statistically robust gene as a possible cell-type-restricted biomarker while avoiding overcalling a pathway from one gene.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene response only; the Alx3 transcript did not show detectable on-target depletion.

summary: Twenty-two of 23 cell classes showed no FDR-significant downstream Alx3 response.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset result is a broad negative or buffered phenotype; even high-cell-count neuronal classes lacked corrected responses.
main_caveats: Because Alx3 mRNA engagement was not detected, the result cannot separate biological buffering from an off-context or ineffective perturbation.

summary: Alx3, Alx1, and Alx4 perturbations were orthogonal or disjoint rather than convergent in the neuronal Perturb-seq panel.
why_it_matters: Developmental genetic interaction among aristaless-like factors does not translate into a shared adult neuronal expression module in this screen.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Alx1 had low perturbed-cell counts in several classes, and the signature-neighbor correlations are exploratory score-vector summaries.

summary: Craniofacial and hypothalamic Alx3 literature was not recapitulated as a broad postnatal neuronal Alx3 response.
why_it_matters: The null Pomc/Mc3r and HY/TH results suggest that ALX3 disease and metabolic mechanisms are likely developmental, specialized, or absent from these sampled classes rather than broadly maintained across adult neurons.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq classes may not match embryonic craniofacial tissue or the arcuate-hypothalamic neurons in the whole-animal metabolic study.

summary: Arhgap32 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: This prevents individual nominal genes from being interpreted as validated downstream effectors and makes weak target engagement a central constraint on the experiment.
main_caveats: The table does not expose guide-level knockdown or protein activity; a transcriptome-wide negative result can reflect weak perturbation rather than absence of ARHGAP32 biology.

summary: Nominal Arhgap32 self-knockdown was concentrated in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but neither cell type showed FDR-level downstream effects.
why_it_matters: The best cell types for follow-up are glutamatergic, yet the absence of FDR support and the broad brain expression reported by HPA make this an engagement-biased rather than definitive lineage-specific result.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Self-transcript rows were not FDR significant; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had only 53 perturbed cells.

summary: Arhgap32 knockdown did not transcriptionally activate or repress the expected NMDA receptor, cadherin, Rac1/Cdc42, or Pak/MAPK mRNA module.
why_it_matters: The literature places ARHGAP32/RICS in a postsynaptic small-GTPase and receptor-complex pathway, so the dataset indicates that this mechanism is not captured as a robust acute mRNA program.
main_caveats: The canonical scan tests transcript abundance only and cannot measure Rho-family GTP loading, receptor trafficking, or spine morphology.

summary: Arhgap32 signatures did not converge with stronger Ctnnb1, Apc, Grin1, Grin2b, Rac1, Cdc42, Pak, Dlg4, or Arhgap18 perturbations.
why_it_matters: Direct perturbations of the pathway can elicit strong DE in this atlas, so Arhgap32's failure to align with them is a specific cross-perturbation contrast rather than only a globally insensitive dataset.
main_caveats: Similarity was assessed from weak Arhgap32 signatures; a true protein-level effect could occur without score-vector correlation.

summary: A screen-wide nearest-neighbor search failed to reveal a recurrent Arhgap32-like perturbation module.
why_it_matters: Because the top positive and negative neighbors were all very weak, the dataset does not support replacing the canonical pathway with an alternative transcriptomic mechanism.
main_caveats: The finding is restricted to Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors and does not rule out shared phenotypes outside mRNA abundance.

summary: ARHGAP32 loss-of-function disease biology should be modeled with synaptic trafficking and small-GTPase activity assays rather than with this weak acute mRNA signature alone.
why_it_matters: PX-RICS/ARHGAP32 deficiency is linked to GABA_A receptor trafficking and autism-like phenotypes, but the Perturb-seq signature lacks both FDR-level genes and disease-neighborhood convergence.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment is not a behavioral, receptor-trafficking, or electrophysiology assay; the ChEMBL-negative search is database coverage, not proof of undruggability.

summary: Ebf1 generated no FDR-supported transcriptional response and no RNA-level target depletion across the 22 modeled brain cell groups.
why_it_matters: The perturbation cannot be used as evidence for an Ebf1-regulated adult neuronal program without demonstrated target engagement.
main_caveats: Absence of a DE signature may reflect low Ebf1 expression or ineffective transcript knockdown rather than biological dispensability.

summary: The CNU-LGE/LSX GABA group lacked a detectable Ebf1 response despite being the assayed group closest to the published striatal Ebf1 developmental context.
why_it_matters: This prevents overgeneralization from embryonic or direct-pathway striatal knockout phenotypes to all mature LGE-derived GABAergic neurons.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset cell group is broad and mature; it is not a purified embryonic mantle or direct-pathway striatonigral MSN population, and on-target depletion was weak.

summary: Ebf1, Ebf2, and Ebf3 perturbations converged on a nearly silent phenotype rather than producing correlated COE-family transcriptomic programs.
why_it_matters: The weak Ebf1 phenotype is not rescued by considering Ebf2 or Ebf3 as obvious interchangeable signature neighbors in the same dataset.
main_caveats: Ebf2 and Ebf3 also showed weak engagement in many groups; absence of correlated scRNA-seq signatures does not rule out COE-family functions in other stages or cell types.

summary: The strongest Ebf1 nominal genes and signature neighbors were too weak for pathway assignment.
why_it_matters: It explicitly down-weights tempting but unsupported assignments from the 009 nominal tail or from the weak Tgfbr2/Lman2l neighbor correlations.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: This is a robustness finding, not mechanistic evidence about the named neighbor perturbations.

summary: Hoxd13 produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic effect in 22 assayed mouse-brain cell types and no measurable reduction of its own transcript.
why_it_matters: This frames Hoxd13 as an off-context or weakly engaged target in this dataset rather than as a neuronal regulator with a hidden broad signature.
main_caveats: The target may have been edited at DNA level despite uninformative RNA; the dataset lacks Hoxd13 rows for 215 MB Dopa.

summary: The known Hoxd13 distal-limb and digit-patterning network was absent or FDR-null after Hoxd13 perturbation in the brain screen.
why_it_matters: It prevents extrapolating these neuronal Perturb-seq signatures to HOXD13 synpolydactyly mechanisms, which depend on limb chromatin and target-gene context.
main_caveats: Several limb genes are weakly expressed or filtered out in brain; this is a named-gene check, not a significant enrichment result.

summary: HOX-family paralog and PBX/MEIS cofactor perturbations did not phenocopy the Hoxd13 signature.
why_it_matters: Related developmental factors should not be treated as interchangeable in this dataset; the absence of convergence is itself evidence that the Hoxd13 profile lacks a HOX13 core response.
main_caveats: The Hoxd13 signature is weak, so near-zero correlations should not be overinterpreted as biological opposition.

summary: Large Hoxd13 perturbation cell counts in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut still produced FDR-null signatures.
why_it_matters: The global null is not explained only by the lowest-count Hoxd13 cell types, although lack of target expression remains the leading limitation.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is not proof of molecular buffering because the Hoxd13 transcript was not measurably engaged.

summary: Nominal Hoxd13 peaks were largest in 308 CB GABA, 053 Sst Gaba, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, but none survived FDR correction.
why_it_matters: These rows are the only cell-type hints in the dataset and should be treated as exploratory QC leads rather than Hoxd13 biology.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|053 Sst Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: All adjusted p values were greater than 0.12; the implicated genes were not recurrent canonical Hoxd13 targets.

summary: Il4ra targeting did not produce measurable Il4ra RNA knockdown or any 5% FDR downstream transcriptional response in the assayed neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Without detected on-target engagement, the experiment is best interpreted as a negative Perturb-seq result rather than evidence that IL-4Rα protein is dispensable in every brain context.
cell_types: 23 assayed neuronal cell groups
main_caveats: Sparse Il4ra expression and variable guide activity can make logFC values unstable; several groups had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: Canonical IL-4/IL-13 receptor and JAK/STAT/SOCS transcripts remained FDR-null after Il4ra targeting.
why_it_matters: Known IL4R signaling should couple ligand-bound receptor complexes to STAT and SOCS programs, so the absence of these transcript changes argues that the basal neuronal assay did not engage a canonical IL-4/IL-13 response.
cell_types: 23 assayed neuronal cell groups
main_caveats: The readout is mRNA abundance rather than receptor protein, phospho-JAK, or phospho-STAT6; many core pathway genes were measured but not themselves perturbed.

summary: The broad neuronal null refines prior CNS IL-4Rα reports toward a context-restricted requirement rather than a universal baseline neuronal program.
why_it_matters: Published work links neuronal IL-4Rα to inhibitory-neuron memory circuits, synaptic homeostasis, and ischemic neuroprotection, whereas this unstimulated screen saw no pan-neuronal gene-expression program and did not sample IL4R-enriched macrophage, endothelial, or vascular populations.
cell_types: 23 assayed neuronal cell groups
main_caveats: The screen lacks injury, exogenous IL-4/IL-13, T-cell spatial context, glia, and vascular cells; it may also miss rare inhibitory subtypes used in genetic mouse studies.

summary: The available IL4RA complex member Il2rg and several cytokine-receptor neighbors were null and did not converge with Il4ra signatures.
why_it_matters: The result prevents over-interpreting Il4ra as the lone inactive receptor: in this neuronal panel, multiple related cytokine inputs looked silent or weakly engaged, and most canonical type-II IL-4/IL-13 comparators were not targeted.
cell_types: 21-23 assayed neuronal cell groups, depending on comparator
main_caveats: Il13ra1, Il13ra2, Jak1, Jak2, Jak3, Stat6, Il4, and Il13 were absent from the perturbation target list, and receptor comparators also lacked corrected on-target knockdown.

summary: Sf3b1/Wtap and the 308 CB GABA signature-neighbor block are only exploratory, not robust Il4ra biomarkers.
why_it_matters: The smallest p values and highest correlations can otherwise look biologically directional, but they were FDR-negative, isolated, and disconnected from IL-4/JAK-STAT biology.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to nominal genes and correlation analysis of a very weak Il4ra signature.

summary: The neuronal null should not be used as evidence that antibody-grade IL4R blockade is transcriptionally inert in the CNS.
why_it_matters: IL4R is an approved-antibody target associated with allergic disease, but this dataset lacks target engagement and omits HPA IL4R-enriched non-neuronal brain compartments, so it is not a CNS safety or efficacy model for IL4R blockers.
cell_types: 23 assayed neuronal cell groups
main_caveats: The perturbation modality is CRISPR-based loss of mouse Il4ra RNA in neurons, not pharmacologic blockade of human IL4Rα in immune, epithelial, glial, or vascular cells.

summary: Champ1 perturbation produced neither detectable Champ1 transcript depletion nor any 5% FDR downstream gene in the measured neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This makes weak target engagement the dominant interpretation of the dataset response and prevents a false conclusion that CHAMP1 loss is biologically silent in neurons.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an imperfect readout for nuclease editing, and the parquet has no protein or editing-efficiency measurement.

summary: The only near-corrected Champ1 downstream row was Eid2 upregulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
why_it_matters: If any true transcriptomic response occurred, the dataset localizes the strongest candidate to one glutamatergic class rather than to a broad CHAMP1 program.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Eid2 stopped at FDR 0.083789 and all other adjusted p values were at least 0.390, so this is not a 5% FDR hit.

summary: Champ1 did not induce a coherent same-direction cross-class module; Gaa was the most recurrent nominal gene and was down in eight classes only nominally.
why_it_matters: A recurrent gene with weak nominal support is a better biomarker hypothesis than a pathway claim and emphasizes that the screen captured a shallow response.
main_caveats: The recurrence is based on nominal p<0.05 rows and no Gaa row reached FDR<0.05.

summary: Pogz, the direct CHAMP1-associated comparator present in the panel, did not show robust global convergence with Champ1.
why_it_matters: Prior CHAMP1 disease alleles can lose POGZ and HP1 binding, so a strong same-direction POGZ signature would have supported a shared complex-level response; the dataset instead points to weak or context-limited recovery of that relationship.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Both target transcripts were weakly engaged, and the 151 TH alignment used the top 200 Champ1-ranked genes rather than FDR-significant genes.

summary: The neuronal-class Perturb-seq result did not reproduce the developmental CHAMP1 loss program described in patients and knockout mice.
why_it_matters: The mismatch argues that CHAMP1 neurodevelopmental pathology depends on developmental timing, mitotic progenitor biology, perturbation strength, or a combination of these contexts.
main_caveats: The dataset does not directly assay embryonic progenitors, mitosis, chromosome segregation, or protein loss.

summary: This Champ1 perturbation does not nominate a corrected downstream biomarker or therapeutic rescue direction.
why_it_matters: CHAMP1 is a high-confidence NDD gene, but selecting a rescue target from this weak signature would overfit nominal single-cell effects.
main_caveats: The warning is about this dataset and does not rule out CHAMP1-targeted rescue strategies in stronger models.

summary: Gfi1b perturbation did not measurably reduce Gfi1b RNA in any cell class in which the target transcript appeared.
why_it_matters: Without target-transcript engagement, a downstream null phenotype is more consistent with a non-expressed or inefficient perturbation than with proven dispensability of GFI1B protein.
main_caveats: On-target RNA abundance is a proxy; guide editing and protein depletion were not directly measured.

summary: Gfi1b knockdown produced no FDR < 0.05 downstream genes and no recurrent nominal multi-cell-type module across 22 mouse-brain signatures.
why_it_matters: The absence of a coherent response argues that canonical GFI1B erythroid/megakaryocytic repression circuitry was not engaged in the sampled glutamatergic and GABAergic brain cell classes.
main_caveats: High confidence for the dataset-level null result but limited mechanistic confidence because Gfi1b RNA engagement was not detected.

summary: The strongest Gfi1b-associated row was an exploratory Ankrd13a increase in 145 MH-LH TH Glut rather than a repeated pan-neuronal program.
why_it_matters: If reproduced with target-engaged guides, this thalamic/hypothalamic excitatory class would be the first place to test a subtle non-hematopoietic Gfi1b response.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Ankrd13a missed FDR 0.05 and all other highlighted genes had FDR at least 0.323.

summary: The Gfi1 paralog did not phenocopy or oppose Gfi1b in the mouse-brain panel.
why_it_matters: The comparison tests whether a shared GFI-family SNAG repressor architecture hides a neuronal module; the data instead support context-restricted biology.
main_caveats: Both signatures are weak, so the comparison is a negative audit rather than an epistasis experiment.

summary: The dataset does not reproduce a normal-brain loss-of-function counterpart of GFI1-family enhancer hijacking in medulloblastoma.
why_it_matters: It separates ectopic GFI1/GFI1B oncogene activation in tumor genomes from a requirement for endogenous Gfi1b transcription in ordinary sampled brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The perturbation is loss-of-function in mouse brain cells, not enhancer-driven GFI1B overexpression in group 3/4 medulloblastoma.

summary: A brain-transcriptome null result for Gfi1b should not be used to infer hematopoietic safety of GFI1B/LSD1-axis inhibition.
why_it_matters: The strongest literature liability for GFI1B perturbation is platelet and megakaryocyte biology, a compartment absent from this mouse-brain Perturb-seq screen.
main_caveats: Therapeutic inference is indirect because the dataset did not perturb Gfi1b in megakaryocytes or test LSD1 inhibitors.

summary: Lbx1 perturbation showed no measurable Lbx1 RNA depletion in any of the 22 assayed cell-type strata.
why_it_matters: Without detectable on-target knockdown, downstream DE has to be interpreted as weak-engagement or out-of-context evidence rather than as a clean Lbx1 loss-of-function phenotype.
main_caveats: The DE table lacks raw target expression, so near-zero scores can demonstrate absence of a rank shift but cannot separate failed CRISPRi from no baseline expression.

summary: Vps35l down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only FDR<0.05 Lbx1 response, with Tspan14, Fbxo21, and Sarnp remaining exploratory sub-FDR candidates.
why_it_matters: These genes are the only practical transcript-level handles for follow-up, but the isolation of the Vps35l hit argues against a broad LBX1 fate program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The only significant hit is unreplicated across cell types; Lbx1 target engagement was not detectable; pineal support used only 27 perturbed cells.

summary: Several high-cell-count Lbx1 strata remained transcriptionally silent.
why_it_matters: The null result is not restricted to the lowest-powered strata, strengthening the interpretation that many sampled brain classes lack an accessible LBX1-dependent program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: No stratum had strong Lbx1 RNA depletion, so apparent buffering may reflect absence of target expression rather than active compensation.

summary: Known LBX1 developmental neighbors Tlx3 and Phox2b did not show opposing or convergent Perturb-seq signatures in the assayed brain classes.
why_it_matters: The lack of a LBX1-TLX3 or LBX1-PHOX2B signature contrast prevents over-interpreting the Lbx1 null as a specific break from developmental genetics; the whole pathway neighborhood appears inactive in this screen context.
main_caveats: The signature-neighbor analysis was restricted to 50 Lbx1 extreme genes per cell type, and comparator perturbations also lacked target-transcript depletion.

summary: The dataset gives no inhibitory or activating direction for LBX1-linked congenital hypoventilation or scoliosis biology.
why_it_matters: LBX1 disease genetics map to developmental respiratory-neuron and skeletal/spinal programs, whereas the Perturb-seq data show a near-null, weakly engaged profile in broad mouse-brain classes.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The relevant embryonic retrotrapezoid and spinal contexts were not resolved as matched cell types, and the disease variants are not equivalent to acute Lbx1 knockdown.

summary: Creb1 perturbation recurrently induces the CREB-family gene Crem, with Crem becoming the top positive gene in five responsive neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: A paralog-family feedback signal is the dominant dataset-grounded output of Creb1 perturbation and matches the known ability of CREM to compensate for CREB loss, while raising the possibility that the measured Crem reads include repressive ICER isoforms.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The parquet reports gene-level Crem expression and cannot distinguish activating CREM isoforms from ICER repressor isoforms; no direct Crem or Atf1 perturbation was available for reciprocity.

summary: The Creb1 response is concentrated in thalamic/hypothalamic and midbrain subclasses: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut has a 10-gene program, 155 MB Glut has a 3-gene program, three other classes are Crem-only, and most tested classes have no FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: Bulk CREB genetics established a CNS requirement, but this dataset resolves a basal adult perturbation response into a small set of susceptible neuronal subclasses rather than a pan-neuronal transcriptional collapse.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The largest Creb1 cell count is only 126 perturbed cells, and absence of FDR hits in several classes may reflect limited power rather than complete biological buffering.

summary: Crem induction is specific to Creb1 perturbation rather than a generic consequence of disrupting upstream cAMP, NMDA-receptor, or CaMKII inputs.
why_it_matters: Although PKA, Ca2+/CaMK, and glutamatergic signaling converge on CREB phosphorylation, efficient Prkaca, Camk2b, Grin2b, Grin2a, and Adcy3 perturbations did not recreate the Creb1-to-Crem signature in the same classes, arguing that the signal is a CREB-family identity or compensation response rather than simple loss of upstream drive.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and basal; loss of an upstream transcript does not exactly equal loss of acute kinase activity or ligand-evoked CREB phosphorylation.

summary: Classic activity-dependent CREB targets are not significant in the Creb1 perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: The absence of Arc, Bdnf, Fos/Jun, Egr, Npas4, Nr4a1, Per1, and Vgf responses separates this perturbation state from the canonical stimulated pCREB immediate-early program.
main_caveats: The dataset measures guide-assigned basal transcriptomes, not synchronized neuronal depolarization or cAMP pulses; weak or transient immediate-early responses could be missed.

summary: The Creb1 transcript itself is not depleted by Creb1 guide assignment and is significantly increased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Target mRNA is therefore a poor engagement marker for this CRISPR perturbation; downstream Crem induction should be interpreted as a perturbation signature rather than as proof of Creb1 mRNA knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The table contains RNA differential expression only and not guide cut sites, protein abundance, CREB Ser133 phosphorylation, or DNA-editing genotypes.

summary: Gal perturbation produced no adjusted transcriptional hits in any of 22 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: A secreted neuropeptide ligand with curated GALR1-3 receptor biology failed to produce a large basal mRNA phenotype under this assay.
main_caveats: Negative downstream interpretation is constrained by weak measured Gal target engagement.

summary: The Gal mRNA target row was unperturbed despite being measured in every Gal cell-type signature.
why_it_matters: Without detectable target-transcript depletion, the clean downstream negative is more consistent with poor engagement, low/sparse expression, or buffering than with a definitive Gal loss-of-function phenotype.
main_caveats: CRISPR perturbation could affect unmeasured peptide output even when the assayed mRNA row is unchanged, but the dataset gives no evidence for that.

summary: The few nominal Gal hits were not recurrent across cell types and did not define a coherent module.
why_it_matters: Genes with the smallest nominal P values should be carried forward only as weak hypotheses, not as Gal-regulated pathway members.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is a statistical recurrence statement; it does not test protein secretion or neuronal firing.

summary: Gal and the only assayed canonical receptor, Galr1, were both weak; their score signatures were orthogonal rather than convergent.
why_it_matters: A known ligand-receptor relationship did not translate into similar cell-autonomous Perturb-seq profiles, and the screen lacked Galr2/Galr3 coverage needed to probe the full receptor family.
main_caveats: Galr2, Galr3, Galp, and Spx were absent from the perturbation library; Gal and Galr1 themselves lacked strong engagement.

summary: CA/DG glutamatergic Gal perturbations did not recapitulate the seizure and neuronal-injury biology known from Gal loss-of-function models.
why_it_matters: Galanin disease mechanisms linked to epilepsy may depend on paracrine neuropeptide tone, receptor-bearing postsynaptic cells, mature circuitry, or evoked activity rather than a basal mRNA state in the assayed hippocampal glutamatergic classes.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Only two broad CA/DG glutamatergic classes were assayed for Gal, and neither showed measured Gal mRNA knockdown.

summary: A negative Gal/Galr1 transcriptomic result should not be extrapolated to all galanin receptor pharmacology.
why_it_matters: GALR1, GALR2, and GALR3 have distinct GPCR coupling and ChEMBL activity corpora, but the Perturb-seq library excluded Galr2 and Galr3 and gave no engaged Galr1 signature.
main_caveats: This is a scope warning, not evidence of efficacy or inefficacy for any receptor agonist or antagonist.

summary: Significant Pdhb mRNA knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was buffered at the transcriptome-wide level: Pdhb was the only FDR-significant gene.
why_it_matters: PDHB is a core PDH enzyme subunit, so a clean on-target perturbation without any FDR-significant downstream individual gene argues that acute partial Pdhb loss was not converted into a large transcriptional state change in this neuronal class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Transcript counts do not measure PDHB protein, PDH flux, lactate, or ATP; the result is compatible with metabolic effects that are post-transcriptional or below the power of this assay.

summary: Resolved Pdhb target engagement was highly cell-type restricted in this dataset.
why_it_matters: The same gene target was tested across 22 neural cell classes, yet only thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons passed FDR for the target transcript; a second midbrain glutamatergic class was nominal but not FDR-significant.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a cell-type pattern of observed target-transcript depletion, not proof that Pdhb biology is intrinsically thalamus-specific; guide activity, Pdhb baseline expression, and cell number all contribute.

summary: Pdhb, Pdha1 and Dlat converged only at self-knockdown despite encoding coupled PDH-complex components.
why_it_matters: PDH E1 alpha, E1 beta and E2 are expected to act in one mitochondrial enzymatic assembly, but their acute single-gene Perturb-seq score vectors in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut were essentially uncorrelated and the nearest Pdhb signature neighbors were very weak.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to transcriptomic DE scores from a largely null signature; several regulatory comparators, including PDK and PDP genes, were not present as perturbations.

summary: The mild Perturb-seq readout should not be interpreted as evidence that neuronal PDHB loss is benign.
why_it_matters: Human PDHB loss-of-function reduces PDH-complex activity and causes lactic acidosis with severe neurodevelopmental disease, whereas the dataset measured only short-term mRNA consequences and found a buffered transcriptome after partial knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The disease literature concerns inherited, often biallelic human enzyme deficiency rather than acute partial guide perturbation in mouse neurons; no metabolite or viability endpoints were available.

summary: Measured Nrg2 perturbations were target-engagement limited and produced no conventional FDR<0.05 transcriptomic program in any cell class.
why_it_matters: The primary observation is not that NRG2 is dispensable, but that this Perturb-seq contrast gives a weak test of Nrg2 loss of function because the measured target transcript was not consistently depleted.
main_caveats: The assay measures target mRNA and downstream steady-state RNA, not NRG2 protein, ectodomain release, or acute ErbB phosphorylation.

summary: Sparse near-significant Nrg2 hits were concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with a separate singleton Noc3l hit in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: This nominates a small thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic candidate response, but the absence of any FDR<0.05 gene keeps the module hypothesis-generating.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The strongest five genes did not pass FDR<0.05 and the L2/3 cortical observation was a single gene.

summary: Nrg2 signatures did not phenocopy Erbb3, Erbb4, or assayed RAF-MEK-ERK and PI3K neighbors despite curated placement of NRG2 in ErbB signaling.
why_it_matters: NRG2 should not be treated as a generic proxy for ErbB receptor or ERK-pathway inhibition in this dataset; the ligand perturbation was transcriptomically uncoupled from receptor and intracellular signaling-node perturbations.
main_caveats: Nrg2 target engagement was weak, Erbb2/Egfr/Nrg4 were not available as assayed target rows, and correlation of whole-transcriptome CRISPR signatures is an indirect pathway-readout comparison.

summary: The broad Pvalb Gaba class did not show a constitutive Nrg2 transcriptional effect even though Erbb4 could be depleted robustly in that same class.
why_it_matters: The result cautions that the published NRG2-ErbB4 interneuron feedback loop may be state-, subtype-, or protein-processing-dependent rather than a strong steady-state RNA program in every Pvalb population.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba

summary: Hsp90ab1 signatures lacked strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbors and were nearly uncorrelated with the available Hsf1, Hspa8, and Hspd1 perturbations.

direction: Klhl7 down; downstream genes not FDR-resolved
summary: Klhl7 knockdown produced consistent target-transcript depletion but no FDR-resolved transcriptome response in any of 22 tested mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: KLHL7 is a CUL3-RING ubiquitin-ligase adaptor; the data therefore argue that partial loss of the adaptor is buffered at the mRNA level, at least in this assay, rather than causing an immediate broad proteostasis or differentiation signature.
main_caveats: Target rows were not FDR<0.05 in individual cell classes, protein depletion and ubiquitination substrates were not measured, and a post-translational defect could occur without an mRNA signature.

direction: nominal Klhl7 down with no FDR downstream
summary: The lack of downstream response was not restricted to the lowest-cell-count strata; the two largest Klhl7 strata, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, still had zero FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: This reduces the chance that Klhl7 looked quiet only because every assayed population was underpowered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Even 120-153 perturbed cells may be underpowered for small effects, and the Klhl7 target row itself remained FDR=1.0 in both classes.

direction: Cul3 active; Klhl7 buffered; signatures uncorrelated
summary: Klhl7 did not phenocopy the core BCR component Cul3: Cul3 had small FDR-resolved signatures in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Klhl7 had none and the paired signatures were nearly uncorrelated.
why_it_matters: Complex membership alone is not predictive here; a shared CUL3 scaffold can yield a measurable neuronal mRNA phenotype while a single KLHL7 substrate adaptor remains silent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Cul3 signatures were also small, Cul3 had fewer perturbed cells than Klhl7 in 155 MB Glut, and the comparison is transcriptomic not proteomic.

summary: Other measured BTB/Kelch-related perturbations, Klhl20, Btbd9, and Rhobtb2, did not converge with Klhl7; their maximum score-vector correlations with Klhl7 were only 0.165, 0.068, and 0.153.

main_caveats: These are pathway-neighbor rather than obligate same-complex comparisons, and each individual related perturbation had weak FDR support.

summary: Restricted-signature searches did not reveal a credible Klhl7 module: the closest transcriptome neighbors had |r|<=0.316, all came from 308 CB GABA, and a Safe_target signature appeared among the top 20 by absolute correlation.
why_it_matters: The observed nominal genes should not be promoted into a biological pathway without orthogonal support.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only on measured mRNA signatures and are not tests of protein interaction or pathway membership.

direction: human disease gene; mouse-brain transcriptome largely silent
summary: Human KLHL7 retinal and multisystem genetics were not mirrored by a broad acute mouse-brain mRNA failure after partial Klhl7 knockdown.
why_it_matters: The disease link remains strong, but this assay points away from a pan-neuronal transcriptional collapse and toward retina-specific, developmental, substrate-level, dosage, or protein-turnover mechanisms that would need direct testing.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain rather than human retina or PERCHING-relevant peripheral tissue, and CRISPR guide effects on KLHL7 protein were not measured.

summary: Robust Fgf13 transcript depletion was restricted to three of 23 assayed cell classes: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA.

main_caveats: Cell classes with only nominal depletion, including MB Dopa and Pvalb Gaba, may be underpowered rather than biologically resistant.

summary: Fgf13 knockdown produced a narrow RNA response: two strongly engaged cell classes showed target knockdown with no non-target FDR genes, and the third added only Rell2.
why_it_matters: Known FGF13 phenotypes involve ion-channel function, microtubules, and synapse development; their acute or post-developmental consequences may be molecularly buffered, post-transcriptional, or invisible to a single-cell mRNA endpoint.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The screen measured mRNA, not sodium currents, FGF13 protein, microtubule dynamics, or axonal synapses.

summary: Fgf13 loss did not transcriptionally phenocopy voltage-gated sodium-channel knockdowns or coordinately regulate sodium-channel/AIS transcripts.
why_it_matters: This separates FGF13's established Nav-binding role from a broad transcriptional sodium-channel feedback program and argues that electrophysiology, channel localization, or protein interaction assays are required as orthogonal readouts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Low score-vector correlations exclude shared mRNA programs in this dataset but do not test channel biophysics or protein trafficking.

summary: Fgf12 and Fgf14 signatures failed to converge with Fgf13 in the Fgf13-engaged cell classes, but the comparison is exploratory because Fgf12/Fgf14 self-depletion was weak.
why_it_matters: Reactome treats FGF11-14 as one FHF set, and Nav channels can bind multiple FHFs; the screen should not be read as evidence of paralog interchangeability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Fgf12 and Fgf14 perturbations did not reach FDR-level self knockdown in the focal cell classes, so divergence could be technical.

summary: Human genetics makes FGF13 directionality bidirectional and channel-centric, whereas Fgf13 transcript knockdown here left Nav mRNAs largely unchanged.
why_it_matters: FGF13 gain-of-function missense variants can cause DEE90 and reduced FGF13 translation can cause intellectual disability; a therapy or biomarker strategy that simply tracks FGF13 mRNA or Nav-transcript compensation could miss the pathogenic sodium-channel state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The dataset tests mouse Fgf13 knockdown, not human missense gain-of-function alleles or patient developmental time points.

direction: Mapk9 mRNA down, strongest in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 155 MB Glut
summary: Mapk9 target-transcript depletion was directional across the dataset but strongest in a small set of hypothalamic, midbrain, and thalamic glutamatergic classes.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Even the strongest on-target rows were not FDR<0.05; the expression reference is a human/mouse atlas context, not this Perturb-seq experiment.

summary: Partial Mapk9 knockdown produced no FDR-significant transcriptome response in any assayed basal brain cell class.
why_it_matters: JNK2 loss alone appears transcriptionally buffered in this basal neuronal setting, so lack of differential expression should not be mistaken for absence of JNK signaling capacity under stress.
main_caveats: The assay measured mRNA after partial perturbation and did not quantify kinase activity, phosphorylation, stress responses, or cell death.

summary: Mapk9 perturbation did not induce a detectable AP-1 or JNK-feedback transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: The missing Jun, Atf2, Fos/Jund, Mapk8/Mapk10, and MAP2K transcriptional response shows that basal Mapk9 transcript reduction is uncoupled from the canonical stress-activated JNK phosphorylation cascade at the mRNA level.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was tested; AP-1 protein phosphorylation and transient immediate-early responses could be missed.

summary: Assayed JNK-pathway neighbors and AP-1-related perturbations did not converge with the weak Mapk9 high-leverage signatures.
why_it_matters: A simple interchangeability model for Mapk9 and nearby JNK nodes is not supported by the restricted Perturb-seq signatures, which matters when using paralogs or scaffolds as mechanistic proxies.
main_caveats: The Mapk9 signatures had no FDR-significant genes, top-neighbor lists included Safe_target guides, and Map2k1/Map2k2 are ERK MAP2Ks rather than canonical JNK MAP2Ks.

direction: basal dataset insufficient for stress-apoptosis therapeutic direction
summary: The dataset does not directly test the stressed dopaminergic context in which JNK2/JNK3 biology has been linked to neuronal apoptosis.
why_it_matters: Mapk9 was not assayed in 215 MB Dopa, and basal non-dopaminergic signatures were buffered, so JNK2/3 inhibitor hypotheses for dopamine-neuron stress must be validated in a stress- and subtype-matched assay.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: This is a coverage and context warning, not evidence for or against JNK2/3 protection in dopaminergic toxin models.

summary: Dnajb4 perturbation produced no FDR-significant gene-expression response in any of 21 assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: This makes the absence of a robust acute basal transcriptomic phenotype the main result, rather than allowing isolated nominal genes to be overinterpreted as a chaperone pathway.
main_caveats: Target transcript reduction was nominal and FDR=1.0 in every cell type, so the result cannot distinguish biological buffering from inadequate CRISPRi knockdown.

direction: Dnajb4 nominally down; downstream genes not FDR-significant
summary: The clearest Dnajb4 mRNA reductions occurred in 191 MB P MY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but both were disconnected from any adjusted downstream response.
why_it_matters: The two best on-target contexts provide a stringent internal check: even where Dnajb4 moved in the expected direction, the screen did not reveal a transcriptional effector program.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: On-target changes were nominal only, and the downstream negative result is based on transcript counts rather than DNAJB4 protein abundance.

direction: Dnajb4 absent from adjusted Hsf1/Hspa8 output
summary: Basal Hsf1 and Hspa8 perturbation signatures did not place Dnajb4 in the adjusted heat-shock/chaperone output, despite Hsf1 and Hspa8 showing small downstream chaperone modules.
why_it_matters: HSP90 inhibitors and heat shock can increase DNAJB4, so Dnajb4 knockdown or basal Hsf1 perturbation should not be assumed to model indirect HSP90-inhibitor pharmacology in these neurons.
