main_caveats: Prior literature is mostly heat shock, HSP90 inhibition, or transformed-cell proteomics; the dataset is basal CRISPR perturbation in mouse brain cell classes.

summary: Dnajb4 and Dnajb6 were FDR-null, whereas Hsp90ab1, Stub1, Hsf1, and Hspa8 produced stronger but still restricted chaperone-related readouts.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates weak DNAJB-branch perturbations from more readily detected core chaperone or heat-shock regulator perturbations and cautions against treating all linked chaperone genes as interchangeable.
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations had different cell counts and target-engagement profiles; Hsp90ab1 and Stub1 FDR signals were mainly self-transcript depletion.

direction: disease mechanism not recapitulated transcriptionally in basal brain cells
summary: The brain Perturb-seq result does not reproduce the strong muscle chaperonopathy caused by complete DNAJB4 loss of function.
why_it_matters: It points toward a tissue-, client-, and timescale-specific DNAJB4 disease mechanism rather than a universal acute neuronal transcriptional stress response.
main_caveats: The disease literature concerns germline or knockout muscle loss of function, while this dataset tested partial guide-mediated perturbation in neuronal cell classes.

summary: The apparent top Dnajb4 signature-neighbor structure is confined to 308 CB GABA and is not on-target.
why_it_matters: This prevents an artifact-like correlation cluster, including Safe_target-labeled guide groups, from being promoted into a false Dnajb4 pathway.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Safe_target labels are interpreted only as dataset annotations; raw guide behavior was not available.

summary: Cox4i1 guide engagement was detectable in most profiled classes but crossed FDR only in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, with near-FDR target depletion in a small set of midbrain/hypothalamic classes.
why_it_matters: The measured phenotype is defined first by where the target RNA was actually depleted; weak forebrain target engagement argues against treating every nominal Cox4i1 profile as a biological loss-of-function state.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: This is target-transcript engagement rather than protein knockdown or cytochrome-c-oxidase activity; the dopamine class lacked a Cox4i1 profile.

summary: Cox4i1 depletion was an isolated self-transcript phenotype: no non-Cox4i1 gene passed FDR<0.05 in any of the 22 profiles.
why_it_matters: COX4I1 is a structural/regulatory complex-IV subunit, so a broad mitochondrial RNA program might be expected after strong respiratory dysfunction; its absence indicates either buffering of partial acute depletion, long protein half-life, or failure of RNA-seq DE to report the early biochemical lesion.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: A negative RNA signature does not prove normal complex-IV protein assembly, oxygen consumption, or ATP production.

summary: The engaged mouse neuronal profiles did not induce a COX4I2/HIF1/LONP1 compensation module after Cox4i1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Prior COX4-1-deficient human fibroblasts upregulated COX4-2 and hypoxia/glycolysis genes; lack of Cox4i2, Hif1a, Lonp1, Ldha, or Slc2a1 RNA induction in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA suggests that this compensation is not a universal acute brain-cell response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is cross-species and cross-cell-type; COX4I2 is very weakly expressed in these single-cell profiles, and protein-level HIF-1α stabilization cannot be excluded.

summary: Cox5a perturbation, an early complex-IV assembly neighbor of COX4, converged with Cox4i1 on an own-transcript-only outcome rather than a shared OXPHOS response.
why_it_matters: Cox5a had substantially stronger FDR-significant knockdown in several of the same midbrain classes yet also had zero non-target FDR hits, making the Cox4i1 buffering result less likely to be solely a weak-guide artifact.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only RNA endpoints were compared; Cox5a and Cox4i1 score-vector correlations were near zero because both signatures were dominated by their own target transcripts.

summary: Cox4i1 had no robust positive or negative whole-transcriptome signature neighbor in the two FDR-engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a large reusable perturbation module downstream of Cox4i1 in this dataset and makes links to unrelated top-ranked perturbations hypothesis-generating at best.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are restricted to RNA score vectors and the Cox4i1 vector itself contains almost no FDR-significant non-target structure.

summary: Partial Cox4i1 RNA depletion in postnatal mouse brain cells did not recapitulate a disease-like mitochondrial stress transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic COX4I1 deficiency causes syndromic and neurodevelopmental mitochondrial disease, but the Perturb-seq data imply that a stronger, longer, or protein-level lesion may be required before complex-IV dysfunction becomes visible as a broad RNA phenotype.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Human disease involves germline recessive variants and chronic organismal pathology; the dataset measures acute transcriptomic knockdown in mouse cell classes.

direction: Arih1 down; mixed synaptic and ubiquitin-ligase module
summary: Arih1 knockdown generated its clearest multi-gene response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where target depletion was FDR-significant and the responsive genes were enriched for synaptic, vesicle, endomembrane, and Cul3-RING-complex annotations.
why_it_matters: ARIH1 is a general ubiquitin-system enzyme, yet the dataset converts that broad biochemical role into a selective neuronal transcriptional module rather than a pan-neuronal collapse.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The strongest pathway labels use a 49-gene nominal p<0.001 set; only seven genes in this cell type reached FDR<0.05.

summary: Most Arih1 guide-defined cell types showed negative Arih1 logFC but little downstream transcriptional output, with 20/22 cell types having no FDR<0.05 genes and 155 MB Glut showing nominal target depletion without any FDR<0.05 downstream gene.
why_it_matters: The result separates transcript knockdown from a detectable state change and argues that ARIH1 dependence is strongly context-buffered despite broad brain expression.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: On-target Arih1 FDR was 0.076 in 155 MB Glut, so the buffered call relies on strong nominal depletion rather than FDR<0.05 depletion.

summary: The cullin-RING neighbor Cul3 was the nearest positive Arih1 signature neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but was only a partial phenocopy.
why_it_matters: This supports the ARIH1-CRL relationship in the responsive thalamic cells while showing that loss of the RBR priming ligase is not interchangeable with loss of a CUL3 scaffold in a transcriptomic assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Signature correlation was small and Cul3 had weaker on-target depletion than Arih1 in this cell type.

summary: 191 MB P MY GABA contained a separate, isolated Trim23 down-regulation that was the only FDR-significant Arih1 response outside the thalamic glutamatergic signal.
why_it_matters: The result nominates Trim23 as a candidate marker of a low-cell-count GABAergic Arih1 response and prevents the non-thalamic signal from being hidden by aggregate sparsity.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only 66 perturbed cells supported this stratum; Arih1 itself was nominal but not FDR-significant, and Trim23 was a single-gene hit.

summary: The basal mouse-brain Arih1 response did not activate a detectable ISG15/EIF4E2 antiviral transcriptional program, even though ARIH1 is curated in ISG15 biology.
why_it_matters: This negative result constrains interpretation of Reactome ISG15 annotations: without interferon or viral stimulation, Arih1 knockdown primarily exposed neuronal organelle/synaptic features instead of an ISG transcriptional state.
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA induction is an indirect readout of an antiviral ubiquitin-like pathway and does not test ISGylation activity.

summary: Gsk3b knockdown produced a resolved downstream transcriptome almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: GSK3B is a broadly annotated kinase, but the single robust non-target RNA response in this experiment was concentrated in a thalamic glutamatergic class, arguing that the measured post-perturbation program is strongly state dependent rather than a universal Gsk3b loss signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut also had the largest Gsk3b perturbed-cell count, so sensitivity and biology are partly confounded.

summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba and 191 MB P MY GABA cells achieved FDR-significant Gsk3b transcript repression but did not pass FDR for any non-target gene.
why_it_matters: The result separates target engagement from a detectable steady-state mRNA program and cautions that PV-related GSK3B phenotypes may be electrophysiological, post-transcriptional, later, or anatomically narrower than this pooled Pvalb cluster.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Absence of an FDR signal is not proof of no biology; the assay may miss acute kinase substrates, electrophysiology, or finer PV substates.

summary: Single Gsk3b knockdown did not reproduce the beta-catenin destruction-complex transcriptional output of Apc or Ctnnb1 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: Apc and Ctnnb1 generated strong Axin2/Lef1-associated Wnt signatures, whereas Gsk3b left Axin2 unchanged; this is consistent with GSK3A/GSK3B redundancy in Wnt control and means that this Perturb-seq contrast should not be read as pan-GSK3 or canonical Wnt activation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Gsk3a itself was not targeted in the parquet, so redundancy is inferred from the literature rather than directly tested.

summary: Within the thalamic Gsk3b signature, Tsc2 and Tsc1 were the strongest same-direction restricted-signature neighbors and Mtor was the strongest opposite neighbor.
why_it_matters: The direction of convergence matches prior biochemistry in which GSK3 activity can support TSC2-mediated repression of mTOR; it places the strongest neuronal Gsk3b RNA output closer to a TSC/mTOR module than to canonical Wnt receptor or beta-catenin responses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The convergence is strongest when restricted to the top 50 Gsk3b-responsive genes; all-gene Pearson correlations were modest.

summary: Nrbp2, Rock2, Cck, Rsrp1, Faah, Bhlhe40, Abca2, and Nap1l5 form a candidate RNA marker panel for the productive thalamic Gsk3b state.
why_it_matters: These markers are easier to track than a global pathway score and distinguish the one cell type with an FDR-resolved Gsk3b response from all other measured Gsk3b contrasts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The panel is hypothesis-generating and requires validation because it is derived from a single cell type with 108 perturbed cells.

summary: Several low-count glutamatergic groups had weak measured Gsk3b repression and no downstream FDR signal.
why_it_matters: The cortical/hippocampal non-response should be treated as under-engagement or under-power rather than evidence that GSK3B is irrelevant in those neurons.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Only the target mRNA and differential-expression table were available; protein knockdown and guide identities were not inspected here.

summary: The dataset supports a pathway- and cell-type-specific caution for GSK3B targeting rather than a simple expectation of broad Wnt activation or uniform CNS transcriptional rescue.
why_it_matters: GSK3B is chemically tractable, but the Perturb-seq readout separates a thalamic TSC/mTOR-like response, buffered Pvalb and hindbrain GABA responses, and a lack of single-Gsk3b canonical Wnt output; inhibitor studies should therefore verify cell type and pathway engagement explicitly.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: CRISPRi knockdown of mouse Gsk3b is not equivalent to acute small-molecule inhibition of both GSK3 isoforms.

summary: Atp11c perturbation produced no FDR-supported basal transcriptional phenotype in any of the 20 assayed neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: The strongest nominal genes cannot support pathway claims by themselves; the dominant dataset result is the absence of a robust scRNA-seq differential-expression signature.
cell_types: 20 Atp11c-assayed neuronal cell types
main_caveats: A negative Wilcoxon result does not exclude non-transcriptional lipid, protein-localization, or injury-conditioned phenotypes; the target transcript was also not significantly depleted.

summary: The Atp11c mRNA itself was not detectably knocked down.
why_it_matters: Weak and mixed self-transcript effects make the downstream negative result primarily a target-engagement caveat rather than proof that neurons are biologically insensitive to ATP11C loss.
cell_types: 20 Atp11c-assayed neuronal cell types
main_caveats: mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for guide cutting or protein loss, but no cell type showed a convincing Atp11c transcript drop.

summary: Within the assayed P4-ATPase family, Atp9a showed strong recurrent self-depletion whereas Atp11c and Atp8a2 did not.
why_it_matters: The Atp11c null result should not be blamed on a universal inability to perturb membrane P4-ATPases in this experiment; guide or transcript-specific factors are more likely.
cell_types: 20 Atp11c-assayed neuronal cell types
main_caveats: This is a transcript-level comparator analysis; Atp9a is a related P4-ATPase but is not the ATP11C-TMEM30A plasma-membrane flippase itself.

summary: Atp11c targeting did not trigger a consistent transcriptional response of the TMEM30/P4-ATPase flippase module.
why_it_matters: ATP11C function depends on membrane lipid flipping with accessory subunits, but this dataset does not show compensatory mRNA regulation of nearby flippases or Tmem30a.
cell_types: 20 Atp11c-assayed neuronal cell types
main_caveats: The assay measured steady-state mRNA after weak Atp11c engagement and cannot test ATP11C-TMEM30A protein localization, flippase activity, or phosphatidylserine exposure directly.

summary: Neuronal ATP11C-preserving hypotheses require injury and lipid-readout validation; basal Atp11c knockdown did not model that state.
why_it_matters: A mouse intracerebral-hemorrhage study links ATP11C downregulation to non-apoptotic neuronal phosphatidylserine exposure and reports benefit from neuronal ATP11C overexpression, but this Perturb-seq profile lacks target engagement and microglial engulfment context.
cell_types: 20 Atp11c-assayed neuronal cell types
main_caveats: The ICH evidence is injury-specific and uses phosphatidylserine exposure and neuron-microglia phenotypes; the current screen measured basal neuronal scRNA profiles.

summary: The Htr3a perturbation did not produce measurable Htr3a mRNA depletion in any tested cell type.
why_it_matters: The target-engagement failure is the dominant constraint on interpretation: downstream nulls should not be read as proof that 5-HT3A is dispensable.
main_caveats: DE rows report rank statistics, not absolute Htr3a UMI counts; low receptor expression can make logFC unstable, so the Wilcoxon score and adjusted p value are more informative.

summary: Across the Htr3a panel, the basal transcriptome was essentially silent: no gene reached FDR 0.20, and the best nominal rows did not survive correction.
why_it_matters: There was no cell-type-wide RNA module on which to build a pathway activation or repression model for Htr3a.
main_caveats: True electrophysiological or stimulus-dependent phenotypes could be missed by an unstimulated steady-state transcriptomic perturbation assay.

summary: The expected cortical CGE interneuron compartment did not rescue the Htr3a signal in the coarse 046 CTX-CGE GABA class.
why_it_matters: Prior work localizes functional 5-HT3A signaling to specialized VIP/CCK and NPY/neurogliaform cortical interneurons; the dataset suggests that broad cell classes plus weak knockdown were insufficient to resolve that biology.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The dataset uses broad transcriptomic classes and does not isolate VIP, CCK, or NPY/neurogliaform subtypes; target engagement was also weak in CTX-CGE cells.

summary: Htr3a and the receptor subunit Htr3b showed no shared Perturb-seq signature, and the isolated Htr3b Myadm hit should remain exploratory.
why_it_matters: Because 5-HT3A and 5-HT3B can assemble into the same receptor family, this prevents over-interpreting a single Htr3b FDR hit as a reproducible 5-HT3 transcriptomic program.
main_caveats: Both subunit perturbations lacked measured target-transcript depletion, and the Htr3b adjusted hit occurred in only one 40-cell hippocampal excitatory contrast.

summary: The Htr3a null signature is pathway-uncoupled from clinical 5-HT3 antagonist pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Setrons acutely block HTR3A-containing cation channels; this dataset lacks serotonin challenge or electrophysiological readouts, so it should not be used to infer antiemetic or IBS drug-response direction.
main_caveats: The conclusion applies only to basal mouse-brain CRISPRi transcriptomes; it does not test acute receptor currents, peripheral vagal circuits, human colon, emesis, or drug blockade.

summary: Kctd8 produced no FDR-supported target-transcript depletion in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset readout does not establish efficient Kctd8 mRNA loss, so downstream null phenotypes must be interpreted as either biological buffering or weak detectable engagement rather than as definitive loss-of-function silence.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measures target mRNA, not protein; sparse transcripts can yield large logFC values with non-significant p values.

summary: Kctd8 perturbation generated a globally flat steady-state RNA response.
why_it_matters: Across all 371,818 Kctd8 gene-by-cell-class tests, no gene reached FDR<0.05 and the nominal hit rate was below the nominal 5% threshold, consistent with a strongly buffered or weakly engaged perturbation.
main_caveats: Negative RNA output cannot exclude altered synaptic physiology or protein-complex function.

summary: The only near-FDR signal was an exploratory Rpgr increase in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: Any Kctd8 cell-type hypothesis in this dataset is concentrated in corticofugal L5 extratelencephalic neurons, but it rests on one FDR 0.0809 gene and does not form a pathway-level program.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Rpgr did not cross FDR 0.05; Kctd8 itself was only nominal in this cell class; the link to GABAB biology is not established.

summary: Measured GABAB-GIRK module transcripts did not compensate detectably after Kctd8 perturbation.
why_it_matters: KCTD8 is a GABAB auxiliary subunit, so transcriptional feedback onto Gabbr1, Gabbr2, Kctd16, Gnb1 or Kcnj6 would have suggested receptor-level homeostasis; the matrix instead shows no FDR-supported regulation of these module components.
main_caveats: The inference is restricted to assayed mRNAs; Kctd12 and Kctd12b were not perturbation targets, and receptor localization or GIRK currents were not measured.

summary: Kctd8 signatures were orthogonal to related GABAB, KCTD, G protein and GIRK perturbations.
why_it_matters: Although KCTD8, KCTD16, GABBR1/GABBR2, GNB1 and KCNJ6 lie in the same inhibitory GPCR signaling axis, same-cell-type RNA signatures did not converge, arguing against using Kctd8 transcriptomic neighbors as a proxy for acute GABAB receptor signaling.
main_caveats: Correlations use weak Kctd8 score vectors; the strongest Gabbr1/Gabbr2 effects were their own target rows rather than broad downstream programs.

summary: Known KCTD8 biology points to localized electrophysiological roles that this broad nuclear RNA assay is poorly positioned to detect.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse work places KCTD8 in GABAB receptor kinetics and axonal receptor expression, including a habenula cholinergic circuit; the absence of a robust broad-cell-class RNA program suggests follow-up should measure receptor localization or GABAB/GIRK currents in matched circuits rather than expect a large transcriptional signature.
main_caveats: The habenula cholinergic context is more specific than the broad cell classes in this dataset; Kctd12 was not available as a perturbation comparator.

summary: Cep164 showed weak target-transcript engagement and no FDR < 0.05 downstream response in any of 23 mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: CEP164 loss is expected to perturb basal-body ciliogenesis, so the absence of a corrected transcriptomic response should be interpreted primarily as a weak or buffered Perturb-seq state rather than as a strong negative genetic result.
main_caveats: Endogenous mRNA was barely changed; protein depletion at mother centrioles was not measured; no Cep164 row reached FDR < 0.05.

summary: 191 MB P MY GABA contained the strongest nominal Cep164 signature, led by decreased Ypel4, Vgf, Dnaja2, Aftph, Eri3, Twsg1, and Khdrbs1 plus increased mt-Nd3.
why_it_matters: These genes preserve the most responsive measured Cep164 context for follow-up, but they should be treated as exploratory markers because even the top row was only near-FDR and the genes did not form a broad recurrent module.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The strongest row had FDR 0.092, Vgf had FDR 0.307, and same-direction ciliary-comparator support for Vgf was nominal with FDR 1.0.

summary: Cep164 did not phenocopy the distal-appendage neighbors Cep83 and Sclt1 in restricted top-score signatures.
why_it_matters: CEP83, SCLT1, and CEP164 are in one ordered distal-appendage assembly pathway, so lack of transcriptional agreement warns against using the weak Cep164 signature as a proxy for distal-appendage loss.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Cep164 itself was weakly engaged; the Sclt1 agreement in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut was isolated; restricted correlations use 100 selected genes per cell type.

summary: Other ciliary and ciliopathy-associated perturbations in the same panel produced stronger corrected signals than Cep164 but did not converge on the Cep164 score signature.
why_it_matters: The weak Cep164 result is not merely because the panel cannot detect any ciliary perturbation; it is target and context specific, refining how human CEP164 ciliopathy genetics should be mapped onto this neuronal Perturb-seq readout.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparator rows measure different perturbations and cell counts; stronger FDR rows were not necessarily in the same cell types as Cep164's near-FDR Ypel4 row.

summary: No positive or inverse whole-panel signature neighbor was strong enough to nominate a Cep164 modifier or rescue direction.
why_it_matters: CEP164 is a structural ciliogenesis factor, and the dataset did not reveal a robust anti-correlated perturbation that could be interpreted as transcriptomic suppression of the measured Cep164 state.
main_caveats: The neighbor scan was restricted to Cep164 top-100 score genes per cell type and is appropriate for detecting similarity, not for proving genetic rescue.

summary: Ifngr1 did not show convincing on-target transcript knockdown or any FDR-significant downstream response in the cell classes where it was tested.
why_it_matters: This prevents interpreting the dataset as a clean IFNGR1 loss-of-function experiment and makes FDR-negative pathway signals hypothesis-generating.
main_caveats: The absence of mRNA loss may reflect low basal Ifngr1 expression, inefficient perturbation, low guide-cell counts, or discordance between RNA and receptor-protein loss.

summary: A selected IFNγ/STAT1/MHC-I module was coherently but nominally down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA after Ifngr1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The direction matches loss of tonic IFNGR-to-STAT1 signaling and nominates a small antigen-presentation module as the most biologically interpretable Ifngr1 signal.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: All module rows in Ifngr1 contrasts were FDR=1.0; the module was selected from prior knowledge rather than discovered by unbiased enrichment.

summary: Ifngr2 and Stat1 perturbations anchor the 151/191 STAT1-MHC signal, but Ifngr1 does not globally phenocopy either pathway neighbor.
why_it_matters: The receptor-subunit and downstream-transcription-factor comparison separates a restricted canonical module from broad, likely noisy Ifngr1 signatures.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Ifngr1 itself lacked confirmed knockdown, so weak correlation cannot be taken as proof that IFNGR1 and IFNGR2 have different biology.

summary: The dataset only partially samples IFNγ-responsive neuronal contexts: nominal Ifngr1 pathway movement is strongest outside cortical IT classes, and the 215 MB Dopa class lacks an Ifngr1 result.
why_it_matters: This limits direct comparison with ventral-midbrain dopamine-neuron IFNγ studies and argues that the screen refines rather than contradicts published neuronal cytokine-response work.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Cell classes are broad, the assay lacked IFNγ stimulation, and Ifngr1 was not analyzable in the dopaminergic class.

summary: Top restricted Ifngr1 signature neighbors were dominated by a 308 CB GABA pattern involving unrelated perturbations and Safe_target guide sets rather than IFN-pathway genes.
why_it_matters: The neighbor result is a guardrail: CB GABA top genes should not be overread as a specific IFNGR1 mechanism.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to the top 200 Ifngr1 genes; no claim is made that the unrelated neighbors are mechanistically connected to IFNGR1.

summary: The basal neuronal Ifngr1 negative result should not be used as evidence that IFNγ/STAT1 blockade is inert in inflamed brain or in IFNγ-linked disease settings.
why_it_matters: IFNGR1 is an upstream receptor in a clinically important immune pathway, while this experiment had weak Ifngr1 engagement and no cytokine challenge or glial compartment.
main_caveats: This is a scope warning rather than a measured drug response; the perturbation dataset did not assay pharmacologic JAK or IFNGR inhibition.

summary: Bptf-targeting perturbation produced a sharply cell-type-skewed transcriptomic phenotype, with thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, midbrain glutamatergic, and pontine/medullary GABA neurons accounting for most FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: BPTF is a general chromatin reader/remodeler subunit, yet the measurable brain response was not uniform; discrete neuronal classes were far more permissive to downstream transcriptional change.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The strongest cells also had moderate to high recovered Bptf-cell counts, and the Bptf transcript itself was not FDR-depleted.

summary: A recurrent positive Zcwpw2/Grk4 axis marked Bptf responses across thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, Pvalb, and hindbrain classes.
why_it_matters: Zcwpw2 was repeatedly the top or near-top induced gene, making it a candidate transcriptional sentinel for Bptf perturbation even where only a handful of genes passed FDR.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The module is defined by recurrence in this dataset, not by a known BPTF-bound pathway; no direct Zcwpw2/Grk4 BPTF literature was used.

summary: Upper-layer cortical Bptf signatures were sparse and Gaa-centered rather than dominated by the Zcwpw2/Resp18/Abhd14b module seen in thalamic and midbrain classes.
why_it_matters: The cortical response was not simply a weaker copy of the thalamic program, suggesting that Bptf-dependent regulation resolves into different effector genes by neuronal context.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Each cortical class had only two FDR-significant genes, so this is a restricted-signature result.

summary: More than half of the assayed Bptf cell classes lacked any FDR-significant downstream gene despite some having 46-67 recovered perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: The absence of strong responses in several forebrain and interneuron classes prevents interpreting Bptf as a uniformly active transcriptional dependency in the measured atlas.
comparators: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|053 Sst Gaba|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Weak measured Bptf transcript depletion means these null signatures cannot be distinguished from poor target engagement or inadequate power for small effects.

summary: The Bptf signature diverged from Chd4, another chromatin-remodeling perturbation, with Chd4 scoring as the strongest restricted negative neighbor in both 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The result argues against collapsing chromatin remodelers into one expected transcriptomic direction: NURF-linked Bptf and NuRD-linked Chd4 can drive opposing expression on the genes most diagnostic of Bptf perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The opposition was computed on Bptf-significant genes and was strongest by projection; many individual Chd4 gene effects were nominal or not FDR-significant.

summary: Human BPTF haploinsufficiency is a neurodevelopmental disorder mechanism, but the mouse Perturb-seq response localized most strongly to selected differentiated thalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain neurons rather than to all cortical classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset suggests a neuron-class-specific transcriptional vulnerability that could refine how BPTF dosage is modeled beyond progenitor and early embryonic contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Disease references concern human germline haploinsufficiency and developmental model systems; the dataset assayed acute perturbations in mouse neuronal classes.

summary: Because BPTF is being pursued as a cancer-relevant bromodomain/PHD target, the neuronal Zcwpw2/Resp18/Abhd14b responses nominate thalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain expression programs to monitor in BPTF-inhibitor safety studies.
why_it_matters: The strongest transcriptomic effects occurred in brain neurons, so even an oncology-directed BPTF inhibitor may need counterscreens for neuronal transcriptional liabilities.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: No BPTF inhibitor was tested here, the perturbation was genetic, and the measured Bptf transcript engagement was weak.

summary: Ica1 guide assignment produced only weak Ica1 mRNA reduction and no FDR-resolved downstream transcriptomic response in any profiled neuronal class.
why_it_matters: This makes the main phenotype a buffered or low-engagement perturbation rather than a conventional knockdown signature; downstream nominal genes should be interpreted as hypotheses.
main_caveats: RNA on-target effects were small and adjusted p values for the target transcript were 1.0, so the assay may understate ICA1 protein perturbation or may reflect inefficient guide engagement.

summary: The largest nominal Ica1 signatures were cell-class-specific but not consistently aligned with direct target engagement.
why_it_matters: 155 MB Glut showed the lowest dataset FDR together with nominal Ica1 reduction, whereas 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut had the most nominal p<0.01 genes despite little measured Ica1 reduction; apparent cell specificity therefore cannot be separated from engagement variability.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All cited downstream genes are nominal because no row passed FDR<0.20; the 008 class has weak on-target support.

summary: Ica1 did not converge transcriptionally with assayed vesicle, endocytic or synaptic-receptor perturbations, and no close positive or negative whole-signature neighbor was detected.
why_it_matters: ICA69 is a BAR-domain PICK1 partner in secretory-vesicle and AMPAR trafficking, but this dataset does not show that basal Ica1 perturbation launches the same mRNA program as available synaptic-vesicle pathway neighbors.
main_caveats: Pick1 and Ica1l were absent from the perturbation panel, so the most direct complex and paralog comparisons were unavailable; correlation values are signature-level and weak.

summary: The basal transcriptomic null refines the known neuronal ICA69 mechanism toward post-transcriptional or activity-gated trafficking rather than a large resting-state mRNA program.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse work found a selective LTP and learning phenotype despite normal basal CA1 AMPAR currents and dendrite architecture; the Perturb-seq result is consistent with a phenotype that may emerge during synaptic activity or protein trafficking rather than in resting single-cell RNA profiles.
main_caveats: The dataset did not stimulate neurons or measure AMPAR localization, LTP, secretion, or ICA69 protein abundance.

summary: If ICA1 is pursued through Alzheimer- or secretion-linked biology, basal neuronal mRNA signatures are likely to be a low-sensitivity efficacy readout.
why_it_matters: The strongest Perturb-seq effects were nominal and uncoupled from a repeated module, whereas the literature implicates ICA1 in APP/PICK1/PKCα and insulin-granule trafficking; functional protein-processing, membrane-trafficking and endocrine assays are likely to be more decisive than broad unstimulated transcriptomics.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: The Alzheimer citation used disease-model systems rather than the cell classes in this Perturb-seq dataset, and no drug perturbation or APP-processing assay was performed here.

summary: Pnpt1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant target-transcript depletion in any measured mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: The primary interpretation of the Pnpt1 experiment is weak target engagement, which limits mechanistic claims from all downstream null results.
main_caveats: Target mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for coding loss after some CRISPR modalities.

summary: No Pnpt1 cell class had an FDR-significant downstream DE signature.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not identify a Pnpt1-sensitive neuronal population or a recurrent response module.
main_caveats: Cell counts were modest and the lack of target depletion prevents distinguishing true buffering from under-perturbation.

summary: The mitochondrial RNA/OXPHOS arm expected from PNPT1 biology was not detectably engaged in the measured transcriptome.
why_it_matters: PNPT1 disease mechanisms involve mitochondrial RNA import, processing, and degradation, but the assayed mitochondrial-encoded mRNAs showed no significant response.
main_caveats: Single-cell RNA-seq does not directly assay mitochondrial antisense RNAs or imported tRNAs, and Pnpt1 itself was not detectably depleted.

summary: Pnpt1 perturbation did not induce the MDA5/type-I-interferon sentinel genes that efficient PNPase loss can activate through mitochondrial dsRNA leakage.
why_it_matters: This prevents interpreting the dataset as evidence for PNPT1-driven antiviral signaling in the assayed neurons.
main_caveats: The literature used efficient loss or patient material, whereas this dataset has weak target engagement and neuronal cell-type context.

summary: Available related RNA-processing and innate-immune perturbations did not converge with the weak Pnpt1 signature, and direct mtEXO comparators were absent from the library.
why_it_matters: The cross-perturbation audit found no hidden phenotype that would rescue biological interpretation of the Pnpt1 null profile.
main_caveats: The most relevant direct comparator, Supv3l1, was not perturbed; correlations with a nearly null Pnpt1 vector are intrinsically low-confidence.

summary: The Perturb-seq null result should not be treated as neuronal safety evidence for PNPT1 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Human hypomorphic or biallelic PNPT1 variants cause mitochondrial disease, and efficient mtEXO loss can trigger dsRNA stress; this experiment did not achieve a comparable loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: This is a warning about interpretation, not a direct drug-toxicity measurement.

summary: Gabra3 target-transcript depletion was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, with no nominally significant self-depletion in the other 17 assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: The interpretable Gabra3 perturbation is restricted to two subcortical classes, preventing broad conclusions about cortical, hippocampal, or cerebellar GABA-A alpha3 biology from this dataset.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The two best on-target rows remained above 5% FDR, and the cell labels are broader than the nuclei emphasized in alpha3 histology studies.

summary: Gabra3 depletion produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome and no corrected transcriptional compensation among measured GABA receptor, GABA synthesis, GABA transport, gephyrin, or collybistin genes.
why_it_matters: Loss of one receptor alpha subunit appears buffered at the mRNA level, so the primary cell-autonomous consequences are more likely to be channel assembly, synaptic localization, or conductance changes than a large transcriptional feedback response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The conclusion is transcriptomic only; it does not test receptor localization, chloride currents, or synaptic inhibition.

summary: Gabra3 signatures were weakly correlated with related GABA-A receptor subunit perturbations even in shared cell types, and Gabrg2 produced a midbrain Vgf response absent after Gabra3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Complex membership did not translate into transcriptomic interchangeability; alpha3, gamma2, and beta2 perturbations should be interpreted as subunit-specific rather than as one generic GABA-A receptor signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are based on weak transcriptomic signatures; they do not measure shared effects on GABA currents.

summary: Gabra3 had no strong positive or negative global transcriptomic signature neighbor across the perturbation collection.
why_it_matters: Top-neighbor analyses should not be used to infer a Gabra3 pathway here; the top correlations were near zero and even included safe-target controls.
main_caveats: The negative neighbor result is expected for a perturbation with no corrected downstream expression program.

summary: The near-silent mRNA response suggests that GABRA3 epilepsy and circuit phenotypes can be driven by receptor or synaptic physiology rather than by large autonomous transcriptional remodeling.
why_it_matters: This prevents a false-negative interpretation: the Perturb-seq result is compatible with known GABRA3 functional genetics if the pathogenic layer is channel assembly, gephyrin clustering, inhibitory current amplitude, or circuit oscillation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The assayed clusters are not the thalamic reticular nucleus itself, and no human variant was modeled.

summary: Druggability of alpha3-containing GABA-A receptors does not imply an easily monitored Gabra3 transcriptional biomarker in all target cells.
why_it_matters: Alpha3-positive allosteric modulators and alpha3 antagonism are both biologically plausible intervention directions, but this dataset implies that target engagement may need electrophysiological, protein-localization, or spatial biomarkers rather than a GABA-pathway mRNA score.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Therapeutic inference is indirect; the perturbation is genetic, the cell classes are mouse neuronal clusters, and the data do not report pharmacologic modulation.

summary: Met perturbation was a genome-wide negative result: neither the Met transcript nor any downstream gene reached even FDR<=0.25 in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: This prevents treating isolated nominal genes as a robust MET loss-of-function program and makes target engagement the central interpretive limitation.
main_caveats: FDR-level absence is clear, but it could reflect weak guide editing, low Met expression, or an assay time point that misses MET signaling rather than true dispensability.

summary: The strongest Met responses were cell-type-restricted and nominal-only rather than a recurrent cortical, hippocampal, thalamic, or GABAergic module.
why_it_matters: The top Pink1, Kdm4a, Zfp365, and Ift172 signals should be used as hypothesis seeds only, not pathway-defining biomarkers.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: All highlighted single-gene effects failed FDR correction, and the most recurrent nominal genes changed with mixed signs.

summary: Met did not phenocopy active receptor-tyrosine-kinase/PI3K perturbations in the same cell-type panel.
why_it_matters: Canonical MET signals feed into GRB2/GAB1-PI3K/RAS/STAT branches, yet measured pathway transcripts were not FDR-regulated by Met and Met score vectors had only weak correlations with Pik3cb, Nrg1, Nrg3, Pten, or any other perturbation; in contrast, Pten, Nrg3, Erbb4, Fgfr1, Mapk1, Mtor, and Nrg1 produced significant DE in overlapping cell types.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and perturbation-based, not an HGF stimulation or phosphoproteomic assay; weak Met target engagement can explain part of the uncoupling.

summary: The screen refines neurodevelopmental MET models by showing little acute cell-autonomous RNA output in the profiled brain classes.
why_it_matters: Published mouse work links MET to time-delimited forebrain dendritic growth, synapse maturation, plasticity, and learning, while the dataset shows no robust immediate mRNA program; MET biology may therefore depend on developmental timing, ligand availability, phosphorylation, morphology, or circuit readouts that this CRISPR/scRNA endpoint does not capture.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The biological contexts are only partially matched: the cited studies use developmental or conditional mouse models and structural/electrophysiological phenotypes, whereas this dataset measures acute RNA responses in dissociated cells.

summary: The Met null signature should not be read as evidence that MET inhibition is transcriptionally inert or CNS-safe.
why_it_matters: MET is a druggable HGF receptor with clinical inhibitors, and HGF/MET has reported neurotrophic and neuroprotective roles; the dataset instead reports an under-engaged mRNA perturbation with no FDR-significant markers.
main_caveats: No drug exposure, kinase inhibition, HGF agonism, or injury/neurodegeneration model was tested in the parquet dataset.

summary: Ddx3x loss produced a sharply restricted FDR-resolved transcriptomic response, concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut rather than across all measured neurons.
why_it_matters: DDX3X is a core RNA helicase, so a pan-neuronal response could have been expected; the dataset instead points to high state or cell-type dependence, with the caveat that the most responsive classes were also the best powered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: 151 and 155 had the two largest Ddx3x perturbed-cell counts, so power contributes to the apparent selectivity.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ddx3x knockdown reproducibly lowered a junctional/NMDA-adjacent gene set headed by Grin2b, Synpo2 and Plekhg1.
why_it_matters: The affected genes make the strongest on-target class look synaptic and cell-junctional, extending DDX3X neurodevelopmental literature beyond neural-progenitor cell cycle and bulk translation mechanisms to a mature glutamatergic-state hypothesis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only four genes in this module passed 5% FDR under Ddx3x; several cell-junction and Wnt-neighbor genes are nominal and should be treated as a focused hypothesis.

summary: 155 MB Glut showed the single strongest downstream change, Thy1 repression, together with induction of Inha, Ppp2r5b and Bicd2 despite only nominal target-transcript FDR support.
why_it_matters: This separates a midbrain glutamatergic phenotypic marker set from the thalamic Grin2b/Synpo2 program and flags Thy1 as a sensitive reporter for this cell class.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The endogenous Ddx3x row was nominally reduced but FDR=0.223, so the strong Thy1 response should be interpreted as downstream signature evidence rather than the cleanest on-target class.

summary: A nominal recurrent module, especially Bicd2 induction and Ddx5 induction, appeared in several posterior or GABAergic classes even when per-class FDR was weak.
why_it_matters: Ddx5 is a STRING functional partner of DDX3X, so recurrent Ddx5 up-regulation is a plausible but exploratory RNA-helicase compensation marker; Bicd2 was the most recurrent nominal positive gene and may mark a broader Ddx3x-stress response.

summary: Pparg perturbation produced no FDR-controlled differential-expression signature in the assayed neuronal classes.

main_caveats: Rb1 was assayed in only 11 of 23 cell types, and the contrast is based on transcriptomic perturbation outputs rather than direct measurement of RB phosphorylation or CDK activity.

summary: Cdkn2a did not converge with the available p53, E2F1/E2F5, or MYC-family neighbors.
why_it_matters: The absence of FDR < 0.05 signatures for Trp53, E2f1, E2f5, Myc, and Mycn, together with very low correlations to Cdkn2a, argues that the Cdkn2a null is not hiding a strong ARF-p53 or MYC/E2F-like program.
main_caveats: Comparator guide efficacy was not independently verified; Mycn had weak FDR < 0.10 rows in 053 Sst Gaba but no FDR < 0.05 rows.

summary: Mouse neural progenitor literature on p16Ink4a/p19Arf does not translate into a broad mature-neuron Cdkn2a transcriptional phenotype in this dataset.
why_it_matters: This keeps two observations compatible: Cdkn2a-family programs can regulate proliferative neural stem or progenitor compartments, while acute Cdkn2a perturbation in the sampled differentiated brain classes remains buffered or unmeasured.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq table does not include a matched adult neural stem-cell compartment, so the finding is a context refinement rather than a direct contradiction.

summary: Lst1 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut was the only Cdkn2a row below FDR 0.10, but it did not reach FDR 0.05.
why_it_matters: Preserving this lone near-threshold hit prevents it from being overinterpreted as a pathway while marking it as a possible validation target or QC flag.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Single cell type, FDR = 0.091549, no FDR < 0.05 Cdkn2a genes, and no recurrence across the other 22 classes.

summary: Dhdds perturbation activated an ER unfolded-protein and chaperone program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The dominant downstream program matches the known requirement for the DHDDS:NUS1 complex in dolichol-phosphate synthesis for ER glycosylation, connecting the Perturb-seq phenotype to the expected biochemical lesion.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset measured mRNA, not Dol-P pools, N-glycans, or DHDDS protein; Dhdds self-transcript knockdown was only nominal after multiple testing.

summary: Robust Dhdds responses were concentrated in two glutamatergic populations while most tested neuronal classes had zero corrected hits.
why_it_matters: This turns a broadly required ER-glycosylation factor into a context-specific vulnerability in the mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Only two cell types had high-confidence signatures; the apparent 215 MB Dopa recurrence was based on 22 perturbed cells and one significant gene.

summary: Sensitive 151 TH neurons combined ER-stress induction with a CHOP/amino-acid-stress branch and loss of Kcnc2/Pcp4/Scg5/GABA-receptor and glutamate-receptor transcripts.
why_it_matters: Chac1, Sesn2, Slc7a5, Asns, Ddit3, Kcnc2, Pcp4, and Scg5 nominate a thalamic Dhdds stress-state marker panel that is more specific than generic Hspa5 induction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The neuronal-output interpretation is based on transcript markers; electrophysiology and secretion were not measured.

summary: Dhdds signatures were positively related to perturbations of Gfpt1, Hspa9, Atp2a2, Hspa5, proteasome, and ER trafficking genes, while opposing full-transcriptome neighbors were weak.
why_it_matters: The sensitive-cell Dhdds state sits inside a broader ER and secretory homeostasis module rather than representing an isolated single-enzyme artifact.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation does not prove identical primary lesions; negative-neighbor results were weak and exploratory.

summary: Other assayed glycosylation-related perturbations failed to phenocopy Dhdds in the two responsive glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: DHDDS was the visible glycosylation-route liability in this library, implying either position-specific biology or more effective target engagement rather than a generic response to every glycosylation gene perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The direct DHDDS partner Nus1 and the nearest dolichol genes Dolk and Srd5a3 were not assayed; self-knockdown of comparators differed from Dhdds and limits causal interpretation.

summary: Dhdds loss in mouse brain neurons produced stress signatures in the same loss-of-function direction implicated by human DHDDS/NUS1 neurologic disease genetics.
why_it_matters: The combined evidence cautions against direct DHDDS inhibition in the CNS and points rescue strategies toward restoring dolichol or ER glycosylation capacity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is mouse and transcriptional; human disease variants include diverse missense mechanisms and are not modeled allele-specifically here.

summary: Irf1 perturbation did not measurably reduce the Irf1 transcript in any of the 23 profiled cell types.
why_it_matters: Without transcript-level target engagement, downstream null effects cannot be interpreted as proof that IRF1 is dispensable.
main_caveats: A Wilcoxon mRNA row cannot distinguish failed editing from low basal Irf1 expression or dropout.

summary: Irf1 produced no FDR<0.05 downstream gene in any cell type, even in the four contrasts with at least 112 perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: The primary phenotype is a dataset-wide lack of corrected transcriptomic response, not a hidden strong cell-type-specific module.
main_caveats: The negative result is conditional on weak Irf1 target engagement and limited power in low-count classes.

summary: Canonical IFN/IRF1 effector genes were not coordinately downregulated after Irf1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: IRF1 is expected to activate many IFN-inducible host-defense, antigen-presentation, and apoptotic genes, so their uniform FDR=1.0 argues that the basal neuronal signatures do not report an active IRF1-to-ISG axis.
main_caveats: The mismatch is not a clean mechanistic contradiction because Irf1 itself was not significantly depleted.

summary: The interferon/TLR/IRF neighborhood was also weakly responsive across the atlas, with only six corrected rows among 399 related target-cell contrasts.
why_it_matters: The Irf1 null is embedded in a broader basal quiescence of IFN-linked perturbations rather than standing out as a lone paradox within a strongly active interferon circuit.
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation contrasts are transcriptomic and several related targets also lacked on-target validation.

summary: 308 CB GABA was the only cell type with a near-threshold Irf1-associated gene, but the signal was a singleton rather than a coherent IFN module.
why_it_matters: This preserves the strongest scalar Irf1 result while preventing Zfp687 or Ly6e from being overinterpreted as validated IRF1 biomarkers.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Zfp687 missed FDR 0.05, Ly6e and B2m were nominal only, and no strong all-gene signature neighbor supported the effect.

summary: The atlas does not support a strong basal neuronal benefit of suppressing Irf1 and should not be extrapolated to activated glial IFN states.
why_it_matters: IRF1 and IFN signaling are implicated in microglial inflammatory biology, but those cell states were not the responsive context represented by this perturbation dataset.
main_caveats: This is an inference from cell-type coverage and negative neuronal signatures; no microglial Irf1 perturbation was measured in the dataset.

summary: Notch2 targeting produced no FDR-supported transcriptional phenotype in any assayed neuronal class, and the target transcript itself did not show measurable depletion.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset result is a robust negative at the differential-expression layer, but it is also a target-engagement warning: downstream silence cannot be interpreted as proof that Notch2 is dispensable if Notch2 RNA was not detectably perturbed.
main_caveats: Direct guides, editing efficiency, and raw baseline Notch2 expression were not available; a coding-disruptive perturbation could also fail to lower RNA abundance.

summary: Canonical Notch output genes remained uncoupled from Notch2 perturbation: Hes1, Hes5, Hey1, Hey2, Heyl, and Nrarp were FDR=1.0 in every Notch2 signature.
why_it_matters: HES/HEY-family repression or activation would be the clearest transcriptomic sign of altered NICD-RBPJ-MAML signaling; its absence argues that the perturbation did not reach active canonical Notch signaling in these cells.
main_caveats: Because on-target Notch2 RNA was not reduced, the result shows absent pathway readout in the experiment rather than genetically proven pathway inactivity.

summary: A broader assayed Notch module was transcriptionally sparse: Notch1, Notch3, Notch4, Dll1, Adam10, Psen1, and Fbxw7 perturbations produced only three FDR<0.05 genes across 140 target-cell-type signatures.
why_it_matters: The Notch2 null signature was not an isolated outlier among pathway neighbors; receptor, ligand, receptor-cleavage, and FBXW7-associated perturbations were all muted in the annotated neuronal classes.
main_caveats: Fbxw7 is pleiotropic, Adam10 and Psen1 had fewer assayed and lower-count signatures, and the isolated related-target hits do not establish direct Notch regulation.

summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq context failed to reproduce the strong Notch2 dependence reported for adult mouse neural stem-cell quiescence.
why_it_matters: Adult V-SVZ and dentate-gyrus studies place Notch2 upstream of NSC quiescence, whereas the present Glut/GABA/Dopa neuronal classes showed no genome-wide, HES/HEY, or receptor-ligand response; mature neuronal classes are therefore a poor proxy for that stem-cell-niche phenotype.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay ventricular-subventricular-zone or dentate-gyrus neural stem cells directly, and target engagement was not detected.

summary: The negative neuronal Notch2 signature should not be used to de-risk systemic NOTCH2 or pan-Notch interventions.
why_it_matters: Human NOTCH2 disorders and Open Targets disease evidence are dominated by developmental, skeletal, renal, hepatic, and cancer contexts, while the assay here was transcriptionally silent in neuronal classes and did not test ligand-rich non-neuronal niches.
main_caveats: This is a clinical extrapolation from absence of a neuronal transcriptomic effect; no drug treatment or systemic tissue was assayed.

summary: Oprm1 perturbation was transcriptionally silent at FDR scale and did not measurably deplete the Oprm1 transcript in any sampled cell class.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset signal is absence of a validated cell-autonomous RNA response, so downstream nominal hits should not be interpreted as a strong MOR loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: A silent transcriptome can reflect true buffering, low basal Oprm1 expression, or ineffective guide target engagement; the perturbation was assayed without opioid ligand stimulation or electrophysiology.

summary: The apparent Oprm1 response was not concentrated in a validated cell type; the best MH-LH thalamic and CNU-HYa/HY-MM hypothalamic signals were only nominal and the highest-cell-count thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic groups still had no FDR hits.
why_it_matters: This argues against assigning an Oprm1-responsive neuronal subclass from this screen, even though a few scalar scores were larger in small cell groups.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Top genes in 145 and 110 were tested in only 29 and 23 perturbed cells, respectively, and none passed pvals_adj < 0.05.

summary: Opioid receptor perturbations were uniformly buffered, whereas the shared downstream G-protein components Gnao1 and Gnb1 produced a small number of FDR-significant hits including on-target depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The contrast localizes detectable transcriptional liability to core Gi/Go signaling components rather than to individual opioid GPCRs under this screening condition.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The Gnao1/Gnb1 effects were sparse and do not prove that opioid receptors feed those transcriptional changes in the same cells.

summary: Oprm1 had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor, including near-zero correlations with opioid receptor paralogs and Gi/Go-cAMP pathway neighbors.
why_it_matters: Shared receptor family membership or pathway annotation did not translate into interchangeable single-cell loss-of-function signatures; the Oprm1 vector is effectively noise-like in this matrix.
main_caveats: Correlations used Wilcoxon score vectors rather than raw single-cell expression and weak Oprm1 engagement limits mechanistic interpretation.

summary: The silent Oprm1 Perturb-seq transcriptome should not be read as MOR dispensability for opioid analgesia, reward, dependence, or antagonist/partial-agonist therapy.
why_it_matters: MOR is a ligand-regulated membrane receptor with acute second-messenger, channel, and circuit effects; a no-ligand transcriptional Perturb-seq endpoint is poorly matched to the pharmacology that makes OPRM1 druggable.
main_caveats: This warning is inferential: the dataset did not test morphine, fentanyl, naloxone, buprenorphine, withdrawal, or circuit-level physiology.

summary: Kctd16 perturbation produced no FDR-resolved transcriptomic response in any of the 20 measured neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The central dataset result is a robust null at adjusted significance; any pathway or cell-type interpretation of Kctd16 must be treated as underpowered or post-transcriptional rather than as a confident mRNA program.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
