summary: The broader GABA_B receptor module also showed target-only or near-target-only mRNA responses when core receptor subunits were perturbed.
why_it_matters: Gabbr1 and Gabbr2 knockdowns demonstrate that even strong perturbation of the same receptor complex can be buffered at the transcriptome level, supporting a model in which this module primarily changes receptor trafficking or signaling kinetics rather than acute mRNA abundance.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The buffering inference uses related perturbations; the Kctd16 perturbation itself was weak.

summary: Kctd16 did not phenocopy Kctd8, Gabbr1, or Gabbr2 at the same-cell transcriptome level despite physical and pathway proximity.
why_it_matters: This prevents a simplistic complex-member substitution: GABA_B receptor composition is informative for electrophysiology, but it did not create interchangeable Perturb-seq signatures.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed over weak Kctd16 signatures; absence of mRNA phenocopy does not test shared GIRK physiology.

summary: A global same-cell signature-neighbor search did not reveal a strong convergent or opposing module for Kctd16.
why_it_matters: The Kctd16 null was not rescued by an unanticipated transcriptomic neighbor; the strongest genome-wide correlations were small and not a recurrent interpretable pathway.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Correlation of rank-score signatures can highlight technical or stochastic similarity; the top correlations were below |0.15|.

summary: KCTD16 should not be assigned a therapeutic activation or inhibition direction from these mRNA data.
why_it_matters: KCTD16 has a structurally defined GABA_B2 interface and early binding-assay chemistry, but the Perturb-seq signatures lack both target engagement and downstream biomarkers, so functional receptor assays are required for target validation.
main_caveats: No electrophysiology, baclofen response, or KCTD16 protein measurement was available in the parquet.

summary: Glra1 perturbation produced a single adjusted hit, Slc5a3 down, confined to 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not show a broad glycinergic synapse program; the interpretable positive signal is a cell-type-restricted single-gene response.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only one gene survived FDR correction, and the literature source annotates SLC5A3 function rather than a direct GLRA1-to-SLC5A3 pathway.

summary: Most Glra1 perturbation contrasts were either weakly engaged or transcriptionally buffered.
why_it_matters: The absence of adjusted Glra1 knockdown means downstream negative results cannot be interpreted as clean evidence that GLRA1 is dispensable in those cells.
main_caveats: The DE table lacks basal expression and guide-efficiency measurements, so failed knockdown, low baseline expression, and biological buffering cannot be separated.

summary: The only adjusted Glra1 response arose outside the canonical hindbrain and brainstem-enriched GLRA1 context.
why_it_matters: GLRA1 biology is classically tied to mature spinal and brainstem glycinergic inhibition; the dataset instead points to a forebrain CNU-MGE GABA Slc5a3 response and no FDR response in midbrain/pons/medulla-associated classes.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Dataset cell classes are broad and do not include spinal cord; target engagement in the hindbrain-associated classes was nominal only.

summary: Glra1 signatures were not shared with receptor paralogs, the Glrb beta subunit, Slc6a5, Gphn, or Arhgef9.
why_it_matters: Known physical and genetic proximity within the glycinergic inhibitory synapse did not translate into interchangeable Perturb-seq transcriptional signatures.
main_caveats: Comparisons are restricted to transcriptome-wide score correlations; many comparator perturbations also had sparse off-target responses.

summary: Slc5a3 is a low-confidence candidate biomarker linking the Glra1 perturbation to myo-inositol/osmolyte biology in CNU-MGE GABA cells.
why_it_matters: SLC5A3 function suggests an ion-channel-adjacent osmolyte/phosphoinositide response that could be followed experimentally even though it falls outside canonical glycine-receptor annotations.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The claim is generated from one adjusted gene; no direct GLRA1-SLC5A3 regulatory literature was identified.

summary: This dataset should not be used to infer a GLRA1 therapeutic direction for hereditary hyperekplexia.
why_it_matters: The clinical disease is a glycinergic inhibitory-transmission disorder, but the measured mouse-brain perturbation lacked spinal cord circuitry, adjusted Glra1 target engagement, and a reproducible GLRA1/GLRB/SLC6A5 module.
main_caveats: This is a model-suitability warning, not evidence against GLRA1 being causal in hyperekplexia.

summary: Top Glra1 signature neighbors were too weak to support a convergent transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Weak correlations, including safe-target-adjacent maxima in other cell types, argue against overinterpreting Gabrg2, Wdr26, or Ranbp2 as mechanistic neighbors of Glra1 from this dataset alone.
main_caveats: Correlation cutoffs were not pre-registered; the conclusion is limited to the score vectors in this DE table.

summary: Cacna1d perturbation caused an extremely sparse transcriptional response across the assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: CACNA1D is a voltage-gated calcium-channel pore-forming subunit, so the absence of a reproducible FDR-level RNA program suggests either strong buffering of reduced Cacna1d dosage or insufficient effective channel loss in most assayed cells.
main_caveats: The target mRNA row is not a protein or editing assay; perturbed-cell counts were modest with a median of 59 cells.

summary: Only two cell types produced FDR-significant genes, and each produced only a single supported gene: Vps28 down in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and Ddx24 up in 053 Sst Gaba.
why_it_matters: The response is cell-type restricted but not pathway-like, preventing assignment of a shared downstream Cav1.3 transcriptional module from the FDR-supported data alone.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Both significant cell types had low perturbed-cell counts, and the supported hits were isolated single genes.

summary: Cacna1d perturbation showed an exploratory voltage-gated calcium-channel family compensation pattern, led by nominal Cacna1c induction when Cacna1d was nominally reduced in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: A rise in an L-type paralog after Cacna1d reduction would be a plausible calcium-entry preservation marker, but the signal needs validation because it did not pass multiple-testing correction.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: All paralog rows had pvals_adj=1.0; Cacna1e and Cacna1i are voltage-gated calcium-channel family members but not L-type Cav1.3 paralogs in the narrow pharmacologic sense.

summary: Related calcium-channel and calcium-signaling perturbations did not share Cacna1d transcriptome signatures in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: Physical or functional calcium-channel proximity does not imply interchangeable steady-state RNA phenotypes in this dataset.
main_caveats: The Cacna1d signature itself was weak, so near-zero correlations may partly reflect poor target engagement or low signal-to-noise.

summary: Buffered Cacna1d loss in the screen should not be treated as a phenocopy of human CACNA1D gain-of-function neurodevelopmental alleles.
why_it_matters: Human CACNA1D disease mechanisms are direction-specific: loss of Cav1.3 causes bradycardia/deafness, whereas PASNA and ASD-associated variants increase channel activity; a weak loss-of-function Perturb-seq signature therefore cannot rule out pathogenic or therapeutically relevant gain-of-function biology.
main_caveats: The dataset contains transcriptomic readouts after perturbation, not electrophysiology or mutant channel gating.

summary: Auh knockdown was measurable but sharply cell-type weighted, with 155 MB Glut the only block in which the target transcript passed FDR correction.
why_it_matters: The perturbation should be interpreted as a midbrain-glutamatergic target-engagement result plus several nominally engaged neuronal classes, not as a uniformly active Auh loss across the library.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Self-transcript depletion is an mRNA readout; lack of FDR in other classes may reflect expression, guide efficiency, cell count, or multiple-testing burden.

summary: Even where Auh mRNA was reduced, the downstream transcriptome was strongly buffered: no non-Auh gene reached 5% FDR in any Auh block.
why_it_matters: AUH is a mitochondrial leucine-catabolic enzyme, so a broad adaptive BCAA or mitochondrial-expression program might have been expected after loss; the dataset instead supports an immediate transcriptional response dominated by the target transcript itself.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Transcriptomics cannot exclude metabolite, protein, electrophysiologic, or viability phenotypes below the DE detection threshold.

summary: Measured branched-chain amino-acid pathway neighbors did not phenocopy Auh in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Auh, Ivd, Bckdhb, Dld, Acat1 and Bckdk are connected by leucine/BCAA catabolism, but their perturbation score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Auh, arguing against a shared acute transcriptional module for this metabolic pathway in the main Auh-engaged cell class.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only five Auh-neighbor perturbations were present in the dataset, and several had weak self-knockdown in 155 MB Glut.

summary: The human loss-of-function disease link is not mirrored by a broad acute neuronal DE program after partial guide-based Auh mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: Biallelic AUH mutations cause 3-methylglutaconic aciduria type I with variable neurological manifestations; the mouse-brain dataset suggests that disease phenotypes can occur through enzymatic/metabolite or developmental mechanisms that are largely invisible to short-term single-cell mRNA DE in most assayed neuronal classes.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison uses mouse brain cell classes and partial mRNA depletion, whereas 3-methylglutaconic aciduria type I is a human germline enzymatic deficiency.

summary: The 155 MB Glut Auh signature had no robust whole-library signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Top positive and negative correlations were close to zero and included safe-target controls, so signature-neighbor names such as Rrn3 should not be over-interpreted as biology linked to AUH.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a correlation-based negative result restricted to one cell type and to the perturbations represented in the library.

summary: Itga6 perturbation was transcriptionally weak across the 22 assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: The screen does not provide a robust neuronal Itga6 loss-of-function program: the target mRNA was not significantly reduced after multiple testing and downstream FDR-controlled effects were almost absent.
main_caveats: This is an mRNA readout; weak guide activity, sparse Itga6 expression, or post-transcriptional integrin regulation could all obscure protein-level biology.

summary: The only Itga6-associated hits were isolated Spopl and Pcmt1 increases in two different cell classes.
why_it_matters: The significant signal is not a coherent recurrent module; Spopl reached FDR<0.05 only in 191 MB P MY GABA, and Pcmt1 reached only FDR<0.10 in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Each hit is single-gene and non-recurrent; the Itga6 transcript itself was not engaged in either cell type, so these are best treated as exploratory biomarkers or false-positive-sensitive observations.

summary: Itga6 did not phenocopy nearby laminin-receptor perturbations.
why_it_matters: Despite known alpha6-beta1/alpha6-beta4 laminin-receptor biology, Itga6 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Agrn, Itgb1, Itga7, and Dag1 perturbations, and the Itga6 perturbation did not induce receptor-neighbor compensation.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptional and most individual perturbations were themselves FDR-silent; ITGB4, LAMA, LAMB, and LAMC genes were not directly perturbed in the available neighbor set.

summary: The weak mature-neuron response is consistent with ITGA6 biology being concentrated in endothelial, neural-stem, neuroblast, and glioblastoma-stem contexts rather than the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Prior brain literature places alpha6-beta1 at perivascular neural-stem/progenitor interfaces and in glioblastoma stem cells; the Perturb-seq result refines that biology by showing little evidence for a broad cell-autonomous program in mature glutamatergic or GABAergic neurons.
main_caveats: The expression atlas is human whereas the screen is mouse, and stem-cell, neuroblast, endothelial, and glioblastoma contexts were not directly assayed in these neuronal Perturb-seq strata.

summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq data should not be used alone to choose a pro- or anti-ITGA6 therapeutic direction for glioblastoma or repair contexts.
why_it_matters: ITGA6 is a plausible extracellular target in glioblastoma stem cells, but this normal-neuron dataset lacks a coherent Itga6 signature and ChEMBL contains no curated single-protein ITGA6 drug mechanism in the queried target record.
main_caveats: The warning concerns extrapolation only; the screen did not model glioblastoma stem cells, endothelial niches, antibody blockade, or extracellular ligand competition.

summary: Grip1 knockdown was directionally recurrent but statistically weak at the target mRNA itself.
why_it_matters: The experiment should be interpreted as partial or buffered loss of Grip1 rather than a clean loss-of-function; strong downstream negatives and positives must be weighed against the absence of FDR-level target-transcript engagement.
main_caveats: mRNA was the only assayed readout; a weak target mRNA change does not exclude stronger guide effects on unmeasured isoforms or delayed protein effects.

summary: The only FDR-resolved downstream response to Grip1 was a Tuba1a-led, top-negative synaptic program in 145 MH-LH TH Glut cells.
why_it_matters: GRIP1 is known to organize dendritic receptor transport, so a synapse-enriched negative list in this hypothalamic/thalamic glutamatergic class is the dataset's clearest literature-adjacent phenotype, but it extends hippocampal studies to a new cell class.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only Tuba1a survived FDR; the synapse enrichment was computed on the 50 most negative genes, and Grip1 target mRNA was not nominally significant in this same cell type.

summary: Pvalb interneurons showed an exploratory Edf1/Nrg3-down and Rasgrf1/Slc9a5-up response in the setting of one of the better Grip1 mRNA shifts.
why_it_matters: This Pvalb pattern is not an established GRIP1 pathway, but it is a plausible cell-class biomarker panel to test if future guides achieve stronger target engagement in inhibitory neurons.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: All Pvalb response genes failed FDR after multiple testing, so this is a nominal candidate rather than a confirmed interneuron program.

summary: Grip1 perturbation did not induce an AMPA-receptor-subunit or postsynaptic-density mRNA program and did not phenocopy perturbations of its AMPAR/PSD neighbors.
why_it_matters: GRIP1 is embedded in GluR2/GluA2 trafficking protein complexes, but this dataset argues that the assayed response is not a simple transcriptional surrogate for Gria2, Gria3, Dlg4, Kif5a, or SHANK-family perturbation.
main_caveats: The Grip1 signature itself was weak; absence of receptor-subunit mRNA changes does not test AMPAR localization, phosphorylation, or synaptic currents.

summary: A Kif5a decrease in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut cells is a literature-connected but weak candidate for GRIP1 motor-feedback biology.
why_it_matters: GRIP1 uses KIF5 for dendritic receptor trafficking; Kif5a appearing near the top of one Grip1 signature is a mechanistically coherent biomarker hypothesis even though it is not FDR significant.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Kif5a had FDR=0.582 and the Grip1 transcript was essentially unchanged in this cell type, so off-axis or sampling effects remain plausible.

summary: Disease interpretation of this CRISPRi-like Grip1 dataset should not be equated with reported autism-associated GRIP1 gain-of-function variants.
why_it_matters: The human variants were described as faster GluA2 recycling/surface-distribution gain-of-function alleles, whereas the dataset is a weak transcript-reduction experiment with no Gria2 mRNA readout; rescue logic therefore needs protein-trafficking assays and direction-matched alleles.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay autistic-behavioral cells directly, AMPAR surface trafficking, or GRIP1 missense gain-of-function variants.

summary: Full-transcriptome neighbor analysis found no strong positive or negative Grip1 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: A maximum nonself correlation of only 0.176, with safe-target controls among the highest positives, implies that the Grip1 response is low-amplitude or idiosyncratic rather than a member of a robust recurrent perturbation module.
main_caveats: Correlation is a transcriptomic metric; it can miss shared phenotypes that are post-transcriptional or temporally shifted.

summary: Cd4 perturbation had no measurable on-target transcript effect in any of the 22 Cd4-profiled mouse neuronal strata.
why_it_matters: Without demonstrable Cd4 transcript engagement, the screen cannot support a cell-intrinsic Cd4 loss-of-function phenotype in these glutamatergic and GABAergic brain classes.
main_caveats: The table contains rank-based differential-expression statistics, not guide-level editing or raw expression measurements; extremely sparse target expression can make logFC values unstable.

summary: Cd4 produced no FDR-significant downstream gene in 371,818 target-by-cell-type tests.
why_it_matters: The strongest apparent genes, including Cntn2 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut and Unc45a in the largest thalamic stratum, remain nominal and should be treated as statistical tail events rather than Cd4 biology.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell counts were modest, from 20 to 179 cells per stratum, so the result excludes only moderate-to-large transcriptomic shifts in the assayed neuronal populations.

summary: Canonical TCR-CD3/MHC-II signaling is not transcriptionally engaged by Cd4 in the neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: CD4 normally functions as a coreceptor that cooperates with peptide-MHC-II, CD3 chains, and Lck; the same dataset shows no robust effects for Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd3g, or Cd247 and near-zero Cd4-to-CD3 signature correlations, arguing that the immune receptor complex is absent or inactive in these cells.
main_caveats: The library did not contain every proximal immune signaling component, and the inference is transcriptomic rather than a direct protein-complex assay.

summary: Neither curated CD4-associated immune neighbors nor unbiased whole-library signatures converge with the weak Cd4 signature.
why_it_matters: Ccr5, Cxcr4, and H2-Eb1 are STRING-linked immune or MHC neighbors of CD4, yet their perturbational signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Cd4; among 2,045 assayed targets the top positive Cd4 neighbor was only r=0.0268, so there is no hidden high-confidence Cd4-like module.
main_caveats: A near-zero transcriptomic correlation does not exclude shared protein-level biology in true immune cells; Lck, Zap70, Cd8a, and H2-Ab1 were STRING partners but were not available as matched perturbations in this dataset.

summary: The neuronal Cd4-null signature should not be extrapolated to CD4-directed HIV or T-cell pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Human CD4 is antibody-tractable and direct CD4-binding antibodies can block HIV entry, whereas the assayed mouse brain classes lacked Cd4 and TCR-CD3 transcriptional engagement; the dataset is therefore a lineage-restriction result, not a prediction that CD4 blockade is biologically inert.
main_caveats: The therapeutic literature is human and extracellular-antibody based; the Perturb-seq assay used mouse-cell genetic perturbations and contained no CD4 T-cell or HIV-entry model.

direction: Dld transcript down; downstream RNA response absent at FDR<0.05
summary: Dld guides produced a reproducible sign of on-target transcript reduction but no FDR-significant transcriptome in any brain cell type.
why_it_matters: DLD is a catalytic mitochondrial E3 enzyme, yet this Perturb-seq readout mainly detects a weak self-transcript effect; downstream physiology may be metabolic, post-transcriptional, buffered, or below the power of the available cell counts.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not FDR-significant in any single cell type, and most Dld strata contained fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

direction: nominal Dld down in selected cell types
summary: The clearest nominal Dld self-knockdown concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, without robust non-self marker genes.
why_it_matters: These are the only contexts worth prioritizing for follow-up within this dataset, but their top non-self genes remain nominal rather than a reliable Dld response module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The apparent selectivity follows nominal self-transcript ranks and may reflect higher sample size rather than a true cell-type-specific biological susceptibility.

summary: Transcripts for expected PDH, OGDH, BCKDH, and TCA partners were not coherently regulated after Dld perturbation.
why_it_matters: A biochemical hub in mitochondrial alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes did not trigger a matching compensatory mRNA program for its partner complexes in this assay.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was measured; the relevant PDH/OGDH/BCKDH defect is expected to be enzyme-flux and redox based.

summary: Dld signatures were nearly orthogonal to perturbations of Dlat, Dlst, Pdha1, Pdhb, Pdhx, Ogdh, and Bckdhb despite known complex membership.
why_it_matters: The Dld RNA signature in this dataset should not be used as a proxy for PDH or OGDH complex inhibition, even in brain cell types where other mitochondrial enzyme perturbations achieved strong self-knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The contrast is signature-based and restricted to weak Dld signatures; it does not contradict the shared biochemical E3 role of DLD.

direction: no strong positive or negative neighbor
summary: Whole-library signature-neighbor searches found no robust positive or negative Dld neighbor.
why_it_matters: The Dld phenotype cannot be rescued by relabeling it as another transcriptional module; top neighbors have absolute correlations below 0.1 in the best-engaged cell types.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Neighbor analysis is limited to cell types with nominal on-target Dld reduction and to score-vector correlations over measured transcripts.

summary: The disease literature makes DLD loss a high-risk direction for brain or systemic inhibition, and the dataset supplied no robust compensatory mRNA signature that would reassure against acute mitochondrial flux defects.
why_it_matters: DLD deficiency damages multiple energy-producing alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase systems; a therapeutic strategy that suppresses DLD would need metabolite and enzyme assays rather than relying on the weak Perturb-seq RNA response.
main_caveats: The screen models partial CRISPR perturbation of mouse neuronal transcripts, not biallelic human DLD deficiency or pharmacologic inhibition.

summary: Hnrnpa1 perturbation had weak measured on-target transcript depletion and almost no genome-wide FDR-significant response across 21 neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: hnRNP A1 is a broadly expressed RNA-processing factor, so the dataset is best read as a poorly engaged or buffered perturbation rather than as evidence that Hnrnpa1 loss is inert in brain neurons.
main_caveats: The target is an RNA-splicing factor, but this assay scored gene-level abundance rather than isoform usage or RNA-binding changes; all conclusions are limited by absent FDR-level self-knockdown.

summary: A single FDR-level candidate, down-regulation of Rbm5, was restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA under Hnrnpa1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The result nominates a narrow RNA-regulatory readout to re-test if stronger Hnrnpa1 depletion becomes available, but it is too isolated to define a pathway response.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The Hnrnpa1 self transcript was only nominally lower in this cell type and the genome-wide result consists of one adjusted significant gene.

direction: Hnrnpa1 much weaker than active related RNA-binding perturbations
summary: The same screen readily detected other RNA-binding and splicing-factor perturbations, especially Srsf1, Snrnp70, Tardbp, and Fus, while Hnrnpa1 and its paralog Hnrnpa2b1 remained nearly silent.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the Hnrnpa1 negative result is target-specific and not a general failure of the brain Perturb-seq design to detect consequences of RNA-processing perturbations.
main_caveats: The comparison is based on total gene-abundance DE burdens and self-transcript rows, not on matched protein depletion or isoform-splicing measurements.

direction: screen modality mismatched to mutant RNA-binding protein disease
summary: This mouse knockdown-like Hnrnpa1 readout is not a matched model of HNRNPA1 ALS and multisystem proteinopathy mechanisms, which center on prion-like/low-complexity-domain mutations and RNA-granule or splicing dysfunction.
why_it_matters: A weak loss-of-transcript signature should not be used to down-rank HNRNPA1 genetic disease relevance or to claim that HNRNPA1 silencing would be harmless.
main_caveats: The dataset measured mouse gene-abundance changes after perturbation rather than human mutant HNRNPA1 proteinopathy, stress granules, or alternative splicing.

direction: no strong positive or negative neighbor
summary: In the only Hnrnpa1 cell type with an FDR hit, all-gene signature-neighbor analysis failed to reveal a strong HNRNP/FUS/TARDBP/SRSF1-like neighbor.
why_it_matters: Rbm5 down-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA is therefore not embedded in a broader, recognizable RNA-binding-protein signature within that cell type.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Only one cell type was examined for full signature correlations; weak Hnrnpa1 engagement compresses any correlation estimate.

summary: Iqsec1 knockdown was statistically clear in Pvalb GABA and midbrain glutamatergic cells, yet the significant signal stopped at the target transcript.
why_it_matters: A postsynaptic trafficking GEF can be measurably depleted without triggering a broad steady-state RNA program, so the primary phenotype in these cells is likely missed by transcript counts alone.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measured RNA rather than Arf6 activity, AMPAR endocytosis, synaptic physiology or dendritic-spine morphology.

summary: On-target depletion was widespread but highly uneven: two cell types passed FDR, four more had Iqsec1 as a top nominal hit, and several low-count or weak-engagement classes were uninformative.
why_it_matters: Downstream negatives should be interpreted mainly in the engaged Pvalb and MB Glut contexts; absence of a signature in weakly depleted or 20-cell dopamine/pineal contrasts is not evidence that Iqsec1 is dispensable there.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: FDR loss outside the top two cell types may reflect smaller cell numbers, different baseline expression, guide performance, or true cell-state differences.

summary: Strong Iqsec1 depletion did not change Arf6, AMPA-receptor or PSD-95/Dlg4 mRNAs.
why_it_matters: Known BRAG2 biology is a GRIA2/AMPAR-to-Arf6 endocytic mechanism; this dataset refines that expectation by showing no compensatory transcription of Arf6, Gria1, Gria2 or Dlg4 in the two engaged cell types.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No protein abundance, receptor-surface, Arf6-GTP or electrophysiology measurements were available.

summary: The quiet RNA phenotype after partial Iqsec1 loss argues that IQSEC1-linked neurodevelopmental defects can be expressed as local synaptic or structural phenotypes rather than as a large cell-autonomous transcriptional cascade.
why_it_matters: Human IQSEC1 loss-of-function causes intellectual disability and mouse cortical deletion affects dendritic-spine maturity; the Perturb-seq result prioritizes spine, receptor-trafficking and physiology assays over bulk RNA biomarkers for this mechanism.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Disease alleles are chronic and developmental, whereas the dataset is a partial cellular knockdown assayed by RNA in selected mouse-brain classes.

summary: No paralog, AMPAR/PSD neighbor or unbiased signature neighbor provided a robust transcriptional phenocopy of Iqsec1.
why_it_matters: The lack of a convergent RNA module is itself informative for an endocytic synapse pathway; however the Iqsec2 paralog comparison is engagement-confounded because Iqsec2 was not significantly reduced in any assayed cell type.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations used full Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by non-significant genes; related-target comparisons are limited to perturbations with usable engagement.

summary: IQSEC1/BRAG2 is chemically inhibitable, but transcriptomic target engagement would be a poor safety or efficacy biomarker in the engaged neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Bragsin-like inhibitors should be evaluated with proximal BRAG2-Arf and AMPAR-trafficking endpoints and with synaptic developmental safety assays, because the dataset shows that depleting Iqsec1 can leave almost no FDR-significant mRNA footprint.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The small-molecule evidence is chemical-biology rather than clinical; perturbation is genetic and does not test inhibitor selectivity or exposure.

summary: Pdgfrb produced no RNA-level on-target depletion and no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response across 22 assayed neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: This rules out a large autonomous Pdgfrb program in the sampled glutamatergic and GABAergic neuron classes, and it fits the known mural/pericyte enrichment of PDGFRB.
cell_types: all 22 Pdgfrb-assayed neuronal subclasses
main_caveats: The table measures RNA, not editing or protein loss; several subclasses had fewer than 60 perturbed cells; 215 MB Dopa was not assayed for Pdgfrb.

summary: The best nominal Pdgfrb genes and signature neighbors were isolated and did not define a recurrent Pdgfrb module.
why_it_matters: The absence of recurrence prevents overinterpreting Chka, Zmym5, Khdrbs3, Camk2a, or other nominal rows as biomarkers of PDGFRB biology.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|multiple other neuronal subclasses
main_caveats: This is a negative statement about bulk DE summaries; weak cell-type-specific effects below the current power could be missed.

summary: PFBC-relevant Pdgfrb, Slc20a2, and Xpr1 perturbations were FDR-null in the assayed neurons, refining PDGFRB brain-disease interpretation toward neurovascular-unit and phosphate-handling contexts absent from the table.
why_it_matters: Pdgfrb loss of function causes human brain calcification, but the neuronal null indicates that the current assay is unlikely to capture the pericyte and microvascular phenotypes implicated by the disease literature.
cell_types: all 22 Pdgfrb-assayed neuronal subclasses
main_caveats: The comparator panel is disease- and vascular-motivated rather than a single biochemical complex, and non-neuronal cell classes were not sampled.

summary: Pten yielded a detectable PI3K-adjacent transcriptional response while Pdgfrb did not, implying receptor-layer uncoupling of PDGFRB rather than wholesale invisibility of intracellular growth-factor pathways.
why_it_matters: This contrast narrows the negative result: the neuronal assay can report at least some PI3K-pathway perturbations, but a mural RTK upstream of that pathway is silent in the assayed cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|all 22 Pdgfrb-assayed neuronal subclasses
main_caveats: PTEN is an intracellular PI3K brake, not a PDGFRB complex member, so the comparison localizes signaling competence only coarsely.

summary: The Pdgfrb neuronal null should not be interpreted as evidence that PDGFRB blockade is CNS-benign or mechanistically irrelevant.
why_it_matters: PDGFRB is pharmacologically tractable and its key brain biology is in pericyte recruitment and BBB regulation, cell types missing from the assayed neuronal DE table.
cell_types: all 22 Pdgfrb-assayed neuronal subclasses
main_caveats: The dataset supports a warning about assay scope, not a direct measurement of drug response or BBB integrity.

direction: Epb41l1 down; non-target RNA response buffered
summary: Epb41l1 perturbation produced a target-only corrected response in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The most reliable phenotype is successful target mRNA depletion without an FDR-significant downstream transcriptional program, consistent with a scaffold whose immediate output may be receptor localization rather than mRNA abundance.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Transcriptome-only readout; modest logFC and possible residual 4.1N protein could hide synaptic effects.

direction: mostly negative target logFC where engaged
summary: Detectable Epb41l1 knockdown was graded across brain classes rather than uniform.
why_it_matters: Only one cell class had corrected target depletion, while several cell classes with nominal depletion had low perturbed-cell counts and other high-count classes did not deplete the target, making downstream absence outside MB Glut hard to interpret as biological resistance alone.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The parquet lacks raw target expression and guide-level efficiency, so selectivity cannot be separated into expression, sampling, and CRISPR efficiency components.

summary: Epb41l1 score vectors were not correlated with AMPA, neurexin/CASK, or membrane-cytoskeleton comparator perturbations.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues that membership in the same synaptic scaffold pathway does not translate into a shared scRNA-seq perturbation signature for Epb41l1.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak RNA signatures; absence of similarity does not test receptor trafficking, protein localization, or synaptic physiology.

summary: No recurrent non-target RNA biomarker for Epb41l1 loss was detected.
why_it_matters: Even relaxed nominal thresholds failed to reveal a cell-class-spanning downstream marker, so single nominal genes should not be promoted without validation.
main_caveats: A subtle, sparse, or time-dependent module could be missed by the cell numbers and sampling time in this Perturb-seq experiment.

direction: target depletion without broad downstream module
summary: The Perturb-seq profile does not reproduce a broad neurodevelopmental or neuroendocrine disease-like RNA module after acute Epb41l1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse genetics motivate EPB41L1 as a brain-relevant synaptic gene, but this dataset points toward post-transcriptional, developmental, or circuit-level mechanisms rather than an immediate mature-cell mRNA cascade.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Disease variants and germline knockouts differ from partial acute knockdown in mixed mouse brain cell classes.

summary: The Epb41l1 signature is not sufficient to infer a disease-rescuing direction or small-molecule strategy.
why_it_matters: Without corrected downstream markers and without curated EPB41L1 chemical probes, RNA reversal would be a weak basis for therapeutic prioritization; functional synaptic assays are required.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Open Targets curation can lag the literature, and the Perturb-seq dataset was not designed to test receptor trafficking or electrophysiology.

summary: Prkag2 targeting produced a globally buffered or weak brain transcriptomic response.
why_it_matters: PRKAG2 is an AMPK gamma regulatory subunit, but the assayed target transcript was not consistently depleted and no cell type produced a 5% FDR transcriptomic signature, so the dataset provides little evidence for basal PRKAG2-dependent mRNA programmes in these brain classes.
main_caveats: The finding is a transcript-level negative result; AMPK can act through phosphorylation and metabolic flux, and guide engagement was weak by target mRNA.

summary: CTX-CGE GABA contained the only near-FDR Prkag2 single-gene signal, but it remained exploratory.
why_it_matters: Faf1 and Acap3 marked the strongest cell-type-localized nominal response, preventing the global null from hiding the best outlier while making clear that it did not pass 5% FDR or define a pathway.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Only 40 perturbed cells; Faf1 reached FDR 0.0868 rather than FDR<0.05 and the other CTX-CGE genes had FDR>=0.304.

summary: The TSC branch of mTORC1 was strongly inducible where Prkag2 and Prkaa2 were quiet.
why_it_matters: Tsc1/Tsc2 targeting generated hundreds of FDR-significant changes, especially in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Prkag2, Prkaa2, Rptor, and most Mtor tests were muted; this separates the assayed AMPK gamma2/alpha2 perturbations from a downstream mTORC1-responsive module expected from pathway maps.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to perturbations present in the screen; absent Prkag2 engagement and different guide efficacies could explain the contrast without proving biological independence.

summary: No recurrent same-direction Prkag2 marker gene emerged across brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The nominal hits were mostly private to one cell class, so Faf1, Dnajb12, Nipbl, Plscr3, and similar top-ranked genes should not be treated as general PRKAG2 biomarkers in this experiment.
main_caveats: The recurrence threshold used nominal p<0.01 because no gene passed FDR<0.05.

direction: cardiac gain_of_function direction absent in Prkag2 brain perturbation
summary: The brain Perturb-seq result should not be read as reproducing PRKAG2 gain-of-function cardiomyopathy or as evidence that gamma2 inhibition engages mTOR growth programmes in neurons.
why_it_matters: Disease literature links activating PRKAG2 mutations to cardiac Akt/mTOR hyperactivity and hypertrophic growth, but the screened mouse brain Prkag2 perturbation was weak and mTOR-readout-like signatures were reserved for Tsc1/Tsc2; a PRKAG2 therapeutic hypothesis therefore needs allele direction, tissue, and biochemical AMPK activity measurements rather than only basal brain mRNA output.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Species, tissue, developmental context, and perturbation mode differ from human PRKAG2 syndrome and the N488I mouse heart model.

summary: Ndufb3 perturbation did not measurably repress the Ndufb3 transcript in any profiled cell type.
why_it_matters: Because NDUFB3 is a mitochondrial complex-I accessory subunit, the absent self-transcript signal makes most downstream effects difficult to interpret as clean complex-I loss of function.
main_caveats: The transcript table cannot distinguish poor guide activity from post-transcriptional protein loss or guide effects outside the assayed transcript; the statement is limited to Ndufb3 mRNA.

summary: Ogdh down-regulation is the best-supported downstream feature of the weak Ndufb3 signature.
why_it_matters: Ogdh encodes the E1 enzyme of 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase, a TCA-cycle source of NADH that is metabolically upstream of complex I; its decrease in 191 MB P MY GABA and nominal recurrence in 155 MB Glut nominate Ogdh as a hypothesis-generating readout of midbrain mitochondrial stress.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only the 191 MB P MY GABA Ogdh row is FDR<0.05; the 155 MB Glut repetition is nominal, and no enzyme or metabolite measurement verifies lower OGDH activity.

summary: FDR-supported Ndufb3 downstream expression changes are confined to 191 MB P MY GABA, while the other 21 profiled cell types are FDR-silent.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a uniform brain-wide transcriptional stress response to this perturbation and makes the apparent midbrain signal more notable despite the weak scalar strength of the knockdown.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The restriction may reflect weak target engagement, limited power in small cell classes, or multiple-testing loss rather than true biological absence in every non-191 class.

summary: The Ndufb3 score vector does not converge with other complex-I-family perturbations in the responsive 191 MB P MY GABA class.
why_it_matters: Even in the cell type with the only FDR-supported Ndufb3 downstream hit, related Nduf perturbations showed much stronger self-depletion and near-zero rank correlation with Ndufb3, so the Ogdh/Pcbp3 signature should not be treated as an interchangeable complex-I module.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptomic and restricted to one cell type; zero correlation may be driven by poor Ndufb3 target engagement rather than subunit-specific biology.

summary: This Perturb-seq profile is not a faithful model of pathogenic NDUFB3 deficiency.
why_it_matters: Human NDUFB3 variants can produce isolated complex-I deficiency with assembly defects, but the mouse Ndufb3 perturbation lacks self-transcript repression and broad complex-I transcriptional consequences; therapeutic or disease conclusions should therefore require orthogonal engagement and respiration assays.
main_caveats: Absence of a transcriptomic disease-like response is not evidence that Ndufb3 is dispensable; the assay did not measure complex-I assembly, NADH oxidation, or oxygen consumption.

summary: Brwd1 perturbation was nominally engaged but produced an extremely sparse corrected transcriptomic response across the 22 assayed neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: A broadly expressed bromodomain/WD chromatin regulator might be expected to shift many genes, so the sparse RNA phenotype reframes Brwd1 loss as either buffered, weakly engaged, or dependent on contexts not captured by this acute neuronal screen.
main_caveats: No Brwd1 target row passed FDR correction; low perturbed-cell counts and incomplete knockdown can masquerade as buffering.

summary: Jund induction in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was the only FDR<0.05 downstream event after Brwd1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: It nominates Jund/AP-1 as the clearest measurable RNA marker of Brwd1 loss in this dataset, but only in a restricted GABAergic hypothalamic/amygdala class.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Shank1 was only nominal and the corrected component of the signature is a single gene in 52 perturbed cells.

summary: Brwd1 perturbation did not converge with perturbations of assayed BAF-complex genes despite BRWD1 being connected to SMARCA4/BAF in prior work.
why_it_matters: This separates partial Brwd1 loss from generic BAF loss of function in brain Perturb-seq and argues against annotating the Brwd1 RNA phenotype simply as BAF-complex collapse.
main_caveats: The comparison uses RNA signature correlations only; BRWD1 and BAF could still converge at chromatin loci without a matched steady-state RNA response.

direction: response restricted to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
summary: Large thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic Brwd1 strata were transcriptionally quiet despite nominal target reduction.
why_it_matters: The absence of corrected hits in the two highest-cell-count strata shows that the CNU-HYa/HY GABA Jund response is cell-context restricted rather than merely the best-powered result.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Different guide efficiencies by cell type are not measured at the protein level.

summary: The screen does not support direct extrapolation from Down-syndrome Brwd1 copy-number rescue to broad BRWD1 inhibition in euploid neurons.
why_it_matters: Prior disease data involve trisomic BRWD1 overexpression and BAF mistargeting, whereas this perturbation is partial Brwd1 loss; the lack of hippocampal corrected hits and lack of BAF-like signatures flag disease-direction specificity.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Perturb-seq did not assay trisomic neurons, BRWD1 dosage normalization, hippocampal LTP, or chromatin accessibility.

summary: In the only FDR-positive cell type, Brwd1 had no close whole-transcriptome positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: This reduces the chance that a strong but differently named pathway-module comparator was missed in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor analysis was focused on the 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA stratum.

direction: 151-selective; RNA-processing arm down with a smaller up-regulated arm
summary: Nop56 depletion produced a broad, FDR-significant, mixed-direction RNA-processing response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: A core nucleolar snoRNP factor did not cause a uniform neuronal rRNA-stress transcriptome; the major downstream state was a thalamic glutamatergic splicing/RNA-processing response despite broad NOP56 expression annotations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: 151 had the largest Nop56 perturbed-cell count, and these are transcript-level rather than protein or rRNA-processing measurements.

summary: Strong Nop56 transcript depletion was buffered in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 155 MB Glut and only weakly propagated in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The result separates target knockdown from global transcriptional collapse and shows that some neuronal classes tolerate partial reduction of a core rRNA-processing factor at steady-state mRNA resolution.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This does not show that complete Nop56 loss is tolerated; complete zebrafish loss of function is severe, and this dataset measures partial transcript depletion in mouse brain cells.

summary: The Nop56 151 signature partially converged with Srsf1 and Rbm28 but not Las1l or Son, and canonical box C/D partners were not in the perturbation library.
why_it_matters: This prevents the 151 Nop56 signature from being overgeneralized to all ribosome-biogenesis perturbations and preserves a potentially meaningful bridge between nucleolar stress and splice-factor biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Rbm28 and Las1l perturbations had weak target-transcript engagement and no FDR genes in 151, while Fbl, Nop58, and Snu13 were absent, so direct complex-member equivalence was not tested.

summary: The mouse perturbation data support SCA36 ASO strategies that remove expanded repeat RNA without lowering the normal NOP56 transcript.

main_caveats: The strongest significant comparators include neuronal Chrna4/Chrnb2 and secreted or enzymatic cholinergic genes, not only strict CHRND complex members.

summary: The dataset does not support a central-neuronal Chrnd branch for congenital-myasthenic-syndrome biology.
why_it_matters: Known CHRND disease biology centers on muscle endplate receptor function; the mouse-brain perturbation was largely invisible even in cholinergic-associated comparisons, reinforcing that these cell types are an indirect model for CHRND motor-endplate disease.
main_caveats: A null brain Perturb-seq result does not test skeletal muscle fibers, motor endplates, fetal AChR assembly, or receptor electrophysiology.

summary: The Chrnd brain signature should not be used as evidence for a CNS efficacy or safety window of CHRND-directed pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Because CHRND is a muscle-type AChR component with skeletal-muscle-enriched RNA and no on-target engagement here, therapeutically relevant CHRND perturbations must be evaluated in neuromuscular models rather than inferred from this neuronal negative.
main_caveats: This is a model-selection warning, not direct drug-toxicity evidence; the experiment measured RNA abundance after genetic perturbation, not acute ion-channel block.

summary: Cspp1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any profiled cell type and did not measurably deplete the Cspp1 transcript.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset-level result is a negative or under-engaged perturbation rather than a strong Cspp1 loss-of-function state; downstream absences should therefore not be interpreted as showing that CSPP1 biology is dispensable.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an imperfect proxy for genome editing or protein loss, and each cell type had only 21-68 Cspp1 cells.

summary: The weak Cspp1 signal was not uniform: 052 Pvalb Gaba contained the nearest-to-significant event, while CA3/CA2-FC/DG showed a low-cell-count bipolar nominal signature and the largest thalamic sample stayed buffered.
why_it_matters: If Cspp1 is re-tested, the dataset points to Pvalb and hippocampal glutamatergic classes for extra power while showing that the largest available Cspp1 sample did not automatically produce a downstream program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The leading cell-type effects are nominal only and are dominated by isolated genes, not by a validated Cspp1 pathway.

summary: Known CSPP1 ciliary, ciliopathy, and Hedgehog-associated transcripts were not coherently changed after Cspp1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: CSPP1 protein is linked to ciliary axoneme formation, CEP104-dependent Hedgehog competence, and ciliary microtubule stability, yet this mouse-brain transcriptome readout did not expose a matching Hedgehog or ciliary module.
main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA in mouse brain cells, whereas several ciliary phenotypes are structural, developmental, or Hedgehog-stimulation dependent; poor Cspp1 transcript engagement can mask a pathway response.

summary: Cspp1 did not converge strongly with ciliary perturbations or direct CSPP1 network neighbors in the same cell types.
why_it_matters: Direct and disease-family ciliary genes should not be treated as interchangeable perturbations in this dataset: B9d1, Ahi1, Cplane1, Cep290, and Rpgrip1l signatures were weakly correlated with Cspp1 at best, and Ahi1/Cplane1 target engagement in midbrain glutamatergic neurons contrasted with the inactive Cspp1 signature.

main_caveats: The contrast is partly driven by weak Cspp1 engagement, and many ciliary comparator signatures were themselves small.

summary: The Perturb-seq non-response refines, rather than overturns, CSPP1 Joubert-syndrome biology.
why_it_matters: Human genetics and ciliated-cell models show that CSPP1 loss can disrupt primary cilia and mid-hindbrain development, but the present mouse-brain signatures report little acute transcriptomic consequence; CSPP1 disease mechanisms are therefore likely to be developmental, structural, or context-dependent relative to this assay.
main_caveats: Assay species, developmental stage, cell types, perturbation modality, and protein-editing efficacy are only partially matched to the human and zebrafish disease literature.

summary: Epha10 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed brain cell type, even though the Epha10 transcript trended downward in most cells.
why_it_matters: This converts a dataset-wide negative result into biology: acute Epha10 loss is either buffered in these neuronal contexts or not captured by a steady-state mRNA readout of an Eph pseudokinase.
main_caveats: The strongest target-transcript row was not itself FDR-significant, so incomplete CRISPRi knockdown remains a major alternative explanation.

summary: Detectable Epha10 self-depletion was concentrated in 191 MB P MY GABA and a few cortical or Pvalb signatures, whereas the best adjusted non-target row occurred in CTX-CGE GABA without target engagement.

cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA

summary: Epha10 signatures were not correlated with Epha4, Epha5, Epha7, or Ephb2 signatures despite those receptors belonging to the broader Eph family and Epha4/Epha7/Epha5 showing stronger self-knockdown in some matching cells.

summary: Canonical EPH-ephrin and axon-guidance annotations were not accompanied by a recurrent downstream Epha10 mRNA module.
why_it_matters: The expected pathway identity is real at the receptor/domain level, but the Perturb-seq output suggests that this library and assay did not read out a stable cell-autonomous axon-guidance program after Epha10 loss.
main_caveats: No Efna/Efnb ligands were themselves perturbed, and transcript abundance may not capture Eph receptor signaling.

summary: Mouse brain Epha10 loss did not reproduce the strong gain-of-EPHA10 disease phenotypes reported in pancreatic cancer and human hearing loss literature.
why_it_matters: It distinguishes acute loss-of-function in postmitotic brain cells from settings where EPHA10 is upregulated or overexpressed, which is essential for directional therapeutic reasoning.
main_caveats: Cancer cells, cochlea, and mouse brain neurons differ in species, baseline expression, and disease direction.

summary: EPHA10 surface-targeting strategies should not assume absolute normal-tissue silence, because human data report EPHA10 RNA in brain and this mouse dataset observed perturbable Epha10 in neuronal populations.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq result is reassuring at the mRNA level but still flags brain as a tissue to evaluate pharmacologically for antibodies, bispecifics, ADCs, or CAR-T approaches to EPHA10-positive tumors.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba

summary: Kbtbd7 perturbation produced no FDR-significant target knockdown or downstream gene in any assayed mouse-brain cell class.

summary: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut contained the strongest nominal Kbtbd7 signature, led by Ctnnb1 down-regulation, but it failed FDR correction and lacked Kbtbd7 target reduction.

summary: Rac1 knockdown was an inverse neighbor of restricted Kbtbd7 signatures in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.

summary: Detectable Cyld transcript depletion was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with much weaker or absent target-transcript effects across the rest of the Cyld-sampled neuronal classes.

summary: Nominal Oprd1 depletion in Pvalb did not induce a coordinated PI3K-Akt-mTOR mRNA module.
why_it_matters: A DOR agonist can use PI3K-Akt-mTORC1 phosphorylation in mouse IL-PFC PV interneurons, so the flat mRNA module argues that the therapeutic receptor pathway is probably post-translational, ligand-state dependent, or diluted in this pooled Perturb-seq class.

summary: In Pvalb, the Oprd1 signature was nearly orthogonal to perturbations of Prkaca, Gnao1, Gnb1, Adcy1, and Adcy5.

summary: Oprd1 did not show a strong Pvalb signature match to Oprm1, Oprk1, or Oprl1, nor to any top non-self perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: The lack of convergence prevents treating opioid receptor paralogs as interchangeable transcriptomic surrogates for Oprd1 in this dataset and is consistent with prior mouse genetics showing mu- and delta-receptor functions can diverge.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Oprm1, Oprk1, and Oprl1 were weakly engaged in Pvalb, so this is a failure to find convergence rather than proof of receptor-family divergence.

summary: The absence of an adjusted Oprd1 knockdown transcriptional state should not be read as evidence against delta-opioid agonist biology.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic DOR hypotheses in mood and pain are based on ligand-evoked GPCR, phosphorylation, synaptic, and behavioral effects; a negative pooled knockdown scRNA contrast is a poor proxy for those acute pharmacological mechanisms.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: This warning does not validate any specific DOR agonist; it only limits interpretation of the negative Perturb-seq result.

summary: Mc2r perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptional effect in any profiled brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This is the primary dataset result: isolated nominal genes should not be treated as validated downstream MC2R biology.
main_caveats: A null DE signature can reflect absent receptor expression, inefficient editing or CRISPRi, small perturbed-cell numbers, or a nontranscriptional phenotype.

summary: The Mc2r transcript was almost never assayed and showed no Wilcoxon evidence of knockdown where present, matching an off-adrenal brain context rather than an engaged ACTH receptor state.
why_it_matters: The lack of target engagement makes the global null result biologically interpretable as absence of an adrenal ACTH-receptor program from these cells, not as proof that MC2R signaling is intrinsically inert.

summary: Mc2r signatures were essentially uncorrelated with available melanocortin paralog, Agrp, Gnas, Adcy3, and Adcy5 perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues against pooling Mc2r with central melanocortin MC3R/MC4R or generic cAMP perturbations in this brain dataset; an MRAP-dependent ACTH receptor is not interchangeable with the neural melanocortin receptors.

summary: The brain Perturb-seq null is an off-target-tissue result relative to MC2R disease genetics and MC2R agonist drug mechanisms.
why_it_matters: FGD and corticotropin/cosyntropin pharmacology center on adrenal ACTH-MC2R-MRAP signaling; a negative neuronal transcriptomic screen should not be used to deprioritize adrenal MC2R agonism or to infer adrenal safety.

summary: Measured phenylalanine-catabolism, BH4-regeneration, and monoamine-synthesis transcripts were not detectably regulated after Pah targeting.

summary: Pah had no close same-cell positive or negative perturbation neighbor by whole-score correlation.

summary: The null brain-cell-autonomous response reinforces that PAH therapeutic biology should not be inferred from neuronal Pah perturbation signatures alone.

summary: Clpp loss-of-function produced a sparse, mostly buffered brain transcriptional phenotype, and the target transcript itself showed only nominal depletion.
why_it_matters: CLPP is a conserved mitochondrial matrix protease and recessive CLPP loss causes organismal disease, so the near absence of corrected expression changes argues that partial acute transcript depletion in these neuronal cell classes is not enough to trigger a broad steady-state RNA response.
main_caveats: The target transcript did not pass FDR correction in any cell type, so the negative result could reflect incomplete guide activity, transcript detectability limits, or a protein-level phenotype not captured by single-cell RNA-seq.

summary: Rbm45 up-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was the only FDR-significant Clpp-associated event.

summary: Clpp knockdown did not induce a detectable ATF5/ATF4/DDIT3 mitochondrial unfolded-protein or integrated-stress transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: The result separates partial Clpp depletion from the canonical stress-response readouts that are often used to detect mitochondrial proteotoxic stress, which cautions against scoring CLPP activity from Ddit3, Atf4, Atf5, Hspd1, or Hspe1 alone in this dataset.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was measured; transient, translational, or proteolytic stress responses could have been missed.

summary: Clpp and its ClpXP unfoldase partner Clpx were not transcriptomic phenocopies.
why_it_matters: CLPP and CLPX form the same mitochondrial ATP-dependent protease, so an orthogonal Clpp-Clpx signature argues that low-efficiency loss-of-function of the proteolytic barrel and unfoldase should not be treated as interchangeable in this screen.
main_caveats: Both perturbations individually had no FDR<0.05 downstream rows, so the near-zero correlation may reflect weak perturbations rather than a true mechanistic opposition.

summary: Lonp1, but not Clpp, elicited a corrected stress-like response in mitochondrial proteostasis space, led by Ddit3 and Herpud1 in specific brain cell types.

main_caveats: The compared perturbations differ in perturbed-cell counts and guide efficacy, and Lonp1 effects were used as a dataset-internal contrast rather than a matched rescue experiment.

summary: A buffered Clpp knockdown signature should not be read as evidence that pharmacologic CLPP activation is silent in brain cells.
why_it_matters: ONC201-like compounds directly bind and activate CLPP and can drive ATF4/CHOP-linked mitochondrial stress; the Perturb-seq assay modeled partial loss of Clpp rather than hyperactivation, and it did not induce Atf4 or Ddit3.
main_caveats: Drug exposure, dose, cell state, and gain-of-function CLPP activation are not represented in the CRISPR knockdown readout.

summary: The best-engaged Ctnnd2 perturbations were self-only at q<0.05, indicating a buffered or non-transcriptional acute response.

summary: Npy2r perturbation is transcriptionally buffered across the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.

summary: The apparent L5 ET CTX Glut tail is nominal and should be treated as a validation lead, not as a discovered Npy2r-regulated program.

summary: Npy1r and Npy5r did not behave as interchangeable Npy2r paralog signatures.

summary: Npy2r did not map onto the expected inhibitory-cAMP or melanocortin appetite neighborhoods at the transcriptome level.

summary: Known synaptic and appetite effects of Y2R are more likely ligand-, compartment-, and circuit-dependent than constitutive transcriptional outputs in these broad cell classes.

summary: Otx2, Nr2e3, Nrl, Rax, Rorb and Rxrg did not reveal a Crx-like retinal transcription-factor module in the brain dataset.

summary: A transcriptome-wide Crx signature-neighbor scan found only weak positive and negative correlations.

summary: Ror1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the analyzed mouse-brain cell types.

summary: The Ror1 run yields no corrected neuronal biomarker that could be used to infer CNS liabilities of ROR1-targeted cancer therapies.

summary: Kcnq1 targeting produced neither measurable Kcnq1 transcript depletion nor FDR-significant downstream expression changes in the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The safest biological interpretation is that this perturbation did not create a usable neuronal Kcnq1 loss-of-function state, consistent with the gene being very low or absent in adult brain rather than revealing a silent ion-channel program.

summary: No Kcnq1-responsive neuronal subtype emerged; the largest nominal genes, led by Gas6 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, remained below FDR significance and recurrent nominal genes changed with mixed signs.

why_it_matters: If Kcnq1 loss were sensed by a neuronal Kv7 feedback circuit, one might expect family-level RNA compensation; none was FDR-supported in this assay.

summary: The Kcnq1 Perturb-seq result should not be used as a central nervous system Kv7 drug-response surrogate.

main_caveats: The dataset is genetic perturbation in mouse neuronal cell classes, not an acute channel-opener or blocker experiment.

summary: A dataset-wide signature-neighbor search did not uncover a strong convergent or anti-correlated program for Kcnq1.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive and negative neighbors were weak CA3 correlations with unrelated perturbations, so there is no hidden pathway neighbor that rescues the otherwise null Kcnq1 phenotype.

main_caveats: Pearson correlations were computed over Wilcoxon scores without replicate-level uncertainty or null calibration; weak correlations should not be interpreted mechanistically.

summary: Gfm2 targeting produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response across 22 neuronal cell-type result sets.

summary: Gfm2 targeting did not alter mtDNA-encoded OXPHOS mRNA abundance, even though GFM2 acts at mitochondrial translation termination.

main_caveats: The dataset assays RNA rather than nascent mitochondrial translation, OXPHOS protein abundance, or respiration; weak Gfm2 mRNA depletion limits the inference.

summary: No robust Gfm2-selective cell type emerged; the lowest adjusted p values were two non-significant singleton genes in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.

why_it_matters: Human recessive GFM2 variants cause early neurological mitochondrial disease with OXPHOS defects, so an intervention that lowers GFM2 would be expected to carry mitochondrial liability even if this acute mouse screen was quiet.
