main_caveats: The comparison uses weak Foxa2 signatures and mostly mismatched assayed cell types rather than embryonic Foxa2-positive ventral midbrain progenitors.

summary: The largest Foxa2 nominal hits were cell-type singletons with no recurrent module and no strong positive or negative signature neighbor.

summary: The negative neuronal Perturb-seq result is consistent with GATA2 biology being primarily hematopoietic/endothelial in the disease setting rather than a broad postmitotic-neuron dependency.

summary: Guk1 perturbation reproducibly lowered the target transcript but produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome in any assayed brain cell class.

summary: Pde1a and Uqcrc2 upregulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut forms a small, pathway-adjacent but exploratory candidate response to Guk1 perturbation.

main_caveats: Single cell type, q=0.116156, no direct GUK1 to APP literature identified, and no broader APP module was FDR-significant.

summary: The represented nucleotide-related perturbations Nt5c2 and Nme7 did not phenocopy Guk1 across matched cell types.

main_caveats: Most proximal STRING neighbors were not targeted in the library, and Nme7 target engagement was weak.

summary: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed the strongest nominal Guk1 self-depletion and Tjp1/Pdzd8 induction but still lacked a significant downstream program.
why_it_matters: This localizes the best candidate cell-type response while emphasizing that the signature is not robust enough for pathway assignment.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Tjp1 and Pdzd8 did not pass FDR 0.05; the all-target correlation scan found no strong signature neighbor.

summary: RNA buffering after partial Guk1 perturbation should not be interpreted as evidence that enzymatic GUK1 inhibition or guanosine-analog prodrug activation would be biologically silent in neurons.
why_it_matters: GUK1 is catalytically upstream of guanine nucleotide and guanosine-analog metabolite phosphorylation, processes that may change without a large mRNA signature.
main_caveats: No GUK1 inhibitors, prodrugs, metabolites, or protein activity were profiled in this Perturb-seq experiment.

summary: The E2f1 perturbation showed no statistically supported on-target E2f1 RNA reduction in any of 23 assayed neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: Without target-transcript engagement, the experiment cannot be interpreted as a successful E2F1 loss-of-function screen in these cells.
main_caveats: The perturbed cells may still have altered E2F1 protein or guide effects not visible at the E2f1 RNA measurement; no protein data were available.

summary: E2f1 had no FDR-significant downstream genes, including in the three best-powered cell classes.
why_it_matters: The sparse nominal hits should not be organized into a strong E2F1 pathway signature or overinterpreted as cell-type-specific biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: FDR correction was gene-wise within each contrast; weak effects below the detection limit could be missed.

summary: E2f4 and Rb1, but not E2f1, induced a DNA-replication/G1-S module in multiple neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the dataset can detect E2F/RB cell-cycle transcriptional de-repression, while the E2f1 perturbation does not phenocopy related RB/E2F nodes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations also had weak target-transcript knockdown, so the contrast is at the level of observed transcriptomic signatures rather than validated protein loss.

summary: E2f6 was nominally up-regulated after E2f1 perturbation in two subclasses, making it a possible E2F-family repressor feedback marker.
why_it_matters: E2F6 could buffer E2F transcriptional output if the nominal recurrence is real, but the evidence is only hypothesis-generating.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Both E2f6 rows had FDR=1.0; recurrence was limited to 2 of 23 cell classes.

summary: Basal E2f1 perturbation did not activate or suppress a detectable E2F1 neuronal-apoptosis or G1/S marker panel.
why_it_matters: Reports of E2F1 in neuronal death are largely stress-dependent; these data indicate that unstressed mouse-brain perturbation with weak E2f1 RNA engagement is insufficient to reproduce that program.
main_caveats: The experiment lacked stroke, DNA-damage, or activity-deprivation stimuli and therefore did not directly test the contexts in which E2F1-dependent neuronal apoptosis was reported.

summary: Restricted top-signature neighbor scans did not uncover a robust hidden convergence or opposing module for E2f1.
why_it_matters: The weak nearest-neighbor correlations reduce support for assigning the E2f1 response to a receptor, disease-family, or pathway-neighbor program on signature similarity alone.
main_caveats: Top-neighbor scans used the 200 strongest E2f1 scores per cell class; they are sensitive to nominal outliers when the seed signature has no FDR-supported genes.

summary: Bckdhb perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: BCKDHB is a causal metabolic-enzyme subunit in BCAA catabolism, so the dataset argues that acute partial Bckdhb repression is metabolically relevant but transcriptionally buffered or underpowered in this Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was only nominally changed and perturbed-cell counts were modest.

summary: Nominal on-target Bckdhb reduction was confined to six of 21 cell classes and was clearest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest evidence for engagement is not pan-neuronal; downstream interpretation should weight cell classes by their measured target-transcript shift rather than pooling all 21 equally.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type specificity is based on nominal self-expression statistics; no Bckdhb target row survived FDR correction.

summary: Core BCKDH and BCAA-catabolic transcripts were not transcriptionally compensated after Bckdhb targeting.
why_it_matters: Bckdha, Dbt, Dld, Bckdk, Ppm1k, Bcat1, Bcat2, and Ivd are biochemical neighbors of BCKDHB, but their RNA abundances did not form a feedback signature after partial Bckdhb depletion.
main_caveats: The conclusion is limited to mRNA abundance and does not assay BCKDH enzymatic flux or BCKDHA phosphorylation.

summary: Available BCAA-pathway perturbations Bckdk, Dld, and Ivd did not converge with Bckdhb at the transcriptomic-signature level.
why_it_matters: The absence of score correlation separates Bckdhb RNA depletion from perturbations of a BCKDH regulator, a shared E3 dehydrogenase subunit, and downstream branched-chain catabolism, despite their curated biochemical proximity.
main_caveats: All compared perturbations were weak by FDR, and Bckdha plus Dbt were absent as perturbation targets.

summary: No strong positive or inverse whole-signature neighbor was detectable for Bckdhb in the two best-engaged cell classes.
why_it_matters: The weak global neighbor structure suggests that the Bckdhb result is not hiding a reproducible module under a different target name.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to two cell types and to correlation of weak transcriptomic signatures; the top neighbor gene identities should not be interpreted mechanistically.

summary: Bckdhb transcript depletion should not be treated as a transcriptional surrogate for BCKDK loss or BCKDK inhibition.
why_it_matters: BCKDHB loss disables the E1 decarboxylase arm that is deficient in MSUD, whereas BCKDK loss relieves inhibitory phosphorylation of BCKDH; the dataset shows no Bckdk-Bckdhb RNA convergence, so therapeutic hypotheses should be tested with BCAA/BCKA flux and phospho-BCKDH readouts.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure metabolites or BCKDH phosphorylation, and Dbt was not directly perturbed in this dataset.

summary: Flnb-targeting cells showed a consistent weak downward shift of the target transcript but no FDR-significant downstream DE in any of 21 cell types.
why_it_matters: FLNB is an actin-cytoskeleton scaffold, so the lack of a stable RNA module suggests either incomplete mRNA knockdown, protein-level buffering, or biology not captured by steady-state single-cell transcriptomes.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was only nominal in 5/21 cell types; protein knockdown and morphology were not measured.

summary: Nominal Flnb target engagement was concentrated in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while several cortical and cerebellar classes had very weak target-row effects.
why_it_matters: The cell-type restriction helps avoid overinterpreting the full 21-cell-type panel as a uniform perturbation and points to hindbrain/midbrain classes as the only contexts with measurable target RNA response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The subset is defined by nominal target rows only; no target row passed FDR correction.

summary: The strongest nominal genes in Flnb signatures were isolated outliers rather than a recurrent effector module.
why_it_matters: Without recurrent or FDR-significant downstream genes, genes such as Pgm2l1, Snhg11, Gsk3b, and Sys1 should not be promoted as FLNB biomarkers from this dataset.
main_caveats: This rules out a recurrent mRNA signature at the measured depth, not post-transcriptional cytoskeletal phenotypes.

summary: Flnb signatures were uncoupled from Actg1, Actb, Itgb1, Cdc42, and Rac1 perturbation signatures despite FLNB's focal-adhesion and actin-cytoskeleton network context.
why_it_matters: This argues against treating Flnb knockdown as a simple transcriptional proxy for integrin, Rho-GTPase, or core actin perturbation in these mouse-brain cell types.
main_caveats: Related perturbations differ in knockdown strength and Flnb itself showed weak engagement; correlations used genome-wide Wilcoxon scores rather than protein phenotypes.

summary: Published FLNB skeletal, chondrocyte, and actin-reorganization phenotypes are not reproduced as a strong neuronal mRNA program after Flnb targeting in this dataset.
why_it_matters: The result cautions that FLNB disease variants and Flnb neuronal CRISPR perturbation need not have the same direction, magnitude, or readout, especially when disease alleles can alter actin binding or focal adhesions directly.
main_caveats: The literature is mostly skeletal or fibroblast/chondrocyte based, whereas the dataset is mouse-brain single-cell RNA; lack of FDR hits is also partly confounded by weak target engagement.

summary: Chrna2 perturbation did not measurably deplete the Chrna2 transcript in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: The target encodes a ligand-gated ion-channel subunit, so a null downstream signature is only interpretable if the receptor transcript is actually reduced. Here the primary result is weak RNA-level target engagement rather than evidence that alpha2 nAChRs are dispensable.
main_caveats: Wilcoxon target-RNA scores are indirect single-cell RNA measurements; sparse target rows produced uninformative large logFC values, so interpretation should rely on the near-zero scores and non-significant p values.

summary: No cell type produced an FDR-significant Chrna2 downstream transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a robust, recurrent transcriptomic program in the assayed broad classes; the strongest Acap3 and Dennd6b peaks were close to but above FDR 0.05 and were not recurrent pathway anchors.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: FDR failure does not exclude electrophysiological effects or rare-subclass effects; the L5-6 IT Glut nominal peak used only 43 perturbed cells.

summary: The negative Chrna2 profile is probably a resolution mismatch with the narrow alpha2-interneuron populations described in the literature.
why_it_matters: Alpha2 biology is reported in sharply defined OLM, Martinotti, Renshaw, and striatal Chrna2 interneurons, with many striatal Chrna2 interneurons being parvalbumin fast-spiking cells, whereas this analysis perturbed broad Pvalb, Sst, and CNU-LGE GABA classes with no measurable Chrna2 target shift. Dilution of rare Chrna2-positive interneurons is therefore a more plausible explanation than pan-GABAergic buffering.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset labels are broad and do not prove which OLM, Martinotti, Renshaw, or striatal Chrna2-positive subclasses were present; target engagement was weak even in the broad classes.

summary: Chrna2 signatures did not converge with available nicotinic receptor subunits or cholinergic neighbors, even where Chrnb2, Chrna4, or Ache perturbations had clear target-RNA depletion.
why_it_matters: Complex membership or pathway membership did not translate into a shared transcriptional attractor. The contrast is strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, where related perturbations knocked down their own mRNAs but remained essentially uncorrelated with Chrna2.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is a restricted signature-correlation analysis; lack of Chrna2 target engagement means that the absence of convergence cannot be assigned to true alpha2-specific biology alone.

summary: The Chrna2 null transcriptome should not be taken as evidence that lowering alpha2 nAChR activity is safe or inert.
why_it_matters: Human CHRNA2 coding variants are linked to sleep-related hypermotor epilepsy and benign familial infantile seizures, with both increased-sensitivity and loss-of-function functional data reported. Because the mouse Perturb-seq signature did not knock down Chrna2, it provides no directional support for alpha2 activation versus inhibition.
main_caveats: Disease variants are human coding changes in receptors, not mouse guide-induced transcriptome signatures; the dataset is target-engagement limited.

summary: Cacng2 perturbation was transcriptionally silent at genome-wide FDR thresholds in every tested brain cell class.
why_it_matters: Cacng2 encodes the synaptic AMPAR auxiliary protein stargazin, but this Perturb-seq readout did not reveal a robust cell-autonomous RNA program downstream of the perturbation.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not FDR depleted, so the negative result establishes absence of a detected RNA signature rather than dispensability of the Cacng2 protein.

summary: The few cell classes with nominal Cacng2 mRNA reduction still showed no FDR-supported downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The result argues that partial target-transcript displacement, when present, was below the threshold needed to launch a broad RNA response, consistent with a synaptic trafficking molecule whose primary effect may be post-transcriptional.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The Cacng2 transcript FDR was 1.0 in these contrasts; the buffered interpretation is nominal and should be treated as subthreshold.

summary: Cacng2 did not transcriptionally phenocopy direct AMPAR/PSD complex perturbations that showed measurable self-transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: Even though stargazin is curated as an AMPAR complex component and is linked to Dlg4 and Gria receptors, the Cacng2 score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Gria1-4, Dlg4, and other postsynaptic comparator signatures.
main_caveats: Comparator correlations used weak genome-wide score vectors, and the strongest Cacng2 limitation remains weak self-transcript engagement.

summary: TARP gamma paralogs Cacng2, Cacng3, and Cacng8 shared a family-level absence of FDR-significant RNA responses rather than a common induced module.
why_it_matters: The pattern is compatible with the literature view that AMPARs are regulated by a partially redundant TARP family, but the dataset did not identify a compensatory Cacng3/Cacng8-like transcriptional state after Cacng2 perturbation.
main_caveats: All three TARP perturbations had weak or non-significant target-transcript effects, so this is suggestive of transcriptional buffering but cannot test protein-level redundancy.

summary: CACNG2 disease mechanisms are more likely to be missed by single-cell RNA-state readouts than by synaptic physiology or localization assays.
why_it_matters: Stargazer and V143L models link CACNG2 to seizures, hippocampal transmission, and intellectual-disability-like behavior; the Perturb-seq null narrows the expected proximal assay from cell-body transcriptomics toward AMPAR trafficking, synaptic structure, and electrophysiology.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure AMPAR currents, receptor localization, dendritic spines, seizures, or developmental phenotypes.

summary: The absence of a reproducible scRNA signature warns against using Cacng2-regulated mRNA biomarkers alone to track AMPAR/TARP target engagement.
why_it_matters: Human CACNG2 is associated with neurologic phenotypes and marked as small-molecule tractable, but the mouse screen indicates that AMPAR/TARP modulation may need pharmacodynamic assays closer to receptor localization or synaptic function.
main_caveats: The warning is based on partial genetic perturbation with weak target-transcript depletion, not on an acute pharmacologic Cacng2 or AMPAR modulator.

summary: Cog5 perturbation produced a sparse transcriptional phenotype: Cog5 was measured in 21 cell types but never reached on-target FDR<0.05, and only one downstream row reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: COG5 is a core Golgi tethering subunit, so the result argues that partial Cog5 perturbation in this assay did not produce a broad canonical mRNA stress or trafficking program.
main_caveats: The negative result is confounded by weak target engagement and small cell counts in most signatures.

summary: Smarcal1 up-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut was the sole FDR-significant Cog5-associated gene.
why_it_matters: It is the only corrected marker that can label the Cog5 response in the dataset, but its lack of recurrence makes it exploratory.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Only 40 Cog5-targeted cells; Cog5 itself was not nominally significant in this cell type; no other cell type reproduced the Smarcal1 effect.

summary: 145 MH-LH TH Glut had the largest nominal Cog5 decrease but no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The observation is compatible with buffering of partial Cog5 loss or with COG biology being expressed at Golgi-trafficking and glycosylation levels rather than as a large RNA program.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only 37 perturbed cells and the Cog5 row itself had FDR=1.0 despite a nominal p value.

summary: Cog4, the only other assayed COG1-COG8 member, did not show a detectable Cog5-like signature.
why_it_matters: COG4 directly contacts COG5 in the COG assembly, so the lack of convergence prevents the weak Cog5 signature from being generalized to the full COG complex in this Perturb-seq dataset.
main_caveats: Cog4 itself had low cell counts and no strong on-target or downstream signal; COG1, COG2, COG3, COG6, COG7, and COG8 were not available as perturbation comparators.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Vps54 and Stx16 Golgi/TGN-neighbor perturbations were much stronger than Cog5 and did not align with the Cog5 score vector.
why_it_matters: This shows that the Cog5 null result is not simply because this cell class cannot produce a trafficking-related Perturb-seq response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Vps54 and Vps53 are GARP-associated pathway neighbors rather than COG subunits; Stx16 is a SNARE, so this is a neighborhood contrast, not a same-complex comparison.

summary: Cog5 had no strong positive or negative Perturb-seq signature neighbor across its profiled cell types.
why_it_matters: A weak isolated target can sometimes be interpreted through phenocopying neighbors; that rescue strategy did not reveal a coherent Cog5 transcriptional module.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations summarize whole-gene score vectors and may miss localized pathway effects.

summary: Human loss of COG5 causes COG5-CDG, so the sparse mouse neuronal RNA phenotype should not be interpreted as safety of COG5 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Known COG5 pathology involves glycosylation and trafficking defects that can be developmental or post-transcriptional; ChEMBL also did not return a directional COG5 mechanism-of-action record.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain Perturb-seq rather than a human developmental CDG or glycomics assay.

summary: Arnt2 perturbation did not produce an FDR-significant transcriptional response in any of the 23 measured mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: ARNT2 is a nuclear bHLH-PAS transcription factor, so the absence of corrected DE hits makes the central result a negative Perturb-seq result rather than a pathway activation map.
main_caveats: The targeted transcript itself was only weakly and nominally reduced; the result rules out a strong detected response in this screen but not ARNT2 biology after deeper knockout, developmental loss, stimulation, or in absent lineages.

summary: The dataset does not recapitulate the developmental ARNT2 loss-of-function phenotype linked to hypothalamo-pituitary and neuroendocrine biology.
why_it_matters: Mouse Arnt2 null alleles and SIM1/ARNT2 studies point to embryonic hypothalamic neuroendocrine differentiation, and human ARNT2 loss of function causes Webb-Dattani syndrome; the broad negative mouse-brain Perturb-seq response suggests that those phenotypes are stage-, lineage-, or perturbation-depth dependent.
main_caveats: The assayed HYa/HY/TH labels are broad and may not contain the PVN/SON neuroendocrine populations or developmental windows in which Arnt2 and Sim1 are essential; Arnt2 knockdown was weak.

summary: ARNT2 did not form a correlated perturbation module with bHLH-PAS partners or with the measured NPAS4/BDNF activity-dependent axis.
why_it_matters: ARNT2 is known to dimerize or functionally connect with AHR, HIF-family proteins, SIM1, and NPAS4; the near-zero score-vector correlations argue that this basal Perturb-seq setting did not engage a shared AHR/HIF/SIM1/NPAS4 transcriptional program.
main_caveats: The comparison uses weak Arnt2 signatures and genome-wide score correlations; HIF, AHR, and NPAS4 programs are ligand-, hypoxia-, developmental-, or activity-gated, none of which is guaranteed to be present in the observed cells.

summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed the only nominal on-target Arnt2 decreases below p < 0.01, yet neither cell type had any FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: These two classes provide the best internal test of whether partial Arnt2 transcript loss was sufficient; the answer was no, consistent with either buffering, residual ARNT2 protein, or inadequate perturbation depth.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: On-target reductions were nominal, modest, and not FDR-significant, so a technical explanation is at least as plausible as biological compensation.

summary: The strongest nominal downstream genes were isolated cell-type signals and should not be treated as Arnt2 biomarkers in this screen.
why_it_matters: Slc4a10/Mbtps2 in 191 MB P MY GABA, Scpep1 in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, and Acvr2b/Bbip1/Vps4b/Scn2a in 217 P MY Pineal Glut looked large by raw p value or logFC but failed FDR correction, with the pineal result coming from only 23 perturbed cells.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: This is a robustness interpretation, not proof that the named genes are unrelated to ARNT2 in other systems.

summary: Dst perturbation produced no transcriptome-wide significant differential-expression response and did not measurably deplete the assayed Dst transcript in any of the 22 sampled neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: The safest primary readout is a negative or buffered result rather than a Dst-regulated gene program; every downstream interpretation must account for weak gene-level target engagement.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The gene-level Dst transcript may not report all isoform-specific knockdown or editing events; structural axonal phenotypes and protein localization were not assayed.

summary: The apparent Dst hotspots in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 155 MB Glut, Pvalb and thalamic glutamatergic neurons were only isolated nominal hits, with no same-direction recurrent gene module.
why_it_matters: Nominal top genes such as Efnb2 or Pak1 should not be promoted to pathway biomarkers without replication because the most extreme rows had FDR values of 0.967 to 1.0 and recurred poorly across cell types.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a statistical interpretation of the dataset only; no external pathway claim is made for the nominal genes.

summary: Dst was essentially orthogonal to spectraplakin/plakin and microtubule-transport perturbations, even though related cytoskeletal perturbations such as Macf1, Map1b, Dync1h1 and Tubb3 showed effective self-depletion in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: The Dst null result is not explained by a general inability to detect perturbation of cytoskeletal genes; it is more consistent with a Dst-specific engagement, isoform, or sampled-cell-context limitation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations use weak Dst score vectors and therefore mainly show absence of co-signature, not true antagonism.

summary: The central glutamatergic and GABAergic Perturb-seq assay did not reproduce the sensory-neuron axonal-transport and cytoskeletal-collapse biology known from Dst loss-of-function models and human HSAN-VI.
why_it_matters: Literature points to long-projecting sensory/autonomic neurons and protein-level axonal architecture as the disease-relevant context; this dataset argues against treating acute Dst perturbation in sampled central neurons as a direct HSAN-VI state.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset does not include dorsal-root or autonomic neurons and has weak evidence for Dst mRNA depletion.

summary: This Perturb-seq result offers no evidence for a beneficial direction of DST inhibition or activation, and loss-of-function genetics make indiscriminate DST suppression a plausible sensory-neuron and skin-liability risk.
why_it_matters: The combination of weak on-target response, known human recessive DST disease, and absence of ChEMBL mechanism-of-action drugs argues that Dst should be followed with isoform- and cell-type-resolved functional assays before any directional therapeutic hypothesis is advanced.
main_caveats: This is a warning about evidence strength and safety context, not proof that partial DST modulation is toxic in every tissue.

summary: Dnal1 transcript engagement was detectable but weak and uneven, with the clearest nominal decrease in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only 5/22 cell types reaching nominal p<0.05 for Dnal1 itself.
why_it_matters: The partial on-target effect limits how strongly downstream negative results can be interpreted as complete Dnal1 loss of function.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Even the strongest Dnal1 self-decrease had FDR=0.215; raw guide-level expression data were unavailable.

summary: Dnal1 perturbation produced no FDR<0.05 transcriptomic changes in any analyzed cell type.
why_it_matters: The screen does not reveal a robust downstream module or pathway output for Dnal1 in the assayed neuronal classes.
main_caveats: FDR buffering may reflect incomplete Dnal1 depletion; a few nominal top genes should be treated as hypothesis-generating only.

summary: Dnal1 signatures did not converge with screened ciliary-neighbor perturbations, and direct outer-dynein-arm comparators were absent from the screen.
why_it_matters: DNAL1 is an outer-dynein-arm axonemal protein, so the lack of alignment with broader IFT/BBS/Foxj/Rfx/Cep ciliary signatures argues against a general neuronal ciliary transcriptional program after partial Dnal1 suppression.
main_caveats: Correlation was transcriptome-wide and restricted to available perturbations; the closest known DNAL1/DNAH5 outer-arm machinery was not directly tested.

summary: The buffered Dnal1 response in neuronal classes refines DNAL1 primary-ciliary-dyskinesia biology to the expected motile-ciliated context rather than contradicting it.
why_it_matters: DNAL1 disease relevance is strongest in multiciliated airway, nodal, sperm, and ependymal biology; this screen should not be used to claim that DNAL1 loss is benign in those tissues.
main_caveats: The conclusion compares mouse neuronal Perturb-seq with human and database evidence from ciliated tissues; no ependymal perturbation signature was present.

summary: The apparent Dnal1-Cep290 similarity in 308 CB GABA was no stronger than Safe_target background and occurred with weak Dnal1 target engagement.
why_it_matters: This prevents a small scalar correlation from being misread as biological convergence between Dnal1 and Cep290.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to one cell type; correlations do not measure guide efficacy or direct pathway activity.

summary: Nkx6-2 guide-positive neurons did not show an FDR-supported transcriptomic response in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation of this target in the current file is absence of a detectable neuron-autonomous response, not a positive pathway activation or repression signature.
cell_types: 22 sampled Nkx6-2 neuronal Glut/GABA classes
main_caveats: The null is conditional on modest per-class perturbation counts and the failure to measurably reduce Nkx6-2 RNA; glial cell states were not represented.

summary: The screen samples the neuronal compartment in which Nkx6-2 is not measurably engaged, whereas prior biology places NKX6-2 in oligodendrocytes, myelin paranodes, and hypomyelinating disease.
why_it_matters: This reconciles a strong disease/myelin gene with a flat Perturb-seq profile: the dataset is testing mostly the wrong cellular context for known NKX6-2 biology.
cell_types: 22 sampled Nkx6-2 neuronal Glut/GABA classes
main_caveats: A neuronal null cannot exclude roles in rare neurons, developmental progenitors, or oligodendrocytes absent from the differential-expression table.

summary: Nkx6-2 perturbation did not move an oligodendrocyte/myelin transcript module, including Mbp, Plp1, Myrf, Sox10, Olig1, Olig2, Sox9, and Tcf7l2.
why_it_matters: NKX6-2 is linked to myelination and to MBP/PLP1 promoter regulation, so the absence of these transcripts confirms that the guide-positive neuronal cells did not enter a glial or myelin regulatory state.
cell_types: 22 sampled Nkx6-2 neuronal Glut/GABA classes
main_caveats: These genes are themselves expected to be low or absent in many neuronal classes, limiting sensitivity for myelin-module repression or induction.

summary: Nkx6-2 did not converge with screened oligodendrocyte-lineage, SOX-family, or NKX-family perturbations, and unbiased signature neighbors were weak and partly safe-target-like.
why_it_matters: The lack of shared signatures argues against rescuing the weak Nkx6-2 phenotype by transferring pathway labels from related transcription factors or from top nearest neighbors.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All comparisons used weak restricted signatures; the strong SOX10/OLIG2/NKX6.2 literature is an overexpression reprogramming context, not neuronal Nkx6-2 loss.

summary: The only cell-type-biased Nkx6-2 signal was a subthreshold nominal cluster in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, with isolated Ensa and Ogdh nominal peaks elsewhere.
why_it_matters: This preserves the strongest measured genes while preventing an overcall of a validated Nkx6-2 response or pathway.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Minimum adjusted p value was 0.452; this should be treated as a subthreshold hint only.

summary: The flat neuronal Perturb-seq profile should not be read as safety de-risking for NKX6-2 inhibition in myelinating cells.
why_it_matters: Human NKX6-2 variation causes hypomyelination, and the dataset lacks the oligodendrocyte/white-matter compartment where loss would be expected to matter most.
cell_types: 22 sampled Nkx6-2 neuronal Glut/GABA classes
main_caveats: This is a context warning, not evidence for a specific drug effect; NKX6-2 is a transcription factor and no compound perturbation was profiled.

direction: Ddit3 and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases up; Kcnc2 down
summary: Bdp1 perturbation produced a multiple-testing-significant response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Ddit3 and six cytosolic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase genes were induced and Kcnc2 was repressed.
why_it_matters: A nominally ubiquitous RNA polymerase III initiation factor resolved into a sharply thalamic, amino-acid/tRNA-stress-like response rather than a broad neuronal transcriptional collapse.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The assay measured mRNAs rather than Pol III tRNA products; the dataset does not prove that uncharged tRNAs or ATF4 protein increased.

summary: The Bdp1 thalamic signature was a weaker member of a tRNA-handling stress state that is strongest after Elp1 or Elp2 perturbation in the same cell type.
why_it_matters: Convergence with Elongator complex perturbations links Pol III-dependent tRNA production and wobble-uridine tRNA modification to the same Ddit3/aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase output in thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Bdp1-to-Elp1/Elp2 correlations were modest and signature-based; there is no direct evidence here that BDP1 biochemically acts through Elongator.

summary: Bdp1 and Polr3b diverged in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut despite belonging to the same RNA polymerase III transcriptional system.
why_it_matters: The result argues that the Bdp1 Ddit3/aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase program is not a generic consequence of perturbing any Pol III component in the dataset and may depend on lesion strength, subcomplex architecture, or guide efficacy.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Polr3b was the only exact Pol III pathway neighbor available, target transcript knockdown was weak for both Bdp1 and Polr3b, and the contrast is transcriptomic rather than a Pol III activity assay.

summary: Ddit3 plus cytosolic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase mRNAs, especially Mars1, are candidate readouts for Bdp1-driven tRNA/amino-acid stress.
why_it_matters: These genes were the top FDR Bdp1 hits in thalamic cells and reappeared as nominal hits in 155 MB Glut, making them a compact hypothesis-generating marker panel for follow-up validation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only the thalamic genes passed FDR; the midbrain observation was nominal and should be treated as an echo, not a replicated cell-type effect.

summary: The acute Bdp1 response refines Pol III disease expectations to a vulnerable neuronal ISR module rather than simply reproducing the broader Polr3a/Polr3b disease program.
why_it_matters: POLR3 disease models connect tRNA depletion to ISR and neurodegeneration; this single-cell perturbation nominates a thalamic glutamatergic population as an early stress-responsive context while warning that direct TFIIIB inhibition could be neurotoxic even when Bdp1 mRNA knockdown appears modest.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The published Polr3a model is a chronic organismal mutant whereas this dataset is an acute pooled perturbation in selected neuronal classes; oligodendrocytes and tRNA abundances were not represented in the DE table.

direction: no significant target-transcript knockdown or downstream response outside 151
summary: Most Bdp1-assayed cell types showed no FDR-significant downstream mRNA response, but this is better interpreted as weak or unverified target engagement than as true buffering.
why_it_matters: It prevents overcalling universal resilience to Bdp1 loss: the target transcript itself never reached FDR significance, and non-thalamic classes therefore remain inconclusive.
main_caveats: Target mRNA is an imperfect guide-efficiency metric in CRISPR perturbation data and does not measure BDP1 protein or Pol III transcriptional output.

summary: Adarb1 target-transcript reduction is FDR-significant in only 3 of 22 assayed cell classes, with the clearest engagement in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: Downstream claims are strongest in these engaged classes; nonresponsive classes cannot be read as definitive biological absence because target engagement was often nominal or nonsignificant.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The table is target-level, not guide-level, and perturbation cell counts are modest.

summary: Flnb is a recurrent negative Adarb1-response transcript, decreasing in every tested cell class and reaching FDR significance in 12 of 22.
why_it_matters: Flnb is more recurrent than the Adarb1 mRNA row itself and is the strongest candidate abundance biomarker of the perturbation, but it is not established as a direct ADAR2 substrate.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|308 CB GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Recurrent transcript loss still needs guide-level and edit-site validation before it can be called a direct ADAR2 effect.

summary: The strongest thalamic response is a four-gene downregulated module containing Flnb, Adarb1, Flna, and Zfp941.
why_it_matters: The paired Flnb/Flna decrease highlights cytoskeletal/filamin expression as the dominant abundance phenotype in the best-engaged cell class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only four genes pass FDR in this class; the link to filamin editing is inferential because RNA edit fractions were not measured.

summary: Adarb1 perturbation does not activate a core MDA5/interferon abundance program.
why_it_matters: This separates ADAR2/Adarb1 loss from the canonical ADAR1 self-dsRNA immune phenotype and argues against treating ADAR family members as interchangeable in this brain dataset.
main_caveats: The literature benchmark is ADAR1 editing loss in non-identical systems, while this dataset is a single-cell mouse brain perturbation abundance assay.

summary: Canonical ADAR2-edited neural substrate mRNAs are unchanged in abundance after Adarb1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The pathogenic ADAR2 axis can act through editing ratios rather than substrate mRNA levels, so receptor transcripts being flat is expected to be invisible to ordinary DE while still biologically important.
main_caveats: Absence of differential abundance does not test the Q/R or other A-to-I edit fractions directly.

summary: No same-dataset paralog, antiviral neighbor, or top restricted signature neighbor cleanly phenocopies the Adarb1-Flnb state.
why_it_matters: The comparator scan keeps the Flnb result from being overgeneralized into an ADAR-family or interferon-neighborhood effect.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The signature-neighbor comparison used only the top 25 151-class genes and produced moderate scores, including nonbiological safe-target controls.

summary: ADAR2-modulating RNA-editing therapies should monitor cytoskeletal mRNAs such as Flnb in addition to intended edit sites and antiviral markers.
why_it_matters: ADAR2 deaminase is used for programmable A-to-I editing, and endogenous ADARB1 loss is epileptogenic; this dataset suggests that partial perturbation in brain cells can repeatedly move Flnb without a compensatory interferon signature.
main_caveats: This is a safety-biomarker hypothesis from perturbation DE, not a direct test of therapeutic guide RNAs or ADAR2 editor specificity.

summary: Adgrg1 CRISPRi produced no FDR-significant transcriptional phenotype in any of 22 assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset interpretation is a null or non-engaged perturbation; nominal single-gene outliers should not be promoted to pathway claims.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic CRISPRi readout; Adgrg1 target mRNA depletion itself was not significant, so the result does not establish that a well-suppressed ADGRG1 receptor is dispensable.

summary: The neuronal null refines, rather than overturns, the established ADGRG1 cortical-malformation mechanism toward developmental matrix, glial, and OPC contexts that were not the main responsive compartments in this dataset.
why_it_matters: ADGRG1 is a strong developmental-disease gene, but its best-supported brain functions involve collagen III/Gα12/13/RhoA signaling in developing cortex and TGM2-dependent OPC biology; a weak perturbation in GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons therefore is not a stringent test of the BFPP mechanism.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq cell annotations are neuronal, target knockdown was weak, and the dataset did not assay developmental pial basement membrane cells, OPCs, astrocytes, or microglia as Adgrg1 perturbation classes.

summary: Expected ADGRG1 ligand/G-protein/RhoA-axis transcripts stayed FDR-null and ADGRG1-associated perturbations failed to phenocopy Adgrg1 signatures.
why_it_matters: Canonical ADGRG1 signaling is receptor-proximal and post-transcriptional; the dataset gives no evidence that the weak Adgrg1 perturbation propagated to the COL3A1-TGM2-GNA12/GNA13-RhoA module at mRNA level.
main_caveats: RhoA activation may occur without steady-state mRNA changes, and Gna12, Gna13, Col3a1, and Tgm2 were measured transcripts rather than perturbation targets in the comparison.

summary: The few lowest Adgrg1-adjusted p values were scattered across CNU-LGE GABA, MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic, and CNU-MGE GABA classes and did not define a recurrent gene program.
why_it_matters: This prevents an apparent top gene such as Dpp6, Pex13, Zkscan2, or Fbxl5 from being mistaken for a reproducible Adgrg1 effector.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: All named genes had FDR values well above 0.05 and should be treated as exploratory nominal leads only.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor scans found no strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor for Adgrg1.
why_it_matters: The Adgrg1 null is not hiding a coherent all-target convergence detectable by whole-transcriptome score correlation in the three cell types with the smallest adjusted p values.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak, non-FDR Adgrg1 signatures, so the absence of a neighbor is more reliable than the identities of the nominal nearest neighbors.

direction: weak target decrease with no FDR-significant downstream response
summary: Igf1r perturbation produced no multiple-testing-significant transcriptomic response in any of the 20 assayed cell types and only weak on-target mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not supply a robust Igf1r loss-of-function signature even though IGF1R is an upstream receptor tyrosine kinase with canonical PI3K-AKT and RAS-MAPK outputs.
main_caveats: Igf1r mRNA may not report coding disruption or residual protein; each cell type had only 22-112 matched perturbed cells.

direction: nominal down in three cell types
summary: Only 308 CB GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut showed nominal on-target Igf1r decreases, and none had any FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: The apparent engagement was patchy rather than a broad excitatory or inhibitory neuronal response.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The cell-type pattern is based on nominal target p values with target FDR=1.0.

summary: Igf1r nominal signatures did not converge on the expected IRS, PI3K, mTOR, or MAPK pathway-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: A bona fide IGF1R perturbation would be expected to share signal with proximal IGF/insulin signaling nodes or to oppose PTEN/TSC loss, but the restricted correlations were near zero on average.
main_caveats: Correlations used only the 30 strongest nominal Igf1r genes per cell type because no FDR-significant Igf1r signature was available.

summary: Direct Pten and Tsc2 perturbations produced many significant downstream responses where Igf1r was silent.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the dataset can detect PI3K/mTOR-axis transcriptional consequences when downstream negative regulators are perturbed, so Igf1r silence is not simply a universal failure of growth-signaling DE readout.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: PTEN and TSC2 are downstream negative regulators and need not phenocopy weak upstream receptor perturbation.

direction: Igf2r on-target stronger than Igf1r or Insr
summary: Igf1r, Insr, and Igf2r showed heterogeneous target engagement and did not behave as interchangeable IGF-family receptor perturbations.
why_it_matters: Shared receptor-family membership and IGF1R-INSR pathway overlap do not justify pooling these perturbations in this screen.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The comparison is dominated by target-transcript engagement and does not isolate receptor-specific biology.

summary: The Igf1r Perturb-seq null should not be taken as evidence that pharmacologic IGF1R blockade lacks neuronal or organismal consequences.
why_it_matters: IGF1R is druggable and disease relevant, but this dataset did not achieve strong mRNA engagement for Igf1r.
main_caveats: Clinical pharmacology and human growth genetics are indirect relative to mouse-brain Perturb-seq.

summary: 155 MB Glut had FDR-significant Kif1b transcript depletion but no FDR-significant secondary gene.
why_it_matters: This separates successful local target engagement from a broad expression response and suggests that acute partial loss of a motor protein can be buffered at the mRNA level.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only RNA was measured; an axonal transport phenotype could occur without large soma transcriptional changes.

summary: Kif1b perturbation produced a selective Pvalb-interneuron Snap25 decrease with nominal decreases in Stx4a, Gad1, Pvalb, and Got2.
why_it_matters: The only FDR-significant downstream hit falls on the presynaptic/GABAergic biology most compatible with published KIF1Bβ synaptic-vesicle transport.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Snap25 was the only non-target FDR hit; the broader Pvalb marker module is nominal and hypothesis-generating.

summary: Kif1a and Kifbp did not phenocopy Kif1b in Pvalb or MB Glut despite being close KIF1B-related perturbations.
why_it_matters: A shared KIF1A/KIF1Bβ vesicle-transport pathway does not imply interchangeability at the whole-transcriptome level in this dataset.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is based on RNA signatures; KIF1A or KIFBP may still share cargo-transport biology not captured transcriptionally.

summary: Most measured cell types had no FDR-resolved Kif1b phenotype even when the Kif1b row was nominally depleted.
why_it_matters: The Kif1b response is not pan-neuronal; many classes either lacked strong target engagement or were buffered below single-gene FDR significance.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Many classes had low perturbation counts, so weak effects could be missed.

summary: Kif1b perturbation did not transcriptionally regulate Igf1r, Madd, Rab3a, Egln3, Dnm1l, or Xaf1 at FDR significance in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: Published KIF1Bβ neuropathy and tumor-suppressor mechanisms involve IGF1R transport, Rab3/MADD transport, and EglN3-linked apoptosis, but those axes were not recovered as gene-expression programs here.
main_caveats: Absence of transcript changes does not test protein trafficking, axon growth, developmental survival, or tumor suppression.

summary: Kmt2d loss is almost silent after correction in most assayed populations but produces a large, bidirectional signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The result localizes a broad enhancer regulator to a narrow neuronal response state, rather than a pan-neuronal collapse of transcription.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The assayed Kmt2d transcript itself was not significantly reduced after FDR correction, so the cell restriction could be affected by Perturb-seq sensitivity, guide activity, or protein persistence.

summary: The 151 TH response is a mixed synaptic-neuronal module: Ntng1, Nell1, Hcn3, Cntn4, Cadm2, and Nrxn1 increase, whereas Plch2, Mical2, Celf3, Prkcg, Sez6, and Dlg4 decrease.
why_it_matters: These high-ranking genes provide a compact candidate readout of Kmt2d loss in the responsive thalamic glutamatergic state and show that the response is not a uniform loss of neuronal transcripts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The marker set is transcriptomic and hypothesis-generating; individual genes were not validated by chromatin or protein assays.

summary: Kdm6a, a Kabuki gene and MLL3/4 accessory factor, is the strongest positive Kmt2d signature neighbor in 151 TH, whereas the Kmt2c paralog is weak and nonsignificant in the same cell type.
why_it_matters: The data support a Kmt2d-Kdm6a axis in this neuronal context while arguing against simple interchangeability of the Kmt2c and Kmt2d paralogs here.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The strongest Kdm6a-Kmt2d agreement appears on the restricted 314-gene Kmt2d signature; Kdm6a itself had only one FDR-level gene, and Kmt2c had only 55 perturbed cells in 151 TH.

summary: Kmt2a is one of the most anticorrelated perturbations to Kmt2d in 151 TH despite belonging to the H3K4 methyltransferase family.
why_it_matters: This separates the Kmt2d enhancer module from other KMT2-family chromatin regulators and warns against treating all H3K4 methyltransferase perturbations as equivalent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The all-gene anticorrelation is modest and transcriptomic; the mechanistic basis of the Kmt2a contrast was not tested in the dataset.

summary: Nominal Kmt2d mRNA decreases in several populations, including Pvalb and Sst GABA classes, did not translate into FDR-significant downstream programs.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpreting every directionally engaged cell type as Kmt2d dependent and highlights buffered or underpowered contexts.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Kmt2d transcript reductions were nominal rather than FDR-significant, so these are conservative negative results rather than proof of biological buffering.

summary: Because the Kmt2d-loss signature contains both up- and down-regulated synaptic genes and is highly cell-type restricted, chromatin-opening rescue strategies should be expected to have state-specific and gene-specific effects.
why_it_matters: HDAC inhibition and KDM1A inhibition can rescue phenotypes in Kmt2d-mutant mice, but the Perturb-seq signature suggests that the desired direction may differ across synaptic transcripts and cell states.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No HDAC, KDM1A, or Kmt2d-rescue perturbation was profiled in this dataset; the implication is a direction-of-effect caution, not a test of those therapies.

summary: Htr2c knockdown produced no FDR-level transcriptional response in any broad brain cell class despite a weak, mostly negative target-transcript trend.
why_it_matters: The main dataset result is negative rather than a pathway hit: basal Htr2c perturbation did not generate a reproducible DE program detectable at the broad-class Wilcoxon level.
main_caveats: Target-transcript knockdown was not FDR-significant; classes were broad and had 20-126 perturbed cells, so sparse responsive subtypes or ligand-evoked acute signaling could be missed.

summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut was the only class with nominal Htr2c target repression, but it still lacked FDR-supported downstream markers.
why_it_matters: This broad hypothalamic/cerebral-nuclei class is the best follow-up location in the assay, yet the evidence is a cell-context hint rather than a resolved POMC-neuron program.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The on-target row is nominal only and the strongest downstream rows fail FDR correction; the broad class is only indirectly matched to arcuate POMC neurons described in the literature.

summary: Htr2c signatures did not phenocopy Gq/PLC/Ca2+ effector perturbations even though HTR2C is a curated Gq/G11-coupled PLC-beta receptor.
why_it_matters: The result separates receptor loss in an unstimulated pooled transcriptome from knockdown of core Plcb1-Itpr1-Prkca/Prkcg signaling components, arguing against a constitutive linear PLC transcriptional output for Htr2c in these broad classes.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed from weak score vectors; absence of correlation is not proof that Htr2c cannot use these effectors after serotonin stimulation.

summary: 5-HT2 family and other serotonin-receptor perturbations showed near-zero transcriptional similarity to Htr2c.
why_it_matters: Htr2c should not be treated as interchangeable with Htr2a or Htr2b at the level of broad-cell-class CRISPRi transcriptomes; the weak Htr2c profile lacks a shared serotonin-receptor-family module.
main_caveats: Most serotonin-receptor perturbations also had weak on-target rows, so the finding is a lack of shared transcriptomic signal rather than a functional receptor-family hierarchy.

summary: The obesity-relevant HTR2C-POMC mechanism from genetics and physiology is not recapitulated as an Agrp/Lepr/Mc4r-like broad-class transcriptional program in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse loss-of-function data make HTR2C biologically important, so the Perturb-seq negative result should be read as a modality and cell-resolution limitation rather than as evidence against HTR2C appetite biology.
main_caveats: Pomc itself was not perturbed in the parquet, and broad group_name classes may dilute rare arcuate POMC subpopulations.

summary: A genome-wide target-signature search found no strong positive or negative Htr2c neighbors.
why_it_matters: Even the best scalar neighbors were weak and included a Safe_target control, so the Htr2c profile does not define a robust convergent module that could be interpreted biologically.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Score-vector correlations can be inflated by weak low-cell-count signatures and do not validate Trem2, Pex1, or Gfra1 as Htr2c biology.

summary: Bmpr2 RNA depletion was directionally broad but statistically concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, with 145 MH-LH TH Glut just below FDR 0.1.
why_it_matters: Cell classes without FDR-significant self-depletion cannot be treated as clean negative biology, whereas the two strongest classes provide interpretable buffered knockdown contexts.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Directional target reduction was widespread, but many classes had 25-58 perturbed cells and did not pass FDR for Bmpr2 itself.

summary: FDR-significant Bmpr2 knockdown did not drive an FDR-significant canonical BMP/SMAD/ID RNA program.
why_it_matters: BMPR2 is expected to activate type-I BMP receptors and SMAD transcriptional regulators; failure of Id1-Id4 and related readouts to move suggests ligand limitation, redundancy, or non-transcriptional signaling in these assayed neuronal states.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: RNA readout only; BMP ligand exposure and SMAD phosphorylation were not measured.

summary: Perturbations of related BMP/TGFβ receptors and SMADs did not reproduce Bmpr2 signatures.
why_it_matters: The result prevents over-interpreting Bmpr2 from the receptor wiring diagram alone; the observable single-cell RNA phenotype was not a shared receptor-family module.
main_caveats: Most comparators lacked FDR-significant self-transcript depletion, so the comparison is a negative observability result, not proof of biological divergence.

summary: The BMPRII-LIMK/Rho dendrite branch was not detected as a transcriptional response to Bmpr2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Prior neuronal work places BMPRII upstream of dendritic cytoskeletal remodeling; the absent RNA module points to a likely post-translational or morphology-only phenotype that needs a different assay.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The literature assays examined BMP ligand response, dendrite remodeling, or developing mitral cells; this dataset measured steady-state RNA in cell classes rather than phosphoprotein or morphology.

summary: Buffered Bmpr2 loss in neuronal RNA profiles should not be extrapolated to vascular BMPR2 loss-of-function disease biology.
why_it_matters: BMPR2 loss is causal in familial pulmonary arterial hypertension and impairs BMP/Smad signaling in PAH mutation models, so systemic BMPR2 inhibition would remain directionally concerning despite the muted brain-cell RNA response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The dataset contains neuronal mouse-brain classes rather than pulmonary endothelial or smooth-muscle cells.

summary: Eif4a1 was the sole FDR-significant non-target hit under Bmpr2 perturbation and was confined to 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: It identifies the one measured secondary transcript that passes conventional correction, but its isolation and weak target FDR make it a follow-up marker rather than a mechanism.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only 41 perturbed cells; Bmpr2 itself was nominal but not FDR-significant in the same class; no recurrence in other cell types.

direction: Wnt feedback up; selected glutamatergic and peptide/neurosecretory genes down
summary: Apc perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut activated a canonical Wnt negative-feedback module while repressing selected glutamatergic and peptide/neurosecretory markers.
why_it_matters: Axin2, Nkd1 and Notum induction makes the strongest Perturb-seq response interpretable as beta-catenin pathway activation rather than an unstructured stress signature; the concurrent fall in Grin2c, Grin2d, Gls, Cck and Chgb shows that the Wnt response is coupled to thalamic neuronal-state genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The assay is RNA-only; nuclear beta-catenin, APC protein abundance, and Wnt transcriptional reporter activity were not measured directly.

summary: The Apc response was highly cell-type restricted: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had 303 corrected genes, 145 MH-LH TH Glut had an Axin2-centric one-gene FDR<0.05 response, and the remaining 20 Apc-sampled classes had no corrected hits.
why_it_matters: Apc perturbation therefore should not be treated as a pan-neuronal Wnt activator in this dataset; major cortical, midbrain, and interneuron groups with similar or larger edited-cell counts were transcriptionally buffered or not detectably engaged.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Absence of FDR hits in a cell type may reflect weak guide editing, chromatin accessibility, or power; Apc mRNA itself did not validate target engagement.

summary: Ctnnb1 loss opposed Apc perturbation on the Wnt-feedback program in the same 151 thalamic class.
why_it_matters: This reciprocal direction is the expected topology for an inhibitory destruction-complex component versus the beta-catenin transcriptional effector, and it validates Axin2 and Notum as directional readouts of the local Wnt response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The strongest quantified correlation was restricted to the 303 Apc-significant genes; not every Apc-responsive gene was a corrected Ctnnb1 hit.

direction: Apc strong; Gsk3b/Lrp5/Fzd3 weak; Lrp6 small and anti-correlated on the Apc-restricted signature
summary: Measured Gsk3b and proximal Wnt receptor perturbations were not interchangeable with Apc perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates the downstream APC gatekeeper from upstream receptor inputs and from GSK3β alone: Lrp5 and Fzd3 had no corrected hits, Lrp6 produced only four, and Gsk3b knockdown did not induce Axin2/Nkd1/Notum despite a corrected Gsk3b self-hit.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Lrp5/Lrp6/Fzd3 target transcripts were not FDR-validated self-hits, Lrp6 and Fzd3 correlations used the Apc-restricted gene set, and Gsk3a plus Axin paralogs were not assayed as perturbation targets.

summary: Apc and Tcf7l2 perturbations converged on a thalamic gene set but usually with opposite signs, indicating that APC/Wnt activation intersects rather than simply phenocopies Tcf7l2 loss.
why_it_matters: TCF7L2 is a thalamic differentiation regulator; the Apc signature changed Cck, Spock3, Nexn and other genes that were also Tcf7l2-responsive, but the mostly opposite directions argue that Apc perturbation is an upstream signaling distortion superimposed on a Tcf7l2-dependent identity program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only 29 genes were corrected hits in both Apc and Tcf7l2 contrasts; the mechanistic relationship could be indirect and stage-dependent.

summary: Apc mRNA abundance was not a usable on-target knockdown readout in this experiment.
why_it_matters: The corrected Axin2/Nkd1/Notum response in 151 and the Axin2 response in 145 provide functional evidence for pathway perturbation, but direct Apc transcript logFC did not confirm loss of the target RNA in any cell type.
main_caveats: CRISPR coding indels can alter protein without lowering transcript abundance; the negative transcript result therefore does not prove failed editing.

summary: Fgfr2 perturbation did not produce detectable Fgfr2 transcript knockdown in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The lack of self-repression makes all downstream nonresponses difficult to interpret as true biological buffering; it points first to weak perturbation or low expression of the target transcript.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance may be sparse and the parquet does not expose guide-level efficiency or raw expression.

summary: The residual Fgfr2 response was concentrated in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, with Ccsap as the only adjusted hit and a larger CA3 nominal tail.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only cell class where the perturbation generated more than scattered nominal genes, while avoiding overstatement of the near-threshold tail.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Only Ccsap passed pvals_adj<0.05; the next CA3 genes were just above 0.10 adjusted p value.

summary: Fgfr2 perturbation did not recover canonical FGF-FRS2-RAS/MAPK feedback transcripts.
why_it_matters: Curated FGFR2 signaling predicts receptor-proximal FRS2/PLCG1 and RAS/MAPK/AKT signaling, but Dusp, Spry, Etv, Fos/Jun, and core cascade genes were not adjusted hits, including in the otherwise most responsive CA3 class.
main_caveats: Absence of canonical feedback is expected if the Fgfr2 transcript was not efficiently perturbed.

summary: Related receptor and MAPK-node perturbations showed that the atlas can detect FGFR/RAS-module effects that Fgfr2 did not show.
why_it_matters: Fgfr1 self-knockdown and Braf/Map2k1 downstream responses make the Fgfr2 null less likely to be solely a global limitation of the Wilcoxon pipeline or MAPK gene detectability.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations differ in guides, cell counts, targets, and cell types and are not quantitative potency controls.

summary: A weak adult mouse neuronal Fgfr2 loss-of-function signature should not be interpreted as evidence against activating FGFR2 disease mechanisms or FGFR2 inhibitor use in epithelial tumors.
why_it_matters: The main clinical and developmental FGFR2 contexts are gain-of-function craniosynostosis and FGFR2-altered cholangiocarcinoma; the perturbation here lacked clear target engagement and did not model those mechanisms.
main_caveats: No tumor, cranial-suture, ligand-stimulated, or gain-of-function perturbation was assayed.

summary: Htr6 showed weak RNA-level target engagement in every tested cell class.
why_it_matters: Without a measurable decrease of the perturbed transcript, negative downstream results are more consistent with weak target-RNA engagement, sparse receptor expression, or assay mismatch than with definitive absence of 5-HT6 biology.
main_caveats: RNA-level target abundance may be sparse and may not perfectly report receptor protein disruption.

summary: The Htr6 perturbation produced no 5%-FDR downstream differential-expression rows across 23 broad brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A true HTR6 response in this experiment would be expected to generate at least a recurring cell-state or second-messenger transcriptional footprint if many assigned cells were engaged; instead the output is near the multiple-testing floor.
main_caveats: A fast cAMP, ciliary, mTOR, or phosphoprotein response may be invisible to endpoint scRNA-seq.

summary: The strongest Htr6 gene-level hints were isolated and cell-type restricted: Ndufs1 in 308 CB GABA, Hnrnpm in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, Ncoa1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and Acp1/Pibf1 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: These rows are the only plausible biomarkers to carry forward, but their adjusted P values show they should be tracked as exploratory rather than used as a pathway call.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: No listed row passed q<0.05 and none forms a recurrent serotonin, cAMP, mTOR, Cdk5, or ciliary module.

summary: Htr6 did not phenocopy serotonin-family receptors, Gs-pathway neighbors, or Mtor in matched Wilcoxon-score signatures.
why_it_matters: Known receptor-family or STRING proximity was insufficient to predict a shared broad transcriptional program in this data, so pathway-neighbor comparisons should not be used to rescue the weak Htr6 signature.
main_caveats: The contrast is restricted by a weak Htr6 query signature and by broad cell-class averaging.

summary: The dataset supplies no robust transcriptional marker for choosing HTR6 agonism, antagonism, inverse agonism, or genetic loss.
why_it_matters: HTR6 is druggable and 5-HT6 antagonists have reached phase-3 Alzheimer testing, but this perturbation should not be used as evidence that an HTR6-directed drug would or would not work in a specific direction.
main_caveats: Genetic perturbation, receptor antagonism, and inverse agonism are not equivalent, and the dataset lacks target-RNA engagement.

summary: Gnptab perturbation did not measurably deplete the Gnptab transcript in any scored neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: The canonical catalytic alpha/beta subunit is the intended lesion; without target-RNA engagement, downstream null results should be interpreted as perturbation failure or a very incomplete allele rather than absence of GNPTAB biology.
main_caveats: Target mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for genome editing, protein loss, and Golgi enzyme activity.

summary: The Gnptab perturbation produced a globally null transcriptomic response: zero FDR-significant genes across 371,818 gene-by-cell-type tests.
why_it_matters: No cell type, top gene, or nominal marker should be treated as a reproducible Gnptab response in this dataset.
main_caveats: The conclusion is about the observed Perturb-seq transcriptional phenotype; it does not prove that complete Gnptab loss is buffered.

summary: The weak Gnptab result is selective: multiple selected endolysosomal perturbations in the same file showed significant target depletion or FDR-significant signatures.
why_it_matters: This argues against a blanket inability of the experiment to detect related or lysosomal genes and makes GNPTAB-specific guide efficacy, transcript dynamics, or enzyme turnover the leading caveat.
main_caveats: Comparator genes are not all in the M6P-tagging complex; some evidence reflects on-target transcript depletion rather than a shared pathway-response score.

summary: Gnptab score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Gnptg, Atp6v0c, and lysosomal comparator perturbations and lacked any strong genome-wide positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Although GNPTAB and GNPTG participate in the same M6P-tagging machinery, the measured Gnptab program cannot be interpreted as a resolved M6P or lysosomal-trafficking module.
main_caveats: Correlations are dominated by a null Gnptab signature and should not be used to infer antagonism or pathway rewiring.

summary: This neuronal Perturb-seq profile did not recapitulate the chronic neurodegenerative phenotype reported after complete Gnptab loss in mice.
why_it_matters: The result points to a mismatch between acute, weak transcriptomic perturbation of neuronal clusters and the months-long, post-Golgi lysosomal storage process in mucolipidosis II, rather than to irrelevance of GNPTAB in brain.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks a validated complete knockout, lysosomal enzyme activity readouts, secreted hydrolase measurements, and long-term pathology.

summary: Fgfrl1 guide assignment did not produce measurable Fgfrl1 RNA depletion in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Because FGFRL1 is a membrane FGF receptor-like protein without a catalytic kinase domain, the RNA self-row is the clearest dataset-level check that the intended loss-of-function was engaged before interpreting downstream FGF biology.
main_caveats: The row measures transcript abundance in the same single-cell RNA assay, not protein abundance or guide cutting; sparse basal expression can reduce power.

summary: The Fgfrl1 perturbation produced no FDR-qualified transcriptomic response across 388046 cell-type/gene tests.
why_it_matters: The dataset provides no robust neuronal marker, pathway, or cell-type response for this perturbation, so the safe interpretation is a null Perturb-seq signature rather than a reproducible FGFRL1-regulated program.
main_caveats: The biological null is inseparable from absent measured target engagement; FDR was evaluated within the provided DE table only.

summary: The apparent Pineal Glut enrichment is exploratory: it contains the lowest nominal Fgfrl1 P values but remains non-significant after FDR correction and has only weak signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: Sh3bgrl2, Ppp3r1, and Ddx10 should be treated as triage genes for replication, not as FGFRL1 biomarkers, despite their scalar rank in the strongest nominal cell class.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only 42 perturbed Pineal Glut cells; FDR values were 0.46-0.78 for the top three genes and all-library correlations were |r|<=0.156.

summary: Fgfrl1 did not converge with available FGF/FGFR-related perturbations, whereas Fgfr1 and Fgf13 showed detectable self-transcript depletion in selected overlapping cell types.
why_it_matters: Literature places FGFRL1 next to FGF ligands, FGFR1, and Sprouty/SPRED feedback proteins, so the absence of correlated score vectors argues against using weak Fgfrl1 signatures as evidence for canonical FGFR-pathway modulation.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Secreted FGFRL1-binding ligands were not present as perturbation targets, and the Fgfrl1 vector itself lacks on-target depletion.

summary: This mouse-brain dataset does not recapitulate the developmental diaphragm/kidney FGFRL1 disease axis.
why_it_matters: Mouse and human genetics link FGFRL1 to perinatal diaphragm and congenital diaphragmatic hernia phenotypes; the present null result confines this Perturb-seq experiment to brain follow-up and should not be used to argue that developmental mesenchymal or myogenic FGFRL1 biology is dispensable.
main_caveats: The assay species matches mouse but not the embryonic diaphragm, kidney, or human CDH contexts in the references.

summary: Ifih1 targeting did not produce measurable Ifih1 mRNA depletion or any FDR-controlled transcriptional phenotype across the 22 neuronal cell-type contrasts in which the target transcript was measured.
why_it_matters: This makes failed or unobservable target engagement the dominant interpretation; the dataset cannot be read as evidence that Ifih1 biology is dispensable in these neurons.
main_caveats: No target mRNA knockdown was detected; sparse basal Ifih1 expression can make the logFC values unstable; protein and viral-challenge readouts were not measured.

summary: The Ifih1 response was not selectively strong in a hidden neuronal subclass; even high-count classes were null and nominal hits were mostly singletons.
why_it_matters: Cell-type specificity would have been the main discovery mode in this brain Perturb-seq panel, but the Ifih1 contrasts instead look scattered and below genome-wide support.
main_caveats: Moderate rather than high interpretive confidence because 10 of 22 classes had 50 or fewer Ifih1-targeted cells and the target itself was not detectably depleted.

summary: Canonical interferon-stimulated genes stayed flat after Ifih1 targeting and also after Adar or Stat1 perturbations that did deplete their own transcripts in selected neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: ADAR1 loss is expected to expose endogenous dsRNA to MDA5 and STAT1 is a core interferon-output transcription factor; their isolated self-effects indicate that this unchallenged neuronal assay is not carrying an active IFIH1-ADAR-STAT interferon module.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: ADAR and STAT1 were evaluated at mRNA output only; the dataset does not test acute viral dsRNA stimulation or complete protein loss.

summary: Ifih1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with available RLR, TLR3, type-I-IFN receptor, and interferon-transcription-factor perturbations in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: Reactome and STRING place these proteins in a connected antiviral RNA-sensing network, but the basal neuronal signatures do not behave as an interchangeable IFIH1 pathway module.
main_caveats: The closest RIG-I-like receptor paralogs Ddx58 and Dhx58 and the adaptor Mavs were not available as perturbations in the filtered dataset; correlations compare mostly weak signatures.

summary: The mouse neuron panel is not a positive model for testing IFIH1 suppression despite strong human genetics pointing to both pathogenic IFIH1 gain of function and protective rare IFIH1 alleles.
why_it_matters: IFIH1 inhibition could be directionally interesting for interferonopathies or type 1 diabetes, but this dataset offers neither target engagement nor a neuronal interferon biomarker response, so its null phenotype should not be overused for efficacy or safety de-risking.
main_caveats: The disease evidence is human and often systemic or inflammatory, whereas these data are unchallenged mouse neuronal transcriptomes with failed Ifih1 mRNA engagement.

summary: Mouse-brain Hnrnpdl perturbation was broadly buffered at the total-mRNA level.
why_it_matters: HNRNPDL is a DNA/RNA-binding hnRNP annotated for RNA metabolism and transcriptional regulation, so a one-gene FDR response across 22 cell types argues that this dataset does not reveal a broad acute abundance program downstream of Hnrnpdl.
main_caveats: Target-transcript engagement was also weak and never FDR-significant; the assay tests total transcript abundance, not protein depletion, RNA binding, or alternative splicing.

summary: A small, cell-type-restricted Hnrnpu increase was the only FDR-significant Hnrnpdl response.
why_it_matters: HNRNPU is in HNRNPDL's RNA-processing interaction neighborhood, making the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Hnrnpu hit a plausible compensatory RBP marker rather than a generic stress signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Single gene in one cell type; Hnrnpu up-regulation is indirect and the target self-transcript in the same cell type was only nominally decreased.

summary: Hnrnpdl did not behave like the active Hnrnpc or Hnrnpu perturbations despite belonging to the hnRNP/RBP disease neighborhood.
why_it_matters: The result separates Hnrnpdl from other RNA-binding proteins in the same broad network and argues against treating assayed hnRNP perturbations as interchangeable in mouse-brain total-RNA space.
main_caveats: The comparison uses score correlations and FDR burden, not matched protein depletion estimates for each hnRNP target.

summary: The Perturb-seq result is not a transcriptomic surrogate for HNRNPDL limb-girdle muscular dystrophy biology.
why_it_matters: Published HNRNPDL disease biology centers on adult muscle, RNA processing, isoform-regulated phase separation, and aggregation-prone prion-like-domain mutations, whereas these Hnrnpdl guide assignments in mouse brain produced almost no robust total-mRNA changes.
main_caveats: Different species, cell type, tissue, perturbation class, and readout; the dataset does not quantify HNRNPDL aggregation, protein solubility, muscle physiology, or alternative splicing.

summary: The 308 CB GABA nominal signature should not be promoted to a cerebellar Hnrnpdl pathway call.
why_it_matters: 308 CB GABA had the largest nominal Hnrnpdl gene count and the strongest all-target correlations, but it had no FDR genes and its restricted signature was highly correlated with multiple Safe_target controls.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Safe-target correlation does not prove a technical artifact, but it makes the 308 CB GABA signature exploratory.

summary: Nominal target-transcript movement did not predict the only downstream FDR response.
why_it_matters: 053 Sst Gaba had the largest nominal Hnrnpdl self decrease but no FDR hits, while 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut carried the only FDR response with a smaller self-transcript decrease; this separates weak target engagement from downstream sensitivity.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
