main_caveats: Both cell-type inferences are limited by single-guide assignment counts, especially 38 perturbed cells in 053 Sst GABA, and Hnrnpdl self-transcript changes were not FDR-significant.

summary: Herc1 produced only one multiplicity-corrected transcriptomic hit, Dnm1 down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells.
why_it_matters: The response is not a broad pan-neuronal HERC1 loss signature; it localizes the clearest acute readout to an MGE-derived inhibitory class, with only nominal support for other genes.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The key group had only 31 perturbed cells and Herc1 itself was only nominally reduced; all other genes in the same group were not FDR-significant.

direction: Dnm1 down; Cplx1 and Nefm nominally down; no Dnm1 or Cltc phenocopy
summary: Dnm1 is the strongest candidate transcriptional biomarker linking Herc1 perturbation to presynaptic membrane/endocytosis biology.
why_it_matters: HERC1 is known to participate in clathrin-linked membrane trafficking, and DNM1 is an endocytic vesicle-scission gene; the CNU-MGE Dnm1 decrease therefore gives the sparse signature a plausible vesicle-recycling interpretation.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only Dnm1 passed FDR; Cplx1 and Nefm were nominal, and direct Dnm1 or Cltc perturbations did not resemble the Herc1 score vector in this cell type.

summary: The neuronal Herc1 signature was transcriptionally uncoupled from Tsc1/Tsc2 loss despite the known HERC1-TSC2-mTOR connection.
why_it_matters: This argues that acute Herc1 perturbation in these cells should not be interpreted as a simple TSC2-destabilizing or mTORC1-activating perturbation, and weakens a direct mTORC1 therapeutic-direction inference from this dataset alone.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: In 054 CNU-MGE GABA, Tsc1/Tsc2 had 62 and 57 perturbed cells versus 31 for Herc1; HERC1 effects can be post-translational and may require starvation or gain-of-function contexts not modeled here.

direction: no FDR-supported marker induction or repression
summary: Herc1 knockdown did not evoke a robust autophagy, lysosome, or proteasome-assembly transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: Tambaleante and proteasome-assembly studies put HERC1 in autophagy/proteostasis biology, but this Perturb-seq readout did not show corrected changes in Sqstm1, Atg5, Atg16l1, Ulk1, Tfeb, or vesicle/trafficking pathway neighbors.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The assay measured mRNA rather than LC3 flux, TFEB localization, mTOR phosphorylation, ubiquitination, or proteasome assembly; under-engagement of Herc1 is a major limitation.

summary: Several larger Herc1 cell-type samples looked buffered or under-engaged rather than strongly responsive.
why_it_matters: The absence of FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, together with non-significant Herc1 self-depletion, means that most negative cell-type calls should be treated as inconclusive rather than as evidence of dispensability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Buffered biology cannot be separated from weak CRISPR target engagement because the Herc1 target transcript never passed FDR.

summary: Atad1 transcript depletion occurred in the expected direction in all 22 tested cell classes but was FDR-supported in only six classes.
why_it_matters: Downstream interpretation should be restricted primarily to the six classes with verified target depletion; weak cortical and Sst/LGE signatures are not clean negative biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The selectivity is assay-level target engagement, not proof that ATAD1 protein or function is absent from the other cell types.

summary: Robust Atad1 knockdown was self-transcript-only at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: ATAD1 is an ATP-dependent membrane-protein quality-control factor, but its partial loss did not induce a broad stress, mitochondrial, peroxisomal, or synaptic mRNA program in the engaged neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: FDR-level absence of non-target mRNAs does not exclude protein-level cargo accumulation or physiology changes.

summary: The known ATAD1-Thorase AMPAR mechanism was uncoupled from AMPAR-related mRNA abundance.
why_it_matters: AMPAR receptor trafficking and perampanel rescue are central to ATAD1 neurologic disease, yet Gria-family, Grip1, Dlg4, Pick1, and Shisa/TARP transcripts were unchanged; these mRNAs should not be used as pharmacodynamic surrogates for ATAD1-dependent AMPAR recycling in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset did not measure surface AMPAR abundance, EPSCs, or perampanel rescue.

summary: Atad1 was transcriptionally buffered in cell classes where Opa1 and Dnm1l produced broad mitochondrial-dynamics signatures.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the self-only Atad1 result is not simply an inability of the screen or the overlapping neuronal classes to detect mitochondrial perturbation responses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: OPA1 and DNM1L are mitochondrial dynamics factors rather than direct ATAD1 complex members, so this is a functional benchmark rather than a same-complex comparison.

summary: Pex14 matched Atad1 with strong target knockdown but no FDR-supported downstream transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Two organelle-surface protein-trafficking perturbations affecting peroxisome-linked biology can be cleanly edited yet transcriptionally quiet, suggesting that membrane import and extraction defects may need protein or organelle assays rather than scRNA pathway scores.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: PEX14 and ATAD1 occupy related peroxisomal membrane homeostasis space but are not the same import reaction; the convergence is transcriptomic and limited to one comparator.

summary: Atad1 had no strong positive or negative whole-signature neighbor after the target gene was excluded.
why_it_matters: The Atad1 perturbation should not be grouped with another transcriptional state on the basis of weak correlations alone.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The correlation screen was restricted to FDR-engaged Atad1 cell classes and used full Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by null genes.

direction: down in 151; mostly weakly down elsewhere
summary: Mapre2 perturbation produced FDR-significant on-target transcript depletion only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Interpretation of Mapre2 biology in this screen should be anchored mainly on the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class rather than averaged over weakly engaged classes.
comparators: 21 other Mapre2-assayed cell classes|215 MB Dopa
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The engaged class also had the largest perturbed-cell count, so observed cell-type selectivity combines biology with statistical power and guide recovery.

direction: target down; no robust downstream mRNA direction
summary: The engaged Mapre2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: Mapre2 itself was significant, whereas no non-target gene reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: EB2 is a cytoskeletal adaptor, so an acute post-mitotic neuronal phenotype may be structural, trafficking, or electrophysiological rather than a large mRNA program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Buffering is inferred from mRNA differential expression only; the dataset did not measure microtubule growth, focal adhesion turnover, neurite morphology, or EB2 protein.

summary: Mapre2 did not phenocopy the available microtubule plus-end, motor, or tubulin perturbations in signature space.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating every microtubule or +TIP perturbation as an interchangeable transcriptional module in adult neurons, and is consistent with literature in which EB2 has functions separable from EB1/EB3-driven microtubule growth.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Mapre1, Mapre3, Clip1, Ckap5, Clasp1, and Clasp2 were not perturbation targets, and the Mapre2 signatures themselves were weak in most cell types.

summary: The adult mouse-brain screen does not reveal a broad neuronal stress or microtubule-transcription program downstream of Mapre2, despite strong MAPRE2 links to cranial neural crest migration and ventricular conduction in other systems.
why_it_matters: Disease-relevant MAPRE2 biology may be developmental, morphological, adhesion-based, or electrophysiological; a negative adult-neuronal mRNA readout should not be interpreted as absence of MAPRE2 function.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The literature phenotypes come from human neural crest, zebrafish heart, and iPSC-cardiomyocyte systems, not adult mouse thalamic neurons, and the screen did not quantify morphology or sodium currents.

summary: Med13l perturbation produced an extremely sparse loss-of-function transcriptome: the target transcript was never significant after FDR correction and only two single-gene FDR responses were detected across 22 measured cell types.
why_it_matters: MED13L is annotated as a nuclear Mediator coactivator, so an acute, broad transcriptional collapse might have been expected; instead the dataset argues that most profiled postmitotic brain classes either buffered the perturbation or did not achieve enough functional knockdown to create a large RNA phenotype.
main_caveats: Single-guide CRISPR perturbation; direct Med13l mRNA was only nominally reduced in a subset of cells, so null signatures may reflect incomplete knockdown as well as biological buffering.

summary: The only FDR-significant Med13l readouts were cell-class-specific single genes: Arpp21 decreased in L4-5 IT cortical glutamatergic cells and Grm1 decreased in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells.
why_it_matters: These two genes are the most defensible dataset biomarkers for Med13l perturbation, but each is a sentinel rather than a resolved pathway because no second gene in the same target-cell contrast survived FDR correction.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Each cell type had exactly one FDR-significant gene; downstream pathway identity is therefore unresolved.

summary: Thalamic Grm1 repression was shared by Med13l, Med13, Med15, and Med23 perturbations, and Med13, Med15, and Med23 uncovered a broader downregulated Prkcd/Pcp4/Plekhg1/Grin2b-associated neuronal module in the same cell class.
why_it_matters: The recurrence of Grm1 across several Mediator subunits points to a thalamic glutamatergic program that is sensitive to multiple Mediator entry points, while the broader response is attenuated in Med13l itself.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Genome-wide correlations were weak and the common high-confidence Med13l component was Grm1 alone; comparisons use separate perturbations rather than combinatorial perturbation rescue.

summary: The L4-5 Arpp21 response did not behave as a generic Mediator-complex signature: related Mediator perturbations had near-zero full-signature correlations with Med13l and none reproduced Arpp21 at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: Database and biochemical evidence place MED13L near MED12, CDK8, and MED13, but the cortical output of Med13l is not interchangeable with those pathway neighbors in this dataset.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted to one cortical cell class and one FDR-significant gene; the closest genome-wide correlations were very small.

summary: Nominal Med13l target-transcript decreases in CTX-CGE GABA and L5 extratelencephalic glutamatergic neurons produced no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: These contexts separate detectable target mRNA movement from a large transcriptional phenotype and are therefore the clearest cell-type examples of buffering or under-threshold engagement.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Direct-target rows were nominal rather than FDR-significant, and the assay cannot distinguish compensation from insufficient protein depletion.

summary: The restricted Grm1/Arpp21 loss signatures are directionally consistent with MED13L being a loss-of-function-sensitive neurodevelopmental gene rather than an obvious target for neuronal inhibition.
why_it_matters: Human MED13L haploinsufficiency and mouse cortical knockdown data already implicate MED13L dosage in neurodevelopment; the Perturb-seq data add neuronal gene readouts that decrease after loss perturbation, arguing that any therapeutic strategy would more plausibly need to restore or carefully tune MED13L-dependent programs than broadly inhibit them.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse, single-guide, and transcriptional; it does not measure dendritic morphology, heart/neural-crest phenotypes, or therapeutic rescue.

summary: Chrnb3 was measured but not detectably knocked down in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The central result is failed or extremely weak target engagement, so the screen cannot be interpreted as a successful loss-of-function test of β3 nicotinic receptor biology.
main_caveats: The target transcript may be sparse, and some logFC values are inflated despite near-zero Wilcoxon scores; protein or channel-level effects were not assayed.

summary: The residual Chrnb3 signatures were nominal, sparse, and non-recurrent rather than a reproducible downstream program.
why_it_matters: Even the best cell-type hits fall short of FDR significance and do not nominate a robust marker gene or pathway.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic statement only; a channel-current or neurotransmitter-release phenotype could occur without a stable mRNA program.

summary: Other cholinergic receptor or pathway perturbations achieved clear on-target knockdown in some overlapping contexts, whereas Chrnb3 did not.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the absence of a Chrnb3 response is not simply a universal failure of nicotinic/cholinergic perturbations in the screen, but it also means Chrnb3/Chrnb2/Ache differences should be attributed first to target engagement rather than receptor-subunit specificity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Related perturbations often produced mainly on-target rows rather than broad downstream signatures; guide efficacy and cell number differ among perturbations.

summary: Chrnb3 biology is disease- and drug-relevant in prior nicotinic-receptor literature, but this dataset provides no usable agonist-versus-antagonist or loss-of-function direction.
why_it_matters: CHRNB3 sits in α6/β2/β3 nicotinic receptor complexes linked to dopamine release and nicotine-dependence genetics; a non-engaged Perturb-seq signature should therefore not be taken as evidence that CHRNB3 inhibition would be transcriptionally inert or safe.
main_caveats: The strongest physiologic literature is dopaminergic or heterologous-channel based, while the dataset is broad-cell-class mouse-brain transcriptomics without a dedicated dopamine-release assay.

summary: Chrnb3 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor across matched cell types.
why_it_matters: A weak target could still reveal a reproducible off-target or shared stress program through correlation with other perturbations; that did not occur here.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed over Wilcoxon score vectors and were not pathway-informed; absence of correlation is most informative as a lack of a dominant transcriptomic program.

summary: Kcna1 target mRNA fell nominally in selected cell classes but was not uniformly or FDR-significantly depleted.
why_it_matters: Every downstream interpretation must be conditioned on partial target engagement rather than treated as a clean pan-neuronal Kcna1 loss-of-function state.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The strongest nominal contrasts had 21-38 perturbed cells except 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 155 MB Glut; all Kcna1 target rows had FDR=1.0.

summary: The strongest nominal Kcna1 knockdown did not propagate to an FDR-significant transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: A weak mRNA response is consistent with Kv1.1 acting primarily through membrane conductance and spike timing, so Perturb-seq RNA is likely an insensitive proximal readout for this channel.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Buffering is inferred from transcript abundance only; the experiment did not directly measure K+ current, axonal excitability, or seizure-like activity.

summary: Kcna1 perturbation did not induce recurrent FDR-level compensation among measured Kv1, Kv7, or NaV-channel transcripts.
why_it_matters: The assayed cells did not mount an obvious transcriptional replacement program for the lost Kv1.1 message, separating immediate ion-channel function from compensatory channel-gene remodeling.
main_caveats: The negative result is limited by weak Kcna1 target depletion and by assaying mRNA, not channel localization or activity.

summary: Kcna1 signatures were near-orthogonal to Kcna2, Kcnab1, Kcnab2, Kcnq2, and Kcnq3 perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: Complex or ion-channel-family membership alone did not predict a shared transcriptional state in this atlas, despite stronger detectable on-target effects for Kcnab2 and Kcnq2.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak Kcna1 RNA signatures; absence of RNA convergence does not rule out electrophysiological convergence at the channel level.

summary: The weak Kcna1 mRNA phenotype should not be interpreted as evidence that KCNA1 loss is safe or therapeutically desirable.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse evidence support KCNA1 loss-of-function as hyperexcitability disease biology; the dataset instead suggests that electrophysiology, not secondary single-cell RNA signatures, should be prioritized for rescue and opener studies.
main_caveats: The dataset used mouse broad brain cell classes and did not test KCNA1 openers, blockers, human variants, or seizure phenotypes.

summary: Gfra1 did not produce a reproducible FDR-significant transcriptional phenotype in any profiled cell type.
why_it_matters: GFRA1 is an upstream GDNF co-receptor, so the dataset had to first show on-target depletion before a missing RET-pathway phenotype could be treated as biology; it did not.
main_caveats: The negative result is dominated by weak Gfra1 mRNA engagement; it should not be read as proof that GFRA1 protein is dispensable in these cells.

summary: Canonical RET, NCAM/Fyn, PI3K, AKT, and MAPK transcripts were not detectably mobilized after Gfra1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The literature places GFRA1 at the plasma-membrane entry point to RET and alternative NCAM signaling, but Gfra1 guide assignment did not generate a coordinated transcript-level response in these pathway genes.
main_caveats: The assay measured steady-state RNA, not ligand-evoked RET phosphorylation; weak Gfra1 depletion is the parsimonious reason for uncoupling.

summary: Gfra1 did not phenocopy Ncam1, even though NCAM can participate in GDNF-family signaling with GFRα1.
why_it_matters: A direct NCAM receptor comparator was strongly depleted in ten shared cell classes, whereas Gfra1 was not, and the full signatures were essentially uncorrelated; the alternate-receptor relationship therefore was not interchangeable in this Perturb-seq readout.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The contrast may reflect unequal knockdown efficiency rather than a true absence of GFRA1-NCAM coupling.

summary: The Gfra1 perturbation did not test the dopaminergic GDNF/GFRα1 axis.
why_it_matters: GDNF-family biology is clinically tied to dopaminergic and motor-neuron support, but the only dopaminergic class in this file, 215 MB Dopa, had no Gfra1 profile; the weak thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic profiles cannot stand in for substantia-nigra-like biology.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a coverage finding, not an observed dopaminergic response.

summary: Pvalb GABA showed the strongest nominal Gfra1 decrease without any corrected downstream response.
why_it_matters: This restricted signal is the closest the file comes to an engaged GFRA1 phenotype and may mark buffering, insufficient knockdown, or ligand absence in an interneuron context.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All downstream genes and the Gfra1 transcript itself had FDR=1.0; treat this as a hypothesis, not a validated cell-state switch.

summary: GDNF-family paralog and ligand interchangeability could not be evaluated.
why_it_matters: Reactome treats GFRA1-4 as related RET co-receptors with different preferred ligands, but this file lacked Gdnf, Gfra2, Gfra3, Gfra4, Nrtn, Artn, and Pspn perturbations and the available Ret profiles were not FDR-engaged.
main_caveats: Absence of perturbation rows is informative for interpretation but gives no direction of effect for the missing family members.

summary: Hmgcr guide cells showed reproducible but modest target-mRNA depletion, with the most convincing engagement in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and only nominal engagement in six additional classes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation attacked a druggable rate-limiting mevalonate enzyme, but interpretation should be concentrated on cell types where the target transcript actually declined.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Only 022 L5 ET CTX Glut approached FDR significance for the target transcript; the other target-depletion calls are nominal.

summary: The best-engaged L5 extratelencephalic cells buffered Hmgcr loss at the transcriptome level: Hmgcr was the top-ranked gene, but SREBP/cholesterol genes did not form a downstream response.
why_it_matters: If HMGCR knockdown had caused an immediate transcriptional cholesterol deficit, SREBP-regulated genes would be expected readouts; their absence makes Hmgcr mRNA itself the only clear biomarker in this class.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Transcriptomic buffering does not rule out protein or metabolite changes after Hmgcr knockdown.

summary: Across all Hmgcr cell types, core cholesterol-biosynthesis transcripts failed to show the coordinated induction expected from sterol depletion and SREBP2 feedback.
why_it_matters: HMGCR inhibitors often activate SREBP2-dependent compensatory transcription; the neuronal CRISPRi signatures did not reproduce that canonical feedback program.
main_caveats: The expected feedback is based largely on sterol depletion or statin-like enzyme inhibition; CRISPRi may have been too partial or too early to deplete HMGCR protein and mevalonate.

summary: Srebf2 loss is not interchangeable with Hmgcr loss: in 191 MB P MY GABA, Srebf2 knockdown repressed multiple sterol genes whereas Hmgcr knockdown did not, despite nominal Hmgcr depletion.
why_it_matters: The same assay can detect a SREBP2-dependent sterol module, so the weak Hmgcr phenotype is unlikely to be explained solely by poor capture of cholesterol transcripts.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The Srebf2 perturbation was better engaged than the Hmgcr perturbation; comparison is strongest for showing pathway measurability, not equal perturbation strength.

summary: Isolated significant or broad nominal Hmgcr signatures in poorly engaged classes were not cholesterol-pathway phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Hdac11 in CA3, Hnrnpul1 in hindbrain GABA, and the broad CB GABA nominal signature would be misleading without target-engagement filtering.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: These observations diagnose likely nonspecific or underpowered signatures; they should not be treated as mechanistic HMGCR outputs without replication.

summary: The muted neuronal Hmgcr response is consistent with a buffered adult-neuron cholesterol program rather than with collapse of mevalonate metabolism.
why_it_matters: Mouse genetics shows that adult neurons can obtain cholesterol non-cell-autonomously whereas glial SREBP2 activity is important for brain function; this dataset therefore argues that neuronal Hmgcr knockdown alone is a weak model for whole-brain cholesterol insufficiency.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq data do not directly measure cholesterol metabolites, astrocyte rescue, protein depletion, or developmental stage-specific demand.

summary: Nsd1 loss produced an FDR-supported multi-gene response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: NSD1 is a chromatin writer with developmental brain functions, but the acute mouse-brain Perturb-seq effect was concentrated in one thalamic glutamatergic class rather than being pan-neuronal.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The cell-class specificity is robust in this dataset, but Perturb-seq measures an acute RNA phenotype and not H3K36me2 or DNA methylation.

summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response nominates Ddo, Pygm, Capn3, Ptgds and Myo5c induction with Ptprz1 and Trpc3 repression as a compact RNA readout of Nsd1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: These genes were the strongest measured downstream changes and form a practical signature even though they do not by themselves define a known NSD1 pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The marker set is restricted to one cell type and the top up-regulated genes mix neuronal, metabolic and ectopic marker biology; it should be treated as a signature hypothesis, not a mechanistic pathway.

summary: Most Nsd1 cell-type tests had weak target-transcript depletion and no FDR-supported downstream response.
why_it_matters: The many negative cell types should not be interpreted as proof that NSD1 is dispensable there; low perturbation counts and weak FDR-level target engagement dominate the negative result.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only two non-151 classes had nominal Nsd1 p<0.001 and both had only 40-46 perturbed cells; target knockdown was not FDR-significant outside 151.

summary: The Nsd1 signature was not a generic acute H3K36-writer signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: A related perturbation, Ash1l, gave significant self-knockdown with no non-self FDR hits, while Nsd2 and Setd2 did not phenocopy Nsd1 and genome-wide correlations to Nsd1 were near zero; Nsd1 therefore marks a more specific state than simple loss of any H3K36-associated methyltransferase in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Nsd2 showed no detectable target knockdown and the Setd2 test had fewer cells, so the safest conclusion is lack of acute signature convergence rather than proven biological non-equivalence.

summary: The acute Nsd1 RNA phenotype did not converge with Dnmt3a knockdown despite the known NSD1-H3K36me2-DNMT3A axis in neurons.
why_it_matters: Published work links NSD1-deposited H3K36me2 to DNMT3A-mediated non-CG methylation, but this dataset suggests that that chromatin-DNA-methylation pathway is not captured as an immediate Dnmt3a-like transcriptome in adult 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset contains RNA readouts only; it cannot measure H3K36me2, H3K27me3, non-CG methylation, or delayed methylome-dependent consequences.

summary: The direction of biology is loss-of-function sensitive, making systemic NSD1 inhibition a neurodevelopmental risk rather than an obvious therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: NSD1 haploinsufficiency causes Sotos syndrome, and in this dataset even partial Nsd1 mRNA depletion was sufficient to move a thalamic neuronal RNA program; the Open Targets profile also lacked NSD1 clinical candidates or chemical probes, consistent with an immature and potentially hazardous target class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset models mouse guide-mediated partial transcript reduction, not human germline haploinsufficiency or pharmacologic enzymatic inhibition.

summary: Partial Dalrd3 depletion across 23 brain cell classes produced no adjusted p<0.05 transcriptional response, refining the known DALRD3 loss-of-function disease mechanism as buffered at the acute mRNA level in this assay.
why_it_matters: DALRD3 is a METTL2 arginine-tRNA m3C targeting factor and a developmental epileptic encephalopathy gene, but the main measured consequence here was not a broad transcriptome-wide collapse.
main_caveats: The dataset measures acute mRNA abundance, not DALRD3 protein, METTL2 binding, m3C, or translation.

summary: L2-3 IT cortical glutamatergic and cerebellar GABA cells showed nominal Dalrd3 mRNA depletion but no adjusted downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The strongest target row in the dataset occurred in a cell type with no adjusted downstream response, indicating true buffering or a missing non-transcriptional endpoint rather than simple absence of target RNA.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Adjusted downstream nulls could reflect insufficient duration, protein persistence, or lack of tRNA modification readout.

summary: Mcl1 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut was the only adjusted p<0.1 downstream event after Dalrd3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Mcl1 is an anti-apoptotic CNS survival factor, so its induction is a plausible homeostatic response to cellular stress from impaired RNA modification, but the row is only q=0.0928 and occurred with weak measured Dalrd3 mRNA engagement.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene near-FDR signal; direct DALRD3-to-MCL1 regulation was not shown.

summary: Rtn4 and Gabra1 were co-up-regulated as the top sub-FDR candidate markers in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
why_it_matters: This nominates a cell-type-restricted validation pair for recurrent testing of Dalrd3 perturbation, but the adjusted p values near 0.4 make it hypothesis-generating only.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: No component reached adjusted p<0.1; no causal link among these markers was tested.

summary: Rars2 and Polr3b did not phenocopy Dalrd3, and the top 012 signature neighbors were nearly uncorrelated with Dalrd3.
why_it_matters: Available RNA/tRNA-neighborhood comparators do not support a large shared transcriptional state downstream of Dalrd3 partial knockdown.
main_caveats: Rars2 and Polr3b are indirect STRING-neighborhood comparators, not METTL2 complex members, and their own target-transcript knockdown was weak.

summary: 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut lacked usable Dalrd3 target engagement and had no adjusted downstream response.
why_it_matters: These null cell classes should be treated as perturbation-delivery or transcript-detection failures rather than evidence that DALRD3 is biologically silent in those neuronal lineages.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Only Dalrd3 mRNA was quantified for engagement; protein depletion could differ.

summary: Across all 23 profiled mouse-brain cell types, Bmal2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant DE genes and did not show reproducible depletion of the measured Arntl2 transcript.
why_it_matters: This makes the Bmal2 perturbation a globally weak or buffered single-cell phenotype, so nominal genes from any one cell type should not be read as a definitive BMAL2 transcriptional program.
main_caveats: Arntl2 mRNA is an imperfect readout for guide-induced loss of BMAL2 protein; lack of FDR-significant DE can reflect weak editing, low endogenous expression, phase mixing, or true buffering.

summary: Bmal2 was uncoupled from the thalamic circadian-output module that responded strongly to Bmal1, Clock, Nr1d1, and Rora in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: BMAL2 is annotated as a CLOCK/NPAS2 E-box activator, so the same-cell contrast shows that Bmal2 is not simply interchangeable with the Bmal1-CLOCK/Nr1d1/Rora axis in this neuronal context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Bmal2 contrast itself lacked Arntl2 transcript depletion, so the divergence may combine biology with less efficient perturbation of Bmal2.

summary: The largest nominal Bmal2 effects were restricted to individual cell classes, with 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 308 CB GABA showing the highest counts of p<0.001 genes but no shared FDR-supported program.
why_it_matters: The dataset suggests a cell-class-dependent response or noise floor rather than a pan-neuronal BMAL2 module; recurrence rather than single nominal ranks is required for biomarker nomination.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: All genes in these cell types failed FDR<0.05; the strongest nominal genes were not recurrent at p<0.001 across cell types.

summary: Bmal2 perturbation in hypothalamus-labeled cell classes did not reproduce an adjusted single-cell analogue of reported global Bmal2-knockout hypothalamic phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Whole-animal Bmal2 loss alters hypothalamic clocks and energy-balance behavior, but this dataset does not identify an acute HYa/HY MM/MH-LH transcriptomic driver cell class.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The sampled labels are broad and may not include the SCN or mediobasal hypothalamic populations assayed in the knockout study; transcriptional phase and long-term organismal physiology are unmatched.

summary: A perturbome-wide signature-neighbor search found no strong convergence between Bmal2 and its clock-family partners or paralogs.
why_it_matters: The negative neighbor result argues against a hidden Bmal2 state that is simply captured by Bmal1, Clock, Cry, ROR, or REV-ERB perturbations elsewhere in the screen.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from transcriptomic score vectors only; one non-clock cerebellar GABA neighbor reached r=0.340, so low clock-family correlation does not prove absence of every possible Bmal2-related state.

summary: Hoxa13 perturbation did not produce a validated target-transcript perturbation or any FDR-significant downstream gene in the measured mouse-brain classes.
why_it_matters: The screen should be interpreted as weak or ectopic Hoxa13 guide assignment rather than a robust loss-of-function response; the absence of FDR-significant genes prevents strong mechanistic claims from single nominal rows.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript was tabulated in only one cell type, so most cell types could not report transcript-level target engagement.

summary: The nominal Hoxa13 response was uneven across neuronal classes, with the largest pre-FDR tails in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut rather than in the largest perturbed-cell sets.
why_it_matters: This makes the few transcriptional changes exploratory and cell-state-restricted instead of a pan-neuronal Hoxa13 program.
comparators: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No cell type reached FDR<0.05; 027 and 217 had only 76 and 48 perturbed cells, respectively.

summary: Hoxa13 signatures were decoupled from Hox13 paralogs and from Meis/Pbx TALE cofactor perturbations, despite known Hox/TALE and Hoxa13-Hoxd13 biology.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating Hoxa13 as interchangeable with Hoxd13, Hoxc13, Meis1, Meis2, Pbx1, or Pbx3 in this mouse-brain assay.
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation correlation uses transcriptomic output, not direct binding, and the literature comes largely from embryonic limb or reproductive tissues rather than adult brain neurons.

summary: A screen-wide signature-neighbor search did not reveal a recurrent Hoxa13-like perturbation module.
why_it_matters: The nearest perturbations should not be overread as pathway partners because they were weak, concentrated in 308 CB GABA, and overlapped the empirical negative-control range.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlation is based on expression signatures only; the top neighbor coefficients were small and a Safe_target guide reached a similar magnitude in the same cell class.

summary: The mouse-brain data refine human HOXA13 disease biology by showing that a limb-urogenital Hox13 transcription factor is largely buffered in these neuronal populations.
why_it_matters: Human HOXA13 genetics point to developmental hand, foot, genital, and urinary malformations; the Perturb-seq responses do not provide evidence for a broad neuronal mechanism or CNS-directed therapeutic direction.
main_caveats: The assay perturbed postmitotic mouse-brain cell classes, whereas the strongest literature and disease evidence concern embryonic limb and urogenital development.

summary: Cebpe perturbation was not detectably engaged and produced no FDR-significant brain-cell transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: The strongest interpretation is loss of an effective target state, not a subtle CEBPE-regulated neuronal program.
main_caveats: The result is based on transcript-level Wilcoxon summaries and lacks protein or guide-level knockdown QC.

summary: No Cebpe-sensitive brain cell type survived FDR correction; the nominally strongest signatures were weak and not coherent.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-calling upper-layer or limbic glutamatergic nominal tails as CEBPE biology.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The conclusion is about tested brain classes; rare immune cells or unprofiled developmental states were not assessed.

summary: Cebpe perturbation did not move measured transcripts from the granulopoiesis regulatory circuit.
why_it_matters: CEBPE's canonical pathway is hematopoietic; the expected SPI1/GFI1/CSF3R/RARA/RXRA-associated program was silent in the brain screen.
main_caveats: Only genes passing the dataset's expression filters can be evaluated; lack of transcript changes does not test granulocytes.

summary: Myeloid-lineage neighbor perturbations Csf3r, Spi1, Gfi1, Gfi1b and Rxra were buffered like Cebpe.
why_it_matters: The null Cebpe phenotype is not an isolated anomaly; several assayed members or neighbors of granulopoietic regulation formed the same inactive class in these brain cells.
main_caveats: CEBPA/CEBPB/CEBPD paralog perturbations were absent, so the direct C/EBP-family comparison could not be made.

summary: Restricted Cebpe nominal-hit signatures lacked a stable biological nearest-neighbor module.
why_it_matters: Safe-target controls appearing among nearest restricted neighbors warn that the residual correlations are compatible with noise.
main_caveats: The neighbor analysis used nominal top-200 Cebpe genes because there were no FDR-significant genes.

summary: Cebpe brain-screen rows should not be used to infer activation or inhibition strategies for CEBPE-linked neutrophil deficiency or leukemia.
why_it_matters: Disease genetics point to immune and hematologic contexts, whereas this dataset never established an engaged Cebpe perturbation state.
main_caveats: This is a warning about context and assay interpretation, not evidence against CEBPE as a hematopoietic disease gene.

summary: Celsr2 perturbation achieved pan-cell-type target-RNA depletion but produced an almost exclusively on-target differential-expression pattern.
why_it_matters: The result argues that acute Celsr2 loss is transcriptionally buffered in the assayed mouse brain cell states; failure to observe a pathway module is not explained simply by absent target knockdown.
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA, not PCP protein localization, cilia orientation, axon morphology, or synapse physiology.

summary: Gtf2f1 up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut was the only FDR-significant non-target response to Celsr2 knockdown.
why_it_matters: The row is the strongest trans biomarker candidate in the dataset, but its absence from other cell types makes it a restricted candidate rather than a general Celsr2 effector.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Single FDR-level trans gene; Celsr2 itself was only FDR 0.0877 in this cell type; no mechanistic link to Celsr2 was established.

summary: Available Wnt/PCP-neighbor perturbations did not strongly phenocopy Celsr2 despite known pathway proximity; Fzd3 was only a weak, exploratory Celsr2 neighbor in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: Celsr2 and Fzd3 can cooperate genetically in forebrain wiring, so weak acute transcriptomic convergence suggests that the shared biology is developmental, structural, or cell-contact dependent rather than a robust mRNA module in these signatures.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Fzd3 convergence is based on a small Pearson r=0.1056 and Fzd3 had no FDR-significant response in the same cell type; several canonical PCP genes were not assayed as comparators.

summary: Celsr2 knockdown did not evoke a recurrent ciliary, CSF-flow, or neuronal-migration transcriptional program in assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This refines hydrocephalus and Joubert-literature expectations by placing major disease-relevant Celsr2 actions in ependymal, developmental, and morphogenetic settings not captured as a generic acute neuronal mRNA response.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks a direct ependymal-cilia perturbation readout and cannot test CSF-flow or developmental migration phenotypes.

summary: The dataset provides no broad repair-like transcriptional activation after Celsr2 knockdown, even though Celsr2 inhibition is pro-regenerative in motor-neuron injury models and Celsr2 supports adult cortical synapses.
why_it_matters: A CELSR2 loss-of-function strategy is likely to be cell-type and phenotype dependent; transcriptionally silent knockdown in many brain neurons should not be equated with either efficacy or safety.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is not an axon-injury or adult cortical synapse assay, so this is a directional caution rather than a direct therapeutic test.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only class with FDR-level Kcnq3 self-knockdown, yet the verified knockdown did not propagate to any FDR-significant non-target transcript.
why_it_matters: This separates successful transcript depletion from an absence of an acute RNA-state response, consistent with a channel whose primary phenotype may be electrophysiologic or subcellular rather than a broad mRNA program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Perturb-seq did not assay channel conductance, axonal localization, or protein abundance; the strongest non-target nominal genes still had FDR=0.866.

summary: Kcnq3 perturbation was dominated by weak or absent transcript engagement across the screen, with only two FDR hits in 371818 rows and no FDR-significant genes in 20 of 22 assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: The dataset should be treated primarily as a negative or under-engaged Kcnq3 perturbation survey rather than as a map of KCNQ3-regulated transcriptional pathways across the brain.
main_caveats: FDR correction was genome-wide within each contrast, and moderate nominal shifts may still be real; several Kcnq3 cell-type bins had fewer than 60 perturbed cells.

summary: Kcnq3 did not reproduce Kcnq2 or Kcnq5 transcriptomic signatures, even though KCNQ2 and KCNQ3 are canonical M-channel partners.
why_it_matters: Known channel coassembly does not translate into interchangeable scRNA perturbation signatures in this dataset; the Kcnq3 arm was much more limited by on-target engagement than Kcnq2.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is signature-based and Kcnq3 signatures were themselves weak, so lack of correlation cannot prove functional divergence of the ion channels.

summary: Coq2 up-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut was the sole non-target FDR hit and occurred without measurable Kcnq3 self-knockdown.
why_it_matters: Coq2 is the only downstream transcript that survives correction, but its isolation and absent target engagement make it an exploratory biomarker or off-mechanism quality-control signal rather than a confident Kcnq3 pathway output.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Single gene in one cell type; no Kcnq3 target knockdown in the same contrast; no supporting recurrent mitochondrial or Kv7 module was detected.

summary: The Perturb-seq loss-of-transcript phenotype is weaker than the known KCNQ3 seizure biology, warning that absence of an acute mRNA response should not be read as evidence that KCNQ3 inhibition is safe or therapeutically aligned.
why_it_matters: Human genetics and Kv7 opener pharmacology point toward preserving or increasing KCNQ2/KCNQ3 current in seizure settings, whereas this screen only weakly depleted Kcnq3 mRNA and did not measure excitability or channel localization.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Clinical evidence concerns human germline variants or pharmacologic channel openers, not partial CRISPR knockdown in adult mouse neurons; the dataset lacks seizure or electrophysiology readouts.

summary: Ets1 loss of function was transcriptionally silent across the assayed neuronal brain classes.
why_it_matters: The main dataset conclusion is absence of a detectable neuronal Ets1 program, not a weak pathway hit hidden below stringent FDR thresholds.
cell_types: all 23 assayed Glut/GABA/Dopa neuronal classes
main_caveats: The null response occurs together with weak on-target transcript engagement, so it cannot distinguish failed guide activity from lack of Ets1 expression or requirement in these neurons.

summary: The top Ets1 nominal genes were isolated events rather than a recurrent module.
why_it_matters: Nominal genes such as Sox6 in Pvalb cells or Gabbr1 in dopaminergic cells should be treated as triage hints, not as validated Ets1-regulated neuronal biomarkers.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|215 MB Dopa|other assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: This finding is a rejection of nominal hits as a module; it does not prove that any listed gene is directly regulated by ETS1.

summary: Known Ras/Raf/MEK/ERK neighbors did not phenocopy Ets1 in the neuronal screen.
why_it_matters: Although ETS1 is a curated MAPK effector, perturbing Braf, Hras, Kras, Map2k1, Map2k2, Mapk1, or Raf1 did not yield Ets1-like transcriptomes, suggesting that the MAPK-ETS axis is either inactive, indirect, or context-restricted in these classes.
cell_types: all shared assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: Whole-transcriptome correlation is an indirect pathway readout; MAPK perturbations have many ETS1-independent effects, and Ets1 had no strong signature to match.

summary: Screened ETS-family perturbations failed to converge with Ets1, while Ets2 was absent.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not support interchangeability between Ets1 and the screened ETS genes Elf2, Etv6, or Spi1 in neurons, but it also cannot test the best documented Ets1/Ets2 buffering relationship.
cell_types: all shared assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: Elf2, Etv6, and Spi1 are ETS-family contrasts rather than close Ets2 substitutes; all of these neuronal correlations are limited by the weak Ets1 signature.

summary: The neuronal null result redirects disease interpretation toward immune and vascular ETS1 biology rather than a cell-autonomous neuronal ETS1 mechanism.
why_it_matters: ETS1 has autoimmune and endothelial literature support, including SLE risk alleles associated with lower ETS1 expression in peripheral blood cells; the Perturb-seq result argues that the assayed neuronal classes are a poor context for modeling that direction of effect.
cell_types: assayed neuronal classes absent of vascular and immune lineages
main_caveats: The dataset lacks endothelial, pericyte, leukocyte, and lymphoid cells; it therefore refines the cell type in which to test ETS1 rather than testing the immune or vascular mechanisms directly.

summary: F2-targeting perturbations did not measurably engage the F2 transcript in any profiled cell type.
why_it_matters: Without target repression, downstream F2 DE signatures cannot be interpreted as loss of prothrombin within the assayed cells; the result is consistent with F2 being a liver-derived secreted plasma factor rather than a robust neuronal transcript.
main_caveats: Transcript only; sgRNA DNA editing or unmeasured protein effects were not assayed, and fold changes are unstable around near-zero expression.

summary: F2 produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response, with only isolated nominal peaks in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The largest scalar changes do not establish a cell-type-specific F2 program and should not be promoted to pathway enrichment or biomarker claims.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The absence of significant DE is interpretable only for this cell-intrinsic brain assay; two low-count cell types are underpowered.

summary: F2 targeting did not move the assayed coagulation, thrombomodulin, or protease-activated receptor transcript set.
why_it_matters: Canonical F2 biology is an extracellular coagulation/PAR pathway; the lack of transcriptional movement in F2, Thbd, F2r, F2rl2, F2rl3, and related clotting factors argues against an autocrine thrombin-feedback loop in these Perturb-seq cells.
main_caveats: PAR signaling can be acute and post-transcriptional; some fibrinogen genes were only detected in a subset of cell-type DE tables.

summary: Neither Thbd nor any genome-wide signature neighbor produced a strong F2-like or anti-F2-like expression pattern.
why_it_matters: The weak F2 result is not part of a hidden related-target module; even the closest available thrombin cofactor and all top positive and negative signature neighbors are near zero in correlation.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Because F2 itself is not engaged, correlations are a quality-control negative result rather than evidence against the biochemical F2-THBD relationship.

summary: This Perturb-seq negative result should not be extrapolated to therapeutic thrombin inhibition or extracellular CNS thrombin/PAR signaling.
why_it_matters: F2 is a drugged coagulation target with vascular disease genetics, but direct thrombin inhibitors block extracellular protease activity; the screen measured an unengaged intracellular transcript in mouse brain cell classes.
comparators: direct thrombin inhibitor pharmacology|CNS PAR activation literature
main_caveats: The dataset has no thrombin activity measurement, plasma compartment, vascular injury model, astrocyte-enriched assay, or drug exposure.

summary: Btbd9 guide targeting produced at most weak nominal depletion of the target transcript and no FDR-significant downstream gene in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq assay does not expose a robust acute mRNA program downstream of Btbd9, so the strongest interpretation is buffering or inadequate transcriptional target engagement rather than a large cell-autonomous expression phenotype.
main_caveats: The dataset measures transcript abundance, not protein loss, sleep, motor, iron, dopamine, or electrophysiological phenotypes; all Btbd9 target-transcript FDR values were 1.0.

summary: Cell classes that approximate striatal, cerebellar, or dopaminergic contexts emphasized by Btbd9 animal work were not the places where this dataset captured a Btbd9 response.
why_it_matters: Published RLS models place Btbd9 biology in striatal MSNs, Purkinje neurons, and dopaminergic systems; the null 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 308 CB GABA responses plus absence of a 215 MB Dopa Btbd9 signature make those mechanisms under-sampled here rather than disproven.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|308 CB GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 308 CB GABA are broad taxonomy classes, not purified medium spiny or Purkinje neurons; 215 MB Dopa was absent for Btbd9 rather than tested.

summary: The RLS genetics neighbors Meis1 and Ptprd did not converge with Btbd9 at the acute transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: Human genetics groups BTBD9, MEIS1, and PTPRD as RLS risk loci, but the mouse Perturb-seq signatures were near-orthogonal, arguing against a shared immediate mRNA module as the point of convergence in this assay.
main_caveats: Meis1 and Ptprd were themselves weak in the dataset, with no FDR<0.05 gene rows, so the result cannot exclude chronic developmental or circuit-level convergence.

summary: Btbd9 signatures were not aligned with dopamine/adenosine receptor, iron-regulatory, or core clock perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: Btbd9 models implicate dopamine, iron, rest-phase sleep, and circadian behavior; the absence of correlation with direct perturbations of those modules suggests that any Btbd9 effect on them is indirect, protein-level, chronic, or restricted to cell states not effectively perturbed here.
main_caveats: Correlation used restricted score vectors and does not assay dopamine, iron, ubiquitination, or clock physiology directly.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor search found no convincing positive or negative Btbd9 transcriptomic neighbor.
why_it_matters: If Btbd9 had a strong hidden module, unrelated perturbations should have recapitulated or opposed it; the maximum |r| was below 0.20, reinforcing that the Btbd9 program is dominated by cell-count-limited noise or buffered biology.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations over all measured genes can miss sparse nonlinear responses; the top neighbors are treated as a negative-control result, not as mechanistic candidates.

direction: weak nominal decrease of Copa mRNA; no FDR-significant downstream direction
summary: Copa perturbation produced no within-cell-type FDR-significant transcriptional response and only weak measured target depletion.
why_it_matters: COPA is a core coatomer protein, but this guide set does not create a decisive loss-of-function state; the dominant interpretation of the Perturb-seq result is therefore target-engagement limited rather than a mapped COPI stress program.
main_caveats: FDR was evaluated within each cell-type table; absence of significant differential expression does not prove that strong biallelic COPA loss would be silent.

direction: exploratory nominal depletion in a subset of classes without transcriptome-wide propagation
summary: The most negative Copa self-effects were nominal and did not coincide with any FDR-significant downstream response; the largest cell-count classes were also buffered or unengaged.
why_it_matters: This separates apparent cell-type restriction from guide performance: L5 ET and CTX-CGE cells had the lowest nominal target logFC, whereas thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c and Pvalb groups had more cells but little target repression.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Target self-depletion never survived multiple testing; the cell-type pattern may reflect stochastic guide efficacy or low cell counts rather than true biology.

summary: Copa did not transcriptionally converge with measured early-secretory neighbors despite belonging to the COPI coatomer module.
why_it_matters: COPG1 is a high-confidence COPA-associated coatomer subunit and SEC23A/SAR1B report adjacent COPII traffic, yet Copg1 and Sec23a perturbations mainly changed their own mRNAs and the Copa score vector was nearly uncorrelated with Copg1, Sec23a, or Sar1b.
main_caveats: Most COPI subunits were not in the perturbation library, and Copa itself was weakly engaged, so the contrast is strongest as a warning against assuming complex-level interchangeability from this dataset.

direction: expected inflammatory and UPR induction absent
summary: The mouse neuronal Copa perturbation did not trigger the interferon, Th17-cytokine, or ER-stress markers that define immune COPA-syndrome models.
why_it_matters: Published COPA-syndrome mechanisms are dominated by mutant-COPA/COPI-STING biology in patient immune cells and engineered models; their absence here narrows the dataset-supported context to weak loss of Copa expression in profiled brain neurons, not pathogenic WD40-domain COPA signaling.
comparators: COPA syndrome patient cells|CopaE241K/+ mice|COPI-deficient immune cell models
main_caveats: The key STING transcript Tmem173 was not measured in the Copa rows; guide engagement was weak and the assayed cell classes were not patient immune cells.

direction: clinical STING axis not induced in the neuronal perturbation data
summary: STING-directed therapeutic logic from COPA syndrome should not be read out as a neuronal COPA-knockdown signature in this dataset.
why_it_matters: STING blockade is mechanistically attractive in COPI-deficient inflammatory models, but the Perturb-seq data lack the interferon/UPR biomarkers that would connect partial Copa repression in these mouse brain cells to that treatment axis; direct-COPA small-molecule benchmarking was also not available from the limited ChEMBL binding records.
comparators: STING inhibitor H-151|COPA syndrome PBMCs|COPI-deficient cell lines
main_caveats: This is a context warning, not evidence against STING inhibition for COPA-syndrome immune disease.

summary: Hivep1 perturbation was FDR-null across all 22 assayed cell types despite direct measurement of the target transcript.
why_it_matters: This prevents pathway or biomarker claims from being built on nominal one-off genes and identifies Hivep1 as weakly engaged or buffered in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq assay.
main_caveats: The result is transcriptomic and depends on weak RNA-level target engagement; protein loss and editing efficiency were not measured in the parquet.

summary: The two cell types with nominal Hivep1 transcript decreases, 052 Pvalb Gaba and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, had no downstream FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: Even the most directionally engaged strata did not show a detectable secondary program, so apparent cell-type differences should not be elevated to positive biology.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The target rows themselves remained FDR = 1.0, so this is a conditional buffered-response interpretation rather than proof of successful knockout.

summary: Hivep1 did not converge with HIVEP paralogs or NF-kB-family neighbors in whole-transcriptome score space.
why_it_matters: HIVEP1 should not be treated as an interchangeable neural proxy for HIVEP2/HIVEP3 or for Nfkb1/Nfkb2/Relb in this dataset.
main_caveats: The comparator signatures were also mostly weak, so the contrast is most informative as absence of detectable convergence.

summary: The immune HIVEP1/NF-kB regulatory axis was not detectably activated by Hivep1 perturbation in the unstimulated brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A loss-of-HIVEP1 inflammatory expectation from monocytes/macrophages does not transfer directly to the neural Perturb-seq context.
main_caveats: The literature system was TLR/bacterial stimulation in immune cells, whereas the dataset profiles brain cells without a defined inflammatory challenge.

summary: Hivep1 produced neither a repeated nominal biomarker module nor a strong positive or negative signature neighbor, limiting translational interpretation.
why_it_matters: The current data do not support an RNA biomarker panel, a rescue signature, or a clear drug-development direction for HIVEP1 perturbation.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor analysis used weak Hivep1 score vectors; only three representative cell types were searched for unrestricted neighbors.

direction: Gpi1 down; downstream mRNA response buffered
summary: FDR-confirmed Gpi1 RNA depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut produced a nearly target-only transcriptomic phenotype.
why_it_matters: GPI is a core dimeric glycolytic enzyme, so the lack of broad FDR-level mRNA remodeling after measurable knockdown argues that acute partial Gpi1 loss is buffered at the transcriptional level in these adult brain neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only mRNA was measured; residual GPI protein, metabolites, glycolytic flux, and delayed responses were not assayed.

direction: mostly weak or subthreshold target engagement
summary: Most Gpi1 cell-type tests were not interpretable as successful knockdowns after multiple testing.
why_it_matters: Directionally negative on-target rows alone are insufficient: only 2 of 22 target rows reached FDR<0.05, two additional target rows were FDR near-misses, and hippocampal CA1/DG and CA3/CA2-FC/DG examples showed essentially no Gpi1 reduction despite dozens of perturbed cells.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Some failures may reflect guide efficiency, transcript capture, or sample size rather than true cell-type resistance to Gpi1 perturbation.

summary: Gpi1 signatures were transcriptionally uncoupled from perturbations of neighboring glycolysis or hexosamine-pathway genes.
why_it_matters: Although Gpi1 is directly connected to Tpi1, Pfkm, Pgk1, Gapdh, Hk1, and related enzymes, the same-cell-type Gpi1 score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with those perturbations, so shared pathway membership did not translate into interchangeable Perturb-seq signatures.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic, not metabolic; Gpi1 produced little downstream signal and gRNA efficacy differs across target genes.

summary: Ogt is an exploratory recurrent nominally downregulated marker in the two strongest Gpi1 knockdowns.
why_it_matters: Because glucose carbon can feed the hexosamine biosynthetic pathway upstream of OGT's UDP-GlcNAc donor, repeated Ogt mRNA decreases could mark a weak carbohydrate-flux response to Gpi1 loss worth testing with O-GlcNAc or metabolite measurements.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Ogt was not FDR<0.05 in either cell type, the 155 MB Glut Ogt FDR was 1.0, and Ogt transcript abundance is only an indirect proxy for O-GlcNAc signaling.

direction: partial knockdown without broad acute mRNA program
summary: The dataset separates adult-neuron partial Gpi1 knockdown from genetic GPI deficiency or complete Gpi1 loss.
why_it_matters: Human GPI deficiency and mouse Gpi1 loss-of-function show clinically severe hematologic, developmental, and occasional neurologic phenotypes, whereas the Perturb-seq state after partial adult neuronal RNA depletion lacked a broad acute transcriptional disease program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This does not test biallelic null disease, erythrocytes, embryogenesis, extracellular neuroleukin biology, or metabolic flux; the result is a limitation of the model as much as a buffering phenotype.

summary: Elf2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant reduction of its own transcript and almost no genome-wide adjusted response across 23 assayed brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The core result is a context-specific or engagement-limited null phenotype; it prevents assigning most nominal rows to ELF2 loss of function.
main_caveats: The DE table does not report raw expression or per-guide concordance, so guide inefficacy and low Elf2 expression cannot be separated.

summary: Stxbp2 induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only FDR-significant Elf2 response and was directionally recurrent but not FDR-significant in several other cell types.
why_it_matters: This nominates a vesicle-trafficking marker as the only concrete Elf2-associated output in the screen, but not as a proven direct target.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Stxbp2 event was single-gene at FDR and occurred in a cell type where Elf2 itself was not significantly reduced.

summary: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut had the strongest nominal Elf2 decrease but no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This is the best example of a possible buffered cell-type response to Elf2 perturbation.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Target decrease was nominal only, n=47 perturbed cells, and all adjusted downstream p values were 1.0.

summary: Ets1, Etv6, and Spi1 perturbations did not phenocopy Elf2, with Etv6 and Elf2 affecting different genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating ETS-family perturbations as interchangeable in this screen and matches promoter- and isoform-specific ELF2 biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and most Elf2 responses were weak.

summary: Elf2 perturbation in neuronal brain classes was uncoupled from reported RUNX1/B-cell and Tie2/endothelial ELF2 programs.
why_it_matters: Canonical ELF2 annotations should not be projected onto these neuronal phenotypes without evidence that those programs are coexpressed and responsive.
main_caveats: The literature is from immune, endothelial, or transformed cells, and the mouse Reactome pathway is electronically inferred.

summary: The dataset does not justify a direct ELF2 therapeutic direction or repurposing hypothesis.
why_it_matters: Weak on-target evidence, low-cell nominal hits, modest restricted signature neighbors, and absent curated ChEMBL ELF2 target records leave no actionable ELF2 modulation axis.
main_caveats: This is an absence-of-evidence warning, not a proof that ELF2 is biologically or pharmacologically irrelevant in other contexts.

direction: weak target decrease; no FDR-significant downstream response
summary: Crppa perturbation did not generate any FDR-significant transcriptomic phenotype in the 22 tested brain cell types, and target-transcript knockdown itself was only nominal.
why_it_matters: This makes the correct first interpretation a weak-engagement/negative Perturb-seq result rather than a silent but confident CRPPA-loss state.
main_caveats: RNA depletion was not FDR-significant in any cell type, so buffered biology cannot be separated from incomplete perturbation.

summary: Crppa reduction failed to trigger detectable mRNA feedback in measured alpha-dystroglycan O-mannosylation or extracellular-matrix pathway genes.
why_it_matters: CRPPA supplies the CDP-ribitol donor used for a post-translational alpha-dystroglycan glycan; the dataset suggests that mild neuronal Crppa perturbation is not reported back through steady-state transcription of that module.
main_caveats: The input Crppa knockdown was weak and the assay measured RNA, not alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation.

summary: Functionally connected dystroglycan-network perturbations were not interchangeable with Crppa in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Agrn and Large1 showed clearer on-target signatures than Crppa, whereas Crppa score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Agrn, Dag1, Fktn, Large1, Lrp4, Rxylt1, and Dpm1; a biochemical pathway relationship did not translate into a shared brain-cell RNA signature.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from weak Crppa signatures, so the contrast is strongest as a non-phenocopy result, not as mechanistic antagonism.

summary: The largest individual Crppa-associated genes are exploratory, cell-type-localized nominal candidates rather than validated biomarkers.
why_it_matters: Casc3, Pex5l, Fgf1, Slc7a1, Hp1bp3, and Klhl29 ranked at the top of specific Crppa contrasts, but none survived FDR and several came from low-n cell types, so they should only seed follow-up checks.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: All adjusted p values were at least 0.186, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 33 and 31 perturbed cells.

direction: protein-glycan endpoint favored over mRNA endpoint
summary: This dataset does not support using a cell-type mRNA signature as a near-term pharmacodynamic endpoint for CDP-ribitol restoration of CRPPA deficiency.
why_it_matters: Published rescue strategies target metabolite replacement and alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation, whereas the Perturb-seq response supplied no robust transcript or pathway biomarker under mild Crppa perturbation.
main_caveats: Therapeutic work was largely in muscle-selective Ispd deficiency and fibroblasts, whereas this dataset assayed mouse brain RNA after weak perturbation.

direction: ER chaperone and ERAD genes up; Erc1 down
summary: Hspa5 perturbation produced a multiple-testing-corrected ER chaperone and ERAD response primarily in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The dataset response lands on the expected BiP/UPR biology, but the corrected signal is sharply concentrated in one thalamic glutamatergic population rather than uniformly present wherever Hspa5 was sampled.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The cell type has only 47 Hspa5-perturbed cells, and mRNA DE does not demonstrate BiP protein depletion directly.

summary: The Hspa5 transcript itself was not detectably depleted even where downstream ER-stress genes were induced.
why_it_matters: Direct target mRNA is therefore a poor engagement readout for this perturbation; the positive or neutral Hspa5 mRNA values are consistent with a buffered autoregulatory UPR target rather than a simple transcript knockdown signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Guide editing could affect protein sequence without lowering mRNA; without protein or genotype measurements the exact engagement mechanism remains unresolved.

summary: Several other neuronal classes carried the same ER-proteostasis genes as only nominal hits, implying that strict FDR thresholds partially mask a recurrent but low-power Hspa5 response.
why_it_matters: This prevents a false binary interpretation in which all non-151 cell types are biologically inert; Pdia and Hyou1 family markers repeatedly trended upward but rarely with enough support to survive testing.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All examples outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut are nominal or near-FDR trends, not FDR<0.05 discoveries.

summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Hspa5 signature converged with Hspa9, Hspa8, Uba5, and Ufc1 perturbations much more than with Atf6, Manf, Hsp90ab1, or Hspd1.
why_it_matters: The result links ER BiP stress to mitochondrial Hsp70 and UFMylation/proteostasis perturbation states instead of to every chaperone or upstream UPR neighbor indiscriminately.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Signature similarity is correlative, and the Uba5/Ufc1 relationship is based on whole-transcriptome similarity rather than direct epistasis.

summary: Beyond ER folding genes, Hspa5 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut recruited an ISR-like amino-acid and mitochondrial-stress tail including Asns, Slc38a2, Vars, Shmt2, Cyb5r1, Ddit3, and Chac1.
why_it_matters: This suggests that Hspa5-axis stress in this neuronal context is read out not only as a compensatory chaperone/ERAD program but also as nutrient-redox and ATF4-linked stress that could become maladaptive if sustained.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Several tail genes, including Chac1 and Shmt2, are nominal at FDR≈0.2 in Hspa5 and should be treated as biologically motivated, not stand-alone, hits.

summary: Pcyt2 perturbation induced a strong cholesterol/SREBP-like transcriptional module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Rather than a generic stress response, the largest Pcyt2 phenotype was membrane-lipid specific and centered on Insig1, Hmgcr, Ldlr, Srebf2, and multiple sterol enzymes, extending the known PCYT2-PE reaction to a neuron-intrinsic sterol response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Pcyt2 transcript itself was not depleted in this class, so the module supports pathway engagement but does not quantify residual PCYT2 enzyme activity.

summary: The Pcyt2 response was sharply concentrated in thalamic glutamatergic classes, with a dominant 151 response, a weaker 145 sterol shadow, and no FDR-level response in 21 of 23 classes.
why_it_matters: Cell identity is a larger determinant of the transcriptional consequence than the presence of a Pcyt2 guide, arguing against a uniform neuronal lipid-stress program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The absence of FDR hits in most classes may reflect true buffering, lower effective editing, or insufficient power in low-count classes; cell-type-specific lipid measurements are unavailable.

summary: Pcyt2 and Selenoi perturbations converged on the 151 sterol/lipogenic module, even though their whole-transcriptome signatures were only weakly correlated.
why_it_matters: Selenoi/EPT1 acts downstream of PCYT2 in the same CDP-ethanolamine PE pathway, so shared induction of Insig1, Msmo1, and Fdft1 supports the interpretation that the Pcyt2 response reflects PE-synthesis strain rather than an isolated off-target signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The convergence is strong within the sterol/lipogenic gene panel but not across the entire transcriptome.

summary: The 151 sterol response was not accompanied by transcriptional upregulation of the closest measured Kennedy-pathway or phosphatidylserine-rescue enzymes.
why_it_matters: Pcyt2-perturbed neurons did not simply compensate by increasing Etnk, Selenoi, Cept1, Pisd, Ptdss1/2, or Pcyt1a/b mRNAs; the detectable compensation was displaced toward sterol and lipid-remodeling genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is an mRNA-only negative result; flux through PE, PC, PS, Lands-cycle, and etherlipid reactions could change without corresponding transcript changes.

summary: Pcyt2 perturbation also downregulated Cpe and Pcsk2 in the responsive 151 class, adding a secretory peptide-processing axis to the lipid signature.
why_it_matters: Human PCYT2 disease affects the brain, but prior lipidomic studies emphasize etherlipids; this dataset nominates a neuron-specific Cpe/Pcsk2 decrease as a possible downstream consequence of PCYT2-pathway stress.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Cpe and Pcsk2 passed FDR<0.05; Vgf and Scg5 were nominal, and no peptide abundance or secretion assay was performed.

summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba showed the strongest nominal decrease of the Pcyt2 transcript but no significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: A cell type can show measurable target-transcript movement without converting it into a detectable lipid-stress program, implying buffering or a perturbation threshold.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Pcyt2 mRNA decrease was nominal and FDR=1.0; this is a buffered-response hypothesis, not proof of unchanged PE flux.

direction: Fam149b transcript down; downstream FDR response absent
summary: Fam149b perturbation was transcriptome-buffered even in the cell type with the cleanest nominal target-mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: The strongest direct target readout occurred in cortical L2/3 IT glutamatergic cells, yet no gene passed multiple-testing correction, arguing that the achieved perturbation did not trigger a broad neuronal mRNA program in the assayed state.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: On-target depletion was nominal rather than FDR-significant in all cell types; Perturb-seq mRNA output cannot measure cilium length, IFT turnaround, or developmental morphogenesis directly.

summary: Fam149b signatures did not converge on the expected primary-cilium/SHH transcriptional neighborhood.
why_it_matters: FAM149B1 is curated and experimentally linked to protein localization to cilium, cilium assembly, SHH/Smoothened signaling, and TBC1D32-dependent IFT turnaround, so the near-zero correlations with Tbc1d32, Ift88, Smo, Ptch1, and Gli-family perturbations indicate that this dataset did not resolve the canonical ciliary mechanism as a shared neuronal transcriptional module.
main_caveats: Correlation analysis used mRNA ranks after perturbation, not ciliary protein localization or morphology; many of the cilium-gene perturbations also had weak target-transcript readout.

summary: Sin3b down-regulation in pineal glutamatergic cells was the only FDR-significant gene-level event but was decoupled from target knockdown.
why_it_matters: This keeps the lone formal hit visible while preventing it from being mistaken for a robust Fam149b-loss biomarker.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The cell type had only 37 perturbed cells, all other genes had FDR=1.0, and the measured Fam149b transcript was not reduced.

summary: Stronger cilium-gene knockdowns in MB Glut did not phenocopy the Fam149b signature.
why_it_matters: Ahi1 and Cplane1 showed FDR-significant self-depletion in the same MB Glut class where Fam149b had only weak self-depletion, yet their signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Fam149b; this argues against treating all assayed ciliopathy-gene perturbations as interchangeable transcriptional surrogates.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The literature reference is through shared ciliary biology rather than a direct FAM149B1-AHI1-CPLANE1 complex; only mRNA endpoints were compared.

summary: Weak Fam149b responses were present even in well-sampled cell types.
why_it_matters: The null result should not be attributed solely to rare-cell sampling: several classes had 142-230 Fam149b-perturbed cells yet still lacked FDR target depletion or downstream FDR hits.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba

summary: The dataset gives no support for a universal neuronal mRNA signature of FAM149B1-related Joubert ciliopathy.

summary: Known Ago2, Src/PI3K, and SREBP1 pathway neighbors and unbiased signature neighbors did not converge on Fam120a.

summary: Cd3d perturbation produced no FDR-significant neuronal transcriptomic response in any profiled cell class.
why_it_matters: The dominant biological conclusion is absence of a detectable Cd3d-dependent state in these mouse-brain neuronal populations, in line with CD3D being an immune TCR-chain gene rather than a neuronal effector.
cell_types: all 21 Cd3d-profiled neuronal classes
main_caveats: Cd3d was tested in 21 of 23 file-wide cell types, and many groups had only 22-45 perturbed cells.

summary: The Cd3d target transcript did not show rank-based knockdown in the measured Cd3d cells.
