cell_types: all 21 Cd3d-profiled neuronal classes
main_caveats: Transcript-level target engagement cannot distinguish a biologically absent target from an expressed protein that is not captured by this scRNA-seq assay, but the p values give no evidence of mRNA depletion.

summary: Screened CD3/TCR-complex perturbations converged on the same FDR-null phenotype rather than producing subunit-specific neuronal signatures.
why_it_matters: Cd3d, Cd3e, Cd3g, Cd247, and Cd4 are related immune-receptor components; their shared inactivity supports loss of the whole TCR module in the assayed neuronal context instead of a Cd3d-specific assay failure.
main_caveats: This comparison covers only subunits and CD4 present in the screen; Lck, Zap70, Cd8a, and Cd8b1 were measured as transcripts but were not Cd3d comparator perturbations.

summary: Cd3d perturbation failed to move the measured proximal TCR/CD3 signaling genes.
why_it_matters: The canonical CD3 chain signals through a multi-protein TCR pathway, but Cd3d loss in these brain cells did not propagate to Cd3e, Cd3g, Cd247, Lck/Fyn, Zap70, Lat, Cd4/Cd8, Ptpn6, Skap1, or Cd6 transcripts.
cell_types: all 21 Cd3d-profiled neuronal classes
main_caveats: The measurement is transcriptomic; it does not assay ITAM phosphorylation or acute protein signaling.

summary: No robust Cd3d-response biomarker emerged; the largest nominal genes were isolated or directionally mixed.
why_it_matters: Fam91a1, Skic2, Sp3, Tlcd4, Add3, Lrch2, and Opcml should be treated as exploratory nominal hits, not as Cd3d biomarkers.
main_caveats: This is a negative biomarker assessment based on corrected p values and recurrence; it does not exclude subtle effects detectable with many more cells.

summary: CD3D disease biology is not reproduced in this neuronal Perturb-seq context.
why_it_matters: CD3D mutations can block human and mouse T-cell development, so the FDR-null brain-cell response redirects mechanism and therapeutic reasoning toward thymocytes or T-lineage cells rather than mature neurons.
cell_types: all 21 Cd3d-profiled neuronal classes
main_caveats: The dataset tests cultured/assayed mouse brain cell classes and cannot address CD3D function in thymus, peripheral T cells, or infiltrating immune cells.

summary: The Perturb-seq signature did not reproduce the strong neurogenetic phenotypes expected from complete MICU1 loss-of-function.

main_caveats: The screen lacks calcium imaging, mitochondrial phenotyping, protein quantification, and long-term degeneration endpoints.

summary: Grhl2 perturbation was essentially silent across the profiled mouse brain cell types.

summary: The largest Grhl2 cell populations still had no downstream response, arguing that the null is not explained only by very small perturbation counts.

summary: The GRHL2 epithelial-state circuit was not co-engaged in brain: Grhl2, Ovol2, and Gata3 were flat, whereas Zeb1 and Cdh2 produced separate effects in selected thalamic and midbrain populations.

direction: immune disease link not mirrored by neuronal DE

summary: Stat1, an Irf8 network neighbor, showed on-target knockdown in selected neuronal classes but almost no downstream response.

summary: IRF-family perturbations did not converge into an Irf8-like signature in the neuronal data.

summary: Jarid2 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic change in any of the 23 measured mouse-brain cell classes.

summary: The only structured nominal Jarid2 response was concentrated in 308 CB GABA.

summary: The smallest Jarid2 cell groups generated large isolated single-gene scores but not actionable cell-type programs.

summary: Jarid2 did not converge with or oppose the available H3K27-demethylase, Trithorax, or SWI/SNF-family chromatin perturbations.
why_it_matters: Because canonical PRC2 subunit perturbations were absent, the best in-library pathway-neighbor test was correlation with Kdm6a, Kdm6b, Arid1b, Smarca4, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Kmt2a, Kmt2d, Setd1a, and Kdm5b; their near-zero score correlations argue that the weak Jarid2 signatures are not a generic chromatin-regulator or H3K27-axis response.

summary: The mouse-brain dataset does not show a mature pan-neuronal acute signature that mirrors human JARID2 haploinsufficiency.
why_it_matters: Human JARID2 loss-of-function causes a variable neurodevelopmental disorder, while the perturb-seq result is FDR-null even in well-sampled neuronal classes; this points follow-up toward developmental progenitor timing, chromatin-state readouts, or gene-dosage models instead of expecting a large uniform RNA response in every mature neuron class.
main_caveats: Species, developmental stage, assay, and perturbation modality differ from human germline haploinsufficiency; the dataset does not exclude rare or earlier susceptible cells.

summary: Irf5 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic response and no significant self-transcript decrease across the 22 assayed Glut/GABA groups.

summary: The weak adult neuronal mRNA response contrasts with FRMD5 human and mouse neurodevelopmental phenotypes, pointing to developmental, synaptic-structural, proteomic, or non-cell-autonomous mechanisms that this acute transcriptomic assay may not capture.

summary: Glud1 targeting was directionally on-target in every assayed cell type, but FDR-level target engagement was confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

summary: In the best-engaged thalamic class, Glud1 weakly converged with Got2 but not with Gls, Got1, or glutamate-receptor subunit perturbations.

summary: The canonical mitochondrial glutamate-to-alpha-ketoglutarate pathway was not accompanied by a coherent TCA-cycle or neurotransmitter-pathway mRNA module after Glud1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: GLUD1 catalysis directly changes carbon and nitrogen flux; the transcriptome instead shows that guide-induced Glud1 loss can be largely pathway-uncoupled at the mRNA level in the assayed steady state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: A transcriptome without metabolites cannot test alpha-ketoglutarate production, ammonia handling, NAD(P)H, or TCA flux directly.

summary: The dataset models reduced Glud1 expression, whereas the main GLUD1 Mendelian hyperinsulinism mechanism is activating mutation.
why_it_matters: Clinical extrapolation has to keep directionality straight: a knockdown signature is closer to GDH deficiency than human HI/HA gain of function, and a sparse mRNA response alone should not be read as evidence that GDH inhibition is benign in brain.
main_caveats: The perturbation reduces transcript rather than introducing catalytic GOF or LOF alleles, and no endocrine cells were assayed.

summary: Cacnb2 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic response in any assayed brain cell type and only weak nominal on-target transcript decreases.

direction: Cacnb2 weaker than related CaV subunits

summary: Human CACNB2 genetics implicate calcium-channel gating in psychiatric and cardiac disease, but this mouse-brain perturbation generated no transcriptional biomarker of that activity.

summary: Gli1 perturbation lacked detectable on-target Gli1 transcript suppression in all 23 profiled cell types.

summary: Mctp1 in 052 Pvalb Gaba and Amph in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut were the only FDR-significant Gli1-response genes, and both decreased in a single cell type.

summary: Cdon was an exploratory positive restricted-signature neighbor of Gli1 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.

summary: The dataset's GLI1 silence fits a context in which adult Hh/Gli signaling is concentrated in neural stem cells and astrocyte subsets rather than broadly in the assayed neuronal classes.

main_caveats: The parquet does not include explicit astrocyte or neural-stem-cell contrasts for direct comparison.

summary: Upstream SMO druggability should not be equated with broad GLI1-dependent transcriptional vulnerability in adult neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: SMO inhibitors are clinically developed Hh-pathway drugs, but these neuronal contrasts were mostly insensitive to Gli1 and neighboring Hh perturbations, cautioning against direct extrapolation to neuronal GLI1 biology.
main_caveats: The result is transcriptomic, mouse, neuronal, and engagement-limited; it should not be used to infer systemic CNS safety or efficacy of SMO inhibitors.

summary: FDR-significant Chrnb2 self-depletion was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.

summary: Cblb did not phenocopy assayed FYN/SH3KBP1/PI3K or antigen-receptor pathway neighbors in neuronal RNA signatures.

summary: A reported neuronal Cbl-b-GluN2B mechanism was not mirrored by Grin2b or NMDA-receptor mRNA changes in this mouse-brain panel.
why_it_matters: The mismatch is biologically plausible because the published mechanism is ubiquitination and receptor trafficking; a transcript-only Perturb-seq assay would miss GluN2B protein turnover unless it secondarily changes RNA abundance.

direction: immune activation expected outside assayed neurons
summary: The neuronal FDR-null phenotype should not be read as evidence that CBL-B inhibition is biologically inert, because the disease and therapeutic axis is immune-cell activation.
why_it_matters: Mouse and human loss-of-function data link CBLB to hyperactive antigen-receptor responses and autoimmunity, and a clinical CBL-B inhibitor is being developed for cancer immunotherapy outside the cell types assayed here.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq panel contains neuronal classes rather than T cells, B cells, NK cells or mast cells and does not model systemic small-molecule CBL-B inhibition.

summary: Unbiased restricted-signature neighbors of Cblb were weak and did not nominate a high-confidence compensatory target.
why_it_matters: The nearest positive neighbor was a safe-target control and the strongest full-coverage correlations were small, so mechanistic interpretation from signature neighbors would be overfit.
main_caveats: The neighbor search was restricted to the top 15 nominal Cblb genes per cell type and should be treated as a diagnostic, not full transcriptome clustering.

summary: Lingo2 guide assignment did not yield an FDR-significant transcriptional program in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Lingo2 is a CNS-expressed, synapse-linked receptor family member, so the dominant dataset conclusion is buffering or weak engagement rather than a broad neuronal mRNA phenotype.

summary: Opcml upregulation in Sst GABA cells was the peak Lingo2-associated response but remained below FDR significance.

summary: Lingo2 perturbation did not trigger transcriptional feedback in LINGO/NgR/TFF3-associated receptor genes.

summary: Lingo2 did not phenocopy Lingo1 or Rtn4r despite literature-supported proximity to the Lingo/NgR receptor family.

summary: The dataset did not recapitulate the known Ank2-Scn2a and developmental synaptic disease axis as a broad single-cell RNA program.

main_caveats: The literature mechanisms are developmental, proteomic, dendritic, and cardiac, whereas this dataset uses broad mouse-brain cell labels and mRNA readout after partial Ank2 depletion.

summary: Measured Lrp6 mRNA showed only weak, uncorrected depletion across the screen, with no Lrp6 target-transcript row reaching FDR significance.

summary: A 217 P MY Pineal Glut signature placed App as the top nominal Lrp6-upregulated gene, suggesting a low-confidence link between Lrp6 loss and APP-family biology in a restricted glutamatergic context.

main_caveats: Only 21 perturbed cells were available and no gene in this cell type passed FDR<0.05; App transcript abundance is not the same as amyloidogenic APP processing.

summary: Kcnq2 perturbation produced robust depletion of the target RNA but almost no significant secondary transcriptome.

main_caveats: The scalar is target RNA knockdown significance and can reflect baseline expression, guide efficiency, and sample size as well as true cell biology.

summary: The best RNA biomarker of successful perturbation was Kcnq2 itself, not a downstream excitability or compensatory KCNQ-family module.
why_it_matters: For Kv7.2 opener or genetic-rescue studies, this dataset argues that rescue should be read out with electrophysiology or direct Kcnq2/Kv7.2 restoration rather than an assumed immediate-early-gene or paralog-expression signature.
main_caveats: This is a biomarker hypothesis from knockdown RNA data; it was not tested in drug-treated or patient-derived KCNQ2-DEE neurons.

summary: Rogdi down-regulation was the only significant non-target RNA hit and was restricted to 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.

main_caveats: One non-target gene in one cell type with no recurrence across the Kcnq2 series.

summary: Ndufa9 perturbation did not produce detectable Ndufa9 mRNA loss or any FDR-significant transcriptomic response in the 21 assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset cannot be read as a clean Ndufa9 loss-of-function phenocopy; any biological interpretation must first account for weak measured target engagement and the possibility that CRISPR editing affected protein without reducing RNA.

why_it_matters: COMT is a small-molecule catabolic enzyme; the data argue that acute cell-autonomous mRNA loss does not by itself launch a large, reproducible transcriptional program in the assayed neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: No COMT protein, catecholamine, or methylated-metabolite measurements were present, so metabolic compensation without mRNA change could not be excluded.

summary: On-target Comt depletion was strongly cell-type-variable, from four FDR-supported classes to nearly absent engagement in Sst GABA cells.
why_it_matters: Downstream negatives in weakly engaged classes should not be interpreted as biological resistance; the perturbation was measurably effective only in a subset and the largest pineal logFC came from only 41 cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Cell number and basal Comt detectability are confounded with apparent cell-type selectivity; this finding is about measured transcript engagement, not proven cell-intrinsic sensitivity.

summary: Nominal downstream genes did not form a recurrent Comt-responsive module, and genome-wide signature neighbors were very weak.
why_it_matters: The lack of recurrence prevents assigning a robust synaptic, stress, or homeostatic expression module to Comt loss in this screen.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Nominal genes may contain true low-amplitude signals, but none were FDR-supported and correlations were computed from rank-score signatures rather than independent validation.

summary: Comt did not phenocopy the assayed dopamine or adrenergic receptor perturbations or Ache, while the closest catecholamine-metabolism enzymes were missing from the library.
why_it_matters: This prevents treating receptor or Ache perturbations as interchangeable surrogates for COMT and sharply limits in-dataset reconstruction of the catecholamine-catabolic pathway.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The receptor and Ache contrasts are transcriptomic and exploratory; several receptor perturbations also had weak target-transcript engagement in the same cell classes.

direction: transcriptionally buffered despite predicted metabolic effect
summary: The Perturb-seq phenotype is more consistent with COMT acting through local catecholamine chemistry than through a large autonomously encoded neuronal state change.
why_it_matters: COMT-deficient animals show altered prefrontal dopamine overflow, yet here strong Comt mRNA depletion produced no FDR-supported downstream expression markers; future disease-mechanism assays should measure dopamine turnover or circuit physiology directly.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The literature physiology is mouse cortex/striatum in vivo; the Perturb-seq classes do not provide regional dopamine measurements and omit the 215 MB Dopa class for Comt.

direction: target down; no efficacy transcriptome surrogate
summary: Comt mRNA itself is the only robust knockdown biomarker in this screen and should not be used as a broad transcriptomic proxy for COMT-inhibitor efficacy in Parkinson's disease.
why_it_matters: Clinically used COMT inhibitors act by preserving levodopa or catecholamines; the screen shows target engagement without an accompanying neuronal DEG panel, so clinical direction must come from pharmacology rather than from downstream DE genes here.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Guide-targeted Comt loss in mouse neurons differs in modality and tissue exposure from pharmacologic COMT inhibition in treated patients, and the assay lacks levodopa, peripheral tissues, and dopaminergic midbrain Comt data.

summary: Epm2a yielded a screen-wide null in the scRNA-seq readout: no gene in any of 22 tested cell-type signatures passed FDR correction.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpretation of isolated nominal genes as Lafora biology or cell-type-selective downstream programs.
main_caveats: The null is for the Wilcoxon mRNA readout only; glycogen phosphorylation, Lafora bodies, neuronal firing and chronic degeneration were not measured.

summary: The Epm2a transcript itself was not consistently or significantly depleted, so the downstream null is best treated as weak target engagement rather than proof of biological buffering.
why_it_matters: Laforin is a loss-of-function disease gene; without verified transcript or protein loss, a missing downstream signature cannot establish that neurons tolerate Epm2a perturbation.
main_caveats: Transcript loss may underestimate genome editing for coding indels, but there was no corrected self-depletion signal and no corrected downstream response.

summary: The weak Epm2a result is target-specific within this file: Dnm1, Ppt1 and Scarb2 perturbations produced significant self-depletion at overlapping neuronal cell counts.
why_it_matters: This contrast argues against dismissing the Epm2a null as an inevitable consequence of all cell classes being underpowered; other genes in the same matched framework reached strong on-target statistics.
main_caveats: The comparison is anchored on on-target transcript behavior rather than matched biology; Dnm1, Ppt1 and Scarb2 are not laforin complex members.

summary: Known laforin glycogen-pathway neighbors did not move as an mRNA module after Epm2a perturbation.
why_it_matters: EPM2A is biochemically embedded in glycogen dephosphorylation and NHLRC1/malin ubiquitin biology, but this perturbation did not evoke a transcriptional glycogen/stress response detectable by corrected scRNA-seq statistics.
main_caveats: Most of the known mechanism is post-translational and metabolic; Nhlrc1 and several other STRING/Reactome neighbors were measured only as response genes, not as perturbations.

summary: The Epm2a null should not be read as a safety signal for laforin inhibition; human genetics and curated pathway knowledge point in the opposite direction, toward preserving laforin or reducing downstream glycogen synthesis.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL contains laforin biochemical inhibitor activity, but loss of EPM2A causes Lafora disease, whereas experimental Lafora strategies reduce Gys1-driven glycogen synthesis rather than further inhibiting laforin.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq screen is not a drug assay and did not verify laforin protein loss; this is a direction-of-effect warning, not a quantitative safety estimate.

summary: Notch1 perturbation was transcriptionally quiet across the profiled neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: The absence of target-transcript knockdown and the one-gene FDR response mean this experiment should be interpreted as a weak or inactive Notch1 perturbation in terminal neuronal classes, not as a broad canonical Notch loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: The data demonstrate weak measured Notch1 engagement; they do not distinguish guide failure from very sparse basal Notch1 expression or ligand-limited pathway inactivity.

summary: Camk2g induction in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut was the only multiple-testing-significant Notch1 hit.
why_it_matters: This nominates a narrow calcium/calmodulin-kinase response in corticofugal L5 extratelencephalic neurons, but the result is a solitary FDR hit and should be treated as a hypothesis-generating biomarker rather than a canonical Notch readout.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only one FDR-significant gene was detected; the dataset does not show that Camk2g is a direct NOTCH1 target.

summary: Available Notch-family and Notch-processing perturbations did not phenocopy Notch1.
why_it_matters: Notch receptors, DLL1 ligand, PSEN1 gamma-secretase, and ADAM10 are pathway neighbors, yet their concatenated signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Notch1 and failed to reproduce the L5 ET Camk2g response, arguing against treating Notch-pathway perturbations as interchangeable in this neuronal screen.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Some comparator perturbations had fewer cells than Notch1 in a given class, and correlation was performed on ranked DE score vectors rather than raw single-cell profiles.

summary: Notch1 perturbation did not move the canonical HES/HEY/NRARP/DTX transcriptional arm.
why_it_matters: Canonical NOTCH1 activation is defined by proteolytic release of NICD and RBPJ/MAML-dependent target-gene regulation; the lack of these target changes shows that the lone Camk2g hit was uncoupled from the expected nuclear Notch program.
main_caveats: The selected target genes are canonical markers but not an exhaustive Notch regulon for every neuronal context.

summary: The neuronal loss-of-function screen is context-mismatched to the dominant clinical NOTCH1 disease mechanisms.
why_it_matters: NOTCH1 disease and druggability evidence is concentrated in developmental vascular disease and cancers with pathway-activating lesions or gamma-secretase-sensitive signaling, whereas this dataset tested weak Notch1 loss-of-function in mature mouse neurons and detected no canonical response.
main_caveats: The result should not be extrapolated to NOTCH1-mutant leukemia, squamous cancers, vascular disease, or dividing neural stem cells.

summary: FDR-validated Hdac5 transcript depletion was restricted to 155 MB Glut, with a second strong but FDR-subthreshold on-target shift in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The interpretable Hdac5 loss-of-function signal is not pan-neuronal; most subclasses had weak or absent measured target engagement.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA, not HDAC5 protein or nuclear localization; some nominally engaged cell types did not survive FDR correction.

summary: Even where Hdac5 was depleted, the downstream transcriptome was buffered: 155 MB Glut retained only Hdac5 itself at FDR<0.05 and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: HDAC5 is a signal-gated corepressor; a small steady-state mRNA knockdown in basal cells did not reproduce a broad activity-dependent derepression program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Buffering could reflect incomplete target depletion, low Hdac5 expression, compensation at protein level, or lack of activity stimuli in the captured state.

summary: The only non-target FDR hit was Chd5 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, a cell type with no detectable Hdac5 transcript knockdown.
why_it_matters: This separates the most statistically significant downstream-looking event from canonical on-target Hdac5 loss, preventing the Chd5 outlier from being overread as a generalized HDAC5 target.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic singleton from 79 perturbed cells; without target-transcript depletion or guide-level replication it could be indirect or guide-associated.

summary: Hdac5 signatures in the best-engaged cell types were essentially uncorrelated with available perturbations of Hdac4, Mef2c/Mef2d, Camk2b, Ppp3ca, and Ppp2r1a despite these genes lying near HDAC5 in class IIa HDAC and calcium-signaling biology.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues against treating class IIa HDAC paralogs or proximal CaMK/calcineurin/PP2A perturbations as interchangeable transcriptional proxies for Hdac5 in the assayed basal brain states.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Several direct interactors, including Hdac3, Hdac7, Hdac9, Ncor1, and Ncor2, were not present as perturbations; low Hdac5 signal amplitude depresses correlation power.

summary: Npas4 was nominally upregulated in 155 MB Glut after Hdac5 knockdown, matching the reported direction for HDAC5-mediated Npas4 repression but not passing FDR.
why_it_matters: Npas4 is one of the few genes connecting the weak basal Perturb-seq signature to a named neuronal HDAC5 target, making it a hypothesis-generating biomarker rather than a validated dataset hit.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Npas4 had FDR=1.0, and the best-described HDAC5-Npas4 mechanism is in nucleus accumbens activity and cocaine contexts, not midbrain glutamatergic cells in an unstimulated Perturb-seq assay.

summary: Basal Hdac5 mRNA reduction did not phenocopy activity-regulated HDAC5 network manipulations, so transcript loss, catalytic HDAC inhibition, and localization-changing stimuli should not be assumed to be equivalent in brain cells.
why_it_matters: For HDAC5-directed drug concepts, the key biology may be scaffolding and nuclear-cytoplasmic trafficking; the Perturb-seq result warns that partial mRNA knockdown alone can look nearly silent.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is an inference about modality, not a direct small-molecule test; no protein deacetylase activity or subcellular localization was measured.

direction: 151-specific; mostly positive among top genes with Clpp down
summary: Kmt5b produced an FDR-resolved transcriptional phenotype almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: The target is a shared H4K20 methyltransferase, but the screen localizes the clearest response to one thalamic glutamatergic class rather than to all excitatory neurons, refining KMT5B neurodevelopmental disease biology toward state- or lineage-restricted vulnerability.
comparators: all other Kmt5b-tested cell groups|155 MB Glut
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation was not represented in 215 MB Dopa, many non-151 groups had fewer than 60 Kmt5b cells, and FDR-level evidence comes from transcriptomics only.

direction: postsynaptic genes mostly up; translation factors mixed
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response links Kmt5b perturbation to a postsynaptic and translation-related gene module.
why_it_matters: Up-regulation of Ache, Syngap1, Grik1, near-threshold Nlgn2, Rab3a, Rab3gap2, and translation-initiation genes ties the strongest Kmt5b effect to neuronal communication rather than to a nonspecific chromatin-only readout.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: STRING enrichment used a nominal p<0.001 input list; only four of the postsynaptic genes were FDR-significant or borderline in the primary DE table.

summary: The strongest downstream Kmt5b phenotype occurred without detectable depletion of the Kmt5b mRNA row.
why_it_matters: The result argues that guide identity, not measured Kmt5b RNA logFC, is the interpretable perturbation variable in this dataset; the absence of transcript depletion could reflect RNA buffering, isoform or guide-position effects, sparse capture, or other assay limitations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: This observation does not prove absence of protein or H4K20 methylation loss, because neither protein abundance nor histone methylation was measured.

direction: near-zero correlation with ASD chromatin comparators
summary: Kmt5b did not phenocopy Chd8, Arid1b, or any other perturbation in the responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class.
why_it_matters: Human organoid literature motivates a shared ASD-chromatin program for KMT5B, ARID1B, and CHD8 haploinsufficiency; the mouse thalamic Kmt5b signature was instead isolated, with only a very weak top neighbor and no appreciable negative neighbor.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison uses whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon-score correlations in one mouse cell group, whereas the prior convergence was measured during human cortical organoid development.

summary: Because pathogenic KMT5B biology is loss-of-function-like, pharmacologic KMT5B inhibition should be treated as a potential neuro-synaptic liability rather than an obvious disease-rescue direction.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL contains preclinical KMT5B/SUV420H1 inhibition assays, but human disease records and mouse PFC knockdown both point to harm from reduced KMT5B activity; this screen adds cell-class-restricted synaptic transcript changes after Kmt5b perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset tested guide perturbation, not drug exposure; no ChEMBL KMT5B inhibitor is linked to an approved mechanism of action in the queried records.

summary: Mnt perturbation produced a sparse aggregate transcriptomic response and no FDR-significant change of the Mnt transcript itself in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: MNT is annotated as a MAX-binding E-box repressor, so the sampled mouse-brain signatures do not support interpretation as a strong wholesale perturbation of the MYC/MAX/MNT network.
main_caveats: Aggregate Wilcoxon results do not reveal guide sequences, protein abundance, or perturbation direction; target mRNA can be an imperfect proxy for MNT activity.

direction: up for Per/Cry genes in Mnt-labeled, Max, and Sin3a signatures
summary: A nominal Period/Cryptochrome clock-gene module recurred after Mnt perturbation and was much more strongly recapitulated by Max and Sin3a perturbations.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA

summary: Mnt was not globally interchangeable with Max, Myc, Mycn, Mga, Sin3a, Tcf4, or Usf1 perturbations despite belonging to an interacting bHLH/MAX network.
why_it_matters: Physical interaction with MAX did not translate into a high-dimensional transcriptomic phenocopy in these mouse-brain cell types, implying that individual network nodes are buffered or engage different contexts.
main_caveats: Full-transcriptome Pearson correlations can miss concordance in small modules such as Per/Cry and are attenuated by weak Mnt engagement.

summary: The assayed mouse-brain neuronal cell classes showed little adjusted transcriptional response to Mnt perturbation, refining embryonic and Miller-Dieker literature toward a developmental or context-dependent role for MNT.
why_it_matters: MNT lies in a developmental disease interval and Mnt loss perturbs mouse embryogenesis, but this dataset does not show that acute Mnt perturbation is sufficient to remodel most assayed neuronal transcriptomes.
main_caveats: The dataset measures transcript abundance after perturbation, not embryonic viability, cortical migration, craniofacial development, or long-term neurodevelopmental phenotypes.

summary: An unbiased scan did not identify any strong positive or negative Mnt signature neighbor among other perturbations in the same cell classes.
why_it_matters: The Mnt signature was not a hidden copy of another perturbation program; even the best neighbors had |r| below 0.19 and were therefore not interpreted mechanistically.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from Wilcoxon score vectors, so weaker pathway-specific convergence may be diluted.

summary: Ptprf perturbation did not yield any FDR-significant gene in any assayed brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The main scalar result is a transcriptome-wide negative result, so mechanistic interpretation must be based on weak nominal patterns rather than called DE genes.
main_caveats: The input contains only guide-level DE summaries, not raw counts or protein-level PTPRF measurements.

summary: Nominal target-transcript depletion was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 054 CNU-MGE GABA and was weak or absent in several larger Ptprf cohorts.
why_it_matters: Apparent cell-type specificity is dominated by engagement quality; cell types with no Ptprf self-depletion are poor places to infer downstream Ptprf biology.

main_caveats: Even the best self-depletion calls did not survive FDR correction; differences may reflect guide efficacy, target expression, or power rather than biology.

summary: The two cell types with the clearest Ptprf self-depletion still showed only sparse, non-FDR downstream changes.
why_it_matters: A measurable fall in the targeted transcript was not followed by a broad mRNA cascade, consistent with a buffered or primarily post-transcriptional acute response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The buffered interpretation is inferred from mRNA DE; the dataset did not assay synaptic localization, phosphatase activity, or NMDA-receptor physiology.

summary: Known receptor-PTP and LAR/synaptic-neighborhood perturbations did not phenocopy Ptprf in its engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: The Ptprf signature was not a generic LAR-RPTP, receptor-PTP, or synaptic-adhesion signature; even stronger Nrxn1 or Ptprt perturbations in MB Glut were essentially uncorrelated with Ptprf.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Correlations used precomputed Wilcoxon signatures and are restricted to two cell types; Ptprs, the third type-IIA LAR-RPTP paralog, was not targeted.

summary: The Perturb-seq readout uncoupled Ptprf knockdown from the synaptic adhesion and NMDA-receptor biology emphasized in LAR-RPTP literature.
why_it_matters: A negative mRNA result does not falsify PTPRF synaptic function; it more specifically argues that single-gene acute Ptprf knockdown in mature brain cells did not create a broad transcriptional surrogate of that pathway.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The assay measured RNA abundance after one perturbation modality, not electrophysiology or ultrastructure.

summary: The screen did not reveal a robust mature-neuronal transcriptional correlate for the established human PTPRF loss-of-function phenotype.
why_it_matters: Reported human PTPRF truncation causes a developmental epithelial athelia phenotype; the weak neuronal mRNA response in this dataset argues against using this Perturb-seq result alone to nominate a brain disease transcriptome.
main_caveats: This is a context comparison; it does not test epithelial development and does not exclude non-transcriptional synaptic effects in neurons.

summary: Add3 perturbation was globally weak at the mRNA-response level: none of 371,818 per-gene tests across 22 neuronal cell groups reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The screen does not support a robust acute transcriptional cascade downstream of partial Add3 perturbation, so the main Add3 signal is a buffered/negative perturbation rather than a pathway activation signature.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant RNA changes does not exclude protein-level or cytoskeletal phenotypes, and many cell groups had few perturbed cells.

summary: Sst GABA cells showed the clearest on-target Add3 transcript decrease, but the response remained restricted to nominal statistics.
why_it_matters: This separates failure of global response from total guide failure: one neuronal population showed a measurable Add3 self-knockdown signal, yet downstream DE still did not survive correction.
comparators: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Sst had only 57 perturbed cells and the Add3 self p_adj was 0.958; the apparent cell-type selectivity may reflect guide efficacy or Add3 detectability rather than Sst-specific biology.

summary: Add3 was not transcriptomically interchangeable with Add1 or Add2, even though ADD3 is an ADD1 complex partner in the adducin membrane-skeleton module.
why_it_matters: Physical membership in an adducin complex did not translate into shared Perturb-seq signatures in these neurons, arguing against using Add1/Add2 signatures as surrogates for Add3 in this dataset.
main_caveats: All three adducin perturbations were weak by FDR, so the lack of correlation could arise from weak engagement rather than true biochemical divergence.

summary: The Add3 Perturb-seq result refines ADD3 disease biology toward structural actin/spectrin phenotypes rather than an early, cell-autonomous mRNA program.
why_it_matters: Human ADD3 loss-of-function disease is linked to defective alpha-adducin association and actin capping; the mouse-brain data suggest that a standard expression readout may miss the relevant cytoskeletal, developmental, or morphology endpoint.
main_caveats: The disease report involved inherited human variants and Drosophila/fibroblast assays, whereas this dataset is an acute mouse neuronal CRISPR-expression assay without morphology or protein measurements.

summary: Nominal Add3 hits did not converge on a recurrent downstream gene module or on a strong signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top nominal genes should be treated as hypotheses for individual cell groups, not as a reproducible Add3-regulated transcriptional module.
main_caveats: The recurrence analysis used a nominal p<0.001 threshold and full-vector correlations on weak signatures.

summary: Glce perturbation produced no FDR-corrected transcriptomic phenotype across the 22 assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: GLCE is a core HS-GAG editing enzyme, yet the Perturb-seq readout was dominated by absence of a recurrent RNA program rather than by the developmental morphogen phenotypes known from HS genetics.

summary: In 155 MB Glut, Hs6st2, Ext2, and Agrn showed clear self-transcript depletion whereas Glce did not, despite belonging to the HS/HSPG neighborhood.
why_it_matters: The comparison separates a likely weak Glce guide/readout from a generic inability of this dataset to detect target rows for HS-related genes.

main_caveats: The comparator panel is incomplete because HS2ST1, HS6ST1, and NDST genes were not perturbation targets; self-transcript depletion is an RNA proxy, not glycan depletion.

summary: Glce did not trigger corrected feedback in measured HS biosynthesis or HSPG-neighbor genes and did not phenocopy related HS/HSPG perturbations.
why_it_matters: A biochemical pathway can be essential through extracellular HS structure without generating an acute transcriptional compensation module in the perturbed neuron.

summary: The strongest cell-type peaks were isolated nominal rows and do not establish a Glce-selective neuronal subtype.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of visually large single-cell-type scores, especially in low-count or multiple-testing-limited profiles.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The peaks are discussed as negative controls on interpretation; none reached FDR < 0.05.

summary: The stringent Chd2 response is concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than being a broad pan-neuronal phenotype.
why_it_matters: This localizes the strongest observed consequence of a CHD2-family neurodevelopmental-disorder gene to a thalamic glutamatergic state in this dataset, extending literature that has emphasized cortical and GABAergic interneuron development.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The Chd2 mRNA itself was not detectably depleted, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 34 perturbed cells.

summary: The measured Chd2 transcript was not reduced in any cell type, and most cell types had no FDR<0.05 downstream genes.
why_it_matters: A loss-of-function disease gene without measured transcript depletion should be interpreted as a partial or weak perturbation in this assay rather than a full model of CHD2 haploinsufficiency.
main_caveats: Unchanged target mRNA does not exclude an unmeasured isoform or protein-level loss; no direct CHD2 protein readout is available here.

summary: Within the main 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response, Chd2 perturbation downregulated RNA-splicing components and several potassium/ion-channel transcripts.
why_it_matters: The affected genes nominate RNA processing and neuronal excitability effectors as nearby transcriptomic outputs of Chd2 disruption rather than merely confirming a generic chromatin-remodeling label.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset shows expression changes, not altered splicing, potassium currents, or direct CHD2 binding at these loci.

summary: Snhg11 is a recurrent low-amplitude but statistically strong Chd2 response marker across five cell types.
why_it_matters: Snhg11 recurrence is useful as a candidate readout of Chd2-sensitive neuronal state; independent Snhg11 knockdown data make even small decreases worth following, although Snhg11 is not Chd2-specific in the broader screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Snhg11 fold changes were modest and Snhg11 was also affected by many other perturbations, so it should be treated as a response marker rather than a CHD2-specific target.

summary: Chd2 did not phenocopy Chd4, Chd7, or Chd8 in the responsive thalamic glutamatergic class.
why_it_matters: Broad CHD-family membership was a poor predictor of the Chd2 signature in this cell state, consistent with curated separation of CHD subfamilies rather than interchangeability among CHD-family ATPases.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Chd2 had weak measured target engagement; the contrast establishes non-phenocopying in this assay but not necessarily biochemical independence.

summary: The closest Chd2 signature neighbors were local to its 34-gene high-confidence module, with Elp1 and Xpo1 positive and Nalcn negative only in a restricted-signature comparison.
why_it_matters: This separates module-level co-movement from genome-wide similarity and prevents overcalling Elp1, Xpo1, or Nalcn as full Chd2 mimics or suppressors.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations across all 17,259 measured genes were only -0.064 to 0.117, so this is a hypothesis-generating module comparison.

summary: Casr perturbation had no FDR<0.05 downstream genes and no rank-based Casr transcript knockdown across 22 tested neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: This is the gating result for interpretation: downstream absences are more consistent with weak target engagement or sparse Casr RNA than with a confidently buffered knockout state.
main_caveats: The rank statistic, not the unstable sparse logFC estimate, was used to judge on-target engagement; low cell counts leave false negatives possible.

summary: Only two cell classes produced near-threshold Casr rows: Ago3 down in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and Srrm4 up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: These two genes are the only Casr rows surviving to FDR<0.1 and could be revisited as biomarkers, but their isolation argues against a recurrent pan-neuronal Casr module.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Neither row reached FDR<0.05 and each came from a single cell class.

summary: Casr was transcriptionally uncoupled from represented family-C GPCR and calcium signaling perturbations.
why_it_matters: The weak Casr result is not simply an assay-wide inability to perturb GPCR/calcium genes, because several related genes had strong signatures in the same table; expected neighbors also did not correlate with Casr over full vectors.
main_caveats: Pathway-neighbor set was curated, not exhaustive; correlations use steady-state RNA signatures rather than acute GPCR signaling.

summary: The 308 CB GABA restricted Casr signature converged weakly with Gpr68 and other GPCR or transcriptional perturbations.
why_it_matters: GPR68 is an extracellular proton sensor with reported reciprocal regulation with CaSR, making this the most biologically plausible signature-neighbor hint despite the otherwise weak Casr profile.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to the 100 largest weak Casr scores in one low-response cell class; Casr itself had no FDR<0.05 DE in 308 CB GABA.

summary: CASR druggability and endocrine disease genetics are not recapitulated by a robust mouse neuronal Casr loss-of-function transcriptome in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Clinically validated agonist or calcimimetic mechanisms in parathyroid and kidney should not be used to infer a strong adult neuronal transcriptional effect here; conversely, this negative signature should not be taken as CNS safety evidence.
main_caveats: No drug treatment, rescue, endocrine tissue, or acute second-messenger assay was tested in the Perturb-seq data.

summary: Ago2 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptional signature in any of the 22 tested mouse-brain cell groups.
why_it_matters: AGO2 is a core RISC effector, so the absence of q<0.05 genes means this experiment does not provide a robust cell-type-resolved loss-of-function transcriptome for the target.
main_caveats: CRISPR perturbation can mutate protein without lowering the target mRNA, and per-group perturbed-cell counts were only 22-158.

summary: 155 MB Glut was the closest case to on-target Ago2 mRNA engagement, yet the nominal Ago2 decrease itself was not significant after FDR adjustment and no other gene passed FDR.
why_it_matters: This is the strongest place to look for an Ago2 response in the dataset, and even there the measured steady-state RNA response is buffered, delayed, post-transcriptional, or underpowered rather than a clear RISC transcriptional collapse.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Ago2 row had FDR 0.291, not a statistically significant knockdown, and protein abundance or guide editing was not measured.

summary: The nominal Ago2 signal was concentrated in a small set of thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and cortical classes, but the genes driving those windows were almost entirely cell-type-specific one-offs.
why_it_matters: A visual or scalar ranking could overemphasize Akap7, Zcchc12, Numa1, Stk10, Rasd2, or Slc2a13; the recurrence analysis argues against a shared pan-neuronal Ago2 effector module.

summary: Ago2 signatures did not phenocopy Ago1, Dicer1, Tnrc6a, or Tnrc6b, despite those factors occupying the same AGO/RISC small-RNA pathway.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not support treating these related perturbations as interchangeable pathway replicates for adult mouse-brain cell transcriptomes.
main_caveats: Most compared perturbations were also weak, so the contrast is restricted to observed RNA signatures rather than proven protein loss-of-function states.

summary: The best-engaged 155 MB Glut Ago2 signature had no meaningful positive or negative perturbation neighbor in the full same-cell-type library.
why_it_matters: Neither Ogt, Grin2d, nor any other perturbation supplied a plausible rescue or mimic signature for the observed Ago2 state in this cell class.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only 155 MB Glut was scanned and correlations were computed on weak full-transcriptome score vectors.

summary: The dataset does not nominate an adult mouse-brain cell type as selectively vulnerable to AGO2-linked neurologic disease mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Human AGO2 mutations impair RNAi and neurological development, but this acute adult mouse Perturb-seq readout shows no FDR-supported adult neuronal subclass response, pointing to developmental timing, dosage, protein-level mechanisms, or insufficient engagement as unresolved variables.
main_caveats: The human evidence is germline and developmental, whereas the dataset is mouse, perturbational, and filtered by matched adult brain cell groups.

summary: The weak Ago2 Perturb-seq response should not be read as evidence that AGO2 inhibition would be silent or safe in neurons.
why_it_matters: AGO2 is an essential small-RNA effector with human neurodevelopmental disease links, while ChEMBL has no curated AGO2 mechanism-of-action drugs; the observed lack of FDR signal is more consistent with assay limitation than with a validated, buffered therapeutic window.
main_caveats: This is a direction-of-evidence warning, not a direct drug experiment and not a complete druggability assessment.

summary: Plcb1 knockdown produced a corrected self-transcript hit in L4-5 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons but did not yield any corrected downstream mRNA response.
why_it_matters: PLCB1 is a proximal PIP2-to-IP3/DAG signaling enzyme, so the result separates biochemical pathway membership from a readily detectable steady-state RNA module in this assay.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA rather than PLCβ1 protein, IP3, DAG, calcium flux, or excitability; the knockdown was partial.

summary: Statistically reliable Plcb1 target-transcript depletion was concentrated in the 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut class and was weaker or not FDR-significant in the other 21 measured cell classes.
why_it_matters: Most cell types cannot be treated as clean biological negatives because absence of downstream DE is confounded by modest perturbation counts and weak target-transcript engagement.
main_caveats: The DE table does not report raw Plcb1 expression, guide identity, or protein depletion, so cell-type differences may reflect assay power or CRISPRi efficiency rather than true PLCB1 dependence.

summary: Plcb1 and Itpr1 were both significantly depleted in L4-5 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons, yet their genome-wide perturbation scores were uncorrelated and each perturbation produced only a self-transcript FDR hit.
why_it_matters: IP3 receptors are downstream calcium-release effectors of PLCβ-generated IP3; loss of a shared RNA signature argues that this canonical second-messenger chain was not converted into a stable common transcriptomic state.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is based on one cell class and on RNA scores; IP3/Ca2+ coupling could be fast, post-translational, or spatially localized.

summary: Neither curated Gq/IP3/PKC/phosphoinositide pathway neighbors nor an unbiased same-cell-type nearest-neighbor scan produced a strong positive or inverse Plcb1 RNA-signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak neighbor structure makes it unlikely that the missing Plcb1 response is simply hidden under a different assayed upstream receptor or downstream effector perturbation.
main_caveats: Correlation of weak signatures is a restricted transcriptomic readout; some related genes were absent from the perturbation panel and pathway activation direction was not directly measured.

direction: loss of function deleterious in vivo; RNA response weak in the screen
summary: The severe epilepsy literature for PLCB1 loss contrasts with a quiet acute RNA phenotype after partial Plcb1 knockdown, warning that a negative Perturb-seq transcriptional signature should not be read as absence of neuronal risk.
why_it_matters: PLCB1 loss-of-function disease is likely mediated by developmental, circuit, or electrophysiological failure modes that can be missed by steady-state single-cell mRNA screens.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Human disease and Plcb1-null mouse phenotypes reflect germline or constitutive severe loss, whereas the dataset measures partial acute transcript knockdown in broad cell classes.

summary: Chmp4b was an under-engaged perturbation in this mouse-brain table: no measured cell type showed FDR-level depletion of the Chmp4b transcript and almost no downstream genes reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: CHMP4B is a core ESCRT-III membrane-remodeling protein, so a strong loss-of-function would be expected to perturb endosomal or autophagy biology; the dataset instead primarily supports a weak or buffered neuronal transcriptomic response.
main_caveats: Absence of transcript depletion does not exclude protein-level perturbation or selection against strongly perturbed cells.

summary: The only conventional FDR hit was a 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut decrease of Pip5k1c, decoupled from detectable Chmp4b transcript knockdown in the same stratum.
why_it_matters: The most statistically robust Chmp4b-associated effect is cell-type restricted and single-gene rather than a broad ESCRT program.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Single DE feature; no target-transcript engagement in the same cell type.

summary: Despite weak direct DE, Chmp4b signatures converged with ESCRT-II Snf8 and ESCRT-I Vps37a perturbations in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: This is the clearest place where the restricted transcriptome recovers the expected ESCRT pathway relationship rather than a generic neuronal response.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut

summary: Across all Chmp4b cell-type signatures, proteasome and V-ATPase perturbations ranked above most ESCRT targets, indicating that the recurrent Chmp4b-neighbor axis is proteostasis/acidification-skewed rather than ESCRT-only.
why_it_matters: The result expands interpretation from canonical ESCRT cargo sorting to a coupled endolysosomal quality-control state, consistent with but not diagnostic of CHMP4B autophagy and late-endosomal functions.
main_caveats: Global correlations were small and are useful as module-level hints, not as proof that Chmp4b directly regulates proteasome or V-ATPase genes.

summary: Several ESCRT or ESCRT-adjacent transcripts were nominally induced in restricted cell classes, including Stam2, Ptpn23, Vps4a, Chmp3, Snf8, and Vta1.

summary: The weak and sparse neuronal Chmp4b response does not phenocopy a pan-neuronal ESCRT collapse and should not be equated with dominant human CHMP4B cataract mutations.
why_it_matters: Human CHMP4B disease is a rare lens disorder driven by missense alleles with gain-of-function behavior and lens-fiber biology; the mouse-brain guide data provide at most a context-restricted neuronal perturbation readout.
main_caveats: Species, tissue, allele class, and assay differ between mouse Perturb-seq and human cataract genetics.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only 44 Chmp4b-perturbed CB GABA cells contributed to this signature; no direct literature link to CHMP4B is asserted for most of these neighbors.

summary: Mapk8 loss failed to produce any FDR-significant basal transcriptional program in the 21 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: MAPK8 is a canonical JNK stress kinase, so the absence of adjusted differential expression separates basal Mapk8 depletion from stress-activated JNK/AP-1 output in this dataset.
main_caveats: The target transcript decrease was modest and never FDR significant; the assay captures basal surviving cells rather than an acute oxidative, cytokine, or amyloid stress challenge.

summary: CTX-CGE GABA, CNU-HYa HY GABA, and TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the clearest nominal Mapk8 self-depletion yet still had only 3-4 total genes at nominal p<0.001 and none at FDR<0.05.

main_caveats: The target rows are only nominal; FDR values remain 1.0, so the apparent cell-type restriction could reflect guide performance or power.

summary: The few nominal Mapk8-responsive genes were almost entirely cell-type private rather than a recurrent stress or AP-1 effector set.
why_it_matters: A conserved JNK output would be expected to reuse downstream genes across related neurons; instead, only Mapk8 itself recurred at nominal p<0.001.
main_caveats: Recurrence was judged on unadjusted thresholds because no non-target gene survived FDR correction.

summary: Mapk8 signatures were nearly orthogonal to Mapk9, Mapk8ip1, Map3k7, Atf2, Jund, Bcl2, and Trp53 perturbations across matched cell types.
why_it_matters: STRING and Reactome place these genes near JNK signaling, but the basal Perturb-seq signatures do not behave as an interchangeable JNK module.
main_caveats: The Mapk8 signature itself is weak, and several canonical upstream kinases or AP-1 components were unavailable as direct perturbations.

summary: The dataset should not be read as evidence that JNK blockade is inert in diseased or stressed neurons.
why_it_matters: JNK is pharmacologically tractable and is discussed as a stress-activated neurodegeneration target; basal Mapk8 perturbation gives little AP-1 output, so it is a poor standalone proxy for oxidative-stress or amyloid-driven JNK inhibition.
main_caveats: No disease stimulus, acute kinase inhibition, phospho-JNK readout, or protein-level target engagement was measured.

summary: Ctsb RNA knockdown was repeatedly measurable, yet the neuronal signatures were almost completely buffered at the transcriptome level.
