why_it_matters: The primary interpretation of this perturbation is a buffered or under-engaged response, not a strong loss-of-KIF3B transcriptional state.
main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA abundance; KIF3B acts mainly as a motor protein, and the target transcript itself did not pass FDR correction.

summary: Canonical ciliary, Hedgehog, and NMDAR-transport transcripts were not mobilized after Kif3b perturbation.
why_it_matters: Known KIF3B biology centers on protein transport in cilia and dendrites; the Perturb-seq readout did not convert that biology into a detectable transcriptional program over Kif3a, Kifap3, Ift20, Ift88, Hedgehog readouts, or Grin2a/Grin2b/Apc/Dlg4.
main_caveats: Absence of transcript changes does not exclude altered ciliary trafficking, cilium length, receptor localization, or other protein-level phenotypes.

summary: 155 MB Glut was the strongest Kif3b cell class by adjusted p value, whereas the Sst Gaba raw-p-value outlier was low-count and lacked target engagement; neither was an FDR-level cell-type-specific program.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-calling isolated Gsk3a or Braf nominal hits as midbrain or interneuron-specific KIF3B biology.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Both cell classes had no FDR<0.05 genes; the Sst estimate used only 20 perturbed cells.

summary: Kif3b did not converge with the available IFT/dynein perturbations or with any strong positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Even though KIF3B belongs to the Kinesin-2 intraflagellar-transport machinery, the screen did not reveal a shared IFT-like expression state for Kif3b; this favors weak engagement or non-transcriptional physiology over pathway-wide transcriptional convergence.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Kif3a and Kifap3 were not available perturbation comparators, and Kif3b itself was weakly engaged.

summary: The nominal Kif3b hits did not recur across cell types as a stable module.
why_it_matters: Genes with exciting raw p values should be treated as local, hypothesis-generating outliers rather than a reproducible KIF3B effector set.
main_caveats: The recurrence analysis used nominal p-value thresholds because there were no FDR-significant rows.

summary: Transcriptomic buffering in this assay should not be read as safety of KIF3B inhibition.
why_it_matters: Loss of KIF3B disrupts cilia and human KIF3B variants cause ciliopathy, so a KIF3B-directed drug program would need ciliary and neuronal-transport safety assays even when a mouse-brain Perturb-seq mRNA signature is small.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay photoreceptors, embryonic node cilia, cilium morphology, or protein trafficking directly.

summary: Copg1 knockdown was detected as a negative self-transcript effect in every profiled class but reached FDR 0.05 in only seven neuronal classes: thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, midbrain glutamatergic, midbrain/pons/medulla GABA, Pvalb GABA, CNU-HYa/HY GABA, CNU-MGE GABA, and MH-LH/TH glutamatergic cells.
why_it_matters: The screen provides a usable Copg1 loss-of-function axis in a specific subset of brain classes rather than a uniform pan-neuronal perturbation, so absence of a phenotype in weaker classes should not be interpreted as biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The apparent cell-type restriction is based on transcript-level sgRNA engagement and is partly confounded by different perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Even where Copg1 itself was robustly depleted, the downstream mRNA response was strongly buffered: no non-Copg1 transcript passed FDR 0.05 anywhere in the Copg1 screen.
why_it_matters: COPI is a core ER/Golgi trafficking machine, so an isolated self-transcript signature argues that partial knockdown in these brain cells did not produce a broad transcriptional trafficking, stress, or death program at the assayed time point.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The assay is RNA-based; a buffered transcriptome does not rule out altered Golgi morphology, protein trafficking, secretion, electrophysiology, or later toxicity.

summary: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was the only class with a near-FDR non-target Copg1 response, with Ndrg4 increased at FDR 0.056.
why_it_matters: This weak, cell-type-restricted signal is the main candidate reporter of a secondary neuronal response to Copg1 depletion and nominates 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA for targeted validation rather than implying a pan-cell-type COPI stress program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Ndrg4 did not pass the conventional 0.05 FDR cutoff and the observation is single-cell-type and transcriptomic.

summary: Partial Copg1 depletion in brain neurons did not measurably induce a canonical unfolded-protein-response module, contrasting with ER-stress phenotypes reported for COPG1 K652E lymphocytes.
why_it_matters: The result narrows disease extrapolation: ER-stress liability from a pathogenic γ1-COP allele in activated immune cells should not be assumed to appear as an acute Hspa5/Ddit3/Atf4/Xbp1 transcriptional program after partial Copg1 knockdown in brain cell classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation is knockdown rather than the K652E missense allele, and the dataset does not measure activated T or B cells, secreted proteins, or ER morphology.

summary: The same-complex COPI subunit Copa did not phenocopy Copg1, but Copa target engagement was weak, making the contrast a guide-performance warning rather than evidence that COPA and COPG1 are biologically separable in neurons.
why_it_matters: COPA was the only other core COPI subunit in this library; recognizing that its self-transcript never reached FDR prevents over-interpreting the lack of α-COP/γ1-COP signature convergence.
main_caveats: Copa had fewer perturbed cells and no FDR-significant self-knockdown, so this is a negative comparator quality assessment, not a mechanistic divergence.

summary: A scan of all perturbation signatures found no strong positive or negative Copg1 signature neighbor; every non-self target had a near-zero global Pearson correlation with Copg1.
why_it_matters: The lack of neighborhood structure is consistent with the target-only Copg1 profile and means that scalar similarity scores would miss the most interpretable result: direct Copg1 depletion with little secondary transcriptional effect.
main_caveats: The calculation used global Wilcoxon-score correlations and can miss cell-type-local or non-transcriptional convergence.

summary: Flrt3 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response and no FDR-supported decrease of the Flrt3 transcript in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant result: the Perturb-seq readout cannot be used as strong evidence that FLRT3 biology is absent, because the target mRNA itself was not detectably reduced.
main_caveats: The dataset reports transcript-level differential expression, not editing or protein loss; a coding knockout could be active without lowering mRNA.

summary: The only near-threshold Flrt3 signals were in superficial intratelencephalic glutamatergic classes, led by Odc1 in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and Dapk1 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The pattern provides a cell-type-resolved hypothesis consistent with cortical FLRT biology, but it remains below 5% FDR and should be treated as an exploratory lead rather than a definitive effector program.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Both cell-type responses have FDR values above 0.05; Odc1 and Dapk1 are not recurrent across cell types at p < 0.001.

summary: Flrt3 did not show the on-target transcript depletion seen for several adhesion and guidance perturbations in the same broad neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: FLRT3 is a curated extracellular partner of ADGRL/UNC5/ROBO/FGFR biology, yet membership in that molecular neighborhood did not make the Flrt3 perturbation behave like readily engaged ADGRL1/2/3, TENM3, ROBO1/2, NCAM1, or FGFR1 perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is dominated by target-transcript rows rather than off-target pathway output; Flrt1/Flrt2 and Unc5a/Unc5b were not available as perturbation targets in the queried file.

summary: The Flrt3 signature did not reveal either a recurrent downstream module or a strongly correlated perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: This argues against rescuing the weak Flrt3 result by lowering the threshold: the top genes were not repeated across cell types, and the nearest signatures in the two best cell types had absolute genome-wide correlations of only about 0.1.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Correlation used all genes in restricted cell-type score vectors; absence of a transcriptomic neighbor does not rule out post-transcriptional FLRT3 biology.

summary: The dataset does not reproduce the developmental axon-guidance, neuronal-migration, or congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism biology linked to FLRT3 in the literature.
why_it_matters: Known FLRT3 phenotypes are strongly developmental and extracellular; the null or buffered mouse-brain Perturb-seq profile therefore warns that broad acute transcriptomic readouts are likely a poor proxy for FLRT3-dependent migration, synapse, or FGF-pathway disease mechanisms.
main_caveats: This is a context argument, not a contradiction: the dataset need not include embryonic GnRH neurons, migrating cortical neurons, thalamocortical axons, or direct protein-adhesion phenotypes.

direction: Kcnc1 transcript down only after FDR in two GABAergic classes
summary: FDR-confirmed Kcnc1 self-repression was restricted to 052 Pvalb Gaba and 191 MB P MY GABA, even though the Kcnc1 target row was tested in 23 cell classes.
why_it_matters: The signal concentrates in GABAergic classes that are plausible Kv3.1-bearing fast-firing neurons rather than forming a brain-wide knockdown phenotype; most other classes are not interpretable as confident Kcnc1 loss of function.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Perturbation efficiency rather than endogenous expression alone can determine the apparent restriction; the assay measured mRNA, not Kv3.1 protein or current.

direction: buffered downstream expression after Kcnc1 down-regulation
summary: The two classes with significant Kcnc1 target depletion showed a target-only FDR response, with no downstream transcript passing FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: Kv3.1 loss is expected to alter excitability, but short-term Kcnc1 knockdown did not trigger a broad cell-autonomous mRNA program, separating the channel's acute electrical role from bulk transcriptional homeostasis in this assay.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant non-target genes is not evidence that firing, channel density, splicing, or late activity-dependent genes were unchanged.

direction: near-zero same-cell score-vector correlations among related potassium-channel perturbations
summary: Kcnc2 and Kcnc3, and in Pvalb also Kcnq2, knocked down their own transcripts in overlapping classes, but their Wilcoxon-score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with the Kcnc1 vector.
why_it_matters: Kv3-family members can assemble together and are coexpressed in fast-spiking interneurons, so the near-zero Kcnc1-Kcnc2/Kcnc3 correlations argue that related potassium-channel perturbations are not interchangeable at the transcriptomic layer.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The correlations compare mRNA differential-expression scores, not channel coassembly, ionic currents, or firing phenotypes; Kcnc4/Kv3.4 was unavailable as a direct comparator.

direction: no strong matching or opposing perturbation signature
summary: A whole-cell-type signature-neighbor scan found no strong positive or negative Kcnc1 neighbor in the two FDR-engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpretation of isolated nominal genes as a convergent pathway: the largest non-self Pearson correlations were only 0.072 in Pvalb and 0.069 in 191 MB P MY GABA.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Pearson correlations used all measured genes and will miss sparse modules, nonlinear relationships, or post-transcriptional convergence.

direction: nominal Kcnc1 decrease without FDR support
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut had nominally negative Kcnc1 target rows but no adjusted target or downstream discovery despite the largest perturbed-cell counts.
why_it_matters: These groups are biologically tempting because Kcnc1 acts in distributed high-frequency neuronal populations, but their conventional evidence is weaker than the GABAergic hits and should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than a replicated glutamatergic response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Both target rows failed FDR correction; the leading non-target genes in 155 MB Glut had comparable nominal P values, so the target signal was not unambiguous.

direction: mRNA biomarker weak relative to functional phenotypes
summary: Because Kcnc1 knockdown yielded a target-only mRNA signature while disease and rescue data point to altered Kv3.1 excitability, transcript abundance is likely a weak standalone pharmacodynamic readout for Kv3.1 functional rescue.
why_it_matters: Screens for KCNC1 loss-of-function therapeutics should prioritize channel localization, potassium current, high-frequency firing, or network activity rather than expecting large reversal of a downstream mRNA module.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment assayed knockdown rather than patient missense alleles or Kv3-positive modulators, so the therapeutic implication is indirect.

summary: Adgrg2 perturbation yielded neither detectable Adgrg2 mRNA depletion nor any FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic response across the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset fact is a strong null: Adgrg2 should not be interpreted as having a robust neuronal expression program in this Perturb-seq assay unless target editing can be shown by an orthogonal readout.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: High confidence for the measured FDR-null result, but the experiment did not show mRNA-level target knockdown; a protein-level knockout could still have occurred without detectable transcript loss.

summary: The weak Adgrg2 nominal tail was sparse and did not reveal a recurrent response module or a meaningful signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: This argues against rescuing a hidden pathway interpretation from uncorrected p values: the lowest-q cell type still had q=0.379 and its strongest genome-wide perturbation correlations were close to zero.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to transcriptomic scores; nominal p-value counts and correlations are exploratory because Adgrg2 has no validated FDR-level signature.

summary: The established ADGRG2 male-fertility/CFTR/G-protein mechanism was not recapitulated as a brain-neuronal transcriptional state.
why_it_matters: ADGRG2 loss causes a strong epithelial reproductive phenotype in mice and humans, but this dataset supports a narrow context: neuronal Adgrg2 perturbation in the sampled brain classes did not trigger a comparable transcriptional response.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is indirect because the references study epididymal or efferent-duct epithelia, human infertility, or curated protein function, whereas the dataset assays mouse brain cells and lacks cAMP, CFTR-current, and protein readouts.

summary: Adgrg2 diverged from brain-relevant latrophilin adhesion-GPCRs: Adgrl1, Adgrl2, and Adgrl3 were measurably self-depleted in the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic stratum, while Adgrg2 was not.
why_it_matters: The flat Adgrg2 profile is not simply a universal failure of adhesion-GPCR perturbations in this library; it is more consistent with target-specific guide, expression, or buffering context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to target-transcript depletion, not matched downstream FDR signatures; latrophilins and ADGRG2 are family members rather than a shared protein complex.

summary: Nfe2l1 guide assignment produced only shallow target-transcript depletion across the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The target row itself never reached 5% FDR, so pathway absences should be interpreted as acute partial perturbation or detection limits rather than as a definitive Nfe2l1 null phenotype.
main_caveats: The dataset reports transcript output only; residual NFE2L1 protein or unedited cells could mask a loss-of-function program.

summary: The controlled Nfe2l1 signal was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while the only 5% FDR gene in any cell type was an isolated Snhg11 hit in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a broad, cortex-wide acute response and localizes the modest FDR-controlled signal to a thalamic class plus one midbrain GABA lncRNA event.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The thalamic genes were only FDR<0.1, not FDR<0.05, and the midbrain Snhg11 result came from just 55 perturbed cells with the target row itself at FDR=1.

summary: Nfe2l1 perturbation did not recapitulate proteasome-subunit or Pomp perturbations in the same neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Because NFE2L1 is the canonical proteasome bounce-back transcription factor, the large Psmc1, Psmb4, Psmc5, and Pomp signatures show that these cells were capable of producing proteasome-stress transcriptomes that partial basal Nfe2l1 perturbation did not trigger or mimic.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The contrast is between direct proteasome component perturbations and a weak Nfe2l1 transcript depletion measured without proteasome inhibitor challenge.

summary: Pvalb GABA and midbrain glutamatergic cells buffered nominal Nfe2l1 mRNA loss with essentially no FDR-controlled downstream response.
why_it_matters: This points to either biological buffering of a partial Nfe2l1 decrease in unstressed neurons or a requirement for stronger and longer Nfe2l1 loss before the ER/proteasome homeostasis circuit becomes visible.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The target rows in both classes were nominally decreased but were FDR=1 after genome-wide correction.

summary: The strongest exploratory Nfe2l1 signature neighbors in thalamic glutamatergic cells were Uba5 and Ufc1, the E1/E2 enzymes of UFMylation.
why_it_matters: This nominates a possible ER/proteostasis convergence between an ER-membrane NFE2L1 sensor and UFMylation machinery, but the relationship is signature-based rather than a proven direct regulatory edge.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All-gene correlations were small, especially outside the thalamic class, and no direct NFE2L1-UFMylation mechanism is established by these data.

summary: The basal Perturb-seq near-negative should not be read as evidence that NFE2L1 inhibition is neuronally safe.
why_it_matters: Published mouse brain knockout and proteasome-inhibitor studies show that NFE2L1 becomes critical when neurons must sustain proteasome-gene expression or recover proteasome activity, whereas this dataset observed only weak acute transcript depletion under unchallenged conditions.
main_caveats: The warning is inferred by comparing assay context to prior loss-of-function and stress models; no degeneration or protein-turnover phenotype was measured here.

summary: Actn4 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome in any assayed neuronal subclass, largely because on-target RNA suppression was weak.
why_it_matters: The first-order interpretation should be lack of a robust RNA phenotype, not assignment of the largest nominal genes to an ACTN4 pathway.
main_caveats: The screen reports mRNA-level DE; weak guide activity or residual ACTN4 protein could mask a structural phenotype.

summary: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was the only class with nominal Actn4 RNA reduction and contained a weak actin/adhesion-flavored tail involving Enah, Ywhab, Cdc42, and Ctnnal1.
why_it_matters: This is the only place where the measured target and nearby cytoskeletal regulators move in the same contrast, so it is the best biomarker hypothesis for follow-up despite failing FDR.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: All L4/5 genes had pvals_adj = 1.0; Ctnnal1 was just outside p < 0.001; this is a hypothesis-generating nominal pattern.

summary: The numerically strongest adjusted result, Unc80 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, is not supported by on-target Actn4 knockdown.
why_it_matters: It prevents a misleading scalar call: the smallest q value in the Actn4 table points to a cell type where Actn4 itself was unchanged.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The Unc80 pvals_adj was 0.159944, so even this disconnected scalar was not FDR-significant.

summary: Actn4 failed to phenocopy high-confidence actin / junction perturbations such as Actg1, Ctnnb1, and Cdc42, and its L4/5 signature was nearly uncorrelated with matched cytoskeletal perturbations.
why_it_matters: ACTN4 resides in the same actin-adhesion network, but the Perturb-seq phenotype separates Actn4 from perturbations that are efficiently knocked down and transcriptionally active in the dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and partly restricted to the top 200 nominal Actn4 L4/5 genes; Actb target RNA could not be quantified because Actb was not part of the measured-gene rows.

summary: Known ACTN4 structural and nuclear functions are not recapitulated as an NF-kappaB-like or actin-remodeling RNA program in this mouse-brain survey.
why_it_matters: Published neuron and podocyte work make ACTN4 biologically plausible, but the perturbation readout suggests that spine architecture or podocyte transcriptional mechanisms are uncoupled from bulk neuronal RNA changes here.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks morphology, protein localization, synaptic stimulation, and podocytes; it cannot rule out non-transcriptional ACTN4 activity.

summary: No alpha-actinin paralog or major core actin-junction partner showed FDR-significant transcriptional compensation after Actn4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The weak phenotype is therefore not explained by an obvious Actn1, Actn2, Actn3, Vcl, or Actg1 mRNA feedback loop in the measured data.
main_caveats: Compensation could occur through unmeasured protein abundance, localization, mechanics, or non-targeted paralog perturbations.

summary: The dataset offers no CNS RNA benefit for lowering Actn4, while human and mouse genetics warn that ACTN4 loss or altered F-actin binding can damage podocytes.
why_it_matters: Any strategy that systemically inhibits ACTN4 should treat kidney podocytes as a liability context; the mouse-brain Perturb-seq result does not provide a counterbalancing neuronal rescue signature.
main_caveats: No direct ACTN4 inhibitor was tested, and FSGS mutations can be gain-of-function rather than simple haploinsufficiency.

summary: Appl1 loss produced a globally buffered acute transcriptome: the strongest row was the Appl1 transcript itself in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, but no Appl1-profiled gene in any cell type reached pvals_adj<0.05.
why_it_matters: APPL1 is a membrane/endosomal adaptor with signaling roles; a near-null FDR result therefore argues that the screen is not capturing APPL1 biology as a broad steady-state mRNA program.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The strongest cell type had only 30 perturbed cells and the on-target row itself had pvals_adj=0.437899, so the finding is a negative transcriptomic result rather than proof of complete APPL1 loss.

summary: Detectable Appl1 transcript depletion was uneven, with the dominant nominal signal confined to 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and weaker nominal rows in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: This makes cell-type comparisons hard to interpret: several apparently quiet cell types may simply lack enough measured target knockdown for a downstream APPL1 response.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: All p-adjusted values for Appl1 outside 110 were 1.0, and one borderline cortical row had p=0.05096.

summary: Known APPL1-associated receptor and PI3K-AKT-mTOR perturbations did not form a shared APPL1-like transcriptional state across the 20 profiled cell types.
why_it_matters: APPL1 is annotated and experimentally reported as a receptor/endosomal scaffold, but this dataset suggests that acute neuronal APPL1 knockdown is usually not interchangeable with perturbing Adipor2, Insr, Igf1r, Ntrk1/2/3, or core PI3K-mTOR neighbors at the mRNA-signature level.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed from weak Appl1 signatures; APPL2, ADIPOR1, and Rab5 isoforms were absent from the perturbation panel; metabolic muscle-cell literature is only indirectly matched to brain cell types.

summary: A cerebellar GABAergic Akt/Tsc signature was recoverable only as a restricted, exploratory neighbor signal: Appl1 correlated with Akt3 and anticorrelated with Tsc2 in 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: The sign is compatible with APPL1 acting upstream of AKT and opposite the AKT-inhibited TSC2 brake on mTOR, so it is the main hint that an expected signaling axis is present in the perturbation space despite weak scalar DE.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Appl1 itself was not depleted in 308 CB GABA, and the comparison uses genome-wide score correlations rather than significant Appl1 marker genes.

summary: The APPL1-APP/Rab5 Alzheimer axis left only a nominal App-containing trace in one upper-layer glutamatergic stratum and no FDR-level response.
why_it_matters: Published APPL1-APP biology centers on APP-βCTF recruitment of APPL1 to Rab5 endosomes, so this weak mRNA response suggests that therapeutic or disease-direction tests of APPL1 need endosomal APP/Rab5 and protein-trafficking readouts rather than relying on acute DE alone.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The 009 App row and the neighboring transcripts were nominal only, Appl1 was not knocked down in that cell type, and the dataset did not assay APP-βCTF, Rab5 activity, or endosome morphology.

summary: Cdin1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the sampled brain cells: no gene reached FDR<0.05 across 355,046 tests, and the measured Cdin1 transcript itself was never significantly depleted.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant result. It argues that this experiment did not create a high-confidence acute neuronal CDIN1 loss-of-function signature and that downstream nominal rows must be treated as hypotheses rather than pathway-level discoveries.
main_caveats: Direct target engagement was weak, so the result cannot distinguish biological buffering from ineffective perturbation; the assay sampled mouse brain cells rather than erythroid progenitors.

summary: The only appreciable Cdin1-associated signals were sub-threshold and cell-type restricted, led by Pcdh10 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, Zfp638/Slit1 in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and Zcchc18/Celf6/Qpct in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: The sparse nominal structure localizes any possible neuronal response to a few classes instead of supporting a pan-neuronal CDIN1 program.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: No listed gene reached FDR<0.05; each response came from 46-64 perturbed cells; directions were not replicated across multiple cell types.

summary: Weak scalar signal was not explained solely by small perturbation groups: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut had 94-171 Cdin1 cells but no adjusted hit below FDR 0.25.
why_it_matters: Higher cell counts would have made large downstream effects easier to detect, so the absence of signal in these classes supports broad neuronal buffering or weak biology rather than only low sampling depth.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cell count does not guarantee perturbation strength; target transcript knockdown was also not significant in these cell types.

summary: The Perturb-seq readout did not reproduce an erythroid CDIN1/CDAN1-like program in neurons despite strong human genetics linking CDIN1 to CDA-I and biochemical evidence that CDIN1 complexes with Codanin-1.
why_it_matters: The result is better viewed as a context refinement than as a contradiction: CDIN1 disease alleles act in erythropoiesis, whereas these were mouse brain cell classes and the most direct CDAN1/ASF1 comparator perturbations were absent.
main_caveats: The comparison to CDAN1 and ASF1 is indirect because those perturbations were not present in the staged parquet.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor scans yielded only modest correlations and no interpretable CDIN1 pathway neighbor; safe-target controls appeared among top opposite or same-direction neighbors in the two most nominal Cdin1 cell types.
why_it_matters: This argues against elevating any unrelated top-neighbor convergence to mechanism and makes the weak nominal Cdin1 signatures look fragile.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The scan used only the 200 largest-magnitude Cdin1 genes in each cell type and was intended as an exploratory neighbor check, not as a genome-wide network reconstruction.

summary: Assayed G-protein/R7-neighbor perturbations were essentially uncorrelated with the Gnb5 signature, including in the Pvalb context where Gnb5 itself was depleted.

summary: Absence of a broad transcriptional response is not evidence that inhibiting GNB5 would be safe.

summary: The Mpc2 partner transcript did not increase detectably after Mpc1 perturbation, including in the Pvalb and thalamic classes with the clearest nominal Mpc1 decrease.

summary: The expected integrin-laminin/ECM neighborhood was not transcriptionally engaged after Itga7 perturbation in neurons.

cell_types: 22 assayed non-dopaminergic neuronal classes
main_caveats: Only transcript-level pathway members that were measured in these neuronal contrasts could be evaluated; ECM signaling can be post-transcriptional.

summary: Itga7 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with beta1-integrin, integrin-paralog, and dystrophin-glycoprotein-family perturbations.
why_it_matters: Alpha7/beta1 integrin and the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex are related basement-membrane linkages in muscle, but their CRISPR signatures were not interchangeable in the neuronal dataset.
cell_types: 22 assayed non-dopaminergic neuronal classes
main_caveats: The contrast is weakened by poor Itga7 target-transcript engagement and by comparing neuronal transcriptomes to literature from muscle.

summary: The negative neuronal result fits a model in which brain Itga7 effects are concentrated in astrocyte/perivascular ECM biology rather than in the assayed neurons.

cell_types: assayed neuronal classes|astrocytes/perivascular cells not assayed

summary: The neuron-only, weak-engagement Itga7 result should not be used to dismiss ITGA7 blockade in glioblastoma stem-like cells or other laminin-rich disease settings.
why_it_matters: Glioblastoma literature links ITGA7 to laminin-induced signaling, growth, and invasion, so the key therapeutic context is malignant ECM adhesion rather than the buffered neuronal response measured here.
cell_types: assayed neuronal classes|glioblastoma stem-like cells not assayed
main_caveats: Cancer stem-like cells were not present in the mouse-brain neuronal Perturb-seq assay; this is a scope warning, not a direct efficacy result.

summary: Igf2r perturbation had one multiplicity-adjusted on-target RNA effect, concentrated in 052 Pvalb Gaba, and no adjusted off-target genes.

summary: Several cell classes showed nominally strong Igf2r knockdown but no FDR-significant downstream response.

why_it_matters: The dataset argues against using a cross-cell-type Igf2r signature or any recurrent nominal top gene as a robust biomarker of Igf2r loss.
main_caveats: This is a negative transcriptomic statement; a protein-trafficking phenotype could recur without changing mRNA abundances.

summary: In Pvalb cells, Igf2r knockdown was transcriptionally uncoupled from profiled endolysosomal trafficking and IGF-growth pathway perturbations.

summary: The Igf2r brain signature did not look like acute activation of the developmental IGF2-IGF1R growth axis.
why_it_matters: Mouse genetics links Igf2r loss to systemic excess IGF2 and IGF1R-dependent fetal overgrowth, whereas this dataset suggests that reducing Igf2r mRNA in profiled brain neurons is not by itself enough to impose an IGF1R/INSR/TSC/MTOR-like transcriptional state.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The assay did not measure IGF2 ligand levels, IGF1R phosphorylation, mTOR activity, or developmental overgrowth endpoints.

summary: Sparse mRNA changes after Igf2r depletion should not be interpreted as evidence that neuronal IGF2R loss is functionally silent.

main_caveats: This is a caution inferred from known receptor biology plus a negative RNA phenotype; it requires direct protein, trafficking, and ligand measurements.

summary: Safe_target_14 behaved as a transcriptomically inert artificial control across its 20 measured mouse-brain cell classes.

summary: The strongest Safe_target_14 rows were nominal cell-type tails rather than robust cell-type-selective biology.

summary: The observed null is consistent with GP1BA being outside the transcriptional repertoire of the assayed neural populations.

summary: Several hemostasis or hematopoietic perturbations behaved like Gp1ba by remaining FDR-silent in brain cell types, while the most direct GPIb members and Vwf were not present as perturbation comparators.

summary: Nominal Gp1ba hits and restricted signature neighbors did not resolve to VWF/GPIb-IX-V signaling, hemostasis, or a coherent compensatory pathway.

summary: The brain Perturb-seq result refines GP1BA disease biology toward platelet and megakaryocyte mechanisms, not neuronal mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Human GP1BA disorders are driven by altered GPIb-IX-V expression or VWF binding; the lack of a neural response warns against using this dataset to infer Bernard-Soulier or platelet-type von Willebrand disease mechanisms in neurons.

summary: The Gp1ba null response was retained in the highest-cell-count contrasts, so it is not explained solely by low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Atr produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any assayed mouse-brain neuronal class, and the Atr transcript itself was not significantly depleted.

summary: The absence of a brain transcriptional response should not be used to de-risk clinical ATR inhibition.
why_it_matters: Human ATR is genetically disease-linked and chemically tractable, but this dataset neither achieved strong Atr knockdown nor assayed kinase inhibition.
main_caveats: The warning concerns interpretation of a negative dataset; it does not measure ATR inhibitor toxicity directly.

summary: Pou5f1-targeting guides produced no FDR-significant neuronal transcriptomic phenotype, and the target transcript itself was absent from the measured DE feature space.

main_caveats: Signature correlations were exploratory and remain hard to interpret when Pou5f1 itself appears transcriptionally absent.

summary: Pou5f1 perturbation in this brain dataset should not be used to infer cancer-stemness, Oct3/4-activation, or reprogramming mechanisms.
why_it_matters: POU5F1 is biologically and chemically annotated in pluripotency and tumor contexts, but the neuronal Perturb-seq readout is FDR-null and outside those target-active states.

summary: The Oprk1 Perturb-seq null is non-directional for kappa-opioid-receptor agonism or antagonism despite strong external druggability and disease links.
why_it_matters: OPRK1 is clinically and pharmacologically actionable, but this dataset cannot rank KOR activation versus blockade for pain, mood, pruritus, or addiction indications because neither receptor knockdown nor ligand-state signaling was detected.
main_caveats: KOR drugs can be agonists, partial agonists, or antagonists in different indications; knockdown in unstimulated mouse neurons is not equivalent to biased or ligand-specific receptor modulation.

summary: Kmt2e perturbation did not significantly reduce Kmt2e mRNA in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: Weak mRNA-level target engagement makes downstream signatures difficult to interpret as simple Kmt2e loss of transcript and explains why most contrasts were small.
main_caveats: mRNA abundance is not edit efficiency or protein abundance; coding disruption could occur without detectable RNA depletion.

summary: FDR-resolved Kmt2e transcriptional responses were confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The result nominates two glutamatergic contexts for follow-up while showing that most assayed classes were buffered or underpowered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The two positive classes had the two largest Kmt2e matched-cell counts, so statistical power may contribute to the apparent restriction.

summary: Snhg11, Atp6v0b, and Eno2 were consistently induced in both FDR-resolved Kmt2e signatures.
why_it_matters: These three genes are compact candidate readouts of the perturbation state across the only two resolved Kmt2e cell types.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only three shared genes passed FDR<0.25, and two of the six gene-by-cell observations were weaker than FDR 0.10.

summary: Kmt2e signatures were nearly uncorrelated with active KMT2A/B/D and SETD1A writer signatures in the same glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues against treating Kmt2e as interchangeable with enzymatic H3K4 writer perturbations in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Comparators had unequal perturbation strength, and several KMT2-family targets had much larger DE burdens than Kmt2e.

summary: Ogt perturbation was strongly engaged but did not phenocopy Kmt2e in the two Kmt2e-responsive classes.
why_it_matters: A proximal biochemical stabilizer of MLL5 cannot be used as a simple transcriptomic proxy for Kmt2e loss in these neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Ogt is pleiotropic, Usp7 and Hcfc1 were not assayed as matched comparators in this evidence row, and Kmt2e itself showed weak mRNA engagement.

summary: Hnrnpu and Ddx23 were recurrent weak positive empirical neighbors of Kmt2e, whereas the strongest anticorrelations were also small.
why_it_matters: This preserves a dataset-derived follow-up direction that would be missed by considering only annotated H3K4 machinery.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Whole-transcriptome correlations were low, and the relationship is signature-level rather than a demonstrated direct interaction.

summary: Kmt2e mouse-brain Perturb-seq produced a much smaller and more restricted response than the broad human KMT2E neurodevelopmental genetics might suggest.
why_it_matters: The result warns that this assay should be used to nominate cell-state markers, not to infer a direct therapeutic direction for O'Donnell-Luria-Rodan syndrome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Human disease alleles, developmental timing, species, and protein dosage are not matched to the mouse single-cell perturbation readout.

summary: Adgrl3 knockdown was strongest in a small subset of glutamatergic neuronal classes rather than uniformly across the 22 measured Adgrl3 contrasts.
why_it_matters: ADGRL3/LPHN3 is a brain-biased adhesion GPCR and ADHD-linked gene, so the screen localizes the most efficient acute perturbation to thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic classes while leaving the dopaminergic class untested.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction partly reflects guide recovery and power: the 217 P MY Pineal Glut effect was large but had only 25 perturbed cells, and 215 MB Dopa had no Adgrl3 contrast.

summary: Even where Adgrl3 was knocked down at FDR<0.05, the transcriptome contained no significant non-target response.
why_it_matters: Known LPHN3 biology centers on synaptic adhesion, G-protein signaling, alternative splicing, and scaffold recruitment; the Perturb-seq endpoint therefore argues for an acute response that is transcriptionally buffered or mainly post-transcriptional in these cell states.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The assay measures steady-state RNA rather than synapse number, receptor signaling, protein localization, or LPHN3 splice isoforms.

summary: Adgrl3 did not phenocopy engaged latrophilin paralogs or its Tenm3/FLRT ligand neighborhood at the whole-transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: LPHN3 physically binds FLRT and teneurin partners, but loss of different nodes in that adhesion system should not be treated as interchangeable transcriptional perturbations in this dataset.
main_caveats: Flrt3 and Tenm4 had weak or absent self-knockdown at FDR<0.05, and the comparison uses score-vector correlations rather than a direct synaptic phenotype.

summary: Flrt3, a canonical latrophilin ligand, was a nominally induced candidate feedback marker in Adgrl3-perturbed Pvalb GABA cells.
why_it_matters: The sign is consistent with the possibility of ligand-level compensation inside the latrophilin-FLRT adhesion axis, but it is only a hypothesis-generating single-cell-type signal.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Neither the Adgrl3 row nor the Flrt3 row reached FDR<0.05 in 052 Pvalb Gaba, and the pattern did not recur across cell types.

summary: A genome-wide signature scan found no strong positive or inverse perturbation neighbor for Adgrl3.
why_it_matters: The Adgrl3 phenotype is not part of a large shared transcriptional module in this screen; the strongest apparent neighbors were weak and occurred in a cell type without significant Adgrl3 target engagement.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Neighbor calling used Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon scores and is sensitive to noisy weak signatures.

summary: Hoxb8 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome in any of the 23 assayed neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant result: a homeobox transcription factor with known developmental roles did not generate a detectable cell-autonomous neuronal DE module in this brain panel.
main_caveats: Target engagement was not demonstrated at the Hoxb8 transcript, so buffering and weak or absent expression cannot be disentangled.

summary: The Hoxb8 transcript itself was sparsely measured and nonsignificant, leaving on-target perturbation unquantified for most cell types.
why_it_matters: A null downstream signature is much less interpretable when the target mRNA is not observed or not depleted after perturbation.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Absence from the DE result table records lack of a tested Hoxb8 row after expression filtering, not necessarily absence of genomic editing.

direction: neuronal panel negative; microglial/spinal mechanisms not tested
summary: The negative neuronal Hoxb8 screen points away from the assayed glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic classes as primary surrogates for published Hoxb8 grooming and sensory mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Mouse Hoxb8 disease-like phenotypes are tied to Hoxb8-lineage microglia and spinal dorsal horn biology, whereas those contexts were not represented as Hoxb8 Perturb-seq cell types here.
main_caveats: The dataset cannot directly test Hoxb8-lineage microglia or embryonic spinal dorsal horn neurons.

summary: HOX-family perturbations and the assayed HOX cofactors Pbx1 and Meis1 were largely buffered and did not converge with Hoxb8 signatures.
why_it_matters: STRING and HOX biology nominate Pbx/Meis cofactors and HOX relatives as natural comparators; their near-zero correlations argue against a hidden common HOX transcriptional module in these cells.
main_caveats: The group-8 paralogs Hoxa8, Hoxc8, and Hoxd8 and several Hoxb-cluster STRING partners were not present as comparators.

summary: Pigk down-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut is the nearest Hoxb8 cell-type candidate but remains only exploratory.
why_it_matters: Preserving the best near-hit prevents overcalling a null screen while flagging the one cortical glutamatergic context that would be worth re-testing with stronger target engagement.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Pigk had FDR 0.16094 and all other 022 L5 ET CTX Glut genes had FDR 1.0, so this is not a validated downstream target.

summary: HOXB8 should be treated as a lineage biology factor rather than an obvious directly druggable neuronal target.
why_it_matters: A direct HOXB8 inhibitor has little database support and the perturbation screen did not expose a robust neuronal effector program, while mouse genetics link the gene to specialized microglial and spinal phenotypes.
main_caveats: Absence of ChEMBL/Open Targets/Reactome support is not proof that HOXB8 can never be modulated; it only argues against an established direct pharmacology.

summary: Cnr1 was an under-engaged, transcriptionally near-null perturbation across sampled neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: A large fraction of brain CB1 biology is acute GPCR signaling at terminals; in this dataset there is not enough on-target mRNA reduction or adjusted downstream DE to infer a Cnr1 loss-of-function transcriptional program.
main_caveats: Loss of Cnr1 coding function could occur without lowering the assayed transcript; the source table lacks guide-level indel or protein measurements.

summary: The lone adjusted hit, Srcap induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, was isolated from measurable Cnr1 transcript knockdown.
why_it_matters: The only FDR-significant signal should not be treated as a high-confidence thalamic CB1 effector; it marks an exploratory, cell-type-restricted anomaly that is stronger for Srcap than for the target itself.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene adjusted result; Cnr1 mRNA increased numerically in the same contrast; no independent Srcap-CB1 mechanism is established here.

summary: Available CB1/GPCR/cAMP-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Cnr1 signatures.
why_it_matters: Cnr1 is curated as a Gi/o-coupled receptor and STRING links it to Gnao1, Drd2, Gnai proteins, and adenylyl cyclases; the near-zero related-target correlations argue that the weak Cnr1 signatures are not a coherent projection of canonical CB1 signaling onto steady-state mRNA.
main_caveats: Correlation used only the top 200 Cnr1 score genes per cell type; Cnr2, Gnai1, Gnai2, Gnai3, Gpr55, and Adcy8 were absent from the perturbation catalog, so several direct STRING partners could not be tested.

summary: The dataset gives no central CB1 agonist-versus-antagonist transcriptional direction despite clear pharmacologic tractability of CNR1.
why_it_matters: CB1 has approved or clinical ligands, and brain-penetrant orthosteric antagonism has a known neuropsychiatric liability; the near-null mouse-brain Perturb-seq result should therefore be used as a safety/biomarker negative rather than as support for a central therapeutic direction.
main_caveats: scRNA loss-of-function signatures are indirect with respect to acute ligand pharmacology, species differ, and central adverse effects are clinical phenotypes rather than single-cell transcriptional endpoints.

summary: Gnal itself was absent from the measured DE feature universe, so the Perturb-seq table cannot quantify on-target Gnal transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: A weak phenotype could reflect incomplete perturbation or absence of target-expressing cells rather than biological buffering; target engagement is therefore the primary interpretive limitation.
main_caveats: Absence from the DE table does not prove absence of protein perturbation; it only prevents direct transcript-level validation.

direction: one isolated up-regulated FDR hit against a pan-dataset null background
summary: Gnal produced an extremely sparse endpoint transcriptional response, with only 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut containing any FDR-significant gene.
why_it_matters: The effect is not a broad neuronal stress or state-conversion program; any biological interpretation has to focus on a single low-cell-count class and on negative results elsewhere.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: FDR significance occurred in a class with only 33 matched perturbed cells, and the strongest high-count classes were all negative with unmeasured target engagement.

summary: Pde4a was the second-ranked induced gene in the only FDR-positive Gnal cell type, making it a weak candidate readout of cAMP-linked feedback.
why_it_matters: PDE4A sits in the same second-messenger space as Gαolf, so the nominal Pde4a increase is more interpretable than the isolated Muc3a hit, but it remains below FDR and should be validated independently.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Pde4a had FDR 0.183; the cell type is not a matched striatal medium spiny neuron context; no direct cAMP measurement is available.

direction: weak related-target convergence and weak Adcy5/Adcy1 opposition
summary: Known GNAL/Golf-cAMP neighbors failed to form a strong Gnal-like transcriptomic module, and Adcy5/Adcy1 were weakly anti-correlated with Gnal in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: The weak and partly inverse related-target signatures argue that this endpoint scRNA-seq assay is not reading out the curated Gαolf–adenylyl-cyclase pathway as a simple linear transcriptional state.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: All correlations were small; most comparator perturbations are themselves target-engagement-limited; transcriptomic correlation is an indirect proxy for cAMP activity.

direction: negative in closest coarse striatal-context class
summary: Gnal did not generate a robust disease-like transcriptional signature in the coarse LGE/GABA or other broad neuronal classes despite GNAL being a striatal cAMP dystonia gene.
why_it_matters: DYT-GNAL biology may require striatal medium spiny neuron, cholinergic-interneuron, synaptic, or biochemical cAMP/PKA assays rather than broad endpoint scRNA-seq DE to capture the causal mechanism.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA is only a coarse proxy for striatal projection neurons; no D1- versus D2-SPN-specific DE was available.

summary: Il10ra perturbation was transcriptionally inert across the assayed glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: A flat result across all measured contexts means this screen does not provide evidence for a neuron-intrinsic IL10RA loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not measurably depleted, so the result is best interpreted as absent/weak transcript engagement in these cell types rather than proof that edited IL10RA protein is irrelevant.

summary: The obligate IL-10 receptor subunits Il10ra and Il10rb did not behave as an interchangeable receptor pair in this dataset.
why_it_matters: The known biochemical coupling of IL10RA and IL10RB would predict shared downstream signaling only in IL10-responsive cells; their near-zero signature correlations here argue that the neuronal guide-positive cells were outside that active receptor state.
main_caveats: Both receptor-subunit signatures were weak, so the apparent uncoupling should not be read as an opposing molecular mechanism.

summary: The negative neuronal response is consistent with IL10RA biology being concentrated in immune and CNS macrophage/microglial compartments rather than in the assayed neurons.
why_it_matters: IL10RA is a high-confidence inflammatory-bowel-disease and anti-inflammatory receptor gene, but this screen indicates that a brainwide neuronal sampling frame is the wrong context for recovering that disease mechanism.
main_caveats: The dataset did not test microglia, macrophages, intestinal cells, or ligand stimulation, so the conclusion is a context refinement rather than a test of IL-10 signaling in its canonical cells.

summary: A global signature-neighbor scan did not uncover a robust hidden Il10ra module.
why_it_matters: Weak nominal Il10ra genes could have been rescued by repeated convergence with other perturbations; instead the strongest correlations were small, confined to 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and included safe-target controls.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: This is a scalar whole-signature scan; it does not exclude a small pathway-specific effect below transcriptome-wide correlation sensitivity.

summary: Stat1, unlike Il10ra, produced direct on-target RNA depletion in several neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The internal positive contrast argues against explaining the Il10ra result solely by the Wilcoxon pipeline or by a blanket lack of power for every immune-associated perturbation.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Stat1 and Il10ra differ in baseline expression, guide cutting, and transcript stability; Stat1 is an assay contrast, not an IL-10 receptor subunit.

summary: The flat Il10ra neuronal signature should not be used to deprioritize IL-10 receptor modulation for neuroinflammatory biology.
why_it_matters: Prior CNS work implicates IL-10 signaling in microglial silencing after inflammatory challenge, whereas this dataset sampled neuronal classes with weak Il10ra transcript engagement.
main_caveats: No therapeutic perturbation, ligand exposure, or microglial cell class was assayed directly.

summary: The strongest Epha7 perturbation is a true self-knockdown in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut with no FDR-supported downstream RNA response.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from pathway output: Epha7 mRNA can be depleted in a neuronal class while the steady-state transcriptome remains buffered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: RNA only; the known EphA7 phenotypes are developmental and may be mediated by phosphorylation, morphology, or survival rather than broad acute transcription.

summary: Epha7 self-depletion is broad at the nominal level but FDR-supported mainly in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c and L2/3 IT CTX glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: Literature emphasizes cortical EphA7 functions, but the dataset shows uneven guide engagement and suggests that cortical RNA phenotypes are modest despite detectable Epha7 knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Most non-thalamic rows are nominal after genome-wide correction; inhibitory-class rows are exploratory.

summary: Measured EphA7 ligand and effector transcripts were not detectably rewired in the best-engaged thalamic Epha7 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Epha7 sits in a ligand-rich Eph/ephrin neighborhood, so absence of Efna/Efnb/Abl1/Ngef/Rasa1 mRNA feedback narrows the observed phenotype to receptor loss rather than a self-amplifying transcriptional Eph module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No protein phosphorylation or ligand-presentation measurements were available; partner genes with low or zero expression can have unstable logFC values.

summary: Epha7 signatures were nearly orthogonal to other Eph-family perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: Eph receptors are related cell-surface tyrosine kinases, but either Epha7 has a weak RNA phenotype or its transcriptional consequences are not interchangeable with Epha4/Epha5/Epha6/Ephb perturbations in the assayed neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Correlation analysis used weak score vectors dominated by non-significant genes; it can detect large shared programs but not shared non-transcriptional signaling.

summary: Mouse-brain Epha7 knockdown does not model the soluble EPHA7/TR restoration mechanism reported for follicular lymphoma.
why_it_matters: The perturbation lowers endogenous neuronal Epha7 RNA and is buffered, whereas the lymphoma intervention restores a soluble antagonistic protein; inhibitor-like and replacement-like directions should not be conflated.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The disease literature is human lymphoma, not mouse brain; this finding is a directionality warning rather than a lymphoma efficacy test.

summary: Sst GABA, MB Dopa, and pineal glutamatergic rows are uninformative negative results because Epha7 itself was not detectably depleted.
why_it_matters: Weak self-depletion prevents over-calling those classes as biologically resistant to Epha7 perturbation.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is a technical-interpretive negative result, not a mechanistic claim about EphA7.

direction: Mef2d transcript mostly down; no FDR-resolved downstream direction
summary: Mef2d perturbation was globally buffered or under-engaged: the target transcript usually moved downward, but no row reached FDR<0.05 in any of 23 cell classes.
why_it_matters: MEF2D is a transcription factor, so the absence of a multi-gene adjusted signature is itself biologically informative and prevents strong claims about canonical MEF2D effector programs in this dataset.
main_caveats: The best self-knockdown only reached FDR=0.099, so incomplete CRISPRi can explain part or all of the buffered downstream response.

direction: strongest down in 155 MB Glut, weaker elsewhere
summary: The most localized on-target signal was in 155 MB Glut, where Mef2d was the top-ranked row; hypothalamic/pineal classes had weaker nominal Mef2d depletion and several classes had little detectable target engagement.
why_it_matters: This narrows any transcriptomic interpretation to a small number of classes and makes pan-brain negative calls unsafe for low-cell or weak-knockdown strata.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Even 155 MB Glut did not meet FDR<0.05 for the target transcript, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 59 perturbed cells.

direction: Mef2c active where Mef2d is weak
summary: Mef2d did not phenocopy Mef2c in cortical IT, Pvalb, or thalamic classes where Mef2c knockdown produced FDR-supported signatures and direct Mef2c depletion.
why_it_matters: MEF2 paralogs are structurally and functionally linked, yet this Perturb-seq panel resolves Mef2c as the responsive paralog in these neuronal contexts while Mef2d remains weak.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Mef2d guide activity was weaker than Mef2c guide activity in the same classes, so the contrast mixes paralog biology with perturbation efficacy.

summary: The restricted Mef2d signature did not align with measured MEF2-family, HDAC, calcium-kinase, CREB1, or NFATC3 perturbations and had no strong positive or negative whole-panel signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Canonical MEF2 activity is coupled to CaMK/MAPK/CREB and HDAC regulation, but the dataset offers no transcriptional evidence that acute Mef2d knockdown entered that module.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak Mef2d signatures and does not test protein-level MEF2 activity.

summary: Mef2d knockdown did not trigger FDR-supported transcriptional induction of the measured paralogs Mef2a or Mef2c.
why_it_matters: Paralog buffering, if present, is not visible as increased Mef2a/Mef2c mRNA in this single-cell readout; compensation could instead be constitutive or post-transcriptional.
main_caveats: Only mRNA abundance was measured; Mef2a and Mef2c activity could change by phosphorylation, localization, or dimer usage without changing transcript levels.

direction: buffered partial loss, not gain of function
summary: The mouse-brain loss-of-transcript phenotype does not resemble a strong neuronal-death or leukemia-like MEF2D activation program, so disease links to MEF2D should not be modeled as simple acute partial Mef2d loss in the assayed brain cells.
why_it_matters: Parkinson-related reports implicate MEF2D protein quality control, whereas MEF2D-rearranged ALL is a gain-of-function fusion state; the Perturb-seq result instead looks like a weak partial-loss perturbation with little downstream propagation.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks stress, alpha-synuclein, developmental, blood-lineage, and fusion-oncoprotein contexts, and it measures transcript abundance rather than MEF2D protein activity.

summary: Magel2 did not show measurable target-transcript depletion and had no genome-wide FDR<0.05 downstream genes in this atlas.
why_it_matters: This makes the Perturb-seq result primarily a negative target-engagement result rather than evidence against the established genetic requirement for MAGEL2 in Prader-Willi/Schaaf-Yang biology.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was measured; the result cannot rule out protein-level or developmental MAGEL2 functions, and failed or weak target engagement is the dominant caveat.

summary: The lowest Magel2 adjusted P values were confined to nominal midbrain, hindbrain, LGE, and medial/lateral hypothalamic rows, with the only FDR<0.10 row being Kalrn down in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The data do not define a robust pan-neuronal module; they nominate 155 MB Glut as the least-null context while showing that even the strongest outliers remain below conventional FDR support.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: All highlighted genes except Kalrn had FDR=1.0, and Kalrn reached only FDR=0.09595.

summary: Magel2 was much weaker and transcriptionally orthogonal to active imprinted or Prader-Willi-region perturbations in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Ndn, Snrpn, and Peg3 generated strong FDR-supported 155 MB Glut signatures, so Magel2 cannot be treated as interchangeable with other imprinted PWS-neighbor genes in this Perturb-seq readout.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is based on full DE score correlations in one cell type and does not test shared protein-complex activity directly.

summary: Broad hypothalamic Magel2 perturbations did not recapitulate the oxytocin, leptin, or melanocortin neuropeptide axes emphasized by mouse and human MAGEL2 studies.
why_it_matters: The key disease mechanisms are likely restricted to specific POMC, oxytocin, or neurosecretory neurons or to developmental/protein-trafficking phenotypes that are diluted in the coarse hypothalamic classes present here.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The dataset uses broad cell classes and showed weak Magel2 target-transcript engagement, so absence of these marker responses is not evidence that MAGEL2 is irrelevant in specialized hypothalamic neurons.

summary: The canonical MAGEL2 retromer/WASH and neurosecretory biology was not recovered as a robust transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Nominal Snx27, Rab5b, and Cpe changes point in the direction of endosomal or secretory biology but were not FDR-supported, consistent with a protein-trafficking mechanism being poorly captured by acute single-cell mRNA DE.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Snx27, Rab5b, and Cpe were selected post hoc from nominal rows and had FDR values from 0.3667 to 1.0.

summary: No strong positive or negative genome-wide signature neighbor emerged for Magel2 in the least-null 155 MB Glut context.
why_it_matters: The top nonself correlations were near zero, arguing against an obvious convergent perturbation module or an interpretable opposite-direction neighbor for this weak Magel2 profile.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor analysis was restricted to the 155 MB Glut cell type; correlations are dominated by a weak Magel2 query vector.

summary: Hbs1l perturbation produced no reliable on-target Hbs1l mRNA depletion and almost no FDR-controlled transcriptome response across 22 cell types.
why_it_matters: The screen should not be read as a clean test of Hbs1l loss of function; the expected ribosome-rescue factor was either weakly engaged, post-transcriptionally perturbed, or buffered in this scRNA-seq endpoint.
main_caveats: Target engagement was inferred from the target transcript row rather than from HBS1L protein abundance or per-guide effects.

summary: The only FDR<0.05 response to Hbs1l was Usp48 down-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: This preserves the one statistically conventional hit while flagging that it is isolated and low-powered.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only 22 perturbed cells; Phf21a was subthreshold; no recurrence of the module in other cell types.

summary: Pvalb and CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells had the strongest subthreshold single-gene peaks despite negligible Hbs1l mRNA change.
why_it_matters: These peaks can seed follow-up but are not evidence for a robust Hbs1l-dependent transcriptional program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: No listed gene reached FDR<0.05 and Hbs1l was not reduced in either cell type.

summary: Weak Hbs1l score signatures converged with Uba5, Ufc1 and Rrn3 perturbations in a small subset of neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: UFMylation is a ribosome-associated quality-control pathway, so repeated Uba5/Ufc1/Rrn3 neighborhood structure is the most biologically interpretable signal in an otherwise sparse Hbs1l result set.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to score-vector correlations; Hbs1l had zero FDR<0.05 genes and no significant on-target knockdown in the implicated cell types.

summary: Hbs1l did not phenocopy the available indirect Xrn1 or Rack1 surveillance perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues against treating the modest Hbs1l score vectors as a generic mRNA-decay or ribosome-associated perturbation artifact.
main_caveats: Xrn1 and Rack1 are indirect comparators; core PELO and ABCE1 perturbations were not available.

summary: Cplx2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response across 22 assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: Cplx2 is a presynaptic SNARE regulator, so the absence of an RNA cascade separates acute vesicle-fusion biology from this weak steady-state Perturb-seq phenotype.
main_caveats: The null is inseparable from weak target-transcript depletion; electrophysiological or protein phenotypes were not measured.

summary: The strongest Cplx2 self-transcript decreases were nominally concentrated in Sst, NP-CT-L6b-OB, and MB Glut cells, while several higher-count cell types showed little or no depletion.
why_it_matters: This marks the Cplx2 signal as a weak engagement pattern rather than a confidently cell-type-restricted downstream program.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: All Cplx2 self-transcript rows had FDR 1.0; nominal differences could reflect guide efficacy, basal detectability, or sampling.

summary: Across all Chl1 perturbation tests, no non-Chl1 transcript survived FDR correction, even in the three classes with significant Chl1 depletion.
why_it_matters: The data argue that reducing Chl1 mRNA mainly reports the target itself and does not acutely trigger a strong cell-autonomous transcriptional cascade in this assay, despite CHL1 being a membrane adhesion molecule with neurodevelopmental and synaptic roles.

summary: The Perturb-seq readout does not reproduce the hippocampal PV/GABAergic or cortical developmental phenotypes reported for Chl1-null mice.

summary: Nfkb1 perturbation produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response in 22 mouse-brain cell classes.

summary: An unbiased signature-neighbor search found no meaningful positive or inverse perturbation partner for Nfkb1.
