cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Pvalb cells had nominal target-row depletion but the target row itself was not FDR-significant; group-level labels may mask finer Pvalb subtypes.

summary: Ppargc1a is an exploratory positive restricted-signature neighbor of Esrra.
why_it_matters: Because PGC-1α is a canonical ERRα coactivator, the restricted correlation nominates a shared transcriptional module worth validating.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Ppargc1a mRNA was not depleted and the Ppargc1a-targeted perturbation had no FDR genes, so this is a signature-neighbor hypothesis only.

summary: 155 MB Glut shows nominal Esrra lowering without a corrected downstream program.
why_it_matters: This separates target transcript reduction from a guaranteed systems-level response and argues that cellular context can buffer or fail to propagate Esrra loss.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Esrra target depletion in 155 MB Glut was nominal but not FDR-significant, so weak engagement rather than biological buffering could explain the result.

summary: Genetic Esrra loss in brain neurons raises a safety hypothesis for brain-penetrant ERRα antagonism.
why_it_matters: ERRα can be inhibited pharmacologically in preclinical cancer models, but the mouse-brain signature shows loss of neuronal energy and synaptic transcripts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The pharmacology reference is from tumor-cell models, not neurons; no drug exposure or dose response was tested in this Perturb-seq dataset.

summary: Drd4-targeting cells produced no FDR-supported transcriptional phenotype and no measurable Drd4 RNA knockdown in any profiled brain cell class.
why_it_matters: The central interpretation is absence of target engagement, not absence of DRD4 biology; downstream nominal genes should therefore be treated as noise or at most weak hypotheses.
main_caveats: The parquet contains Wilcoxon summary statistics rather than raw UMI distributions or individual guide sequences, so guide-specific efficacy and basal Drd4 expression cannot be inspected directly.

summary: Silencing was receptor-layer selective: Drd2, Drd3, Drd5, and Adora2a resembled Drd4 by lacking FDR-supported target RNA loss, whereas Comt, Gnao1, Gnb1, and Adcy3 had clear on-target decreases in selected cell types.
why_it_matters: This separates a dopamine/adenosine receptor accessibility or expression problem from wholesale assay failure, because catecholamine metabolism and intracellular GPCR/cAMP nodes were measurably perturbed in the same file.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The engaged G-protein and adenylyl-cyclase perturbations were themselves transcriptionally sparse, so the contrast should not be read as a complete pathway epistasis map.

summary: The only sizable Drd4 signature-neighbor structure was confined to 308 CB GABA and was confounded by correlations to safe-target controls.
why_it_matters: Top neighbors such as Cckar or Wdr26 should not be promoted to DRD4 effectors without validation, because the same correlation axis also captured negative controls.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: This finding is based on score-vector correlations, not FDR-significant Drd4 genes; safe-target correlations make a technical or state-composition axis plausible.

summary: A null Drd4 Perturb-seq signature should not be interpreted as negative evidence against acute D4 receptor pharmacology, D2-D4 heteromer biology, or human DRD4 polymorphism biology.
why_it_matters: DRD4 is a ligand-activated GPCR with documented Gi/cAMP signaling, heteromerization, and drug mechanisms; this screen primarily reports a failure to lower a lowly expressed receptor transcript in these mouse cell classes.
main_caveats: The literature is largely human or heterologous-cell pharmacology, whereas the dataset is mouse single-cell transcriptomics after genetic perturbation.

summary: Across the measured target rows, Gclc CRISPRi produced no FDR-supported depletion of Gclc mRNA and only one FDR-supported downstream DE gene in the entire screen slice.
why_it_matters: The dominant biological readout is therefore an engagement-limited null result rather than a robust glutathione-depletion state.
main_caveats: Transcript loss is inferred from scRNA-seq target rows only; protein, glutathione, and guide-level estimates were not available.

summary: The only FDR-significant Gclc response was Zfp512b down-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: This localizes the sole multiple-testing-robust transcriptomic response but also shows that the effect did not manifest as a broad glutathione or oxidative-stress program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Single-gene signal from 44 perturbed cells; no direct Zfp512b-Gclc literature link established here.

summary: Transcripts in a glutathione, NRF-family, thioredoxin, and ROS-buffering panel were not coordinately remodeled after Gclc targeting.
why_it_matters: For an enzyme expected to sit at the first, rate-limiting step in glutathione synthesis, the Perturb-seq response is transcriptionally uncoupled from the canonical redox circuit.
main_caveats: A weak perturbation may not have lowered GCLC protein or glutathione enough to recruit NRF-family compensation.

summary: Gclc signatures were nearly orthogonal to Gclm, Gpx4, Nfe2l2, Prdx1, Sod2, and Fth1 signatures in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: Even within the antioxidant and glutathione network, acute single-gene perturbations in this dataset should not be treated as interchangeable phenocopies of Gclc loss.
main_caveats: The contrast is weakened by poor Gclc and Gclm target-transcript knockdown and by transcriptome-only endpoint comparisons.

summary: The sparse Gclc Perturb-seq phenotype should not be interpreted as evidence that neuronal GSH synthesis is dispensable or safe to inhibit.
why_it_matters: Mouse CNS deletions and human GCL deficiency implicate this pathway in neurodegeneration, whereas BSO-like inhibition is pursued to deplete glutathione in cancer cells; the brain dataset instead indicates that this specific perturbation did not create a strong loss-of-function transcriptomic state.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks drug treatment, oxidative injury, aging, and metabolite measurements, so the clinical warning is direction-of-effect reasoning rather than a direct therapeutic test.

summary: The exploratory top restricted-signature neighbors of the 066 signal were not glutathione-complex or NRF2-pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues against a missed coherent redox-neighbor attractor immediately around the only FDR-supported Gclc cell type.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on only the 100 highest-absolute-score Gclc genes in one cell type and are hypothesis-generating.

summary: Htr1b produced a dataset-wide transcriptional null: no gene reached 5% FDR in any of the 22 assayed Htr1b cell classes.
why_it_matters: Isolated nominal genes such as Gpr153 or Dph6 should not be interpreted as a reproducible Htr1b program without follow-up, because the corrected signal never rises above the experiment-wide noise floor.
main_caveats: The null combines biology with assay limitations: several cell classes have few perturbed cells and the target transcript itself was not significantly depleted.

summary: The Htr1b guide did not give statistically secure on-target Htr1b mRNA loss in any cell class.
why_it_matters: The broad absence of downstream DE is therefore not a clean test of cellular Htr1b loss of function; it may reflect ineffective knockdown, low baseline Htr1b mRNA, or expression in cellular compartments not well sampled by the DE contrast.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only DE summary rows were available; raw counts and baseline Htr1b expression were not available to distinguish absent expression from failed repression.

summary: Htr1b did not transcriptionally converge with other assayed serotonin receptors or assayed Gi/o transducer neighbors.
why_it_matters: Reactome and UniProt put HTR1B in serotonin-receptor and Gi/o signaling biology, but the screen did not recover a shared Htr-family or Gi/o perturbation state; receptor paralogs and pathway neighbors therefore should not be treated as interchangeable in this readout.
main_caveats: The contrast is itself signature-based and most serotonin-receptor perturbations also lacked target-transcript FDR, so it cannot prove that the proteins have unrelated signaling.

summary: Even strongly engaged Gnao1 and Gnb1 perturbations were target-only at 5% FDR in the relevant cell classes.
why_it_matters: Because HTR1B is annotated as a Gi/Go-coupled receptor, the lack of broad downstream DE after knockdown of core G-protein subunits supports the idea that this GPCR module is buffered at the steady-state mRNA level in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Gnao1 and Gnb1 are ubiquitous transducers rather than the receptor itself, and only five engaged target-cell contexts support the target-only pattern.

summary: The Perturb-seq null fits a model in which 5-HT1B biology is dominated by presynaptic, projection-defined, and behavioral circuit effects rather than a large cell-autonomous steady-state RNA program.
why_it_matters: Published Htr1b phenotypes involve autoreceptor and heteroreceptor control of neurotransmitter release and circuit-specific aggression or impulsivity; a soma transcriptome screen can miss terminal release effects and developmental circuit outcomes even when the receptor is biologically important.
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure neurotransmitter release, projections, behavior, or developmental timing, so the proposed explanation is inferential.

summary: The Htr1b DE null should not be used to deprioritize acute HTR1B agonist pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Human HTR1B is druggable and clinically precedent agonist mechanisms exist, whereas the dataset perturbs the mouse transcript and reads out steady-state single-cell RNA; the disease-relevant triptan axis need not create a persistent knockdown-like transcriptional signature.
main_caveats: This warning does not validate HTR1B for all neuropsychiatric indications; it only prevents over-reading a weakly engaged transcriptomic null as negative pharmacology.

summary: Foxn1 perturbation was transcriptionally silent across the assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is off-context or unavailable target biology rather than a coherent neuronal Foxn1 program: no brain cell type had an FDR-detectable response, and the target transcript itself was not measurably reduced.
main_caveats: A null differential-expression signature cannot distinguish complete buffering from absent basal Foxn1 expression or ineffective guide activity; matched perturbed counts were modest.

summary: The largest nominal Foxn1 rows were isolated cell-type events rather than recurring biomarkers.
why_it_matters: Mta2, Sar1b, Zdhhc17, Rnf121, Shisa9, Vps33b, Echs1, and Cope are useful as a false-discovery audit but should not be promoted to Foxn1 effectors because every row failed FDR control and occurred in only one nominal context.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|308 CB GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: These are exploratory nominal rows with FDR 0.31-0.89 and cell counts of 37-140; they are not validated DE genes.

summary: The canonical FOXN1 thymic epithelial target program was not mobilized by Foxn1 perturbation in brain cells.
why_it_matters: Known FOXN1-dependent TEC and T-cell-support genes such as Dll4, Ccl25, Ctsl, Cd40, Pax1, MHC-II genes, Psmb11, and Kitl did not respond, indicating that the neuronal dataset is uncoupled from the epithelial FOXN1 gene-regulatory circuitry described in thymus.
main_caveats: Many canonical TEC genes have low or sporadic brain expression, so absence of their response is expected and should not be treated as a thymic Foxn1 loss-of-function benchmark.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a robust Foxn1-like module or an interpretable anti-Foxn1 module.
why_it_matters: Because Foxn-family paralogs were not perturbed and the strongest non-self correlations were very small, the dataset does not support a cross-perturbation convergence or divergence claim for Foxn1.
main_caveats: The neighbor calculation used non-significant top Foxn1 rows and should only be read as a guard against overclaiming, not as evidence of a real network.

summary: Dnajc19 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response across the 22 assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: DNAJC19 is a mitochondrial import and cardiomyopathy gene, so a zero-FDR result means this dataset should not be read as a loss-of-function neuronal response atlas for Dnajc19.
main_caveats: The negative call is statistically strong for the provided DE output but is confounded by weak measured Dnajc19 target depletion and several low-count contrasts.

summary: The only nominal target-transcript decreases, in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, were not followed by any FDR-level downstream program.
why_it_matters: If these two nominal decreases reflect real partial loss, midbrain glutamatergic and brainstem/hindbrain GABAergic neurons transcriptionally buffer modest Dnajc19 depletion; if not, they mark the ceiling of target engagement in this dataset.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Both own-gene p values were only nominal and remained FDR=1.0; the assay measured RNA abundance rather than mitochondrial import, cardiolipin, or cristae phenotypes.

summary: Dnajc19 had no recurrent nominal response gene and no stable positive or negative whole-library signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The apparent top genes are isolated single-cell-class events rather than a shared Dnajc19 stress or mitochondrial module.
main_caveats: This is calculated from transcriptomic rank signatures; a non-transcriptional mitochondrial phenotype could be missed.

summary: Dnajc19 signatures were nearly orthogonal to available mitochondrial import, chaperone, and metabolic perturbations.
why_it_matters: Documented TIM23-PAM biology would motivate comparison to Hspa9 and TOM/import neighbors, yet the observed Dnajc19 signatures did not converge with Hspa9, Hspd1, Tomm40, Ndufa13, Ndufs8, Got2, Lrpprc, Aco2, or Abcb7 signatures.
main_caveats: Many direct TIM23-PAM partners were absent from the perturbation library, Dnajc19 itself was weakly engaged, and Hspa9 lacked FDR-level Hspa9 mRNA knockdown.

summary: The mouse neuronal RNA result refines DCMA interpretation toward severe or post-transcriptional mitochondrial phenotypes rather than an acute shared neuronal RNA module after partial Dnajc19 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Human DNAJC19 loss affects mitochondrial import, cardiolipin/cristae biology, and cardiomyocytes; the brain Perturb-seq negative result suggests those disease processes are not captured by this partial guide perturbation in neuronal transcriptomes.
main_caveats: Species, cell type, developmental context, perturbation strength, and assay modality differ from human cardiomyocyte and patient studies.

summary: There is no dataset support for direct Dnajc19 inhibition as a beneficial brain-neuron direction, and human genetics makes loss of DNAJC19 a mitochondrial disease mechanism.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL did not return a curated Q96DA6 target entry, and a loss-of-function disease gene with no favorable knockdown signature should be approached as a rescue or replacement target rather than as an inhibition target.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay was not a therapeutic screen; the ChEMBL result is absence of a curated target record, not proof that DNAJC19 is undruggable.

direction: strongest in 191 MB P MY GABA; isolated Miga2 induction in 308 CB GABA; minimal elsewhere
summary: Ddx39b produced a multi-gene FDR-resolved program almost exclusively in 191 MB P MY GABA, with only a single additional FDR<0.05 gene in 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: This makes cell identity the dominant axis of the observed Ddx39b response and prevents overinterpreting the perturbation as a pan-neuronal RNA-export phenotype.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The strongest class still had only 26 perturbed cells, and the Ddx39b transcript itself was not FDR-significantly reduced.

summary: The 191 MB P MY GABA Ddx39b signature converged on a THO/TREX and nuclear RNA-processing neighbor module headed by Thoc1.
why_it_matters: A top-ranked Thoc1 neighbor anchors the Ddx39b phenotype in the known mRNA export machinery rather than in an arbitrary stress signature.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The convergence is correlation-based and restricted to the Perturb-seq signature; proteasome subunits among the top neighbors indicate that some shared signal may reflect general essential-gene stress.

direction: nominal target-transcript decrease with absent FDR-level downstream response in most classes
summary: Most Ddx39b comparisons showed weak partial target knockdown with no corrected downstream response.
why_it_matters: UAP56 is a core RNA-splicing/export factor, so the many null cell types are more plausibly buffered, underpowered, or under-engaged than truly independent of Ddx39b.
main_caveats: No protein, splicing, or mRNA-export readout is available, and the own-transcript FDR never reached 0.05.

direction: Thoc1-biased convergence with weak divergence from other RNA-processing factors
summary: Ddx39b in 191 MB P MY GABA was Thoc1-like but not strongly similar to broader spliceosome or nuclear-speckle perturbations such as Rnpc3, Srrm2, or Srsf1.
why_it_matters: The contrast refines a generic RNA-processing interpretation: the Ddx39b response tracks a TREX-coupled state more than it tracks the very large signatures produced by other splicing factors.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only transcriptional consequences were compared; the library lacked several direct TREX partners such as Alyref and Nxf1.

direction: selective TREX-like sensitivity under partial Ddx39b perturbation
summary: The mouse-brain Ddx39b profile points to a selective TREX-sensitive neuronal context relevant to, but weaker than, known THOC2 and THOC6 neurodevelopmental disease mechanisms.
why_it_matters: TREX perturbations can cause neurodevelopmental phenotypes, so the MB P/MY GABA Ddx39b-Thoc1 convergence nominates a follow-up cell state while warning against broad disease extrapolation from a weak knockdown.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The disease literature cited concerns THOC2 and THOC6 rather than DDX39B itself, and the Perturb-seq assay measured acute transcript levels rather than development.

summary: Ndufc2 perturbation produced real target-mRNA depletion in a restricted subset of the assayed neuronal classes, with the strongest corrected losses in midbrain, hypothalamic, thalamic, Pvalb, CNU-MGE, CNU-HYa, and piriform/olfactory L2/3 IT groups.
why_it_matters: The direct knockdown validates interpretation of downstream silence in the eight FDR-significant classes, while the remaining 15 classes should not be treated as equivalent knockdowns.

main_caveats: The screen reports mRNA-level perturbation and not NDUFC2 protein, Complex I abundance, or respiratory flux; several non-significant classes still showed negative nominal Ndufc2 scores.

summary: FDR-significant Ndufc2 loss was almost decoupled from a nuclear mitochondrial-stress program: only one non-target gene reached FDR<0.05 anywhere, and curated ATF4/ISR, mitochondrial proteostasis, mitophagy, biogenesis, and glycolysis markers were all FDR-negative.
why_it_matters: NDUFC2 is a Complex I assembly-linked subunit whose genetic loss can cause severe OXPHOS disease, so a transcriptionally sparse response in successfully perturbed neurons implies buffering, slow protein turnover, or assay timing rather than a canonical acute mitochondrial stress burst.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant stress transcripts does not prove normal respiration; the dataset lacks protein stability, Complex I assembly, ATP, ROS, and time-course measurements.

summary: Pdcd6ip was the only FDR-significant secondary gene and was induced only in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
why_it_matters: This makes Pdcd6ip a narrow, hypothesis-generating sentinel for the one neuronal class in which Ndufc2 knockdown was not purely restricted to the target transcript.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene, single-cell-class signal with no recurrence across the other 22 Ndufc2 contexts; no pathway-level inference was made.

summary: Sparse downstream transcription was shared across many Complex I perturbations rather than unique to Ndufc2.
why_it_matters: The comparison argues that in this assay, loss of mRNAs encoding Complex I components often remains a direct-target event instead of converging on a common nuclear OXPHOS-stress signature.
main_caveats: The aggregate includes genes with variable guide performance and cell coverage; it compares transcriptomes, not Complex I assembly or enzymatic activity.

summary: Ndufc2 had no strong positive or negative all-gene signature neighbor among the other perturbations.
why_it_matters: The lack of a robust transcriptome-wide neighbor prevented an unsupported mechanistic assignment from a weak correlation to an unrelated target.
main_caveats: Score correlations are insensitive to small cell-class-specific hits and are affected by the mostly flat Ndufc2 signatures.

direction: weak target-transcript decrease; no downstream FDR signal
summary: Diaph2 targeting produced no measurable Diaph2 mRNA knockdown and no FDR-significant transcriptional response in either recovered glutamatergic stratum.
why_it_matters: The experiment should be read primarily as a weak-engagement negative test; nominal downstream genes are not sufficient to define a Diaph2 loss-of-function program without validation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The table measures RNA, not guide editing or protein depletion, and both Diaph2 strata had the minimum perturbation cell count within their cell type.

direction: Agtpbp1 up and Map1b down, nominal only
summary: Agtpbp1 was the only high-rank nominal gene reproducibly induced by Diaph2 perturbation, with Map1b nominally decreased in both cell types, suggesting a possible but unconfirmed microtubule-linked residual signal.
why_it_matters: mDia3/Diaph2 proteins are cytoskeletal formins with microtubule roles, and AGTPBP1/CCP1 is a neuronal tubulin deglutamylase; therefore recurrent Agtpbp1 up-regulation is a biologically plausible follow-up marker despite weak statistics.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Both genes missed FDR correction; the global Diaph2 signatures were nearly uncorrelated between cell types, and no source establishes a direct Diaph2-to-Agtpbp1 regulatory edge.

summary: Diaph2 signatures were essentially orthogonal to same-cell perturbations of Rho/Cdc42, other formins, actin-family targets, Arhgap/Arhgef regulators and Mrtfa.
why_it_matters: Because DIAPH2/mDia3 is a RHO-family diaphanous-related formin, the absence of a correlated actin/SRF or Rho-formin transcriptome argues that this dataset did not capture a canonical RHO→formin pathway state for Diaph2.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Near-zero correlations may reflect the underpowered, weakly engaged Diaph2 signatures rather than true biochemical independence from RHO/formin signaling.

summary: Whole-genome signature-neighbor searches did not identify a robust positive or inverse Diaph2-like perturbation.
why_it_matters: The computed nearest neighbors had Pearson correlations close to zero, so the Diaph2 profile is too weak or idiosyncratic for convergence analysis against the full Perturb-seq library.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The correlation screen is limited to perturbations present in the same two cell types and was run on noisy Diaph2 signatures with no FDR-significant genes.

summary: Diaph2 was represented only in two of the 23 assayed cell-type strata, and both were glutamatergic thalamic/midbrain populations with bottom-ranked Diaph2 cell counts.
why_it_matters: The apparent restriction should be treated as a recovery and power constraint, not as evidence that Diaph2 biology is limited to these two neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: A missing cell-type signature can arise from guide recovery or filtering; the parquet does not show whether Diaph2 was unexpressed, uninfected or simply below cell-count thresholds in the other classes.

summary: Fkbp1a knockdown was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, with additional large nominal target depletion in 155 MB Glut and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA rather than uniform engagement across all 23 cell classes.
why_it_matters: This constrains interpretation of every downstream Fkbp1a signature to the few cell classes where the target transcript was detectably reduced.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Large nominal effects in 155 MB Glut and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA did not pass FDR correction.

summary: Even when Fkbp1a itself was depleted, the perturbation had no adjusted off-target transcriptional response in any measured cell class.
why_it_matters: A null downstream RNA phenotype is the central outcome: it prevents assignment of a confident FKBP12-regulated transcriptional module and suggests that partial FKBP12 loss is buffered or post-transcriptional in these brain contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset is RNA-only; FKBP12 effects on receptors or calcium channels could be post-translational and invisible to this assay.

summary: Fkbp1a depletion did not converge with calcineurin-pathway perturbations, even in a cell class where Ppp3ca, Ppp3r1, and Calm1 were robustly depleted and produced adjusted downstream genes.
why_it_matters: It separates loss of FKBP12 protein from the FKBP12-FK506 drug complex that inhibits calcineurin, limiting any interpretation that Fkbp1a CRISPRi is equivalent to calcineurin-inhibitor treatment.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Correlation used each Fkbp1a signature's top 200 nominal off-target genes; calmodulins control many processes beyond calcineurin.

summary: Fkbp1a CRISPRi was not rapamycin-like: mTOR-family neighbor signatures correlated only weakly with Fkbp1a, and Fkbp1a knockdown did not significantly change Mtor, Rptor, TSC, calcineurin, TGF-beta receptor, RyR, IP3R, or calmodulin transcript rows after correction.
why_it_matters: Approved rapalogs require FKBP12 as an adapter to inhibit mTOR; partial FKBP12 depletion should not be interpreted as mTORC1 inhibition in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Mtor and TSC guide groups are pathway-neighbor signatures, not a pharmacologic rapamycin exposure; some TSC rows had weak target-transcript engagement.

summary: The top restricted positive and negative Fkbp1a signature neighbors were weak and biologically incoherent, including safe-target controls among near-neighbors.
why_it_matters: This keeps the analysis from over-promoting a nominal gene or unrelated perturbation as a convergent FKBP12 module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The neighbor scan used nominal, non-FDR genes; safe-target controls among near-neighbors argue that these associations are not mechanistic.

summary: Il12b guides produced no measurable Il12b transcript depletion in any profiled neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The primary assay readout gives no evidence that the perturbation engaged an expressed target transcript; this makes downstream null effects biologically plausible rather than surprising.
cell_types: 22 Il12b-profiled glutamatergic/GABAergic neuronal classes
main_caveats: Transcript engagement can only be measured for expressed scRNA-seq features; CRISPR editing of a silent locus may still occur without generating an mRNA phenotype.

summary: Il12b perturbation was globally buffered: no gene reached FDR<0.05 among 371,818 tests.
why_it_matters: The absence of any corrected transcriptional response argues against a robust cell-autonomous IL-12/IL-23 program in these glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes.
cell_types: 22 Il12b-profiled glutamatergic/GABAergic neuronal classes
main_caveats: Many cell types had fewer than 100 perturbed cells, so small effects or protein/secreted-cytokine phenotypes could be missed.

summary: Il12b did not phenocopy the cognate IL-12/IL-23 receptor perturbations or nearby JAK/STAT and NF-kB pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: IL12B and IL12RB1 form a shared physical interface in both IL-12 and IL-23, but that expected pathway relationship was not visible as correlated neuronal Perturb-seq signatures.
cell_types: matched neuronal classes
main_caveats: Comparisons use weak restricted signatures; the receptor perturbations themselves also lacked strong on-target transcript depletion.

summary: The neuronal null result should not be read as weakening the immune rationale for anti-p40 therapy.
why_it_matters: IL12B is a clinically drugged p40 cytokine subunit in psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease; the mouse dataset instead tests sparse neuronal Il12b guides and therefore mainly suggests that p40 blockade is unlikely to act by lowering neuron-intrinsic Il12b transcription in these classes.
cell_types: 22 Il12b-profiled glutamatergic/GABAergic neuronal classes
main_caveats: The experiment used mouse neuronal transcriptomes, not activated dendritic cells, macrophages, T cells, or clinical anti-p40 blockade.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor scan found no hidden Il12b-like convergent or opposing module.
why_it_matters: The strongest all-perturbation correlations with Il12b were very small, so neither the positive nor negative nearest neighbors rescue an interpretable pathway from the nominal gene list.
cell_types: matched neuronal classes
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from Wilcoxon-score signatures and can miss nonlinear or post-transcriptional relationships.

summary: The few largest nominal genes were cell-type-private exploratory markers rather than recurrent Il12b biomarkers.
why_it_matters: Csde1/Rspo2 in MEA-LA-CA1-DG glutamatergic neurons and Mbtd1/Gabra1 in L5-6 IT neurons are the only visible local peaks, but their effects did not survive FDR correction and p<0.001 hits did not recur across cell types.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: Nominal p values were not FDR significant; 001 L5-6 IT had only 35 perturbed cells.

summary: Pax2 perturbation produced an FDR-null transcriptome across all 23 sampled neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: For a nuclear developmental transcription factor, the assayed adult brain populations looked buffered or unengaged rather than showing a broad acute PAX2 program.
main_caveats: High confidence for the statistical null in this dataset, but it does not prove Pax2 dispensability because target-transcript depletion was not observed.

summary: No cell type showed measurable reduction of the Pax2 transcript itself.
why_it_matters: The target row converts every downstream null result into a weak-engagement result: the dataset cannot distinguish biological buffering from guide inactivity, low basal Pax2 expression, or failure of transcript-level knockdown.
main_caveats: mRNA self-DE is an imperfect proxy for genome editing or protein perturbation, and extreme logFC values for near-undetected transcripts should not be overinterpreted.

summary: The only near-discovery Pax2 response was an exploratory L2/3 IT cortical Pdia6 decrease, accompanied by weaker nominal Bmp1 and growth-factor-adjacent genes.
why_it_matters: If follow-up editing validates Pax2 engagement, Pdia6 would be the first transcript to check; in the present data it remains below the FDR 0.05 threshold and lacks recurrence.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Single cell-type, single-gene near-hit; Pdia6 FDR was 0.0566 rather than <0.05, all other genes were weaker, and the signature had no strong positive neighbor.

summary: Adult GABAergic classes, including broad cerebellar and hindbrain classes closest to known Pax2-positive inhibitory lineages, were FDR-null.
why_it_matters: Pax2 marks developing cerebellar GABAergic interneurons and Pax2/Pax8 specify inhibitory fates in spinal interneurons; the dataset indicates that those developmental dependencies are not recapitulated by acute Pax2 perturbation in the sampled adult inhibitory populations.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The literature is developmental and often spinal or cerebellar, whereas the dataset uses broad adult classes and lacks a measurable Pax2 mRNA knockdown.

summary: Pax2 did not converge with the related Pax5 or Pax8 perturbations despite known PAX2/5/8 developmental cooperation and redundancy.
why_it_matters: The data argue against treating PAX-family developmental interchangeability as an acute adult-brain transcriptomic module in these cell types.
main_caveats: All three PAX perturbations are weak or null, so the contrast detects absence of convergence rather than opposing biology.

summary: Perturbations of assayed PAX2 developmental-neighborhood genes En1, Lmx1b, Otx2, Six1, and Wt1 were also FDR-null.
why_it_matters: The Pax2 null sits inside a broader silence of embryonic patterning and kidney/eye developmental regulators, suggesting that the adult neuronal assay is uncoupled from PAX2's canonical developmental network.
main_caveats: STRING edges are mostly compiled from heterogeneous human evidence; several STRING partners were not perturbed, and the null may reflect lack of expression or target engagement.

summary: The adult-brain Pax2 signatures do not model the renal-coloboma or FSGS disease direction that dominates human PAX2 genetics.
why_it_matters: PAX2 is a kidney/eye/CNS developmental transcription factor with genetic renal disease links but no obvious small-molecule or modality tractability; these weak adult neuronal signatures should not be used to infer a therapeutically useful CNS direction.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay did not sample kidney, eye, embryonic organizers, or validated PAX2_LOF tissue contexts.

summary: Las1l perturbation is globally FDR-null across assayed neuronal classes despite weak nominal reduction of the target transcript.
why_it_matters: A known ribosome-biogenesis factor did not generate the broad mRNA destabilization or stress signature expected from severe LAS1L loss, so the Perturb-seq result is best interpreted as buffered or under-engaged rather than as an active 60S-biogenesis phenotype.
main_caveats: Target-transcript depletion was nominal and FDR=1 in every cell type; several cell-type bins had fewer than 45 perturbed cells, so absence of FDR-significant genes cannot prove full biological buffering.

summary: The largest Las1l nominal tails are isolated to individual cell types and do not recur as the same gene module.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Otud4, Zdhhc1, Rnf150, and Csnk2a1 are tempting cell-type markers, but the adjusted p values and recurrence analysis argue that they should remain hypothesis-generating rather than LAS1L biomarkers.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|053 Sst Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: No listed gene passed FDR<0.1; Otud4 came from the lowest-cell-count Las1l group with only 27 perturbed cells.

summary: Las1l knockdown did not transcriptionally co-move measured LAS1L-NOL9, Rix1/5FMC, or MLL1-complex components.
why_it_matters: The expected LAS1L network is a nucleolar pre-rRNA-processing assembly; its lack of coordinated polyadenylated mRNA changes suggests that this assay did not read out direct ribosomal-precursor processing or that residual LAS1L activity was sufficient.
main_caveats: Complex proteins can change localization, modification, pre-rRNA processing, or rRNA cleavage without changing their own polyadenylated mRNAs; five core partners were absent as perturbation targets.

summary: Las1l is not Kmt2a-like in matched cell types even though LAS1L is annotated in MLL1/5FMC-associated assemblies.
why_it_matters: Kmt2a knockdown produced FDR-significant transcriptional remodeling, whereas Las1l remained null and same-cell Las1l-Kmt2a correlations were near zero, separating the LAS1L result from a canonical KMT2A chromatin-loss state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: KMT2A is a broad chromatin regulator and not a direct LAS1L-NOL9 catalytic partner, so divergence does not contradict the physical-complex literature.

summary: A same-cell signature-neighbor search found no robust positive or negative Las1l neighbor.
why_it_matters: The null is stronger than any individual nominal hit: if Las1l had engaged a shared toxicity, stress, or receptor pathway, another perturbation would be expected to show a coherent correlated signature, but the strongest absolute Pearson correlation was only 0.186.
main_caveats: The Las1l signature itself was weak, so low correlations partly reflect limited signal-to-noise rather than definitive pathway isolation.

summary: LAS1L neurodevelopmental disease links are not mirrored by an acute postmitotic-neuron mRNA program in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Disease alleles causing Wilson-Turner or SMARD-like syndromes may act through developmental, proliferative, motor-unit, or pre-rRNA/ribosomal readouts that are poorly captured by this partial poly(A) Perturb-seq endpoint.
main_caveats: The experiment did not model inherited missense or splicing alleles, development, motor neurons specifically, organismal lethality, or rRNA processing.

summary: FDR-significant Atrn knockdown in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut produced no FDR-significant gene other than Atrn itself.
why_it_matters: Strong target engagement without a broad downstream mRNA program points away from an acute transcription-factor-like mechanism and toward post-transcriptional or longer-timescale ATRN functions.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was measured; downstream protein trafficking or delayed degeneration could be missed.

summary: Cnnm2 up-regulation is the only FDR-significant non-target event after Atrn perturbation and is restricted to 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: A single cerebellar signal could mark a cell-type-specific ATRN response that would be invisible in pooled analysis, but it requires validation because target engagement was only nominal.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only 29 Atrn-perturbed cells; Atrn target row FDR was 1.0 in this cell type; no second non-target gene passed FDR.

summary: Atrn perturbation did not induce a recurrent FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic module across the 20 assayed neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: The absence of a repeated mRNA signature is itself informative for a broadly expressed membrane glycoprotein with neurodegenerative loss phenotypes.
main_caveats: The assayed panel lacked glial labels and the result is transcriptome-only.

summary: The literature melanocortin/Agouti neighborhood was not represented by engaged perturbations around Atrn in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Direct comparison to a canonical ATRN pathway is limited: Mgrn1, Atrnl1, and Agouti were not targeted, and Agrp/Mc receptor perturbations were present but unengaged.
main_caveats: This is a coverage and target-engagement result, not a contradiction of the melanocortin literature.

summary: The mouse-brain Perturb-seq data refine whole-animal Atrn hypomyelination and spongiform phenotypes by showing that assayed neuronal Atrn knockdown is largely transcriptionally silent.
why_it_matters: Classic Atrn pathology may require glia, cell-cell interactions, protein trafficking, or age-dependent stress rather than an immediate neuron-autonomous mRNA cascade.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The screen did not assay labeled oligodendrocytes, OPCs, astrocytes, or microglia and does not address chronic organismal phenotypes.

summary: Atrn's strongest positive and negative signature neighbors were confined to 308 CB GABA and included Ranbp2/Fbxo11/Dnajb4 versus Wdr26/Cckar/Msx2 rather than known ATRN partners.
why_it_matters: The finding prevents over-reading scalar signature similarity as an ATRN complex; it nominates a cerebellar state for follow-up while flagging weak neighbor target engagement.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Computed from restricted transcriptome signatures in one low-cell-count cell type; several neighbor target transcripts were not FDR-engaged.

summary: Chrna3 perturbation was globally transcriptionally silent at FDR control in the measured mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: Chrna3 encodes an ion-channel subunit, but this Perturb-seq target should not be interpreted as producing a validated loss-of-function state because neither downstream genes nor the target transcript itself passed FDR.
main_caveats: A CRISPR edit can change protein function without reducing mRNA; FDR-negative does not prove absence of electrophysiologic change.

summary: The only apparent Chrna3 cell-type preference was a weak nominal tail in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, with smaller nominal tails in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: The scalar minimum highlights where any follow-up would start, but the lack of FDR support makes Sybu, Aifm3/Inpp5f/Adam22/Virma, and Mtf2/Kansl2 exploratory markers rather than a reproducible module.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA

summary: The dataset does not effectively test the Chrna3-rich habenulo-interpeduncular nicotine-aversion circuit.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse work places alpha3/beta4 nAChRs in the medial habenula-interpeduncular pathway, but the closest coarse MH-LH/thalamic glutamatergic Chrna3 stratum had only 25 perturbed cells and no detectable target engagement.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The label is broader than medial habenula, and no raw anatomical metadata were available to select MHb-IPN neurons directly.

summary: Chrna3 failed to phenocopy engaged cholinergic perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Chrnb2, Chrna4, and Ache each produced an FDR-significant on-target response in the same thalamic glutamatergic class, so the Chrna3 null result is target-specific rather than evidence that all cholinergic perturbations were invisible in that cell type.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Chrna4/beta2 and alpha3/beta2/beta4 receptors are related nAChRs but are not obligate members of one identical pentamer.

summary: Exploratory restricted-signature correlations did not show nAChR-complex convergence around Chrna3.
why_it_matters: Although curated resources connect Chrna3 to beta and accessory subunits, top-300-gene Chrna3 vectors were weakly correlated or anti-correlated with Chrnb2, Chrnb4, Chrna4, and Chrna1 in the nominally strongest contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

summary: Known CHRNA3 disease genetics and druggable receptor biology are not directionally resolved by this perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: CHRNA3 sits in a nicotine-dependence/smoking locus and loss-of-function human alleles can cause autonomic and urinary disease, but the Perturb-seq readout provides no support for choosing alpha3 agonism versus antagonism or for nominating a transcriptional biomarker.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain, not human urinary/autonomic tissue or a nicotine-exposure assay.

direction: target transcript mostly down; no downstream FDR-significant response
summary: The Lgr4 perturbation produced a globally buffered transcriptomic response across the 21 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant dataset-grounded interpretation: subsequent Lgr4 claims should be treated as weak or context restricted because neither the target transcript nor any downstream gene reached FDR significance.
main_caveats: The negative result is conditioned on small perturbed-cell counts and weak mRNA engagement; it does not rule out protein-level, developmental, or ligand-dependent Lgr4 biology.

summary: 308 CB GABA showed the strongest nominal Lgr4 mRNA reduction but still lacked a corrected downstream program.
why_it_matters: The cerebellar trace is biologically plausible given prior Purkinje-cell work, yet this Perturb-seq readout detects only nominal target engagement rather than a robust cerebellar transcriptional phenotype.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Nominal p=0.00196 for Lgr4 itself still had FDR=1.0; 308 CB GABA is a broad class and the dataset does not identify Purkinje cells directly.

summary: The expected RSPO/LGR4 canonical Wnt module was not coherently induced or suppressed after Lgr4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: LGR4 is a plasma-membrane RSPO receptor that potentiates Frizzled/LRP-dependent Wnt signaling, so the absence of corrected Wnt-component or Axin2/Ctnnb1 responses argues that mature brain cell classes were not in a ligand-competent Lgr4-Wnt state under this assay.
main_caveats: Only transcript-level pathway components were assayed; weak Lgr4 knockdown can hide a true Wnt effect.

summary: Lgr4 signatures did not converge with available perturbations of Frizzled receptors, Lrp5/6, Ctnnb1, or Apc.
why_it_matters: The near-zero same-cell correlations separate Lgr4 from direct Wnt-receptor and beta-catenin/APC perturbations despite strong prior evidence that LGR4 participates in this receptor complex.
main_caveats: The closest paralogs and RSPO/ZNRF3/RNF43 module members were not perturbation targets; correlations are signature-level contrasts and do not prove receptor inactivity.

summary: Broad hypothalamic and thalamic classes did not recapitulate the developmental LGR4-Wnt-GnRH delayed-puberty mechanism.
why_it_matters: Human and animal work links LGR4 deficiency to embryonic GnRH neuron formation and migration, whereas this dataset suggests that the disease mechanism is not reproduced as a broad mouse-brain transcriptomic Wnt response.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: GnRH neurons are rare developmental cells and may be absent from these broad classes; 151 TH had only a nominal Lgr4 decrease with FDR=1.0.

summary: Lgr4/RSPO3-LGR4 druggability does not make broad neuronal Wnt transcripts good pharmacodynamic markers in this dataset.
why_it_matters: An RSPO3-LGR4 inhibitory antibody exists in drug databases, but this perturbation indicates that brain-cell Wnt marker panels would be insensitive unless the assayed cells are receptor-engaged and downstream-competent.
main_caveats: No therapeutic compound was applied, and rosmantuzumab targets the ligand interface rather than perturbing mouse Lgr4 exactly as in this screen.

direction: up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA for the two leading hits

why_it_matters: The strongest phenotype is restricted to a CNU/MGE inhibitory class rather than being broadly shared across cortical glutamatergic, Pvalb, or Sst classes that might have been expected from Htr2a cortical literature.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only two genes passed 10% FDR; 054 CNU-MGE GABA had 62 perturbed cells.

direction: Kcnma1 and several GABA/ion-channel genes up, with selected synaptic and channel genes down

why_it_matters: A calcium-activated potassium-channel hit links the GPCR perturbation to an electrophysiology-testable inhibitory-neuron excitability phenotype.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only Kcnma1 was significant at 5% FDR; the broader module is nominal and hypothesis-generating.

direction: opposing for Htr2b; weakly aligned to neutral for Htr2c
summary: Htr2b was anti-correlated with Htr2a in the Htr2a-responsive CNU-MGE class, while Htr2c was near-neutral.

cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Restricted-signature correlation; Htr2b and Htr2c had only 39 perturbed cells in this class.

summary: Receptor-neighbor perturbations split into Htr2a-like and Htr2a-opposed directions in 054 CNU-MGE GABA rather than clustering by broad GPCR or Gq/PLC identity.
why_it_matters: The chronic transcriptional output appears to depend on receptor identity and cell context, so downstream interpretation should not be reduced to a single canonical Gq pathway diagram.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA

summary: The Htr2a transcript itself was not FDR-depleted in any assayed cell class, including the Pvalb class with the strongest nominal self decrease.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not provide a strong measured target-engagement gradient, which limits causal ranking of cell classes by Htr2a knockdown efficacy.
main_caveats: The DE table measures transcript abundance, not guide editing efficiency, receptor protein, or signaling output.

summary: A restricted chronic mouse CNU/MGE signature should not be mapped directly onto approved 5-HT2A antagonist pharmacology or acute psychedelic agonism.
why_it_matters: HTR2A is a psychiatric drug target, but the Perturb-seq result emphasizes cell-state selectivity and weak cortical FDR support, so translational direction requires pharmacologic and circuit validation.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Mouse genetic knockdown, single time point, single-cell mRNA readout, and small Htr2a-positive subclasses do not model acute, dose-dependent human receptor pharmacology.

summary: Significant Mdh2 mRNA repression was usually transcriptionally silent beyond the target transcript.
why_it_matters: MDH2 sits in the mitochondrial TCA cycle and malate-aspartate shuttle, yet three of the four cell types with FDR-significant target depletion had no FDR-significant downstream gene, and the fourth had only one non-target hit.

summary: Tcaf1 up-regulation was a Pvalb-GABA-restricted candidate reporter of Mdh2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb contrast was the only Mdh2 comparison with a non-target FDR<0.05 transcript, making Tcaf1 the only resolved downstream RNA biomarker in this dataset rather than part of a broad stress program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Single cell type and single non-target gene; the dataset does not establish that Tcaf1 is mechanistically linked to MDH2 or mitochondrial metabolism.

summary: Mdh2 knockdown did not transcriptionally induce the assayed malate-aspartate-shuttle, TCA-neighbor, or mitochondrial-stress genes.
why_it_matters: This separates MDH2's core enzymatic pathway membership from the RNA phenotype: surviving perturbed neurons did not compensate by changing Mdh1, Got1/Got2, Slc25a12/Slc25a13, or nearby TCA transcripts at FDR level.
main_caveats: The gene panels were transcript-level readouts; enzyme flux could change without detectable mRNA changes.

summary: Cytosolic Mdh1 and mitochondrial Mdh2 are not transcriptomically interchangeable in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The two MDH isoforms share the malate-aspartate shuttle, but only Mdh1 perturbation produced a multi-gene signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, including Gls up-regulation and Nrxn1/Grin2b down-regulation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to one cell class and may reflect different knockdown depth, protein half-life, or compartment-specific metabolic bottlenecks in addition to paralog biology.

summary: A buffered neuronal RNA signature should not be read as evidence that MDH2 inhibition is neurologically benign.
why_it_matters: Loss-of-function MDH2 variants cause pediatric epileptic encephalopathy, while MDH2 is being explored as a tumor vulnerability; the mouse Perturb-seq data show that transcriptomics alone can miss the relevant metabolic liabilities.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset used partial genetic repression in mouse brain cell types, not a systemic MDH2 inhibitor, biallelic human deficiency, or glioblastoma stem cells.

summary: Signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a strong convergent or opposite perturbation state for Mdh2.
why_it_matters: The largest absolute genome-wide score correlation to any other perturbation was below 0.10 in each robustly engaged Mdh2 cell type, so top neighbors are not a reliable mechanistic anchor for this target.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Score-vector correlations over mostly target-only signatures are a blunt negative test and do not exclude metabolic similarity at the protein or metabolite level.

summary: Ccser1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant differential-expression response in any assayed brain cell class.
why_it_matters: The target was measured in 21 classes, but both on-target depletion and downstream transcriptional changes were weak after correction; strong Ccser1 biology should therefore not be inferred from isolated low nominal p values.
main_caveats: A negative Wilcoxon signature can reflect genuine buffering, weak guide activity, low transcript abundance, or low power; the dataset does not separate these possibilities.

summary: The largest nominal hits were confined to individual cell classes rather than a recurrent Ccser1 module.

summary: Stxbp5l down-regulation is the sharpest candidate marker of a Ccser1-responsive state, but only in CTX-CGE GABA and only at exploratory confidence.
why_it_matters: The Stxbp5l row was the only Ccser1-associated test with FDR below 0.2, making it the most concrete follow-up transcript if the CTX-CGE GABA phenotype is replicated.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: FDR=0.191 is not a discovery-level result; this is a prioritization marker, not a validated biomarker.

summary: The best-powered thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class showed the best nominal on-target depletion yet very little downstream response.

main_caveats: The on-target row did not pass FDR correction; calling this buffering would require validation of Ccser1 knockdown at RNA and protein levels.

summary: Published FAM190A/circFam190a interactor biology did not appear as an HSP90β/AKT1, WWOX, or GRID2-like brain signature.
why_it_matters: The osteoclast AKT1-HSP90β mechanism and the FAM190A mitotic-interactor literature are real external clues, but the assayed brain perturbations nearest those clues were absent or weak and directionally inconsistent.

summary: ASD genetics make CCSER1 biologically plausible in brain, but this Ccser1 Perturb-seq readout did not expose a rare-variant neurodevelopmental network.
why_it_matters: The result separates human inherited loss-of-function risk from the assayed mouse cell-class transcriptome: the experiment is not positive evidence against CCSER1 in ASD, but it provides no strong cell-type module for the genetic association.
main_caveats: The disease literature concerns rare germline human variation during neurodevelopment, whereas the dataset measures guide perturbations in mouse brain cell classes and has weak target engagement.

summary: Therapeutic hypotheses at the Ccser1/Fam190a locus should be isoform- and tissue-specific.
why_it_matters: The only directional therapeutic literature points to circFam190a inhibition for osteoclast-mediated bone loss, while the brain dataset does not show a matching Hsp90ab1/Akt1-like axis and ChEMBL has no curated CCSER1 target pharmacology.
main_caveats: The perturbation was not designed to distinguish linear Ccser1 from circFam190a, and no bone cells were assayed.

direction: Wdr26 same direction; Ranbp2 opposite direction

main_caveats: Wdr26 and Ranbp2 are dataset signature neighbors, not demonstrated DSTYK physical interactors or pathway members.

direction: anti-correlated with Braf/Hras/Mapk1/Kras/Fgf1 and no FDR-grade ERK-output response
summary: The 308 CB GABA Dstyk signature did not phenocopy the expected FGF/RAS/ERK axis and instead anti-correlated with several MAPK-pathway perturbations.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The literature context is kidney/HEK FGF stimulation rather than cerebellar GABA CRISPRi, and several comparator perturbations were weak in 308 CB GABA.

direction: exploratory CB GABA synaptic module under partial Dstyk loss
summary: The weak Dstyk Perturb-seq response should not be interpreted as CNS derisking; human and mouse genetics already implicate DSTYK loss in neurological phenotypes, and 308 CB GABA provides only an exploratory synaptic/ion-channel biomarker hypothesis.
why_it_matters: A small scRNA effect size could still coexist with circuit or stress phenotypes after stronger or chronic DSTYK loss.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The nominated genes are not validated DSTYK pharmacodynamic markers; the dataset did not measure behavior, chronic stress, ERK phosphorylation, or full genetic ablation.

direction: Mapt down in the two FDR-positive cell classes
summary: Robust Mapt target-transcript depletion was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Most downstream interpretation should be anchored in these two cell classes; the remaining cell classes cannot reliably separate Mapt biology from weak or underpowered target engagement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: On-target engagement was measured at Mapt mRNA, not tau protein; several lower-count classes had nominal but non-FDR Mapt depletion.

direction: direct target down; no FDR downstream genes
summary: The two FDR-engaged Mapt perturbations were transcriptionally buffered: Mapt itself was the only FDR-significant gene in each cell class.
why_it_matters: Acute, partial Mapt lowering did not trigger a broad mRNA stress, cytoskeletal, or synaptic program, consistent with tau's major biology being structural and post-translational rather than an obligate short-timescale transcriptional regulator.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut

summary: Edar perturbation was correction-level silent in nearly all neuronal contexts and showed no measurable Edar transcript engagement.

summary: The sterol-gene response was restricted to a subset of subcortical Far1-perturbed classes and absent from many classes with measurable Far1 downshifts.

summary: Far1 sterol induction did not generalize to all peroxisome or ether-lipid perturbations.

summary: Far1-directed rescue or inhibition experiments should track sterol-buffering biomarkers such as Insig1 alongside plasmalogens.

summary: Ncoa3 perturbation produced a near-null mouse-brain transcriptome response rather than a broad nuclear-receptor coactivator-loss program.
why_it_matters: NCOA3 has the annotated functions and interaction partners of a major transcriptional coactivator, so a single adjusted hit across all Ncoa3 contrasts argues that the assayed mouse-brain state was either strongly buffered or only weakly perturbed.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not significantly depleted after correction; a null downstream signature could therefore reflect poor guide efficacy, low target detectability, or absence of the required hormonal state.

summary: The only adjusted single-gene response was Anapc4 down-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.

main_caveats: Per-contrast FDR support comes from one gene; Ncoa3 mRNA was not detectably knocked down in this same cell class.

summary: The largest Ncoa3 cell counts were still transcriptionally quiet.
why_it_matters: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba had the most Ncoa3-assigned cells yet no FDR<=0.05 downstream genes, arguing that the near-null result cannot be attributed only to the smallest 23-50 cell contrasts.

summary: Ncoa3 did not phenocopy Ncoa1, CREBBP/EP300, or measured steroid/thyroid/glucocorticoid receptor perturbations.
why_it_matters: The direct NCOA3 network contains NCOA1/2, CBP/p300, ESR1/2, AR, and other nuclear-receptor machinery, yet the measured brain signatures were essentially uncorrelated; this argues against interchangeable p160 or receptor-complex outputs in this assay.
main_caveats: A lack of convergence is difficult to interpret when the Ncoa3 target transcript was not significantly depleted; Ncoa2 was absent from the perturbation library.

summary: The dataset should not be read as evidence that NCOA3 inhibition is transcriptionally or neurologically inert in brain.
why_it_matters: SRC-3/NCOA3 is an oncology-relevant coactivator with experimental assayable chemistry, and mouse studies implicate SRC3 in hippocampal plasticity through transcriptional and calmodulin-acetylation mechanisms that an unstimulated scRNA-seq contrast may miss.
main_caveats: The perturbation readout is mRNA abundance in mouse cell classes, not SRC3 catalytic activity, receptor stimulation, learning behavior, or cancer dependency.

summary: Exploratory Ncoa1 measurements do not support compensatory paralog induction after Ncoa3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: If p160-family buffering were operating through Ncoa1 up-regulation, Ncoa1 should rise after Ncoa3 loss; instead, the only repeated Ncoa1 changes were weak nominal decreases in three glutamatergic classes and Ncoa1 signatures were not similar to Ncoa3 signatures.

summary: Gata6 perturbation produced no measurable on-target Gata6 mRNA depletion in the assayed mouse brain cell types.

main_caveats: Gata6 protein was not measured, and failure to detect target mRNA depletion can reflect low basal transcript abundance rather than failure of the guide at the DNA locus.

summary: Nsun2 up-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA was the only adjusted-significant downstream gene after Gata6 perturbation.
why_it_matters: If the 059 response is reproducible, Nsun2 is a candidate marker for the rare neuronal state in which Gata6 perturbation is not completely silent; its RNA-cytosine-methyltransferase function points to an RNA-processing readout rather than to a canonical GATA6 mesendoderm program.

main_caveats: This is a single FDR-significant gene in one cell type; the nearby nominal genes all had FDR=1.0 and the finding is not supported by measured Gata6 knockdown.

summary: Outside 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, Gata6 responses were sparse, non-recurrent, and failed FDR correction even in the highest-count cell types.

main_caveats: The negative result is transcriptome-wide and multiple-testing based; it does not rule out effects in unassayed non-neuronal or developmental cell states.

summary: Gata6 signatures were nearly orthogonal to Gata paralogs, Zfpm2, and TGF/BMP-SMAD pathway neighbors.
why_it_matters: Prior developmental biology connects GATA6 to GATA4, ZFPM-family cofactors, and SMAD-dependent endoderm/cardiac circuits, but those relationships did not translate into correlated neuronal Perturb-seq signatures.
main_caveats: Correlations used whole-signature Wilcoxon scores rather than validated pathway readouts; some comparator perturbations also had weak target engagement.

summary: The mouse-brain neuronal screen points away from mature neuronal GATA6 effector programs and back toward developmental or non-neuronal GATA6 biology.
why_it_matters: Human GATA6 disease evidence is dominated by cardiac outflow, endodermal, pancreatic, and epithelial biology; the Perturb-seq negative result warns against assigning those mechanisms to the mature neuronal classes sampled here without direct target engagement.
main_caveats: This finding is an absence-of-evidence interpretation from neuronal transcriptomes; congenital disease mechanisms may occur in transient progenitors or non-neuronal tissues absent from this dataset.

summary: The dataset models a CACNA1A loss direction, the direction already linked to episodic ataxia and absence-epilepsy biology.
why_it_matters: CACNA1A is pharmacologically blockable, but decreasing CaV2.1 activity carries channelopathy risk and produced no corrected protective transcriptomic response here.
