main_caveats: Correlations were computed on weak, high-FDR signatures; they are useful mainly to rule out a strong hidden convergence, not to rank subtle paralog biology.

summary: No reproducible non-Chchd2 transcript biomarker emerged; the largest nominal hits were isolated genes with adjusted p values from 0.219 to 0.936.
why_it_matters: Krba1, R3hdm1, Adamts3, Eif2d, and Hnrnpul2 should be treated as exploratory row-level outliers rather than biomarkers of CHCHD2 loss.

direction: weak Brd1 transcript depletion; sparse downstream response
summary: Brd1 perturbation produced weak RNA-level target engagement and an almost fully buffered downstream transcriptome across the assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: BRD1 is a scaffold for histone acetyltransferase complexes, so the dominant Perturb-seq result is not a broad chromatin-collapse phenotype but a near-null response under this modality and cell-count regime.
main_caveats: All target-transcript FDR values were 1.0, so weak guide activity cannot be separated from biological buffering without protein or chromatin-acetylation measurements.

summary: Adra1a achieved statistically reliable on-target depletion only in 052 Pvalb Gaba.

summary: The Pvalb Adra1a score vector was effectively uncorrelated with adrenergic-family and available PLC/PKC pathway perturbations.

summary: Pvalb Adra1a depletion refines alpha1A interneuron literature by separating acute excitability phenotypes from basal transcriptional maintenance.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The dataset did not measure firing, evoked norepinephrine responses, fear conditioning, hippocampal CA1 physiology, or BLA-specific Pvalb neurons.

summary: The muted neuronal transcriptome should not be used to infer that alpha1A agonists or antagonists lack CNS effects.
why_it_matters: ADRA1A is a clinical small-molecule target, and astrocytic Adra1a also regulates cortical state; a neuronal resting transcriptome can miss acute, ligand-dependent, and glial liabilities or mechanisms.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The perturbation is receptor depletion rather than agonism or antagonism, and the analyzed cell classes did not include astrocytes.

summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response combined cation-homeostasis repression with induction of cholinergic, secretory, oxidative-stress, and excitatory synaptic transcripts.

summary: The thalamic Atp1a3 program was not reproduced by the related Na,K-ATPase alpha perturbations Atp1a1 or Atp1a2.

main_caveats: The comparison is mRNA-only and uses one thalamic cell class; protein-level SERCA2 abundance and ER Ca2+ were not assayed.

direction: avoid loss-of-function inhibition; restore or stabilize ATP1A3 activity
summary: The disease-relevant direction for ATP1A3 is loss of sodium-pump function, so nonselective Na,K-ATPase inhibition would be predicted to move opposite to rescue.
why_it_matters: Atp1a3 RNA depletion was sufficient to remodel neuronal ion/synaptic transcripts, while human AHC mutations reduce ATPase activity and ChEMBL-annotated ligands for the Na,K-ATPase class are inhibitors; this frames restoration or stabilization, not pump blockade, as the rational therapeutic direction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset did not test any drug and measured mouse RNA after perturbation, not human mutant pump rescue.

summary: Mga perturbation releases a sparse ectopic response centered on the meiotic cohesin gene Stag3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The direction of Stag3 induction matches the known MAX/MGA-ncPRC1.6 role in repressing germline and meiosis genes, extending that mechanism to a restricted neuronal Perturb-seq context.

main_caveats: Only Stag3 was significant in both classes; the broader meiotic program was not detected.

summary: Corrected Mga responses were confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The same two classes also had the largest Mga perturbed cell counts, so selectivity is confounded by power.

summary: The Mga transcript itself was not measurably knocked down in any tested cell class.

main_caveats: A coding perturbation could reduce protein function without causing nonsense-mediated mRNA loss.

summary: Max converges with Mga on Stag3, while available Mnt, Myc, Mycn, DP, and E2F paralog perturbations do not.
why_it_matters: This points to the MAX/MGA repressive branch as the relevant comparator rather than a nonspecific response shared by all assayed MAX-network transcription factors.

main_caveats: Pcgf6, L3mbtl2, and E2f6 were absent as perturbations; E2f1/E2f4/E2f5 are imperfect substitutes for E2F6.

summary: The Max/Mga relationship is concentrated on a few genes rather than a shared whole-transcriptome signature.
why_it_matters: It prevents overcalling the Mga perturbation as a complete Max phenocopy or a broad meiotic-state transition.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed over noisy single-cell Wilcoxon score vectors and may dilute a small true module.

summary: Stag3 is a candidate functional biomarker for sparse MAX/MGA-ncPRC1.6 release in the brain dataset.
why_it_matters: Stag3 stays interpretable when the Mga target transcript is flat, because it is recurrently induced by Mga and independently induced by Max in the two main classes.

main_caveats: Nominal Stag3 recurrence outside 151 and 155 did not survive FDR correction.

summary: The neuronal Mga phenotype is not a generic MYC-like signature despite MGA cancer literature emphasizing an anti-MYC tumor-suppressor role.
why_it_matters: Disease interpretation should separate ncPRC1.6/meiotic escape from broad MYC activation; Myc and Mycn perturbations did not reproduce the Stag3 response in the relevant neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The cancer references are human tumor studies rather than mouse neurons, and mouse Myc/Mycn perturbations may have had their own engagement limitations.

summary: Csmd1 knockdown was transcriptionally weak and buffered across the assayed neuronal subclasses: the target RNA trended down in most groups but never reached FDR significance and produced no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: A weak Perturb-seq signature for a synaptic complement regulator should be interpreted primarily as a limited cell-autonomous RNA response, not as evidence that CSMD1 is biologically dispensable.
main_caveats: Knockdown was incomplete at the RNA level and the experiment measures short-term transcript abundance rather than CSMD1 protein at synapses.

summary: The largest nominal gene tail was concentrated in 001 L5-6 IT Glut but was decoupled from measurable Csmd1 repression, whereas the best-engaged 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group showed only two p<0.001 genes.
why_it_matters: The apparent L5/6 IT response is biologically weaker than its raw p values suggest; target-engaged thalamic neurons look more buffered than cortical L5/6 IT neurons in this dataset.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The L5/6 IT result used only 25 perturbed cells and lacked target knockdown; neither cell type had FDR-significant downstream genes.

summary: Csmd1 perturbation did not trigger a classical-complement transcript module, even though CSMD1 protein is a synaptic and astrocytic inhibitor of classical-pathway activation.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates the known CSMD1 protein-level complement checkpoint from bulk induction of complement component mRNAs in the targeted neuronal populations.
main_caveats: The perturbation may not deplete CSMD1 protein at synapses strongly enough, and the assay lacks direct measurements of C3/C4b deposition, factor-I cofactor activity, microglial engulfment, or astrocyte responses.

summary: Csmd1 signatures were nearly orthogonal to selected complement or neuroimmune perturbations and to the strongest genome-wide signature neighbors in six evaluated cell types.
why_it_matters: A CSMD1 loss-of-function phenotype in neurons is unlikely to be captured by a reusable transcriptional state shared with C3, Cd46, Cr2, or Trem2 perturbation under these assay conditions.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

summary: The flat complement-mRNA response should not be used as a safety proxy for CSMD1 inhibition: knockout literature places CSMD1 upstream of synaptic C3 deposition and CR3-dependent microglial engulfment, processes absent from this RNA readout.
why_it_matters: Potential CSMD1 antagonism, strong knockdown, or loss-of-function disease mechanisms could be harmful at the synapse even when neuronal Perturb-seq detects little acute complement transcription.

direction: weak target decrease; no FDR-resolved downstream signal
summary: Dgkd loss did not produce an FDR-resolved transcriptional program in any assayed brain cell group.
why_it_matters: DGKδ is a DAG-to-phosphatidic-acid enzyme with mouse loss-of-function phenotypes, but this Perturb-seq contrast provides no high-confidence downstream RNA markers for the target.
main_caveats: The negative result is conditional on weak transcript engagement; lipid signaling, protein activity, acute electrophysiology, or longer perturbations could still be affected.

summary: The clearest Dgkd self-depletion was nominal and concentrated in glutamatergic or pineal glutamatergic annotations.

direction: divergent target engagement and uncorrelated signatures
summary: Dgke was efficiently depleted in a target-only pattern while Dgkd remained weak, and the two DGK isoforms had near-zero score correlations.

summary: DGKD has enzymatic assayability but no strong Perturb-seq biomarker in this brain screen.

summary: Fzd3 perturbation was mostly a target-transcript event rather than a broad RNA phenotype: Fzd3 RNA trended down in 19 of 20 tested cell classes, but the target row never reached FDR<0.05 and only one non-Fzd3 gene reached FDR<0.05 anywhere.
why_it_matters: Canonical mouse Fzd3 biology is robust at the level of axon guidance and PCP morphogenesis, so the Perturb-seq result warns that this experiment is probably not reading out the main developmental or protein-localization phenotypes of FZD3.
main_caveats: Target mRNA depletion was nominal rather than FDR-significant; several cell classes had fewer than 40 perturbed cells; the assay cannot measure axon-tract morphology or PCP protein localization.

summary: L4-5 IT cortical glutamatergic cells were the only Fzd3 context with an FDR-significant transcriptional hit, a decrease in the postsynaptic scaffold gene Dlgap4/Sapap4; Dvl2 was the top nominally increased gene but was not FDR-significant.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only one gene passed adjusted testing in this cell class, and the Dvl2 component is nominal only with FDR=1.

summary: MB glutamatergic and CNU-HYa/HY GABA cells showed nominal Fzd3 self-depletion but no FDR-significant downstream response.
why_it_matters: These cell classes separate apparent target engagement from downstream transcriptional activation and identify contexts where Fzd3 loss is either buffered, captured too weakly, or manifested outside steady-state mRNA abundance.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The self-row FDR was 1 in both profiles, so these are nominal target-engagement examples rather than high-confidence knockdown classes.

summary: Fzd3 signatures were nearly orthogonal to Frizzled paralogs and Wnt/PCP or canonical-Wnt neighbors available in the screen, including Fzd2, Fzd4, Fzd6, Fzd9, Ryk, Ror1/2, Lrp5/6, Celsr2, Prickle1, Apc, Ctnnb1, and Gsk3b.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating loss of different Wnt receptors or downstream β-catenin regulators as interchangeable perturbations in these mouse-brain transcriptomes.
main_caveats: Correlations used single-cell-class Wilcoxon score vectors and the Wnt/PCP comparators themselves varied in effect size.

summary: Whole-screen signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a strong Fzd3-like or anti-Fzd3-like module; the largest positive and negative correlations with non-Fzd3 perturbations were only 0.244 and -0.261.
why_it_matters: This reduces the likelihood that the Fzd3 result was a missed member of a high-amplitude shared perturbation module and makes top-neighbor hypotheses exploratory rather than mechanistic.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Pearson correlations of approximately 0.25 are small; 308 CB GABA also had weak Fzd3 self-knockdown, so those neighbors should be viewed as quality-control observations, not mechanisms.

summary: Because Fzd3 perturbation produced synapse-linked and highly cell-contextual RNA effects rather than a shared Wnt transcriptional program, direct FZD3 modulators should be profiled in neuronal systems for DLGAP4/SAPAP4 and other synaptic markers instead of assuming a simple canonical-Wnt readout.
why_it_matters: FZD3-selective nanobody modulators now make the receptor experimentally targetable, but the dataset suggests that neuronal consequences could be narrow and easy to miss in broad assays.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: No drug, disease model, or dose-response data were present in the parquet; this is a biomarker and assay-design warning rather than a validated therapeutic claim.

summary: Lyrm4 targeting produced weak, nonsignificant target-transcript depletion and an almost empty adjusted differential-expression profile across 22 cell types.
why_it_matters: This establishes that the negative Fe-S readout is dominated by limited perturbation strength rather than proving that neurons tolerate LYRM4 loss.
main_caveats: The finding concerns measured scRNA-seq transcriptional engagement only; protein knockdown and Fe-S enzyme activity were not measured.

summary: Gmpr up-regulation in 155 MB Glut was the only FDR-significant downstream row in the full Lyrm4 subset.
why_it_matters: It flags a possible midbrain-glutamatergic single-gene marker for follow-up but not a validated pathway response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Single gene, single cell type, and the target transcript was not significantly knocked down in the same stratum.

summary: Measured Fe-S biogenesis and transfer transcripts did not form an adjusted response to Lyrm4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: LYRM4/ISD11 is a core ISC factor, so the dataset should not be interpreted as showing pathway-level Fe-S shutdown at the mRNA level.
main_caveats: Fe-S disruption can be enzymatic or post-transcriptional; the screen did not directly assay Fe-S protein activity.

summary: Lyrm4 signatures were nearly uncorrelated with same-pathway Nfs1 and Isca2 perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: A physical and pathway relationship did not translate into a shared Perturb-seq signature, warning against inferring ISC activity from this weak Lyrm4 profile.
main_caveats: The contrast is limited by sparse target engagement for both Lyrm4 and Nfs1; Isca2 was significant only for its self transcript in one cell type.

summary: Top positive and negative whole-screen signature neighbors of Lyrm4 were all weakly correlated.
why_it_matters: No hidden high-correlation transcriptional module or inverse module emerged to rescue interpretation of the sparse direct DE hits.
main_caveats: Restricted to vector correlations of Wilcoxon scores; the largest correlations occurred in low-count strata and are not mechanistically specific.

summary: The mouse-brain Lyrm4 profile should not be used as a directional therapeutic or disease model for human LYRM4 respiratory-chain deficiency.
why_it_matters: Human LYRM4 loss can impair Fe-S and OXPHOS biochemistry, but this experiment lacks strong knockdown and lacks a robust Fe-S/OXPHOS transcriptomic phenotype.
main_caveats: Disease variants, tissue context, developmental timing, and genotype are not matched; ChEMBL absence is a database search result, not proof that the protein is chemically intractable.

summary: Acute Cc2d1a perturbation produced no FDR-resolved transcriptome in any profiled neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The main dataset result is absence of a reproducible cell-state shift, so nominal individual genes should not be treated as a Cc2d1a-regulated program.
main_caveats: The negative call is transcriptomic and power-limited by 29-209 perturbed cells per class; partial on-target knockdown could miss protein or activity changes.

summary: Measurable target-transcript reduction was concentrated in midbrain/thalamic profiles, led by 155 MB Glut, rather than being uniform across the atlas.
why_it_matters: Interpretation of downstream responses should be anchored on classes with actual Cc2d1a mRNA decrease; weakly engaged cortical and hypothalamic profiles are less informative for biology.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Selectivity may reflect guide delivery, expression, or sampling rather than true cell-type-specific dependence; even these three profiles were nominal after genome-wide correction.

summary: Cc2d1a knockdown did not derepress the Freud-1 receptor targets Htr1a or Drd2 in any profiled class.
why_it_matters: Freud-1/CC2D1A is a documented transcriptional repressor of 5-HT1A biology; the absence of Htr1a/Drd2 induction argues that this module is not broadly engaged by partial Cc2d1a loss across these brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The best-matched serotonergic raphe context was not isolated in the cell-class labels; receptor transcripts may be sparse, and the assay measured mRNA only.

summary: Canonical NF-kB/Rac1 readouts were not transcriptionally resolved after Cc2d1a knockdown.
why_it_matters: Prior work places CC2D1A upstream of NF-kB homeostasis and Rac1-dependent synaptic phenotypes, but the Perturb-seq profiles did not show coordinated changes in Nfkb1, Rela, Map3k7, or Rac1 mRNA.
main_caveats: NF-kB and Rac1 are regulated strongly by localization, phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and GTP loading, none of which are assayed by a cell-class mRNA Wilcoxon test.

summary: Cc2d1a signatures were orthogonal to ESCRT, NF-kB, serotonin-receptor, and intellectual-disability comparator perturbations.
why_it_matters: Physical or disease relationships did not translate into interchangeable transcriptomic phenotypes; Cc2d1a should not be modeled as a simple CHMP4B, NFKB1/MAP3K7, HTR1A, or CRBN phenocopy in this assay.
main_caveats: Whole-signature correlations are insensitive if Cc2d1a itself generated only a weak, partially engaged response.

summary: The best-engaged 155 MB Glut profile lacked a strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: The strongest Cc2d1a profile was still too weak to define a high-confidence convergent module or assign it to a pathway by nearest-neighbor signature matching.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut

summary: Partial acute knockdown in mature cell classes is a poor transcriptional proxy for CC2D1A loss-of-function neurodevelopmental disease.
why_it_matters: Human recessive CC2D1A disease and mouse conditional knockouts can involve developmental, synaptic, circuit, NF-kB, or Rac1 mechanisms without generating a large immediate mRNA cascade in this Perturb-seq assay.
main_caveats: This does not refute Cc2d1a disease causality or synaptic phenotypes; it only constrains what was visible in an acute cell-class mRNA assay.

summary: Hnf1b perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream genes and no statistically measurable Hnf1b target-transcript depletion in any of 23 brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The strongest conclusion for Hnf1b is a negative or operationally buffered RNA phenotype, which prevents assigning a robust HNF1B-regulated brain program from this dataset.
main_caveats: High confidence for the measured absence of adjusted hits, but biological interpretation is limited by absent measurable target-transcript knockdown and likely low endogenous Hnf1b expression.

summary: The only near-threshold Hnf1b response was a weak, exploratory 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut signature led by Ncam2.

why_it_matters: This argues that the shared HNF1 family biochemical prior is not sufficient to assume interchangeable transcriptional effects in the profiled brain cells.
main_caveats: The contrast is in a weak-Hnf1b setting, and the cited direct regulatory literature is kidney/pancreas-biased rather than brain-specific.

summary: The HNF1B kidney/pancreas disease network is uncoupled from the Hnf1b brain Perturb-seq phenotype.
why_it_matters: HNF1B is a strong renal cysts and diabetes gene, but the brain data do not reproduce a renal/pancreatic developmental target program, consistent with tissue-restricted HNF1B expression and function.
main_caveats: The experiment assayed brain cell types and acute RNA responses, not embryonic kidney or pancreas; several disease-network target genes such as Pkhd1 were literature context rather than perturbed comparators.

summary: Tcf7l2 produced a strong thalamic transcriptional phenotype where Hnf1b remained silent.
why_it_matters: A diabetes-linked transcription factor can be detected in the same dataset and cell type, so the Hnf1b null result is target/context-specific rather than a universal limitation of transcription-factor perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: TCF7L2 is a Wnt-associated diabetes locus rather than an HNF1B paralog or complex member; the comparison establishes assay sensitivity but not direct pathway equivalence.

summary: A top-200 restricted Hnf1b signature-neighbor search in L4/5 cortex found only modest Camta1-positive and Kat6b-negative neighbors.

summary: Grin3a perturbation yielded no FDR-significant transcriptomic effect in any assayed cell type, and even the target transcript was never significantly depleted after correction.

summary: The strongest nominal Grin3a self-depletion was concentrated in GABA populations, led by 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 053 Sst Gaba, which is directionally consistent with literature emphasizing persistent/high Grin3a expression in somatostatin interneurons.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Only nominal target depletion was observed; the dataset cell-class labels are broader than the SST-positive interneuron populations characterized electrophysiologically in the literature.

summary: Grin3a did not behave like an interchangeable core NMDA receptor subunit: Grin1, Grin2a, and Grin2b perturbations produced strong self-knockdown in matched cell types whereas Grin3a did not, and Grin3a score vectors were nearly uncorrelated with Grin1/Grin2a/Grin2b/Grin2d.

summary: The known GluN3A-GIT1/Rac1/PAK spine-maturation pathway was not recovered as a corrected transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: A negative RNA signature in Git1, Arhgef7, Rac1, and Pak genes is compatible with this pathway being controlled by receptor localization and protein-complex signaling rather than by rapid changes in transcript abundance.
main_caveats: Only a small hand-curated gene set was checked, and mRNA abundance is an indirect readout for actin regulatory signaling.

summary: The densest local nominal signatures in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 054 CNU-MGE GABA remained uncorrected and occurred without significant target-transcript depletion.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA

summary: Bcl11b perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome-wide response in any assayed brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This converts many isolated nominal ranks into a negative biological result: in this class-level mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout, Bcl11b loss did not recover the large cortical or striatal transcriptional programs expected from developmental Bcl11b biology.
main_caveats: The dataset supports absence of corrected DE, not absence of BCL11B function; on-target transcript engagement was weak and the assay used broad cell classes.

summary: The target transcript itself was only weakly and nominally shifted, with no cell type showing FDR-significant Bcl11b depletion.
why_it_matters: Weak direct engagement is the most parsimonious technical explanation for the downstream near-null signature and prevents over-interpreting nominal downstream rows as loss-of-function biology.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|155 MB Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Bcl11b was measured at the RNA level only; guide activity, protein depletion, and subtype-restricted depletion were not measured in this parquet.

summary: Pcsk1n was the only same-gene nominal response recurring in ten cell classes, usually increasing after Bcl11b perturbation.
why_it_matters: If the weak perturbation contains a reproducible residual signal, Pcsk1n is its clearest candidate reporter; its FDR=1.0 rows make the claim hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Every Pcsk1n row had FDR 1.0, the logFC values were small to moderate, and one of ten nominal rows was in the opposite direction.

summary: The broad CNU-LGE/LSX GABA class did not reproduce the robust medium-spiny-neuron marker losses expected from Bcl11b-deficient striatum.
why_it_matters: Mouse literature places Bcl11b at the center of medium spiny neuron differentiation and adult striatal transcriptional maintenance, but this dataset shows only weak, non-corrected trends in a broad striatal-related GABA class.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset has a broad 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA class rather than purified D1/D2 medium spiny neurons, and the Bcl11b target row was only nominal in that class.

summary: Bcl11b resembled Bcl11a, Satb2, and Foxp2 in having no FDR-significant rows, whereas Tbr1 and especially Setd1a produced corrected signatures in the same source matrix.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues against treating the Bcl11b null as a universal failure of transcription-factor perturbations, while showing that several developmentally important BCL11/cortical-neuron regulators are silent in this class-level assay.
main_caveats: The comparison used scalar FDR burdens, not full matched signature correlations.

summary: The dataset offers no corrected support for Bcl11b inhibition as a neuronal disease-modifying direction.
why_it_matters: Human genetics and mouse striatal deletion both associate BCL11B loss with disease-relevant nervous-system and immune consequences, while this Perturb-seq slice supplies only weak engagement and no FDR-corrected rescue-like program.
main_caveats: No disease model, BCL11B activator or inhibitor, immune readout, or protein-level depletion was assayed here; this is a directionality warning, not a preclinical efficacy test.

summary: Elp2 knockdown produced a broad FDR-significant response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
why_it_matters: The result localizes the strongest acute transcriptional consequence of losing an Elongator core subunit to one thalamic glutamatergic subclass rather than to every neuronal population in which Elp2 guides were recovered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Target mRNA engagement was strong at FDR<0.05 only in the same 151 class; many negative cell classes therefore remain ambiguous between buffering and weak effective perturbation.

summary: The 151 response couples amino-acid/ATF4 stress induction to loss of synaptic and dendritic transcripts.
why_it_matters: The induced genes point to amino-acid starvation and integrated-stress-response biology, while the down-regulated genes indicate that the response is accompanied by reduced mature neuronal structural and glutamatergic features.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA end points, not tRNA modifications, translation speed, ATF4 protein, or neuronal electrophysiology.

summary: Elp2 and the Elongator core subunit Elp1 converge in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Elp1 is quantitatively broader across cell types.
why_it_matters: Same-direction overlap supports an Elongator-complex mechanism rather than an isolated guide artifact, whereas the broader Elp1 response warns that subunits are not interchangeable at the observed Perturb-seq effect size.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Elp1 and Elp2 guide efficiencies and protein depletion were not directly measured, so the broader Elp1 footprint could be technical, biological, or both.

summary: Elp2 preferentially activated the ATF4/Ddit3 branch without a uniform ER-chaperone UPR transcriptome.
why_it_matters: This refines the stress call: Asns, Chac1, Ddit3 and amino-acid transporters were clearly induced, but Hspa5, Dnajb9 and Xbp1 did not form a parallel FDR-significant ER-chaperone module in the same cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Xbp1 splicing and ATF4 translation are not captured by these mRNA rows, and single-cell dropout can weaken detection of chaperone genes.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor analysis linked Elp2 most strongly to Elp1 and then to other stress-perturbation signatures, with no strong inverse neighbor.
why_it_matters: The second-tier neighbors Hspa9, Gfpt1 and Atp2a2 converged on the same 151 FDR genes, while the best negative neighbor, Pten, was weak; the Elp2 state therefore looks like a positive stress module rather than one side of a clean bidirectional axis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlation across ranked gene scores is hypothesis-generating and does not establish that Hspa9, Gfpt1 or Atp2a2 act in the Elp2 pathway.

summary: The Perturb-seq direction is deleterious-loss-of-function-like, so ELP2 inhibition should not be treated as a restorative therapeutic direction in neurons.
why_it_matters: Human ELP2 loss is associated with intellectual disability and ASD, and in this dataset acute Elp2 reduction activates stress genes in neurons; the immediate pharmacologic implication is to avoid interpreting the knockdown signature as a desired disease-correcting state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No disease rescue experiment or drug perturbation was performed in the Perturb-seq dataset.

summary: Alkbh8 was an uninformative tRNA-wobble pathway-neighbor negative rather than a true contradiction of the Elp2 program.
why_it_matters: ALKBH8 also acts on wobble uridines, but the Alkbh8 perturbation neither reduced the Alkbh8 transcript nor produced FDR-significant genes in the Elp2-responsive class, so equivalence between Elongator and ALKBH8 cannot be evaluated from this signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The negative result is dominated by failed target-transcript engagement, not by a clean ALKBH8 knockdown with no phenotype.

summary: Ndufb9 mRNA depletion was FDR-significant only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, despite being measured in 22 Ndufb9 signatures.
why_it_matters: The perturbation engages the target transcript in a restricted subset of neuronal classes, giving a concrete place to start follow-up while avoiding a false claim that all Ndufb9 guide contexts were equally effective.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The compared Leigh-model literature used Ndufs4 and organismal phenotypes, not Ndufb9 CRISPR perturbation in this single-cell assay.

summary: Ndufb9 perturbation produced self-transcript depletion without any FDR-significant non-self downstream transcript.
why_it_matters: NDUFB9 is a bona fide mitochondrial complex-I accessory subunit, so the absence of a corrected RNA stress program implies buffering, slow protein-complex turnover, or nontranscriptional phenotypes rather than lack of biological relevance.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure NDUFB9 protein, complex-I activity, ROS, ATP, or cell survival.

summary: Ndufb9 did not share a strong transcriptome-wide signature with other targeted complex-I subunits or assembly factors.
why_it_matters: The expected relationship among subunits of the same respiratory complex was not visible as a convergent mRNA module; complex-I guide effects in this dataset were dominated by self knockdown rather than by a shared OXPHOS response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The contrast uses mRNA signatures only; it cannot rule out convergent effects on assembled complex I or respiration.

summary: Several Ndufb9-negative cell classes are statistically unresolved because target engagement was nominal, near-threshold, low-count, or absent.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpreting zero downstream FDR genes as resistance in contexts where the guide may not have achieved enough corrected on-target depletion.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The finding is a caveat about power and FDR correction, not a positive biological pathway claim.

summary: Transcriptome neutrality after acute Ndufb9 knockdown should not be used as evidence that complex-I function is intact.
why_it_matters: Human NDUFB9 lesions can reduce complex-I abundance and activity, and NDUFB9 loss can have broad metabolic consequences in other contexts; this dataset says those effects are not reliably captured by downstream mRNA FDR hits in the sampled mouse-brain cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The disease and cancer references differ by species, cell type, perturbation duration, and endpoint.

summary: Ndufb9 mRNA is the only reproducible transcript-level biomarker of Ndufb9 guide engagement in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Follow-up designs can use the target row as an mRNA engagement check, but should not rely on a non-self response gene panel because no such panel recurred after FDR correction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is an engagement biomarker, not a biomarker of complex-I enzymatic inhibition.

direction: Mdh1 down with mixed downstream up and down genes
summary: Mdh1 perturbation produced a clear FDR-significant downstream transcriptional program only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: MDH1 is a core cytosolic malate-aspartate-shuttle enzyme, but the transcriptomic consequence of its acute depletion was concentrated in one neuronal class rather than following its broad brain expression.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is an RNA readout from one perturbation dose/timepoint and does not prove that only this cell type is metabolically sensitive.

direction: Mdh1 down with no non-target FDR response
summary: Strong Mdh1 target depletion was transcriptionally buffered in 15 other cell classes.
why_it_matters: The negative result separates target engagement from downstream RNA remodeling and warns against treating absence of DE as absence of a metabolic phenotype.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Six additional assayed classes had weak target engagement, so they were not used as strong buffering examples; FDR-based absence of RNA changes cannot exclude metabolite or electrophysiologic effects.

summary: The 151 downstream module included downregulation of an excitatory-synapse gene subset.
why_it_matters: Nrxn1, Cadm3, Lrrtm1, and Grin2b connect MDH1 loss to a neuronal connectivity/readout module rather than to a generic mitochondrial transcriptome alone.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The pathway call rests on four FDR-significant genes; it is a transcript-level synaptic signature, not a measured synapse phenotype.

direction: Got1 similar; Mdh2 near-neutral; Got2 and Slc25a12 anti-correlated on the restricted module
summary: The Mdh1 signature converged with Got1 but not with mitochondrial or transporter MAS perturbations in the same 151 cell type.
why_it_matters: Although Reactome places MDH1, GOT1, MDH2, GOT2, and SLC25A12 within one malate-aspartate shuttle, the data support a cytosolic-arm-specific transcriptional state for Mdh1/Got1 rather than interchangeable phenotypes across all MAS components.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The correlations use a 91-gene Mdh1-nominal module from a single cell type; only Mdh1 itself had a broad non-target FDR module.

direction: Gls up after Mdh1 perturbation; Gls perturbation anti-correlated with the Mdh1 module
summary: Gls induction is a candidate marker of the Mdh1-deficient 151 state.
why_it_matters: GLS controls glutamine-to-glutamate conversion, and its upregulation plus reciprocal restricted-signature relationship suggest glutamate/glutamine handling as a tractable readout of the MDH1 response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The direct Gls perturbation in this cell type had only nominal target engagement after FDR correction, so the anti-correlation is hypothesis-generating.

summary: Kalrn perturbation was globally transcriptionally buffered: no cell type produced an FDR<0.05 downstream gene despite 22 measured Kalrn comparisons.
why_it_matters: Kalirin is a synaptic RhoGEF and disease gene, so the absence of a strong steady-state mRNA state change argues that this assay is mostly missing localized cytoskeletal, postsynaptic, activity-dependent, or developmental consequences rather than disproving Kalrn biology.
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell counts were modest and target-transcript knockdown did not itself pass FDR, so a strong KO or protein-level phenotype could be absent because target engagement was weak.

summary: The clearest direct Kalrn transcript decrease was confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and was not accompanied by a broad downstream signature.
why_it_matters: A nominal target-only response in this thalamic glutamatergic class separates measurable guide action from robust propagation through Kalirin effector pathways and makes region/cell-state accessibility a leading caveat.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The on-target Kalrn row was nominal only and FDR=0.424; this is evidence for the best observed target engagement, not for complete knockdown.

summary: The largest nominal cell-type clusters were split across 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 155 MB Glut rather than concentrating in one canonical cortical excitatory class.
why_it_matters: These peaks nominate Nlgn2, Clns1a, and Patj as cell-state-specific readouts to retest, but they should be treated as hypotheses because none passed FDR<0.05.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The leading adjusted p values were 0.104-0.693 and the 054 CNU-MGE GABA response used only 45 perturbed cells.

summary: Kalrn did not broadly phenocopy its paralog Trio; the only visible convergence was a weak restricted-signature correlation in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut.
why_it_matters: This keeps Kalirin-Trio non-interchangeability as a first-class result: a paralog expected to share RhoGEF biology was not a robust positive neighbor of Kalrn in most mouse neuronal classes.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The comparison used the 200 largest absolute Kalrn scores in weak signatures; it is not an FDR-supported shared DE program.

summary: Kalrn knockdown did not transcriptionally induce a coordinated Rac/PAK/MAPK or postsynaptic NMDA-receptor module.
why_it_matters: Kalirin-7 is known to couple PSD localization and Rac signaling to spine morphology, but the measured effector genes stayed at FDR=1.0, indicating that the Perturb-seq endpoint is uncoupled from the canonical local signaling pathway at the mRNA level.
main_caveats: An mRNA readout cannot assay Rac1-GTP, RhoA-GTP, kinase activity, receptor localization, spine morphology, or synaptic transmission directly.

summary: No non-Kalrn transcript recurred as a global biomarker of Kalrn perturbation.
why_it_matters: The top nominal genes are inappropriate as universal Kalrn-activity sentinels; future validation should be cell-type-specific and should start with on-target engagement rather than a single downstream RNA marker.
main_caveats: This conclusion is about repeated nominal RNA hits, not about protein activity or morphology markers.

summary: Gapdh elicited a statistically significant transcriptional response in only 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where six genes were downregulated; 21 of 22 assayed cell types had no FDR < 0.05 genes.
why_it_matters: A central glycolytic enzyme did not yield a pan-neuronal mRNA program in this screen; the interpretable response was sharply thalamic.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Most silent cell types had modest Gapdh guide-cell counts, and the two closest misses were single-gene signals with FDR just above 0.05.

summary: Gapdh target-mRNA knockdown could not be quantified because Gapdh itself was absent as a measured output gene in the DE table.
why_it_matters: Any downstream Gapdh signature must be interpreted without a direct on-target efficacy measurement, unlike many neighboring glycolytic targets whose own transcripts were measured.
main_caveats: The result proves absence from this DE table, not absence of Gapdh expression or protein perturbation in the cells.

summary: The thalamic Gapdh signature partially converged with Pgk1 but not with most assayed upstream glycolytic or pyruvate-dehydrogenase neighbors.
why_it_matters: Consecutive glycolytic nodes were not interchangeable: Pgk1 reproduced the Pnisr/Rsrp1/Ogt/Grm1 arm of the response, whereas Tpi1, Hk1, Pfkm, Gpi1, and Dlat were dominated by on-target self-reduction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Gapdh-Pgk1 whole-transcriptome correlation was only modest and target engagement for Gapdh could not be measured.

summary: Gapdh did not induce a detectable transcriptional glycolytic-feedback, ER-stress, or apoptosis program in the only cell type with significant DE.
why_it_matters: The response appears to be a restricted Pnisr/Rsrp1/Grin1/Ogt module rather than a broad compensatory mRNA increase in glycolysis or a canonical death/stress signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only mRNA abundance was assayed; GAPDH's metabolic, redox, and apoptotic activities are strongly post-translational and could change without these transcripts changing.

summary: Grin1 was a modest but significant component of the Gapdh thalamic response, with nominal Grm1 reduction recurring in the Pgk1-convergent arm.
why_it_matters: NMDA and metabotropic glutamate receptor transcripts may be sensitive readouts of the Gapdh/Pgk1 state in this thalamic class, even though they are not canonical glycolysis genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The logFC values were modest, Grm1 did not pass FDR < 0.05 for Gapdh, and no electrophysiology or receptor-protein measurements were made.

summary: The weak Perturb-seq output should not be read as evidence that broad GAPDH inhibition is benign in brain cells.
why_it_matters: GAPDH is an essential glycolytic and moonlighting enzyme; this dataset mostly reports buffered mRNA states and lacks direct Gapdh target engagement, so it is poorly powered to exclude metabolic or post-translational toxicity.
main_caveats: This is a direction-of-interpretation warning, not a direct drug experiment; no GAPDH enzymatic activity, viability, or metabolite measurements were present.

direction: no FDR-supported response; weak nominal Dock7 depletion in three cell types
summary: Dock7 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic response in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant dataset result: any mechanistic interpretation of Dock7 has to start from weak target-RNA depletion and zero q<0.05 genes rather than from the nominal top-ranked rows.
main_caveats: Negative transcriptomic result under a guide-based Perturb-seq assay; protein depletion and Rac/Cdc42 activity were not measured.

direction: nominal Dock7 RNA down with mixed nominal surrounding genes
summary: 054 CNU-MGE GABA was the best-engaged Dock7 stratum yet still lacked a corrected downstream signature.
why_it_matters: A GABAergic stratum is biologically interesting because DOCK7 is known to control migration of interneuron precursors, but the measured response here was nominal, small-cell-number, and not a strong cell-state program.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only 33 perturbed cells and all adjusted p values were 1.0, so this is a best-engaged negative/buffered observation, not proof of compensation.

summary: Dock7 signatures did not converge with Dock3 or with Rac1/Cdc42-PAK/JNK neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: Prior work places DOCK7 upstream of Rac1 and Cdc42, so a near-zero score-vector relationship argues that the acute Dock7 RNA signature in this dataset does not read out the canonical small-GTPase module.
main_caveats: Correlation used transcriptome score vectors, including a top-200 Dock7-gene restriction; weak Dock7 engagement can mask true pathway relationships.

summary: An all-perturbation scan found no strong Dock7 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The lack of a high-correlation positive or negative neighbor, together with Safe_target guides among several top neighbors, makes a hidden robust Dock7 module unlikely in these data.
main_caveats: Restricted to the 200 largest-absolute Dock7 genes per cell type; permutation or replicate-guide statistics were not available.

direction: loss-of-function risk despite weak perturb-seq readout
summary: The dataset's weak acute RNA phenotype does not de-risk DOCK7 loss of function.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic DOCK7 mutations cause a severe neurodevelopmental epilepsy/blindness syndrome, so the absence of FDR hits after partial transcript depletion should be interpreted as an assay-sensitivity result rather than as evidence that lowering DOCK7 is benign.
main_caveats: The disease evidence is human, developmental, and genetic; the dataset is mouse single-cell RNA with modest on-target transcript changes.

summary: Hoxa1 targeting produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response and no observable Hoxa1 mRNA depletion in any sampled mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This prevents interpreting the Hoxa1 guide label as a successful Hoxa1 loss-of-function state; the dataset is most consistent with either a buffered response, lack of Hoxa1 expression, or insufficient target engagement in the assayed cell classes.
