summary: Hoxa1 perturbation did not activate or repress the embryonic Hoxa1/Raldh2 retinoic-acid program in the sampled brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse embryology places Hoxa1 upstream of hindbrain, neural-crest and inner-ear targets, but those genes were statistically unchanged here, arguing that the assayed cells are not in the developmental state in which the canonical Hoxa1 program is wired.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: A null result in a non-embryonic Perturb-seq context does not contradict Hoxa1 requirements during E7.75-E8.5 hindbrain development.

summary: Hoxa1 signatures were essentially orthogonal to available Pbx/Meis, retinoic-acid receptor, and other Hox-family perturbations.
why_it_matters: Hoxa1 is embedded in Hox-Pbx-Meis and retinoic-acid regulatory biology, but no same-cell transcriptional convergence was detectable with Pbx1, Meis2, Rarb, or posterior Hox perturbations in this dataset.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The Hoxa1 signature itself is weak, Hoxb1 was not part of the available comparator set, and correlations were computed from restricted same-cell signatures rather than from raw counts.

summary: Kif21a was the top Hoxa1 nominal hit in 191 MB P MY GABA, creating an ocular-motility disease-space lead that remains below FDR significance.
why_it_matters: HOXA1-related disorders and KIF21A-related CFEOM both involve eye-movement phenotypes; the dataset raises a narrow hypothesis that Hoxa1 perturbation may touch an axonal/ocular-motor module in brainstem GABAergic cells, but the signal should be treated as exploratory.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Single gene and single cell class; Kif21a did not pass 10% FDR and there is no direct HOXA1-KIF21A mechanism in the cited literature.

summary: Kctd1 targeting did not significantly deplete the Kctd1 transcript in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: The lack of on-target mRNA reduction constrains every downstream interpretation and favors weak engagement or buffering over a clean loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: mRNA engagement may miss protein-level or isoform-specific perturbation; some classes had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: FDR-resolved downstream effects were restricted to 052 Pvalb Gaba and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with almost all other classes silent.
why_it_matters: Kctd1 does not produce a broad neuronal transcriptome in this dataset; the interpretable signal is a sparse two-class response plus one borderline Tnnc1 event.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction could reflect true biology, guide efficacy differences, power differences, or ambient target expression.

summary: Resp18 up-regulation is the only recurrent FDR-significant gene-level response to Kctd1 targeting.
why_it_matters: The repeated Resp18 increase nominates a compact biomarker of the responsive Kctd1 guide state and links the signal to regulated secretory biology rather than to a broad AP-2 program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only two cell types showed the hit; no direct KCTD1-to-RESP18 mechanism was identified.

summary: Screened AP-2/KCTD15, Hedgehog, and ADCY5/cAMP sentinels were not transcriptionally activated or repressed after Kctd1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: KCTD1 is known to repress AP-2 activity, cooperate with KCTD15 complexes, modulate Hedgehog signaling, and regulate AC5 biology, yet those axes were silent in these mature mouse brain contrasts.
main_caveats: Weak Kctd1 engagement can hide pathway effects; AC5/cAMP can be regulated post-transcriptionally; the exact literature cell types differ from this neuronal panel.

summary: Kctd1 lacked a robust convergent signature neighbor and did not phenocopy the screened KCTD-family perturbations Kctd8 or Kctd16.
why_it_matters: The significant Resp18/Cluap1 rows should not be treated as the visible tip of a larger KCTD-family or cross-perturbation module.
main_caveats: KCTD15, the most relevant KCTD1 partner, was not a screened perturbation; Kctd8 and Kctd16 are broader family comparators.

summary: The Kctd1 dataset does not provide a pathway-aligned or druggability-aligned rationale for neuronal KCTD1 targeting.
why_it_matters: Sparse DE, absent target-transcript engagement, no robust signature neighbor, and no ChEMBL KCTD1 target record argue against making a therapeutic nomination from this result alone.
main_caveats: ChEMBL absence is not proof of undruggability, and the screen may have under-perturbed Kctd1.

direction: no robust differential expression; target transcript not reduced
summary: Csrnp3 perturbation produced a dataset-wide null or buffered transcriptomic phenotype: the Csrnp3 mRNA itself was not detectably reduced and no downstream gene reached FDR<0.05 in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: The primary interpretable result is absence of a robust acute RNA program, so isolated nominal genes should not be treated as a Csrnp3 target network unless target engagement is independently verified.
main_caveats: Target mRNA is an imperfect engagement marker for protein-disrupting perturbations; the parquet lacks guide-level indel or protein measurements.

summary: The Csrnp3 cell-type pattern consisted only of isolated nominal peaks, including examples in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 308 CB GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, rather than reproducible FDR-resolved programs.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-calling cell-type selectivity from scalar ranks: the top cortical, cerebellar, and thalamic hits each disappear under multiple testing or remain near-threshold and do not recur by gene or direction across classes.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|308 CB GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The named genes are nominal only; the finding is the absence of a robust recurring module, not validation of those genes as biomarkers.

direction: no strong positive or negative convergence
summary: Csrnp3 had no informative positive or negative perturbation neighbor: the most extreme same-cell signature correlations to other targets were only r=0.125 and r=-0.107.
why_it_matters: If the Csrnp3 vector is mostly noise or buffering, similarity searches can elevate unrelated targets or internal controls; the screen offers no evidence for convergence with a receptor, complex, disease family, or pathway-neighbor module.
main_caveats: Correlations used Wilcoxon score vectors from the same parquet and were not replicated with an external perturbation dataset.

summary: CSRNP-family redundancy provides a plausible explanation for a Csrnp3-only null, but the dataset does not show acute Csrnp1 or Csrnp2 mRNA induction as the buffering mechanism.
why_it_matters: Literature indicates CSRNP members can compensate genetically; this dataset narrows that idea by showing that any compensation in these brain cell classes is not a simple transcript-level switch-on of the two closest family members.
main_caveats: Csrnp1 and Csrnp2 were measured as transcripts but were not perturbation targets, and buffering could be constitutive, protein-level, or developmental.

direction: overexpression apoptosis literature not reproduced after Csrnp3 perturbation
summary: The Perturb-seq loss-perturbation signatures do not recapitulate the DNA-binding/transactivation and apoptosis biology reported for CSRNP3/TAIP2 overexpression assays.
why_it_matters: CSRNP3 can be nuclear, DNA-binding, and cell-death competent in biochemical or overexpression systems, but those properties did not translate into an acute corrected apoptosis-like RNA output here.
main_caveats: The literature perturbs TAIP2 by overexpression whereas this dataset tests a Csrnp3 loss perturbation with weak mRNA-level target engagement.

summary: Aifm1 failed to generate an FDR-significant single-cell transcriptomic state in all 20 assayed cell types, and the Aifm1 transcript itself was only weakly and nominally reduced.
why_it_matters: AIFM1 is a mitochondrial oxidoreductase/apoptosis protein annotated to respiratory-chain assembly and AIF-CHCHD4 biology, so the principal result is a high-confidence dataset null rather than an OXPHOS or death signature.
main_caveats: Aifm1 mRNA is an imperfect proxy for gene editing at the protein level; most cell types had only 26-52 perturbed cells, and the assay has no protein, respiration, or apoptosis readout.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the clearest nominal on-target context for Aifm1, but even there Aifm1 had FDR=1 and no downstream gene reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The apparent thalamic skew should be treated as a prioritization hint, not as evidence for a resolved Aifm1-sensitive neuronal subtype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The finding is based on nominal self-transcript behavior; the assayed cell type is broad and FDR correction erased all detected genes.

summary: Mitochondrial neighbors Hspa9, Dnm1l, and Opa1 produced broad differential-expression programs in thalamic and midbrain classes where Aifm1 remained silent.
why_it_matters: The Aifm1 null is not simply a failure of the dataset to detect mitochondrial perturbations; other mitochondrial proteostasis and dynamics perturbations were readily detected in the same atlas.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: These are functional mitochondrial neighbors, not obligate AIFM1 complex members; their guide efficiencies and loss-of-function mechanisms may differ from Aifm1.

summary: Respiratory-chain and intermembrane-space comparator perturbations in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut often showed strong self-transcript loss but only the targeted transcript at FDR<0.05, whereas Aifm1 did not even reach self-transcript FDR significance.
why_it_matters: Known AIFM1 biology flows through CHCHD4-dependent import and respiratory-chain biogenesis, but this steady-state mRNA assay only weakly reports that protein-assembly axis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The direct AIFM1 partner CHCHD4 was absent from the library, and respiratory-chain failure is usually a protein-complex and metabolic phenotype rather than a guaranteed mRNA program.

summary: The acute mouse neuronal Perturb-seq data do not phenocopy chronic AIFM1-linked neurodegenerative disease at the mRNA level.
why_it_matters: Human AIFM1 variants and the mouse Harlequin hypomorph implicate long-timescale mitochondrial and neuronal vulnerability; a null acute mRNA signature should therefore not be read as evidence that Aifm1 loss is benign.
main_caveats: Species, developmental stage, partial versus complete loss, chronicity, and molecular readout differ from patient disease and Harlequin mouse studies.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor analysis found no robust Aifm1 convergence with assayed perturbations, and several direct literature comparators were not in the perturbation library.
why_it_matters: The absence of a strong positive or negative neighbor prevents assignment of the weak Aifm1 rows to a surrogate apoptosis, CHCHD4, or respiratory-chain module.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on already weak Aifm1 signatures; the best non-self neighbor occurred in 308 CB GABA, where Aifm1 itself had a positive, nonsignificant self-transcript estimate.

summary: Gtf2ird1 produced its only FDR 0.05 downstream response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The perturbation is not broadly active across measured neuronal classes; the interpretable positive signal is a sparse thalamic glutamatergic response led by F11r, Sparcl1, Rab30, and Abca3.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not FDR-depleted, and the output set is only four genes at FDR 0.05 and seven at FDR 0.10.

summary: Most measured classes showed weak target-transcript engagement and no genome-wide response.
why_it_matters: For a nuclear transcriptional regulator, the screen mainly reports a buffered or weak response rather than a broad knockdown-like transcriptional collapse.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an imperfect readout of CRISPR coding perturbations; many classes had fewer than 100 perturbed cells.

summary: The thalamic Gtf2ird1 signature was not interchangeable with Gtf2i or Williams-region comparator signatures.
why_it_matters: Although Gtf2ird1 and Gtf2i are related Williams-region transcription factors, the mouse-brain Perturb-seq output separates Gtf2ird1 from Gtf2i, Baz1b, Clip2, Limk1, Fzd9, and Eif4h.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to one broad thalamic class and based on signed-score correlations; a near-zero Perturb-seq signature does not exclude shared developmental roles.

summary: F11r, Sparcl1, Rab30, and Abca3 are exploratory thalamic readouts of Gtf2ird1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: These genes provide a compact candidate marker set for follow-up in thalamic glutamatergic neurons without claiming that they are direct GTF2IRD1 targets or a canonical Williams-syndrome pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The marker hypothesis is transcriptomic only and needs guide-level replication, perturbation validation, and direct binding or rescue evidence.

summary: The only non-thalamic FDR 0.10 outliers were isolated Cckbr and Smarcc2 rows, not coherent cell-type programs.
why_it_matters: L5 extratelencephalic cortical and CNU-MGE GABA classes should be logged as borderline contexts, but the data do not support elevating either to a positive Gtf2ird1 response at FDR 0.05.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Both genes are FDR 0.10, not FDR 0.05, and neither is recurrent across classes in this perturbation.

summary: Il1rapl1 perturbation produced weak on-target RNA engagement and almost no FDR-level downstream transcriptomic response across 22 measured brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The result is a negative but interpretable Perturb-seq outcome: established IL1RAPL1 loss changes synapses, yet this mRNA assay mostly buffered the perturbation or failed to capture sufficient target loss.
main_caveats: Target transcript was not FDR-depleted in any cell type, so weak editing or target detectability could contribute to the buffered RNA phenotype.

summary: The only FDR-significant downstream genes were Taok3 up in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Kcnma1 up in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The high-confidence RNA hits were isolated to non-cortical classes rather than to the cortical glutamatergic cultures and cortex emphasized in much of the IL1RAPL1 literature.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Each cell type had only one FDR hit, the 110 contrast had only 32 perturbed cells, and the Il1rapl1 target row was FDR-negative in both contrasts.

summary: Known physical, paralogous, IL-1-family, and synaptic neighboring perturbations did not phenocopy Il1rapl1 at the transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: PTPδ is a direct, splice-dependent IL1RAPL1 partner, so the near-zero Ptprd and Il1rapl1 signature correlations argue that the core trans-synaptic mechanism is not represented as a shared RNA state in this dataset.
main_caveats: Signature correlations were computed from scRNA DE scores rather than protein localization or cell-contact phenotypes; pathway activity may be splice-, phosphorylation-, or compartment-dependent.

summary: A nominal, mixed-direction synaptic adhesion and vesicle module appeared in a small set of cell types.
why_it_matters: The module is closer to the known synaptogenic role of IL1RAPL1 than the two FDR hits and nominates follow-up markers for protein or morphology validation.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All genes in this module were nominal only with FDR=1.0, and the affected gene set was not recurrent across most cell types.

summary: Adcy5 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any of 22 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: This prevents assignment of a robust Adcy5-dependent gene module despite strong prior evidence that AC5 is a central cAMP effector in striatal neurons.
main_caveats: The negative result is transcriptomic and coincides with weak target-transcript engagement.

summary: Adcy5 target-transcript reduction was weak, purely nominal, and most evident in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA rather than pan-neuronal.
why_it_matters: A downstream null phenotype is hard to interpret when the target RNA itself is not significantly depleted.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: FDR was 1.0 for every Adcy5 self-test; some cell types had fewer than 40 perturbed cells.

summary: Adcy3 self-repression was FDR-significant in midbrain classes where Adcy5 self-repression was weak and nonsignificant.
why_it_matters: The paralog contrast argues that the screen can detect an adenylyl-cyclase transcript when engagement is strong, and that Adcy5 and Adcy3 should not be treated as interchangeable perturbations.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is based on self-transcript engagement, not matched cAMP activity or shared downstream FDR modules.

summary: The Adcy5 gene-disruption signature is too weak to validate or reject AC5 inhibition as a strategy for gain-of-function ADCY5 movement disorder.
why_it_matters: Human ADCY5 dyskinesia often involves increased AC5 signaling, whereas this dataset supplies a weak loss-of-transcript perturbation with no FDR-level cAMP/CREB response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No cAMP or AC5 enzymatic activity was measured, and the disease direction is not modeled by a weak knockout-like perturbation.

summary: Adcy2 rose nominally in the 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA profile in which Adcy5 showed its best nominal reduction.
why_it_matters: The opposite Adcy5/Adcy2 direction could mark adenylyl-cyclase isoform compensation and is aligned with Adcy5-null mouse evidence for small induction of other cyclase isoforms.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Adcy2 p=0.006 and Adcy5 p=0.00497 were nominal only with FDR=1.0; the cited mouse paper did not establish Adcy2 specifically as the compensating isoform in this cell class.

summary: In 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, the restricted Adcy5 top-gene signature opposed several cAMP/G-protein neighbors, but the effect was weak genome-wide and confounded by safe-target neighbors.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-interpretation of top-rank signature neighbors as biological Gs/Gi pathway activity scores when the primary Adcy5 perturbation is itself weak.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on the Adcy5 top-200 absolute-score genes; whole-transcriptome correlations were small and safe-target controls were also prominent.

summary: Kat6a perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional program across 22 mouse-brain cell types despite target-transcript measurement in every profile.
why_it_matters: A disease-linked histone acetyltransferase was much quieter than expected from its core chromatin function, so the main biological readout is buffering or inadequate acute engagement rather than a pathway activation signature.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not significantly depleted after FDR correction; transcript abundance may not perfectly measure perturbation at the protein or chromatin-mark level.

summary: No Kat6a cell type passed FDR correction; 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 001 L5-6 IT Glut were nominal-only high-score contexts.
why_it_matters: The screen gives no statistically secure cell-type-selective Kat6a response, but it identifies which apparent hotspots are most likely to be false starts for follow-up.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: All highlighted genes failed FDR<0.05; 001 L5-6 IT Glut had only 23 Kat6a cells.

summary: The directly assayed KAT6 paralog/complex neighborhood was weak, whereas several other chromatin regulators were strongly active in the same parquet.
why_it_matters: Kat6a flatness is not explained by a general inability of the experiment to detect chromatin-regulator phenotypes; it is concentrated around Kat6a, Kat6b, and Brd1/Brpf2.
main_caveats: BRPF1, BRPF3, ING5, and MEAF6 were not assayed as perturbation targets, and BRD1 had a small but nonzero corrected response.

summary: Kat6a nominal outliers were idiosyncratic rather than a recurrent multi-cell-type transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of visually large Wilcoxon scores as a shared Kat6a program when the same genes do not recur after thresholding.
main_caveats: The recurrence test used an exploratory |score|>3 threshold and does not exclude rare cell-type-restricted effects.

summary: Rspo2/Wnt and TP53-response genes were measured but not altered in the Kat6a CA3/CA2/DG glutamatergic profile.
why_it_matters: A reported Kat6a-to-RSPO2/Wnt cognitive mechanism and curated TP53 acetylation pathway do not appear as acute bulk transcriptomic readouts in this pooled brain class.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Only 58 Kat6a cells were assayed in a pooled CA3/CA2/DG class with weak Kat6a transcript engagement; the literature used a stronger and more specific KAT6A-deficiency context.

summary: Neuronal Kat6a/Kat6b transcriptomic flatness should not be used as evidence that pharmacologic KAT6A/B inhibition is inert in the brain or that oncology inhibitor biology will translate to neurons.
why_it_matters: KAT6A/B are druggable acetyltransferases in senescence-based cancer models, but this dataset lacks the engagement and assay endpoints needed to evaluate that therapeutic direction.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq data are transcriptomic and neuronal; the inhibitor literature used catalytic inhibitors in cancer models and is pharmacologically rather than genetically matched.

summary: Aopep sgRNAs did not create convincing knockdown of the measured Aopep transcript in any profiled cell class.
why_it_matters: The central dataset limitation is target engagement: a flat transcriptome after an unverified perturbation should not be read as proof that AOPEP loss is silent.
main_caveats: Only mRNA was measured; the data cannot test AOPEP protein abundance or catalytic inhibition.

summary: No Aopep target-cell signature contained a gene passing FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The perturbation lacks a reproducible genome-wide transcriptional response; nominal top genes such as Sec24a should be treated as leads, not pathway evidence.
main_caveats: Many tests had fewer than 50 perturbed cells, and weak Aopep engagement prevents separation of failed perturbation from a genuinely buffered AOPEP loss-of-function state.

summary: The basal forebrain/hypothalamic GABA class 066 had the only nominal Aopep decrease, but it still had no FDR-supported downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This weakly marks 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA as the only cell class worth re-testing, while arguing that the present neuronal panel does not reveal a robust AOPEP-responsive cell type.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The on-target row was not FDR-significant and the broad dataset did not include an explicit vascular cell population described in prior Aopep work.

summary: Aopep signatures did not resemble Agtr1a, Agtr2, or Agtrap perturbations despite database and prior vascular/RAS context for AOPEP.
why_it_matters: The mouse-brain perturbation does not support collapsing Aopep with renin-angiotensin receptor-adjacent transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: The RAS link is indirect and the Aopep signature itself is weak, so this is a failure to find similarity rather than evidence against a biochemical substrate relationship.

summary: Aopep did not converge transcriptionally with selected dystonia-gene perturbations Gnal, Kmt2b, Thap1, or Vps41.
why_it_matters: Human AOPEP loss-of-function causes recessive dystonia, but these mouse Perturb-seq signatures do not expose a shared immediate transcriptomic module with other dystonia genes.
main_caveats: Low correlation is heavily conditioned on weak Aopep target engagement and does not exclude shared protein-level, developmental, or circuit mechanisms.

summary: The nearest whole-signature neighbors of Aopep were weak, cerebellar-GABA-localized correlations rather than a recurrent convergent module.
why_it_matters: Even the best unbiased perturbation neighbors are too weak to nominate Zic3, Wdr26, or Ranbp2 as AOPEP pathway partners from this dataset alone.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All reported correlations were |r|<=0.230 and occurred where Aopep itself trended upward, not down.

summary: Ifnar1 loss produced a globally buffered transcriptional phenotype: no assayed cell type contained an FDR-significant gene and the target transcript itself was only weakly reduced.
why_it_matters: This makes the target a negative/buffered result rather than a strong basal interferon regulator in the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
main_caveats: All perturbed groups had only 25-127 cells, the Ifnar1 transcript was not FDR-significantly knocked down, and the assay did not include an exogenous type I interferon stimulus.

summary: The canonical IFNAR-JAK/STAT antiviral module was not detectably repressed after Ifnar1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: IFNAR1 is expected to feed STAT1/STAT2/IRF9-dependent interferon-stimulated genes after ligand engagement, so the absence of basal ISG movement argues that pathway output is either inactive, redundant, or below detection in this context.
main_caveats: The canonical gene list was manually selected and transcriptomic; absence of a basal decrease does not rule out acute phospho-STAT defects after IFN-alpha or IFN-beta stimulation.

summary: CA3-family glutamatergic and CNU-MGE GABA neurons carried the densest nominal Ifnar1 tails, but the genes were noncanonical and did not reach FDR significance.
why_it_matters: The nominal tails nominate follow-up cell types and genes, while their lack of FDR support prevents them from being treated as established cell-type-specific IFNAR biology.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Nominal p-value concentration only; FDR minima were 0.107 in CA3 and 0.182 in CNU-MGE GABA, with 43-52 perturbed cells.

summary: Ifnar1 did not converge transcriptionally with Ifnar2, STAT/IRF pathway neighbors, IFN-gamma receptor subunits, IL10 receptor family members, or any high-correlation library neighbor.
why_it_matters: A simple pathway guilt-by-association interpretation failed in the dataset; the Ifnar1 rows are best interpreted as weakly engaged and idiosyncratic rather than as a clean type I IFN receptor signature.
main_caveats: Signature correlations were computed from same-cell-type Wilcoxon scores; several comparator perturbations, especially Ifnar2, also showed weak target engagement.

summary: The muted neuronal phenotype should not be read as evidence that IFNAR1 inhibition is biologically inert or uniformly safe.
why_it_matters: IFNAR1 blockade is clinically useful in IFN-high autoimmunity and can suppress chronic cerebral interferonopathy, but IFNAR1 is also protective against viral spread in neurons; the present dataset samples basal unchallenged neuronal states rather than IFN-high or infected states.
main_caveats: Clinical and infection studies differ in species, disease state, ligand tone, cell composition, and intervention modality from this Perturb-seq screen.

direction: up in 005; no FDR-significant genes elsewhere
summary: Kcnb1 produced a compact FDR-significant transcriptional response only in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, where Bdnf, Vgf, Zbtb16, Scg2 and Nptx2 were all upregulated.
why_it_matters: Kv2.1 is broadly neuronal, so the screen localizes the strongest acute RNA response to one cortical intratelencephalic context instead of showing uniform sensitivity across every Kcnb1-expressing class.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Other cortical glutamatergic classes showed only nominal recurrence, and Kcnb1 protein or electrophysiology was not measured.

summary: The robust 005 response converged on an activity-dependent neurotrophin/secretory plasticity module rather than on a broad stress or cell-death program.
why_it_matters: Upregulation of Bdnf, Vgf, Scg2 and Nptx2 links Kcnb1 perturbation to neuronal activity and synaptic-plasticity transcription, the direction expected when a delayed-rectifier K+ conductance that restrains firing is impaired.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The dataset is transcriptomic; it did not directly record firing, Kv2.1 gating, or BDNF secretion.

summary: The Kcnb1 mRNA itself did not show FDR-significant depletion in any of the 22 matched cell-type tests.
why_it_matters: The L4/5 downstream signature is biologically coherent, but its interpretation is limited because target engagement cannot be verified from the measured Kcnb1 transcript.
main_caveats: Absence of transcript knockdown does not exclude effects on unmeasured isoforms or protein, but it is the main dataset-level caveat.

summary: Nominal induction of Kcns2 and Kcnma1 in the Kcnb1 L4/5 signature suggests exploratory potassium-channel compensation.
why_it_matters: KCNS2/Kv9.2 is a regulatory Kv subunit that can assemble with KCNB1/KCNB2, so even weak Kcns2 induction points to remodeling of delayed-rectifier channel composition as a plausible homeostatic follow-up to Kv2.1 perturbation.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Kcns2 and Kcnma1 did not pass FDR correction, and no channel-complex stoichiometry was assayed.

summary: The Kv2 paralog Kcnb2 did not phenocopy Kcnb1 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: KCNB1 and KCNB2 can occupy related delayed-rectifier channel complexes, but the low Kcnb2--Kcnb1 signature correlation argues that the L4/5 Bdnf/Vgf/Nptx2 response is not a generic consequence of perturbing any Kv2-family paralog in this dataset.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Kcnb2 also lacked significant on-target transcript depletion, so the contrast may underestimate true Kcnb2 biology.

direction: Kcnb1-like for the first group and Kcnb1-opposing for the second
summary: Restricted-signature neighbors split L4/5 comparator perturbations into Kcnb1-like and Kcnb1-opposing groups.
why_it_matters: Kcnb1 was positively aligned with Grin2a, Arhgef9, Gabrb3, Kcnq2, Gabrg2 and Scn2a, but opposed to Grin2b, Ank3, Syngap1, Shank2, Camk2a and Kcnd3, so the named perturbations should not be collapsed into a single direction of transcriptomic effect.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: This used only Kcnb1's top 100 genes in a single cell type; several correlated comparator signatures had few or no FDR-significant downstream genes.

summary: Kv2.1 negative modulation or loss-of-function is directionally plausible to induce a L4/5 Bdnf/Vgf/Nptx2 activity program and should be distinguished from rescue of KCNB1 disease variants.
why_it_matters: KCNB1 disorders arise from function-altering channel variants, and ChEMBL already contains Kv2.1 blocker assays; the dataset cautions that simple channel blockade could mimic part of the Kcnb1-loss transcriptional state rather than reverse it.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The screen did not test drugs or human disease variants; the target transcript was not detectably knocked down.

direction: partial Dip2b down; no FDR-significant downstream expression response
summary: Dip2b perturbation caused only a buffered transcriptomic response despite nominal target-RNA depletion in a subset of cells.
why_it_matters: The adult single-cell transcriptional state did not strongly amplify a 0.56-0.67 logFC Dip2b target decrease into FDR-significant gene-expression changes.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: On-target depletion was nominal rather than FDR-significant, protein loss and tubulin acetylation were not measured, and the downstream claim is a negative result.

direction: target engagement concentrated outside the measured hippocampal-associated and L2/3 IT bins
summary: The clearest Dip2b target-transcript knockdown was in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut rather than the hippocampal-associated or L2/3 IT bins emphasized by prior hippocampal culture work.
why_it_matters: This separates true Dip2b biology from a major technical determinant: many expected glutamatergic populations cannot be interpreted mechanistically because the target RNA was only weakly shifted there.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity may reflect guide capture, cell number, or basal expression differences rather than intrinsic Dip2b-dependence.

direction: Camsap2 up after Dip2b perturbation in 110
summary: Camsap2 was an exploratory microtubule-state marker for Dip2b perturbation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: CAMSAP2 is itself a neuronal microtubule minus-end stabilizer, so its up-regulation is the one nominal 110 signal that biologically aligns with the known DIP2B/tubulin axis.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Camsap2 reached FDR=0.107, not FDR<0.05, and the marker was not recurrent across cell types.

summary: Dip2b signatures were essentially orthogonal to perturbations of measured tubulin components and fragile-site/neurodevelopmental genes.
why_it_matters: DIP2B binds α-tubulin, but the mouse-brain transcriptomes did not look like Tuba1a or Tubb3 perturbation and also did not converge with Fmr1 or Aff2, arguing that the observed adult response is not a generic tubulin or fragile-site disease signature.
main_caveats: The Dip2b signature itself was weak; Dip2a, Dip2c, ATAT1, HDAC6, and DMAP1 were absent as perturbations, so the closest mechanistic comparators were unavailable.

direction: acute adult perturbation weaker than chronic developmental models
summary: The Perturb-seq result is more consistent with developmental or chronic DIP2B deficiency than with a large acute adult transcriptional collapse.
why_it_matters: Human FRA12A and mESC knockout reports implicate reduced DIP2B in neurodevelopmental phenotypes, while this dataset shows that partial adult Dip2b mRNA depletion leaves only nominal cell-state changes.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The dataset cannot distinguish inadequate protein knockdown from true compensation and does not assay developmental neural induction or axon morphology.

summary: Cntnap2 knockdown produced FDR-supported loss of its own transcript in only 5 of 22 profiled cell classes, concentrated in Pvalb, thalamic/habenular, and midbrain or brainstem-associated classes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation is interpretable in those classes, but cortical and hippocampal classes cannot be assumed to have strong target engagement from this transcript readout.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cntnap2 mRNA depletion is only a transcript-level target-engagement proxy; low basal expression or dropout can hide successful guide activity in some classes.

summary: The five classes with the clearest Cntnap2 transcript depletion had no non-target gene that survived FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: Cntnap2 transcript depletion did not coincide with a broad, cell-autonomous transcriptional cascade at this Perturb-seq endpoint, even where the target mRNA itself was detectably reduced.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: RNA-seq cannot test CASPR2 protein localization, Kv1-channel clustering, electrophysiology, or axonal compartment morphology.

summary: Cntnap2 perturbation did not produce a recurrent non-target transcriptomic module across cell classes.
why_it_matters: The nominal DE tail appears cell-class-specific or noisy rather than a shared Cntnap2 response pathway suitable for pooled pathway interpretation.
main_caveats: This statement uses a nominal p<0.001 recurrence screen; weaker polygenic effects below that threshold could still exist.

summary: Cntnap2 depletion was uncoupled from mRNA changes in Kcna1, Kcna2, and Dpp6 in the target-engaged classes.
why_it_matters: The canonical CASPR2/Kv1-channel relationship is post-transcriptional and spatial; Kcna1 or Kcna2 transcript abundance is therefore a poor response biomarker for this perturbation in the assayed cells.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay measured whole-cell mRNA, not channel localization at juxtaparanodes or Kv1 protein abundance.

summary: Cntnap1 and Cntn1 perturbations converged with Cntnap2 on strong self-transcript depletion with little or no FDR-supported downstream DE.
why_it_matters: The buffered phenotype is not unique to Cntnap2; it also appears in adjacent contactin/Caspr axo-glial adhesion genes in the same Perturb-seq table.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Cntnap1/Cntn1 were used as related adhesion comparators, not as direct Cntnap2 complex members; the comparison uses FDR hit counts rather than full matched signature correlations.

summary: Rbfox2 down-regulation in 001 L5-6 IT Glut was the only non-target transcriptome hit at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: This is the sole FDR-supported candidate marker of a Cntnap2 perturbation response outside the target transcript, but its biological status is hypothesis-generating because Cntnap2 itself was not measurably depleted in that class.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript had p=0.382 and FDR=1.0 in the same L5-6 IT contrast, so this row could reflect an indirect, context-specific, or guide-composition effect.

summary: The Perturb-seq signature refines CNTNAP2 disease models toward structural, developmental, or electrophysiologic mechanisms rather than a large endpoint transcriptional stress program.
why_it_matters: CNTNAP2 loss is genetically and experimentally linked to epilepsy and autism-related phenotypes, but this dataset suggests those phenotypes are unlikely to be explained by a conserved, high-amplitude cell-autonomous mRNA module downstream of Cntnap2 depletion at the assayed endpoint.
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure developmental timing, circuit wiring, migration, protein localization, or seizures; it only constrains the bulk mRNA response within recovered single cells.

summary: Gabrb3 RNA was reproducibly reduced, but the perturbation produced no FDR-supported trans-gene program in any tested neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The strongest measured effect was target engagement itself; this points to a channel/receptor perturbation whose immediate consequences are not captured as a robust steady-state mRNA pathway in the sampled classes.
main_caveats: The analysis uses precomputed Wilcoxon gene-level tests; 13 of 21 strata had fewer than 40 perturbed cells, so weak downstream effects may be underpowered.

summary: The clearest direct transcript loss was concentrated in L4/5 IT cortical and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, with near-threshold or nominal effects in thalamic glutamatergic and midbrain GABAergic neurons.
why_it_matters: Literature emphasizes Gabrb3 requirements in particular developing projection-neuron circuits, so the dataset supports RNA engagement in major neuronal classes but does not resolve the finer projection subtypes expected to carry circuit phenotypes.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Differential FDR strength is confounded by cell count, endogenous expression, and guide performance; it should not be read as a definitive expression atlas.

summary: Gabrb3 did not share a coherent transcriptional signature with other GABA-A receptor subunits or inhibitory postsynaptic neighbors despite belonging to the same receptor/synapse biology.
why_it_matters: Physical receptor membership did not imply interchangeability at the perturbational transcriptome level; Gabrb3 loss, other subunit loss, and scaffold-neighbor loss mostly produced self-limited or uncorrelated RNA signatures.
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptomic and many individual comparator signatures were themselves weak; electrophysiology or receptor-surface measurements could still converge.

summary: The dataset models a Gabrb3-loss direction, which is aligned with many epilepsy loss-of-function mechanisms but opposite to positive allosteric enhancement of GABA-A receptor function.
why_it_matters: Human GABRB3 disease is direction-sensitive; absence of a compensatory GABA-module mRNA increase means rescue biomarkers should not be inferred from these knockdown-like transcriptomes.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: CRISPR-scale RNA reduction is not equivalent to patient missense gain- or loss-of-function, chronic developmental disease, or acute pharmacologic potentiation.

summary: Afg3l2 knockdown was partial and the acute transcriptome was almost silent.
why_it_matters: The screen supports a buffered or under-engaged phenotype rather than the broad mitochondrial failure expected from complete loss of an essential m-AAA protease.
main_caveats: No target-transcript row reached FDR<0.05 and mRNA does not measure m-AAA protein or activity.

summary: The best nominal Afg3l2 repression in Pvalb, hypothalamic GABA, midbrain glutamatergic, and thalamic glutamatergic neurons produced no FDR-significant trans program.
why_it_matters: Sparse output persisted even where target mRNA was most detectably reduced.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Engagement was nominal and may not deplete a stable mitochondrial complex.

summary: Cdh7 down-regulation in L2/3 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons was the sole genome-wide significant Afg3l2-associated hit.
why_it_matters: Cdh7 is the clearest cell-type-restricted sentinel of the Afg3l2 perturbation, but remains a hypothesis-generating marker.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Afg3l2 itself was only nominally reduced in this cell type; Cdh7 was not recurrent elsewhere.

summary: Canonical mitochondrial stress, OPA1-processing, and fission/fusion transcripts were not induced after Afg3l2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Known AFG3L2 biology is mainly proteolytic, so the mRNA readout did not report a compensatory mitochondrial stress module.
main_caveats: No mRNA induction does not rule out altered cleavage or abundance of OPA1, EMRE, or other substrates.

summary: Afg3l2 did not transcriptionally phenocopy Opa1 or available mitochondrial protease/import neighbors.
why_it_matters: The data argue against assuming that upstream m-AAA protease knockdown mimics direct Opa1 depletion in an acute transcriptomic assay.
main_caveats: Spg7, Afg3l1, and Oma1 were not perturbed; weak Afg3l2 engagement could mask convergence.

summary: Cerebellar GABA cells showed no acute Afg3l2 DE program despite the Purkinje-cell bias of AFG3L2 disease models.
why_it_matters: The screen likely under-models the chronic, stronger Afg3l2 loss needed for spinocerebellar-ataxia biology.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA is broad and not purified Purkinje cells; knockdown was only nominal.

summary: A near-silent acute transcriptome should not be read as evidence that reducing AFG3L2 activity is safe or therapeutic.
why_it_matters: Human genetics and mouse loss-of-function studies point to neuronal toxicity from impaired AFG3L2 dosage or function.
main_caveats: The dataset contains no pharmacologic or long-term neurodegeneration endpoint.

summary: Mphosph9 perturbation showed weak, inconsistent on-target mRNA depletion and no FDR-significant transcriptional consequence.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is limited target engagement rather than a strong silent knockout; all downstream claims must therefore stay nominal or negative.
main_caveats: Mphosph9 mRNA is only a proxy for MPP9 protein depletion; the dataset lacks direct guide-efficiency and protein readouts.

summary: The curated MPHOSPH9-CP110-CEP97 ciliogenesis mechanism did not appear as a reproducible mRNA program after Mphosph9 perturbation.
why_it_matters: MPHOSPH9 is a centriolar negative regulator of ciliogenesis, so the lack of significant changes in Ccp110, Cep97, Kif24, Ttbk2, Cep83, Cep164, Cep290, or Ift88 argues that this Perturb-seq assay is not reading out the known protein-localization mechanism.
main_caveats: Weak target depletion and an RNA end point cannot exclude altered centriole localization, ciliogenesis, or ciliary morphology.

summary: Mphosph9 signatures did not converge with ciliary-neighborhood perturbations that were present in the library.
why_it_matters: The direct CP110-CEP97-KIF24 branch was not available as perturbation targets, but neighboring ciliogenesis genes also failed to reveal a shared transcriptomic state, reducing confidence in a hidden ciliary module.
main_caveats: Comparators are ciliary-neighborhood genes rather than the direct MPHOSPH9 interactors CCP110, CEP97, and KIF24; all signatures are weak.

summary: The only plausible on-target nominal responses concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: These two glutamatergic classes combined the largest Mphosph9 cell counts with the strongest nominal target-transcript decreases, making them the least underpowered contexts for follow-up despite the absence of any corrected hit.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All listed secondary genes had FDR=1.0; this is a prioritization of weak same-dataset signals, not a validated cell-type phenotype.

summary: The largest scalar outliers were disconnected from cells with measurable Mphosph9 self-depletion.
why_it_matters: 308 CB GABA and 217 P MY Pineal Glut contained some of the smallest nominal p values, but the target transcript was unchanged, so ranking by nominal p value alone would overstate off-context peaks.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The outlier genes are nominal and mostly FDR=1.0; 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 23 perturbed cells.

summary: Ctnna2 perturbation produced no genome-wide significant differential-expression response in any reported cell type.
why_it_matters: A protein with strong neuronal adhesion and morphogenesis literature did not yield an acute high-confidence transcriptomic program in this assay, so individual nominal genes should not be read as a Ctnna2 pathway without orthogonal support.
main_caveats: The target transcript was only modestly reduced and never significant after correction.

summary: The detectable on-target signal was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, but even these two best cell types showed only nominal Ctnna2 depletion.
why_it_matters: Downstream-null interpretations are strongest in these two higher-cell-count contexts; null calls in small or weakly engaged cell types are less informative.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Transcript knockdown, guide activity per cell, and protein depletion were not available in the Wilcoxon summary file.

summary: Ctnna2 did not activate or suppress the thalamic beta-catenin/APC transcriptional module that was obvious after Apc and Ctnnb1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Although CTNNA2 sits in the cadherin-catenin adhesome, the Perturb-seq response separates alpha-N-catenin from the Wnt/APC beta-catenin transcriptional arm.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is a transcriptional comparison in one strongest related-response cell type, not a direct biochemical Wnt assay; Ctnna2 engagement was partial.

summary: The assayed partial Ctnna2 knockdown did not induce a transcriptional ARP2/3 or actin-branching signature despite literature linking complete CTNNA2 loss to ARP2/3 overactivity and cortical migration disease.
why_it_matters: CTNNA2 disease biology is likely to depend on developmental timing, protein-level actin regulation, cell migration, or spine morphology that this acute DE readout is poorly positioned to capture.

summary: Whole-dataset signature search found no robust positive or inverse Ctnna2 neighbor.

summary: The canonical immune KLF13-CCL5 axis is not detectably engaged by Klf13 perturbation in the strongest neuronal class.

summary: Genome-scale signature-neighbor searches found no strong positive or negative phenocopy of Klf13 in the two leading nominal cell classes.

summary: Cdk13 perturbation repeatedly induced Rnpc3 and Amy1 and repressed Bend6 across many cell types rather than causing a broad expression collapse.

main_caveats: RNA processing is inferred only from gene identity and prior CDK13 biology; the dataset does not measure splicing, CTD phosphorylation, or direct CDK13 substrates.

summary: Cdk13 responses were concentrated in thalamic, midbrain, pons/medulla, and hypothalamic/CNU classes, while several other neuronal classes were quiet.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA

summary: Measured Cdk13 transcript depletion was not FDR-supported in any cell type, including the cell types with the strongest downstream responses.

summary: Cdk13 had no close expression phenocopy among 2045 scanned perturbations and was nearly orthogonal to Cdk8, Med12, and Med13.

summary: Neuronal Cdk13 perturbation signatures overlap the same kinase-centered biology that is genetically linked to human CDK13 developmental disorders and chemically targeted by CDK12/13-Cyclin K inhibitors or degraders.
why_it_matters: Any strategy that inhibits CDK13 or removes Cyclin K should consider on-target transcriptional liabilities in neuronal populations, especially because human disease variants already implicate kinase-domain disruption in neurodevelopment.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut

summary: Herc2 targeting produced consistent but weak target-transcript lowering and almost no FDR-supported mRNA cascade.

summary: Herc1, Ube3a, and Igf1r perturbations did not phenocopy Herc2 in matched neuronal contexts.

summary: Brain HERC2 inhibition is directionally risky because the human disease and mouse genetics are loss-of-function while partial neuronal Herc2 knockdown already shifts synaptic/endomembrane transcripts.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq data give no evidence for a beneficial HERC2-loss program, and the literature argues that decreasing HERC2 activity can be deleterious during nervous-system development.
main_caveats: The dataset captures partial acute mRNA perturbation in mouse neurons, whereas human HERC2-related disease is chronic and recessive and no direct HERC2 drug program was identified in ChEMBL.

summary: Iqsec2 perturbation was assayed broadly but was weakly target-engaged and almost transcriptionally silent, with only Arfgap1 at FDR<0.05 and Cux1 at FDR<0.1 across 388046 rows.

summary: Arfgap1 down-regulation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut was the only FDR-significant Iqsec2 response and points to a one-cell-class ARF-cycle biomarker hypothesis.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

summary: Iqsec2 did not phenocopy NMDAR/PSD-neighbor perturbations even in cell classes where Grin1, Nrxn1, Dlg4, Dlgap4, Grin2b, or Tsc1 perturbations were readily detected.

summary: Lrrn3 knockdown produced no transcriptome-wide FDR-level differential-expression response in any of the 22 matched adult brain cell classes.

main_caveats: Therapeutic tractability was assessed only from public ChEMBL target/mechanism/activity endpoints and not from proprietary degrader or oligonucleotide programs.

summary: No assayed perturbation strongly phenocopied or inverted the Csnk2b signature, and CK2 catalytic complex members were absent.

summary: The largest Hsd17b4 group, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, had the clearest nominal Hsd17b4 mRNA decrease but still no corrected downstream genes.

summary: The mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout did not reproduce chronic HSD17B4/MFP2 cerebellar, ciliary, or glial disease biology.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse loss-of-function literature links HSD17B4/MFP2 to ataxia, Purkinje degeneration, ciliary defects, and glial pathology; the silent 308 CB GABA and 151 TH profiles indicate that this acute neuronal transcriptome dataset should be treated as a model of early cell-autonomous RNA response, not of chronic metabolic storage or Purkinje degeneration.

main_caveats: 308 CB GABA is a broad class rather than purified Purkinje cells, and microglia, astrocytes, lipid accumulation, and cilia were not directly assayed.

summary: The combined dataset and disease literature favor restoration or metabolic bypass of HSD17B4 loss over inhibition, and the Perturb-seq signatures provide no rescue biomarker for monitoring that direction.

main_caveats: The dataset tested loss rather than restoration, did not perturb acetyl-CoA pathways, and therefore cannot rank rescue interventions directly.

summary: Acvr1 perturbation produced reproducible but statistically modest on-target mRNA depletion rather than a uniformly strong knockout-like signature.
why_it_matters: The intended target transcript moved in the expected downward direction in nearly every cell type, but every Acvr1 self-row remained non-significant after gene-wise adjustment, so all downstream biology should be treated as nominal or exploratory.
main_caveats: On-target depletion is inferred from mRNA; protein abundance and BMP-SMAD phosphorylation were not measured.

direction: downstream response buffered after Acvr1 reduction
summary: Even cell types with the clearest Acvr1 transcript loss showed no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome response.
why_it_matters: ACVR1 is a BMP type-I kinase, so depletion of the receptor might have been expected to release a coherent SMAD-dependent transcriptional program; in these broad mouse-brain classes, the measured mRNA response was buffered, redundant, or too weak for FDR detection.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: No phospho-SMAD endpoint was measured, and the Acvr1 self-row itself had adjusted p=1.0.

summary: Canonical BMP-ID/MSX transcriptional readouts were not detectably engaged by Acvr1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: The absence of Id1, Id2, Id3, Id4, Msx1, or Msx2 nominal shifts argues that the nominal Acvr1 signatures are not simply basal BMP-SMAD1/5/8 output running backward.
main_caveats: Some BMP targets are lowly detected in neurons; Smad6 was measured in only two Acvr1 contrasts.

summary: The strongest nominal non-self response was concentrated in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, whereas the clearest Acvr1 self-depletion occurred in 155 MB Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: This decoupling between target-transcript rank and top downstream nominal genes points to a context-specific and noisy response rather than a single recurrent Acvr1 module shared across cortical, thalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain classes.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The finding is driven by nominal p values only; the best adjusted p was 0.0865.

summary: Acvr1 loss was not transcriptomically interchangeable with Bmpr2 loss or with perturbation of nearby BMP/TGF-beta receptor-SMAD genes in the same glutamatergic cell types.
why_it_matters: ACVR1 and BMPR2 are connected in BMP receptor complexes, but depleting BMPR2 gave strong self-targeting while the Acvr1 score vector was almost uncorrelated with Bmpr2 and all tested pathway neighbors in 005 and 155 glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on mRNA differential-expression scores, not on receptor phosphorylation or ligand-response assays.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor search did not reveal a strong positive or negative Acvr1 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The best correlations in the three strongest Acvr1 contexts were only |r|<=0.121 and included unrelated or safe-target perturbations, so no robust convergent module emerged from the scalar signature comparison.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The all-target neighbor scan was restricted to three cell types selected for Acvr1 signal strength.

direction: wild-type loss-of-function is not equivalent to mutant activation
summary: Wild-type mouse-brain Acvr1 knockdown should not be treated as a direct surrogate for ACVR1 activating-mutant disease pharmacology.
why_it_matters: FOP and DIPG are driven by activating or neomorphic ACVR1 mutations, whereas this dataset assayed partial loss of wild-type Acvr1 and showed no clear ID/MSX module; the clinically relevant mutant receptor can use activin A as an aberrant agonist, a direction and ligand context absent from this assay.
main_caveats: The dataset does not include ACVR1-mutant cells, ligand stimulation, heterotopic ossification cell types, or glioma cells.

summary: Il31ra perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic phenotype in the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The main biological result is absence of a detectable central-neuronal IL31RA program, not a specific downstream pathway hit.
main_caveats: The result is high confidence for this DE table, but the table does not prove that every guide achieved protein depletion or that ligand-stimulated peripheral IL31RA biology would be absent.

summary: Osmr, Il6ra, and Il6st perturbations did not reveal a hidden Il31ra-like IL-6-family receptor program.
why_it_matters: OSMR is the direct IL31RA partner; its lack of a correlated response argues that the Il31ra null is not simply a missed single-gene readout but reflects an unengaged receptor branch in these cells.
main_caveats: The comparator perturbations also show weak target-level evidence, so the contrast is informative mainly as an absence of phenocopy rather than a directional mechanistic split.

summary: Canonical JAK/STAT, MAPK, and cytokine-feedback transcripts were uncoupled from Il31ra perturbation.
why_it_matters: IL31RA is expected to signal through JAK/STAT and MAPK after ligand-driven receptor assembly; no basal transcriptional output of that pathway was detectable in the central brain panel.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay tests receptor perturbation without an explicit IL-31 ligand challenge and uses transcript abundance rather than phospho-STAT or phospho-ERK readouts.

summary: The central-brain null narrows IL31RA neuroimmune biology away from the sampled glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic cell classes.
why_it_matters: IL31RA is compelling in itch, skin inflammation, and peripheral sensory neurons, but those contexts are not reproduced by the assayed mouse-brain neurons.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks dorsal-root-ganglion neurons, keratinocytes, and immune cells, so it cannot test the best-matched itch and skin-disease states directly.

summary: A global signature-neighbor scan found only weak Il31ra neighbors, with the largest correlations confined to 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: The scan reduces the risk that a biologically meaningful but subthreshold Il31ra module was missed by single-gene FDR filtering.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from weak score vectors without FDR-supported Il31ra genes; the 308 CB pattern is exploratory.

summary: The dataset does not support central-neuronal transcriptomic biomarkers for IL31RA blockade despite the target's skin-pruritus druggability.
why_it_matters: Clinically successful IL31RA inhibition should not be extrapolated to central brain neuronal programs using this Perturb-seq dataset.
main_caveats: The perturbation direction is genetic loss in mouse central neurons, whereas nemolizumab is an antibody against human IL31RA used in inflammatory skin disease.

summary: Gabrg3 perturbation had no FDR-supported depletion of its own transcript in any profiled mouse brain cell type.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant result: without robust engagement of the target mRNA, the dataset should not be interpreted as a clean gamma-3 GABA-A receptor loss-of-function experiment.
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA, not channel protein or chloride currents; weak transcript depletion could reflect guide inefficiency, low captured expression, or both.

summary: Gabrg3 produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptomic program and only isolated nominal hits.
why_it_matters: The absence of a reproducible DE program means nominal genes such as Lrrc59, Rell2, or Arhgef4 should be treated as hypotheses rather than as a gamma-3 response module.
main_caveats: Multiple small effects may be below power, especially in strata with fewer than 80 perturbed cells.

summary: Gabrg3 was transcriptionally disconnected from better-engaged GABA-A receptor subunit perturbations, including Gabrg2, Gabrd, Gabra1, and Gabrb2.
why_it_matters: Gamma-3 is annotated as a subunit of the same receptor family, but this Perturb-seq profile does not phenocopy gamma-2, delta, alpha, or beta subunit knockdown.
main_caveats: The contrast is dominated by a weak Gabrg3 signature, so it distinguishes non-convergence from true opposite biology.

summary: Gabrg3 cells did not show FDR-supported transcriptional induction of alternative GABA-A receptor subunits or GABAergic synapse genes.
why_it_matters: A successful receptor-subunit perturbation could have triggered receptor replacement or inhibitory-synapse compensation; those programs were not detectable here.
main_caveats: Because on-target Gabrg3 knockdown was weak, this is evidence for absent compensation after the tested perturbation, not after full genetic loss of Gabrg3.

summary: Nearest-neighbor signature analysis found no meaningful Gabrg3 convergence with any perturbation in Pvalb Gaba or in the largest thalamic Gabrg3 stratum.
why_it_matters: The weak nearest-neighbor correlations are consistent with a largely noise-like or biologically buffered Gabrg3 profile and argue against a missed strong upstream pathway neighbor.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor search was restricted to two relevant cell types and used full-score correlations, which are conservative for sparse signatures.

summary: The Gabrg3 null signature should not be used to infer that gamma-3 GABA-A modulation is functionally inert or therapeutically safe.
why_it_matters: GABRG3 sits in a neurodevelopmental GABA-A receptor locus and gamma3-containing receptors are druggable complexes; human GABA-A variants can act through gain, loss, or mixed functional mechanisms that a weak mouse mRNA perturbation cannot resolve.
main_caveats: This is a translational interpretation of a negative experimental signature; it does not test disease variants or acute pharmacology.

summary: Fzd9 perturbation did not produce detectable Fzd9 mRNA knockdown or any FDR-significant downstream gene in the 23 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: The primary result is failed measurable target engagement; without Fzd9 transcript depletion, absence of downstream DE cannot be interpreted as true Fzd9 dispensability.
main_caveats: Failure to reduce Fzd9 mRNA could reflect guide inefficiency, low transcript detection, stable protein abundance, or timing; protein-level receptor loss was not measured.

summary: The few strongest Fzd9 DE rows were isolated nominal singletons rather than a reproducible transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: The sparse nominal hits should not be promoted into a pathway signature because none passed FDR and no gene recurred at nominal p<0.001 across cell classes.
main_caveats: This is a transcript-level negative result and does not exclude non-transcriptional or morphological Fzd9 phenotypes.

summary: The canonical Wnt core was perturbable in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Fzd9 did not activate that transcriptional readout.
why_it_matters: Ctnnb1, Apc, Tcf7l2, Gsk3b, and Lrp6 responses show that Wnt-related perturbations can be detected in this cell class; Fzd9 therefore sits upstream of a competent pathway but was functionally uncoupled or insufficiently knocked down in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Fzd9 lacked on-target mRNA depletion; the result cannot distinguish receptor redundancy from ineffective perturbation.

summary: Hippocampal-containing glutamatergic classes did not show the Fzd9 sensitivity suggested by developmental hippocampal knockout literature.
why_it_matters: Reported Fzd9 roles in dentate-gyrus development and WNT5A-dependent spine formation do not necessarily manifest as an acute mRNA signature in the profiled MEA/LA/CA/DG and CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic classes.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The dataset cell classes are broad and the perturbation did not knock down Fzd9 mRNA; developmental, synaptic, calcium, or morphological endpoints were not assayed.

summary: Fzd9 was much weaker than several stronger Williams-region perturbations, especially Gtf2i, Baz1b, Gtf2ird1, and Eif4h in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The common Williams-Beuren deletion is multigenic, and the dataset separates Fzd9 from interval genes that behave as stronger transcriptional regulators in the same Perturb-seq setting.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparator set is a locus-based disease-family comparison, not a shared protein complex; differences may reflect guide performance and target expression as well as biology.

summary: Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor Wnt-restricted neighbors exposed a hidden Fzd9-like perturbation state.
why_it_matters: The weak maximum correlations argue against rescuing the Fzd9 result by pointing to a single highly concordant pathway neighbor or paralog; the top all-library neighbors in 308 CB GABA were modest and not Wnt-specific.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Score-vector correlations are restricted to genes measured in each class and can miss post-transcriptional pathway similarity.

summary: Itpr1 knockdown was transcriptionally detectable in most assayed cell types, yet the FDR-controlled response was almost completely buffered: among 388046 Itpr1 rows, the only adjusted-significant entry was Itpr1 itself in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: An IP3-gated ER calcium channel can be measurably depleted without forcing a broad steady-state mRNA program in adult mouse-brain neurons, so the absence of downstream DE is a biological negative result rather than simple absence of guide activity.
main_caveats: Knockdown was partial at the mRNA level and protein depletion, IP3-evoked calcium release, and electrophysiology were not measured.

summary: The cerebellar GABA class, the broad class expected to include Purkinje-lineage inhibitory neurons, showed nominal Itpr1 depletion and nominal Slc36a1/Ptprn/Crem changes but no FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: Human SCA15 and mouse Purkinje-cell work predict cerebellar vulnerability to ITPR1 loss; this dataset samples that axis but shows that a 61-cell mixed cerebellar GABA contrast is too weak to expose a resolved ataxia transcriptome.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only 61 perturbed cells were available; the cell class is broad, the best FDR was 0.103, and Purkinje-cell identity was not separated from other cerebellar inhibitory neurons.

summary: Itpr1 loss and Atp2a2 loss were not interchangeable ER-calcium perturbations in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells: Atp2a2 triggered 187 FDR-significant genes including Ddit3, Xbp1, Hspa5, and Chac1, whereas Itpr1 had a larger cell count and zero FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: The result separates ER Ca2+ refilling by SERCA2 from IP3-gated ER Ca2+ release at the transcriptional level and argues that only the pump perturbation created a robust ER-stress-like state in this neuronal class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The two targets had different knockdown magnitudes and different perturbed-cell counts, so the contrast should not be read as equal biochemical inhibition of two channels.

summary: The canonical PLCβ-to-IP3-to-ITPR relationship did not produce a shared L4/5 IT cortical transcriptome: Itpr1 and Plcb1 were each the sole FDR hit of their own perturbation, and their full Wilcoxon-score signatures were essentially uncorrelated.
why_it_matters: A direct upstream pathway neighbor with target knockdown in the same cell class failed to phenocopy Itpr1, implying that this Perturb-seq readout did not capture pathway flux through the PLCβ/IP3R step.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: This comparison is restricted to one cell type and to mRNA signatures; Plcb1 and Itpr1 depletion may occur in different subcellular signaling contexts.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor scan found no strong Itpr1-like perturbation: the largest absolute Pearson correlation of Wilcoxon scores was only 0.262 across 44110 within-cell comparisons.
why_it_matters: The Itpr1 phenotype cannot be confidently assigned to a hidden convergent target module; the best positive and negative neighbors were weak and localized to the same low-powered cerebellar GABA class.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on weak signatures and do not test non-transcriptional phenotypes; direct Itpr2/Itpr3 perturbations were absent.

summary: The perturbation is loss-of-function-like and mostly buffered, but human ITPR1 loss is an ataxia mechanism; therefore the dataset offers no support for indiscriminate ITPR1 inhibition as a protective neuronal strategy.
why_it_matters: Any therapeutic hypothesis based on dampening ER calcium release should consider that the disease genetics point in the opposite safety direction for the ITPR1 channel itself.
main_caveats: The experiment did not assay behavior or calcium physiology and did not evaluate pharmacologic partial inhibition.

summary: Epha5 knockdown was cell-class selective, with FDR-confirmed on-target reduction concentrated in 052 Pvalb Gaba and only nominal target reduction in a subset of cortical, limbic, midbrain, and striatal classes.
why_it_matters: The clearest Epha5 signal in this atlas was an inhibitory Pvalb class rather than a pan-neuronal or purely hippocampal response, so averaging across brain regions would obscure the on-target cell context.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only the Pvalb target-transcript row survived FDR; other classes are nominal and several had 28-57 perturbed cells.

summary: The strongest Pvalb GABA perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: Epha5 itself was significant, but Gfm2 and every other secondary row failed FDR.
why_it_matters: A robust decrease in the receptor transcript without a broad distal response argues that assayed Epha5 loss was not sufficient to drive a large steady-state mRNA program in this Pvalb context, or that the effect is post-transcriptional, activity-dependent, or spatially buffered.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measured RNA, not EPHA5 protein, phosphorylation, growth-cone behavior, synaptic currents, or ephrin reverse signaling.

summary: The sole FDR-significant distal hit was Lnpep down in the MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic class, whereas the NMDAR/PSD-95 synaptogenic genes highlighted by EphA5-ephrin-A5 hippocampal studies were at most nominal and directionally mixed.
why_it_matters: The limbic class aligns anatomically with known hippocampal EphA5 biology, but the measured mRNA response points to an atypical distal marker rather than a simple loss of the published early-development NMDA/PSD95 program.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Lnpep is a single FDR distal gene from only 40 perturbed MEA/LA/CA1/DG cells; the synaptic-gene contrast is based on mRNA rather than electrophysiology or synapse morphology.

summary: Epha5 perturbation did not produce a coherent transcriptional activation or repression of the Eph/ephrin-Rho signaling cascade; expected components appeared only as isolated nominal changes and usually with p_adj=1.0.
why_it_matters: EPH signaling is organized through phosphorylation, membrane complexes, and cytoskeletal effectors, so the lack of a coordinated mRNA cascade cautions against equating receptor knockdown with a transcriptomic pathway score in this dataset.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The receptor-signaling panel was a targeted follow-up rather than a genome-wide enrichment test, and nominal rows should not be treated as validated pathway activity changes.

summary: Epha5 was not interchangeable with other Eph receptors or any top whole-library signature neighbor: Epha4 and Epha7 knocked down strongly in different classes, but their genome-wide signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Epha5 in the main Epha5-responsive classes.
why_it_matters: Shared EPHA pathway membership did not translate into a shared Perturb-seq signature, preserving a biologically important divergence among receptor paralogs rather than collapsing the data to a generic Eph receptor effect.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations compare restricted scRNA-seq signatures within broad classes; absence of correlation does not exclude shared phosphorylation or morphology phenotypes.

summary: EPHA5 is a tractable cell-surface kinase, but this loss-of-function dataset gives a narrow and partially buffered RNA biomarker set rather than a broad canonical pathway readout.
why_it_matters: If EPHA5 is inhibited pharmacologically, Pvalb on-target loss and MEA/Lnpep-like limbic markers are more plausible cell-type-resolved sentinel readouts than a bulk Eph/Rho transcriptional score, and lack of a distal FDR program should not be mistaken for lack of receptor biology.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: This is an exploratory direction-of-effect warning from CRISPR loss in mouse brain cells; Open Targets tractability does not mean that EPHA5 is the primary target of an approved brain drug.

direction: weak Dicer1 mRNA decrease; no FDR-significant downstream response
summary: Dicer1 perturbation was weakly engaged and produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in the 22 assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: DICER1 is central to miRNA production, so the dataset's absence of significant downstream genes is best interpreted as under-engagement or timing rather than evidence that neuronal Dicer1 is dispensable.
main_caveats: On-target depletion was only nominal at the mRNA level and mature miRNA or protein depletion was not measured.

summary: The Dicer1 score signature did not converge with the available Argonaute/TNRC6-family perturbations Ago1, Ago2, Tnrc6a, or Tnrc6b.
why_it_matters: Genes in the same miRNA-silencing network might have been expected to share part of a transcriptomic signature; their near-zero correlations argue that this screen did not capture a coherent RISC-loss state.
main_caveats: The comparator perturbations were also weak, and several core miRNA-biogenesis genes were not present as perturbations, including Drosha, Dgcr8, Tarbp2, Prkra, Xpo5, Ago3, and Ago4.

summary: A caudal/hypothalamic GABA-enriched nominal module upregulated Atp1b1 and Atp1a3, with recurrent Nefh/Nefm induction, after Dicer1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: If reproducible, these genes could mark an early neuronal excitability or structural response to partial miRNA-pathway stress in selected inhibitory populations.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: No member of the module was FDR-significant; the finding is based on repeated nominal p values only.

summary: Measured Argonaute and TNRC6 transcripts did not show a consistent compensatory response within Dicer1-perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: The dataset provides no evidence that partial Dicer1 loss triggers transcriptional upregulation of the measured miRNA effector machinery.
main_caveats: Only mRNA abundance of four effector genes was assessed; compensation at protein activity, localization, or miRNA loading would not be detected.

summary: The screen should not be used to infer that Dicer1 inhibition is benign in neurons or as a straightforward therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: Chronic mouse knockouts and human genetics implicate Dicer1 loss in neuronal dysfunction and tumor predisposition, whereas the Perturb-seq result reflects an acute, weak, mRNA-level perturbation with no mature-miRNA readout.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks long-term survival phenotypes, biallelic loss, and disease-relevant second-hit contexts.

summary: Lrp4 perturbation produced no measurable Lrp4 transcript depletion and an almost completely FDR-null transcriptome across the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The primary interpretation is a weak or buffered perturbation, not proof that Lrp4 is dispensable in brain cells.
