main_caveats: Wilcoxon rows show RNA abundance only; cell counts are modest in multiple classes and no protein-level LRP4 or guide-efficiency measurement is available.

summary: Arglu1 up-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA was the single FDR-significant Lrp4-associated gene.
why_it_matters: This creates a narrow candidate readout for the only cell class with a corrected signal, while showing that the response was not broadly reused across neuronal classes.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The hit is one gene with modest logFC, no measurable Lrp4 knockdown, and no recurrence in the other 21 assayed Lrp4 cell types.

summary: The 191 MB P MY GABA Lrp4 signature had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The Arglu1 hit did not sit inside a larger transcriptomic module shared with another perturbation, so top signature-neighbor analysis did not rescue a mechanistic program from the weak scalar signal.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only for the one cell class with an Lrp4 FDR hit and use transcriptome-wide score vectors, not independent phenotypes.

summary: Canonical AGRN-LRP4-MUSK biology did not appear as a shared neuronal transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Lrp4 belongs to an agrin receptor complex, so the lack of Lrp4-Musk-Agrn convergence argues that Agrn hits in this neuronal table should not be automatically interpreted as canonical LRP4/MUSK pathway output.

main_caveats: The literature mechanism is anchored in muscle/NMJ assays; in this dataset Lrp4 and Musk themselves lack target-transcript engagement, so the contrast is context and efficacy sensitive.

summary: The neuronal null response does not test the astrocytic Lrp4 mechanisms reported for CNS glutamatergic transmission and Aβ clearance.
why_it_matters: A negative neuronal Perturb-seq result should not be taken as evidence against Lrp4 brain disease biology because the assayed Lrp4 groups were Glut/GABA neuronal classes rather than astrocytes.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset cannot measure the astrocytic ATP-release or Aβ-clearance phenotypes; it only shows that the available neuronal classes were mostly transcriptomically silent after Lrp4 targeting.

summary: LRP4-SOST/Wnt biology was not converted into a corrected Wnt transcriptional response in the neuronal dataset.
why_it_matters: LRP4 can facilitate sclerostin-mediated Wnt inhibition and human LRP4 mutations alter Wnt/beta-catenin signaling, but the only measured Axin2 increase after Lrp4 targeting was nominal, leaving Wnt directionality unsupported here.

direction: Ndufaf5 transcript mostly down; downstream RNA response absent
summary: Ndufaf5 perturbation produced recurrent nominal target-transcript depletion but no FDR-resolved downstream expression response in any tested cell class.
why_it_matters: NDUFAF5 acts directly on complex-I assembly; the dataset indicates that partial transcript depletion in neurons is either buffered at the RNA level or requires protein, enzymatic, or longer-term assays to expose the phenotype.
main_caveats: Ndufaf5 itself did not pass FDR<0.05, so the result is nominal at the target-transcript level.

summary: Related NDUFAF and Nduf-family perturbations did not form a shared complex-I biogenesis transcriptomic signature with Ndufaf5.
why_it_matters: It prevents overinterpreting Reactome or STRING pathway membership as evidence that partial perturbations of neighboring assembly genes are interchangeable in this mouse-brain scRNA endpoint.
main_caveats: Comparator analysis is restricted to genes targeted in the screen; Ndufaf8 and Pyurf were not available as perturbations.

direction: target down in the strongest nominal classes
summary: The strongest nominal Ndufaf5 engagement was concentrated in thalamic, pineal, and L4/5 cortical glutamatergic classes, but this did not translate into significant trans-gene changes.
why_it_matters: The apparent cell-type effect is a technical/engagement gradient that should not be mistaken for selective dependence of those neurons on complex-I biogenesis.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Two of the strongest classes had only 47 and 22 perturbed cells, and target-row FDRs remained above 0.05.

direction: loss of function is disease-associated; no protective compensatory RNA signature detected
summary: The muted neuronal RNA phenotype does not argue for NDUFAF5 inhibition: human recessive loss of C20orf7/NDUFAF5 disrupts OXPHOS and causes severe mitochondrial disease.
why_it_matters: A therapeutic or screening program that used only acute neuronal transcriptional DE could under-rank a target whose primary liability is complex-I assembly failure.
main_caveats: The dataset assays partial mouse neuronal perturbations and cannot measure mitochondrial respiration or patient-like developmental disease.

summary: A weak 308 CB GABA Ndufaf5 signature correlated with Lonp1, Ptcd3, and Ndufb9 perturbations, but the same tail contained Safe_target controls.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only suggestive signature-neighbor pattern while marking it as an exploratory hypothesis rather than a validated mitochondrial module.

main_caveats: Ndufaf5 engagement in 308 CB GABA was weak and negative-control signatures correlated at similar magnitudes.

direction: nominal Kcnh1 down; downstream absent at FDR < 0.05
summary: Kcnh1 guide targeting produced nominal target-transcript decreases in a subset of neurons but no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any of the 22 measured cell types.
why_it_matters: A pore-forming neuronal potassium channel can be partially reduced without a strong steady-state RNA cascade, so the dominant result is buffering or weak engagement rather than a pathway activation signature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The target row itself was not FDR-significant, perturbation was RNA-level, and most cell types had fewer than 120 perturbed cells.

summary: The best scalar downstream p values arose mainly in cell types where Kcnh1 itself was not knocked down, separating nominal downstream hits from credible on-target biology.
why_it_matters: Thalamic, Sst, cerebellar GABA, and hippocampal/amygdalar glutamatergic nominations should be deprioritized unless replicated, because the same signatures lack measurable target engagement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|053 Sst Gaba|308 CB GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: This is a statistical prioritization claim from target-transcript behavior, not proof that the nominal genes are false positives.

direction: dataset loss/weak knockdown versus literature gain of function
summary: The knockdown-like Kcnh1 perturbation did not reproduce a strong neurodevelopmental disease program, consistent with human TBS and ZLS variants being gain-of-function channel alleles.
why_it_matters: Loss-of-transcript Perturb-seq is directionally mismatched to the established KCNH1 disease alleles, so the absence of a robust signature should not be read as absence of pathogenic KCNH1 channel hyperactivity.
main_caveats: The dataset measures mouse brain cell classes after gene perturbation, not human developmental missense channel gating.

summary: Kcnh1 and the EAG-family paralog Kcnh5 were both weak perturbations and were not transcriptomically interchangeable in shared cell types.
why_it_matters: Although EAG1 and EAG2 are related delayed-rectifier channels that can participate in the same KCNH channel family, their Perturb-seq score vectors in L4-5 IT cortex and thalamus were nearly uncorrelated.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Both EAG signatures lacked FDR-significant hits; the comparison is restricted to weak score-vector structure.

direction: KCNH weak versus KCNQ/KCNC/KCNAB strong in the same cell type
summary: The weak Kcnh1/Kcnh5 result is not a general failure to perturb voltage-gated potassium-channel genes in the same neuronal class.
why_it_matters: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Kcnq2, Kcnq3, Kcnab2, and Kcnc3 target transcripts were each significantly depleted while Kcnh1 was unchanged and Kcnh5 remained FDR-negative, arguing for target-family-specific rather than assay-wide channel resistance.

main_caveats: The contrast is strongest in one cell type and does not identify whether guide efficiency, transcript detectability, or biological compensation explains the EAG-family weakness.

summary: Assigned Lhcgr perturbation did not measurably shift the Lhcgr transcript or any downstream gene in the assayed brain subclasses.

summary: Lhcgr/Fshr/Tshr receptor perturbations were largely inert, whereas downstream Adcy3, Prkar1a, Creb1, and Crebbp perturbations produced significant effects in overlapping neuronal subclasses.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA

summary: The mouse-brain Lhcgr Perturb-seq result does not validate a broad cell-autonomous CNS loss-of-function program for this druggable receptor despite literature showing sparse brain expression and functional hCG effects.
why_it_matters: LHCGR agonists are clinically real, and central agonism has been tested in memory models, but this screen suggests that therapeutic hypotheses should focus on rare Lhcgr-positive cells, activation state, reproductive context, and non-transcriptional endpoints rather than broad neuronal knockdown signatures.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Literature evidence uses germline loss or receptor agonism, not the same age, cell type, exposure duration, or perturbation modality as this dataset.

summary: Adra2b perturbation produced a globally buffered transcriptomic phenotype with no FDR<0.05 genes across 22 analyzed cell types.
why_it_matters: A catecholamine GPCR could have been expected to perturb G-protein and activity-dependent transcription, but the aggregate response was nearly adjusted-null.
main_caveats: The global null is downstream of a perturbation whose target transcript was not measurably depleted.

summary: The Adra2b transcript itself was measured but was not significantly reduced in any analyzed cell type.
why_it_matters: Without RNA-level on-target engagement, lack of downstream FDR hits cannot be interpreted as definitive genetic dispensability of ADRA2B protein signaling.
main_caveats: Perturb-seq mRNA DE cannot exclude protein perturbation or sparse-transcript dropout.

summary: Nominal Adra2b signals were restricted to isolated cell types, led by Macroh2a1 in MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic cells, a broader L4-5 IT CTX nominal tail, and P3h3 in CNU-MGE GABA.

main_caveats: Only Macroh2a1 reached FDR<0.10; none of these genes reached FDR<0.05.

summary: The canonical adrenergic Gi/o-cAMP axis and immediate-early activity genes were transcriptionally uncoupled from Adra2b perturbation.
why_it_matters: The negative panel result separates the measured weak Adra2b guide phenotype from the receptor's validated biochemical ability to regulate adenylyl cyclase, ERK, and calcium channels.
main_caveats: Panel genes are mRNA readouts in unstimulated cells and may miss acute cAMP, calcium, or phosphorylation events.

summary: Adra2b did not converge with Adra2a or assayed adrenergic/cAMP pathway-neighbor perturbations by all-gene signature correlation.
why_it_matters: The weak correlation with the closest assayed α2 paralog argues against treating α2A and α2B guides as interchangeable neuronal transcriptomic perturbations in this dataset.
main_caveats: Correlations are restricted to transcriptomic scores under guide perturbation; Adra2b's own weak engagement probably contributes to the lack of convergence.

summary: Known α2B developmental and vascular phenotypes were not recapitulated as a broad neuronal Adra2b transcriptional program in thalamic, CNU, or cerebellar brain classes.
why_it_matters: This warns against extrapolating ADRA2B placental, lung, or vascular biology directly to cell-autonomous neuronal mRNA phenotypes without matching the responding tissue and ligand context.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA

direction: weak target-transcript decrease; no FDR-resolved downstream direction
summary: Nfia perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in the assayed neuronal populations: the Nfia transcript trended downward in many cell types but never reached nominal p<0.05, and no downstream target gene reached FDR<=0.05.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is a high-confidence negative one: this table does not contain a robust neuronal Nfia loss-of-function expression program despite 371,818 tests.
main_caveats: The target-engagement readout is Nfia mRNA, not editing or NFIA protein, and CRISPR indels can disrupt protein without lowering transcript abundance.

direction: gliogenesis program not detected in neuronal classes
summary: The dataset refines the canonical NFIA gliogenesis model to a missing-context result: Nfia was perturbed almost exclusively in Glut/GABA neuronal classes, where the known glial-competence and astrocyte programs were not detectably activated or collapsed.
why_it_matters: NFIA is a potent developmental glial regulator, so the absence of an FDR-resolved neuronal signature argues that the Perturb-seq assay sampled a cell type or maturation stage in which the NFIA glial network is not engaged.
main_caveats: No astrocyte or neural-stem-cell groups are present in the Nfia result; absence of a neuronal expression response is not evidence that NFIA is dispensable in glial progenitors or astrocytes.

summary: Apparent Nfia cell-type selectivity is exploratory and nominal, with the largest tails in 053 Sst Gaba, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut but no FDR-confirmed gene in any of them.
why_it_matters: This preserves the strongest cell-type-specific observations without upgrading them into a validated Sst, corticofugal, pineal, or hippocampal mechanism.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The strongest nominal classes had only 42 to 80 perturbed cells, and every row failed FDR correction.

summary: Nfia, Nfib, Nfic, and Nfix perturbations were not interchangeable at the whole-transcriptome signature level in neuronal cell types: all 66 Nfia-versus-paralog correlations stayed between -0.061 and 0.0876.
why_it_matters: Despite NFI-family relatedness and an NFIA/NFIB relationship in astrocytes, the neuronal signatures contain no evidence for a shared NFI-family module or for a compensatory Nfib/Nfic/Nfix transcriptional response after Nfia perturbation.
main_caveats: The contrast is limited by the weak Nfia own-gene response; low correlation is therefore consistent with true specialization, insufficient Nfia perturbation strength, or both.

direction: no strong positive or negative neighbor
summary: A same-cell-type signature-neighbor scan did not reveal any strong convergent or opposing perturbation for Nfia; the best non-self neighbors had |r|<=0.124.
why_it_matters: The weak Nfia result is not rescued by hidden similarity to another perturbation axis, and Safe_target-named entries appearing as top neighbors further cautions against overinterpreting the small correlations.
main_caveats: Only transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon-score correlations within the same coarse cell type were tested.

summary: The disease-relevant prior is NFIA loss of function and dosage sensitivity, whereas acute neuronal Nfia perturbation in this assay produced no coherent FDR-resolved signature; these data therefore should not be read as support for neuronal NFIA inhibition as a therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: The clinically directional interpretation is cautionary: NFIA reduction causes developmental brain and urinary-tract malformations in human and mouse genetics, and the Perturb-seq readout lacks a compensatory or beneficial neuronal program.
main_caveats: The assay is mouse single-cell RNA in mature neuronal classes and does not model human embryonic development, rescue, or chronic NFIA haploinsufficiency.

summary: Ank knockdown was transcriptionally real in several neuronal classes but was almost completely self-limited to the Ank transcript.
why_it_matters: ANKH is a transmembrane mineralization regulator tied to extracellular nucleotide, citrate, and pyrophosphate homeostasis; in these mouse-brain Perturb-seq profiles, efficient mRNA depletion did not trigger a broad cell-autonomous mRNA program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The conclusion is transcriptomic only; ANKH activity may be reflected in extracellular ATP, citrate, PPi, or mineralization measurements that were not assayed.

direction: target transcript down in all measured cell types but significance was uneven
summary: On-target depletion was heterogeneous across Ank-positive cell-type tests: five cell types reached FDR<0.05, three more were suggestive at FDR<0.20, and three had little or no nominal target repression.
why_it_matters: Downstream-negative cell types with weak Ank knockdown cannot be interpreted as biologically buffered, whereas the five well-engaged classes provide the cleanest negative downstream result.
main_caveats: Cell counts ranged from 29 to 161 perturbed cells, so FDR sensitivity varied; mRNA depletion is used as a proxy for perturbation strength.

summary: The neuronal signatures did not resolve a shared ANKH/phosphate-calcification module with phosphate-transporter neighbors or with any recurrent positive or negative perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: Prior work places ANKH in an extracellular PPi network that also includes nucleotides, citrate, ENPP1, and ALPL; the dataset argues that acute cell-autonomous neuronal differential expression is not a robust readout of that network in this assay.
comparators: Slc20a2|Xpr1|top positive signature neighbors|top negative signature neighbors
main_caveats: Slc20a2 and Xpr1 themselves had weak target-transcript engagement, ENPP1 and ALPL were not informative Ank comparators in this subset, and the signature-neighbor analysis used the 200 largest non-Ank Ank scores rather than a genome-wide significant gene set.

summary: Ubr5 up-regulation in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and Cdh10 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut were the only non-target rows approaching a relaxed FDR threshold.

cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Neither gene reached FDR<0.05; Ubr5 occurred in a cell type where Ank itself was only suggestive at FDR=0.132.

direction: therapeutic mRNA readout not induced despite target depletion
summary: Ank target knockdown is not accompanied by a scalable transcriptional disease surrogate in the assayed brain cell types.
why_it_matters: Human ANKH alleles cause mineralization disorders, and newer work emphasizes ATP and citrate efflux; this dataset warns that mRNA panels alone could miss ANKH pathway effects and should be paired with extracellular metabolite or mineralization endpoints.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset does not perturb cartilage, osteoblasts, choroid plexus, vasculature, or other mineralizing or barrier contexts; absence of an mRNA signature is not absence of ANKH transport activity.

direction: Abcb7 down with no adjusted downstream DE
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed the strongest Abcb7 target-transcript depletion, but the perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This separates measured target engagement from pathway activation and suggests that acute Abcb7 depletion was buffered, weak, or primarily biochemical in the best-engaged brain cell class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Abcb7 target row itself was only nominally significant and adjusted p=1.0; scRNA-seq does not read out Fe-S cluster export directly.

direction: down in a subset and weak or absent in others
summary: Abcb7 target engagement was heterogeneous across brain cell types rather than uniform.
why_it_matters: Cell-type comparisons that lack Abcb7 mRNA depletion should not be interpreted as negative biology; inefficient editing, transcript dropout, or guide representation could mask downstream effects.

main_caveats: The apparent selectivity is based on target mRNA statistics, not protein loss; several engaged strata had fewer than 35 perturbed cells.

summary: Abcb7 did not converge with sampled Fe-S assembly or Fe-S enzyme perturbations and did not coordinately regulate Fe-S/heme module transcripts.
why_it_matters: ABCB7 belongs to the mitochondrial Fe-S export and ABCB7-FECH-ABCB10 heme/iron module, so the near-zero correlations argue that this Perturb-seq signature is uncoupled from the expected biochemical pathway at the mRNA level.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The compared genes are pathway neighbors rather than ABCB7 complex members, and transcriptomic similarity is an indirect expectation for a metabolite transporter.

summary: No high-confidence Abcb7 downstream biomarker was detected.
why_it_matters: The strongest nominal genes and weakly recurrent candidates should be treated as hypotheses only, preventing overinterpretation of isolated p-values in a target with no adjusted DE support.
main_caveats: This is a negative statement about this dataset and DE model only; it does not exclude protein, metabolite, survival, or late transcriptional biomarkers.

direction: known loss-of-function disease; muted mRNA response
summary: The acute mouse-brain Abcb7 transcriptome did not reproduce the heme/iron failure implied by ABCB7 loss-of-function disease and erythroid models.
why_it_matters: Human disease and mouse knockout data establish ABCB7 as essential, but this scRNA-seq result indicates that brain-cell partial loss may first manifest through biochemical Fe-S or iron defects rather than a large canonical mRNA program.
main_caveats: Literature contexts include human pedigrees, yeast complementation, hematopoietic cells, liver, and cell lines rather than acute mouse neuronal CRISPR perturbations.

summary: ABCB7 inhibition is an exploratory safety concern, not a supported beneficial direction, in this readout.
why_it_matters: Disease alleles reduce ABCB7 function and the best Abcb7 knockdown failed to induce a robust compensatory program, while ChEMBL did not return a curated ABCB7 drug mechanism in the lookup.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset is not a pharmacologic exposure, rescue, or toxicity assay, and ChEMBL absence of mechanisms is not proof that probes do not exist.

summary: Foxg1 perturbation was weak or buffered at the RNA-signature level, and the Foxg1 transcript itself was not detectably depleted.
why_it_matters: This is the gating result for interpretation: most downstream claims are constrained by poor target-transcript engagement and by an almost complete absence of FDR-level expression changes.
main_caveats: Target mRNA is an imperfect engagement readout for some coding perturbations, and this parquet does not contain guide-level genotype or protein validation.

summary: The only corrected Foxg1 response was Gtf2ird1 up-regulation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, with Plxnd1 and Slc24a4 remaining sub-FDR cortical signals.
why_it_matters: The screen does not reveal a pan-neuronal FOXG1 loss-of-function program; instead it nominates a narrow cortical L4/5 IT readout and two weaker cortical follow-ups.

main_caveats: Only Gtf2ird1 passed 5% FDR; the Plxnd1 and Slc24a4 observations are suggestive only, and no direct FOXG1-GTF2IRD1 relationship was established.

summary: Tle2 was recurrently, but only nominally, down-ranked after Foxg1 perturbation across several neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: FOXG1 is known to work with Groucho/TLE co-repressors, so repeated Tle2 repression is a mechanistically plausible hint that a co-repressor-family circuit is perturbed even when no individual Tle2 test survives FDR correction.

main_caveats: Correlation was computed from weak Foxg1 signatures and restricted to three cell classes; low similarity may reflect inadequate Foxg1 perturbation as well as true pathway specificity.

summary: Canonical FOXG1 developmental subtype markers were measured but not FDR-remodeled by Foxg1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The result supports the idea that FOXG1 disease biology is highly developmental-stage and dosage dependent; an acute Perturb-seq signature in sampled neuronal classes cannot be read as a full replay of embryonic cortical projection-neuron fate specification.
main_caveats: Absence of corrected marker changes is most interpretable as a negative result in the assayed context, not as evidence that FOXG1 lacks developmental functions.

summary: Cd3e perturbation produced no measurable on-target knockdown and no FDR-supported transcriptomic response in the 22 tested neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: The most parsimonious interpretation is target non-engagement, likely because Cd3e is an immune TCR-CD3 transcript rather than an active program in these sorted brain classes; Cd3e perturbation should therefore not be treated as a neuronal loss-of-function phenotype here.
cell_types: 22 tested Cd3e brain cell classes
main_caveats: A negative Wilcoxon result does not prove zero Cd3e expression; large on-target log-fold changes appear sparse-count driven because the on-target scores and p values were near null.

summary: No Cd3e-sensitive brain cell class emerged; even the highest guide-count thalamic, midbrain, cortical, and Pvalb GABA strata lacked significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The broad absence argues against a missed robust response being hidden solely by low cell number, although the smallest classes remain individually underpowered.

main_caveats: The conclusion is a detection statement within this file; small groups with 25-49 perturbed cells cannot exclude subtle effects.

summary: Cd3e did not converge with perturbations of the CD3/TCR complex members Cd3d, Cd3g, or Cd247, nor with Cd4, even by restricted signature-neighbor correlation.
why_it_matters: A true TCR-CD3 program would be expected to show some related-subunit coherence; the absence of co-convergence is consistent with the entire receptor module being inactive or unmeasured in these neuronal cell classes rather than with a Cd3e-specific downstream pathway.
cell_types: 22 tested Cd3e brain cell classes
main_caveats: All CD3-family perturbations also lacked on-target transcript evidence, so the result should not be read as biochemical divergence of expressed CD3 subunits.

summary: Canonical CD3 phosphorylation, ZAP70 recruitment, and downstream TCR signaling were uncoupled from Cd3e perturbation in the brain dataset.
why_it_matters: Reactome places CD3E immediately upstream of CD3/TCR-zeta phosphorylation and ZAP70-dependent TCR signaling; no Cd3e-induced gene set supports activation or repression of those pathways in any tested brain class.
cell_types: 22 tested Cd3e brain cell classes
main_caveats: Transcriptomic DE is an indirect readout of proximal phosphorylation cascades and the assay did not measure ZAP70 or ITAM phosphorylation.

summary: Published mouse neuronal CD3ζ biology does not generalize to a detectable pan-brain Cd3e program in this perturbation atlas.
why_it_matters: CD247/CD3ζ has documented roles in retinal ganglion and amacrine-cell development, but this dataset did not show Cd3e-Cd247 transcriptional convergence in the sampled non-retinal brain classes, refining the prior neural literature to be subunit- and context-specific.
cell_types: 22 tested Cd3e brain cell classes
main_caveats: The dataset did not sample retinal ganglion or displaced amacrine cells, and the Cd247 perturbations themselves showed no on-target transcriptional validation.

summary: CD3E's disease and drug evidence is T-cell-centered and should not be projected onto these neuronal Cd3e perturbations.
why_it_matters: Human CD3E loss causes TCR/CD3 immunodeficiency and CD3E is directly drugged by anti-CD3 antibodies, yet this mouse-brain screen provides no evidence that partial neuronal Cd3e targeting phenocopies either CD3E immunodeficiency or therapeutic CD3E modulation.
cell_types: 22 tested Cd3e brain cell classes
main_caveats: The dataset has non-targeting controls and neuronal cell classes, not T cells or antibody-mediated receptor cross-linking.

summary: Ogdh mRNA fell in every assayed Ogdh perturbation class, but statistically confirmed target engagement was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: Downstream Ogdh biology should be interpreted primarily in the two FDR-confirmed classes; weak cortical, hippocampal, hypothalamic, and cerebellar rows are difficult to distinguish from partial knockdown plus limited power.

main_caveats: The dataset measures RNA rather than OGDH protein or enzymatic activity, and Ogdh was not assayed in the 215 MB Dopa class.

summary: FDR-confirmed Ogdh knockdown produced almost no downstream transcriptional response: only Ogdh itself was significant in the two engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: OGDH is a rate-limiting mitochondrial TCA enzyme, so the absence of a broad mRNA program after partial knockdown suggests strong acute buffering at the transcriptome level or a perturbation that did not cross the protein/activity threshold required for a metabolic stress response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No metabolomics, respiration, ROS, or OGDH protein measurements were available; FDR correction over ~17k genes and modest cell counts can hide subtle downstream events.

summary: Ogdh knockdown did not transcriptionally phenocopy OGDH-complex partners or adjacent TCA perturbations despite those targets being engaged in the same neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Known membership in the same enzymatic module did not translate into interchangeable single-cell RNA signatures, so OGDH, DLST/DLD, and neighboring TCA genes should not be collapsed into one loss-of-function signature in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison used correlations of Wilcoxon DE scores, not matched metabolic phenotypes, and Dld/Dlst themselves were often weakly engaged.

summary: A single Prdx5 induction in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut was the only non-Ogdh FDR hit, making peroxide detoxification a hypothesis-generating marker rather than a robust OGDH response.
why_it_matters: PRDX5 is a mitochondrial peroxidase and OGDHC can generate ROS, so Prdx5 is biologically plausible, but the missing Ogdh target FDR in the same cells makes off-target sampling or a rare-state effect equally plausible.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: One FDR gene in 48 perturbed cells; Ogdh itself was not significantly depleted in that cell type.

summary: The flat transcriptional phenotype should not be read as evidence that OGDH inhibition is safe in neurons.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic OGDH variants cause a neurodevelopmental movement/metabolic disorder, and Ogdh loss can drive neuronal degeneration in vivo; the screen instead indicates that adult acute partial RNA knockdown lacks an easily read out protective or toxic mRNA direction.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset has no viability measurement, no chronic developmental context, and no direct small-molecule OGDH inhibition assay.

summary: The OGDH-like E1 transcript Ogdhl was not induced after Ogdh perturbation.
why_it_matters: If KGDHC flux was buffered, the buffering was not visible as compensatory up-regulation of the brain E1 isoenzyme transcript, focusing follow-up on pre-existing OGDHL protein, DLST/DLD stoichiometry, substrate supply, or post-transcriptional control.
main_caveats: Only mRNA compensation was tested; Ogdhl was not itself a perturbation target in the library.

summary: Lepr produced its only 10%-FDR transcriptional hit in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, led by Ankrd24 up and a weaker Srsf11 down trend.

main_caveats: Only Ankrd24 passed FDR<0.1 and no gene passed FDR<0.05; Ankrd24 and Srsf11 are not established canonical LEPR effectors.

summary: Lepr perturbation lacked measurable Lepr transcript knockdown in every assayed cell type.

main_caveats: Perturbations of Lep, Jak2, Socs3, Sh2b1, and Pomc were not available; transcriptomic CRISPR loss is not equivalent to acute leptin stimulation.

summary: Lepr was weaker than obesity/energy-balance comparators that hit different cell types: Mc4r in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and Fto in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Genes in the same clinical energy-balance space did not share a generic obesity transcriptional module; the dataset instead separates upstream leptin receptor, downstream melanocortin receptor, and Fto-linked biology by cell context.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: FTO is an obesity-associated gene rather than a direct LEPR receptor subunit; the comparison is disease-family and circuit-level, not a same-complex test.

summary: Lepr showed no robust response in the broad 215 MB Dopa stratum despite literature support for leptin signaling in VTA dopamine neurons.
why_it_matters: The negative result argues that the Perturb-seq dopamine label is insufficiently resolved or underpowered for rare VTA LepR biology, rather than that dopamine leptin signaling is absent.

summary: The Lepr screen did not yield a strong nearest-neighbor or canonical pharmacodynamic module, so the weak 110 Ankrd24/Srsf11 signature should not be treated as a biomarker of LEPR agonism.
