cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The warning is based on one weak cell-type-restricted loss-of-function signature and computational correlations, not on drug treatment data.

summary: Gabrb1 knockdown produced a consistent but transcriptionally buffered response: the Gabrb1 transcript shifted downward in nearly every assayed cell class, yet no downstream gene reached FDR < 0.20 in any contrast.
why_it_matters: Gabrb1 encodes a core postsynaptic GABA-A chloride-channel subunit, so the Perturb-seq result argues that partial chronic transcript depletion is not sufficient to elicit a large cell-autonomous mRNA program in these mouse-brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The programmed target transcript itself never passed FDR correction; the result could reflect incomplete guide efficacy, low detectability of Gabrb1 mRNA, or buffering rather than true absence of channel-level effects.

summary: Gabrb1 failed to phenocopy the activity-gene response caused by related GABA-A subunits: in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Gabrb2 significantly upregulated Nr4a1 and Vgf and drove near-threshold Fos/Npas4 increases while Gabrb1 left the same genes near baseline; Gabrg2 significantly induced Vgf in 155 MB Glut whereas Gabrb1 did not.
why_it_matters: Beta and gamma GABA-A subunits participate in the same heteropentameric receptor family, but this dataset separates beta1 from beta2/gamma2 at the transcriptional-phenotype level instead of supporting simple subunit interchangeability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparator perturbations had much stronger on-target FDRs than Gabrb1; therefore divergence could combine beta1-specific biology with weaker Gabrb1 perturbation.

summary: Gabrb1 depletion did not trigger a coordinated compensatory increase of other assayed GABA-A receptor, anchoring, GABA synthesis, or GABA transport transcripts.
why_it_matters: If beta1 loss were transcriptionally substituted by neighboring inhibitory-synapse components, selected subunit or pathway genes should have been enriched among Gabrb1 responses; instead their nominal hit rate matched statistical background.
main_caveats: The test was limited to selected transcripts detectable in the matrix; protein trafficking or receptor assembly compensation would not be captured by mRNA Wilcoxon statistics.

summary: Nono in 191 MB P MY GABA and Kif3c/Ptchd4/Pten in 308 CB GABA are only exploratory Gabrb1 readouts, not validated biomarkers.
why_it_matters: These genes were the strongest scalar outliers for Gabrb1, but they did not pass FDR correction and the cerebellar signal occurred without target-transcript engagement, preventing a pathway-level claim.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All adjusted p values were >= 0.2319; 308 CB GABA had only 38 perturbed cells and no nominal Gabrb1 depletion.

summary: The weak Gabrb1 Perturb-seq profile should not be interpreted as evidence that beta1-containing GABA-A receptor modulation is biologically inert.
why_it_matters: Human GABRB1 variants can alter channel behavior, ChEMBL curates GABRB1-containing pharmacologic receptor targets, and this dataset shows that different GABA-A subunits create different mRNA phenotypes; acute channel pharmacology and chronic partial transcript knockdown are therefore directionally distinct modalities.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset contains transcriptional knockdowns, not electrophysiology or ligand exposures; no drug was tested.

summary: Gabrb1 target-trace strength was cell-type selective and was weakest in canonical Pvalb, Sst, and cortical CGE interneuron labels.
why_it_matters: The negative result is not simply an inhibitory-neuron result: the strongest nominal Gabrb1 self-depletion occurred mostly in glutamatergic or thalamic/hypothalamic labels, while classic forebrain interneuron classes showed little detectable target depletion.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This may reflect baseline expression, dropout, or guide sampling rather than true cell-type-specific receptor biology; all self-depletion rows had FDR = 1.0.

summary: Nfx1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any tested mouse-brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is buffering or weak target engagement rather than a robust neuronal transcriptional program, so downstream pathway claims should not be made from nominal genes alone.
main_caveats: Differential expression is transcriptomic; on-target editing at the DNA or protein level was not observed directly.

summary: The only interpretable on-target RNA depletion was nominal and concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba cells.
why_it_matters: These two cell types were the only contexts where Nfx1 itself was the strongest absolute response gene; even there, the putative downstream signatures remained below FDR support.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Both signatures are nominal only; 052 Pvalb Gaba has only 39 perturbed cells and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut has adjusted p = 1.0 for all genes.

summary: Several apparent Nfx1 signatures are better explained as non-engaged or buffered responses, with 308 CB GABA as the clearest example.
why_it_matters: The smallest raw p value in the entire Nfx1 subset occurred in CB GABA, but the Nfx1 transcript was not reduced there; this prevents over-interpreting isolated high Wilcoxon scores as target biology.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The conclusion is based on the measured target transcript; edited cells could still lose Nfx1 protein without strong mRNA loss.

summary: Canonical NFX1 immune and telomerase outputs were uncoupled from Nfx1 perturbation in these neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: Prior work places NFX1 at the MHC class II X-box and in isoform-specific TERT/PABPC regulation, but H2-Aa, H2-Ab1, H2-Eb1, Cd74, Ciita, Tert, Pabpc1, and Pabpc4 were not FDR-responsive here, refining those mechanisms to their permissive immune or HPV-epithelial contexts rather than basal mouse neurons.
main_caveats: MHC class II and Tert-family transcripts may be lowly expressed in many neurons; absence of derepression is therefore a context-specific negative result.

summary: Nfx1 did not converge with curated STRING-neighbor perturbations or with any strong same-cell signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating NFX1 network proximity as functional interchangeability in this dataset; even Sin3a, Ube3a, Psen1, Syncrip, and H2-Eb1 signatures were essentially orthogonal to Nfx1, and the strongest unbiased neighbor had only |r| = 0.148.
main_caveats: Using full-signature score correlations is exploratory, and the Nfx1 anchor signatures themselves are weak.

summary: The dataset does not support Nfx1 as a neuronal disease-modifying or druggable direction.
why_it_matters: NFX1 has literature and database links to HPV-associated cancer biology but no robust mouse-neuron transcriptomic consequence here; perturbing it in these conditions offers no FDR-supported biomarker, pathway, or disease-rescue direction.
main_caveats: This is a therapeutic interpretation of a negative in vitro Perturb-seq result, not an in vivo efficacy test.

direction: Hk1 transcript down in perturbed cells
summary: Hk1 perturbation engaged the target transcript unevenly across neuronal classes, with the clearest FDR-level depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and rank-1 target depletion in six additional classes.
why_it_matters: The target itself is the dominant measured response; stratifying on Hk1 transcript depletion is essential before interpreting weak downstream signatures as biology rather than weak engagement or low power.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay measured mRNA, not HK1 protein or enzymatic activity; several classes had only 37-60 perturbed cells.

direction: target down; downstream mRNA response absent at FDR<0.05
summary: Even when Hk1 mRNA was detectably reduced, the perturbation produced no FDR-significant non-Hk1 transcriptomic program across 21 neuronal signatures.
why_it_matters: HK1 catalyzes the entry step of glycolysis, so the dataset separates a real target-transcript effect from changes in steady-state mRNA programs and suggests buffering or a non-transcriptional acute impact under this perturbation regime.
main_caveats: No metabolite, ATP, mitochondrial-potential, or protein measurements were available; partial transcript depletion could leave enough HK1 protein for flux.

summary: Hk1 signatures were nearly uncorrelated with perturbations of profiled glycolysis neighbors, including engaged Pfkm, Pgk1, and Gpi1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: The low correlations argue against treating every glycolytic-gene perturbation as the same transcriptional state in these neurons, despite their shared Reactome and STRING pathway context.
main_caveats: The comparison is based on whole-transcriptome score correlations; metabolic phenocopying could occur without a correlated mRNA signature, and several paralogs or VDAC genes were not perturbed.

direction: no strong positive or negative neighbor
summary: A same-cell-type search over all profiled targets found no strong Hk1-like or Hk1-opposing signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The Hk1 response was not embedded in a broader recurrent transcriptional module among approximately two thousand target perturbations per cell type; the largest absolute neighbor correlation was only 0.161.
main_caveats: Very low-amplitude signatures make correlations conservative; this screen cannot exclude convergence at unmeasured metabolic or protein levels.

direction: partial loss buffered in assayed neurons
summary: Partial Hk1 mRNA depletion in assayed mouse neuronal classes was transcriptionally buffered, which is more compatible with HK1 neuroretinal diseases involving allele-, isoform-, or cell-context-specific mechanisms than with a uniform immediate neuronal mRNA-collapse model.
why_it_matters: Human HK1 genetics spans neurodevelopmental, retinal, peripheral-nerve, and erythroid phenotypes; the Perturb-seq result narrows the interpretation by showing that reducing the shared Hk1 transcript in these neurons is not sufficient to elicit a broad short-term stress or glycolysis transcription program.
main_caveats: The patient variants are human germline alleles, often missense or regulatory, whereas this dataset is a mouse brain transcript perturbation with no retina, red-cell, peripheral-nerve, or developmental readout.

direction: safety concern despite buffered Perturb-seq readout
summary: The absence of a broad neuronal differential-expression response should not be used as evidence that systemic HK1 inhibition would be safe.
why_it_matters: HK1 is broadly expressed and genetically linked to erythroid, peripheral-nerve, retinal, and neurodevelopmental disease; a partial mRNA perturbation in selected neurons is likely to under-sample acute catalytic blockade and non-neuronal liabilities.
main_caveats: No drug treatment, dose response, protein depletion, or peripheral tissue was assayed; this is a direction-of-interpretation warning, not a toxicity measurement.

summary: Prkaca knockdown was often strong but produced a self-only FDR signature.
why_it_matters: PKA catalytic alpha is a central cAMP effector, yet acute transcript depletion in mouse brain cells did not propagate into a broad steady-state mRNA program; the primary validated readout is target loss itself.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Steady-state RNA was measured, not PKA catalytic activity, substrate phosphorylation, cAMP dynamics or stimulated CREB output.

summary: The canonical PKA-CREB/MECP2 activity axis had no FDR-supported transcript-level echo after Prkaca depletion.
why_it_matters: The result separates loss of the catalytic kinase transcript from immediate loss of basal activity-regulated gene expression and suggests that protein phosphorylation or stimulation assays are needed to read this axis.
main_caveats: The experiment was not a neuronal-depolarization or cAMP-stimulation time course; CREB and MECP2 can be regulated by phosphorylation without changing their mRNAs.

summary: Prkaca and Prkar1a did not show opposite transcriptomes despite encoding antagonistic catalytic and regulatory arms of PKA.
why_it_matters: If basal PKA amplitude were transcriptionally rate-limiting, catalytic-subunit loss and RIα-regulatory loss would be expected to diverge. Instead both knockdowns were nearly self-only where they engaged, consistent with transcriptomic buffering of core holoenzyme dosage.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Prkar1a guide cell counts were smaller than Prkaca in overlapping classes, and the comparison uses score-vector correlations rather than matched phospho-PKA measurements.

summary: No upstream cAMP neighbors or unbiased signature neighbors phenocopied Prkaca knockdown.
why_it_matters: The absence of a high-correlation Adcy/Gnas/Pde/Creb or global neighbor argues that Prkaca loss was not simply a generic cAMP-pathway transcriptional state in this assay.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Many pathway-neighbor perturbations showed weak target-transcript engagement, and the largest global correlations were small enough to be sensitive to noise or safe-target structure.

summary: Apparent Prkaca phenotypic selectivity is dominated by variable target engagement and low cell counts, not by a clear downstream cell-type program.
why_it_matters: Negative calls in weakly engaged forebrain glutamatergic classes and in the 23-cell dopaminergic comparison should not be interpreted as biological resistance to PKA loss.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is a measurement-quality finding; it does not prove that the corresponding brain cell types are insensitive in vivo.

summary: Brain-cell Prkaca knockdown is a poor transcriptomic proxy for PRKACA gain-of-function tumor genetics.
why_it_matters: PRKACA disease genetics often increase catalytic signaling through activating mutation or DNAJB1 fusion, whereas this dataset depletes wild-type mouse Prkaca and observes almost no basal mRNA response; therapeutic hypotheses should therefore track direction, isoform and disease context rather than treating all PRKACA perturbations as interchangeable.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay used mouse brain loss-of-function and did not model adrenal steroidogenic cells, hepatocytes or the DNAJB1-PRKACA fusion protein.

summary: Fgf14 perturbation produced a sparse, buffered transcriptomic response despite mostly downward target-transcript shifts.
why_it_matters: FGF14 biology can be missed by scalar DE counts because its best-established role is NaV-channel regulation at the axon initial segment rather than transcriptional control of channel-gene abundance.
main_caveats: Fgf14 itself did not reach FDR significance in any cell class, so guide efficacy is a competing explanation for sparse downstream DE.

summary: Cirbp in 053 Sst Gaba was the only FDR < 0.05 gene, with Scarb2 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut as the only FDR < 0.10 candidate.
why_it_matters: These isolated markers identify the narrowest reproducible mRNA readouts of Fgf14 perturbation and prevent overcalling a broad pathway program.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cirbp was called from only 47 perturbed cells; Scarb2 was nominal at 10% FDR rather than 5% FDR; neither marker is a known direct FGF14 target here.

summary: Canonical NaV/KCNQ/AIS transcripts were not FDR-significantly regulated by Fgf14 perturbation in any tested cell class.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates FGF14-dependent channel localization and gating from transcriptional regulation of Scn, Kcnq, Ank3, or Kcnab genes.
main_caveats: mRNA abundance was measured, whereas the known mechanism depends on channel gating, protein targeting, and AIS localization.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, a restricted Fgf14 signature was closest to Ap2m1, Ap2s1, Ank3, Dlgap4, and Grip1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: The presence of Ank3 among the top neighbors links the exploratory thalamic Fgf14 mRNA signature to the axon-initial-segment scaffold that organizes NaV channels.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cosines used only the top 100 absolute Fgf14 score genes; the Fgf14 thalamic signature itself did not pass FDR < 0.05.

summary: Fgf14 did not globally phenocopy Fgf12, Fgf13, FGFR-family, or NaV/Kcnab knockdowns, even where those comparators engaged their own transcripts strongly.
why_it_matters: This argues that an FGF14 perturbation should not be treated as interchangeable with FHF paralogs, extracellular FGF receptor signaling, or even direct NaV subunit knockdown in acute scRNA signatures.
main_caveats: Correlation analyses are blunt for weak Fgf14 signatures; lack of phenocopy may partly reflect weaker Fgf14 knockdown than Scn or Kcnab comparator knockdowns.

summary: Sparse Fgf14 mRNA responses, including in nominally depleted cerebellar and hindbrain GABA classes, should not be read as evidence that FGF14 loss is functionally benign.
why_it_matters: Human FGF14 repeat expansions and mouse/adult Purkinje Fgf14 loss converge on ataxia and firing defects, so an inhibitor or degrader of FGF14 could carry electrophysiological toxicity that single-cell DE does not capture.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq classes are broad embryonic or developmental brain populations and are not adult human Purkinje neurons.

summary: Detectable Gprc5b engagement was confined to two of 22 analyzed cell classes and, in both, the significant readout was loss of Gprc5b mRNA itself rather than a broad downstream program.
why_it_matters: For an abundant brain orphan GPCR, acute cell-body RNA abundance is therefore a weak proxy for receptor pathway output; the result prioritizes target-transcript engagement over pathway-level DE as the immediately measurable phenotype.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The Pineal result has only 35 perturbed cells, and a transcriptionally buffered response does not exclude synaptic, electrophysiological, trafficking, or metabolic phenotypes.

summary: The only non-target FDR-significant Gprc5b hit, Pde1a down-regulation in L4-5 IT cortical glutamatergic neurons, occurred without measurable Gprc5b transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: Pde1a should not be promoted as a Gprc5b downstream biomarker from this dataset alone; it is the strongest statistical hit but is dissociated from target engagement in the same contrast.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: This is a single cell class and a single downstream gene; the finding is a target-engagement caveat rather than a mechanistic assignment.

summary: A beta-catenin developmental axis was not phenocopied by mature-neuron Gprc5b perturbation: Ctnnb1 knockdown drove hundreds of thalamic DE genes whereas Gprc5b in the same class had only nominal target reduction and no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: Prior Gprc5b-beta-catenin coupling comes from embryonic cortical progenitors; the Perturb-seq contrast argues that this developmental pathway is not automatically active downstream of Gprc5b in mature thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Gprc5b target reduction in this class was nominal rather than FDR-significant, and the literature context is embryonic progenitor biology rather than adult thalamic neurons.

summary: The 308 CB GABA class produced no interpretable cerebellar Gprc5b phenotype because neither Gprc5b nor any downstream gene reached FDR significance.
why_it_matters: This prevents the dataset from adjudicating published Purkinje-cell roles for GPRC5B in axon development, synapse formation, and motor learning; the cerebellar null is best treated as lack of engagement in a broad cell class.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset cell class is broad and may not isolate Purkinje neurons; target transcript depletion was weak.

summary: In Pvalb GABA cells, several neuronal receptor perturbations converged on a self-transcript-only signature: Gprc5b, Gpr158, Gabbr1, and Gabra1 each had exactly one FDR-significant row, the targeted transcript.
why_it_matters: The convergence suggests that receptor genes can be efficiently reduced yet buffered at the steady-state mRNA level in mature inhibitory neurons, so absence of a broad DE module should not be read as absence of receptor physiology.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The comparator set is restricted to the profiled genes and a single cell class; it does not test electrophysiological outputs.

summary: Gprc5b mRNA itself is the only robust short-timescale pharmacodynamic biomarker in this dataset; Pde1a and broader pathway scores are not reliable proximal biomarkers.
why_it_matters: For an orphan receptor with no curated ChEMBL mechanism entries, ligand or perturbation screens will need either direct target-mRNA confirmation or non-transcriptomic phenotypes rather than assuming a canonical DE signature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The statement is limited to this Perturb-seq readout and should not be generalized to protein localization, receptor signaling, or behavior without functional assays.

summary: Fzd6 single-gene perturbation produced no reproducible transcriptional phenotype in the measured mature-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A Wnt receptor perturbation with no FDR-supported genes across 371,818 tests should be interpreted as absent or unmeasured transcriptomic engagement, not as a weak cell-type-specific pathway hit.
main_caveats: CRISPR disruption may preserve the target mRNA; the parquet does not contain raw expression or indel measurements, so this is a transcript-level negative result rather than proof that all guides failed at the DNA level.

summary: Lack of a Fzd6 response is shared by most assayed Frizzled receptors, not unique to Fzd6.
why_it_matters: The Frizzled family comparison argues against overinterpreting isolated nominal Fzd6 genes and is consistent with strong buffering or poor mature-cell transcriptomic readout of single receptor paralogs.
main_caveats: The comparison captures mRNA phenotypes only; several Frizzled target rows were not transcriptionally depleted, so sparse DE can also reflect weak transcript-level engagement or low receptor expression.

summary: Fzd6 loss was uncoupled from the beta-catenin transcriptional program that was evident after Ctnnb1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: FZD6 is annotated to multiple Frizzled pathways, but in this assay its signature was nearly orthogonal to Ctnnb1 and did not alter beta-catenin-responsive genes such as Axin2 in the TH class where Ctnnb1 disruption was broad.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Ctnnb1 is downstream of all canonical Wnt receptors, so the contrast does not prove the absence of receptor-proximal PCP or calcium signals.

summary: Efficient Celsr2 depletion showed that a core PCP membrane component can be transcriptionally self-targeted yet almost downstream-silent.
why_it_matters: This pathway-neighbor control makes a non-transcriptional or buffered PCP interpretation plausible for Fzd6 instead of forcing weak nominal Fzd6 genes into an mRNA pathway model.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Celsr2 is a PCP cadherin rather than Fzd6 itself, and one isolated Gtf2f1 hit in L5 ET cortex could be unrelated noise or a narrow cell-type effect.

summary: The apparent Fzd6 nominal hotspots were not credible cell-type-specific programs.
why_it_matters: The two most tempting strata illustrate opposite limitations: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the largest Fzd6 cell count but no adjusted genes, whereas 145 MH-LH TH Glut contained the global minimum p value but only 45 Fzd6 cells and FDR 0.557.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: A subtle effect below the power of these strata cannot be excluded.

summary: The mature-brain negative result should not be read as evidence that FZD6 inhibition is developmentally safe.
why_it_matters: Human FZD6 variants and mouse Fzd3/Fzd6 genetics point to developmental PCP requirements, whereas the current assay perturbs single genes in sampled postmitotic brain populations and shows weak transcript-level Fzd6 engagement.
main_caveats: No drug, dose response, fetal exposure, or non-neuronal developmental tissue was assayed in the Perturb-seq dataset.

summary: Foxi1 perturbation was transcriptionally inert across the assayed mouse-brain classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset behaves as an in-brain lineage-mismatch test for an epithelial ionocyte transcription factor rather than as an informative model of Foxi1 effector biology.
main_caveats: The conclusion is a negative transcriptomic result from small perturbed cohorts; target protein editing cannot be measured from the DE table.

summary: The canonical Foxi1 epithelial SLC26A4/V-ATPase acid-base cassette was not engaged in brain cells.
why_it_matters: The strongest known Foxi1 disease mechanism is not simply portable into neuronal glutamatergic or GABAergic populations, so the dataset should not be interpreted as a Pendred or distal renal tubular acidosis model.
main_caveats: The relevant kidney, inner-ear, epididymal and ionocyte cell states were not assayed; absence of response in brain is expected from expression context.

summary: The only sub-FDR-0.6 peaks were restricted to 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: If these nominal peaks are revisited, validation should focus on these two classes, especially the low-count 008 class, rather than on a pan-neuronal Foxi1 response.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: FDR values were 0.412-0.504, the 008 class had only 22 perturbed cells, and no coherent Foxi1-linked pathway was implicated.

summary: Restricted Foxi1 signatures showed no robust convergence with Forkhead-family perturbations or with biologically interpretable signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-reading weak apparently similar signatures as Foxi1 paralog compensation or shared forkhead transcription-factor biology.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Correlations used only the 200 largest absolute Foxi1 scores from weak signatures; the result is a screen for missed convergence, not a validated network analysis.

summary: Arhgap18 targeting produced no FDR<0.05 transcriptional response in any of the 22 tested neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: Known ARHGAP18 biology centers on Rho-driven actin and microtubule remodeling, so the Perturb-seq data argue that any neuron-intrinsic effect in this assay is buffered, protein-level, morphologic, or poorly engaged rather than a broad mRNA program.
main_caveats: The null response is high confidence for this Wilcoxon table, but the same table shows weak direct Arhgap18 mRNA depletion, so it cannot distinguish biology from low perturbation efficacy.

summary: The only near-threshold event was a Myo6 increase in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, and it occurred without detectable Arhgap18 mRNA knockdown.
why_it_matters: This keeps the strongest biological lead visible while preventing it from being upgraded to a cytoskeletal module: it is consistent with ARHGAP18's actin/Rho literature but is a single exploratory transcriptomic hit.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Myo6 missed the 0.05 FDR cutoff, the target self-row was not depleted, and no enrichment or recurrence supports a multi-gene cytoskeletal program.

summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba showed the best nominal reduction of the Arhgap18 transcript but essentially no downstream response.
why_it_matters: Target engagement and downstream amplitude were decoupled; the cell type with the most negative Arhgap18 self-row had every downstream FDR equal to 1.0.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Arhgap18 decrease itself was only nominal and not FDR significant.

summary: Arhgap18 did not phenocopy available Rho-family perturbation neighbors and had no high-correlation signature neighbor in its strongest cell type.
why_it_matters: ARHGAP18 is a Rho GTPase-activating protein, but the best Arhgap18 signature was almost uncorrelated with related Rho-family signatures and with every other perturbation, indicating that these targets are not interchangeable in this dataset.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and is partly limited by weak Arhgap18 target engagement; Rhoa and Rhoc themselves were not available as perturbations under their canonical gene symbols.

summary: Nominal Arhgap18-responsive genes were cell-type-private rather than recurrent biomarkers.
why_it_matters: The table does not support a pan-neuronal Arhgap18 loss-of-function reporter gene; even low-p-value genes rarely reappeared with the same direction across cell classes.
main_caveats: The audit uses nominal p-value cutoffs to assess recurrence, not to claim individual gene significance.

summary: The brain-neuron Perturb-seq result cautions against treating ARHGAP18 as a generic neuronal transcriptional drug target.
why_it_matters: Prior disease-adjacent work links ARHGAP18 to mechanically active endothelial, cancer, and cardiac RhoA/RhoC pathways; the dataset instead shows broad buffering across neuronal classes despite public-atlas brain expression, pointing to cell context and non-transcriptional phenotypes as primary considerations.
main_caveats: This is an inference from neuronal transcriptomes; the dataset does not assay endothelial cells, tumor invasion, RhoA/ROCK activity, or cytoskeletal morphology.

summary: Chrnb1 perturbation showed no measurable cis depletion of the Chrnb1 transcript in any assayed brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The primary quality check for a CRISPRi loss-of-function interpretation failed, so downstream Chrnb1 hits should be read as a weak or unengaged perturbation rather than a clean β1 nicotinic receptor knockdown.
main_caveats: The table reports RNA ranks, not raw UMI detection or protein abundance; failure to deplete the RNA is consistent with a low or sparse transcript but does not prove guide inactivity.

summary: Chrnb1 produced no FDR<0.05 downstream gene in 22 brain cell classes, and the two FDR<0.10 peaks were isolated, up-regulated GABAergic signals.
why_it_matters: There is no credible cell-type-restricted transcriptional program to attach to Chrnb1; Rnf227 in Sst and Nova1 in CNU-HYa HY GABA are only hypothesis-generating peaks.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The absence of a downstream signature cannot be interpreted as cellular dispensability because the target transcript itself was not engaged.

summary: The muscle nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit set failed to behave as a coordinated perturbation module in this mouse-brain assay.
why_it_matters: Chrnb1 is a physical/channel subunit with Chrna1, Chrnd and the gamma/epsilon partners at the neuromuscular junction, yet brain transcriptional signatures for these perturbations were essentially uncorrelated and lacked recurrent receptor-family neighbors.
main_caveats: This is a restricted transcriptomic comparison among mostly weak cis perturbations; it should be treated as absence of detectable convergence, not proof that the proteins never share a complex.

summary: Other nicotinic-receptor subunit perturbations, especially Chrnb2 and Chrna4, showed transcript-level knockdown in selected thalamic and midbrain groups, whereas Chrnb1 did not.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the Chrnb1 null is not simply a universal failure of receptor-subunit guides or of the Wilcoxon pipeline; it is specific to the β1/muscle-subunit context assayed here.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparator result is about cis transcript depletion, not necessarily a broad downstream functional response.

summary: The Chrnb1 brain Perturb-seq profile is a context-mismatch warning for congenital myasthenia biology rather than a CNS regulatory signature for the disease gene.
why_it_matters: Known pathogenic CHRNB1 mechanisms affect acetylcholine receptor assembly and abundance at the postsynaptic neuromuscular junction; a brain dataset with no Chrnb1 RNA knockdown should not be used to infer a therapeutic direction for those endplate disorders.
main_caveats: This is a model-context inference; the dataset did not assay skeletal muscle fibers, motor endplates, or electrophysiologic AChR function.

summary: Bcl11a perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome response in any measured mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: BCL11A is a disease-linked transcription factor, so the primary dataset result is not a positive pathway hit but a global null that must be interpreted through weak target-RNA engagement.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not significantly depleted after FDR correction, coding CRISPR perturbation can affect protein without lowering mRNA, and 215 MB Dopa was not assayed for Bcl11a.

summary: The two cell classes with nominal Bcl11a transcript decreases did not activate a Sema3c/Tbr1/Bcl11b/Satb2 cortical projection-neuron program.
why_it_matters: Developmental mouse studies place Bcl11a upstream of Sema3c and cortical projection-neuron migration; the Perturb-seq result implies that this embryonic cortical circuitry is not acutely reconstituted in the assayed postmitotic cell classes or was missed because perturbation strength was low.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only targeted marker genes were checked; Sema3c and laminar-marker absence cannot exclude other Bcl11a biology.

summary: The paralog Bcl11b converged with Bcl11a only in being weak, not in a reproducible shared transcriptional signature.
why_it_matters: BCL11A and BCL11B are related BAF-associated transcription factors, but the dataset gives no evidence that perturbing either gene generates a strong interchangeable acute signature in the sampled brain cell types.
main_caveats: The correlation analysis used only the top 200 Bcl11a-scored genes per cell type and both perturbations had weak target-transcript readouts.

summary: Bcl11a was uncoupled from the strong chromatin-remodeler phenotypes seen for several BAF/SWI/SNF or CHD4 perturbations in the same result table.
why_it_matters: Because Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Chd4, Arid1a, Smarce1, Arid1b, Smarca2, and Smarcc1 produced FDR-significant hits while Bcl11a did not, the null Bcl11a result is target-specific rather than a blanket failure to score chromatin regulators.
main_caveats: These comparators are not equivalent subunits; several are core remodeler genes likely to have broader essential functions than Bcl11a.

summary: The neuronal null does not de-risk systemic BCL11A loss, even though erythroid BCL11A down-regulation is a validated therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: Approved ex vivo enhancer editing intentionally reduces BCL11A in erythroid cells to raise fetal hemoglobin, whereas germline BCL11A loss causes an intellectual-developmental disorder; weak knockdown in this mouse-brain table means the absence of an FDR signature should not be read as evidence that neuronal BCL11A loss is silent.
main_caveats: The dataset is not an erythroid enhancer-editing assay and did not demonstrate robust loss of Bcl11a RNA or protein in brain cells.

summary: Homer2 perturbation did not generate a corrected differential-expression signature in any measured neuronal subclass.
why_it_matters: The dataset is dominated by absence of robust target engagement, so lack of downstream pathway effects should be interpreted as inconclusive buffering or perturbation inefficiency rather than evidence that HOMER2 is dispensable.
main_caveats: High confidence for the measured null result, but it is confounded by all Homer2 target-transcript rows having FDR=1.0.

summary: The only high-rank on-target Homer2 decreases were nominal and concentrated in 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Any downstream interpretation should be weighted toward these two subclasses and away from pan-neuronal claims.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Both target rows are only nominal; neither survives FDR correction and neither cell type has any downstream FDR-significant gene.

summary: Canonical mGluR/IP3R/Shank pathway members were transcriptionally uncoupled from Homer2 despite their known physical links to HOMER scaffolds.
why_it_matters: Physical membership in the postsynaptic Homer scaffold did not translate into interchangeable Perturb-seq signatures, warning against interpreting GRM1, GRM5, SHANK2, SHANK3, DLG4, or ITPR1 perturbations as Homer2 substitutes in this assay.
main_caveats: Comparator knockdown was often stronger than Homer2 knockdown; near-zero correlations could reflect insufficient Homer2 perturbation rather than a true absence of shared biology.

summary: Dlgap4 was a recurrent positive restricted-signature neighbor of Homer2, suggesting a faint SAPAP/PSD scaffold footprint.
why_it_matters: DLGAP/SAPAP proteins sit between PSD-95 and Shank/Homer assemblies, so repeated Dlgap4-Homer2 co-signature is the main dataset hint that any postsynaptic scaffold biology was captured.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Computed only over Homer2 top-100 genes; four of five contributing cell types had weak Homer2 transcript engagement, and safe-target controls also reached extreme restricted-neighbor scores.

summary: 308 CB GABA showed a mixed restricted signature in which Homer2 aligned with Gria3, Gria4, Grid2, Grm1, and Dlg4 but opposed Syngap1, Fmr1, and Tsc2.
why_it_matters: This cerebellar pattern is the strongest hint that the Homer2 signature can intersect glutamatergic and synaptic-disease perturbations, but the opposite signs argue that the relationship is not a simple PSD-complex knockdown phenocopy.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Homer2 itself was not detectably lowered in 308 CB GABA, and a safe-target perturbation was also an extreme positive top-100 neighbor in this subclass.

summary: The mGluR5-Homer2-PI3K addiction-related pathway was not recapitulated as a coherent RNA module after Homer2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Alcohol-related Homer2 biology reported in nucleus accumbens is likely signaling- and region-specific; the present broad subclass screen should not be used to nominate PI3K or GRM transcripts as HOMER2 knockdown biomarkers.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq data do not isolate nucleus accumbens shell neurons and the Homer2 perturbation was weak, so this is a failure to observe a transcriptomic module, not a disproof of the published signaling mechanism.

direction: upregulation of S-phase and DNA-replication genes after Rb1 perturbation
summary: Rb1 perturbation strongly derepressed an E2F/G1-S DNA-replication program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: This is the clearest in-dataset readout expected for loss of a pRB brake: DNA-replication licensing, fork, and S-phase genes rose in a neuronal mouse-brain class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Rb1 mRNA itself was not significantly reduced, and the dataset measures RNA rather than DNA synthesis or apoptosis.

summary: Dnmt1-centered replication markers recur in 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, nominating Dnmt1, Tipin, Rfc2, and Rrm1 as compact biomarkers of functional Rb1 loss in this dataset.
why_it_matters: The Rb1 response is not a one-gene outlier restricted to the strongest cell type; the same DNA-replication axis appears at lower amplitude in additional neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only three cell types reached FDR for individual markers; recurrence outside those classes is based on nominal or score-level support.

summary: Several Rb1 strata showed little or no replication-gene induction despite measured Rb1 rows, with the weakest responses in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
why_it_matters: Rb1 perturbation is therefore strongly cell-type-selective in scalar DE output; negative cell classes should not be collapsed with the thalamic and midbrain responders.
comparators: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The nonresponsive groups had only 20-40 Rb1 cells and no transcript-level proof of Rb1 knockdown, so failed guide activity could contribute.

summary: The Rb1 S-phase signature converged most with Tfdp1, but not with E2f1, Cdkn2a, or Trp53 perturbation, in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class.
why_it_matters: The closest informative signature neighbor sits in the E2F/DP transcriptional apparatus, whereas upstream p16/CDK regulation and p53 did not mimic the Rb1 loss-of-brake phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Tfdp1 relationship was computed only on 37 Rb1-responsive genes; on-target mRNA engagement for several comparators was weak or not significant.

summary: E2f4 perturbation activated cell-cycle genes in overlapping classes but an FDR gene set that was non-identical to the Rb1 G1/S program.
why_it_matters: RB-family cell-cycle repressors were not interchangeable in this neuronal atlas: Rb1 preferentially exposed a G1/S replication module, whereas E2f4 exposed a distinct DREAM-like module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Rbl1 and Rbl2 perturbations were absent, so the comparison samples E2f4 rather than the full p107/p130-DREAM pocket-protein arm.

summary: In neuronal mouse-brain contexts, reducing Rb1 function points toward ectopic DNA-replication pressure rather than a benign quiescent state.
why_it_matters: Mouse genetics show that Rb loss can drive abnormal S-phase entry and neuronal loss; the perturb-seq signature gives a cell-class-resolved warning that functional RB1 inhibition in brain cells can derepress the same axis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay apoptosis, DNA content, or long-term neuronal survival.

summary: Lrpprc perturbation produced reproducibly negative target-transcript shifts but no FDR-significant single-gene collapse in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The dataset is compatible with partial acute loss of a mitochondrial RNA-stability factor rather than complete loss of LRPPRC function; this sets the confidence ceiling for all downstream pathway calls.
main_caveats: Single-cell mRNA was the only engagement readout; LRPPRC protein and oxidative phosphorylation activity were not measured.

summary: A mitochondrially encoded mRNA decrease was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and was weaker in two GABA classes.
why_it_matters: The responsive genes are direct products of the mitochondrial transcriptome stabilized by the LRPPRC-SLIRP RNP, so the 155 MB Glut signature is a mechanistically coherent Lrpprc loss-of-function footprint despite weak per-gene FDR.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The mitochondrial module was defined from nominal p values and a pre-specified 13-gene set; all Lrpprc rows for these genes had pvals_adj=1.0.

summary: Measured Lrpprc mRNA reduction was not sufficient to predict mitochondrial mRNA loss across cell types.
why_it_matters: The strongest target-transcript decreases occurred in 191 MB P MY GABA and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, but these classes lacked the coherent mitochondrial mRNA response seen in 155 MB Glut, refining the effect from a generic knockdown marker to a cell-context-dependent mitochondrial state.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Target engagement may differ at the protein level; 054 and 191 had only 31 and 48 perturbed cells.

summary: The 155 MB Glut mitochondrial mRNA module aligned with Opa1 and Lonp1 perturbations but not with all mitochondrial RNA or translation factors.
why_it_matters: This separates a convergent mitochondrial RNA-abundance endpoint from whole-transcriptome interchangeability: perturbing cristae/proteostasis genes could phenocopy mt-mRNA depletion, whereas PNPT1, PTCD3, GFM2, and DAP3 did not in this cell type.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: SLIRP, the direct complex partner, was not perturbed; Opa1 and Lonp1 are not LRPPRC-complex members, and the comparison is restricted to transcript abundance.

summary: mt-Nd1, mt-Co3, mt-Nd4, and companion mitochondrial transcripts form a candidate readout of Lrpprc/Opa1-like mitochondrial RNA loss in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: In Lrpprc-perturbed 155 MB Glut these RNAs occupied top p-value ranks, and Opa1 drove an even stronger same-direction mitochondrial transcript collapse in the same cell type, suggesting that the small mt-mRNA set is more informative than any single nuclear stress gene.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The proposed marker panel is hypothesis-generating and based on transcript counts in one cell type, not a validated respiratory-chain assay.

summary: Hcn2 transcript depletion was reproducible but concentrated in a subset of neuronal classes, led by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 191 MB P MY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: HCN2 is a broadly expressed neuronal Ih channel, but this Perturb-seq readout shows where the guide achieved enough on-target RNA depletion to interpret loss-of-Hcn2 biology in the atlas.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Readout is Hcn2 mRNA rather than Ih current; cell-type labels are transcriptomic classes and do not prove a match to the exact thalamocortical relay populations studied electrophysiologically.

summary: Strong Hcn2 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: after the target transcript was removed, no gene in any of the 22 Hcn2 cell-type signatures reached even FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Known HCN2 loss has large membrane and seizure phenotypes, so a flat non-self RNA signature indicates that electrophysiological dysfunction can be missed by early or cell-autonomous differential expression.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure Ih, firing, protein abundance, dendritic localization, or network synchrony; it therefore cannot rule out strong physiology without strong RNA changes.

summary: Hcn2 loss did not induce RNA-level compensation by its closest HCN-channel paralogs or by the TRIP8b/Pex5l auxiliary subunit.
why_it_matters: Because HCN2 can assemble with HCN1 and is regulated by TRIP8b, induction of Hcn1, Hcn3, Hcn4, or Pex5l would have suggested a direct homeostatic repair loop; the dataset instead supports post-transcriptional or electrophysiological regulation as the likely adaptive layer.
main_caveats: The tested RNA panel cannot exclude channel relocalization, altered gating, TRIP8b isoform changes, or protein-level compensation.

summary: The Hcn1 paralog was not an interpretable phenocopy of Hcn2 in this dataset because Hcn1 itself never reached adjusted on-target depletion, while Hcn2 perturbation also failed to move Hcn1 RNA.
why_it_matters: HCN1-HCN2 coassembly makes Hcn1 the obvious comparator, but weak Hcn1 target engagement prevents treating its flat signature as evidence that the paralogs are interchangeable or jointly buffered.
main_caveats: This is a perturbation-quality contrast rather than a definitive biological divergence between HCN1 and HCN2 proteins.

summary: The Hcn2 loss-of-function transcriptomic signature is potentially hazardous to ignore: thalamic Hcn2 depletion was robust yet non-self RNAs were silent, whereas mouse literature places HCN2 loss in absence-seizure and cardiac-rhythm mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Small-molecule HCN2 programs should not rely on a downstream RNA biomarker to certify neuronal safety; direct target RNA, electrophysiology, and circuit assays are more plausible primary readouts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq cells are mouse brain neurons, not heart or nociceptors; the dataset tests RNA depletion rather than acute pharmacologic pore block.

summary: Hippocampal/limbic glutamatergic classes did not achieve enough Hcn2 RNA depletion to adjudicate Hcn2 biology there.
why_it_matters: HCN1-HCN2 heteromers are relevant in hippocampal biology, so the lack of a CA1/CA3 transcriptional phenotype here should be read as weak target engagement rather than true absence of an effect.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Only two broad glutamatergic classes are represented by this evidence, and neither provided a significant self-transcript hit.

summary: Flt3 CRISPR perturbation was transcriptionally silent across all 22 assayed brain cell classes: the Flt3 transcript itself was never significantly reduced and no gene reached 5% FDR.
why_it_matters: This is a strong negative result for a broad FLT3-dependent steady-state neuronal program in this screen, and it prevents over-interpreting nominal isolated hits as FLT3 biology.
main_caveats: Target mRNA was also not depleted, so the screen cannot separate true biological buffering from poor DNA editing, low target expression, or sparse mRNA detection.

summary: Canonical FLT3 effector transcripts in the GRB2/SOS, PTPN11/GAB2/STAT5, and PI3K/MTOR arms were not coordinately changed by Flt3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Reactome places these adaptors and kinases immediately downstream of FLT3; their uniform FDR=1.0 behavior supports pathway inactivity or transcriptional uncoupling rather than a missed downstream module.
main_caveats: The assay measured mRNA only; weak pathway phosphorylation could occur without detectable transcriptional changes.

summary: Flt3 did not produce a cerebellar, thalamic, pontomedullary, or cortical-specialized response despite prior reports of regionally patterned Flt3 brain expression.
why_it_matters: The result refines Flt3 brain literature by showing that a region where Flt3 mRNA can be detected is not automatically a CRISPR-responsive FLT3-dependent cell type in this Perturb-seq assay.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The historical brain-expression studies do not necessarily match the age, neuronal subclasses, guide efficiency, or mRNA readout of this dataset.

summary: Flt3 was not interchangeable with related type III or FLT-family RTKs and pathway neighbors: Kit, Kdr, Flt4, Mapk1, and Mtor had isolated FDR hits in other contexts, but Flt3 had none and its signatures correlated only weakly with all queried neighbors.
why_it_matters: This keeps a family-level negative result from being mistaken for shared RTK biology; in these neurons, related receptors and downstream kinases behave as sparse, context-specific perturbations rather than a single FLT3-like module.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The strongest FDR events in related targets were isolated and may be self-transcript effects or off-target/idiosyncratic responses; correlations were computed in four representative Flt3 contexts, not every class.

summary: The neuronal Flt3 loss-of-function negative result should not be used to deprioritize FLT3 inhibition in FLT3-mutant AML.
why_it_matters: FLT3 is a validated hematologic oncogene and drug target, whereas this dataset lacks AML blasts or hematopoietic progenitors and shows no Flt3 mRNA engagement in brain cells.
main_caveats: The screen does not test activating FLT3 mutations, ligand-rich hematopoietic cells, or pharmacologic inhibitor response.

summary: Adgrl1 transcript lowering reached FDR significance only in four subcortical neuronal classes even though the target transcript was measured and shifted downward in all 22 Adgrl1 signatures.
why_it_matters: This separates true target engagement from cell types where the guide produced only nominal or weak evidence, and it identifies the contexts in which downstream interpretation is most defensible.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Human Protein Atlas expression is human and broad; several dataset cell types had low perturbed-cell counts, and non-FDR target rows should not be treated as engaged.

summary: FDR-level Adgrl1 mRNA loss was buffered at the transcriptome level: no non-Adgrl1 gene passed FDR<0.05 in the four strongest cell types.
why_it_matters: The main readout is target loss itself; synaptic phenotypes expected from Lphn1 biology are not represented as a coherent cell-autonomous RNA module in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Negative result in mRNA only; synapse number, localization, GPCR signaling, and neurotransmitter release were not measured.

summary: Latrophilin paralogs were directly engaged in overlapping cells but had nearly orthogonal Perturb-seq signatures and no detectable Adgrl2/Adgrl3 compensation after Adgrl1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Shared adhesion-GPCR family membership does not imply that acute Adgrl1, Adgrl2, and Adgrl3 loss are interchangeable at the RNA-signature level.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Full-signature correlations are descriptive and each paralog perturbation is dominated by a different self-transcript row.

summary: Perturbations of TENM/FLRT/UNC5 adhesion-neighborhood genes did not phenocopy Adgrl1 in any FDR-engaged Adgrl1 cell type.
why_it_matters: The dataset decouples acute cell-autonomous RNA output from the known extracellular synaptic adhesion network, preventing a misleading pathway-equivalence interpretation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Some core ligands such as Tenm2 were not present among assayed mouse perturbations, and RNA signatures may miss non-cell-autonomous ligand-receptor effects.

summary: Because disease literature supports ADGRL1 loss-of-function as deleterious, the dataset’s target-lowering signatures should be interpreted as a liability model rather than evidence for a beneficial inhibitory direction.
why_it_matters: ADGRL1 is a GPCR but not a conventional ChEMBL-supported drug target; additional antagonism or knockdown could move in the same direction as human haploinsufficiency.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The disease evidence is developmental and systemic, whereas the dataset is acute single-cell transcriptomics; no rescue or gain-of-function perturbation was assayed.

summary: Hcrtr2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response and no significant Hcrtr2 self-knockdown row in any of 22 tested cell types.
why_it_matters: This establishes the perturbation as functionally silent in the DE table and prevents overinterpretation of nominal genes as an OX2R loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: The DE table lacks raw baseline expression and guide-level validation; absence of an expression signature does not prove absence of receptor physiology.

summary: 145 MH-LH TH Glut was the only cell type with a visible nominal Hcrtr2 response, led by Cars and B4galt5 upregulation and Esf1 and Cdk14 downregulation, but all adjusted P values were >0.27.
why_it_matters: The MH-LH/TH glutamatergic group is the best place to look for follow-up Hcrtr2 effects in this dataset, while the statistics mark the gene list as exploratory rather than validated.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only 58 perturbed cells and no FDR-significant genes; the nominal top genes were not recurrent across cell types.

summary: The lack of a Hcrtr2 Perturb-seq signature refines animal narcolepsy genetics toward circuit and state dependence rather than contradicting OX2R biology.
why_it_matters: Hcrtr2 disruption and OX2R restoration have strong organismal sleep-wake effects, so a silent basal transcriptional profile indicates that the screen is not sampling the key receptor-expressing wake circuit or activation state needed to phenocopy narcolepsy.
main_caveats: The comparison is indirect: animal sleep phenotypes arise from intact circuits and ligand signaling, whereas the dataset measures cell-autonomous basal mRNA.

summary: An annotated orexin/Gq GPCR did not yield a detectable basal orexin-pathway transcriptional module after Hcrtr2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Reactome and UniProt support HCRTR2 as an orexin receptor in G-protein signaling, so the missing transcriptomic module flags pathway uncoupling or failed target engagement rather than absence of pathway membership.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure acute second messengers, calcium, ligand-evoked activity, or behavior.

summary: Hcrtr2 did not have a robust same-pathway or same-signature perturbation neighbor; all best neighbors were weak and often no stronger than safe-target structure.
why_it_matters: This prevents spurious assignment of Hcrtr2 to a transcriptomic module based on small correlations such as the 145 MH-LH TH Glut anticorrelation with Adcy5.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor calculations compare scalar score vectors and are especially noisy in the 25-cell 217 P MY Pineal Glut stratum.

summary: The Hcrtr2 DE table is not directionally informative for HCRTR2 agonism or antagonism.
why_it_matters: OX2R-selective activation has a pro-wake, anticataplectic effect in narcoleptic mice, but this dataset lacks the receptor knockdown and downstream signature needed to infer whether blocking or activating HCRTR2 would be favored in a disease context.
main_caveats: This is a translational interpretation of a negative perturbation result, not a pharmacology experiment.

summary: Glis3 target-transcript engagement was not detectable in any of the 23 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: Without measurable movement of the target transcript, downstream null results are best interpreted as weak engagement or transcript-level buffering rather than definitive absence of GLIS3 biology.
main_caveats: mRNA abundance may not capture DNA editing or protein loss.

summary: The Glis3 perturbation produced an almost pan-cell-type null transcriptomic response after FDR correction.
why_it_matters: A strong GLIS3-dependent neuronal gene program would be expected to yield recurrent corrected DE; instead, only one of 388,046 rows was FDR-significant.
main_caveats: The weak response may be driven by poor perturbation rather than true biological buffering.

summary: Cpe downregulation in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut is the lone FDR-significant Glis3-associated downstream hit.
why_it_matters: CPE participates in endocrine and neuronal peptide maturation and regulated secretion, making this single corrected hit a plausible neurosecretory follow-up marker.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene result; no corrected companion module; literature does not establish direct GLIS3-to-Cpe regulation in these neurons.

summary: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut showed the densest nominal Glis3 signature but no FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: This class is the best exploratory direction for a weak cell-type-restricted response, while still failing conventional correction.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: All highlighted genes have FDR 0.482, so the pattern is hypothesis-generating only.

summary: Glis3 signatures did not phenocopy Glis2 or GLI-family perturbations.
why_it_matters: It argues against treating GLIS/GLI C2H2 zinc-finger paralogs or relatives as interchangeable in this adult-brain Perturb-seq context.
main_caveats: The contrast is limited by the weak Glis3 source signature and by absence of Glis1 from the comparator perturbation set.

summary: Pancreatic GLIS3 pathway neighbors failed to converge with Glis3 in the adult brain panel.
why_it_matters: The neonatal-diabetes and beta-cell developmental literature should not be projected onto these adult neuronal Perturb-seq states without direct evidence.
main_caveats: Comparators are pathway neighbors rather than a single physical complex; cell type, developmental stage, and disease context are indirect.
