main_caveats: The contrast is based on whole-transcriptome score correlations; weak Acp1 target engagement could attenuate its correlations with true pathway neighbors.

summary: The Acp1 brain null should not be read as evidence that LMPTP inhibition is CNS-silent or intrinsically safe.
why_it_matters: LMPTP/ACP1 is a proposed small-molecule target for insulin resistance, and ACP1 is broadly detected in brain; a weak, FDR-null Acp1 Perturb-seq signature provides little support for either neuronal efficacy or absence of neuronal liability.
main_caveats: The experiment measured scRNA responses in mouse brain cell classes rather than enzyme phosphorylation, insulin stimulation, behavior, or chronic drug exposure.

summary: B3gat3 perturbation produced little genome-wide acute transcriptional output across the assayed mouse-brain neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: B3GAT3 is a core Golgi enzyme for proteoglycan GAG-linker completion, but the data show that partial transcript lowering rarely propagates into a cell-autonomous mRNA program in this assay.
main_caveats: The table measures mRNA differential expression only; B3gat3 itself did not pass FDR in any cell type, so weak CRISPRi engagement could contribute to the apparently buffered downstream response.

summary: The only genome-wide significant B3gat3 response was an exploratory Ndor1/Herc1 up-regulation restricted to 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-summarizing B3gat3 as entirely inert, but because the target transcript was not decreased in the same cells the two-gene signal should be treated as a candidate LSX GABA marker rather than a validated proteoglycan-biosynthesis response.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Only two genes reached FDR<0.05 and B3gat3 mRNA was not detectably knocked down in this contrast.

summary: B3gat3 did not share a coherent transcriptional signature with other assayed GAG-biosynthetic perturbations.
why_it_matters: Even enzymes in the same proteoglycan-linker/heparan-sulfate pathway were essentially uncorrelated, arguing that this screen does not recover a common acute mRNA module for GAG-chain initiation or modification.
main_caveats: Correlations are transcriptomic and several pathway members, especially B3gat3, had incomplete target-transcript knockdown.

summary: 155 MB Glut showed the best nominal B3gat3 target lowering but no broad downstream response.
why_it_matters: The midbrain glutamatergic class is the clearest case where B3gat3 itself moved in the intended direction, yet the response remained less transcriptionally penetrant than those of Ext2 or Hs6st2 in the same class.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: B3gat3 target lowering was nominal and not FDR-significant; a proteoglycan glycan defect could occur without a matched mRNA signature.

summary: The mostly negative Perturb-seq signature should not be interpreted as safety evidence for B3GAT3 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Human B3GAT3 loss of function decreases multiple proteoglycan classes and causes linkeropathy, and preclinical inhibitors are now indexed; the screen used partial CRISPRi knockdown in mature mouse-brain cell types and did not assay glycan chains or congenital matrix phenotypes.
main_caveats: The warning is grounded in human loss-of-function and inhibitor literature rather than a positive toxicity signature in this dataset.

summary: Esr1 perturbation produced a single corrected transcriptomic hit, Nfic up-regulation, in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest dataset-grounded biomarker is a lone putative downstream transcript rather than a broad estrogen-response module, so it should be treated as a local response marker, not as a validated ESR1 pathway readout.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only one gene passed FDR<0.05 and the Esr1 transcript itself was not detectably depleted.

summary: The Esr1 transcript was not detectably reduced in any cell type in which it was measured.
why_it_matters: Weak on-target RNA engagement is the dominant constraint on mechanistic interpretation; downstream effects could be rare-subpopulation effects, guide effects that do not lower steady-state Esr1 mRNA, or off-target/noisy effects.
main_caveats: The table reports cell-type-level RNA differential expression only; it does not report guide efficiency, allele editing, or protein abundance.

summary: Corrected Esr1-associated expression change was restricted to 155 MB Glut despite sampling 22 broad classes.
why_it_matters: The result refines expectations from established estrogen actions in glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons: this screen does not show a pan-neuronal ERα loss-of-function signature, and it picks out one midbrain glutamatergic class instead.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The atlas classes are broad; sparse Esr1-expressing subtypes may be diluted within classes that appear negative.

summary: Esr1 and Esr2 were not interchangeable in 155 MB Glut: each had a different single FDR hit and their full score vectors were only weakly correlated.
why_it_matters: Reactome and UniProt place ESR1 and ESR2 in the same signaling system, but the Perturb-seq data do not show a shared paralog signature in the only responsive Esr1 cell type.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Both paralog signatures were one-gene signatures without detectable depletion of the receptor transcript, so the contrast is qualitative and hypothesis-generating.

summary: The Esr1/Nfic response in 155 MB Glut did not co-cluster with perturbations of assayed steroid receptors, estrogen-related receptors, or receptor coactivators.
why_it_matters: A canonical ESR transcriptional module would be expected to involve receptor cofactor machinery; the lack of convergence argues that the observed Nfic hit is not a broad pathway-level ESR program in this cell type.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations may have different guide efficiencies in 155 MB Glut, and some nuclear receptors such as Rora and Esrra are pathway-family rather than direct ESR1-complex members.

summary: The mouse-brain Esr1 signature is too narrow to serve as a generic pharmacodynamic model for the clinically drugged ESR1 axis.
why_it_matters: ESR1 has strong clinical precedence, but ERα agonists and modulators perturb ligand state rather than simply reproducing this weak single-cell CRISPR loss-of-function RNA signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The screen is mouse brain, single-cell RNA loss-of-function; ChEMBL and Open Targets summarize mostly human systemic and oncology evidence.

summary: No close positive or inverse restricted-signature neighbor was found for Esr1 in its only FDR-positive cell type.
why_it_matters: The absence of a high-correlation neighbor prevents assigning the Esr1/Nfic phenotype to a larger convergent module based on transcriptome similarity alone.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed only within 155 MB Glut and on broad Wilcoxon score vectors; the weak Esr1 signature limits module discovery.

summary: Jund transcript depletion was strongest in 155 MB Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, with additional nominal depletion in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut rather than uniform knockdown across the brain subclasses.
why_it_matters: This separates cell types with credible on-target engagement from contexts where downstream genes cannot be safely interpreted as Jund biology.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only two target rows survived FDR <0.05; 008 and 005 are nominal on-target calls.

summary: Corrected downstream transcription was buffered: after excluding the target transcript, no gene reached FDR <0.05 anywhere in the Jund signatures, including the two FDR-significant target-engagement cell types.
why_it_matters: The primary phenotype of the perturbation is target knockdown itself, not a robust secondary gene module, arguing against a strong basal AP-1 transcriptional collapse under these conditions.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The assay measured basal transcriptomes; weak, delayed, stimulus-dependent, or non-transcriptional AP-1 effects could be missed.

direction: near-zero signature correlation with related perturbations
summary: Jund loss did not phenocopy the assayed AP-1/JNK neighbors Fosl2, Atf2, Map2k1, Mapk8 or Mapk9 in the best-engaged neuronal contexts.
why_it_matters: Known physical and signaling proximity within AP-1 does not imply interchangeability in this Perturb-seq map; Jund behaved as a weak, context-specific node rather than as a generic readout of the FOS/JUN/JNK module.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Jun, Junb, Fos, Fosb, Fosl1 and Jdp2 were not perturbed, and the observed correlations are restricted to whole-signature transcriptome correlations.

summary: The two largest non-target scalar excursions in 308 CB GABA and 215 MB Dopa are poor Jund phenotypes because they occurred without convincing Jund target engagement.
why_it_matters: A high absolute Wilcoxon score alone would falsely prioritize Zkscan2 or Magee1; the target row and cell count instead flag these as caveated or likely off-target/noisy signatures.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: This does not prove off-target editing; it only shows that the measured Jund transcript was not significantly depleted in these signatures.

summary: The basal mouse-neuronal perturbation does not reproduce the canonical JunD oxidative-stress phenotype described in endothelium.
why_it_matters: JunD can gate ROS genes in vascular aging models, but this dataset narrows that prior to a context- and stimulus-dependent mechanism rather than a default consequence of Jund loss in every post-mitotic cell type.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The dataset did not measure ROS, endothelial cells, aging, or challenge conditions; the comparison is mechanistically indirect.

direction: direct inhibition unsupported by this basal dataset
summary: The dataset gives no support for a large direct neuronal transcriptional effect from partial Jund inhibition, and ChEMBL did not show curated single-target JUND mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic reasoning should not treat JUND as an already tractable, neuron-wide AP-1 switch; if JUND is pursued, target engagement and stimulated disease contexts would need to be demonstrated directly.
main_caveats: ChEMBL coverage is not proof that no direct ligands exist, and this Perturb-seq dataset is not a pharmacology assay.

direction: up for sterol genes after Dync1h1 loss
summary: Dync1h1 knockdown activates a compact SREBP/sterol-biosynthetic transcriptional program in hypothalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant response to dynein-1 heavy-chain loss is lipid-homeostatic induction rather than a broad unbiased stress signature, suggesting a cholesterol or endomembrane state that a Dync1h1 perturbation repeatedly engages in specific neuronal contexts.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The pathway call is transcriptomic; cellular cholesterol, SREBP cleavage, and dynein motility were not directly measured.

summary: Dync1h1 transcript depletion can be statistically clear yet downstream transcriptional output remains near or below the FDR boundary.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from the sterol-response threshold: thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c neurons had significant Dync1h1 depletion but only nominal sterol induction, and Pvalb neurons had the strongest nominal target score in that class with no FDR-scale response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The reasoning is based on mRNA knockdown and per-cell-class FDR; sub-FDR coherent sterol shifts in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut argue against a fully absent response.

summary: Dync1h1 loss is much closer to dynactin Dctn1 loss than to weak dynein-family controls, and the shared component is the sterol module.
why_it_matters: A dynein heavy-chain perturbation and a dynactin p150 perturbation converge in the same regional neuronal classes, preserving the expected dynein-dynactin relationship while showing that the transcriptional output is not generic to every gene with a dynein prefix.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Pafah1b1 had few cells and no FDR-positive direct signature; the Dync2h1 target transcript was not measured, so the dynein-2 contrast is negative but not a clean on-target comparison.

summary: Restricted-signature neighbors place Dync1h1 with Rab7 and ESCRT/late-endosomal perturbations in the responsive sterol states.
why_it_matters: The dataset links the SREBP output not only to the dynein-dynactin motor core but also to endosome-lysosome trafficking nodes that can couple cargo transport to sterol sensing.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The ESCRT/Rab7 statement comes from top-500 score correlations rather than a direct physical assay or a cholesterol-trafficking readout.

direction: Dync1h1 loss up; Srebf2 loss down
summary: Dync1h1 perturbation has the opposite direction from direct Srebf2 knockdown on the same sterol genes, consistent with compensatory SREBP activation.
why_it_matters: The Dync1h1 response should be interpreted as activation of an endogenous lipid-synthesis feedback circuit, whereas Srebf2 loss collapses that circuit; this polarity is important for predicting interventions that block dynein or SREBP nodes.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Opposite transcript direction does not prove that Dync1h1 acts upstream of SCAP-SREBP; it only shows that the observed module has SREBP-like polarity.

summary: Dync2h1 and Dync2i1 did not provide a significant dynein-2 mirror of the Dync1h1 response.
why_it_matters: The analysis did not find a broad dynein-family effect that would explain the Dync1h1 signature, but the negative comparison is mostly a quality filter rather than mechanistic evidence.
main_caveats: Dync2h1 was not measured as an output gene, and Dync2i1 did not reach FDR-significant self-knockdown; absence of a signature cannot be read as biology without better target engagement.

summary: Ndufs7 perturbation produced weak global transcriptomic output: no on-target FDR support and only one of 388046 tested Ndufs7 rows at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The file should not be mined as though it contains a clean Complex I loss-of-function program; most downstream observations are negative or nominal.
main_caveats: Target mRNA depletion is an imperfect proxy for CRISPR protein loss; negative transcriptomics cannot exclude DNA editing or physiological defects.

summary: Nominal Ndufs7 transcript depletion was concentrated in six posterior, thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, pontine, or medullary classes rather than being even across all cell classes.
why_it_matters: This is the only reproducible directionality within the Ndufs7 rows themselves, but it is exploratory because all adjusted values were 1.0.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The pattern may reflect guide capture, expression, detection, or small perturbed-cell counts rather than true cell-type-selective NDUFS7 biology.

summary: Ndufs7 was much weaker than related Complex I NDUF perturbations, many of which achieved strong on-target FDR support in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: NDUFS7 is expected to behave as part of the same Complex I/IP subcomplex neighborhood as NDUFS2, NDUFS3, NDUFS8, and multiple NDUF accessory subunits; the observed outlier behavior identifies Ndufs7 as a perturbation-quality exception.
main_caveats: The comparison uses mRNA recovery and DE-score correlations, not direct protein depletion or Complex I enzyme activity.

summary: The Ndufs7 signature did not activate a recurrent Atf4/Ddit3/Chac1/Trib3/Xbp1 mitochondrial stress or ISR program.
why_it_matters: For a core Complex I subunit, absence of ISR output is a key negative pathway result and suggests that any biological interpretation should first account for weak engagement.
main_caveats: The literature used diverse mitochondrial stressors, often outside developing mouse brain; lack of ISR here may be a false negative caused by weak Ndufs7 perturbation.

summary: Capn2 is a low-confidence CA3/CA2-FC/DG biomarker candidate because it was the only FDR<0.05 Ndufs7-responsive row, but it occurred without detectable Ndufs7 mRNA depletion in the same cell type.
why_it_matters: This prevents the sole adjusted hit from being over-promoted to a general NDUFS7 effector while preserving it as an exploratory local observation.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Single gene, single cell type, only 85 perturbed cells, and no same-cell nominal on-target Ndufs7 depletion.

summary: NDUFS7 loss should still be treated as pathogenic despite the weak mouse Perturb-seq signature.
why_it_matters: Human NDUFS7 loss-of-function causes Complex I deficiency and Leigh syndrome, and the screen lacks enough engagement to de-risk NDUFS7 or Complex I inhibition in neurons.
main_caveats: The dataset contains transcriptomic contrasts only, not survival, respiration, or organismal disease phenotypes.

summary: Ift88 perturbation produced consistent but weak target-transcript depletion and a globally sparse differential-expression profile.
why_it_matters: Interpretation should be driven by the few cell classes with nominal on-target signal rather than by treating every cell-class contrast as a full loss of Ift88 function.
main_caveats: The table contains transcript-level differential expression only; IFT88 protein and ciliary structure were not measured, and several cell classes had only 30-50 perturbed cells.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the most biologically coherent Ift88 context, with nominal co-down-regulation of Ift88, the IFT-B partner Ift57, and Tulp3.
why_it_matters: The co-directional Ift57 signal is the strongest hint that the perturbation may have touched ciliary transport machinery in a specific thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic class, even though it did not survive FDR correction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Nominal-only support; no gene in this cell class was FDR<0.05.

summary: Pcsk1n was a statistically strong but isolated 155 MB Glut marker response to the Ift88 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Pcsk1n is the only transcriptome-wide significant Ift88-associated row in the entire table, so it is useful as a marker hypothesis but should not be read as proof of canonical ciliary pathway engagement.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Ift88 transcript was not reduced in the same cell class, and the Pcsk1n hit was a singleton FDR-significant gene.

summary: Ift88 did not transcriptionally converge with same-complex IFT perturbations or nearby ciliary/Hedgehog perturbations.
why_it_matters: Despite Ift88, Ift81, and Ift43 belonging to the curated IFT machinery, their signatures were essentially uncorrelated or weakly anticorrelated, arguing against simple interchangeability of low-efficiency ciliary perturbations in this screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Contrast is restricted to transcriptional scores; all related perturbations were themselves weak, and the absolute correlations were small rather than strongly opposite.

summary: Canonical Smoothened/Gli target-gene output was not detectably coupled to the Ift88 perturbation in the highlighted thalamic or midbrain glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: Developmental mouse genetics predicts that Ift88 loss can perturb Gli activator and repressor logic; the Perturb-seq result instead suggests that these sampled neuronal populations either lacked acute Hedgehog transcriptional output, were buffered, or were insufficiently perturbed.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The canonical readout genes are lowly expressed in some neuronal classes; absence of differential expression for Gli targets is not a direct assay of ciliary trafficking or Gli protein processing.

summary: 191 MB P MY GABA showed the largest Ift88 logFC decrease but no transcriptome-wide significant downstream response.
why_it_matters: This separates nominal target engagement from a scalar count of FDR-significant genes and flags a possible buffered or underpowered Ift88 response in an MB/P/MY GABAergic class.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only 65 perturbed cells were available, the Ift88 row itself had FDR=1.0, and no independent ciliary phenotyping was performed.

summary: Dnmt3a perturbation produced a globally buffered acute scRNA-seq response: the target mRNA trended downward in many cell types, but no gene reached FDR<0.10 in any of 22 cell-type tests.
why_it_matters: DNMT3A is a catalytic writer of neuronal DNA methylation, so a weak acute mRNA phenotype suggests that partial single-cell perturbation, assay timing, or methylome-first biology can hide functionally important DNMT3A loss from one-time-point transcriptomics.
main_caveats: Target transcript FDR did not pass 0.1; the dataset has transcriptomic, not methylome, readout and may be too early or too partial for DNMT3A-dependent methylation phenotypes.

summary: The strongest nominal on-target Dnmt3a depletion was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, whereas multiple cortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar classes had essentially no Dnmt3a mRNA change.
why_it_matters: Apparent Dnmt3a cell-type specificity in this table is driven at least partly by differential target engagement, so negative cortical or hippocampal results should not be interpreted as biological resistance to DNMT3A loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type differences are not FDR-supported and can reflect guide delivery, baseline target expression, or cell number rather than true lineage-specific dependency.

summary: Pvalb Gaba cells showed Dnmt3a and Gls as the top two nominal decreases, but both remained sub-FDR, giving no acute support for the broad GABAergic knockout program reported after genetic Dnmt3a deletion.
why_it_matters: The result separates a weak acute Perturb-seq signature in mature Pvalb cells from long-term inhibitory-neuron Dnmt3a biology, preventing overinterpretation of the Pvalb nominal hit as a Rett-like or Mecp2-like transcriptional state.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The literature used conditional knockout across GABAergic inhibitory neurons and profiled chronic outcomes, whereas this dataset is an acute Pvalb-class transcriptomic perturbation with target mRNA FDR 0.4339.

summary: Dnmt3a was far weaker than Kmt2a and Kmt2b in matched thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic contexts and was essentially uncorrelated with Kmt2a, Kmt2b, Mbd2, Mecp2, Tcf4, or Zbtb18 score vectors.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the weak Dnmt3a profile is not a generic inability of these cell types to mount chromatin-regulator responses and that methyl-DNA readers do not acutely substitute for the Dnmt3a signature in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Kmt2a and Kmt2b are chromatin regulators rather than DNA methyltransferases; Mecp2/Mbd2 target engagement was not always validated by target-mRNA loss in the same cell types.

summary: An all-perturbation scan over the top 500 genes from each of nine nominally target-engaged Dnmt3a signatures found only weak, non-recurrent neighbors, with maximum absolute correlations below 0.39.
why_it_matters: This makes Dnmt3a unsuitable as a member of a reusable acute co-expression module in this dataset and warns against elevating any one nominal top gene to a pathway without external evidence.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only on the top 500 absolute Dnmt3a genes per cell type, so they are exploratory and enriched for nominal noise when the seed signature itself lacks FDR hits.

summary: Because DNMT3A is clinically druggable but this neuronal Perturb-seq assay produced no corrected acute biomarkers, DNMT3A-directed perturbations in brain should be monitored with methylome or long-term functional readouts rather than only same-state scRNA-seq.
why_it_matters: Approved hypomethylating agents have DNMT3A mechanism annotations, but the dataset indicates that immediate transcript downregulation is a poor stand-alone pharmacodynamic proxy in mature brain cell types.
main_caveats: This is an inference from CRISPR perturbation, not a drug treatment; nucleoside DNMT inhibitors have DNMT-family effects and oncology indications, not demonstrated cell-type-selective CNS DNMT3A pharmacology here.

summary: Isca2 achieved FDR-supported target-transcript depletion only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut among 22 profiled contexts.
why_it_matters: Most apparent cell-type differences in downstream signal must be interpreted through unequal target engagement rather than as pure biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Target engagement is assessed only from the Isca2 mRNA row; protein depletion and guide-level efficacy were not measured in the Wilcoxon table.

summary: The FDR-supported 151 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered for the late mitochondrial iron-sulfur pathway.
why_it_matters: A direct ISCA2 mRNA decrease did not propagate to FDR-supported changes in core late-ISC partners or 4Fe-4S client/iron transcripts, narrowing the interpretable biology to partial or compensated loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: FDR-supported absence is transcript-level only and cannot exclude mitochondrial protein, lipoylation, enzymatic, or metabolite defects.

summary: 191 MB P MY GABA carried the largest weak downstream tail despite only nominal Isca2 depletion.
why_it_matters: This separates a hypothesis-generating MB/GABA response from the cleaner target-engagement phenotype in 151.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Isca2 was not FDR-depleted in 191; the top non-target FDR was 0.164713, so this is not a genome-wide significant gene program.

summary: Restricted Isca2 signatures did not converge strongly with Fe-S pathway-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: Available mitochondrial neighbors failed to substitute for missing ISCA1/IBA57/NFU1/GLRX5 perturbations, and the weak 191 signature aligned more with neuronal receptor/channel perturbations than with Fe-S genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations used top-500 nominal Isca2 genes in two contexts; the direct late-ISC complex members were measured genes but were not perturbation targets in the 2,046-target library.

summary: The mouse Perturb-seq phenotype did not recapitulate a strong ISCA2-loss/MMDS4 transcriptional state.
why_it_matters: Human ISCA2 loss is a severe neurodevelopmental mitochondrial disease, but this dataset supports under-engaged or buffered acute perturbation rather than a faithful disease-like collapse of mitochondrial Fe-S biology.
main_caveats: MMDS4 arises from inherited strong loss of function in humans, whereas this assay is an acute mouse-brain transcriptome with partial target knockdown.

direction: Cadm2 down in the four FDR-significant classes; weak or non-significant in many cortical/hippocampal classes
summary: FDR-level Cadm2 transcript depletion is concentrated in four non-cortical populations: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The directly interpretable Cadm2 perturbation contexts are thalamic, hypothalamic, and midbrain classes rather than broad cortex/hippocampus, even though CADM/SynCAM proteins are broadly neuronal adhesion molecules.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Selectivity is measured as target-transcript engagement in this Perturb-seq summary and may reflect expression level, guide efficiency, or power rather than intrinsic CADM2 biology alone.

direction: buffered downstream mRNA response after Cadm2 knockdown
summary: Cadm2 loss produced a target-only FDR signature: Cadm2 itself was the only transcript reaching FDR<0.05 across all 371818 Cadm2 differential-expression rows.
why_it_matters: The result argues that acute loss of this membrane adhesion transcript does not trigger a large cell-autonomous mRNA programme in the sampled adult brain classes; SynCAM/CADM phenotypes may be more visible at protein localization, synapse, or circuit levels.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: A lack of FDR-significant mRNA changes does not rule out synaptic structural, electrophysiological, extracellular, or delayed effects.

summary: Cadm2 perturbation did not induce mRNA compensation by Cadm1, Cadm3, or Cadm4.
why_it_matters: CADM2 can form heterophilic SynCAM-family adhesion pairs, so an acute transcriptional switch among CADM paralogs would have been a plausible buffering mechanism; it is not supported here.
main_caveats: This tests mRNA abundance only; Cadm1, Cadm3, and Cadm4 were not themselves perturbed, and compensation at protein localization or adhesion strength would be missed.

direction: Cadm2 down with feeding-marker mRNAs unchanged at FDR level
summary: Hypothalamic Cadm2 loss is visible, but canonical feeding and neuropeptide markers are not detectably rewired at the mRNA level.
why_it_matters: Cadm2 has published links to body weight and hypothalamic expression; this dataset points away from an acute, bulk change in Agrp/Npy/Pomc/Lepr-class transcripts as the dominant immediate readout.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The hypothalamic groups are broad transcriptomic classes, two Cadm2 effects are only nominal after FDR correction, and the assay was not a metabolic challenge.

summary: A CADM2-lowering strategy motivated by metabolic phenotypes would need to account for robust Cadm2 engagement in non-hypothalamic thalamic and midbrain GABA/glutamate populations.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse literature links CADM2 to both metabolic and behavioral traits; the Perturb-seq response was distributed across brain classes rather than restricted to the hypothalamic energy-balance axis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset reports transcriptomic responses only and contains no behavior, body-weight, synapse-structure, or circuit-activity assays.

summary: The target-centric, buffered response is shared across several related neuronal-adhesion perturbations rather than being unique to Cadm2.
why_it_matters: Related synaptic adhesion genes often achieved strong on-target depletion but very few off-target FDR effects, suggesting that this Perturb-seq assay under-resolves the downstream biology of adhesion molecules as a class.
main_caveats: This is a related-target comparison, not a direct perturbation of CADM1/CADM3/CADM4, and the absence of transcriptomic hits should not be read as absence of synaptic phenotypes.

summary: Npy5r perturbation was not detectably engaged at the transcript level in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: Without a significant fall in the assayed Npy5r transcript, the dataset cannot cleanly distinguish biological buffering from incomplete on-target editing or low target expression; this limits all downstream mechanistic inference.
main_caveats: The DE table measures Npy5r RNA, not receptor protein or indel status, so absent RNA depletion is a conservative engagement caveat rather than proof of no genetic edit.

summary: Across 321647 tests, Npy5r produced no FDR-significant downstream gene and no recurrent nominal module.
why_it_matters: The strongest Npy5r effects are isolated nominal outliers rather than a replicated neuronal state change, which argues against a broad acute cell-autonomous transcriptional program from single Npy5r loss in these assayed populations.
main_caveats: FDR silence is a direct observation, but the biological cause could be weak target engagement, low expression, insufficient power, or physiologic buffering.

summary: 308 CB GABA carried the most coherent subthreshold Npy5r signature, including nominal Gnaz and Pde4a induction.
why_it_matters: Because NPY5R is a peptide GPCR linked to Gi-mediated adenylate-cyclase inhibition, the nominal appearance of Gnaz and the cAMP regulator Pde4a highlights cerebellar GABA cells as the only dataset context worth prioritizing for receptor-protein and cAMP follow-up.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: No CB GABA gene reached FDR<0.05; only 39 perturbed cells were available; the Gnaz/Pde4a relationship is pathway-adjacent and not evidence that NPY5R directly regulates their transcription.

summary: Single Npy5r, Npy1r, and Npy2r perturbations were all silent at FDR<0.05 and their nominal signatures were not aligned.
why_it_matters: The same-family receptor panel does not show simple interchangeability at the single-cell transcriptome level, fitting a model in which NPY receptor effects depend on ligand, circuit, and combinatorial receptor context rather than creating a universal receptor-family signature.
main_caveats: This is a negative and correlation-based comparison among weak receptor signatures; ligand genes were not assayed as perturbations.

summary: Npy5r did not phenocopy the broader Gi/o pathway neighbor Gnao1.
why_it_matters: Even in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic classes where Gnao1 RNA knockdown was statistically clear, Npy5r showed no target-transcript depletion and near-zero score correlation with Gnao1, indicating that the receptor perturbation does not behave like wholesale Gi/o loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Gnao1 is a broad G-protein alpha subunit used by many receptors, so full phenocopy was not expected; the contrast mainly shows that the Npy5r guide phenotype is not a strong Gi/o transcriptomic proxy.

summary: The Perturb-seq phenotype and human antagonist trials both caution that single-agent NPY5R blockade may produce only small effects unless the relevant circuit context is engaged.
why_it_matters: A silent mouse single-cell signature is consistent with mouse and human evidence that Y5R is not a stand-alone obesity node; it argues for testing NPY5R activity in ligand-rich hypothalamic circuits or receptor combinations rather than inferring efficacy from receptor druggability alone.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain Perturb-seq rather than an adult human obesity assay, and weak Npy5r transcript engagement prevents strong claims about loss-of-function efficacy.

summary: Bicra perturbation produced neither measurable Bicra RNA knockdown nor any FDR-significant transcriptomic response in the 22 tested mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: BICRA is a nuclear ncBAF/GBAF chromatin-remodeling subunit, so the biologically safest interpretation is failed or weak functional engagement rather than neuronal dispensability.
main_caveats: CRISPR coding edits can leave target mRNA intact, so the RNA row is not a direct protein-loss assay; however the total lack of downstream FDR signal leaves effective perturbation uncertain.

summary: The L2/3 IT ENT/PPP/RSP glutamatergic class contained the lowest-FDR Bicra nominal hits, but even this apparent cell-type preference remained below significance.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not nominate a confident Bicra-responsive neuronal subclass; the L2/3 signal is only a triage point for future validation.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: All genes had FDR>=0.174 and the Bicra transcript itself was unchanged in this cell type.

summary: Bicra was uncoupled from a strong TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic BAF-neighbor module driven by Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Smarce1, and Arid1a perturbations.
why_it_matters: Shared mSWI/SNF biology was readily detectable in the same cell type, so the flat Bicra profile is target-specific and not simply a failure of thalamic neurons to respond to chromatin-remodeler perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The available comparators were mostly broader BAF assembly neighbors; the direct BICRA paralog and ncBAF partners Bicral, Brd9, and Ss18 were absent from the queried perturbation results.

summary: A transcriptome-wide neighbor scan found no strong Bicra-like or anti-Bicra-like perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: The negative result was not hiding an obvious alternative pathway neighbor, paralog substitute, or opposite-response perturbation among the assayed genes.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations were calculated on Wilcoxon score vectors rather than raw single-cell profiles; the conclusion is signature-level only.

summary: Known BICRA-linked Coffin-Siris/neurodevelopmental biology was not resolved to a responsive adult mouse-brain cell class in this experiment.
why_it_matters: The disease association makes BICRA a high-value neurodevelopmental gene, but the dataset should be treated as uninformative for CSS12 cell-of-origin rather than as a negative disease model.
main_caveats: Human heterozygous germline disease, developmental timing, and organismal phenotypes are only indirectly matched to acute mouse single-cell perturbation.

summary: The flat Bicra signature should not be used as evidence that ncBAF or BRD9 inhibition is transcriptionally silent in neurons.
why_it_matters: BRD9/ncBAF is a therapeutic vulnerability in SMARCB1-perturbed cancers and has been pursued clinically; this mouse Bicra run lacked enough target engagement to answer safety or efficacy questions for that axis.
main_caveats: The perturbation targeted Bicra rather than Brd9, was transcriptomic rather than viability-based, and did not include the tumor contexts in which ncBAF dependencies were reported.

summary: Mast1 perturbation produced a globally weak transcriptional phenotype across the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset message is absence of a corrected downstream mRNA program rather than a missed pathway hit; this constrains acute Mast1 loss to either subtle, protein-level, developmental, or poorly engaged effects in this assay.
main_caveats: Target-transcript reduction was mostly nominal and never FDR-significant, so a true loss-of-function may not have been achieved in every cell type.

summary: Two inhibitory populations showed nominal Mast1 self-knockdown among the most negative genes but no FDR-significant downstream response.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from response amplitude: even the best RNA-level engagement in CNU-HYa HY GABA and Pvalb GABA cells did not propagate to a detectable mRNA state change.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Self-transcript FDR remained 1.0, and buffering is inferred from RNA only.

summary: The only near-threshold Mast1 responses were single up-regulated genes in two GABA classes rather than a recurrent cell-type program.
why_it_matters: Dnaja2 in CNU-MGE GABA and Vps41 in CTX-CGE GABA mark hypotheses for follow-up, but their singleton nature argues against a robust pan-inhibitory Mast1 pathway in the current data.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Both genes were only FDR<0.1, neither was FDR<0.05, and the nearest positive or negative signature neighbors had very small correlations.

summary: Disease-relevant cortical and cerebellar classes did not show a corrected acute Mast1-targeting mRNA phenotype, paralleling reports that Mast1-null mice are phenotypically normal whereas a human-disease single-amino-acid deletion is pathogenic.
why_it_matters: Mega-corpus-callosum syndrome biology should not be modeled as simple acute Mast1 haploinsufficiency in these cells; variant-specific dominant-negative or developmental axon effects are more consistent with the literature and the dataset null.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is not a knock-in of disease alleles and does not measure embryonic corpus-callosum or cerebellar morphogenesis.

summary: Mast1 signatures were uncoupled from the available PTEN/dystrophin-neighborhood perturbations and lacked strong positive or negative transcriptomic neighbors.
why_it_matters: Known syntrophin and PTEN links did not translate into an interchangeable mRNA signature, so MAST1 network membership is not sufficient to predict its acute Perturb-seq state.
main_caveats: Sntb2 and MAST-family paralogs were not perturbed in this dataset, and the correlation screen is restricted to transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon score vectors.

summary: MAST1 is a kinase with biochemical ligand evidence, but the brain Perturb-seq data provide no strong transcriptional efficacy or liability biomarker for MAST1 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Small-molecule follow-up should prioritize direct kinase, cytoskeletal, and developmental phenotypes rather than assuming that partial Mast1 mRNA reduction will produce a robust RNA biomarker in neurons.
main_caveats: ChEMBL and Open Targets establish biochemical tractability, not a clinical MAST1 inhibitor program or a desired direction of modulation for neurodevelopmental disease.

summary: Arl6ip1 perturbation produced broad on-target mRNA depletion, with the strongest FDR-supported target knockdown in hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset contains a real Arl6ip1 perturbation rather than a failed guide set, but FDR-level engagement is uneven across cell classes and is therefore a key constraint on downstream interpretation.
main_caveats: Target FDR is partly coupled to sample size and baseline detectability; several nominally strong cell types missed FDR<0.05 after transcriptome-wide correction.

summary: Most FDR-supported Arl6ip1 knockdowns were transcriptionally buffered: the perturbed target was significant but downstream genes were not.
why_it_matters: ARL6IP1 has ER-shaping, anti-apoptotic, and disease roles, so the absence of a broad acute mRNA program implies that the first-order phenotype in this assay is likely structural, post-transcriptional, chronic, or dependent on unmeasured cell states rather than a large cell-autonomous transcriptional cascade.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Single-cell transcriptomics will miss ER morphology, mitochondrial contacts, protein turnover, and late neurodegenerative phenotypes; CRISPRi knockdown may also leave residual protein.

summary: Acute neuronal Arl6ip1 knockdown did not trigger a transcriptome-wide ER-stress, integrated-stress, apoptosis, or autophagy sentinel response.
why_it_matters: This narrows interpretation of the buffered signature: even where the target transcript was depleted, canonical Ddit3/Xbp1/Hspa5-type stress readouts were not robust, arguing against strong acute UPR induction as the main measured response.
main_caveats: The sentinel panel was manually selected and mRNA-only; absence of FDR does not exclude localized ER remodeling or autophagy flux changes.

summary: Shared ER-shaping/HSP or glutamate-transporter annotations did not make ATL1, REEP1, REEP2, or SLC1A1 acute signatures interchangeable with Arl6ip1.
why_it_matters: ARL6IP1 can bind atlastin and modulate EAAC1/SLC1A1 activity, while ATL1 and REEP1 are canonical ER-shaping HSP genes; the weak Arl6ip1 correlations indicate that related membrane-remodeling genes should not be collapsed into one transcriptomic module in this assay.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison used top-500 restricted correlations rather than full multivariate modeling; several related targets had fewer perturbed cells or weaker target engagement outside the specified cell types.

summary: Atp9a up-regulation is a single-cell-type candidate marker of Arl6ip1 loss in 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: It is the only non-target gene that survived transcriptome-wide correction after Arl6ip1 knockdown, making it the sharpest dataset-derived candidate for follow-up despite the otherwise buffered response.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Observed in only one cell type with modest logFC; no recurrence across other Arl6ip1 signatures and no mechanism is inferred here.

summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq readout is much weaker than chronic Arl6ip1-loss disease phenotypes, so rescue of HSP-like pathology should not be expected to appear as a broad acute neuronal mRNA reversal signature.
why_it_matters: AAV9-ARL6IP1 can reduce phenotypes in a KO mouse model, but this dataset indicates that standard neuronal single-cell mRNA endpoints may under-report the most relevant ER--mitochondrial, myelin, and inflammatory biology.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measured acute neuronal knockdown, not lifelong complete knockout, AAV rescue, glia, white matter, protein, or ER morphology.

summary: Pik3r1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response despite a weak negative trend in the target transcript.
why_it_matters: The primary biological readout is absence of a coherent RNA phenotype; a single p85α knockdown should therefore not be assumed to inhibit or activate PI3K output in these neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The negative result is strongly supported statistically, but it may reflect weak knockdown and low cell counts rather than complete biological buffering.

summary: Class-IA PI3K subunit perturbations were FDR-silent, whereas Tsc1, Tsc2, and Pten perturbations triggered large responses in the same dataset and in several matched cell types.
why_it_matters: This separates an upstream PI3K regulatory/catalytic-subunit layer from a highly readable TSC/PTEN-mTOR layer, arguing that the Pik3r1 null is local to the perturbation/pathway position rather than a universal inability to detect mTOR-family biology.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Tsc1/Tsc2/Pten are not direct paralogs of Pik3r1; their effects represent downstream negative-regulator loss rather than matched biochemical perturbations.

summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA were the nominal Pik3r1 hotspots, but neither was significant after FDR correction.
why_it_matters: The pattern offers focused validation contexts for a weak target rather than treating all cell types as equally silent.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: All highlighted rows were FDR>0.23, so this is a hypothesis-generating cell-type pattern only.

summary: Pik3r1 and Pik3r2 failed to converge, including an exploratory anticorrelation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA.
why_it_matters: The assayed p85-family subunits should not be collapsed into a single interchangeable regulatory-subunit phenotype in this brain dataset.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The anticorrelation was computed on a restricted top-200 nominal Pik3r1 set; the individual genes were not FDR-significant.

direction: loss-of-expression silent versus disease-allele activation and TSC/PTEN robust activation contexts
summary: Neuronal Pik3r1 guide phenotypes did not resemble activated PIK3R1 disease alleles or downstream TSC/PTEN loss.
why_it_matters: PIK3R1 cancer and APDS2 alleles can be allosteric or dimer-selective gain-of-function events, so a weak Pik3r1 loss-of-expression signature should not be used as a direct map for PI3K-inhibitor or mTORopathy directionality.
main_caveats: The dataset tested guide-based Pik3r1 perturbation in mouse brain cells, not patient mutations or pharmacologic catalytic PI3K inhibition.

summary: Myo6 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across the assayed mouse-brain cell classes, with no gene reaching pvals_adj<0.10 in 371,818 target-cell-gene tests.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is a negative whole-transcriptome response rather than a strong cell-state program; any MYO6 phenotype in these cells is likely below the resolution of this mRNA assay, post-transcriptional, or limited by perturbation strength.
main_caveats: No protein, indel, or phenotypic readout was available; pvals_adj are the stored values; target transcript engagement was weak.

summary: On-target Myo6 mRNA depletion was weak and did not survive multiple-testing correction in any measured cell class.
why_it_matters: Weak RNA engagement prevents a clean distinction between true buffering of MYO6 loss and insufficient perturbation of a stable motor protein.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The Myo6 transcript row is only a proxy for guide activity and does not measure MYO6 protein or allelic editing.

summary: B4galnt4 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and Plxna3/Ina in 001 L5-6 IT Glut were the only near-threshold nominal readouts, but they were exploratory rather than discovery-level hits.
why_it_matters: These genes mark the only possible cell-type-restricted follow-up handles; the absence of recurrence among 85 p<0.001 rows argues against a robust shared Myo6 marker module.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: FDR values were 0.198-0.222 and the L5-6 IT estimate used only 40 perturbed cells, so these are hypotheses only.

summary: Known MYO6 endocytic and autophagy partners were not coordinately regulated at the mRNA level after Myo6 perturbation.
why_it_matters: MYO6 is a trafficking motor that binds AP-2/clathrin-associated and TOM1/OPTN autophagy machinery, so the dataset refines this biology by showing that disrupting Myo6 did not trigger a matching transcriptional endocytosis/autophagy module in the profiled brain cells.
main_caveats: The negative result is transcriptional; MYO6 partner recruitment, vesicle movement, or autophagic flux could change without detectable partner mRNA changes.

summary: Myo6 signatures did not phenocopy other cytoskeletal or vesicle-trafficking perturbations, even when those perturbations generated stronger DE signatures of their own.
why_it_matters: The low correlations argue that MYO6 is not interchangeable with AP-2, clathrin, WASH/VPS, dynein, kinesin, actin, or related myosin perturbations at the scalar expression-signature level in this dataset.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations of weak Myo6 score vectors can understate pathway similarity; the comparison is transcriptomic and same-cell-type, not a direct protein-interaction assay.

summary: The brain-wide negative Myo6 signature should not be read as a safety signal for inhibiting MYO6, because the strongest human and model-organism disease evidence centers on hearing-loss biology outside the profiled brain classes.
why_it_matters: MYO6 loss is linked to sensorineural deafness and specialized hair-cell structure, while the queried tractability resources do not show an approved or high-quality small-molecule MYO6 pharmacology; follow-up should prioritize auditory and cardiac contexts rather than relying on this buffered brain transcriptome alone.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq panel lacks cochlear hair cells and cardiomyocytes, and the dataset did not establish complete MYO6 loss in the assayed cells.

summary: Nf2 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered in the best-engaged neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The strongest direct Nf2 transcript loss did not produce any 5% FDR downstream transcript, so the primary result is a negative, buffered response rather than a Hippo-activation program.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The Nf2 row itself reached only FDR 0.3036, and the assay measures RNA rather than Merlin protein, phospho-LATS, phospho-YAP, or PAK activity.

summary: Apparent Nf2 engagement was concentrated in two cell types, leaving most cell-type negatives guide-limited.
why_it_matters: Cell types without a nominal Nf2 decrease cannot be interpreted as Merlin-independent biology because the target transcript itself was not detectably reduced in 19 of 22 tested classes.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not separate low guide activity from low Nf2 basal expression or rapid compensation in the unresponsive classes.

summary: Nf2 loss did not measurably induce a YAP/TEAD transcriptional program in the target-engaged neurons.
why_it_matters: NF2 loss is expected in several proliferative systems to activate YAP/TEAD, but Ccn1, Ccn2, Ankrd1, Amotl2, Areg, and Ptgs2 were not coordinately upregulated after Nf2 perturbation in the two clearest Nf2-transcript knockdown classes.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only steady-state transcripts were measured; Hippo regulation can be post-translational, and the perturbations sampled mature mouse neuronal classes rather than Schwann, meningeal, mesothelial, or liver cells.

summary: Assayed ERM/Hippo/PAK neighbors did not phenocopy Nf2.
why_it_matters: Near-zero same-cell-type correlations to Rdx, Tead1, and Rho/Rac/PAK perturbations argue against a broad Merlin-to-PAK or Merlin-to-TEAD transcriptomic module in this neuronal Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and correlation-based; it does not test PAK kinase activity or direct protein-level effects.

summary: Nf2 was much quieter than Nf1 and Tsc1/Tsc2 neurocutaneous growth-regulator perturbations in the same screen.
why_it_matters: The absence of Nf2 hits is not a generic failure of tumor-suppressor perturbations in the dataset; it points instead to NF2-specific lineage requirements, perturbation sensitivity, or both.
main_caveats: Nf1 and Tsc1/Tsc2 are disease-family comparators rather than members of the Merlin complex, and their guides had different cell counts and target-engagement profiles.

summary: A restricted signature-neighbor scan did not reveal a reproducible Nf2-like positive or opposite module.
why_it_matters: The top Nf2 correlations were cell-type-specific and weak-to-moderate, so there was no hidden recurrent pseudopathway that would rescue interpretation of the all-gene FDR-negative Nf2 result.
main_caveats: Neighbors were chosen on the top 200 absolute-score Nf2 genes in each cell type rather than on an independently significant Nf2 signature.

summary: Mitf perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across all 22 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The strongest dataset-level interpretation is absence of a robust Mitf loss signature, not a cell-type-specific neuronal program; this is consistent with MITF biology being most evident outside the sampled neuronal classes but is limited by weak measured target-transcript engagement.
cell_types: all 22 Mitf-tested cell classes
main_caveats: Target-transcript depletion was not significant, and the dataset lacks glial, choroid plexus, melanocyte, retinal pigment epithelium, mast-cell, and osteoclast contexts where MITF is more canonical.

summary: The expected MITF-M lysosome/autophagy output was not coherently activated or repressed by Mitf perturbation.
why_it_matters: MITF is known to bind CLEAR elements and control lysosomal and autophagosomal genes in melanocytic contexts, so the mixed nominal neuronal V-ATPase and lysosomal changes argue that this pathway is uncoupled from Mitf in the measured brain cells or was not engaged by the guides.
cell_types: all 22 Mitf-tested cell classes
main_caveats: The lysosome audit was restricted to measured transcripts visible in this neuronal dataset and individual rows were only nominal.

summary: mTOR/TSC and lysosome-neighbor perturbations were active in some of the same neuronal classes where Mitf was silent.
why_it_matters: Large Tsc1/Tsc2 signatures show that the assay can detect mTOR-adjacent perturbations in these cells; therefore, the Mitf-negative result is more specific than a complete inability of neurons to mount mTOR/lysosome transcriptional responses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: TSC1/TSC2 regulate many processes beyond MITF/TFEB; the comparison is pathway-adjacent rather than a direct epistasis experiment.

summary: The dataset did not reveal a Mitf-like signature neighbor or allow direct Tfe3/Tfeb/Tfec paralog testing.
why_it_matters: MITF, TFEB, TFE3, and TFEC are tightly related, but weak Mitf correlations and the absence of Tfe3/Tfeb/Tfec perturbations mean that redundancy or functional compensation cannot be inferred from this screen.
cell_types: all 22 Mitf-tested cell classes
main_caveats: Signature correlations were computed from weak Mitf signatures; absence of a paralog perturbation is an assay-design limitation.

summary: Canonical melanocytic and pigment-disease MITF outputs were absent in the assayed neurons.
why_it_matters: The result separates this brain-neuron screen from MITF disease mechanisms in melanocytes and pigment lineages, including Waardenburg syndrome and melanoma/RCC predisposition, and warns against using the neuronal null result to argue that MITF is unimportant in those lineages.
cell_types: all 22 Mitf-tested cell classes
main_caveats: Markers were measured in neuronal groups where many pigmentation transcripts are likely lowly expressed, so large logFC estimates for rare transcripts were not treated as reliable without Wilcoxon support.

summary: Fgf1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant on-target depletion or downstream transcriptomic response in any tested neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Loss of a secreted FGFR ligand would be expected to perturb MAPK/PI3K output only if the assayed cells depend on their own Fgf1 transcript; the measured single-cell response was instead essentially null.
main_caveats: The dataset is an intracellular CRISPR Perturb-seq assay with 30-165 perturbed cells per Fgf1 cell class; low Fgf1 expression or ineffective guide activity cannot be separated from true ligand buffering without raw guide and UMI counts.

summary: The Fgf1 null signature did not phenocopy receptor-proximal or MAPK/PI3K-node perturbations that were active in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: This argues against a blanket inability of these neurons or this assay to report FGFR/MAPK/PI3K transcriptional biology; the uncoupling is more specific to Fgf1 ligand loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Comparisons use selected related perturbations and Wilcoxon score correlations, not a full causal pathway reconstruction.

summary: The strong Fgf13 response diverged from the Fgf1 response in thalamic glutamatergic neurons, which is consistent with FGF13 being an intracellular FGF homologous factor rather than a substitute extracellular FGFR ligand.
why_it_matters: FGF-family perturbations should not automatically be treated as interchangeable FGF/FGFR pathway probes in brain Perturb-seq data.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is strongest for Fgf13 in one cell class; Fgf12 and Fgf14 were not exhaustively analyzed mechanistically.

summary: FLRT1 and EPHA7 are weak, exploratory markers of the only interpretable Fgf1 nominal tail, centered in NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and partly echoed by nominal Epha7 induction in MH-LH TH Glut.
why_it_matters: These genes point to guidance/adhesion biology, a known neuronal FGFR context, but they should be used only as follow-up candidates because no row survived FDR correction.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Flrt1 and Epha7 had raw p values of 0.000151 and 0.000400 in one cell class but FDR=1.0; this is a hypothesis, not a discovery call.

summary: The absence of a robust single-cell Fgf1-loss program is biologically plausible in light of whole-animal FGF1 knockout mice with essentially no isolated FGF1-null abnormalities.
why_it_matters: The result refines broad statements about FGF ligands in neural development by showing that acute loss of endogenous Fgf1 transcript in these assayed neuronal classes is buffered or below detection.
main_caveats: The mouse knockout reference is organism-level and developmental, whereas the dataset measures cell-autonomous transcriptomes; the agreement does not prove the same compensation mechanism.
