cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Usp9x missed FDR 0.05, did not recur across cell types, and was not connected mechanistically to MEK2 by the sources used here.

direction: no strong positive or negative convergence
summary: A restricted signature-neighbor screen did not reveal a coherent Map2k2-matching or anti-matching perturbation; even the strongest nonself correlations were low in the four strongest Map2k2 contexts.
why_it_matters: The Map2k2 signatures are not reusable modules that obviously converge with RAF-MEK pathway neighbors or with unrelated CRISPR signatures in the same cell types.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only four cell types were screened for neighbors, and low correlation may simply follow from partial Map2k2 knockdown.

summary: The experiment models partial Map2k2 loss, whereas the canonical MAP2K2 cardiofaciocutaneous-syndrome alleles activate MEK2; the weak Perturb-seq loss phenotype therefore does not negate gain-of-function RASopathy biology.
why_it_matters: Clinical interpretation should preserve perturbation direction: partial MEK2 loss in mouse brain cells is not equivalent to chronic, organismal MAPK activation by human pathogenic alleles.
main_caveats: No activating MAP2K2 allele, chronic developmental exposure, phospho-ERK readout, or organismal phenotype was assayed.

summary: Lztfl1 perturbation produced nominal target knockdown but no 5% FDR gene in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: The main phenotype is a negative transcriptome result, consistent with LZTFL1 acting through ciliary cargo localization rather than as a strong acute transcriptional regulator.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Target knockdown itself was nominal and did not pass FDR correction; protein and ciliary-localization endpoints were not measured.

summary: Detectable Lztfl1 transcript depletion was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, while several other neuronal classes showed little on-target movement.
why_it_matters: Cell types with weak on-target depletion cannot be treated as true biological nonresponders.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The apparent selectivity may reflect guide representation, expression, or sampling rather than true neuronal specificity.

summary: Lztfl1 perturbation did not phenocopy BBSome or IFT perturbations at the bulk mRNA-signature level.
why_it_matters: LZTFL1 is physically and pathway-linked to the BBSome, but the mouse-brain RNA signatures argue that loss of its regulator is not transcriptomically interchangeable with loss of complex subunits.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to detectable mRNA signatures; weak knockdown of several related targets limits pairwise interpretation.

summary: The Lztfl1 brain dataset favors a nontranscriptional ciliary-trafficking disease mechanism over a resolved mature-neuron Shh/BBS transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Human BBS17 and mouse knockout phenotypes can occur through altered SMO, Ptch1, BBSome, or GPCR localization, none of which would necessarily be visible in nuclear RNA-seq.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The assay did not quantify SMO/PTCH1/GPCR ciliary localization and used adult mouse brain rather than patient fibroblasts, developing tissues, retina, or kidney.

summary: Lztfl1 and Ttc8 mRNA signatures should not be used alone as pharmacodynamic biomarkers of BBSome rescue or inhibition.
why_it_matters: The transcriptome remains nearly silent even when a BBSome subunit is efficiently depleted, and LZTFL1 lacks curated ChEMBL pharmacology; candidate interventions would need direct ciliary-trafficking readouts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a biomarker warning, not a drug-efficacy test; no compound perturbation was assayed.

summary: Cfl2 knockdown was multiple-testing-significant only in two caudal neuronal classes, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, with weaker nominal target decreases elsewhere.
why_it_matters: Downstream phenotypes in most cell classes are difficult to interpret because the target transcript itself was not FDR-level reduced; the confident perturbation contexts are restricted to one midbrain glutamatergic and one brainstem/pontine/myelencephalic GABAergic class.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Target engagement was assessed at RNA level only; several FDR-negative classes had small perturbed-cell counts or nominal Cfl2 decreases.

direction: Cfl2 down with buffered trans response
summary: Even where Cfl2 RNA was strongly depleted, it was the only FDR-significant gene and the nonself response remained nominal and nonrecurrent.
why_it_matters: Cofilin-2 is an actin-filament depolymerization factor, but acute neuronal knockdown produced little steady-state transcriptional evidence for a broad actin-stress or compensatory program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA, not actin polymerization, cofilin phosphorylation, actin rods, or neuronal morphology; nominal genes should not be treated as validated effectors.

summary: Actin-pathway and thin-filament neighbor perturbations did not robustly phenocopy Cfl2 in the two FDR-engaged Cfl2 contexts.
why_it_matters: Cfl2 sits in an actin-turnover network regulated by PAK/LIMK and functionally linked to actin, so a simple shared transcriptomic module might have been expected; the screen instead suggests that Cfl2 loss is either post-transcriptionally buffered or not captured by the restricted signature comparison.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations used only the top 100 Cfl2 genes per cell type; Tpm3 itself was not an FDR-level knockdown, and transcriptome similarity is an indirect proxy for actin dynamics.

direction: brain response buffered despite loss-of-function disease biology
summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq phenotype is buffered relative to the established skeletal-muscle loss-of-function biology of CFL2, so it should not be used to deprioritize CFL2 rescue for nemaline myopathy.
why_it_matters: Human CFL2 variants and mouse Cfl2 knockout converge on striated-muscle pathology; a brain-cell RNA phenotype that stops at on-target knockdown is compatible with CNS buffering and with the disease mechanism being concentrated in muscle sarcomeres.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay skeletal muscle, sarcomere organization, animal phenotypes, or long-term compensation.

summary: Hsf4 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across mouse-brain cell classes: the target transcript was usually directionally depleted, yet no gene reached FDR<0.10 in any of 23 cell types.
why_it_matters: The main result is a negative/buffered perturbation, not a hidden pathway activation; any Hsf4 interpretation in this dataset must account for weak target engagement and a complete absence of genome-wide significant downstream genes.
main_caveats: All on-target Hsf4 self tests also had FDR=1.0; low protein abundance or guide efficiency cannot be separated from true buffering using this DE table alone.

summary: Hsf4 was not interchangeable with Hsf1 for the neuronal heat-shock chaperone module: Hsf1 repressed Hsph1, Hsp90aa1/Hsp90ab1, Ahsa2, Rsrp1, Stip1, or Mat2a in several classes, whereas corresponding Hsf4 tests were FDR=1.0 and Hsf4 versus Hsf1 signatures were nearly uncorrelated.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates a canonical HSF1-dependent proteostasis program from Hsf4 loss, preventing annotation transfer from HSF family membership to Hsf4 in these brain cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Hsf2 was not present among the inspected perturbations, and the Hsf4 signature itself is weak, so the claim is limited to lack of Hsf1-like output rather than a full map of all HSF paralogs.

summary: The lens/cataract HSF4 program was silent in this mouse-brain assay: crystallins plus Dnase2b, Rad51, and Atg9a were all FDR=1.0 after Hsf4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Human cataract genetics and mouse Hsf4-null lens phenotypes are strong, but this brain Perturb-seq dataset did not reproduce the lens-fiber structural, denucleation, autophagy, or DNA-repair outputs that explain ocular disease.
main_caveats: Many lens structural genes are likely lowly expressed in brain cells; failure to change them is a context refinement, not evidence against HSF4 function in lens.

summary: Nominal Hsf4 self-depletion was concentrated in a small set of subcortical or midbrain-adjacent classes, but the apparent cell-type pattern stopped at the target transcript and did not extend to downstream FDR hits.
why_it_matters: The strongest nominal Hsf4 self rows identify where the perturbation was most measurable, but they should not be overinterpreted as cell-type-specific biology because even the highest-count classes remained buffered.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Hsf4 self-depletion was only nominal, all adjusted p values were 1.0, and human atlas expression is an indirect comparison to this mouse perturbation assay.

summary: A restricted signature-neighbor scan found no robust Hsf4-like or inverse perturbation; the strongest positive and negative Pearson correlations in representative classes were all below |0.092|.
why_it_matters: This makes it unlikely that the weak Hsf4 rows hide a large convergent module shared with another assayed perturbation, including the heat-shock neighbor Hsp90ab1 or the paralog Hsf1.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The scan used three classes with the strongest nominal Hsf4 self-depletion and score-vector Pearson correlations only; it is a guard against large missed signatures, not a network reconstruction.

summary: Lrrtm1 perturbation produced an almost completely buffered mRNA phenotype across 22 profiled neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: A strong synaptic-organizer literature would make a coordinated synaptic response plausible, but the Perturb-seq readout instead indicates little acute cell-autonomous transcriptional remodeling.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not FDR-depleted, and the assay measures mRNA rather than synaptic protein localization or dendritic-spine phenotypes.

summary: A small R3hdm2 increase in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only FDR-significant Lrrtm1 downstream response.
why_it_matters: It nominates a thalamic, cell-type-restricted marker for any detectable Lrrtm1 transcriptional response, matching LRRTM1's thalamic expression context but not yet connecting to a known LRRTM pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Single cell class, small logFC, weak Lrrtm1 self-depletion in the same block, and no independent R3hdm2 literature link to LRRTM1.

summary: Upper-layer and L5 extratelencephalic cortical excitatory classes showed the best nominal Lrrtm1 mRNA decreases but no FDR-level downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This separates target-transcript direction from downstream response and argues that the absence of a large signature is not confined to classes with perfectly null target rows.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Lrrtm1 decreases were nominal only with FDR=1.0, so the result may still reflect weak perturbation.

summary: Lrrtm1 did not show coherent positive or negative signature convergence with LRRTM paralogs, neurexins, neuroligins, or postsynaptic scaffold perturbations.
why_it_matters: The physical LRRTM/neurexin pathway is not interchangeable at the acute mRNA-signature level in this dataset, so related synaptic perturbations should not be assumed to rescue or mimic Lrrtm1 by transcriptomics alone.
main_caveats: The low correlations come from weak Lrrtm1 signatures; the finding is compatible with shared protein-level synapse biology that does not manifest as a shared scRNA-seq program.

summary: Lrrtm1 perturbation did not elicit FDR-level Cadm1/SynCAM1, Lrrtm2-4, neurexin, neuroligin, or PSD-gene mRNA compensation.
why_it_matters: Known buffering by LRRTM2 or SynCAM1 may operate at synaptic-protein, circuit, region, or developmental levels rather than as a pan-cell-class transcriptional mRNA feedback loop.
main_caveats: The mouse PFC SynCAM1 result was not a matched single-cell transcriptomic time point, and target-transcript engagement of Lrrtm1 was weak in this dataset.

summary: Naa10 perturbation produced neither target-transcript suppression nor any FDR-resolved downstream differential-expression response across assayed mouse brain cell types.
why_it_matters: NAA10 is the catalytic subunit of NatA, so an efficient loss of function would be expected to perturb a core co-translational acetylation process; the dataset instead reads primarily as an under-engaged or selected-escape perturbation rather than as evidence that neurons tolerate Naa10 loss.
main_caveats: Target protein, indel editing, and guide identity were not measured; CRISPR edits that leave Naa10 mRNA intact or survival of unedited cells could both produce this transcriptomic null.

summary: Naa10 was transcriptionally orthogonal to the NatA auxiliary subunit Naa15 and to the Naa-family comparator Naa20 even though Naa15 and Naa20 generated many significant signatures in the same experiment.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates the Naa10 result from a global inability of the Perturb-seq assay to detect N-terminal-acetyltransferase biology and is unexpected from the known NAA10-NAA15 complex relationship.
main_caveats: The divergence is almost certainly affected by weak Naa10 engagement; Naa20 is a related family member rather than a NatA core subunit.

summary: The 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut classes are response-competent for N-terminal-acetyltransferase-family perturbations but still show a Naa10-specific null.
why_it_matters: These two cell classes had the largest Naa10 sample sizes and strong Naa15/Naa20 comparator signatures, so their Naa10 nulls are more informative than low-count nulls in smaller strata.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a within-dataset response-competence argument, not proof that these neuronal classes are biologically insensitive to fully engaged Naa10 loss.

summary: The Naa10 signatures did not align with Mtor, Tsc1, or Tsc2 perturbation signatures, despite curated evidence that NAA10 can acetylate and stabilize TSC2 to repress mTOR signaling.
why_it_matters: A reported NAA10-TSC2-mTOR axis is not transcriptionally recovered in this screen, so mTOR-direction hypotheses should not be inferred from the weak Naa10 data.
main_caveats: The test is signature-correlation based and Naa10 itself lacks a strong DE signature; absence of correlation does not rule out NAA10 regulation of TSC2 protein acetylation.

summary: The screen should not be used as reassuring loss-of-NAA10 safety evidence for neurons because the perturbation lacked measurable engagement while human NAA10 is broadly expressed and NAA10/NAA15 variants cause multisystem neurodevelopmental disorders.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic down-modulation or variant modeling of a core NatA catalytic subunit needs an engaged model; this dataset mainly flags Naa10 as a failed or buffered target in this assay.
main_caveats: Human disease genetics and human expression data are indirect for mouse Perturb-seq cell states, and ChEMBL absence of mechanisms is not a complete druggability assessment.

summary: No reproducible same-direction target gene or biomarker module emerged from the Naa10 signatures; nominal hits were sparse and directionally inconsistent.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting isolated nominal genes such as Tvp23a or Pfn2 as Naa10-responsive biomarkers.
main_caveats: The lack of recurrent genes follows from an under-engaged perturbation and does not prove that fully engaged Naa10 loss has no transcriptional program.

summary: Plec guide perturbation produced directionally consistent but weak target-transcript engagement across neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Most Plec self rows moved downward, so the guides were not random, but the absence of any corrected Plec mRNA depletion makes every downstream interpretation conditional on partial knockdown.
main_caveats: The assay measured Plec RNA only; protein depletion, isoform coverage, and residual plectin were not measured.

summary: The apparent Plec knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: the strongest nominal target-depleted cell types had no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This separates on-target directionality from functional transcriptional output and argues against a large acute neuronal stress, differentiation, or cytoskeletal-feedback program in these contrasts.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|053 Sst Gaba|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All five highlighted cell types had only nominal Plec RNA depletion; sample sizes were modest and the readout was single-cell RNA, not morphology or mechanics.

summary: Eprs up-regulation in 001 L5-6 IT Glut is the sole corrected Plec downstream hit and is not part of a recurrent Plec module.
why_it_matters: Eprs is the only gene that should be carried forward as a concrete Plec-responsive transcript from this dataset, but its isolation makes it a hypothesis-generating marker rather than a pathway-level call.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: Only 46 Plec-perturbed L5-6 IT cells supported the Eprs hit, and the Plec self row in that cell type had FDR=1.0.

summary: Canonical plectin-associated cytolinker and hemidesmosome neighbors did not phenocopy Plec in the neuronal perturbation panel.
why_it_matters: Although PLEC is curated with DST/DAG1/ITGA6/ITGB4-centered structural networks, assayed neighbors mostly had no corrected neuronal signatures and the Plec L5-6 signature had essentially no whole-transcriptome neighbors.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: The comparison was restricted to targets present in the dataset extract; ITGB4 and COL17A1, two canonical hemidesmosome genes, were not assayed as perturbations in this comparison.

summary: A neuron-only Perturb-seq panel refines broad CNS plectin expression to an acutely buffered neuronal RNA phenotype.
why_it_matters: Plectin is reported broadly in brain and is discussed as a CNS cytolinker, especially in astrocyte intermediate-filament biology; the dataset shows that labeled glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons do not mount a strong acute transcriptional response to partial Plec knockdown.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks astrocytes and directly measures RNA rather than the intermediate-filament organization or mechanics emphasized in the CNS literature.

summary: The weak neuronal RNA phenotype should not be read as evidence that PLEC loss is biologically or clinically benign.
why_it_matters: Human PLEC loss-of-function is tied to severe skin and muscle disorders, and Open Targets does not indicate an approved or advanced clinical modality; an acute neuron-only RNA screen is therefore a poor de-risking assay for systemic PLEC inhibition.
main_caveats: The screen did not assay skin, muscle, peripheral nerve, long-term structure, or organismal phenotypes.

summary: Guide-defined Minpp1 perturbation produced reproducible Minpp1 mRNA depletion but no FDR-significant non-target transcript in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: MINPP1 is an ER inositol-polyphosphate hydrolase, so the positive control effect is target knockdown itself; the absence of downstream FDR hits argues that acute Minpp1 RNA loss is buffered at the steady-state mRNA layer in these neuronal populations.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: RNA, protein, and inositol-phosphate metabolites were not measured after perturbation; lack of FDR genes does not prove lack of biochemical effect.

summary: The mouse-brain Perturb-seq response does not recapitulate the large developmental toxicity expected from biallelic human MINPP1 loss.
why_it_matters: Loss-of-function MINPP1 causes pontocerebellar hypoplasia and cellular IP6/cation imbalance, but strong target depletion in several sampled mouse neuronal classes was transcriptionally quiet; this points to developmental timing, complete loss versus partial mRNA depletion, metabolite-level readouts, or unsampled vulnerable cell states as likely requirements for observing disease biology.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset is not a prenatal human cerebellar or pontine differentiation assay; the cerebellar 308 CB GABA group had weak target engagement.

summary: Minpp1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Inpp5k, Plcb1, and Itpr1 perturbations in the cell types where Minpp1 was most strongly depleted.
why_it_matters: MINPP1 sits in an ER-luminal soluble-inositol branch; failure to converge with linked inositol/phosphoinositide genes argues against a generic PI-cycle or IP3-receptor transcriptional program being the immediate output of Minpp1 knockdown.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is a same-cell-type scalar score-correlation comparison; some related perturbations had weaker on-target knockdown than Minpp1 and the compared genes do not form a single physical complex.

summary: The small nominal tail after Minpp1 perturbation was not a recurrent downstream module.
why_it_matters: Only one non-target gene, Jund, recurred at nominal p<0.001, and no recurrent or single-cell-type gene survived FDR; pathway interpretation should therefore not be driven by the isolated nominal tail.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: This conclusion is transcriptome-only and uses the supplied DE summaries rather than raw-cell re-estimation.

summary: Pcdhgb5 in Sst cells and Pard3 in hindbrain GABA cells are the best dataset-internal candidate responders but remain sub-FDR hypotheses.
why_it_matters: These genes mark the two lowest non-target adjusted p values in strongly engaged cells and could be useful for follow-up if Minpp1 perturbation is repeated with more cells or metabolite validation.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Both candidates have FDR just above 0.10, are not recurrent, and should not be treated as validated MINPP1 effectors.

summary: The absent downstream mRNA response should not be interpreted as evidence that MINPP1 inhibition would be benign in the brain.
why_it_matters: Human MINPP1 loss is a recessive neurodevelopmental disease mechanism; this dataset instead shows that a standard Perturb-seq mRNA endpoint can miss the metabolic and cation-homeostasis effects expected upstream of transcription.
main_caveats: No MINPP1-directed therapeutic perturbation, enzyme activity assay, or rescue experiment was present in the dataset.

summary: FDR-secure Ash1l target engagement was confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and consisted of Ash1l repression itself rather than a downstream gene program.
why_it_matters: ASH1L is an enzymatic chromatin regulator, so a verified target-transcript decrease is a real positive control; in this screen it identifies one assayed thalamic glutamatergic context as engaged but not transcriptionally expanded.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The 151 class also had the largest Ash1l perturbed-cell count, so FDR validation may reflect both stronger engagement and higher power; the assay measures RNA loss, not ASH1L protein or H3K36 methylation.

summary: Most nominal Ash1l transcript decreases were buffered at the whole-transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: Eleven non-151 classes showed nominal loss of the target transcript but zero FDR-significant genes, making broad acute transcriptional collapse unlikely in this experiment.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|001 L5-6 IT Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: These are nominal on-target observations with FDR=1.0 for Ash1l in each class; guide efficiency, scRNA dropout and small n from 23 to 78 cells can hide weak downstream effects.

summary: Ash1l was not transcriptionally interchangeable with related SET-domain and chromatin perturbations.
why_it_matters: Although ASH1L sits in the H3K36/chromatin regulatory space, Setd1a, Kmt2d, Kmt2b, Kmt2a and Nsd1 produced many more FDR calls in the 151 thalamic class, and full-signature correlations to Ash1l were near zero, arguing against a common generic KMT-loss program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparators are pathway neighbors or STRING-associated chromatin regulators, not obligate ASH1L complex subunits; some comparator guide effects also showed weak self-transcript depletion.

summary: The published Ash1l-Epha7 synapse-pruning axis was not robustly detected at Epha7 RNA in this screen.
why_it_matters: Epha7 is a mechanistic downstream gene in Ash1l haploinsufficient mouse forebrain, so its absence as an FDR hit here narrows that biomarker hypothesis to stronger, developmental or forebrain contexts rather than universal acute Ash1l knockdown.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Epha7 moved in the expected negative direction nominally in two excitatory classes, so this is a failure of robust detection rather than an opposite-direction result.

summary: The Perturb-seq phenotype is much weaker than developmental and juvenile-prefrontal Ash1l loss-of-function phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Mouse models show that Ash1l loss can alter neural-developmental and synaptic transcription and cause autistic-like behavior or seizures, whereas the acute single-cell signatures here were almost entirely target-only; the disease mechanism is therefore likely stage-, brain-region-, dosage- or duration-dependent.
main_caveats: The dataset does not report chromatin marks, protein loss, seizure phenotypes or behavior, and it should not be equated with germline, forebrain-deletion or juvenile-PFC models.

summary: The weak acute expression signature should not be read as evidence that ASH1L inhibition is biologically inert.
why_it_matters: Human disease aggregation and mouse loss-of-function studies support ASH1L dosage sensitivity, while ChEMBL records show that biochemical ASH1L inhibitors exist; a target-only Perturb-seq response could miss developmental liabilities of catalytic inhibition.
main_caveats: Existing public ASH1L pharmacology is preclinical in this query, and RNA knockdown in mosaic mouse-brain Perturb-seq is not the same modality as chronic systemic enzyme inhibition.

direction: Arid1b down; downstream genes not FDR significant
summary: Arid1b perturbation was dominated by loss of the Arid1b transcript itself; no non-target gene reached 5% FDR in any tested cell class.
why_it_matters: The strongest interpretable phenotype is immediate on-target depletion without a genome-wide transcriptional cascade, so the Perturb-seq readout looks buffered rather than pathway-activating.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is an mRNA endpoint; chromatin, protein abundance, morphology, and longer developmental consequences were not assayed.

direction: negative target logFC in all 22 tested cell classes; strongest FDR support in 052, 151, and 155
summary: FDR-level target engagement was concentrated in Pvalb GABA, TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic, and midbrain glutamatergic cells, with near-threshold engagement in two cortical excitatory classes.
why_it_matters: Apparent absence of downstream DE should be interpreted mainly in the cell classes where Arid1b itself was detectably depleted.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Several classes had small Arid1b guide-cell counts or weak Arid1b p values, so cell types such as Sst GABA are poor tests of resistance.

direction: Pvalb Arid1b down without significant downstream genes
summary: Pvalb GABA neurons, a literature-relevant interneuron context for Arid1b, showed the clearest Arid1b transcript knockdown but still no FDR-significant non-target response.
why_it_matters: Developmental mouse studies implicate PV/SST interneurons in Arid1b haploinsufficiency phenotypes; the dataset separates that disease relevance from an acute, cell-intrinsic Pvalb scRNA cascade.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The literature is developmental and conditional-genetic, whereas this dataset measures matched guide-positive single cells; Sst GABA had weak target engagement and cannot be interpreted as SST sparing.

summary: A weak canonical-BAF loss imprint was clearest in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: Smarcb1, Smarcc2, and Arid1a were the nearest BAF-related positive neighbors of Arid1b, and shared down-regulation markers such as Ptpn3 and Reep2 appeared only nominally in the Arid1b signature.
why_it_matters: This rescues biological signal that would be missed by an FDR-only Arid1b gene list and ties the small Arid1b effect to the expected SWI/SNF module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The score correlations were small and Ptpn3/Reep2 did not pass FDR after Arid1b perturbation.

summary: Arid1b was not interchangeable with Arid1a or core cBAF subunits in the same TH Prkcd cells: Arid1b produced only its own FDR hit, whereas Arid1a, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, and Smarce1 produced 22, 286, 185, and 11 FDR-significant genes, respectively.
why_it_matters: The result argues that an ARID1B-specific perturbation is a much weaker acute transcriptomic input than disruption of the core assembly and should not be modeled as generic cBAF collapse.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations do not have identical guide-cell counts or knockdown strengths; effect-size differences are transcriptomic, not direct biochemical measurements of cBAF abundance.

summary: The dataset and genetics point away from ARID1B inhibition as a brain therapeutic direction: reducing Arid1b is the disease direction in human LoF syndromes, is achievable in several neuronal classes, and produces no obvious acute compensatory activation of an alternative transcriptomic program.
why_it_matters: If ARID1B is therapeutically considered, restoration or compensation for haploinsufficiency is biologically more aligned than direct inhibition; direct ARID1B small-molecule pharmacology also appears undeveloped in ChEMBL.
main_caveats: This inference is directional only; the Perturb-seq experiment was not a rescue or drug study and did not test overexpression or chromatin-targeted treatments.

summary: Kdm4b perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any measured brain cell class.
why_it_matters: KDM4B is a chromatin enzyme with strong neurodevelopmental literature, so the Perturb-seq result is a genuine negative in the measured acute single-cell assay rather than an obvious reproduction of published loss-of-function phenotypes.
main_caveats: No adjusted hit does not prove KDM4B dispensability because direct target-transcript reduction was weak or only nominal.

summary: Nominal Kdm4b self-knockdown was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, yet neither stratum produced an adjusted downstream signature.
why_it_matters: These two strata are the best places in this table to look for acute Kdm4b effects; their lack of FDR-supported secondary genes frames the screen as partially engaged and transcriptionally buffered.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Self-knockdown p values were unadjusted only and all Kdm4b self FDR values were 1.0.

summary: Kdm4c, the closest assayed KDM4-family comparator, did not phenocopy Kdm4b and its score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Kdm4b across shared cell types.
why_it_matters: Reactome groups KDM4A-D in the same methylated-H3 demethylation reactions, but the mouse-brain perturbation signatures do not behave as an interchangeable transcriptomic module.
main_caveats: Both signatures were weak and Kdm4c had fewer perturbed cells than Kdm4b, so the comparison is suitable for module triage but not for enzyme-specific mechanistic ranking.

summary: Kdm4b had no strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor among selected nominally informative cell types.
why_it_matters: The weak nearest-neighbor correlations argue against a robust Kdm4b-centered module in this dataset and make isolated nominal top genes poor pathway anchors.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only for selected strata; the Kdm4b seed signatures themselves lacked adjusted hits.

summary: The buffered acute Perturb-seq readout should not be interpreted as developmental or clinical safety for KDM4B inhibition.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse loss-of-function studies link KDM4B to brain development, hippocampal structure, seizures, and cognitive phenotypes, whereas this dataset tests partial acute perturbation in recovered cell classes and shows weak target engagement.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks organismal development, anatomy, behavior, chromatin marks, and confirmed protein depletion; ChEMBL shows assay tractability, not an approved therapy.

direction: Mtor transcript down; downstream RNA mostly unchanged
summary: Mtor perturbation produced a uniformly negative but weak target-transcript shift and almost no adjusted downstream RNA response across the 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: mTOR is a central kinase in TORC1/TORC2 signaling, so the absence of a broad FDR-level RNA program indicates that this CRISPR transcript perturbation mainly reports a partial or buffered loss state rather than full kinase shutdown.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not FDR-significant in any cell type, and Perturb-seq RNA does not measure mTOR protein abundance or mTORC1/mTORC2 phosphorylation output.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the sole cell class with FDR<0.05 genes after Mtor perturbation.
why_it_matters: The FDR-level Mtor response is not a panneuronal signature; the interpretable direct DE signal is restricted to two genes in one thalamic glutamatergic label, with Rims3 increasing and Tmed8 decreasing.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only two genes passed FDR<0.05 and the Mtor self row in this cell type was nominal but not FDR-significant.

direction: Mtor loss-signature opposite to mTORC1-repressor loss-signatures
summary: The modest Mtor signatures rank Tsc1/Tsc2/Pten, and in 151 also Depdc5, as the strongest negative signature neighbors in the responsive brain classes.
why_it_matters: TSC1/TSC2 and DEPDC5 are mTORC1 repressors, and PTEN antagonizes the PI3K-AKT input; their opposite transcriptomic direction is the clearest dataset link between the weak direct Mtor perturbation and canonical mTORC1 regulation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The absolute correlations were modest and were computed from RNA signatures; several Mtor cell classes were too weak to show this ranked relationship.

direction: core-complex perturbations weak; Tsc1/Tsc2 perturbations strong
summary: The direct mTORC1 scaffold target Rptor was transcriptionally buffered like Mtor and did not phenocopy Tsc1/Tsc2 loss.
why_it_matters: Pathway membership alone did not predict interchangeability: upstream mTORC1-repressor perturbations generated large RNA programs, whereas knockdown of Mtor or Rptor produced little adjusted signal in this dataset.
main_caveats: Rptor target-transcript engagement was also weak, so the contrast is evidence for perturbation-specific buffering in this assay rather than evidence that RPTOR is biologically dispensable.

direction: therapeutic-like Mtor loss is opposite to mTORC1-repressor loss but much weaker
summary: The dataset should not be read as a strong mTOR-inhibition rescue model for mTORopathy, even though its weak Mtor signature is oriented opposite to hyperactivating TSC/PTEN/DEPDC5 loss signatures.
why_it_matters: Human focal cortical dysplasia and MTOR-pathway overgrowth diseases involve mTOR-pathway activation, and MTOR is druggable; the Perturb-seq Mtor RNA phenotype is too small to infer whether pharmacologic mTOR inhibition would normalize disease-like transcriptional states in any one cell class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The disease comparison is indirect: disease studies involve activating variants or biallelic repressor loss during development, whereas the dataset perturbs mouse-brain RNA and lacks direct phospho-S6 or phospho-4EBP1 readouts.

summary: Measured Crebrf mRNA did not show FDR-level depletion in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: The strongest interpretation of the Perturb-seq signatures is limited by the absence of transcript-level on-target confirmation; downstream hits should be treated as guide-associated responses rather than proven loss-of-function consequences.
main_caveats: The gRNA could perturb Crebrf protein or regulatory output without a large steady-state mRNA drop, and sparse Crebrf expression could underpower the transcript readout.

summary: Ddx5 down-regulation was the dominant and recurrent Crebrf-associated output.
why_it_matters: Because every corrected hit was Ddx5 and the same direction recurred nominally in additional inhibitory and cerebellar classes, Ddx5 is the most compact candidate marker of successful Crebrf perturbation in this dataset.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only Ddx5 survived FDR; Nap1l5, Srsf5, Zkscan16, and Mfsd12 were nominal, and weak measured Crebrf knockdown leaves room for guide or sampling effects.

summary: FDR-level Crebrf responses were confined to three glutamatergic populations rather than scaling with broad CREBRF brain expression.
why_it_matters: The result argues that adult mouse neuronal state, not simple detectability of CREBRF RNA, gates the response to Crebrf perturbation.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Human Protein Atlas expression summary is human-biased and not the same assay or cell-type taxonomy; many nonresponsive Perturb-seq classes had fewer than 75 perturbed cells.

summary: Crebrf perturbation did not collapse onto canonical CREB3/UPR/autophagy or mTOR/TSC transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: A CREB3- or mTOR-centric model would predict movement of UPR/autophagy markers or similarity to pathway-neighbor perturbations, but the neuronal signatures were narrow and Ddx5-dominated.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and performed in adult mouse brain cells, whereas some prior CREBRF-mTOR data came from goat endometrial cells and overexpression systems.

summary: Known CREBRF links to adiposity, diabetes risk, and glucocorticoid physiology were not mirrored by a corrected hypothalamic-neuropeptide or glucocorticoid-marker response.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq data caution against assuming an acute, cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional route for systemic CREBRF phenotypes.
main_caveats: The literature phenotypes are systemic, chronic, or adipocyte-associated, while this screen is an acute neuronal transcriptomic assay with weak measured Crebrf mRNA engagement.

summary: Baiap2 knockdown was measured broadly but reached FDR significance only in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: Downstream phenotypes should be interpreted as cell-type restricted and power-limited rather than as a uniform pan-neuronal Baiap2 response.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Target mRNA reduction is only a proxy for protein depletion; some nominally negative groups may be underpowered, while the lowest-count groups lacked target engagement.

direction: Baiap2 down; non-target genes not FDR-significant
summary: Even the best Baiap2 knockdown produced little FDR-resolved downstream mRNA remodeling.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq result is compatible with BAIAP2 acting mainly as a local PSD/actin scaffold whose acute loss may change synaptic architecture or receptor physiology without driving a large steady-state transcriptomic program.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Transcriptome-only inference cannot exclude strong effects on dendritic spine morphology, actin dynamics, or synaptic physiology.

summary: In L4-5 and L2-3 IT cortical glutamatergic cells, Baiap2 signatures weakly converged with a postsynaptic/NMDAR perturbation module.
why_it_matters: Grin2b, Ap2s1, Shank2, Syngap1, and Dlg4 ranked among the closest positive Baiap2 neighbors in one or both IT subclasses, connecting the dataset signal to the known IRSp53 postsynaptic scaffold network despite small absolute correlations.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were low in magnitude and came from nominal Baiap2 signatures; this is a rank-based module rather than a set of FDR-significant downstream genes.

summary: The BAI1/Rho-family actin branch did not phenocopy Baiap2 in the same cortical signatures.
why_it_matters: Adgrb1, Rac1, and Srgap3 showed near-zero or negative correlations to Baiap2 while Cdc42 was only weakly positive, suggesting that the detected Baiap2 state is not simply any perturbation of a physical BAIAP2 actin interactor.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Several actin effectors and Baiap2 paralogs were not assayed as targets, and the Adgrb1/Rac1/Cdc42/Srgap3 comparator guides did not show FDR-significant depletion of their own transcripts in these cell types.

summary: Cortical Baiap2 signatures were Grin2b-like but Grin2a- and Kcnb1-opposed, which should not be simplified to the NMDAR hyperfunction reported in IRSp53-null physiology studies.
why_it_matters: The dataset refines the NMDAR disease model by showing a compensatory or cell-state transcriptional axis around NMDA-receptor subunits rather than a direct readout of receptor activity direction.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The mismatch is indirect because the literature measured chronic IRSp53-null synaptic physiology, whereas the dataset measures early transcriptional signatures in cortical IT subclasses.

summary: A broad Baiap2-loss mRNA biomarker is weakly supported, and direct BAIAP2 small-molecule pharmacology is not established in ChEMBL.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic hypotheses should prioritize downstream circuit or receptor readouts rather than expecting direct BAIAP2 ligands or a large FDR-significant transcriptional correction signature.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: An empty ChEMBL target-name query is not proof that BAIAP2 is undruggable, and the perturbation experiment did not test NMDAR or mGluR5 antagonists.

summary: Gsdme perturbation produced no FDR-resolved downstream transcriptional phenotype in any assayed broad mouse-brain class.
why_it_matters: The screen does not place Gsdme among strong basal transcriptional regulators in these neuronal classes; the quiet phenotype fits an executioner whose best-known activity is proteolytic pore activation, but direct target knockdown was not measured.

summary: Gsdme perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the measured caspase, gasdermin, inflammasome, interleukin, or necroptosis markers.
why_it_matters: Known GSDME biology is mainly post-translational: CASP3 or granzyme cleavage releases a pore-forming N terminus. The data therefore argue against a tonic Gsdme-to-inflammatory-transcript feedback loop in this basal mouse-brain assay, not against inducible pyroptotic execution.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA

why_it_matters: Zfp955a in L2/3 entorhinal/parasubicular/retrosplenial glutamatergic cells and Sh3bp5/Ttc7b in CA3/CA2-related glutamatergic cells are hypothesis-generating local signals, but the absence of recurrence prevents treating them as a robust Gsdme program.

main_caveats: The highlighted rows are nominal only, have FDR values from 0.3399 to 1.0, and come from 34 or 43 perturbed cells in the two named classes.

summary: Basal CRISPR perturbation of Gsdme in mouse brain cells is not equivalent to the toxic DFNA5/GSDME activation states emphasized in hearing-loss and cancer literature.
why_it_matters: Dominant DFNA5 alleles and anti-tumor GSDME biology center on cytotoxic pore activation or mutant exon-skipping products; a silent loss-of-function transcriptome in the brain screen should therefore not be read as evidence that activated GSDME would be inert in neurons or sensory epithelia.
