main_caveats: The dataset lacks cochlear hair cells, apoptotic or immune challenge conditions, and direct target-transcript measurements.

summary: No gasdermin-family, caspase, or inflammasome neighbor perturbation was available for a direct within-screen Gsdme comparison.
why_it_matters: The report should not claim redundancy, interchangeability, or divergence between Gsdme and Gsdmd/Casp3/Pycard/Nlrp3 perturbations; those target perturbations were absent from the parquet.
main_caveats: This is an assay-coverage negative result, not evidence for or against functional similarity among these genes.

summary: Pld3 knockdown was broad and mostly reduced only Pld3 itself.
why_it_matters: The dominant phenotype of Pld3 perturbation in this neuronal Perturb-seq matrix is buffering: strong loss of the target transcript rarely propagated to FDR-significant secondary mRNAs, despite PLD3 being a lysosomal nuclease/lipid enzyme.
main_caveats: The assay measures steady-state transcripts after the perturbation; it does not assay lysosomal nucleic acids, lipid products, APP fragments, TLR ligands, or PLD3 protein activity.

summary: The single non-Pld3 FDR hit, Ncapd2 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA, is not interpretable as a PLD3 response because that cell type lacked Pld3 target engagement.
why_it_matters: Without the self-knockdown control this row would look like the strongest downstream gene; preserving the on-target failure prevents over-calling a cerebellar condensin/cell-cycle phenotype.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: This is a quality-control interpretation, not a claim that Ncapd2 is biologically downstream of PLD3.

summary: Five cell populations did not achieve FDR-significant Pld3 self-knockdown, so their downstream nulls are weak negative results.
why_it_matters: The strongest biological statement should come from the 18 engaged populations; weak or failed self-rows in hippocampal/amygdalar, cortical CGE, dopaminergic, and cerebellar GABA populations are better treated as target-engagement caveats than evidence of cell-type resistance.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|215 MB Dopa|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Four groups still showed nominal Pld3 decreases, and 215 MB Dopa had only 27 perturbed cells; lack of FDR can reflect power as well as biology.

summary: Pld3 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor, did not converge with APP/endolysosomal Alzheimer-gene signatures, and could not be contrasted directly with absent PLD-family paralogs.
why_it_matters: PLD3 is genetically and mechanistically tied to AD-relevant lysosomal and APP biology, but the Pld3 transcriptional signature was essentially orthogonal to App, Cst3, Sorl1, Grn, and Tmem106b in matched neuronal contexts; the closest PLD paralog, Pld4, was not perturbed.
main_caveats: Correlation analysis is signature-based; several other AD genes in the downloaded related set had poor self-engagement, and the PLD-family paralogs were absent rather than measured as divergent.

summary: APP/TLR/interferon sentinel transcripts were not induced by neuronal Pld3 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Published PLD3/PLD4 biology predicts lysosomal nucleic-acid handling and, in stressed contexts, TLR or cytosolic DNA-sensor signaling; the Perturb-seq readout shows that reducing Pld3 alone did not measurably turn on App, Sorl1, Tlr7, Tlr9, Ifit1, Ifnb1, Irf7, or Isg15 mRNA in normal brain cell types.
main_caveats: Mb21d1/cGAS and Tmem173/STING were not tested in the extracted Pld3 rows, and TLR or cGAS-STING activation can be post-transcriptional.

summary: The dataset and human genetics favor caution around PLD3 inhibition rather than nominating a protective knockdown state.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq loss-of-transcript state was buffered but not overtly beneficial, whereas PLD3 loss in the literature is connected to risk alleles, lysosomal nucleic-acid accumulation, and inflammatory sensor activation; ChEMBL also did not reveal established PLD3 mechanism-of-action drugs.
main_caveats: Therapeutic direction is inferred from knockdown and disease literature, not from rescue experiments or pharmacology in this dataset.

summary: Alx4 perturbation was transcriptomically silent across the 23 assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The absence of on-target Alx4 mRNA shifts and the absence of any FDR-significant downstream genes argue that these neuronal and GABAergic contexts are not active ALX4-response contexts in this screen.
main_caveats: Because the endogenous Alx4 transcript was nearly absent, the data do not prove efficient protein-level perturbation; low-count classes further reduce power.

summary: The only hint of cell-type structure was a weak nominal peak in inhibitory populations, led by 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: If followed up, these GABAergic classes are the least negative contexts, but every gene-level effect remains exploratory because no 054, 053, or 066 hit survived FDR correction.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Nominal p-value pattern only; strongest FDR was 0.3748 in 054 and all listed Sst and CNU-HYa HY hits had FDR=1.0.

summary: Alx1 and Alx3 behaved like Alx4: their own transcripts were not measurably engaged and ALX-family perturbations did not form a recurrent brain signature.
why_it_matters: Although ALX proteins are related developmental homeobox factors, the dataset supports absence of the ALX developmental program rather than a paralog-specific Alx4 neural module.
main_caveats: Alx1 was assayed in fewer groups and Alx1/Alx3 had one isolated FDR hit each; the conclusion rests on lack of target-transcript shifts and lack of a coherent recurrent module.

summary: Alx4 was uncoupled from the Wnt/LEF/β-catenin branch that is detectable through Ctnnb1 perturbation in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: Prior ALX4-LEF1 promoter biology does not generalize to a detectable mouse-brain Alx4 signature; the dataset can detect Wnt-effector perturbation, but Alx4 does not phenocopy or oppose it.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is a correlation of separately summarized perturbation signatures; it does not test direct ALX4 and CTNNB1 co-occupancy or protein interaction in neurons.

summary: The Perturb-seq result points ALX4 disease liability away from intrinsic assayed brain-cell transcriptional programs and toward its established craniofacial, skeletal, limb, and epidermal developmental lineages.
why_it_matters: For ALX4-linked parietal foramina and frontonasal dysplasia, the silent mouse-brain result is consistent with developmental mesenchymal loss of function rather than broad sensitivity of the sampled brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The screen does not assay embryonic cranial neural crest, limb bud mesenchyme, osteoblasts, epidermis, or developmental time points at which ALX4 disease mechanisms are expected.

summary: Gnas perturbation produced no FDR-supported loss of the Gnas transcript and no adjusted downstream transcriptional program in any of 23 cell classes.
why_it_matters: A Gs alpha perturbation would be expected to impinge on adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, PKA and CREB signaling; this screen instead provides a weak or inactive Gnas loss-of-function signature.
main_caveats: Transcript knockdown, Gαs protein, cAMP and CREB phosphorylation were not directly measured; CRISPR indels can fail to reduce mRNA.

summary: The strongest Gnas-associated rows were weak and concentrated in cortical intratelencephalic classes, led by Snx29 in 001 L5-6 IT Glut and Clstn3/Snap47 in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: If the nominal pattern is real, cortical IT neurons may be the most sensitive population; however, the signal is below FDR 0.05 and should guide validation rather than mechanism.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: No gene crossed FDR<0.05; 001 L5-6 IT Glut had only 72 perturbed cells.

summary: Prkaca was robustly depleted in 10 cell classes while Gnas was not, indicating that the assay can record target engagement of a cAMP/PKA node even though Gnas itself is silent.
why_it_matters: This separates a Gnas-specific engagement or buffering problem from a generic inability to assay the cAMP pathway, while also showing that acute PKA catalytic-subunit loss was mostly transcriptionally buffered.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The downstream Prkaca response was also buffered at the transcriptome level; no kinase activity measurements were available.

summary: Gnao1 and Gnb1 showed strong on-target depletion in thalamic and midbrain classes where Gnas did not, arguing against a shared generic heterotrimeric G-protein perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: Related G-protein complex components should be compared empirically; in this screen, Gnas is not interchangeable with either inhibitory/o-family alpha or beta-subunit perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Gnao1 and Gnb1 are not exact paralogs of Gnas; the contrast may reflect target-specific guide performance and regional expression as well as biology.

summary: The striatal-like 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA class lacked a Gnas response but responded to Pde10a, consistent with literature in which striatal projection neurons preferentially use Gnal/Gαolf rather than Gnas/Gαs for D1/A2A cAMP signaling.
why_it_matters: This turns an apparent absence of cAMP biology in CNU-LGE cells into a plausible Gs-family division of labor and prioritizes Gnal or Pde10a over Gnas for striatal cyclic-nucleotide perturbations.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset cell class is broad; direct Gnal engagement in 059 was not established, and Gnas itself was weakly engaged.

summary: The absent acute neuronal Gnas transcriptomic response does not derisk systemic GNAS inhibition because human GNAS disorders are dose-, parent-of-origin-, tissue-, and direction-dependent.
why_it_matters: GNAS can cause both loss-of-function endocrine/skeletal syndromes and gain-of-function mosaic or tumor phenotypes, so a quiet mouse-brain CRISPR signature is not evidence that direct Gαs antagonism would be broadly benign.
main_caveats: The dataset lacked endocrine and skeletal tissues and did not test activating GNAS alleles.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor analysis failed to identify a robust Gnas-like related perturbation; cAMP/G-protein relatives in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut were only modest and mixed.
why_it_matters: The lack of a strong positive or negative neighbor prevents overinterpretation of the Gnas nominal rows as a reproducible pathway module.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Correlations used only the top 100 absolute-score Gnas genes per cell class and are intended as a restricted neighbor screen, not genome-wide signature replication.

summary: Drd2 loss produced no FDR-resolved transcriptional program in any of the 23 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant result is not a pathway activation but a broadly buffered or under-engaged receptor perturbation, so nominal top genes should not be interpreted as a dopamine-response module.
cell_types: 23 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: Absence of FDR hits can reflect low target expression, weak CRISPR engagement, chronic compensation, or the inability of endpoint scRNA-seq to capture acute Gi/o signaling.

summary: The only convincing nominal on-target decrease of Drd2 was confined to 215 MB Dopa and remained low-powered and transcriptionally isolated.
why_it_matters: Midbrain dopamine neurons are the class where an autoreceptor response would be expected, yet only the target transcript moved nominally and dopamine identity genes did not follow.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The cell count was only 20; Drd2 FDR stayed at 1.0, so this is evidence of nominal target engagement rather than a resolved autoreceptor transcriptional phenotype.

summary: The broad 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA population did not show striatal D2/cAMP engagement.
why_it_matters: Prior biology concentrates DRD2 in medium spiny neurons and indirect-pathway signaling, so the flat LGE/LSX result argues that broad cell-class aggregation or weak receptor expression can mask a classic D2 module.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset label is broader than purified D2 medium spiny neurons; the inference is a dilution/context explanation, not proof that D2-MSNs are insensitive.

summary: Drd2, Drd3, Drd4, Drd5, and Adora2a receptor perturbations were mutually non-convergent and individually weak.
why_it_matters: Dopamine-family membership or D2/A2A network proximity was insufficient to make receptor-level CRISPR signatures interchangeable in this assay.
cell_types: 23 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: The compared receptor signatures also lacked strong on-target depletion, so near-zero correlations mostly reinforce a negative result rather than proving mechanistic divergence.

summary: Core G-protein transducers were detectably knocked down in selected cell classes whereas Drd2 was not.
why_it_matters: The dataset could identify strong self-transcript loss for Gnao1, Gnb1, and Gnb5, separating a receptor-specific engagement failure from a universal failure of Gi/o-pathway genes to be assayed.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Gnao1/Gnb1/Gnb5 are shared transducers with broader expression than Drd2, so their knockdown is a technical and pathway-neighbor contrast, not a direct phenocopy test.

summary: The Drd2 Perturb-seq profile should not be used to infer the direction of approved D2 agonists or antagonists.
why_it_matters: DRD2 is a heavily drugged receptor, but the genetic signature lacked corrected downstream genes and modeled chronic transcript loss rather than acute ligand occupancy.
cell_types: 23 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: This screen cannot distinguish receptor antagonism, agonism, biased D2 signaling, or cell-surface occupancy; it only reports endpoint mRNA abundance after CRISPR perturbation.

summary: Hdac4 perturbation produced no FDR-controlled transcriptional response in any of the 22 assayed neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset result is absence of a robust acute scRNA-seq signature, not a hidden pathway activation; downstream nominal genes therefore have to be interpreted as exploratory.
main_caveats: The guide may have incompletely depleted HDAC4 protein even when Hdac4 mRNA was measured, and some cell types had fewer than 80 perturbed cells.

summary: The cell classes with the clearest nominal lowering of the Hdac4 transcript still showed no FDR-controlled downstream genes.
why_it_matters: Even when the target transcript moved in the intended direction, the response was buffered or undetectable at the transcriptome level.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All four Hdac4 measurements were nominal rather than FDR-significant; absence of downstream FDR genes may reflect partial knockdown, compensation, or limited power.

summary: An exploratory L2/3 IT cortical signature touched the HDAC4 synaptic-gene literature through nominal Grin2a and Shank2 decreases, but it did not look like broad derepression of central-synapse genes.
why_it_matters: Grin2a and Shank2 are plausible synaptic readouts to follow up, while their shared downward direction cautions that the Perturb-seq result is not a simple loss of an HDAC4 nuclear repressor.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: No Grin2a or Shank2 row passed FDR, the local Hdac4 mRNA change in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut was weak, and the observation is based on RNA rather than synaptic physiology.

summary: The Hdac4 guide signature was essentially uncorrelated with perturbations of the represented HDAC-family, MEF2, CaMK, 14-3-3, and RUNX2 neighbors.
why_it_matters: HDAC4 belongs to a biochemically well-connected MEF2/class-IIa regulatory module, so the near-zero single-cell signatures argue that this acute perturbation did not engage a shared module in the assayed states.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from noisy differential-expression score vectors; Hdac4 itself had weak target engagement, so this is evidence for lack of a detectable shared signature rather than proof of biochemical independence.

summary: Human HDAC4 haploinsufficiency cannot be modeled in this dataset as a broad, immediate transcriptional collapse across mature mouse neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The disease literature makes HDAC4 dosage clinically important, but the single-cell data point toward developmental timing, subcellular localization, and cell-state context as requirements for seeing a strong neuronal phenotype.
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measured acute mouse brain RNA, not human development, skeletal phenotypes, nuclear HDAC4, or synaptic physiology.

summary: HDAC4-directed pharmacology should not be treated as equivalent to the weak Hdac4 guide phenotype observed here.
why_it_matters: The data provide no robust neuronal response marker for Hdac4 mRNA loss, while curated pharmacology is dominated by broader HDAC-family inhibition rather than an HDAC4-specific mechanism.
main_caveats: No compound was tested; this warning is an inference from guide-based transcriptomics plus curated target annotations.

summary: E2f4 perturbation derepressed a one-sided mitotic, kinetochore, and DNA-repair-associated transcript program, strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The direction fits loss of an E2F4 repressor, but the genes induced in postmitotic neurons clustered in chromosome, spindle, and repair machinery rather than in a generic stress response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was assayed; postmitotic cell-cycle gene induction was not validated as cell-cycle entry or cell death.

summary: The E2f4 program was recurrent but sharply restricted to a handful of neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Aaas, Tube1, Rad18, Ddx11, Blm, and Polq recurred across subcortical excitatory and GABAergic contexts, whereas most other profiled neuronal classes had no FDR-level response, arguing that E2f4 loss is not uniformly wired in all brain cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The secondary cell types have fewer FDR genes than 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; the 191 and 066 classes are supported by Aaas alone at FDR<0.05.

summary: The significant E2f4 response did not become a full canonical G1/S E2F-RB program.
why_it_matters: Known E2F4/DREAM promoter targets such as Mybl2, Cdk1, Ccna2, Mcm2, and Pcna were not significant after E2f4 perturbation in the strongest cell type, while Rb1 perturbation in the same neurons induced Dnmt1, Tipin, Prim1, Mcm2, E2f1, Ccne2, and Pcna.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Gene detection and neuronal state could mask some canonical targets; the conclusion is based on mRNA FDR rather than chromatin occupancy.

summary: E2f4 was not interchangeable with paralog E2f5, activator-family E2f1, or its DP partner Tfdp1 in thalamic neurons.
why_it_matters: Although these proteins belong to the same E2F wiring diagram, the E2f4 perturbation produced 32 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while E2f1 and E2f5 produced none and Tfdp1 produced only two, with near-zero whole-signature correlations to E2f4 except a weak Tfdp1 correlation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Negative related-perturbation signatures could reflect guide editing efficiency, protein half-life, or basal expression rather than biology alone.

summary: Reducing E2f4 activity in vulnerable neurons may be hazardous because this dataset derepressed cell-cycle and DNA-repair genes while neuronal E2F4-p130 complexes are reported to support survival.
why_it_matters: The dataset shows the same sign expected from loss of a repressor, and injury literature links E2F4-p130-HDAC/Suv39H1 integrity to neuronal survival, so interventions that simply inhibit E2F4 in brain should be evaluated for ectopic cell-cycle transcription.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The perturb-seq assay did not apply ischemia, DNA damage, or measure apoptosis; therapeutic inference is indirect.

summary: Measured E2f4 mRNA depletion was weak even when downstream signatures were strong.
why_it_matters: The lack of FDR-level target-transcript reduction means the guide assignment should be interpreted as genetic perturbation rather than as a measured knockdown series, and cell types with no response cannot be assumed to have had no E2F4 protein disruption.
main_caveats: The parquet does not report indel efficiency or E2F4 protein abundance, so target editing could have occurred without a large mRNA decrease.

summary: Ptcd3 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome in any tested mouse-brain neuronal class and did not achieve FDR-significant Ptcd3 mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: The dataset should not be interpreted as a successful neuronal loss-of-function model of the mitochondrial translation factor PTCD3; the primary signal is weak target engagement plus low per-cell-type perturbation counts.
main_caveats: This conclusion is about the Perturb-seq transcriptome and Ptcd3 mRNA rows, not about protein depletion; perturbed-cell counts were only 21-79 per cell type.

summary: No corrected mitochondrial-encoded mRNA response accompanied Ptcd3 perturbation, so the expected mitochondrial-translation biology was not visible at the single-cell RNA readout.
why_it_matters: PTCD3 loss is expected to impair mitochondrial protein synthesis and respiration rather than necessarily destabilize mitochondrial mRNAs; the absence of mt-mRNA FDR hits is therefore more a readout limitation and engagement warning than evidence that the pathway is dispensable.
main_caveats: Only steady-state mRNAs were assayed; mitochondrial translation products, respiratory-chain assembly, ATP synthesis and respiration were not measured.

summary: The apparent 308 CB GABA enrichment was only nominal and should be treated as an exploratory artifact-prone signature rather than a Ptcd3-selective cerebellar response.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-calling Mdm2, Pkd2, Snd1, Snap25 or top restricted signature neighbors as biomarkers of PTCD3 loss when the same CB GABA profile had 0 FDR-significant genes and FDR=0.916 for Ptcd3 itself.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Moderate confidence is assigned only to the negative interpretation; the CB GABA genes and signature neighbors are hypothesis-generating and non-significant.

summary: A related mitochondrial small-subunit perturbation, Dap3, and several respiratory-chain perturbations were deeply knocked down in overlapping neuronal classes, whereas Ptcd3 remained unengaged.
why_it_matters: The Ptcd3 null result is not explained by a universal inability of this screen to recover mitochondrial transcripts; the most parsimonious explanation is Ptcd3-specific guide or expression limitations, so lack of convergence with Dap3 should not be read as mitoribosome biology diverging.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Comparator links are partly structural or downstream of mitochondrial translation; most comparator signatures were dominated by their own target transcript rather than a broad downstream state.

summary: The screen provides no support for beneficial PTCD3 inhibition, while human genetics and target databases indicate that PTCD3 loss is a mitochondrial-disease liability with little curated pharmacologic tractability.
why_it_matters: A weak mouse-brain Perturb-seq response should not be used as safety evidence for suppressing a human mitochondrial-translation factor whose biallelic deficiency causes Leigh-spectrum combined OXPHOS disease.
main_caveats: The dataset did not produce efficient Ptcd3 loss, and it lacks organismal neurologic, metabolic, and mitochondrial respiration phenotypes.

direction: Kmt2a down; 151 mixed downstream; 155 Kmt2a and Fnbp1l down
summary: Kmt2a knockdown produced one clearly resolved mature-brain regulon, concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with a smaller two-gene response in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: KMT2A is a general chromatin writer, but the dataset argues that its acute transcriptional requirement is sharply context-dependent across mature mouse-brain neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The 151 regulon is transcriptomic and acute; direct KMT2A-bound loci or H3K4 changes were not measured.

direction: target transcript down with absent corrected downstream response
summary: Several cell types showed nominally strong Kmt2a transcript reduction but no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The result separates target engagement from transcriptional vulnerability and suggests either buffering, delayed chromatin effects, or insufficient power in multiple mature neuronal classes.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: 191 MB P MY GABA missed target-transcript FDR at 0.103, and 054/217/308 had only 31-66 perturbed cells, so low power and partial knockdown cannot be excluded.

direction: noncanonical neuronal genes mixed; canonical readouts unchanged
summary: The leading Kmt2a response was bidirectional and did not use the canonical HOX, Dlx2, Meis2, or Arc readouts often associated with KMT2A biology.
why_it_matters: The perturbation is better interpreted as a mature, cell-type-specific neuronal regulon than as a simple collapse of all known KMT2A-activated developmental or activity-induced targets.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: HOX genes and immediate-early genes may be lowly expressed in these mature cell types, so the negative result is an uncoupling of this assay rather than evidence that KMT2A cannot regulate them elsewhere.

direction: Kmt2a versus Kmt2d weakly opposing; other comparators near zero
summary: Kmt2a did not phenocopy other H3K4/chromatin perturbations; Kmt2d was the strongest negative signature neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Even paralogous or physically connected chromatin regulators were not interchangeable in this neuronal state, so shared chromatin neighborhoods were a poor predictor of acute regulon direction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Absolute correlations were small and the contrast is restricted to same-assay score vectors, not matched chromatin occupancy.

summary: Fnbp1l is an exploratory 155 MB Glut marker of Kmt2a perturbation.
why_it_matters: The midbrain glutamatergic response had strong target knockdown but only one non-target FDR hit, making Fnbp1l a compact candidate readout if this cell class is revisited.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene downstream signature; no recurrence across cell types or mechanistic validation.

summary: Singleton FDR hits in three additional glutamatergic classes did not resolve into local Kmt2a programs.
why_it_matters: Ptprk, Aff4, and Nap1l2 should be treated as cell-type-specific leads rather than as evidence for broad Kmt2a pathway activation.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Each cell type had exactly one FDR-significant gene and the Kmt2a transcript did not reach FDR<0.05 in those types.

summary: Wild-type Kmt2a loss-of-function signatures in mouse brain should not be read as direct menin-inhibitor or KMT2A-rearranged leukemia pharmacology.
why_it_matters: KMT2A-rearranged leukemia is clinically druggable through a menin-KMT2A interaction inhibitor, but this Perturb-seq experiment assays partial wild-type transcript depletion in mature neurons and yielded neuronal, not leukemic, response genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset contains no malignant hematopoietic cells, KMT2A fusions, menin inhibitor, or KMT2A protein-complex occupancy measurement.

summary: Chchd10 mRNA depletion was reproducible but restricted to a subset of neuronal classes, with seven FDR-significant target rows and eight classes with only weak or absent on-target mRNA reduction.
why_it_matters: The dominant biological observation is target engagement rather than a downstream program; cell classes with weak self knockdown should not be scored as Chchd10-resistant biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: mRNA engagement does not measure CHCHD10 protein depletion, and two assayed classes had fewer than 30 perturbed cells.

summary: Even where Chchd10 itself was significantly reduced, the perturbation produced no FDR-supported non-target genes and did not induce the ASNS/DDIT3/CHAC1/SLC7A5 stress module.
why_it_matters: This indicates that acute Chchd10 transcript loss is transcriptionally buffered in the assayed mouse-brain populations, distinguishing simple loss from the mutant mtISR phenotypes reported for CHCHD10 disease alleles.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The result is transcriptomic and may miss delayed, protein-level, or stress-unmasked mitochondrial defects.

summary: Chchd10 loss was uncoupled from the ISR-like mitochondrial stress program that appeared after Opa1 and Dnm1l perturbation in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: Because CHCHD10/CHCHD2 have been linked to OMA1 and OPA1 processing, the absence of the Opa1/Dnm1l-like ASNS-CHAC1-DDIT3 response argues that this guide-driven Chchd10 loss is upstream-buffered or incomplete rather than a generic cristae-collapse lesion.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Opa1 and Dnm1l are pathway neighbors rather than CHCHD10 complex members, and their own target-transcript FDR was not uniform in every responsive cell type.

summary: The CHCHD10 paralog Chchd2 showed the same buffering pattern: stronger self knockdown than Chchd10 in several classes but zero non-target FDR hits.
why_it_matters: The shared negative output prevents over-interpreting the lack of a Chchd10 signature as only a failed target; instead, two homologous mitochondrial IMS perturbations were transcriptionally silent except for self depletion.
main_caveats: The single-cell dataset assays mRNA responses, not CHCHD10-CHCHD2 complex abundance, respiration, or stress-challenge phenotypes.

summary: Chchd10 loss did not converge with the robust Fus or Tardbp ALS/FTD perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: CHCHD10 is genetically linked to ALS/FTD, but the dataset places simple Chchd10 transcript depletion outside the RNA-binding-protein response class and is more consistent with CHCHD10 disease requiring mutant proteotoxic or mitochondrial stress contexts.
main_caveats: The assay sampled mouse brain cell classes, not spinal lower motor neurons, and modeled target loss rather than dominant CHCHD10 missense aggregation.

summary: No FDR-supported Chchd10-loss biomarker or high-confidence positive/negative signature neighbor was recovered.
why_it_matters: The leading non-target genes and all genome-wide signature correlations were too weak for mechanistic nomination, so biomarker discovery should use stronger CHCHD10 perturbation models or stress sensitization.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|053 Sst Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The signature-neighbor result is restricted to Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors and was not independently replicated.

summary: The perturb-seq loss phenotype should not be used as a direct efficacy proxy for CHCHD10-linked disease, and CHCHD10 itself has little evidence of conventional direct ligandability.
why_it_matters: A therapeutic screen around this locus should model mutant CHCHD10 or downstream OMA1/mtISR biology rather than expect partial wild-type transcript loss to phenocopy disease or yield a simple rescue marker.
main_caveats: Open Targets and ChEMBL absence of direct drug records is not proof that CHCHD10 cannot be modulated experimentally.

summary: Nr2e3 perturbation was transcriptionally inert across the assayed mouse-brain neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: A target with no FDR-controlled downstream genes and no detectable target-transcript depletion should be treated as an unengaged or biologically silent perturbation in this dataset rather than as evidence for a brain NR2E3 program.
main_caveats: The data prove lack of a measured RNA response under this library and sampling scheme, not complete absence of NR2E3 protein activity under every brain condition.

summary: The canonical NR2E3 rod/cone and phototransduction program was not mobilized, including in the pineal glutamatergic class.
why_it_matters: Prior work places NR2E3 at RHO, S-opsin, M-opsin, and rod phosphodiesterase regulation in photoreceptors; the mouse-brain Perturb-seq cells lacked any measurable response in an explicit retinal marker panel.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is an absence call in a non-retinal dataset; the pineal subgroup contained only 39 perturbed cells.

summary: Retinal transcriptional regulators and nuclear-receptor relatives did not converge with Nr2e3 signatures.
why_it_matters: CRX and NRL are close NR2E3 network partners in retina, yet their brain perturbation signatures were also weak and nearly uncorrelated with Nr2e3, arguing against a hidden shared retinal-like module in the screened cells.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The strongest statement is lack of convergence in broad score vectors; Nrl had two isolated FDR hits but no coherent shared module.

summary: The brain negative result should not be extrapolated as evidence against retinal NR2E3 augmentation or retinal NR2E3 loss-of-function disease mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Human genetics, retinal organoids, and mouse AAV studies all implicate NR2E3 in photoreceptor fate or rescue; the Perturb-seq result says the necessary rod-like regulatory context is absent from the sampled brain classes.
main_caveats: This is a directionality guardrail, not a therapeutic-efficacy test; no diseased retina or AAV overexpression perturbation was assayed.

summary: Pfkm perturbation achieved reproducible on-target repression, but the FDR-significant engagement concentrated in six thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, and GABAergic classes rather than all assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Interpretation of downstream absence has to be stratified by target engagement; the strongest conclusions come from the six classes where the target transcript itself was depleted.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: FDR-significant target repression is a hybrid of biology, guide recovery, and power; HPA brain data are bulk or atlas summaries and do not match these mouse Perturb-seq subclasses exactly.

summary: Pfkm knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: after removing Pfkm itself, no assayed cell type contained any non-target gene with FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: PFKM is a core glycolytic enzyme, so the absence of a broad RNA program argues that neuronal glycolytic perturbation can be absorbed post-transcriptionally or metabolically at the time point of this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The dataset measures steady-state mRNA only; flux, fructose-2,6-bisphosphate, ATP, protein abundance, and PFK tetramer composition were not measured.

summary: Within the glycolytic pathway, Pfkm and Pgk1 were not interchangeable perturbations in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons: Pgk1 produced 21 non-target FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Pfkm produced none.
why_it_matters: The result prevents a simple same-pathway extrapolation from later glycolytic enzymes to the metabolite-regulated PFK step in these neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Pgk1 had stronger target repression and more perturbed cells than Pfkm in the thalamic class, and Pfkl/Pfkp were absent as direct paralog comparators, so enzyme identity, perturbation strength, and power cannot be fully separated.

summary: Three forebrain excitatory classes had essentially no Pfkm target engagement and therefore should not be interpreted as resistant downstream biology.
why_it_matters: This guards against overcalling null signatures in classes where the perturbation did not measurably lower the target transcript.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Weak target engagement may reflect low guide activity, stochastic recovery, or transcript detection rather than true biological unresponsiveness.

summary: The muted neuronal mRNA response should not be read as evidence that PFKM loss is safe: Pfkm was successfully repressed in several neuronal classes, but the assay did not reproduce the severe skeletal-muscle, erythrocyte, and cardiac pathology caused by organismal Pfkm deficiency.
why_it_matters: PFKM/PFK1 inhibition around the brain would need metabolic and systemic safety readouts rather than relying on a lack of acute neuronal FDR genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The disease reference is a germline mouse knockout dominated by muscle, blood, and heart physiology; it is not a matched neuronal CRISPR experiment.

summary: Pfkm did not have a robust atlas-wide transcriptomic neighbor, positive or negative, when all perturbations were projected onto the top Pfkm nominal genes.
why_it_matters: The weak neighbor structure argues against inferring a latent pathway module from single cell-type restricted nominal hits.
main_caveats: This is a restricted-signature correlation over Pfkm-selected genes, not a precomputed full-rank similarity metric; correlations were small and should be used only as a null comparison.

summary: Productive Atcay transcript knockdown was concentrated in four subcortical classes: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: Interpretation of the perturbation should be anchored to the classes with transcriptome-wide target engagement rather than to all assayed neuronal classes.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction reflects observed target-transcript knockdown and may include guide abundance or CRISPRi-efficiency effects as well as biology.

summary: Even where Atcay was knocked down strongly, the downstream steady-state mRNA response was buffered: no non-Atcay gene passed FDR in the four target-engaged classes.
why_it_matters: The phenotype is not a broad transcriptional stress or degeneration program, which is compatible with Caytaxin acting through cargo localization and neurite transport instead of transcriptional control.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: FDR buffering does not exclude protein-localization, axonal-transport, electrophysiologic, or late degenerative phenotypes.

summary: Atcay loss was not transcriptomically interchangeable with core kinesin-1 light-chain or heavy-chain knockdown despite the known Caytaxin-KLC interaction.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates a Caytaxin adaptor branch from general kinesin-1 depletion; cargo-specific perturbations may not phenocopy loss of Klc1, Klc2, Kif5a, or Kif5c at the mRNA level.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison used same-cell-type score-vector correlations; the transcriptional signatures of all five knockdowns were sparse and may miss subcellular transport defects.

summary: The assay did not yield a transcriptome-wide cerebellar or dopaminergic Atcay phenotype, but the relevant classes were underpowered or weakly engaged.
why_it_matters: This negative result should not be read as evidence against the established ATCAY ataxia mechanism; chronic Caytaxin loss and specific cerebellar populations may be required to expose disease biology.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The cerebellar and pineal signatures had 87 and 29 perturbed cells, respectively, and the dopaminergic class had only 25 cells with weak Atcay reduction.

summary: A single Atcay-engaged hypothalamic glutamatergic class showed a weak Acly mRNA increase, pointing to a hypothesis that ACL-pathway transcripts can compensate when Caytaxin-mediated ACL transport is impaired.
why_it_matters: Acly is a literature cargo of the BNIP-H/Caytaxin-KLC1 pathway, so even a nominal, opposite-direction transcript change is mechanistically worth preserving as a hypothesis for validation.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Acly was not FDR-significant and the observation was confined to one cell class; it should be treated only as a biomarker/compensation hypothesis.

summary: The strongest Atcay signature in 155 MB Glut had no meaningful positive or negative genome-wide signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The signature-neighbor search did not reveal a hidden convergent module that could replace a direct Atcay mechanism; the 155 MB Glut response was essentially target-transcript dominated.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The search was summarized for 155 MB Glut because it had the strongest Atcay self knockdown; weak correlations could still reflect shared noise or subtle biology.

direction: mostly weak target decrease; no adjusted downstream program
summary: Gria3 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across the assayed mouse-brain classes: no comparison reached FDR < 0.05 and only one gene, Jmjd1c in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, reached FDR < 0.1.
why_it_matters: GRIA3 encodes a core AMPA receptor pore-forming subunit, but the dataset does not yield a robust RNA state that can be treated as a successful GluA3-loss signature.
main_caveats: This is a negative transcriptomic result, not proof that Gria3 is biologically dispensable; most cell types had 26-62 perturbed cells and no target row survived FDR correction.

direction: nominal Gria3 down with buffered downstream expression
summary: The best on-target signal occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Gria3 itself was the top nominal hit, yet no downstream gene reached FDR < 0.1.
why_it_matters: The matched on-target and no-downstream pattern argues that the cleanest observed transcript depletion was still insufficient to create a stable cell-state conversion detectable by this Wilcoxon screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: On-target Gria3 depletion was nominal rather than FDR-significant, and the strongest comparison still had only 132 perturbed cells.

summary: The lone FDR < 0.1 signal, Jmjd1c up-regulation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut, occurred in a cell type where Gria3 was not lowered.
why_it_matters: This prevents the single adjusted gene from being over-interpreted as an AMPA receptor loss-of-function pathway and marks it as an isolated, hypothesis-generating signal.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only 37 perturbed cells supported this comparison, and Jmjd1c crossed only an exploratory FDR < 0.1 threshold.

summary: Gria3 knockdown did not induce transcriptional compensation among other AMPA receptor subunits or canonical auxiliary/scaffold partners.
why_it_matters: Known GRIA3-containing receptor assemblies include GRIA1/2/4, CACNG/TARP, CNIH, GRIP/PICK, and DLG proteins; none showed adjusted RNA feedback after Gria3 perturbation, so the assay does not reveal a receptor-subunit replacement program.
main_caveats: Absence of RNA compensation is conditional on weak Gria3 perturbation and does not test AMPAR trafficking, assembly, surface abundance, or channel biophysics.

summary: Gria3 did not phenocopy related AMPA subunits or strongly engaged excitatory postsynaptic neighbors in the same thalamic glutamatergic class.
why_it_matters: Gria2 and Gria1 achieved adjusted on-target knockdown in other classes, and Grin1, Dlg4, and Dlgap4 were more robustly engaged than Gria3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; therefore paralogous AMPAR membership did not make Gria3 an interchangeable perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast combines different guide efficiencies and perturbed-cell counts, and the transcriptome is an indirect readout of synaptic receptor physiology.

direction: no detectable cerebellar transcriptional knockdown response
summary: A cerebellar Gria3 requirement known from Purkinje-cell physiology was not recovered in the broad 308 CB GABA Perturb-seq class.
why_it_matters: GluA3 is required for mouse parallel-fiber-to-Purkinje-cell LTP and motor learning, yet the cerebellar GABA-labeled class showed no Gria3 depletion and no adjusted DE, warning that this dataset cannot adjudicate that highly synapse- and cell-type-specific phenotype.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA is not Purkinje-cell-resolved, had only 42 perturbed cells, and the assay measures RNA rather than parallel-fiber synaptic potentiation.

direction: disease direction is bidirectional in literature; dataset direction is weak loss of transcript
summary: The dataset provides no allele-directional GRIA3 disease model; pathogenic human GRIA3 variants can be either loss- or gain-of-function, while the Perturb-seq perturbation was a weak loss-of-transcript experiment.
why_it_matters: Because both excess and deficient AMPAR function can be pathogenic, the buffered Gria3 RNA signature should not be used to justify unstratified AMPAR activation or inhibition strategies.
main_caveats: Mouse guide-based transcript reduction in heterogeneous brain classes is not the same perturbation as human missense or deletion alleles assayed electrophysiologically.

summary: Pak1 mRNA was strongly depleted in five neuronal classes, yet the response was almost completely limited to the Pak1 transcript itself.
why_it_matters: PAK1 is a canonical Rho-GTPase-regulated actin and synaptic kinase, so a target-only single-cell RNA phenotype indicates buffering of steady-state transcription or a post-transcriptional endpoint mismatch rather than absence of PAK1 biology.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Perturbation was transcript depletion, not an acute kinase inhibitor or phosphoproteomic readout; actin, spine, and synaptic phenotypes could occur without large mRNA changes.

summary: Measured Pak1 target engagement was cell-type selective, with five FDR-significant self rows, one near-threshold self row in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and several cell types with little target depletion.
why_it_matters: Downstream negative results are only interpretable where Pak1 mRNA was actually reduced; weak self depletion in some cell types is a guide-delivery or expression caveat, not evidence that PAK1 is dispensable there.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The dataset gives mRNA knockdown statistics, not PAK1 protein or kinase activity; some non-engaged groups also had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Canonical Pak1 neighbors did not converge on a Pak1-like transcriptomic state.
why_it_matters: PAK1, PAK3, CDC42, RAC1, and LIMK1 form a biochemical actin-signaling neighborhood, but their perturbation score vectors were nearly orthogonal in this dataset, arguing that the measured single-cell RNA phenotype is not a linear readout of the Rho-GTPase/PAK/LIMK cascade.
main_caveats: Most related perturbations also had weak own-target mRNA depletion, so absence of convergence is strongest as evidence against a detectable shared transcriptomic module rather than against biochemical pathway connectivity.

summary: The Perturb-seq phenotype does not recapitulate the gain-of-function PAK1 disease mechanism reported in human neurodevelopmental disorders.
why_it_matters: Human PAK1 disorders are driven by activating missense variants that relieve autoinhibition; partial Pak1 mRNA loss in assayed mouse neuronal classes was transcriptionally quiet, so this dataset is a better test of loss or inhibition in the assayed cells than of developmental kinase hyperactivation.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Species, developmental timing, perturbation direction, and readout differ from human activating variants; a silent mRNA signature does not exclude developmental or electrophysiological defects.

summary: Pak1 itself is the only robust RNA biomarker of Pak1 knockdown in this screen, so downstream phospho-cytoskeletal markers are likely required for pharmacodynamic studies.
why_it_matters: PAK1 is chemically tractable and selective PAK1 degraders/inhibitors have been described, but the screen provides no recurrent non-target transcript that could substitute for direct PAK1, LIMK, cofilin, spine, or synaptic measurements.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is a biomarker warning from mouse single-cell RNA after genetic perturbation; small molecules may have different kinetics, occupancy, and off-target profiles.

summary: Dctn1 knockdown robustly activated a SREBP-like cholesterol and fatty-acid synthesis program rather than a broad mixed stress response in the most responsive neurons.
why_it_matters: The primary transcriptomic readout of partial dynactin loss was sterol demand, linking a microtubule motor adaptor to lipid/endolysosomal homeostasis.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA only; SREBP2 protein cleavage, sterol content and dynein cargo movement were not directly measured.

direction: responsive in selected subcortical/GABA classes; buffered in many cortical/hippocampal classes
summary: The sterol response was concentrated in subcortical glutamatergic, hindbrain/midbrain GABAergic and MGE-derived GABAergic classes, while many cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic classes were buffered.
why_it_matters: A ubiquitous motor adaptor produced a geographically restricted neuronal state, so Dctn1 expression loss alone was insufficient to predict the downstream program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Nonresponsive classes often had fewer Dctn1-perturbed cells or weaker adjusted on-target significance; absence of FDR genes is not proof of no proteomic phenotype.

summary: Cytoplasmic dynein heavy-chain perturbation phenocopied the Dctn1 sterol program and was the top non-Dctn1 signature neighbor in the strongest responsive classes.
why_it_matters: The Dctn1 program is not an idiosyncratic guide effect; it tracks the known dynein-dynactin transport axis.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The strongest all-gene correlations were modest, other dynactin subunits were not perturbed, and Dync1h1 did not reproduce every Dctn1-responsive cell type.

summary: A Rab7 late-endosomal perturbation partially converged on Dctn1, placing the cholesterol response near a Rab7/RILP/p150Glued trafficking module.
why_it_matters: This points to late endosome positioning or cholesterol export, rather than a generic cytoskeletal stress, as a plausible upstream lesion for SREBP-like activation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Rab7 was a modest whole-transcriptome neighbor and the dataset did not measure late-endosome localization or ORP1L cholesterol-state directly.

summary: Srebf2 knockdown moved the same sterol genes in the opposite direction from Dctn1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: The inverse comparator argues that the Dctn1 signature is an upstream activation of a SREBP-regulated demand program, not loss of the Srebf2 transcriptional effector itself.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Opposition was inferred from perturbation-level transcriptomes; SREBP2 cleavage and direct chromatin binding were not assayed.

direction: compensatory sterol upregulation after Dctn1 loss
summary: For a DCTN1 neurodegeneration gene, the observed neuronal knockdown state was a compensatory lipid-synthesis program, making Hmgcr/Ldlr/Fdps better stress biomarkers than direct DCTN1 drug targets.
why_it_matters: DCTN1 is genetically linked to Perry syndrome, motor neuronopathy and ALS, but the dataset suggests that regulating downstream cholesterol enzymes may be a homeostatic consequence of transport failure; direct DCTN1 pharmacology is also poorly supported in ChEMBL.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation is mouse CRISPR-interference transcript knockdown, not a human dominant DCTN1 disease allele or a long-term degeneration model.

summary: FDR-level Adam22 knockdown in the two strongest glutamatergic contexts was transcriptionally target-only.
why_it_matters: The expected LGI1-ADAM22-MAGUK synaptic adhesion receptor can be measurably depleted without evoking a broad acute mRNA program, so this Perturb-seq experiment is reporting a buffered or structurally encoded synaptic response rather than a large stress-like cascade.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The measured endpoint is mRNA after partial single-guide perturbation; electrophysiology, protein localization, and long-term circuit maturation were not assayed.

summary: Adam22 loss did not transcriptionally compensate the LGI1, PSD-95, AMPA/NMDA-receptor, or Kv-channel partner module.
why_it_matters: ADAM22 is physically embedded in a synaptic complex, but the partner genes remained unchanged at mRNA level, arguing against a simple expression-feedback model for the acute response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only selected partner transcripts were tested; unchanged RNA does not rule out altered receptor trafficking or nanodomain organization.

summary: The ligand Lgi1 and other STRING-connected synaptic perturbations did not phenocopy Adam22 transcriptomically.
why_it_matters: A strong physical interaction map should not be interpreted as perturbation-signature interchangeability in this dataset; Adam22 behaves mostly as a target-only perturbation.
main_caveats: Lgi1 itself had weak target-transcript engagement, and most Adam22 signatures had no downstream FDR genes, which compresses correlation dynamic range.

summary: Adam22 target engagement was reproducible in direction across the panel but reached FDR significance only in L4/5 cortical and Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports broad guide activity with a strong-cell-type subset; biological interpretation should focus on the two FDR-level contexts and treat other classes as nominal evidence only.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cell types differ in perturbed-cell counts, baseline target expression, and detection; two cell classes in the full dataset had no Adam22 result row.

summary: Disease genetics favor ADAM22 loss as pathogenic even though acute Adam22 mRNA depletion was not broadly cytotoxic transcriptionally.
why_it_matters: The negative downstream Perturb-seq result should not be read as evidence that ADAM22 inhibition is safe: mouse null alleles and human biallelic variants cause severe neurological disease through a synaptic organizing complex.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The dataset models partial acute transcript knockdown in mouse brain-cell classes, whereas the disease literature concerns inherited or full loss of ADAM22 function and organismal phenotypes.

summary: Adam22 lacked a robust global positive or inverse perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: The absence of a high-correlation neighbor suggests the Adam22 phenotype should not be assigned to a pre-existing transcriptomic module in this screen without orthogonal validation.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors and are restricted to target-cell combinations present in the same cell classes.

summary: Other synaptic perturbations could produce downstream FDR genes in the same cell classes where Adam22 remained target-only.
why_it_matters: This guards against the technical explanation that L4/5 cortical or Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic neurons were globally unable to report any synaptic-gene response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The comparators are synaptic or neuronal genes but are not all direct ADAM22-complex members and had different cell counts and on-target strengths.

direction: downstream genes down in 151; no FDR-significant genes elsewhere
summary: Med15 perturbation produced a conventional FDR-significant response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
why_it_matters: A broadly expressed Mediator coactivator resolved into a discrete thalamic glutamatergic liability rather than a pan-neuronal transcriptional collapse.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Med15 mRNA row itself was not FDR-significantly reduced, and several nonsignificant cell classes had fewer than 60 Med15 cells.

summary: The 151-class Med15 response is a coordinated down-regulation of synaptic and dendritic membrane genes rather than mixed activation and repression.
why_it_matters: The all-negative 19-gene FDR set links Med15 activity to maintenance of a neuronal structural/signaling module that includes calcium handling, receptor, adhesion, and Prkcd-class marker transcripts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The pathway label comes from enrichment of only 19 genes and is compartmental; it does not prove direct MED15 binding at those loci.

direction: partial convergence for Med13 and Med23; divergence for Med12 and Cdk8
summary: Med13 and Med23 partially phenocopied the Med15 thalamic signature, whereas Med12, Med13l, and Cdk8 were weak or absent despite all belonging to the Mediator family assayed in this cell type.
why_it_matters: The response cannot be explained as generic loss of any Mediator subunit; it separates a Med15/Med13/Med23-sensitive neuronal regulon from CDK8-module or other Mediator perturbations with larger cell counts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Genome-wide score correlations were weak, so the convergence is driven by the restricted down-gene set rather than a global one-to-one phenocopy.

direction: Srebf2 sterol targets down after Srebf2 perturbation but not after Med15 perturbation
summary: Med15 and Srebf2 perturbations were uncoupled in the same thalamic neurons even though MED15 is a known SREBP cofactor.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues that the neuronal Med15 program is not simply the canonical SREBP2 cholesterol-biosynthesis program; Srebf2 knockout robustly lowered sterol genes that Med15 perturbation left nonsignificant.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Weak Med15 transcript-level engagement could mask a lipid effect; absence of FDR response does not exclude MED15-SREBP biochemistry in other cells or stimulation states.

summary: The Med15-sensitive synaptic module overlaps the Med23 perturbation in a brain cell class, suggesting a candidate neuronal output for a Mediator subunit already linked to intellectual disability.
why_it_matters: Because MED23 variants cause neurodevelopmental disease, the Med15/Med23 shared down-regulation of Grm1, Pcp4, Plekhg1, Prkcd, Atp2a2, and related synaptic genes nominates this module as a mouse-brain hypothesis for Mediator-associated neuronal dysfunction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: MED23 literature concerns human inherited disease, not acute mouse Med15 perturbation in thalamic neurons; no direct MED15 neurodevelopmental genetics are established here.

summary: Loss of Med15 mRNA itself was not detected at FDR significance in any tested cell class, so transcript-level target engagement is weak in this table.
why_it_matters: The negative target row limits interpretation of nonsignificant cell types as true buffering and requires downstream phenotypes to be treated as guide-associated transcriptomic signatures rather than confirmed protein loss.
main_caveats: The perturbation could modify protein function without depleting mRNA; no protein or editing measurements are present in the parquet.

summary: Safe_target_71 behaved as a transcriptionally inert safe-targeting perturbation rather than as a gene knockdown.
why_it_matters: The result should be read as a negative-control baseline for Cas9 targeting, not as loss of a named neuronal gene or drug target.
main_caveats: The dataset contains no target transcript for Safe_target_71, and most contrasts had only 20-25 perturbed cells.

summary: The apparent 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut and 046 CTX-CGE GABA spikes were isolated nominal outliers, not a reproducible Safe_target_71 cell-type program.
why_it_matters: Rprd1b and Usp7 could otherwise be mistaken for cell-type-specific downstream genes; the FDR and recurrence patterns instead argue for exploratory singletons.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Each named outlier is non-significant at 5% FDR and based on 21-25 perturbed cells.

summary: The highest-count Safe_target_71 contrasts were also flat, consistent with a buffered or undetectable transcriptional response to the safe-targeting event.
why_it_matters: Lack of hits was not confined to the smallest cell bins; even the four largest Safe_target_71 cell types had no transcript passing FDR correction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The largest group still had only 60 perturbed cells, so subtle safe-DSB responses remain underpowered.

summary: Safe_target_71 did not stand out from the Safe_target control family, where rare singleton FDR tails were already present.
why_it_matters: The lone Safe_target_71 FDR < 0.10 observation is better treated as empirical safe-guide background than as a mechanistic Rprd1b phenotype.
main_caveats: This comparison addresses only the annotated Safe_target controls, not every possible non-targeting or gene-targeting guide design.

summary: An all-target signature-neighbor pass found no strong positive or negative perturbation that phenocopied Safe_target_71.
why_it_matters: The absence of a correlated real-gene neighbor reinforces that Safe_target_71 lacks a masked pathway-level phenotype in this Wilcoxon score space.
main_caveats: Correlations used unweighted score vectors within each cell type; a weak or nonlinear phenotype could be missed.

summary: Kcnh5 targeting produced a globally null mRNA phenotype across the 21 sampled brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: KCNH5 is a voltage-gated potassium-channel alpha subunit, yet this Perturb-seq readout contains no reproducible downstream marker after multiple-testing correction; nominal top genes should therefore not be interpreted as a Kcnh5 program.
main_caveats: High confidence for the absence of an FDR-level transcriptional response; it does not prove absence of an electrophysiologic phenotype because Kcnh5 mRNA knockdown was only nominal and never FDR-significant.

summary: The only cell classes with nominal Kcnh5 mRNA depletion were thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons and cortical L4-5 IT glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: These are the only assayed contexts where the guide appeared to move the target transcript in the intended direction, so they are the most plausible follow-up sites for Kcnh5 perturbation despite the weak statistics.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Both target decreases had FDR=1.0 and there were no FDR-significant downstream genes in either cell type.

summary: Kcnh5 and its EAG paralog/STRING neighbor Kcnh1 were not transcriptomically interchangeable in shared cell classes.
why_it_matters: EAG1 and EAG2 can form related voltage-gated potassium channels, but treating them as equivalent would be unsupported here because their full-score signatures were essentially uncorrelated, their top same-cell signature neighbors were weak, and neither generated an FDR-level KCNH-family transcriptional module.
main_caveats: Both EAG perturbations were weak in this dataset, so the finding is stronger as a warning against claiming convergence than as proof of divergent channel biology.

summary: The Kcnh5 perturbation did not propagate into measured voltage-gated potassium-channel or Kcnh5-neighborhood transcripts, even though the same dataset detected target-transcript loss for several other potassium-channel genes.
why_it_matters: The null is not a generic failure to measure ion-channel knockdown: Kcnq2 and KCNC-family perturbations sometimes depleted their targets at FDR<0.05, whereas Kcnh5 did not and Kcnab/Camk2/Cask neighbors were unchanged.
main_caveats: The comparison uses target-transcript engagement, not identical downstream phenotypes; potassium-channel paralogs differ in expression and guide performance.

summary: Human KCNH5 epilepsy genetics point to channel gating/pore dysfunction, whereas partial Kcnh5 transcript lowering in the mouse Perturb-seq panel did not create a stable disease-like mRNA state.
why_it_matters: This argues that KCNH5 pathogenicity is likely to be read out by voltage-gating biophysics, development, or electrophysiology before it is read out as a broad cell-class-average transcriptional program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Species, developmental stage, perturbation modality, and patient variant type are not matched; electrophysiology and splicing/isoform effects were not measured.

summary: No downstream gene qualifies as a robust Kcnh5-response biomarker in this analysis.
why_it_matters: The largest nominal hit, Setd4 in cerebellar GABA cells, remained far from FDR significance and occurred in a cell class with no target-transcript decrease, so it should be deprioritized until replicated.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative biomarker conclusion from the present dataset only; it does not test protein abundance or electrophysiologic biomarkers.

direction: Agrn down in five FDR-significant subcortical classes; not FDR-significant in the other 18 classes
summary: Agrn mRNA knockdown was FDR-significant in only five of 23 measured brain cell classes, concentrated in thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, and brainstem-associated classes.
why_it_matters: Downstream interpretation should be restricted to the cell classes where the perturbation demonstrably reduced the target transcript; the major cortical and hippocampal classes did not show corrected on-target engagement.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The pattern may reflect baseline Agrn expression, CRISPRi power, guide accessibility, or cell counts rather than true biological restriction of Agrin protein function.

direction: Agrn down; secondary transcriptome absent after FDR correction
summary: Significant Agrn depletion was transcriptionally buffered: no non-Agrn gene reached even FDR<0.10 anywhere in the Agrn perturbation matrix.
why_it_matters: Agrin has strong synaptic and extracellular matrix biology, so the response being limited to the target transcript indicates that this Perturb-seq assay did not capture a robust cell-autonomous transcriptional effector program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Single-cell mRNA DE does not measure extracellular Agrin protein, synapse morphology, acetylcholine receptor clustering, filopodia, or electrophysiology.

direction: uncoupled; Agrn correlations with related perturbations all |r|<=0.095 in engaged groups
summary: The Agrn signature did not converge with the Agrn-Lrp4-MuSK, dystroglycan, or glycosaminoglycan neighborhood, nor with any all-panel signature neighbor, despite strong curated physical and functional relationships in those pathways.
why_it_matters: The canonical Agrin pathway is a receptor/ECM system; near-zero score-vector correlations argue that partial Agrn mRNA loss in these brain cells is not transcriptionally equivalent to perturbing nearby ECM or synaptic-adhesion genes.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Several canonical receptor perturbations, especially Lrp4 and Musk, had weak or unmeasurable on-target engagement in these neuronal groups; this is a signature-level nonconvergence, not proof of receptor independence.

summary: This screen does not directly test the published cortical-excitatory Agrin synapse-loss model, because cortical and hippocampal classes lacked FDR-significant Agrn transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: The absence of a corrected cortical response should be treated as target-engagement failure or low power rather than as a contradiction of Agrin-dependent cortical excitatory synapse maintenance reported in rescued null mice.
main_caveats: Nominal Agrn decreases were present in some cortical or inhibitory classes but did not survive correction; the perturbation modality and developmental timing differ from genetic rescue or activity-cleavage studies.

summary: AGRN remains a loss-of-function NMJ disease gene, while this brain Perturb-seq matrix supplies no robust downstream biomarker of AGRN suppression beyond the target transcript itself.
why_it_matters: Any strategy that inhibits extracellular Agrin for a CNS indication would need explicit neuromuscular safety and target-engagement monitoring, because expected disease biology is structural and synaptic, not a large mRNA program in the assayed brain cells.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay muscle, the neuromuscular junction, or Agrin protein; the statement is a safety and biomarker caution rather than efficacy evidence.

summary: Klrk1 perturbation produced no FDR-resolved target or downstream transcriptomic response in any tested brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This converts many scattered nominal rows into a biologically interpretable null: the screen does not support a cell-autonomous Klrk1 program in the assayed glutamatergic or GABAergic cells.
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell counts were modest, no raw expression matrix was available, and the target transcript appears near absent, so failed guide activity cannot be separated from lack of expression.

summary: The null response is concordant with KLRK1 being an NK/T-lineage immunoreceptor rather than a neuronal receptor in the tested brain classes.
why_it_matters: The relevant cell context for KLRK1 biology is immune surveillance; the Perturb-seq result argues against interpreting Klrk1 hits in these brain neurons as direct neuronal signaling events.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay NK cells, cytotoxic T cells, or inflamed brain immune infiltrates.

summary: Klrk1 did not phenocopy broad NKG2D-downstream signaling nodes, while Mapk1 and Rac1 perturbations were capable of yielding FDR-resolved signatures.
why_it_matters: This separates an inactive upstream receptor/adaptor context from general inability of the cells to transcriptionally respond to MAPK- or Rac-linked perturbations.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Mapk1, Rac1, Fyn, Pik3r1, and Cd247 are broad signaling genes rather than NKG2D-specific subunits; Hcst and Tyrobp were not targeted, so the core receptor complex could not be tested directly.

summary: The weak nominal Klrk1 rows failed to form a reproducible cross-cell-type module or stable signature-neighbor neighborhood.
why_it_matters: Top nominal genes such as Gabrg2 or Arfgef1 should not be promoted to pathway biomarkers without independent validation.
main_caveats: The neighbor analysis used only the top 50 Klrk1 genes per cell type and is diagnostic of instability rather than a formal null distribution.

summary: The dataset provides no neuronal transcriptional support for manipulating KLRK1 as a brain-cell-intrinsic disease target.
why_it_matters: KLRK1 has cancer and immune-disease rationale, but those mechanisms should be modeled in NK/T cells or immune-infiltration settings rather than inferred from a quiescent neuronal Perturb-seq signature.

main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA, not extracellular complement cleavage, C3 deposition, or opsonization.

summary: Available complement and innate-immune perturbations did not converge with the Mbl2 signature, and the closest MBL complex and paralog perturbations were largely absent from the library.

main_caveats: Correlation comparisons were restricted to pathway-adjacent targets that were present; the direct MASP and Mbl1 perturbations were unavailable.

summary: The lowest nominal Mbl2 rows were concentrated in a few cortical subclasses but remained below discovery strength.

summary: The screen does not support using basal neuronal Mbl2 transcriptional signatures as biomarkers for anti-MBL therapies in stroke or traumatic brain injury.

main_caveats: The dataset is not a stroke, TBI, infection, endothelial, microglial, or serum-complement assay.

main_caveats: The analysis used RNA score correlations rather than independent replicate-level guide behavior.

summary: Htr2b perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the assayed neuronal panel.

summary: The Htr2b transcript itself did not show an on-target RNA shift.

cell_types: 21 sampled Htr2b neuronal classes

summary: The few Htr2b nominal outliers were isolated cell-type hints rather than a recurrent cell-type program.

main_caveats: Astrocytes, cardiovascular cells, and several rare neuromodulatory populations were not tested by the Htr2b slice of this table.

summary: The absence of a neuronal DE signature should not be interpreted as systemic HTR2B safety.

cell_types: 21 sampled Htr2b neuronal classes
main_caveats: The finding is a translational boundary condition, not evidence that Htr2b perturbation changes cardiac genes in the brain dataset.

summary: The nominal Kif2a response lacked a recurrent microtubule or cytoskeletal transcriptional module.

summary: The weak Kif2a transcriptome should not be read as evidence that reducing KIF2A is benign in neurons.

summary: The negative brain signature should not be read as evidence that GnRHR blockade is biologically inert or free of reproductive-axis liability.

main_caveats: The dataset lacks pituitary gonadotropes and measures RNA rather than ligand-evoked hormone release.

summary: The adult neuronal Acvr2b screen did not reproduce the developmental NODAL/left-right-axis disease program linked to ACVR2B.

summary: High-powered thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic signatures strongly depleted Acsl4 but were buffered against the sterol module and broader downstream differential expression.

summary: ACTG1 disease genetics can coexist with a sparse acute knockdown transcriptome in mouse-brain neurons.

main_caveats: Human disorders are often dominant missense alleles; the dataset is a partial perturbation of Actg1 RNA in mouse cell classes.

summary: Flna upregulation is an exploratory marker of cytoplasmic-actin compensation.

summary: Sparse brain-cell responses after weak perturbation do not demonstrate that CTNNBL1 inhibition would be safe.
why_it_matters: External annotations mark CTNNBL1 as essential and in mRNA splicing while showing no advanced clinical tractability, so the dataset should not be read as systemic-tolerability evidence.

summary: Ctnna3 perturbation produced no measurable Ctnna3 mRNA depletion and no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any of the 22 assayed cell classes.

summary: Nod2 produced no FDR-significant genes and no detectable Nod2 transcript depletion in any profiled neuronal cell class.

summary: Itga9-targeted mouse-brain cells showed no verified depletion of the Itga9 transcript and no FDR-supported downstream DE in any tested cell class.

summary: The apparent Sst GABA enrichment was only nominal, low powered, and not recurrent across cell types.

summary: Itga9 perturbation did not transcriptionally feed back onto the canonical alpha9-beta1 ligand/coreceptor axis.

summary: The ITGB1 partner and other integrin alpha/beta subunit perturbations did not converge with Itga9 at the signature level.

summary: The uninjured brain Perturb-seq result should not be used to infer the direction of ITGA9 activation therapies for injured sensory axons or immune/lymphatic disease.

summary: Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no strong Itga9-like or Itga9-opposite perturbation module.

summary: Only two of the 22 measured Gprasp2 perturbation profiles achieved FDR-confirmed depletion of the Gprasp2 transcript.
