summary: Canonical LXRα/RXR cholesterol-efflux and lipogenic target genes were uncoupled from Nr1h3 perturbation in the Glut/GABA classes.
why_it_matters: ABCA1, ABCG1 and APOE are expected LXR/RXR transcriptional outputs in ligand-responsive cholesterol-export programs, so their flat response argues that these neuronal Perturb-seq profiles did not engage the canonical oxysterol-responsive LXR module.
main_caveats: The experiment perturbed Nr1h3 genetically and did not add an LXR ligand; all assayed Nr1h3 cell classes were neuronal rather than astrocytic or microglial.

summary: The data can reveal a sterol transcriptional module when it is effectively hit: Srebf2, not Nr1h3 or the LXR/RXR-adjacent targets, drove reproducible repression of cholesterol-biosynthesis genes.
why_it_matters: This contrast argues against a dataset-wide inability to detect lipid-metabolic transcriptional responses and localizes the strong sterol signal to Srebf2 rather than to the LXRα/RXR efflux arm in these cells.
main_caveats: Srebf2 is a pathway-neighbor comparison rather than a direct LXR complex member; guide potency differs between target genes.

summary: Global signature-neighbor analysis found no strong Nr1h3-like or Nr1h3-opposing perturbation; the most notable related-target anti-neighbor was an exploratory Rxrg anti-correlation in CA3.
why_it_matters: An RXR paralog would be a plausible LXRα partner, but the full-vector relationship was weak, so Rxrg should not be treated as a validated opposing node for Nr1h3 from this dataset alone.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The maximum related-target correlation was only |r|=0.173 and the underlying Nr1h3 CA3 signature had no FDR<0.10 genes.

summary: The negative neuronal response narrows LXRα-linked CNS disease hypotheses toward glial and ligand-activated states rather than bulk neuronal Nr1h3 loss-of-function markers.
why_it_matters: Prior Alzheimer-model work connected LXRα activation to astrocytic ABCA1/ApoE and microglial Aβ phagocytosis; the present Glut/GABA profiles did not up-regulate Abca1 or Apoe, so Abca1/Apoe remain better glial activation biomarkers than neuronal knockdown readouts in this assay.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks astrocyte, microglia and oligodendrocyte perturbation contexts, so it refines but does not directly test the reported glial mechanism.

summary: Nr1h3 is pharmacologically tractable, but this neuronal CRISPR signature does not nominate an on-target CNS efficacy biomarker.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL records direct LXRα agonist/modulator mechanisms, yet drug-development interpretation should require ligand-responsive ABCA1/APOE or inflammatory readouts in the relevant glial states rather than the flat neuronal Nr1h3 transcriptome seen here.
main_caveats: Genetic knockdown/inhibition is not equivalent to agonism, and the dataset did not assay compound exposure.

summary: Gls target engagement is concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with weaker nominal hints in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA rather than a pan-neuronal knockdown signature.
why_it_matters: GLS is a core glutamine-to-glutamate enzyme, so the screen refines its detectable perturbation response to selected neuronal contexts.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only 155 MB Glut reaches q<0.05; 145 and 191 are low-count nominal rows with FDR=1.0.

summary: Strong or near-strong Gls mRNA depletion produced little FDR-supported downstream transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: The result warns that a metabolic enzyme perturbation can be real at the target transcript yet mostly invisible to conventional downstream scRNA-seq differential-expression thresholds.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA, not glutamate, glutamine, GABA, ammonia, flux, or electrophysiology.

summary: Gls signatures did not converge with Got1, Got2, Glud1, Slc1a2, Gad1, or Gad2 perturbations even where those related targets were engaged.
why_it_matters: Biochemical adjacency in glutamate handling was not enough to make transcriptome-scale perturbation phenotypes interchangeable.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are mRNA-score correlations; flux-level convergence could still exist without a matching transcriptomic signature.

summary: The Gls score vector had no strong positive or negative genome-wide perturbation neighbor in the queried nominally engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: The weak scalar response is not explained by a hidden high-correlation perturbation module elsewhere in the screen.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only four Gls-nominal cell types were searched genome-wide for neighbors; all interpretations are score-vector based.

summary: Human disease genetics and oncology druggability make GLS biologically consequential, but partial neuronal knockdown gives few mRNA biomarkers beyond Gls itself.
why_it_matters: For GLS-targeting strategies, a narrow single-cell transcriptome should not be mistaken for absence of neuronal metabolic or neurotransmitter risk.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset used mouse brain perturbations and did not test systemic GLS inhibitors, chronic human exposure, or metabolite depletion.

summary: Gls mRNA itself is the only robust biomarker of successful Gls perturbation in this dataset.
why_it_matters: The intended transcript is a better guide-performance readout than any downstream panel because no other gene survived q<0.10 in the engaged signatures.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: A self-transcript biomarker confirms mRNA depletion but not enzyme inhibition or glutamate depletion.

summary: Rfx3 targeting produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic response in any tested cell type.
why_it_matters: Known RFX3 loss of function has large ciliary developmental effects, so the null Perturb-seq result is most consistent with inefficient Rfx3 RNA engagement and/or strong context dependence rather than evidence that the gene is dispensable.
main_caveats: The result is a negative transcriptomic result with weak measured target knockdown; it cannot exclude RFX3 function after efficient protein depletion or in unassayed ciliated cells.

summary: The canonical RFX3 cilium program was not detectably induced or repressed by Rfx3 guides.
why_it_matters: RFX3 is expected to control ciliary assembly and motility genes in ciliated contexts; the measured neuronal signatures did not move Foxj1, IFT, BBS, Ttc, Cep, or Hedgehog effector transcripts after correction.
main_caveats: The pathway test used measured transcripts and related perturbations rather than direct cilia phenotypes; Dync2h1 was not measured as an Rfx3 response gene and target engagement was weak.

summary: The experiment largely missed the ciliated ependymal and choroid-plexus compartment in which RFX3-linked hydrocephalus biology is described.
why_it_matters: Failure to see a hydrocephalus or motile-cilium signature is interpretable because the Rfx3 guides were analyzed in Glut/GABA neuronal classes rather than in subcommissural-organ, choroid-plexus, or ventricular-wall ependymal cells.
main_caveats: Cell-type labels were used to infer missing ependymal/choroid coverage; the processed DE file does not contain raw taxonomy metadata beyond group_name.

summary: Rfx3 did not converge with the only screened RFX-family comparator, Rfx7, or with focused ciliary-neighbor perturbations in restricted signature space.
why_it_matters: The weak Rfx3 signature should not be interpreted as a generic RFX-family or ciliary module; true RFX3 heterodimer partners Rfx1, Rfx2, and Rfx6 were not present as perturbations, and Rfx7 behaved nearly orthogonally to Rfx3.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only on the top 100 absolute Rfx3 genes per cell type; both the Rfx3 and Rfx7 signatures lacked corrected hits.

summary: The data provide no support for a therapeutically useful Rfx3 knockdown direction in brain neurons.
why_it_matters: RFX3 is a developmental transcription factor with loss-of-function ciliary and neurodevelopmental liabilities and no obvious ChEMBL target record, so a weak neuronal Perturb-seq profile should be treated as a safety and assay-context warning rather than as a drugging rationale.
main_caveats: No pharmacologic perturbation was tested; the ChEMBL statement is a database search negative, not a complete druggability assessment.

summary: Nr1i2 perturbation lacked convincing target-transcript engagement in the assayed brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: Without detectable repression of the Nr1i2 transcript, most downstream rows should be interpreted as off-target, indirect, or underpowered until validated rather than as a clean PXR loss-of-function program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Target transcript rows were absent rather than measured in 15/22 cell types, and the DE table does not expose raw guide-level counts.

summary: The only FDR-supported Nr1i2 response was a two-gene mixed-direction signature in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA.
why_it_matters: Akr1a1 up-regulation and Nup214 down-regulation should be retained as the only statistically supported readouts, but their specificity to one GABAergic class argues against a broad neuronal PXR program.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The responding cell type did not contain a measurable Nr1i2 row, so the two FDR genes need guide-level or rescue validation.

summary: Canonical xenobiotic-metabolism and transporter effectors were not activated or repressed after Nr1i2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: PXR is normally interpreted through CYP and ABC transporter induction; the absence of these genes separates the brain Perturb-seq signature from the textbook hepatic or intestinal PXR/RXR state.
main_caveats: Loss of a lowly expressed, unliganded receptor in neurons is not equivalent to ligand activation in hepatocytes or enterocytes.

summary: Nr1i2 did not phenocopy RXR-partner, CAR-paralog, or neighboring nuclear-receptor perturbations in the CNU-LGE class where Nr1i2 had FDR hits.
why_it_matters: The Akr1a1/Nup214 signature is unlikely to be a generic RXR-heterodimer or ligand-activated nuclear-receptor response.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: This is a transcriptome-level comparison in a weak Nr1i2 signature; biochemical RXR heterodimerization was not assayed.

summary: Nominal Nr1i2 hits outside CNU-LGE were idiosyncratic and did not define a recurrent multi-cell-type module.
why_it_matters: The many subthreshold top-ranked genes should not be promoted into a pathway story merely because they rank highly in individual small cell classes.
main_caveats: Recurrent weak effects could still be missed if different neuronal classes use nonoverlapping adapters or if powers differ.

summary: Ligandable PXR biology should be interpreted as expression-gated in this neuronal Perturb-seq assay, with Akr1a1 and Nup214 as exploratory internal markers rather than pharmacodynamic PXR biomarkers.
why_it_matters: NR1I2 has a druggable ligand-binding pocket, but this dataset does not support a robust basal neuronal program that could be used as a CNS target-engagement readout.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Open Targets and HPA are human resources, and this mouse dataset used CRISPRi knockdown rather than ligand activation or systemic knockout.

direction: Cpe down in all measured classes; largest logFC in subcortical pineal, midbrain, thalamic, and hypothalamic classes
summary: Cpe knockdown was broad rather than sharply cell-type restricted, with the target transcript itself ranking as the strongest negative feature in all 22 measured neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This validates the Cpe guide across diverse cortical, GABAergic, thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and cerebellar contexts and shows that later negative results are not explained by a single nonresponsive cell type.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: FDR support was absent in five classes despite nominal negative Cpe scores, and the largest Pineal logFC used only 35 perturbed cells.

direction: target transcript down; downstream mRNA response absent after FDR correction
summary: Acute Cpe transcript depletion was buffered at the mRNA level: no non-Cpe gene passed FDR 0.05 in any Cpe block, even in the two classes with Cpe scores below -16.
why_it_matters: CPE biology is centered on secretory-granule sorting and peptide maturation, so a clean single-gene mRNA signature warns that the main consequences of CPE loss may be invisible to endpoint scRNA differential expression.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The assay did not measure neuropeptides, prohormone intermediates, secretion, electrophysiology, or delayed circuit phenotypes.

direction: Cpe-Pcsk2 score correlation near zero; Pcsk5 unengaged
summary: Cpe and the serial prohormone convertase Pcsk2 did not converge transcriptionally in the screened brain cells, while Pcsk5 lacked interpretable on-target engagement.
why_it_matters: Reactome and STRING place CPE and PCSK2 in the same dense-core granule prohormone-processing neighborhood, but the Perturb-seq signatures were orthogonal, consistent with a biochemical pathway whose acute perturbations are not buffered through a shared mRNA program.
main_caveats: Pcsk2 itself was FDR-engaged in only 4 of 20 shared cell classes, and Pcsk5 could not be used as a functional comparator because its transcript was not depleted.

direction: no correlated neighbor; max absolute global r=0.036
summary: The Cpe signature had no strong positive or antagonistic perturbation neighbor anywhere in the 2,046-target library.
why_it_matters: The absence of even a modestly correlated neighbor argues against treating Cpe as a member of a broad transcriptomic stress, secretory, or neuropeptide-response module in this dataset.
main_caveats: The correlation used transcript-level Wilcoxon score vectors; a peptide-level neighbor could be missed.

direction: Cpe loss buffered at mRNA level despite known loss-of-function organismal phenotypes
summary: The loss-of-function transcriptome refines CPE disease biology toward secretory-peptide and long-timescale circuit mechanisms rather than an immediate pan-neuronal mRNA cascade.
why_it_matters: Cpe(fat) mice and humans with biallelic CPE loss have obesity, dysglycemia, and neurodevelopmental or cognitive phenotypes, but the dataset suggests that single-cell RNA is a poor proximal biomarker for those phenotypes after acute neuronal Cpe knockdown.
main_caveats: The screen is mouse brain Perturb-seq with modest perturbed-cell counts; it does not model germline endocrine tissues or chronic whole-organism CPE deficiency.

summary: Folr1 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptional response and no detectable Folr1 transcript shift across the 22 assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: This is the primary result: the dataset should be interpreted as a near-null Folr1 profile rather than a neuronal folate-transport phenotype.
main_caveats: No protein readout; transcript-level nonresponse might miss a protein-level knockout.

summary: Measured folate transport and one-carbon metabolism genes remained unchanged under Folr1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The lack of a Dhfr/Mthfd/Mthfr/Shmt/Mtr/Tyms or transporter response argues against reading the weak nominal hits as a folate-homeostasis program in the sampled neurons.
main_caveats: A transcript panel can miss altered metabolite flux; the Folr1 perturbation itself was weak.

summary: Folr1's few largest nominal hits were split across L4-5 CTX, MEA/LA/CA1/DG, CNU-LGE/LSX, and MH-LH/TH classes without FDR support or recurrence in the best-powered TH and MB glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: This separates isolated near-miss genes from a reproducible cell-type-specific response.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a negative selectivity call; none of the named genes reached conventional adjusted significance.

summary: The neuronal null result is most consistent with FOLR1 cerebral folate disease acting through choroid plexus or developmental contexts that are not represented in this perturbation panel.
why_it_matters: FOLR1 loss causes a severe brain folate disorder, but the Perturb-seq data do not support an acute cell-autonomous transcriptional defect in the sampled neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks choroid plexus and embryonic neural tube lineages and lacks a protein-level FOLR1 knockout assay.

summary: Folr1 did not show strong restricted-signature convergence with a targeted STRING folate neighbor or with any aggregate top signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The negative phenocopy analysis reduces confidence that a hidden Folr1-related pathway was captured by a different perturbation in this dataset.
main_caveats: Signature similarity was restricted to top Folr1 genes; Folr2, Slc19a1, and Slc46a1 were not perturbation targets.

summary: The Folr1 neuronal null profile should not be used to de-risk choroid-plexus folate transport or FOLR1-directed antibody-drug conjugate biology.
why_it_matters: FOLR1 is clinically targetable at the cell surface, but ADC uptake and choroid-plexus transport occur in epithelial contexts outside this mouse neuronal Perturb-seq assay.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq modality is gene knockout, not antibody binding, and choroid plexus cells were not assayed.

summary: Ano3 guide assignment did not produce significant Ano3 mRNA depletion in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: Without clear target knockdown, the dataset should be treated as a weak Ano3 engagement experiment rather than a complete loss-of-function model.
main_caveats: The DE table measures transcript abundance only; it does not report guide editing, baseline Ano3 expression, or protein depletion.

summary: The downstream Ano3 transcriptome was almost entirely buffered, with one FDR-significant gene among 321,616 tested rows.
why_it_matters: A near-empty FDR landscape is compatible with ineffective guide engagement and also with ANO3 acting primarily through membrane lipid or ion-channel physiology rather than broad transcriptional state changes.
main_caveats: Post-transcriptional buffering cannot be separated from weak target knockdown using this summary table alone.

summary: CNU-LGE LSX GABA contained the sole FDR event, Emc3 up-regulation, with a nominal ER and lipid-associated tail.
why_it_matters: Because ANO3 is a TMEM16-family scramblase/channel regulator, Emc3 and neighboring lipid genes are plausible sentinel markers for membrane-protein or lipid stress, but the claim is hypothesis-generating.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Only Emc3 survived FDR control; the stratum had 37 perturbed cells and the ER/lipid annotation is based on nominal genes.

summary: The CNU-LGE LSX GABA Ano3 signature did not phenocopy KCNT1/Slack, SOCE, or GNAL/cAMP dystonia-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues against treating the small Emc3-centered Ano3 response as a generic readout of Slack, SOCE, or striatal cAMP pathway inhibition.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Correlations compare noisy mRNA signatures, while the cited mechanisms are protein, calcium, or electrophysiology mechanisms.

summary: This Perturb-seq result should not be used to infer whether DYT-ANO3 disease requires ANO3 inhibition or activation.
why_it_matters: Human DYT24 is caused by dominant missense ANO3 variants with altered calcium handling; in contrast, the mouse guide experiment showed weak transcript engagement and almost no downstream FDR signal.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks pathogenic ANO3 alleles, ORAI1 protein data, calcium flux, and electrophysiology.

summary: Drd5 perturbation did not produce a detected Drd5 transcript decrease or any FDR-significant downstream gene in the sampled brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The primary interpretation is absence of a robust transcriptional phenotype under the measured conditions, not evidence for a specific D5-receptor effector program.
main_caveats: CRISPR coding perturbations can alter protein without lowering the captured mRNA; the strongest statement is that the transcriptomic readout lacked target-transcript validation and FDR-significant DE.

summary: The closest nominal Drd5 signals were restricted to CTX-CGE GABA, MH-LH/TH glutamatergic, and MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic classes, but none survived FDR and the MB Dopa class lacked a Drd5 contrast.
why_it_matters: These weak minima should be treated as locations to remeasure with better engagement rather than as confirmed D5-responsive cell types.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Based on minimum adjusted p values that all exceeded 0.05; the dopaminergic MB class is a coverage gap, not a measured negative.

summary: Drd5 perturbation was not transcriptionally coupled to dopamine-receptor or Gs/olf-adenylyl-cyclase pathway neighbors at baseline.
why_it_matters: Although DRD5 is a D1-like GPCR linked to adenylyl cyclase and phospholipase-C signaling, individual perturbation of Drd5 did not phenocopy available receptor paralogs or immediate cAMP regulators in any shared cell type.
main_caveats: Absence of correlated whole-transcriptome output is indirect for fast GPCR second-messenger biology; Drd1 and several downstream dopaminergic markers were not available as perturbations.

summary: An all-perturbation search did not reveal a strong positive or negative Drd5 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak Drd5 response cannot be rescued by assigning it to another transcriptional module; even the best same-cell-type whole-genome correlation was only r=0.1349.
main_caveats: Restricted to Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors; very weak correlations may be dominated by noise.

summary: This Drd5 Perturb-seq profile is not directionally informative for DRD5 pharmacology or disease indications despite the receptor being druggable and clinically contextualized.
why_it_matters: DRD5 has small-molecule mechanisms and disease links, and germline D5 loss has physiological and behavioral consequences, but a profile with weak target engagement, no FDR hits, no strong neighbors, and no MB Dopa contrast should not be used to nominate agonist, antagonist, or biomarker direction.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The warning is about this transcriptional dataset, not about absence of DRD5 biology; drug records are not evidence that a compound is D5-selective.

direction: strongest in thalamic and midbrain classes; absent or minimal in many cortical and GABAergic classes
summary: Phf12 produced a sharply selective subcortical response, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut rather than by cortical IT or broad GABAergic classes.
why_it_matters: The phenotype is not a uniform consequence of losing a chromatin corepressor; a small set of thalamic/midbrain/hypothalamic classes carries most of the detectable transcriptional burden.

main_caveats: FDR gene counts are influenced by cell number; the 217 P MY Pineal Glut response is based on only 37 perturbation cells.

summary: Responsive Phf12 cell types repeatedly induced a compact Ptcd3/Chpf2/Atp6v0b/Stx16/Sf3b2/Stk16 module, with spliceosome and ribonucleoprotein genes enriched among the strongest thalamic up-regulated genes.
why_it_matters: Recurrence across excitatory and inhibitory subcortical classes distinguishes this from isolated noisy top genes and points to a shared RNA-processing/organellar maintenance response downstream of Phf12 perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Many recurrent genes encode general RNA-processing or organellar proteins; the dataset does not prove they are direct PHF12 targets.

direction: mixed: RNA-processing up, neuronal/synaptic genes down
summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, the induced spliceosome/RNP program was coupled to repression of synaptic, glutamatergic and neuronal-projection genes such as Gls, Syt7, Grin2c, Snap25 and Tubb3.
why_it_matters: A PHF12 loss-like perturbation can downshift neuronal effector genes while upshifting RNA-processing genes, so the response cannot be summarized as simple de-repression by loss of a transcriptional repressor.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The down-regulated synaptic genes are probably indirect components of the endpoint state; the Wilcoxon table lacks chromatin occupancy or nascent-transcription data.

direction: Gatad1 concordant; Sin3a near-zero to weakly discordant
summary: The Phf12 signature converged with Gatad1 but was uncoupled from Sin3a, even though PHF12 is a SIN3-associated subunit.
why_it_matters: The closest phenotypic neighbor in the screened brain cells was not the canonical SIN3A scaffold; this argues that PHF12 perturbation resolves only selected chromatin protein relationships in this cellular context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: GATAD1 is supported here by STRING functional association and transcriptomic convergence, not by a proven PHF12-GATAD1 biochemical complex in these neurons.

summary: Several adequately sampled Phf12 contrasts, including L4/5 IT cortical excitatory, CTX-CGE GABA and Pvalb GABA, were largely buffered at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The zero or near-zero rows provide biologically useful negatives: absence of a detected response was not confined to cell types with only a few edited cells.
comparators: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Because Phf12 RNA itself was not depleted, a no-DE result could indicate either biological buffering or inefficient editing in that cell type.

direction: PHF12 loss-of-function genetics aligned to Phf12-restricted mouse neuronal signatures
summary: For an ASD/NDD risk gene, the Phf12 perturbation emphasizes subcortical neuronal vulnerability and synapse/RNA-processing axes rather than a pan-cortical signature.
why_it_matters: The mouse-brain signature nominates cellular contexts and readouts that could be followed when interpreting human PHF12 loss-of-function genetics.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Human ASD evidence is genetic and organismal, whereas these observations are mouse single-cell transcriptomic endpoints with no behavioral or developmental phenotyping.

direction: Atp6v1b2 down with a mixed downstream Pvalb signature
summary: Atp6v1b2 loss produced a genome-wide FDR-resolved response only in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: ATP6V1B2 is a core proton-pump subunit with broad expected endolysosomal and synaptic-vesicle roles, but the dataset localizes the clearest loss-of-transcript consequence to Pvalb inhibitory neurons.

summary: Several non-Pvalb classes showed nominal Atp6v1b2 depletion but no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The result separates target-transcript engagement from overt transcriptional remodeling and argues that absence of an FDR signature is not always identical to absence of guide activity.
