main_caveats: No non-Pvalb target row was FDR-significant after whole-transcriptome correction, and 22-31 perturbed cells in three of the four classes limits power.

direction: canonical transcripts mostly unchanged at FDR level
summary: The Pvalb response was not a transcriptional induction of measured V-ATPase, Ragulator-mTORC1, or TFEB/MITF lysosome-biogenesis genes.
why_it_matters: V-ATPase is embedded in lysosomal acidification, amino-acid sensing, and autophagy biology; the dataset instead highlights a compact neuronal/secretory and stress-response mRNA signature.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The absence of mRNA changes does not test V-ATPase assembly, pump activity, lysosomal pH, autophagic flux, mTORC1 phosphorylation, or TFEB localization.

summary: Atp6v1b2 weakly converged with the V0 subunit Atp6v0c in Pvalb neurons, but Atp6v0c was much stronger and the complex members were not transcriptional phenocopies.
why_it_matters: A shared V-ATPase complex membership would predict related consequences, yet the whole-transcriptome similarity was modest; disease-family subunits should therefore not be treated as interchangeable perturbations in this cell class.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The comparison used score-vector correlations from one cell class; Atp6v1b2 had fewer perturbed cells than Atp6v0c and the full-transcriptome correlation is diluted by many genes with no response.

summary: Hcn3, Dusp1, Gadd45g, Scg2, Slc6a17, Ptprn, Lpcat1, and Serpini1 form a candidate Pvalb Atp6v1b2-response panel.
why_it_matters: These FDR-significant genes capture the dominant measured Pvalb signature and provide a more actionable readout than grouping all genes under a generic lysosome label.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The panel is based on one Perturb-seq cell class; the individual genes are biomarkers of the measured response, not proven mediators of V-ATPase dysfunction or seizures.

summary: Cacna2d2 perturbation was FDR-silent across the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The primary result is a genome-wide negative result: downstream mechanistic interpretation should not be based on the nominal rank tails as if they were a robust transcriptional program.
main_caveats: The absence of FDR hits may reflect weak guide engagement, low mRNA sensitivity for a membrane channel subunit, protein perdurance, or true buffering; the dataset is transcriptomic and does not measure channel current.

summary: The two clearest nominal Cacna2d2 self-depletion events occurred in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, yet each remained FDR-silent outside the target row.
why_it_matters: This separates possible on-target mRNA depletion from a lack of resolved secondary response, suggesting that alpha2delta-2 reduction in these inhibitory contexts is either buffered or not well captured by mRNA ranks.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The Cacna2d2 self rows were not significant after multiple testing, and the GABAergic literature is from curated annotations and cultured mouse neurons rather than the exact adult brain classes assayed here.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Cacna2d2 failed where several assayed voltage-gated calcium-channel partners produced strong on-target signals.
why_it_matters: The thalamic contrast argues against a blanket inability of the experiment to detect calcium-channel perturbations; the Cacna2d2 outcome is target-specific within a complex whose pore-forming and beta-subunit members were measurable.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only one cell class is used for this contrast; the strongest interpretation is about target engagement and transcriptomic detectability, not alpha2delta-2 biochemical dispensability.

summary: Cacna2d2 had no strong positive or negative full-signature neighbors, including among calcium-channel subunit perturbations.
why_it_matters: If the weak Cacna2d2 ranks contained a reproducible CaV-like program, related perturbations should have correlated; the near-zero correlations make the nominal tails inappropriate for pathway discovery.
main_caveats: Correlations used Wilcoxon-score vectors rather than raw expression and may miss nonlinear or post-transcriptional convergence.

summary: The FDR-silent mRNA phenotype should not be read as evidence that CACNA2D2 is biologically or clinically inert.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic CACNA2D2 disease and mouse Cacna2d2 loss-of-function phenotypes show that alpha2delta-2 biology is electrophysiological, developmental, and cerebellar; a Perturb-seq mRNA scalar would under-rank that channelopathy and could miss drug-safety liabilities.
main_caveats: The dataset did not demonstrate FDR-significant Cacna2d2 mRNA knockdown and does not measure chronic development, Purkinje-cell physiology, seizures, ataxia, or drug binding.

summary: Hsf1 loss most strongly suppressed a compact heat-shock chaperone module containing Hsph1, Hsp90aa1, Hsp90ab1, Ahsa2, and Stip1.
why_it_matters: The leading dataset response is the expected transcriptional arm of HSF1 rather than a broad, unspecific neuronal stress program, supporting that the perturbation reached a canonical HSF1 output even when the Hsf1 transcript itself was not FDR-significant.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The direct Hsf1 transcript row was nominal but not FDR-significant in every cell type; the assay measures basal neuronal mRNA rather than induced heat shock.

direction: FDR-supported response restricted to a minority of cell types
summary: Only four of twenty-two Hsf1-perturbed brain cell-type groups produced any FDR-significant differentially expressed genes.
why_it_matters: Basal HSF1 transcriptional output in this Perturb-seq experiment is strongly gated by cellular context; apparent negative groups should not be pooled with the strongly responsive thalamic, midbrain, Pvalb, and hypothalamic groups.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type sample sizes were unequal and several non-FDR cell types had only tens of perturbed cells.

summary: Several GABAergic groups carried the expected Hsf1/Hsph1/Stip1 decrease only as nominal signal, indicating buffering or underpowered detection rather than a clean absence of biology.
why_it_matters: The 191 MB P MY GABA and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA signatures would be missed by a strict FDR-only summary even though their top genes align with the HSF1 module.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Nominal p values did not survive multiple testing, so these are moderate-confidence buffered responses rather than definitive cell-type hits.

summary: Rsrp1 emerged as a recurrent non-HSP marker of Hsf1 perturbation in neurons.
why_it_matters: Rsrp1 was FDR-significant in the three strongest multi-gene Hsf1 signatures and was down in every Hsf1 cell type, making it a useful transcriptomic sentinel even though its mechanistic placement downstream of HSF1 is unknown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The report found no direct HSF1-Rsrp1 literature grounding; this is a dataset biomarker hypothesis, not a curated pathway assignment.

direction: non-phenocopying; weak HSP increases after Hsp90ab1 loss versus decreases after Hsf1 loss
summary: Direct Hsp90ab1 knockdown did not phenocopy Hsf1 knockdown despite Hsp90ab1 being an HSF1-responsive transcript.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates an upstream transcription-factor perturbation from loss of one downstream chaperone and is consistent with feedback in which HSP90 complexes restrain HSF1 activity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The Hsp90ab1 feedback response was weak and not FDR-significant for most HSP transcripts; the contrast is transcriptomic, not a direct HSF1-activity assay.

summary: The Hsf4 paralog was not interchangeable with Hsf1 in the assayed brain cell types.
why_it_matters: Even though HSF proteins share heat-shock-element biology, Hsf4 perturbation yielded no FDR-supported HSF1-like chaperone signature, fitting HSF4's more tissue-specialized developmental role.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Hsf4 target-transcript knockdown itself was weak and not FDR-significant, so absence of a phenotype cannot be separated fully from limited Hsf4 engagement.

summary: Hsf1 perturbation did not produce FDR-level regulation of Hspa5, Hspa9, or Hspd1.
why_it_matters: The most reproducible signal stayed within the Hsph1/Hsp90 branch rather than collapsing all measured chaperone systems, a useful negative result for annotating the perturbation as a selective basal HSF1 output.
main_caveats: This negative result is transcript-specific and basal; it does not rule out regulation of these genes under heat shock or other stresses.

direction: loss of chaperone transcripts after Hsf1 loss
summary: The neuronal Hsf1 loss signature points in the direction of reduced proteostasis capacity, not a compensatory chaperone induction.
why_it_matters: Because experimental HSF1 can support neuronal survival in stress contexts, the dataset argues that sustained HSF1 inhibition in neurons could lower HSPH1/HSP90/STIP1 support unless cells mount a separate stress-induced rescue program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The cells were not challenged with a proteotoxic disease stress and the dataset did not measure survival, so this is a directional warning rather than a demonstrated toxicity phenotype.

summary: Cxcr2 perturbation did not produce measurable target knockdown or any FDR-significant mature-neuronal transcriptional effect.
why_it_matters: This prevents the dataset from being read as a Cxcr2 loss-of-function map; the best interpretation is that the receptor was weakly expressed, weakly engaged, or both in the assayed basal neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The parquet contains DE summaries but not raw Cxcr2 detection rates or guide identities, so sparse target expression and guide inefficacy cannot be separated.

summary: The lowest Cxcr2 nominal p values were isolated, not a recurrent downstream module.
why_it_matters: Tatdn1 in hippocampal/amygdalar glutamatergic cells, Anapc5 in L5 extratelencephalic cells, and Papss1/Ywhaq in pineal glutamatergic cells mark possible local responses, but the lack of recurrence and FDR support argues for a buffered or noisy basal response.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: All named genes are nominal; none passed FDR<0.05 and the 217 P MY Pineal Glut signal used only 28 perturbed cells.

summary: Cxcr2 signatures were nearly orthogonal to chemokine receptors and canonical inflammatory signaling perturbations in the same cell classes.
why_it_matters: CXCR2 is normally interpreted through CXC-ligand, G-protein, PI3K/MAPK/Rac, and inflammatory pathways; the perturbation did not phenocopy Cxcr4, Ccr2/Ccr5/Cx3cr1, TLR/interleukin receptors, or Mapk1/Akt3/NF-kB neighbors in basal neurons.
main_caveats: Several receptor comparators also had weak self-transcript engagement, so the comparison mainly shows absence of a shared basal transcriptomic program in this dataset.

summary: The screen favors an immune, vascular, or glial reading of CXCR2 disease biology rather than a mature-neuron-autonomous effect.
why_it_matters: CXCR2 is druggable and linked to inflammatory diseases, and CNS papers implicate endothelial recruitment or oligodendrocyte-lineage contexts; the mature neuronal subclasses here did not show a significant autonomous response to Cxcr2 targeting.
main_caveats: This dataset lacks endothelial, neutrophil, oligodendrocyte precursor, and inflammatory ligand-stimulation conditions where CXCR2 biology is expected to be strongest.

summary: The cerebellar GABA Cxcr2 profile showed an exploratory anti-correlation to Akt3 rather than a canonical same-direction PI3K/Akt relationship.
why_it_matters: Akt3 was the strongest related negative neighbor in 308 CB GABA, so even the largest pathway-adjacent scalar pointed to uncoupling rather than clean canonical CXCR2 signaling.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Cxcr2 itself was not in the 308 CB GABA target-transcript rows and none of the cerebellar GABA Cxcr2 DE rows passed FDR.

summary: Top restricted signature neighbors were unstable and should not be promoted to Cxcr2 biology.
why_it_matters: Safe-target controls and singletons appeared among the highest restricted correlations, indicating that top-neighbor scans on a 50-gene nominal signature can overfit the weak Cxcr2 pattern.
main_caveats: This is a scalar-signature quality-control finding; it does not test physical interaction or pathway membership.

summary: Lrrfip1 targeting produced no FDR-significant gene-level response in any of the 21 profiled mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The screen provides little support for a broad cell-autonomous Lrrfip1 transcriptional program under its basal assay conditions, even though LRRFIP1 is annotated as a transcriptional and innate-signaling regulator.
main_caveats: Target mRNA knockdown was weak and never FDR-significant, so a coding edit could be ineffective or its mRNA change could underestimate protein perturbation.

summary: Nominal loss of the Lrrfip1 transcript was concentrated in a few glutamatergic classes rather than being shared across all neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The modest on-target signal was not pan-neuronal and therefore should not be pooled as one uniform brain response; this also makes direct comparison with ischemic rat brain work context-dependent.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The four cell types were identified by nominal target-gene p values only; no cell type had an FDR-significant Lrrfip1 row or a reproducible downstream module.

summary: The perturbation did not activate or repress a detectable IFN/TNF/NF-kappaB marker program.
why_it_matters: LRRFIP1 can couple cytosolic nucleic acids and TLR regulation to IFN-beta and TNF biology, but that role appears stimulus- and context-dependent rather than constitutive in these mostly neuronal basal profiles.
main_caveats: The assay was not a dsDNA, dsRNA, LPS, or infection challenge and the target transcript was weakly depleted; cytokine secretion and phospho-signaling were not measured.

summary: Lrrfip1 did not phenocopy beta-catenin/Wnt or innate nucleic-acid-signaling neighbors that were present in the same Perturb-seq compendium.
why_it_matters: Reactome and STRING connect LRRFIP1 to CTNNB1, IRF3, DHX9, and TLR-associated partners, but the available single-gene perturbations were transcriptomically divergent, arguing against a shared basal neuronal axis in this dataset.
main_caveats: The direct partner Flii and the paralog Lrrfip2 were not available as perturbations, and correlations can be deflated by weak Lrrfip1 perturbation.

summary: An unbiased scan did not recover a strong positive or negative Lrrfip1 signature-neighbor module.
why_it_matters: The weak global and per-cell correlations make the nominal Lrrfip1 genes difficult to convert into a new pathway hypothesis.
main_caveats: The neighbor scan used Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors and should be interpreted as exploratory signature geometry, not as a formal pathway-enrichment test.

summary: The screen gives no positive neuronal-efficacy signal to offset the sparse LRRFIP1 druggability and disease-evidence base.
why_it_matters: Before LRRFIP1 is treated as a brain-therapeutic target, stronger target engagement and a challenged innate-immune or ischemic model are needed; the existing drug databases do not indicate a mature LRRFIP1 pharmacology.
main_caveats: Open Targets and ChEMBL do not prove the target is undruggable, and a negative basal transcriptome cannot test secreted IFN/TNF, injury responses, or protein-level beta-catenin signaling.

summary: Nrg1 perturbation did not detectably reduce the assayed Nrg1 transcript in any of 21 cell types.
why_it_matters: Weak self-transcript engagement is the primary caveat for interpreting downstream Nrg1 effects.
main_caveats: mRNA self-depletion is an imperfect proxy for editing of NRG1 protein isoforms.

summary: Nrg1 loss produced almost no FDR-significant or recurrent steady-state RNA response.
why_it_matters: This argues against a robust cell-autonomous ERBB-to-transcriptome module after the observed Nrg1 perturbation, despite curated ERBB/PI3K/MAPK pathway membership.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The interpretation is constrained by weak target engagement and by the fact that ERBB signaling may be post-transcriptional.

summary: The only FDR-significant Nrg1-associated row was Top1 up in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: Any positive Nrg1 signal is narrowly localized and exploratory rather than a broad brain-cell response.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The cell type had only 37 perturbed cells, the next row had FDR=0.185, and Top1 did not recur in other cell types.

summary: Erbb4, but not Nrg1, showed significant self-transcript depletion in inhibitory Pvalb and CTX-CGE classes.
why_it_matters: The comparator result matches the literature-expected GABA/PV ERBB4 axis and shows that the receptor limb is more detectable than the ligand limb in this dataset.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Comparison uses broad taxonomy labels rather than purified PV subtypes; Erbb4 produced self-transcript hits with little additional FDR-significant RNA output.

summary: Nrg3 self-depletion was detectable in selected cell types, but Nrg1 did not phenocopy Nrg3 or other NRG/ERBB family perturbations.
why_it_matters: Known ERBB ligand relationships do not translate into interchangeable single-cell signatures in this screen.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Part of the divergence may reflect different transcript abundance, guide efficacy, and perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Nrg1 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor anywhere in the perturbation library.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpreting isolated nominal Nrg1 genes as a hidden disease or pathway-like module.
main_caveats: The correlation analysis used steady-state Wilcoxon score vectors and can miss non-transcriptional convergence.

summary: The Nrg1 negative signature is not a directional argument for pan-NRG1 inhibition or activation.
why_it_matters: NRG1/ERBB biology is clinically interesting but region- and interneuron-subtype-dependent; this weakly engaged screen should not be used alone for therapeutic direction.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks a robust Nrg1 loss-of-function transcriptional signature and does not assay VIP or PV interneuron subtypes directly.

summary: Katnip perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptional response in any of 22 assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: KATNIP is a ciliary basal-body and Joubert-syndrome gene, so the absence of a robust mRNA response argues that this Perturb-seq experiment should not be read as a successful neuronal loss-of-function phenocopy of KATNIP ciliopathy.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The Katnip transcript was absent from the response-gene matrix, so on-target depletion could not be measured; 18 of 22 signatures had fewer than 100 Katnip-targeted cells.

summary: The only Katnip cell class with near-threshold outliers was 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and even that hippocampal signature stopped at FDR=0.1166 for Man1b1 and Wnk2.
why_it_matters: This preserves the strongest localized signal without promoting it to a pathway claim; it is a hypothesis-generating CA3/CA2/dentate-glutamatergic tendency rather than a significant Katnip program.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: No gene reached FDR<0.05, the nearest positive signature neighbor was only r=0.238, and the genes do not define a known KATNIP mechanism.

summary: Katnip perturbation did not transcriptionally recruit the expected ciliary, CILK1, or katanin neighborhood.
why_it_matters: Published work places KATNIP at the ciliary base as a microtubule/katanin and CILK1 regulatory scaffold; the dataset instead shows no FDR-supported shifts among measured ciliary and katanin readouts, pointing to a structural or post-translational biology that is invisible to this mRNA endpoint.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The curated readout list was restricted to genes measured in the matrix; the Perturb-seq assay does not measure cilia number, axonemal ultrastructure, CILK1 phosphorylation, or protein localization.

summary: Other ciliary/Joubert perturbations in the library did not phenocopy Katnip, and Ahi1 showed a self-limited on-target response rather than a broad disease-family module.
why_it_matters: A shared Joubert or primary-cilium label was not sufficient to create a shared acute neuronal transcriptomic state: Katnip correlated almost zero with Ahi1, Cep290, and Tbc1d32 signatures, while the one decisive comparator effect was depletion of Ahi1 itself in midbrain glutamatergic cells.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only Ahi1, Cep290, and Tbc1d32 were used for whole-transcriptome disease-family correlations; Katnip target engagement itself remains unmeasured.

direction: Foxk2 transcript down; no adjusted-significant downstream response
summary: Foxk2 targeting was directionally on-target across all assayed cell types but produced no adjusted-significant transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: A consistent drop in the target transcript argues that the perturbation was not random, while 0 adjusted-significant rows mean the main biological result is weak or buffered rather than a large FOXK2-dependent gene-expression program.
main_caveats: Adjusted P values never passed 0.05; mRNA depletion is an imperfect readout of CRISPR protein loss.

summary: Foxk2 mRNA engagement was strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only nominal in a subset of other neuronal classes, while several well-sampled classes showed little target-transcript change.
why_it_matters: Downstream Foxk2 interpretation should be restricted to classes with measurable target engagement; the pattern refines the broad public brain-expression annotation into an assay-specific engagement map.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The cell-type pattern could reflect editing efficiency, transcript detection, or power rather than true FOXK2 biology.

summary: Foxk2 perturbation did not de-repress the canonical macroautophagy program expected from FOXK/SIN3A-HDAC studies.
why_it_matters: The result suggests that steady-state mouse-brain neurons do not automatically convert Foxk2 loss into ATG/ULK/BECN1/LC3 transcriptional activation, sharpening the context in which FOXK proteins regulate autophagy.
main_caveats: Autophagy genes were tested at the mRNA level only; the assay was not starvation- or insulin-stimulated, and individual ATG rows were nominal at best.

summary: Foxk2 signatures remained near-orthogonal to available SIN3A/BAP1 chromatin and mTOR/TSC pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: Physical interaction or pathway proximity did not translate into matching whole-transcriptome phenotypes in this neuronal Perturb-seq atlas, arguing against a strong shared FOXK2 module under the assayed conditions.
main_caveats: Correlation uses weak single-perturbation signatures; the closest FOXK paralog Foxk1 was absent from the screen.

direction: no strong positive or negative neighbor
summary: A screen-wide signature-neighbor search found no robust perturbation phenocopy for Foxk2.
why_it_matters: The lack of any |r|>=0.2 neighbor prevents overinterpretation of specific positive or negative comparators and frames Foxk2 as a weak, idiosyncratic signature in this dataset.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Uses global Pearson correlations on Wilcoxon-score vectors; a weak linear correlation does not exclude local pathway overlap.

summary: Alk guide assignment did not measurably deplete Alk mRNA and produced no FDR-significant transcriptome-wide response in any measured cell class.
why_it_matters: A receptor tyrosine kinase with known neuronal roles was present in the Perturb-seq design, but this dataset does not provide a strong loss-of-function Alk signature to interpret mechanistically.
main_caveats: The negative call is at the mRNA differential-expression level; guide editing, protein abundance, and kinase activity were not measured.

summary: The expected hypothalamic Alk energy-homeostasis biology was not recovered in the two explicit HY-labeled classes.
why_it_matters: Mouse Alk has been linked to hypothalamic control of energy expenditure, so the absence of FDR-level responses in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut argues that the present broad classes and perturbation readout do not resolve that physiology.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The HY labels are broad and may not contain the specific hypothalamic neurons or physiological state used in the published thinness experiments; 145 MH-LH TH is thalamic/habenular rather than explicitly HY; leading Pvalb and TH genes were nominal only.

summary: Alk perturbation did not resemble perturbation of canonical RTK/RAS/PI3K pathway neighbors.
why_it_matters: ALK can signal through MAPK, PI3K, IRS, PLCγ, and related adapter modules, but the measured Alk score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with assayed neighboring RTKs and downstream nodes, making canonical pathway directionality uninterpretable here.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed at the transcriptomic-signature level; Ltk and ALKAL ligand perturbations were absent; the result cannot exclude biochemical ALK signaling in cell states not captured or in cells with poor Alk guide activity.

summary: The weak Alk phenotype is not explained by a universal inability of this assay to detect RTK/MAPK-axis perturbations in neurons.
why_it_matters: Ntrk2 and Mapk1 showed FDR-level target engagement or downstream responses in several cell classes where Alk remained silent, pointing to Alk-specific guide expression, target-expression, or context limitations rather than a blanket loss of sensitivity for receptor-kinase signaling genes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Ntrk2 and Mapk1 are pathway-context comparators, not ALK complex members; their stronger signatures do not identify the specific reason for weak Alk engagement.

summary: The only appreciable Alk signature-neighbor structure was an exploratory cerebellar GABA module, not an ALK-pathway module.
why_it_matters: Among all non-self perturbations, 308 CB GABA Alk was most correlated with Wdr26 and most anti-correlated with Fbxo11, highlighting a possible cell-restricted transcriptional state comparison but also showing that the strongest neighbors were not canonical Alk partners.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Alk itself had no target engagement or FDR-significant genes in 308 CB GABA, so this is a weak signature-neighbor observation only.

summary: This wild-type mouse-brain Alk loss-of-function profile should not be used as a proxy for ALK-addicted cancer pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Clinical ALK dependencies usually arise from activating alterations that constitutively engage ALK kinase signaling, whereas the dataset measured weak native Alk perturbations in neuronal cell classes and lacked a canonical RTK response.
main_caveats: The warning concerns extrapolation from this dataset; it does not question ALK as a validated cancer drug target.

summary: Htr4 loss of function yielded an essentially null single-cell transcriptomic phenotype: the target transcript was assayed in 23 broad cell types, but neither Htr4 itself nor any downstream gene reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: HTR4 is a canonical Gs-coupled serotonin receptor, so the absence of target knockdown and downstream FDR hits makes this perturbation unsuitable as a direct readout of 5-HT4R signaling in the sampled steady-state transcriptomes.
main_caveats: High confidence for the dataset-level null result, but it may reflect weak CRISPR engagement, low receptor mRNA capture, or an acute signaling endpoint not represented in steady-state RNA.

summary: Atxn7l1, Slitrk1, Slc6a6, and other high-score genes are only exploratory Htr4 biomarker candidates because the strongest nominal cell-type signals still failed FDR correction.
why_it_matters: The largest absolute Wilcoxon scores concentrate in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, but their adjusted p values of 0.305-0.506 argue against interpreting these genes as validated Htr4-response markers.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative biomarker finding; the named genes are retained only to document why the top nominal scores were not promoted to mechanistic hits.

summary: The expected basal-ganglia/GABAergic context for 5-HT4R did not emerge as a robust Htr4-responsive compartment in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Prior brain literature emphasizes high 5-HT4 receptor density in basal ganglia and a D2 striatopallidal mouse mechanism, yet the broad CNU-MGE, CNU-LGE/LSX, and CNU-HYa/HY GABA classes showed no target engagement and no FDR-significant response.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The assayed classes are coarse and have 49-71 Htr4-perturbed cells, so a rare D2 medium-spiny-neuron subpopulation or ligand-evoked response could be diluted.

summary: Htr4 did not align with the shared HTR4/HTR6/HTR7 Gs-serotonin pathway or with assayed Gs/cAMP neighbors.
why_it_matters: Reactome groups HTR4, HTR6, and HTR7 as serotonin receptors feeding G alpha(s) signaling, but Htr4-Htr6 and Htr4-Htr7 correlations were near zero, all three receptor perturbations had zero FDR hits, and broader Htr4 correlations to Gnas, Adcy3, Adcy5, Prkaca, and Pde4d were also negligible.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and CRISPR-based; receptor mRNAs all had weak self-depletion, so the result is better read as absence of a detectable module than evidence that these receptors cannot converge biochemically.

summary: The perturbation is directionally uninformative for HTR4 agonist or antagonist development despite strong druggability of the human receptor.
why_it_matters: HTR4 has approved small-molecule agonist mechanisms, including prucalopride, and Open Targets lists HTR4 as small-molecule tractable with clinical candidates; the mouse Htr4 loss-of-function transcriptome provides no FDR-supported biomarker or disease-direction signature to extrapolate to CNS 5-HT4R pharmacology.
main_caveats: This warning does not challenge acute pharmacology or peripheral gastrointestinal efficacy; it only limits interpretation of this particular CRISPR transcriptomic readout.

summary: Acvr2a perturbation was globally weak and produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any measured brain cell class.
why_it_matters: ACVR2A is a ligand-gated receptor expected to feed SMAD transcription, so the dataset argues that basal receptor knockdown alone was insufficient to trigger a robust cell-autonomous transcriptional state in these classes.
main_caveats: Weak on-target FDR support and low perturbed-cell counts in many classes mean complete loss of ACVR2A signaling was not demonstrated.

summary: 308 CB GABA was the clearest Acvr2a-engaged class, but even there the response stopped at nominal self-depletion.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from pathway activation: the class with the best Acvr2a transcript loss still did not show a multiple-testing-significant SMAD or stress program.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only 36 perturbed cells; Acvr2a itself had FDR=1.0, so this is rank/nominal evidence rather than a robust DE call.

summary: A small cortical/limbic excitatory subset also showed nominal Acvr2a self-depletion, without downstream FDR hits.
why_it_matters: The nominal signal was not confined to one lineage, but it was restricted to a few glutamatergic classes and did not rise to pathway-level significance.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Each class had only 26-28 perturbed cells and no gene passed FDR correction.

summary: Acvr2a did not phenocopy Acvr2b or other TGF-beta-family receptor perturbations in the engaged 308 CB GABA signature.
why_it_matters: Pathway diagrams allow ACVR2A and ACVR2B to substitute as type-II receptors, but the dataset found no coherent paralog or receptor-neighbor transcriptomic convergence.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The contrast uses weak individual signatures and transcriptome correlations; absence of phenocopy may reflect incomplete knockdown or missing ligand stimulation.

summary: A 308 CB GABA signature-neighbor search found no strong positive or inverse Acvr2a module.
why_it_matters: Because the top correlations were small and top-rank overlaps were below 10%, the most similar perturbations should not be treated as a convergent biological pathway.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Calculated only for 308 CB GABA, the class with the strongest Acvr2a transcript depletion.

summary: ACVR2A-Fc ligand traps should not be interpreted as equivalent to neuronal Acvr2a transcript knockdown.
why_it_matters: Approved sotatercept sequesters activin A and other TGF-beta-family ligands to rebalance vascular ActRIIA/SMAD2/3 and BMPRII/SMAD1/5/8 signaling, whereas the dataset measured cell-autonomous receptor-gene perturbation and showed little basal brain response.
main_caveats: The dataset does not assay PAH vascular cells, ligand traps, or circulating ligand pharmacology.

direction: no target-transcript depletion; no FDR-supported response
summary: Il6ra was not productively target-engaged in any Il6ra-tested neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The most direct interpretation is a failed or low-expressed receptor perturbation rather than a bona fide IL6RA loss-of-function transcriptional null.
cell_types: 22 Il6ra-tested Glut/GABA neuronal classes
main_caveats: The DE table reports transcript-level Wilcoxon statistics only; the raw guide identities and baseline Il6ra expression are unavailable.

direction: no FDR-supported change among curated pathway transcripts
summary: Il6ra perturbation did not recruit an IL-6/JAK/STAT/MAPK transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: IL6RA requires IL6ST/gp130 and ligand-dependent receptor assembly, so the absence of downstream STAT, MAPK, SOCS, and PI3K gene changes is expected if membrane Il6ra is low and the pathway is not acutely stimulated.
cell_types: 22 Il6ra-tested Glut/GABA neuronal classes
main_caveats: Expression of pathway genes was inspected at the RNA level; phosphorylation or ligand-induced pathway activity was not measured.

direction: weak CB GABA-skewed signal with Rtn4 down
summary: The apparent 308 CB GABA response is a weak, Rtn4-led tail rather than a resolved cerebellar IL-6 module.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only cell-type-skewed signal while preventing an isolated FDR 0.059 hit and modest 308-restricted signature correlations from being overcalled as pathway activation.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: No gene reached FDR<0.05; all top signature neighbors were modest and confined to the same cell type, and a Safe_target perturbation was among the strongest anti-neighbors.

summary: Il6ra, Il6st, Osmr, and Stat3 did not phenocopy one another despite belonging to the gp130 cytokine signaling neighborhood.
why_it_matters: Shared receptor membership in Reactome does not imply interchangeable basal Perturb-seq signatures in neuronal classes; in this screen the receptor-family perturbations were all weak and nearly uncorrelated.
cell_types: Il6ra/Il6st/Osmr shared Glut/GABA neuronal classes
main_caveats: Correlations compare weak restricted signatures; most receptor-subunit target transcripts themselves were not robustly depleted.

direction: Stat1/Mapk1 depleted where Il6ra was unchanged
summary: The pipeline could detect depletion of Stat1 and Mapk1 transcripts in selected cells, separating the Il6ra null from a universal DE failure.
why_it_matters: This makes low receptor expression/engagement a more plausible explanation for the Il6ra result than an inability to call any perturbation effect in large neuronal matched comparisons.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Stat1 and Mapk1 are intracellular nodes with different basal expression and guide performance; this is not a matched receptor perturbation.

direction: do not extrapolate neuronal silence to organism-level anti-IL6R efficacy
summary: A neuronal Il6ra null result should not be used to down-rank IL6R inhibition for brain inflammatory disease.
why_it_matters: Human IL6R biology and approved antibodies act in immune and IL6 trans-signaling contexts, whereas this mouse table tests only Glut/GABA neuronal classes and misses the macrophage, endothelial, fibroblast, and other non-neuronal compartments where HPA reports richer brain IL6R expression.
cell_types: 22 Il6ra-tested Glut/GABA neuronal classes
main_caveats: Therapeutic evidence is human and disease-level; the perturbation dataset is mouse, neuronal, basal, and transcriptomic.

summary: Cnnm2 targeting produced recurrent nominal reduction of the target RNA but no FDR-significant genome-wide transcriptomic response in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: CNNM2 is a magnesium-homeostasis protein, so a mild RNA readout despite target depletion argues that this perturbation is buffered at steady state, incompletely engaged, or primarily executed through ion flux and protein physiology rather than large secondary transcriptional programs.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself never passed FDR<0.05, so part of the apparent buffering may reflect partial guide activity or sparse RNA detection rather than complete CNNM2 loss of function.

summary: Nominal Cnnm2 RNA depletion was concentrated in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than in the largest cortical and Pvalb contrasts.
why_it_matters: The dataset refines the broad brain expression of CNNM2 to a response that is detectably engaged only in selected neuronal classes, which should steer follow-up validation toward the cell classes where the guide actually moved the target transcript.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Differences could reflect target expression, guide capture, or power; the strongest cell-type effects remain nominal after FDR correction.

summary: Cnnm2 perturbation did not induce a coherent transcriptional compensation module among measured magnesium transporters, Cnnm paralogs, or TRPM-family pathway genes.
why_it_matters: The absence of Trpm7, Nipa, Slc41, Magt1, Mmgt, Mrs2, or Cnnm paralog compensation suggests that neuronal buffering of Cnnm2 loss is not implemented by simply transcriptionally replacing CNNM2 with another known magnesium transporter.
main_caveats: Only RNA-level compensation was tested; transport activity, membrane localization, magnesium concentration, and unmeasured regulators could still compensate.

summary: Cnnm2 full-transcriptome signatures were not recapitulated by available Trpm7, Nipa1, Mt3, or Slc12a2 perturbations and had no strong positive or inverse signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: CNNM2 and TRPM7 are coupled at the protein and ion-transport level, but in this Perturb-seq readout the relationship is not visible as a shared transcriptional state; this prevents assigning weak Cnnm2 effects to a generic TRPM7-like divalent-cation program.
main_caveats: Most compared perturbations were themselves weak and some exact CNNM2 complex partners, including Ptp4a1/Ptp4a2/Ptp4a3 and Cnnm paralogs, were not available as perturbation targets.

summary: A pineal glutamatergic Cnnm2 signature contained an exploratory nominal decrease of Ube2 E2 ubiquitin-conjugating genes.
why_it_matters: Ube2b, Ube2k, and Ube2r2 provide a compact biomarker hypothesis for validating this low-cell-count pineal response, but the signal should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than a proven CNNM2 pathway.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The cell count was 43, Cnnm2 engagement was nominal, and none of the pineal genes reached FDR<0.05.

summary: The weak mouse-brain transcriptional response contrasts with genetic evidence that CNNM2 loss of function can cause hypomagnesemia, seizures, intellectual disability, and developmental brain defects.
why_it_matters: Disease mechanisms for CNNM2 should not be inferred solely from steady-state neuronal RNA changes; developmental timing, systemic renal magnesium wasting, membrane ion transport, and electrophysiology may dominate the phenotype.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse, cell-type-resolved, and transcriptomic; it did not measure serum magnesium, kidney handling, development, or neuronal excitability.

summary: Ift81 produced a directionally plausible but statistically weak perturbation, with no FDR-significant transcript in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The primary interpretation is a loss of detectable transcriptomic effect rather than a broad IFT81-loss program; follow-up should first establish stronger on-target depletion or protein/cilium phenotypes.
main_caveats: The target transcript trended down in most cell types, so a small effect may be present but below this screen's adjusted threshold.

summary: The best-engaged Ift81 classes, especially 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, had only nominal downstream tails instead of an FDR-stable response.
why_it_matters: Even where the perturbation was most visible, the transcriptome did not amplify Ift81 depletion into a reproducible stress, ciliary, or neuronal-state module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The strongest cell type still had Ift81 FDR=1.0, so the apparent buffering could reflect incomplete perturbation rather than biological compensation.

summary: Ift81 perturbation did not activate or suppress a detectable Smoothened-GLI or ciliary-gene transcript module.
why_it_matters: IFT81 is a ciliary IFT-B component, so a Hedgehog or cilium-assembly readout would be the expected pathway-level positive control; its absence shows that this mature mouse-brain transcriptome is not reporting canonical IFT81 pathway failure.
main_caveats: The conclusion is limited to mRNA in mostly neuronal classes; ciliary trafficking, axoneme length, receptor localization, or Hedgehog responsiveness were not measured.

summary: Ift81 signatures failed to converge with perturbations of other ciliary network genes despite their known functional proximity.
why_it_matters: The absence of a shared score-vector signature argues against treating the weak Ift81 profile as a generic primary-cilium state or as interchangeable with Ift88, Ift43, Ttc21b, Kif3b, BBSome, dynein-2, Smo/Ptch1, or GLI perturbations in this dataset.
main_caveats: Most related perturbations also showed weak own-transcript depletion, and the correlations are transcriptome-wide ranks rather than direct protein or ciliary-phenotype measurements.

summary: The leading nominal Ift81 genes are poor biomarkers because they are isolated to single cell types and rarely recur.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Atl3, Cit, Lrp3, Cttn, Peg3 and Map7d1 should be treated as hypothesis-generating cell-local tails, not as an Ift81-loss signature.
main_caveats: A larger or better-engaged perturbation could reveal a recurrent biomarker that is absent here.

summary: This adult neuronal Perturb-seq readout should not be used to assign a disease-reversal or drugging direction for IFT81 ciliopathy biology.
why_it_matters: Published IFT81 disease mechanisms involve loss of an IFT-B core protein, abnormal cilia and Hedgehog signaling in skeletal cells; the screen instead shows a weak neuronal knockdown with no canonical pathway transcript and no curated direct ChEMBL target entry.
main_caveats: The dataset may still be informative for neuronal cilia if protein-level ciliary phenotypes are assayed; it simply lacks a robust mRNA marker in this table.

summary: Acat1 knockdown was recurrently negative but FDR-resolved only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The one corrected on-target signal provides the best cell context for interpreting Acat1 biology, while the many nominal-only cell types should not be treated as equally engaged knockdowns.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The apparent cell-type pattern is confounded with perturbed-cell count: the FDR-positive 151 class had 123 Acat1-perturbed cells, whereas several nominal cell types had only 32-54 perturbed cells.

summary: Acat1 loss produced a target-only corrected signature rather than a broad downstream transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: ACAT1 is a mitochondrial thiolase with known metabolic roles, so the absence of any non-target FDR hit argues that partial Acat1 transcript depletion in these neurons was transcriptionally buffered under the profiled condition.
main_caveats: The dataset contains RNA responses only; mitochondrial ACAT1 protein, acetoacetyl-CoA, ketone-body flux, and isoleucine intermediates were not measured.

summary: The Acat1 signature in 151 was uncoupled from an SREBF2/mevalonate transcriptional response and should not be read as SOAT1/ACAT1 cholesterol-esterification inhibition.
why_it_matters: ACAT1 nomenclature is ambiguous: mitochondrial ACAT1 is distinct from sterol O-acyltransferase 1, also called ACAT1 in cholesteryl-ester literature. The same cell type showed a clear sterol module after Srebf2 perturbation, but Acat1 perturbation left measured SREBF and mevalonate genes at FDR=1.0.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic contrast in one cell class; SOAT1 itself was not perturbed in the screened Acat1 cell types.

summary: The human beta-ketothiolase-deficiency gene Acat1 did not trigger a neuronal stress or sterol-homeostasis crisis at the mRNA level when partially depleted in vivo.
why_it_matters: Human ACAT1 disease reflects disruption of ketone-body and isoleucine metabolism; these data suggest that early partial transcript depletion in unstressed mouse neurons is a poor proxy for the systemic metabolic decompensation seen in biallelic enzymatic deficiency.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: A negative RNA signature does not exclude altered enzyme abundance, acyl-CoA pools, or vulnerability during fasting/ketoacidotic stress.

summary: Acat1 lacked a robust positive or inverse signature neighbor, including among assayed lipid and mitochondrial metabolic perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues against treating Acat1 as a member of a recurrent Perturb-seq co-regulation module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and prevents over-interpretation of the few nominal secondary genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was measured on Wilcoxon score vectors, not on raw single-cell expression or metabolomic profiles; weak Acat1 secondary effects reduce power to discover neighbors.

summary: Foxj1 perturbation produced no FDR<0.05 transcriptional response in any tested neuronal cell class, and the Foxj1 transcript itself was not detectably engaged.
why_it_matters: The screen does not support an acute Foxj1-dependent neuronal program; the safest first interpretation is a silent or ineffectively engaged perturbation rather than a subtle ciliary pathway change.
cell_types: 22 Foxj1-sampled cell types
main_caveats: Absence of Foxj1 transcript knockdown means the cells may not have expressed the target or the guide may not have produced measurable engagement; several classes had fewer than 70 perturbed cells.

summary: The canonical motile-cilium / FOXJ1 network was not recovered: Rfx3, Trp73, Cep164, Ift genes, Foxj3, and Rfx7 were nearly inactive and their signatures were not correlated with Foxj1.
why_it_matters: RFX3, p73, MCIDAS/GMNC, and IFT/CEP proteins are functional neighbors of Foxj1 in multiciliated cells, so their failure to converge argues that this neuronal dataset is not reading out multiciliogenesis.
cell_types: 22 Foxj1-sampled cell types
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to transcriptional score vectors in mouse neuronal classes; Rfx2, Mcidas, and Gmnc were not available as perturbations.

summary: E2f4, unlike Foxj1 and E2f5, elicited a strong positive chromosome/kinetochore/microtubule signature in a subset of thalamic, midbrain, Pvalb, hypothalamic GABA, and hindbrain GABA classes.
why_it_matters: E2F4 can cooperate with MCIDAS during multiciliogenesis, but in this atlas its output separates from the Foxj1 motile-cilium branch and instead exposes cell-cycle or centriole-associated gene regulation in postmitotic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only E2f4, not E2f5, was strong in these signatures; the dataset does not demonstrate centriole amplification or cilia formation at the protein or morphology level.

summary: Susd4 down-regulation in Pvalb interneurons is the only Foxj1-associated gene to approach FDR control.
why_it_matters: This gives a concrete first marker to validate if Foxj1 guides are repeated in Pvalb cells, but it should be treated as a single-gene, hypothesis-generating outlier rather than a pathway-level response.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Susd4 missed the 5% FDR cutoff and no second Pvalb gene reached FDR<0.25.

summary: For hydrocephalus and primary ciliary dyskinesia biology, Foxj1 perturbation should be interpreted through FOXJ1-positive ependymal or other ciliated cells rather than the sampled neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse FOXJ1 disease mechanisms center on motile ependymal and epithelial cilia, whereas this screen saw neither target engagement nor a downstream neuronal response, making neuronal transcriptomics a poor stand-alone assay for FOXJ1 disease rescue or inhibition.
cell_types: 22 Foxj1-sampled cell types
main_caveats: The evidence is negative in neuronal classes only; it does not test ependymal cells, airway epithelium, CSF flow, or ciliary beating.

summary: Kcnt1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome in any assayed mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: KCNT1 has a strong ion-channel and epilepsy literature, so its absence of corrected RNA effects is itself informative: this CRISPRi readout did not reveal a robust mRNA program downstream of wild-type Kcnt1 reduction.
main_caveats: The result is transcriptomic only; the direct Kcnt1 transcript was not FDR-significantly depleted, so lack of downstream response could reflect weak engagement or dropout.

summary: Several cell types showed nominal Kcnt1 self-depletion but still no corrected downstream response.
why_it_matters: The strongest 191 MB P MY GABA self hit and weaker 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut self hits did not propagate into FDR-significant transcriptional biomarkers, consistent with a buffered or underpowered RNA response.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only nominal Kcnt1 self-depletion was observed; low perturbed-cell counts, especially 26 cells in 217 P MY Pineal Glut and 37 cells in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, limit cell-type claims.

summary: The Slo2 paralog Kcnt2 was also weak and was not transcriptionally concordant with Kcnt1.
why_it_matters: Slack/KCNT1 and Slick/KCNT2 are related sodium-activated potassium channels with overlapping mouse-brain expression, but this dataset did not support treating Kcnt2 as a transcriptional proxy for Kcnt1.
main_caveats: Both paralog perturbations had weak target engagement, so the comparison rules out a strong shared RNA signature only within this assay.

summary: Kcnt1 and Kcnt2 were weak outliers relative to several other assayed neuronal ion-channel perturbations: Kcnq2, Scn1a, Hcn2, Kcnc3, Scn8a, and Kcnma1 achieved corrected self-depletion far more often.
why_it_matters: The same analysis pipeline can detect multiple neuronal ion-channel knockdowns, so Kcnt1 failure is not simply a universal inability to assay channels.
main_caveats: The comparator list is restricted to assayed ion-channel perturbations, and corrected effects counted here are dominated by direct self-transcript depletion rather than broad downstream programs.

summary: The weak wild-type Kcnt1 knockdown signature should not be interpreted as evidence against KCNT1 inhibition or antisense strategies.
why_it_matters: Human KCNT1 epilepsies are primarily gain-of-function channel disorders and Kcnt1 reduction has genetic-modifier efficacy in Scn1a and Scn8a mouse models; an RNA-seq null after partial CRISPRi is therefore a poor proxy for acute channel blockade or disease-allele correction.
main_caveats: Therapeutic studies used mutant epilepsy contexts, systemic antisense oligonucleotides, or pharmacology; those contexts do not match wild-type CRISPRi in dissociated mouse-brain cells.

summary: A restricted signature-neighbor scan did not reveal a reproducible Kcnt1-positive or Kcnt1-negative neighbor.
why_it_matters: Potential top neighbors were dominated by a single 308 CB GABA scan and even included a safe-target control, arguing against overinterpreting modest scalar correlations as pathway convergence.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The scan was restricted to the strongest 500 Kcnt1 rows per cell type and is vulnerable to nominal noise because Kcnt1 has no FDR-significant signature.

summary: Adrb1 perturbation was globally buffered at the scRNA-seq endpoint: the target transcript trended downward in most assayed classes but no Adrb1 DE row was FDR-significant.
why_it_matters: ADRB1 is a ligand-gated GPCR, so the absence of corrected basal transcriptional phenotypes means this assay should not be read as a successful receptor loss-of-function screen for canonical catecholamine signaling.
main_caveats: The evidence is decisive for the assayed endpoint but does not quantify receptor protein or ligand-evoked cAMP signaling.

summary: The only nominal Adrb1 transcript decreases occurred in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with the thalamic class showing a weak, downward activity-gene pattern involving Nr4a1, Fos, Egr1 and Bdnf.
why_it_matters: These two classes are the only plausible starting points for an Adrb1 neuronal follow-up in this dataset; all cell-type selectivity is exploratory because neither class had any q<0.05 downstream gene.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to nominal p values; the L5 ET class had target-only support, and the thalamic activity-gene pattern failed FDR correction.

summary: Adrb1 did not phenocopy strongly engaged Gs/cAMP/PKA/CREB/MAPK pathway perturbations; meanwhile Adrb2 and Adrb3 paralog perturbations were themselves unengaged.
why_it_matters: Canonical databases put ADRB1 upstream of Gs and adenylate cyclase, but the Perturb-seq response is not a simple loss-of-upstream-cAMP transcriptome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Adrb1 itself was weakly engaged, and Adrb2/Adrb3 were also unengaged, so lack of correlation cannot distinguish true biological divergence from insufficient receptor knockdown.

summary: A restricted top-400 signature-neighbor scan did not reveal a stable Adrb1-like module; the strongest neighbors were cell-type-specific and the most interpretable Map2k1 match in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was only r=0.346 in the restricted vector and r=0.092 transcriptome-wide.
why_it_matters: This prevents weak scalar similarity to Map2k1 or unrelated top hits such as Ifnar1 and Tspoap1 from being over-promoted to pathway convergence.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed after selecting Adrb1-responsive genes, so they are useful only as a triage scan.

summary: The neuronal Adrb1 screen gives no robust disease-direction or beta-blocker-like biomarker despite ADRB1 being an approved, clinically tractable cardiovascular target with documented CNS genetics.
why_it_matters: ADRB1 pharmacology is clinically important, but this basal mouse-brain perturbation should be used as a negative/buffered neuronal result rather than as efficacy or safety evidence for beta-1 antagonism in brain.
main_caveats: Many approved drugs act acutely on receptor activity, whereas the dataset measures steady-state transcriptomes after genetic perturbation with weak target-transcript depletion.

summary: Kdr behaved as an unengaged or biologically silent perturbation across the assayed mouse-brain classes.
why_it_matters: The screen sampled 22 Kdr Glut/GABA profiles but did not detect Kdr transcript depletion and detected only one downstream FDR hit in 371,818 tests, matching the expectation that canonical KDR biology is concentrated in vascular endothelial contexts rather than most brain neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The DE table does not report absolute expression or guide editing efficiency; the conclusion is about measured transcriptome output in the assayed classes.

summary: Clasp1 is an isolated CNU-MGE GABA marker of the Kdr condition rather than a VEGFR2 pathway signature.
why_it_matters: Clasp1 was the only FDR-significant gene for Kdr, with Srebf2, Nsmf and Tbpl1 remaining nominal; the profile lacked a depleted Kdr transcript and had no close full-transcriptome neighbor, so the result is a hypothesis-generating cell-class marker rather than a coherent angiogenic program.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only 42 perturbed cells; no significant Kdr self-depletion; all non-Clasp1 genes in the local signature are nominal after correction; the references support canonical VEGFR2 context rather than a direct Clasp1 link.

summary: The weak Kdr phenotype is shared by VEGF/vascular receptor neighbors rather than rescued by an interchangeable related receptor signature.
why_it_matters: KDR is embedded in a FLT/neuropilin vascular receptor network, but Kdr, Flt4, Ephb4, Tek, Nrp1, Nrp2, Pdgfrb and Plxnd1 perturbations were nearly flat in the neuronal dataset, arguing that the required endothelial receptor context is missing.
main_caveats: Most candidate ligands such as Vegfa and Vegfc were not assayed as perturbation targets in this file, and the related-receptor contrast remains transcriptomic.

summary: Kdr is uncoupled from detectable PI3K/MAPK transcriptional output even though other RTK/MAPK-neighbor perturbations score in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: Canonical VEGFR2 signals through PLCG1, PI3K, AKT and ERK; robust Fgfr1, Mapk1 and Braf signatures show that kinase perturbations can be detected, while Kdr stays flat in the same kinase-responsive cell classes.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Fgfr1, Mapk1 and Braf are not obligate KDR-complex members, and their responses occur in a subset of cell classes.

summary: Reported developmental neuronal VEGFR2-Sema3E biology does not generalize to Kdr responses in the assayed hippocampal/forebrain excitatory classes.
why_it_matters: A mouse developing-brain study placed VEGFR2 downstream of Sema3E for subicular axon growth, but Kdr showed no target depletion or downstream hits in the CA1/dentate and CA3/dentate/forebrain glutamatergic classes included here.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The literature context is developing subiculum neurons, whereas the Perturb-seq labels are broader hippocampal/forebrain glutamatergic classes.

summary: The neuronal Kdr null result should not be read as evidence that VEGFR2 blockade is biologically inert.
why_it_matters: KDR is a druggable endothelial receptor, and the Kdr rows lack the endothelial cell state in which VEGFR2 drives angiogenesis and shear-stress signaling; the negative screen result is therefore a context warning for brain-neuron interpretation, not a vascular safety result.
main_caveats: No endothelial perturbation profile for Kdr was observed in the analyzed file.

summary: The Hnrnpu perturbation produced a reproducible positive Hnrnpu transcript shift rather than a measured transcript decrease.
why_it_matters: The sign of the target row constrains every downstream interpretation: these contrasts are best read as Hnrnpu target-transcript gain or paradoxical compensation, not as a direct model of Hnrnpu haploinsufficiency.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is not protein abundance; several cell types had weak target-row FDR despite positive logFC.

summary: Hnrnpu responses were sharply cell-type-selective, with the broadest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: A broadly expressed nuclear RNA/chromatin factor did not produce a uniform brain-wide transcriptional program; downstream propagation was strongest in selected thalamic and midbrain populations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell counts differed across contexts, and higher counts increase FDR power.

summary: Several cell types showed statistically clear Hnrnpu target-transcript increase but almost no FDR-level downstream response.
why_it_matters: The target transcript could move without obligatorily reprogramming thousands of genes, pointing to cellular buffering or to context-specific requirements for converting Hnrnpu dosage into a broader signature.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Low non-target discovery can reflect true buffering, limited cell number, or both.

summary: The recurrent Hnrnpu response combined positive Dmtf1, Atxn2l, Gpr180, Macf1, Hdac3, and Depdc5 effects with negative Ahi1 and Rsrp1 effects.
why_it_matters: These genes are more reproducible Hnrnpu-response markers than single-cell-type top hits and form candidate biomarkers for the perturbation state in responsive neurons.
main_caveats: The module is transcriptomic and recurrent, but it has not been shown here to be direct Hnrnpu binding or splicing regulation.

summary: Hnrnpu converged most with spliceosome/proteasome perturbation signatures and only weakly with other measured hnRNP or neurodevelopmental RNA-binding perturbations.
why_it_matters: The screen does not support a generic hnRNP-family response; Hnrnpu sits closer to a spliceosome/proteostasis neighborhood in the strongest contexts while remaining distinct from Hnrnpc, Hnrnph2, Hnrnpa1, Hnrnpa2b1, Fus, Tardbp, Matr3, Rbfox1, and Srrm2.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Signature correlations were modest, especially outside 155 MB Glut, and they do not prove direct biochemical interaction.

summary: The dataset supports Hnrnpu dosage sensitivity in neurons but warns that increasing Hnrnpu transcript is not automatically equivalent to rescuing HNRNPU loss-of-function disease.
why_it_matters: HNRNPU haploinsufficiency causes a neurodevelopmental epilepsy syndrome; these data show that positive Hnrnpu transcript shifts can themselves be transcriptionally active, so any replacement or activation strategy would need dosage and cell-type control.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The literature centers on heterozygous loss of function and developmental disease, whereas this screen measured transcriptomic consequences of guide-defined perturbation in mouse brain cell types.

summary: Kcnt2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant self-depletion or downstream transcriptomic hit in any measured mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: KCNT2 is an excitable-membrane potassium channel, but this CRISPR Perturb-seq readout does not provide a reliable Kcnt2 loss-of-function transcriptional signature.

direction: Gad1 loss-of-function risk despite a buffered transcriptome
