why_it_matters: Human and mouse loss-of-function data show that GAD1/GAD67 is critical for nervous-system development and excitability, whereas this Perturb-seq assay saw strong mRNA knockdown with little secondary transcriptional output; therapeutic programs would need biochemical and electrophysiologic rescue readouts.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The clinical genetics involve germline biallelic variants, whereas the dataset measures partial acute perturbation in mouse brain cell classes.

summary: Hjv perturbation was nearly silent across the assayed mouse-brain subclasses, and target-transcript engagement was not detectable in the DE table.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset signal is absence of a robust neuronal transcriptional phenotype rather than a distributed BMP or iron-homeostasis response; this prevents strong mechanistic inference from most Hjv contrasts.
main_caveats: The perturbation may have edited protein-coding sequence without changing steady-state Hjv mRNA, and several subclass tests had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: A single Sst GABA signal, Rxylt1 up-regulation, was the only 5% FDR hit for Hjv.
why_it_matters: If validated, Rxylt1 could mark a narrow Sst interneuron state sensitive to Hjv perturbation; however the current support is a one-gene transcriptomic hit from 54 perturbed cells.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Only Rxylt1 crossed FDR; no mechanistic tie to hemojuvelin, hepcidin, or BMP signaling was established in the dataset.

summary: The assayed brain Hjv perturbations did not recapitulate the canonical HJV-BMP-hepcidin iron-regulatory program that is central in hepatocytes.
why_it_matters: Human HJV/HFE2 loss and mouse Hjv loss are strongly linked to hepcidin deficiency and iron overload; the absence of Hamp, BMP receptor/SMAD, and iron-transporter responses in this neuronal Perturb-seq panel argues that those systemic mechanisms were not engaged here.
main_caveats: A negative neuronal RNA-seq result cannot exclude non-transcriptional BMP signaling, sparse baseline expression, or peripheral liver/muscle functions of Hjv.

summary: In cerebellar GABA cells, the Hjv score vector weakly converged with BMP R-SMAD/Bmpr1b perturbations but diverged from Neo1 and from Acvr2a/Bmpr2.
why_it_matters: The restricted comparison argues against treating every HJV-binding or BMP-receptor neighbor as interchangeable in brain cells; even pathway members had opposite or near-zero similarity to Hjv.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The correlations were computed from full DE score vectors for one cell class; Hjv itself had no FDR-significant CB GABA gene and the absolute correlations were modest.

direction: no robust knockdown or downstream DE
summary: Fgfr3 CRISPRi was transcriptionally buffered across the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: A nearly complete absence of both on-target depletion and FDR-significant downstream genes argues that these glutamatergic and GABAergic subclasses are not the cell types in which endogenous Fgfr3 loss produces a strong acute transcriptomic phenotype.
main_caveats: The input is a DE summary rather than raw counts; low basal Fgfr3 expression can make logFC unstable, so target engagement was judged from Wilcoxon scores and p values.

direction: Map2k1/Braf/Ntrk2 down-regulated the module; Fgfr3 was neutral
summary: Fgfr3 loss did not couple to the neuronal MAPK-output module that was readily detected after Map2k1, Braf, and Ntrk2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The null Fgfr3 result is not explained by a global inability of this assay to detect ERK/MAPK-linked transcriptional programs; instead it is specific to the receptor perturbation in the available neuronal cell state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The convergent module was observed in one neuronal subclass, and Ntrk2 is not an FGFR-family member.

summary: Fgfr3 was not interchangeable with Fgfr1, Fgfr2, or Fgfrl1 perturbations despite FGFR-family pathway overlap.
why_it_matters: Shared receptor nomenclature and shared downstream cascades did not predict transcriptomic similarity in these cells, emphasizing that receptor abundance and cell context dominate over pathway diagrams.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Fgfr2 and Fgfrl1 produced few robust events in this comparator set, so the contrast is based mainly on all-gene correlation plus the strong Fgfr1 on-target event in 155 MB Glut.

summary: No reliable Fgfr3-responsive biomarker emerged from the nominal top genes or the signature-neighbor search.
why_it_matters: Hook3, Sugp2, Fhip1b, Ppm1e, and Trafd1 could look interesting in isolation, but their FDR values and the very small genome-wide signature correlations make them hypothesis-generating at most.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: This is a negative biomarker finding; absence of a robust transcriptomic marker does not exclude non-transcriptional FGFR3 signaling.

direction: healthy-neuron loss-of-function negative; activated-disease contexts remain unresolved
summary: The dataset should not be used as direct evidence that FGFR3 inhibition is inert in FGFR3-driven brain disease or cancer contexts.
why_it_matters: FGFR3 is druggable and pathogenic when activated, but the assayed perturbation was loss-of-function in healthy neuronal subclasses that lacked measurable on-target engagement; glial or gain-of-function models are required before drawing therapeutic-direction conclusions.
main_caveats: This warning is inferential: the dataset did not assay FGFR3 inhibitors, activating FGFR3 alleles, tumors, radial glia, or astrocytes.

summary: Aimp1 perturbation produced a dataset-wide buffered transcriptional response: the target transcript trended downward in most measured neuron classes, but no Aimp1-target row passed FDR correction.
why_it_matters: The primary result is a corrected negative result, so the acute single-cell perturbation should not be interpreted as a high-engagement model of germline AIMP1 loss-of-function disease.
main_caveats: The conclusion is about transcriptomic DE after this perturbation, not Aimp1 protein depletion, long-term neuronal morphology, or organismal loss of function.

summary: Nominal target engagement was concentrated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 155 MB Glut, whereas the largest 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut arm had the best downstream adjusted p value but weak Aimp1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: It separates probable guide engagement from downstream outliers and points to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 155 MB Glut as the only classes worth treating as engaged, still exploratory Aimp1 responses.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Nominal p values survive neither per-cell-type FDR nor cross-cell-type correction.

summary: The canonical multi-tRNA synthetase complex was not transcriptionally co-regulated after Aimp1 perturbation; measured cytosolic MSC transcripts stayed FDR-negative and Mars1 was only an isolated nominal increase in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: AIMP1 protein is a physical MSC accessory factor, so the neuronal phenotype is more consistent with no detectable complex-wide mRNA feedback than with an acute transcript-level collapse of tRNA-aminoacylation machinery.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only transcript levels were assayed; most core cytosolic MSC genes were measured as response genes but not perturbed as separate dataset targets.

summary: Neither disease-family aminoacyl-tRNA-synthetase perturbations nor whole-transcriptome signature neighbors showed robust convergence with Aimp1.
why_it_matters: The analysis found no convincing related-target or opposite-signature perturbation that can be used to infer a shared Aimp1 mechanism in the measured neuron classes.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Direct Aimp1 complex partners were absent as perturbation targets; the correlation screen is restricted to same-cell-type Wilcoxon score vectors.

summary: Aimp1 disease interpretation remains neuron-intrinsic/axoglial rather than oligodendrocyte-only in this dataset: the measured Aimp1 perturbations were in glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes, and prior work supports neuronal p43/Aimp1 axon biology.
why_it_matters: Human AIMP1 disorders are often annotated as hypomyelinating leukodystrophy, but the present experiment cannot test oligodendrocyte-autonomous myelination and is better aligned to neuronal consequences of Aimp1 loss.
main_caveats: The dataset showed no FDR-passing Aimp1 response, so this is a context refinement, not a validated neuronal disease module.

summary: The absence of a corrected acute transcriptomic phenotype should not be used to de-risk direct CNS inhibition of AIMP1.
why_it_matters: Open Targets and ChEMBL show no established AIMP1 drug mechanism, and human loss-of-function genetics argues that reducing AIMP1 activity can be neurologically hazardous even when this dataset shows only weak acute DE.
main_caveats: The dataset is not a toxicity screen and does not establish the direction or reversibility of any intervention.

summary: Caml knockdown produced the clearest FDR-supported neuronal programs in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, not uniformly across the 23 assayed brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: CAMLG is a core ER tail-anchor insertion factor, so the concentration of large transcriptional outputs in two glutamatergic classes separates acute transcriptional sensitivity from the broad housekeeping role of the protein.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only the target transcript and steady-state RNA were measured; target engagement reached FDR<0.05 in only two cell types.

summary: Several cell types tolerated nominal Caml transcript lowering with no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This negative result argues that the absence of a Caml signature in most classes is not simply absence of target transcript detection, and it flags strong buffering or inadequate functional knockdown in cortical glutamatergic and CTX-CGE GABA contexts.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: FDR correction was over ~16,000-17,000 measured genes per test; some buffered examples had only 52-122 perturbed cells and Caml mRNA FDR itself was not <0.05.

summary: Caml loss depressed GABA-receptor-family transcripts in a thalamic glutamatergic class and inhibitory-receptor transcripts in midbrain glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: Prior neuronal work showed CAML is needed for surface recycling and function of postsynaptic GABA(A) receptors; the Perturb-seq data place receptor-subunit RNA changes downstream of Caml in only selected neuronal populations and extend the affected receptor set to Gabbr1 and Glrb in 155 MB Glut.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The prior study measured receptor trafficking and inhibitory currents, whereas this dataset measured transcript abundance; the Pvalb Gabrg2 effect was nominal rather than FDR-significant.

summary: The two strongest target-engaged classes lost synaptic-vesicle and neuron-projection transcripts, overlapping the membrane-trafficking theme of CAMLG-CDG.
why_it_matters: A human CAMLG splice-loss case connected TRC failure to Golgi SNARE mislocalization and neurological glycosylation disease; down-regulation of Sv2a, Syp, Slc12a5, Atp1a3, Gabbr1, Glrb, and Thy1 nominates neuronal membrane and synaptic-output programs as brain-cell readouts of partial Caml loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay protein insertion, glycosylation, Golgi SNARE localization, vesicle release, or surface receptor abundance.

summary: Stmn4 up-regulation was the recurrent inhibitory-class readout of Caml perturbation.
why_it_matters: Stmn4 was the only FDR-significant gene shared across three GABAergic response classes, including the single significant transcript in 191 MB P MY GABA, making it a compact candidate reporter of the non-glutamatergic Caml state rather than a generic marker of the stronger thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic programs.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Two of the three Stmn4-positive classes lacked measurable Caml RNA knockdown, so this is a response marker hypothesis rather than proof of an on-target mechanism.

summary: Caml signatures weakly but recurrently resembled V-ATPase, clathrin/vesicle, and proteasome perturbations more than they showed any strong opposite neighbor.
why_it_matters: Direct WRB/ASNA1/GET-family comparisons were not available in the perturbation panel, but the nearest positive neighbors point to organelle acidification, vesicle traffic, and protein turnover machinery as transcriptomic neighbors of CAML loss in neurons.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The correlations were modest, score-based, and do not show physical interaction with CAML; they should be read as hypotheses about shared cellular state.

summary: The loss-of-function signature argues against treating CAMLG as a safe neuronal inhibition target.
why_it_matters: Human CAMLG loss causes a neurological congenital glycosylation disorder, CAMLG is a core ER receptor rather than a pathway-specific receptor subunit, and partial Caml lowering in mouse neurons suppressed synaptic and receptor transcripts; systemic CAMLG antagonism would therefore be expected to carry membrane-trafficking and neurodevelopmental liabilities.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No drug perturbation, rescue, dose-response, or adult behavioral outcome was assayed.

summary: Dnm1l loss activates a recurrent ATF4-like amino-acid stress module in five subcortical neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation phenotype is not dominated by generic down-regulation of mitochondrial transcripts; it repeatedly induces amino-acid biosynthesis, transport, tRNA-charging, and Ddit3/Chac1 stress genes that provide a mechanistic readout of mitochondrial fission stress.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The report infers an ISR-like state from marker genes; ATF4 protein, eIF2 phosphorylation, mitochondrial morphology, and mitochondrial function were not measured in the parquet.

summary: The Dnm1l response is strongly cell-type selective rather than proportional only to target-transcript knockdown.
why_it_matters: This narrows Dnm1l vulnerability to thalamic, hypothalamic, and midbrain/brainstem neuronal contexts in this assay while several cortical excitatory classes tolerated nominally similar transcript depletion with no FDR-significant downstream response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Sensitive groups include some cases with few perturbed cells or non-significant target-transcript FDR; resistant cortical classes have only nominal target knockdown, so buffering and incomplete perturbation cannot be fully separated.

summary: Dnm1l and Opa1 perturbations converge on the same stress-metabolic program despite perturbing opposite sides of mitochondrial dynamics.
why_it_matters: The shared Asns/Cars/Ddit3/Chac1/Mars1 response identifies imbalance of mitochondrial shape control, not only loss of the fission GTPase itself, as a route to ISR-like neuronal stress.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor correlations were restricted to the top 300 Dnm1l genes rather than the whole transcriptome, and convergence was evaluated at RNA level only.

summary: Classical Dnm1 is efficiently depleted but transcriptionally buffered, showing that the Dnm1l phenotype is specific to mitochondrial dynamics rather than a generic response to any dynamin-family GTPase knockdown.
why_it_matters: Dnm1 and Dnm1l are related GTPases, but only Dnm1l loss triggered the strong amino-acid stress program in the sensitive neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic; it does not test acute synaptic-vesicle recycling phenotypes that could follow Dnm1 protein loss without changing steady-state RNA.

summary: Mff did not phenocopy Dnm1l, but the Dnm1l-receptor comparison is limited by weak Mff target engagement.
why_it_matters: MFF is a DRP1 recruitment factor, so an apparent absence of Dnm1l-like ISR after Mff guides could be tempting to interpret as receptor specificity; the target row shows that this is more safely treated as an uninformative or underpowered perturbation.
main_caveats: Mff transcript depletion never reached FDR<0.05, so absence of FDR downstream genes is not evidence that neurons do not require MFF.

summary: Full Dnm1l inhibition is predicted to be stress-inducing in brain cells, creating a narrow therapeutic-direction window for DRP1 inhibitors.
why_it_matters: Human DNM1L loss-of-function causes severe mitochondrial/peroxisomal fission disease, and this dataset shows that reducing Dnm1l in neuronal classes directly turns on stress and amino-acid salvage genes; inhibitors that mimic strong loss of function could therefore carry central nervous system liability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Guide-based transcript reduction is not identical to partial, acute, or tissue-restricted enzymatic inhibition; the queried druggability databases do not establish clinical exposure or toxicity.

direction: Hs6st2 down only at FDR<0.05 in 155 MB Glut
summary: Hs6st2 perturbation achieved stringent on-target transcript depletion in only one measured population, 155 MB Glut, even though the target transcript was measured in 22 cell types.
why_it_matters: Interpretation should be centered on 155 MB Glut; most other cell-type signatures are likely weak-engagement or low-power views rather than equivalent Hs6st2 loss-of-function states.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA depletion, not HS 6-O-sulfation; weak signatures in other cell types may reflect low baseline Hs6st2 expression, insufficient guide cells, or inefficient editing.

direction: Hs6st2 down; other tested pathway transcripts unchanged at FDR<0.05
summary: Strong Hs6st2 depletion in 155 MB Glut was almost completely buffered at the mRNA level: Hs6st2 itself was the only FDR-significant gene, and paralogous HS writers, extracellular 6-O-endosulfatases, and candidate FGF/Slit-Robo transcripts did not shift significantly.
why_it_matters: A Golgi glycosaminoglycan-modifying defect can change heparan-sulfate chemistry without producing an immediate cell-autonomous transcriptional cascade; absence of RNA changes should not be read as absence of altered HSPG structure.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Transcript stability, extracellular HS modification, ligand availability, and morphology were not measured; Fgf1 and Slit2 had only nominal trends.

direction: transcriptome buffered despite disease loss-of-function context
summary: The Perturb-seq result is much narrower than chronic Hs6st2 brain knockout and human HS6ST2 disease genetics would predict: an acute, sparse knockdown in adult/sampled neuronal classes revealed self-depletion but not a dendrite/synapse disease program.
why_it_matters: Intellectual-disability biology linked to HS6ST2 may depend on chronic loss of HS 6-O-sulfation, hippocampal anatomy, development, extracellular matrix remodeling, or structural synaptic phenotypes that are invisible to a short-term single-cell RNA endpoint.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay hippocampal CA1 morphology, memory, glycan sulfation, or organismal development; 155 MB Glut is not a one-to-one match to the hippocampal and cortical bulk regions profiled in the knockout study.

summary: In 155 MB Glut, robust self-knockdown of Agrn, Ext2, Fgfr1, and Robo2 did not converge on an Hs6st2-like transcriptome, and Glce lacked a robust on-target mRNA response.
why_it_matters: HS6ST2 should not be treated as interchangeable with generic HSPG polymerization enzymes or HS-dependent cue receptors in this dataset; the measured RNA phenotypes are dominated by target depletion rather than a shared FGF or Slit/Robo module.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and restricted to targets present in the Perturb-seq panel; Hs6st1, Hs6st3, Hs2st1, and Ndst perturbations were unavailable.

summary: Hs6st2 had no meaningful whole-transcriptome positive or negative signature neighbor in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Follow-up should prioritize the on-target cell type and glycan or morphological assays, not the tiny top correlations from scalar transcriptomic-neighbor analysis.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: A weak Hs6st2 signature constrains similarity discovery; correlations on restricted top-gene subsets were larger but unstable and not used for interpretation.

summary: Igsf8 perturbation produced consistent target-transcript depletion in all assayed cell classes but FDR-significant depletion in only seven of 23.
why_it_matters: The direct knockdown pattern, rather than downstream DE, defines which cell classes are interpretable for Igsf8 loss of function.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Target engagement was measured at the RNA level; IGSF8 surface protein depletion was not measured.

summary: Igsf8 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: no non-Igsf8 gene reached FDR 0.05 in any of the 23 cell classes.
why_it_matters: It separates target engagement from mRNA-state remodeling and suggests that Igsf8 phenotypes in this setting may be post-transcriptional, structural, synaptic, or too small for the sampled cell counts.
main_caveats: A negative FDR result does not exclude protein localization, electrophysiologic, or morphology phenotypes.

summary: The CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic composite did not show useful Igsf8 target engagement, leaving the published CA3 mossy-fiber role largely untested by this Perturb-seq slice.
why_it_matters: The strongest neural Igsf8 literature is CA3-synapse based; weak CA3 target depletion prevents the dataset from adjudicating that mechanism.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The dataset cell class is a composite label rather than purified CA3 mossy-fiber presynaptic neurons, and it had only 46 perturbed cells.

summary: Direct membrane-neighborhood perturbations, especially Cd81 and Bsg, did not phenocopy the Igsf8 score vector in matched brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: Although IGSF8 is a CD81/CD9 tetraspanin partner, the transcriptomic consequence of partial Igsf8 loss was not interchangeable with knocking down Cd81, Bsg, Tspan7, Tspan12, Actn4, Itga4, or Itgb1.
main_caveats: Cd9, Cd82, Cd151, and Ptgfrn were unavailable as perturbations; some comparator targets, such as Actn4 and Itga4, had weak own-transcript engagement in these neuronal classes.

summary: A high-engagement signature-neighbor scan did not reveal a strong positive or negative Igsf8-like perturbation.
why_it_matters: The weak top correlations argue against burying a hidden convergent module among unrelated targets, and against interpreting any one low-rank nominal gene as a pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The all-target scan was run in three high-engagement classes rather than all 23 classes; restricted top-500 correlations were vulnerable to safe-target artifacts.

summary: A negative neuronal scRNA response should not be read as brain de-risking for IGSF8-directed cancer immunotherapy.
why_it_matters: IGSF8 is an extracellular immune-checkpoint target, but its best-supported brain role is synaptic organization; this dataset lacks both CA3 engagement and non-transcriptional synapse phenotyping.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The warning is directional and mechanistic, not evidence that IGSF8 blockade is neurotoxic.

summary: Gpr45 perturbation produced neither detectable target knockdown nor any FDR-significant transcriptomic response across the 21 tested cell types.
why_it_matters: This makes the primary interpretation a null or failed-engagement result rather than a map of Gpr45 biology.
main_caveats: The data are differential-expression summaries only; guide identity, editing or CRISPRi efficiency, and raw UMI-level target detection were not available.

summary: The reported hypothalamic Pomc/JAK2/STAT3 axis was not recovered at RNA level after Gpr45 perturbation in the broad mouse-brain cell classes assayed here.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse genetics tie Gpr45 loss to obesity through hypothalamic Pomc and JAK/STAT signaling, so the absence of Pomc, Jak2, Stat3, Gnas, Adcy3, or Mc4r responses argues that this Perturb-seq contrast did not capture that specialized endocrine-neuronal state.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The assayed classes are broad, target engagement was weak, and the known phenotype was measured in mouse hypothalamus and primary hypothalamic cultures rather than the same single-cell assay.

summary: Gpr45 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with related GPCR and cAMP-module perturbations, including Gnas, Adcy1/3/5, and melanocortin receptors.
why_it_matters: This argues against treating weak Gpr45 signatures as a latent cAMP or melanocortin transcriptional program; the largest restricted correlation was no stronger than safe-target null correlations.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from summary signatures and is exploratory; the Gpr45 query signature itself is not FDR-supported.

summary: Nominal Gpr45 peaks were private to individual cell types instead of forming a recurrent module.
why_it_matters: The largest z-scores identify possible cell-type-local noise or context-specific weak effects, but the lack of repeated p<0.001 genes prevents assigning a robust pathway to them.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative pattern in the summary statistics, not proof that the listed genes are false positives.

summary: The dataset does not provide functional support for pharmacologically targeting GPR45.
why_it_matters: Mouse loss-of-function made Gpr45 an attractive obesity gene, but this Perturb-seq run lacks target engagement and ChEMBL contains only screening-level GPR45 activities with no curated mechanism rows, so activation or inhibition hypotheses require orthogonal validation in Gpr45-expressing hypothalamic neurons.
main_caveats: A null transcriptome under weak target engagement cannot falsify Gpr45 obesity biology or non-transcriptional GPCR signaling.

direction: stress genes up with recurrent Srsf5/Ddx17 down
summary: Elp1 perturbation activates an ATF4-like amino-acid-starvation program in the responsive neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The strongest Elp1 effect centers on Atf4, Ddit3, Chac1, Asns, aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, amino-acid transporters, and one-carbon enzymes, matching the translational stress expected when Elongator-dependent tRNA decoding is impaired.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The matched transcriptome implies an ISR/amino-acid-starvation state but does not directly measure tRNA U34 modification, translation speed, ATF4 protein, or ELP1 protein loss.

summary: The Elp1 response is sharply cell-type restricted rather than proportional only to cell count.
why_it_matters: Four TH/MB-enriched classes account for 696 of the 700 Elp1 FDR-significant gene-cell-type tests, whereas many cortical, hippocampal, striatal, and cerebellar classes were FDR-silent even when the target row moved nominally.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Some silent classes had few perturbed cells and the Elp1 transcript itself was not FDR-depleted, so absence of a broad response could reflect lower power or lower perturbation efficiency in part of the atlas.

summary: Elp2 phenocopies Elp1 in the dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut state, whereas Alkbh8, Nsun2, and Eif2ak4 do not.
why_it_matters: A second assayed core Elongator subunit landing as the top nonself positive neighbor converts the 151 response from an isolated guide effect into an Elongator-complex phenotype, while the weak matches to other comparators argue against a generic RNA-modification or ISR-kinase knockdown signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The quantitative neighbor calculation used the top 100 Elp1 genes in one cell type; Alkbh8 and Nsun2 were used as nearby perturbation controls, not as biochemical paralogs of Elp1.

summary: Cars, Aldh1l2, Mars1, Asns, Slc7a5, Mthfd2, and Srsf5 form a compact recurrent signature for Elp1 loss-of-function stress.
why_it_matters: These genes retain direction across the large 151 response and the smaller 145, 155, and 191 responses, so they are better monitoring candidates than any single top gene from one cell type.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Srsf5 down-regulation is empirical in this dataset and is not itself established here as an ATF4 target; validation should use independent Elp1 loss and protein- or reporter-level stress assays.

summary: The mouse-brain Elp1 signature extends known ELP1 translation/proteostasis pathology into discrete central neuronal states.
why_it_matters: ELP1 disease literature emphasizes peripheral neurons in familial dysautonomia and protein-homeostasis failure in ELP1-associated tumors; the Perturb-seq data point to thalamic and midbrain neurons as central contexts in which reduced Elongator function is sufficient to elicit a similar stress module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell taxonomy, species, developmental stage, and cancer versus noncancer context differ from the cited studies; the signature-neighbor comparison is restricted to 100 genes and is hypothesis-generating.

summary: Elp1 reduction drives stress genes in susceptible neurons, reinforcing ELP1 restoration rather than inhibition as the disease-relevant direction.
why_it_matters: Familial dysautonomia is caused by reduced functional ELP1 transcript and preclinical therapy aims to correct ELP1 splicing; the dataset shows that further lowering Elp1 can trigger Chac1/Ddit3/Atf4 stress outputs in specific brain neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay tested knockdown, not rescue; no neuronal survival or proprioceptive/autonomic phenotype was measured.

summary: Mcph1 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptomic response in any represented neuronal cell group.
why_it_matters: This makes the dominant dataset result a pan-cell-type negative rather than a hidden cell-type-specific effect; the result contrasts with the strong cell-cycle and DNA-repair roles known for MCPH1 but is restricted by weak target-transcript readout.
main_caveats: Negative at RNA level only; target editing or protein loss was not measured, and many cell types had tens rather than hundreds of Mcph1 cells.

summary: The two cell types with approximately one-logFC nominal Mcph1 mRNA decreases still lacked downstream FDR hits.
why_it_matters: 191 MB P MY GABA and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut are the closest cases to target engagement, but the self-transcript tests had q=1.0 and did not uncover a downstream module, so they are better treated as exploratory putative buffering than as proof of successful knockdown.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Both self-transcript decreases are nominal only and based on 61 and 40 perturbed cells, respectively.

summary: Known MCPH1 DNA-damage-response and Condensin II/chromosome-condensation genes stayed transcriptionally flat after Mcph1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: MCPH1 is linked to BRCT-mediated DNA repair, RAD51/BRCA2 homologous recombination, and Condensin II biology, but those canonical partners did not become RNA markers in this neuronal Perturb-seq setting.
main_caveats: MCPH1 checkpoint and repair functions are largely post-translational and cell-cycle dependent, so mRNA abundances of pathway genes are an indirect readout.

summary: The neuronal-subclass negative result is more consistent with a progenitor-stage MCPH1 disease window than with a strong autonomous transcriptional role in the assayed neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: Human MCPH1 loss causes congenital primary microcephaly, and mouse work places Mcph1 activity in rapidly dividing apical radial glia during corticogenesis; the assayed neuronal classes represented for Mcph1 did not recapitulate that developmental program.
main_caveats: The experiment may miss embryonic radial glia and proliferating intermediate progenitors; weak transcript-level engagement means the negative neuronal result cannot distinguish no biology from inefficient perturbation.

summary: Available MCPH1-related comparators were not interchangeable with Mcph1: Ncapd3 was also FDR-silent, whereas Wdfy3 produced a strong TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic signature that was uncorrelated with Mcph1.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the Mcph1 null result is not simply failure of the analysis to detect every brain-size gene, while the absence of most top STRING partners from the perturbation set limits direct reconstruction of the MCPH1 network.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Wdfy3 is a broader neurodevelopmental comparator rather than a direct MCPH1 complex member, and most high-confidence MCPH1 partners were not perturbed.

summary: Hspa8 depletion elicits a compensatory heat-shock/chaperone program rather than a single-cell-type idiosyncratic hit list.
why_it_matters: Dnaja1, Hspa4l, Hsp90aa1, Hsph1, Stip1 and related folding genes are direct neighbors of the Hsp70 machinery, so their induction is the clearest biological readout that the perturbation stresses cytosolic protein quality control.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Hsf1 activity was not assayed directly, and recurrence outside the three FDR cell types is based on nominal p values.

summary: FDR-controlled Hspa8 responses are narrowly concentrated in three of twenty-one assayed neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: A constitutive chaperone perturbation does not create a uniform brain-wide transcriptome; specific thalamic, cortical-projecting, and hypothalamic classes cross the statistical threshold while most classes remain weak or buffered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Cell counts differ from 28 to 115 perturbed cells, so some apparent selectivity may reflect power as well as biology.

direction: on-target RNA down with downstream buffering
summary: The cell type with the largest measured Hspa8 RNA decrease, 308 CB GABA, has no FDR-controlled downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This disconnect warns that Hspa8 mRNA loss, chaperone protein abundance, and the downstream stress transcriptome are not linearly coupled in every neuronal state.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Fifty-two perturbed cells gave limited power; several chaperone genes were nominally induced but lost FDR control.

summary: Hspa8 signatures converge more with proteasome-subunit perturbations than with most annotated chaperone perturbations.
why_it_matters: The recurrent Psmb4/Psmc1/Psmc5/Pomp neighborhood places Hspa8 loss in a broader proteotoxic protein-quality-control state coupled to ubiquitin-proteasome capacity, not just in an Hsc70-specific branch.
main_caveats: All correlations are modest, with a maximum r=0.334 among non-self signatures; correlation does not define direct epistasis.

summary: Hspa8 is not transcriptionally interchangeable with Hsp90ab1, Hspd1, or targeted DnaJ co-chaperones.
why_it_matters: The related-target comparison preserves a negative result: components of the chaperone web share interactors but produce distinguishable perturbation states, with only partial similarity to Hspa9 and Hspa5.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison uses whole-transcriptome score correlations, not a matched double-perturbation or biochemical assay.

direction: no FDR-level induction of measured pathway components
summary: Known HSPA8 effector pathways for chaperone-mediated autophagy and clathrin uncoating are not transcriptionally induced at FDR level.
why_it_matters: The acute RNA response to Hspa8 loss is dominated by compensatory chaperones; it does not by itself prove CMA or synaptic vesicle uncoating failure, both of which may be activity- or protein-level phenotypes.
main_caveats: Absence of transcript changes in Lamp2/Cltc/Picalm/Dnajc6 does not exclude altered LAMP2A-specific CMA flux or clathrin-uncoating activity.

direction: inhibition predicted to induce compensatory chaperone feedback
summary: Drugging HSPA8 in neurons is likely to trigger compensatory proteostasis transcription rather than a silent loss of a single chaperone node.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL records show HSPA8 can be pharmacologically engaged, while the Perturb-seq data show that reduced Hspa8 dosage pushes neuronal subclasses toward HSP70/HSP90 feedback; any inhibitor program should plan for heat-shock compensation and cell-type-selective stress liability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset is CRISPR perturbation in mouse brain cells, not acute small-molecule inhibition in a dosing study.

summary: Egr2 guide assignment produced no detectable on-target Egr2 transcript reduction and no FDR-level genome-wide response in any tested neuronal class.
why_it_matters: The primary atlas readout should be interpreted as a negative Egr2 loss-of-function screen result rather than as evidence for a robust neuronal Egr2 program.
cell_types: 21 Egr2-tested neuronal classes
main_caveats: FDR-level nulls are frequent in the full file, and direct target engagement was not observed at the Egr2 transcript.

summary: The null Egr2 phenotype was not confined to low-sampled guide pools or to one missing cell type.
why_it_matters: The largest Egr2 guide pools still had zero FDR-significant genes, and nominal outliers were non-recurrent, arguing against a hidden, coherent response in a single high-power neuronal class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Power still varied from 31 to 184 Egr2 cells per class, and the lack of on-target knockdown prevents assigning the null to biological buffering alone.

summary: Egr2 perturbation did not trigger FDR-level compensation through the measured Egr paralogs, NAB corepressors, or AP-1/immediate-early transcripts.
why_it_matters: Prior EGR/NAB work makes feedback through NAB genes plausible, but this neuronal Perturb-seq context did not show a detectable Egr/Nab/Fos/Jun transcriptional feedback loop after Egr2 guide assignment.
cell_types: 21 Egr2-tested neuronal classes
main_caveats: Egr paralogs and NAB cofactors were measured but not themselves perturbed; the cited feedback literature used neuroectodermal or epithelial cell models rather than the same mouse neuronal classes.

summary: Weak Egr2 signatures had no strong top signature neighbor and were essentially uncorrelated with selected activity/neurotrophin-neighbor perturbations available in the same atlas.
why_it_matters: Some pathway-neighbor perturbations, especially Mef2c and Ntrk2, generated FDR-level transcriptional effects, so the Egr2 null did not simply mirror all activity-responsive regulators in the experiment.
cell_types: 21 Egr2-tested neuronal classes
main_caveats: Comparator set was restricted for biology and correlation-based for signature-neighbor search; Egr1, Egr3, and Egr4 were not available as perturbations.

summary: The negative neuronal Egr2 result should not be used to de-prioritize EGR2 mechanisms in peripheral myelin disease or embryonic hindbrain patterning.
why_it_matters: EGR2/Krox20 disease biology is strongly tied to Schwann-cell myelination and early hindbrain segmentation, whereas the Egr2 contrast here sampled postnatal brain neuronal classes and showed no target engagement.
cell_types: 21 Egr2-tested neuronal classes
main_caveats: The parquet file does not contain the Schwann-cell or embryonic rhombomere contexts that dominate the cited literature.

summary: Micos13 knockdown produced measurable depletion of its own transcript but no genome-wide significant downstream transcriptional response in any assayed mouse brain cell type.
why_it_matters: MICOS13 is a cristae-organizing inner-membrane subunit, so the absence of any FDR<0.05 response indicates that this Perturb-seq readout is buffered, underpowered, or not measuring the structural mitochondrial phenotype expected from stronger MICOS13 loss.
main_caveats: The negative result is statistically strong, but the mechanistic interpretation is limited by incomplete FDR support, unknown protein depletion, and a transcriptomic rather than ultrastructural or respiratory readout.

direction: nominally up in Zfp687; nominally down in Ppm1f and Micos13
summary: The closest-to-significant Micos13 effects were concentrated in subcortical GABAergic classes rather than forming a pan-neuronal signature.
why_it_matters: The two only FDR<0.10 rows arose in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and the strongest on-target depletion was in 191 MB P MY GABA; this suggests that any captured Micos13 response is cell-type restricted and should be followed up in those inhibitory populations.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: No response gene reached FDR<0.05; the apparent restriction is hypothesis-generating and could reflect guide abundance, baseline expression, or power differences.

direction: Micos13 weaker and uncorrelated with comparators
summary: The Micos13 signature was uncoupled from stronger Opa1, Dnm1l, and respiratory-chain perturbations present in the same screen.
why_it_matters: MICOS and OPA1 both control cristae, and several OXPHOS subunits produced significant signatures, but Micos13 had zero FDR<0.05 rows and near-zero full-vector correlations with Opa1, Dnm1l, and Mff; MICOS13 loss therefore did not collapse onto a generic mitochondrial-dysfunction transcriptome.
main_caveats: Opa1, Dnm1l, fission, and respiratory-chain genes are pathway neighbors rather than MICOS13 paralogs; differences in target engagement could drive some contrast.

direction: negative in CB GABA and weak globally
summary: The broad mouse brain mRNA response does not reproduce the cerebellar and oxidative-phosphorylation disease phenotype reported for human MICOS13 deficiency.
why_it_matters: Human MICOS13 mutations cause a structural mitochondrial hepato-encephalopathy with cristae and OXPHOS defects, including cerebellar/vermis atrophy in one report, whereas 308 CB GABA showed no Micos13 target engagement and the full perturbation lacked a recurring OXPHOS stress signature.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA is a broad class and may not match vulnerable human cerebellar neurons; the guide did not measurably reduce Micos13 transcript in that class.

summary: The screen did not expose a MICOS core-member convergence or a robust nonself signature neighbor for Micos13.
why_it_matters: Most core MICOS/MIB partners were absent as perturbation targets, and whole-transcriptome nearest-neighbor correlations were very weak even in the nominally engaged Micos13 classes; the dataset therefore should not be used to infer interchangeability among MICOS components.
main_caveats: The absence of targeted MICOS subunits is a screen-design limitation, not evidence that the complex lacks coordinated function.

direction: loss of function is potentially deleterious
summary: The loss-of-function perturbation and human disease genetics argue against interpreting Micos13 inhibition as a safe or useful therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: Biallelic MICOS13 loss is pathogenic in humans, Open Targets listed no chemical probes or clinical small-molecule/antibody tractability for MICOS13, and the mouse loss-of-function screen produced no robust compensatory neuronal program, making inhibition biology more consistent with toxicity than rescue.
main_caveats: The screen did not test MICOS13 activation, replacement, or long-term organismal phenotypes; the warning is directional rather than a drug-efficacy result.

summary: Acute Dlat knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: the target transcript could be depleted, but non-self FDR-significant genes were absent.
why_it_matters: Dlat encodes the central PDH-complex E2 enzyme, so a broad mitochondrial or compensatory gene program might have been expected; the Perturb-seq readout instead mainly captured the primary knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: A lack of transcriptomic DE does not measure PDH enzymatic flux, acetyl-CoA, lactate, ATP, or chronic viability.

direction: 21 of 22 cell types had negative Dlat logFC, but only 151 reached FDR<0.05
summary: Measurable Dlat guide activity was strongly cell-type restricted, with one FDR-scale self knockdown and many weak or low-powered contrasts.
why_it_matters: Most apparent cell-type differences in downstream genes should be interpreted after conditioning on target engagement, not as primary Dlat biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut|053 Sst Gaba|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Some large logFC estimates came from only 32-55 perturbed cells, and the experiment measured RNA rather than protein.

summary: PDH-complex membership did not translate into shared single-cell transcriptional signatures for Dlat, Pdha1, Pdhb, Pdhx, or Dld.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating all PDH-complex perturbations as interchangeable in this assay; their common metabolic complex is not visible as a common acute RNA module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Most compared perturbations had sparse downstream DE, so low correlations may partly reflect guide strength and noise rather than different metabolic consequences.

direction: partial transcript down with little downstream RNA change
summary: The dataset supports an RNA-buffered, partial-loss model rather than an immediate PDH-deficiency-like transcriptional collapse after Dlat knockdown.
why_it_matters: Human DLAT loss is linked to neurological pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 deficiency, but the disease mechanism is likely metabolic flux, development, and longer exposure rather than a large early transcriptional module detectable in every neuronal class.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment was in mouse brain cells and did not model biallelic congenital DLAT loss, metabolic acidosis, basal ganglia pathology, or long-term selection.

direction: no overt acute RNA toxicity under partial knockdown
summary: Absence of a stress program after partial Dlat RNA knockdown should not be mistaken for safety of manipulating DLAT or lipoylated-TCA/cuproptosis biology in the brain.
why_it_matters: DLAT sits in an essential mitochondrial complex and is in the lipoylated-protein biology exploited by copper-dependent killing, while human DLAT deficiency is neurological; transcriptomic quiescence is therefore a weak safety endpoint.
main_caveats: No copper challenge, inhibitor, metabolic flux, protein loss, or survival assay was performed, and ChEMBL contains only sparse direct DLAT pharmacology.

summary: Dlat signatures did not have a reproducible positive or negative perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak, non-recurrent nearest-neighbor structure prevents a strong claim that Dlat knockdown phenocopies another receptor, transcription factor, or metabolic target in this screen.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from Wilcoxon score vectors within each cell type and is still affected by guide efficiency and cell count.

summary: Nr5a2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response and its own RNA was not Wilcoxon-detectably reduced in the measured rows.
why_it_matters: NR5A2 is a DNA-binding nuclear receptor, so a strong knockdown in an expressing cell would be expected to affect target genes; the dominant interpretation here is low expression, undetectable RNA-level engagement, or both, rather than a robust LRH-1 program.
main_caveats: Only differential-expression summaries were available; guide cutting or protein depletion could not be measured directly, and low/zero target counts can create large logFC values with near-zero Wilcoxon scores.

summary: The nominal Nr5a2 hits were sparse singleton events rather than a recurrent downstream module or a reproducible best-matching perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-reading isolated genes such as Cd47, Sfxn3, Ensa, Atf7, or Bdnf as LRH-1 effectors in this dataset.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative interpretation from recurrence and correlation summaries; no pathway enrichment on raw cells was available.

summary: Brain Nr5a2 signatures were uncoupled from Wnt/beta-catenin pathway-neighbor signatures despite the known physical LRH-1/beta-catenin interaction.
why_it_matters: NR5A2 can cooperate directly with beta-catenin in other systems, but in the thalamic and broader brain screen Ctnnb1, Apc, and Tcf7l2 perturbations generated strong signatures while Nr5a2 remained weak and nearly uncorrelated.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The strongest contrast is driven by the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class; Nr5a2 was not itself significantly engaged, so the finding is best read as absence of an endogenous LRH-1/Wnt module in these cells.

summary: The dataset does not recapitulate the reported NR5A2 pro-neurogenic program, refining it to neural stem/progenitor and dentate-gyrus contexts rather than broad mature brain cell types.
why_it_matters: Published gain- and loss-of-function studies make LRH-1 attractive for neurogenesis, but the Perturb-seq atlas argues that most assayed adult neuronal classes, including hypothalamus-labeled classes, are not transcriptionally poised for a large cell-autonomous response to Nr5a2 perturbation.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The screen did not isolate adult neural stem/progenitor cells or dentate-gyrus developmental trajectories, so it cannot test the contexts in which the literature found positive NR5A2 activity.

summary: Nr5a2 and its NR5A1/SF-1 paralog did not behave as interchangeable brain perturbations.
why_it_matters: Some LRH-1 chemical scaffolds also activate SF-1, but the mouse-brain signatures showed near-zero Nr5a2-Nr5a1 correlation and only one Nr5a1 FDR hit across matched cell types; dual agonist results should therefore not be assumed to represent a shared neuronal NR5A module.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic contrast with weak Nr5a2 target engagement and does not directly assay ligand pharmacology or SF-1 protein activity.

summary: Abhd12 CRISPRi produced broad, directionally consistent target-transcript loss, but the FDR-significant response was confined to Abhd12 itself.
why_it_matters: The main measurable effect of knocking down a brain lyso-PS and 2-AG hydrolase was loss of the target RNA rather than a neuronal transcriptional cascade, shifting interpretation toward lipid-level, protein-level, non-cell-autonomous, or chronic mechanisms.

main_caveats: The assay measured RNA rather than ABHD12 protein or lyso-PS, and CRISPRi knockdown left residual Abhd12 transcript.

summary: The dopaminergic Abhd12 result is underpowered and weakly engaged rather than a convincing dopaminergic-specific absence.
why_it_matters: A disease-relevant midbrain/pontine dopaminergic label had only 21 perturbed cells and no nominal Abhd12 depletion, so it should not be used to argue that dopaminergic neurons are ABHD12-insensitive.

main_caveats: This is a data-quality interpretation, not evidence for biology in dopaminergic neurons.

summary: Uncorrected non-target hits failed to cohere into recurring biomarkers or a pathway module.
why_it_matters: Fold-change outliers such as Fgfr1op2, Ptcd3, Trub2, Atp11a, Sez6, and Edil3 were all FDR-insignificant, and nominal p<0.001 genes were mostly singletons, so they should not be promoted as ABHD12 response markers.
main_caveats: Nominal p-value patterns can be useful for follow-up selection but are not robust discoveries here.

direction: literature microgliosis not mirrored by acute neuronal RNA response
summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq panel did not reproduce the microglial inflammatory PHARC axis despite strong Abhd12 RNA knockdown.
why_it_matters: ABHD12 loss is known to elevate brain lyso-PS before microglial activation and PHARC-like auditory or motor phenotypes in mice; the acute neuronal transcriptomic silence narrows that biology to lipid remodeling, glial/innate-immune responses, non-cell-autonomous signaling, or longer time scales rather than an immediate neuronal gene-expression program.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks explicit microglial perturbation groups, has no lipidomics, and may assay an earlier or weaker loss-of-function state than germline Abhd12-null animals.

summary: A silent acute neuronal RNA profile is not a safety argument for ABHD12 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Human loss-of-function causes PHARC, and selective ABHD12 blockade can elevate brain lyso-PS and stimulate innate immune responses in vivo; therefore a neuronal CRISPRi panel that detects only target-RNA loss would miss the major predicted pharmacodynamic and chronic safety liabilities.
main_caveats: Genetic CRISPRi and acute pharmacological enzyme blockade are not identical, and the dataset contains no infection, auditory, lipid, or microglial readouts.

summary: The dataset could not test the expected ABHD12 lyso-PS/endocannabinoid neighborhood directly.
why_it_matters: STRING and biochemical work place ABHD12 near ABHD16A, ABHD6, MGLL, FAAH, NAPEPLD, DAGLA and DAGLB, but these genes were absent from the perturbation library; the only other Abhd-family target, Abhd2, had no FDR-level self knockdown, making lack of convergence uninterpretable.
main_caveats: This finding concerns library coverage and comparator engagement rather than a confirmed ABHD-family divergence.

direction: no strong positive or negative correlation
summary: A whole-library score-vector scan found no strong Abhd12 signature neighbor or inverse neighbor.
why_it_matters: The nearest positive and negative correlations were small, so biologically meaningful target convergence or opposition should not be inferred from global transcriptional profile similarity.
main_caveats: The scan is restricted to transcriptional scores and is less informative when the query perturbation is itself nearly self-only.

direction: Gnao1 down; trans response absent after FDR correction
summary: The clearest Gnao1 phenotypes are clean cis knockdowns in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with essentially no FDR-significant trans transcriptional program.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The assay measures RNA rather than Gαo protein, receptor-coupled second-messenger flux, synaptic release, or gain-of-function disease alleles.

summary: Gnao1 did not phenocopy the engaged heterotrimeric G-protein beta subunit Gnb1 or the engaged Gi/o-coupled receptor Grm7 in cell types where target knockdown was effective.
why_it_matters: The result argues that loss of one alpha subunit produces a much narrower transcriptional state than simply disabling the same heterotrimer or an upstream Gi/o receptor.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Comparison is transcriptomic; Grm7 engagement was decisive only in the thalamic class; GNB/Gα stoichiometry can be buffered post-transcriptionally.

summary: Canonical Gs/cAMP and nearby phospholipase perturbations were essentially uncorrelated with Gnao1 in the two clean Gnao1 cell classes and in the L4/5 cortical class.
why_it_matters: Gαo is linked to adenylyl-cyclase and cAMP regulation, but this dataset does not show a simple cAMP-transcriptomic axis after Gnao1 RNA loss.

main_caveats: Several cAMP-effector perturbations had weak direct target engagement, so the contrast is strongest as absence of Gnao1-like transcriptomic convergence rather than proof that second-messenger signaling was unchanged.

summary: The Rho/Rock transcript response reported after Gnao1 depletion in differentiating Neuro2a/iPSC systems was not evident in the three most informative brain-cell Gnao1 profiles.
why_it_matters: It cautions against using a developmental Rho-GTPase expression module as a universal biomarker of Gnao1 loss in postmitotic brain Perturb-seq data.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only a small canonical marker panel was inspected; the literature used neuroblastoma and developing human neuronal models rather than acutely perturbed adult-like mouse neuronal classes.

summary: Layer 4/5 IT cortical neurons nominated Puf60 as the only FDR-significant trans marker of Gnao1 perturbation, but this is an isolated exploratory signal.
why_it_matters: The Puf60 hit is the only adjusted trans response in the entire Gnao1 scan and therefore deserves preservation even though it is not a canonical Gαo effector.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Gnao1 itself was just above FDR<0.05 in this cell type and Puf60 was not recurrent in the clean thalamic or midbrain cell classes.

summary: A genome-wide perturbation-neighbor scan did not identify a robust positive or negative Gnao1 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The absence of a high-correlation neighbor prevents a spurious assignment of Gnao1 to a novel pathway based solely on weak rank correlations.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Pearson correlations used whole-score vectors and will miss sparse, post-transcriptional, or temporally offset convergence.

summary: The null Cd27 response is consistent with CD27 being an immune costimulatory receptor rather than a neuron-autonomous receptor in glutamatergic, GABAergic, or dopaminergic brain classes.

cell_types: Glutamatergic neuron classes|GABAergic neuron classes|Dopaminergic neuron class
main_caveats: The experiment lacks a CD27-positive lymphocyte population, and the HPA expression context is mostly human or regional mouse atlas evidence rather than cells from this exact perturbation.

summary: Cd27 signatures did not converge with assayed TNFR/NF-kB family perturbations, including Cd40, Traf3, Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Chuk, Tnfrsf4, and Tnfrsf9.

summary: The neuronal Cd27 loss-of-function null should not be used to de-risk or deprioritize CD27 agonism in cancer immunotherapy.
why_it_matters: Clinical and ChEMBL records describe agonist antibodies to CD27; those drugs are intended to activate immune costimulation, whereas this dataset performs loss-of-function perturbations in mostly CD27-silent neuronal classes.
main_caveats: A null neuronal CRISPRi/CRISPR response can only argue against neuron-autonomous Cd27 activity in this assay; it does not test antibody crosslinking, CD70 engagement, or tumor-immune microenvironments.

direction: Lamp2 down; downstream response not FDR-detectable
summary: Lamp2 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered in the two cell types with FDR-significant target depletion.
