main_caveats: The assay measures steady-state mRNA after a partial perturbation and cannot score lysosomal flux, LAMP2A protein at lysosomes, or protein aggregation directly.

direction: stronger target knockdown in selected non-cortical classes; weak or wrong-way target estimates in several others
summary: Effective Lamp2 depletion was concentrated in non-cortical GABAergic, hypothalamic/thalamic, and midbrain classes rather than being uniform across neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The Human Protein Atlas describes LAMP2 as broadly expressed, so the dataset’s cell-type gradient is most safely interpreted as perturbation engagement and buffering context rather than simple absence of the gene from brain.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|053 Sst Gaba|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Guide delivery, guide efficacy, basal expression, cell number, and cell survival can all shape apparent engagement; the cell-type pattern should not be read as a Lamp2 dependency map.

summary: Rgs11 was a singleton exploratory marker of Lamp2 perturbation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut cells.
why_it_matters: Rgs11 was the only non-target FDR hit in the entire Lamp2 analysis, making it a compact candidate state marker for follow-up even though it does not define a recurrent lysosomal program.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only 49 perturbed cells supported the contrast, Lamp2 itself was FDR 0.0937 rather than FDR<0.05, and the Rgs11 response was not recurrent across Lamp2 cell types.

summary: Canonical CMA and macroautophagy transcripts did not show mRNA compensation after Lamp2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Because LAMP2A works with HSPA8 on the lysosomal membrane in CMA, an Hspa8- or Atg/Sqstm1/Map1lc3a-level compensatory RNA signature would have been straightforward to detect if it were large; it was absent at FDR<0.05.
main_caveats: The absence is an mRNA-level result for selected measured genes; autophagic flux, LAMP2 splice isoforms, lysosomal pH and protein turnover were not assayed.

summary: Lamp2 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with available Hspa8, macroautophagy, lysosomal, and mTOR-pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: Reactome and STRING place LAMP2 in a lysosomal/CMA neighborhood, but the Perturb-seq signatures did not form a shared transcriptomic module with the tested neighboring genes, while Tsc1/Tsc2 perturbations showed that strong responses were detectable in the same cell classes.
main_caveats: Several ideal comparators, including Lamp1, Cd63, Tfeb and Tfe3, were not present as perturbation targets; some tested autophagy targets had weak on-target repression.

direction: partial neuronal knockdown buffered relative to full LAMP2 deficiency
summary: The mouse neuronal Perturb-seq phenotype is far milder than the organismal LAMP2-deficiency phenotype, so lack of an acute RNA program should not be interpreted as functional null tolerance.
why_it_matters: Human Danon disease and Lamp2-null mice show that complete LAMP2 deficiency causes autophagic vacuolar disease, whereas this dataset mainly shows partial, cell-type-limited mRNA depletion with little corrected RNA response.
main_caveats: Disease evidence comes from full genetic deficiency and non-neuronal pathology as well as neuronal Lamp2a models; the Perturb-seq data do not measure heart or skeletal muscle.

summary: Lamp2 knockdown signatures are not a useful argument for pharmacologic LAMP2 inhibition, and Danon translation is instead restoration-oriented.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL did not reveal annotated mechanism-of-action LAMP2 modulators, while Danon trials are evaluating AAV9.LAMP2B restoration; a buffered mRNA response after partial neuronal knockdown does not establish that reducing LAMP2 function would be safe or beneficial.
main_caveats: The dataset contains perturbational transcriptomics only and no drug exposure, cardiac readout, AAV restoration, or lysosomal rescue experiment.

summary: Ogfrl1-targeting perturbation did not produce a reproducible FDR-significant neuronal transcriptomic phenotype in this Perturb-seq panel.
why_it_matters: The safest global interpretation is a negative or under-engaged perturbation rather than a pathway hit; broad brain expression annotations are not sufficient evidence that acute Ogfrl1 knockdown reprograms adult neuronal mRNA profiles.
main_caveats: This cannot distinguish true biological buffering from weak CRISPR engagement or insufficient power for small effects.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the strongest observed on-target context, but the partial Ogfrl1 decrease was buffered at the downstream DE level.
why_it_matters: This cell type is the best candidate for validation because the target row moved in the expected direction with the largest cell count, yet even here no transcript passed FDR correction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Target logFC was small and the target FDR was 1.0; the result supports prioritization for re-assay, not a confirmed TH Prkcd-specific function.

summary: Ric8a, Hs3st1, Ppa1, Itm2c, and Rreb1 were the largest nominal Ogfrl1-responsive genes, but their signals were isolated and below FDR significance.
why_it_matters: These genes should be treated as weak follow-up biomarkers rather than as an Ogfrl1 pathway, because the best nominal hits clustered in low-engagement or low-count cell types and did not recur across contexts.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: All adjusted p values were at least 0.230; the two strongest contexts either lacked target depletion or had only 28 perturbed cells.

summary: Ogfrl1 signatures were uncoupled from canonical opioid receptor perturbations in the same cell types.
why_it_matters: The protein name could suggest opioid-receptor-like signaling, but the Perturb-seq signatures for Oprd1, Oprk1, Oprl1, and Oprm1 neither converged with nor opposed Ogfrl1; database paralogy instead points to Ogfr, which was not assayed.
main_caveats: The strict Ogfr paralog was absent, so the comparison tests canonical opioid receptors rather than the closest growth-factor receptor paralog.

summary: Autoinflammatory MAPK/NF-kB/TNF biology reported for OGFRL1 loss was not recapitulated by Ogfrl1-targeting perturbation in neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: Existing disease reports point toward myeloid and osteoclast inflammatory contexts; the absence of Il6, Tnf, Ccl2, or NF-kB/MAPK induction here argues that this mouse-brain neuronal assay is not a surrogate for CRMO or cherubism mechanisms.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment assayed neuronal steady-state RNA after CRISPR perturbation and did not include myeloid cells, osteoclasts, bone microenvironment, or inflammatory challenge.

summary: An unbiased signature-neighbor search found no strong recurrent Ogfrl1 neighbor, positive or negative.
why_it_matters: The lack of a nearest-neighbor module further weakens pathway assignments from single nominal genes and suggests that Ogfrl1 did not phenocopy an assayed pathway member under these conditions.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on weak Ogfrl1 signatures, so low similarity may reflect noise in the query signature as well as biological disconnection.

summary: Efemp1 guide assignment produced no detectable on-target mRNA reduction in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Without target engagement, the experiment is best interpreted as a neuronal null test rather than evidence that fibulin-3 biology is dispensable.
main_caveats: The result reports Efemp1 mRNA ranks in the captured cells; it cannot exclude editing of non-expressed loci or extracellular protein carry-over from other cell types.

summary: Efemp1 lacked any FDR-supported downstream transcriptomic response across 338,323 tested gene rows.
why_it_matters: The few nominal hits do not form a recurring module and are compatible with weak engagement plus low cell numbers rather than a reproducible Efemp1 program.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Nominal p values identify cells to inspect but were not reliable after testing roughly seventeen thousand genes in each cell type.

summary: The neuronal null result fits a model in which EFEMP1 is mainly an extracellular/glial or epithelial effector that is poorly assayed in Glut/GABA Perturb-seq cells.
why_it_matters: It narrows the negative result: EFEMP1-linked matrix and retinal-deposit mechanisms should be tested in astrocytes, choroid/ependymal cells, vascular or RPE-like systems rather than inferred from these neuronal signatures.
main_caveats: Human atlas and retinal-disease evidence are not matched to mouse neuronal perturbation; the inference is based on absence of engagement in the assayed cell types.

summary: Known EFEMP1 EGFR/TIMP3 extracellular relationships did not resolve into a neuronal EGFR/MAPK or TIMP-family transcriptomic module.
why_it_matters: The dataset should not be used to assign a neuronal direction of EGFR, Akt/MAPK, or TIMP3 signaling downstream of Efemp1; the pathway evidence comes from extracellular protein systems with very different context.
main_caveats: The Timp2 relationship is restricted-signature-only and exploratory; Egfr itself was not an Efemp1 dataset comparator.

summary: Cdkl5 self-knockdown was highly cell-type selective and reached FDR significance only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Most cell-type signatures should be treated as weak-engagement readouts rather than as evidence that Cdkl5 loss is inert in those neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Selectivity may reflect gRNA delivery, CRISPRi efficacy, Cdkl5 basal expression, or power; several cell types had fewer than 50 Cdkl5-perturbed cells.

summary: The best-engaged Cdkl5 perturbation lowered Cdkl5 mRNA in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut without producing any FDR-significant downstream transcript.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from downstream RNA propagation and is consistent with CDKL5 acting primarily through phosphorylation, synaptic, cytoskeletal, or circuit endpoints that may not be captured by a single-cell RNA snapshot.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No CDKL5 protein, kinase-activity, phosphoproteomic, electrophysiology, or long time-course measurement is available.

summary: Cdkl5 perturbation yielded no recurrent FDR-level gene module in any of the 22 assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: Nominal hits should not be promoted to pathway biomarkers unless they are replicated by an orthogonal assay or a stronger Cdkl5 perturbation.
main_caveats: The conclusion is limited to the measured RNA endpoint and depends on the adjusted p values already present in the parquet.

summary: The engaged Cdkl5 thalamic signature was not MECP2-, FOXG1-, or broader DEE-like at the whole-transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: CDD overlaps clinically with Rett and other DEEs, but this dataset argues against a shared acute RNA state in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to scRNA signatures in a single well-engaged Cdkl5 cell type, and some comparator perturbations may have different target-engagement strengths.

summary: Knocking down Mapre2, the EB2 substrate gene available in the library, did not phenocopy Cdkl5 even in the same thalamic cell class where both transcripts were depleted.
why_it_matters: The CDKL5-to-EB2 relationship is a phosphorylation relationship; simply reducing Mapre2 mRNA is not the same perturbation as blocking EB2 phosphorylation by CDKL5.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Most known CDKL5 substrates were not targets in the perturbation library, and Hdac4 itself was not significantly depleted.

summary: The weak Cdkl5 RNA signature should not be read as evidence that CDKL5 is dispensable or that kinase inhibition would be tolerated.
why_it_matters: Human genetics and mouse rescue studies point to loss of CDKL5 activity as pathogenic, so disease-correction screens need CDKL5 protein or phospho-substrate markers in addition to steady-state mRNA.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation dataset did not test CDKL5 restoration, antiseizure drugs, or phenotypic rescue.

summary: Lrif1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant differential-expression hit in any measured brain cell type.
why_it_matters: This is the primary dataset-grounded interpretation: apparent cell-type extrema remain nominal and do not define a reliable Lrif1 transcriptional program.
main_caveats: The null is at the RNA level and depends on modest per-cell-type perturbed-cell counts; 215 MB Dopa was not represented.

summary: The measured Lrif1 transcript was not significantly reduced in any Lrif1-tested cell class.
why_it_matters: Weak target engagement keeps the downstream null from being interpretable as definitive biological buffering of LRIF1 loss.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Target mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for editing and protein depletion.

summary: Lrif1 did not phenocopy Smchd1 even though prior work places LRIF1 with SMCHD1 and HP1 proteins in heterochromatin compaction.
why_it_matters: This prevents assignment of the weak Lrif1 signature to the canonical SMCHD1-HP1 module in this brain screen.
main_caveats: Lrif1 and Smchd1 were both weak perturbations at the expression level; HP1 paralogs were not direct perturbation comparators.

summary: Lrif1 and Rara perturbations were nearly uncorrelated despite the reported LRIF1-RARalpha corepressor interaction.
why_it_matters: The RARA link is not sufficient to explain the neuronal Lrif1 score pattern; ligand state and assay context probably dominate that relationship.
main_caveats: The screen did not assay retinoic-acid stimulation or RARA reporter activity.

summary: An unbiased screen-wide comparison found no robust positive or negative Lrif1 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Weak individual gene p values did not conceal a coherent perturbation module shared with another target.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Pearson correlation across all assayed genes can miss very sparse shared effects.

summary: The literature-supported disease direction is LRIF1 loss of function, while the brain dataset shows no beneficial response to Lrif1 reduction.
why_it_matters: A null mouse-brain signature should not be reinterpreted as support for LRIF1 inhibition; human FSHD2 biology predicts that insufficient LRIF1 can derepress pathogenic DUX4.
main_caveats: FSHD2 is a human skeletal-muscle repeat-silencing disease and is not directly modeled by the mouse-brain transcriptome.

summary: Cd2ap targeting did not achieve FDR-significant depletion of the Cd2ap transcript in any profiled neuronal cell type.
why_it_matters: The primary expected RNA readout was absent, so downstream nulls should be interpreted as weak target engagement rather than as evidence that CD2AP is dispensable in neurons.
main_caveats: The DE table reports RNA abundance only; it does not measure guide efficiency, CD2AP protein, or guide alleles directly.

summary: Across all 371,818 Cd2ap differential-expression tests, no gene passed FDR<0.05 and the nominal p-value tail was smaller than expected under a uniform null.
why_it_matters: No cell class produced a statistically supported Cd2ap response module, including the best-sampled groups, so pathway and biomarker interpretation should not be based on isolated nominal genes.
main_caveats: All signatures had modest numbers of perturbed cells, and the buffered response is confounded by the weak on-target Cd2ap transcript effect.

summary: A targeted panel of CD2AP interactome, actin/endocytic, and Alzheimer-neighbor genes was not transcriptionally reprogrammed after Cd2ap perturbation.
why_it_matters: CD2AP is annotated as an adaptor for actin, nephrin/podocin, CBL-family, RIN3, SH3BP1, and endocytic partners, yet those prior-knowledge neighbors did not become differentially expressed in this assay.
main_caveats: The selected genes are a literature and database panel, not a prespecified enrichment set; lack of RNA changes cannot rule out CD2AP protein-complex or subcellular phenotypes.

summary: The same experiment could deplete several Alzheimer or endocytic transcripts, especially App, Dnm1, and Sorl1, whereas Cd2ap and local adaptor neighbors were mostly unengaged at RNA level.
why_it_matters: This separates Cd2ap from an assay-wide failure of endocytic or Alzheimer-gene perturbations: the Cd2ap result is a target-specific null, while convergence with disease-family signatures cannot be inferred.
main_caveats: The comparison uses on-target transcript depletion counts, not full-signature correlations; guide efficacy and basal expression differ by target.

summary: The dataset offers no support for direct CD2AP inhibition as a neuronal therapeutic direction, while prior work shows dose-sensitive neuronal and renal phenotypes from CD2AP loss.
why_it_matters: CD2AP biology is dominated by scaffolded actin, endosomal, and slit-diaphragm protein complexes rather than a ligandable enzymatic activity; a weak neuronal RNA knockdown screen is therefore insufficient to predict benefit or safety of reducing CD2AP.
main_caveats: No drug, rescue, morphology, amyloid, synaptic-activity, vascular, or kidney phenotypes were measured in this Perturb-seq table.

direction: Dpm1 target transcript mostly down; downstream response buffered
summary: Dpm1 knockdown produced consistent but shallow target depletion and an almost completely FDR-buffered whole-transcriptome response.
why_it_matters: DPM1 is the catalytic Dol-P-Man synthase subunit, so a strong loss should affect several ER glycosylation branches. The screen instead reads as partial depletion with substantial residual pathway capacity.
main_caveats: The result is transcriptional only and weak guide engagement can mask protein or glycan changes.

direction: strongest nominal downregulation in midbrain/thalamic and hypothalamic classes
summary: Nominal target engagement was concentrated in a few subcortical neuronal classes rather than being uniform across the brain cell types assayed.
why_it_matters: A broadly expressed core glycosylation gene would not predict this restricted nominal mRNA depletion pattern; it identifies the cell types in which Dpm1 data are most interpretable.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Defined by target-transcript ranks and nominal p values, not by FDR-significant Dpm1 depletion.

direction: ER folding genes nominally up; Dpm1 and Ttyh3 down
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained the only sub-FDR-0.10 Dpm1 response and showed a narrow nominal ER folding / lipid-linked-glycan compensation pattern.
why_it_matters: The co-upregulation of Pdia6, Hspa5, Pdia3, Rft1 and Ddit3 is directionally consistent with a small ER proteostasis challenge from reduced Dol-P-Man production, making this the best biomarker hypothesis rather than a robust pathway call.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Ttyh3 and Pdia6 reached FDR<0.10; the ER interpretation depends on several nominal genes.

summary: Upstream dolichol synthesis and the Manf perturbation produced strong ER-stress signatures where Dpm1 was nearly silent.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the screen was capable of detecting chaperone induction, but that partial Dpm1 knockdown did not phenocopy a stronger disturbance to ER glycoprotein homeostasis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Dhdds target transcript knockdown itself was not FDR-significant, so its stronger downstream phenotype could include perturbation-specific or guide-specific effects.

summary: Dpm1 did not align with the STT3B N-glycosylation perturbation nor with any strong recurrent signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Even among glycosylation-related targets, the Dpm1 signature was not a generic N-glycosylation block; the exact DPM2/DPM3 complex comparison was unavailable in this panel.
main_caveats: The correlation used Dpm1 top-100 nominal genes and the strongest global neighbors were extremely weak.

direction: avoid loss-of-function as a therapeutic strategy
summary: The muted Perturb-seq phenotype should not be interpreted as evidence that DPM1 inhibition is safe in neurons.
why_it_matters: Human DPM1 loss of function causes congenital glycosylation disease and dystroglycanopathy, while this dataset used partial transcript knockdown with no glycan readout and no mature inhibitor context.
main_caveats: Disease evidence is human germline loss of function, whereas the screen is acute mouse-brain CRISPRi.

summary: Litaf perturbation was globally buffered or unengaged: the target transcript was not significantly reduced and no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 in any profiled class.
why_it_matters: This establishes that the primary dataset result for Litaf is negative; nominal genes should not be read as a full LITAF loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: The assay may have weak guide activity or sparse Litaf target RNA, and four profiles had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: The only cell-type structure was weak and nominal, with the smallest adjusted P values in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 054 CNU-MGE GABA but no corrected genes or shared module.
why_it_matters: These two profiles should be treated as prioritization hints for validation rather than as evidence of a real selective Litaf response.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: No gene passed FDR<0.10, and Litaf target engagement was not significant in either cell class.

summary: Litaf did not phenocopy active endolysosomal perturbations in the same dataset, despite literature placing LITAF with ESCRT/NEDD4 endosome-to-lysosome trafficking.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates LITAF from core neuronal lysosome acidification and Rab7-like programs; LITAF may be specialized, redundant, or simply not knocked down in these cells.
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations differ in target engagement and essentiality; Litaf correlations are restricted to mRNA signatures and weak Litaf engagement limits causal interpretation.

summary: The inflammatory LPS/TNF branch of LITAF biology was transcriptionally silent in the assayed neuron-rich brain panel.
why_it_matters: A gene first defined by LPS-driven TNF regulation in monocytes did not couple to TLR/TNF-receptor responses in these baseline neuronal contrasts, arguing against interpreting Litaf here as an innate-cytokine perturbation.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks stimulated macrophages or microglia and many TLR target transcripts were sparsely detected, so it only tests basal neuronal responsiveness.

summary: The Litaf negative result should not be used to dismiss CMT1C biology, because the dataset is central-neuronal and under-engaged whereas CMT1C is a dominant LITAF-domain membrane disease of peripheral nerve and Schwann-cell contexts.
why_it_matters: It prevents a false disease conclusion from a mismatched perturbation: pathogenic missense variants can mislocalize or destabilize LITAF even if partial mRNA loss in central neurons is buffered.
main_caveats: The experiment measured transcriptomic effects rather than LITAF protein topology, endosome ultrastructure, or Schwann-cell myelination.

summary: Avpr1a perturbation did not show measurable Avpr1a transcript engagement in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: Without detectable target depletion, downstream nulls are most safely interpreted as an under-engaged or low-expression perturbation rather than definitive AVPR1A biology.
main_caveats: Self logFC values are unstable for sparse transcripts; absence of mRNA depletion does not prove that every guide failed.

summary: The Avpr1a perturbation was nearly transcriptomically silent across the full 22-cell-type panel.
why_it_matters: A curated AVP GPCR would be expected to have downstream signaling capacity, yet the measured steady-state response contained only one FDR-significant gene, emphasizing either technical under-engagement or buffering outside ligand-gated states.
main_caveats: The finding is about this transcriptomic assay; it does not rule out electrophysiologic, calcium, circuit, or behavior-level AVPR1A effects.

summary: Srsf6 up-regulation in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut was the only genome-wide significant Avpr1a-associated expression change.
why_it_matters: This preserves the lone cell-type-specific positive result while separating it from a pathway claim.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene hit with no FDR-supported companions and no measured Avpr1a self-knockdown in the same cell type.

summary: AVP/OXT receptor-family and Plcb1 perturbations did not converge with Avpr1a despite receptor-family relatedness.
why_it_matters: The data argue against treating Avpr1a, Avpr1b, Avpr2, Oxtr, and Plcb1 perturbations as interchangeable transcriptomic proxies in this mouse-brain screen.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Most related receptor perturbations were themselves weak, and no matched receptor protein or ligand-response assay was measured.

summary: Avpr1a perturbation did not elicit detectable transcriptional compensation in AVP/OXT ligands, receptor paralogs, or sampled Gq/Gs effector transcripts.
why_it_matters: The absence of local ligand-receptor feedback prevents a compensatory AVP/OXT-family model from explaining the dataset.
main_caveats: Only mRNA changes in broad cell classes were tested; neuropeptide release and receptor protein adaptation were not assayed.

summary: This Avpr1a Perturb-seq profile should not be used as an AVPR1A antagonist efficacy or pharmacodynamic signature.
why_it_matters: AVPR1A is druggable and genetically linked to mouse social behavior, but this dataset lacks target engagement and robust downstream biomarkers, paralleling the broader challenge of translating V1a antagonism to ASD social endpoints.
main_caveats: Mouse guide perturbation, human pharmacologic antagonism, and clinical ASD outcomes are indirect comparators.

summary: The strongest scalar Avpr1a signature neighbors were unrelated Wdr26 and Eef2 signatures in 308 CB GABA and should be treated as low-confidence.
why_it_matters: This guards against post hoc mechanism assignment from a correlation scan when the Avpr1a signature in that cell class had no FDR-significant genes.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Records a neighbor-screen caveat, not a mechanistic Wdr26 or Eef2 claim.

direction: Ctbp1 decreased; non-target response largely absent
summary: Ctbp1 RNA knockdown was detectable in most assayed brain cell classes, but the response was transcriptionally buffered in nearly every class.
why_it_matters: CTBP1 is a multifunctional corepressor and membrane-fission protein; these data argue that partial Ctbp1 loss does not automatically propagate into a broad acute mRNA program in differentiated mouse brain neurons.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only Ctbp1 mRNA, not protein editing or CTBP enzymatic activity, was measured; FDR control is stringent over 16000-17000 genes and may hide small effects.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only cell type with a clear multi-gene Ctbp1 downstream program, marked by strong up-regulation of Stxbp2, St3gal4, F11r, Mal2, Ap1m2, Hook2, Arap2, and Usp43.
why_it_matters: The response points to a thalamic/habenular Ctbp1-sensitive output rather than a pan-neuronal CTBP program, and several induced genes encode vesicle, adaptor, or junction-associated proteins.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Ctbp1 self-transcript decrease in 151 TH was nominal but not FDR-significant; the gene set is small and lacks a formal enrichment hit.

direction: restricted Zeb1 convergence with one caveated Zeb2 anti-correlation
summary: Ctbp1 and Zeb1 converged on the 151 TH Stxbp2/Ap1m2/F11r/Hook2 module, but CTBP-related signatures were otherwise near zero across cell types.
why_it_matters: A direct CTBP-ZEB physical relationship is visible in one thalamic transcriptomic state, yet the same relationship is not interchangeable across the brain panel and should be treated as cell-state restricted.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Signature correlations were computed from all measured genes and can be dominated by weak ranks; the CB GABA Zeb2 anti-correlation was not promoted to a mechanism because Zeb2 RNA was not reduced in Zeb2-targeted cells.

summary: Stxbp2 was the most recurrent non-target readout of Ctbp1 perturbation, with one genome-wide hit and additional nominal-to-near-FDR recurrences in TH and GABA classes.
why_it_matters: Stxbp2 is a stronger candidate marker of a Ctbp1-sensitive vesicle-fusion response than any single canonical CTBP chromatin cofactor transcript in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Only the 151 TH Stxbp2 effect survived 5% FDR; the 145, 052, and 053 signals are weaker follow-up candidates.

summary: Brain Ctbp1 perturbation is not uniformly silent, so CTBP1/2 inhibitor development should account for neuronal cell-state liabilities.
why_it_matters: Human CTBP1 cleft mutations cause a neurodevelopmental ataxia syndrome, and CTBP dehydrogenase-pocket inhibitors are being structurally optimized for cancer; the mouse data identify thalamic neurons where partial Ctbp1 loss changes vesicle/junction transcripts despite only modest Ctbp1 mRNA reduction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset models mouse perturbations in brain cell classes, not human CTBP1 R342W gain/loss of interaction or pharmacologic CTBP1/2 inhibition; blood-brain-barrier exposure of candidate inhibitors was not evaluated.

summary: FDR-validated Map1lc3a mRNA depletion was transcriptionally isolated in four neuronal classes: Pvalb GABA, TH Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, MB glutamatergic, and MB/P/MY GABA.
why_it_matters: LC3A is a canonical autophagosome ATG8 protein, so the absence of any FDR-significant secondary gene after strong target knockdown is a biologically meaningful buffered-response result rather than simply a failed perturbation.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The result is mRNA-based and does not assay LC3A protein, LC3 lipidation, autophagic flux, or stress-induced selective autophagy.

summary: Map1lc3a engagement was highly cell-type selective: only four of 22 assayed cell-type rows reached target FDR<0.05, another L4/5 IT cortical row was target-rank-1 at FDR 0.088, and several rows had weak or no target engagement.
why_it_matters: Negative pathway calls outside the engaged classes are underpowered by guide performance and cell sampling; interpretation should focus on the four FDR-positive classes and treat nominal rank-1 rows as exploratory.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity could reflect basal Map1lc3a expression, guide efficacy, matched-cell counts, or detection power rather than different biological requirement for LC3A.

summary: Autophagy-neighbor perturbations were not generally buffered: Rb1cc1, Becn1, Atg5, and Depdc5 produced FDR-level secondary genes in overlapping midbrain or thalamic classes where Map1lc3a remained self-only.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the Map1lc3a null transcriptome is specific to the LC3A/ATG8 layer, not an inevitable property of this dataset or of every macroautophagy perturbation in neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparator phenotypes are not isogenic pathway-ordering experiments; each guide has its own efficiency, target expression, and downstream biology.

summary: The four validated Map1lc3a knockdowns did not trigger mRNA compensation of measured ATG8 paralogs or core autophagy transcripts, including Map1lc3b, Gabarap, Gabarapl1/2, Sqstm1, Atg5, Becn1, Rb1cc1, Lamp2, Mtor, or Rptor.

why_it_matters: Other junctional or synaptic genes generated strong signatures in the same dataset, so Nectin1's quiet profile is not simply a universal failure to perturb synaptic adhesion genes.
main_caveats: The true Nectin paralogs, Afdn, Pard3, Cadm1, and Cadm3 were not present as target perturbations; correlations with a weak Nectin1 signature are noise-sensitive.

summary: The dataset supports interpreting NECTIN1 congenital and viral phenotypes as contact-architecture or receptor biology rather than as a robust acute neuronal transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: Human NECTIN1 is linked to cleft lip/palate-ectodermal dysplasia and serves as an alphaherpesvirus entry receptor, but this mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout did not expose a disease-like transcriptional axis to activate or suppress therapeutically.
main_caveats: The disease literature is developmental, epithelial, craniofacial, auditory, or viral-entry focused, whereas the dataset perturbs mouse brain cells and measures steady-state RNA.

summary: App knockdown was strong at the target transcript but produced no FDR-level non-App downstream transcript in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant App phenotype: guide engagement was visible, but the acute mRNA state was buffered or insensitive to App transcript loss.
main_caveats: APP protein, APLP redundancy, amyloid-beta peptides, and chronic phenotypes were not measured.

direction: stronger target depletion in 151 TH and 155 MB; weak nominal target depletion in 009 and 017
summary: Cell-type variation in the App perturbation was mainly variation in target engagement strength, with two weak-engagement cell types and no cell-type-restricted downstream gene program.
why_it_matters: The dataset should not be interpreted as showing an App-responsive pathway in one neuronal class; even the most engaged classes were target-only.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Several cell types had modest matched perturbed-cell counts; target engagement is inferred from App mRNA only.

summary: Mef2c, but not App, drove a multi-gene upper-layer cortical excitatory response among Alzheimer's-linked perturbations.
why_it_matters: It separates an AD-linked transcription-factor program from direct App depletion and cautions against treating all AD-risk perturbations as mechanistically similar transcriptomic events.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is disease-family based rather than a direct APP-processing interaction; only transcriptomic effects were compared.

summary: The App signature did not phenocopy measured alpha/gamma-secretase neighbors, and several canonical processing or APP-family comparators were absent.
why_it_matters: A negative App transcriptome cannot be mapped onto APP proteolysis without engaged Adam10, Psen1, Bace1/gamma-complex, and APLP-family controls.
main_caveats: Adam10 and Psen1 were themselves not FDR-engaged; absent Bace/gamma-complex/APLP perturbations prevent a decisive pathway test.

summary: Top positive and negative whole-dataset signature neighbors based on the nominal non-App tail did not reveal a convincing hidden App module.
why_it_matters: It closes a common loophole in weak DE signatures: the leading nonself genes can correlate with other perturbations, but here those correlations were restricted, cell-type-specific, and included Safe_target-labeled neighbors.
main_caveats: The screen used only 40 nominal non-FDR genes per cell type and should not be treated as pathway evidence.

summary: The buffered App mRNA signature should not be treated as a safety or efficacy proxy for APP/Aβ-directed therapeutic strategies.
why_it_matters: BACE1 and gamma-secretase act through protein processing with many substrates, while this Perturb-seq endpoint measures acute RNA abundance after App transcript depletion.
main_caveats: No APP protein fragments, amyloid-beta peptides, Notch cleavage products, electrophysiology, or chronic toxicity measures were available.

direction: no FDR-significant DE; target transcript unmeasured
summary: Magi2 produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response, and its own transcript was absent from the DE matrix so knockdown could not be verified from the readout.
why_it_matters: This makes any downstream interpretation conditional: the Perturb-seq assay does not show a validated, robust Magi2 loss-of-function state even though external atlases detect MAGI2 in brain.
main_caveats: Absence of a Magi2 row is an assay/readout fact, not proof that the guide failed or that Magi2 is not expressed.

summary: The only visible Magi2 response was a narrow subthreshold nominal tail in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 308 CB GABA, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest genes do not support a pan-neuronal MAGI2 program; they instead identify specific cell classes that may merit follow-up if target engagement can be confirmed.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: All genes in these cell types had FDR >= 0.108; the leading genes are nominal and should be treated as markers for validation rather than discoveries.

summary: Magi2 signatures were not interchangeable with perturbations of its PTEN, NMDA-receptor, neuroligin, CACNG2, or DLG4 postsynaptic neighborhood.
why_it_matters: Physical membership in the MAGI2 postsynaptic scaffold did not translate into a matched bulk transcriptomic signature in this dataset, warning against using Pten or receptor-subunit knockdown as a proxy for Magi2.
main_caveats: The contrast uses RNA signatures with weak Magi2 target engagement and cannot rule out shared protein-localized synaptic phenotypes.

direction: Magi2 correlated positively with Akt3 and Adam10 and negatively with Tsc2, Syngap1, and Grin2b
summary: In 308 CB GABA, Magi2 had an exploratory Akt3-like and Tsc2/Syngap1-opposed signature despite the absence of significant individual genes.
why_it_matters: The polarity touches MAGI2's known PTEN/AKT signaling axis but is not a clean PTEN-loss signature, so it is best treated as a low-confidence candidate network.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The correlations were modest, derived from a 30-cell Magi2 contrast, and the nearest all-target neighbors were not a clean PTEN complex.

summary: The dataset did not recapitulate the large GABAergic or epileptic MAGI2 biology reported in synaptic and copy-number studies as a robust acute mRNA program.
why_it_matters: MAGI2 disease mechanisms may be developmental, structural, or post-transcriptional; GABAergic synapse phenotypes should not be inferred from this weak mRNA response alone.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The literature comes from human copy-number genetics and cultured hippocampal neurons, whereas the dataset uses pooled mouse-brain cell classes and an RNA readout.

summary: Mc4r CRISPRi did not produce measurable depletion of the Mc4r transcript in any assayed broad cell group.
why_it_matters: The perturbation cannot be interpreted as a clean cellular MC4R loss-of-function model without lower-level validation; downstream null results are therefore dominated by target-engagement uncertainty.
main_caveats: The result is based on Wilcoxon DE rows rather than raw guide-level expression, and a sparse receptor transcript can yield unstable logFC estimates.

summary: A selective Smox-up signal appeared in 145 MH-LH TH Glut after Mc4r perturbation, but it stood alone after FDR correction.
why_it_matters: SMOX links the only robust transcriptional hit to polyamine catabolism, making it a narrow hypothesis-generating readout rather than a validated MC4R pathway marker.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only Smox reached FDR<0.05; Adam22 and the rest of the local signature were nominal only.

summary: The 145 MH-LH TH Glut Mc4r signature was nearly orthogonal to melanocortin-family, cAMP-effector, and obesity-pathway perturbations, including engaged Cpe and Prkaca knockdowns.
why_it_matters: MC4R is expected to signal through GNAS, adenylyl cyclase, cAMP, MRAP2 modulation, and POMC/AGRP inputs; the dataset did not recover that neighborhood at the transcriptome level.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on score vectors; several related perturbations may affect only restricted subpopulations or non-transcriptional signaling.

summary: Outside the single Smox hit, Mc4r produced no recurrent FDR-supported transcriptional module and no strong positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: This argues against a broad, reproducible stress, GPCR, neuronal-activity, or obesity-gene module in the captured cells.
main_caveats: The absence of an FDR-supported module should not be read as absence of MC4R biology because the on-target transcript was not measurably depleted.

direction: dataset loss signature is weak; clinical direction is MC4R activation
summary: The Mc4r Perturb-seq profile is not a reliable proxy for pharmacologic MC4R agonism or for the in vivo obesity phenotype of Mc4r loss.
why_it_matters: MC4R has human obesity genetics and approved agonist pharmacology, but this loss-of-function Perturb-seq arm lacks target engagement and pathway recovery; using the isolated Smox response for therapeutic direction would be unsafe.
main_caveats: The warning is about this transcriptomic perturbation arm, not about MC4R as a therapeutic target.

summary: Cert1 perturbation caused no transcriptome-wide significant differential-expression hit in any measured mouse brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The most robust result is a negative mRNA result: partial Cert1 depletion did not generate a broad FDR-level transcriptional stress or lipid-metabolic program in this assay, so any biological effect is either buffered, post-transcriptional, lipid-level, delayed, or obscured by power and engagement limits.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself never reached FDR<0.05 and many cell types had only 30-55 perturbed cells; failure to detect FDR-level expression does not prove absence of lipid or protein phenotypes.

summary: The only Cert1 signature anchored by the target transcript was in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas 155 MB Glut had comparable nominal target reduction with little additional response.
why_it_matters: This separates an interpretable thalamic glutamatergic trend from a global effect: Cert1 was the top absolute row in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but a larger MB Glut sample with similar nominal knockdown still produced no FDR-significant genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All non-target genes are nominal only; the comparison is between cell classes with different guide-cell counts and does not measure ceramide or sphingomyelin.

summary: The canonical ER-Golgi ceramide and sphingomyelin pathway did not compensate transcriptionally in the most engaged Cert1 cell type.
why_it_matters: CERT1 is a direct ceramide transporter, but the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature did not show coordinated induction or repression of Sgms1/Sgms2, Vapa/Vapb, de novo sphingolipid, ceramidase, or sphingosine-kinase transcripts, consistent with a pathway controlled mainly by lipid flux, localization, and phosphorylation rather than acute mRNA feedback.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was tested; compensatory lipid flux, CERT phosphorylation, ER-Golgi contact-site localization, and sphingomyelin mass were not measured.

summary: Cert1 signatures were nearly orthogonal to VAPB and assayed sphingolipid/lipid-transfer perturbations rather than phenocopying adjacent pathway nodes.
why_it_matters: Although VAPB is a physical ER-contact partner for CERT1 and Sptlc2, Smpd3, Asah1, Sphk1, Stard7, and Osbpl2 lie near lipid metabolism, perturbing those genes did not reproduce the Cert1 score vector; the screen therefore argues against treating these transcriptomic perturbations as interchangeable pathway surrogates.
main_caveats: The correlations were computed on weak Cert1 signatures; VAPA, PPM1L, OSBP, and sphingomyelin synthases were not all available as perturbation targets.

summary: Dhcr24 is an exploratory lipid-homeostasis marker for Cert1 loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Dhcr24 was the top positive and third strongest absolute row in the only cell type whose signature was anchored by Cert1 knockdown, suggesting a possible sterol-homeostasis echo of ER-Golgi sphingolipid perturbation that would be missed by a pathway list restricted to ceramide enzymes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Dhcr24 did not pass FDR correction, and the nearest signature neighbor Pcyt2 had only r=0.125; this is a hypothesis for lipidomic follow-up, not a validated biomarker.

summary: The mouse Cert1 knockdown signature is directionally mismatched to human CERT1 neurodevelopmental missense disease, where pathogenic alleles can disrupt autoinhibition and increase sphingolipid flux.
why_it_matters: A weak partial-loss Cert1 Perturb-seq result should not be interpreted as evidence that CERT1 is dispensable in neurons or that inhibition lacks therapeutic logic for gain-of-function CerTra variants; conversely, rescue of a lipid-flux disorder may require lipid or morphology biomarkers rather than a bulk transcriptional efficacy readout.
main_caveats: The dataset did not introduce patient missense alleles, assay development, or measure sphingolipid species; the therapeutic inference is a directionality caution.

summary: Cox6a1 knockdown was directionally recurrent but FDR-fragile, with the clearest target engagement in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and only nominal engagement elsewhere.
why_it_matters: The all-negative target row confirms that the guide set generally pushed Cox6a1 in the intended direction, but most cell types are under-engaged by FDR criteria; global absence of phenotypes therefore cannot be read as a definitive Cox6a1-null result.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only one cell type reached FDR<0.10 for the target transcript and none reached FDR<0.05; several nominal rows, especially 217 P MY Pineal Glut, have low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: The best-engaged thalamic Cox6a1 perturbation reduced the target without producing any FDR-resolved non-target transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Cox6a1 encodes a complex-IV subunit, so loss of the mature protein is expected to impair respiration; this experiment instead shows that partial target-mRNA depletion in this neuronal class is buffered at the steady-state mRNA level.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The target FDR was 0.0726 rather than <0.05, and this mRNA assay did not measure complex-IV protein abundance, enzyme activity, respiration, or delayed stress.

summary: Cox6a1 knockdown did not evoke detectable transcriptional compensation by Cox6a2 or by other assayed cytochrome-c-oxidase subunit transcripts.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues against a simple mRNA-level COX6A paralog switch or complex-IV subunit remodelling response in post-mitotic brain cells.
main_caveats: Cox6a2 is expected to be low in brain, and failure to change by Wilcoxon testing does not exclude translational, assembly-level, or metabolic compensation.

summary: Available complex-IV neighbors, especially Cox5a and Ndufa4, achieved stronger on-target FDRs than Cox6a1 but still produced almost exclusively single-gene signatures and did not phenocopy Cox6a1.
why_it_matters: Complex membership did not translate into a shared acute transcriptional state; respiratory-chain structural subunits can be efficiently depleted at the mRNA level while leaving little FDR-corrected transcriptomic footprint.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison uses transcriptome correlations rather than complex-IV activity; the library assayed only a subset of STRING COX6A1 partners.

summary: A recessive neuropathy gene can be partially suppressed in central neuronal classes without an immediate broad mRNA stress signature.
why_it_matters: COX6A1 loss of function causes axonal or mixed Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease, but these mouse-brain Perturb-seq data suggest that acute partial central-neuron depletion is not enough to reproduce that disease biology transcriptionally.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset lacks peripheral motor and sensory axons, Schwann cells, chronic organismal consequences, protein measurements, and homozygous null dosage.

summary: Neither the perturbation nor ChEMBL context supports COX6A1 inhibition as a buffered neuronal therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: The dataset showed no transcriptional rescue program after Cox6a1 suppression, whereas human loss-of-function genetics put COX6A1 on the liability side of mitochondrial neuropathy; small-molecule records are limited to binding-agent observations rather than validated functional agonists or antagonists.
main_caveats: This is a safety-direction hypothesis from transcriptomic buffering plus genetic disease, not a drug efficacy or toxicity experiment.

summary: Mcts1 target-transcript knockdown was measurable only in a minority of profiled neuronal classes, with the clearest depletion in 155 MB Glut and weaker nominal depletion in thalamic, pontine/myelencephalic, hippocampal-amygdalar, and CTX-CGE GABA strata.
why_it_matters: The experiment should be interpreted through target engagement: Mcts1 is broadly expressed, but the guide-associated mRNA decrease was cell-type restricted in this dataset.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: All Mcts1 transcript effects are nominal after cell-type-wise multiple testing; the assay measured RNA, not MCTS1 protein or guide editing efficiency.

summary: Detectable Mcts1 mRNA depletion did not expand into a transcriptome-wide FDR-significant response.
why_it_matters: MCTS1-DENR controls translation reinitiation and ribosome recycling, so a large secondary RNA response would have been plausible; instead, the dominant reproducible RNA effect was the target transcript itself.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Single-cell RNA-seq can miss translational and proteomic outputs; absence of FDR-significant mRNA hits is not evidence that uORF translation was unchanged.

summary: The strongest adjusted non-target signal, Lpgat1 up-regulation in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, was uncoupled from Mcts1 transcript engagement.
why_it_matters: This near-hit should be treated as an unstable or off-target-associated marker rather than as evidence for a basal-ganglia GABA-specific Mcts1 lipid-acyltransferase program.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Lpgat1 narrowly missed FDR<0.05 and no orthogonal guide or protein measurement is available to prove off-target origin.

summary: Mcts1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with available translation-factor, RNA-surveillance, and Hbs1l perturbations, and the direct DENR/EIF2D comparators were not present in the library.
why_it_matters: The neuronal phenotype is not a generic translational-stress state and does not phenocopy strong core translation-factor perturbations such as Eef1a2 or Eef2 knockdown.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Signature correlations are restricted to perturbations present in the library; Denr and Eif2d, the most direct mechanistic comparators, were absent.

summary: The weak adult-neuronal RNA response refines prior DENR/MCTS1 neurodevelopment and immune literature toward a context-specific, mainly translational model rather than an obligatory broad mRNA program.
why_it_matters: Prior work links DENR/MCTS1 activity to cortical neuronal migration and human MCTS1-dependent JAK2 translation, but the present perturbation does not show collapse of mature neuronal mRNA states.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The external studies involve development or human immune cells; the dataset lacks protein synthesis, JAK2 protein, IFN-γ signaling, and developmental migration readouts.

summary: Mcts1 itself is the only recurrent nominal biomarker of on-target perturbation, whereas downstream markers are non-recurrent and MCTS1 has no clinical tractability flag in Open Targets.
why_it_matters: Any attempt to pharmacologically tune this node, for instance from oncology or immune biology, would need protein-level pharmacodynamics rather than relying on an acute neuronal mRNA signature such as Lpgat1.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Therapeutic tractability is database-derived and not a definitive medicinal-chemistry assessment; the perturbation is CRISPR-based, not a small-molecule titration.

summary: FDR-supported Epha4 mRNA depletion in five glutamatergic or cortical projection classes produced no FDR-supported non-target transcriptomic response.
why_it_matters: This separates guide efficacy from downstream engagement: even where the receptor transcript was clearly reduced, an acute Perturb-seq RNA readout did not report the expected large EPHA4 signaling cascade.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The assay measured RNA abundance at one perturbation state; EPHA4 can signal through phosphorylation, localization, morphology, and residual protein that would be invisible or delayed in this readout.

summary: Epha4 transcript knockdown was statistically detectable in only a subset of measured cell classes.
why_it_matters: Negative downstream signatures in classes without a target FDR, particularly inhibitory classes, should be read primarily as lack of measurable target engagement rather than evidence that EphA4 is biologically inert there.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Target RNA depletion is an imperfect proxy for protein loss; sparse baseline Epha4 expression could make a real protein perturbation difficult to detect by Wilcoxon testing.

summary: The sole non-target FDR hit, Tmsb10 in Sst GABA cells, was disconnected from detectable Epha4 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Treating this low-count hit as an EPHA4 effector would overinterpret the screen; it is better handled as a caveated outlier or possible off-target/stochastic event.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Only 26 perturbed Sst cells were analyzed and Epha4 itself had p=0.534 and FDR=1 in the same comparison.

summary: Canonically relevant axon-guidance and cytoskeletal genes appeared only as scattered nominal hits, not as a recurrent Eph/ephrin transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: The data favor an interpretation in which EPHA4 perturbation may alter membrane-proximal or structural signaling without a robust secondary RNA program; nominal genes such as Slit3, Sema4d, Plxna1, Unc5a, Unc5c, and Wasl are hypotheses, not validated effectors.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All named downstream genes are FDR-negative; the L5-6 IT cluster is especially weak because Epha4 itself was only nominal in that class.

summary: Epha4 lacked a strong whole-signature neighbor among Eph receptors or other guidance perturbations; in the best same-cell-family test, Epha7 was knocked down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but was uncorrelated with Epha4.
why_it_matters: Reactome groups EPHA receptors into the same growth-cone-collapse pathway, but this dataset does not support replacing Epha4 by an EphA paralog signature as a transcriptomic surrogate.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on full Wilcoxon score vectors dominated by null genes, and many non-Epha4 receptor perturbations were not independently FDR-confirmed for target knockdown.

summary: EPHA4 remains a disease-linked and chemically perturbable receptor, but the mouse-brain RNA signature is a poor standalone biomarker for EPHA4 inhibition.
why_it_matters: ALS and regeneration programs based on EPHA4 should prioritize motor-neuron, axonal, phosphoproteomic, and circuit phenotypes rather than expecting broad cell-autonomous RNA changes in every neuronal class.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The screen did not include spinal motor neurons, ALS genotypes, injury paradigms, or chronic protein antagonism; it therefore refines biomarker expectations rather than testing clinical efficacy.

direction: weak knockdown; no FDR-significant downstream response
summary: Lgi1 perturbation produced directional but weak target-transcript depletion and no FDR-significant transcriptional program in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset result is absence of robust RNA-seq consequences, so downstream interpretation must not treat nominal genes as a clean Lgi1 loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: Negative result is conditioned on target mRNA knockdown being nominal and incomplete.

summary: Nominal Lgi1 target depletion was uneven across neuronal subclasses, being clearest in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 046 CTX-CGE GABA and absent in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-aggregating all Lgi1 cells and highlights that apparent responses in Pvalb or cerebellar GABA cells occurred without evidence of on-target depletion.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All target rows were FDR 1.0; the selectivity is nominal and may reflect guide efficiency or expression detectability rather than true neuron-subclass biology.

summary: The LGI1–ADAM22/Kv1/AMPA synaptic module was not transcriptionally remodeled by Lgi1 perturbation, and direct Adam22 depletion was itself largely buffered beyond the Adam22 transcript.
why_it_matters: LGI1 and ADAM22 are direct extracellular synaptic partners, so the lack of Adam22, PSD-95, Kv1, AMPA, or NMDAR mRNA regulation suggests that the pathway operates mainly through protein localization, extracellular protein supply, or electrophysiology in this assay window.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Lgi1 perturbation was weak and the assay lacks extracellular LGI1 protein, synaptic localization, and electrophysiology measurements.

summary: A direct NMDAR perturbation, Grin1, generated many FDR-significant responses whereas Lgi1 and Adam22 were quiet, separating core ionotropic receptor loss from extracellular LGI1–ADAM22 scaffold perturbation.
why_it_matters: The dataset could detect strong synaptic perturbation biology, so the muted Lgi1 result is more consistent with pathway-specific buffering or assay mismatch than with blanket insensitivity of neuronal Perturb-seq.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Grin1 is a downstream synaptic neighbor rather than a direct LGI1 receptor; its perturbation had somewhat larger cell counts and stronger target depletion.

summary: Chchd2 up-regulation in 308 CB GABA is only an exploratory near-FDR biomarker because it occurred in a cell type with no detectable Lgi1 mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: The lowest adjusted p value in the entire Lgi1 screen should not be promoted to a canonical LGI1 biomarker without independent validation and on-target support.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Single near-FDR row; q=0.0916; no Lgi1 knockdown in the same cell class.

summary: Because human genetic, autoimmune, and mouse data all make reduced LGI1–ADAM22 signaling pro-epileptic, the quiet Lgi1 Perturb-seq signature should not be read as evidence that lowering LGI1 is safe or beneficial.
why_it_matters: The clinically aligned direction is stabilization or restoration of LGI1–ADAM22 complexes, not additional LGI1 suppression.
main_caveats: Therapeutic direction is inferred from prior disease biology plus an absence of a compensatory dataset signal; the screen is not a seizure or rescue assay.

direction: Calm1 down; 151 module mostly up with sparse Resp18 up and Maf down outside 151
summary: Calm1 knockdown was measurable in many cell types, but FDR-supported downstream transcription was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Calmodulin is a ubiquitous calcium sensor, so the dataset changes interpretation from a broadly propagating transcriptional response to a sharply context-gated response dominated by one thalamic glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The 151 class also had the largest Calm1 perturbed-cell count; the sparse 007 and 052 hits should not be overinterpreted as full modules.

direction: Calm1 down with minimal downstream RNA change
summary: Many cell types showed strong Calm1 target depletion with no non-target FDR hits.
why_it_matters: The result argues that partial Calm1 transcript loss is buffered or expressed mainly through non-transcriptional calcium signaling in most profiled neuronal classes.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Absence of DE is not absence of calcium, channel, phosphatase, or kinase activity changes; transcriptomics is an indirect readout for CaM pathways.

direction: Calm1-specific downstream expansion relative to Calm3; Calm2 weakly engaged
summary: Calm1 and Calm3 were not interchangeable in the responsive 151 class despite encoding the same calmodulin protein.
why_it_matters: The contrast elevates gene-specific calmodulin regulation as a plausible brain mechanism rather than treating the three Calm loci as redundant copies.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Calm2 was poorly knocked down in this screen, so the strongest paralog contrast is Calm1 versus Calm3.

summary: The strongest negative signature neighbor of Calm1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the calmodulin-binding transcription factor Camta1.
why_it_matters: Several genes induced by Calm1 loss were repressed by Camta1 perturbation, placing the Calm1 module near a CaM-linked transcriptional regulator but in the opposite direction from a simple loss-of-CAMTA1 model.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The anti-correlation was restricted to one 500-gene signature and does not prove direct CAMTA1 regulation of the Calm1-responsive genes.

direction: Rasgrp2 up and Atp2b1 down after Calm1 perturbation; Atp2b1 perturbation did not mimic
summary: Rasgrp2 was the top non-target Calm1-induced transcript and tracked a calcium/Rap-GEF branch that was not reproduced by Atp2b1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Rasgrp2 is a calcium-regulated EF-hand RapGEF, so its strong induction is a candidate marker of the 151-specific Calm1 state; the Atp2b1 non-phenocopy warns against assigning the state solely to reduced PMCA pump transcript.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: RASGRP2 is not established here as a direct CaM target; the claim is a marker and pathway-branch hypothesis.

direction: weak or absent transcript changes in canonical partners; no strong global signature neighbor
summary: Canonical CaM partners were largely transcriptionally uncoupled from Calm1 knockdown, and no screened perturbation strongly phenocopied the Calm1 151 signature.
why_it_matters: CaM controls many targets post-translationally; the dataset indicates that this Perturb-seq readout captures a selective transcriptional module rather than wholesale remodeling of CaMK, calcineurin, NMDA-receptor, or PMCA-pathway mRNAs.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The all-perturbation neighbor search was restricted to the 151 class and the top 500 Calm1 genes; absence of RNA changes does not test protein phosphorylation, Ca2+ flux, or channel gating.
