main_caveats: Gigyf2 mRNA depletion in L4/5 IT was nominal but not FDR-significant, and the assay cannot prove that GIGYF2 protein was effectively reduced.

summary: An exploratory top-300 restricted-signature comparison placed proteasome perturbations and Tsc1/Tsc2 among the strongest positive Gigyf2 neighbors in the two main glutamatergic response cell types.
why_it_matters: The convergence suggests that Gigyf2 loss may intersect a broader translation/proteostasis stress axis rather than only a narrow RQC complex; it prioritizes proteasome and mTOR/TSC neighbors for validation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only on the 300 most nominal Gigyf2 genes per cell type; full-transcriptome correlations were much smaller.

summary: The acute single-cell response to partial Gigyf2 knockdown was sparse even though genetic GIGYF2 disruption is developmental and neurodegenerative in mouse models.
why_it_matters: A weak acute mRNA phenotype should not be interpreted as lack of neuronal risk for a translation-quality-control adaptor, and direct GIGYF2 modulation would need proteostasis and long-duration safety assays.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq data measure acute transcript abundance after partial knockdown, whereas the mouse phenotypes come from germline disruption and likely include protein-level and developmental effects.

summary: Pcsk5 perturbation lacked measurable on-target Pcsk5 mRNA depletion in every sampled brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is target-engagement failure or very weak depletion, so absent downstream programs should not be read as proof that neurons are insensitive to PCSK5 loss.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance, not PCSK5 protein or guide cutting, was measured; some cell types had only 25-68 perturbed cells.

summary: The only genome-wide Pcsk5 signal was a single Ssb decrease in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, with a separate near-threshold Ccdc90b increase in low-count 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: The response is cell-type restricted but not a recurrent pathway; Ssb and Ccdc90b are best treated as weak biomarkers or stochastic/off-target candidates rather than a PCSK5 program.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The Ssb effect was the only FDR<0.05 row among 371,818 Pcsk5 tests; Ccdc90b did not cross 0.05 FDR and was estimated from only 25 perturbed cells.

summary: Annotated PCSK5 substrate biology was not coupled to a transcriptional neurotrophin, TGF/BMP, or lipase-complex response in this screen.
why_it_matters: PCSK5 acts as a secretory-pathway endoprotease, so immediate substrate maturation can change without changing mRNA levels of Bdnf/Ngf/Ntf3 receptors, BMP/TGF pathway genes, or lipase-assembly genes.
main_caveats: The tested transcript sets are proxies; they do not measure immature versus mature NGF, BDNF, NT3, GDF11/BMP2, or lipase proteins.

summary: Pcsk5 did not phenocopy Pcsk2 or downstream TGF/BMP receptor-SMAD perturbations, and its best whole-dataset signature neighbors were near zero.
why_it_matters: A shared proprotein-convertase or TGF/BMP response would have produced a correlated transcriptional signature; the observed Pcsk5 signature is too weak and idiosyncratic to define such a module.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors in selected Pcsk5 contexts and are exploratory; they cannot exclude protein-level convergence.

summary: The weak brain-cell Pcsk5 transcriptomic phenotype does not de-risk systemic or developmental PCSK5 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Mouse Pcsk5 loss is embryonically essential and tied to Gdf11/VACTERL-like developmental mechanisms, whereas this dataset sampled brain neuronal classes, produced no on-target mRNA knockdown, and did not assay proteolytic substrate maturation.
main_caveats: The warning is inferential: the screen was not an embryogenesis, congenital-malformation, or drug-safety assay.

summary: Gpx4 perturbation was transcriptionally silent at FDR scale and the target transcript itself was absent from the DE matrix.
why_it_matters: GPX4 is a brain-expressed selenoprotein lipid-peroxide repair enzyme; therefore the dataset should be interpreted as failed or unverified acute engagement, not as evidence that neurons tolerate GPX4 loss.
main_caveats: The strongest caveat is that Gpx4 mRNA was not measured, so guide cutting or transcript depletion cannot be demonstrated.

summary: The only visible structure in the Gpx4 result was a weak nominal enrichment of top-ranked genes in 155 MB Glut, with scattered single nominal leaders in other classes.
why_it_matters: This argues against a recurrent pan-neuronal GPX4 loss program in the observed data while preserving a possible midbrain glutamatergic exploratory signal for follow-up.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: All rows had FDR greater than 0.19; the pattern is hypothesis-generating only.

summary: Gpx4 perturbation did not move measured ferroptosis, GPX-family, glutathione, iron, NRF2, or Aifm2 marker transcripts, although Fth1 and Acsl4 perturbations showed clear on-target knockdown elsewhere in the same assay.
why_it_matters: The expected lipid-peroxide defense axis was not transcriptionally engaged by Gpx4 guides, whereas at least some ferroptosis-modifier transcripts were perturbable and measurable in the screen.
main_caveats: Absence of marker response may reflect low protein depletion or missing Gpx4 expression rather than true biological buffering.

summary: The Gpx4 transcriptome was not similar to its direct STRING ferroptosis/redox neighbors and its strongest all-target neighbors were weak, cerebellar, and partly control-like.
why_it_matters: Neighbor analysis failed to rescue a hidden GPX4 module; the weak top correlations are more consistent with a low-amplitude or technical signature than with a specific lipid-peroxidation network state.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: STRING links are functional, not predictions of same-direction transcriptomic correlations; all correlations are restricted to DE score profiles, not phenotypic ferroptosis assays.

summary: The negative Perturb-seq readout should not be used to de-risk GPX4 inhibition in brain.
why_it_matters: Published genetic and chemical work predicts that effective GPX4 loss promotes lipid-peroxidation death, including neuronal degeneration in mice; the dataset lacked direct Gpx4 target readout and therefore cannot counter that safety liability.
main_caveats: The assay was acute single-cell RNA measurement and did not assay lipid peroxidation, protein abundance, or cell death over the time scale used in knockout models.

summary: Hdac8 perturbation was FDR-null and showed no detectable Hdac8 mRNA knockdown across the sampled mouse-brain neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: HDAC8 is annotated as a chromatin and SMC3 deacetylase, so a broad derepression or cohesin-like transcriptional response might have been expected; instead the direct RNA phenotype was absent or below detection in every measured cell type.
main_caveats: Target-transcript abundance is only a proxy for editing or protein inhibition; sixteen of twenty-two cell types had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: The strongest Hdac8 gene-level hint was a nominal Dusp6/Egr1/Erf/Per1/Nr4a1-positive response in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: If Hdac8 has a real neuronal response in this experiment, the top-ranked signal points to a restricted cortical L2/3 nominal positive module rather than to global histone deacetylase derepression.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Dusp6 had the best Hdac8 FDR in the whole panel but still did not pass 0.05 FDR; the cell type had only 38 perturbed cells.

summary: A cohesin/Cornelia-de-Lange-like relationship for Hdac8 was visible only as weak 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature alignment with Nipbl, Smc1a, and Smc3.
why_it_matters: The same thalamic population strongly detected several cohesin-family perturbations, but Hdac8 itself remained FDR-null, arguing that adult neuronal Hdac8 loss does not simply phenocopy NIPBL, SMC1A, STAG2, or SMC3 transcriptional loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Hdac8-to-cohesin correlations were small, Hdac8 had no FDR genes in the cell type, and direct SMC3 acetylation was not measured.

summary: Hdac8 was uncoupled from the large chromatin-regulator phenotypes produced by Sin3a and Zmynd8 and from the weak Hdac4/Hdac5 HDAC-family signatures.
why_it_matters: The dataset can detect chromatin regulator perturbations when they matter, so HDAC8 should not be treated as an interchangeable catalytic component of generic neuronal HDAC or SIN3-associated repression in this assay.
main_caveats: Hdac1, Hdac2, and Hdac3, the closest class-I nuclear HDAC comparators, were not present in the assayed target set.

summary: The neuronal FDR-null signature does not de-risk HDAC8 inhibition for neurodevelopmental or progenitor contexts.
why_it_matters: HDAC8 is a small-molecule target and a CdLS/cell-cycle SMC3 deacetylase; a mouse adult SVZ study found Hdac8 perturbation impaired neural stem/progenitor proliferation and differentiation, whereas this Perturb-seq panel sampled differentiated neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay SVZ neural stem cells, early development, biochemical SMC3 acetylation, or chronic pharmacologic inhibition.

summary: A genome-scale signature-neighbor search did not identify a strong recurrent Hdac8 positive or negative neighbor.
why_it_matters: This argues against elevating isolated low-FDR-ranked Hdac8 genes into a reproducible network module; even the best global correlations were close to zero.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations were computed on per-target Wilcoxon score vectors and do not test nonlinear or post-transcriptional similarity.

summary: In 155 MB Glut, Fgfr1 perturbation produced a clean receptor-transcript hit but almost no FDR-resolved downstream transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Canonical FGFR1 activation can feed several intracellular cascades; the measured acute loss in this broad midbrain glutamatergic class was dominated by Fgfr1 mRNA itself rather than a large MAPK, PI3K, or PLC transcriptional program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Single-cell mRNA measurements do not assay receptor protein or phospho-ERK/AKT; Qki and Hecw1 were nominal only and are not interpreted mechanistically.

summary: Detectable Fgfr1 knockdown was concentrated in a small subset of the 22 assayed Fgfr1 cell classes.
why_it_matters: Most broad neuronal classes either lacked target-transcript engagement or were below FDR correction, so absence of downstream genes in those classes should be read primarily as weak or buffered perturbation rather than proof that Fgfr1 is dispensable.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: All non-155 examples were nominal for Fgfr1 after FDR correction; cell numbers ranged down to 27 cells in the weakest class.

summary: FGFR1 loss did not phenocopy engaged Map2k1 or Mapk1 perturbations in the same 155 MB Glut cells.
why_it_matters: FGFR1 is upstream of RAS-MAPK signaling in curated pathways, yet the two MAPK-cascade knockdowns that were FDR-engaged in 155 MB Glut had essentially zero genome-wide score correlation with Fgfr1, arguing that the acute Fgfr1 phenotype in this assay was not a simple transcriptional readout of ERK loss.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations use Wilcoxon z-score signatures; Fgfr1 may signal post-transcriptionally, require ligand, or act in a subset hidden inside the broad 155 MB Glut cluster.

summary: Fgfr2 and Fgfr3 were not interchangeable with Fgfr1 at the transcriptomic-signature level.
why_it_matters: FGF ligands can engage several FGFR isoforms, but the dataset did not reveal a shared receptor-family signature; this supports treating the FGFR1 result as isoform- and engagement-specific rather than a pan-FGFR neuronal state.
main_caveats: Fgfr2 and Fgfr3 self-transcripts were not FDR-depleted, so the contrast is limited by poor measurable receptor engagement.

summary: The mature Pvalb GABA class showed only nominal Fgfr1 self-depletion and no corrected downstream response despite developmental Fgfr1 requirements for parvalbumin interneuron maturation.
why_it_matters: The mismatch points to developmental timing, progenitor context, or inadequate acute target engagement as key qualifiers when projecting Fgfr1 neurodevelopmental literature onto mature interneuron Perturb-seq readouts.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Fgfr1 in Pvalb GABA had FDR=1.0, and the Perturb-seq cell class is not the radial-glial developmental context used in the mouse knockout study.

summary: The neuronal signatures warn against treating pan-FGFR pharmacology as equivalent to Fgfr1 mRNA loss in brain cells.
why_it_matters: Clinically used FGFR inhibitors inhibit FGFR-family kinases, whereas in this dataset Fgfr1, Fgfr2, and Fgfr3 perturbations were weakly or non-convergently read out; possible CNS effects of FGFR blockade should therefore be evaluated by receptor, cell type, and target engagement instead of extrapolating from Fgfr1 alone.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The experiment assayed CRISPR-mediated transcript loss rather than acute kinase inhibition, and many therapeutic inhibitors also hit FGFR4 or non-FGFR kinases.

summary: Cyfip1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream genes in any of 23 measured cell types.
why_it_matters: CYFIP1 is a translation- and actin-regulatory protein; the result warns that acute single-cell mRNA differential expression is a weak readout for this target even when the target transcript trends downward.
main_caveats: Cyfip1 self-depletion was only near-significant in the best stratum and was not FDR-significant in any cell type.

summary: The measurable Cyfip1 on-target effect was restricted to a subset of cell types and was clearest in 155 MB Glut rather than in the highest-count 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut stratum.
why_it_matters: Apparent cell-type-specific absence of downstream biology cannot be interpreted without first checking whether the Cyfip1 mRNA was depleted in that cell type.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is primarily a perturbation-engagement finding; it does not prove that MB glutamatergic neurons are the most CYFIP1-sensitive neurons biologically.

summary: Cyfip2, the assayed CYFIP paralog, achieved significant self-knockdown in six cell types but still produced no significant non-self genes.
why_it_matters: A stronger CYFIP-family perturbation sharing WAVE-complex membership was also mRNA-silent, supporting the interpretation that CYFIP loss is buffered or post-transcriptional in this scRNA endpoint rather than uniquely failed for Cyfip1.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: CYFIP2 is a paralog and alternative WRC component, not a perfect substitute for CYFIP1; the assay measures RNA only.

summary: Cyfip1 did not produce the EIF4E/TSC-like transcriptional programs seen for Eif4e, Tsc1, and Tsc2 in TH and MB glutamatergic contexts.
why_it_matters: CYFIP1 binds eIF4E in a translational repression complex, but in this dataset Cyfip1 KO should not be used as a proxy for eIF4E loss or TSC/mTOR pathway activation.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Eif4e and TSC perturbations target different molecular nodes; contrast is pathway-level rather than a direct complex-member comparison.

summary: No strong positive or negative Cyfip1 signature neighbor was detected after score-vector correlation against all other perturbations.
why_it_matters: This reduces support for an unrecognized transcriptional module converging on Cyfip1 and keeps very weak correlations from being overinterpreted as biology.
main_caveats: Correlation used weak Cyfip1 signatures; the largest all-strata neighbor occurred in a cell type without Cyfip1 target engagement.

summary: The Cyfip1 Perturb-seq result does not recapitulate the synaptic, dendritic-spine, and translation phenotypes reported for CYFIP1 dosage loss.
why_it_matters: For neurodevelopmental-disease follow-up, protein synthesis, WAVE/actin, dendritic-spine, and synaptic assays are more biologically aligned biomarkers than a bulk count of DE genes in this screen.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The screen lacks protein, morphology, and electrophysiology readouts and used acute CRISPR perturbation rather than chronic heterozygosity.

summary: Gigyf1 perturbation produced a globally buffered steady-state mRNA phenotype across the assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: GIGYF1 is a translational regulator, but this Perturb-seq RNA readout detected almost no FDR-significant transcriptional consequence after targeting it, so absence of a large mRNA signature should be treated as a biological result rather than as a strong loss-of-function phenocopy.
main_caveats: Target-transcript depletion was modest and never reached FDR<0.05, so the buffered mRNA phenotype cannot distinguish biological compensation from incomplete perturbation.

summary: Even the two cell types with the clearest Gigyf1 transcript depletion, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, lacked any downstream gene at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The cells most likely to reveal direct consequences of Gigyf1 targeting were target-dominated rather than pathway-dominated, consistent with uncoupling between a translation-initiation regulator and bulk steady-state RNA changes.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: No protein, ribosome profiling, cap-binding, or IGF1R phosphorylation measurements were present.

summary: 054 CNU-MGE GABA contained the only FDR<0.05 non-target gene, Nap1l3, making it an isolated candidate responder rather than a recurrent Gigyf1 program.
why_it_matters: Preserving this single positive result prevents the global negative result from hiding the one cell-class-restricted signal, while its isolation keeps it hypothesis-generating.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Only one gene passed FDR<0.05, it was not Gigyf1, and Gigyf1 itself was only nominal in this cell type.

summary: Gigyf1 was much less RNA-active than its paralog Gigyf2 and the translation factor Eif4e, and its score vector did not covary with those related perturbations.
why_it_matters: GIGYF1 should not be assumed to be transcriptionally interchangeable with the broader GIGYF/translation-initiation module in these cells; Gigyf2 and Eif4e exposed larger, cell-selective RNA phenotypes in the same dataset.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Eif4e is the canonical cap-binding factor rather than Eif4e2/4EHP; Ddx6, Zfp598, and Eif4e2 were not assayed; differing guide counts and target-protein depletion may contribute.

summary: Gigyf1 targeting did not yield an FDR-significant basal IGF1R/insulin/ERK mRNA output signature, despite literature connecting GIGYF1 disruption to IGF-1R signaling and autism risk.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq result narrows what this assay can report: a basal single-cell RNA profile in these mouse cell types does not phenocopy the IGF-1R receptor-trafficking and ERK-signaling mechanism described in disease-oriented models.
main_caveats: IGF1R signaling is controlled by ligand stimulation, trafficking, and phosphorylation; those endpoints were not measured by this mRNA screen.

summary: The assayed AGO/TNRC6/CNOT post-transcriptional neighbors did not reveal a shared Gigyf1-like mRNA state.
why_it_matters: Although GIGYF proteins are embedded in mRNA-repression and decay networks, loss of Ago2, Tnrc6a, Tnrc6b, or Cnot1 did not produce a broad transcriptomic module that could explain the Gigyf1 perturbation behavior.
main_caveats: Ago2/Tnrc6/Cnot perturbations also showed weak or absent FDR output, so this is primarily a network-neighborhood negative result rather than evidence against biochemical coupling.

direction: Grik3 down in Sst; weaker nominal down in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
summary: Transcript-level Grik3 target engagement was concentrated in Sst GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: The clearest RNA evidence for perturbing the kainate subunit itself occurs in an inhibitory interneuron class rather than broadly across excitatory glutamatergic populations.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Transcript reduction is a proxy for CRISPR editing; most cell types lacked a detectable mRNA decrease, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was nominal only after FDR correction.

direction: Grik3 down with no additional FDR-significant genes
summary: The Sst GABA Grik3 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered.
why_it_matters: A direct reduction of Grik3 mRNA did not propagate into a broad FDR-significant glutamate-receptor or synaptic-expression program, consistent with GluK3 acting primarily as a membrane ion-channel subunit rather than a transcriptional regulator.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: The assay captures RNA abundance, not receptor protein, channel assembly, or synaptic physiology; 53 perturbed Sst cells limit power for small effects.

direction: Gdpd5 and Kcng3 up; Gpm6b and Htr1b nominally down; Grik3 mRNA unchanged
summary: L5 ET CTX glutamatergic neurons carried the strongest non-target Grik3 response, but it was uncoupled from Grik3 mRNA loss.
why_it_matters: The Gdpd5/Kcng3 signal marks a cortical projection-neuron response that could reflect productive protein-disrupting edits, DNA-damage or guide effects, or an indirect state shift; it should not be interpreted simply as a graded consequence of Grik3 transcript depletion.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only Gdpd5 passed FDR<0.05; Kcng3 was FDR<0.10; no matched decrease of the target transcript was detected.

summary: Grik3 perturbation signatures were nearly orthogonal to other kainate-receptor subunit perturbations.
why_it_matters: Although GluK3 belongs to a coassembling GRIK receptor family, the Perturb-seq endpoint does not support treating Grik1, Grik2, Grik4, Grik5, and Grik3 loss as interchangeable transcriptomic states.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on same-cell score vectors and test transcriptional similarity, not biochemical coassembly or electrophysiological interchangeability.

summary: Cnr1 was the largest L5/6 IT cortical change after Grik3 perturbation, but only at exploratory FDR.
why_it_matters: CNR1 and kainate receptors both belong to presynaptic-modulatory signaling space, so a reproducible Cnr1 decrease would be a useful cortical biomarker candidate; the present dataset makes it a hypothesis rather than a confirmed pathway.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: Cnr1 did not pass FDR<0.05, the Grik3 target transcript was not significantly reduced in this cell type, and the direct Cnr1-perturbation signature was not correlated with the Grik3 signature.

summary: Disease interpretation of GRIK3 loss should emphasize sparse, cell-type-restricted receptor modulation rather than a pan-glutamatergic transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Human genetic and database evidence connect GRIK3/kainate receptors to epilepsy and psychiatric traits, while ChEMBL shows GluK3 is assayable without an established selective mechanism; the mouse RNA response was split between a clean Sst target knockdown, a separate L5 ET non-self response, and weak genome-wide signature neighbors.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: Disease links are human and mostly non-directional; the dataset is mouse brain RNA after CRISPR perturbation, not a seizure, psychiatric, or pharmacologic model.

direction: Cck decreased only in three FDR-supported cell types
summary: Cck transcript depletion was strongly engaged only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The perturbation should be interpreted as a successful Cck precursor-mRNA loss in a small set of glutamatergic populations, not as uniform brain-wide CCK depletion.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Self-transcript engagement is an RNA measure; mature peptide abundance and baseline Cck expression per cell were not directly measured.

direction: Cck down with buffered downstream mRNA response
summary: Strong Cck knockdown caused little FDR-supported downstream transcriptional remodeling.
why_it_matters: A secreted neuromodulator can be depleted at the mRNA level without forcing a large-autonomous RNA response, so weak DE should not be equated with absence of peptide or circuit biology.
comparators: all non-Cck perturbations by score-vector correlation
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only transcriptomic output was assayed; regulated release, pre-existing peptide stores, and receptor activation were not measured.

direction: processing-enzyme knockdown uncoupled from Cck transcript
summary: Cpe and Pcsk2 knockdowns did not phenocopy Cck mRNA loss or reduce Cck transcript abundance.
why_it_matters: CPE and PCSK2 act in peptide maturation downstream of precursor transcription, so Cck mRNA is a poor proxy for mature active CCK in processing-enzyme perturbations.
main_caveats: The dataset did not measure CCK peptide forms; Pcsk2 was assayed in fewer and often lower-cell-count strata than Cpe.

direction: absent Cck self-depletion in tested broad GABA classes
summary: Broad cortical GABA classes lacked detectable Cck on-target knockdown despite prior expression of CCK in inhibitory/CGE neurons.
why_it_matters: This prevents a simple conclusion that the screen perturbed canonical CCK interneuron biology; CCK-positive interneurons may be rare within broad GABA labels or poorly engaged.
comparators: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Broad taxonomy can dilute rare CCK interneuron subclasses; no Cck baseline expression distribution was available in the parquet.

summary: Cck ligand perturbation was transcriptionally decoupled from Cckar and Cckbr receptor perturbations in the engaged Cck cell types.
why_it_matters: Even though CCKAR and CCKBR are the canonical receptor arms, this dataset does not support treating Cck precursor knockdown as receptor antagonism or as equivalent to receptor perturbation.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cckar and Cckbr did not show their own FDR-supported knockdown, so technical non-engagement is a major alternative to receptor-pathway biology.

summary: The Perturb-seq result is insufficient to infer whether reducing CCK signaling would benefit or worsen anxiety- or schizophrenia-relevant biology.
why_it_matters: CCK receptors are druggable GPCRs and have neuropsychiatric literature, but the dataset reports precursor mRNA knockdown with minimal downstream RNA response and no mature peptide or receptor pharmacology readout.
main_caveats: Clinical directionality requires receptor-, region-, circuit-, and peptide-form resolution that the mRNA screen lacks.

summary: Meis2 perturbation produced no multiple-testing-corrected transcriptomic response and no corrected depletion of the Meis2 transcript in any of 22 assayed cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: MEIS2 is a sequence-specific developmental transcription factor, so the absence of target-transcript depletion and downstream FDR hits makes this perturbation difficult to interpret as an effective acute loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an imperfect readout for a genome-editing perturbation; a frameshift can leave mRNA detectable, and several cell types had fewer than 60 perturbed cells.

summary: The LGE/LSX GABA class did not recapitulate the strong embryonic MEIS2 requirement reported for basal-ganglia and striatal GABAergic specification.
why_it_matters: The result narrows the likely window in which Meis2 loss is transcriptionally consequential: developmental progenitors and differentiating neurons remain the literature-supported context, whereas this mature LGE/LSX-like class showed no corrected acute response.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset cell class is not the embryonic lateral ganglionic eminence, and target-transcript knockdown was weak.

summary: MEIS/PBX/HOX-family perturbations that should be mechanistically related to Meis2 lacked a strong shared signature with Meis2.
why_it_matters: PBX and HOX proteins are expected MEIS2 cofactors or network neighbors, but the dataset argues that these related perturbations were mostly silent or context-mismatched in the assayed brain-cell panels.
main_caveats: Most related factors also showed weak signatures, so the contrast may reflect poor engagement or absence of the relevant developmental context rather than true pathway divergence.

summary: A per-cell-type all-target signature-neighbor scan found no robust Meis2-positive or Meis2-negative neighbor.
why_it_matters: If Meis2 had a coherent but subthreshold program, another perturbation in the same screen might have converged on it; the maximum absolute genome-wide score correlation was only 0.154.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations were computed on rank-like Wilcoxon scores, and a low correlation cannot exclude convergence in a small unmeasured gene set.

summary: Actr1b, Srrm4, Cd81 and Adipor1 are only exploratory sentinels for the weakest nominal Meis2 responses, not validated biomarkers.
why_it_matters: These genes mark the four smallest cell-wise adjusted p values and should be kept as audit-trail leads while being excluded from mechanistic interpretation until replicated.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: None of the four genes passed FDR correction; the hypothesis is purely signature triage.

summary: Il1rap perturbation generated no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any of the 22 assayed neuronal cell classes, and the Il1rap target transcript itself was only weakly and non-significantly reduced.
why_it_matters: All higher-level mechanistic claims must be interpreted as negative or weak-engagement observations rather than as a clean Il1rap loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: The lack of Il1rap mRNA depletion by FDR leaves open failed guide activity, protein-level knockout without RNA decay, or an underpowered perturbation.

summary: The annotated IL-1 receptor-to-NF-kappaB transcriptional program was not detectably engaged by Il1rap perturbation in basal Glut/GABA neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: IL1RAP is a necessary accessory receptor for IL-1-family signaling, so absence of Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Socs3, cytokine, and chemokine responses indicates that those annotations do not imply a constitutive neuronal mRNA signature in this assay.
main_caveats: Could reflect no IL-1-family ligand stimulation, neuronal rather than immune cell context, or weak Il1rap perturbation.

summary: Il1r1 did not converge with Il1rap despite being the ligand-binding partner in the IL-1 receptor complex.
why_it_matters: A shared core IL-1 receptor loss-of-function program would predict positive Il1rap-Il1r1 signature correlations; the observed mean Pearson r was near zero and the strongest shared classes were weakly anti-correlated.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Il1r1 itself had no FDR-significant response or target-transcript FDR signal, so this is a weak-signature contrast.

summary: Il1rap did not robustly phenocopy IL1RAP-family synaptic paralogs Il1rapl1 or Il1rapl2.
why_it_matters: The PTPdelta/IL1RAP-family literature predicts related synaptic adhesion biology, but the Perturb-seq states were almost orthogonal except for a weak 308 CB GABA similarity.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Paralog perturbations were also weak; two Il1rapl1 FDR hits were isolated single-gene results rather than a module.

summary: The Alzheimer’s IL1RAP association is not mirrored by a basal neuronal cytokine/NF-kappaB signature after Il1rap perturbation.
why_it_matters: Human AD genetics nominated IL1RAP in amyloid accumulation and microglial activation; the mouse Perturb-seq result redirects mechanistic follow-up toward microglia, glia/vascular contexts, cytokine challenge, or nontranscriptional synaptic phenotypes rather than a constitutive neuronal inflammatory module.
main_caveats: Different species, human regulatory variant versus mouse CRISPR perturbation, neuronal rather than microglial readout, and weak target transcript engagement.

summary: An all-target signature-neighbor search failed to reveal a coherent hidden IL-1/TIR/NF-kappaB module for Il1rap.
why_it_matters: The absence of Il1r1, Traf6/IRAK, Toll-like receptor, or NF-kappaB targets among the strongest Il1rap neighbors supports the direct gene-level observation that pathway output was not captured under another perturbation label.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were modest, and top neighbors in 308 CB GABA were not mechanistically interpretable.

direction: Chuk transcript mostly down; downstream effects not FDR-supported
summary: Chuk perturbation produced a statistically directional but weak on-target transcript decrease and no FDR-supported downstream transcriptome in any profiled neuronal class.
why_it_matters: CHUK is a central IKK/NF-κB kinase, but in these basal brain cell states the scRNA-seq signature was buffered rather than a broad inflammatory or survival program.
main_caveats: The interpretation depends on modest transcript knockdown; no target-transcript row itself survived multiple-testing correction.

direction: nominal Chuk down; heterogeneous downstream directions
summary: The clearest nominal target engagement was concentrated in a few inhibitory, thalamic, and midbrain classes, yet those classes still lacked coherent downstream programs.
why_it_matters: This separates guide engagement from biological response: cell types with nominal Chuk depletion, such as 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 046 CTX-CGE GABA, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, were still not converted into an NF-κB-high or NF-κB-low state.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: All downstream genes in these cell types had FDR >=0.727 or FDR 1.0; the reported cell-type pattern is nominal.

summary: Direct inspection of an NF-κB and inflammatory-response panel showed no coordinated suppression or induction after Chuk perturbation.
why_it_matters: The result argues that basal neuronal CHUK depletion is insufficient to read out the canonical cytokine/TLR/TNFR NF-κB program that dominates pathway annotations.
main_caveats: The panel was manually chosen and the dataset is unstimulated; activity-dependent or cytokine-induced NF-κB outputs could be missed.

summary: Chuk signatures were effectively orthogonal to perturbations of NF-κB/TLR/TNFR neighbors and to all unbiased signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: Even though Reactome and STRING place CHUK adjacent to Nfkb1, Nfkb2, Relb, Traf3 and receptors, those direct perturbations did not phenocopy Chuk in matching cell types, suggesting context-dependent pathway deployment rather than a single linear transcriptomic module.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on weak Chuk signatures; Ikbkb, Ikbkg, Rela and Nfkbia were not available as perturbation targets in the dataset.

direction: dataset negative in basal neurons despite immune disease relevance
summary: The neuronal loss-of-function readout should not be interpreted as evidence that CHUK inhibition would be anti-inflammatory or safe in immune contexts.
why_it_matters: Human CHUK kinase defects perturb noncanonical NF-κB and cause immunodeficiency, whereas this dataset shows little response in unstimulated neuronal subclasses; target validation for CHUK needs stimulated immune or glial contexts, not only basal neurons.
main_caveats: This is a context warning, not direct drug testing; CRISPR perturbation generated modest RNA depletion and was not a kinase inhibitor.

direction: Dlgap4 down with sparse Vgf or Vgf/Scg2 down

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only one or two non-target genes passed FDR in each engaged class.

summary: Vgf is the most reproducible downstream Dlgap4 marker and is paired with Scg2 specifically in L5 ET neurons.

main_caveats: Scg2 passed FDR only in 022; the Grin2b comparison is directional, not proof of mechanism.

direction: Scn1b and Tacc1 down while Dlgap4 is not down
summary: The 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA signature has strong Scn1b and Tacc1 decreases without detectable Dlgap4 mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: This flags the largest inhibitory-class hits as noncanonical, post-transcriptional, guide-composition-driven, or off-target until replicated.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The two downstream genes are FDR-significant, but Dlgap4 logFC is positive and nonsignificant.

direction: nominal Dlgap4 down with no FDR non-target genes
summary: Several high-count Dlgap4 tests show nominal target depletion but no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome.
why_it_matters: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 155 MB Glut suggest that partial Dlgap4 depletion can be transcriptionally buffered in some glutamatergic contexts.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Target depletion itself did not pass 5% FDR in these classes.

direction: exploratory NMDA-neighbor convergence with direct-scaffold divergence
summary: Dlgap4 signatures align more with NMDA receptor perturbations than with direct PSD95-SAPAP-SHANK scaffold perturbations.
why_it_matters: Grin1 or Grin2b appeared among the top Dlgap4 positive neighbors, whereas Dlg4, Shank3, and Grid1 were weaker neighbors despite physical scaffold membership.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Global score correlations were small and hypothesis-generating.

summary: The dataset reframes SAPAP4 disease biology as circuit- and cell-context dependent rather than uniformly disruptive.
why_it_matters: Disease models show synaptic, behavioral, and developmental consequences of SAPAP4 loss; this screen localizes adult-brain transcriptomic liabilities to two main glutamatergic classes and a Vgf/Scg2 output.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The assay measures acute transcriptomic effects, not synaptic ultrastructure, migration, plasticity, or behavior.

summary: Auts2 perturbation produced an unusually sparse transcriptomic phenotype across the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The absence of a broad RNA program is itself informative because AUTS2 is disease-linked, loss-of-function constrained, and mechanistically connected to transcriptional and cytoskeletal neurodevelopmental pathways.
main_caveats: Target-transcript abundance is not a direct editing or protein readout, and many contexts had fewer than 70 perturbed cells.

summary: The only FDR-significant downstream Auts2 effect was Dpysl4 induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: This nominates a thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic context for follow-up while preventing nominal changes in many other cell types from being overinterpreted as a recurrent AUTS2 program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Dpysl4 passed FDR; nearby nominal genes did not; the thalamic Auts2 transcript itself was not significantly depleted.

summary: Auts2 signatures did not converge with assayed AUTS2-complex, NRF1, Rac/Cdc42, or β-catenin perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: Prior work places AUTS2 in nuclear PRC1/EP300/CK2/NRF1 biology and cytoplasmic RAC1/CDC42 regulation; the dataset argues that those relationships are not interchangeable RNA-seq signatures in the assayed mouse-brain cells.
main_caveats: Correlations use whole-transcriptome score vectors from the same cell type but do not prove editing efficiency or rule out non-transcriptional AUTS2 phenotypes.

summary: The WNT/β-catenin rescue direction from AUTS2-deficient human organoids was not recapitulated as a Ctnnb1-linked signature in this Auts2 perturbation dataset.
why_it_matters: It cautions against generalizing WNT inhibition as a broad AUTS2-loss response marker without first demonstrating that an assayed cell state has actually engaged a WNT-like AUTS2 program.
main_caveats: The literature context is human cerebral organoid knockout, whereas the dataset is mouse-brain Perturb-seq with no protein or WNT activity reporter.

summary: Gp6 produced a pan-assay null response: no gene in any of 21 assayed neuronal cell classes passed FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset result is absence of a reproducible cell-autonomous neuronal transcriptional phenotype, not a hidden GPVI pathway program.
main_caveats: This does not prove organismal dispensability; platelets, megakaryocytes, and injured vasculature were not assayed.

summary: The null response coincided with no measurable Gp6 target-transcript depletion, consistent with perturbing a transcript that is essentially absent from these neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: FDR-negative downstream data should be interpreted as lack of target engagement or baseline receptor expression rather than as compensation downstream of an active GPVI receptor.
main_caveats: Extreme positive or negative logFC values on the Gp6 self rows conflict with near-zero Wilcoxon scores and p values near 1, so target engagement is judged from scores and p values rather than logFC.

summary: Pvalb, Sst, MEA/CA1/DG, and cerebellar GABA classes contained the largest nominal Gp6 outliers, but these peaks were isolated and FDR-negative.
why_it_matters: Cpsf2, Ddx5, Lrrfip1, Eef2k, Mphosph8, and Sumo1 should not be treated as validated GPVI-response biomarkers without replication.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: These are weak conventional signals with FDR values from 0.302 to 0.841 and small perturbed-cell counts in several cell types.

summary: Canonical GPVI-FcR gamma cascade transcripts remained unchanged after Gp6 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not show activation or repression of the Fcer1g-Fyn/Lyn-Syk-Lat-Lcp2-Plcg2 axis that defines platelet GPVI signaling.
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measures mRNA, whereas acute GPVI signaling is dominated by receptor complex formation and tyrosine phosphorylation.

summary: Available GPVI-adjacent and platelet/microglial receptor perturbations were also FDR-silent and were not strong positive or negative Gp6 signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: The related-target comparison argues against a missed neuronal collagen-receptor module and makes the weak Gp6 signature look target-class-wide rather than unique to Gp6.
main_caveats: Most core GPVI effectors, including Fcer1g, Lyn, Syk, Lat, Lcp2, and Plcg2, were measured only as response genes and were not independent perturbation targets in this library.

summary: The neuronal null does not directionally test GPVI inhibition for stroke or thrombosis, where the relevant biology is platelet collagen signaling.
why_it_matters: GP6 has platelet bleeding/thromboembolic disease links and a clinical GPVI inhibitor, so the absence of a neuronal cell-autonomous response should not be used as evidence for or against antithrombotic efficacy.
main_caveats: The screen lacks injured vessels, circulating platelets, collagen exposure, thrombin/fibrin endpoints, and bleeding phenotypes.

summary: Kmt2b perturbation produced a dominant, mostly downregulated program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Single-cell RNA measures transcript rather than protein depletion, and the screen does not localize direct KMT2B chromatin binding.

summary: A small negative marker panel recurred across Kmt2b-responsive cell types, with Stxbp2 and Csf2ra as the most replicated FDR-supported genes.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparison used rank/score similarity of RNA signatures; some comparator perturbations may differ in guide potency and protein turnover.

summary: Neuronal Kmt2b loss drove loss-of-function-like downregulatory states, so further KMT2B suppression is a poor mechanistic match for KMT2B haploinsufficiency disorders.
why_it_matters: The screen aligns Kmt2b knockdown with transcriptional loss rather than rescue, supporting caution for any CNS strategy that directly or indirectly disables KMT2B-containing H3K4 complexes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No compound was tested, the disease cell of origin is not specified by the screen, and KMT2B protein or H3K4 methylation was not assayed.

main_caveats: The dataset did not contain pericytes, vascular smooth muscle, endothelial cells, or direct potassium-current measurements.

summary: Kif11 produced no transcriptome-wide FDR-significant response and no measurable Kif11 target-transcript shift across 19 represented neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset result is a high-confidence negative mRNA phenotype, so isolated nominal genes should not be interpreted as a Kif11 program.
main_caveats: Kif11 mRNA is an incomplete proxy for DNA editing or protein loss; perturbation cell counts were small.

summary: Kif11 perturbation did not move a canonical mitotic-spindle/KIF11-neighbor mRNA module.
why_it_matters: KIF11's best-established role is spindle bipolarity in dividing cells; the absent Nek6/Nek9/Tpx2/Kif23/Cdc20/Cdk1 response indicates that this literature-derived pathway was not engaged in the sampled neuronal DE readout.
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA changes does not exclude altered spindle protein, progenitor phenotypes, or morphology outside the measured postmitotic classes.

summary: Kif11 was weaker than most assayed KIF/KLC genes and far weaker than structural tubulin perturbations, with near-zero KIF-family signature correlations.
why_it_matters: The result argues against extrapolating from axonal/cargo kinesins or tubulin perturbations to Kif11, a mitotic Kinesin-5 motor.
main_caveats: Comparator cell counts and guide efficacies differ; the correlation analysis used transcriptome scores only.

summary: CB GABA, Pvalb GABA, and CA3/CA2/DG glutamatergic cells carried the largest Kif11 nominal tails, but none yielded a reproducible or FDR-significant biomarker.
why_it_matters: The nominal peaks identify where a follow-up might start, while preventing overinterpretation of Sar1b, Lifr, or Ppp6r2 as validated Kif11 response genes.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: All highlighted genes are nominal only; the top three cell types had 30-52 matched perturbed cells and no repeated p<0.001 gene was seen across cell types.

summary: KIF11-linked microcephaly is not recapitulated as a broad acute mRNA program in the postmitotic mouse neuronal classes assayed here.
why_it_matters: The genetic and neuronal-migration literature remains compatible with KIF11 acting through progenitor mitosis or neuronal cytoskeletal morphology rather than through a strong endpoint transcriptional shift in these classes.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks direct progenitor mitosis, live migration, dendrite/axon morphology, and KIF11 protein assays.

summary: Although KIF11 is directly druggable, this Perturb-seq experiment does not provide a neuronal mRNA pharmacodynamic signature for KIF11 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Clinical KIF11 inhibitors should be evaluated with mitotic and cytoskeletal endpoints; the Kif11 nominal DE genes in this dataset are too weak and Safe_target-like to serve as response markers.
main_caveats: The dataset is genetic Perturb-seq in mouse brain cell classes, not acute small-molecule exposure in a proliferating tumor or progenitor system.

summary: The Fhit perturbation did not produce measurable Fhit mRNA depletion or any FDR-significant transcriptome in the 22 profiled cell types.
why_it_matters: The primary biological conclusion is assay-level: this screen cannot support a strong acute loss-of-Fhit interpretation even though FHIT encodes a defined Ap3A hydrolase that is expressed in brain atlases.
main_caveats: Editing, protein depletion, and protein activity were not measured; a nuclease knockout can retain mutant transcript even when protein is perturbed.

summary: The apparent strongest cell-type effects were isolated nominal CA3, NP-CT, and CNU-MGE hits rather than an FDR-supported selective Fhit program.
why_it_matters: The low adjusted significance and lack of recurrence argue against promoting Snd1, Senp6, Phf3, Tfdp1, or Ubr2 as Fhit effectors in mouse brain without validation.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The conclusion is about absence of robust differential expression; subtle protein or activity changes could be missed.

summary: Fhit signatures were uncoupled from beta-catenin/Ctnnb1 perturbation despite literature placing FHIT in a beta-catenin transcriptional repressor complex.
why_it_matters: This prevents transferring FHIT-Wnt expectations from cancer-cell overexpression assays directly onto this acute mouse-brain perturbation readout.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a pathway-neighbor contrast, not a biochemical test; weak Fhit target-transcript engagement makes the negative Fhit arm underpowered.

summary: The TK1-linked replication-stress mechanism described for FHIT loss in proliferating cancer models was absent from the neuronal Fhit signatures.
why_it_matters: A pathway that depends on replication fork progression is unlikely to be scored by acute perturbation of largely postmitotic brain cell classes, especially without measurable Fhit mRNA loss.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay DNA damage, cell-cycle state, dNTP pools, or long-term genome instability.

summary: A global signature-neighbor scan found no robust convergent or opposing perturbation for Fhit.
why_it_matters: The broad Fhit score vector behaved like a weak/null signature rather than a hidden member of a larger perturbation module.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and do not establish direct genetic or physical interactions.

summary: Hecw2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the assayed mouse-brain atlas: no cell class contained an FDR<0.05 gene.
why_it_matters: The absence of multiplicity-controlled mRNA effects means that the perturbation cannot be interpreted as a strong Hecw2 loss-of-function transcriptomic state; HECW2 biology may be post-transcriptional, developmentally timed, or insufficiently engaged in this assay.
main_caveats: Negative at the transcriptome/FDR level only; nominal genes exist, and HECW2 substrates can be regulated at protein rather than RNA level.

summary: Nominal on-target transcript reduction was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, whereas the lowest-count pineal glutamatergic class moved in the opposite direction.
why_it_matters: The dataset gives the clearest Hecw2-guide readout in two subcortical neuronal classes, but even these classes lack FDR-controlled downstream genes; the pineal result is a warning that small cell classes can invert the target readout.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: All target-transcript adjusted p values were 1.0; 217 P MY Pineal Glut contains only 33 Hecw2-targeted cells.

summary: The p73 and GDNF/RET/AKT/NEDD8 axes linked to NEDL2 in prior studies were not recovered as coordinated mRNA modules after Hecw2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This separates the mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout from protein-stability and enteric/kidney mechanisms described for HECW2/NEDL2, so absence of Ret, Gdnf, Akt, Trp73, or Nedd8 transcriptional changes should not be read as absence of biochemical HECW2 activity.
main_caveats: The literature mechanisms are protein-level and were defined mostly in p73 assays or enteric/kidney development, not in the profiled brain cell classes.

summary: Hecw2 did not behave like a generic HECT/E3-ligase perturbation; Huwe1 produced robust FDR-controlled signatures in several overlapping cell classes and Hecw2 correlations with Huwe1, Hectd4, and Ube3a stayed near zero.
why_it_matters: This contrast argues that the weak Hecw2 response is not simply a limitation of the Wilcoxon pipeline or of all E3-ligase perturbations; another ubiquitin-ligase target could be detected with fewer cells in the same cell classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Comparators are related by E3-ligase annotation but are not HECW2 complex members or paralog knockouts.

summary: The weak knockdown transcriptome contrasts with severe human HECW2 missense neurodevelopmental disease, cautioning that patient mechanisms may be domain-specific, dominant, protein-level, or stage-restricted rather than a broad mature-neuron mRNA loss-of-function state.
why_it_matters: HECW2 is a clinically relevant neurodevelopmental gene, but this Perturb-seq result provides no strong cell-type-resolved biomarker for therapeutic rescue and should not be overused to select a disease-vulnerable cell class.
main_caveats: The assay is mouse, guide-based, and mRNA-only; the dataset does not test recurrent patient missense alleles or early embryonic timing.

summary: Top-Hecw2 restricted signature-neighbor searches should be treated as exploratory because weak Hecw2 signatures correlated with annotated Safe_target perturbations as well as biological targets.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpretation of modest top/bottom-gene correlations as mechanistic convergence for Hecw2.

main_caveats: The search was restricted to the top and bottom 300 Hecw2-ranked genes rather than all genes.

direction: no coherent basal IFN or ISG response

summary: Axl perturbation produced neither measurable Axl transcript knockdown nor any FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in the assayed neuronal classes.

summary: The Axl null is most consistent with a neuronal-cell context mismatch: the screen sampled glutamatergic and GABAergic classes, whereas established CNS AXL biology centers on microglia, macrophage-like CNS cells, and vascular-associated cells.
why_it_matters: This reframes the negative screen result as evidence about where AXL signaling was not engaged, rather than evidence that the TAM pathway is irrelevant in brain disease.
main_caveats: The cell-type inference uses cell labels and an external human atlas; raw Axl expression in the perturbed cells was not available.

summary: Mertk, the only assayed TAM paralog, did not converge with Axl, and the other TAM receptor Tyro3 and ligands Gas6 and Pros1 were absent.
why_it_matters: Published microglial biology often treats AXL and MERTK as cooperating phagocytic TAM receptors, but this screen does not contain an engaged TAM module from which paralog interchangeability can be tested.
main_caveats: The contrast is driven by weak Axl and Mertk signatures, so it should not be read as biological antagonism between the receptors.

summary: Neither top nominal genes nor whole-signature neighbors yielded a credible Axl biomarker module.
why_it_matters: A few small nominal p values can look suggestive in isolation, but their high FDR values, lack of recurrence, weak nearest-neighbor correlations, and appearance of safe-target controls argue against treating them as Axl-regulated genes.

summary: The Axl null should not be used to deprioritize pharmacologic AXL inhibition in cancer or microglial disease settings.
why_it_matters: AXL is druggable and disease-linked, but this Perturb-seq subset lacks the responsive ligand-receptor and phagocyte contexts in which AXL/MERTK biology and AXL-targeted therapies are usually motivated.
main_caveats: The claim is directional for interpretation, not a drug-efficacy test; no inhibitor, cancer cell, activated microglia, or amyloid model was profiled in this dataset.

summary: Mnx1 perturbation produced no FDR<0.05 transcriptomic response and no measurable Mnx1 self-knockdown in the assayed brain classes.
why_it_matters: A guide-defined perturbation with 2,300 matched cells can still be biologically silent if the target gene is not active in the sampled states; this prevents overinterpretation of nominal rows as MNX1 biology.
main_caveats: Failure to observe target mRNA reduction can reflect low basal expression or missing target transcript rows; the assay does not prove absence of DNA editing or guide activity.

direction: Ell2 up in Sst GABA; Nalf1 down in MB Glut
summary: Ell2 in Sst GABA and Nalf1 in MB Glut were the only near-FDR Mnx1 candidate responses.

cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Both rows miss FDR<0.05 and each is isolated to one cell type.

summary: Mnx1 nominal hits did not collapse into a recurrent cross-cell-type or all-panel signature module.
why_it_matters: The weak global response was not simply split among many subthreshold members of a repeated pathway; recurrence and correlation analyses both failed to reveal a coherent hidden program.
main_caveats: This is a restricted transcript-level analysis of weak signatures and does not test chromatin occupancy or protein-level perturbation.

direction: developmental neighbors not convergent with Mnx1
summary: Mnx1 did not phenocopy represented ISL1-LHX3/Foxa2/Neurod developmental neighbors in the brain panel.
why_it_matters: The result argues that Mnx1, Isl1, Lhx3 and allied embryonic transcription factors are not interchangeable outside the spinal motor-neuron developmental context, even when all are perturbed in the same brain-wide screen.
main_caveats: STRING edges are functional associations, not proof of a stoichiometric complex in these cell types; the dataset lacks embryonic spinal motor neurons.

summary: The parquet is poorly matched to MNX1 Currarino, spinal motor-neuron and pancreatic biology.
why_it_matters: A brain-screen negative result should not be used to deprioritize MNX1 in congenital caudal-patterning or pancreatic contexts where the gene is developmentally active.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: This is an inference from sampled cell-type coverage and public expression biology, not a direct assay of sacral, spinal-cord, or pancreatic tissue.

summary: Kifbp was transcriptionally knocked down in a broad set of neuronal classes rather than in one lineage only.
why_it_matters: The perturbation was sufficiently engaged to ask whether Kifbp loss couples to downstream state changes, with the caveat that only 8 of 23 classes survived transcript-level FDR correction.

summary: Most well-engaged Kifbp contrasts were target-only or nearly target-only transcriptional signatures.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: A sparse transcriptome does not rule out changes in axonal transport, organelle positioning, neuronal morphology, or later developmental consequences.

summary: Srebf2 downregulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut nominates a weak SREBP/cholesterol-biosynthesis readout of Kifbp loss.
why_it_matters: SREBF2 and several mevalonate/sterol genes trended downward, suggesting a possible metabolic biomarker to test in deeper KIFBP loss-of-function models.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA

summary: Kifbp did not transcriptionally phenocopy available kinesin-family, STMN2/DCTN1, or RET-neighborhood perturbations.

main_caveats: The comparison used bulk score-vector correlations within cell types; weak guide counts for some comparator perturbations and transcriptomic readout only could obscure local transport phenotypes.

summary: The buffered mature-neuron transcriptome should not be interpreted as benign KIFBP loss-of-function biology.
why_it_matters: Human reduced or absent KIFBP expression causes Goldberg-Shprintzen syndrome and mouse Kif1bp loss is perinatally lethal; the dataset shows that even clear RNA knockdown may leave few immediate DE markers in sampled brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is an acute partial knockdown in mouse brain cell classes, whereas Goldberg-Shprintzen syndrome and the mouse knockout reflect organismal developmental loss of function.

summary: Fntb perturbation was weak at the transcript level and produced only one FDR<0.05 gene across all assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: FNTB is the beta subunit of an enzyme complex that farnesylates CaaX proteins, so transcript abundance is only an indirect handle on pathway flux; the dataset therefore supports cautious interpretation rather than a broad farnesylation-loss state.
main_caveats: The dataset measured mRNA, not FNTB protein, farnesyltransferase activity, or protein prenylation.

summary: The only stringent Fntb response was an exploratory Nefl/Nefh/Nefm neurofilament upshift restricted to 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: A cell-restricted axonal-cytoskeletal marker is more interpretable than a single isolated Nefl row and is directionally compatible with literature showing that neuronal farnesyltransferase can influence neuronal morphology or AD-related neuronal signaling.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only Nefl passed FDR<0.05; the cell type had only 27 perturbed cells and Fntb itself was not significantly decreased after FDR correction.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the strongest nominal Fntb mRNA reduction and the largest Fntb-matched cell count, yet no robust downstream DE.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from phenotypic output and suggests that partial Fntb mRNA loss can be buffered transcriptionally in at least one well-sampled thalamic glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Fntb transcript decrease itself had FDR=1.0, so the buffering call is relative to the best observed on-target row rather than to a confirmed knockout.

summary: Fntb did not phenocopy available Hras or Kras knockdowns, despite FNTB acting upstream of mature RAS membrane targeting.
why_it_matters: The result argues against reading Fntb mRNA knockdown as a simple RAS-transcript knockdown surrogate in this assay; an enzyme perturbation, multiple CaaX substrates, and limited knockdown can decouple the signatures.
main_caveats: Fnta and RAS-processing enzyme perturbations were missing, several GTPase knockdowns were weakly engaged, and the top-neighbor audit used only the strongest 200 Fntb genes per cell type.

summary: Fntb knockdown did not elicit FDR-level transcriptional compensation by measured CaaX-processing or prenylation genes.
why_it_matters: If neurons compensated for reduced FTase by inducing FNTA, GGTase, RCE1, ICMT, or isoprenoid-supply transcripts, that would change the mechanistic interpretation; the dataset instead shows no robust mRNA feedback at these pathway nodes.
main_caveats: Unchanged mRNA does not rule out compensation by enzyme activity, alternative prenylation, substrate localization, or protein turnover.

summary: Col25a1 perturbation did not produce FDR-supported depletion of its own transcript in any of 22 profiled cell types.
why_it_matters: Without measurable on-target depletion, downstream null effects cannot be interpreted as proof of biological buffering or dispensability.
main_caveats: The statement is about measured RNA engagement; it does not test collagen XXV protein loss.

summary: Col25a1 caused no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any cell type, and the numerically strongest thalamic response remained nominal.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not support a cell-type-specific Col25a1 RNA program to carry forward into pathway interpretation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Nominal genes were not significant after multiple testing and are secondary to weak target engagement.

summary: The APP/Aβ-linked Col25a1 perturbation did not significantly change App, Bace1, or Syp expression.
why_it_matters: Known COL25A1 Alzheimer mechanisms involve Aβ binding, BACE1 increase under overexpression, and plaque remodeling; the Perturb-seq negative result argues against inferring acute reversal of that protein-level plaque biology from this weak knockdown dataset.
main_caveats: Col25a1 on-target depletion was not significant, and the literature perturbation direction and plaque context differ from acute brain-cell Perturb-seq.

summary: Ptprs and Ptprd did not show significant feedback under Col25a1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This separates the developmental collagen XXV-PTPσ/δ motor-axon attraction mechanism from the assayed mouse-brain transcriptional context.
main_caveats: The PTPσ/δ mechanism is muscle-derived and developmental; absence of Ptprs/Ptprd RNA feedback in brain neurons does not falsify that pathway.

summary: App and Syp perturbations had strong target-only depletion signatures, whereas Col25a1 and other APP-processing neighbors were FDR-null.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that target transcript depletion was detectable for some neuronal genes in the same dataset, so Col25a1 failure is perturbation-specific, while also showing that acute App-family perturbations need not yield broad AD-like RNA states.
main_caveats: Syp is a neuronal depletion comparator rather than a direct COL25A1 pathway member; Adam10, Psen1, and Ptprd were themselves weak perturbations.

summary: No recurrent top positive or top negative signature neighbor of Col25a1 was found across cell types.
why_it_matters: The weak Col25a1 signal was not rescued by a reproducible convergent module among all perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations used only the top 200 nominal Col25a1 genes in each cell type; because the seed signatures were FDR-null, one-off neighbors are not mechanistic evidence.

summary: Atp2a2 knockdown was widespread but the downstream transcriptional response was dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: The target transcript moved in the expected direction in all tested classes, so the sparse response elsewhere is not simply absence of guide activity; it indicates strong cell-context dependence of SERCA2 loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only 21 of the 23 dataset cell classes had enough Atp2a2-targeted cells to test; low n_pert in some classes decreases power.

main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA only; it does not measure ER calcium, XBP1 splicing, CHOP protein, or cell death.

summary: Multiple classes buffered a strong Atp2a2 transcript knockdown without any downstream FDR-significant genes.

summary: A compact ER/ISR marker set recurred outside 151 even when the whole signature was small.
why_it_matters: Chac1-Ddit3-Slc3a2 in 155 MB Glut, Hspa5-Creld2 in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and Eprs/Mbd2 with nominal Chac1 in 191 MB P MY GABA flag candidate sentinel readouts for partial Atp2a2 stress responses that would be missed by counting FDR genes alone.

summary: The Atp2a2 151 signature aligned more with stress/proteostasis neighbors than with the available Ryr, Itpr, Stim, or Atf6 calcium-pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues that the measured Atp2a2 state is not just a generic ER-calcium-homeostasis perturbation captured by other channels or sensors; however, the top-neighbor analysis also exposes that several high correlations lack clean target-transcript knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Most top positive signature neighbors in 151 did not verify by self-transcript FDR, and several calcium-pathway comparators had weak or nominal-only target engagement.

summary: The dataset is directionally consistent with restoring or activating SERCA2 rather than inhibiting it in vulnerable neurons.
why_it_matters: The transcriptomic consequence of Atp2a2 depletion is an ER-stress/ISR program, while curated pharmacology and neuronal excitotoxicity work emphasize SERCA2 activation or restoration as the protective direction; ATP2A2 inhibition would be expected to intensify the same stress axis.

summary: Atp2a2-sensitive neuronal subclasses offer a cell-type hypothesis for why ATP2A2 loss-of-function biology can include inconsistent neuropsychiatric manifestations in Darier disease.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Darier disease is heterozygous human germline ATP2A2 mutation, whereas the dataset is acute mouse neuronal perturbation and does not assay behavior or epidermis.

summary: Mpdz targeting produced weak on-target transcript depletion and no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome in any of 22 assayed neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: The perturbation should not be read as a clean MPDZ loss-of-function screen; the strongest biological conclusion is that this dataset did not achieve a robust Mpdz-loss state in the measured neuronal populations.
main_caveats: The negative result is confounded by modest cell recovery and the absence of statistically significant Mpdz transcript depletion.

summary: The only coherent Mpdz-associated signature was an exploratory CA3/CA2-fasciola-cinereum/dentate-gyrus glutamatergic program containing nominally up-regulated ion-exchange, potassium-channel, plexin, and trafficking genes.
why_it_matters: MUPP1 is a synaptic and membrane scaffold, so a CA3-restricted membrane-excitability readout is biologically plausible even though it remains a validation hypothesis rather than an FDR-supported pathway.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Mpdz itself was not significantly depleted in this cell type, no CA3 Mpdz-regulated gene passed FDR, and the pathway label is inferred from a small nominal gene set.

summary: Perturbing known MUPP1 receptor and postsynaptic partners did not phenocopy the Mpdz signature; the closest Htr2c, GABAB, NMDAR-SynGAP-CaMKII, and Dlg4 comparators were near-zero or opposite to Mpdz.

cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The comparison uses whole-transcriptome score correlations from weak primary Mpdz signatures and does not measure receptor localization or synaptic physiology.

summary: The neuronal Mpdz Perturb-seq screen does not model the ependymal Crumbs/Pals1/tight-junction mechanism that explains MPDZ congenital hydrocephalus.
why_it_matters: A lack of robust neuronal tight-junction transcription after Mpdz targeting should not be taken as evidence against the established epithelial/ependymal barrier disease mechanism.
main_caveats: The dataset assayed neuronal classes, not fetal ependyma or choroid plexus epithelium; several core polarity partners were not perturbation targets.

summary: The dataset provides no transcriptomic support for beneficial MPDZ inhibition, while the prior loss-of-function literature and sparse ChEMBL profile argue that MPDZ suppression would be a safety-sensitive and poorly ligandable direction.
why_it_matters: MPDZ is a scaffold whose loss damages ependymal integrity and worsens alcohol-withdrawal convulsions in mouse RNAi experiments, so any attempt to lower MPDZ should be benchmarked against hydrocephalus and neuronal-excitability liabilities.
main_caveats: The perturbation screen is weak and does not test long-term organismal toxicity or target ligandability directly.

summary: Outside the CA3/CA2-fasciola-cinereum/dentate-gyrus class, Mpdz signature-neighbor structure was too small and safe-target-like to nominate a recurrent biological module.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of isolated top neighbors in entorhinal, thalamic, or other groups whose correlations were on the order of safe-target controls.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Safe-target comparisons identify weak neighbor structure, not the source of all residual nominal genes.

summary: Ffar1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic signature in any analyzed neuronal cell type.
why_it_matters: The direct Perturb-seq readout argues against a broad cell-autonomous FFAR1 transcriptional program in this mouse-brain screen, despite FFAR1 being a well defined fatty-acid GPCR.
main_caveats: The absence of FDR-significant DE is strong, but the result does not prove biological dispensability because target engagement was not detected for Ffar1 itself.

summary: The Ffar1 transcript was analyzable in only 2 of 22 Ffar1 perturbation contrasts and neither showed self-depletion.
why_it_matters: A null perturbation with the target transcript missing from most tests is best interpreted as expression- and engagement-limited, not as evidence that all brain cells buffer loss of the receptor.

main_caveats: A missing DE row records failure to pass the dataset gene filter, not a direct zero-expression measurement; guide cutting and Ffar1 protein loss were not measured.

summary: The absent Ffar1 self-targeting signal contrasts with detectable on-target knockdown for several available Gq/PLC or downstream signaling neighbors.
why_it_matters: The same analysis table can recover direct depletion of Itpr1, Plcb1, Mapk1, and Prkcg, so the uninterpretable Ffar1 phenotype is not simply a universal failure of GPCR-proximal signaling genes in the dataset.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: These are pathway-neighbor perturbations rather than FFAR paralogs, and most neighbor effects are on-target transcript rows rather than shared downstream FFAR1 signatures.

summary: Hypothalamus-associated Ffar1 perturbation contrasts were also flat, even though mouse literature assigns hypothalamic FFAR1 roles in energy balance and neurogenesis.
why_it_matters: The dataset narrows where the published hypothalamic phenotype is likely to appear: it is not captured as a strong steady-state transcriptional response in the screened broad HY GABA or HY/MM glutamatergic classes.

main_caveats: The cell types are broad labels and the target transcript was not itself detected in these two contrasts, so this should not be read as a contradiction of hypothalamic FFAR1 biology.

summary: The strongest nominal rows, including Dyrk1b, Cacna1b, and Vegfa, were isolated and failed FDR correction.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: All cited genes are nominal only for Ffar1; none was significant after multiple-testing correction.

summary: The screen supplies little CNS therapeutic-direction information for FFAR1 agonism or antagonism.
why_it_matters: FFAR1 is a druggable type 2 diabetes target, but a brain CRISPR null with no confirmed Ffar1 knockdown should not be used as evidence for either CNS safety or CNS efficacy of FFAR1-directed drugs.
main_caveats: The dataset measures transcription after genetic perturbation in mouse brain cell classes, whereas the clinical literature concerns small-molecule FFAR1 agonism for metabolic disease.

summary: Cep290 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response and no confirmed RNA-level target-transcript depletion in any profiled brain cell class.

summary: The ciliary transition-zone neighborhood was usually transcriptionally quiet even when related targets were measurably self-depleted.
why_it_matters: Ahi1, Cplane1, and Ttc8 examples argue that absence of broad trans-DE is not unique to Cep290 and may reflect buffering or post-transcriptional cilium biology in the profiled brain classes.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This inference is cross-perturbation and RNA based; the on-target examples are not Cep290, and a self-only transcript phenotype can reflect perturbation efficiency, compensation, or lack of a short-term transcriptional branch.

summary: A weak cerebellar GABA overlap between Cep290 and B9d1 nominated a possible 308 CB GABA ciliary-neighbor module, but it is exploratory.
