main_caveats: Cep290 did not reach FDR on the overlapping genes, neither Cep290 nor B9d1 showed RNA-level self-depletion in 308 CB GABA, and high cerebellar correlations included safe-target guides, so this module could be technical or guide-set specific.

summary: A whole-panel signature-neighbor search did not reveal a reproducible biological Cep290 agonist or antagonist signature outside the 308 CB GABA tail.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpreting individual nominal genes as pathway output; top same-cell-type correlations were weak in the other 19 cell classes and showed no coherent ciliopathy-neighbor structure.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on full Wilcoxon score vectors, and the primary Cep290 vectors themselves were weak, making all neighbor calls secondary.

summary: The dataset supports using direct CEP290 RNA/protein or ciliary localization endpoints, not broad mouse-brain trans-DE, as biomarkers for CEP290-restoring therapies.
why_it_matters: Human CEP290 treatment efforts are allele-specific mRNA-splicing interventions for retinal LCA10, whereas this mouse-brain perturbation output contains no reliable downstream transcript module to monitor rescue.
main_caveats: Sepofarsen acts on a human intronic splice mutation in photoreceptors; the dataset is mouse brain and does not test drug exposure, splicing correction, or retinal cells.

summary: Cltc knockdown was target-engaged in only a subset of assayed neuronal classes, and the transcriptional response was concentrated in seven to eight classes rather than being pan-neuronal.
why_it_matters: A core endocytic coat protein produced a highly state- or cell-type-dependent RNA phenotype; absence of a broad signature in many classes should not be read as absence of clathrin biology because target depletion was often only nominal and perturbation cell counts were small.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Every cell-type comparison used only 21-58 perturbed cells, and several classes lacked FDR-level depletion of the Cltc transcript.

summary: The reproducible Cltc response was a Jun/Stmn4-high stress and remodeling program, not a uniform transcriptional induction of the clathrin machinery.
why_it_matters: Jun and Stmn4 were the most recurrent positive genes across responsive cell types, while each cell class carried different synaptic, secretory or excitability genes; these transcripts provide candidate early biomarkers of failed endomembrane homeostasis after Cltc perturbation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Jun and Stmn4 are not specific reporters of clathrin failure; several recurrent genes were supported at FDR<0.1 rather than FDR<0.05.

summary: Cltc loss preferentially repressed synaptic-vesicle, neurotransmission and ion-channel genes in selected glutamatergic classes, especially 155 MB Glut and 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: Human CLTC disease models emphasize defective synaptic transmission; the dataset refines that prior mechanism by showing that the strongest synaptic transcript loss occurs in particular neuronal classes rather than across all Cltc-guide cells.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The L4-5 intratelencephalic response had no detectable Cltc mRNA depletion, and scRNA-seq does not directly measure synaptic-vesicle recycling.

summary: Several classes showed nominal Cltc transcript reduction but little or no FDR-level downstream transcription, most notably 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: The measured response is compatible with buffering, delayed protein turnover, insufficient power, or a functional defect without a large steady-state mRNA signature; these classes should not be scored as simple biological resistance.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cltc transcript FDR was not significant in these comparisons despite strong nominal scores; low perturbed-cell numbers could mask weak effects.

summary: Top positive Cltc signature neighbors were repeatedly Vps, Atp6, Psm/Psmc and Sec31a perturbations, whereas AP-2, dynamin and Synj1 neighbors mostly failed to rank with the top Cltc-like signatures.
why_it_matters: CLTC is physically and functionally tied to AP-2, so the restricted-signature result suggests that the Cltc RNA state is closer to broader endomembrane/proteostasis perturbations than to knockdown of every canonical endocytic partner.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The comparison used only the 100 lowest nominal-p Cltc genes per cell type and can be biased by unequal guide potency and by the fact that AP-2 or dynamin loss may affect different cargoes or kinetics.

summary: Target-engaged Cltc depletion in GABAergic and glutamatergic neurons induced stress or apoptosis-associated genes such as Jun, Ddit3 and Bcl2l11, so acute CLTC inhibition in brain would be expected to carry mechanism-based neuronal liability.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL contains experimental clathrin inhibitors, but the dataset and synaptic genetics argue against treating CLTC as a benign CNS target without cell-type and exposure control.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset reports mRNA after guide perturbation, not pharmacologic CLTC inhibition or cell death; Ddit3 support was FDR<0.1 in only two discussed cells and Bcl2l11 was confined to 308 CB GABA.

summary: Dab1 perturbation did not measurably deplete the Dab1 transcript in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The direct mRNA readout gives no support for strong target engagement, so downstream null results should be interpreted as uninformative or buffered responses rather than as evidence that Dab1 is dispensable.
main_caveats: Single-cell mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for DNA editing or DAB1 protein loss, and most contrasts had few perturbed cells.

summary: No Dab1 cell-type contrast contained an FDR-significant differentially expressed gene, even in the three contrasts with at least 50 perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: The dataset contains only weak nominal structure for Dab1; it does not support a cell-type-selective transcriptional module downstream of Dab1 perturbation.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a high-confidence statement about the Wilcoxon results, but biological buffering cannot be separated from weak target engagement.

summary: Dab1 did not form a detectable transcriptional module with the canonical Reln/Vldlr/Lrp8/Fyn Reelin pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: DAB1 is a core Reelin signaling adaptor, so correlated effects might have been expected if the perturbations engaged the pathway; their absence argues that this Perturb-seq readout did not capture canonical Reelin signal transduction.
main_caveats: Exploratory cross-perturbation comparison; Reln, Vldlr, Lrp8, and Fyn perturbations also lacked FDR-significant target-transcript depletion in this matrix.

summary: The null Dab1 transcriptional signature refines, rather than rejects, the established mouse-developmental requirement for Dab1.
why_it_matters: Mouse null and hypomorphic Dab1 alleles disrupt embryonic cortical, hippocampal, and cerebellar lamination; a weak single-cell RNA response in sampled brain cell classes therefore points to assay timing and modality rather than to absence of Dab1 function.
main_caveats: The dataset does not directly assay neuronal migration, embryonic lamination, DAB1 phosphorylation, or protein abundance.

summary: The Dab1 perturbation should not be interpreted as functional support for lowering DAB1 in spinocerebellar ataxia type 37 or other DAB1-linked indications.
why_it_matters: Human SCA37 is linked to a regulatory DAB1 repeat, but the Perturb-seq arm neither lowered Dab1 mRNA nor produced a disease-relevant cerebellar Purkinje-cell signature; the observed direction is therefore not a validated therapeutic direction.
main_caveats: SCA37 human cerebellar pathology is only indirectly represented by the mouse brain cell classes in the dataset.

summary: The weak Dab1 signatures did not yield a stable transcript biomarker or interpretable positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Nominal genes and nearest-neighbor correlations are useful for hypothesis generation only when they recur or align with biology; here they were singleton, mixed-direction, or nearly uncorrelated.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The all-perturbation neighbor scan was restricted to 155 MB Glut, a better-powered Dab1 contrast with a small but non-significant nominal top cluster.

direction: Fmn2 RNA mostly down with weak downstream DE
summary: Fmn2 knockdown was directionally recurrent at the RNA level but yielded a low-amplitude, mostly sub-FDR transcriptome.
why_it_matters: FMN2 is a cytoskeletal effector; a weak mRNA signature could reflect incomplete guide engagement, post-transcriptional structural biology, or true buffering, so the dataset should not be interpreted as showing a large canonical transcriptional program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|155 MB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Fmn2 target transcript itself never passed FDR correction; protein depletion, editing rate, and cytoskeletal morphology were not measured in the parquet.

direction: Ss18 up in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut; Pign up in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
summary: Ss18 and Pign were isolated Fmn2-response candidates rather than members of a recurring multi-gene module.
why_it_matters: The only FDR<0.05 hit, Ss18 in L4/5 IT cortex, and the only other FDR<0.1 hit, Pign in LGE GABA, provide narrow follow-up biomarkers but do not yet define a coherent FMN2 pathway.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Both hits occurred in cell types where Fmn2 mRNA was not nominally depleted, and Pign was just above the 0.05 FDR threshold.

direction: Fmn2 uncoupled from actin-compensatory transcription; Actb strongly upregulated Actg1 and Flna
summary: Fmn2 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the measured FMN/SPIRE/profilin/actin module, unlike Actb perturbation.
why_it_matters: Known FMN2 biology predicts actin-nucleation machinery, yet the Fmn2 signatures left transcripts for Spire1, Spire2, Fmn1, profilins, Cdc42, Actg1, and Flna nonsignificant while direct Actb perturbation robustly induced Actg1/Flna compensation in the same analysis framework.
main_caveats: This is an mRNA comparison; it does not test FMN2-dependent actin polymerization, protein localization, or actin filament morphology directly.

summary: The Fmn2 and Fmn1 paralog perturbations were not transcriptionally interchangeable.
why_it_matters: Fmn1 and Fmn2 both sit near the Spire actin-nucleation network, but their ranked DE signatures were essentially uncorrelated in every shared cell class, arguing against using Fmn1 as a simple transcriptional proxy for Fmn2 in this dataset.
main_caveats: Both Fmn1 and Fmn2 perturbations produced weak single-cell signatures, so low correlation mainly excludes a strong shared mRNA program rather than a shared cytoskeletal role.

direction: weak acute mRNA response despite neurodevelopmental actin literature
summary: The FMN2 intellectual-disability link is better aligned with structural neuronal phenotypes than with a broad acute transcriptional program in this Perturb-seq readout.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic FMN2 truncations and neuronal growth-cone studies implicate F-actin-dependent neurodevelopmental architecture; the mouse-brain perturbation data show broad Fmn2 sampling but little corrected mRNA response, refining the expected disease readout toward morphology, axon guidance, or synaptic architecture.
main_caveats: The dataset does not include developmental time courses, dendritic-spine measurements, growth-cone assays, or human patient cells.

summary: A genome-wide same-cell signature-neighbor search found no robust recurrent positive or negative neighbor for Fmn2.
why_it_matters: The lack of a strong neighbor makes Fmn2 a sparse and cell-context-dependent perturbation rather than part of a high-amplitude transcriptomic cluster in this screen.
main_caveats: The neighbor search used Wilcoxon score correlations from the DE table rather than raw single-cell expression or morphological phenotypes.

summary: Cd14 perturbation was transcriptionally inert across all 22 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not support a cell-autonomous CD14 program in the sampled excitatory, inhibitory, hindbrain, thalamic, pineal or cerebellar neurons; this is consistent with CD14 being primarily an innate-immune receptor rather than a broadly active neuronal regulator.
main_caveats: The parquet contains DE summaries rather than raw UMIs or edit calls, so absent Cd14 expression and failed guide engagement cannot be separated.

summary: Canonical CD14/TLR inflammatory output genes were flat after Cd14 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Cd14 sits upstream of LPS/TLR4 and TLR1/2 signaling in immune cells, so the absence of Tnf, interleukins, chemokines, NF-kappaB feedback genes and interferon-stimulated genes indicates that these neuronal baseline cultures were not in a ligand-activated CD14 state.
main_caveats: The experiment was loss-of-function under basal conditions, not acute LPS or lipoteichoic-acid stimulation of immune cells.

summary: Cd14 failed to converge with the present Tlr2, Tlr4 and Nfkb1 perturbations despite these genes belonging to the same innate signaling neighborhood.
why_it_matters: A true recurrent innate-response module should have produced at least same-direction score correlations or FDR-significant targets among pathway neighbors; instead all available receptor/pathway neighbors were also weak in these cell types.
main_caveats: Ly96, Lbp and Myd88 were not available as perturbation targets, and correlations compare weak basal signatures rather than ligand-driven signaling.

summary: High Cd14 cell counts did not unmask a downstream program.
why_it_matters: The negative result is not confined to tiny perturbation bins: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut had the two largest Cd14 cell counts but only FDR=1.0 nominal leaders, arguing that low count alone is insufficient to explain the lack of signal.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Because Cd14 transcript was not measurably engaged, this is best viewed as apparent buffering or target absence, not proven post-knockout compensation.

summary: The strongest nominal Cd14 genes are not credible biomarkers of CD14 biology in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Top genes such as Sh3glb2, Jdp2, Cd46 and Zzz3 were private to single cell types, failed FDR correction, and lacked strong all-library signature neighbors; promoting them would overfit rank tails rather than reveal a reproducible CD14 module.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The statement addresses reproducibility within this Perturb-seq screen only; it is not a claim about these genes in stimulated macrophages or microglia.

summary: The dataset is a poor efficacy model for anti-CD14 neuroinflammatory therapy because it lacks the microglial CD14 context.
why_it_matters: CD14 blockade is being clinically explored and microglia use TLR/CD14 circuitry, but the screen interrogates mostly neuronal basal states with no Cd14 target engagement or cytokine output; drug conclusions should therefore be moved to microglia-rich, ligand-challenged assays.
main_caveats: This is a direction-of-follow-up warning, not evidence that CD14 blockade is beneficial or harmful in vivo.

summary: Insr-targeting guides produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any of the 23 measured neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: INSR is a signaling receptor with canonical IRS/PI3K and Ras/MAPK outputs, so the absence of corrected single-cell mRNA changes indicates that acute Insr loss is buffered, weakly engaged, or primarily post-transcriptional in this dataset rather than a broad transcriptional driver.
main_caveats: The parquet contains only mRNA differential-expression summaries; receptor protein abundance, acute phosphorylation, insulin ligand exposure, guide identity, and raw-cell QC were not measured here.

summary: The only recurrent Insr signal was a weak, nominal on-target decrease, most evident in a few subcortical classes rather than a corrected cortical or pan-neuronal program.
why_it_matters: This weak selectivity argues against interpreting individual nominal off-target-row genes as a shared Insr program, but it leaves open that some midbrain, pontine, medullary, or hypothalamic neurons were more permissive for target-transcript reduction.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All Insr on-target FDR values were 1.0, the rarest dopamine and pineal classes had only 21-29 perturbed cells, and apparent cell-type selectivity could reflect guide efficiency or baseline Insr expression rather than true signaling dependence.

summary: The upstream insulin/IGF-PI3K arm was as muted as Insr, whereas the Tsc1/Tsc2/Pten brake on mTOR produced large, cell-restricted transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: INSR, IGF1R, IRS1, PI3K, PTEN, TSC, MTOR, and RPTOR occupy one curated signaling network, but the Perturb-seq phenotypes separate receptor/PI3K entry nodes from the negative mTOR regulators, localizing the transcriptome-sensitive branch to the TSC/PTEN region rather than to Insr itself.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The strong comparator signatures do not prove mTORC1 activation in the assayed cells, and differences in sgRNA cutting, transcript stability, and baseline expression can contribute to cross-perturbation contrasts.

summary: The lack of an acute Insr stress or death-like transcriptome is consistent with chronic NIRKO phenotypes arising through circuit physiology, dopaminergic metabolism, or post-translational signaling rather than immediate broad neuronal mRNA remodeling.
why_it_matters: NIRKO mouse studies demonstrate important brain-level consequences of neuronal insulin-receptor loss; the Perturb-seq result narrows the expected cell-autonomous readout of Insr perturbation in these cell classes.
main_caveats: Dataset cells, age, assay timing, and guide modality are not the same as chronic whole-brain NIRKO animals, and the dataset lacks behavioral, metabolic, dopamine, and mitochondrial assays.

summary: Insr inhibition should not be treated as a transcriptomic proxy for mTORC1 inhibition in these neurons.
why_it_matters: Although insulin can activate PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 through TSC2, Insr perturbation neither opposed nor phenocopied Tsc1, Tsc2, or Pten programs; therapeutic reasoning aimed at neuronal mTOR-like disease signatures should therefore focus on the pathway node and cell type, not just the upstream receptor map.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: No drug treatment, rapamycin-sensitive phospho-S6 readout, or rescue experiment was performed; this is a warning about directional inference, not evidence that INSR pharmacology is ineffective in vivo.

summary: A scan for all-gene signature neighbors found no strong Insr-like or anti-Insr perturbation in the cell types where Insr looked least null.
why_it_matters: The weak correlations, including control-like top neighbors in some cell types, argue that the absence of FDR-significant Insr hits is not hiding a coherent module shared with another perturbation.
comparators: all perturbations in the same cell type
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The scan used Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon-score vectors and was summarized for the five cell types with the smallest Insr minimum FDR values; weaker local correlations may still reflect technical or biological programs.

summary: Manba targeting produced no FDR-significant differential-expression signature in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: This prevents assignment of a robust Manba downstream program from the dataset and makes the nominal top genes exploratory only.
main_caveats: A null FDR signature can reflect weak target engagement or missing protein/storage phenotypes, not necessarily absence of MANBA biology.

summary: Only 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut showed nominal Manba mRNA decreases, and none passed FDR correction.
why_it_matters: The only apparent cell-type restriction is weak and target-row-only, so it should be used to prioritize validation rather than to infer a GABA or thalamic Manba pathway.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Nominal p values only; pvals_adj=1.0 in all three cell types.

summary: Lysosomal glycan-catabolism genes were not detectably co-regulated after Manba targeting, and broader lysosomal perturbations in the panel were mostly self-transcript depletion events without secondary FDR genes.
why_it_matters: The expected MANBA biology is lysosomal N-glycan/oligosaccharide catabolism, but this Perturb-seq readout appears poorly coupled to that enzymatic pathway at the mRNA level.
main_caveats: The restricted neighbor test used non-FDR Manba genes; the direct sequential hydrolases MAN2B1 and MAN2B2 were absent from the panel.

summary: CA3- and piriform/retrosplenial-related neuronal classes did not show an acute Manba signature despite chronic beta-mannosidase-deficient mice showing selective neuropathology in overlapping brain regions.
why_it_matters: The result separates this weak Perturb-seq mRNA perturbation from lifelong enzyme deficiency and warns against using the null signature to rule out neuronal storage vulnerability.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type mapping to disease regions is approximate, and the dataset did not demonstrate strong Manba depletion in these classes.

summary: The absence of a Manba transcriptomic phenotype should not be interpreted as evidence that MANBA loss is benign or inhibitor-safe.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse loss-of-function evidence points to beta-mannosidase deficiency as the pathogenic direction, whereas this dataset mostly failed to create a strong on-target knockdown.
main_caveats: The dataset measured mRNA changes rather than enzymatic activity or substrate accumulation.

summary: Galr1 guide cells did not show detectable depletion of the Galr1 transcript in any measured cell class.
why_it_matters: This makes the experiment a weak loss-of-function test of the receptor itself; downstream null results should be read as absence of an RNA phenotype under uncertain target engagement, not as proof that GALR1 protein is dispensable.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is only a proxy for CRISPR editing; productive coding indels without mRNA decay, baseline expression, and receptor protein loss were not measured in this parquet.

summary: Galr1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream gene and no recurrent same-direction nominal module.
why_it_matters: The strongest apparent genes are likely isolated sampling fluctuations or very weak cell-specific effects; they should not be promoted to a Galr1 pathway without orthogonal support.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: All downstream claims are transcriptomic; a rare Galr1-responsive state below the cell-class resolution would be averaged out.

summary: The Galr1 null is not explained solely by the smallest cell counts; several 133-266-cell comparisons were also completely FDR-null.
why_it_matters: Low n weakens 31-98 cell classes, but the absence of signal in larger thalamic, midbrain, cortical IT, Pvalb, and CNU-HYa/HY GABA groups argues against a broad high-amplitude Galr1 transcriptional program in the assayed cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Higher perturbed-cell count does not establish Galr1 expression or editing efficiency; HPA and review expression data are regional or literature summaries rather than matched single-cell guide measurements.

summary: The galanin ligand/GALR1 upstream axis was silent and uncorrelated with Gi/o and adenylyl-cyclase neighbors that were detectable when directly perturbed.
why_it_matters: GALR1 is a Gi/o-coupled galanin receptor, so the contrast points to an inactive or unengaged receptor-ligand node rather than a global failure to detect GPCR second-messenger perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Gnao1, Gnb1, and Adcy3 are shared by many GPCRs and are not GALR1-specific; Galr2 and Galr3 paralog perturbations were not available in the dataset.

summary: Known GalR1 seizure-protection biology was not recovered as a basal Galr1-dependent RNA program in the hippocampal glutamatergic classes sampled here.
why_it_matters: Mouse GalR1 loss worsens seizures in some status-epilepticus models, but this dataset suggests that such biology may require evoked network activity, receptor activation, electrophysiology, or hippocampal subpopulations not resolved by these basal CA/MEA/DG classes.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The screen was not a seizure, galanin-agonist, or electrophysiology assay and showed no Galr1 transcript depletion in these classes.

summary: An all-target signature search found no meaningful positive or negative Galr1 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The best genome-wide correlations were close to zero, including correlations with Gal, Gnao1, and Gnb1; therefore neither related-target convergence nor an opposing compensatory program should be inferred from the weak Galr1 scores.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on noisy Galr1 scores; a true but non-transcriptional or state-restricted GALR1 response would not be detected.

summary: The Galr1 null should not be read as evidence against pharmacologic GALR1 activation.
why_it_matters: GALR1 is ligand-bound and assayable in exogenous systems, whereas the screen lacked target-transcript knockdown and had no downstream RNA phenotype; agonist-versus-antagonist prioritization therefore needs receptor activation, electrophysiology, or disease-challenge assays.
main_caveats: This is an assay-translation warning rather than a direct therapeutic efficacy test.

summary: Atp6ap2 transcript knockdown was detected broadly but did not pass FDR in every subclass.
why_it_matters: The cell types with weak target engagement should be treated as uninterpretable for downstream biology, whereas the 11 FDR-engaged subclasses provide the main basis for target-directed interpretation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|053 Sst Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Ten assayed Atp6ap2 signatures had negative target logFC but did not pass FDR; 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 21 perturbed cells.

summary: Most FDR-engaged Atp6ap2 perturbations were transcriptionally buffered, with no significant non-target genes.
why_it_matters: Loss of an essential V-ATPase accessory protein did not automatically create a large acute mRNA stress or lysosomal signature in mature neuronal subclasses, so the perturbation is not equivalent to a generic lysosome-collapse phenotype in this assay.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is transcriptomic buffering only; V-ATPase assembly, organelle pH, proteostasis, and delayed degeneration were not measured.

summary: Atp6v0a1 emerged as the recurrent downstream V0 transcript after Atp6ap2 targeting and after related V-ATPase perturbations.
why_it_matters: The recurrence nominates ATP6V0A1/a1 as a sensitive marker of disturbed V0-sector homeostasis rather than a random two-cell-type hit.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only two Atp6ap2 cell types passed FDR for Atp6v0a1; the pan-cell signal is based partly on nominal p values and sign recurrence.

summary: The strongest restricted-signature neighbor of Atp6ap2 was the core V0 perturbation Atp6v0c in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Although Atp6ap2 had only two FDR genes in this subclass, its nominal tail aligned with the much larger Atp6v0c program, suggesting a weak V-ATPase-related response concentrated in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This finding is restricted-signature-based; most overlapped Atp6ap2 genes were nominal rather than FDR-significant.

summary: Atp6ap2 and Atp6ap1 were not interchangeable with core Atp6v0c loss even though all converge on the V-ATPase network.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates an accessory-subunit/autoregulation phenotype from a broad core V0 transcriptional failure state, preventing overinterpretation of Atp6ap2 as simply a weaker copy of every V-ATPase perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Atp6v0c and accessory-subunit guides had different target knockdown magnitudes and perturbed-cell counts, so quantitative effect sizes are not directly normalized.

summary: Atp6ap2 targeting did not induce a canonical renin-angiotensin transcriptional response in mouse-brain neurons.
why_it_matters: Despite the historical identity of ATP6AP2 as the prorenin receptor, the dataset points toward V-ATPase/V0 effects rather than a detectable angiotensin-production or angiotensin-receptor feedback program.
main_caveats: Renin-angiotensin biology is often ligand- and protein-activity-driven; Ren2 was not measured, several RAS genes may be lowly expressed, and absence of FDR mRNA changes does not rule out non-transcriptional signaling.

summary: The buffered acute mRNA phenotype should not be read as evidence that ATP6AP2 inhibition is safe in neurons.
why_it_matters: Human reduced-dosage variants and mouse/fly loss models show that ATP6AP2 loss can damage the nervous system through V-ATPase-dependent mechanisms; this dataset shows that such liability can be under-represented in an acute transcriptome-only readout.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay measured mouse neuronal mRNA responses, not human variant severity, organelle acidification, survival, or long-term neurodegeneration.

summary: Eif4a2 transcript depletion was directionally consistent but FDR-detectable in only a subset of assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: This separates successful local target engagement from the many classes where the target row was only nominal after correction, which is essential before interpreting downstream biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The 145 MH-LH TH Glut row was only borderline at FDR=0.059; transcript depletion is not direct protein or helicase-activity measurement.

direction: Eif4a2 down with sparse non-target mRNA changes
summary: Most Eif4a2 knockdown signatures collapsed to the target transcript itself rather than a broad steady-state mRNA program.
why_it_matters: A central translation factor can be measurably depleted without hundreds of corrected mRNA changes, arguing that the immediate consequence of partial Eif4a2 loss in these cells is buffered, post-transcriptional, below detection, or only present in unmeasured cell states.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Wilcoxon scRNA-seq tests steady-state RNA abundance, so a translational or proteomic response could be missed.

summary: Cadm4 and Dbn1 were the only non-target genes that survived correction after Eif4a2 perturbation, each in a different target-engaged cell class.
why_it_matters: These two genes are candidate readouts for the rare cell-class-specific downstream mRNA response to Eif4a2 depletion, whereas nominal-only genes should not be overinterpreted.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Each marker appeared in only one cell class, and neither recurrence nor perturbation-rescue evidence was present in this differential-expression table.

summary: The closest assayed eIF4-family perturbations were not interchangeable with Eif4a2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Even within the same translation-initiation neighborhood, eIF4E depletion produced a much broader mRNA signature than Eif4a2 or Eif4g1, so complex membership alone would have been a poor predictor of the Perturb-seq phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Eif4e target depletion was weaker than Eif4a2 or Eif4g1, Eif4h itself was not FDR-depleted, and the comparison is transcriptomic rather than biochemical.

summary: EIF4A2's annotated eIF4F and miRNA-repression functions did not map to a recurrent corrected mRNA module after partial Eif4a2 depletion.
why_it_matters: The measured phenotype is compatible with EIF4A2 acting mainly through translation or selective RNA substrates in these cells, rather than through a large shared change in steady-state transcript abundance.
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure ribosome occupancy, protein abundance, miRNA targeting, or EIF4A2 ATPase activity.

summary: Human EIF4A2 loss-of-function and rare-variant genetics make brain EIF4A2 suppression a liability even though the adult mouse scRNA response was buffered.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq data should not be read as evidence that EIF4A2 is dispensable in neurons; human disease reports connect altered EIF4A2 dosage or sequence to neurodevelopmental disease and dystonia.
main_caveats: The literature is human germline genetics, whereas the dataset is acute or subacute CRISPR perturbation assayed by mouse single-cell RNA-seq.

summary: Atp1a1 knockdown was target-transcript dominated: every assayed neuronal class trended downward for Atp1a1, but FDR-level downstream genes were rare.
why_it_matters: A core Na+/K+ pump transcript can be partially reduced in vivo without a broad scRNA-seq stress or ion-transport transcriptional program, so direct pump physiology is likely buffered or hidden from this endpoint.

summary: Inhibiting INPP5K would be loss-of-function and is directionally aligned with a recessive human disease mechanism, while the dataset gives no robust corrected mRNA biomarker for safety monitoring.
why_it_matters: Pathogenic variants can decrease or abolish phosphatase activity, so pharmacologic inhibition should be treated as potentially disease-mimetic unless a context-specific benefit is proven; the only recurring dataset biomarker candidate was the weak sterol module.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Perturb-seq knockdown is not a small-molecule exposure, ChEMBL absence is a database negative rather than a complete ligandability assessment, and recessive disease genetics do not quantify inhibitor dose tolerance.

summary: Notch4 perturbation produced a pancohort sparse neuronal response rather than a broad transcriptomic state transition.
why_it_matters: A single receptor perturbation was expected to have cell-contact-dependent Notch consequences, yet the measured neuronal classes were largely buffered; this pushes interpretation toward weak target engagement, low receptor expression, or a compartment absent from the dataset rather than toward a large canonical Notch program.
main_caveats: Notch4 itself was not measured, so CRISPR effect on the target transcript is unknown; five contrasts had fewer than 70 perturbed cells.

summary: Mpc2 up-regulation in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut was the only FDR<0.05 Notch4 response.
why_it_matters: The result nominates a very narrow molecular readout for follow-up, while emphasizing that the only conventionally significant marker is not a recurrent Notch effector across cell types.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: The contrast used only 63 perturbed cells, and Mpc2 did not recur as an FDR-supported hit in other Notch4 cell types.

summary: Notch4 perturbation did not transcriptionally engage measured canonical Notch receptors, Dll1, Adam10, Psen1, Mib1, Hes7, or Hesx1.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not show the expected downstream receptor-to-NICD-to-transcriptional module that would make a neuronal Notch4 knockdown easy to interpret through the canonical pathway.
main_caveats: The measured genes are pathway sentinels, not a full Notch nuclear reporter panel; many canonical HES/HEY targets were not present as perturbation targets.

summary: Notch4 signatures were only weakly related to Notch1/2/3, Dll1, Adam10, Psen1, or Mib1 perturbations, even though Mib1 produced much stronger responses in several matched cell classes.
why_it_matters: Shared membership in the Notch pathway was not sufficient to make these perturbations interchangeable in this dataset, and the Mib1 contrast shows that some Notch-neighbor perturbations were able to generate larger expression changes when target engagement was evident.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All whole-transcriptome correlations were small; Mib1 has Notch-ligand and potentially non-Notch roles, and the Notch4 target transcript was not quantified.

summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq silence of Notch4 is more compatible with NOTCH4 disease activity in the vascular compartment than with a strong cell-autonomous neuronal role.
why_it_matters: Brain vascular literature links endothelial Notch4 activation to arteriovenous malformation, whereas the profiled classes are glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic neurons; the negative neuronal result therefore localizes follow-up toward endothelial or mural cells instead of contradicting NOTCH4 vascular biology.
main_caveats: The dataset did not include endothelial or smooth-muscle/mural cell classes, and it used perturbative loss rather than endothelial NOTCH4 gain of function.

summary: These data do not support using a selective neuronal Notch4 knockdown signature as a proxy for broad pharmacologic Notch pathway inhibition.
why_it_matters: Gamma-secretase, ADAM, or ligand-level interventions would be expected to affect multiple Notch receptors and processing steps, while Notch4 perturbation left measured pathway transcripts unchanged and ChEMBL lacks curated selective NOTCH4 mechanisms.
main_caveats: The dataset tested genetic perturbation in neurons, not a small molecule, gamma-secretase inhibitor, or endothelial assay.

summary: Max perturbation produced a sharply cell-type-restricted neuronal response: six of 22 tested subclasses contained all 167 FDR-significant gene responses, with the largest signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The data argue that the MAX network is buffered in most assayed neuronal classes but can be limiting for specific thalamic, midbrain/hindbrain, hypothalamic, and Pvalb programs.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Target Max mRNA was not FDR-significantly depleted in any cell type, and one responsive class had only 23 Max-perturbed cells.

summary: In Max-responsive glutamatergic neurons, Max perturbation increased a biosynthetic/nucleolar program rather than decreasing the canonical MYC-associated ribosome-biogenesis program.
why_it_matters: Because MAX is required for both MYC activators and MNT/MGA/MXD repressors, the observed upregulation of Mdn1, Gnl3, Ltv1, Pno1, Nop2, Dctd, Shmt1 and related genes indicates that loss of a repressive MAX branch can dominate over loss of MYC:MAX activation in mature neuronal contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The mismatch is inferred from mRNA signatures and the exact MAX dimer responsible for these genes was not assayed.

summary: Per2 and Cry1 formed a recurrent Max-induced clock module across four responsive subclasses.
why_it_matters: This agrees with prior evidence that MAX can directly repress E-box-containing circadian genes with MNT and suggests that neuronal Max perturbation releases a clock-repressor circuit, not only generic growth genes.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The cited circadian mechanism was defined primarily in human cell-line systems, whereas the dataset is mouse brain and lacks time-series sampling.

summary: Max and Mga perturbations converged on strong de-repression of the meiotic cohesin gene Stag3, extending the MAX/MGA germline-silencing axis into post-mitotic neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: STAG3 is a meiosis-specific cohesin, and its repeated induction after Max perturbation links the brain phenotype to the MAX-PRC1.6 germ-cell repression literature rather than to a purely mitotic MYC program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only Stag3 was recurrently significant genome-wide; 217 P MY Pineal Glut had very few Max-perturbed cells.

summary: Max was not interchangeable with Myc, Mycn, Mnt, Mlxip, Tfap4 or Usf1 in this dataset; Myc and Mycn had no FDR-significant genes despite large cell counts in the strongest Max-responsive class.
why_it_matters: This separates the Max phenotype from a generic E-box or MYC-family perturbation and implies that partner abundance, chromatin state, or guide efficacy restricts which branch of the MAX network is limiting in neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Negative comparator signatures are hard to interpret because their own target transcripts also lacked FDR-significant depletion.

summary: Max perturbation induced Mga or Mnt transcripts in a subset of responsive GABA and thalamic cells.
why_it_matters: The response is compatible with an attempt to rebalance the MAX network, but extra MNT/MGA may be ineffective if the limiting component is edited MAX protein itself.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only two Max-perturbed classes significantly induced Mga and one induced Mnt; no protein or chromatin measurements tested compensation.

summary: A dataset-wide signature-neighbor scan found no strong phenocopy or anti-phenocopy of Max; Sin3a was recurrently the top positive neighbor, but even that similarity was weak.
why_it_matters: The weak correlations caution against assigning the Max state to one simple neighboring perturbation, while the recurrent Sin3a proximity is at least directionally plausible for a MAX-network repressor that can recruit SIN3 corepressor complexes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Top absolute Pearson correlations were below 0.24, so this is a restricted signature-neighbor observation, not a strong mechanistic equivalence.

summary: Experimental MAX or MYC:MAX inhibition should not be modeled as pure MYC loss in neuronal cells, because Max perturbation released clock, meiotic, nucleolar, and metabolic genes in selected brain subclasses.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL contains Protein max and c-MYC/MAX bioactivity targets, but the Perturb-seq signature warns that disrupting MAX-containing dimers could also disable repressive MNT/MGA/MAX functions and induce off-state neuronal transcriptional programs.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut

summary: Dync2h1 did not transcriptionally converge with the available dynein-2, IFT, kinesin, or BBS perturbations.

summary: Dync1h1 triggered a strong recurrent sterol-response module, whereas Dync2h1 was inert by FDR despite being another cytoplasmic dynein heavy-chain target.

summary: Canonical Hedgehog transcripts did not move after Dync2h1 perturbation, refining DYNC2H1 ciliopathy biology away from a basal Hh mRNA program in these mouse-brain cells.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse genetics implicate DYNC2H1 in ciliary Shh-dependent development, but this dataset suggests that the captured brain-cell phenotype is not a broad cell-autonomous Gli/Ptch/Smo/Shh transcriptional response.
main_caveats: The assay was not a ligand-stimulated Shh experiment, and very low basal expression of Hh readouts could make transcriptional changes difficult to detect.

summary: Robust Pex14 transcript depletion in the three FDR-supported cell types was almost isolated to the target RNA itself.
why_it_matters: PEX14 is a core importomer protein, so the lack of FDR-significant non-target RNAs argues that acute partial loss in these neuronal classes is either transcriptionally buffered or primarily expressed through peroxisomal import, lipid, or protein-localization phenotypes not captured by global mRNA changes.

main_caveats: The dataset measures RNA after partial perturbation, not PEX14 protein, peroxisomal matrix import, plasmalogens, or very-long-chain fatty acids.

summary: The interpretable Pex14 knockdown is concentrated in midbrain/thalamic and hypothalamic neuronal classes, with only weaker self-knockdown elsewhere.
why_it_matters: This limits cell-type interpretation: MB Glut, TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and CNU-HYa HY GABA provide the cleanest PEX14-loss signatures, while nominal effects in MH-LH TH Glut and MB P MY GABA are useful only as moderate-support extensions.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Cell types have unequal perturbed-cell counts; low counts in MB Dopa and Pineal Glut make absence of knockdown hard to interpret.

summary: Pex14 loss shows a recurrent upward bias in SREBF2/cholesterol-homeostasis genes, strongest in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and exploratory in several additional classes.
why_it_matters: The ranking of Cyp51, Dhcr24, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Insig1, Fdft1, and related genes suggests a sterol-homeostatic compensation to impaired peroxisome biogenesis rather than a generic stress response; Srebf2 knockdown drives the same panel in the opposite direction in this dataset.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: This is a post hoc rank-based module; most individual Pex14-induced cholesterol genes remain FDR=1, and the Pineal Glut signal occurs with weak Pex14 self-knockdown and 30 perturbed cells.

summary: Other assayed peroxins, Pex1 and Pex13, did not provide a clean phenocopy test because their own transcripts were not significantly depleted.
why_it_matters: Because PEX13 and PEX14 are in the same docking apparatus, a direct phenocopy would have been informative; the observed Pex1/Pex13 contrast, including a Pex13/Insig1 sterol echo with no Pex13 self-knockdown, is best treated as an engagement caveat rather than evidence that the PEX14 program is unique.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Pex1 and Pex13 guide activity or transcript detectability, rather than biology downstream of those peroxins, likely limits the comparison.

summary: The SREBF2/cholesterol signature is a candidate host-cell biomarker to monitor if PEX14-PEX5 inhibition is pursued pharmacologically.
why_it_matters: Small-molecule disruption of PEX14-PEX5 is tractable in glycosome biology, and ChEMBL records human PEX14 peptide-binding assays; the neuronal Perturb-seq response warns that host PEX14 inhibition could perturb sterol adaptation even when broad transcriptional toxicity is muted.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Trypanosome glycosome inhibitors are not equivalent to mammalian CNS PEX14 inhibitors; the dataset used genetic knockdown, not acute receptor-docking blockade.

summary: The Pex14 whole-transcriptome signature lacked a strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor in the three cleanly engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: This argues against assigning a single unrelated pathway neighbor from genome-wide correlation; the interpretable signal is the low-amplitude sterol module, not a broad recapitulation of another perturbation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations used Wilcoxon score vectors within each cell type and can miss nonlinear or protein-level convergence.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Protein-level ankyrin-G localization, AIS morphology, and electrophysiology were not measured.

direction: target down with minimal secondary response
summary: Several cell types with FDR-level Ank3 self-knockdown had little or no downstream FDR response.
why_it_matters: Ank3 mRNA reduction was not sufficient to trigger a large transcriptional program in every neuronal context, implying buffering, isoform differences, or insufficient protein depletion outside the thalamic population.

main_caveats: The perturbation was judged by total Ank3 transcript, not isoform-specific or protein depletion.

direction: Ank3 active; Ank1 and Ank2 buffered or orthogonal
summary: Ank1 and Ank2 did not phenocopy Ank3 in the Ank3-responsive thalamic class.
why_it_matters: This argues that the 151 TH response is Ank3-specific and not a generic consequence of perturbing ankyrin paralogs.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

summary: Scn8a, Scn1b, and Fgf14 were weak but high-ranking same-direction signature neighbors of Ank3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.

summary: Gabrb2 and Atp2b1 were the top negative Ank3 signature neighbors, and direct Atp2b1/Gabrb2 perturbation upregulated several genes that Ank3 perturbation downregulated.

main_caveats: The literature links ATP2B1 and GABRB2 to calcium and inhibition, respectively, but does not establish a direct Ank3 coupling in this thalamic cell type.

direction: mRNA-reducing perturbation with disease-relevant synaptic suppression
summary: Ank3 suppression in the sensitive thalamic population reduced rather than rescued synaptic and ion-related genes, warning against a nonspecific ANK3-lowering strategy for psychiatric disease.
why_it_matters: ANK3 is a human psychiatric risk locus, so perturbation direction matters: a loss-of-function-like intervention would need to avoid reproducing the deleterious thalamic program observed here.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Mouse Perturb-seq readouts are not human clinical outcomes; common ANK3 GWAS variants do not define a simple loss-of-function mechanism.

summary: Cep83 perturbation did not produce an FDR-resolved transcriptome in any profiled cell type, and target-mRNA reduction was not FDR-detectable.
why_it_matters: CEP83 is a core cilium-initiation scaffold, but the measured mouse-brain response contains no accepted DE genes; downstream interpretation must therefore treat this as a weak-engagement, mostly negative Perturb-seq result rather than a ciliary activation signature.
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA knockdown does not exclude protein depletion or cilium-structure phenotypes; several cell types had only 25-47 perturbed cells.

summary: Cep83 did not converge transcriptionally with perturbations of tested distal-appendage or ciliopathy neighbors despite strong prior physical and pathway links.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates the structural cilium-initiation module from an acute mRNA module: even Sclt1, Cep164 and Ift88 correlations with Cep83 were tiny, and ciliary comparators produced only four isolated FDR hits across 199 comparable signatures.
main_caveats: Comparator analysis is restricted to the guide targets present in the dataset, and all signatures being compared are weak at the FDR level.

summary: 145 MH-LH TH Glut carried the lowest adjusted p value and a mixed nominal set including Cacnb3, Kcna1, Grin1, Cacng8 and Gabrb2.
why_it_matters: If Cep83 has a brain transcriptional consequence at all, the thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic class is the only place in this run that nominates a follow-up marker set; every gene remained far above FDR 0.05, so this is hypothesis-generating only.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only 33 Cep83 cells were available in this class and the best adjusted p value was 0.372.

summary: For a CEP83-linked ciliopathy gene, the mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout suggests that disease-relevant assays should prioritize cilium assembly or signaling morphology over a broad mRNA signature.
why_it_matters: Human CEP83 mutations cause nephronophthisis-related disease and CEP83 loss blocks ciliary docking in cell-biological assays, whereas the brain Perturb-seq response was flat even across related ciliary genes; this argues against using a simple bulk transcriptional rescue panel as the main efficacy readout.
main_caveats: Low target-transcript engagement is a major alternative explanation, and the disease literature is human renal/developmental rather than the profiled mouse neuronal cell classes.

summary: Lrig2 self-depletion was directional but nominal, with the clearest self-hit confined to 308 CB GABA and weaker nominal self-hits in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The Lrig2 self-row never passed FDR correction, and the two secondary self-hits had only nominal p<0.05.

summary: Lrig2 perturbation produced no FDR-resolved downstream RNA response in any assayed cell type, and the strongest nominal genes were nearly all cell-type singletons.
why_it_matters: This makes a large, shared LRIG2-dependent neuronal transcriptional module unlikely under the power and perturbation strength of this experiment.
main_caveats: A null RNA signature does not rule out a post-translational or slower phenotype; perturbed-cell counts were low.

summary: Known LRIG2 RTK, NEO1/ADAM17/RGMA, HPSE2, and BMP/SMAD transcript sentinels were FDR-negative and did not form a coherent expression response after Lrig2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The main published LRIG2 mechanisms center on membrane receptor regulation; their absence as RNA signatures suggests that the Perturb-seq assay is not reading out those mechanisms robustly in these mature brain cell types.
main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA abundance, not receptor cleavage, RTK phosphorylation, protein stability, or surface localization.

summary: Lrig2 expression signatures were weakly correlated with all other perturbations, including RTK/RAS/PI3K/mTOR neighbors, and Lrig1/Lrig3 paralogs were not available for direct comparison.
why_it_matters: Perturbing Lrig2 in this dataset does not phenocopy loss of a single canonical receptor or downstream effector, which argues against assigning the weak signatures to EGFR, AXL, RAS, PI3K, or mTOR from transcriptomics alone.

summary: Gas6, a reported mediator of LRIG2-driven GAS6/AXL/SRC signaling in glioblastoma, moved only nominally and with opposing signs across Lrig2-perturbed neuronal classes.

summary: The mouse brain dataset does not provide a robust mature-neuron RNA correlate of LRIG2-associated urofacial or GBM mechanisms, despite the established human LRIG2 disease link and reported tumor-promoting LRIG2 axes.
why_it_matters: Partial, weak Lrig2 loss in mature neurons should not be overinterpreted as evidence for target safety, efficacy, or disease direction; human disease involves peripheral bladder innervation and GBM literature involves tumor RTK/immune circuits.
main_caveats: The inference is a warning about this dataset's limits, not a negative genetic-safety study; peripheral bladder neurons, tumor cells, and protein-level immune mechanisms were not assayed.

summary: Cep112 perturbation produced neither measurable Cep112 mRNA depletion nor any FDR-significant downstream gene in the profiled neuronal classes.

summary: Neuronal Cep112 profiles did not recapitulate the spermiogenesis RNA-granule circuit reported for CEP112.

summary: Available ciliary, centrosomal, and kinesin perturbations were not generally interchangeable with Cep112 perturbation.

summary: A weak cerebellar GABA-specific signature neighborhood linked Cep112 to B9d1 and Cep290, two ciliary transition-zone genes.

summary: Mbd5 guide assignment did not generate a confident Mbd5 loss-of-function transcriptomic state in this screen.
why_it_matters: MBD5 is a highly dosage-sensitive neurodevelopmental gene, so the absence of FDR-resolved responses is interpretable mainly as failed or insufficient target engagement rather than as evidence that neurons tolerate real Mbd5 loss.

summary: Deep-layer L5-6 IT glutamatergic neurons were the only Mbd5 context with a near-threshold FDR signal.
why_it_matters: If any Mbd5-sensitive program is present in the dataset, it is concentrated in a cortical excitatory class where Mbd5 also showed its largest measured transcript decrease.

main_caveats: Map2k4 stopped just short of FDR 0.05, the cell type had only 35 perturbed cells, and the target transcript row was nominal but not FDR-significant.

summary: Mbd5 did not converge with measured PR-DUB-associated perturbations despite the established MBD5-BAP1-ASXL biochemical connection.
why_it_matters: The expected complex-level readout was absent: Bap1 was detectable in the same table but Mbd5-Bap1, Mbd5-Asxl3, and Mbd5-Foxk2 score correlations were all near zero.
main_caveats: The literature is largely from human chromatin and cancer-cell systems, and Mbd5 knockdown was weak; therefore the lack of convergence should not be taken as proof that Mbd5 is PR-DUB-independent in mouse neurons.

summary: Fbxo38 perturbation generated a near-null transcriptomic profile with no adjusted-P evidence for depletion of the Fbxo38 mRNA itself.
