main_caveats: mRNA abundance is an indirect target-engagement readout for an F-box protein; protein depletion and guide cutting were not measured in this DE table.

summary: The only 5% FDR event was Hdac2 up-regulation in 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and it did not recur in other Fbxo38-profiled cell classes.
why_it_matters: This converts the strongest scalar hit into a cell-type-restricted biomarker hypothesis rather than a pan-neuronal FBXO38 response.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only 26 perturbed pineal cells were available and the same cells did not show a measurable decrease in Fbxo38 transcript.

summary: Trappc11 down-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA is a network-proximal candidate, but it missed the conventional 0.05 FDR cutoff.
why_it_matters: TRAPPC11 was among high-scoring STRING partners for human FBXO38, so the mouse Trappc11 transcript is worth carrying forward as a hypothesis-generating readout even though the dataset support is subthreshold.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: FDR was 0.060 rather than <0.05; STRING proximity is not proof of a direct neuronal FBXO38-TRAPPC11 mechanism.

summary: Nominal Fbxo38-responsive genes were not recurrent across cell classes and the strongest cell classes lacked a clear positive or negative perturbation-signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The response appears idiosyncratic and sparse instead of converging on a shared disease module, SCF module, or cell-stress program.
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor correlations were computed in four selected cell classes, not all 22, and all involved weak Fbxo38 signatures.

summary: Fbxo38 loss did not transcriptionally phenocopy Klf7 or the assayed F-box paralog perturbations.
why_it_matters: Prior FBXO38/MoKA literature motivates a KLF7-axis expectation, but the Perturb-seq signatures show near-zero Fbxo38-Klf7, Fbxo38-Fbxw7, and Fbxo38-Fbxo11 correlations and no adjusted response of Klf7 or Cdkn1a after Fbxo38 perturbation.
main_caveats: Klf7, Fbxw7, and Fbxo11 guide effects were themselves transcriptionally weak, so the result argues against detectable convergence rather than against a biochemical interaction.

summary: The neuronal Fbxo38 screen did not engage the immune-checkpoint FBXO38 readouts Pdcd1, Fgl1, or Cgas, so it is uninformative about the disputed PD-1 cancer-immunity mechanism.
why_it_matters: FBXO38 has been proposed as an immuno-oncology regulator of PD-1 degradation, but this mouse-brain dataset profiles glutamatergic and GABAergic classes and should not be used to infer T-cell checkpoint directionality.
main_caveats: The screen lacks T cells; Pdcd1 and Fgl1 are low or absent in these neuronal classes, and PD-1 is regulated mainly at the protein level in the cited immune literature.

summary: Dnajc13 perturbation produced clear on-target transcript reduction only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: This cell type is the only internally well-engaged context for interpreting primary Dnajc13 loss in the screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Dnajc13 mRNA decreased only modestly and only the target transcript passed FDR<0.05 in this cell type.

summary: Nominal knockdown in two high-count glutamatergic classes did not propagate to any FDR-significant transcriptome-wide response.
why_it_matters: The result separates partial target engagement from downstream transcriptional sensitivity and argues that some Dnajc13-expressing neuronal classes buffer Dnajc13 mRNA loss.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was only nominal in these cells, so absence of downstream FDR hits could mix biological buffering with incomplete perturbation.

summary: The Dnajc13 TH signature was almost orthogonal to retromer, Rab7, clathrin, WASH, Hspa8, and Atp13a2 perturbations even though those genes occupy the same endosomal trafficking neighborhood.
why_it_matters: RME-8/DNAJC13 is usually interpreted through WASH, SNX-retromer, Hsc70, and clathrin biology; the mouse-brain Perturb-seq response shows that loss of Dnajc13 is not interchangeable with perturbing Vps35, Rab7, or Cltc at the mRNA-signature level.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon mRNA scores; direct trafficking, cargo recycling, or endosomal morphology phenotypes were not measured.

summary: Spred1 up-regulation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut is an isolated, exploratory non-target hit rather than a secure Dnajc13-loss biomarker.
why_it_matters: It is the only non-target corrected hit in the Dnajc13 subset, but its cell-type restriction and absent Dnajc13 self-knockdown make it a validation candidate, not a mechanistic anchor.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Target transcript engagement was not detected in the same cells, so the Spred1 result may be indirect, guide-composition driven, or off-target.

summary: The Parkinson/endolysosomal disease link remains biologically plausible but is not supported here by a dopaminergic or broad transcriptional Dnajc13-loss program.
why_it_matters: DNAJC13 variants have been linked to Parkinson disease through endosomal trafficking, yet this dataset lacks a Dnajc13 215 MB Dopa result and shows a mostly target-limited response elsewhere; disease hypotheses should therefore be tested with trafficking, proteostasis, and dopaminergic assays rather than relying on a Dnajc13 mRNA signature.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Absence of a row for MB Dopa is an absence of data, not evidence of no dopaminergic phenotype; PD models often involve mutant DNAJC13 or alpha-synuclein stress rather than simple transcript reduction.

summary: Nr2f1 knockdown produced an FDR-level response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Sorl1 was induced and Sema7a was repressed.
why_it_matters: This converts an orphan nuclear-receptor perturbation into a narrowly localized thalamic glutamatergic transcriptional phenotype rather than a pan-neuronal response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript decrease in 151 was nominal but not FDR-significant, so unmeasured protein knockdown or guide activity is inferred from the presence of the downstream signature rather than directly proven.

summary: Nominal Nr2f1 mRNA depletion was not by itself sufficient to create an FDR-level transcriptome: 046 CTX-CGE GABA and 001 L5-6 IT Glut showed stronger measured target decreases than 151 but no FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: A developmental transcription factor can be transcriptionally buffered in some adult/postnatal neuronal contexts; the strongest biological response was not simply the cell type with the largest measured Nr2f1 logFC.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: 046 and 001 had fewer perturbed cells than 151; absence of FDR hits could reflect lower power, cell-state buffering, or both.

summary: The 151 signature nominates a Sorl1/Sema7a-centered, neuron-surface and endosomal-trafficking readout of Nr2f1 loss.
why_it_matters: Sorl1 is the top up-regulated gene and an Alzheimer-linked endosomal sorting receptor, while Sema7a is the top down-regulated gene and a semaphorin with axon-growth activity; together they provide a concrete marker pair for following Nr2f1 perturbation in this thalamic glutamatergic context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Sorl1 and Sema7a reached FDR<0.05; the broader surface/ECM interpretation uses nominal genes and the dataset does not prove direct NR2F1 binding at any locus.

summary: The close paralog Nr2f2 partially converged with Nr2f1 on Sorl1 induction in 151 cells, whereas Nr2f6 did not, and neither paralog phenocopied the full Sema7a-containing Nr2f1 signature.
why_it_matters: COUP-TFI/II homology does not translate into interchangeability in this neuronal state; Sorl1 appears to be the shared sensitive node while the rest of the Nr2f1 response is paralog-selective or guide-efficiency-limited.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Nr2f2 and Nr2f6 self-transcript knockdown was not significant in this cell class; the comparison is restricted-signature-based and should not be read as a definitive loss-of-function epistasis test.

summary: Unbiased score-vector matching did not reveal a strong positive or negative signature neighbor for Nr2f1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: The Sorl1/Sema7a signal should be treated as a sparse, target-specific response instead of as a member of a large shared perturbation state in this matrix.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Global correlations across all expressed genes are conservative and can miss pathway relationships captured only on a small subset of direct targets.

summary: Safe_target_13 behaved as a genome-wide null perturbation at 5% FDR across 20 mouse-brain neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: This establishes the target as an empirically inert safe-targeting control in the measured transcriptomic contrasts rather than a guide with a reproducible downstream expression program.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Target engagement is not directly measurable because no Safe_target_13 transcript appears in the measured-gene column; many contrasts have fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: The isolated Hspa4l and Ahcyl2 rows are consistent with the empirical Safe_target_* null distribution.
why_it_matters: A 10% FDR tail in one low-cell cell type could look cell-type selective if viewed alone, but other safe-targeting controls produce comparable or stronger isolated rows.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The safe-target panel is an internal negative-control distribution, not an external mechanistic comparator.

summary: Safe_target_13 did not generate a recurrent nominal gene module across cell types.
why_it_matters: The absence of genes recurring in more than two cell types, even at p < 0.001, prevents a pathway-level interpretation of the nominal tails.
main_caveats: This recurrence check used nominal p < 0.001 as an exploratory filter; all repeated genes still failed FDR correction.

summary: The strongest Safe_target_13 cell-type signature had no strong positive or negative real-target neighbor.
why_it_matters: Weak correlations to all other perturbations in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA argue against an off-target program that mimics a real gene perturbation.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The neighbor analysis was restricted to the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA contrast because it contained the lowest Safe_target_13 adjusted p value.

summary: Safe_target_13 should not be assigned target biology, druggability, disease direction, or a biomarker mechanism from this dataset.
why_it_matters: The guide label has no measured transcript in the table, no robust downstream genes, and no mapped molecular family, so interpreting the isolated Hspa4l or Ahcyl2 rows as causal target biology would overstate the evidence.
main_caveats: The parquet lacks genomic coordinates for the safe-targeting guide, so this warning is based on the expression table and exact database/literature searches for the literal label.

summary: Kif1a knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: the target transcript was reproducibly reduced, yet the strongest cell type had no significant non-target mRNA response.
why_it_matters: KIF1A is a cargo motor, so an mRNA-only readout can substantially underestimate a real transport perturbation.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay measures cell-body RNA abundance, not axonal cargo transport, vesicle localization, or protein abundance.

summary: High-confidence target engagement was selective for several inhibitory, hypothalamic/thalamic, and midbrain/hindbrain classes, whereas cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic classes were weak by FDR.
why_it_matters: The apparent response map should not be interpreted as pan-neuronal KIF1A biology; it is partly limited by cell class, expression, and guide-cell sampling.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cell classes with low Kif1a expression can fail the target-transcript FDR test even if CRISPR editing occurred; cell counts also ranged down to 32 perturbed cells.

summary: A modest sterol/cholesterol-biosynthetic module was the main recurrent non-target response to Kif1a perturbation.
why_it_matters: The response pointed to lipid-state compensation rather than to the annotated KIF1A kinesin/cargo pathway, nominating Hmgcs1, Dhcr24, Insig1, and Msmo1 as exploratory readouts.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only Hmgcs1 and Dhcr24 passed FDR<0.05 individually; the broader module is recurrence- and nominal-p-value based and was inspected after seeing the Kif1a signature.

summary: Kif1a did not phenocopy perturbations of kinesin paralogs, KLC subunits, dynein, Rab3/SV genes, or any high-correlation library neighbor.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues against a generic anterograde-transport stress signature and preserves Kif1a as a mostly private, weak mRNA state in this assay.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations are transcriptome-level comparisons; several comparator perturbations have their own variable target engagement.

summary: The Kif1a guide-perturbation signature is compatible with KAND mechanisms acting through transport biophysics and cargo localization rather than through a large acute transcriptional cascade.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic or validation screens that rely only on total mRNA rescue could miss pathogenic defects in vesicle motility, distal cargo delivery, or dominant-negative motor behavior.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Guide-based perturbation of mouse Kif1a is not equivalent to every human missense, gain-of-function, or dominant-negative KAND allele.

summary: Tanc2 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is an exploratory KIF1A-interactor biomarker candidate.
why_it_matters: TANC2 is a postsynaptic scaffold that recruits KIF1A-carried dense-core vesicles, so even a weak cell-type-restricted RNA change is more mechanistically interpretable than most nominal rows.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Tanc2 did not pass FDR<0.05 and was not recurrent across other Kif1a cell types.

summary: Kremen1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant target-transcript or downstream response in any of the 23 assayed cell groups.
why_it_matters: Kremen1 is a membrane DKK receptor linked to LRP5/6 Wnt regulation, so the dataset primarily supplies a high-confidence negative result rather than a Wnt pathway activation or repression signature.
main_caveats: The Kremen1 transcript itself was not significantly depleted, so this cannot distinguish true biological buffering from ineffective RNA-level target engagement.

summary: The leading nominal Kremen1 effects showed weak cell-class skew but no corrected cell-type-selective program.
why_it_matters: The observation prevents overinterpretation of raw p-value hot spots in LGE GABA, Pvalb, or corticothalamic/extratelencephalic neurons as a stable Kremen1 module.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Based on unadjusted p values; recurrent nominal genes were few and mostly sign-inconsistent across cell groups.

summary: Kremen1 did not phenocopy Lrp6 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Lrp6 but not Kremen1 had a small FDR-supported Axin2-containing response.
why_it_matters: This separates Kremen1 from an immediately related Wnt co-receptor in the same assay and argues against treating Kremen1 perturbation as a generic proxy for LRP6 pathway loss in these neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Lrp6 response was small, Kremen1 was not detectably knocked down at the RNA level, and Dkk/Kremen2 perturbations were not available as direct comparators.

summary: Top-500 Kremen1 signature neighbors were strongest in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA but were not Wnt co-receptors and included safe-target-labeled perturbations.
why_it_matters: The nearest-neighbor result cautions that the strongest ranked Kremen1 features may include cell-class or technical structure rather than a specific Kremen1-Wnt pathway output.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only over the top 500 absolute Kremen1 score genes per cell type, and the presence of safe-target-labeled neighbors weakens target-mechanistic interpretation.

summary: Published KREMEN1 disease and neuronal-culture effects do not translate into a broad corrected Kremen1 transcriptional phenotype in these mouse brain Perturb-seq cell groups.
why_it_matters: Kremen1 has been proposed as a Wnt-linked disease and neuronal survival regulator, but these data argue that perturbing it should not be assumed to broadly rewire canonical Wnt or synaptic-survival transcription in all neuronal contexts.
main_caveats: The cited disease and neuronal studies used human developmental genetics, sensory neurons, or cultured amyloid-beta models rather than the assayed mouse brain cell groups.

summary: Nsun2 perturbation produced shallow but coherent on-target mRNA depletion, with the clearest single-cell-class engagement in 155 MB Glut and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: The guide group is directionally on target, but most single cell classes are underpowered for the target transcript on their own; downstream effects must therefore be interpreted as partial-loss phenotypes.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: No individual Nsun2 transcript row passed cell-type-level FDR; the stronger call comes from aggregating the signed target effect across cell types.

summary: The mRNA program downstream of Nsun2 was strongly buffered: no non-target gene reached FDR < 0.05 even in the classes with nominal target depletion.
why_it_matters: Known NSUN2 biology is centered on cytosine-5 methylation of tRNAs and other RNAs, tRNA stability, tRNA fragments, and proteomic consequences, so a near-null scRNA differential-expression readout is compatible with an enzymatic or translational phenotype that is not well captured by total mRNA abundance.
main_caveats: The dataset contains only aggregated Wilcoxon mRNA statistics; it does not assay tRNA methylation, tRNA fragments, translation, protein abundance, or later survival phenotypes.

summary: Several Nsun2 guide groups are best treated as low-engagement negatives rather than resistant cell types.
why_it_matters: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 053 Sst Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA had logFC values within approximately 0.03 of zero for Nsun2 itself, so lack of downstream DE in those classes does not imply that NSUN2 activity is dispensable there.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|053 Sst Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Target mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for guide editing efficiency and protein or enzymatic depletion.

summary: Nsun2 depletion did not trigger transcriptional compensation by the proximal tRNA/ncRNA modification network.
why_it_matters: Despite database evidence placing NSUN2 with Trdmt1, Ftsj1, Pus7, Nat10, Mettl1 and other RNA-modification factors, these genes remained near zero across cell types, arguing that acute Nsun2 perturbation is not sensed through a compensatory mRNA-feedback loop for this pathway.
main_caveats: Only transcript levels of selected network genes were examined; unchanged partner mRNA levels do not exclude changed enzyme activity, localization, RNA substrates, or modifications.

summary: Loss-of-function genetics make NSUN2 inhibition a neurodevelopmental liability even though the Perturb-seq mRNA signature is quiet.
why_it_matters: Human NSUN2 loss causes autosomal-recessive intellectual disability, mouse and neural-stem-cell models connect Nsun2 loss to tRNA-fragment and neuronal phenotypes, and ChEMBL contains human NSUN2 inhibitor/binding assays; therefore absence of FDR transcriptional stress markers should not be used as a safety argument for chronic CNS NSUN2 inhibition.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment does not test small molecules, chronic inhibition, development, or organismal behavior; the clinical direction comes from external human and mouse genetics.

summary: No robust Nsun2 signature neighbor emerged, and the available methylation-enzyme comparators Dnmt3a and Alkbh8 were essentially uncorrelated with Nsun2.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting any single top correlated Perturb-seq target or nearby methyltransferase as a phenocopy pathway for NSUN2; the dataset mainly supports a standalone, weak Nsun2 mRNA signature.
main_caveats: The comparison uses mRNA-score correlations from weak signatures; direct NOL1/NOP2/SUN paralogs were not present as informative comparators in the perturbation set.

summary: Atf6 knockdown was nominally detectable but transcriptionally buffered across mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A basal Atf6 loss-of-function state did not collapse global gene expression or create a broad neuronal UPR signature, even in the two better-powered cell types with the strongest nominal Atf6 depletion.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Atf6 transcript itself did not pass FDR correction; perturbation efficacy is therefore nominal and transcript-level data do not test stress-induced ATF6 proteolytic activation directly.

summary: Canonical UPR and ERAD transcripts were not coordinately changed after Atf6 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Xbp1, Ddit3, Herpud1, Dnajb9, Pdia-family genes, Hyou1, and Sel1l are expected UPR/ER quality-control nodes, but only scattered nominal effects were seen, arguing against constitutive ATF6 control of the measured chaperone program in this basal brain screen.
main_caveats: Only mRNA readouts were available; the experiment was not an acute tunicamycin/thapsigargin ER-stress challenge and weak Atf6 target engagement could mask a true dependency.

direction: chaperone genes up after Manf or Hspa5 perturbation; absent after Atf6
summary: The dataset can detect an ER-chaperone stress module through Manf and Hspa5 perturbations, whereas Atf6 loss does not enter that state.
why_it_matters: Manf knockdown repeatedly increased Hspa5 and other ER folding genes, and Hspa5 perturbation increased Hsp90b1, Pdia4, and Derl3 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells. This provides an internal positive contrast showing that the absence of an Atf6 UPR signature is not simply because UPR genes were absent from the expression matrix.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Manf loss is not the same molecular perturbation as ATF6 activation or inhibition; the comparison establishes assay sensitivity and pathway adjacency, not epistasis.

direction: Srebf2 sterol module down; Atf6 buffered
summary: Srebf2, a membrane-tethered transcription factor using the same S1P/S2P protease logic as ATF6, showed a strong sterol-gene loss-of-function program that Atf6 lacked.
why_it_matters: Shared regulated intramembrane proteolysis did not translate into similar basal transcriptomes: Srebf2 knockdown was on-target and repeatedly decreased Dhcr24, Insig1, Cyp51, Msmo1, Hmgcr, and related sterol genes, while Atf6 signatures were near-null.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Mbtps1, Mbtps2, and Scap were not available as perturbation targets, so the contrast is between the terminal transcription factors rather than the shared proteases.

direction: brain basal response weak versus retinal genetic disease
summary: The weak basal brain response is consistent with ATF6 disease biology being highly context dependent rather than uniformly penetrant in every neuronal population.
why_it_matters: Human genetics links ATF6 loss to cone dysfunction and achromatopsia, but this mouse-brain Perturb-seq panel lacked a retinal cone population and showed no broad neuronal UPR failure. The dataset therefore supports a context/stress-load model instead of a universal constitutive requirement for ATF6 in all neurons.
main_caveats: The screen was in mouse brain cells, not human foveal cones; it cannot test photoreceptor development, retinal proteostasis, or patient alleles.

direction: no strong positive or negative correlation
summary: Whole-transcriptome signature-neighbor analysis did not identify a robust Atf6 phenocopy or anti-phenocopy.
why_it_matters: The strongest non-self correlations to Atf6 were small, and available UPR/lipid neighbors had median absolute correlations near zero, so hidden convergence with a related perturbation should be treated as exploratory rather than a substitute for significant Atf6 differential expression.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The Atf6 signatures themselves are weak, so correlation discovery has limited dynamic range; the Manf correlation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA was only r=0.162.

summary: Epha6 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptional response in any measured brain cell class.
why_it_matters: Epha6 is an annotated Eph/ephrin receptor, so the all-cell-type absence of corrected RNA changes makes the dominant result a transcriptomic null rather than a pathway activation signature.
main_caveats: The statement is limited to RNA differential expression in this dataset; the target transcript itself was not depleted at FDR<0.05, so a biological null cannot be separated from incomplete perturbation.

summary: Six cell classes showed nominal Epha6 transcript decreases, yet none converted that target trend into FDR-supported downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The downstream null was present even in the cell classes with the clearest measured on-target trend, arguing that the dataset does not contain a hidden high-confidence responder among inhibitory, thalamic, midbrain/hindbrain, or cerebellar classes.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Target engagement in these six classes was only nominal, with Epha6 adjusted p=1.0 in every class.

summary: Epha6 was weaker than Epha4 and Epha7 in a matched thalamic glutamatergic class and Epha6 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with EphA paralogs or Fyn/Rac1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: Shared membership in the Eph receptor family did not make Epha6 an interchangeable transcriptomic proxy for more strongly engaged Eph receptors in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast may reflect guide or transcript-detection efficiency as well as receptor biology; most related perturbations also produced very sparse corrected downstream effects.

summary: Epha6 knockdown did not transcriptionally mobilize a measured Eph/ephrin ligand-receptor or canonical Rho/MAPK signaling module.
why_it_matters: The curated Eph/ephrin neighborhood stayed indistinguishable from background, which is consistent with Eph signaling being primarily contact-dependent and post-translational rather than a broad acute RNA program in this assay.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was tested; phosphorylation, receptor clustering, axonal localization, or cell-cell contact outputs were not measured.

summary: Known mouse EphA6 learning/memory phenotypes and EphA5/EphA6 neuronal-morphology phenotypes did not have a strong Epha6 cell-autonomous RNA correlate in this Perturb-seq readout.
why_it_matters: The result cautions against equating germline EphA6 brain phenotypes with an acute, large transcriptional program in the sampled cell classes; the relevant biology may be developmental, structural, circuit-level, or engagement-limited here.
main_caveats: The literature used germline or deletion models and morphological or behavioral outputs, whereas this dataset measures RNA after Perturb-seq perturbation and showed weak corrected target engagement.

summary: Epha6 had no robust positive or negative all-target signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The strongest individual correlations were confined to 308 CB GABA and remained below |r|=0.3, while cross-cell mean correlations were near zero, so neither top positive nor top negative neighbors justify a convergence claim.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed over Wilcoxon scores and can be attenuated by weak Epha6 target engagement.

summary: Hectd4 mRNA was reduced in most assayed neuronal classes, but only the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class reached target-transcript FDR significance.
why_it_matters: The perturbation is best interpreted as a partial knockdown with one strong cell-type anchor rather than as uniformly efficient loss of Hectd4 across the atlas.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Several classes had weak measured knockdown and many p values did not survive per-cell-type FDR correction.

summary: Acute Hectd4 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: beyond the target transcript itself, no gene passed FDR<0.05 in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: HECTD4 is annotated as a ubiquitin ligase, but its basal loss did not trigger a broad recurrent mRNA stress, protein-homeostasis, or ubiquitination-response program in this dataset.
main_caveats: Absence of DE is an mRNA result only; HECTD4 substrates, ubiquitination, and phosphorylation were not measured.

summary: The published HECTD4-GluN2B/MALT1 injury axis was uncoupled from basal Hectd4 transcriptional signatures.
why_it_matters: A post-translational stroke mechanism cannot be inferred from Grin2b or Malt1 mRNA in unchallenged Perturb-seq cells; the dataset argues that any HECTD4 effect on this axis is likely protein-level or injury-context-dependent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

direction: loss-of-function disease risk despite weak RNA phenotype

summary: Npas3 guide assignment did not produce measurable target-RNA suppression or any FDR-significant downstream gene in the 22 assayed neuronal classes.

summary: The expected NPAS3-ARNT/ARNT2 axis was not recovered: Arnt and Arnt2 perturbations were also FDR-silent and their score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Npas3.

why_it_matters: The stress response is branch-specific to HBP/GFPT1 perturbation rather than a generic consequence of perturbing a glycolytic gene feeding fructose-6-phosphate pools.

summary: Multiple neuronal classes, including Pvalb GABA and CA3/CA2/DG glutamatergic cells, show little or no FDR-significant response to Gfpt1 perturbation.

summary: FDR-null Cacng8/Cacng2/Cacng3 signatures contrast with sparse but detectable Dlg4, Grip1, Gria1, and Gria2 perturbation effects.

summary: The Perturb-seq null should not be read as evidence that TARP-gamma8 antagonism is biologically inactive.
why_it_matters: Gamma-8-selective AMPAR antagonists act by receptor allostery and pharmacology; the lack of a Cacng8 mRNA program in this screen warns against using this single-cell transcriptomic endpoint as a stand-in for acute AMPAR current, seizure, or behavioral phenotypes.

summary: Il1r1 perturbation did not produce measurable on-target Il1r1 mRNA depletion in any assayed cell type.

summary: The Il1r1 transcriptome was genome-wide null, with no FDR<0.05 genes in 355046 tests.
why_it_matters: The screen offers no strong cell-intrinsic downstream target for Il1r1 in these neuronal clusters, even in the cell types with the best nominal genes.
main_caveats: Several cell types had only 26-50 perturbed cells, and the best nominal genes are not validated hits.

summary: Canonical IL-1/NF-kappaB/AP-1 inflammatory transcripts were not mobilized by Il1r1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Known IL1R1 signaling is built to recruit IL1RAP, IRAK/MYD88/TRAF6 and activate NF-kappaB/MAPK; the absence of corrected Nfkbia, Tnfaip3, Ptgs2, chemokine, Il6, Fos, Jun, or Junb responses argues that these assayed neurons were not in a tonic canonical IL-1 state.
main_caveats: Basal CRISPR perturbation is not an acute IL-1 stimulation assay, and weak Il1r1 engagement can mask true receptor-dependent responses.

summary: The negative phenotype was shared by glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes rather than confined to one resistant subtype.
why_it_matters: Mouse-brain studies emphasize strong endothelial and other non-neuronal IL1R1 actions plus specialized neuronal IL1R1 programs; this dataset refines that model by showing that broad neuronal Il1r1 targeting, as implemented here, did not recreate a robust inflammatory transcriptional program.
main_caveats: The screen did not assay endothelial, choroid-plexus, ependymal, astrocytic, microglial, or peripheral myeloid compartments where brain IL1R1 biology can be prominent.

summary: Il1r1 and its required co-receptor Il1rap failed to generate convergent signatures.
why_it_matters: IL1R1 and IL1RAP are a receptor pair in the canonical pathway, so the lack of similarity is an important negative control on pathway-level interpretation of this screen rather than evidence for a new IL1R1-independent Il1rap mechanism.
main_caveats: Both receptor-subunit perturbations had weak on-target mRNA evidence, and the compared signatures were all basal single-cell transcriptomes.

summary: Unbiased Il1r1 signature-neighbor search did not recover a coherent IL-1-like module.
why_it_matters: The weak nearest neighbors were concentrated in 308 CB GABA and were not IL-1 receptor complex members, limiting follow-up value of raw scalar signature correlations for this target.

main_caveats: This is a restricted signature-correlation result; the maximum absolute r was only 0.269 and came from a cell type with no FDR-significant Il1r1 response.

summary: The neuronal negative result should not be used as a pharmacodynamic template for systemic IL-1 receptor blockade.
why_it_matters: IL1R1 is a clinically actionable inflammatory node, but this dataset did not support neuronal canonical NF-kappaB/AP-1 transcripts as biomarkers of IL-1 antagonism.
main_caveats: The clinical evidence is human systemic cytokine blockade, whereas the dataset is mouse basal neuronal genetic perturbation with weak Il1r1 mRNA engagement.

summary: Osmr did not converge with same-family receptor perturbations or with assayed STAT perturbations.

summary: The Osmr negative result is restricted to basal Glut/GABA neuronal classes and is consistent with OSMR biology being glial, progenitor, or inflammatory-state gated in the CNS.

summary: This dataset gives no neuronal transcriptomic liability signal for anti-OSMRβ therapy, but it also does not test inflammatory OSMRβ programs that motivate vixarelimab and OSM/IL-31 disease biology.
why_it_matters: OSMRβ is clinically druggable and disease-linked; a flat neuronal Perturb-seq result should be interpreted as absence of evidence in these cell states, not as CNS or systemic safety de-risking.

direction: loss-of-function disease biology may be mRNA-silent
summary: Bulk transcriptomic quietness after Sms perturbation should not be read as neural safety for SMS inhibition or as failure of the SRS disease mechanism.

summary: Nr4a1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered or weakly engaged at the RNA level across all tested neuronal classes: the target transcript was not consistently depleted and no downstream gene reached 5% FDR.
why_it_matters: NR4A1 is a DNA-binding nuclear receptor, so a productive loss-of-function could plausibly rewire many genes; the whole-screen result instead says this dataset should be interpreted as a largely negative basal neuronal perturbation rather than a confident NR4A1 regulon map.
main_caveats: Target mRNA abundance is only a transcript-level proxy for an indel perturbation; many cell types had tens rather than hundreds of perturbed nuclei.

summary: The strongest Nr4a1 signals were weakly cell-type skewed toward 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut and 308 CB GABA, but both were nominal-only signatures.

summary: Nr4a1, Nr4a2, and Nr4a3 did not act as interchangeable transcriptomic perturbations in most neuronal classes; only 308 CB GABA showed a moderate positive Nr4a1-Nr4a2/Nr4a3 full-signature alignment.

cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are computed on weak signatures and are not evidence of direct regulatory relationships.

summary: Broad Pvalb and Sst GABA classes did not reproduce the large PV/SST Nr4a1 transcriptional programs reported after interneuron-focused Nr4a1 loss.

summary: The absence of a basal neuronal Nr4a1 loss signature should not be used as evidence that NR4A1 modulation is transcriptionally inert or safe, because key literature mechanisms are activity-, stress-, or microglia-dependent contexts not captured by this screen.

main_caveats: Restricted to correlation of scRNA-seq differential-expression scores; Ppp2r2b, Ppp2r5d, and Set did not show strong FDR target engagement in 151.

summary: PTPA/PP2A biology has opposing disease-direction contexts, and the Ptpa screen shows that lowering Ptpa can be buffered in some neurons but measurably active in one glutamatergic state.
why_it_matters: PTPA loss can cause human parkinsonism with intellectual disability, yet reducing PTPA/PP2A was beneficial in a Ube3a model; the Perturb-seq data warn that any PTPA-directed strategy needs context-specific neuronal safety readouts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The screen is mouse, acute, and transcriptomic; it does not model human biallelic missense disease, dopaminergic degeneration, or the Ube3a Angelman context directly.

summary: Safe_target_11 produced a near-null transcriptome-wide signature and had no measurable target transcript.

main_caveats: The assay likely sampled surviving cells at a later endpoint and was not designed as an acute DNA-damage time course.

summary: Within the 100-guide Safe_target family, Safe_target_11 was conventionally null but had the highest nominal p<0.001 hit count.
why_it_matters: A nominal-hit scalar alone would rank this negative-control guide as relatively active even though no row reached FDR<0.05, illustrating why safe guides still need per-guide QC.
main_caveats: The comparison was limited to Safe_target labels present in this DE parquet and did not inspect guide sequences or genomic cut sites.

summary: Nominal Safe_target_11 hits failed to recur as a same-direction gene module across cell types.

direction: mostly weak target-transcript decrease without downstream FDR response
summary: Nsmf perturbation produced almost no FDR-supported transcriptomic response across the profiled mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: This is the primary result: biological interpretation should focus on buffering, weak engagement, or missing developmental contexts rather than on nominal top genes.
main_caveats: The target transcript decreased nominally in most cell types, so a low or heterogeneous perturbation dose may contribute; FDR was computed within many thousands of genes per cell type.

direction: Nsmf down; downstream response not FDR-supported
summary: The only near-FDR on-target signal is restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but even there secondary genes remain nominal.
why_it_matters: The data point to a thalamic Nsmf-responsive compartment rather than a cortex- or striatum-wide effect, consistent with curated evidence that Nsmf is expressed in adult thalamus.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only the target transcript reached FDR<0.10; the cell-type interpretation rests on relative rather than FDR<0.05 support.

summary: Nsmf does not phenocopy NMDA-receptor or synaptic-neighbor perturbations in the thalamic cell type where it is best engaged.
why_it_matters: NSMF/Jacob is annotated and experimentally described as an NMDA-to-nucleus messenger, yet direct Grin1, Grin2b, Syn1, Camk2b, Dlg4, and Grin2a perturbations were much stronger and their score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Nsmf.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Transcriptomic comparisons are restricted to basal perturbation signatures; Jacob/NSMF may act after patterned synaptic or extrasynaptic NMDA stimulation rather than as a constitutive determinant of Grin1-like expression.

summary: Nsmf and dataset-tested hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism network neighbors show little convergence in mature brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The weak signatures of Nsmf, Prokr2, Kiss1r, Gnrhr, Fgfr1, Chd7, and Tacr3 argue that this Perturb-seq atlas is not sampling the embryonic olfactory/GnRH migration state central to NSMF-linked Kallmann and hypogonadotropic-hypogonadism biology.
main_caveats: The perturbation panel contains only a subset of the congenital GnRH-migration network and lacks direct embryonic olfactory placode or GnRH-neuron measurements.

summary: An unbiased signature-neighbor scan found no strong positive or inverse surrogate for Nsmf.
why_it_matters: Because neither known neighbors nor all assayed targets recapitulated the Nsmf score vector, the safest interpretation is that the measured Nsmf response is isolated and low amplitude rather than part of a broader convergent module.
main_caveats: Correlation magnitudes are so small that ranked neighbors should be treated as a falsification of strong convergence, not as mechanistic leads.

summary: Pacs2 produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic perturbation in any measured mouse brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This is the primary interpretation constraint: downstream pathway effects cannot be called absent with confidence when the target transcript itself was not significantly reduced.
main_caveats: Negative transcriptome result with weak target engagement; no protein-level PACS2 measurement.

summary: Pacs2 self-depletion was nominally strongest in caudal or hypothalamic/pineal classes, led by 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: The nominal pattern suggests where a stronger Pacs2 perturbation might be easiest to read out, while flagging 217 P MY Pineal Glut as low-count.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: All on-target FDR values were 1.0; one of the strongest rows used only 21 perturbed cells.

summary: Known PACS2 ER-mitochondria, autophagy, UPR, and apoptosis marker genes were not FDR-shifted after Pacs2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The result separates literature-defined PACS2 organelle-contact functions from the weak steady-state RNA response in this screen and argues for morphology, calcium, autophagy-flux, or disease-allele assays before inferring mechanism.
main_caveats: The pathway-negative call is limited by weak Pacs2 knockdown and by an RNA-only readout of post-transcriptional organelle biology.

why_it_matters: Cadps, Stac2, and Sema3e are tempting neuronal candidates by nominal p value, but their cell-type contrasts did not show target engagement, so they should not be elevated to Zfp397 pathway readouts.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: All highlighted non-target rows had FDR 0.298-0.381 and came from 37-54 perturbed cells.

summary: The partially engaged 155 MB Glut signature had no strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: A weak nearest-neighbor landscape argues against a clear shared module elsewhere in the screen and reduces confidence that the MB Glut nominal genes are a reproducible pathway.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed only over the top 500 Zfp397-ranked genes; the Zfp397 seed signature itself was not FDR-significant.

direction: Ar and Tet2 unchanged after partial Zfp397 decrease
summary: The AR/TET2 lineage-plasticity axis described after ZNF397 loss in prostate cancer was not detectably induced in mouse 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The disease literature gives a clinically directional consequence of ZNF397 deficiency, but the brain Perturb-seq data do not support transferring that TET2/AR mechanism to neurons.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Species, tissue, disease state, perturbation strength, and selection context differ from the prostate-cancer studies.

summary: Phactr2 perturbation was transcriptionally quiet and lacked detectable depletion of the measured Phactr2 mRNA.
why_it_matters: This is the primary interpretive constraint: downstream PP1/actin biology cannot be confidently read as a Phactr2 loss-of-function phenotype when the target transcript itself was not significantly reduced.
main_caveats: The screen measures total transcript abundance; it cannot exclude isoform-specific promoter repression, protein-level depletion, or non-transcriptional effects.

summary: The only FDR-significant Phactr2-responsive transcript was the synaptic adhesion gene Lrfn4 in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA cells.
why_it_matters: LRFN4/SALM3 biology places the lone hit in a synapse-organization context rather than a broad cytoskeletal stress program, making Lrfn4 a narrow biomarker candidate for follow-up in this GABAergic class.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Only Lrfn4 passed FDR; nearby synaptic genes were nominal only; Lrfn4 up-regulation was not validated by protein or morphology assays.

summary: Phactr2 did not evoke the canonical actin-cytoskeleton response that was detectable after perturbing core actins in the same cells.
why_it_matters: PHACTR2 is expected to sit near PP1 and actin, but the dataset separates the one Lrfn4 signal from the stronger Actb/Actg1-dependent cytoskeletal program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Ppp1ca was not an available perturbation; weak Phactr2 engagement means failure to see an actin module is not proof that PHACTR2 is uncoupled at the protein level.

summary: Phactr2 signatures were not interchangeable with available Phactr1 or Mrtfa perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: Even where a Phactr paralog and Mrtfa were assayed, their score correlations with Phactr2 were close to zero, arguing against a reusable PHACTR-family transcriptional module in this experiment.
main_caveats: Phactr3 and Phactr4 were not assayed, and Phactr1 itself had weak target engagement and no FDR-significant expression hits.

summary: In the only cell type with an FDR-significant gene, no other perturbation showed a strong whole-transcriptome similarity or opposition to Phactr2.
why_it_matters: The CNU-HYa HY GABA effect does not map to an obvious receptor or pathway-neighbor signature; the strongest non-self correlations had |r| only about 0.13.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The analysis used Pearson correlation on Wilcoxon scores, so it can miss nonlinear or sparse single-gene relationships.

summary: The dataset provides no neuronal therapeutic direction for PHACTR2 despite external actin and disease evidence.
why_it_matters: Existing PHACTR2 disease evidence is strongest outside this mouse neuronal context, and the Perturb-seq result is too weak to infer whether increasing or decreasing PHACTR2 would be beneficial in a brain disease setting.
main_caveats: No cardiomyocytes or disease models were profiled; the screen lacks actin-polymerization, migration, and protein-interaction readouts.

summary: Smad1 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any of 23 assayed cell classes and did not measurably deplete Smad1 RNA.
why_it_matters: The Smad1 nominal genes should not be interpreted as a definitive BMP-SMAD transcriptional program because the primary screen readout is dominated by weak on-target engagement and a genome-wide FDR null.
main_caveats: A high-confidence null in the measured RNA table is not proof of SMAD1 dispensability; inefficient perturbation, low baseline target expression, protein stability, or untested protein phosphorylation could mask biology.

direction: no robust response despite 108-179 perturbed cells
summary: Better-powered Smad1 cell classes remained negative, so the pan-dataset null is not confined to rare classes.
why_it_matters: Large matched contrasts in cortical, thalamic, and midbrain glutamatergic cells and in Pvalb GABA cells still had no FDR<0.05 genes, arguing that low cell number alone does not explain the absence of a Smad1 RNA signature.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The four contrasts are larger than the rest of the Smad1 table but still not definitive perturbational knockdowns because Smad1 RNA itself was not significantly reduced.

summary: The Pvalb GABA contrast did not reproduce the adult PV-interneuron BMP2-SMAD1 activity-response module.
why_it_matters: PV-specific BMP-SMAD1 signaling has been linked to cortical excitation-inhibition balance and seizure protection, but basal Smad1 perturbation in the broad 052 Pvalb Gaba class left Fos, Bdnf, Id1, Id3, Smad7, Arc, and Npas4 unchanged at FDR level.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The literature used adult barrel-cortex activity manipulations and PV-specific BMP2-SMAD1 pathway disruption, whereas the dataset is a basal pooled cell-class RNA contrast with weak measured Smad1 depletion.

summary: Smad1 showed little transcriptional convergence with assayed canonical BMP/TGF-family receptors, SMAD partners, or the SMAD corepressor Ski.
why_it_matters: SMAD1 is expected to operate with SMAD4, SMAD9, BMP receptors, and ACVR-family receptors, yet most related perturbations were themselves sparse and Smad1 correlations with them were weak, so the screen does not reveal a shared basal canonical BMP module.
main_caveats: Correlations compare weak perturbation signatures; Smad5 was not targeted; absent convergence could reflect guide efficacy rather than pathway insulation.

direction: weak positive and weak negative correlations
summary: Unbiased Smad1 signature neighbors were too weak to define a stable positive or negative module.
why_it_matters: The strongest all-target correlations were only about |0.25| and concentrated in 308 CB GABA, with unrelated genes and a negative-control target in the local neighborhood, making the restricted signature unsuitable for pathway inference.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Nearest neighbors were computed from score-vector correlations and may capture cell-class-specific noise or shared technical structure rather than direct biology.

summary: The screen does not support Smad1 nominal hits as biomarkers or a direct SMAD1 drug-response signature.
why_it_matters: The top candidate genes were only subthreshold and nonrecurrent, while the queried ChEMBL target record for SMAD1/5/9 contains phenotypic BMP-SMAD assays but no curated direct mechanism entries, so translational hypotheses should focus on better-engaged pathway contexts rather than Borcs5, Capn2, or Ehbp1 from this null profile.
main_caveats: ChEMBL absence of curated mechanisms is database- and query-limited; the warning is against interpreting this particular weak Smad1 RNA signature, not against all BMP-pathway pharmacology.

summary: Safe_target_16 behaved as a non-transcript safe-targeting control with no FDR-resolved transcriptomic phenotype in any of its 20 assayed mouse brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The correct biological interpretation is an inert Cas9-cutting control, not a silent knockout of a protein-coding pathway.
main_caveats: The table contains transcriptomic DE rather than indel or copy-number measurements, so absence of RNA response does not prove absence of editing or local genomic repair outcomes.

summary: The absence of a Safe_target_16 response was retained in the two best-sampled contexts, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This argues that the global negative call is not driven only by the lowest-cell-count strata.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Even these contexts have fewer than 105 Safe_target_16 cells, so small shifts remain underpowered.

summary: Safe_target_16 did not induce a reproducible p53, apoptosis, immediate-early, or heat-shock RNA signature despite literature showing that Cas9 double-strand breaks can trigger such stress programs in other systems.
why_it_matters: Safe-targeting guides are meant to control for nuclease cutting; this result says this specific control did not itself create a detectable stress confound in the assayed brain-cell transcriptomes.
main_caveats: The literature is largely from editing assays in proliferative or pluripotent human cells; this mouse brain Perturb-seq readout can miss DNA repair scars, transient responses, or edited cells lost before capture.

summary: The strongest Safe_target_16 nominal peaks were restricted to low-count cell types and remained below FDR significance, led by Nsd1 in 054 CNU-MGE GABA and Lemd2 in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: These rows are useful caveats but should not be promoted into Nsd1, Lemd2, chromatin, or nuclear-envelope biology for a safe-targeting control.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Nsd1 and Lemd2 had FDR 0.130 and 0.178 respectively, with only 30-31 perturbed cells in the implicated classes.

summary: Safe_target_16 lacked a convergent low-level module across cell classes: the global raw-p tail was depleted rather than enriched, and the most recurrent nominal genes appeared in mixed directions.
why_it_matters: A safe-target control could still be problematic if many weak, same-direction events added up to a stress or state-change program; that pattern was not present here.
main_caveats: This is a screen-level recurrence check using raw p < 0.05 and direction; it is not a formal gene-set enrichment test.

summary: Safe_target_53 behaved as a transcriptomic null across the assayed mouse-brain cell groups.
why_it_matters: The guide is best interpreted as a negative-control perturbation rather than as a gene knockdown with a downstream brain-cell phenotype.
main_caveats: The target label has no measured transcript, and most groups have fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: Hdac5 in 191 MB P MY GABA was the lone Safe_target_53 row below FDR 0.10, but it remained above the 5% FDR threshold.
why_it_matters: The row is a guide-QC candidate that should not be promoted to a hindbrain GABA pathway without validation.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: One adjusted p value just under 0.10 from 39 perturbed cells; no 5% FDR support.

summary: Safe_target_53 fell within the sparse empirical-null behavior of the 100 safe-targeting controls.
why_it_matters: The weak Safe_target_53 tail is not an outsized safe-guide artifact relative to the other negative-control-like perturbations.
main_caveats: The family-level comparison is descriptive because pvals_adj values were stored per perturbation and cell group, not refit as a shared 29.8-million-test FDR.

summary: The Safe_target_53 profile did not form a recurrent gene module or align with any perturbation signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: There is no evidence that a true target pathway, complex, paralog family, receptor system, or disease module is hiding behind the isolated nominal rows.
comparators: Ago2|Grin3a|2016 other perturbations in 191 MB P MY GABA
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor testing was done in the one group with the strongest Safe_target_53 row, not in every cell group.

summary: Pank2 perturbation produced a transcriptionally buffered or weak response in the assayed mouse-brain cells rather than a robust loss-of-function signature.
why_it_matters: The dataset-wide absence of FDR-significant genes and inconsistent Pank2 transcript reduction fit the idea that acute Pank2 disruption in mouse brain can be buffered, especially because mouse PanK1 and PanK2 can compensate for CoA production and Pank2-null mice do not reproduce the basal-ganglia syndrome of human PKAN.
main_caveats: Moderate biological confidence because the perturbation had few cells per type and weak on-target RNA knockdown; no protein, CoA, or editing-efficiency measurement is available.

summary: The canonical pantothenate-to-CoA pathway and mitochondrial energy genes were not coherently induced or repressed after Pank2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: PANK2 catalyzes the first CoA-biosynthetic reaction, so a strong CoA-depletion state would be expected to connect to PANK paralogs, COASY/PPCS/PPCDC, or oxidative metabolism; their FDR-level silence argues that the observed single-gene nominal hits should not be read as a canonical CoA transcriptional program.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic negative result; CoA metabolites and mitochondrial respiration were not assayed.

summary: A low-confidence MH-LH TH Glut signal nominated Rheb up-regulation, accompanied by nominal Ddit4 down-regulation, as the only near-FDR Pank2-associated stress marker.
why_it_matters: RHEB sits in the mTORC1 energy-growth signaling axis, so this isolated thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic response could flag a nutrient-signaling state to follow up if Pank2 perturbation can be strengthened.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Rheb did not pass FDR<0.05, the cell type had only 35 perturbed cells, and the Ddit4 observation was nominal with FDR=1.0.

summary: Pank2 did not occupy a stable cross-perturbation signature neighborhood and did not converge with stronger Atp13a2, Fth1, or Cisd2 perturbations.
why_it_matters: This prevents rescue of the weak Pank2 result by nearest-neighbor inference: the top restricted-signature neighbors were mostly one-off and stronger comparator perturbations in the same panel were not Pank2-like.
main_caveats: The neighbor analysis used only the 200 strongest Pank2 genes per cell type and is undermined by weak Pank2 target engagement.

summary: The assayed perturbation should be treated as a weak loss-of-function challenge, not as a proxy for therapeutic PanK activation.
why_it_matters: Human PKAN is caused by PANK2 loss or reduction, whereas a preclinical therapeutic strategy activates remaining PanK enzymes to restore brain CoA; the near-null single-cell response here is therefore useful mainly for detecting buffered loss-of-function cell states and not for nominating inhibition biomarkers.
main_caveats: The dataset does not include a PanK activator, CoA metabolites, or rescue experiments; the warning is based on disease directionality plus the lack of a robust Pank2 knockdown signature.

summary: Ptf1a produced no FDR-supported within-cell-type DE phenotype and no measurable target-transcript depletion across the assayed mouse-brain panel.
why_it_matters: This prevents a conventional downstream-gene or pathway interpretation and indicates that Ptf1a was inactive, unexpressed, or insufficiently engaged in the sampled states.
main_caveats: The table measures within-cell-type DE only and cannot detect Ptf1a-driven changes in cell abundance or earlier fate choice.

summary: The 308 CB GABA stratum did not show a robust Ptf1a response even though cerebellar GABAergic development is the best-known neural Ptf1a context.
why_it_matters: It narrows the literature expectation to embryonic Ptf1a-positive cerebellar progenitors rather than broad post-annotation cerebellar GABAergic cells.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only 79 perturbed CB GABA cells were present, and the assay may miss developmental fate or abundance effects.

summary: Nominal Ptf1a hits were cell-type isolated rather than a repeated downstream module.
why_it_matters: This argues against rescuing the perturbation through an exploratory module built from raw p-value hits.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is a negative statistical pattern; it does not prove biological compensation, especially without target engagement.

summary: Assayed PTF1A complex-adjacent and developmental-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy the weak Ptf1a signature.
why_it_matters: A true PTF1A fate program would be expected to share structure with E-protein or Atoh1/Notch-related perturbations in a permissive context, but the observed correlations were near background.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Rbpj and Rbpjl were not targeted, and correlation of a weak Ptf1a vector can only rule out large phenocopies.

summary: The mouse-brain negative result should not be interpreted as evidence that developmental PTF1A loss is safe or biologically dispensable.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse data tie PTF1A loss to pancreas and cerebellum formation; this dataset instead shows that the assayed brain-cell DE endpoint is outside the main vulnerable developmental window.
main_caveats: The perturbation report alone has no developmental abundance readout and no direct pancreas assay.

summary: Safe_target_17 did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptomic program in its only analyzable cell type.
why_it_matters: This prevents assignment of a gene program, pathway activation, or guide-cutting stress response from the nominal gene list alone.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only 30 Safe_target_17 cells were tested, so a subtle response could be missed.

summary: Safe_target_17 is coverage-restricted rather than biologically cell-type selective in this table.
why_it_matters: The perturbation cannot be compared across neuronal classes because the DE output contains Safe_target_17 only in one thalamic glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Absence from other cell-type result rows should be read as lack of analyzable DE output, not proof of zero edited cells or a resistant biology.

summary: Safe_target_17 was not one of the idiosyncratic same-cell-type Safe-target guides and had no recurrent Safe-target signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: Cas9 cutting can in principle trigger DNA-damage biology, but this Safe-target guide sat near the low-effect end of the same-class Safe-target distribution rather than joining the small number of Safe-target guides with FDR hits.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Safe-target genomic sites and guide sequences were not present in the DE table, so the comparison is phenotypic rather than mechanistic.

summary: The weak Safe_target_17 vector did not converge on an endogenous perturbation program in the same thalamic class.
why_it_matters: Nominal Safe_target_17 genes should not be interpreted by borrowing mechanisms from the nearest full-dataset positive or negative neighbors, because those neighbors were essentially uncorrelated.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The neighbor screen used DE score vectors within one cell type and should be considered a signature-level comparison, not a raw-cell reanalysis.

summary: Safe_target_17 should be treated as a control guide label, not as a mouse disease gene or therapeutic node.
why_it_matters: No endogenous transcript named Safe_target_17 was measured for target engagement, and a mouse gene database query returned no Safe_target_17 record, so complexes, paralogs, druggability, and disease mechanisms are not applicable.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This does not identify the genomic coordinate cut by the guide; it only rules out a measured mRNA target in the DE table and a standard mouse gene-symbol match.

summary: Six6 perturbation did not measurably reduce the Six6 transcript in any tested cell type.
why_it_matters: The absence of a downstream signature should be read first as absent or undetectable target engagement, not as proof that Six6 is dispensable in its native retinal, pituitary, or GnRH contexts.
main_caveats: The available file contains Wilcoxon DE summaries rather than raw guide efficiencies; self-row DE is an indirect engagement assay.

summary: Six6 produced no FDR-significant downstream differentially expressed gene across 371818 tests.
why_it_matters: No cell class supplied a robust transcriptional phenotype for pathway inference or biomarker nomination.
main_caveats: The null may reflect the missing target engagement quantified in F001.

summary: The nominal Six6 signal had weak cell-type peaks in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut but no reproducible gene module.
why_it_matters: These cell types are useful audit points, yet their top rows are exploratory rather than evidence for a cortical or interneuron Six6 program.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: All highlighted rows fail FDR correction and nominal recurrence was sparse and directionally mixed.

summary: The weak Six6 signatures did not converge with Six-family, eye-field, STRING-neighbor, or top signature-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: Although SIX6 has developmental links to SIX3, PAX6, DACH, OTX2, and Wnt/eye-field programs, those relationships were not reconstructed in mouse-brain cell classes by Six6 transcriptome similarity.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor analysis used weak Six6 profiles; lack of correlation is informative only as an absence of detectable convergence.

summary: The dataset supports a retina/pituitary/GnRH-biased boundary for SIX6 disease biology rather than a broad neuronal response to Six6 loss.
why_it_matters: Human SIX6 genetics emphasize ocular disease, and adult retinal-ganglion stress can make SIX6 activity harmful through p16INK4a; the brain Perturb-seq null argues against extrapolating those mechanisms to all neuronal classes or using this atlas to select a generic CNS SIX6 biomarker.
main_caveats: The dataset did not sample retina, pituitary precursors, optic stalk, or a validated GnRH-neuron population.

summary: Safe_target_4 produced no transcriptome-wide significant differential-expression response in any of the six assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The target behaves like a negative or safe-targeting control rather than a biological knockdown, so the result should anchor background behavior instead of a pathway model.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The perturbed matched-cell counts were small, ranging from 20 to 54 cells per cell type, so weak effects may be underpowered.

summary: Safe_target_4 is not interpretable as a measured gene knockdown because no Safe_target_4 transcript row was present and the label did not resolve as an exact mouse gene symbol.
why_it_matters: Without a transcript target, there is no on-target RNA depletion statistic, disease gene, paralog, receptor subunit, or pathway membership to interpret.
main_caveats: The database check was an exact MyGene.info mouse-symbol query; it does not identify the genomic safe-targeting locus or guide sequence.

summary: Nominal Safe_target_4 rows did not form a reproducible cross-cell-type expression module.
why_it_matters: The lack of nominal recurrence prevents the FDR-null top genes from being promoted to stress markers, biomarkers, or hidden pathway readouts.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a recurrence analysis over nominal p < 0.05 rows only; it should be read as a guard against overinterpretation, not as proof that every weak effect is absent.

summary: Tbl1x did not yield a target-engaged transcriptomic phenotype in this screen.
why_it_matters: TBL1X is a nuclear NCoR/SMRT-associated transcriptional regulator, so the absence of Tbl1x RNA depletion and the complete absence of FDR<0.05 downstream genes make the dataset unsuitable for inferring the normal brain function of a successfully suppressed Tbl1x allele.
main_caveats: Negative at the transcript level only; the perturbation may have altered unmeasured isoforms or protein in a subset of cells, but guide-level data are not present in the parquet.

summary: Dner up-regulation in 155 MB Glut was the only near-FDR Tbl1x response and is a Notch-linked biomarker hypothesis rather than a validated pathway call.
why_it_matters: The lead subthreshold gene connects a midbrain glutamatergic response to neuron-to-glia Notch biology, a pathway family containing TBL1X in Reactome, but no broader corrected signature accompanied it.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Dner was FDR=0.077553 rather than FDR<0.05, the next two genes had FDR=0.792898, and DNER is a Notch ligand rather than direct evidence of Notch target-gene activation.

summary: Tbl1x failed to phenocopy its NCoR/SMRT paralog and STRING neighbor Tbl1xr1.
why_it_matters: A close complex-neighbor perturbation produced corrected responses in matched neuronal classes, showing that at least some TBL1-family biology was recoverable in the dataset while Tbl1x itself remained flat.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Tbl1xr1 itself also did not show a corrected decrease in its own transcript, so the comparison is signature-based rather than a fully target-engaged paralog titration.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Rora, Nr1d1 and Bmal1 perturbations were strong whereas Tbl1x was silent.
why_it_matters: Reactome places TBL1X in RORA/REV-ERB and BMAL/CLOCK/NPAS2 transcriptional regulation; the thalamic glutamatergic results therefore separate robust DNA-binding circadian/nuclear-receptor programs from the ineffective Tbl1x perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The tested neighbors are pathway transcription factors rather than TBL1X-complex subunits, so the result shows pathway-level uncoupling, not biochemical dispensability of TBL1X.

summary: The flat mouse-brain Tbl1x signature should not be used to de-risk pharmacologic TBL1X degradation.
why_it_matters: Human TBL1X has disease links and degraders are experimentally assayed through CRBN/TBL1X ChEMBL entries; the screen did not establish target engagement in neurons, so an apparent lack of brain transcriptional toxicity is not an interpretable safety margin.
main_caveats: The dataset used genetic perturbation in mouse brain cells whereas the ChEMBL entries are acute PROTAC assays in a human cell line; neither setting demonstrates in vivo CNS efficacy or toxicity for a degrader.

summary: Nr1h2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the assayed neuronal classes: the target mRNA was measured everywhere but was never significantly depleted, and no downstream gene reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: This is the primary interpretation anchor: most Nr1h2 contrasts should be treated as a null or weak-engagement experiment rather than as a map of LXRβ-dependent neuronal target genes.
main_caveats: Target-transcript abundance is only a readout of RNA-level engagement; if the perturbation used nuclease editing, an edited but stable transcript could still score as unchanged.

summary: Canonical LXR cholesterol-efflux genes were not coherently regulated by Nr1h2 perturbation in neurons; Abca1, Abcg1, Apoe, Mylip, and Srebf1 had no FDR-supported changes.
why_it_matters: NR1H2 is curated as an oxysterol-responsive LXR/RXR transcription factor for cholesterol efflux, so the absent ABCA1/ABCG1/APOE response separates the observed neuronal perturbation from the established efflux program.
main_caveats: The strongest lipid-gene row was nominal only and no raw guide-editing or baseline-expression data were available in the parquet.

summary: The Perturb-seq null is most consistent with LXRβ CNS effects being glial or state-dependent rather than acutely neuron-autonomous in the assayed classes.
why_it_matters: Prior CNS work places LXR-regulated APOE/ABCA1 cholesterol handling and PD-related protection largely in astrocytes or microglia; the Nr1h2 tables contain neuronal labels and do not test those glial compartments directly.
main_caveats: This is an inference from the available cell-type labels; absence of glial Nr1h2 contrasts in this file is not proof that glia would respond in the same assay.

summary: The dataset can detect sterol transcriptional programs: Srebf2 knockdown gave a strong multi-cell-type cholesterol-biosynthesis signature, whereas Nr1h2, Nr1h3, RXR-subunit, Abca1, and Srebf1 perturbations did not.
why_it_matters: The Nr1h2 null is not simply a failure of all lipid genes or all sterol regulators in this Perturb-seq experiment; it is branch-specific relative to SREBP2-controlled cholesterol synthesis and uptake.
main_caveats: Srebf2 controls a synthesis branch rather than the same LXR/RXR efflux branch, so it is an assay/pathway contrast rather than a direct complex-member rescue experiment.

summary: The midbrain dopaminergic Nr1h2 contrast—the closest assayed label to the LXRβ Parkinson-disease literature—was too small and transcriptionally silent to evaluate dopaminergic vulnerability mechanisms.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-reading a disease-relevant null: adult LXRβ protection of substantia nigra dopaminergic neurons has been linked to microglia/astroglia, while this assay contributed only 23 MB Dopa perturbed cells and no target-RNA effect.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The cell label is broad, the perturbed-cell count is low, and the measured cells are not equivalent to an adult MPTP substantia-nigra microenvironment.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut showed a weak, same-direction nominal decrease of several lipid genes, including Abca1 and Abcg1, and is the only Nr1h2 class worth carrying forward as an exploratory LXR-efflux biomarker hypothesis.
why_it_matters: Although not significant after correction, ABCA1 and ABCG1 are canonical LXR efflux genes; a concordant trend in the largest Nr1h2 contrast is biologically interpretable enough to nominate for validation rather than to discard silently.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: All four rows had FDR=1.0 and the Nr1h2 target transcript itself was not significantly reduced in this same cell class.

summary: Mmaa perturbation was effectively FDR-silent across the assayed neuronal atlas.
why_it_matters: Human MMAA is a core mitochondrial cobalamin-processing factor, but the mouse perturbation produced no genome-wide FDR-significant transcript in 22 cell types; the dataset therefore should not be read as a successful acute loss-of-function model for cblA biochemistry.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR signal is robust in this parquet, but the biological interpretation is constrained by weak on-target transcript suppression and low perturbed-cell counts in several cell types.

summary: The only nominal Mmaa self-decreases were concentrated in TH/MB-related glutamatergic groups and a very small pineal group.
why_it_matters: These cell types are the only places where the perturbation appears to have moved the target transcript in the intended direction, so any cell-type hypothesis from this experiment should start there rather than averaging all neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut

main_caveats: Phosphorylation and F-actin polymerization were not measured; weak Pak2 knockdown could also erase this response.

summary: A flat Pak2 transcriptomic profile should not be interpreted as evidence that PAK2 inhibition is silent or benign in brain cells.

summary: Purb and Purg perturbations did not phenocopy the Pura signature in the two Pura-responsive classes.

summary: The assayed Prkn perturbation did not measurably lower the Prkn transcript itself.
why_it_matters: A missing on-target mRNA effect makes every downstream null compatible with weak guide engagement or with a perturbation effect not captured at the transcript level.
main_caveats: mRNA depletion is only one readout of perturbation; protein loss or genome editing was not measured.

summary: Prkn was not profiled in the MB dopaminergic class and was negative in the non-dopaminergic classes that were profiled.

summary: The combination of human loss-of-function disease genetics and a buffered neuronal transcriptome suggests that pharmacologic PREPL inhibition would need vesicle-trafficking, neuromuscular, or mitochondrial biomarkers rather than relying on large neuronal mRNA signatures.
why_it_matters: Open Targets and ChEMBL point to a genetically linked but weakly chemically prosecuted target; if PREPL were inhibited, the dataset suggests that on-target RNA knockdown can be substantial while conventional transcriptional safety markers remain nearly silent.

summary: Psen1 CRISPR effects were uneven across neuronal classes: Psen1 mRNA decreased in most assayed classes, but only four contrasts had nominal P<0.05 target depletion and none passed FDR.
why_it_matters: Interpretation should be anchored on 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, and 053 Sst Gaba for target engagement; cell types with near-zero Psen1 depletion cannot distinguish buffering from failed perturbation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
