summary: Grm1 induction in 052 Pvalb Gaba was the single non-target FDR signal after Nrxn1 perturbation, but it occurred without corrected Nrxn1 RNA loss in the same cells.
why_it_matters: This makes Grm1 a narrow exploratory marker rather than a validated NRXN1 response; the result is worth preserving because it is the only FDR off-target event in the Nrxn1 dataset.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The target transcript was not significantly reduced after FDR correction in this cell type, so Grm1 could be a subtype-specific weak response, an indirect effect, or a false positive from a broad multiple-test panel.

summary: Available neurexin/neuroligin gene perturbations showed the same self-only pattern rather than a reciprocal ligand-network transcriptional cascade.
why_it_matters: Although Nrxn1 is physically connected to neuroligins and other trans-synaptic partners, perturbing Nrxn1, Nrxn2, Nlgn1, Nlgn2, or Nlgn3 did not uncover a shared high-amplitude RNA module in the assayed cell bodies.
main_caveats: Comparators had different guide efficiencies and cell counts; Nrxn3 lacked a self-transcript row, and absence of RNA cascades does not test trans-synaptic adhesion directly.

summary: Nrxn1 was buffered in cortical IT neurons where Grin2a or Grin2b perturbation produced broad FDR transcriptional programs with comparable perturbed-cell numbers.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the dataset can detect synaptic-network perturbations when they couple to RNA output; Nrxn1 is therefore not simply hidden by a universal lack of power in 005/007 IT glutamatergic cells.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The GRIN2A/GRIN2B contrast is strongest in two cortical IT classes and should not be extrapolated to all Nrxn1-expressing neurons.

summary: For NRXN1-linked neurodevelopmental disease, this dataset supports a physiology-first readout strategy rather than a bulk transcriptional rescue strategy.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse literature tie NRXN1 loss to synaptic transmission and behavior; the in-dataset self-knockdown without RNA propagation warns that screening for reversal of a large Nrxn1 mRNA signature would likely miss key phenotypes.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The inference is indirect because the dataset uses mouse broad cell classes and RNA endpoints, whereas disease studies include human deletions, developmental exposure, and electrophysiology.

summary: Pbx1 perturbation produced a globally sparse response with weak measured Pbx1 mRNA engagement.
why_it_matters: PBX1 is a nuclear developmental transcription factor, so the near-absence of FDR-level expression changes across mature brain cell classes is more consistent with buffering, incomplete perturbation, or stage restriction than with a broadly cell-autonomous acute transcriptional requirement.
main_caveats: Target mRNA depletion was not FDR-significant in any class, so a true PBX1-null phenotype could be much stronger.

summary: The only FDR-significant Pbx1-associated downstream transcript was Usp48 down-regulation in CNU-LGE/LSX GABAergic neurons.
why_it_matters: This isolates a small forebrain inhibitory-neuron response rather than a pan-neuronal PBX1 program, connecting only indirectly to PBX1 literature in adult forebrain neurogenesis.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Only Usp48 passed FDR<0.05 and the local Pbx1 target row was not significant; the other genes are nominal and hypothesis-generating.

summary: NP-CT-L6b-OB glutamatergic and cerebellar GABAergic cells showed the strongest nominal Pbx1 RNA decreases but no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The result separates target-transcript reduction from a detectable transcriptional cascade and argues that some mature neuronal classes buffer partial Pbx1 loss better than developmental progenitors do.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Pbx1 p values were nominal rather than FDR-significant and protein-level knockdown was not assayed.

summary: Pbx1 score signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Pbx3, Meis1, Meis2, Pknox2/Prep, Hoxa1, and Hoxa3 perturbations.
why_it_matters: Biochemistry and curated networks place PBX1 in PBX-MEIS/PREP-HOX assemblies; the Perturb-seq signatures therefore do not support simple interchangeability or shared acute output among assayed TALE/HOX inputs in these mature cell classes.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to mRNA score signatures; weak Pbx1 target engagement could erase real overlap.

summary: The Perturb-seq data do not recapitulate the broad developmental consequences expected from congenital PBX1 loss-of-function.
why_it_matters: Human damaging PBX1 variants cause intellectual disability and pleiotropic malformations, so the adult neuronal negative result warns that this assay is probing an acute, partial, post-developmental state rather than embryonic PBX1 dosage biology.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks embryos, organ primordia, and organismal phenotypes; it cannot test congenital PBX1 functions directly.

summary: FDR-significant Sptlc2 mRNA depletion in Pvalb and TH Prkcd/Grin2c neurons did not propagate to any 5% FDR downstream transcript.
why_it_matters: SPTLC2 catalyzes the first committed step of de novo sphingolipid synthesis; these neurons tolerate partial transcript loss at the scRNA-seq level rather than mounting a broad ER-lipid or stress program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation is mRNA based; lipid intermediates, SPT enzymatic activity and SPTLC2 protein abundance were not measured.

summary: Core SPT subunits and ORMDL regulators showed no detectable transcriptional compensation after Sptlc2 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Known SPT homeostasis is controlled by assembly and ORMDL/ceramide regulation, so the lack of Sptlc1, Sptlc3, Sptssa, Sptssb or Ormdl1-3 induction argues that any compensation in these neurons is not captured as simple mRNA feedback.
main_caveats: Only transcript levels were tested; ORMDL-dependent inhibition is expected to be post-transcriptional and lipid responsive.

summary: The apparent cell-type restriction of the Sptlc2 phenotype is dominated by heterogeneous guide engagement rather than a reproducible downstream neuron-class program.
why_it_matters: Twenty-one measured cell types showed Sptlc2 decreases in the same direction, but most did not pass on-target FDR and none gained a corrected non-target signature; high-count weak-engagement cell types therefore should not be read as resistant SPT biology.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Human Protein Atlas expression is orthogonal and adult/human; the Perturb-seq result is limited by 29-161 perturbed cells per tested class and by missing Sptlc2 rows in two classes.

summary: Available sphingolipid pathway-neighbor perturbations, Asah1 and Smpd3, were transcriptionally uncoupled from Sptlc2.
why_it_matters: Ceramide synthesis, degradation and sphingomyelin hydrolysis are biochemically connected, but the neuronal CRISPRi screen did not resolve a shared sphingolipid-stress module across these enzyme perturbations.
main_caveats: Asah1 and Smpd3 target transcripts were themselves weakly engaged, so absence of convergence may reflect incomplete knockdown as well as true pathway separation.

summary: This loss-of-function Perturb-seq signature should not be used as a direct model of SPTLC2-linked HSAN1C gain-of-function chemistry.
why_it_matters: Human HSAN1C mutations alter SPT substrate choice and raise toxic 1-deoxysphingolipids; partial mRNA depletion in central neurons gives a quiet scRNA-seq phenotype, emphasizing that variant substrate promiscuity and lipidomics are the clinically relevant axes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset lacks dorsal-root/autonomic neurons, sphingoid-base measurements and disease missense alleles.

summary: A global signature-neighbor scan found no strong Sptlc2-like perturbation, only weak 308 CB GABA correlations with unrelated targets.
why_it_matters: Nearest-neighbor analysis can reveal pathway bypasses or convergent stress states; here the weak maximum absolute correlation argues that Sptlc2 did not sit in a robust shared transcriptional module in this screen.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The leading neighbors come from a cell type with only nominal Sptlc2 on-target depletion, so they are not mechanistic pathway assignments.

summary: Spata7 produced no FDR-supported transcriptional response in any measured mouse-brain subclass.
why_it_matters: The main dataset result is a negative one: 22 subclasses were tested, including one with 144 perturbed cells, yet no individual downstream gene reached FDR<0.10.
main_caveats: Spata7 mRNA was not measured, so this is a downstream-signature negative result, not confirmed target disengagement or protein loss.

summary: The brain negative result fits a photoreceptor-distal-connecting-cilium model better than a generic neuronal cilium requirement.
why_it_matters: SPATA7 disease biology is centered on a specialized photoreceptor ciliary compartment; the lack of a broad neuronal response in the screen argues that mouse brain subclasses do not recapitulate that vulnerable LCA/RP context.
main_caveats: The screen did not assay retinal rods or cones, and the target transcript was absent from the brain DE table.

summary: Spata7 was not interchangeable with other ciliary or retinal-ciliopathy perturbations that yielded sparse significant hits in the same brain dataset.
why_it_matters: Ahi1, Adcy3, Cplane1, Ift88, B9d1, and Bbs5 produced FDR-supported rows in specific classes, whereas Spata7 did not; this separates SPATA7 from broader BBSome, IFT, transition-zone, or ciliary-cAMP effects in the assayed neurons.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Most related-target signals were small and in several cases consisted only of target-transcript depletion; guide efficiency and expression are not matched to Spata7.

summary: The only notable ciliary-family signature relationship for Spata7 was a cerebellar GABA anti-correlation with transition-zone genes rather than a coherent shared module.
why_it_matters: B9d1, Ahi1, and Cep290 are ciliary disease-family neighbors, yet their 308 CB GABA signatures pointed opposite to the weak Spata7 signature; this is best viewed as exploratory evidence against a single brain-wide ciliary transcriptomic module for SPATA7.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The Spata7 cerebellar signature had only 46 perturbed cells and no FDR-supported genes; correlations used weak whole-transcriptome score vectors.

summary: A cortical L2/3 Grin2b-Cacng3-Mef2c nominally down signature is only a hypothesis-generating biomarker set.
why_it_matters: This was the most interpretable cell-type-restricted nominal pattern, but the adjusted p values were far from significance, so these genes should be treated as follow-up features rather than claimed SPATA7 effectors.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to nominal p values in 44 perturbed cells; the known SPATA7 literature concerns retinal cilia, not cortical synaptic-gene regulation.

summary: The screen supplies no brain transcriptional rescue marker or direct druggability rationale for SPATA7.
why_it_matters: For a loss-of-function photoreceptor scaffold, the dataset does not identify a robust downstream brain biomarker and ChEMBL has no curated direct SPATA7 target entry; perturbation follow-up should therefore prioritize target-engaged retinal photoreceptor systems.
main_caveats: Absence of ChEMBL records is not proof of undruggability, and Perturb-seq measured RNA rather than connecting-cilium structure or photoreceptor survival.

summary: Syne1 mRNA knockdown was statistically clear only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, despite nominal target reduction in several other classes.
why_it_matters: The usable perturbation is concentrated in one thalamic glutamatergic class; interpreting absent responses in other classes as Syne1 independence would overstate experiments with weak target engagement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is transcript-level engagement; the dataset does not quantify SYNE1 protein, nuclear-envelope localization, or isoform-specific depletion.

summary: The best-engaged Syne1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: Syne1 itself was the only FDR<0.05 gene in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: A nuclear-envelope LINC scaffold can alter nuclear positioning or cytoskeletal mechanics without a large steady-state mRNA cascade, so the absence of secondary DE in this cell class is biologically informative rather than simply a failed screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Moderate confidence because Syne1 mRNA depletion was modest and may be insufficient to deplete a large structural protein; the conclusion is limited to gene-expression readout.

summary: The disease-relevant cerebellar GABA class did not recapitulate SYNE1 ataxia biology, but the result is inconclusive because on-target depletion there was weak.
why_it_matters: Human SYNE1 loss is linked to recessive cerebellar ataxia and mouse LINC perturbations affect cerebellar Purkinje-cell development; the Perturb-seq result should therefore be read as a need for stronger cerebellar/Purkinje and structural assays, not as evidence against cerebellar SYNE1 dependence.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The cell-class label is broad, only 77 Syne1-perturbed cells were available, Syne1 FDR was 1.0, and the assay is gene-level rather than isoform-, protein-, or morphology-resolved.

summary: Syne1 did not show a strong convergent or opposing transcriptomic signature with any available target, including nuclear-envelope and cytoskeletal substitutes for missing SUN-nesprin partners.
why_it_matters: Canonical interactors such as Sun1, Sun2, Syne2, Lmna, and Emd were absent from the library, and the nearest available score-vector neighbors were weak; this prevents assigning the Syne1 phenotype to a broader LINC or cytoskeletal co-perturbation module.
main_caveats: The closest physical LINC partners were not perturbed, so this is a negative result for the screened substitutes and all-library score neighbors only.

summary: FDR-supported Macf1 transcript knockdown was confined to 155 MB Glut in this DE table.
why_it_matters: Biological interpretation should be centered on the one cell class with convincing on-target engagement rather than averaging many weak guide-cell groups.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction may reflect guide recovery, baseline expression, cell counts, or power; target transcript was only partially reduced.

summary: Strong Macf1 knockdown in 155 MB Glut yielded zero FDR-significant non-target genes.
why_it_matters: The main effect of lowering a large cytoskeletal scaffold may occur at the level of microtubule and actin organization rather than as a broad endpoint mRNA program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No protein abundance, morphology, microtubule capture, or Wnt-stimulation measurements were available; partial knockdown could leave enough MACF1 protein for function.

summary: Atp1a3 was the leading recurrent nominally down non-target gene in the largest Macf1 signatures.
why_it_matters: A repeated Atp1a3 decrease offers a focused follow-up readout for Macf1 perturbation even though no non-target gene passed FDR.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Atp1a3 did not reach FDR<0.05 in any Macf1 signature and recurrence was based on nominal p values.

summary: Macf1 was transcriptomically uncoupled from inspected Wnt and cytoskeletal neighbors in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: MACF1 is linked to the AXIN/APC/CTNNB1/GSK3B/LRP6 Wnt module and to microtubule organizers, yet the Macf1 Perturb-seq signature did not resemble Ctnnb1, Apc, Gsk3b, Lrp6, Fzd3, Map1b, Actg1, Dst, Dctn1, or Dync1h1 signatures; Dctn1/Dync1h1 instead induced a strong Insig1/Msmo1/Fdps/Hmgcs1/Hmgcr sterol module absent from Macf1.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Several comparators, especially Dst, Apc, Gsk3b, Lrp6, and Fzd3, had weak self-knockdown in 155 MB Glut; signature correlations use mRNA only.

summary: Macf1 perturbation in this brain Perturb-seq dataset is a better model of partial transcript loss than of human GAR-domain lissencephaly variants.
why_it_matters: The human syndrome implicates MACF1 in neuronal migration and axon guidance, but the assayed partial knockdown produced a narrow, buffered mRNA signature rather than a large disease module.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset lacks migration and axon-guidance phenotypes, and human disease is dominated by specific heterozygous domain variants rather than complete mouse Macf1 loss.

summary: The Macf1 response does not support a simple MACF1-inhibition therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: A gene with dominant human brain-malformation alleles, LOF constraint, no clinical tractability in Open Targets, and no ChEMBL drug mechanism should not be advanced as a generic inhibition target based on a buffered knockdown signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a directionality warning, not a formal safety analysis; only transcriptomic knockdown output was measured.

summary: Oxtr perturbation produced one FDR<0.05 gene, Acly in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, plus two FDR<0.10 candidates in 191 MB P MY GABA and 215 MB Dopa.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports a narrow cell-state response rather than a broad OXTR transcriptional cascade, consistent with region-specific Oxtr biology.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Only Acly reached FDR<0.05; the other two genes were FDR<0.10 only, and the dopamine contrast had 24 perturbed cells.

summary: Oxtr mRNA was not detectably reduced in any cell type where the target transcript was measured.
why_it_matters: Weak on-target transcript engagement limits interpretation of absent or sparse downstream effects.
main_caveats: mRNA preservation does not prove absence of protein editing or receptor loss; Perturb-seq target rows can miss coding disruption.

summary: Oxtr was not phenocopied by its vasopressin-receptor paralogs Avpr1a, Avpr1b, or Avpr2.
why_it_matters: Shared receptor-family membership did not imply exchangeable transcriptomic effects in these mouse-brain cell classes.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Most family-member signatures were themselves weak, so the contrast should be read as non-convergence rather than proof of distinct physiology.

summary: Odr4 up-regulation in 215 MB Dopa nominates an exploratory Oxtr-sensitive marker in a dopamine class.
why_it_matters: The cell class overlaps a known OXTR-relevant circuit theme in which VTA dopamine neurons express Oxtr and respond to oxytocin during social reward.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: FDR was 0.0805, only 24 perturbed cells were available, and the dataset cell class is not a nucleus-resolved VTA label.

summary: Oxtr perturbation did not transcriptionally regulate nearby G-protein, PLC/IP3, PKC, or arrestin signaling genes in the candidate-responsive classes.
why_it_matters: Canonical OXTR activity is dominated by acute second-messenger signaling, so an scRNA-seq perturbation may miss receptor function even when physiology is strong.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The analysis tested transcript abundance of pathway components, not ligand-evoked calcium, IP3, PKC activity, ion-channel state, or receptor desensitization.

summary: Smarcc1 perturbation showed weak target-transcript engagement and an almost null genome-wide response across measured neuron classes.
why_it_matters: The screen result should be interpreted as an under-engaged or buffered Smarcc1 loss-of-function experiment rather than as evidence that SMARCC1 is unnecessary for SWI/SNF biology.
main_caveats: No raw guide identities or protein measurements are available; mRNA non-depletion could reflect guide inefficiency, low transcript detection, long-lived protein, or true buffering.

summary: The only FDR-significant Smarcc1 downstream gene was an isolated Srpk1 increase in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This makes Srpk1 a narrow candidate readout for follow-up, but the lack of recurrence or pathway support prevents broad interpretation of a Smarcc1 program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene signal; Smarcc1 itself was not FDR-significantly depleted in this cell type; no independent replication in the table.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Smarcc1 failed to induce the strong BAF-sensitive Ptpn3/Reep2/Prkcd/Tiam1 module seen after Smarcc2 and Smarcb1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The contrast prevents assigning the 151 TH BAF module to every core SWI/SNF subunit and highlights Smarcc1 as a non-phenocopy within a cell type where the assay could detect BAF biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The biological divergence cannot be separated from the absent Smarcc1 mRNA knockdown in this cell type.

summary: The SMARCC paralog Smarcc2 was far more engaged and far more phenotypic than Smarcc1 in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: Paralogy and physical interaction do not justify treating the Smarcc1 guide set as a proxy for SMARCC-dimer loss; Smarcc2 is the positive paralogous benchmark in this screen.
main_caveats: Smarcc2 had better target-transcript knockdown, so the contrast is not a clean test of SMARCC1 versus SMARCC2 protein function.

summary: Smarcc1 had no strong positive or negative perturbation-signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak Smarcc1 signature should not be used to infer convergence with unrelated target programs or to nominate pathway neighbors from full-transcriptome correlations.
main_caveats: Correlations were calculated on Wilcoxon score vectors, not raw expression or protein phenotypes.

summary: This mature-neuron screen was essentially uninformative for SMARCC1-associated developmental dysgenesis rather than contradictory to a neural-progenitor disease mechanism.
why_it_matters: Human SMARCC1 disease alleles perturb fetal neural development; the present mouse neuron data lacked both a progenitor cell context and convincing Smarcc1 engagement, so disease follow-up should use stronger depletion in relevant progenitors.
main_caveats: The dataset does not test human fetal ventricular progenitors, aqueduct development, or structural hydrocephalus phenotypes.

summary: Sorbs1 perturbation produced a reproducible but weak target-transcript decrease rather than FDR-confirmed knockdown in the profiled neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: All downstream interpretations must be limited by target engagement: the guide behavior suggests partial transcript lowering, not a saturated Sorbs1 loss-of-function state.
cell_types: 22 Sorbs1-profiled neuronal classes|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Target mRNA, not SORBS1 protein, was assayed; every Sorbs1 self-row had FDR=1.0 despite a negative median logFC.

summary: The Sorbs1 transcriptional phenotype was globally buffered: no cell type had any gene with FDR<=0.20 and nominal hits were not reproducible across cell types.
why_it_matters: SORBS1/CAP has documented roles in insulin-linked trafficking and adhesion signaling, but those scaffold functions did not become a detectable steady-state mRNA program in these neuronal Perturb-seq profiles.
cell_types: 22 Sorbs1-profiled neuronal classes
main_caveats: The buffered-response interpretation is confounded by weak transcript knockdown and by the fact that scRNA-seq will miss acute protein relocalization, phosphorylation, and focal-adhesion turnover.

summary: Sorbs1 did not phenocopy available perturbations from the CAP/CBL/Rho/adhesion neighborhood, and core SORBS1 partner transcripts were not robustly regulated.
why_it_matters: A gene-by-gene search could have linked Sorbs1 to adhesion or synaptic-adaptor perturbations, but the observed signatures were essentially orthogonal, arguing against a coherent transcriptional CAP-adhesion module in this screen.
cell_types: 22 Sorbs1-profiled neuronal classes
main_caveats: The closest biochemical nodes Cbl, Flot1, Vcl, Pxn, Tln1, Afdn, Sorbs2, and Sorbs3 were not present as perturbation targets, and Sorbs1 engagement itself was weak.

summary: The screen mainly tests neuronal Sorbs1 biology and therefore does not exclude SORBS1 functions in astrocytes or peripheral adhesion/metabolic tissues.
why_it_matters: This cell-context boundary prevents over-interpreting a negative Glut/GABA neuronal transcriptome as evidence against published CAP functions in insulin-responsive or focal-adhesion-rich cells.
comparators: human astrocyte-enriched single-nucleus brain signal|adipocyte and fibroblast adhesion models
cell_types: 22 Sorbs1-profiled neuronal classes
main_caveats: The Human Protein Atlas context is human expression, not matched mouse Perturb-seq; the dataset also lacks a direct measurement of endogenous Sorbs1 abundance by cell type.

summary: Basal Tlr4 perturbation was transcriptionally silent across the 20 assayed Glut/GABA cell-type labels.
why_it_matters: A canonical innate immune receptor produced neither measurable Tlr4 transcript knockdown nor an FDR-supported downstream module in these neuronal contexts, making a strong positive TLR4 program unlikely in the unstimulated dataset.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The negative result may reflect sparse Tlr4 expression or missing ligand/co-receptor state rather than an efficient knockdown of an active receptor.

summary: The most responsive Tlr4 cell types contained only isolated subthreshold genes, with Cops7b up in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and Ctsl down in 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut.
why_it_matters: These rows bound the strongest apparent effects but argue against a robust cell-type-selective program because neither nominal hit survived FDR correction and no broader module accompanied them.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Both genes are FDR-negative; the finding is a negative interpretation of the strongest scalar hits, not validation of Cops7b or Ctsl as Tlr4 effectors.

summary: Available TLR-family and downstream NF-kappa-B-neighbor perturbations failed to converge with Tlr4, and whole-library signature neighbors were very weak.
why_it_matters: Known TLR4 biology predicts a CD14/MD-2/adaptor network under LPS stimulation; lack of convergence among available pathway perturbations shows that this network is not active as a shared basal neuronal transcriptional module.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to perturbations present in the parquet; Ly96, Myd88, Ticam1, Tirap, and Traf6 were absent as direct perturbation targets.

summary: The CNS TLR4 inflammatory disease axis is not reproduced by unstimulated Tlr4 perturbation in the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The result shifts interpretation from broad cell-autonomous neuronal Tlr4 activity toward ligand-driven microglial or injury-state biology when relating this screen to neuroinflammation.
cell_types: Tlr4-assayed Glut/GABA neuronal panel
main_caveats: The dataset lacks an explicit LPS, DAMP, infection, ischemia, or microglial stimulation context.

summary: TLR4/MD-2 is pharmacologically targetable, but the dataset does not support broad direct basal neuronal response biomarkers for Tlr4 blockade.
why_it_matters: Clinical TLR4 antagonism aims at ligand-driven cytokine signaling; a silent neuronal Perturb-seq signature means efficacy or safety biomarkers should be sought in stimulated innate compartments rather than in the basal Glut/GABA rows analyzed here.
cell_types: Tlr4-assayed Glut/GABA neuronal panel
main_caveats: CRISPR perturbation of an unexpressed receptor is not equivalent to acute pharmacologic antagonism of a ligated MD-2/TLR4 complex.

summary: Stag2 produced FDR-corrected downstream differential expression only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut among the 22 measured Stag2 cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: The biology should be interpreted as a specific neuronal-state vulnerability rather than a uniform mouse-brain consequence of Stag2 perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Stag2 self-transcript down-regulation was nominal and not FDR-corrected, so cell-type selectivity could combine biology with variable perturbation efficiency.

summary: The corrected Stag2 program in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is enriched for neuronal projection, synapse, and cell-junction genes.
why_it_matters: It nominates neuronal adhesion and projection-gene regulation as the dominant transcriptomic consequence of Stag2 loss in the responsive brain cell class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The pathway assignment comes from enrichment of 37 genes and does not measure synapses or projections directly.

summary: Smc1a, Smc3, and Nipbl phenocopied the Stag2 top-gene signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, whereas Stag1 and Pds5a did not.
why_it_matters: The contrast preserves a complex-member result: the Stag2 response follows the core cohesin/loader axis more than the Stag1 paralog or Pds5a in this neuronal cell type.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Signature correlations were computed over the Stag2 top 200 genes only, and Stag1/Pds5a target engagement was weak at the transcript level.

summary: Several Stag2 contrasts had nominally lower Stag2 RNA but no FDR-corrected downstream genes.
why_it_matters: These nulls argue against treating every nominal Stag2 self-decrease as a sufficient driver of the 151 TH Prkcd program.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The target transcript did not pass FDR correction, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 20 perturbed cells.

summary: The robust mouse-brain Stag2 response points to synaptic and neuronal-projection genes rather than to a directly mitotic cohesin program.
why_it_matters: Human STAG2 variants cause neurodevelopmental cohesinopathy; this dataset proposes a concrete neuronal downstream module in a Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic population.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain Perturb-seq rather than a human congenital STAG2 model, and the parquet contains RNA only.

summary: Nipbl and Stag2 shared many down-regulated adhesion genes but drove Gabra1 and Brinp1 in opposite directions.
why_it_matters: These two genes warn that a NIPBL perturbation should not be used as a simple directional substitute for Stag2 at every synaptic locus.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The direction split is gene-level and was not validated by protein or chromatin assays.

main_caveats: The Nfs1 self-row did not pass FDR 0.05, and target protein depletion was not measured.

direction: Hspa9 stress genes up; Nfs1 lacks the program
summary: Hspa9, but not Nfs1, drove a recurrent Shmt2/Cyb5r1/Chac1 mitochondrial-stress signature in shared cell types.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the dataset can resolve a mitochondrial stress state and that the weak Nfs1 perturbation is not interchangeable with perturbing the downstream HSPA9 ISC chaperone.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: HSPA9 has broader mitochondrial chaperone functions than NFS1, and Hspa9 perturbation was much stronger transcriptionally.

direction: no meaningful positive or negative convergence
summary: Direct and indirect Fe-S pathway perturbations, including Lyrm4, did not converge with Nfs1 score signatures; global top neighbors were also negligible.
why_it_matters: The result argues against rescuing the weak Nfs1 interpretation by borrowing signatures from complex partners or nearby iron-handling genes.
main_caveats: Correlations use RNA score signatures, and Lyrm4 itself was weakly perturbed.

summary: Nfs1 partial loss did not activate canonical iron-starvation, ATF4, or ferroptosis-adjacent markers in neurons.
why_it_matters: Cancer studies motivate NFS1 inhibition as a ferroptosis-sensitizing strategy, but this brain dataset neither reproduces that state nor tests strong systemic inhibition; the absence of a stress signature is therefore a context-specific negative, not a safety signal.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Published ferroptosis work used high-oxygen cancer contexts and stronger NFS1 suppression than achieved here.

summary: Zbtb21-targeting guides did not deplete the measured Zbtb21 transcript in any of the 21 cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: Without target-RNA depletion, downstream nominal genes should be interpreted as guide-associated signatures rather than validated Zbtb21 loss-of-function biology.
main_caveats: RNA abundance is an imperfect readout for perturbation modalities that disrupt DNA while leaving mutant transcripts stable, but the data do not show target RNA loss.

summary: The Zbtb21 perturbation had no FDR-significant downstream transcriptomic response in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: A transcriptional repressor perturbation with no corrected DE genes is a strong constraint on mechanistic interpretation and suggests either ineffective engagement, strong buffering, or insufficient power.
main_caveats: The result cannot distinguish genuine biological buffering from failed target engagement or modest cell counts.

summary: Ralgapa1 was the only recurrent nominally up-regulated transcript, ranking near the top of eight Zbtb21 cell-type signatures.
why_it_matters: If Zbtb21 is re-perturbed with stronger guides, Ralgapa1 is a candidate transcriptional readout to check across cortical, thalamic/midbrain, and hypothalamic classes.
