main_caveats: The canonical genes may be expressed in rare PVN/SON subtypes that are not resolved in the broad cell-class labels; all target and marker transcript tests were weak.

summary: Sim1 did not converge with its expected ARNT2 partner, while Bmal1 and Clock showed robust signatures in the same matrix.
why_it_matters: Loss of Sim1-Arnt2 convergence warns against inferring the published SIM1/ARNT2 developmental complex from this dataset, but the Bmal1/Clock comparator shows that robust transcription-factor phenotypes were recoverable elsewhere.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Sim1-Arnt2 comparison is between two weak perturbations, so it is a warning against claiming convergence rather than proof of biological opposition.

summary: Pdp1 down-regulation in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA is the only Sim1 result below FDR 0.20.
why_it_matters: If this target is followed up experimentally, Pdp1 in this GABAergic hypothalamic-region class is the only transcript-level hint in the DE table, but it is isolated and does not meet conventional FDR thresholds.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: FDR was 0.148, no other gene in the cell class reached FDR<0.20, and no direct SIM1-Pdp1 mechanism was established.

summary: Current Sim1, Arnt2, Mc4r, Agrp, and Lepr perturbation signatures do not provide a robust Perturb-seq direction for SIM1-linked obesity biology or a direct druggability route.
why_it_matters: SIM1 loss of function is disease-relevant, but these transcriptional data are too weak for ranking an agonist-versus-antagonist strategy or for nominating a direct SIM1 ligand program.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The warning is about this dataset and current target annotations; it does not exclude indirect modulation of SIM1-lineage circuits or successful perturbation in a PVN-enriched assay.

summary: Sptb perturbation left a recurrent weak downward trace on the Sptb transcript but no FDR-significant downstream gene in any tested cell type.
why_it_matters: The main interpretable result is a buffered or weakly engaged transcriptional phenotype, which fits a membrane-cytoskeleton scaffold better than a target expected to drive broad mRNA remodeling.
main_caveats: No per-cell-type Sptb row passed FDR; transcript counts do not measure βIΣ2 protein abundance or localization.

summary: Nominal Sptb self-target depletion only partially overlapped the anatomic pattern reported for βIΣ2 spectrin.
why_it_matters: Known protein enrichment in CA1/dentate, layer-2 cortex, medial habenula, ventral thalamus and cerebellar granule neurons does not translate into uniformly detectable Sptb mRNA knockdown in the broad Perturb-seq cell classes.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type labels are not one-to-one matches for the protein-localization regions; all self-target effects were nominal only.

summary: Sptb did not converge with Sptan1, ankyrin, adducin or Epb41l1 perturbation signatures, and was much weaker than Sptan1 or Ank3 in a matched thalamic glutamatergic class.
why_it_matters: The spectrin/ankyrin cytoskeleton cannot be treated as a single interchangeable transcriptomic module in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Signature correlations compare weak Sptb vectors; divergence could reflect weaker guide activity as well as biology.

summary: Pvalb GABA cells had a plausible AnkR/β1-spectrin scaffold but no FDR-significant Sptb response.
why_it_matters: A structural interneuron phenotype involving AnkR, Kv3.1b and perineuronal nets may be invisible to bulk gene-level scRNA DE, so absence of broad mRNA changes should not be read as absence of β1-spectrin function.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Ank1 perturbation also produced only a target-level FDR signal in this cell type; electrophysiology and PNN phenotypes were not assayed.

summary: Sptb perturbation did not produce FDR-level mRNA compensation by measured spectrin, ankyrin, adducin or protein-4.1 family members.
why_it_matters: The dataset provides no transcriptomic evidence for replacement by nearby membrane-cytoskeleton genes, consistent with compensation being incomplete or post-transcriptional.
main_caveats: Sptbn4 was not measured; protein relocalization and isoform-specific compensation were not tested.

summary: Raf1 up and Gabra2 down in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA were the top nominal Sptb-associated readouts but remained exploratory.
why_it_matters: This pair marks the strongest individual Sptb panel for follow-up while making clear that it is not a corrected or target-engaged pathway call.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: FDR values were 0.163 or larger and Sptb itself was not nominally depleted in this cell class.

summary: Safe_target_62 behaved as an inert synthetic control: it had no measured endogenous target-transcript row and produced no FDR-significant genes in any of 12 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: The result supports using this guide as part of the null distribution for this dataset, while also showing that it should not be assigned a mouse gene mechanism.
main_caveats: The DE table lacks guide sequence, genomic cut-site annotation, raw target-site editing, and expression counts.

summary: The largest Safe_target_62 nominal rows were isolated cell-type outliers rather than a reproducible neuronal response.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Grin1, Inha, and Ube2v2 can look striking before correction, but their FDR values and lack of recurrence argue against interpreting them as Safe_target_62 biology.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: This is a statement about recurrence and FDR within the Wilcoxon output, not about raw expression kinetics.

summary: No sampled brain cell class showed a corrected downstream Safe_target_62 response, including the best-powered 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class.
why_it_matters: The null is not solely driven by one tiny stratum: the cell with 73 matched perturbed cells still had no FDR hit, although several 20-25-cell classes remain underpowered.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Matched perturbed-cell counts are modest throughout, so subtle effects below the Wilcoxon/FDR detection boundary could be missed.

summary: Restricted signature neighbors were detectable but weak and localized, with the strongest 200-gene Safe_target_62 tail alignment in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: The 008 alignments to Pax6/Egr2-like positive neighbors and Zfp961/Irf9-like negative neighbors flag a QC-sensitive cell class, but they do not establish whole-transcriptome convergence.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations used the 200 largest Safe_target_62 rows in each cell type, which enriches nominal noise and is not an unbiased transcriptome-wide similarity estimate.

summary: The realized Sacs perturbation produced no FDR-significant single-gene response in any of 20 assayed cell-type strata.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant result: Sacs should be treated as transcriptionally silent or under-engaged in this screen rather than as a strong acute regulator of any sampled neuronal transcriptome.
main_caveats: The target transcript showed weak depletion, so the null is a null for the achieved perturbation rather than proof that complete Sacs loss is inert.

summary: The broad cerebellar 308 CB GABA stratum did not show Sacs transcript depletion or a downstream signature, despite the cerebellar vulnerability reported in ARSACS models.
why_it_matters: The local dataset does not recapitulate chronic Purkinje-cell degeneration or neurofilament pathology; it is more consistent with those phenotypes requiring stronger, cell-subtype-resolved or longer sacsin loss.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only 45 perturbed 308 CB GABA cells were assayed, and the broad class need not equal the Purkinje-cell population most affected in ARSACS.

summary: Sacs did not phenocopy Hsp70/proteostasis or ataxin-1-neighbor perturbations at the transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: Sacsin is annotated and experimentally supported as an Hsp70/proteasome-linked co-chaperone, but acute Sacs guides did not drive an Hspa8, Hsp90ab1, Hspa9, Hsf1, Stub1, Vcp or Atxn1-like program in the same cell types.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and score-correlation based; sacsin could modulate client folding post-transcriptionally without changing chaperone mRNAs.

summary: The Sacs signature did not converge with mitochondrial fission or fusion perturbations even though SACS loss has been linked to Drp1 recruitment and mitochondrial dysfunction.
why_it_matters: The screen separates the chronic Drp1/mitochondrial-quality-control phenotype from an acute nuclear RNA signature: Dnm1l and Opa1 perturbations can be read out in the dataset, but Sacs did not align with them.
main_caveats: Prior transcriptomic evidence came largely from knockdown cells and patient fibroblasts; the Perturb-seq cells, species and time scale are different and the Sacs transcript was weakly reduced.

summary: Known sacsin neurofilament/intermediate-filament biology was not mirrored by Nef, tubulin, Map1b or Kif5a-like acute signatures.
why_it_matters: Sacs-null neurons accumulate abnormal neurofilament bundles, but that apparent cytoskeletal homeostasis defect is not a simple transcriptional reduction of neurofilament or microtubule genes in this assay.
main_caveats: Intermediate-filament bundling is a structural phenotype; single-cell RNA is an indirect and possibly insensitive readout.

summary: Smarca2 mRNA knockdown is FDR-significant only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, even though the target transcript is measured in all 22 Smarca2 comparisons.
why_it_matters: The interpretable on-target perturbation is concentrated in two glutamatergic classes; most cell types have either weak or only nominal target-transcript evidence.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Target engagement is inferred from Smarca2 mRNA, not protein or chromatin occupancy.

summary: The two cell types with the strongest Smarca2 mRNA depletion show almost no FDR-level downstream transcriptome: Smarca2 itself is the only FDR hit in both 151 TH and 155 MB.
why_it_matters: A catalytic SWI/SNF ATPase can be detectably repressed without a broad acute expression collapse in these mouse brain cell classes, suggesting buffering of partial Smarca2 loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation is partial and transcriptomic; rare enhancers or chromatin-accessibility effects could be missed.

summary: Smarca2 does not phenocopy several mSWI/SNF members in 151 TH: Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Arid2, Arid1a, and Smarce1 produce 11 to 286 FDR-significant genes, while Smarca2 produces only itself.
why_it_matters: The complex-level expectation that SWI/SNF subunits act together is refined by a brain cell type in which core or signature subunits are much less buffered than the Smarca2 ATPase.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Cell counts differ across perturbations; Smarca4 itself was weakly engaged, making the direct SMARCA2-SMARCA4 paralog comparison underpowered.

summary: Five additional cell classes show nominally lower Smarca2 but zero FDR-significant genes, extending the buffered-response pattern beyond the two FDR-engaged glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: Large conventional scores are not hidden in these cell types; nominal Smarca2 depletion in thalamic, hypothalamic, cortical, and Pvalb GABA contexts failed to produce an FDR-level expression program.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Smarca2 itself did not pass FDR in these five comparisons; each had only 59 to 120 perturbed cells.

summary: The dataset is a poor stand-in for Nicolaides-Baraitser syndrome: partial Smarca2 mRNA repression is buffered, whereas the human syndrome is driven by heterozygous ATPase-motif missense variants.
why_it_matters: Failure to see a broad gene-expression phenotype after knockdown should not be read as evidence that SMARCA2 disease alleles are benign; dominant catalytic variants may perturb SWI/SNF differently from simple loss of transcript.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No patient variants, developmental time course, or protein-level ATPase measurements were assayed.

summary: Ppfia2 is the only FDR-significant non-Smarca2 gene in the entire Smarca2 table, but it occurs in CA3/CA2-FC/DG cells where Smarca2 itself is not measurably depleted.
why_it_matters: This preserves the isolated strongest off-target transcriptional event while flagging that it is decoupled from measured target engagement and should not anchor a SMARCA2 mechanism on its own.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Only 60 perturbed cells were available and the Smarca2 target row was nonsignificant in the same comparison.

summary: Normal mouse brain cell classes tolerate partial Smarca2 transcript depletion at the level of scRNA-seq differential expression, but this cannot be extrapolated to near-complete SMARCA2 degradation or to SMARCA4-deficient tumor cells.
why_it_matters: SMARCA2 is being pursued through the SMARCA4-mutant synthetic-lethal strategy; the brain data are reassuring for partial loss yet warn that disease and oncology settings are paralog- and dose-dependent.
main_caveats: The dataset does not include SMARCA4-deficient cells, small-molecule degradation, chronic dosing, or safety endpoints.

summary: Smad9 perturbation produced no FDR-significant target knockdown or transcriptome-wide differential expression in any of the 23 measured cell-type signatures.
why_it_matters: This makes failed or weak Smad9 engagement the first-order interpretation for the perturbation and prevents over-calling downstream pathway absence as true SMAD9 loss of function.
main_caveats: The inference is strong for the measured mRNA readout but cannot exclude unmeasured protein depletion, altered phospho-SMAD9, or effects in unsampled non-neuronal cells.

summary: Smad9 perturbation did not alter canonical BMP/TGF response genes Id1, Id2, Id3, Bambi, or Smad7 at nominal or FDR-supported levels.
why_it_matters: These genes are expected sentinels of BMP-SMAD transcription, so their silence shows that the Smad9 perturbation did not engage a recognizable canonical BMP program in the neuronal panel.
main_caveats: The negative marker response is pathway-specific but remains confounded by the absent FDR-level decrease of Smad9 itself.

summary: Assayed BMP/TGF-beta neighbors, especially Bmpr2, generated stronger effects than Smad9 and Smad9 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with receptors or other SMAD perturbations.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating all members of the BMP receptor-SMAD module as interchangeable in this neuronal Perturb-seq assay.
main_caveats: Related-target divergence may be driven by guide efficacy and on-target knockdown differences; Smad5 and Smad7 perturbations were not available as gene-target comparators.

summary: The absence of a neuronal Smad9 transcriptional phenotype is compatible with SMAD9 disease biology being vascular, endothelial/glial, or noncanonical rather than a broad acute neuronal program.
why_it_matters: SMAD9 is linked to pulmonary arterial hypertension through BMP signaling and microRNA processing, but this mouse-brain neuronal screen should not be used as a negative test of those disease mechanisms or of vascular therapeutic hypotheses.
comparators: human brain endothelial/glial expression|pulmonary arterial endothelial and smooth-muscle PAH models
main_caveats: The expression comparison is between human atlas data and a mouse Perturb-seq dataset, and PAH vascular cells were not assayed.

summary: All-library signature matching did not reveal a stable Smad9 module; only 308 CB GABA had modest Smad9-correlated neighbors, and that signature lacked Smad9 target engagement.
why_it_matters: This prevents biologically interpreting the top nominal genes or the 308 CB GABA correlations as a hidden strong SMAD9 program.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to a weak Smad9 signature with minimum FDR 0.840 in 308 CB GABA; correlations are modest and not evidence of mechanistic interaction.

summary: Safe_target_77 behaves as an inert safe-targeting perturbation across all assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: A genome-wide absence of FDR-supported DE is the expected biological result for a negative-control guide and argues against a guide-specific off-target program.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Safe_target_77 has no endogenous target transcript in the DE rows, and perturbed-cell counts are small, so this rules out large transcriptome-wide effects rather than tiny effects.

summary: The strongest apparent cell-type-specific responses are isolated nominal outliers, not FDR-supported Safe_target_77 biology.
why_it_matters: The lowest-p genes point to different single genes in NP-CT/L6b/OB glutamatergic, hindbrain GABA, and thalamic glutamatergic classes; preserving their failed FDR status prevents one-off nominal genes from being promoted into pathways.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: These are nominal Wilcoxon leads with FDR values from 0.233 to 0.890 and should be treated as examples of the null tail.

summary: Safe_target_77 lacks a recurrent cross-cell-type gene module.
why_it_matters: A reproducible off-target or stress response would be expected to recur across cell classes; the nominal tail was sparse, and even Ube2z only recurred at p < 0.01 in three cell classes.
main_caveats: The recurrence scan used nominal thresholds because no gene survived FDR correction.

summary: Safe_target_77 is not an empirical outlier among nearby safe-targeting guide controls.
why_it_matters: Adjacent Safe_target controls occasionally produced FDR hits, so empirical QC of negative guides remains useful; Safe_target_77 itself had no FDR < 0.05 event across the sampled safe-control neighborhood.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison covers the Safe_target labels that co-occurred with Safe_target_77 in the same source row groups, not every safe-targeting control in the entire 10 GB parquet.

summary: Rapgef4 perturbation was globally buffered at the steady-state RNA level across the 22 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: EPAC2 is a cAMP-regulated Rap GEF, so a strong scRNA program might have been expected for some neuronal contexts; its absence suggests that acute Rapgef4 loss is either weakly engaged or primarily affects post-transcriptional synaptic signaling in this dataset.
main_caveats: All Rapgef4 target-transcript rows were FDR=1.0, and partial transcript knockdown could miss protein-level EPAC2 function.

summary: Measured Rapgef4 target-transcript depletion was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, but neither class converted that depletion into FDR-supported downstream genes.
why_it_matters: These two classes are the best places in this dataset to look for cell-autonomous Rapgef4 RNA effects; their silence argues against a broad transcriptional program even where nominal target engagement was most visible.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The cell-type restriction is based on nominal p values for the target transcript, not FDR-significant target knockdown.

summary: Rap1gap down-regulation in 046 CTX-CGE GABA is a candidate compensatory Rap-cycle response to Rapgef4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: A decrease in a Rap GTPase-activating protein would be directionally consistent with buffering reduced Rap GEF activity, making Rap1gap the most mechanistically aligned nominal biomarker in the screen.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Rap1gap did not pass FDR correction and the Rapgef4 transcript itself was only weakly reduced in CTX-CGE GABA.

summary: Known cortical spine and autism-related EPAC2 biology did not manifest as a strong cortical or Pvalb mRNA signature after Rapgef4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Prior Rapgef4 studies emphasize synaptic structure, AMPA-receptor trafficking, and mouse social phenotypes; the Perturb-seq result warns that those disease mechanisms may require synaptic readouts or stronger genetic loss rather than resting transcriptomics.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq cell classes and conditions are not the same as in utero electroporation, knockout mice, or cultured-neuron spine assays.

summary: Rapgef4 was not interchangeable with nearby cAMP/Rap perturbations: Pde10a produced an FDR-supported CNU-LGE response while Rapgef4 and Rapgef2 remained largely buffered.
why_it_matters: This contrast separates a detectable PDE10A-linked cAMP transcriptional response from the EPAC/Rap GEF branch in the same broad dataset and discourages treating all cAMP nodes as equivalent perturbations.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Pde10a had direct FDR-supported target knockdown in CNU-LGE whereas Rapgef4 did not, so the difference may reflect engagement and expression as much as pathway wiring.

summary: A restricted signature-neighbor search did not identify a recurrent high-confidence Rapgef4-like perturbation.
why_it_matters: The absence of a repeated positive or negative neighbor prevents over-interpreting isolated similarities to individual GPCR, cAMP, or synaptic genes.
main_caveats: The scan used only the 100 strongest Rapgef4 genes per cell type and should be viewed as a triage calculation rather than a full latent-space perturbation map.

summary: Stt3b on-target mRNA depletion was directionally reproduced in every measured cell type but reached FDR significance only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: This separates genuine guide activity from the much narrower subset with statistically secure target engagement for downstream interpretation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: FDR support may reflect power and variance as well as biology; perturbed matched-cell counts were small in several cell types.

summary: The two FDR-supported Stt3b perturbations were target-only transcriptomic events with no non-target gene surviving whole-transcriptome correction.
why_it_matters: STT3B is a core ER N-glycosylation catalyst, so a nearly target-only RNA output implies strong buffering or a primary phenotype outside steady-state mRNA.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Transcriptomics cannot exclude protein, OST-complex, or glycopeptide-occupancy phenotypes.

summary: Canonical unfolded-protein-response and ER-stress marker transcripts were not FDR-induced after significant Stt3b depletion.
why_it_matters: STT3B participates in OST-B-dependent glycosylation and secretory-protein quality control, but the mouse brain response does not look like a strong bulk UPR transcriptional state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only selected RNA markers were inspected; Xbp1 splicing, client glycosylation, and acute protein stress were not measured.

summary: The Perturb-seq phenotype refines STT3B-CDG by showing that acute partial Stt3b knockdown in differentiated mouse brain cells can lack a broad corrective or stress transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Human STT3B disease may be driven by glycoprotein-site occupancy, developmental timing, or substrate-specific proteostasis rather than a universal cell-autonomous stress mRNA signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Mouse acute CRISPRi-like transcript depletion is not equivalent to inherited human biallelic developmental STT3B hypofunction.

summary: No interpretable N-glycosylation pathway-neighbor or global signature-neighbor convergence with Stt3b was detected.
why_it_matters: The absence of convergence should not be overread as pathway divergence because Dpm1 was weakly engaged and core OST subunits were not available as direct comparators.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to available gene targets and Pearson score correlations; Dpm1 itself lacked FDR-level target knockdown.

summary: Sparse STT3B ligand records plus disease genetics make the muted RNA phenotype an inadequate safety readout for STT3B inhibition.
why_it_matters: Negative modulation of a human OST-B catalytic subunit could perturb N-glycosylation even when a mouse brain transcriptomic screen shows few downstream FDR genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset did not test small molecules, dose response, chronic exposure, or glycosylation toxicity.

summary: Prox1 guide-associated differential expression was sharply restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: A Prox1 perturbation in this mouse-brain screen should be interpreted as a narrow thalamic neuronal response rather than a pan-neuronal or pan-glutamatergic phenotype.
comparators: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cell counts differ across strata, and zero FDR hits do not prove biological absence in rare subtypes nested inside broad cell labels.

summary: The measured Prox1 transcript increased in the only significant context.
why_it_matters: Because the target mRNA moved upward, the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature is not a straightforward Prox1 loss-of-function signature and should not be read as equivalent to Prox1 deletion phenotypes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset reports transcript-level differential expression rather than edited allele state, guide efficiency, or Prox1 protein abundance.

summary: The thalamic response was positive-skewed and marked by Vgf, Tafa4, Hrh2, Vipr2, Adora1, Prkcd, Calb1, and Mef2c induction with a compact Rreb1/Kcnd2-centered negative arm.
why_it_matters: These genes provide a compact biomarker panel for the measured response and point to a neuronal state shift rather than a generic stress or endothelial fate program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a gene-level module label from the DE signature; no external pathway enrichment was needed to establish the direction of these measured genes.

summary: Canonical lymphatic PROX1/COUP-TFII/VEGFR3 markers did not move with Prox1 in the thalamic neuronal signature.
why_it_matters: The result separates the neuronal Prox1 perturbation state from the best-known PROX1 program in lymphatic endothelial specification and argues against interpreting the response as ectopic lymphatic fate activation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only transcripts present in the DE table could be checked, and lack of lymphatic-marker induction in neurons does not test lymphatic endothelial biology directly.

summary: Broad hippocampal/dentate glutamatergic classes did not recapitulate the canonical Prox1 dentate-granule literature.
why_it_matters: Although mouse studies place Prox1 at the center of dentate granule maturation and identity, the assayed MEA/LA/CA1/DG and CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic aggregates lacked significant target engagement or downstream hits.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The relevant Prox1-positive dentate granule cells may be diluted within broad atlas classes, and both DG-labeled contexts had about 60 matched perturbed cells.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor correlations did not identify a robust full-transcriptome Prox1 surrogate, and Prox2 was absent from the queried panel slice.
why_it_matters: The empirical Prox1 state appears more idiosyncratic than interchangeable with any close 50-gene neighbor tested here; positive and negative restricted neighbors lost most of their similarity when evaluated over the full measured transcriptome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor ranks were computed on the 50 Prox1 FDR genes, so they are intentionally signature-restricted and should be treated as a diagnostic contrast rather than a mechanistic network.

summary: Kpna3 perturbation produced consistent but FDR-weak target-transcript reduction across 21 neuronal subclasses with almost no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: A housekeeping nuclear-import adaptor can be partially reduced without an acute, broad cell-autonomous mRNA collapse in this assay, suggesting buffering or insufficient knockdown should be assumed before pathway-level interpretation.
main_caveats: The Kpna3 target row itself did not reach FDR<0.05; mRNA does not measure importin-alpha cargo localization or protein transport.

summary: Txnl4a up-regulation in CNU-MGE GABA was the only FDR-significant Kpna3 downstream event.
why_it_matters: The result prioritizes one interneuron-class candidate but, because no other cell type recapitulated it and the comparison used 26 perturbed cells, it should be treated as exploratory rather than a shared Kpna3 module.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Low perturbed-cell count; Kpna3 reduction in the same cell type was only nominal and FDR=1.0.

summary: The two best-powered Kpna3 contexts, MB Glut and TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, showed the strongest nominal Kpna3 repression but no FDR-significant non-target genes.
why_it_matters: This separates true buffered transcriptomes from purely underpowered contexts: even with 94-120 perturbed cells, Kpna3 loss did not trigger a robust DE program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Target-transcript FDR was 0.138-0.170, so the evidence is nominal rather than a confirmed knockout-like state.

summary: Kpna3 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with the available Ran/karyopherin neighbors Ranbp2 and Xpo1.
why_it_matters: Even perturbations in the same nucleocytoplasmic-transport neighborhood do not collapse onto a generic nuclear-transport expression state in this mouse-brain screen.
main_caveats: RANBP2 and XPO1 are pathway neighbors rather than Kpna3 paralogs; Xpo1 perturbation target transcript often changed upward, so the contrast is transcriptomic rather than a clean matched loss-of-function comparison.

summary: Whole-signature search found no strong positive or inverse Kpna3 phenocopy among 1511-2042 assayed perturbations per Kpna3 cell type.
why_it_matters: The weak Kpna3 result is not explained by hiding under a higher-scoring perturbation from an unrelated target; no disease or safe-target neighbor showed a convincing shared vector.
main_caveats: The comparison used score-vector Pearson correlations; very weak or non-transcriptional biology could evade this metric.

summary: The disease literature does not justify reading Kpna3 transcript knockdown as a therapeutic phenocopy of KPNA3 missense disease, and the dataset shows little transcriptional leverage from partial Kpna3 reduction.
why_it_matters: SPG88 variants perturb importin-alpha-4 protein behavior, while no clinical KPNA3-directed mechanism is established; bulk inhibition or degradation would need protein-transport and disease-allele assays before being considered mechanistically aligned.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is mouse, acute, and transcriptional; the cited disease variants are human dominant missense alleles.

direction: nominal target knockdown with no FDR-supported downstream genes
summary: Zkscan1 loss produced no FDR-supported downstream transcriptome in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: For a nuclear KRAB/SCAN C2H2 transcription factor, the dataset argues against an acute, broad cell-state program after this perturbation and turns the main result into a buffered or ineffective-response interpretation rather than a pathway activation call.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR hits could reflect weak editing or low target expression; the dataset has RNA readout only and no protein depletion measurement.

summary: The clearest nominal target-transcript depletion was restricted to 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 308 CB GABA.
why_it_matters: Databases describe Zkscan1/ZKSCAN1 as broadly expressed in nervous and brain tissue, but in this Perturb-seq screen the a priori self-gene response was most evident in a small posterior/limbic subset, directing any validation effort to those classes.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The self-gene p values are nominal and did not survive whole-transcriptome adjustment; the apparent restriction may partly reflect guide performance rather than biology.

summary: Nominal outlier genes did not recur across cell types, leaving no candidate non-target biomarker or pathway marker for Zkscan1 loss.
why_it_matters: Genes such as Abhd17a, Rsu1, Ptdss2, and Pak3 should be treated as isolated weak observations rather than as a Zkscan1 response module.
main_caveats: This conclusion is limited to the measured genes and cell types; it does not exclude non-transcriptional effects.

summary: Assayed ZKSCAN-family perturbations were not interchangeable: Zkscan1 signatures were essentially orthogonal to Zkscan3 and Zkscan16 signatures.
why_it_matters: Zkscan1, Zkscan3, and Zkscan16 share a KRAB/SCAN zinc-finger architecture, and the SCAN domain can support selective oligomerization, but the mouse-brain data do not support a shared neuronal program for these family members.
main_caveats: Zkscan3 and Zkscan16 were themselves weak perturbations, so lack of convergence cannot prove biochemical independence.

summary: Genome-wide signature matching did not reveal a strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor for Zkscan1.
why_it_matters: The absence of a robust neighbor means Zkscan1 cannot be placed into another target program from this screen; the modest Wdr26/Ranbp2 correlations in 308 CB GABA are hypotheses, not pathway evidence.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlation values were computed from weak Zkscan1 signatures and can be driven by technical or low-cell-count effects.

summary: Pax8 targeting produced a globally buffered transcriptional phenotype across the assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The main biological result is a broad negative response: Pax8 is not required to maintain the profiled neuronal and inhibitory transcriptional states, rather than producing a hidden strong effect in a single cell class.
cell_types: 22 assayed brain subclasses
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not detectably depleted, so absence of phenotype is most consistent with a lineage-restricted or unengaged perturbation rather than proof that Pax8 coding sequence was disrupted in every cell.

summary: The dataset provides no RNA-level evidence that Pax8 mRNA was knocked down in Pax8-assigned cells.
why_it_matters: All downstream claims must be interpreted as CRISPR-assignment phenotypes with weak transcript-level target engagement; low endogenous Pax8 expression in brain may make transcript depletion intrinsically hard to observe.
cell_types: 22 assayed brain subclasses
main_caveats: Single-cell mRNA readout cannot distinguish failed editing from successful knockout of a transcript too rare to quantify.

summary: Pax8 perturbation did not engage the thyroid follicular-cell gene program in brain cells.
why_it_matters: Known PAX8 biology centers on activation of thyroid differentiation genes; the brain signatures showed no coordinated movement of Tg, Tpo, Slc5a5, Tshr, Nkx2-1, Foxe1, or Hhex, indicating that this lineage circuit is unavailable in the profiled brain contexts.
cell_types: 22 assayed brain subclasses
main_caveats: These are transcriptomic readouts from brain cells, not thyroid follicular cells; most pathway genes are expected to be near the detection floor.

summary: Pax8 was not transcriptomically interchangeable with PAX paralogs or its thyroid network neighbor Nkx2-1 in the brain dataset.
why_it_matters: A related-target scan found the PAX/NKX neighborhood to be largely inactive and nearly uncorrelated with Pax8, arguing against a shared paired-box or thyroid-transcription-factor module in these cell types.
cell_types: 22 assayed brain subclasses
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors rather than independent validation experiments; weak on-target readout may dampen all comparisons.

summary: Ids and Ttc1 are at most nominal, cell-type-restricted Pax8 response candidates rather than robust biomarkers.
why_it_matters: The two most conspicuous genes occur in different cell classes and neither survives 5% FDR correction, so promoting either as a Pax8-response marker would overinterpret the screen.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Nominal p values are isolated; adjusted p values were 0.082 and 0.134, and a low-cell-count Pineal comparison produced similarly large nominal scores.

summary: The brain-buffered Pax8 phenotype should not be read as evidence that PAX8 is dispensable in thyroid, Müllerian, renal, or ovarian-cancer settings.
why_it_matters: PAX8 is a congenital-hypothyroidism gene and an ovarian lineage dependency, and public target resources do not show an approved direct PAX8 mechanism; this Perturb-seq result narrows the negative finding to brain cell states rather than removing lineage-specific efficacy or safety concerns.
cell_types: 22 assayed brain subclasses
main_caveats: The dataset contains mouse brain cells only and lacks thyroid, kidney, fallopian-tube, ovarian-cancer, or endocrine phenotypes.

summary: Ptch1 perturbation was transcriptionally flat: neither the measured Ptch1 transcript nor any downstream gene reached FDR significance in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: A canonical PTCH1 loss should derepress SMO and GLI signaling, so the dominant dataset-level result is under-engagement or buffering rather than interpretable Hedgehog activation.
main_caveats: CRISPR genotypes and protein loss were not measured; Ptch1 mRNA is an imperfect proxy for editing, and per-cell-type perturbation counts were modest.

summary: The Ptch1 signatures did not activate a measurable Hedgehog/GLI transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: PTCH-family feedback and GLI transcriptional output are expected downstream of ligand-PTCH-SMO signaling; failure to move measured GLI, SMO, Ptch2, Cdon, Gpr161, Adcy3, or Sufu transcripts argues against interpreting the nominal ranked genes as SMO-GLI output.
main_caveats: Hedgehog activity could change by protein localization or ciliary trafficking without changing every pathway transcript; the dataset nevertheless lacks the canonical GLI target-gene readout.

summary: Apparent cell-type peaks after Ptch1 perturbation were nominal, isolated, and did not define a robust Ptch1-responsive cell class.
why_it_matters: The top rows occurred in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA, but all had FDR 0.60-0.96 and involved different one-off genes.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Ranks are based on uncorrected Wilcoxon tails; these genes should not be treated as validated Ptch1 targets.

summary: Ptch1 did not converge transcriptomically with the assayed Hedgehog-neighborhood perturbations Ptch2, Smo, Cdon, Gpr161, Gli1, Gli2, or Gli3.
why_it_matters: CDON, PTCH2/SMO, and GLI factors occupy the same receptor-to-transcription pathway, yet Ptch1 had the weakest best FDR among this local panel and mean Ptch1-versus-neighbor signature correlations were approximately zero.
main_caveats: Most neighboring perturbations were themselves weak; the contrast shows lack of Ptch1-centered convergence, not a validated alternative pathway.

summary: This neuronal Perturb-seq readout did not reproduce the PTCH1-loss Hedgehog activation axis implicated in cancer and neurogenic defects.
why_it_matters: PTCH1 is strongly disease-linked through Hedgehog dysregulation, including basal cell carcinoma, medulloblastoma, and mouse dentate-gyrus neurogenesis phenotypes; the absence of a GLI response suggests that these Ptch1 entries should not be used as a positive disease-like model without direct editing or progenitor-context validation.
main_caveats: Disease evidence is largely germline, tumor, developmental, or progenitor based, whereas this experiment assayed acute perturbations in classified brain cell types with weak transcript-level engagement.

summary: A global signature-neighbor search found no robust positive or inverse perturbation that could rescue the weak Ptch1 scalar signal.
why_it_matters: When a target has no individual FDR hits, a correlated whole-signature neighbor can sometimes reveal a latent module; Ptch1 lacked such structure across all assayed perturbations.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from Wilcoxon-score vectors and are exploratory; the top positive and negative neighbors are not pathway-interpretable.

summary: Tbk1 knockdown was transcriptionally silent at FDR<0.05 across all assayed neuronal cell types despite a broad negative trend in the Tbk1 transcript.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset result is an operationally buffered or weak acute response, not a canonical TBK1 inflammatory signature.
main_caveats: Buffered biology cannot be separated from incomplete CRISPRi engagement; all target-transcript changes were only nominal and 10/21 cell types had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: The best on-target mRNA evidence was restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, where Tbk1 ranked first and fourth by absolute score but still yielded no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: These classes are the only contexts where target knockdown is visible enough to interpret the absence of a broader response as more than simple guide failure.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Nominal p values did not survive FDR correction; these are transcript-level measurements and do not measure TBK1 kinase activity.

summary: Canonical TBK1-IRF/type-I-interferon and NF-kB transcripts were uncoupled from Tbk1 perturbation, and several assayed proximal receptor or kinase neighbors were also FDR-silent.
why_it_matters: The result confines the curated TBK1 antiviral module to signaling states not present in these basal neuronal perturbations rather than supporting a standing IFN program maintained by TBK1.
main_caveats: The experiment was not a TLR, cGAS-STING, or viral-stimulation assay.

summary: Acute Tbk1 loss did not phenocopy ALS/FTD RNA-binding protein perturbations Tardbp and Fus in the same cell types.
why_it_matters: Human TBK1 loss-of-function genetics should not be read as implying the same immediate neuronal transcriptome as TDP-43 or FUS depletion; TBK1 disease mechanisms may require chronic stress, adult vulnerability, kinase substrates, or non-transcriptional adaptor biology.
main_caveats: Tardbp and Fus are disease-family rather than pathway-neighbor comparators; perturbation efficiencies and disease timescales differ.

summary: TBK1 is represented in ChEMBL as a bioactivity target, but loss-of-function disease genetics plus the lack of IFN or OPTN/SQSTM1-module transcript biomarkers argue that neuronal TBK1 inhibition cannot be monitored only by bulk ISG or autophagy mRNA changes.
why_it_matters: A small molecule could reduce TBK1 kinase output without producing an easily detected protective or stress-response transcriptome in these neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Therapeutic inference is indirect: the dataset is mouse Perturb-seq, not a pharmacologic TBK1 inhibitor or chronic human safety model.

summary: Restricted top-signature neighbor analysis found no high-correlation Tbk1 phenocopy or inverse phenocopy.
why_it_matters: The weak nearest neighbors make it unsafe to assign the small nominal Tbk1 signatures to an unrelated pathway on similarity grounds.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only over the top 500 absolute-score Tbk1 genes within each cell type and are exploratory.

summary: Assay-informative Ssr4 perturbation is concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut, with 191 MB P MY GABA just below 10% FDR.
why_it_matters: The target transcript decreased in every measured class, but only a small subset had statistical support strong enough for downstream interpretation; this is selective engagement rather than proof that other brain classes are biologically insensitive.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: 191 MB P MY GABA is near-threshold, and all other nominal classes had target FDR=1.0.

summary: FDR-confirmed Ssr4 mRNA depletion produced no FDR-significant non-target transcriptome in the engaged neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: A TRAP-delta perturbation that survives target-gene FDR without a broad downstream cascade argues that partial Ssr4 loss can be transcriptionally buffered in this assay, which prevents using the absence of an Hspa5-like response as evidence that the perturbation was absent.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Transcriptomic buffering does not rule out selective glycoprotein translocation defects, protein-level TRAP loss, or later stress.

summary: Ssr4 knockdown is uncoupled from the ER-stress/folding module that is visible after Sec63 or Hspa5 perturbation in the same thalamic class.
why_it_matters: Although TRAP sits at the ER translocon, Ssr4 did not induce Hspa5, Hsp90b1, Pdia4, Hyou1, Canx, or Chac1 where Sec63 and Hspa5 perturbations induced multiple FDR-significant UPR/folding genes; Ssr4 therefore should not be treated as a generic ER-stress perturbation in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic; glycosylation-client abundance was not measured.

summary: Other TRAP-subunit transcripts were not reduced after Ssr4 depletion in the engaged or near-engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: The patient-fibroblast finding that SSR4 loss reduces other TRAP proteins is not mirrored as lower Ssr1, Ssr2, or Ssr3 mRNA here, pointing to complex assembly, protein stability, or stronger chronic disease alleles rather than immediate cross-subunit mRNA loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Ssr1/Ssr2/Ssr3 proteins were not measured, and direct Ssr1/Ssr2/Ssr3 perturbations were absent.

summary: No screened ER-import neighbor or unbiased perturbation neighbor reproduced the Ssr4 whole-transcriptome signature.
why_it_matters: The lack of correlation with Stt3b, Sec63, Hspa5, Atf6, or any other perturbation keeps weak Ssr4 data from being inflated into a convergent ER module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Whole-transcriptome correlations are dominated by many near-zero genes; direct Trap subunit perturbations were not available.

summary: Setdb1 perturbation repeatedly derepressed clustered protocadherin-gamma genes rather than producing a generic stress signature.
why_it_matters: Pcdhga and Pcdhgb induction was the most recurrent interpretable positive program and matches the known SETDB1/HUSH role at the neuronal clustered-protocadherin locus.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset measures mRNA, not H3K9me3 or 3D contacts; the strongest recurrence was in a subset of tested neuronal classes.

summary: The strongest Setdb1 signatures induced Atf7ip and Tasor, genes encoding SETDB1/HUSH-associated repressors, consistent with a possible feedback attempt to restore H3K9me3 silencing.
why_it_matters: Because ATF7IP stabilizes SETDB1 and TASOR is a core HUSH component, their induction after Setdb1 perturbation argues that the response is wired through the SETDB1/HUSH silencing apparatus rather than being only an end-stage Pcdh readout.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: mRNA induction does not prove direct feedback regulation or increased protein activity; Tasor reached FDR<0.05 in two cell types and Atf7ip in three.

summary: Setdb1 effects were sharply cell-type restricted: 29 of 37 FDR<0.05 rows concentrated in TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and MB Glut cells, 14 of 22 tested classes had no FDR<0.05 genes, and some responding classes showed only isolated Ccdc84, Atf7ip, or Unc13a hits.
why_it_matters: The same perturbation was not uniformly visible across neuronal populations, refining prior whole-brain and conditional-knockout literature to a small number of transcriptionally responsive cell classes in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Most assayed classes had fewer than 50 Setdb1-perturbed cells and Setdb1 mRNA was not FDR-depleted, so some apparent non-responses may be underpowered false negatives.

summary: Ehmt1, the only available related H3K9 methyltransferase perturbation, did not recapitulate the Setdb1 protocadherin/Atf7ip/Tasor program.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates the Setdb1 response from nonspecific loss of a chromatin writer and is consistent with specialized HUSH/SETDB1 control of the clustered-protocadherin locus.
main_caveats: Core HUSH genes, Trim28, Setdb2, Suv39h1, and Suv39h2 were not perturbation targets, so the comparison is restricted to Ehmt1 rather than a full H3K9-writer panel.

summary: Most Setdb1 cell classes were not interpretable as true biological nulls because target-transcript knockdown was weak and many classes had very low guide-positive cell counts.
why_it_matters: This prevents overcalling the 14 FDR-empty classes as SETDB1-independent; even the strongest nominal Setdb1 decrease occurred in MB P MY GABA cells with only a one-gene downstream signature.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Target mRNA is an imperfect readout for protein depletion and guide activity, but the measured transcript provides little FDR-level evidence of knockdown.

summary: The screen flags clustered-protocadherin and HUSH-cofactor induction as a CNS pharmacodynamic liability to monitor if SETDB1 inhibitors are advanced.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL contains SETDB1 biochemical inhibitor assays, and the mouse-brain data show that reducing Setdb1 activity can move neuronal gene programs already linked to brain architecture and interneuron development.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset used genetic perturbation rather than a small molecule, and ChEMBL did not return a curated clinical SETDB1 drug mechanism.

summary: Sema5a showed decisive on-target knockdown only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while nominal knockdown in CTX-CGE and MB/P/MY GABA was not FDR-significant.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA

summary: The engaged 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response was essentially on-target-only, with Rcc2, Nenf, Stradb, and Pgap6 remaining nominal trans candidates at FDR=1.
why_it_matters: Acute Sema5a RNA loss did not launch a broad steady-state transcriptional cascade in the one cell type with strong knockdown, consistent with local receptor, extracellular-matrix, or morphologic outputs being easier to perturb than to read out by mRNA differential expression.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: A buffered mRNA profile does not exclude changes in growth-cone behavior, glycosaminoglycan binding, spine density, or protein phosphorylation.

direction: shared lack of corrected trans response
summary: Plxna2 and several semaphorin/plexin-neighborhood perturbations in the 151 class were also transcriptionally quiet after correction, despite PLXNA2 and PLXNB3 being prior SEMA5A receptor candidates.

main_caveats: PLXNB3 and Sema5b were not available as measured perturbations here; Plxna2 is a Sema5A receptor in dentate-granule literature, not necessarily in the 151 class.

summary: The MEA/LA/CA1/DG glutamatergic aggregate did not reproduce the dentate-granule Sema5A/PlexinA2 synaptogenesis context because Sema5a itself was not depleted there.
why_it_matters: A negative hippocampal-group result should not be read as contradicting reported Sema5A control of dentate granule-cell spines; the dataset lacks target engagement in that aggregate.

main_caveats: The Perturb-seq class is broad and transcriptional; the literature phenotype is cell-autonomous spine/synapse control in early postnatal and adult-born mouse dentate granule cells.

summary: Autism-linked prior genetics did not translate into a broad acute Sema5a loss-of-function transcriptome in the tested mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports a model in which SEMA5A disease liability is developmental, local, or circuit-level rather than a large disease-like expression state after acute knockdown in these classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The disease literature is human developmental genetics and mouse behavior, whereas the screen is an acute mouse single-cell mRNA endpoint.

summary: No robust trans-mRNA pharmacodynamic marker emerged for Sema5a; the nearest cross-screen and per-cell-type candidates were weak or uncoupled from target knockdown.
why_it_matters: Rcc2-like nominal hits or restricted-signature neighbors should be treated as hypotheses, not biomarkers, and direct SEMA5A chemical tractability is not represented in ChEMBL.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The neighbor search used a weak top-300 Sema5a restricted signature and is exploratory; absence from ChEMBL is not proof that the extracellular protein is undruggable.

summary: Nfic loss produced a selective, FDR-supported Bambi induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

main_caveats: Bambi is a single downstream FDR<0.05 hit; the Nfic target row in this cell type was nominally lower but not FDR-significant.

direction: Nfic-specific Bambi up; pathway-neighbor signatures uncorrelated

summary: Multiple inhibitory or small cell classes with nominal Nfic knockdown lacked an FDR-supported transcriptome response.

cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut

summary: Respiratory-chain perturbations, including major complex III subunits, were strongly engaged in the same dataset while Uqcrh remained flat and uncorrelated with them.

summary: Uqcrh resembled Uqcrb and Uqcrq, not Uqcrc1/Uqcrfs1/Cyc1, at the level of detectable target-mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: Within the same complex, low-molecular-weight subunits produced weak on-target transcript rows, suggesting an assay or guide-engagement blind spot around this subunit class rather than interchangeable biology with core subunits.

summary: The Perturb-seq null should not be interpreted as tolerance of UQCRH loss-of-function relevant to mitochondrial complex III deficiency.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic UQCRH deletion and murine Uqcrh knockout impair complex III and cause systemic disease, so a neuronal DE table lacking target engagement is not a functional rescue of the known disease mechanism.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor scans found no alternative pathway neighbor for Uqcrh.

main_caveats: Neighbor scans were restricted to representative cell types chosen after inspecting Uqcrh; they are useful for triage but not a full dataset-wide correlation analysis.

summary: Unc5d targeting produced a weak, mostly downward on-target mRNA trend but no FDR-resolved differential-expression response in any profiled cell type.
why_it_matters: The primary readout is target-engagement-limited; the dataset should be interpreted as failing to show an acute Unc5d transcriptional program rather than proving that UNC5D is biologically inactive.

summary: Ryk-linked nervous-system disease hypotheses do not gain a mature-neuron transcriptomic biomarker from this screen.

summary: Txndc15 knockdown was broadly measurable but downstream transcriptional remodeling was confined to a small subset of assayed cell classes.

summary: Txndc15 perturbation activates an SREBF/cholesterol module in 155 MB Glut.

summary: 191 MB P MY GABA and, more weakly, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut show partial recurrence of the Txndc15 sterol response.

summary: Multiple cell classes show strong Txndc15 target engagement with no FDR-significant downstream gene.

summary: Zkscan3 perturbation produced no 5% FDR differential-expression program in any measured mouse-brain cell type.

summary: The expected autophagy-lysosome derepression signature was absent after Zkscan3 perturbation.

summary: Assayed Zkscan/Zscan-family perturbations were not interchangeable: Zkscan3 and Zkscan1 were FDR-silent, whereas Zkscan16 and Zscan26 had isolated 155 MB Glut FDR hits.

main_caveats: Only three related Zkscan/Zscan targets were assayed, and two comparator discoveries were single-gene rather than broad signatures.

summary: Ypel5 and Eif4g3 were the only near-FDR residual Zkscan3 signals, marking two exploratory cell-type-restricted candidate readouts.
why_it_matters: The top residual rows localize weak signal to 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut rather than to broad autophagy, but they are below discovery threshold and should not be promoted to pathway markers.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

summary: Disease-model literature makes ZKSCAN3 reduction an attractive autophagy-activating idea, but this mouse-brain screen shows that the first requirement is verifying knockdown and lysosomal target engagement in the intended neuronal context.
why_it_matters: HD and PD studies report benefit from ZKSCAN3 ablation or nuclear exclusion, yet the Perturb-seq data provide no transcriptomic evidence that Zkscan3 guides a comparable autophagy response in the assayed brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The dataset is not a Huntington or Parkinson disease model, and weak measured Zkscan3 suppression prevents a conclusion that neuronal Zkscan3 biology is absent.

summary: Basal Tlr3 targeting was nearly silent across the neuronal atlas: the Tlr3 transcript itself was not measurably reduced and only one of 355,046 tested rows reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: A dsRNA receptor that is potent in ligand-stimulated innate immunity behaved as a buffered or inactive node in these unchallenged mouse brain neuronal states, so absence of a broad response is a central result rather than a lack of analysis power alone.
main_caveats: The target transcript was sparse and not detectably knocked down, so the result may reflect low Tlr3 expression or ineffective RNA-level engagement as well as true buffering.

summary: Rgs4 up-regulation in 145 MH-LH TH Glut was the only FDR-significant gene-level effect of Tlr3 targeting.
why_it_matters: The one FDR signal points to a neuronal GPCR-regulatory marker rather than to interferon-stimulated genes, raising a narrow biomarker hypothesis for a habenula/thalamic glutamatergic response.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only 40 Tlr3-targeted cells supported the 145 MH-LH TH Glut test; Rgs4 was not recurrent across cell types; and no direct Tlr3-Rgs4 mechanism was established.

summary: Tlr3 signatures were not interchangeable with perturbations of TLR receptor paralogs or proximal IRF/NF-kB pathway neighbors.
why_it_matters: Reactome and STRING place TLR3 in a TRIF-centered antiviral network, yet the matched Perturb-seq signatures for Tlr4, Tlr7, Tlr8, Tlr9, Tbk1, Traf3, Irf3, Irf7, and NF-kB-family targets were essentially uncorrelated with Tlr3, arguing that receptor-family membership is not enough to predict basal neuronal loss-of-function phenotypes.
main_caveats: Most innate-immune pathway-neighbor perturbations also had weak one-gene or zero-gene FDR signatures, so the correlations test transcriptome similarity of weak basal signatures rather than ligand-induced signaling capacity.

summary: The dataset does not reproduce the TLR3-dependent CNS antiviral interferon axis implicated in herpes simplex encephalitis, refining it as a challenge-dependent rather than constitutive neuronal program.
why_it_matters: Human genetics and iPSC models make TLR3 clinically important for HSV-1 control in CNS cells, but the Perturb-seq data warn that resting mouse neuronal perturbations lack the IFN-beta/ISG readout needed to model that liability.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse, developmental-brain and unstimulated; the disease literature is human and HSV-1-triggered, so this is a context refinement, not evidence against the HSE mechanism.

summary: A restricted 145 MH-LH TH Glut signature-neighbor scan found only moderate correlations to Apc, Agtr1a, and Ptf1a perturbations and no compelling TLR3-pathway neighbor.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-promoting weak scalar similarities as mechanisms for the lone Rgs4-positive signature.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Correlations used only the 200 lowest-p-value genes from one weak Tlr3 signature and were not validated by full-signature related-target convergence.

summary: Rars2 was an FDR-null perturbation across all 23 assayed brain cell classes and did not reproducibly reduce its own transcript.
why_it_matters: RARS2 is a mitochondrial arginyl-tRNA synthetase whose loss causes mitochondrial encephalopathy, so the Perturb-seq signature should be interpreted as absent or buffered target engagement rather than as a clean RARS2 loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: FDR-null expression data cannot distinguish failed editing, insufficient mRNA depletion, protein buffering, or a real non-transcriptional phenotype.

summary: The lowest Rars2 signal was a weak, CNU-MGE-skewed nominal peak rather than a robust or recurrent cell-type program.
why_it_matters: The Dpysl5-leading 054 CNU-MGE GABA result is the only row near 10% FDR, but 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had a similar number of nominal genes and neither class had any 5% FDR hit; this argues against over-calling a discrete Rars2-responsive neuronal subtype.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The lead CNU-MGE row had FDR=0.0731, all other highlighted genes were only nominal, and the target transcript itself was not significantly depleted.

summary: Canonical mitochondrial-translation impairment was not visible as a coordinated respiratory-chain RNA response.
why_it_matters: RARS2 sits in mitochondrial tRNA aminoacylation upstream of mitochondrially encoded OXPHOS proteins, yet mtDNA and nuclear OXPHOS transcripts were FDR-null and mixed in direction, consistent with a primary defect that may act at translation, respiration, or protein homeostasis rather than through acute mRNA loss.
main_caveats: Only mRNA was tested; the screen does not directly measure aminoacylation, mitochondrial translation, OXPHOS subunit abundance, or respiration.

summary: Other mitochondrial aminoacylation or translation neighbors in the screen did not phenocopy Rars2.
why_it_matters: Fars2, Lars2, and Gfm2 were also weak and nearly uncorrelated with Rars2, so this dataset does not support a generic shared mitochondrial-translation stress module across these perturbations.
main_caveats: All four related signatures were weak, so near-zero correlations show lack of detectable transcriptomic convergence rather than mechanistic antagonism.

summary: High-census Rars2 cell classes were also downstream-null.
why_it_matters: The absence of signal was not confined to the lowest-cell-count classes; three classes with more than 100 Rars2 cells still had no FDR-significant genes and no significant Rars2 self-row.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Higher cell number does not prove that the perturbation depleted Rars2 protein in these cells.

summary: The FDR-null transcriptome should not be taken as evidence that inhibiting Rars2 is safe or disease-reversing.
why_it_matters: Human RARS2 disease is caused by biallelic deleterious variants, and the current screen lacks measurable Rars2 mRNA knockdown; a negative scRNA-seq response therefore cannot overturn the loss-of-function disease mechanism or motivate RARS2 inhibition.
main_caveats: The dataset is transcriptomic and perturbational, not a disease-genotype rescue or toxicity assay.

summary: Smad3 perturbation produced no FDR-significant on-target depletion or downstream differential expression across the 22 assayed Smad3 cell types.
why_it_matters: A canonical TGF-beta transcriptional effector was transcriptionally buffered or weakly engaged in this mouse-brain assay, making downstream pathway claims unsupported for Smad3 itself.
main_caveats: The absence of FDR-significant Smad3 transcript reduction means the downstream null may be caused by poor guide engagement or low target expression, not by true biological dispensability.

summary: The Smad3 null was not rescued by high perturbed-cell counts or by DG/hippocampal glutamatergic contexts.

summary: Several TGF/BMP/SMAD-neighbor perturbations produced corrected DE hits, but Smad3 did not and its signature was uncorrelated with Smad2 or Smad4.

summary: Transcriptome-wide signature neighbors of Smad3 were weak and not pathway-interpretable.

summary: DG-containing steady-state glutamatergic signatures did not show the Smad3 responses expected from adult dentate neurogenesis or injury literature.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse brain studies localize important Smad3 biology to adult dentate progenitors and traumatic-injury responses, whereas this dataset points away from a broad resting neuronal-autonomous transcriptional program.

main_caveats: The dataset does not isolate proliferative intermediate progenitors, post-injury neurons, astrocytes, or microglia, so it should not be interpreted as a direct contradiction of those studies.

summary: The weak neuronal Smad3 phenotype is not a favorable safety or efficacy signal for systemic SMAD3 modulation.
why_it_matters: SMAD3 is linked to vascular/connective-tissue disease and cancer genetics, while direct human SMAD3 drug mechanisms are sparse in ChEMBL; therefore a mouse neuronal Perturb-seq null should only be used as assay-specific evidence.
main_caveats: The dataset used mouse brain cell types and mRNA DE; it did not assay vascular cells, connective tissue, fibrosis, cancer phenotypes, or direct compound pharmacology.

summary: Measured Strada transcript loss was shallow and cell-type uneven rather than a uniform perturbation across the mouse-brain atlas.

main_caveats: Buffering cannot be separated from incomplete target engagement or low per-cell-type cell counts, and phosphorylation-level mTORC1 outputs were not assayed.

summary: Qrich1 perturbation did not FDR-induce canonical UPR or ISR marker RNAs and was not phenocopied by Atf6 or Nfe2l2 perturbation.

summary: The strongest mouse Qrich1 phenotype falls in neuronal classes and affects neurophysiology-related transcripts, refining human QRICH1 haploinsufficiency toward thalamic and brainstem/midbrain neuronal programs.

summary: An unbiased 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neighbor search found no strong Qrich1 phenocopy or anti-phenocopy among the other assayed perturbations.

summary: The mouse neuronal Tgfbr2 signature is too weak and non-canonical to serve as a stand-alone transcriptomic model for TGFBR2-linked Loeys-Dietz disease or pharmacologic TGFBR2 inhibition.
why_it_matters: TGFBR2 is a human disease gene and biochemically assayable kinase target, but the disease tissues and chemistry do not match this sparse neuronal CRISPR response.
main_caveats: The disease literature concerns human germline receptor variants and vascular/connective tissues, not acute mouse neuronal Perturb-seq.

direction: Tanc2 mostly down; downstream DE absent at FDR<0.05

main_caveats: Most cell types had only 28-71 perturbed cells, and all interpretation is limited to transcript abundances in the assayed mouse-brain Perturb-seq snapshot.

direction: nominal target knockdown strongest in 155 MB Glut; weak in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

direction: mixed similarity and opposition in a no-engagement context

cell_types: 308 CB GABA

direction: mRNA response buffered relative to known synaptic-developmental phenotypes
summary: The weak Tanc2 transcriptional signature is more consistent with TANC2 acting through local synaptic, dendritic-spine, developmental, or transport functions than through a large cell-autonomous mRNA program.
why_it_matters: Human and animal genetics make TANC2 biologically important, but this dataset suggests that an mRNA biomarker panel from guide-positive brain cells is unlikely to be a sensitive direct readout of the core mechanism.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay does not measure dendritic-spine morphology, dense-core-vesicle capture, behavior, or developmental timing directly.

direction: Tanc2 is more buffered than several neighboring synaptic perturbations
summary: Tanc2 was not interchangeable with related postsynaptic or neurodevelopmental perturbations: many Dlg4/Shank/Nrxn/Nlgn/Grin/Ctnnb1-family comparators generated FDR-significant signatures, while Tanc2 did not and had only weak score-vector convergence with them.

main_caveats: The comparator set is curated rather than exhaustive, and signature similarity was computed only in the 21 cell types where Tanc2 was assayed.

summary: Slit2 perturbation had weak measured on-target RNA depletion in every Slit2-assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Without clear depletion of the secreted ligand transcript, downstream null effects should be treated as an under-engaged perturbation rather than proof that SLIT2 biology is dispensable.
main_caveats: The dataset contains differential-expression summaries, not raw expression or guide-level editing information; low Slit2 expression and ineffective guides cannot be separated.

summary: No Slit2 cell type produced a multiple-testing-significant transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: The strongest apparent Slit2 hits were isolated nominal rows, so they should drive validation hypotheses only, not a pathway call.

summary: Slit2 signatures did not consistently converge with the direct receptors Robo1/Robo2 or with other assayed axon-guidance comparators.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues against using weak cell-autonomous Slit2 RNA signatures as a proxy for ROBO receptor signaling state in these sampled mouse-brain cell types.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed from weak Slit2 signatures; correlations test transcriptome similarity, not acute ligand-receptor signaling or RHOA activity.

summary: Validated Robo1, Robo2, and Unc5c knockdowns were largely self-limited at the mRNA level.
