summary: The screen gives no support for a robust SLIT2-directed transcriptional pharmacodynamic marker in the assayed mouse-brain cells.
why_it_matters: SLIT2 is a secreted axon-guidance ligand rather than an annotated ChEMBL small-molecule target; the present data suggest that perturbing Slit2 mRNA in individual brain cells is unlikely to yield an easily monitored bulk RNA marker.
main_caveats: ChEMBL absence is database-context evidence only; it does not rule out antibodies, ligand traps, engineered proteins, or indirect modulation.

summary: The strongest Slit2 signature neighbors were modest and cell-type-restricted rather than recurrent Slit/Robo-family convergence.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting the CA3 and cerebellar GABA correlations as a conserved Slit2 module; they are better treated as exploratory restricted-signature hypotheses.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: These correlations are based on weak Slit2 signatures and most top neighbors are not known direct SLIT2 pathway members.

summary: Ttc21b produced no FDR-significant transcriptome in any of the 21 assayed Ttc21b cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: Ttc21b is a curated IFT-A/retrograde-ciliary-transport gene, so the absence of corrected DE argues that this Perturb-seq signature should be treated as unengaged, buffered, or assayed outside its responsive context rather than as a clean loss-of-function readout.
main_caveats: A CRISPR edit can leave the target mRNA intact while disrupting protein; the data quantify transcript-level engagement only.

summary: Ttc21b perturbation did not activate a canonical Gli/Ptch/Hhip Hedgehog transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: Mouse Ttc21b loss can overactivate Shh signaling in embryos and forebrain, while cerebellar conditional loss can reduce Shh output; this dataset instead shows no corrected response in either direction, refining those developmental observations to a weak or absent neuronal transcriptomic phenotype in the assayed panel.
main_caveats: Hedgehog readout genes are sparsely expressed in many mature neuronal classes, and weak Ttc21b target-transcript engagement limits pathway inference.

summary: The strongest downstream and strongest self-depletion summaries fell in different cell types, indicating that nominal Ttc21b signals are decoupled from transcript-level target engagement.
why_it_matters: The near-threshold NP-CT-L6b-OB Klf13/Ranbp2 response could be a real restricted response, but the same cell type had no Ttc21b mRNA decrease; conversely, CNU-HYa HY GABA had the best nominal Ttc21b decrease with no FDR-level downstream gene.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Both cell types had small perturbed-cell counts and all rows discussed here are FDR>=0.0906.

summary: Ttc21b did not show the expected transcriptional convergence with Ift43, Ift81, Ift88, Ttc8, Ahi1, or Rpgrip1l perturbations.
why_it_matters: IFT-A places TTC21B/IFT139 in the same biochemical peripheral module as IFT43, and STRING links the assayed IFT genes, yet the Ttc21b restricted signature was nearly orthogonal to these related perturbations; the dataset therefore should not be summarized as a coherent neuronal IFT module.
main_caveats: Signature cosines were computed only on nominal Ttc21b rows and can be dominated by weak or noisy genes.

summary: A small ciliary trace appears among the low-amplitude positive signature neighbors, but it is too weak to nominate a robust Ttc21b module.
why_it_matters: Arl3 and B9d1 were in the top 16 Ttc21b neighbors and are connected to the ciliary network, but their cosine values were only 0.11 and Safe_target-labelled perturbations ranked similarly; this makes the observation hypothesis-generating rather than a biomarker set.
main_caveats: The strongest cosine was only 0.147 and the nearest-neighbor list was not specific for ciliary biology.

summary: Retreg1 transcript repression was directionally broad but FDR-grade only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: The screen supports on-target CRISPRi activity, but cell-type specificity should be read through power and transcript-detection constraints rather than as proof that other neurons are biologically insensitive.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Several small populations had large nominal Retreg1 decreases but FDR=1.0; on-target mRNA reduction does not guarantee loss of RETREG1 protein or ER-phagy flux.

summary: The three FDR-engaged Retreg1 knockdowns were transcriptionally buffered: Retreg1 itself was the only FDR hit in each class.
why_it_matters: RETREG1 is a direct ER-phagy receptor, so a silent bulk mRNA response suggests that acute loss of this selective receptor does not automatically trigger a large central-neuron stress transcriptome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only single-cell mRNA was assayed; ER morphology, ER-phagy flux, proteostasis, and delayed death were not measured.

summary: Canonical ER-stress and autophagy transcripts were not induced after Retreg1 knockdown and the clearest nominal marker shifts were decreases, not a compensatory UPR.
why_it_matters: This separates an ER-phagy receptor loss from a detectable Hspa5/Ddit3/Xbp1-type mRNA alarm in the assayed brain neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Marker-based and nominal except for Retreg1 itself; the dataset cannot test ER expansion or flux that prior cell-biological papers measured directly.

summary: Retreg1 did not phenocopy available autophagy or ER-shaping perturbations such as Atg5, Becn1, Rb1cc1, Vcp, Atl3, or Map1lc3a despite RETREG1's LC3/GABARAP reticulophagy role.
why_it_matters: The divergence argues against treating Retreg1 as a simple transcriptomic surrogate for core macroautophagy loss in this screen and preserves a selective-ER-phagy interpretation.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was restricted to the top 200 Retreg1 non-target genes because the all-gene Retreg1 signature is weak; key receptors including TEX264, CCPG1, SEC62, RTN3, RETREG2, and RETREG3 were not available as perturbations.

summary: The acute central-neuron screen is milder than the known human and mouse sensory-neuron phenotype of FAM134B/RETREG1 loss.
why_it_matters: FAM134B loss-of-function causes hereditary sensory and autonomic neuropathy type 2, whereas these brain neurons showed target knockdown without a broad stress transcriptome; that points to peripheral-neuron, chronic, or non-transcriptional vulnerability rather than a generic acute UPR across all neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The screen did not profile dorsal-root or autonomic ganglion neurons and cannot measure long-term axon maintenance.

summary: RETREG1 inhibition lacks a clear small-molecule precedent and should not be inferred safe from the weak acute brain transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Human loss-of-function disease makes pathway inhibition directionally risky, while the dataset only shows that several central neuronal classes can buffer acute transcript knockdown at the mRNA level.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: ChEMBL absence is not proof of undruggability; no viability, peripheral-neuron, or RETREG1 protein data are present.

summary: Ubr1 perturbation did not produce an FDR-supported transcriptomic effect in any assayed mouse-brain cell type.
why_it_matters: This is the primary interpretation gate: the dataset should be treated as an under-engaged or buffered Ubr1 experiment rather than as a map of high-confidence UBR1-regulated neuronal genes.
main_caveats: The negative result is at the mRNA-signature level; UBR1 protein depletion, guide activity, and proteomic N-end-rule activity were not measured.

summary: The largest nominal Ubr1-associated genes were scattered across cell types rather than forming a recurrent cell-type-selective module.
why_it_matters: A few p≈10^-4 nominal hits could otherwise be over-read as biology; their poor recurrence and FDR=1.0 status make them hypothesis-generating only.
main_caveats: Recurrence was assessed from ranked Wilcoxon genes and restricted top-200 signature vectors, not from replicated guide-level statistics.

summary: Nominal Ubr1 signatures did not align with available ubiquitin/proteostasis neighbors, and most direct N-recognin comparators were absent from the perturbation library.
why_it_matters: The dataset lacks the independent paralog/pathway-neighbor convergence that would be expected before assigning weak Ubr1 scalar hits to an N-end-rule module.
main_caveats: Correlation used only the top 200 Ubr1-ranked genes per cell type, and the Ubr1 signatures themselves were not FDR-supported.

summary: The assayed neuronal Perturb-seq readout does not recapitulate the strong developmental and pancreatic biology of UBR1 loss of function.
why_it_matters: Human Johanson-Blizzard syndrome and mouse Ubr1/Ubr2 developmental phenotypes establish that UBR1 is biologically important, but this dataset suggests those effects are not converted into a robust mRNA program in the sampled mouse-brain cell types.
main_caveats: The literature involves germline human disease, exocrine pancreas, embryos, or double knockouts, whereas the dataset is a mouse-brain single-perturbation transcriptome with weak target-mRNA knockdown.

summary: The dataset provides no directional mouse-brain transcriptional biomarker for UBR1 inhibition or activation.
why_it_matters: UBR1 is an enzyme and a human disease gene, but the assayed neuronal signatures were weak, ChEMBL contains only sparse binding records without mechanisms, and the strongest human genetics for UBR1 is loss of function; CNS therapeutic hypotheses therefore need orthogonal engagement and proteomic biomarkers.
main_caveats: This is a warning about interpretation, not evidence that UBR1 is undruggable or irrelevant to the nervous system.

summary: Pogz perturbation did not produce any FDR-supported target-transcript or downstream transcriptional effect in the 21 tested mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The primary result is a constrained or weak measurable response, so nominal hits should not be read as a high-confidence Pogz loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: The DE table measures Pogz RNA, not editing or protein depletion, so weak RNA reduction does not prove biological non-engagement.

summary: The small nominal response was uneven and peaked in L4-5 IT cortical glutamatergic, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons/medulla GABA classes, but these peaks were not FDR significant and did not share a recurrent gene module.
why_it_matters: This argues for exploratory cell context rather than a pan-brain Pogz transcriptional signature.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: All genes in these cell types failed FDR control; 191 MB P MY GABA used only 49 Pogz cells.

summary: Pogz signatures were nearly orthogonal to ADNP-, CHD4-, and CHD8-perturbation signatures even though these proteins occupy the same nuclear interaction neighborhood.
why_it_matters: Known physical or chromatin co-occupancy does not imply interchangeability in this Perturb-seq readout; Pogz was much more weakly resolved than its related chromatin regulators.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is confounded by weak Pogz transcript knockdown and weaker Pogz downstream DE, so it demonstrates lack of phenocopying rather than a proven opposite mechanism.

summary: Previously reported POGZ-dependent synaptic, cortical-developmental, cerebellar, and neuroinflammatory programs were not recovered as a robust module; only isolated synaptic or neurodevelopmental genes appeared at nominal p values.
why_it_matters: The dataset narrows the conditions under which POGZ disease biology is visible and suggests that dosage, developmental state, anatomical region, or perturbation strength may gate the known programs.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: No formal pathway enrichment was performed from these uncorrected hits; the conclusion is about absence of robust recurrence, not absence of a synaptic role for POGZ.

summary: The Pogz profile did not nominate a stable reversal target, and POGZ itself is a constrained nuclear chromatin protein without an obvious clinical small-molecule handle.
why_it_matters: POGZ-related disorders are loss-of-function NDDs; the combination of weak dataset signatures, weak signature neighbors, and poor tractability cautions against inferring a simple inhibitor-like or receptor-reversal strategy from this screen.
main_caveats: Therapeutic tractability was assessed from public target annotations, not from a drug screen; weak Perturb-seq effects may be caused by weak target engagement.

summary: Tmem63b guide cells show reproducible target-transcript depletion but an exceptionally sparse downstream transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: The dominant measured effect is loss of Tmem63b RNA itself, consistent with either buffering of partial channel loss, a requirement for osmotic or mechanical stimulation, or a mostly acute electrophysiologic function rather than a constitutive basal transcriptional program.
main_caveats: DE was measured under basal pooled-culture conditions; protein loss and channel current were not measured.

summary: Caln1 in L5 extratelencephalic neurons and Fdft1 in hypothalamic GABA neurons are the only non-target genes approaching experiment-wide significance.
why_it_matters: They are the best candidate readouts for a Tmem63b-loss state, but their narrow cell-type restriction means they should be validated before being treated as a general TMEM63B pathway.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Fdft1 reached FDR<0.1 but not <0.05, and the Caln1 recurrence in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA was nominal only.

summary: The strongest direct Tmem63b knockdown occurred in thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and hypothalamic populations, yet those engaged populations were still transcriptionally buffered.
why_it_matters: This separates target delivery from effect size: high-confidence depletion in several deep neuronal classes did not imply a broad downstream response, arguing that cell identity or stimulus state, not just guide-cell number, gates TMEM63B biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The assayed hypothalamic classes are broad and need not contain the rare subfornical-organ excitatory neurons used in thirst studies.

summary: TMEM63 paralogs could not be used as loss-of-function phenocopies because Tmem63a and Tmem63c perturbations did not deplete their own transcripts detectably.
why_it_matters: The related-channel comparison is therefore a technical negative rather than evidence that Tmem63b has a unique downstream program relative to other TMEM63-family channels.
main_caveats: The dataset cannot distinguish biological paralog divergence from inefficient knockdown for Tmem63a and Tmem63c.

summary: Library-wide signature matching found no robust positive or negative perturbation neighbor for Tmem63b.
why_it_matters: This argues against a hidden strong pathway partner or antagonist in the measured basal transcriptome; the nearest signatures were weak and mechanistically unconvincing.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on noisy rank-score vectors; a stimulus-specific TMEM63B program could be absent from this basal assay.

summary: The perturbation models reduced Tmem63b expression, not the gain-of-function/leak-channel state reported for human TMEM63B developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
why_it_matters: The lack of a broad loss-of-expression signature cautions against reading these data as a direct DEE model or as proof of disease reversal by simple transcript suppression, especially because TMEM63B also has SFO and lung mechanosensory roles.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks patient alleles, electrophysiology, hematologic cells, lung epithelial cells, and hyperosmotic stimulation.

summary: Tpr perturbation produced a highly subclass-restricted response, dominated by 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while many subclasses had no FDR-significant genes.

main_caveats: Score-vector correlations were modest and do not prove direct biochemical interaction.

direction: TPR reduction is genetically and transcriptionally adverse
summary: Human TPR loss-of-function genetics plus broad neuronal DE after mouse Tpr perturbation warn that lowering TPR activity is likely deleterious in brain.
why_it_matters: Any therapeutic idea around TPR should favor restoration or bypass of impaired nuclear-basket export rather than inhibition of TPR function.

direction: Rnf13 transcript decreased only nominally in a five-cell-type subset

main_caveats: Even the target-transcript rows remained FDR=1.0, and the best nominal cell types had only 22 to 148 perturbed cells.

direction: no coherent induction of canonical stress or apoptosis markers

why_it_matters: RNF13 is known to potentiate IRE1α-JNK stress apoptosis, but partial depletion in these unstressed neurons did not produce a matching transcriptional cascade.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is a negative transcriptomic result under basal Perturb-seq conditions; it does not assess RNF13 protein, ubiquitin-chain biochemistry, or neurons exposed to exogenous ER stress.

summary: Rnf13 signatures were weakly coupled to ER-stress, JNK, AP-3/endolysosomal, and RING-ligase-neighbor perturbations and had no strong recurrent positive or negative signature neighbor.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed over rank-score vectors rather than pathway activities, and the weak Rnf13 signatures limit power to detect related perturbations.

summary: The dataset is more consistent with RNF13 developmental epileptic encephalopathy being driven by gain-of-function or mislocalized RNF13 than by simple acute haploinsufficiency.
why_it_matters: Human DEE73 variants enhance IRE1α stress signaling and disrupt endolysosomal sorting; the mouse adult partial-loss signatures here do not recreate that stress-apoptosis state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The screen perturbs wild-type mouse Rnf13 in differentiated neurons and cannot model the exact L311S/L312P mutant proteins, developmental timing, or severe patient genotypes.

summary: RNF13 biology is directionally context-dependent, so both inhibition and activation are plausible liabilities despite the muted basal Perturb-seq phenotype.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
