why_it_matters: Complex membership alone was not enough to create a shared mRNA signature; for this target the strongest explanation is a technical-biological contrast in target engagement, because many neighboring Nduf targets had far stronger own-transcript depletion while Ndufv2 correlations to Ndufv1, Ndufs1, Ndufs2 and related signatures were near zero.
main_caveats: Correlation analysis is transcriptomic and, for E006, restricted to Ndufv2 top genes; weak Ndufv2 knockdown limits subunit-specific interpretation.

summary: The data and human genetics argue against further NDUFV2 or Complex I inhibition as a brain-directed therapeutic strategy.
why_it_matters: Human NDUFV2 deficiency is deleterious, the dataset lacks a coherent compensatory OXPHOS rescue program after Ndufv2 lowering, and ChEMBL did not show curated NDUFV2-directed mechanism-of-action drugs; therapeutic work should therefore prioritize restoring or bypassing Complex I function rather than reducing NDUFV2 activity.
main_caveats: No compound was tested in the Perturb-seq dataset, and absence of a ChEMBL mechanism row is not proof that NDUFV2 is undruggable.

direction: Tuba1a and Tubb5 up after Tbce perturbation; other tubulin isoforms up after direct Tuba1a loss
summary: Tbce perturbation elicited a recurrent Tuba1a-centered tubulin-transcript rebound rather than repression of tubulin mRNAs.
why_it_matters: TBCE is a folding cofactor, so induction of Tuba1a and Tubb5 is better interpreted as a microtubule-homeostasis feedback state than as simple loss of the tubulin genes themselves.
main_caveats: Compensation is inferred from mRNA; soluble tubulin, TTC5 activity, and microtubule polymer mass were not measured.

direction: strongest in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; sparse Tuba1a-only response elsewhere
summary: The only multi-gene FDR-significant Tbce response was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: A ubiquitous tubulin-folding factor did not produce a uniform brain-wide transcriptomic response; the high-confidence signature was restricted to one glutamatergic class, with most other FDR support collapsing to Tuba1a alone.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction is based on the profiled brain cell classes and matched-cell counts, not on equal statistical power across all classes.

direction: same-direction induction of Tuba1a and overlapping positive-response genes
summary: Tbce and the related cofactor Tbcd converged on an inducible tubulin-folding module, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Convergence between two non-interchangeable members of the same curated tubulin biogenesis machinery supports the Tuba1a/Tubb5 signal as pathway-connected rather than an isolated single-gene anomaly.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Whole-transcriptome Tbce-Tbcd correlations were positive but small; convergence is strongest for the tubulin response and for the 151 cell class.

summary: Measured Tbce mRNA knockdown was weak, so many apparently buffered cell types cannot be interpreted as strong-engagement null phenotypes.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports downstream tubulin changes in selected classes, but it does not prove efficient transcript depletion of Tbce itself in any class.
main_caveats: The perturbation may still damage TBCE protein coding sequence without causing mRNA decay; the dataset measures RNA, not TBCE protein.

direction: top positive neighbor opposed Tuba1a; top negative neighbor did not significantly affect Tuba1a/Tubb5
summary: The top positive and negative unbiased 151-cell signature neighbors did not recapitulate Tbce tubulin biology.
why_it_matters: A positive global correlation was not equivalent to matching tubulin biology, preventing overinterpretation of Atp6v0c as a tubulin-folding surrogate.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is correlation of perturbation signatures; no direct Atp6v0c-Tbce physical or regulatory relationship was established.

summary: TBCE inhibition would be mechanistically hazardous in neurons despite causing compensatory Tuba1a induction in this assay.
why_it_matters: Mouse and human genetics link TBCE loss to degeneration and microtubule defects; therefore, deliberately pushing the Tbce-loss state is more consistent with a microtubule-maintenance liability than with a useful way to raise tubulin transcripts.
main_caveats: No TBCE inhibitor, dose response, protein depletion, or long-term neuronal survival endpoint was tested in the Perturb-seq dataset.

summary: Wac loss produced a narrow downstream response concentrated in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, midbrain glutamatergic, and Pvalb GABA neurons rather than a broad response across all Wac-assayed classes.
why_it_matters: WAC is a broadly expressed nuclear adaptor, so this cell-type restriction is the central interpretation layer for the Perturb-seq phenotype.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The endogenous Wac transcript was not FDR-significantly depleted in any class, and high FDR burden partly tracks perturbed-cell count.

summary: The Wac-sensitive classes repeatedly downregulated neuronal and synaptic effector genes including Lgi3, Ache, Eno2, Septin5, C1qtnf4, Gabra1, Gabrd, Gabrb2, Slc17a6, and Pvalb.
why_it_matters: Human WAC disease is loss-of-function neurodevelopmental disease; the mouse neuronal perturbation points to collapse of synaptic or mature neuronal programs as a downstream consequence of Wac insufficiency.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse single-cell RNA after CRISPR perturbation and does not directly assay human development or synaptic physiology.

summary: The strongest Wac response paired loss of synaptic genes with increased nuclear speckle, splicing, and ubiquitin-linked transcripts such as Luc7l2, Luc7l3, Sf3b1, Rbm25, Rbm4, Srsf11, Clk1, Jmjd1c, and Ube2b.
why_it_matters: This suggests that Wac-deficient neurons activate a nuclear RNA-processing or chromatin compensation program rather than simply reducing all transcription.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Upregulated splicing genes are a transcriptomic secondary response; H2Bub, WAC protein binding, and splicing outputs were not measured.

summary: Wac signatures were repeatedly closest to spliceosome and proteasome perturbations, especially Prpf6, Ddx23, Psmb4, Psmc1, Psmc5, and Pomp, in the Wac-active cell classes.
why_it_matters: A repeated cross-perturbation neighborhood argues that Wac loss enters a broader RNA-processing/proteostasis state instead of being an isolated target-specific signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were modest and not evidence of direct physical interaction between WAC and the perturbation targets.

summary: Direct Mtor and Rptor perturbations did not phenocopy Wac in the two strongest Wac cell classes.
why_it_matters: Prior literature links WAC to mTORC1 and autophagy, but the neuronal Wac RNA signature is not well explained as acute Mtor or Rptor loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Mtor and Rptor perturbations themselves had few or no FDR-significant rows in these classes, so this is a negative signature comparison rather than a definitive mTORC1 activity assay.

summary: Because WAC loss causes human neurodevelopmental disease and Wac knockdown depresses neuronal effector genes in the dataset, WAC inhibition is directionally unfavorable; restoration of WAC or downstream synaptic programs is the disease-aligned direction.
why_it_matters: This prevents misreading the Perturb-seq loss signature as support for inhibiting WAC in neurons and highlights the lack of obvious direct small-molecule tractability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The dataset does not test WAC overexpression or rescue, and the tractability statements reflect current annotations rather than a proof that WAC cannot be modulated.

summary: Some classes with nominal Wac self-depletion, especially 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut, had only small downstream FDR burdens, while seven Wac-assayed classes had no FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: This separates target-transcript trends from transcriptional vulnerability and flags either true buffering or limited statistical power outside the dominant thalamic, midbrain, and Pvalb responses.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: No class had robust Wac transcript FDR, and several null classes had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: Stra6 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any of the 22 assayed brain cell-type strata.
why_it_matters: This is the primary dataset result and prevents confident pathway claims from nominal top genes.
main_caveats: A negative DE table is not proof of STRA6 dispensability because RNA-level target engagement was not detected.

summary: Cell types with the largest Stra6 cell counts were still transcriptionally silent after correction.
why_it_matters: The absence of signal was not limited to the 31-57 cell strata, although the highest count was still only 195 cells and target mRNA depletion was weak.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Buffering cannot be separated from ineffective or sparse Stra6 engagement.

summary: Stra6 perturbation did not activate or repress measured retinol-transport, RAR/RXR, or JAK/STAT marker transcripts.
why_it_matters: The expected STRA6 biochemical axis is RBP4-dependent retinol uptake with downstream retinoid and context-dependent JAK/STAT signaling; none of those marker families registered a corrected response.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was assayed; no retinol, retinoic acid, receptor phosphorylation, or STAT phosphorylation was measured.

summary: RAR/RXR perturbations and Stra6 perturbation failed to converge on a common retinoid signature in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: Direct nuclear retinoid-receptor perturbations were available as pathway comparators, but their overall silence and near-zero correlations argue that the profiled cell states did not expose a robust retinoic-acid response module.
main_caveats: RAR/RXR and all-perturbation signature-neighbor correlations are transcriptomic and cannot distinguish low receptor expression from insufficient editing.

summary: The adult brain Perturb-seq negative result is consistent with STRA6 biology being strongest in vitamin-A transport barrier and developmental contexts rather than in the assayed mature neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This reconciles severe STRA6 developmental and barrier phenotypes with a flat adult neuronal single-cell DE signature.
main_caveats: The parquet confirms absence of a response only in the available cell groups; it does not assay choroid plexus, retina, or embryogenesis.

summary: The lack of a neuronal Stra6 signature should not be interpreted as therapeutic de-risking for systemic STRA6 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Database and genetic context point to a retinol-transporter with developmental and barrier-tissue liabilities and without an established small-molecule pharmacology signal to interpret against this Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: This is a cautionary interpretation, not a direct toxicity measurement.

direction: mostly weak; target transcript usually down but downstream DE absent in most groups
summary: Ppm1g perturbation produced a mostly sub-FDR mouse-brain mRNA phenotype across 22 tested cell groups despite recurrent negative movement of the Ppm1g transcript.
why_it_matters: A nuclear phosphatase with developmental and RNA-processing literature did not produce a broad corrected neuronal DE cascade in this gene-level assay, so the dominant dataset result is a weak or negative transcriptomic response rather than a pathway-wide perturbation.
main_caveats: Most cell types lacked corrected target-transcript knockdown, so the screen cannot distinguish true buffering from insufficient perturbation in those groups.

direction: Ppm1g down with downstream response buffered
summary: 155 MB Glut showed the strongest corrected Ppm1g transcript knockdown but no corrected non-target mRNA response.
why_it_matters: This is the clearest instance where measured guide engagement and downstream buffering can be separated: the target mRNA was substantially reduced, yet no other assayed gene passed 10% FDR.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only gene-level mRNA abundance was measured; protein abundance, phosphatase substrates, splicing changes, cell death, and longer-term states were not assayed.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only cell type with corrected non-target hits after Ppm1g perturbation, consisting of Col4a2 down, Col4a1 down, and H2ac25 up.
why_it_matters: The result elevates a small thalamic module as the only downstream Ppm1g-sensitive mRNA response in the screen, rather than treating all cell types as equivalent nulls.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The downstream signature contains only three corrected genes, and the Ppm1g target transcript in the same cell type was borderline at FDR 0.0537.

summary: Srsf1 was the strongest same-direction perturbation match to the corrected Col4a2/Col4a1/H2ac25 triad in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The neighbor relationship links the only Ppm1g downstream module to SR-splicing-factor perturbation in the same cell type, which is coherent with PPM1G literature around SMN and SRSF-family phosphoregulation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The rank is based on three marker genes, and published PPM1G data implicate SMN and SRSF3 rather than proving a direct PPM1G-SRSF1 relationship.

summary: Mouse-brain Ppm1g mRNA responses were sparse compared with the strong proliferative, survival, and splicing phenotypes reported in developmental and HCC systems.
why_it_matters: PPM1G-directed therapeutic hypotheses should not use this weak neuronal mRNA phenotype as evidence that PPM1G inhibition is either broadly disruptive or broadly safe in neurons; the relevant endpoint may be phosphorylation, splicing, dosage, developmental timing, or tumor context.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset lacks direct viability, protein, phosphoprotein, splice-isoform, and long-term readouts and uses mouse brain cells rather than hepatocellular-carcinoma models.

summary: Zic4 perturbation produced no FDR-supported differential-expression hit in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The dataset slice is dominated by a negative or buffered response rather than by a strong Zic4-induced transcriptional module.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-level DE can reflect failed editing, low Zic4 expression, buffering, or missing cellular contexts.

summary: The Zic4 target transcript itself was not measurably depleted in any Zic4 contrast.
why_it_matters: Zic4 is a nuclear DNA-binding transcriptional regulator, so lack of target-mRNA movement makes target engagement the first caveat for this perturbation.
main_caveats: CRISPR frameshifts do not have to reduce mRNA; sparse Zic4 expression makes logFC unstable.

summary: Zic4 failed to phenocopy Zic1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut despite comparable perturbed-cell counts.
why_it_matters: The result separates two linked ZIC-family disease genes in a thalamic glutamatergic context where Zic1, but not Zic4, generated FDR-supported Slc29a1 up-regulation and self-transcript reduction.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Zic1 signal is cell-type-specific and the Zic4 perturbation lacks direct edit-rate information.

summary: Zic4 perturbation did not activate the reported Zic1/4-to-SHH output program.
why_it_matters: Ptch1, Gli1, and Mycn are the expected Shh-output genes from Zic1/4 mutant cerebellar granule-cell biology, but none showed coordinated or FDR-supported down-regulation here.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset lacks an explicitly assayed cerebellar granule progenitor population, so this is a context-mismatch negative result.

summary: Exploratory signature-neighbor analysis did not uncover a recurrent Zic4-like perturbation module.
why_it_matters: The near-zero Zic-paralog correlations and nonrecurrent top-200-gene neighbors argue that the silent Zic4 slice is not hiding a stable compensatory or convergent ZIC/SHH neighbor response.
main_caveats: The top-200 correlation screen is restricted-signature-based and weak Zic4 effects can make neighbor ranking noisy.

summary: The Zic4 screen gives no activation-versus-loss direction for human disease associations.
why_it_matters: Human ZIC4 has genetic and literature disease links but weak tractability annotations; without target engagement or downstream DE, this Perturb-seq slice should not be used to nominate a ZIC4 inhibition or activation strategy.
main_caveats: Open Targets disease rows are directionless associations, and the ChEMBL query was only a text-search target-record check.

summary: Runx2 perturbation was not transcriptionally engaged and produced no FDR-significant downstream gene in any of the 23 assayed subclasses.
why_it_matters: The primary biological result is a lack of interpretable Runx2 loss-of-function signal; downstream null pathway calls should be attributed first to weak target engagement or expression gating rather than to proof that RUNX2 protein is dispensable.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: CRISPR editing can reduce protein without lowering the assayed transcript, but the DE matrix contains no independent protein or indel validation.

summary: The few largest Runx2 nominal peaks were isolated to individual subclasses and did not define a reproducible cell-type-specific module.
why_it_matters: NP-CT-L6b-OB, midbrain glutamatergic, CNU-MGE GABA, and MB/P/MY GABA cells contain the numerical minima, but each remains below FDR significance and the p<0.001 tail is less recurrent than expected for a coherent Runx2 program.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|155 MB Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|215 MB Dopa|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: This is a negative selectivity finding; the named genes are nominal extrema rather than validated Runx2 targets.

summary: The canonical RUNX2 osteogenic axis, including SP7/BMP/Wnt-associated markers, is silent under Runx2 perturbation even though Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 perturbations show that Wnt-linked transcription is recoverable in the same Perturb-seq screen.
why_it_matters: Prior bone literature treats RUNX2, SP7 and canonical Wnt signaling as a coupled osteoblast-differentiation circuit; the brain-neuronal assay instead separates an active Ctnnb1/Tcf7l2 response from Runx2, arguing against a latent osteoblast-like RUNX2 module in these subclasses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The inference is restricted to transcriptomic effects in neuronal and dopaminergic subclasses; Cbfb itself was not a targeted perturbation in the matrix.

summary: The neuronal null result is consistent with expression-gated RUNX2 biology: available brain references emphasize specialized SCN or immune/macrophage contexts rather than broad assayed neuronal dependence.
why_it_matters: RUNX2 can be biologically relevant in the nervous system, but these data argue that any such role is not widespread across the assayed brain-neuronal subclasses and may require unassayed SCN states, macrophage/microglial cells, development, or stronger target knockdown.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The screen did not separately label suprachiasmatic neurons and did not contain microglia or CNS macrophage classes, so it cannot test those reported contexts directly.

summary: The screen provides no neuronal transcriptomic support for pursuing Runx2 as a brain-neuronal perturbation target despite strong skeletal-disease genetics and sparse direct pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Open Targets links RUNX2 most strongly to skeletal dysplasias, while ChEMBL contains only a few reporter activities and no curated mouse Runx2 mechanism; combining that context with the neuronal null result argues against reading this dataset as evidence for a druggable CNS RUNX2 program.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic warning, not a comprehensive safety or efficacy study across bone, glia, development, or peripheral tissues.

summary: Zfp329 perturbation did not achieve FDR-supported on-target transcript knockdown or downstream DE in any of 22 assayed mouse-brain cell groups; the best target-transcript decreases were nominal in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: The main biological conclusion is that this screen cannot presently define a neuronal Zfp329 transcriptional program, despite Zfp329 being annotated as a nuclear zinc-finger transcriptional regulator.
cell_types: 22 assayed Zfp329 cell groups|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: A negative Wilcoxon/FDR result is solid for this dataset, but weak on-target knockdown prevents any claim that Zfp329 is biologically dispensable.

summary: Nominal Zfp329 effects were cell-type idiosyncratic rather than a recurrent RNA-regulatory module; all 110 p<0.001 rows were single-cell-type events.
why_it_matters: A shared transcription-factor program would be expected to recur across related neuronal contexts; lack of recurrence argues against pathway-level interpretation of individual top nominal genes such as Efr3b, Cibar1, or Krt222.
cell_types: 22 assayed Zfp329 cell groups
main_caveats: The recurrence analysis uses DE outputs only and would miss low-amplitude coordinated effects that are not captured by single-gene nominal p values.

summary: Zfp329 did not phenocopy the assayed broad zinc-finger-family perturbations or stable restricted-signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: This reduces the risk of over-interpreting a weak Zfp329 vector as a member of a common zinc-finger regulatory state and flags the neighbor analysis as hypothesis-generating only.
comparators: Zfp/Zbtb/Zic/Zkscan family perturbations|top positive and negative restricted-signature neighbors
cell_types: 22 assayed Zfp329 cell groups
main_caveats: Correlations are limited by the weak Zfp329 signature; the zinc-finger comparator set is broad and not a curated paralog set.

summary: Bcl2 was not a Zfp329-responsive gene in the mouse-brain panel, so the reported human ZNF329-BCL2 adiposity enhancer mechanism was not recovered as a neuronal readout.
why_it_matters: Known ZNF329 disease mechanisms appear highly tissue- and enhancer-context dependent; this dataset should not be used to infer a brain direction for lipid or central-obesity loci.
comparators: human adiposity BCL2 enhancer axis|human liver lipid caQTL/eQTL locus
cell_types: 22 assayed Zfp329 cell groups
main_caveats: The comparison crosses species, tissue, and perturbation modality, and the weak Zfp329 knockdown makes absence of Bcl2 response only suggestive.

summary: Pex13 perturbation most clearly induced an SREBF2/cholesterol-biosynthesis transcriptional module, with Insig1 as the only corrected Pex13 hit and with nominal recurrence of the same module across multiple neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This links a weak Pex13 perturbation to lipid-homeostasis biology rather than to a generic single-gene outlier, and it matches a known peroxisome-to-SREBP stress axis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only Insig1 passed FDR<0.05; all other member genes were nominal, and the sterol panel is a literature-guided post hoc view.

summary: Across the measured mouse-brain classes, Pex13 produced a highly buffered or weak transcriptomic loss-of-function phenotype despite being a disease-causing peroxisome-import gene.
why_it_matters: The absence of broad FDR-significant downstream DE is a real assay result, but it should not be misread as PEX13 dispensability or therapeutic safety because acute transcript change was weak and inherited PEX13 loss disrupts peroxisome biogenesis.
main_caveats: Pex13 transcript was only nominally reduced in one cell class and protein loss was not measured; the strongest cell classes still had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Pex14, the direct docking-complex partner of PEX13, showed strong FDR-level target knockdown in 066, 151, and 155 cells yet no corrected non-target response, while sharing only a nominal cholesterol-gene upshift with Pex13.
why_it_matters: This argues that perturbing a core partner of the same PEX13-PEX14 translocon is not enough to produce an acute broad peroxisome-collapse transcriptome in these neurons, and that the weak sterol signature is the main reproducible downstream program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Pex13 side of the comparison had weak target-transcript engagement, and Pex14 downstream overlap is nominal rather than FDR-level.

summary: Insig1 is a sensitive but non-specific readout of the sterol-response axis in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut: it is the top Pex13 hit, is included in stronger positive sterol-module neighbors, and moves down when Srebf2 is directly perturbed.
why_it_matters: The opposite Srebf2 comparison anchors the Pex13 direction as SREBF2-like activation rather than a random isolated Insig1 observation, but the top positive neighbors show that Insig1 is a module marker, not a Pex13-specific biomarker.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The positive neighbors are defined by a restricted 23-gene signature panel, and their mechanistic routes to the module were not resolved here.

summary: Pex13 and Pex14 were not phenocopied by every peroxisome-family perturbation assayed: Pex1, Abcd3, Acox1, and Hsd17b4 did not generate a corrected TH response comparable to the Pex13 Insig1 event.
why_it_matters: The data caution against treating all peroxisomal import or lipid-metabolism genes as interchangeable transcriptional perturbations in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations mostly had weak target-transcript knockdown, so absence of phenocopy could reflect guide efficacy or power rather than true pathway separation.

summary: Pcdh15 perturbation produced no FDR-supported depletion of the Pcdh15 transcript and no FDR-supported downstream differential-expression row in any tested brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The most important interpretation is a loss-of-function negative result rather than a clean Pcdh15-null signature; nominal genes downstream of this perturbation should not be treated as validated Pcdh15 effectors.
main_caveats: The parquet contains Wilcoxon summaries rather than raw guide-level expression; a weak transcript row could reflect low endogenous expression, incomplete guide activity, long Pcdh15 isoforms, or true buffering.

summary: The canonical PCDH15/CDH23 tip-link and MET-channel network was transcriptionally silent after Pcdh15 perturbation in brain cells.
why_it_matters: PCDH15 is best established as a proteinaceous adhesion and mechanotransduction component; the dataset does not show compensatory Cdh23, Lhfpl5, Myo7a, Tmie, Tmc, or Usher-gene transcription that would indicate reactivation of the sensory hair-cell module in these neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The principal PCDH15 partners are hair-bundle proteins; absence of transcriptional change in brain-cell summaries does not assay tip-link mechanics or protein localization.

summary: The only plausible cell-type-enriched Pcdh15 signal was a weak, positive-skewed L4/5 IT cortical glutamatergic nominal signature, while the pineal signal was similarly nominal but heavily low-count limited.
why_it_matters: If Pcdh15 has a brain-cell effect in this dataset, L4/5 IT neurons are a better follow-up than the lower-count pineal contrast; Hivep3 and Ep300 are candidates from a nominal screen only.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: All rows had FDR>=0.525 in L4/5 IT and FDR=1.0 in pineal; no external literature directly links the listed nominal markers to PCDH15 in these cell types.

summary: Pcdh15 did not induce a recurrent cross-cell transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: A broadly used Pcdh15 stress, adhesion, or synaptic-homeostasis program would be expected to reuse genes across several neuronal classes; instead almost every nominal hit was cell-type-private.
main_caveats: Recurrence was evaluated on nominal p-value cutoffs because no row crossed FDR<0.05.

summary: The Pcdh15 signature was nearly orthogonal to the available Pcdh19, Adgrv1, and Cdh2 perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: The measured brain response is not a generic cadherin-family or Usher-family signature, and most of the physical PCDH15 tip-link partners were not perturbation targets in the panel.
main_caveats: Pcdh15 itself and the Pcdh19/Adgrv1 comparators lacked FDR-supported on-target knockdown, so orthogonality could partly reflect weak perturbations rather than distinct biology.

summary: This brain Perturb-seq result should not be read as evidence for a PCDH15-inhibition strategy; disease literature and preclinical programs point toward restoring or replacing PCDH15 function.
why_it_matters: USH1F and DFNB23 are loss-of-function sensory disorders, and AAV rescue studies try to add PCDH15 back. The absence of a robust brain knockdown signature here provides no biomarker for safe systemic inhibition and no evidence that reducing Pcdh15 is beneficial.
main_caveats: The dataset was brain-cell CRISPR perturbation rather than inner-ear or retinal gene replacement, so the therapeutic statement comes from literature directionality combined with the dataset's failure to produce a reliable knockdown phenotype.

summary: Tfdp1 perturbation was broadly buffered across the assayed adult brain cell types.
why_it_matters: DP1 is a core E2F cofactor, so the scarcity of FDR-significant basal transcriptomic changes argues that most profiled neuronal classes were not acutely dependent on measured Tfdp1 dosage for an E2F cell-cycle program.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was only nominally reduced and never FDR-significant, so buffered biology and weak perturbation efficacy cannot be fully separated.

summary: The only FDR-significant Tfdp1 downstream response was a two-gene, positive signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: This localizes the best high-confidence signal to one cell type and shows that the response was not a broad, multi-cell-type G1/S wave.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The same cell type did not show detectable Tfdp1 target-transcript depletion, so the two FDR hits require validation at guide, protein, or replication level.

summary: Several cell types showed nominal Tfdp1 transcript decrease without any FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The negative result was strongest where Tfdp1 mRNA knockdown looked most apparent, arguing against a ubiquitous immediate transcriptional requirement for TFDP1 in the basal dataset.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Target-transcript tests were nominal rather than FDR-significant; absence of FDR genes can reflect partial knockdown, low expression of cycling genes, or insufficient power for small effects.

summary: In the 151 signature-neighbor analysis, Rb1 and E2f4 were the closest positive neighbors of Tfdp1, but E2F/DP-family perturbations were far from interchangeable.
why_it_matters: The top-neighbor ranks preserve weak convergence with the pRB/E2F module, while the much larger Rb1 and E2f4 signatures and the flat Tfdp2/E2f1/E2f5 profiles show that membership in the same complex does not predict equal perturbation output in adult brain cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations to Tfdp1 were statistically ranked but small in magnitude; the perturbations had different cell counts and only Rb1 was assayed in a subset of cell types.

summary: The basal dataset does not rule out TFDP1 involvement in neuronal injury programs.
why_it_matters: Dominant-negative DP1 can protect neurons in DNA-damage paradigms, but the present unchallenged Perturb-seq profile mainly reports buffered steady-state transcription; using it as a negative test of genotoxic E2F/DP apoptosis would overinterpret the assay context.
main_caveats: No DNA-damage or neurodegeneration challenge was assayed, and on-target transcript engagement was weak.

summary: Lgals3 perturbation produced no detectable on-target Lgals3 transcript depletion and no FDR-level downstream transcriptome in the screened neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The primary biological interpretation is absence of an interpretable Galectin-3 loss-of-function state in this dataset rather than a weak but coherent neuronal Lgals3 program.
main_caveats: The conclusion is constrained to readouts in the assayed neuronal cell classes; most signatures had fewer than 100 perturbed cells.

summary: The neuronal null refines Galectin-3 neuroinflammation biology by placing the productive LGALS3-TLR4/TREM2 axis outside these unstimulated neuronal populations.
why_it_matters: Prior work makes Galectin-3 a microglial damage-response ligand; the Perturb-seq result argues that this module is not cell-autonomous to the profiled neurons and would need glia or inflammatory context for evaluation.
main_caveats: Species overlaps for mouse are good, but the cited responses use microglia, disease or inflammatory stimulation rather than the neuronal Perturb-seq state.

summary: Perturbations of Galectin-3-linked innate receptors and myeloid pathway neighbors were also silent and did not converge with Lgals3.
why_it_matters: This converts an isolated Lgals3 negative into a module-level absence: Trem2, Tlr2/Tlr4, Csf1r, Axl/Mertk, C3, Cd36, Itgb2 and Cx3cr1 were not effectively expressed/engaged by the same transcriptomic criterion.
main_caveats: The comparator list samples known innate and receptor neighbors but is not a complete Galectin-3 interactome; lack of convergence is assessed from restricted transcriptomic signatures.

summary: The only strong Lgals3 signature-neighbor plume was an exploratory 308 CB GABA pattern aligned with Fbxo11/Dnajb4/Gabrb1 and opposed to Wdr26/Dstyk/Cckar rather than to Galectin-3 biology.
why_it_matters: It flags a cell-class-restricted off-axis pattern that should not be mistaken for a Galectin-3 receptor module or therapeutic direction.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Signature cosine is not causal; the Lgals3 transcript itself was not engaged in 308 CB GABA.

summary: Galectin-3 is chemically tractable, but this neuronal screen is a poor standalone pharmacodynamic assay for Galectin-3 inhibitors.
why_it_matters: Galectin-3 ligands can be tested biochemically and some suppress TREM2-Galectin-3 signaling in activated microglia, whereas the dataset lacks the target and receptor context needed to infer neuroinflammatory efficacy or safety.
main_caveats: The dataset tests genetic transcript perturbations rather than extracellular Galectin-3 protein blockade and lacks activated microglia.

summary: St3gal5, a ganglioside GM3 synthase comparator, showed strong target-mRNA depletion but almost no secondary transcriptional cascade.
why_it_matters: This shows that some glycan-surface perturbations can be technically engaged yet transcriptionally buffered in the neuronal panel, making weak transcriptional readout a plausible biology of the assayed state rather than only a guide-delivery issue.
main_caveats: St3gal5 is glycosylation-adjacent rather than an LGALS3 paralog or direct receptor, so it is a context comparator only.

summary: The experiment did not achieve convincing Tbc1d23 mRNA loss in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: TBC1D23 is a recessive neurodevelopmental disease gene, so a null transcriptome cannot be read as neuronal dispensability unless the perturbation first produces loss of target RNA or protein.
main_caveats: The parquet reports mRNA differential expression only; it does not verify guide activity, editing, isoform targeting, or TBC1D23 protein loss.

summary: Sampled neuronal classes, including the cerebellar GABA class and the largest thalamic contrast, showed no FDR-supported acute transcriptional response to Tbc1d23 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Human PCH and developmental models point to brainstem, cerebellar, and cortical-development requirements; the dataset suggests that the assayed state either was not sufficiently depleted or was not the right developmental/subcellular context to expose that mechanism in steady-state mRNA.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Absence of DE is dominated by weak target engagement and modest perturbed-cell counts; it is not proof that TBC1D23 is unimportant in cerebellar or pontine development.

summary: Tbc1d23 failed to converge with the measured WASH/TBC comparators and had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor, despite other trafficking genes being detectable in the same DE workflow.
why_it_matters: The known TBC1D23-WDR11-WASH-golgin machinery did not appear as a shared transcriptional module; the most parsimonious interpretation is an uninformative Tbc1d23 perturbation rather than a specific WASH or endosome-to-Golgi phenotype.
main_caveats: The closest direct AP-1-vesicle partners Wdr11, Fam91a1, Golga1, and Golga4 were not available as perturbations in the analyzed comparator set; correlations were computed on weak subthreshold Tbc1d23 profiles.

summary: A single-cell mRNA Wilcoxon readout did not capture transcriptional consequences of TBC1D23 pathways that are primarily vesicle-tethering, Golgi signaling, or immune-maintenance mechanisms.
why_it_matters: TBC1D23 biology is organized around subcellular localization and protein interactions at the trans-Golgi; failure to induce an mRNA signature argues that future assays should measure Golgi/endosomal trafficking, local LKB1-AMPK activity, or immune challenge responses rather than relying only on basal neuronal transcriptomes.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay vesicle trafficking, Golgi AMPK phosphorylation, or LPS/TLR stimulation, and weak Tbc1d23 knockdown is sufficient to explain the lack of an mRNA response.

summary: Trappc10 perturbation produced consistently negative target-transcript logFCs but no FDR-significant downstream genes across 22 measured mouse brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports broad transcriptional buffering or insufficient functional depletion of a known TRAPP II vesicle-tethering subunit, so the main result is a biologically meaningful negative result rather than a pathway activation signature.
main_caveats: On-target RNA knockdown was weak and never FDR-significant; mRNA measurements may miss trafficking or protein-level phenotypes.

summary: 155 MB Glut contained the strongest Trappc10-associated nominal response, led by Jund, but the cell type still had zero FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: If Trappc10 is revisited, 155 MB Glut is the best dataset-nominated context and Jund is the best candidate transcriptomic sentinel, but both are exploratory.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The best downstream FDR was 0.079, above 0.05; this is a single-cell-type nominal signal.

summary: Trappc9 and Trappc6b, the only closely related TRAPP perturbations available here, were FDR-null like Trappc10 and did not show strong positive signature correlations with it.
why_it_matters: A shared TRAPP loss-of-function mRNA program was not recovered even though TRAPPC10, TRAPPC9, and TRAPPC6B belong to the same annotated trafficking machinery and have neurodevelopmental relevance.
main_caveats: All three signatures are weak, which limits the interpretability of target-target correlations.

summary: Vps35, Sec23a, and Sec31a generated significant signatures whereas Trappc10 did not, separating the quiet TRAPP response from more detectable vesicle/endosomal/COPII perturbations.
why_it_matters: This argues that at least some membrane-trafficking perturbations were observable in the screen; the Trappc10 result is not a blanket failure to detect vesicle biology.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Vps35 is endosomal/retromer and Sec23a/Sec31a are COPII comparators, not TRAPPC10 paralogs or complex members.

summary: Nominal Trappc10 genes were not recurrent across cell types and Trappc10 lacked a high-correlation positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak top genes are better treated as cell-restricted or stochastic candidates than as a conserved TRAPPC10 transcriptional module.
main_caveats: The recurrence analysis used nominal p-value thresholds and the neighbor analysis was score-correlation based.

summary: Safe_target_97 is a transcriptomically inert safe-targeting control at FDR 0.05 across all 19 measured mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The strongest interpretation is a negative control result: the guide label does not perturb a recurrent biological program detectable by Wilcoxon DE against Non_target cells.
main_caveats: The target transcript is not measurable, so this tests downstream expression only; it does not quantify editing at the genomic safe-target locus.

summary: The apparent peaks in CNU-HYa HY GABA and L2/3 IT glutamatergic classes are nominal ranking events, not corrected cell-type-selective Safe_target_97 biology.
why_it_matters: Without this distinction, isolated low p values for Rogdi, Ccnyl1, or Cntnap1 could be mistaken for biomarkers even though their adjusted p values are 0.46-0.78.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The named genes are top nominal rows only and none passes FDR correction.

summary: Safe_target_97 has no reproducible sister-control signature across the Safe_target family.
why_it_matters: A correlated signature among Safe_target controls would have implied a generic guide-class artifact; the observed correlations are essentially zero and argue against preserving any Safe_target_97 pathway module.
main_caveats: The correlation analysis was restricted to other Safe_target controls rather than every programmed gene in the screen.

summary: Even the best-powered Safe_target_97 stratum, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, remained buffered with zero FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: This separates low-count absence from a stronger negative case: 101 perturbed cells were available in this class, yet the best nominal row, Ank3, still had FDR = 1.0.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Absence of corrected DE does not exclude rare DNA-damage responses outside the assayed cells or responses below this study's power.

summary: Zfp1 perturbation was globally buffered, with no q<0.10 DE genes and only one q<0.25 gene across all 23 measured mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: This is the primary result: the perturbation did not elicit a reproducible multi-gene cell-state shift in the measured transcriptomes.
main_caveats: Strongly limited by weak RNA-level target engagement and uneven perturbed-cell counts.

summary: The target transcript itself was not detectably knocked down in any profiled cell type.
why_it_matters: A negative downstream screen is hard to interpret unless the perturbation engages the target; here the on-target RNA rows support non-engagement or an assay modality that does not deplete transcript.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an imperfect proxy if the guides perturb DNA or protein without changing RNA stability.

summary: Fam229b up-regulation in 191 MB P MY GABA was the sole adjusted-P<0.25 downstream effect of Zfp1.
why_it_matters: The result nominates a single exploratory marker for a cell-type-restricted Zfp1 response rather than a shared pathway.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The FDR was 0.135, the effect was single-gene, and Fam229b did not recur across other cell types.

summary: No strong Zfp1-like or anti-Zfp1 signature neighbor was found in the restricted top-100-gene scans.
why_it_matters: Weak neighbors argue that the faint Zfp1 signature should not be over-assigned to another assayed receptor, transcription factor, or signaling pathway.
main_caveats: The comparison used only the 100 largest absolute Zfp1 score genes per cell type and is therefore a restricted, noisy signature analysis.

summary: Zfp1's KRAB/C2H2 transcription-factor annotation did not translate into an observed broad downstream transcriptional response in this mouse-brain assay.
why_it_matters: It refines the prior that a nuclear KRAB zinc-finger protein should perturb transcription by showing that this specific dataset provides little functional pathway readout for Zfp1.
main_caveats: Because target RNA was not reduced, the result cannot distinguish true buffering from an inefficient perturbation.

summary: Existing human ZFP1 disease and druggability annotations are too indirect to infer a therapeutic direction from the weak mouse-brain Perturb-seq signature.
why_it_matters: It prevents a single gastric-cancer biomarker report or low-scoring disease database links from being over-interpreted as evidence that Zfp1 should be therapeutically targeted in brain cells.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment was not a disease model or druggability assay, and the ChEMBL text search is a database absence rather than proof of undruggability.

summary: Tlr8 CRISPRi was largely transcriptionally inert across the profiled mouse neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The main biological readout is a negative one: low or unmeasured Tlr8 target RNA and 1 corrected hit among 321895 tests mean this dataset should not be read as a broad TLR8 loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: DE-only evidence; absent target-gene rows imply low expression or filtering rather than a direct count of zero RNA; many cell types had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: Cnpy3 up-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA was the sole FDR-significant Tlr8 response and points to TLR receptor biogenesis rather than NF-kappaB/IFN effector activation.
why_it_matters: CNPY3 is a known ER cochaperone for TLR folding, so the only robust gene is in a receptor-handling module; the effect did not propagate to cytokine, chemokine, IRF, or ISG markers.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Single-gene corrected signal from 31 perturbed cells; Tlr8 itself was not measured in this cell type's DE table, so the Cnpy3 effect could reflect indirect or guide-specific biology.

summary: The 054 CNU-MGE Cnpy3 response was not shared by Tlr7, Tlr9, Tbk1, or other assayed TLR/NF-kappaB neighbors.
why_it_matters: Reactome groups TLR7/8/9 in endosomal MyD88 biology and mouse immune studies couple Tlr8 to Tlr7 dosage, but the Cnpy3 transcriptomic response was Tlr8-selective in this neuronal class.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Comparator rows were also weakly engaged at their own target transcripts; Cnpy3 after Tbk1 was nominal but lost all FDR support.

summary: The only corrected Tlr8 effect was confined to 054 CNU-MGE GABA and was absent from 052 Pvalb Gaba despite prior adult hippocampal PVALB/SST TLR8 protein reports.
why_it_matters: The result narrows neuronal TLR8 responsiveness to a small MGE-derived population in this assay rather than a pan-GABAergic or broad Pvalb program.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The literature is hippocampus/protein/stimulation focused, whereas the dataset uses broad transcriptomic cell classes and CRISPRi with low Tlr8 RNA.

summary: The mouse-brain Tlr8 perturbation did not model the inflammatory program targeted by human TLR8 agonists or antagonists.
why_it_matters: TLR8 is druggable and disease linked in immune settings, but this neuronal CRISPRi context lacks Tlr8 target engagement and lacks cytokine, chemokine, and interferon output; therapeutic direction should therefore be inferred from myeloid models, not from this negative brain signature.
main_caveats: The dataset tested basal CRISPRi perturbation rather than acute ligand activation or inhibition in human monocytes, macrophages, or dendritic cells.

summary: Zfp961 produced a screen-wide negative result: no gene reached FDR<0.05 in any measured cell type, and the Zfp961 transcript itself was not reproducibly depleted.
why_it_matters: This makes the perturbation primarily a weak-engagement result rather than evidence for a broad neuronal Zfp961 transcriptional program.
main_caveats: The absence of a corrected response is inseparable from weak or inconsistent measured target-transcript engagement.

summary: The only near-corrected Zfp961 response was restricted to 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, where Dctn2 increased and Strn4 decreased at FDR<0.1 but not FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: This nominates a narrow CA1/amygdala glutamatergic context for follow-up while clearly falling below a conventional 5% FDR threshold.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Only 44 perturbed cells were available and neither hit crossed FDR<0.05.

summary: Zfp961 did not yield a recurrent gene module or a robust positive or inverse signature neighbor across cell types.
why_it_matters: The data do not support treating any nominal gene list as a pan-neuronal Zfp961 effector module.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and remain transcriptomic, not chromatin or repeat-element, comparisons.

summary: SETDB1 and CHD4 chromatin perturbations were readily detected in the same dataset, but their signatures remained uncoupled from Zfp961.
why_it_matters: The weak Zfp961 phenotype is not simply a dataset-wide failure to detect chromatin-factor biology; instead, this KRAB-ZFP appears far narrower, weakly engaged, or silent in these neuronal states compared with broader repression machinery perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Trim28/Kap1 itself was not perturbed in this comparison, and CHD4 is not specific to KRAB repression.

summary: The adipose and hepatic PPAR/lipoprotein functions assigned to ZFP961 in the literature were not mirrored by a neuronal PPAR, thermogenic, or apolipoprotein marker response in this screen.
why_it_matters: Peripheral metabolic phenotypes should not be projected onto mouse-brain cell types without context-specific validation of both target engagement and the downstream PPAR/lipogenic axis.
main_caveats: Brain neuronal cell types, basal Perturb-seq, and single-cell mRNA readouts are indirect matches to stimulated adipocytes and liver knockdown models.

summary: Zfp961 remains an indirect and poorly pharmacologically annotated transcription-factor target for brain applications.
why_it_matters: Combining no direct ChEMBL target record with the lack of a corrected neuronal pharmacodynamic signature argues against using this dataset to nominate direct Zfp961 modulation as a brain therapeutic strategy.
main_caveats: Absence from ChEMBL is not proof of undruggability, and human orthology for rapidly evolving KRAB-ZFPs is ambiguous.

summary: Smpd3 mRNA depletion was directionally consistent but only nominal and cell-type dependent across the Perturb-seq atlas.
why_it_matters: Interpretation of downstream Smpd3 phenotypes should be anchored on partial mRNA engagement rather than assuming a uniform knockout.
main_caveats: The target transcript failed FDR correction in every cell type, so engagement is inferred from directional and nominal evidence only.

summary: Pvalb, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, and CNU-LGE GABA cells showed nominal Smpd3 knockdown but almost no downstream transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: This separates target engagement from immediate RNA-state remodeling and suggests that partial Smpd3 depletion is either buffered or not well assayed by steady-state single-cell mRNA.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Negative downstream evidence is constrained by partial knockdown, single time point transcriptomics, and lack of lipid or protein-transport measurements.

summary: The strongest nominal Smpd3 signatures did not coincide with the strongest observed Smpd3 transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: Top genes such as Timm8b, Plekhn1, and Cox19 are not reliable Smpd3 biomarkers without orthogonal validation because their host signatures had weak or absent target engagement and no adjusted hits.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: This is an internal consistency warning, not proof that the nominal genes are false positives.

summary: Smpd3 perturbation did not trigger an adjusted transcriptional feedback program among sphingomyelinase paralogs, ceramide enzymes, or TNF/TNFR1-neighborhood genes.
why_it_matters: The expected biology of SMPD3 is lipid hydrolysis; the dataset argues that any ceramide compensation is not captured as a robust mRNA response of canonical sphingolipid enzymes.
main_caveats: Many lipid enzymes may be regulated post-translationally or by substrate availability, and lowly expressed members have limited power in single-cell RNA-seq.

summary: The measured ceramide/TNFR1-neighborhood perturbations Asah1 and Tnfrsf1a were essentially uncorrelated with Smpd3 signatures in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: Reactome pathway proximity did not translate into an interchangeable transcriptional perturbation module in this assay.
main_caveats: Only two pathway-neighbor perturbations were available, correlations were computed on weak signatures, and absence of mRNA similarity does not exclude shared lipid outputs.

summary: Weak transcriptomic neighbors around Smpd3 should not be read as evidence of weak neuronal liability for SMPD3 inhibition.
why_it_matters: nSMase2 is a membrane lipid enzyme with mouse neuronal Golgi and cognitive loss-of-function phenotypes; a pooled scRNA-seq assay lacking lipid, vesicle-trafficking, and long-term degeneration readouts could miss the disease-relevant axis.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The report does not test pharmacologic SMPD3 inhibition, lipid turnover, or neuronal aging directly.

summary: Nr1d1 generated a genome-wide FDR response only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons.
why_it_matters: The interpretable Nr1d1 effect in this dataset is thalamic and cell-class restricted rather than a broadly shared neuronal response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a statistical restriction in the measured classes; absence of FDR hits elsewhere does not prove absence of subtle biology.

summary: The 151-class Nr1d1 signature activates a clock-output module containing Npas2, Cry2, Dbp, and Nfil3, with nominal movement of Arntl and Rora.
why_it_matters: The significant genes map the strongest dataset response onto the canonical REV-ERB/ROR/BMAL1 circadian network instead of an unrelated stress program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Npas2, Cry2, Dbp, and Nfil3 passed FDR in the thalamic Nr1d1 table; Arntl, Clock, Nr1d2, and Rora were nominal or weaker.

summary: Nr1d2 and Bmal1 are close positive neighbors of the thalamic Nr1d1 signature, whereas Rora is anti-correlated and Rorb/Rorc are weak in the same class.
why_it_matters: Related circadian nuclear receptors split by regulatory role: a REV-ERB paralog partially phenocopies the Nr1d1 signature, while the ROR activator branch is not interchangeable with it.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only over the 116 genes that were FDR-significant for Nr1d1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; Bmal1 full-transcriptome DE was not extracted.

summary: Nr1d1 mRNA was not detectably depleted and 22 of 23 measured classes had no FDR-positive downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation should be interpreted as a guide-associated transcriptional state rather than as a validated transcript-level knockdown in every cell type.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: CRISPR perturbations can affect protein without lowering mRNA; the parquet lacks protein, indel, and guide-level validation.

summary: Erc2, Pdgfa, L1cam, Rnf130, and Timp3 are high-amplitude non-clock markers of the thalamic Nr1d1 state.
why_it_matters: These genes provide dataset-grounded biomarkers for the strongest Nr1d1 response and show that the thalamic phenotype extends beyond named core clock genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The marker ranking is robust in the thalamic DE table, but the mechanistic bridge from NR1D1 to these genes is not established here.

summary: The thalamic Nr1d1 clock signature flags Npas2, Cry2, Dbp, and Nfil3 as neuronal biomarkers to monitor during REV-ERB pharmacology.
why_it_matters: NR1D1 is ligandable and synthetic REV-ERB agonists affect mouse behavior, so brain programs should watch for thalamic clock and clock-output transcription rather than relying only on peripheral liver readouts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset is a genetic Perturb-seq contrast, not timed treatment with a REV-ERB agonist or antagonist.

summary: Rxylt1 depletion was directionally consistent but transcriptionally buffered across neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: RXYLT1 is a Golgi matriglycan enzyme, so a loss of enzymatic glycosylation can be biologically important without immediately generating a large mRNA program.
main_caveats: Target knockdown itself was sub-FDR in every cell type and many cell-type tests had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the clearest engaged Rxylt1 context, while 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had the largest target logFC at lower cell count.
why_it_matters: The best evidence for on-target perturbation is concentrated in a small number of subclasses, but even these did not convert Rxylt1 depletion into FDR-significant downstream transcription.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Both observations remain nominal; the L5 ET estimate used only 45 perturbed cells.

summary: Rbm7 in 191 MB P MY GABA and Czib in 053 Sst Gaba were the closest Rxylt1-responsive marker candidates but neither reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: These two transcripts are useful only as exploratory follow-up markers because they were isolated to different cell classes and were not reproducible components of a matriglycan signature.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Rbm7 had only q=0.0915; Czib had q=0.1589 and occurred where the Rxylt1 transcript was barely depleted.

summary: Rxylt1 did not phenocopy Fktn, Large1, Dag1, or Dpm1 at the scRNA-seq signature level despite belonging to the same dystroglycan glycosylation pathway neighborhood.
why_it_matters: Biochemical pathway membership was not interchangeable with acute neuronal mRNA output in this assay, so pathway-neighbor perturbations cannot be used as redundant readouts for Rxylt1.
main_caveats: The contrast is limited by weak Rxylt1 knockdown and by using scRNA correlations rather than matriglycan abundance.

summary: No strong positive or negative whole-perturbation neighbor was detectable for Rxylt1 in the best engaged 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class.
why_it_matters: The Rxylt1 phenotype was not hiding inside another obvious perturbation module; even unrestricted genome-scale signature matching produced only near-zero correlations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Computed only in the clearest on-target cell class and on score vectors, not validated by protein or glycan assays.

summary: The severe RXYLT1 brain-disease mechanism is not reproduced here as an acute, cell-autonomous neuronal mRNA program.
why_it_matters: Human and model-organism data implicate RXYLT1 in alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation and developmental brain malformation; the Perturb-seq result instead points to a post-translational or non-cell-autonomous structural defect that is delayed or buffered in the sampled neuronal transcriptomes.
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure alpha-dystroglycan glycoforms, basement-membrane integrity, radial migration, or long developmental outcomes.

direction: down in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
summary: Trim2 perturbation produced its only FDR-significant non-self transcriptional response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, led by down-regulation of App and Cntn1 and an exploratory synapse/cell-junction negative module.
why_it_matters: The strongest dataset signal is not a pan-neuronal collapse after target knockdown; it is a thalamic glutamatergic context in which loss of Trim2 is connected to neuronal-adhesion and synaptic genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only App and Cntn1 pass FDR<0.05; the broader synaptic module is based on top-ranked nominal genes and the measured Trim2 self row has FDR=0.129 in this cell type.

summary: Most measured cell types buffered Trim2 perturbation, including three classes with nominal self-transcript reduction but no transcriptome-wide FDR response.
why_it_matters: TRIM2 is a brain-expressed neuronal E3 ligase, yet acute RNA output after partial Trim2 depletion is highly cell-context dependent rather than uniformly neurotoxic.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Buffered calls rest on nominal on-target RNA decreases; lack of RNA response cannot exclude protein-level or delayed phenotypes.

summary: The canonical neurofilament axis was not transcriptionally induced by Trim2 perturbation in the responsive thalamic glutamatergic class.
why_it_matters: Published TRIM2 loss-of-function disease mechanisms center on failure to ubiquitinate NEFL protein; this Perturb-seq response instead reads out App/Cntn1 down-regulation without Nefl, Nefm or Nefh mRNA accumulation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Protein accumulation of NEFL was not measured, and Nefl knockdown is not directionally equivalent to NEFL protein buildup after TRIM2 loss.

summary: Trim3 mRNA did not compensate for Trim2 knockdown, despite the known TRIM2-TRIM3 physical and regulatory relationship.
why_it_matters: The acute response did not engage a simple paralog-transcription feedback loop, so any TRIM3 buffering of TRIM2 is more likely to be post-transcriptional or absent in these contexts.
main_caveats: Only Trim3 RNA abundance was assayed; TRIM3 protein abundance, heteromer stoichiometry and E3 activity were not measured.

summary: The 151 TH Trim2 expression program was not reproduced by the broad TRIM-family comparator Trim37 or by knockdown of the canonical substrate Nefl or output genes App and Cntn1.
why_it_matters: This argues that the observed thalamic module is not a generic consequence of perturbing a TRIM E3 ligase, the NEFL transcript, or the two most significant downstream genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Trim37 is not the direct class-VII paralog TRIM3, and the correlations use RNA profiles from one cell type.

summary: No perturbation in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature space was a strong positive or negative Trim2 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The lack of a close transcriptomic mimic means that a single obvious upstream pathway replacement was not present among the 2045 other targeted genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Pearson correlations were computed on rank-like Wilcoxon scores in one cell type and only over perturbations present in the library.

direction: warning against simple loss-of-function therapeutic interpretation
summary: The modest App transcript decrease after Trim2 perturbation should not be interpreted as evidence that TRIM2 inhibition is a safe APP-lowering strategy.
why_it_matters: Human TRIM2 loss of function is linked to CMT2R/axonal neuropathy, while the APP signal here is small, acute, restricted to one mouse thalamic class and accompanied by other neuronal-adhesion changes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No APP protein, amyloid processing, peripheral nerve or long-term viability phenotypes were measured.

summary: Pik3ca knockdown was directionally detectable at the target transcript level but produced no FDR-significant downstream DE in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: PIK3CA is a catalytic PI3K node, so the observed silence is a biologically meaningful negative or buffered response rather than a search failure.
main_caveats: Target-transcript knockdown was not significant after multiple testing; the dataset measures RNA rather than PIP3, AKT phosphorylation, or mTORC1 activity.

summary: Nominal on-target Pik3ca depletion was concentrated in thalamic and GABAergic/caudal cell classes, with little evidence for a comparable target-transcript response in most cortical glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: This suggests that either Pik3ca expression, knockdown efficiency, or detectable RNA-level tolerance differs across neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type pattern is based on nominal target-transcript p values; none of the target rows passed FDR correction.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut neurons, perturbing Pten, Tsc1, Tsc2, or Mtor yielded FDR-significant DE whereas Pik3ca did not.
why_it_matters: The thalamic data separate strong transcriptomic sensitivity to the TSC/mTOR branch from weak RNA-level sensitivity to upstream PIK3CA depletion.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a between-perturbation contrast with different guide counts and target-engagement strengths; it does not prove that PIK3CA is biochemically inactive.

summary: Pten was the strongest negative Pik3ca signature neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The direction is consistent with PTEN opposing PI3K/PIP3 production and provides a weak but interpretable antagonist relationship inside an otherwise small Pik3ca signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The absolute correlation was small and is useful mainly by rank among same-cell-type perturbations.

summary: Assayed class-IA PI3K catalytic and regulatory relatives did not phenocopy Pik3ca: Pik3cb, Pik3r1, and Pik3r2 all lacked FDR-significant rows and had near-zero median score correlations to Pik3ca.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating single-subunit PI3K perturbations as interchangeable transcriptomic proxies in this dataset.
main_caveats: The comparator perturbations were themselves weak, so absence of convergence may reflect low engagement rather than true biochemical divergence.

summary: The mouse Perturb-seq Pik3ca loss-of-function signature should not be read as a direct PROS or cortical-malformation disease-reversal signature.
why_it_matters: Human PROS and many PIK3CA-associated brain malformations are driven by activating mosaic PIK3CA variants, while this dataset mostly shows partial wild-type Pik3ca depletion with minimal RNA output.
main_caveats: A PI3K-alpha inhibitor is therapeutically relevant to PIK3CA gain of function, but wild-type neuronal knockdown is not equivalent to allele-selective suppression in mutant overgrowth tissue.

summary: Rnf216 produced no FDR-significant transcriptome response in any assayed neuronal group.
why_it_matters: RNF216 has well described ubiquitin-ligase outputs in immune, autophagy, and neuronal protein-turnover systems, so the Perturb-seq layer argues that these programs were not measurably driven at the mRNA level under this perturbation.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant DE does not prove biological dispensability because target engagement was weak and protein ubiquitination was not measured.

direction: weak target-transcript decrease with buffered downstream output
summary: The nominally lower Rnf216 transcript did not create a strong downstream signature.
why_it_matters: The target itself trended downward in most cell types, yet every Rnf216 on-target row had pvals_adj=1.0; the dataset therefore reads as either incomplete knockdown, compensation, or assay buffering rather than a clean loss-of-function model.
main_caveats: Guide activity and RNF216 protein abundance were not measured; several cell types had fewer than 60 targeted cells.

summary: Rnf216 did not phenocopy curated TLR/IL-1/NF-kappaB/IRF or BECN1-autophagy neighbors.
why_it_matters: The library contained many proximal targets or pathway readouts that should expose a broad innate-immune or autophagy module if the neuronal Rnf216 perturbation were driving those axes; instead, same-cell correlations were near zero and direct canonical transcripts were not FDR significant.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptome-based; RNF216 substrates are often regulated by ubiquitination and degradation, and several complex or adaptor genes such as OTUD4, USP8, RIPK1, TIRAP, MYD88, and TRAF6 were not perturbations in this library.

summary: The only concentrated scalar structure around Rnf216 was an exploratory CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic nominal signature.
why_it_matters: Unlike the other 21 Rnf216 contexts, the CA3 group contained the smallest Rnf216 adjusted p value, the largest number of nominal genes, and all high absolute genome-wide signature-neighbor correlations; this makes CA3 the one hypothesis-generating neuronal context, although not an FDR-supported effect.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: No gene in CA3 passed FDR; top positive and negative signature neighbors were low-amplitude correlations and did not map onto a known RNF216 complex.

direction: RNF216 loss-of-function is clinically hazardous despite weak screen readout
summary: The weak neuronal readout should not be interpreted as safety for reducing RNF216 activity.
why_it_matters: Human RNF216 loss-of-function causes Gordon-Holmes neuroendocrine and neurodegenerative disease, and RNF216 inhibition has been proposed mechanistically to de-repress BECN1 autophagy; the dataset did not show a strong neuronal transcriptomic liability, but its weak target engagement means it cannot de-risk loss-of-function strategies.
main_caveats: Therapeutic inference is indirect: the screen used mouse neuronal classes, not human GnRH neurons or cerebellar degeneration assays, and no drug exposure was tested.

summary: Stim1 knockdown was detectable but not FDR-significant, and the best on-target signal was concentrated in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Interpretation of any downstream Stim1 signature should be weighted toward these two cell types; many other groups had weaker transcript loss or small perturbed-cell counts.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The on-target rows were nominally significant but did not pass FDR<0.05.

summary: Stim1 depletion produced essentially no FDR-level transcriptional response across all assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: STIM1 is a core ER calcium sensor, but partial loss of its transcript in this assay did not convert to a broad mRNA program, consistent with buffering, insufficient perturbation depth, or primarily electrophysiological calcium phenotypes.
main_caveats: Negative at the transcriptome/FDR level only; the dataset does not assay acute calcium flux, CRAC currents, or firing.

summary: Stim1 and Atp2a2 were not interchangeable ER-calcium perturbations: Atp2a2 loss induced Ddit3/Chac1/Xbp1/Hspa5/Asns stress genes, whereas matched Stim1 signatures were uncorrelated and lacked those markers.
why_it_matters: Within the same neuronal classes, the ER Ca2+ pump produced a robust ER-stress-like transcriptional state while the store-operated entry sensor did not, separating ER Ca2+ reuptake stress from loss of STIM1-mediated calcium entry.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptional; it does not test whether STIM1 and ATP2A2 have shared calcium-flux phenotypes immediately after stimulation.

summary: No robust positive or negative Stim1 signature neighbor was recovered, and the library did not perturb the closest STIM/Orai complex members.
why_it_matters: The weak Stim1 signature should not be over-clustered with unrelated perturbations; the most mechanistically direct convergence test with Stim2 or Orai1/2/3 was unavailable.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from weak Stim1 score vectors; absence of complex members in the library prevents a direct STIM1-STIM2-ORAI test.

summary: The cerebellar GABA Stim1 result was nominally on-target but transcriptionally silent, despite Purkinje-neuron literature showing calcium and firing phenotypes after Stim1 loss.
why_it_matters: A broad single-cell mRNA signature can miss STIM1 biology that is cell-subclass-specific, late, or physiological rather than transcriptional.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA is not an isolated Purkinje-neuron population, and Stim1 target suppression in this group had FDR=1.0.

summary: Prdm10 produces its clearest transcriptomic responses in thalamic, midbrain, and hypothalamic classes rather than broadly across cortex.
why_it_matters: This moves PRDM10 from a generic developmental transcription-factor expectation to a restricted mouse-brain vulnerability focused in non-cortical neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut

summary: A recurrent Madd/Cadm3/Ptov1-centered negative module follows Prdm10 perturbation across multiple responding neuronal classes.

summary: Many Prdm10 cell classes, including several cortical or CTX-CGE classes, have no FDR-significant downstream response.

summary: Unbiased same-cell signature-neighbor analysis did not find a close Prdm10 phenocopy or strong opposite perturbation.

summary: The PRDM10-FLCN axis is detectable only in MB Glut, while Eif3b and Septin11 canonical developmental targets are not recovered at FDR in the brain contrasts.

main_caveats: Flcn passes FDR in only one cell class; Eif3b and Septin11 absence is transcript-level and does not rule out other translation or cytoskeletal effects.

summary: Rptor perturbation produced a globally buffered transcriptional phenotype: the target transcript was sometimes nominally reduced, but no gene in any assayed cell type reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: RPTOR is the substrate-recruiting scaffold of mTORC1, so this result separates partial transcript knockdown from a robust loss-of-mTORC1 transcriptional state in this perturbation assay.
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA rather than loss of RPTOR protein or phosphorylation of mTORC1 substrates; all Rptor gene-level effects are nominal after correction.

summary: Measurable Rptor mRNA depletion was concentrated in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, whereas several well-sampled cortical and inhibitory classes were nearly silent for the target transcript itself.
why_it_matters: The dominant source of apparent Rptor cell-type selectivity is target engagement, not a downstream pathway that remained strong once the Rptor transcript was equally depleted everywhere.

summary: The weak Rptor signature nonetheless aligned with pathway wiring: Mtor was among the top positive whole-dataset neighbors, while Tsc1 and Tsc2 were the strongest expected negative mTOR-axis neighbors.
why_it_matters: TSC1/TSC2 loss should disinhibit RHEB and activate mTORC1, the opposite of RPTOR or MTOR loss; the neighbor scan recovered this orientation despite very small correlation coefficients.
main_caveats: The absolute correlations were small, with |r| below 0.05, so this is a rank-based directional signal rather than a strong transcriptome-wide match.

summary: 155 MB Glut contained an exploratory SREBP/sterol signal: Rptor nominally decreased Srebf2 and several sterol genes, while Tsc1 or Tsc2 perturbation robustly increased Srebf2 and cholesterol-biosynthesis transcripts in the same cell type.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Rptor-side sterol changes were nominal and confined to one cell type; only the Tsc1/Tsc2 arms were FDR significant.

summary: Upstream inhibitory mTOR-axis perturbations produced far stronger neuronal transcriptomes than Rptor loss, so a Rptor CRISPRi signature should not be treated as a complete mirror image of TSC-complex loss for rescue-biomarker design.
why_it_matters: TSC biology and mTOR inhibitors are clinically tied to excessive mTORC1 signaling, but this dataset shows that inhibitory-gate perturbations and direct scaffold depletion have very different dynamic ranges at single-cell RNA level.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparator asymmetry could reflect guide efficacy, protein stability, and gain- versus loss-of-function biology; the dataset does not test drug rescue.

summary: Zfp846 perturbation produced no reproducible genome-wide differential-expression program across 22 modeled neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: A predicted nuclear DNA-binding transcriptional regulator might be expected to yield a coherent loss-of-function signature, so the dominant result is biologically informative absence of a broad cell-autonomous transcriptomic response.

summary: Zfp846 was transcriptionally orthogonal to other Zfp-family perturbations and to Setdb1 or Chd4 perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: The result argues against interpreting Zfp846 as a generic KAP1/SETDB1/NuRD pathway surrogate and instead supports individualized KRAB/C2H2 zinc-finger behavior.
