summary: Zfp846 signatures did not yield a disease-like or drug-directional transcriptional neighbor.

main_caveats: The dataset is a transcriptomic perturbation screen, not a therapeutic assay; database negatives can reflect absence of curation.

summary: Pkd1 loss did not produce a multiple-testing-significant transcriptional phenotype in any of the 21 profiled neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: PKD1 is a disease gene with ciliary channel biology, so a dataset-wide null in postmitotic neuronal classes refines the operative context rather than negating Pkd1 function in renal, choroid-plexus, or ependymal cilia.
main_caveats: Screen readout was steady-state scRNA-seq in neuronal classes; many Pkd1 groups had 30-60 perturbed cells; raw expression and editing-rate data were not available.

summary: The only nominally expected Pkd1 self-knockdown was restricted to 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and was buffered at the transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: This is the cell type with the clearest on-target RNA decrease, yet its strongest downstream rows remained FDR=1.0; an opposite nominal Pkd1 increase in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut further shows that target engagement was inconsistent.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The L5 ET effect is nominal only and no downstream gene passed FDR correction.

summary: Pkd1 did not converge with the assayed Ift88 or Kif3b ciliary perturbations.
why_it_matters: Polycystin-1 traffics to and functions in cilia and STRING/UniProt place PKD1, IFT88, and KIF3B in a ciliary neighborhood, but the neuronal screen captured no shared Pkd1-IFT transcriptomic module.
main_caveats: Absence of convergence is most interpretable as a negative screen result because Pkd1, Ift88, and Kif3b all had weak signatures.

summary: The strong Tsc1/Tsc2 neuronal signatures contrast sharply with the silent Pkd1 signature despite reported PKD1-TSC2/mTOR coupling in renal cystogenesis.
why_it_matters: This argues that the screen could detect mTOR/TSC transcriptional vulnerability in the same neuronal panel, but Pkd1 loss did not activate that program.
main_caveats: The prior PKD1-TSC2 literature is kidney and cystogenesis focused, whereas the dataset is mouse neuronal scRNA-seq.

summary: Dlg4 was the only repeatedly downregulated top-signature gene, suggesting a weak postsynaptic-scaffold biomarker hypothesis.
why_it_matters: DLG4/PSD-95 is central to excitatory postsynaptic organization, so a three-cell-type nominal decrease is biologically interesting even though it is not a validated Pkd1 mechanism here.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All Dlg4 rows were nominal and FDR>=0.81; no direct PKD1-DLG4 mechanism was found.

summary: Mycn perturbation was globally buffered at the differential-expression level across the sampled mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset did not reproduce the large growth and cell-cycle consequences expected from developmental N-myc loss, so any Mycn biology in this assay is either absent, compensated, outside the sampled state, or masked by weak editing.
main_caveats: The target transcript was not depleted and nominal hits were used only to assess the absence of recurrence; CRISPR editing or protein loss was not directly measured.

summary: 053 Sst Gaba was the only Mycn context with a near-threshold expression tail, led by Sstr1, Rtn1, Srek1, Tubb2a, and Prnp.
why_it_matters: This is the only cell-type-specific hypothesis in the Mycn data, but it is weaker than the FDR<0.05 cutoff and should be treated as a candidate interneuron response rather than a validated pathway.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: All five genes were 0.057-0.091 FDR, there was no Mycn self-knockdown, and this tail was not replicated across other cell types.

summary: MAX and selected MYCN-adjacent cofactors were active in thalamic and midbrain contexts, whereas Mycn, Myc, Alk, and Kdm5b were silent or nearly silent.
why_it_matters: MYCN normally works through MAX and is embedded in MYC/MAX and neuroblastoma networks; the screen therefore separates a robust MAX-centered ribosome-biogenesis/nucleolar module from an acutely buffered Mycn node.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is at the transcriptome-signature level; MAX, BRD4, and HUWE1 have MYCN-independent biology, and AURKA itself was not assayed.

summary: Mycn lacked a measurable self-row knockdown even in high-cell-count contexts that supported robust signatures for Max.
why_it_matters: The negative Mycn phenotype cannot be read as definitive MYCN dispensability unless guide editing or N-Myc protein loss is independently verified; however, the Max control shows that unchanged target mRNA does not preclude a CRISPR phenotype in this dataset.
main_caveats: mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for CRISPR knockout, and no guide-level editing, genotype, protein, or clone data were available in the parquet.

summary: The Mycn-null transcriptomic result argues against using this brain dataset alone to predict either MYCN-targeted efficacy or neuronal safety.
why_it_matters: MYCN is dosage-sensitive in development and an oncogenic neuroblastoma target, and therapeutic approaches often act indirectly through partners such as AURKA; an acute, weakly engaged Mycn guide response in named mouse-brain classes is therefore an indirect disease model.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay MYCN-amplified tumors, developing neural progenitors, or AURKA perturbation, and the Mycn target transcript did not provide evidence of knockdown.

summary: Tspan12 assignment produced a globally sparse, weakly engaged perturbation response in the neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is absence of a robust neuronal loss-of-function program rather than a broad Tspan12-regulated transcriptional state.
main_caveats: Sparse target mRNA could make on-target transcript depletion hard to quantify; genome editing could still alter protein in cells where the transcript is not detected.

summary: B4gat1 induction is the sole transcriptome-wide significant Tspan12 hit and is restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: B4gat1 is the only measured gene that can serve as a dataset-supported marker of any Tspan12 response, but the solitary hit should be treated as a candidate rather than a pathway readout.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: One FDR-significant gene in one cell type; no recurrence across the panel and no direct mechanistic link to TSPAN12/Norrin signaling was established here.

summary: The neuronal Tspan12 signature is uncoupled from the Norrin/FZD4/LRP5/6/beta-catenin output expected from retinal endothelial biology.
why_it_matters: Known TSPAN12 disease biology centers on endothelial Norrin receptor signaling, whereas the assayed mouse-brain neuronal classes did not show Axin2 or beta-catenin target activation after Tspan12 perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not assay retinal or vascular endothelial cells, and weak Tspan12 target-transcript engagement limits loss-of-function strength.

summary: Tspan12 does not converge with Fzd4, Lrp5, Lrp6, Ctnnb1, or Tspan7 perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: Although TSPAN12 is a co-receptor in the Norrin/FZD4/LRP5/6 complex, the Perturb-seq signatures argue against interchangeability of the receptor complex and beta-catenin transducer in these neuronal contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Fzd4 and Lrp5 themselves lacked strong downstream signatures, so the contrast is strongest for Ctnnb1 and only partial for Lrp6.

summary: No high-correlation positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor was found for Tspan12.
why_it_matters: The result supports interpreting the observed response as isolated rather than as part of a recurrent perturbation module shared with another target in the screen.
main_caveats: Correlation analysis used rank-score signatures and may miss nonlinear or protein-level convergence.

summary: The weak neuronal Tspan12 result should not be used to deprioritize endothelial FZD4/Norrin/TSPAN12 agonism.
why_it_matters: Human FEVR genetics and vascular-barrier agonist studies point to an endothelial disease axis, so this neuronal screen is best read as a cell-type boundary on the model system rather than as target invalidation for barrier repair.
main_caveats: No endothelial or barrier phenotypes were measured; the warning is an interpretive boundary, not a direct therapeutic test.

summary: Sox2 perturbation is broadly buffered in the assayed adult neuronal classes: only 2 of 371,818 Sox2 DE rows reached FDR<0.05, and both occurred in one thalamic excitatory class.
why_it_matters: SOX2 is a potent stem/progenitor transcription factor, so the dataset mainly argues that mature neuronal classes do not broadly execute a SOX2-responsive developmental program under this perturbation.
main_caveats: The readout is transcript abundance after perturbation in broad cell classes; lack of FDR hits does not exclude protein-level editing or subtle responses below power.

summary: The statistically supported Sox2 response is restricted to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Tnnt1 and Stam are down-regulated.
why_it_matters: The response is small but cell-type-specific enough that it should be treated as a thalamic-state effect rather than as a pan-neuronal SOX2 signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only two genes pass FDR<0.05, and neither is a canonical SOX2 target in the literature checked here.

summary: The target transcript does not validate strong Sox2 mRNA engagement in any measured class.
why_it_matters: The biological signatures should be interpreted as guide-associated downstream transcriptomes, not as expression-validated Sox2 knockdown or activation states.
main_caveats: A coding-sequence CRISPR perturbation can affect SOX2 protein without changing Sox2 RNA, and sparse Sox2 expression in differentiated neurons can make logFC estimates unstable.

summary: Sox2 and Sox5 diverge in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut despite both being SOX-family perturbations: Sox5 up-regulates Tnnt1 while Sox2 down-regulates Tnnt1, and Sox3 and POU-family comparators do not phenocopy Sox2.
why_it_matters: The adult thalamic response is not a generic SOX-family or OCT/POU-like effect, and the opposite Tnnt1 direction warns against treating related developmental transcription factors as interchangeable in this mature neuronal context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and restricted to one broad thalamic class; related targets also lacked FDR-level target-transcript engagement.

summary: Sox2 lacks a robust positive or negative signature neighbor in the only responsive class.
why_it_matters: Top-neighbor analyses can otherwise overstate weak restricted correlations; the full 17,259-gene signature shows no convincing convergent perturbation for Sox2 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Top-200 restricted correlations are hypothesis-generating only; the strongest full-signature absolute correlation was 0.079.

summary: The mature-neuron dataset does not activate or repress a canonical SOX2 stemness program, so therapeutic or disease interpretations should be routed to progenitor and tumor-stem contexts rather than inferred from broad adult neuronal buffering.
why_it_matters: SOX2 is dosage-sensitive in development and implicated in stem-like cancer states, but this panel mainly tests differentiated neuronal classes where Sox2 transcript engagement and downstream effects are weak.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks a matched adult neural stem-cell or glioma-stem compartment and should not be used as a negative test of those SOX2 functions.

summary: Safe_target_8 behaved as a transcriptomic null across the 22 tested mouse-brain cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: The control perturbation produced no adjusted-p<0.05 gene and had no measurable endogenous target transcript, so downstream cell-type programs should not be inferred from the nominal tails.
main_caveats: Absence of a Safe_target_8 transcript is expected for a control-like label, but the parquet contains no editing-efficiency measurement.

summary: Safe_target_8 did not detectably induce a p53/DNA-damage transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: Cutting controls can, in principle, reveal a Cas9 double-strand-break stress program; here canonical p53 targets stayed below FDR thresholds, arguing either for a buffered response in these cells or for unmeasured weak cutting by this guide group.
main_caveats: Published p53 responses were demonstrated in human cultured cells, not post-mitotic mouse brain cell classes; Safe_target_8 editing rates were unavailable.

summary: The largest Safe_target_8 deviations were isolated nominal calls in low-count cell types rather than robust cell-type-selective programs.
why_it_matters: 217 P MY Pineal Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA contained the strongest single-gene statistics, but adjusted p values of 0.166-0.361 and small perturbed-cell counts make them quality-control outliers rather than interpretable biology.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: These are nominal extremes selected post hoc and should not be pursued without replication or edit-level support.

summary: Safe_target_8 had no meaningful positive or negative signature neighbor among either real targets or other Safe_target controls.
why_it_matters: The strongest within-cell-type correlation to any other target was only |r| = 0.119, arguing against hidden convergence with a disease-gene or pathway signature.
comparators: all other gene_target signatures|other Safe_target controls
main_caveats: Correlations use Wilcoxon score vectors rather than independent validation of phenotypic state.

summary: Pnkd transcript depletion was reproducible but concentrated in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba, with several additional nominal-only classes.
why_it_matters: Only the classes with clear target depletion can be interpreted as successful Pnkd loss-of-function contexts; the uneven pattern prevents pan-neuronal interpretation of weak rows.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: FDR success is target-transcript engagement, not proof that these are the cells initiating PNKD attacks.

summary: Even where Pnkd itself passed FDR, no non-Pnkd gene reached FDR<0.05 anywhere in the Pnkd perturbation.
why_it_matters: The primary Perturb-seq phenotype is target depletion rather than a broad downstream transcriptional state, pointing to buffering, protein-level action, or missing stimulus conditions.
main_caveats: The experiment can miss synaptic physiology, altered protein stability, redox changes, and evoked-release phenotypes.

summary: The RIM/Munc13/SNARE and transmitter-marker genes expected from PNKD synaptic literature were not FDR-regulated after Pnkd knockdown in the three FDR-engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: PNKD can regulate neurotransmitter release without detectably rewiring those release genes at the mRNA level in resting single cells.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only selected sentinel mRNAs were inspected; RIM1/2 protein abundance and vesicle exocytosis were not measured.

summary: Pnkd score vectors were nearly orthogonal to both the top global signature neighbors and movement-disorder or synaptic comparator perturbations.
why_it_matters: Clinically related genes did not collapse onto a shared constitutive transcriptomic module, so Pnkd phenotypes are likely better compared at the protein, circuit, or stimulation-response level.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from four Pnkd contexts, including one nominal-only context; STRING links used for comparator selection are not all physical interactions.

summary: Pnkd had no differential-expression signature in 215 MB Dopa, leaving the published Pnkd dopaminergic phenotype untested in its most direct dataset class.
why_it_matters: A failure to see dopamine-pathway transcriptional effects should not be interpreted as disagreement with mouse nigrostriatal dopamine studies because the dopaminergic class lacked a Pnkd perturbation row.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Absence of a row likely reflects coverage or inclusion thresholds rather than a measured lack of response.

summary: Tsga10 perturbation produced no FDR-significant neuronal transcriptomic response and did not measurably deplete the Tsga10 transcript.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset readout is a global null, so downstream nominal genes should not be interpreted as a robust Tsga10-regulated pathway.
cell_types: all 22 assayed Glut/GABA neuronal classes
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA knockdown does not prove the guides failed at the edited locus or at unmeasured protein/isoform levels; several contrasts had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: The few nominal Tsga10-associated genes were cell-type isolated rather than a recurrent neuronal program.
why_it_matters: A true cell-type-selective program was not hidden under the global null: even the strongest single genes had adjusted p values above 0.26 and nominal p<0.01 genes almost never recurred across neuronal classes.
cell_types: all 22 assayed Glut/GABA neuronal classes
main_caveats: This is a transcriptome-only recurrence test; weaker post-transcriptional phenotypes would be missed.

summary: The neuronal null is consistent with a context mismatch between the assayed Glut/GABA neurons and prior Tsga10 biology in sperm-tail, ciliated, and ependymal contexts.
why_it_matters: The screen should be read as negative for the sampled neuronal populations, not as evidence against Tsga10 function in multiciliated ependyma or spermatogenic cells.
cell_types: all 22 assayed Glut/GABA neuronal classes
main_caveats: The expression evidence comes partly from human HPA and older mouse developmental studies, whereas the perturbation dataset is mouse neuronal single-cell RNA-seq.

summary: Tsga10 did not phenocopy Hif1a or assayed centrosome/ciliogenesis neighbors such as Cep112 and Cep83.
why_it_matters: The known TSGA10-HIF1A interaction and ciliary annotations did not translate into a shared neuronal transcriptional module in this dataset, so mechanistic interpretation should not project a HIF or centriole program onto the Tsga10 nominal genes.
cell_types: all comparable Glut/GABA neuronal contrasts
main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted to mRNA signatures with weak Tsga10 target engagement; HIF1A nuclear localization and ciliary ultrastructure were not measured.

summary: FDR-confirmed Zdhhc17 transcript depletion was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut despite negative target logFC values in all 22 measured cell classes.
why_it_matters: The strongest acute mRNA consequence of Zdhhc17 perturbation is not pan-neuronal; it is dominated by two thalamic/midbrain glutamatergic populations with high perturbed-cell counts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation is partial at mRNA level, and many classes with nominal target depletion did not pass FDR.

summary: Tubb3 was the lone non-target FDR hit and fell with Zdhhc17 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with a weaker nominal recurrence in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This nominates Tubb3 as a compact empirical marker of the engaged Zdhhc17 state in thalamic/midbrain glutamatergic cells while keeping it distinct from the established palmitoylated substrate list.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Tubb3 passed FDR only in one cell class and is not established here as a direct ZDHHC17 substrate.

summary: Strong Zdhhc17 transcript knockdown was followed by very few FDR-significant downstream mRNA changes.
why_it_matters: The most engaged cell classes show that loss of Zdhhc17 mRNA can be largely transcriptionally buffered, consistent with the possibility that the primary ZDHHC17 phenotype is post-translational or delayed.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: FDR sparsity could reflect partial knockdown, protein persistence, or limited power rather than true biological buffering.

summary: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut showed no detectable Zdhhc17 transcript depletion and no FDR-significant downstream response.
why_it_matters: This separates cell classes that are biologically buffered after target engagement from those where the perturbation did not measurably lower the target transcript.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: A negative Wilcoxon result does not prove the guide failed in every cell; it shows absent aggregate mRNA engagement in this class.

summary: The known HIP14/ZDHHC17 palmitoylation substrate network did not appear as a coherent mRNA-loss module after Zdhhc17 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq readout should be interpreted as an acute transcriptional layer that is uncoupled from the protein-palmitoylation biology of HTT, SNAP25, DLG4, DNAJC5, GAD2, SYT1, and MAP6.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation contrasts are based on mRNA signatures, Zdhhc13 could not be tested, and palmitoylation or substrate-mislocalization could occur without changes in substrate transcript abundance.

summary: Small acute mRNA signatures after partial Zdhhc17 knockdown should not be interpreted as evidence that ZDHHC17 inhibition is safe or therapeutically desirable.
why_it_matters: Hip14 loss causes Huntington-like abnormalities in mice, and a successful HD rescue strategy increased rather than decreased brain palmitoylation; the Perturb-seq data therefore provide a cautionary lack-of-transcriptional-toxicity signal, not a go signal for inhibition.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment is not an HD model, does not assay behavior or palmitoylation, and Open Targets shows no current ZDHHC17 clinical candidate.

summary: Prdm2 perturbation produced a globally buffered transcriptomic phenotype across the assayed mouse brain classes.
why_it_matters: PRDM2 is a nuclear H3K9 methyltransferase and transcriptional regulator, so downstream claims from this target must start from the observation that the perturbation had weak measured self-transcript change and almost no correction-stable output.
main_caveats: Self-transcript abundance is an imperfect engagement readout for coding perturbations; a lack of RNA response does not prove no protein editing or no cell-state effect below detection.

summary: Tnrc6a up-regulation in 052 Pvalb Gaba was the only FDR-significant Prdm2 downstream gene.
why_it_matters: The signal nominates a Pvalb-restricted RNA-silencing effector response, but it should be treated as a candidate biomarker rather than a PRDM2-to-miRNA mechanism because Prdm2 mRNA itself was unchanged in the same cells.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Single-gene response in one cell type; no accompanying target-transcript engagement and no broader RNAi/P-body module passed FDR.

summary: Prdm2 did not phenocopy PRDM-family paralogs or predicted chromatin-network partners.
why_it_matters: The lack of convergence argues against interpreting the weak Prdm2 signature as a shared PRDM, H3K9, CtBP, SETDB1, KAT6A, or FOXG1 network response in this dataset.
main_caveats: Correlations used whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon scores and a weak Prdm2 signature; absence of correlation may reflect weak engagement rather than biological insulation.

summary: Published fear-circuit Prdm2 biology was not recapitulated as a broad Bdnf/Creb1 cell-class response.
why_it_matters: The result narrows interpretation of Prdm2 to molecularly or projection-defined stress/fear circuits rather than expecting every captured excitatory or inhibitory class to show the dmPFC knockdown program.
main_caveats: The literature used circuit-targeted Prdm2 downregulation, whereas this screen uses broad atlas cell classes, different perturbation chemistry, and no strong Prdm2 mRNA depletion.

summary: Large nominal chromatin and secretory-stress hits in thalamic, hypothalamic, and pineal classes were not correction-stable.
why_it_matters: This prevents overcalling scalar score outliers such as Kdm1a/Tox/Hdac2 in thalamic glutamatergic cells or Surf4 in low-count pineal glutamatergic cells as Prdm2 pathways.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: These rows may still motivate targeted validation, but the screen provides no FDR-level support for them.

summary: Tbck perturbation produced no FDR-resolved transcriptome in any assayed mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This makes absence of an mTOR, FERRY, or lysosomal program uninterpretable as a true loss-of-function phenotype; the dominant dataset fact is weak guide engagement or buffering.
main_caveats: Only transcript-level on-target evidence is available; protein depletion and guide efficiency were not measured in this table.

summary: The lowest adjusted p values after Tbck perturbation were concentrated in inhibitory GABA classes, especially 052 Pvalb Gaba, but the pattern remained exploratory.
why_it_matters: It nominates Pvalb and subpallial GABA neurons, rather than cortical glutamatergic neurons, as the only cell types worth prioritizing for Tbck validation from this dataset.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Minimum FDR was 0.324, 054 and 059 had only 46 and 28 perturbed cells, and the implicated genes did not recur as a coherent module across cell types.

summary: Tbck score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with represented mTORC1, autophagy, and endolysosomal perturbations.
why_it_matters: Prior work links TBCK loss to mTORC regulation and autophagy-lysosome phenotypes, so a well-engaged Tbck perturbation might have been expected to resemble Mtor, Rptor, Tsc1/Tsc2, Atg, Becn1, or lysosomal acidification signatures; it did not.
main_caveats: The uncoupling is measured in weak Tbck signatures, so it should not be interpreted as disproving the known mTOR-autophagy biology of TBCK.

summary: The screen could not test FERRY-complex equivalence for Tbck, and represented Tbc1d perturbations were not Tbck-like.
why_it_matters: The most current mechanistic model places TBCK in the FERRY Rab5-mRNA transport complex, but other FERRY subunits were absent from the screen, preventing the complex-member convergence test that would now be most informative.
main_caveats: FERRY genes may have untested aliases, and family-neighbor correlations are restricted to transcriptomic score vectors.

summary: An unbiased signature-neighbor search found no convincing Tbck-like perturbation.
why_it_matters: The largest absolute neighbor correlations were below 0.21 and safe-target controls entered multiple top-neighbor lists, so isolated neighbors should not be promoted to biology.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations were computed from DE score vectors rather than cell-level expression profiles.

summary: The mouse Perturb-seq data do not justify choosing mTOR activation, autophagy modulation, or lysosomal rescue as a direction for Tbck in these neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Human TBCK deficiency has been tied to reduced mTOR signaling, aberrant autophagy, and lysosomal-mitochondrial dysfunction, but the present perturbation lacks both on-target knockdown and pathway alignment.
main_caveats: The warning applies to this weak transcriptomic perturbation only; it does not rule out therapy guided by patient-cell or model-organism studies.

summary: Slc6a5 perturbation did not significantly deplete the Slc6a5 transcript in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: The lack of on-target transcript evidence makes every downstream hit engagement-limited and prevents strong loss-of-function interpretation for a canonical presynaptic glycine transporter.
main_caveats: DE summaries do not report guide efficiency or basal Slc6a5 counts; a protein-level or splice-altering effect cannot be excluded.

summary: The only FDR-significant Slc6a5 downstream response was a three-gene Ppat/Foxg1/Ltk signature in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The response is highly cell-class restricted and too narrow to constitute a broad glycinergic or synaptic module.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only three genes passed FDR and the Slc6a5 target transcript was not knocked down.

summary: Twenty-one Slc6a5-tested cell classes showed no adjusted-p<0.05 genes.
why_it_matters: The aggregate result argues that most assayed cells either did not express/engage Slc6a5 or buffered the perturbation without a detectable cell-autonomous transcriptomic program.
main_caveats: Because target knockdown was not detected, lack of downstream DE should not be overread as true biological compensation.

summary: Glycine receptor/scaffold perturbations and the related Slc6a1 transporter perturbation were essentially uncorrelated with Slc6a5.
why_it_matters: Genes connected by inhibitory synapse biology and hyperekplexia genetics were not interchangeable at the transcriptome-signature level in this assay.
main_caveats: The comparison uses restricted Wilcoxon-score signatures; several related perturbations were inactive in the L2/3 class itself.

summary: The Slc6a5 L2/3 Perturb-seq response was uncoupled from the canonical presynaptic glycinergic hyperekplexia pathway.
why_it_matters: The response should not be treated as a faithful cellular model of SLC6A5 startle disease, which is driven by defective GlyT2 glycine recycling in glycinergic neurons.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The conclusion is based on absence of transcriptomic glycinergic markers, not electrophysiologic testing of glycine neurotransmission.

summary: The dataset does not provide an engaged Slc6a5 model for judging GlyT2 inhibition or safety.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL confirms SLC6A5 is ligandable, but weak genetic engagement and absence of reproducible downstream signatures mean the Perturb-seq negative data should not be used as evidence that GlyT2 modulation is transcriptionally silent.
main_caveats: CRISPR perturbation in single cells differs from acute partial pharmacologic inhibition of a membrane transporter.

direction: upregulated polarity/adhesion/trafficking cassette in responsive classes
summary: Zeb1 perturbation elicited a sharply cell-type-selective response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and, more weakly, 155 MB Glut, with single-gene Stxbp2 responses in 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: Prior neural work established Zeb1 as a developmental polarity and differentiation regulator; this dataset narrows the detectable adult mouse-brain response to a few cell states rather than a broad neuronal program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The target Zeb1 transcript was not significantly reduced, and two of the four responding classes had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: The principal Zeb1 downstream program was a compact AP1M2/STXBP2/PATJ/SPINT2/F11R/CDC42BPG cassette rather than a broad canonical EMT signature.
why_it_matters: The module direction matches the idea that Zeb1 suppresses polarity and epithelial-like genes, but its narrow size and composition argue for a specialized neuronal regulon.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The genes are interpreted as a polarity/adhesion/trafficking cassette by annotation and recurrence; the dataset does not demonstrate physical junction formation.

summary: Stxbp2 was the most recurrent Zeb1-induced gene, reaching FDR<0.05 in four otherwise heterogeneous cell types.
why_it_matters: A single recurrent reporter can reveal partial target response in classes where the full Zeb1 module is absent or underpowered.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: STXBP2 alone is not pathway proof; recurrence is transcriptional and needs validation at protein and functional levels.

summary: Ctbp1 is a weak but mechanistically coherent positive Zeb1 neighbor in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The result links the strongest Zeb1 cell-type response to a known ZEB1 corepressor rather than to an unrelated top neighbor, preserving evidence for on-complex convergence even with a small genome-wide correlation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Pearson correlation was only 0.103 and Ctbp2, the cofactor emphasized in embryonic cortex, was not available as a direct comparator in the analyzed gene-target set.

summary: Zeb1 did not behave like Zeb2 or selected TGFβ/SMAD/EMT-neighbor perturbations in the dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut context.
why_it_matters: This argues that the Zeb1 phenotype is not a generic consequence of perturbing the canonical CDH1/EMT regulatory network but is selective for a narrow Zeb1/CtBP-associated regulon in this brain cell class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparator target engagement was not independently validated, and the test used one adult brain cell type rather than ligand-stimulated epithelial EMT.

summary: Most Zeb1 cell classes were FDR-null, including several with substantial matched cell numbers, and no cell class showed significant loss of Zeb1 transcript.
why_it_matters: The negative space prevents overgeneralizing the responsive-cell findings and marks many cell types as buffered, unengaged, or technically insensitive in this assay.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: An FDR-null Wilcoxon result cannot distinguish true biological buffering from low Zeb1 expression, inefficient perturbation, or insufficient guide-level power.

summary: Gata3 perturbation was globally buffered or ineffective in the assayed mouse-brain subclasses.
why_it_matters: The dataset provides little evidence for Gata3-dependent transcription in these subclasses; the result should be treated chiefly as a weak-engagement negative result rather than as a map of GATA3 downstream biology.
main_caveats: The target transcript was not detectably depleted, so buffering cannot be separated from low baseline expression or failed target engagement.

summary: The near-threshold Hectd2 signal in 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut is isolated and exploratory.
why_it_matters: Hectd2 was the only gene below FDR 0.10 in the entire Gata3 analysis, and lack of a second corrected gene or recurrence argues against interpreting it as a coherent hippocampal/amygdalar GATA3 program.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Hectd2 did not reach FDR<0.05 and no pathway-level support was available.

summary: Gata3 was not interchangeable with other GATA perturbations or with Zfpm2 in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Shared GATA-family DNA-binding biology would make paralog convergence plausible, but the observed Gata3 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Gata1, Gata2, Gata4, Gata6, and Zfpm2 perturbations and their few corrected hits were not shared.
main_caveats: The comparison is signature-based and most GATA-family perturbations were themselves weak.

summary: No strong positive or inverse Gata3 signature neighbor was found across the perturbation library.
why_it_matters: Without a high-correlation neighbor, the Gata3 profile does not nominate a robust convergent module or an opposing perturbation suitable for rescue-style interpretation.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score signatures, not on raw single-cell profiles or independent replicate signatures.

summary: The weak mouse-brain response refines, rather than negates, strong developmental GATA3 biology by placing it outside the sampled neuronal contexts.
why_it_matters: GATA3 dosage causes HDR syndrome and Gata3 is required in cochlear development, yet midbrain-labeled subclasses in this Perturb-seq screen were unresponsive; disease-relevant effects are therefore more likely to involve specific developmental windows or non-sampled ear, parathyroid, kidney, immune, or epithelial contexts.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The dataset does not assay embryonic cochlea, parathyroid, kidney, or immune cells, and 215 MB Dopa had only 23 perturbed cells.

summary: Satb2 perturbation produced weak measured target-transcript knockdown and no multiplicity-adjusted differential expression in any assayed brain cell type.
why_it_matters: The dominant biological readout is absence of an acute Satb2-loss program, not a pathway activation signature; this prevents strong mechanistic inference from the nominal genes.
cell_types: all 23 assayed cell types
main_caveats: A null call cannot distinguish true postmitotic buffering from insufficient guide activity, incomplete mRNA capture, or isoform-specific detection issues.

summary: The weak Satb2 nominal signal was not concentrated in Satb2-relevant cortical glutamatergic groups and no P<0.001 gene recurred across cell types.
why_it_matters: A biologically coherent Satb2 response should show either cortical enrichment or gene recurrence; the observed singleton nominal hits are more consistent with underpowered or noisy perturbations.
cell_types: all 23 assayed cell types
main_caveats: The analysis used row-level Wilcoxon output only; subtle coordinated effects below single-gene detectability could still exist.

summary: Satb2 perturbation did not measurably mobilize the Bcl11b-Fezf2-Tbr1/Epha4 cortical projection-neuron fate module in the cortical glutamatergic groups.
why_it_matters: Classic Satb2 mouse genetics is developmental and directionally context dependent; the Perturb-seq result argues that this network was either not engaged or not acutely rewired in the sampled postmitotic brain cells.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Satb2 transcript depletion itself was weak, so failure to move the fate module should not be interpreted as genetic dispensability of Satb2 in development.

summary: Tbr1, a member of the same cortical projection-neuron specification network, generated robust cortical differential expression while Satb2 did not, and Satb2/Tbr1 signatures were only weakly correlated.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the dataset can recover a transcription-factor response in relevant glutamatergic strata and makes the Satb2 null result target-specific rather than a universal failure of cortical TF perturbations.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: This is a perturbation-level contrast, not proof that Tbr1 is downstream of Satb2 in these adult-like groups; Satb2 guide activity was weaker than ideal.

summary: Neither the Satb1 paralog nor unbiased signature neighbors supplied a convincing Satb2-like transcriptomic module.
why_it_matters: Because SATB2 is a chromatin-associated transcription factor with no simple receptor-proximal pathway, correlated perturbations were the main route to rescue pathway interpretation; the correlation scan instead maxed out below |r|=0.20.
cell_types: all 23 assayed cell types|22 shared Satb1/Satb2 cell types
main_caveats: Signature correlations are restricted to tested genes and target-cell combinations; Lonp1 and Wdr26 are nearest mathematical neighbors, not validated Satb2 interactors.

summary: The experiment does not provide a robust acute neuronal Satb2-loss pharmacodynamic signature, and prior human genetics plus tractability resources argue against over-interpreting the weak nominal hits as direct CNS-inhibition biomarkers.
why_it_matters: SATB2 alteration is linked to neurodevelopmental disease, while curated resources show a nuclear DNA-binding protein with limited direct druggability; a weak Perturb-seq signature should therefore be treated as a safety/context warning rather than as an efficacy direction.
cell_types: all 23 assayed cell types
main_caveats: The dataset tested mouse brain CRISPR perturbations, not a drug, dose response, or developmental human model.

summary: Nr2c2 generated a sparse, glutamatergic-biased downstream response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: TR4/NR2C2 has broad developmental roles, but the acute Perturb-seq signature is restricted to a few excitatory classes, narrowing where this perturbation changed transcriptional state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The self-transcript was not reduced, and an absent response in other classes may reflect low guide-cell counts or unmeasured protein disruption rather than biological irrelevance.

summary: Ccdc84 was recurrently down-regulated after Nr2c2 perturbation in all three classes with FDR-significant responses.
why_it_matters: A single gene recurring across the thalamic, CA3, and midbrain glutamatergic signatures provides the clearest transcriptional marker for the otherwise sparse Nr2c2 response.

summary: No corrected Slitrk1-dependent RNA biomarker emerged; top nominal genes such as Clip3 and Washc2 should remain exploratory.

summary: Pou4f3 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any of the 23 profiled mouse-brain cell classes.

summary: Pou4f3 RNA itself was not detectably depleted or induced by the Pou4f3 perturbation.

main_caveats: The table reports DE statistics, not raw target expression or DNA editing efficiency.

summary: The lowest-q neuronal response was confined to nominal mixed-direction genes in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and did not establish a selective Pou4f3-responsive class.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut

summary: Unbiased positive and negative signature-neighbor scans found no strong Pou4f3-like perturbation.
why_it_matters: The absence of a correlated neighbor argues against a hidden paralog, pathway neighbor, or disease-family perturbation reproducing a Pou4f3 program in these profiles.

summary: Ptprc knockdown produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic phenotype in any sampled neuronal class.

summary: The neuron-only Ptprc null should not be used to deprioritize microglial CD45 as an anti-inflammatory disease target.

summary: Trak1 knockdown generated a globally buffered transcriptional phenotype rather than a broad mitochondrial-transport or inhibitory-synapse response.

summary: The only adjusted Trak1 responses were isolated Sst Gaba and midbrain glutamatergic genes rather than a reproducible cell-class program.

summary: A signature-neighbor search found no robust phenocopy or anti-phenocopy of Trak1 anywhere in the screen.

summary: Prdm5 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic response and no supported change in the Prdm5 mRNA row in any assayed neuronal subclass.
why_it_matters: PRDM5 is an annotated nuclear transcriptional regulator, so this Perturb-seq screen should be interpreted as non-informative or weakly engaged for acute Prdm5 biology rather than as evidence for a strong neuronal loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: A flat Prdm5 mRNA row could reflect low basal expression, guide inefficiency, delayed protein turnover, or biology outside the assayed neuronal states; the dataset does not establish that PRDM5 protein activity was removed.

summary: The extracellular-matrix and brittle-cornea PRDM5-ZNF469 program was not reproduced in the adult neuronal Prdm5 signatures.
why_it_matters: Human PRDM5 disease genetics point to corneal and connective-tissue matrix regulation, but the mouse-brain neuronal perturbation did not shift Col4a1, Col11a1, Hapln1, Tgfb2, Edil3, or Zfp469, arguing against an ECM readout in these neuronal cell types under this assay.
main_caveats: Negative ECM evidence is contingent on the weak Prdm5 perturbation and on measuring neuronal classes rather than corneal stroma or other matrix-producing connective tissues.

summary: Within the same PRDM family, Prdm10 generated a robust multi-cell-type signature whereas Prdm5, Prdm12, Prdm16, and nearly all Prdm2 signatures were flat.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that PRDM-family transcription factors were not uniformly silent or undetectable in the screen; Prdm5 behaved as a selectively weak family member in this adult-brain panel.
main_caveats: Prdm10 is a paralog-family comparator rather than a known interchangeable binding partner of Prdm5; stronger Prdm10 activity does not prove equivalent guide efficacy, expression, or protein turnover for Prdm5.

summary: Known PRDM5 chromatin or matrix neighbors did not converge with the Prdm5 signature, and the genome-wide target-neighbor search found no strong positive or negative neighbor.
why_it_matters: Mouse embryonic-stem-cell and STRING data connect PRDM5 to Ctcf/EHMT-related chromatin and matrix-associated proteins, yet Ctcf and Ehmt1 perturbations made detectable signatures without aligning to Prdm5. This keeps PRDM5 from being assigned to a CTCF-, EHMT-, NSD2-, or COL11A1-like neuronal module in this dataset.
main_caveats: Only same-cell transcriptomic correlations were tested; EHMT2, HDAC1, cohesin subunits, and several STRING interactors were not all available as exact perturbation targets, and interaction literature is mostly non-neuronal.

summary: The dataset did not contain a hidden Prdm5-sensitive neuronal subclass; the best nominal cell-type peaks were isolated and not recurrent.

why_it_matters: STAT1 is a central IFN transcription factor, so a self-only FDR signature indicates that basal neuronal cells are not sitting in a fully activated IFN state and buffer much of the canonical response unless cytokine tone is present.
