main_caveats: The experiment measures RNA in basal cells; it does not assay STAT1 phosphorylation, cytokine stimulation, or antiviral challenge.

summary: A nominal MHC-I antigen-presentation module recurred after Stat1, Ifngr1, and Ifngr2 perturbation, especially in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: Module-level convergence links the Stat1 signature to type-II IFN receptor tone and nominates B2m, H2-K1, and Nlrc5 as the basal neuronal STAT1-responsive genes most aligned with canonical IFN-gamma biology.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The shared MHC-I genes were nominal and did not pass FDR; Ifngr1 had only 39 perturbed cells in 191 MB P MY GABA.

summary: Type-I receptor and ISGF3 partner perturbations did not phenocopy the Stat1/Ifngr MHC-I module even though STAT1, STAT2, and IRF9 cooperate in canonical type-I IFN signaling.
why_it_matters: The data separate a basal IFNGR-like MHC-I branch from a type-I IFN/ISGF3 signature under this unstimulated neuronal condition, preventing over-interpretation of Stat1 loss as a complete IFNAR phenocopy.
main_caveats: Whole-transcriptome correlations were weak for all pathway neighbors, and weak self-transcript depletion of partner genes could mask true type-I pathway relationships.

summary: Nlrc5, B2m, and H2-K1 are exploratory transcript biomarkers for neuronal STAT1/IFNGR tone.
why_it_matters: Nlrc5 is upstream of MHC-I transcription, whereas B2m and H2-K1 are antigen-presentation outputs; this combination gives mechanistic and effector readouts of the modest Stat1 signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: All marker calls outside Stat1 itself were nominal in the Stat1 perturbation, and sparse genes produced unstable logFC estimates in some contrasts.

summary: Stat1 did not have a strong unbiased positive or negative signature neighbor among the other perturbations.
why_it_matters: The absence of a high-correlation neighbor argues against a large generic stress, viability, or developmental program dominating the Stat1 result.
main_caveats: Correlation is a broad scalar and can miss small targeted modules such as the MHC-I genes.

summary: Suppressing STAT1-like signaling in neurons may reduce MHC-I antigen-presentation transcripts, so the dataset supports monitoring neuronal Nlrc5/B2m/H2-K1 when considering STAT1 or upstream IFN blockade.
why_it_matters: STAT1 activity can drive protective antimicrobial programs as well as inflammatory disease; the basal neuronal MHC-I trend means pathway inhibition should not be assumed immunologically silent in brain cells.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset is a knockdown experiment without pathogens, cytokines, or drug exposure; the clinical implication is hypothesis-generating only.

summary: Phkb perturbation did not produce significant on-target transcript depletion or any FDR-significant downstream gene in the measured neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant dataset result: the experiment cannot be read as a strong PHKB loss-of-function phenotype, because the target transcript itself was not convincingly reduced.
main_caveats: High confidence for the observed null transcriptomic result, but not for intrinsic PHKB dispensability because target engagement was weak.

summary: The lack of a corrected Phkb response was shared across glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes rather than confined to a single low-powered cluster.
why_it_matters: Even the two classes with the smallest adjusted p values and the class with the best nominal Phkb decrease missed FDR, so the data do not nominate a robust Phkb-sensitive neuronal subtype or biomarker set.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Most rows are nominal only; the dataset contains neuronal classes and does not test astrocytes, the main brain glycogen reservoir.

summary: Measured Phkb signatures were nearly orthogonal to the assayed phosphorylase-kinase alpha subunit Phka1 and to Calm1/2/3, even though calmodulin is the delta subunit of phosphorylase kinase.
why_it_matters: The contrast prevents assigning calmodulin knockdown phenotypes to the PHK glycogenolysis complex and shows that complex membership did not translate into a shared neuronal mRNA signature in this assay.
main_caveats: Both Phkb and Phka1 had weak on-target effects; calmodulin has many PHK-independent Ca2+-signaling functions.

summary: The curated Phkb glycogenolysis neighborhood showed no significant transcriptional feedback after Phkb perturbation.
why_it_matters: PHKB sits in a biochemical pathway controlled by kinase activity, phosphorylation, Ca2+/calmodulin, and glycogen phosphorylase; the Perturb-seq mRNA readout did not recover expression changes in that canonical module.
main_caveats: Weak Phkb knockdown limits causal interpretation, and mRNA abundance is an indirect readout for a post-translational metabolic pathway.

summary: The dataset does not reveal a neuronal transcriptomic vulnerability matching the liver/muscle glycogen-storage phenotype of human PHKB deficiency.
why_it_matters: PHKB is a disease gene, but the Perturb-seq result argues that mouse neuronal steady-state mRNA signatures are unlikely to be a sensitive surrogate for PHKB enzyme inhibition or glycogen-storage disease biology.
main_caveats: No astrocyte or peripheral liver/muscle phenotypes were measured; ChEMBL evidence for PHKB pharmacology was sparse; the Phkb perturbation did not strongly deplete its transcript.

summary: Satb1 perturbation did not yield an FDR-significant transcriptome in any tested mouse-brain cell class, and the Satb1 transcript itself was not significantly depleted.
why_it_matters: A SATB1 loss-of-function biological interpretation is not supported by this contrast; downstream absences are dominated by weak or unverified target engagement.
main_caveats: The parquet contains differential-expression summaries only; protein depletion, guide efficiency and raw target expression were not available.

summary: The literature-relevant Pvalb and Sst GABA classes were transcriptionally silent after Satb1 assignment: neither class showed Satb1 knockdown or any FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: Satb1 is expected to matter most in MGE-derived PV/SST interneuron maturation, so the absent signal is better read as developmental-stage or perturbation buffering, or ineffective CRISPR, than as evidence that Satb1 is dispensable for those lineages.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: The cell classes are broad and may be mature; Pvalb had only nominal Kdm3b down-regulation and Sst had 53 perturbed cells, so absence can reflect assay sensitivity.

summary: The smallest adjusted p values were restricted to 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 052 Pvalb Gaba, but both peaks remained nominal rather than FDR-significant.
why_it_matters: These are the only places where Satb1 produced rankable candidate biomarkers, and they should be treated as hypothesis-generating rather than as a validated Braf or Kdm3b response.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Best FDR values were 0.121 and 0.231; no pathway-level interpretation is justified without validation.

summary: Satb1 and Satb2 perturbations were almost uncorrelated across their 22 shared cell types, despite both encoding special AT-rich DNA-binding chromatin regulators.
why_it_matters: The screen supports non-interchangeability of SATB-family factors: Satb2-like projection-neuron programs cannot be inferred from Satb1 perturbation, and vice versa.
main_caveats: Because Satb1 itself was weak, lack of convergence could arise from poor Satb1 engagement rather than true functional orthogonality in every cell type.

summary: A dataset-wide neighbor scan found no strong positive or negative Satb1 signature neighbor, including among available SATB1 functional neighbors and cortical neurodevelopmental regulators.
why_it_matters: The nominal Satb1 genes did not define a reproducible module shared with a pathway-neighbor perturbation; broad pathway enrichment would overfit noise.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on Wilcoxon score vectors, not independent replicate-level expression profiles.

summary: The Satb1 signature is non-instructive for human SATB1 neurodevelopmental-disorder directionality or druggability.
why_it_matters: Human SATB1 disorders include mutation-specific mechanisms, while this screen produced neither a reliable loss-of-function state nor a ChEMBL-supported small-molecule target context; inhibition versus restoration cannot be inferred.
main_caveats: Disease evidence is human germline genetics; the dataset is pooled mouse-brain transcriptomics with weak target-transcript depletion.

summary: Zbtb7a perturbation repeatedly induced a signed neuronal module with broad Gpc1/Pnma3/Pnck/Usp11/Atp1b2 up-regulation and recurrent Stx16/Ppip5k1/Cacng7/Gpr108 down-regulation.
why_it_matters: The major dataset output is a conserved neuronal/synapse-linked transcriptional state, not a single rare-cell anomaly or one canonical hematopoietic ZBTB7A pathway.
main_caveats: STRING synapse enrichment is database-derived; individual recurrent genes are not demonstrated direct ZBTB7A targets in these neurons.

summary: The Zbtb7a response was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, 191 MB P MY GABA, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, while several cortical/limbic and CGE/LGE GABA classes had at most 10 FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: Zbtb7a is broadly expressed in brain databases, so the perturbation separates expression from functional sensitivity and nominates a restricted set of adult neuronal classes for follow-up.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Response breadth is power-sensitive and the target transcript itself was not FDR-confirmed as knocked down.

summary: The measured Zbtb7a mRNA provided weak on-target support: no cell type had a Zbtb7a row at FDR<0.05, and downstream breadth did not correlate with Zbtb7a target-transcript logFC.
why_it_matters: Large downstream signatures should be interpreted as perturbation-associated phenotypes rather than a clean dose-response series of Zbtb7a transcript depletion.
main_caveats: The target transcript may be lowly captured or edited without a proportional mRNA decrease; no guide-level raw counts were available in the parquet.

summary: Zbtb7a did not phenocopy other assayed Zbtb-family or NuRD-associated perturbations; Gatad2b and Chd4 were only modestly positive neighbors, whereas Yy1, Huwe1, Trrap, and Chd8 were recurrent inverse neighbors.
why_it_matters: Known corepressor relationships are insufficient to predict the neuronal Zbtb7a state; the dataset instead points to a context-specific chromatin-regulatory balance.
main_caveats: Cosines used only the top 100 absolute Zbtb7a score genes per cell type and should be viewed as restricted-signature screening statistics.

summary: Because ZBTB7A inhibition derepresses fetal globin and heterozygous ZBTB7A variants cause a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder, the neuronal Zbtb7a signatures flag brain transcriptional liabilities for any systemic ZBTB7A-lowering strategy.
why_it_matters: The dataset argues that partial or chronic target reduction should be evaluated in neural cells, not only erythroid cells, when considering ZBTB7A as a hemoglobinopathy target.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The assay is mouse adult neuronal Perturb-seq, not human erythropoiesis, germline heterozygosity, or a small-molecule dose-response.

summary: The neuronal Zbtb7a output was not dominated by transcriptional induction of assayed Notch, TGF-beta/SMAD, or fetal-globin-repressor pathway components; among queried canonical genes only Chd4 passed FDR<0.05, in three cell types.
why_it_matters: Canonical ZBTB7A mechanisms from lymphoid, TGF-beta, and erythroid systems are real but do not map one-to-one onto the adult neuronal perturbation signature.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA changes in pathway components does not rule out ZBTB7A binding, chromatin remodeling, or activity-level changes in these pathways.

summary: Sorl1 transcript knockdown was detectable across several neuronal classes but passed FDR in only 9 of 23 cell-type tests, with the strongest engagement in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The target was measurably engaged in enough contexts to interpret a null downstream response, while the response was not uniformly powered or engaged across all assayed cell types.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Target-transcript loss was the readout; the parquet contains no SORLA protein, APP localization, or endosome morphology measurement.

summary: Even in Sorl1-engaged cell types, loss of Sorl1 mRNA was transcriptionally buffered: no non-Sorl1 gene reached FDR<0.05 or FDR<0.10 in any cell type.
why_it_matters: Known SORLA biology is centered on post-Golgi/endosomal cargo sorting, so a target-only Perturb-seq signature argues that immediate consequences of partial Sorl1 depletion are not broad steady-state mRNA programs under these conditions.
main_caveats: A null RNA signature cannot exclude altered cargo localization, endosomal morphology, amyloid processing, or delayed protein-level phenotypes.

summary: The curated SORL1-APP cargo axis was silent at the corrected mRNA level: App knockdown was much stronger than Sorl1 knockdown but, like Sorl1, had zero corrected non-self hits.
why_it_matters: The direct cargo relationship between SORLA and APP does not translate into an acute transcriptional module in this dataset, warning against using generic differential-expression strength as the only readout for APP-trafficking genes.
main_caveats: The App comparison tests mRNA depletion rather than APP processing or endosome-localization phenotypes.

summary: A retromer-core perturbation, Vps35, produced a corrected thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic signature that was absent from the matched weak Sorl1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Although SORLA interacts with retromer to sort APP, core retromer loss and Sorl1 loss were not interchangeable at the transcriptome level; the difference is strongest as a pathway-neighbor contrast, not as evidence that Sorl1 is inactive there.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Sorl1 target engagement in this thalamic class was only nominal, so the contrast may reflect weaker Sorl1 depletion as well as biology.

summary: The VPS10P-family paralog Sort1 and the strongest all-target signature neighbors did not phenocopy Sorl1; Sort1 had no corrected non-self hits, and genome-wide Sorl1 signature correlations were near zero in representative cell types.
why_it_matters: The dataset provides no evidence that another sorting-receptor perturbation substitutes for Sorl1 or that Sorl1 sits in a large mRNA co-response module.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on all measured genes and can be dominated by weak noisy ranks when Sorl1 has no corrected downstream genes.

summary: Because human genetics points to SORL1 loss-of-function as an Alzheimer-risk direction, the knockdown arm studied here is disease-aggravating in sign; its muted mRNA profile should not be read as evidence that SORL1 loss is benign or that SORL1 restoration would lack phenotypic effects.
why_it_matters: For a receptor whose disease mechanism is cargo sorting, therapeutic assessment should include SORLA protein, APP localization, endosomal and lysosomal phenotypes, not only short-term mRNA differential expression.
main_caveats: The dataset does not contain gain-of-function or Sorl1-restoration perturbations and was generated in mouse brain rather than human AD tissue.

summary: Stx5a produced no robust target-transcript knockdown and no FDR<0.05 downstream hit in any measured cell class.
why_it_matters: Because STX5 is a core ER-Golgi SNARE, a true strong loss of function would be expected to stress essential membrane traffic; the sparse response therefore reads primarily as weak perturbation or buffering, not as evidence that Stx5a is dispensable in neurons.
main_caveats: The conclusion is about this Perturb-seq implementation; it does not test protein depletion or viability and cannot exclude unmeasured STX5 loss in a subset of cells.

summary: The only two Stx5a effects surviving FDR<0.1 were cell-type-restricted: Sidt2 up in hippocampal CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic cells and Copg1 down in cerebellar GABA cells.
why_it_matters: The data point to narrow candidate readouts rather than a shared neuronal ER-Golgi collapse; Copg1 is mechanistically close to Golgi traffic, whereas Sidt2 is best treated as an exploratory CA3/DG biomarker.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Each FDR<0.1 event occurred in only one cell class, and the cerebellar GABA call is based on only 28 perturbed cells.

summary: Measured COPI, COPII, and COG pathway neighbors failed to phenocopy Stx5a even when their own on-target knockdown was stronger.
why_it_matters: The lack of correlation argues against transferring annotations from bulk secretory-pathway perturbations to Stx5a in this dataset; STX5-related biology is either too weakly perturbed, protected by paralogous/alternative SNARE wiring, or expressed through cell-specific states.
main_caveats: Direct partners Bet1, Gosr1, Gosr2, Sec22b, Ykt6, and Scfd1 were not available as matched perturbations, so the contrast is with pathway neighbors rather than the canonical SNARE complex itself.

summary: The transcriptome was more consistent with buffered or plastic Golgi trafficking than with a uniform Stx5a-loss state.
why_it_matters: A plasticity model is biologically plausible because STX5 can participate in alternative Golgi SNARE pairings; the dataset adds an in-brain hypothesis that partial Stx5a perturbation may be absorbed differently across neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The same pattern could arise from poor Stx5a guide activity rather than true compensation; this finding should be tested with protein-level STX5 depletion or stronger guides.

summary: The screen did not robustly reproduce reported Syntaxin-5 effects on betaAPP processing, ER/Golgi stress, or Caspase-3 stress responses.
why_it_matters: Prior neuronal-cell work links Syntaxin-5 abundance and Golgi stress to amyloid biology; these Perturb-seq data should therefore not be used to infer an Alzheimer-relevant direction for Stx5a without stronger target engagement.
main_caveats: The literature used overexpression, knockdown, or pharmacologic stress in NG108-15 cells, whereas this screen used CRISPR perturbations in mouse brain cell classes and measured mRNA only.

summary: Even the strongest Stx5a cell-type signatures lacked a high-correlation positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The neighbor analysis makes the Stx5a response hard to annotate by simple signature transfer: CA3/DG glutamatergic cells had essentially no correlated perturbation, and cerebellar GABA cells had only modest Fbxo11/Atp6v1e1/Eef2-positive and Frrs1l/Cckar/Bcap31-negative neighbors.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Pearson correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and are exploratory; the neighbors are not asserted to be direct pathway partners.

summary: Pds5a perturbation lacked both FDR-significant Pds5a transcript knockdown and downstream FDR-significant DE across 21 profiled brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: This makes weak target engagement the primary interpretation of the Pds5a screen outcome and prevents assigning strong neuronal pathways from nominal genes.
main_caveats: A negative transcriptomic result cannot prove absence of PDS5A function because Pds5a mRNA and PDS5A protein depletion were not robustly demonstrated.

summary: Pds5a was much weaker than cohesin-related perturbations in the same assay, including robust Ctcf, Nipbl, Stag2, and Smc1a signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the dataset can detect transcriptional effects of cohesin and chromatin regulators, so the Pds5a null is perturbation-specific rather than a general lack of cohesin sensitivity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Related perturbations may have achieved stronger knockdown of their own targets, so the contrast should not be overinterpreted as a true separation of PDS5A from cohesin biology.

summary: The only moderate all-target Pds5a signature-neighbor structure was restricted to 308 CB GABA, with positive Wdr26 and Sp7 alignment and negative Lonp1 and Fbxo11 alignment.
why_it_matters: This preserves the one cell-type-localized signal for follow-up without promoting it to a confirmed PDS5A pathway.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: No Pds5a row in 308 CB GABA reached FDR significance, Pds5a transcript knockdown was absent, and the signature-neighbor genes are not established PDS5A interactors here.

summary: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had the strongest nominal Pds5a transcript decrease but still no downstream FDR-significant response.
why_it_matters: If the target decrease is real, this cell class may buffer partial Pds5a loss; if not, it defines the upper bound of target engagement achieved by the screen.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The target row itself had FDR=1.0, so the buffered-response interpretation is only nominal.

summary: Pds5a did not produce a recurrent cohesin, replication-stress, or Polycomb-like transcriptional module across brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: PDS5A has established roles in cohesin dynamics and chromatin regulation, but those programs were not engaged detectably by this perturbation in the dataset.
main_caveats: The analysis used DE recurrence and measured pathway-member rows, not a dedicated chromatin-loop, replication-fork, or Polycomb reporter assay.

summary: The Pds5a data provide no actionable direction for PDS5A inhibition or activation.
why_it_matters: The target is an intranuclear cohesin regulator with limited target-class tractability, and this screen did not identify a robust rescue gene, liability marker, or directional neuronal program.
main_caveats: Open Targets and ChEMBL absence of curated mechanisms is not proof of impossibility; it only argues against a current direct-drugging interpretation.

summary: Spred2 targeting produced neither measurable Spred2 mRNA depletion nor any FDR-significant transcriptional response in the 23 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: This makes the dominant interpretation a null or buffered Perturb-seq response rather than a hidden strong SPRED2 program.
main_caveats: Target engagement is judged only from Spred2 RNA; the dataset does not measure SPRED2 protein or ERK phosphorylation.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Spred2 failed to reproduce the Nf1-loss-like, Braf-opposed Ras/MAPK module despite having more perturbed cells than either comparator.
why_it_matters: SPRED2 is curated as a Ras/MAPK suppressor, so lack of an Nf1-like signature argues that the Spred2 guide assignment was not sufficient to release the canonical Ras-ERK transcriptional program in this neuronal class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Moderated by the weak Spred2 self-RNA effect; absence of a transcriptional ERK program cannot exclude nontranscriptional signaling changes.

summary: Whole-signature Spred2 effects were essentially orthogonal to the SPRED/NF1/Ras/FGF neighborhood, including the Spred1 paralog and Nf1.
why_it_matters: The near-zero correlations argue against treating Spred2 as interchangeable with Spred1 or Nf1 in this assay, even though curated pathways place SPRED proteins next to NF1/Ras regulation.
main_caveats: Most correlations involve a weak Spred2 signature with no corrected hits; the result is a divergence from expected pathway proximity, not proof of a distinct SPRED2 effector pathway.

summary: The few nominal Spred2 tail genes were cell-class private and did not form a reproducible cross-cell-type effector or biomarker list.
why_it_matters: Top uncorrected rows such as Zfp598, Tfcp2, Bace1, Sos1, and Hcfc2 should be treated as ranking artifacts or hypotheses, not as a validated SPRED2 module.
main_caveats: Recurrence was assessed from differential-expression summaries rather than raw single-cell effect estimates.

summary: The brain Perturb-seq profile does not recapitulate the disease literature in which chronic SPRED2 loss elevates RAF/MEK/ERK or TrkB/Ras/ERK signaling.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic reasoning from SPRED2 germline loss or whole-body knockout models should not assume that every neuronal cell class has an autonomous, transcriptomically visible SPRED2-loss state.
main_caveats: The literature involves chronic organismal loss, fibroblasts, zebrafish, or whole amygdala tissue; the dataset has weak Spred2 transcript engagement and cell-type-specific scRNA readouts only.

summary: The only multiple-testing significant Por response occurred in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, where Por itself and Mzt1 were the only FDR<0.05 transcripts.
why_it_matters: This concentrates the interpretable downstream signal in one thalamic glutamatergic class rather than across the many neuron classes in which Por was nominally reduced.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut also had the largest Por cell count, so apparent selectivity may be partly power-driven; the literature reference is neuron-level, not this molecular cell type.

summary: Por knockdown was directionally on-target in every tested cell type, yet transcriptional output was highly buffered: 21 of 22 cell types had no FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: POR is an electron-transfer enzyme, so loss of its activity can plausibly alter CYP-dependent metabolites without forcing a strong basal mRNA program; the Perturb-seq readout therefore captures engagement more than pathway activity.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Some cell types had weak measured target engagement and most had only dozens of perturbed cells; enzyme activity, sterols, retinoids, and lipid peroxides were not assayed.

summary: Basal Por knockdown did not produce an FDR-significant oxidative-stress, ER-stress, ferroptosis, cholesterol, or retinoic-acid sentinel transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: Known POR biology is mediated through redox chemistry and metabolite flux; the dataset argues that the disease- and ferroptosis-linked pathways are not automatically transduced into a resting neuronal mRNA stress signature after partial CRISPRi knockdown.
main_caveats: The gene set was a small sentinel panel, not a full metabolomic or lipid-peroxidation assay; absence of mRNA induction does not rule out enzymatic pathway defects.

summary: Mzt1 is a candidate single-gene marker of the responsive 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Por state.
why_it_matters: Because Mzt1 was the only FDR-significant non-target transcript, it preserves the strongest downstream dataset signal even though it is not yet mechanistically connected to POR.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene result at FDR 0.044865; no independent POR-Mzt1 literature was identified and guide/off-target or state-composition effects cannot be excluded.

summary: Por had no robust positive or negative perturbation neighbor in the screened panel.
why_it_matters: The weak nearest-neighbor correlations, together with absence of direct CYP, heme-oxygenase, squalene-monooxygenase, and cytochrome-b5 targets, prevent treating Por as interchangeable with any other perturbation in this dataset.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on transcriptomic score vectors only; true enzymatic partners were mostly absent from the perturbation panel.

summary: The small baseline neuronal transcriptomic phenotype should not be interpreted as evidence that POR inhibition is biologically safe.
why_it_matters: Human PORD and complete mouse Por loss show that POR dosage can matter through steroid, developmental, and retinoid biology, while Open Targets has disease associations but no approved or clinical POR-directed small-molecule modality; a Perturb-seq null should therefore be used as a modality/readout caveat, not as a safety endorsement.
main_caveats: The dataset used partial CRISPRi knockdown in mouse neuronal classes; it did not model biallelic human POR deficiency, embryogenesis, adrenal steroidogenesis, liver drug metabolism, or blood-brain-barrier endothelium.

direction: largest response in thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, and posterior-brain classes
summary: U2af2 perturbation produced a highly cell-type-skewed gene-level response, peaking in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut rather than spreading uniformly across all neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: U2AF2 is a core splice-site factor, but the measured downstream burden in this brain Perturb-seq assay concentrated in a subset of posterior and hypothalamic classes, implying context-dependent vulnerability or detectability.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The 217 P MY Pineal Glut result used only 22 perturbed cells, and cell-type selectivity could reflect differential guide efficiency, expression, or power rather than intrinsic biology alone.

direction: Rsrp1 and many RNA-processing genes lower; a smaller subset including Map7d1 and Iffo1 higher
summary: The most recurrent U2af2 output was a down-shift of Rsrp1 plus an RNA-processing/nuclear-speck module containing multiple splicing regulators.
why_it_matters: The module is concordant with loss of a spliceosome-associated RNA-binding protein, and recurrence across independent cell types argues that Rsrp1 and the RNA-processing genes are a better readout of U2af2 pathway engagement than the U2af2 mRNA row itself.
main_caveats: STRING enrichment was run on a recurrence-filtered gene list and does not measure alternative splicing directly.

summary: U2af2 signatures converged with other spliceosome perturbations but also with proteasome perturbations, and no robust inverse signature neighbor emerged.
why_it_matters: Prpf6, Cdc40, and Snrnp70 convergence supports a spliceosome-neighbor component, whereas top positive Psmc/Psmb/Pomp neighbors suggest that the large U2af2 signatures also contain a generic essential stress or proteostasis component rather than a pure U2AF complex fingerprint.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were modest, based on gene-level Wilcoxon scores, and U2af1 and Prpf19 were not assayed as perturbation targets.

summary: Several forebrain/cortical/hippocampal classes had no FDR-significant gene-level response to U2af2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The absence of broad DE in these classes prevents treating U2af2 as a uniform pan-neuronal transcriptional liability in this assay and highlights cells where splicing changes, if present, were buffered at total-gene expression level.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Weak or absent target-transcript knockdown in most negative classes means the result is a buffered/negative dataset observation, not proof that those neurons tolerate complete U2AF2 loss.

direction: downstream response without FDR-significant U2af2 mRNA decrease
summary: Measured U2af2 mRNA was never significantly reduced at FDR<0.05, even in classes with hundreds of downstream hits.
why_it_matters: The target-transcript row cannot be used as the sole quality-control gate for this perturbation; it also makes the large 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 217 P MY Pineal Glut signatures useful but caveated.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: This is a gene-level RNA readout; guide activity could affect protein or splicing without producing a large captured change in total U2af2 transcript, but off-target or composition effects cannot be excluded from these rows alone.

summary: Rbfox1, a splicing-factor disease-network member linked to U2AF2/PRPF19 biology, did not phenocopy U2af2 in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset.
why_it_matters: Human and fly data place RBFOX1 in a spliceosome-malfunction neurodevelopmental network, but the nearly orthogonal Rbfox1 and U2af2 signatures indicate that this relationship is not a simple one-step transcriptional phenocopy in the sampled mouse neuronal classes.
main_caveats: PRPF19 itself was not an assayed perturbation target, the assay reports gene-level abundance rather than splicing, and the comparison uses mouse brain cells rather than developing human neurons or Drosophila mushroom bodies.

direction: loss or inhibition predicted to be hazardous in neurons
summary: Direct U2AF2 inhibition is a risky therapeutic direction for the nervous system unless exquisitely context restricted.
why_it_matters: The dataset shows that partial U2af2 perturbation can move hundreds of genes in selected neuronal classes, while human genetics links de novo U2AF2 variants to neurodevelopmental disease and ChEMBL shows only early biochemical U2AF2 activity records rather than a validated therapeutic mechanism.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Perturb-seq knockdown is not the same as small-molecule inhibition, and the sampled mouse cell types are not matched to human embryonic neurodevelopmental populations.

summary: Tbc1d32 did not yield an FDR-stable transcriptional phenotype in any measured brain cell type, and the target RNA itself was not robustly reduced.
why_it_matters: The primary interpretation is target non-engagement or an assay-insensitive perturbation rather than a missing brain-wide ciliary program.
main_caveats: This is a negative result from RNA differential expression; coding disruption of Tbc1d32 protein could occur without measurable Tbc1d32 RNA loss.

summary: The pineal glutamatergic cluster was the only context with a large negative Tbc1d32 point estimate, but the response remained below transcriptome-wide FDR thresholds.
why_it_matters: It is the only plausible cell-type-restricted engagement signal, yet it is not strong enough to support a downstream pathway claim.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only 33 perturbed cells were available and the Tbc1d32 on-target row itself had q=0.885.

summary: The expected Hedgehog and ciliary marker transcripts were not detectably coupled to Tbc1d32 perturbation in this single-cell RNA readout.
why_it_matters: Prior work places Tbc1d32/Bromi in primary-cilium assembly and cilia-dependent Gli2/Shh signaling, so the lack of Gli/Ptch/Smo or ciliary-gene regulation argues that this screen did not elicit the canonical developmental output.
main_caveats: Absence of mRNA changes does not exclude structural cilium defects, and the target transcript was weakly engaged.

summary: Tbc1d32 signatures did not converge with assayed ciliary, Hedgehog, or TBC-family neighbors.
why_it_matters: A functional neighbor phenocopy would have rescued interpretation despite a weak scalar Tbc1d32 signature; instead, correlations were near zero and most nearby perturbations were also sparse.
main_caveats: This is a restricted signature-neighbor analysis; several exact TBC1D32 partners such as CDK20 and FAM149B1 were not assayed as perturbations.

summary: Known TBC1D32 disease genetics point to developmental, pituitary, and retinal ciliopathies, while this mouse-brain screen provides no robust neuronal transcriptomic disease signature.
why_it_matters: The perturbation dataset should not be used to infer a protective or deleterious neuronal direction for TBC1D32 loss; it primarily shows that the canonical ciliopathy axis was not captured here.
main_caveats: The disease literature is human and developmental or sensory, whereas the dataset is Perturb-seq RNA profiling of mouse brain cell classes.

summary: Slc22a17 RNA was depleted across most assayed neuronal classes, but the response was dominated by the target transcript itself rather than a broad downstream program.
why_it_matters: This separates guide activity from biological output: the absence of many corrected downstream genes is unlikely to be explained simply by failure to knock down Slc22a17 in the best-engaged strata.
main_caveats: Several individual cell types were low-count or only nominally target-engaged; buffering is based on single-cell RNA rather than receptor protein or iron flux.

summary: Msmo1 up-regulation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut was the only non-target FDR<0.05 event and was accompanied by nominal upward movement of additional sterol genes.
why_it_matters: MSMO1 provides the clearest candidate readout of a Slc22a17 downstream effect, but the surrounding pathway was weak and therefore should be treated as a follow-up biomarker rather than a validated cholesterol program.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only Msmo1 survived correction; other sterol genes were nominal with FDR=1.0 and the effect was seen in one cell type.

summary: Slc22a17 knockdown did not activate a corrected LCN2, alternate-receptor, or iron-homeostasis transcriptomic response.
why_it_matters: The result distinguishes receptor depletion from the ligand-driven apo/holo-LCN2 iron-transport states described in the literature and suggests that basal neuronal cells can buffer loss of this receptor at the mRNA level.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay LCN2 ligand state, iron, receptor internalization, or inflammatory stimulation; absence of RNA changes is not proof that the protein pathway is inactive.

summary: LCN2-receptor and iron-uptake neighboring perturbations did not converge with the Slc22a17 signature.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq data do not support treating Lrp2/Lrp1/Lrp8/Tfrc loss as interchangeable with Slc22a17 loss in these neuronal classes.
main_caveats: Lrp2, Lrp8, and Tfrc were not detectably knocked down at their own transcripts, and Lrp1 engagement was restricted to two cell types.

summary: Robust Slc22a17 depletion with little basal iron/apoptosis transcriptional output argues that SLC22A17 interventions may be highly ligand- and state-dependent in brain cells.
why_it_matters: LCN2-SLC22A17 biology has been linked to iron handling, apoptosis, neuronal structure, and neuroinflammation; this dataset warns that target knockdown alone may not predict behavior in stressed or glia-rich disease settings.
main_caveats: Perturb-seq did not include exogenous LCN2, injury, infection, or direct measurements of neuronal survival.

summary: A sparse whole-library signature-neighbor scan found no strong positive or negative Slc22a17-like perturbation.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpretation of individual nominal genes as a convergent module and supports the view that the Slc22a17 response is weak and idiosyncratic in this experiment.
main_caveats: The screen used only p<0.01 features and zero-filled missing genes, so it is a restricted heuristic rather than a full-rank correlation over every gene.

summary: Uqcrq perturbation was a mostly FDR-silent complex-III loss-of-function signature: nominal Uqcrq mRNA decreases were seen, but only one gene across the 23 cell-type comparisons reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: UQCRQ is a mitochondrial complex-III subunit, so the main biological readout of this dataset is negative: acute Uqcrq targeting in these brain cells did not elicit a broad oxidative-phosphorylation stress transcriptome.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|155 MB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Protein abundance, complex-III enzymatic activity, and raw guide efficiency were not measured in this DE table; Uqcrq transcript FDR was never significant.

summary: Nominal Uqcrq engagement was concentrated in a subset of caudal and thalamic classes and was absent even in some well-powered cortical classes.
why_it_matters: The weak aggregate phenotype should not be treated as a universal absence of effect; some cell classes showed nominal on-target mRNA loss while others with more than 100 perturbed cells showed essentially no Uqcrq shift.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|155 MB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type pattern is based on nominal target-transcript tests; the strongest logFC cases include low cell counts, especially 217 P MY Pineal Glut.

summary: Uqcrq did not phenocopy other respiratory-chain perturbations at the transcriptome level despite curated complex-III membership and network proximity.
why_it_matters: The result argues that Uqcrq cannot be interpreted as interchangeable with Uqcrc1, Cyc1, or Uqcrfs1 in this Perturb-seq readout; other ETC targets had stronger own-transcript depletion and still showed almost no score-vector correlation with Uqcrq.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was calculated over Wilcoxon score vectors; low correlations can reflect weak Uqcrq knockdown as well as true biological buffering.

summary: Gpr180 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the only multiple-testing-significant Uqcrq-associated gene change.
why_it_matters: This isolates Gpr180 as a context-specific Uqcrq-response marker candidate, but its uniqueness also shows that the robust dataset signal was not a recurrent complex-III or pan-mitochondrial module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Single cell class and single FDR-significant gene; no mechanistic link between Gpr180 and complex III is established by these data.

summary: The quiet Perturb-seq phenotype should not be read as evidence that UQCRQ is dispensable or safely druggable in brain.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic UQCRQ mutation causes mitochondrial complex-III deficiency with severe neurologic disease, so an acute mouse single-cell mRNA phenotype with weak on-target knockdown is an underpowered proxy for inherited complex-III enzymology.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks complex-III activity, mitochondrial respiration, protein turnover, and organismal disease phenotypes.

summary: Wnk3 perturbation produced weak apparent target engagement and an extremely sparse transcriptomic response.
why_it_matters: The strongest interpretation is that most Wnk3 guide/cell-type contrasts are underpowered or post-transcriptional rather than a broad transcriptional WNK3 program.
main_caveats: Loss of WNK3 protein or kinase activity was not measured; weak transcript depletion could reflect low Wnk3 expression, inefficient guides, mRNA-independent editing, or limited cells.

summary: Pvalb GABA neurons selectively coupled Wnk3 perturbation to Stim1 down-regulation and Syt3 up-regulation.
why_it_matters: The two FDR hits are both linked to Ca2+-dependent neuronal secretion or store-operated Ca2+ entry, placing the only multi-gene Wnk3 response in a fast-spiking inhibitory class that is relevant to GABA physiology.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only two genes passed FDR and Wnk3 itself was not significantly depleted in the same cells; the connection to chloride handling is indirect.

summary: TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons showed an isolated Ppp2cb decrease after Wnk3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Ppp2cb encodes the PP2A catalytic beta subunit, so this single-cell-type hit suggests a phosphatase-balancing response rather than a shared SLC12 cotransporter transcriptome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a one-gene FDR result with absent Wnk3 self knockdown and no direct WNK3-PP2A literature in this cell class.

summary: Wnk3 did not phenocopy Wnk1, Stk39, Slc12a2, or Slc12a5 perturbations in the Wnk3-responsive classes.
why_it_matters: Although these genes occupy a coherent WNK-SPAK/OSR1-cation-chloride cotransporter network, the Perturb-seq readout argues against treating their transcriptional signatures as interchangeable.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is based on transcriptome score correlations; pathway activity was not assayed at the level of OXSR1/STK39 or KCC2 phosphorylation.

summary: The WNK3-SLC12 pathway was not transcriptionally induced or repressed at the pathway-gene level.
why_it_matters: The absence of Slc12a2, Slc12a5, Stk39, Oxsr1, or Wnk1 RNA changes is consistent with prior neuronal work in which WNK3 altered KCC2 function through phosphorylation and membrane activity rather than total KCC2 or NKCC1 abundance.
main_caveats: A null RNA result cannot prove normal cotransporter activity; phosphoproteomics, surface KCC2, and chloride-flux assays would be required.

summary: No strong same-cell-type positive or negative signature neighbor was found for Wnk3.
why_it_matters: The lack of high-correlation neighbors, including among all assayed perturbations, argues that the few Wnk3 DE genes should be read as local cell-type events rather than a large reusable transcriptional module.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only the two Wnk3 FDR-positive cell types were searched exhaustively for global score-correlation neighbors.

summary: Rpgr perturbation produced no corrected target depletion or downstream transcriptomic response in any of 21 matched mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The screen does not support a broad RPGR-dependent brain expression program, despite strong prior evidence for RPGR function in retinal cilia.
main_caveats: The negative call is conditioned on weak measured Rpgr RNA engagement; no retinal photoreceptor cell type was assayed.

summary: 046 CTX-CGE GABA was the only Rpgr stratum with a sub-0.2 adjusted p value, pairing nominal Rpgr self-decrease with nominal Apc downregulation.
why_it_matters: If Rpgr has any detectable neuronal response in this dataset, CTX-CGE GABA is the least weak candidate context, but its signal is below conventional FDR thresholds.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Apc did not pass 10% FDR and no pathway-level corrected program accompanied it.

summary: B9d1, unlike Rpgr, generated a corrected 308 CB GABA signature.
why_it_matters: The ciliary transition-zone contrast shows that a related ciliary perturbation can be visible in the same brain screen and makes the Rpgr result a target/context-specific null rather than a global inability to observe ciliary biology.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: B9d1 is a related transition-zone/MKS gene, not a direct RPGR complex member; the B9d1 output genes are a cerebellar GABA expression signature, not a validated ciliary pathway.

summary: Curated RPGR ciliary neighbors and the full top-signature scan showed no coherent phenocopy of the weak Rpgr signature.
why_it_matters: Known RPGR ciliary localization partners and disease-family neighbors should not be collapsed into a single Perturb-seq module in these brain data.
main_caveats: The seed Rpgr signature was not FDR-supported; Rpgrip1l is an RPGRIP1-like transition-zone protein rather than the RPGRIP1 interactor described in the ORF15 paper.

summary: Other ciliary targets showed corrected self-transcript effects in high-count midbrain and thalamic strata where Rpgr remained silent.
why_it_matters: Corrected Ahi1, Cplane1, Ttc8, and Arl3 responses demonstrate that the dataset can register ciliary target perturbations, refining the Rpgr null to weak engagement or a non-retinal brain context rather than complete assay failure.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only selected ciliary targets had corrected rows, and their strongest cell types had more perturbed cells than the corresponding Rpgr strata.

direction: negative target engagement with buffered downstream transcription
summary: Sgce knockdown was detected mainly as modest Sgce self-depletion and produced no adjusted downstream DE gene in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: The target is a membrane-complex component and human myoclonus-dystonia gene; the dataset says that acute Sgce loss in these broad brain classes is not a strong cell-autonomous transcriptional switch.
main_caveats: The strongest adjusted p value is 0.1849, so all downstream genes are sub-FDR; per-cell-type perturbation counts never exceeded 199.

direction: nominal in MB/P/MY GABA and thalamic glutamatergic cells; missing or weak in dopamine, cerebellar, Pvalb, and LGE GABA contrasts
summary: The nominal Sgce response was concentrated in 191 MB P MY GABA and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while the dopaminergic and cerebellar contexts emphasized by mouse expression studies were missing or weak.
why_it_matters: Prior mapping highlighted midbrain monoaminergic neurons and Purkinje cells; this dataset cannot be read as a clean validation in exactly those populations and instead localizes the measurable single-cell transcript signal to other broad labels.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|215 MB Dopa|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The 215 MB Dopa result is absence of a post-filtered Sgce contrast, not a measured null; broad cell labels may not isolate Purkinje, serotonergic, or dopaminergic subtypes.

summary: Sgce did not phenocopy the measured sarcoglycan/dystrophin-glycoprotein perturbations Sgcd, Dag1, or Dmd.
why_it_matters: Although these genes are assigned to the same extracellular-matrix-linked sarcoglycan/dystrophin complex, their Perturb-seq score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with Sgce, arguing against simple interchangeability at the acute transcriptomic level.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Sgcd and Dmd were themselves weakly engaged or sparsely measured, so loss of convergence could reflect comparator perturbation quality as well as true biology.

direction: uncoupled from dopamine/A2A-cAMP and other dystonia-gene signatures
summary: Sgce loss did not create a Drd2/Adora2a/Pde10a/Gnal/Adcy5 transcriptional signature, despite prior striatal D2 and A2A pharmacology in Sgce models.
why_it_matters: The disease-relevant dopamine/A2A axis appears likely to be a physiological or circuit phenotype rather than a directly readable acute mRNA module in this dataset; scalar transcriptomic similarity could therefore miss a clinically directional rescue pathway.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The profiled cell classes are not purified striatal medium spiny neurons, and the comparisons are signature correlations rather than receptor physiology or dopamine-release assays.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor search found no high-correlation Sgce-like or Sgce-opposing perturbation.
why_it_matters: The Sgce program is too weak and cell-type-private to support a robust surrogate perturbation or reversal marker in this dataset.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were calculated in the two cell types with the strongest Sgce on-target depletion; a weaker response in another cell type could still have a different neighbor.

summary: Snap25 perturbation achieved broad direct transcript knockdown across glutamatergic and GABAergic brain classes.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset signal is therefore interpretable as engagement of the intended transcript in most assayed neuronal contexts, not as a failed guide globally.
main_caveats: Three cell types did not pass FDR for the target row and the dataset measures RNA rather than vesicle fusion.

summary: Most FDR-engaged Snap25 knockdowns were transcriptionally buffered: 15 of 19 target-significant cell types had no secondary FDR hit, including a very strong 155 MB Glut knockdown.
why_it_matters: Loss of a core exocytosis transcript did not usually convert into a detectable cell-body mRNA state change, so acute transcriptomic readout is likely insensitive to SNAP25 functional loss.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: No electrophysiology or protein measurement is present; several target-only examples have low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Pvalb interneurons were the clearest cell-type-restricted responder, adding Septin4 down-regulation and Syt7 up-regulation to Snap25 knockdown.
why_it_matters: The directionally split Septin4/Syt7 response nominates a Pvalb-specific presynaptic scaffold/calcium-sensor adjustment after SNAP25 loss rather than a pan-neuronal exocytosis program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Only two non-target FDR genes support the module; Septin4 literature is strongest in dopaminergic neurons and Syt7 literature is from hippocampal glutamatergic neurons.

summary: The remaining significant non-target genes were isolated singletons rather than a recurrent Snap25-response module.
why_it_matters: Insig1, Ypel4, and Atp1a3 may be context biomarkers, but the absence of recurrence and weak all-target signature correlations argue against a shared stress or synaptic-gene program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Each singleton is one gene in one cell type; the full-signature correlation search is exploratory and based on weak correlations.

summary: Stxbp1 perturbation generated many more secondary transcripts than Snap25 in matched cell types despite both genes being in the SNARE/SM exocytosis machinery.
why_it_matters: SNAP25 and Munc18-1/STXBP1 should not be treated as interchangeable nodes of one transcriptional response, even though they collaborate during vesicle fusion.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Stxbp1 may have guide potency, expression, or collateral roles distinct from Snap25; the comparison is transcriptomic.

summary: The sparse RNA response to Snap25 loss should not be interpreted as biological tolerance of central SNAP25 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Literature places SNAP25 cleavage or mutation directly upstream of neurotransmitter-release failure and developmental epileptic encephalopathy, so RNA silence is more consistent with poor transcriptional surveillance than with functional safety.
main_caveats: The dataset uses partial mRNA perturbation in mouse neurons, whereas botulinum toxins cleave protein and human disease variants can be dominant missense alleles.

summary: Hippocampal-like glutamatergic and cerebellar GABA classes lacked FDR-confirmed on-target Snap25 knockdown and showed no interpretable downstream response.
why_it_matters: These cell types should be treated as uninformative for SNAP25 biology in this screen rather than as evidence that CA-field or cerebellar neurons are resistant to SNAP25 loss.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All three target rows were nominally negative; the negative finding is failure after multiple-testing correction, not a positive null estimate of protein function.

summary: Plxna2 perturbation produced FDR-level depletion of the Plxna2 transcript in only three of 23 profiled neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The clearest dataset signal is where the reagent demonstrably engaged the target; downstream inferences should be centered on 052 Pvalb Gaba, 155 MB Glut, and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than all profiled classes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: FDR-level target depletion is a technical engagement readout and may reflect expression or power; 11 additional cell types had nominal Plxna2 decreases that did not pass FDR.

summary: The three FDR-engaged Plxna2 cell classes were transcriptionally buffered: no secondary gene reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: PLXNA2 is embedded in semaphorin pathways that remodel cytoskeleton and axons, but perturbing its transcript here did not create a broad mRNA signature in the engaged classes; mRNA is therefore a weak readout of receptor-output state.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a negative transcriptomic result, not proof that PLXNA2 protein, cytoskeletal signaling, neurite morphology, or migration were unchanged.

summary: Med15 was the only non-target FDR hit for Plxna2, but it occurred in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut where the Plxna2 self row did not pass FDR.
why_it_matters: The strongest apparent downstream gene is not anchored by strong on-target engagement, so it should be treated as a context-specific singleton rather than the core PLXNA2 program.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Med15 may still be a real L2/3 PIR-AON-ENT response, but the dataset provides no second FDR-supported transcript or FDR-level target row in this class.

summary: A Sema5a perturbation was strongly engaged in the same 151 thalamic class as Plxna2, and Plxna4 was nominally engaged there, but neither produced a shared FDR-level downstream program.
why_it_matters: Known developmental Sema5A/PLXNA2 and Sema6A/Plxna2/Plxna4 relationships do not translate into simple ligand-paralog interchangeability in this thalamic Perturb-seq state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Sema5A-PlxnA2-Rap1 and Plxna2/Plxna4/Sema6A were defined in developing hippocampal contexts, whereas this comparison is a profiled thalamic transcriptome and Plxna4 self depletion was only nominal.

summary: The disease-relevant developmental PLXNA2 pathway is not recapitulated as a large neuronal mRNA program after partial Plxna2 knockdown in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Human PLXNA2 has schizophrenia and intellectual-disability candidate links, and mouse work ties Plxna2 to dentate and hippocampal development; these data argue that a missing neuronal mRNA signature in this assay should not be read as absence of developmental morphogenetic biology.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Published disease links are genetic and developmental, not direct evidence that the profiled cell classes require PLXNA2-mediated transcription.

summary: Exploratory restricted-signature correlations did not reveal a robust semaphorin/plexin positive or negative neighbor for Plxna2.
why_it_matters: A related-target or pathway-neighbor hypothesis would be stronger if top Plxna2 neighbors repeatedly included Sema or Plexin perturbations; instead, top neighbors were unstable and even included a safe-target control anticorrelation.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on only the 50 most nominal Plxna2 genes, so they are useful as a missed-finding audit but not as evidence for mechanism.

summary: Pibf1 knockdown produced no transcriptome-wide significant differential-expression response in any assayed mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: PIBF1 is a curated cilium/Joubert gene, so the result argues that this screen did not capture an acute mRNA program downstream of Pibf1 rather than revealing a strong ciliary-response transcriptome.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was only weakly reduced, all target-row FDR values were 1, and the assay lacks direct cilium morphology or protein-turnover readouts.

summary: The most target-engaged Pibf1 neuronal contexts still buffered the perturbation at the genome-wide DE level.
why_it_matters: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut each showed nominal Pibf1 mRNA decreases, yet neither generated any FDR-significant downstream gene, separating weak on-target transcript lowering from a detectable transcriptional state change.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Target engagement was nominal rather than FDR-significant; buffering could reflect insufficient CRISPRi, slow turnover of a centrosomal protein, or a non-transcriptional phenotype.

summary: Pibf1 did not converge with a Joubert/ciliary comparator panel despite known centrosomal and ciliary network membership.
why_it_matters: Ahi1, Cep290, Cplane1, Ift88, Kif3b, Bbs genes, Cep genes, and Rpgrip1l are biologically closer to Pibf1 than random targets, but their perturbation signatures were nearly uncorrelated with Pibf1 and had only four FDR hits across 278 target-cell signatures.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Most comparator perturbations were also transcriptionally weak, so absence of convergence does not prove that ciliary protein functions are unrelated.

summary: Pibf1 perturbation was uncoupled from a measurable Shh/Gli/Fgf developmental transcriptional panel.
why_it_matters: Primary cilia specialize in Hedgehog signaling during development, and PIBF1 is required for cilium assembly; the dataset instead shows that neuronal Pibf1 perturbation did not move Shh, Gli, Ptch, Smo, Fgf8, Fgfr1, or Lhx6 after FDR correction.
main_caveats: Many morphogen-readout transcripts are lowly expressed in postmitotic brain cell types, and the Perturb-seq assay did not test embryonic patterning conditions.

summary: Pibf1 lacked even a restricted all-target signature neighbor, positive or negative, in the cell classes with the strongest nominal target decrease.
why_it_matters: The nearest signatures had correlations near zero and included unrelated or safe-target perturbations; therefore the Pibf1 cells should not be clustered into a stronger pathway solely by nearest-neighbor searches.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlation analysis used weak Pibf1 rank vectors, so low correlations mainly serve as a guardrail against overinterpreting nominal genes.

summary: The Timmdc1 guide group did not measurably deplete the Timmdc1 transcript and produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: This is the primary result: downstream absences cannot be interpreted as biological dispensability unless the perturbation is first shown to engage the target.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Transcript absence is an mRNA readout only; low endogenous Timmdc1 detection or guide inefficiency could mask protein perturbation.

summary: The expected complex-I/OXPHOS pathway did not emerge as a coherent Timmdc1 response; mitochondrial hits were isolated, nominal, FDR=1.0, and directionally mixed.
why_it_matters: TIMMDC1 is annotated and experimentally described as a complex-I assembly factor, so a flat, mixed OXPHOS transcriptome points to assay buffering or weak engagement rather than to the canonical biochemical loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: The conclusion is restricted to mRNA signatures after weak Timmdc1 perturbation; complex-I enzyme activity, respiration, and ROS were not measured.

summary: Within the same brain cell classes, Timmdc1 behaved like other weak NDUFAF assembly-factor perturbations and unlike structural respiratory-chain subunits or Uqcrc1 that showed strong self-transcript depletion.
