cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The FDR-resolved phenotype is centered on one cell class; many other cell classes had fewer than 60 perturbed cells.

summary: The Ufsp2 signature converged with the Uba5 and Ufc1 UFMylation signatures in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: UBA5 and UFC1 form the UFM1 E1/E2 cascade, whereas UFSP2 is a UFM1 protease; their ranking as the top positive signature neighbors argues that the Ufsp2 phenotype is pathway on-target rather than an arbitrary stress response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on mRNA Wilcoxon scores; the dataset does not measure UFM1 conjugates or UFSP2 protease activity.

summary: The 155 MB Glut Ufsp2 program emphasized a mixed oxidative-phosphorylation/V-ATPase module and did not resolve as a canonical unfolded-protein-response signature.
why_it_matters: UFMylation is often framed as ER homeostasis and ER-ribosome quality control; the Perturb-seq readout refines that expectation by showing strong Atp6v0c, Cox5a, Timm8b, and Ndufa2 effects while Ddit3, Hspa5, and Xbp1 remained nominal or absent after multiple-testing correction.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only three of the leading 155 MB Glut genes drove the KEGG oxidative-phosphorylation enrichment, and UPR genes were not significant after FDR correction.

summary: Apparent Ufsp2 mRNA depletion was not sufficient to guarantee a corrected downstream response.
why_it_matters: The 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA comparison had the strongest nominal Ufsp2 transcript decrease but no FDR<0.10 downstream genes, so quiet cell types cannot be interpreted simply as unobserved biology without considering weak editing, buffering, or power.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The Ufsp2 target row was only nominal in 066 and had FDR 1.0, so this is an exploratory negative result rather than proof of biological buffering.

summary: Disease-linked UFMylation genes map to a selective thalamic/midbrain neuronal vulnerability rather than an indiscriminate pan-neuronal Ufsp2 response.
why_it_matters: Human UFSP2, UFM1, and UFC1 variants cause neurodevelopmental or epileptic disease, and the dataset shows that the pathway axis is detectable in two glutamatergic classes but differs in depth: shallow Ufsp2 signatures in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut align with massive Uba5/Ufc1 responses, whereas 155 MB Glut is the only cell class with a corrected Ufsp2 program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Human disease genetics do not specify the same mouse cell classes, and the Perturb-seq assay measures acute transcription rather than development or seizures.

summary: The convergent UFSP2–UBA5–UFC1 signature is biologically coherent but not yet a clean small-molecule direction.
why_it_matters: The perturbation signature warns that pharmacologically altering UFSP2 would intersect a neurodevelopmental UFMylation module, while public target resources did not show an approved or high-quality small-molecule UFSP2 tractability flag or a ChEMBL UFSP2 target record.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a target-strategy warning, not evidence for toxicity or efficacy of a UFSP2 inhibitor.

summary: Taf1b perturbation did not yield a corrected on-target or downstream transcriptional phenotype in mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: TAF1B is a core SL1/Pol I initiation factor, so the absence of FDR-supported changes is best interpreted as inadequate or very mild loss of function in this dataset rather than evidence that TAF1B is dispensable.
main_caveats: Raw guide abundance, percent-expressing cells, and rRNA transcription were not available; all target-transcript adjusted p values were 1.0.

summary: The apparent CNU-HYa HY GABA peak is only nominal and should not be promoted to a Taf1b-selective neuronal program.
why_it_matters: Arhgdig in CNU-HYa HY GABA was the lowest-FDR row in the entire Taf1b subset, but q=0.130 and the Taf1b transcript increased nominally in the same stratum, arguing against a robust cell-type-restricted hit or biomarker.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative selectivity call; the CNU-HYa genes are nominal observations and not validated biomarkers.

summary: Pvalb and MB/P/MY GABA cells showed the only nominal decreases of Taf1b mRNA, but those decreases were not strong enough to propagate to FDR-supported downstream changes.
why_it_matters: If these small target decreases are biological, mature GABAergic neurons tolerate about 20-35% Taf1b transcript reduction without a detectable mRNA program in this assay.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Both Taf1b on-target rows have FDR 1.0; post-transcriptional TAF1B protein depletion and rDNA output were not measured.

summary: Rrn3, a Pol I initiation neighbor that recruits Pol I to SL1, produced corrected signatures in shared cell types whereas Taf1b did not.
why_it_matters: The contrast shows that the dataset can recover responses to at least one Pol-I-initiation perturbation, but it does not prove a mechanistic divergence between RRN3 and TAF1B because Taf1b itself was poorly engaged.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Rrn3 is pathway-adjacent rather than an SL1 subunit; its target-transcript FDR in 151 TH was 0.096, and Taf1b-guide efficacy remains the main alternative explanation.

summary: Taf1b lacks a reproducible signature neighborhood in the assayed library.
why_it_matters: Neither curated neighbors nor the strongest empirical positive or negative score correlations converged on a Taf1b module, consistent with the absence of a stable downstream program.
main_caveats: Only Rrn3, Myc, and Taf1 were available among the queried Pol-I/TAF comparators; Tbp and direct SL1 subunits Taf1a, Taf1c, and Taf1d were absent.

summary: Cancer reports of TAF1B-depletion nucleolar stress should not be projected onto these mouse neurons.
why_it_matters: TAF1B knockdown has been proposed to suppress ribosome biogenesis and proliferation in tumor cells, but the brain Perturb-seq data show no corrected Taf1b knockdown program and no consistent Myc decrease, leaving neuronal consequences of potent TAF1B inhibition unresolved.
main_caveats: The cancer studies used proliferating human tumor cells with stronger experimental depletion; the Perturb-seq assay profiled mouse brain mRNA and did not measure 45S pre-rRNA, ribosome assembly, p53 protein, apoptosis, or long-term cell loss.

summary: Tlr9 knockout/knockdown produced no robust transcriptomic phenotype in any profiled glutamatergic or GABAergic neuronal subclass.
why_it_matters: The global null result prevents the weak nominal rows from being interpreted as a constitutive neuronal TLR9 program and is consistent with poor baseline Tlr9 expression in these cells.
main_caveats: The screen reports RNA-level ranks; failure to move the very low Tlr9 transcript does not prove an efficient protein perturbation.

summary: The largest apparent cell-type response was limited to nominal hits in 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and did not survive FDR correction.
why_it_matters: This preserves the one cell type with the lowest Tlr9 p values while explicitly downgrading Kat8, Gria4, Phf12 and related genes to exploratory status.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: All adjusted p values were >=0.539 and most nominal genes appeared in only one cell type.

summary: Measured MyD88/NF-kB/IRF output genes were not activated downstream of Tlr9 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Canonical TLR9 signaling should couple DNA recognition to MyD88-dependent NF-kB and interferon-regulatory transcription; the neuronal screen instead shows pathway silence rather than a muted version of an innate-immune response.
main_caveats: Several cytokines were likely near the detection floor in neurons, so absence of their DE is best read together with the absent Tlr9 target-transcript effect.

summary: Tlr9 did not converge transcriptionally with assayed endosomal or inflammatory TLR-family neighbors.
why_it_matters: Although Tlr9 is functionally linked to Tlr7, Tlr2/Tlr4, MyD88-associated adaptors, and Unc93b1 in immune cells, the Perturb-seq correlations with Tlr2, Tlr3, Tlr4, Tlr7, Tlr8, Chuk, NF-kB, IRF, STAT and Tbk1 perturbations were weak; the Tbk1/Nfkb2 signal in 308 CB GABA was isolated and only hypothesis-generating.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Signature correlations use weak, FDR-negative Tlr9 profiles and should be treated as a screen-level negative comparison, not as evidence that these immune proteins cannot share mechanisms in responsive cells.

summary: The neuronal Tlr9 null is more compatible with an immune-cell effector model than with broad cell-autonomous TLR9 action across brain projection-neuron classes.
why_it_matters: Human expression resources place TLR9 in plasmacytoid dendritic and lymphoid compartments, Open Targets connects TLR9 mainly to immune, infection and oncology indications, and a mouse seizure study assigns hippocampal TLR9 function to microglia; the 22 profiled neuronal classes therefore look like a poor proxy for these disease circuits.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay microglia for Tlr9 perturbation, so it cannot directly confirm the microglial branch.

summary: The screen does not reproduce the activity-dependent CA1 neuronal Tlr9 program reported after learning.
why_it_matters: A 2024 mouse study showed that neuron-specific Tlr9 knockdown blunted fear-conditioning-induced CA1 gene-expression changes; by contrast, unstimulated 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut cells had 49 Tlr9-perturbed cells, no Tlr9 transcript shift, and no FDR-positive genes, implying that any neuronal Tlr9 biology is state- or subcluster-restricted rather than a constitutive CA1/DG signature.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The screen pooled MEA/LA/CA1/DG neurons, used only 49 perturbed cells in this contrast, and did not model fear conditioning, DNA damage, or the specific CA1 ensembles in the literature study.

summary: This dataset should not be used to choose TLR9 agonism versus antagonism for clinical immunomodulation.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL lists both agonist and antagonist mechanisms for human TLR9, whereas the screen shows no direct neuronal target engagement or innate-output response; therapeutic direction is therefore likely to depend on immune-cell stimulation or suppression rather than on the resting neuronal signatures measured here.
main_caveats: The warning concerns inference from this neuronal screen only and does not argue against TLR9 as a druggable immune target.

summary: Wt1 guide assignment did not measurably deplete the Wt1 transcript in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: The downstream null phenotype cannot be interpreted as a verified cellular loss of WT1 protein; it may reflect low baseline Wt1 RNA, ineffective cutting, RNA persistence after DNA editing, or dilution within broad cell classes.
main_caveats: RNA abundance is an indirect target-engagement readout for a CRISPR perturbation and the parquet contains no editing, protein, or guide-efficiency measurements.

summary: Wt1 showed no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response across 22 glutamatergic or GABAergic brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The Wt1 perturbation behaves as a molecularly silent target in this atlas rather than as a broad regulator of neuronal state.
main_caveats: The absence of corrected DE is conditional on weak Wt1 RNA engagement, modest per-cell-type Wt1 cell counts, and bulked analysis within broad transcriptomic labels.

summary: The only Wt1-responsive signals were exploratory, nominal hotspots in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 053 Sst Gaba, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut rather than a recurring Wt1 gene module.
why_it_matters: Ppp4r3b, Mapk14, and Cnot11 nominate possible follow-up markers only if one accepts nominal statistics; the lack of FDR support and cross-cell recurrence argues against treating them as WT1 targets now.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|053 Sst Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: All genes discussed in this finding failed FDR<0.05; the cell types with the lowest adjusted p values contained only 58-81 Wt1-perturbed cells.

summary: Wt1 did not converge with the screened CBP/p300 coactivator perturbations or with any strong same-cell-type signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: A known WT1 chromatin-cofactor mechanism from kidney and epicardium was not detectable as an EP300/CREBBP-like neuronal transcriptomic state, reinforcing that WT1 cofactor biology cannot be transferred uncritically into these brain classes.
main_caveats: Basp1 itself was absent from the perturbation library; EP300 and CREBBP are pleiotropic coactivators, and all correlations use weak Wt1 signatures rather than validated Wt1 loss-of-function signatures.

summary: The dataset refines neural WT1 biology toward rare developmental contexts instead of a shared requirement across the sampled mouse-brain neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: Published Wt1 phenotypes in embryonic cortex, retina, spinal dI6 interneurons, and hindbrain dB4 neurons do not predict a robust acute Perturb-seq signature in the broad Glut/GABA classes sampled here.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq labels may miss or dilute rare WT1-positive retinal, spinal, or hindbrain subtypes; the perturbation stage and assay are not matched to the cited embryonic or circuit studies.

summary: Ndn editing produced reproducible Ndn transcript depletion in a subset of neuronal classes rather than uniformly across all 23 classes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation is interpretable in the engaged subcortical and midbrain/hypothalamic classes, but the screen should not be read as a pan-neuronal Ndn loss-of-function experiment.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Some additional classes were only nominal and target depletion may reflect baseline Ndn detectability as well as editing efficiency.

summary: Strong Ndn mRNA knockdown was buffered: after multiple-testing correction, every significant Ndn-perturbation hit was the Ndn transcript itself.
why_it_matters: Necdin is connected in prior work to E2F/p53, Dlx/MAGE-D1, neurotrophin, and neuronal survival mechanisms, so the absence of an acute FDR-significant downstream mRNA program is biologically informative rather than simply a null result.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The assay measures scRNA steady-state abundance only; nominal hits may exist below FDR, and protein-complex, circuit, migration, or stress-evoked effects could be missed.

summary: Several cortical, hippocampal, and inhibitory classes showed weak Ndn target engagement, making their downstream negative results uninterpretable as evidence of true biological resistance.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb and Sst GABAergic classes, L5-6/L2-3 IT cortical classes, and CA3/CA2-FC DG Glut cannot be used to rule out Ndn function because the target transcript itself was not depleted with confidence.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The weak self signal may arise from low baseline expression, technical dropout, guide performance, or smaller cell numbers; these alternatives cannot be separated from the DE table alone.

summary: PWS/imprinted comparators in the screen converged on self-transcript depletion rather than on a shared Ndn-like downstream state.
why_it_matters: Ndn, Snrpn, Peg3, and Magel2 are related through imprinting or the PWS locus, but the Perturb-seq readout does not support treating their acute transcriptional effects as interchangeable.
main_caveats: Magel2 itself lacked measurable target knockdown, and the Ndn downstream vector used for neighbor analysis was restricted to nominal, non-FDR rows.

summary: The Ndn signature was uncoupled from the E2F/cell-cycle module that was detectable after E2f4 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Prior necdin work predicts interaction with E2F1 and repression of Cdc2/Cdk1 under apoptotic stress; in this dataset, Ndn knockdown did not resemble Trp53, E2f, or Dlx perturbations and did not induce the FDR-level cell-cycle-like genes seen for E2f4.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: E2f4 is an E2F-family proxy rather than E2f1, and several canonical-neighbor perturbations had weak target-transcript depletion.

summary: The disease-relevant readout of Ndn loss is likely developmental, circuit-level, stress-dependent, or protein-level rather than an immediate large mRNA cascade in every neuron.
why_it_matters: Mouse Ndn deficiency causes neonatal respiratory and serotonergic phenotypes, yet the acute cell-class Perturb-seq response after Ndn knockdown was almost pure target loss; this supports using focused developmental or stress assays instead of expecting a robust pan-neuronal transcriptomic biomarker.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not assay neonatal respiratory nuclei as intact circuits and does not measure serotonin transport or protein interactions.

summary: Tnik mRNA self-depletion is the only recurrent strict signal after Tnik targeting.
why_it_matters: The dataset verifies guide activity at the transcript level, but the target transcript itself is more reproducible than any downstream gene, so Tnik mRNA is the only defensible perturbation biomarker in this run.
main_caveats: Self-depletion was partial and never FDR-significant after transcriptome-wide correction.

summary: The strongest Tnik target engagement in 308 CB GABA, 155 MB Glut, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut was transcriptionally buffered.
why_it_matters: These cell types separate on-target knockdown from a large RNA response: Tnik was first or near-first by nominal rank, yet no gene reached FDR<0.05.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: All downstream genes cited in these cell types were nominal only and had FDR>=0.761 or 1.0.

summary: Tnik did not phenocopy canonical Wnt/β-catenin perturbations, including mouse Tcf7l2, despite known TNIK–β-catenin–TCF biology.
why_it_matters: Apc, Ctnnb1, and Tcf7l2 generated FDR-significant signatures in the same screen, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut; Tnik produced no FDR genes and near-zero full-signature correlations with them, refining the published intestinal and colorectal-cancer Wnt model to a neuronal context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Wnt/TCF4 nomenclature was mapped to mouse Tcf7l2 for the comparison; the dataset assay is pooled whole-cell RNA rather than TCF/β-catenin chromatin output.

summary: The expected Traf/NCK–JNK/MAPK branch was not recovered as a Tnik-like RNA signature.
why_it_matters: TNIK can activate JNK in non-neuronal systems and Reactome connects MINK1/TNIK to ROS-MAP3K5 signaling, but Tnik was essentially uncorrelated with Mapk8, Mapk9, Map3k7, or Traf3 perturbations in matched cell classes.
main_caveats: JNK/MAPK activity is phosphorylation-driven, and the JNK-side perturbations themselves had no FDR-significant RNA signatures, so absence of transcriptomic similarity is not proof that the protein pathway is inactive.

summary: Tnik lacked a stable positive or negative signature neighbor across the screen.
why_it_matters: Unbiased correlations show that neither related pathways nor unrelated perturbations formed a robust recurrent Tnik module; this argues against interpreting isolated nominal top genes as a coherent Tnik biology.
main_caveats: Correlations used full differential-expression score vectors rather than guide-level single-cell embeddings.

summary: Sparse neuronal RNA responses should not be read as CNS safety for TNIK inhibitors.
why_it_matters: TNIK is a druggable kinase and a proposed Wnt oncology target, but mouse and human literature connect TNIK to postsynaptic/nuclear signaling and intellectual-disability biology; this Perturb-seq readout mostly tests partial mRNA loss and can miss kinase, PSD, and phosphorylation phenotypes.
main_caveats: The dataset was not a chronic knockout, does not measure protein abundance or phosphorylation, and includes several low-cell Tnik conditions.

summary: Tcf20 produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response and no measurable Tcf20 mRNA depletion in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: TCF20 is a pathogenic neurodevelopmental transcriptional co-regulator; this dataset should therefore be interpreted primarily as a weak or buffered Tcf20 perturbation rather than as a clean loss-of-function map.
main_caveats: Absence of target mRNA depletion does not exclude coding indels or protein loss; some cell types had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: The reported TCF20-TDG-TCF4 neurogenesis axis and synaptic marker set did not change significantly after Tcf20 perturbation.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse and neuronal data predict TCF20-dependent transcriptional programs; their absence in the Perturb-seq readout suggests either insufficient perturbation, mature-cell context dependence, or a weaker acute response in these brain classes.
main_caveats: The literature assays used embryonic mouse neurogenesis or cultured rat cortical neurons, not the same mature single-cell perturbation assay; target engagement in the dataset was weak.

summary: Thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells responded to several neurodevelopmental regulators but not to Tcf20.
why_it_matters: The negative Tcf20 result in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is not simply because that cell type or contrast is universally insensitive: Chd8, Mecp2, Setd5, Crebbp, and Rai1 all produced FDR-significant signatures there.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Comparator guide efficiency and cell numbers differ; this is evidence for assay-specific divergence, not proof that TCF20 is biologically irrelevant in thalamic neurons.

summary: Tcf20 did not converge transcriptionally with its disease-related Rai1 comparator or with a broader set of NDD regulators.
why_it_matters: TCF20 and RAI1 are structurally/functionally related and produce overlapping human syndromic features, so the low same-cell-type correlations argue against treating the weak Tcf20 signatures as a validated RAI1-like module.
main_caveats: The finding is dominated by the weak Tcf20 signature; correlations near zero are expected if the Tcf20 perturbation failed.

summary: Nominal Tcf20 peaks were isolated rather than recurrent or organized into a strong restricted signature-neighbor module.
why_it_matters: The few low nominal p values should not be promoted into biomarker or pathway hypotheses: they were FDR-negative, poorly recurrent across cell types, and had only weak top-200-gene correlations to other perturbations.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The restricted-neighbor analysis used nominal top genes from weak signatures and is intended only as an audit for missed structure.

direction: 151 broad mixed up/down; 308 compact mixed up/down
summary: Zfp423 perturbation produced a dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature and a much smaller 308 CB GABA signature rather than a pan-neuronal response.
why_it_matters: The screen refines a broadly developmental ZFP423 transcription-factor literature to a narrow sampled-neuronal competence window in this assay: one thalamic class carries most of the signal and the cerebellar class is responsive but compact.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Zfp423 rows were absent for 215 MB Dopa, and RNA-level target engagement was FDR-significant only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

summary: The 151 thalamic response is marked by induction of Ntsr1, Drd2, Col27a1, Slc16a11, Kcnab3, and Nptxr together with repression of Grid2ip, Cd47, Syt13, Grin2c, Slc12a5, and Dzip1.
why_it_matters: These genes provide a compact marker panel for the Zfp423-responsive thalamic state; the simultaneous Grin2c decrease and Ntsr1/Drd2 increase suggests state remodeling inside the labeled Prkcd/Grin2c thalamic class rather than a single housekeeping stress signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Marker interpretation is transcriptomic and restricted to one thalamic class; it was not validated with protein, electrophysiology, or lineage-state measurements.

summary: 308 CB GABA retained a statistically significant but seven-gene response, with Rab37, Gusb, Cfap100, Rnd2, and Ahcyl1 increasing and Hpca and Col5a1 decreasing.
why_it_matters: Zfp423 is required for cerebellar development, yet the cerebellar class in this dataset did not mount a broad Purkinje-progenitor-like program; the observed response is real but compact and should be interpreted as a class-specific transcriptomic echo, not a replay of the developmental phenotype.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Only 69 perturbed CB GABA cells were matched, and the signature contains seven FDR-significant genes.

direction: Zfp521 uncorrelated; Bmpr1b/Rarb/Smad1/Smad4 anticorrelated on the Zfp423 FDR genes; Bmp7 nominally induced by Zfp423
summary: The 151 thalamic Zfp423 signature was not phenocopied by Zfp521, EBF-family perturbations, BMP receptors/SMADs, Notch1, retinoid receptors, or Pax6, despite prior evidence that ZFP423 interfaces with EBF, BMP-SMAD, and Notch signaling.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating Zfp521 as interchangeable with Zfp423 or reducing this neuronal response to a linear BMP/Notch relay; ZFP423 appears to occupy a cell-context-specific transcriptional node whose output is not recovered by neighboring perturbations in the same class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only over the 150 FDR genes of the Zfp423 151 signature; comparator perturbations may have had weaker target engagement or biology outside this restricted gene set.

direction: isolated Dzip1 down and Cfap100 up, without broad canonical NPHP/Joubert gene regulation
summary: Known ZNF423 ciliopathy biology was not expressed as a broad canonical NPHP/Joubert transcriptional module in the neuronal Perturb-seq response.
why_it_matters: ZNF423 can participate in cilium-associated and DNA-damage biology in developmental and renal-disease settings, but this screen mainly captured Dzip1 repression in 151 thalamic cells and Cfap100 induction in 308 CB GABA; clinical ciliopathy mechanisms therefore cannot be read directly from this neuronal expression signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The query covered measured transcript rows for selected canonical ciliary genes, not a formal whole-genome cilia enrichment test, and the assay was not performed in kidney, retina, choroid plexus, or neural progenitors.

summary: Most Zfp423-assayed cell classes were transcriptionally buffered or weakly engaged, with no FDR-significant target transcript change and no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This negative result prevents overgeneralizing Zfp423 as an acutely required regulator in every neuronal class and identifies the large set of classes where either the perturbation did not engage Zfp423 RNA or the network absorbed it without a detectable FDR-level response.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Several negative classes had low perturbed-cell counts, and the absence of a Zfp423 RNA change does not exclude protein-level editing or effects on unmeasured genes.

summary: Trpa1 perturbation produced no detectable target-transcript or genome-wide FDR response across 22 assayed mouse-brain neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This is the dominant biological result: the assayed brain neurons do not show a stable Trpa1-dependent RNA state, and the result is consistent with low mouse-brain TRPA1 expression and a stronger peripheral nociceptor role.
main_caveats: A null mRNA signature does not prove absent Cas9 editing; absent or extremely low baseline Trpa1 expression can make the target transcript uninformative.

summary: The L5 ET cortical glutamatergic class was the strongest nominal Trpa1 responder but did not validate after multiple testing.
why_it_matters: Layer-5 pyramidal neurons are the closest sampled population to prior reports of acute cortical TRPA1 pharmacology; the dataset suggests that those acute channel responses, if present, do not translate into a large baseline transcriptional dependency under this perturbation.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to a broad L5 ET transcriptomic class rather than the exact somatosensory L5 neurons and acute agonist assay used in the literature; all dataset genes were FDR-negative.

summary: Hippocampal and dentate-gyrus-labelled glutamatergic pools showed no selective Trpa1 response.
why_it_matters: This constrains atlas observations of TRPA1 signal in human dentate gyrus by showing no perturbable Trpa1 module in the mouse glutamatergic CA/DG pools present here.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The HPA human single-nucleus signal is species- and cell-type-indirect, and pericytes were not represented in these glutamatergic neuronal pools.

summary: Related TRP-channel perturbations were nearly uncorrelated with Trpa1 and did not reveal a shared neuronal brain TRP program.
why_it_matters: TRPA1 and TRPV1 can be coexpressed and functionally coupled in nociceptors, so the absence of convergence with Trpv1, Trpv4, Trpm3, or Trpm7 argues that the TRP-channel pathway is not interchangeable in the sampled central neuronal states.
main_caveats: Comparison is transcriptomic and relies on sparse CRISPR signatures; other TRP channels such as Trpm8 were not assayed.

summary: The central neuronal null should not be treated as evidence against TRPA1 antagonism for peripheral pain indications.
why_it_matters: Human pain disease genetics and TRPA1 antagonist trials point to gain-of-function or excitatory peripheral nociceptor mechanisms, whereas the dataset lacks that disease-relevant cell type and shows no central neuronal target response.
main_caveats: No pain phenotypes, calcium measurements, peripheral sensory neurons, or antagonist exposures were assayed.

summary: Pknox2 perturbation produced neither reliable target-transcript knockdown nor any FDR-significant downstream genes across tested brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The primary biological interpretation is therefore a negative or ineffective perturbation; nominal downstream genes should not be treated as validated PKNOX2 transcriptional targets.
main_caveats: Differential-expression summaries cannot distinguish guide inefficiency, low target expression, and true buffering.

summary: The largest apparent Pknox2 cell-type signal was a nonsignificant, nominal Jag2/Adamts10-positive response in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: It prevents overcalling the lowest nominal P values as a real Notch or extracellular response; even the best cell type had adjusted P values far above 0.05.
cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: All 008 rows were nonsignificant after FDR correction, and the class contained only 32 perturbed cells.

summary: Pknox2 signatures were weakly correlated with measured Pbx1, Pbx3, Meis1, Meis2, and Hox perturbations despite prior PBX/PREP/HOX biochemistry.
why_it_matters: Physical or functional membership in a TALE-PBX-HOX neighborhood was not sufficient to yield interchangeable Perturb-seq signatures in this dataset.
main_caveats: Pknox2 itself was weakly engaged, Pknox1/Pbx2/Pbx4/Meis3 were not assayed, and the correlations are transcriptomic rather than biochemical readouts.

summary: An all-perturbation score-correlation scan did not reveal a high-confidence positive or negative Pknox2 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak Pknox2 phenotype is not rescued by an unanticipated convergent module elsewhere in the screen.
main_caveats: The largest absolute correlation occurred in one cell type, 308 CB GABA, and was only 0.206.

summary: The screen supplies no PKNOX2 biomarker or direction-of-modulation rationale for brain therapeutic hypotheses.
why_it_matters: Human disease resources do not give a clear PKNOX2 dosage direction, ChEMBL did not return a PKNOX2 small-molecule target entry, and the Perturb-seq data did not validate transcript knockdown.
main_caveats: This is a warning against interpreting the present dataset directionally, not proof that PKNOX2 is irrelevant to every disease context.

summary: Rarb perturbation was globally weak and produced no FDR 0.05 transcriptional hits across the 23 assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation of this target in this dataset is an engagement-limited negative result; downstream nominal genes should not be treated as a definitive RARB loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: The data are transcript-level Wilcoxon contrasts only; absence of an FDR hit may reflect weak knockdown, low expression, single-guide efficacy, or cell-state heterogeneity rather than true dispensability.

summary: The only near-threshold Rarb effect was Arhgef4 up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: This keeps the strongest measured cell-type-specific signal visible while labeling it as exploratory rather than converting it into a cortical RARB pathway claim.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Arhgef4 reached only FDR 0.088, no other L5 ET genes were below FDR 0.10, and the Rarb transcript was not measurably reduced in the same cells.

summary: Rarb perturbation did not recover the known striatal/LGE RARB program: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA had the best negative Rarb self-effect but no FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: Published Rarb models implicate LGE-derived striatal projection neurons and adult striatopallidal medium spiny neurons, so the dataset argues that this Perturb-seq contrast is underpowered or biologically mismatched for those chronic and subtype-specific phenotypes rather than refuting them.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset cell class is broad and the assay is a pooled single-cell perturbation rather than developmental or chronic knockout; Rarb transcript knockdown in this cell class was only nominal.

summary: Rarb did not share a stable transcriptomic signature with Rara, Rarg, or Rxr-family perturbations despite the canonical RAR/RXR heterodimeric pathway.
why_it_matters: The result warns against assuming that all retinoid receptor subunits are interchangeable in this single-gene perturbation dataset; RARB may be buffered, ligand-state dependent, or simply insufficiently knocked down.
main_caveats: The receptor comparators also had modest target engagement, so near-zero correlations separate observed signatures but do not prove mechanistic independence of RAR and RXR proteins.

summary: The weak Rarb loss-of-function signature is not suitable for inferring whether RARbeta agonism or antagonism would be therapeutic in striatal or RARB-related disease.
why_it_matters: RARB is a ligandable nuclear receptor, RARbeta agonism can be neuroprotective in striatal models, and human RARB disease includes both loss- and gain-of-function mechanisms; a buffered Perturb-seq result should not be read as target deprioritization.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The dataset did not test ligands, disease alleles, chronic dosing, or RARB gain-of-function states; the therapeutic inference is therefore a warning rather than a positive efficacy claim.

summary: Tuba4a perturbation produced a sparse mRNA response dominated by the target transcript itself.
why_it_matters: This separates successful local target depletion from a broad transcriptional stress program: the perturbation of a structural tubulin gene may be buffered at the RNA level or act primarily through protein polymerization, transport, and tubulin post-translational chemistry.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Sparse FDR calls can reflect real buffering, post-transcriptional biology, or limited power after testing roughly 17000 genes per contrast.

summary: FDR-significant Tuba4a self-depletion was concentrated in two large thalamic/midbrain glutamatergic contexts and one NP/CT/L6b/OB glutamatergic context, despite broad baseline TUBA4A brain expression.
why_it_matters: The target is widely expressed, so the robust Perturb-seq signal is more likely to reflect cell-context sensitivity, capture, guide performance, or statistical power than an absence of Tuba4a from other neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|053 Sst Gaba|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The data quantify target RNA after perturbation, not basal expression, and weak groups have low to moderate perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Major tubulin paralogs and selected neuronal microtubule-associated genes did not show FDR-level mRNA compensation after Tuba4a knockdown.
why_it_matters: If alpha/beta-tubulin stoichiometry is buffered, this dataset does not reveal it through transcriptional upregulation of Tuba1a, Tubb-family genes, Mapt, Map1b, Map6, or Stmn2.
main_caveats: The negative result is limited to mRNA abundance and the inspected gene set; it does not exclude translational, degradation, or tubulin PTM compensation.

summary: Tuba4a knockdown did not phenocopy other connected tubulin and microtubule-associated perturbations by whole-signature correlation.
why_it_matters: Although these genes occupy the same microtubule network, Tuba4a behaved as an idiosyncratic, mostly self-depletion signature rather than as a generic microtubule-disruption transcriptome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to score-vector correlations from DE summaries; weak Tuba4a downstream signal can damp correlations.

summary: Mast1 was the only microtubule-adjacent non-target gene passing FDR in a robust Tuba4a knockdown context.
why_it_matters: The Mast1 increase suggests a narrow kinase-associated sentinel of Tuba4a loss in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but its modest magnitude and single-cell-type occurrence make it a hypothesis rather than a pathway-level conclusion.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Mast1 logFC was only 0.304 and the same response did not recur at FDR level in other Tuba4a-perturbed cell types.

summary: Human ALS evidence supports TUBA4A loss or mutant tubulin as pathogenic, but the mouse-brain dataset shows that Tuba4a knockdown can be transcriptionally quiet outside the matched human motor-neuron context.
why_it_matters: The Perturb-seq result should not be read as contradicting ALS biology; instead it argues that pathogenic TUBA4A downregulation may require axonal geometry, long-term proteostasis, or cytoskeletal readouts that are only weakly visible in an acute single-cell RNA signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: The ALS references are human or zebrafish motor-neuron/brain studies, whereas this Perturb-seq assay sampled mouse brain glutamatergic and GABAergic classes without direct axon morphology or microtubule stability phenotyping.

summary: Safe_target_65 behaved as a quiet safe-targeting negative control rather than as an endogenous gene perturbation across the 22 neuronal contexts in which it was assayed.
why_it_matters: This makes the dominant biological interpretation a null/background response and prevents treating the arbitrary safe-target label as a disease gene or pathway node.
main_caveats: Guide cutting efficiency and the genomic target sequence were not present in the DE table, and median per-context perturbed-cell count was only 39.5.

summary: A single 145 MH-LH TH Glut-specific Trip11 increase was the only FDR-significant Safe_target_65 gene call, with only nominal same-direction Bbs7 and Ift20 changes suggesting a weak Golgi/ciliary hint.
why_it_matters: Trip11/GMAP210 and IFT20 participate in Golgi-to-cilium trafficking, so a true repeatable signal would nominate a coherent organelle module rather than a generic safe-target response.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only Trip11 survived FDR; Bbs7 and Ift20 were nominal with FDR = 1.0, the contrast used 31 perturbed cells, and no guide off-target sequence is available to connect Safe_target_65 mechanistically to Trip11.

summary: Safe_target_65 did not converge with any named perturbation or with another safe-targeting guide at signature level.
why_it_matters: Lack of nearest-neighbor convergence argues against a hidden biological program shared with receptor, pathway, disease-family, or other safe-control perturbations.
main_caveats: The correlation screen used Wilcoxon score vectors and can miss nonlinear effects or genes absent from the measured feature set.

summary: Safe_target_65 did not produce a shared p53/DNA-damage transcriptional state relative to Non_target controls.
why_it_matters: Safe-targeting guides are intended to represent genome cutting at phenotypically inert loci, but this particular guide did not reveal a dominant double-strand-break stress program in the postmitotic brain cell types tested.
main_caveats: This was a targeted marker check, not a full DNA-damage gene-set enrichment analysis; low cell counts could obscure subtle stress responses.

summary: The largest Safe_target_65 cell-type samples remained buffered, with no FDR-significant genes even at 79 to 143 matched perturbed cells.
why_it_matters: The null profile is not confined to the smallest contrasts and is therefore more consistent with a genuinely weak safe-target response than with universal underpowering.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The largest contrasts still have fewer than 150 perturbed cells and absence of FDR hits does not prove absence of small effects.

summary: Sdhb perturbation showed widespread but FDR-subthreshold target mRNA lowering and almost no reproducible downstream transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Complex II is central to respiration, so the lack of an FDR-supported adaptive RNA program argues either that partial Sdhb RNA loss was buffered at this time point or that RNA engagement was too weak to create acute metabolic stress.
main_caveats: The assay measures mRNA rather than SDH protein, enzyme activity, succinate, ROS, or ATP; several contrasts had fewer than 75 perturbed cells.

summary: Enc1 up-regulation was the only FDR-significant Sdhb-associated gene and was confined to 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, a class in which Sdhb itself was not depleted.
why_it_matters: Enc1 is the strongest cell-type-restricted marker raised by this perturbation, but the missing target-transcript effect makes it a hypothesis-generating marker rather than evidence for a canonical SDH response.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: Single FDR-significant gene in one cell class; the Sdhb transcript was slightly positive and nonsignificant in the same cells.

summary: Sdha, the assayed catalytic partner of Sdhb in complex II, had much stronger self-depletion than Sdhb, yet same-cell Sdha and Sdhb full signatures were essentially uncorrelated.
why_it_matters: Although SDHA and SDHB act in the same SDH complex, their perturbation signatures should not be treated as interchangeable in this dataset; the likely explanation is different RNA engagement and buffering rather than a confidently subunit-specific neuronal biology.
main_caveats: Sdhc, Sdhd, and Sdhaf1-4 were not assayed as perturbations, and Sdhb target engagement was weaker than Sdha engagement.

summary: The Sdhb single-cell RNA response did not show a coordinated HIF, glycolytic, or integrated mitochondrial-stress transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: SDH loss is classically connected to succinate, ROS, and HIF stabilization in tumor contexts; the neuronal Perturb-seq result refines that expectation by showing that partial Sdhb mRNA depletion alone did not recapitulate that program at transcript level.
main_caveats: The literature is mostly transformed or adrenal-lineage contexts with stronger SDH loss; this assay has no direct metabolite, HIF protein, or ROS readout.

summary: The dataset provides no evidence that neuronal SDHB loss is acutely compensated by a protective transcriptional program, whereas human genetics link SDHB loss to mitochondrial disease and SDH-deficient tumors.
why_it_matters: Any therapeutic strategy would need to restore or bypass complex-II function rather than further inhibit SDHB; the buffered neuronal RNA phenotype should not be misread as evidence that partial loss is benign at protein or organismal level.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain single-cell RNA after perturbation, not a viability, mitochondrial enzyme, or tumorigenesis screen.

summary: A top-signature-neighbor scan did not reveal a robust Sdhb-convergent perturbation module.
why_it_matters: Restricting to the top 200 Sdhb genes nominated context-specific neighbors, but these did not survive full-transcriptome checking, so no additional pathway neighbor is strong enough to elevate to a mechanistic module.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The screen was restricted to high-absolute-score genes from a weak Sdhb signature and was used only to rule out obvious missed neighbors.

summary: Nkain2 perturbation did not measurably deplete the Nkain2 transcript and produced no FDR-supported downstream differential expression in any profiled cell type.
why_it_matters: The central dataset result is an engagement-limited null: the assay does not show an acute Nkain2-dependent neuronal transcriptional program, but without on-target knockdown it also cannot establish that Nkain2 is biologically dispensable.
main_caveats: Effect size is assessed at the mRNA level; unobserved protein depletion, isoform effects, or low target expression/dropout could leave a functional perturbation invisible in this table.

summary: Nominal Nkain2 outliers and top signature neighbors were too weak and non-recurrent to define a hidden convergent module.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting individual top-ranked genes as biomarkers or pathways when all adjusted signals failed and cross-perturbation correlations stayed near zero.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlation neighbors were computed from full Wilcoxon-score vectors and were not validated by FDR-significant Nkain2 genes.

summary: The same dataset detected Na,K-ATPase alpha-subunit perturbation biology, especially an Atp1a3-centered response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but Nkain2 did not converge with those signatures.
why_it_matters: Nkain2 is molecularly connected to ATPase beta-subunit biology, so the assayed Atp1a1/Atp1a2/Atp1a3 neighbors are informative pathway controls; their divergent outputs show that a pump-related response was observable in the screen while the Nkain2 guides did not elicit one.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The closest beta subunit, Atp1b1, and the Nkain paralogs were not assayed; absence of Nkain2 knockdown means this is a guide-engagement contrast as well as a pathway contrast.

summary: Human NKAIN2 dosage-disruption and psychiatric-genetics literature is not mirrored by an acute FDR-supported neuronal transcriptional phenotype in this mouse perturbation table.
why_it_matters: Case reports and GWAS nominate NKAIN2 in nervous-system phenotypes, but the dataset argues that this particular single-cell readout is not sufficient to reveal the mechanism unless stronger target engagement or developmental contexts are tested.
main_caveats: Human evidence involves chromosomal rearrangements or common noncoding loci, not matched acute mouse Nkain2 knockdown; the GWAS locus may implicate regulatory mechanisms or nearby genes.

summary: The screen provides no Nkain2 response biomarker or direction of desirable pharmacological modulation, and public chemistry databases did not identify an established NKAIN2 small-molecule target entry.
why_it_matters: A null, weakly engaged Perturb-seq profile plus sparse direct pharmacology argues against using this dataset alone to prioritize NKAIN2 activation or inhibition for disease follow-up.
main_caveats: ChEMBL target absence is not proof of undruggability, and unbiased genetic disease associations do not establish the causal direction of target modulation.

direction: Notum up after Zfp612; Axin2 and Nkd1 unchanged after Zfp612; Apc upregulates Notum/Axin2/Nkd1 and Ctnnb1 downregulates Notum
summary: Zfp612 perturbation produced a strong Notum induction in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but this was uncoupled from a broader Apc/β-catenin feedback program.
why_it_matters: NOTUM is a secreted Wnt antagonist, and Apc and Ctnnb1 perturbations validate Notum as Wnt-responsive in the same cell class; selective Notum induction therefore points to a focused Wnt-modulatory output rather than global canonical Wnt activation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Notum evidence is single-gene and transcriptomic; Zfp612 binding at Notum was not measured; mature Zfp612 RNA knockdown was not significant.

summary: In 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, Zfp612 perturbation yielded a sparse but unusually specific Nrcam-down and Impact-up signature.
why_it_matters: Zfp612 was the strongest assayed perturbation for both Nrcam repression and Impact induction in this cell class, nominating these genes as readouts of a hypothalamic Zfp612-sensitive state involving neuronal adhesion and GCN2/eIF2α stress modulation.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Only two genes reached FDR<0.05, and the mechanistic link between Zfp612 and either Nrcam or Impact is not established.

summary: The Zfp612 phenotype was highly cell-type restricted, with FDR-significant responses confined to two subcortical glutamatergic classes among 23 tested classes.
why_it_matters: A KRAB-ZFP with broad brain RNA expression did not generate a ubiquitous repression-release signature; the interpretable dataset signals were instead limited to a Notum response in a thalamic class and an Nrcam/Impact response in a hypothalamic class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction could reflect chromatin state or guide efficacy; the mature target transcript did not verify knockdown in any class.

summary: The dataset gives little evidence for broad Zfp612 target engagement or a reproducible whole-transcriptome neighbor signature.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpreting the individual Notum, Nrcam, and Impact hits as one large coordinated program and makes sparse, cell-type-specific interpretation more appropriate.
main_caveats: The negative result is based on mature RNA and rank-score correlations; unmeasured protein knockdown or chromatin changes could still occur.

summary: Mouse brain Zfp612 perturbation did not mirror the cell-cycle arm reported for human ZNF23 in cancer cells.
why_it_matters: Published ZNF23 work was performed in proliferative human cancer models; the neuronal Perturb-seq data suggest that postmitotic brain cells should not be assumed to use the same p53/p27/cell-cycle program when Zfp612 is perturbed.
main_caveats: This is an indirect cross-species and cross-modality comparison: human ZNF23 was overexpressed in cancer cells, whereas the dataset perturbed mouse Zfp612 in mostly postmitotic brain cells.

summary: Nr2e1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in the assayed mouse-brain neuronal classes: the target transcript itself did not shift and no downstream gene reached FDR 0.10.
why_it_matters: All stronger-looking Nr2e1 effects must be treated as exploratory because the dataset never showed direct molecular engagement or a corrected downstream response.
main_caveats: Own-transcript abundance is only a surrogate for genome editing; negative transcript evidence cannot prove that guides failed to edit the Nr2e1 locus.

summary: The canonical TLX neural-stem-cell program was absent: Pten, Cdkn1a, Gfap, Cyclin-D/Wnt/Sirt1 markers, and Hes1 all remained FDR=1.0 after Nr2e1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: TLX is best established as a progenitor and retinal regulator, so the negative Pten/Cdkn1a/cell-cycle readout argues that these profiled neuronal classes are the wrong context for recovering the developmental TLX-HDAC module.
main_caveats: The expected genes can be silent or poorly measured in some neuronal clusters; absence of RNA response does not exclude developmental or stem-cell functions.

summary: The few lowest nominal p values were cell-type-private rather than a shared Nr2e1 module: CA3/CA2/dentate cells led with Ccdc93, cerebellar GABA with Hspa5, upper-layer cortical cells with Ybx2, LGE GABA with Mtor, and L4/5 IT cortex with Fam120b.
why_it_matters: The pattern looks more like sparse, noisy, or context-restricted responses than a coherent TLX transcriptional program, so no individual nominal leader should be promoted as a biomarker without replication.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|308 CB GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The signals are nominal and none passes FDR 0.10.

summary: Nr2e1 did not phenocopy available TLX-neighbor or nuclear-receptor perturbations, including Hdac5, Foxg1, Nr2e3, Nr2f1, Nr2f2, Nr2c1, retinoic-acid receptors, retinoid-X receptors, or Nr4a receptors.
why_it_matters: Known TLX cofactors and related receptors should not be assumed interchangeable in these neuronal Perturb-seq signatures; the Nr2e1 profile is close to orthogonal to the related perturbations that were present.
main_caveats: The comparison used transcriptome-wide Wilcoxon score correlations; it cannot test direct protein interactions or unprofiled partners such as Atn1, Kdm1a, Ncor1, or Ncor2 because those were not perturbed.

summary: These data provide no pharmacodynamic gene set for TLX agonism or antagonism in the profiled neuronal cells.
why_it_matters: NR2E1 has reporter-assay chemical activity in ChEMBL, but biomarker discovery for TLX-directed ligands should be anchored in TLX-expressing progenitors, retina, or other TLX-active experimental cells rather than in this weak neuron loss-of-function signature.
main_caveats: This is a translational warning from a negative genetic dataset; it does not test ligand exposure, protein abundance, or TLX-active stem-cell states.

summary: Spi1 sgRNAs did not produce detectable on-target transcript engagement in any matched neuronal subclass.
why_it_matters: Without a significant Spi1 transcript change, the perturbation cannot be interpreted as a successful PU.1 loss-of-function test in these cells; the near-zero Wilcoxon scores are more consistent with an unexpressed or inaccessible target transcript.
main_caveats: The parquet contains DE statistics rather than baseline UMIs, and large but non-significant Spi1 logFC values suggest that logFC is unstable for a lowly detected target.

summary: The Spi1 perturbation was transcriptionally silent: no downstream gene reached even 10% FDR across 371,818 tests.
why_it_matters: The absence of corrected genes and the single-cell-type nature of all p<0.001 hits argue against a reproducible Spi1-responsive neuronal program in this dataset.
main_caveats: A FDR-null result cannot exclude very small effects, effects in unassayed non-neuronal cells, or effects masked by weak target engagement.

summary: The canonical PU.1 myeloid axis was collectively inactive in neuronal subclasses: Irf8 and Csf1r, two SPI1-associated network genes, were also FDR-null, as were Abca7, Cx3cr1, P2ry12, Tlr4, and Trem2.
why_it_matters: This separates a literature-supported myeloid regulatory module from the glutamatergic and GABAergic cell states in which these guides were recovered; it cautions against treating disease-gene membership as evidence for a neuronal cell-autonomous response.
main_caveats: The comparator set is pathway-informed but incomplete; several STRING or Reactome SPI1 partners such as RUNX1, CEBPA, JUN, and IRF4 were not present as perturbations.

summary: The dataset refines SPI1 Alzheimer biology away from a cell-autonomous neuronal mechanism and toward microglial or macrophage contexts.
why_it_matters: Human genetics, primary microglia regulomics, and PU.1 knockdown studies place SPI1 in microglial AD-risk regulation, whereas this neuronal Perturb-seq subset has no Spi1 signature and did not include a Spi1 microglial-class test.
main_caveats: This is a cross-species inference from mouse neuronal perturbations and human or mouse microglial literature; the dataset did not test microglia for Spi1.

summary: The absence of a neuronal Spi1 response and opposing microglial dosage literature make the direction of therapeutic PU.1 manipulation unresolved.
why_it_matters: Earlier human genetic and siRNA work supported lowering PU.1 to limit inflammatory AD programs, but a 2024 amyloidosis-model study reported that Spi1 knockdown worsened while overexpression improved amyloid phenotypes; the present dataset supplies no neuronal rescue signature to arbitrate that conflict.
main_caveats: Therapeutic interpretation is indirect because the screen measured neuronal mRNA responses rather than microglial phagocytosis, cytokine release, amyloid clearance, or in vivo pathology.

direction: Zfp106 decreased; downstream differential expression buffered
summary: The strongest measured Zfp106 knockdowns were not followed by FDR-significant downstream programs in sampled brain neurons.
why_it_matters: ZFP106 is a nuclear-speckle RNA-binding protein in chronic neuromuscular disease models, so the absence of acute FDR-level transcriptional collapse marks these cell types as buffered, under-threshold, or insufficiently depleted rather than overtly sensitive.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell counts were small, all Zfp106 target rows had FDR=1.0, and protein or splicing engagement was not measured.

direction: sampled brain classes resistant or under-threshold
summary: The screen did not reveal a pan-neuronal Zfp106-loss injury state, refining published disease biology toward chronic spinal/peripheral motor-sensory and muscle contexts.
why_it_matters: Zfp106 knockout mice degenerate in the neuromuscular axis despite broad CNS expression; the Perturb-seq result supports vulnerability that depends on cell state, anatomy, duration, or level of depletion rather than simple expression across all brain neurons.
main_caveats: Mouse-brain Perturb-seq did not assay spinal motor neurons, peripheral sensory neurons, muscle, chronic knockout states, or mitochondrial/splicing phenotypes.

summary: Zfp106 was transcriptionally distinct from potent RNA-binding perturbations, including Tardbp and Fus, in the same thalamic class.
why_it_matters: Zfp106 has reported physical and disease-model links to ALS RNA-binding proteins, but this dataset does not support treating acute Zfp106 knockdown as an interchangeable TDP-43/FUS-like perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparators had more perturbed cells and the analysis used whole-transcriptome score correlations, not protein interaction assays.

summary: P/MY Pineal glutamatergic cells carried the nearest Zfp106-local nominal response, led by Palm, but the response stayed below FDR significance.
why_it_matters: This prevents loss of a potentially useful follow-up lead while preserving the fact that it is an underpowered, q=0.092 signal rather than a validated pathway.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only 24 perturbed cells were available and no gene in this cell type reached FDR<0.05.

summary: The Pvalb nominal signature is uncoupled from measured Zfp106 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Pvalb GABA contains top-ranked nominal genes, but the target transcript trended upward, so these genes should not be promoted as clean Zfp106 loss-of-function biomarkers.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: FDR remained above 0.05 and mRNA target engagement is the only available validation metric.

summary: A scan of positive and negative perturbation neighbors found no high-correlation Zfp106 module.
why_it_matters: The weak maximum correlation argues that Zfp106 did not collapse onto an obvious receptor, paralog, ALS-RBP, or pathway-neighbor signature in this dataset.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations are dominated by weak Zfp106 signatures and should be interpreted as a negative screen for convergence, not as proof of no biochemical connection.

summary: Sort1 knockdown produced an on-target hit in hypothalamic GABA neurons but no FDR-significant non-target transcriptional response anywhere in the 21 assayed Sort1 signatures.
why_it_matters: A canonical trafficking receptor can be depleted without creating a strong acute mRNA program, so the dataset argues for transcriptional buffering rather than absence of sortilin protein function.
main_caveats: mRNA readout only; several cell types had low perturbed-cell counts.

summary: Interpretable Sort1 target depletion was concentrated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, with only nominal or near-threshold depletion in 155 MB Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: The lack of broad downstream events should be interpreted most strongly for the few cell types where the target transcript moved, not for every assayed class equally.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity may reflect guide capture, target expression, and power rather than true biological restriction.

summary: Sort1 loss did not significantly change Grn, Psap, App, Bace1, Bdnf, Psen1, Vps35, or Sorl1 mRNA despite SORT1 literature centered on PGRN uptake, APP/BACE1 trafficking, neurotrophins, and retromer-linked sorting.
why_it_matters: The result refines these disease mechanisms toward protein trafficking, secretion, and localization endpoints rather than a transcriptional feedback loop detectable by this assay.
main_caveats: Direct PGRN secretion, APP cleavage, and neurotrophin signaling proteins were not measured.

summary: Sort1, Sorl1, App, and Psap signatures were sparse, whereas Ap2s1, Ap2m1, Rab7, Vps35, and Vps54 generated many significant changes in the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut class.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates buffered cargo-receptor/cargo perturbations from strong collapse of core endosomal and clathrin-dependent machinery, so related trafficking genes are not interchangeable phenotypically.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The core-endosomal contrast is strongest in one common cell class; it is transcriptomic, not a direct vesicle-trafficking assay.

summary: All positive and negative global Sort1 signature neighbors were weak in the five cell types with the strongest Sort1 target effects.
why_it_matters: The weak correlation landscape reduces confidence in assigning Sort1 to any dataset-derived compensatory module or to an opposing perturbation program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are restricted to the assayed perturbation library and are affected by the weakness of the Sort1 signature itself.

summary: The SORT1-PGRN therapeutic hypothesis is not invalidated by the weak mRNA signature, because the desired effect of inhibiting SORT1 is extracellular PGRN retention rather than Grn transcriptional induction.
why_it_matters: Perturb-seq would need to be paired with PGRN secretion or lysosomal trafficking measurements before ranking SORT1 programs for FTLD-directed pharmacology.
main_caveats: This is an assay-direction warning; the dataset did not measure extracellular progranulin.

summary: Tlx3 was a global transcriptional negative in the assayed mouse-brain classes: no cell class contained an FDR-supported DE gene.
why_it_matters: This makes the perturbation primarily informative as an absence of adult brain response, not as a map of a Tlx3 effector pathway.

summary: The canonical Tlx3 embryonic dorsal-horn excitatory/GABAergic fate program was not reactivated by Tlx3 perturbation in these brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: Tlx3 biology documented in embryonic spinal neurons should not be projected onto adult brain Perturb-seq cell classes without evidence of target expression and engagement.
main_caveats: The literature is embryonic dorsal spinal cord, whereas the dataset is mouse brain and the Tlx3 row itself lacks knockdown evidence.

summary: The two smallest adjusted p values were isolated, subthreshold decreases of Pde4d in 217 P MY Pineal Glut and Tox3 in 052 Pvalb Gaba.
why_it_matters: If any Tlx3-linked adult brain signal exists, it is weak and cell-class-restricted rather than a broad homeobox fate-switching program.

summary: Neither Tlx3 literature/disease-neighbor perturbations nor the strongest computed signature neighbors produced a robust convergent Tlx3 module.
why_it_matters: The absence of convergence argues against an active Ptf1a/Pax2/Lmx1b/Tlx3 selector-network axis in the profiled brain cells and flags Fbxo11, Dstyk, Max, and Lrp6 correlations as exploratory only.

summary: The mouse-brain perturbation provides no direction for TLX3-linked leukemia biology or drug development.
why_it_matters: Human TLX3 can be ectopically activated in T-ALL, but Open Targets returned no clinical-candidate drugs for TLX3 and this dataset showed no reliable adult brain transcriptional liability signature.
main_caveats: The disease literature concerns human T cells and chromosomal activation, not Tlx3 knockdown in mouse brain neurons.

summary: Unadjusted Tlx3 hits did not reveal a recurring cross-cell biomarker module.
why_it_matters: The weak signature should not be converted into a biomarker list: nearly every p<0.001 gene appeared in only one cell class.
main_caveats: This conclusion uses nominal hits only to show scatter; it does not validate Creld1 as a Tlx3 target.

summary: Ulk4-labeled perturbations were weakly engaged at the Ulk4 mRNA level and produced a globally sparse neuronal response.
why_it_matters: Most downstream interpretation is limited by the lack of significant target-transcript knockdown: the screen mainly reports either buffered biology or ineffective Ulk4 transcript depletion, not a clean loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: Target engagement was assessed only at the assayed transcript; the perturbation could affect unmeasured Ulk4 isoforms or protein with weaker mRNA change.

direction: Ints10 down; Mccc1 down and Srebf2 up only nominally
summary: The only transcriptome-wide significant Ulk4 readout was Ints10 down-regulation in 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

comparators: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
