direction: neuronally weak; ependymal cilium context untested
summary: The negative neuronal Perturb-seq result does not rule out the established ventricular cilium role of Ulk4 because ependymal and choroid-plexus cells were absent from the Ulk4 tests.
why_it_matters: Known Ulk4 phenotypes are concentrated in cilia, CSF flow, and developmental settings, so a neuronal Glut/GABA screen is expected to miss the most proximal disease-relevant cellular context.
main_caveats: Human HPA expression and mouse cilia genetics are indirect comparators to this mouse Perturb-seq experiment.

summary: Ulk4 did not phenocopy the related RB1CC1/FIP200 autophagy-initiation perturbation.
why_it_matters: Despite the ULK family name, the neuronal Ulk4 signature was orthogonal to Rb1cc1, supporting interpretation of ULK4 as a distinct pseudokinase scaffold rather than a proxy for the canonical ULK1-FIP200 autophagy complex in this dataset.
main_caveats: Ulk1, Ulk2, Ulk3, Atg13, and Atg101 perturbations were not available for direct paralog or complex-member comparison.

summary: Available Hedgehog, ciliary, and autophagy-neighbor perturbations did not converge with Ulk4.
why_it_matters: The absence of a shared Gli/Cspp1/Trak1/Sqstm1 signature argues against a broad linear Hedgehog-cilium transcriptional output from Ulk4 in the assayed neurons.
main_caveats: Stk36 and Sufu were absent as perturbation targets, and direct Gli target-transcript engagement was weak; this is a restricted-signature comparison, not a Hedgehog activity assay.

summary: Structural ligandability of ULK4 should not be equated with a clear neuronal pharmacodynamic transcriptomic marker in this screen.
why_it_matters: ULK4 can bind ATP and compounds despite being catalytically inactive, so a drug-like active-site ligand may perturb scaffold functions differently from the weak transcript perturbations, and Ints10 should be viewed only as an exploratory marker.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: No compound perturbations were profiled, and the only FDR-positive transcriptional marker has no direct literature link to ULK4 signaling.

summary: Corrected Ptprm transcript depletion was confined to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: Only one of 21 Ptprm cell-group contrasts showed FDR-controlled target knockdown, so the dataset can localize one interpretable perturbation context but cannot establish equal Ptprm loss in the other neuronal classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity may reflect guide representation, expression/detection, or power; 15 of 21 groups had fewer than 50 Ptprm-perturbed cells.

summary: The one corrected Ptprm knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: Ptprm itself was significant in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, but no other gene reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: PTPRM is an adhesion-linked receptor phosphatase, so an acute post-adhesion or phosphotyrosine phenotype could be missed by mRNA differential expression even when the target transcript is measurably reduced.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The table is transcriptomic only and does not measure tyrosine phosphorylation, cell adhesion, neurite morphology, or synapse number.

summary: Ptprm knockdown did not transcriptionally engage the cadherin/catenin adhesion program, despite PTPRM's known biochemical connection to catenin signaling.
why_it_matters: Ctnnd1, Ctnnb1, and Cdh2 mRNAs were unchanged after Ptprm loss, and direct Ctnnb1 perturbation produced hundreds of thalamic DE genes that were not shared by Ptprm; this places PTPRM upstream of a mostly nontranscriptional or context-gated adhesion output in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: mRNA abundance of adhesion genes is an indirect readout of cadherin/catenin signaling; the experiment does not assay p120-catenin phosphorylation or cell-cell adhesion.

summary: The assayed type-IIB paralog Ptprt did not show a robust shared mRNA phenotype with Ptprm.
why_it_matters: PTPRM and PTPRT share the receptor-type phosphatase adhesion architecture, but in this dataset Ptprt produced only a self-transcript hit in midbrain glutamatergic cells and was not engaged in the Ptprm-positive thalamic group, arguing against treating measured type-IIB RPTP guide sets as interchangeable transcriptomic perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Ptprk and Ptpru were not perturbation targets, Ptprt lacked on-target depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and the comparison is therefore a negative, power-limited family-level check.

summary: The Ptprm data did not reveal an interpretable high-correlation signature neighbor or a corrected non-target marker module.
why_it_matters: The strongest non-target gene, Ddn in L5-6 IT neurons, remained at FDR=0.201 with only 24 perturbed cells, and a thalamic neighbor search had absolute correlations below 0.25 with a safe-target control among the top positives; nominal hits should therefore be treated as hypotheses, not pathways.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The signature-neighbor calculation was restricted to the top 1000 Ptprm scores in one cell type and was used only as a sanity check.

direction: Sod2 transcript down in engaged cell types
summary: Sod2 CRISPRi produced FDR-significant target-transcript depletion in only four of the 22 scored neuronal classes, with the clearest engagement in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, Pvalb GABA, midbrain glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA neurons.
why_it_matters: The interpretable Sod2 response is concentrated in a small set of neuronal populations; the remaining groups should not be treated as biological resistance because many lacked statistically secure knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction is defined by target RNA knockdown in this dataset; it can reflect guide delivery, cell state, baseline expression, power, or RNA detection rather than intrinsic SOD2 dispensability.

direction: target down; no FDR-significant downstream genes
summary: Even where Sod2 itself was the top down-regulated transcript, no secondary gene passed FDR correction, revealing a strongly buffered acute neuronal transcriptome.
why_it_matters: SOD2 is a primary mitochondrial superoxide-detoxifying enzyme, so a self-only signature means ROS detoxification failure was not propagated to a broad mRNA program at the assayed time point.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Wilcoxon differential expression may miss enzyme activity, mitochondrial ROS, damage, or delayed cell-death phenotypes.

summary: Canonical Nrf2/oxidative-stress and mitochondrial-stress marker transcripts were not coordinately induced after Sod2 knockdown.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates loss of the mitochondrial superoxide dismutase transcript from a conventional mRNA oxidative-stress alarm, arguing that direct redox or respiratory measurements are needed to detect the primary biochemical lesion.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The stress panel was selected a priori but manually; absence at FDR<0.05 does not exclude transient, translational, or metabolite-level stress responses.

summary: Sod2 had no close positive or negative genome-wide signature neighbor and did not converge with available antioxidant or oxidative-phosphorylation perturbations.
why_it_matters: Reactome places SOD2 in ROS detoxification, but its measured neuronal CRISPRi phenotype was not interchangeable with Gpx4, Prdx1, Nfe2l2, Sdha, Cox4i1, or Ndufs1 perturbation signatures.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Several antioxidant comparators had weak or unmeasured on-target RNA depletion, so the strongest conclusion is lack of observed convergence rather than mechanistic opposition.

direction: dataset buffered despite deleterious loss in vivo
summary: Acute self-only Sod2 signatures contrast with severe Sod2-loss phenotypes in vivo, warning that a benign Perturb-seq mRNA profile would under-call mitochondrial superoxide toxicity.
why_it_matters: Whole-body and brain-specific mouse Sod2 loss causes neonatal or perinatal lethality with neurodegeneration and complex-II injury; therapies or disease models that reduce SOD2 should be evaluated with ROS, aconitase/complex-II activity, lipid-peroxidation, and survival endpoints rather than mRNA alone.
comparators: mouse whole-body Sod2 knockout|mouse Nestin-Cre brain Sod2 knockout
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The literature is chronic, developmental, and often complete knockout, whereas the Perturb-seq assay measures partial CRISPRi knockdown over a shorter ex vivo window.

summary: Hspa5 was the strongest nominal stress-linked secondary transcript in the best-engaged thalamic Sod2 signature, but it remained FDR-negative and isolated from a wider stress program.
why_it_matters: Hspa5 could be followed as a sensitive, hypothesis-generating readout of thalamic response to mitochondrial redox perturbation, but the present dataset does not support it as a robust Sod2 biomarker.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Hspa5 FDR was 1.0; this is a single-cell-type, nominal observation embedded in an otherwise self-only signature.

summary: Zmym2 perturbation produced an FDR-controlled downstream signature almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: A chromatin-corepressor perturbation that is nearly silent in 21 matched brain cell classes but active in one thalamic glutamatergic class points to strong cell-state gating rather than a uniform housekeeping response.
comparators: 155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: High confidence for the measured cell-type restriction; lower confidence for causal assignment to Zmym2 because the measured target transcript was not depleted.

summary: The 151 response was a sparse, mostly induced effector cassette rather than a broad bidirectional chromatin-collapse program.
why_it_matters: Twenty-two of the 24 genes reaching 10% FDR were induced, which is directionally compatible with loss of a transcriptional repressor but does not recover a known CoREST, TRIM28, retrotransposon, or NuRD pathway module by gene identity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The direction matches a repressor-loss model, but the signature is small, protein complexes were not measured, and the scRNA gene list does not establish direct chromatin targets.

summary: The assayed Zmym2 transcript was not detectably depleted in any tested cell type, including the class with a downstream FDR signature.
why_it_matters: The dataset contains a real downstream 151 signature but weak measured target engagement, so Zmym2 rows should be interpreted as a weak-engagement or buffered perturbation rather than as a clean transcript-knockdown series.
main_caveats: The transcript row may not report guide activity at protein level, at unmeasured isoforms, or in a responsive subpopulation; it only shows that the measured Zmym2 mRNA was not significantly reduced.

summary: Active chromatin-reader and remodeler perturbations in 151 did not reproduce the Zmym2 24-gene cassette.
why_it_matters: Chd4 and Zmynd8 each generated large FDR signatures in the same thalamic class, yet their Zmym2-cassette correlations were near zero; the Zmym2 phenotype therefore is not explained as a generic response to perturbing a NuRD-associated chromatin regulator.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison used only the preselected 24-gene Zmym2 cassette and direct LSD1-CoREST members were not available as perturbations in this cell type.

direction: up in 151; nominally up in 155 and 217
summary: Notum is a strong 151 marker and a weaker posterior-glutamatergic recurrence candidate.
why_it_matters: The secreted Wnt deacylase Notum was FDR-significant in 151 and nominally among the strongest positives in 155 MB Glut and 217 P MY Pineal Glut, suggesting an extracellular Wnt-antagonist readout worth testing even though the recurrence is not FDR-controlled outside 151.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only the 151 Notum effect survived FDR correction; the very large logFC values in 155 and 217 likely reflect sparse baseline detection and need validation.

summary: The neuronal Zmym2 phenotype should not be conflated with ZMYM2-FGFR1 fusion-kinase biology.
why_it_matters: Human ZMYM2 has both loss-of-function developmental genetics and FGFR1-fusion oncology links, but the strongest brain Perturb-seq response showed no Fgfr1-4 induction; the dataset therefore supports a chromatin-regulator loss context, not a kinase-addiction model.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Absence of Fgfr transcript induction does not assay FGFR kinase activity or fusion proteins; it only argues that this neuronal loss-context signature is not transcriptionally FGFR-like.

summary: Zfp664 knockdown is transcriptionally buffered: no gene reached FDR<0.05 in 371,818 Zfp664 tests, even in the Pvalb stratum with the best nominal on-target RNA decrease.
why_it_matters: A nuclear multi-zinc-finger transcription factor might be expected to change many RNAs after depletion; instead, the measured neuronal response is below FDR support and is much weaker than a canonical transcription-factor program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Target mRNA knockdown was nominal rather than FDR-significant; protein depletion was not measured, so buffering and weak guide engagement cannot be separated.

summary: Measurable Zfp664 RNA repression was sparse and did not produce a shared program: only four of 22 cell types had nominal negative target-transcript tests, and their genome-wide Zfp664 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated.
why_it_matters: The result refines broad ZNF664/Zfp664 expression annotations by showing that brain expression does not translate into a uniform acute perturbation response across neuronal classes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: All four target-transcript decreases had FDR=1.0; the apparent cell-type restriction could reflect guide activity, sampling, or low Zfp664 RNA detectability rather than true biology.

summary: The absence of Zfp664 FDR calls is not a generic failure to detect C2H2 zinc-finger perturbations: Zfp236 and Zfp423 generated dozens to hundreds of FDR-supported genes in overlapping cell types.
why_it_matters: This makes Zfp664 a buffered or weakly engaged member of a broad zinc-finger regulator class rather than evidence that the assay cannot read out zinc-finger transcription factors.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The comparator genes are broad C2H2 zinc-finger relatives, not validated paralogs or members of a shared Zfp664 complex.

summary: Zfp664 had no convincing positive or inverse signature neighbor; the strongest same-cell correlations were low, including r=0.133 for Frrs1l and r=-0.112 for Zfp644.
why_it_matters: The perturbation therefore cannot be assigned to a robust receptor, pathway, or complex module from transcriptome geometry; weak anti-correlation with Zfp644 should be treated only as a restricted-screen hint.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed over Wilcoxon score vectors in cell types where Zfp664 was present; a different assay or cell state could still reveal partners.

summary: Zbtb16 perturbation produced a globally weak or buffered single-cell RNA response across the assayed brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The absence of any FDR-significant gene, even among cell types with tens to hundreds of perturbed cells, makes pathway-level interpretation of nominal hits unsafe.
main_caveats: The result could reflect true biological buffering, low basal Zbtb16 expression, incomplete perturbation, guide efficacy, or dilution within broad cell classes.

summary: Pvalb interneurons showed the clearest nominal Zbtb16 mRNA decrease, but the downstream signature remained buffered.
why_it_matters: The best-engaged cell type still had no FDR-supported downstream genes, separating detectable target-transcript reduction from robust network rewiring.

main_caveats: Zbtb16 itself was only nominal with FDR=1.0, so the apparent Pvalb selectivity should be treated as an engagement gradient rather than a confirmed cell-type-specific phenotype.

summary: The known ZBTB16-CUL3-ATG14L autophagy axis was not recapitulated as a transcriptional ATG-module response.
why_it_matters: This argues against using the scRNA signature as evidence that Zbtb16 perturbation mobilized GPCR-autophagy biology in these cells and is consistent with the published axis acting through protein ubiquitination rather than Atg14 mRNA abundance.
main_caveats: Only mRNA abundance was tested; ATG14L protein stability, ubiquitination, flux assays, or GPCR stimulation were not measured.

summary: Zbtb16 did not phenocopy same-family ZBTB perturbations or assayed Rara/HDAC/Cul3/Sin3a network neighbors.
why_it_matters: Although ZBTB16 is a BTB-zinc-finger transcriptional repressor with literature and STRING links to RARA, HDAC/corepressor biology, and CUL3, the measured brain signatures were nearly orthogonal, so no shared module can be inferred from related perturbations.
main_caveats: Correlations are dominated by a weak Zbtb16 signature; corepressors Ncor1, Ncor2, and Hdac1 were STRING partners but were not assayed as perturbation targets.

direction: literature programs absent in broad adult clusters
summary: The dataset refines prior brain and developmental genetics by showing that adult broad neuronal classes did not reproduce the strong Zbtb16 programs described in hypothalamic stress circuits or germline neocortical loss.
why_it_matters: Zbtb16 has in vivo links to PVH/ARC energy-balance neurons, mouse neocortical maturation, ASD/SCZ-related modules, and a human developmental syndrome, but this Perturb-seq experiment provides only weak adult-state transcriptomic evidence.

main_caveats: The literature used energy-deficit stimulation, PVH/ARC targeting, germline knockout, or human congenital genetics; those contexts are only indirectly related to acute perturbation in broad adult cell classes.

summary: Setd1a perturbation gave a sharply cell-class-skewed, mostly down-regulated transcriptome that was maximal in 155 MB Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than uniform across brain classes.

summary: Because SETD1A human disease is loss-of-function and Setd1a perturbation repressed hundreds of neuronal genes in susceptible classes, the perturbation direction warns against direct SETD1A inhibition in CNS contexts.

summary: Usp9x transcript repression was reproducible but reached FDR only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut.

main_caveats: FDR significance is at the mRNA level only and does not prove USP9X protein or deubiquitinase depletion.

summary: Adult neuronal Usp9x knockdown produced a remarkably sparse FDR-level transcriptome despite severe developmental phenotypes after germline or embryonic Usp9x loss.
why_it_matters: The result separates acute, partial perturbation in mostly mature brain cells from the progenitor and forebrain developmental requirements that dominate the USP9X literature.

main_caveats: The dataset contains 22-83 perturbed cells per Usp9x cell class, and transcriptomics can miss post-translational USP9X substrates.

summary: Pcsk1n is the only non-target FDR hit and marks a pontine/medullary GABA-selective Usp9x response.
why_it_matters: Because PCSK1N/proSAAS controls processing of neuroendocrine peptide precursors, Pcsk1n loss is a focused candidate readout for a restricted secretory-peptide consequence of Usp9x perturbation.

main_caveats: Target engagement in the same cell type was nominal rather than FDR-significant, and the response is based on only 47 perturbed cells.

summary: The strongest engaged thalamic class shows a nominal RNA-processing/splicing signature rather than a canonical Wnt, Notch, or TGF-beta transcriptional signature.
why_it_matters: This preserves a noncanonical molecular hypothesis: USP9X loss in adult thalamic glutamatergic neurons may stress RNA-processing factors even when developmental signaling components do not dominate the DE table.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Pabpn1, Srrm2, Hnrnpu, and Srsf11 were high-ranked but did not individually pass FDR<0.05.

summary: The Usp9x signature weakly aligned with UFMylation/proteostasis perturbations but not with the related DUB, ubiquitin-ligase, FMR1, or mTOR perturbations tested in the same cell classes.
why_it_matters: USP9X is not behaving as a generic deubiquitinase, Notch, FMR1, or mTOR node in this adult Perturb-seq matrix; top same-cell neighbors point instead to a weak UFMylation/proteostasis axis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The largest genome-wide correlations were small, so this is a signature-neighbor hypothesis rather than a pathway-activation call.

summary: USP9X has small-molecule inhibitor assays, but the neuronal dataset and human genetics both argue for CNS monitoring rather than assuming a safely silent target.
why_it_matters: A drugging program against USP9X should treat Pcsk1n, RNA-processing, and target-knockdown markers as possible neuronal pharmacodynamic liabilities, even though partial acute knockdown is mostly buffered transcriptionally.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain and genetic transcript knockdown; it does not measure reversible human inhibitor exposure or peripheral therapeutic windows.

summary: Tshr perturbation was essentially unengaged at the target transcript and globally sparse.
why_it_matters: The main biological readout is a near-null perturbation rather than a map of TSHR loss-of-function; downstream negative results must be interpreted through that lens.
main_caveats: Wilcoxon output does not provide raw receptor expression or protein engagement; receptor-low cells can yield FDR=1 while logFC values are unstable.

summary: The few corrected Tshr hits were isolated to NP/CT/L6b glutamatergic, L5/6 intratelencephalic glutamatergic and Pvalb GABA classes and did not form a recurrent module.
why_it_matters: This argues against a broad neuronal TSHR transcriptional program in the assayed atlas; the strongest genes are individual cell-class events.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Kcnj4 and Arfgef3 were only FDR<0.10; Psmd14 was FDR<0.20; the hit genes were not recurrent after correction.

summary: Tshr knockdown did not activate or repress the canonical TSHR-GNAS/GNAQ-thyroid gene module.
why_it_matters: Curated biology places TSHR upstream of Gs/Gq, cAMP and thyroid differentiation genes, but those genes were transcriptionally uncoupled in brain neurons, favoring a context-missing explanation over a canonical thyroid-like response.
main_caveats: Absence of Tshr target engagement prevents a definitive statement about a fully effective loss-of-function perturbation.

summary: A reported hippocampal Tshr-Wnt5a/β-catenin axis was not reproduced in the CA1/dentate-containing Perturb-seq class or elsewhere.
why_it_matters: The contrast suggests that Tshr-dependent hippocampal memory phenotypes may require stronger receptor deletion, hippocampal neurogenic niches or non-cell-autonomous physiology that are not captured by this pooled neuronal transcriptome.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The dataset measured broad CA1/dentate-containing glutamatergic cells, not isolated hippocampal neurons or neural progenitors, and Tshr knockdown was not detectable.

summary: The TSHR/Fshr/Lhcgr glycoprotein-receptor family was quiet while downstream cAMP enzymes could be robustly depleted.
why_it_matters: Family-level silence was not just a blanket failure of the dataset to perturb cAMP-pathway genes; it was concentrated at the ligand-gated endocrine receptors.
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation contrasts use different guide sets and perturbed-cell counts; Adcy3 and Prkaca effects demonstrate target knockdown, not the full presence of a TSHR-dependent program.

summary: Existing TSHR pharmacology and Graves biology should be interpreted as peripheral or ligand/antibody biology rather than direct neuronal transcriptomic liability in this screen.
why_it_matters: Approved TSHR agonist mechanisms and activating autoantibodies show that the receptor is clinically actionable, but the Perturb-seq data provide no neuronal biomarker program to follow for direct brain TSHR antagonism or agonism.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay TSH ligand, Graves antibodies, thyroid cells or systemic thyroid-hormone feedback.

summary: Zscan26 knockdown was FDR-confirmed only in 155 MB Glut and produced no FDR-supported off-target gene in any assayed subclass.
why_it_matters: For a predicted DNA-binding transcription factor, the cleanest interpretable result is transcript engagement rather than a large recovered regulon; downstream claims therefore need to remain nominal or validation-oriented.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq readout measures RNA abundance only; a transcription factor can have protein-level or state-dependent effects that are not visible as broad steady-state mRNA shifts.

summary: Nominal target depletion recurred in several subclasses, including highly sampled thalamic, Pvalb, and L4/5 IT populations, but those contexts were transcriptionally buffered at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The weak response is not explained solely by low perturbed-cell number; even the largest Zscan26 cell set had no corrected downstream transcript.

main_caveats: Most on-target rows outside 155 MB Glut failed FDR correction, so this is a low-amplitude buffering pattern rather than a set of validated cell-type-specific nulls.

summary: The FDR-confirmed MB glutamatergic knockdown did not measurably engage a c-fos/SRE immediate-early module at the RNA level.
why_it_matters: ZSCAN26 was originally cloned as SRE-ZBP, a protein binding the c-fos serum-response element; the neuronal knockdown signature therefore refines that annotation by showing no constitutive Fos/Egr/Jun/Npas4 regulon in this context.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The literature experiment used human cDNA/SRE binding and serum response, not mouse midbrain neurons; Fos-family regulation could require stimulation or post-translational activation not present in this dataset.

summary: Crhr1 was the strongest nominal off-target decrease in 155 MB Glut, making it an exploratory receptor biomarker rather than a validated Zscan26 target.
why_it_matters: CRHR1 is a stress-pathway GPCR, so a reproducible Zscan26-to-Crhr1 link would connect a poorly characterized zinc-finger factor to a neuronally relevant neuromodulatory receptor; the present evidence is suitable for qPCR or pooled validation follow-up only.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Crhr1 and Ep300 were nominal with adjusted p=1.0, and the dataset does not establish direct binding by Zscan26.

summary: A restricted perturbation-neighbor search in the only FDR-confirmed cell type found no strong positive or negative phenocopy, and the screen contained no second Zscan-family comparator.
why_it_matters: SCAN-domain proteins can oligomerize, but this dataset does not identify a partner perturbation that substitutes for, or opposes, Zscan26 loss in 155 MB Glut.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor correlations used only the 200 strongest Zscan26-score genes and do not test physical interactions; direct ZSCAN paralogs were absent from the target list.

summary: Tfdp2 guide assignment produced no FDR-significant downstream gene in any of 21 assayed cell classes, and the Tfdp2 transcript itself was not FDR-significantly depleted.
why_it_matters: A canonical E2F dimerization partner should be capable of altering cell-cycle transcription, so the screen result is best treated as a true negative or unverified on-target perturbation rather than as a weak pathway hit.

summary: A robust E2f4/Rb1 G1/S-like module in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was not reproduced by Tfdp2 or by the Tfdp1 paralog.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

summary: The E2f4/Rb1 comparator program was restricted to a few neuronal classes, but Tfdp2 was negative even in those permissive classes.
why_it_matters: The E2F/RB module was observable in this dataset, especially in thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic cells and more weakly in midbrain glutamatergic and Pvalb/GABA classes, so the Tfdp2 negative result is not simply a panel-wide inability to detect RB/E2F biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity is defined by comparator perturbations; Tfdp2 itself had no significant genes in any class.

summary: Tfdp2 had no robust positive or negative signature neighbor across the perturbation panel.
why_it_matters: Without a reproducible co-signature, the screen does not support a downstream biomarker or an alternative pathway hypothesis for Tfdp2.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on rank-like Wilcoxon score vectors and very weak isolated correlations can reflect noise.

summary: Tbx6 was effectively silent across the measured mouse-brain perturbation contexts.
why_it_matters: The on-target transcript and downstream transcriptome both failed to move, so the screen does not support an autonomous Tbx6 program in these profiled neuronal cell classes and should be treated primarily as an unengaged/negative perturbation.
main_caveats: The assay had no Tbx6 result for 215 MB Dopa; guide editing or repression was inferred only from the target transcript and not independently measured at DNA or protein level.

summary: The only candidate positive signal was a sub-FDR CTX-CGE GABA two-gene outlier.
why_it_matters: Although no gene crossed FDR<0.05, Atosa up-regulation and Dynll2 down-regulation made CTX-CGE GABA the sole cell type with any q<0.1 rows, providing a restricted and explicitly exploratory follow-up hypothesis rather than a pathway-level hit.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Atosa and Dynll2 reached FDR=0.0595, not FDR<0.05; the next-best row in any other cell type was far weaker at FDR=0.2947.

summary: The embryonic WNT/NOTCH/MESP2 somitogenesis circuit was not reconstituted by Tbx6 perturbation in the weak CTX-CGE response.
why_it_matters: Prior work places Tbx6 upstream of Dll1, Mesp2, HES7, and Sox2 fate control in presomitic mesoderm; those direct or canonical neighbors were flat in the CTX-CGE Tbx6 signature, arguing that the nominal CTX-CGE outliers are not the known paraxial-mesoderm network.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The literature is embryonic and mesodermal, whereas the dataset cell type is a brain GABA class with weak target engagement.

summary: Tbx6 lacked convergent T-box-family or nearest-neighbor signatures.
why_it_matters: Even in the cell type with the smallest adjusted p values, Tbx6 did not resemble perturbations of other Tbx paralogs or its canonical Mesp2/Dll1/Notch1/Tcf7l2 neighbors, and the strongest non-self correlations in the top scalar Tbx6 cell types were near zero.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on full score vectors from weak signatures, so the conclusion is absence of a nearby signature rather than evidence of active antagonism.

summary: The screen points TBX6 disease biology away from mature brain neurons and back to dosage-sensitive somitogenesis.
why_it_matters: Human TBX6 congenital vertebral disease is explained by reduced developmental dosage; the mouse-brain signatures show neither TBX6 target engagement nor somite-pathway output, warning against interpreting this dataset as a neuronal disease or drug-discovery model for TBX6.
main_caveats: This uses an indirect adult/neuronal mouse context to comment on an embryonic mesodermal human condition; it narrows interpretation of this screen, not the established disease mechanism.

summary: Tmem106b target repression was FDR-significant in four neuronal subclasses despite negative target logFC in all 22 assayed subclasses.
why_it_matters: The dataset contains a gradient of target engagement; downstream negative results are clearest in the four FDR-engaged classes and less decisive in low-cell or weak-engagement classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: FDR selectivity may reflect both biology and power because n_pert_matched ranged from 24 to 158.

summary: The four cell types with FDR-supported Tmem106b depletion had no FDR-significant non-target genes.
why_it_matters: This separates transcript knockdown from a broad endolysosomal transcriptional state and suggests that acute loss in these neurons is buffered or acts mainly through protein-level lysosome phenotypes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only steady-state mRNA was measured; lysosomal pH, enzyme maturation, endosomal traffic, and protein abundance were not assayed.

summary: Tmem106b knockdown did not FDR-regulate Grn, Sort1, Psap, Ctsb, Lamp2, or v-ATPase transcripts even though the v-ATPase gene Atp6v0c generated a broad response in the same atlas.
why_it_matters: The result argues that Tmem106b is not an acute transcriptional phenocopy of direct lysosomal acidification failure and that the progranulin/TMEM106B neighborhood is not wired as a simple mRNA feedback loop in these neurons.
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation contrast is transcriptomic; guide efficiencies and cell counts differ across target genes.

summary: The acute neuronal dataset makes the Tmem106b/Grn/Sort1/Psap/Ctsb/Lamp2 branch look mostly target-only, pointing away from a fast neuronal FTLD mRNA response.
why_it_matters: TMEM106B is a human FTLD and aging-linked locus, but these data suggest that disease phenotypes may require chronic stress, aging, proteostatic readouts, or glial and myelinating cells rather than short-term transcriptional coupling in neurons.
main_caveats: The assay used developing or young mouse neuronal populations and does not model aging, TDP-43 pathology, oligodendrocytes, or progranulin-null chronic disease.

summary: Cyfip2 down-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut was the only FDR-significant secondary transcript after Tmem106b perturbation.
why_it_matters: Cyfip2 is the only specific non-target marker nominated by the dataset and should be prioritized, if at all, as a narrowly cell-type-specific follow-up readout rather than a general TMEM106B biomarker.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Single-cell-type, single-gene signal; Tmem106b itself was nominal but not FDR-significant in this cell type.

summary: Tmem106b lowering in the profiled neurons should not be read as transcriptional evidence of lysosomal rescue or harm.
why_it_matters: The dataset shows target knockdown without activation of the expected lysosomal/progranulin module, while mouse Grn/Tmem106b literature reports model-dependent beneficial versus detrimental outcomes for Tmem106b loss.
main_caveats: Therapeutic predictions require protein, lysosomal pH, aging, and disease-model readouts rather than this acute neuronal mRNA profile alone.

summary: Pax6 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome-wide response in any of the 22 assayed cell classes.
why_it_matters: A canonical CNS developmental transcription factor was inactive at the level of acute differential expression in this mature neuronal Perturb-seq panel.
main_caveats: The finding is a detected-response null; weak measured Pax6 self engagement prevents it from proving efficient loss of Pax6 function.

summary: Pax6 target-transcript rows were not significantly changed, making target engagement weak or undetectable by this RNA readout.
why_it_matters: This caveat keeps the global null from being overinterpreted as clean biological buffering after a validated Pax6 knockdown.
main_caveats: RNA self-depletion is an imperfect proxy for editing, and no guide efficiency or protein measurement is available.

summary: Pax6 belonged to a largely silent PAX-paralog panel rather than standing alone as a uniquely null perturbation.
why_it_matters: The family-level pattern points to low expression, low engagement, or lack of acute mature-neuron dependence as a broad issue for assayed paired-box factors.
main_caveats: Only assayed PAX-family perturbations were compared, and one Pax7 row did reach FDR<0.05.

summary: Tbr1 produced cortical glutamatergic signatures in the same dataset where Pax6 did not, uncoupling Pax6 from the later Pax6/Tbr2/Tbr1 developmental axis in mature cells.
why_it_matters: The contrast refines the embryonic cascade by showing that a later cortical identity regulator can be transcriptomically visible where the upstream progenitor regulator Pax6 is not.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: This is a cross-gene perturbation contrast; Tbr1 had more perturbed cells in some cortical classes, and no direct Pax6-to-Tbr1 regulation was tested here.

summary: The Pax6 null in mature assayed classes suggests PAX6 disease biology should be sought in developmental or adult neurogenic compartments rather than broad acute responses of the tested differentiated neurons.
why_it_matters: PAX6 dosage is disease-relevant, but this dataset gives no support for a widespread mature-neuron transcriptomic rescue target.
main_caveats: The dataset does not include annotated embryonic radial glia, intermediate progenitors, or adult olfactory-bulb stem cells, so it cannot test the highest-prior Pax6 compartments.

summary: Rxrb CRISPRi had directional on-target RNA reduction in a subset of neuronal classes but no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: RXRB is annotated as a ligand-responsive nuclear receptor transcription factor, so widespread absence of FDR-level output is biologically informative: either RXRB protein/function was not sufficiently depleted, the assayed mature neuronal states buffer partial Rxrb reduction, or key RXR-dependent states were outside the dataset.
main_caveats: All downstream claims are transcriptomic; target RNA knockdown was nominal rather than FDR-significant, and RXRB protein abundance was not measured.

summary: Rxrb target engagement was uneven across neuronal classes, peaking nominally in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 217 P MY Pineal Glut, and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA while CTX-CGE and Sst GABA classes showed little self-depletion.
why_it_matters: The interpretable signal is a sparse target-engagement map, not a set of robust effector genes; cell-type comparisons must therefore separate apparent biology from CRISPRi efficiency and sampling differences.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Uneven self-knockdown may reflect guide delivery or baseline expression rather than true RXRB dependence.

summary: Rxrb did not phenocopy RXR paralogs or nuclear-receptor neighbors; in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Rora and Thra produced FDR-significant programs while Rxrb produced none, and Rxrb score vectors were essentially uncorrelated with 24 related perturbations.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating RXRB as an interchangeable hub whose partial loss automatically collapses RAR/LXR/PPAR/thyroid-receptor transcription in these neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Rora is a nuclear-receptor-family comparator rather than a direct RXRB heterodimer; several RXR/RAR/LXR/PPAR comparators had weak self-knockdown, so the strongest contrast is with Rora and Thra in one cell class.

summary: The neuronal Rxrb loss-of-function signatures failed to recover the retinoic-acid, LXR/PPAR lipid, or bexarotene-associated Wnt/Rho outputs expected from RXR pathway literature.
why_it_matters: Known RXR biology is ligand-, partner-, and context-dependent; absence of Lrp1, Lrp5, Sfrp5, Sema3f, Abca1, and related responses suggests that partial Rxrb repression alone was insufficient to drive those modules in the profiled neurons.
main_caveats: The prior mouse-brain study used pan-RXR agonism and bulk cortex in APOE backgrounds, whereas this dataset used CRISPRi of Rxrb in neuronal clusters.

summary: RXR agonist therapeutic biology should not be inferred as a simple mirror image of neuronal Rxrb knockdown: the CRISPRi dataset lacks a strong neuronal RXRB-loss program and does not assay the RXRγ/oligodendrocyte axis implicated in remyelination.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL drugs act on the RXR family, and remyelination literature points to RXRγ and oligodendrocyte progenitors; the weak mature-neuron Rxrb phenotype is a warning that isoform and cell-type attribution will be essential for RXR agonist interpretation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: No oligodendrocytes, OPCs, microglia, or drug-treated cells were profiled here; the finding is a translational caution rather than a test of RXR agonist efficacy.

summary: Ret perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptome-wide hit in any of the 23 assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The dominant interpretation is technical or biological non-engagement rather than a broad RET-dependent transcriptional state.
main_caveats: Negative at the scRNA Wilcoxon/FDR layer; residual protein or kinase inhibition was not measured.

summary: The MB Dopa population showed the clearest Ret mRNA depletion, but dopaminergic identity genes were not coordinately lost.
why_it_matters: This argues against an acute collapse of midbrain dopaminergic identity after the Ret perturbation in the captured cells, despite RET being a GDNF-family trophic receptor.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Only 23 MB Dopa perturbed cells were available and Ret itself reached only FDR=0.149; the literature comparator is an adult conditional knockout, not the same Perturb-seq condition.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the largest Ret-perturbed sample and nominal Ret knockdown but still lacked an FDR-significant Ret downstream response.
why_it_matters: A higher cell count did not convert Ret depletion into a canonical transcriptional program, indicating that the weak signal is not explained only by the tiny MB Dopa sample.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Ret depletion in this cell class was nominal only; no direct literature establishes that this thalamic glutamatergic class should be RET dependent.

summary: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut carried the strongest nominal non-Ret signature, led by Il34, Zfp654, and Pxdn, even though the Ret transcript itself was not detectably reduced.
why_it_matters: The apparent cell-type hotspot should be treated as an exploratory, restricted-signature signal rather than a validated RET pathway output.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: No gene passed FDR<0.05 and the on-target Ret row had p=0.550.

summary: Canonical GFRA1/RET to RAS-MAPK neighbors did not phenocopy Ret across the Ret-responsive nominal contexts.
why_it_matters: Prior signaling maps predict that GFRA co-receptors use RET to activate SHC1-GRB2-SOS1 and MAPK/AKT modules, so the gene-level uncoupling argues that the screen did not capture a ligand-driven RET cascade.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Most comparator perturbations and Ret itself had weak or incomplete target-transcript depletion, so this is a pathway-level absence of convergence rather than proof that RET cannot signal through MAPK in these neurons.

summary: NCAM1 and EPHA4 perturbations were far more transcriptionally engaged than Ret, yet their score profiles were not Ret-like.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates the Ret negative result from a general failure to deplete neuronal surface receptors and is relevant because NCAM can mediate RET-independent GDNF/GFRα signaling while EphA4 can cooperate with GDNF/Ret in axon guidance.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: NCAM1 and EPHA4 are broad adhesion or guidance receptors, not stoichiometric RET subunits; the comparison uses transcriptomic similarity only.

summary: The Ret loss-of-function signatures should not be used as a positive model for RET inhibitor efficacy or neural liability.
why_it_matters: RET is a highly actionable kinase in MEN2, medullary thyroid carcinoma, and RET-altered lung cancer, but this brain screen mainly reports an absence of robust response to Ret knockdown.
main_caveats: The perturbation was genetic loss of Ret in mouse brain cell types, not oncogenic RET activation or acute pharmacologic kinase inhibition in cancer cells.

direction: Scn2a down in all measured groups; FDR-supported in 145 and 151
summary: FDR-supported on-target Scn2a depletion was concentrated in two thalamic glutamatergic groups, while all assayed GABAergic groups lacked FDR-supported target engagement.
why_it_matters: The strongest perturbation evidence falls in excitatory thalamic programs rather than in the inhibitory groups, refining where this dataset can make confident Scn2a loss-of-function claims.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|GABAergic groups assayed
main_caveats: The DE table reports target transcript changes, not electrophysiology or protein current; several cell groups had fewer than 60 perturbed cells.

direction: Scn2a down with no non-target FDR < 0.05
summary: Even where Scn2a itself was strongly depleted, the genome-wide mRNA response was almost entirely buffered.
why_it_matters: Nav1.2 loss can plausibly alter excitability without forcing a large steady-state transcriptional program, so the absence of many DE genes is biologically interpretable rather than a simple failed screen.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only mRNA abundance was tested, and nominal non-target genes such as Stn1, Dgkd, and Slc6a8 remain hypotheses rather than FDR-supported biomarkers.

summary: Scn2a knockdown did not induce transcriptional compensation by nearby sodium-channel, AIS, or synaptic disease-neighbor genes in the two best-engaged cell types.
why_it_matters: If partial Nav1.2 loss were buffered by up-regulating paralogous channels or Ankyrin/KCNQ machinery, those transcripts should have appeared in the same contrasts; they did not.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Compensation could occur at protein localization, channel gating, cell firing, or later time points rather than through these mRNAs.

direction: divergent; top-200 Pearson r values -0.184 to 0.166
summary: Perturbing available Nav-related and SCN2A-disease-neighbor genes did not phenocopy the Scn2a signature in the strongest Scn2a cell type.
why_it_matters: Genes that share an ion-channel neighborhood or monogenic epilepsy relevance are not interchangeable at the transcriptome level; the perturbation response is target- and isoform-specific.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Similarity used the top 200 Scn2a-ranked genes and RNA signatures; direct channel physiology may show relationships absent from mRNA DE.

direction: Kcnq2 positive neighbor; Ank3 top negative neighbor
summary: A weak cortical Scn2a signature aligned with Kcnq2 but opposed Ank3, despite both belonging to the AIS KCNQ/NaV scaffold module.
why_it_matters: The result nominates a clinically relevant AIS contrast that would have been missed by scalar Scn2a FDR alone, but it should be treated as exploratory.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Scn2a target depletion in this cell type was weak after multiple testing, so the Kcnq2/Ank3 relationship is restricted-signature and hypothesis-generating.

summary: The measured perturbation is transcript lowering, a therapeutic direction that is plausible for SCN2A gain-of-function but potentially wrong for loss-of-function disease states.
why_it_matters: The dataset shows knockdown without an obvious compensatory transcriptional rescue; human SCN2A treatment logic therefore has to remain allele-direction gated rather than simply Nav1.2-lowering.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Mouse CRISPR Perturb-seq does not establish clinical efficacy or safety; the warning follows from combining measured knockdown with human variant-function literature.

summary: Ptprd perturbation produced partial target-transcript reduction but no FDR-resolved downstream mRNA program in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: PTPRD is a synaptic membrane receptor phosphatase, so a complete loss-of-function might be expected to perturb synaptic signaling; this dataset instead argues that the acute transcriptomic response is buffered or below power.
main_caveats: On-target effects were nominal rather than FDR-significant; mRNA does not measure PTPRD protein, splice isoforms, synapse physiology, or phosphorylation.

summary: The most visible Ptprd signals were nominal and concentrated in scattered non-cortical broad classes rather than forming a cortex-wide response.
why_it_matters: The top rows point to possible MB/P/MY, thalamic, and hypothalamic sensitivity, but the lack of FDR means these are triage hypotheses, not validated cell-type hits.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All listed effects are FDR-negative; some contrasts have only 48-72 Ptprd-perturbed cells.

summary: Known PTPRD synapse-adhesion biology was not recovered as a recurrent transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: PTPδ regulates adhesion-mediated synapse organization with IL1RAPL1, IL1RAP, and SLITRK ligands, but Ptprd mRNA perturbation yielded only isolated nominal hits in neuronal adhesion or receptor genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Nrcam, Nrg3, Nfasc, and Ntrk2 were nominal and isolated; they do not establish direct downstream regulation by PTPRD.

summary: Ptprd signatures were nearly orthogonal to family members, extracellular partners, and unbiased top signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: This argues against treating all type-IIa RPTPs or PTPRD-binding organizers as interchangeable in this Perturb-seq readout and is consistent with splice- and partner-selective synaptic codes.
main_caveats: The Ptprd primary signature itself is weak, which limits interpretation of any correlation-based neighbor analysis.

summary: Ptprd perturbation did not evoke a STAT3/JAK-STAT RNA response in mature neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: PTPRD loss activates STAT3 in glioma and regulates RTK-MEK-ERK signaling in embryonic progenitors, but those phosphoprotein mechanisms are not mirrored by Stat3 or Socs3 mRNA changes here.
main_caveats: The assay does not measure pSTAT3, TrkB, PDGFRβ, MEK, or ERK phosphorylation, and the literature contexts are glioma or embryonic progenitors rather than adult neurons.

summary: PTPRD disease genetics are not accompanied by a directional acute neuronal transcriptomic signature strong enough for target-activation or target-inhibition decisions.
why_it_matters: The RLS/sleep/addiction literature makes PTPRD clinically interesting, but this perturbation table supports only a weak, buffered mRNA phenotype and sparse small-molecule precedent.
main_caveats: Open Targets GWAS links do not define effector tissue or direction of effect; the Perturb-seq readout is acute and transcriptional.

summary: Safe_target_33 behaved as a transcriptomically inert safe-targeting control across the measured mouse brain cell groups.

why_it_matters: PC2 is expected to act on stored secretory-granule precursors; the Perturb-seq result says that transcriptome-wide feedback is weak or delayed, so peptide mass/spec or secretion assays would be better primary readouts than bulk mRNA-response magnitude.

main_caveats: The dataset reports mRNA only; an unchanged transcriptome cannot exclude strong changes in mature neuropeptides or secreted peptide pools.

summary: Pcsk2 and the prohormone-processing neighbor Cpe converged on a target-only transcriptome rather than on a shared downstream gene program.
why_it_matters: Two linked peptide-maturation enzymes can be efficiently depleted without triggering a common compensatory mRNA module, arguing that their primary shared biology is post-translational in this assay.
main_caveats: The Cpe and Pcsk2 perturbations were compared by mRNA signatures only; Cpe had larger perturbed-cell counts in many cell types, and the Reactome pathway context is human endocrine proinsulin processing rather than mouse brain.

summary: Pcsk2 loss did not produce detectable transcriptional compensation of Scg5/7B2, Cpe, Pcsk1, granins, or selected neuropeptide precursor genes.
why_it_matters: Known PC2 biology involves 7B2-dependent activation and cleavage of peptide precursors, but the candidate pathway mRNAs themselves were not induced or suppressed at FDR 0.1; mature peptide depletion is therefore a more plausible hidden phenotype than compensatory precursor transcription.
main_caveats: Only a hand-curated precursor/processing list was tested here, and absence of mRNA change does not measure peptide processing products directly.

summary: Rgp1 up-regulation in L5 ET neurons and Rnf25 down-regulation in CA3/DG neurons were the only non-target FDR hits and were not recurrent.

summary: A library-wide signature-neighbor search found no perturbation that robustly mimicked or opposed Pcsk2.
why_it_matters: The lack of a positive or negative transcriptomic neighbor reinforces that the Pcsk2 phenotype is dominated by the target transcript instead of a reusable cell-state program shared with other guides.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from the supplied per-target score vectors; sparse self-contained signatures are intrinsically hard to match, and Pcsk5 was not a usable paralog comparator because its target transcript was not significantly depleted.

summary: Purb perturbation produced a mostly negative target-transcript trend but almost no FDR-corrected transcriptional response across 22 mouse-brain cell types.

summary: Purb knockdown does not provide a broad acute neuronal RNA biomarker for pharmacologic PURB inhibition.

summary: Zfp462 perturbation was transcriptionally weak: the Zfp462 row was not FDR significant in any cell type and the genome-wide Zfp462 screen had no gene-level FDR hit.

summary: Zfp462 perturbation in differentiated mouse-brain classes did not reproduce the published pluripotent-cell Sox2/Nanog or early lineage program.

summary: Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis found no strong positive or inverse Zfp462 neighbor in the leading Zfp462 cell types.

direction: assayed mRNA response is mild despite disease relevance
summary: The weak brain Perturb-seq response should not be interpreted as CNS safety for SETD2 inhibition or partial SETD2 loss.

summary: Six3 perturbation was not detectably validated at the target-transcript level in any assayed cell type.

summary: The Six3 perturbation produced an almost null transcriptomic response across the 23 brain cell classes.

summary: Canonical SIX3-Wnt/SHH developmental effectors were not mobilized by Six3 perturbation, despite strong Ctnnb1 and Tcf7l2 responses when Wnt effectors themselves were perturbed.

summary: Screened SIX-family paralogs Six1, Six5, and Six6 were as weak as Six3 and were not transcriptionally interchangeable with Six3.

summary: The HPE-relevant loss-of-function biology of SIX3 was not reproduced in the assayed differentiated neuronal classes.

summary: Sall4 perturbation was transcriptionally silent at the 5% FDR threshold across all 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes and did not measurably deplete Sall4 RNA.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset signal is absence of a reproducible brain-cell response, so stronger biological conclusions require explaining the expression floor rather than interpreting a hidden pathway activation.

main_caveats: Promoter occupancy and protein-level NuRD recruitment were not assayed; transcript-level FDR=1 does not exclude subtle chromatin effects in rare SALL4-expressing cells.

summary: The weak brain response should not be used to infer low developmental risk for SALL4 loss or SALL4 degradation, because SALL4 disease and CRBN-neosubstrate biology occur in early organogenesis contexts that this assay does not model.

summary: Trio target mRNA was directionally depleted in every measured Trio contrast, but only four of 23 cell types reached FDR<0.05 for the target row.

summary: Rtn4r targeting produced a near-null transcriptional response across 22 sampled neuronal cell classes rather than a broad NgR1-loss state.

summary: Drp2 up-regulation in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut was the only Rtn4r-associated transcript passing FDR control.

summary: The available NgR1 coreceptor perturbations, Lingo1 and Ngfr, were not transcriptional phenocopies of Rtn4r.

summary: An all-target same-cell-type signature-neighbor search failed to uncover a hidden strongly convergent or opposing Rtn4r module.

summary: Safe_target_38 produced no FDR-supported transcriptomic response in any tested mouse-brain cell class.
