main_caveats: The strongest cell type also had the largest Vps35 cell count, and the assay measures RNA rather than retromer protein or cargo trafficking.

direction: mixed; Grin2b/Rims3/L1cam/Kcnc2 down and Ache/Cttnbp2/Lrrc7/Ppp1r9b/Dgkz up
summary: The 151 TH Prkcd response nominates a synaptic-receptor and ion-channel mRNA module as the clearest readout of acute Vps35 loss.
why_it_matters: Grin2b, Rims3, L1cam, Kcnc2, Ache, Cttnbp2, Lrrc7, Ppp1r9b, and Dgkz provide a compact candidate marker set connecting retromer loss to neuronal compartments rather than to a generic stress program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Some module genes are FDR<0.10 rather than FDR<0.05, and mRNA changes do not prove altered receptor recycling.

summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut cells showed one of the strongest Vps35 self-knockdowns but no FDR-supported genes beyond Vps35 itself.
why_it_matters: The result separates target engagement from downstream transcriptome penetrance and warns against reading weak Vps35 signatures in other cell types as failed guides alone.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: A post-transcriptional or longer-latency phenotype could be present despite the sparse RNA response.

summary: The responsive 151 TH Prkcd profile did not transcriptionally compensate the VPS26-VPS29-VPS35 core, sorting nexins, WASH components, or Tbc1d5.
why_it_matters: The perturbation hit the retromer component itself but did not induce a homeostatic replacement program in adjacent endosomal genes, so the FDR signature should be interpreted as downstream neuronal state change rather than autoregulation of retromer biogenesis.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Retromer and WASH activity are primarily membrane-trafficking protein processes; lack of mRNA induction does not exclude altered localization or abundance of the encoded proteins.

summary: In the 151 TH Prkcd cell type, Rab7 was a modest top positive Vps35 signature neighbor, whereas Ap2s1 and Ap2m1 were among the strongest negative neighbors.
why_it_matters: This restricted comparison recovers a known Rab7-retromer connection while also suggesting that loss of the AP-2 endocytic adaptor subunits pushes this neuronal state away from the Vps35-loss program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: All genome-wide correlations were small in absolute value; direct VPS26/VPS29 perturbations were absent, and AP-2 is a signature neighbor rather than a direct retromer subunit.

summary: The Vps35 loss-of-function signature did not phenocopy Snca, Prkn, or Park7 perturbations and did not mount a broad autophagy-lysosome transcriptional response in the main Vps35-sensitive cell type.
why_it_matters: Parkinson-associated VPS35 D620N biology should not be inferred from this CRISPRi loss signature by simple direction reversal; the dataset instead captures a developing glutamatergic synaptic response and lacks a profiled Vps35 midbrain dopaminergic sample.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Snca and Prkn guide effects were weak in this cell type, and the experiment models transcript knockdown, not the D620N missense mutation.

summary: Set did not show transcript-level target engagement or a broad FDR-level response in the 22 assayed neuronal cell-type contrasts.
why_it_matters: This is the primary interpretive constraint: downstream negatives should be read as a weak-engagement or buffered Set perturbation rather than as proof that SET biology is dispensable in neurons.
main_caveats: The target-transcript row is an imperfect proxy for loss of SET protein or individual isoforms; all downstream interpretation is limited by absent measured knockdown.

summary: Man2c1 was the only FDR-significant downstream transcript and was restricted to 155 MB Glut cells.
why_it_matters: The result pinpoints the single conventional hit rather than overgeneralizing many nominal genes; Man2c1 is an exploratory midbrain-glutamatergic marker of this perturbation table, not a validated SET effector.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The signal is a single-gene FDR hit in a weak Set perturbation; the next ranked genes were not significant after FDR correction.

summary: Set nominal hits were cell-type-idiosyncratic rather than a conserved neuronal module.
why_it_matters: SET is a ubiquitous chromatin and PP2A regulator, so a repeated stress, chromatin, or phosphatase transcriptome would have strengthened the perturbation; the observed cross-cell correlations were essentially zero.
main_caveats: This conclusion concerns whole-transcriptome RNA response only; SET could act on phosphorylation, histone acetylation, or localization without a recurrent mRNA signature.

summary: The weak Set signature was uncoupled from an assayed PP2A-scaffold perturbation, Ppp2r1a.
why_it_matters: Because SET is an endogenous PP2A inhibitor, Ppp2r1a provided a within-dataset PP2A-axis positive comparator; Ppp2r1a was highly active while Set was not correlated with it, arguing that Set perturbation did not transcriptionally engage the PP2A module in these cells.
main_caveats: Ppp2r1a loss is not mechanistically the inverse of SET loss; lack of Set target engagement can explain the uncoupling.

summary: Set and its binding partner Setbp1 both produced FDR-level null signatures and did not converge.
why_it_matters: The result separates a reported SETBP1-SET-PP2A leukemia mechanism from these differentiated mouse neuronal contrasts; it is a moderate-confidence negative cross-perturbation result, not evidence that the proteins never function together.
main_caveats: Both Set and Setbp1 target-transcript measurements were weak, and the leukemia SETBP1-overexpression context differs from neuronal loss-of-function Perturb-seq.

summary: The dataset does not provide a broad neuronal transcriptomic rationale for Set inhibition despite cancer and tauopathy literature that makes SET pharmacologically interesting.
why_it_matters: SET antagonism is discussed for PP2A reactivation in disease states; in this dataset, weak Set knockdown and almost absent FDR response mean that therapeutic directionality cannot be inferred from these mouse-brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The assay was pooled single-cell RNA in mostly neuronal classes, not Alzheimer or cancer models, and did not measure PP2A activity, tau phosphorylation, or SET subcellular localization.

summary: The Rfx7 perturbation is globally buffered: the measured Rfx7 transcript was not significantly reduced in any of 22 brain cell classes and the whole Rfx7 table contains no adjusted-p-value hit below 0.2.
why_it_matters: Most downstream absences or weak contrasts must be interpreted as a low-engagement or buffered perturbation rather than as proof that Rfx7 is dispensable.
main_caveats: Target editing could affect protein or rare isoforms without a strong whole-transcript DE row; only mRNA readouts are available.

summary: The largest nominal Rfx7 responses are shallow and concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, whereas the classes with nominal Rfx7-transcript decreases still lack any FDR-supported downstream response.
why_it_matters: This argues against a robustly selective responder cell type in this atlas while preserving the weak thalamic, midbrain, hippocampal/amygdalar, and extratelencephalic cortical signals as hypotheses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All gene-level adjusted p values are at least 0.211, several groups have fewer than 65 perturbed cells, and the highest nominal rows do not coincide with the strongest measured target-transcript suppression.

summary: Rfx5 is the one literature-linked RFX7 target that recurs in the expected down direction after Rfx7 perturbation, with nominal decreases in five hypothalamic, thalamic, LGE-derived, and pineal-related classes.
why_it_matters: If replicated, Rfx5 could be a compact brain readout of residual RFX7 transcriptional activity; it also shows that the otherwise weak dataset still contains a direction that matches known RFX7 promoter regulation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The recurrence is nominal only, one contributing class has only 23 perturbed cells, and other reported RFX7 targets do not form a coherent significant module.

summary: Rfx7 does not phenocopy Rfx3, Trp53, PI3K/mTOR, or any strong signature neighbor, so canonical RFX-family ciliary logic and p53/metabolic-neighbor logic are transcriptionally uncoupled in this perturbation context.
why_it_matters: The result prevents simple substitution of Rfx3 or p53-pathway perturbations for Rfx7 when interpreting this mouse-brain screen.
main_caveats: Correlation is restricted to bulk score vectors within annotated cell classes; weak Rfx7 engagement can itself attenuate true pathway similarity.

summary: The mouse-brain perturbation gives little support for an acute, broad Rfx7-loss transcriptome in differentiated brain classes, refining human RFX7 neurodevelopmental genetics toward developmental timing, chronic dosage, or unmeasured stress and ciliary phenotypes.
why_it_matters: Human RFX7 variants cause neurobehavioral disease, but this dataset suggests that the causal window or phenotype may not be captured by a short single-cell mRNA response in the sampled cell classes.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse, transcriptomic, and weakly engaged at the target-transcript level; it cannot assay embryonic neural-tube closure, primary-cilium morphology, or organismal behavior.

summary: The absence of a strong Rfx7 signature is not evidence that systemic RFX7 inhibition would be benign, because RFX7 is embedded in p53/stress tumor-suppressor programs and Rfx7 deletion has major immune-metabolic effects in NK cells.
why_it_matters: A therapeutic strategy that inhibited RFX7 to reshape neuronal state would face tumor-suppressor and immune-homeostasis liabilities that are orthogonal to the weak mouse-brain readout.
main_caveats: No RFX7 drug was profiled; this is a direction-of-effect warning based on genetic perturbation and target biology, not on pharmacology.

summary: Raf1 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered at genome-wide thresholds across the mouse-brain cell types assayed.
why_it_matters: RAF1 is a curated RAS-to-MEK/ERK kinase, so the absence of any FDR-level single-gene response makes weak engagement and isoform or pathway buffering central to the interpretation rather than treating Raf1 as a strong MAPK hit.
main_caveats: The guide effect on Raf1 mRNA was only nominal and FDR = 1.0 in every cell type, so this is evidence for a buffered or under-engaged perturbation, not proof that RAF1 protein activity is dispensable.

summary: The clearest measurable Raf1 mRNA depletion was limited to a few strata, especially 155 MB Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: The perturbation cannot be interpreted as a uniform pan-neuronal RAF1 loss-of-function experiment; downstream null results in many cell types coincide with little detectable target-transcript movement.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Even in 155 MB Glut, the Raf1 row and all other rows had FDR = 1.0, so this is a target-engagement pattern rather than a corrected downstream program.

summary: Raf1 failed to engage the thalamic Vgf/Ptpn5/Etv5 module that is bidirectionally controlled by Braf, Map2k1, and Nf1 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: This separates C-Raf/Raf1 from a dataset-internal RAS-MAPK axis: Braf and Map2k1 loss repressed the module, Nf1 loss activated it, but Raf1 perturbation left the same markers uncorrected despite a similar cell count.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Raf1 itself was only weakly reduced in this cell type, so the result supports failure of this specific perturbation to phenocopy Braf/Map2k1 rather than a definitive genetic epistasis ordering.

summary: Canonical ERK-output and immediate-early transcripts were not reproducibly altered by Raf1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: If Raf1 knockdown had materially changed ERK activity, Dusp/Spry/Etv/Fos/Egr feedback genes would be plausible readouts; their absence strengthens the view that the experiment did not produce a strong RAF-MEK-ERK state change.
main_caveats: The panel was assessed at the mRNA level in pooled single-cell transcriptomes; transient phospho-ERK changes or early immediate-early pulses could be missed.

summary: Unbiased signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a hidden Raf1-like perturbation, including among Braf, Map2k/Mapk, FGFR/NTRK, or 14-3-3-associated targets.
why_it_matters: RAF1 is embedded in BRAF and 14-3-3 protein complexes, but the weak Raf1 expression signature did not converge with those direct neighborhoods, arguing against rescuing the Raf1 result by a related-target signature alone.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak Raf1 signatures; a post-translational RAF1 protein phenotype could be missed by mRNA score correlations.

summary: The Raf1 Perturb-seq null should not be extrapolated to pharmacologic RAF inhibition or RAF1-driven RASopathy without accounting for mutation direction and RAF dimer pharmacology.
why_it_matters: Human RAF1 disease is often gain-of-function, and small-molecule RAF inhibitors can act through dimer transactivation; therefore a partial guide-mediated loss with no neuronal mRNA program is not evidence that inhibiting RAF1 would be transcriptionally silent in RAS-active disease tissue.
main_caveats: This is an interpretive therapeutic caution, not a drug experiment; no RAF inhibitor, RAF1 activating allele, or phospho-ERK assay was present in the Perturb-seq dataset.

summary: Rorc perturbation was transcriptionally silent at FDR thresholds across the assayed mouse-brain classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset result is an interpretable null: neither a pan-neuronal stress program nor a reproducible Rorc-dependent neuronal module emerged.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was not depleted, so this finding establishes absence of a measured response, not definitive dispensability of Rorc.

summary: Rorc did not phenocopy the ROR-family paralog Rora in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.
why_it_matters: The thalamic class produced a strong Rora program despite a same-family Rorc perturbation with more perturbed cells, arguing against simple interchangeability of ROR-family factors in this neuronal context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Rorc target engagement was poor; the contrast may combine biology with different guide efficacy or baseline expression.

summary: The canonical RORgammat-Th17/IL-17 module was absent from the brain Rorc perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: RORC is clinically pursued largely through immune RORgammat biology, but the measured neuronal perturbations did not induce or repress Il17a, Il17f, Il23r, or Ccr6.
main_caveats: The assayed cells are brain populations rather than Th17 cells or lymphoid-tissue inducer cells; this is an expected absence rather than a contradiction of immune literature.

summary: RORE-linked clock and lipid/steroid genes showed only nominal, uncoordinated tails after Rorc perturbation.
why_it_matters: RORC can regulate peripheral circadian and metabolic transcription, but those known target families were not detectably organized by Rorc in the assayed brain cell types.
main_caveats: The dataset measured an acute perturbation in broad brain classes, whereas much RORC clock and metabolic biology was defined in peripheral tissues or synchronized bulk assays.

summary: A genome-wide neighbor scan found no strong Rorc-like or Rorc-opposed perturbation signature.
why_it_matters: Even without FDR-significant genes, correlated signatures could have exposed a hidden pathway; instead, the strongest correlations were weak, concentrated in 308 CB GABA, and not enriched for known ROR partners.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are signature-level and are dominated by a cell type whose Rorc profile itself lacked adjusted-significant genes.

summary: The lack of an acute neuronal Rorc transcriptomic phenotype should not be read as CNS de-risking for RORgamma antagonists.
why_it_matters: RORgamma is a tractable immunomodulatory nuclear receptor, yet this dataset did not achieve measurable Rorc knockdown in neurons; a silent Perturb-seq profile therefore argues for caution, not for absence of neural or barrier-associated RORC biology.
main_caveats: Clinical directionality is inferred from target class and disease biology, not from a disease model in this dataset.

summary: Zic3 perturbation produced no FDR-supported on-target or downstream transcriptional response in the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset should be interpreted primarily as a weak-engagement or buffered Zic3 experiment rather than as a definitive Zic3 loss-of-function map.
main_caveats: Target expression may be too low in many assayed neuronal cells for transcript knockdown to be quantified; the absence of RNA response is not proof that Zic3 is dispensable in development.

summary: A small 308 CB GABA module was the only Zic3 response that neared gene-level FDR significance.
why_it_matters: If any Zic3-responsive mouse-brain state is present in this screen, it is concentrated in the cerebellar GABAergic contrast rather than broadly distributed across cortical, thalamic, or midbrain classes.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The top genes missed 5% FDR and the contrast used only 70 perturbed cells, so this is a near-threshold module, not a validated cerebellar Zic3 program.

summary: Zic3 was not interchangeable with Zic1, Zic2, or Zic4 in matched mouse-brain signatures.
why_it_matters: Related Zic zinc-finger proteins should not be collapsed into a single functional node in this dataset: Zic1 alone showed a significant thalamic response with detectable on-target depletion, whereas Zic2, Zic3, and Zic4 did not show FDR-significant hits.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The paralog contrast is transcriptomic and may mix biological specificity with different guide efficiency or basal paralog expression.

summary: The weak 308 CB GABA Zic3 signature aligned with Wdr26 and opposed Ranbp2 signature neighbors.
why_it_matters: The proposed CB GABA markers may represent a broader cerebellar perturbation module rather than a pathway unique to Zic3; Wdr26 recapitulated 28 of the 30 nominal Zic3 CB gene directions and Ranbp2 inverted the same restricted list.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The comparison is driven by a nominal Zic3 gene set in one cell type and does not establish a physical or regulatory relationship among the perturbations.

summary: Known ZIC3 developmental partners did not phenocopy Zic3 in the measured neuronal perturbations.
why_it_matters: Prior ZIC3 biology centers on GLI, NODAL, Wnt, and PCP regulation in early embryogenesis; the screen does not show a matched GLI3/ACVR2B/SOX2/POU5F1/RAC1-like neuronal transcriptomic state, arguing that the canonical developmental circuitry was not reconstituted in these cell types.
main_caveats: Several central left-right genes, including Nodal, Lefty2, and Cfc1, were not perturbed, and the literature is embryonic whereas the dataset contains brain neuronal classes.

summary: The dataset and target databases do not support a pharmacologic Zic3 direction from the weak brain signatures.
why_it_matters: ZIC3 is a nuclear developmental transcription factor with congenital-disease genetics rather than an Open-Targets-supported clinical target, so the nominal CB GABA signature should be treated as biology-generating only.
main_caveats: Open Targets tractability is a database summary, not a definitive medicinal-chemistry impossibility statement.

direction: Slc20a2 transcript down in nominally engaged classes
summary: Nominal Slc20a2 self-depletion was concentrated in five neuronal subclasses rather than uniformly detectable across all 22 tested classes.
why_it_matters: Most cross-cell-type differences cannot be interpreted as simple biology unless weak target engagement in the many nonresponsive classes is considered.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: All five on-target rows were nominal p<0.05 but FDR=1.0; target depletion estimates are transcript-level only.

direction: knockdown with no downstream DE at FDR < 0.10
summary: The best-engaged Slc20a2 knockdowns produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptome despite nominal loss of the transporter mRNA itself.
why_it_matters: This separates SLC20A2 phosphate-transport biology from an acute pan-neuronal transcriptional module in this assay.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Partial knockdown, FDR=1.0 even for the self-transcript, and the assay does not measure phosphate flux.

summary: The neuronal Slc20a2 null DE result is more consistent with a chronic phosphate/neurovascular PFBC mechanism than with an immediate neuronal RNA program.
why_it_matters: PFBC mechanisms involve inorganic phosphate, CSF homeostasis, and neurovascular calcification compartments that are absent or indirect in the neuronal Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: The dataset did not profile pericytes, astrocytes, choroid plexus epithelial cells, CSF Pi, or calcification.

summary: Tested PFBC-neighborhood comparators Xpr1 and Pdgfrb did not phenocopy Slc20a2 in the shared neuronal subclasses.
why_it_matters: Although XPR1 and SLC20A2 interact in phosphate homeostasis, the Perturb-seq assay lacked a shared neuronal signature for this disease family.
main_caveats: Xpr1 engagement was weak, Pdgfrb engagement was absent, and Slc20a1 was not available as an exact perturbation.

summary: A global signature-neighbor search found no perturbation strongly correlated or anticorrelated with Slc20a2.
why_it_matters: This reduces the chance that a strong Slc20a2-like pathway was missed simply because a related gene name was not queried manually.
main_caveats: Correlation used Wilcoxon score vectors and is insensitive to non-transcriptional phosphate phenotypes.

summary: The dataset supports Slc20a2 self-mRNA as the only RNA readout more sensitive than downstream neuronal genes, so PFBC rescue screens should prioritize SLC20A2 restoration and phosphate/calcification endpoints rather than acute neuronal DE.
why_it_matters: Loss of SLC20A2 is disease-mimetic and ASO-mediated expression restoration is a therapeutic direction; neuronal RNA signatures would be a poor pharmacodynamic endpoint in this assay.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The ASO evidence applies to splice-disrupting SLC20A2 haploinsufficiency models, whereas this dataset used mouse neuronal CRISPR perturbations.

summary: Stk39 perturbation produced a globally weak or buffered RNA phenotype with no FDR<0.05 genes across 21 cell types.
why_it_matters: The primary result is negative after multiple testing, so downstream interpretation should not convert nominal genes into a SPAK transcriptional pathway.
main_caveats: The target row itself was never FDR significant, so buffering cannot be distinguished from weak sgRNA engagement.

summary: Nominal Stk39 self-depletion was confined to 052 Pvalb Gaba, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and these strata still lacked FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The modest phenotype is not evenly distributed; the few interpretable Stk39 RNA trends are concentrated in two GABAergic and one thalamic glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Cell counts were modest, especially 37 Stk39 cells in 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and all adjusted p values for Stk39 itself were 1.0.

summary: The WNK-SPAK/OSR1-SLC12 pathway was not transcriptionally activated or compensated after Stk39 targeting, and related Wnk or SLC12 perturbation signatures were uncorrelated with Stk39.
why_it_matters: It reconciles the Perturb-seq negative result with the known biochemical model in which SPAK acts by phosphorylation of cotransporters rather than by driving their mRNA abundance.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Correlations are RNA-level and do not test NKCC or KCC phosphorylation or chloride flux directly.

summary: Direct Slc12a5/KCC2 perturbation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut generated a clear immediate-early RNA response that Stk39 did not phenocopy.
why_it_matters: A downstream cotransporter can be captured by the assay, so the Stk39 negative result is not simply a universal inability to detect perturbations in this cell class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Slc12a5 had more perturbed cells than Stk39 in this class, and the comparison is transcriptomic rather than phosphoproteomic.

summary: Top positive and negative restricted Stk39 signature neighbors were weak and did not identify a WNK/SLC12-like convergence module.
why_it_matters: The weak neighbor structure argues against overinterpreting nominal Stk39 extreme genes as a reproducible pathway.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Neighbor correlations were computed only on the top 200 Stk39 genes and should be considered a restricted exploratory scan.

summary: Bulk RNA Slc12a2, Slc12a5, and global DE are poor surrogate biomarkers for SPAK inhibition in this assay; phospho-NKCC/KCC endpoints are more directionally aligned with known SPAK pharmacology.
why_it_matters: A candidate SPAK inhibitor could be biochemically active without producing a large mRNA signature, so RNA silence should not be misread as absent target engagement.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset did not measure protein phosphorylation, NKCC1/KCC2 activity, chloride, or cell volume.

summary: Tlr5 perturbation produced no FDR < 0.05 differential-expression hit across 21 tested neuronal classes, and the Tlr5 transcript itself was never significantly depleted.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset-grounded conclusion is absence of a detectable basal Tlr5-dependent neuronal transcriptomic state, but the missing on-target transcript shift prevents a strong claim that Tlr5 protein function was efficiently removed.
main_caveats: Negative DE under weak or unassessable target engagement; unstimulated neuronal cells rather than ligand-stimulated immune or epithelial cells.

summary: A single CA3/CA2-FC/dentate-family glutamatergic near-hit, Mpp1, was the strongest Tlr5-associated gene but stopped short of FDR < 0.05.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only cell-type-localized signal while preventing a borderline singleton from being overinterpreted as a TLR5 pathway.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: FDR = 0.056; 41 perturbed cells; no recurrence and no supporting cytokine or TLR signature.

summary: Tlr5 perturbation did not regulate measured NF-kappaB cytokine, MyD88-IRAK-TRAF6, or PI3K-Akt-mTOR genes in the neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: Known TLR5 agonism is expected to activate inflammatory and survival signaling, so absence of these modules shows that the Perturb-seq condition is not a neuronal proxy for flagellin-responsive TLR5 activation.
main_caveats: The dataset uses Tlr5 loss of function without exogenous flagellin; absence of ligand-induced genes is not the same as an antagonist experiment in microglia.

summary: Tlr5 failed to converge with available TLR-family and innate-pathway perturbations; related targets were almost all FDR-silent and had near-zero whole-transcriptome score correlations with Tlr5.
why_it_matters: The negative Tlr5 result is not rescued by a shared Toll-like-receptor signature in paralogs, co-receptors, or a downstream NF-kappaB neighbor within these neuronal classes.
main_caveats: Comparison was limited to related perturbations present in the parquet; some proximal adaptors such as Myd88 and Traf6 were not assayed as perturbation targets in the available related-target set.

summary: Neuronal Tlr5 inertness should not be used to infer that TLR5 agonists are inert in CNS immune cells.
why_it_matters: Published CNS TLR5 biology is concentrated in microglia, and ChEMBL/ClinicalTrials show that TLR5 agonism is a translational modality; the present screen lacks microglia and lacks the canonical inflammatory outputs induced by agonism.
main_caveats: This is a warning against overgeneralization, not a direct test of entolimod, flagellin, or microglial Tlr5 perturbation.

summary: Wwox perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional responder in any of the 22 measured brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: This is a robust negative result: the dataset should not be treated as containing a confident Wwox loss-of-function RNA module or individual effector gene.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Target protein editing was not measured, Wwox mRNA itself was only nominally reduced in 3 cell types, and FDR correction across approximately 16k-17k genes per cell type is stringent.

summary: The cell types with the clearest nominal Wwox transcript decrease still lacked corrected downstream DE.
why_it_matters: 052 Pvalb Gaba, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut are the best places to look for Wwox target engagement in this file, but their responses remain subthreshold rather than cell-type-selective programs.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Every Wwox target-transcript FDR is 1.0, so buffering cannot be separated from inadequate editing, scRNA-seq dropout, or low power.

summary: Canonical WWOX apoptotic, Wnt/GSK3β, and ERBB4/TFAP2C interaction axes were not detectably engaged at RNA-FDR level by Wwox perturbation.
why_it_matters: WWOX is annotated as a WW-domain scaffold linked to p53/p73 apoptosis, Wnt repression, and ERBB4/AP-2 binding; the dataset therefore argues against a broad acute transcriptomic readout of those pathways rather than against their post-translational biology.
main_caveats: The comparison uses RNA abundance and perturbation-signature correlation, whereas many reported WWOX mechanisms are WW-domain binding, phosphorylation, localization, apoptosis, or kinase-activity events.

summary: The only sizable Wwox signature-neighbor structure was a cerebellar GABA axis that included top coding-gene neighbors and non-targeting safe-target controls.
why_it_matters: Wdr26, Dstyk, Cckar, B9d1, Ranbp2, and Fbxo11 correlations look numerically stronger than all other Wwox comparisons, but the co-ranking of safe-target controls and the unchanged Wwox transcript in 308 CB GABA make this a nuisance-axis warning rather than a Wwox biomarker module.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to one cell type, uses score correlations of weak Wwox signatures, and contains non-targeting controls among the strongest anti-correlations.

summary: The mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout does not reproduce the severe WWOX developmental-and-epileptic encephalopathy biology as an acute cell-autonomous RNA program.
why_it_matters: Biallelic WWOX loss causes an infantile DEE and Wwox-null mice show cortical, hippocampal, cerebellar, myelination, seizure, and GSK3β-activation phenotypes; the negative Perturb-seq result points to chronic developmental, protein-interaction, kinase-activity, or circuit mechanisms that need assays beyond single-cell mRNA DE.
main_caveats: The disease literature involves human inherited loss or germline mouse knockout, not partial CRISPR perturbation in the assayed cells; absence of an RNA module does not refute protein-level WWOX biology.

summary: The Tcf3 perturbation showed no detectable depletion of its own transcript in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: A downstream null is hard to interpret as Tcf3 dispensability when the measured target mRNA itself was not reduced; weak engagement must be carried as the first caveat for every biological inference.
main_caveats: Tcf3 mRNA is only a proxy for perturbation activity; the assay could miss protein-level, isoform-level, delayed, or baseline-expression-dependent target effects.

summary: Tcf3 perturbation did not yield an FDR-resolved downstream transcriptome in the 22 sampled broad brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset supports a genome-wide negative result rather than a hidden pathway hit: no row reached FDR<0.05, the minimum adjusted P value was 0.111162, and the strongest nominal genes were isolated single-cell-type events.
main_caveats: The finding applies to this single-guide, matched-Wilcoxon readout under modest Tcf3 cell counts and weak target-transcript engagement; it cannot exclude rare subpopulations or developmental programs absent from the sampled cell classes.

summary: No sampled Tcf3 cell type showed a selective resolved response, including the highest-count thalamic, midbrain, and cortical contrasts.
why_it_matters: The lack of response was not confined to the lowest-count cell types, which weakens a simple explanation that one missed rare class carried all of the signal, while still leaving limited power as a global caveat.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut

summary: Tcf3 did not converge with E-protein paralogs or with any positive or inverse transcriptomic neighbor in the all-target score audit.
why_it_matters: Because Tcf3, Tcf4, and Tcf12 belong to the same E-protein family, a shared or opposing signature would have been a high-value clue; the observed score correlations were effectively zero, so the family relationship did not translate into an acute shared Wilcoxon signature here.
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to scalar differential-expression signatures; near-zero correlations are expected to be noisy because the Tcf3 signature itself is FDR-null.

summary: The Tcf3 null signature narrows, but does not negate, E-protein developmental disease biology.
why_it_matters: Mouse Tcf3/Tcf12 double knockouts affect MGE and oligodendrocyte development and the paralog TCF4 is a Pitt-Hopkins gene, yet this dataset shows no single-perturbation Tcf3 signature in the sampled broad neuronal classes; that points toward developmental lineage context, paralog buffering, or poor engagement rather than a general acute Tcf3 transcriptional lever.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks direct oligodendrocyte-lineage rescue/knockout assays, protein measurements, and human disease genotypes; the interpretation is contextual rather than a contradiction of developmental genetics.

summary: Ror2 perturbation produced no confirmed on-target knockdown and no robust downstream transcriptional program in adult neuronal classes.

direction: Ror2 null; Apc/Ctnnb1 strong and Ror2-uncorrelated

direction: dataset lacks highest-expression off-tumor brain contexts
summary: The neuronal Ror2 null does not de-risk ROR2-directed oncology biologics for choroid-plexus or ependymal off-tumor biology.

cell_types: all Ror2-assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: External expression is human bulk/single-nucleus RNA, whereas the dataset is mouse neuronal perturbation; no antibody-drug conjugate, CAR-T, or choroid-plexus cell response was assayed.

direction: developmental disease context not reproduced in adult neurons
summary: The adult-neuron null refines ROR2 Robinow/brachydactyly genetics toward developmental skeletal contexts rather than adult neuronal cell-autonomous transcription.
why_it_matters: Human ROR2 mutations cause developmental morphogenesis disorders, but the assayed adult neuronal cell types did not show acute Ror2-dependent transcriptional programs.
cell_types: all 23 Ror2-assayed neuronal classes
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay was not performed in chondrocytes, limb-bud mesenchyme, embryos, or organoids, and target depletion was not observed.

summary: Most significant signal after Uqcrfs1 perturbation was depletion of the Uqcrfs1 transcript itself, with almost no genome-wide non-target output.
why_it_matters: UQCRFS1 is a catalytic complex III subunit, so the dataset shows that partial transcript depletion in post-mitotic brain cell classes can be transcriptionally buffered rather than producing an immediate broad oxidative-phosphorylation or stress program.
main_caveats: The evidence is mRNA-only and cannot exclude loss of complex III protein, respiration, ATP, or ROS phenotypes without a broad transcriptional response.

summary: Pvalb, CNU-MGE, and midbrain/pontine/medullary GABA neurons had FDR-significant target knockdown but no other FDR-significant gene.
why_it_matters: These are clean examples where the guide-generated decrease in Uqcrfs1 was detected, yet the matched transcriptome stayed below FDR after multiple testing.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Each cell type has 73-117 perturbed cells; weak coordinated effects could remain below Wilcoxon power.

summary: The thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic stratum had the largest Uqcrfs1 cell count and a strong nominal on-target decrease, but still no FDR-significant target or downstream genes.
why_it_matters: This prevents treating all no-FDR cell types as unperturbed; some contain target engagement that is real enough to rank first by absolute score but insufficient, small, or variable enough to fail FDR.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Moderate-confidence because the dataset reports only matched aggregate Wilcoxon results and not guide identity, per-cell Uqcrfs1 expression, or protein depletion.

summary: Uqcrfs1 knockdown did not significantly change mRNAs encoding measured complex III subunits or neighboring Ttc19/Uqcc2 genes.
why_it_matters: Known Rieske chaperoning and TTC19 turnover operate at protein import, Fe-S loading, insertion, and fragment-clearance steps; the dataset places Uqcrfs1 loss upstream of little detectable stoichiometric mRNA feedback to the measured complex III module.
main_caveats: Only genes present in the measured panel were tested and the absence of mRNA compensation does not measure complex III assembly or proteostasis directly.

summary: Complex III-related perturbations were not interchangeable at the transcriptome level, even where several had strong self-knockdown in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Uqcrfs1, Uqcrc1, Uqcrc2, Cyc1, and Ttc19 all hit their own transcripts in the same cell class, but Uqcrfs1 showed near-zero score-vector correlations with those perturbations; same assembly membership therefore did not create a shared neuronal mRNA signature in this assay.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations are restricted to one cell type; because most perturbations had sparse downstream responses, low correlation should be interpreted as absence of a shared transcriptomic program, not evidence of opposite biochemical effects.

summary: Cfl1 is an exploratory midbrain-glutamatergic readout of Uqcrfs1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: It was the only non-target gene that survived FDR correction anywhere in the Uqcrfs1 dataset and it did not become FDR-significant under matched complex III neighbor perturbations in the same cell type, making it a candidate single-cell mRNA sentinel rather than a complex-wide marker.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene, single-cell-type signal; nominal Cfl1 p values under other perturbations show that specificity is FDR-based, not complete absence of fluctuation.

direction: Srr decreased mainly in 155 MB Glut with weaker decreases in a few other classes

why_it_matters: Interpreting a D-serine enzyme perturbation across all brain classes would overstate the dataset: the strongest measured knockdown occurred in a midbrain glutamatergic class, whereas most classes had low guide-cell numbers and weak or absent target-RNA depletion.

main_caveats: No Srr target row reached FDR<0.05, and most highlighted classes had only 22-34 perturbed cells.

summary: Srr knockdown did not create a corrected recurrent transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: SRR controls D-serine availability for NMDAR physiology, but its acute depletion in this Perturb-seq assay produced no dataset-FDR-supported gene and no recurrent nominal marker set, implying either biological buffering or that the primary phenotype is metabolic and electrophysiological rather than a large RNA program.
main_caveats: Absence of RNA FDR hits does not measure D-serine, SRR protein, receptor currents, or long-term synaptic remodeling.

summary: The canonical D-serine, serine-metabolism, and NMDAR neighborhood was not transcriptionally co-regulated after Srr perturbation.
why_it_matters: A direct perturbation of the D-serine synthetic enzyme did not feed back detectably onto nearby metabolic genes, D-serine degradation genes, DISC1, transporters, or Grin receptor transcripts, so the signature should not be read as a coordinated serine-shuttle RNA response.
main_caveats: The neighborhood test was hand-curated and RNA-only; many genes were lowly expressed in some classes, as indicated by unstable extreme logFC values for a few rarely detected genes.

summary: Srr signatures were nearly orthogonal to NMDAR-subunit and adjacent amino-acid perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: D-serine gates NMDARs, but loss of its synthetic enzyme was not transcriptionally interchangeable with Grin1, Grin2, Gls, Glud1, Got1, Got2, Slc1a1, Slc1a2, or Slc32a1 perturbation in matched cell classes.
main_caveats: Correlations are restricted to perturbations and cell classes present in the dataset; weak Srr target engagement may have compressed the Srr signature.

direction: loss-of-Srr gave weak RNA effects despite literature evidence for physiological loss-of-function phenotypes
summary: A flat transcriptome should not be equated with pathway safety or inactivity for SRR-modulating therapies.
why_it_matters: SRR is chemically assayable and sits in a pathway where decreasing D-serine may dampen NMDAR overactivation but also can cause NMDAR hypofunction-like phenotypes; the Perturb-seq result therefore argues that RNA readouts alone are insufficient for selecting SRR inhibitor direction or dose.
main_caveats: The dataset tested genetic RNA perturbation, not a titrated catalytic inhibitor or D-serine supplementation, and did not measure synaptic activity or excitotoxic stress.

direction: no robust convergence or inverse convergence
summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor scan found no robust convergent or inverse Srr partner.
why_it_matters: The lack of strong positive or negative neighbors reduces support for a hidden co-perturbation module and makes the Srr phenotype look isolated or underpowered rather than part of a broader recurrent transcriptional state.
main_caveats: The largest correlations came from 308 CB GABA, where the Srr arm had only 22 perturbed cells, so top-neighbor ranks are exploratory.

summary: Zbtb18 perturbation mostly increased the measured target transcript, but only 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had FDR-significant target-transcript engagement.

main_caveats: Target RNA is only a proxy for functional protein engagement; 20 of 22 cell classes did not show FDR-significant target-transcript movement.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained the only multi-gene adjusted-significant response to Zbtb18, with positive Endou, Pxdn, Clstn2, Man2a2, and Zbtb18.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The thalamic module is transcriptomic and compact; no direct Endou/Pxdn/Clstn2/Man2a2 ZBTB18 binding data were identified.

why_it_matters: The recurrence nominates a concrete non-target marker that connects the otherwise sparse Zbtb18 response to a collagen IV basement-membrane enzyme, while remaining outside the canonical RP58 cortical-target set.

summary: Zbtb18 perturbation did not FDR-engage the embryonic RP58/Rnd2/Id/Neurog2 repression axis.
why_it_matters: This separates the observed Perturb-seq response from the best-characterized RP58 developmental program and argues that the Pxdn/thalamic module should not be overlaid directly onto canonical cortical migration targets.

summary: The Zbtb18 response was globally buffered, with zero FDR-significant genes in all measured GABAergic classes and only the target transcript significant in 001 L5-6 IT Glut.
why_it_matters: The broad null pattern is itself biologically informative because it matches a glutamatergic-skewed RP58 developmental prior while showing that target RNA gain is insufficient to force a large transcriptional state change in most assayed classes.

main_caveats: Several null classes had weak or non-significant target-transcript engagement, so some buffering may reflect low functional perturbation rather than true resistance.

summary: Neither selected neurodevelopmental transcription factors nor the whole perturbation panel contained a strong same-cell Zbtb18 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: This turns the lack of obvious related-target convergence into a measured negative result: the Zbtb18 signature was isolated rather than a generic consequence of perturbing a ZBTB-family member or cortical/NDD transcription factor.
main_caveats: Whole-vector correlations can look small for sparse signatures, and several all-target neighbors were present in only a subset of the 22 Zbtb18 cell classes.

summary: Human ZBTB18 haploinsufficiency disease genetics should not be read directly from this mostly RNA-gain, FDR-sparse Perturb-seq signature.
why_it_matters: The finding prevents a directionality error: known ZBTB18 neurodevelopmental disease centers on damaging variants or reduced dosage, whereas this dataset mainly tests consequences of increasing measured Zbtb18 RNA.
main_caveats: This is an interpretive disease-direction warning, not a therapeutic experiment; the dataset does not include Zbtb18 knockdown, haploinsufficient animals, behavior, or synapse phenotyping.

summary: St3gal3 perturbation produced a transcriptome-wide null response: no cell class contained any FDR-significant gene, including downstream genes.
why_it_matters: ST3GAL3 is a Golgi glycosyltransferase, so a target-product phenotype can be invisible to a short mRNA readout; the dataset should not be interpreted as showing a strong transcriptional pathway hit.
main_caveats: The negative transcriptome-wide result is robust, but biological buffering cannot be separated from incomplete target knockdown because the St3gal3 transcript itself never reached FDR < 0.05.

summary: On-target St3gal3 transcript reduction was directional but only nominal, with the clearest signal in two thalamic glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: The measured response is better read as weak, cell-context-dependent target engagement than as a pan-neuronal ST3GAL3 loss-of-function profile.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The thalamic target rows were nominal only and did not pass FDR; one of the two cell classes had only 40 matched perturbed cells.

summary: The related sialyltransferase St3gal5 achieved much stronger target-transcript knockdown than St3gal3 but also produced no FDR-significant non-target genes.
why_it_matters: The family comparator argues that at least two Golgi sialyltransferase perturbations in this dataset behave as target-only or product-level hits rather than as broad transcriptional stressors.
main_caveats: St3gal5 makes GM3 from lactosylceramide whereas ST3GAL3 has different glycoprotein and glycolipid acceptors; absence of mRNA hits does not test ganglioside or glycoprotein abundance directly.

summary: Slc35a1, the Golgi CMP-sialic-acid transporter, was a nominal top positive gene after St3gal3 perturbation in L5-6 IT Glut cells.
why_it_matters: Because SLC35A1 supplies the CMP-sialic-acid donor used by sialyltransferases, recurrence of this signal in a larger experiment would be a plausible marker of sialylation-pathway compensation.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: Single small cell class, FDR = 1.0, and the St3gal3 target transcript was not nominally reduced in that same class.

summary: St3gal3 perturbation did not transcriptionally induce other ST3Gal-family or polysialyltransferase genes.
why_it_matters: Mouse brain ganglioside synthesis can be buffered biochemically by St3gal2/St3gal3 overlap, but this dataset shows no FDR-level mRNA compensation by St3gal2, St3gal5, or adjacent sialyltransferases.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundances were assayed; enzyme activity, substrate competition, and glycan-product flux were not measured.

summary: The mRNA-null St3gal3 Perturb-seq phenotype should not be read as evidence that ST3GAL3 loss is biologically benign.
why_it_matters: Human ST3GAL3 loss-of-function causes intellectual disability and epileptic encephalopathy, and mouse St3gal3/St3gal2 models show altered sialylation, myelination, and cognition; these phenotypes can arise through developmental glycan mechanisms not captured as immediate neuronal mRNA changes here.
main_caveats: The comparison crosses human genetics, whole-animal mouse development, and a neuronal Perturb-seq mRNA endpoint; oligodendrocytes and glycomics were not directly assayed.

summary: Ppard loss of function was transcriptome-wide silent at FDR<0.05 across the assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The screen does not show a broad acute PPARD-dependent neuronal program, even though prior CNS literature treats PPARβ/δ as a brain-relevant lipid-sensing nuclear receptor.
main_caveats: High confidence for the measured FDR-null result, but weak target-transcript depletion means the dataset cannot distinguish biological buffering from insufficient knockdown or low Ppard detectability.

summary: Only 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA showed recurring nominal Ppard self-depletion, with a weaker single 308 CB GABA nominal signal.
why_it_matters: The useful on-target readout is concentrated in caudal neuronal classes rather than being evenly distributed across cortical, hippocampal, hypothalamic, midbrain, and cerebellar groups.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The cell-type restriction is nominal because Ppard itself had FDR=1.0 in every cell type and the downstream signatures in these classes were also FDR-null.

summary: The Perturb-seq signatures did not activate or repress a coherent PPARD/RXR fatty-acid or lipid-metabolism module.
why_it_matters: PPARD is annotated as a DNA-binding nuclear receptor connected to RXRA and lipid/energy-metabolism regulation, so absence of Acox1, Cpt, Fabp, Angptl4, Pdk4, and related responses argues that the assayed basal neuronal state did not expose the canonical lipid program.
main_caveats: The panel was a priori and not an enrichment result; low expression of some lipid genes and weak Ppard knockdown can mask pathway regulation.

summary: Ppard signatures were nearly orthogonal to Ppara, Pparg, Rxr, Ppargc, and Ncoa perturbations and to the robust Srebf2 lipid-transcription-factor response.
why_it_matters: A simple model in which related nuclear lipid regulators collapse onto a shared neuronal signature is not supported; the strongest all-screen signature neighbors were weak, cell-specific, and not PPARD/RXR components.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations are restricted to transcriptomic score vectors from the same screen; because Ppard signatures are weak, absence of correlation is more reliable than the identity of any weak neighbor.

summary: The FDR-null healthy-neuron Ppard result should not be interpreted as evidence against PPARD agonism in disease or metabolic-challenge settings.
why_it_matters: PPARD is small-molecule tractable and has neurodegenerative and metabolic disease links, while published Huntington and neuronal-knockout studies used disease, dominant-negative, or organismal contexts that are not reproduced by this basal Perturb-seq experiment.
main_caveats: This is a context warning, not a positive therapeutic result; the screen lacks ligand treatment, disease stress, protein measurements, and non-neuronal glia.

direction: Zc3h13 and Atp1b2 up; Aig1, Pik3ca, and Trappc3 nominally down
summary: Vsx1 triggered a very small but FDR-significant transcriptomic response confined to 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, where Zc3h13 and Atp1b2 were up-regulated.
why_it_matters: The only reproducible signal in the brain dataset is cell-class restricted and involves neither Vsx1 itself nor canonical retinal-bipolar markers, so this perturbation should be interpreted as a sparse ectopic response rather than a broad homeobox-lineage program.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Only two genes passed FDR<0.05 and the strongest negative genes were FDR=1.0; the target transcript was not measurably knocked down.

summary: The Vsx1 transcript itself did not show detectable depletion in any measured brain cell class, and 22 of 23 classes had no downstream FDR hit.
why_it_matters: The dominant explanation for the weak perturbation map is poor target engagement or absent baseline target expression, not a confidently buffered homeostatic response.
main_caveats: The parquet contains differential-expression summaries rather than raw UMI counts, so target expression can be inferred only from the presence and statistics of the target row.

summary: Vsx1 perturbation in the only significant brain class was uncoupled from the retinal cone-bipolar genes reported to depend on Vsx1 in retina.

summary: Tia1 perturbation was weakly engaged and produced almost no reproducible RNA-abundance program across the 19 tested mouse-brain cell classes.

summary: Clinical NTRK inhibition should be interpreted against a neuronal on-target backdrop: Ntrk2 loss down-regulated Vgf recurrently and produced a Pvalb GABA signature in mouse brain cells.

summary: Smad4 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the 22 assayed neuronal/pineal cell classes.
why_it_matters: SMAD4 is a shared nuclear effector of TGF-beta and BMP pathways, so a pan-cell-class absence of FDR-significant genes argues that mouse-brain mRNA state is not automatically SMAD4-dependent, or that this guide set did not achieve enough functional SMAD4 loss to reveal such dependence.
main_caveats: The Smad4 transcript itself was not significantly depleted after correction, so the result is a measured negative transcriptomic response rather than proof that SMAD4 protein is dispensable.

summary: Loss of Smad4 did not recover a canonical TGF/BMP feedback module such as Id genes or Smad7 in any cell type.
why_it_matters: If canonical SMAD signaling were tonically driving these assayed neuronal states, Smad4 perturbation should have coherently shifted at least some direct or feedback targets; the measured program instead remained below FDR even for canonical sentinel genes.
main_caveats: The panel was literature-curated rather than an in-dataset enrichment result, and nominal Jun induction in 145 MH-LH TH Glut remained FDR 1.0.

summary: Smad4 signatures were not interchangeable with receptor, R-SMAD, inhibitory-SMAD, or SKI signatures despite those proteins belonging to the same curated pathway neighborhood.
why_it_matters: The contrast separates shared pathway annotation from actual perturbation-state equivalence: several neighbors, especially Bmpr2, Ski, and Smad2, produced sparse significant rows, but none generated a strong Smad4-like transcriptome.

summary: The mouse-brain negative result should not be used to de-risk systemic SMAD4 modulation.
why_it_matters: Human evidence links both reduced SMAD4 tumor-suppressor activity and gain-of-function SMAD4 developmental/fibroproliferative disease to pathology, while this dataset mostly reports weak mouse-brain neuronal transcriptomes with poor Smad4 mRNA knockdown; the modalities and disease windows therefore do not align.
main_caveats: ChEMBL absence of curated mechanisms is not proof that SMAD4 is undruggable, and the Perturb-seq assay did not test developmental exposure, fibrosis, vasculature, gut epithelium, or cancer cells.

summary: Sphk1 perturbation did not measurably depress the Sphk1 transcript in any profiled neuronal cell class.
why_it_matters: The target encodes the kinase that makes S1P; without detectable on-target transcript loss, downstream signatures should not be interpreted as clean SPHK1 loss-of-function biology.
main_caveats: Only transcript-level target engagement is available; SPHK1 protein, lipid S1P, and guide editing efficiency were not measured in the parquet.

summary: No downstream gene reached FDR<0.10 after Sphk1 perturbation across 388046 tested gene-by-cell-class rows.
why_it_matters: This global absence of corrected hits makes a broad basal neuronal SPHK1 transcriptional program unlikely in this assay and is qualitatively compatible with prior evidence that Sphk1-only loss can be buffered in mice.
main_caveats: A buffered biological response cannot be separated from incomplete Sphk1 knockdown.

summary: The largest nominal Sphk1 response was restricted to 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and remained exploratory.
why_it_matters: This prevents the LGE-GABA signature from being discarded outright while preserving that its 149 nominal p<0.01 genes, top Pde4dip/Elmod1/Pde7b/Rgs9/Podxl2/Erc2 hits, and all apparent signature neighbors were FDR-unsupported or weak.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The inference is based on nominal p values only, 53 perturbed cells, FDR>=0.8328, and full-signature correlations below |0.23|.

summary: Sphk1 perturbation was uncoupled from the profiled sphingosine/S1P pathway neighborhood.
why_it_matters: Although SPHK1 sits in a curated pathway that generates S1P and STRING links it to adjacent sphingolipid enzymes, Sphk1 did not reproducibly alter S1P-receptor, S1P-turnover, or ceramide genes and did not correlate with S1pr2, Sptlc2, Asah1, or Smpd3 perturbation signatures.
main_caveats: Related-target correlation is signature-based and transcriptomic; most nearby sphingolipid genes were measured as transcripts but not perturbed.

summary: The dataset refines neuronal SPHK1 disease biology toward stimulus- or lipid-state dependence rather than a constitutive cell-autonomous transcriptional role.
why_it_matters: AD and Niemann-Pick type C models implicate neuronal SPHK1 in COX2 acetylation, resolution mediators, sphingosine storage, and autophagosome-lysosome fusion; the basal Perturb-seq profile instead shows no strong Sphk1-only transcriptional program in many neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The disease studies used stressed adult or disease-model neurons and enzymatic/lipid readouts, whereas the Perturb-seq dataset measured basal RNA in mouse neuronal classes.

summary: These data should not be used as positive support for inhibiting SPHK1 in basal neurons despite the druggability of SPHK1/S1P signaling.
why_it_matters: SPHK1 has biochemical inhibitors and the downstream S1P receptor family is clinically tractable in multiple sclerosis, but the neuronal Perturb-seq result lacks both target engagement and a coherent S1P-axis signature.
main_caveats: The warning addresses neuronal SPHK1 transcriptomic support only; it does not test pharmacologic SPHK1 inhibition, lipid flux, immune cells, or approved S1PR modulators.

summary: Thoc1 perturbation produced a strongly cell-type-skewed transcriptomic phenotype concentrated in four subcortical neuronal classes, not a uniform pan-neuronal response.
why_it_matters: A housekeeping TREX subunit could have been expected to perturb every assayed neuron similarly; instead 98.1% of all FDR<0.05 genes were concentrated in two thalamic/hypothalamic classes and two midbrain/pons/medulla classes.

summary: A recurrent Thoc1-response module is marked by consistent Snhg11 and Rsrp1 repression with Smarcc2, Anxa6, Dgkz, Gtf2i and Ccdc93 induction across responsive classes.

summary: Thoc1 signatures converge with nuclear mRNA export, spliceosome and nuclear-pore perturbations rather than with an unrelated or opposite signature family.
why_it_matters: Tpr, Snrnp70, U2af2, Cdc40, Ddx39b and Thoc2 recur among the nearest positive signature neighbors, matching literature that THO/TREX couples spliced mRNP assembly to NXF1-dependent export through the nuclear pore.

why_it_matters: Membership in the same export assembly did predict positive similarity in MB P MY GABA and Pvalb signatures, yet Ddx39b and Thoc2 failed to reproduce the large Thoc1 thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic responses.

summary: The Thoc1 mRNA itself was not significantly depleted in any assayed cell type, even where downstream signatures were large.
why_it_matters: The screen contains reproducible downstream Thoc1-state signatures, but interpretation should be anchored on the signature rather than assuming that the assayed Thoc1 transcript quantitatively reports protein loss in every cell class.
main_caveats: The self-test uses the measured transcript; guide activity against unmeasured isoforms, delayed protein depletion, and target-expression dropout cannot be distinguished from weak editing in this parquet.

summary: The perturbation profile supports a neuron-subtype vulnerability model for TREX dysfunction rather than a simple uniform housekeeping model.
why_it_matters: Mouse and patient-linked studies show that THO/TREX disruption can compromise embryonic viability, dopaminergic synapse maintenance and THOC2-associated neurodevelopment; the Perturb-seq data refine that biology by pinpointing subcortical glutamatergic and GABAergic classes as especially responsive to partial Thoc1 perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: No R-loop, DNA damage, nuclear-export or survival assays were measured, and Thoc5/Thoc2 disease models are not direct Thoc1 loss-of-function models in these same cell types.

summary: Pax7 perturbation produced a dataset-wide null signature with no detectable Pax7 transcript knockdown and only one corrected downstream hit.
why_it_matters: The dominant biological readout is absence of an active, regulatable Pax7 program in the assayed mature brain cell classes rather than a broad PAX7 loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: Large negative Pax7 logFC values occur beside Wilcoxon scores near zero, so they are likely low-expression artifacts; guide activity cannot be inferred from the target transcript when Pax7 is absent.

summary: The only FDR-significant Pax7-associated response was Ruvbl1 up-regulation in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.

cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut

summary: Known PAX7 developmental, neural-plate-border, and myogenic partner genes remained uncoupled from Pax7 perturbation in brain neurons.
why_it_matters: Pax7 is annotated to developmental transcriptional and myogenic programs, but the perturbation did not induce or repress their measurable components, arguing against transdifferentiation or injury-like reactivation of canonical PAX7 circuitry.

why_it_matters: Prior data place Pax7 activity in dorsal mesencephalic and midbrain-associated development, so the null 155 MB Glut and related results refine the relevant population to rarer or developmental Pax7-positive subtypes rather than all adult midbrain neurons.

summary: The brain Pax7 null result should not be extrapolated to PAX7-FOXO1 rhabdomyosarcoma dependencies.
why_it_matters: Open Targets and sarcoma literature connect human PAX7 disease evidence to muscle-lineage congenital myopathy and PAX7-FOXO1/PAX3-FOXO1 alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, whereas this dataset perturbs wild-type Pax7 in nonmyogenic mouse brain cells with no canonical partner response.

summary: Tpi1 mRNA was depleted in every assayed cell type but reached FDR significance in only a subset, with the clearest direct engagement in thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, Pvalb, L5 ET, and entorhinal L2/3 glutamatergic contexts and the weakest evidence in low-count MB Dopa cells.
why_it_matters: The response map should be interpreted through measured target engagement: several apparently negative cell types had weak or low-powered Tpi1 knockdown rather than proven resistance to loss of TPI1 enzyme activity.

direction: Tpi1 down with minimal FDR downstream response
summary: Successful Tpi1 transcript depletion was usually transcriptionally buffered: after FDR correction, Ogt in 145 MH-LH TH Glut was the only non-target hit across 388023 assayed non-target rows.
why_it_matters: TPI1 is a core glycolytic homodimer and human TPI1 loss causes a severe glycolytic enzymopathy, so the absence of a broad glycolysis, oxidative-stress, or repair program points to either acute metabolic buffering or to disease mechanisms that are not captured by mRNA abundance at this Perturb-seq time point.
main_caveats: Buffered transcription does not prove preserved glycolytic flux; metabolites, enzyme activity, protein abundance, and cell viability were not measured.

direction: Ogt down after Tpi1 or Pgk1 perturbation
summary: Ogt downregulation defines a cell-type-restricted Tpi1/Pgk1 response in 145 MH-LH TH Glut.
why_it_matters: OGT installs O-GlcNAc using the hexosamine-pathway donor UDP-GlcNAc; Ogt therefore gives a focused, testable readout for coupling between glycolytic stress and nutrient-sensitive glycosylation in this hypothalamic-thalamic glutamatergic class.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The biomarker is a single transcript in one cell type; O-GlcNAc, UDP-GlcNAc, and OGT protein were not measured.

direction: shared downregulation of Pnisr/Rsrp1/Ttc14/Ogt strongest for Pgk1 and Gapdh, nominal for Tpi1
summary: Tpi1, Pgk1, and Gapdh converge in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut on a lower-glycolysis signature containing Pnisr, Rsrp1, Ttc14, and Ogt.
why_it_matters: The top Tpi1 positive signature neighbor in this cell type was Pgk1 and Gapdh was also among the nearest neighbors, matching their biochemical adjacency to TPI1 and nominating the Pnisr/Rsrp1/Ttc14/Ogt pattern as a lower-glycolysis stress module rather than an idiosyncratic guide artifact.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The non-target Tpi1 rows are nominal rather than FDR-significant in 151 TH, and global score-vector correlations are low even for the nearest perturbation neighbors.

summary: Upstream or transport glycolysis perturbations did not phenocopy the Tpi1/Pgk1/Gapdh pattern even when their own transcripts were depleted.
why_it_matters: A simple pathway-membership model would group HK1, GPI1, TPI1, GAPDH, and PGK1 together; the data instead split the pathway, with the 151 TH downstream signature concentrated around the TPI1-GAPDH-PGK1 interval and not reproduced by Hk1, Gpi1, or Slc2a1.

main_caveats: Hk1 and Gpi1 may generate weaker metabolic lesions than Pgk1 in these cells, and Gapdh and Eno1 on-target mRNA rows were absent from the measured expression matrix.

direction: avoid TPI1 inhibition; restoration or stabilization would be the disease-compatible direction
summary: The dataset reinforces a loss-of-function liability model rather than a rationale for inhibiting TPI1 in neurons.
why_it_matters: Human TPI1 deficiency is severe and associated with neurodegeneration, ChEMBL lists biochemical records for human TPI1 but no approved mechanism-of-action drugs, and the Perturb-seq signatures show that mouse neuronal classes can lose Tpi1 transcript without activating a robust compensatory RNA program.
main_caveats: The experiment used transcript knockdown rather than patient missense alleles and measured short-term RNA effects, not organismal neuromuscular phenotypes.

direction: downstream sterol genes down after Srebf2 knockdown

why_it_matters: The affected genes include multiple enzymes and feedback genes in the SREBP pathway, so the dataset reads out loss of SREBF2 transcriptional activity rather than only the guide's effect on the target mRNA.

main_caveats: All readouts are mRNA differential-expression results; no SREBF2 protein, nuclear SREBF2, or cholesterol abundance was measured.

direction: selective response in non-cortical neuronal classes
summary: The Srebf2-dependent sterol module is concentrated in hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, and pontine/medullary classes rather than being a uniform consequence of Srebf2 transcript loss.
why_it_matters: SREBP2 is often presented as a broadly acting sterol regulator, but these neuronal perturbations separate target engagement from pathway output and identify the classes in which the program is most transcriptionally coupled to Srebf2.

direction: target down with weak or absent downstream sterol response
summary: Several cell types display strong Srebf2 mRNA knockdown with little detectable sterol-gene propagation.
why_it_matters: These buffered cases argue against using target knockdown alone as proof that the SREBP2 regulon was functionally perturbed in every neuronal subclass.

summary: Dctn1, Dync1h1, and Marchf6 perturbations drive sterol genes upward, opposite to Srebf2 loss, in the same response-capable neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The dataset contains a bidirectional sterol module: direct Srebf2 depletion decreases the pathway, while dynein/dynactin and ER-associated degradation perturbations activate many of the same transcripts.
