direction: candidate negative biomarkers after Srebf2 knockdown
summary: Insig1, Dhcr24, Msmo1, and Cyp51 are more recurrent Srebf2-response transcripts than Hmgcr or Ldlr in this neuronal dataset.
why_it_matters: Hmgcr and Ldlr are classic SREBP2 targets, but relying on either one alone would miss many Srebf2-responsive neuronal classes captured by the recurrent downstream genes.
main_caveats: The ranking is assay- and cell-type-specific and reflects mRNA detectability plus effect size, not necessarily the most important enzymatic control point.

summary: Srebf2 knockdown did not significantly induce a transcript-level Srebf1, LXR, INSIG2, SCAP, or MBTPS processing-axis compensation.
why_it_matters: The sterol-gene decrease is therefore not accompanied by an obvious alternative sterol-regulatory transcriptional arm in the measured data.
main_caveats: This only tests mRNA abundance of a small set of regulators; SREBP regulation is heavily post-translational, and the related perturbations themselves were weakly engaged.

direction: warning against broad SREBP2 pathway suppression
summary: CNS SREBF2 suppression would be expected to depress a broad cholesterol-biosynthetic program in selected neurons, not just Hmgcr.
why_it_matters: The responsive module includes early, intermediate, and late sterol genes in neuronal classes, while CNS literature links Srebp2-dependent cholesterol synthesis to glial support and myelination; indiscriminate SREBP2 inhibition could therefore carry circuit- and myelin-relevant liabilities.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset did not test a drug, a human cell, or a phenotypic endpoint; the warning is based on pathway breadth and CNS prior biology.

summary: Syn3 guides did not measurably deplete the endogenous Syn3 transcript in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: A weak target-transcript change makes downstream negative signatures difficult to interpret as biological dispensability of Syn3.
main_caveats: The dataset measures RNA rather than Synapsin-3 protein, so post-transcriptional guide effects cannot be excluded.

summary: The expected synaptic-vesicle biology of Syn3 was not converted into a corrected transcriptional response: no gene reached FDR<0.10 and the nominal tail was sparse.
why_it_matters: Synapsin biology is presynaptic and vesicle-centered, so the absence of a recurrent RNA module argues that this perturbation should not be pathway-enriched from nominal single-cell hits.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic endpoint; electrophysiological or vesicle-pool effects could exist without large mRNA changes.

summary: Weak Syn3 engagement contrasted with robust self-depletion of paralogous and neighboring presynaptic perturbations in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: In 155 MB Glut, presynaptic genes such as Syn1, Syn2, Syp, Snap25, Stx1b, and Syt2 could be depleted, so the Syn3 null is not explained by a universal failure to detect presynaptic transcripts.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The correlation test is restricted to available RNA signatures and cannot distinguish Syn3-specific guide inefficiency from low or variable Syn3 expression.

summary: The midbrain dopaminergic Syn3 signature is not an adequate test of Syn3 lowering as a Parkinson's-disease-relevant intervention.
why_it_matters: Prior PD-like mouse work motivates Synapsin III silencing in dopamine neurons, but the matching 215 MB Dopa class had only 30 Syn3-perturbed cells, no on-target RNA depletion, and no FDR-supported targets.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: The dataset is underpowered for this cell type and lacks alpha-synuclein aggregation, dopamine-release, and motor phenotypes.

summary: Smad6 perturbation produced no multiple-testing-corrected transcriptional response in any sampled brain cell type, and the target transcript was too sparse to demonstrate knockdown.
why_it_matters: The dominant dataset-grounded interpretation is absence or failure of engagement rather than activation of a detectable BMP/TGF-beta program.
main_caveats: A negative DE signature cannot distinguish biological buffering from inefficient CRISPR perturbation because Smad6 was not measured in 21 of 23 cell types.

summary: The lack of Smad6 response contrasts with corrected responses from several nearby BMP/TGF-beta pathway perturbations in the same screen.
why_it_matters: This argues that the experiment was able to recover at least some signaling-node effects in this pathway family; Smad6 is the weak node, not the entire pathway neighborhood.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Related perturbations had their own cell-count and target-engagement differences, and their signatures are not expected to be identical to derepression of an inhibitory SMAD.

summary: Canonical BMP/TGF-beta feedback components did not form a corrected Smad6 module; Skil, Smad3, and Id2 appeared only as isolated nominal hits.
why_it_matters: The perturbation readout does not support coherent derepression of SMAD transcriptional feedback, even though SMAD6 is a BMP-selective inhibitor of the SMAD1-SMAD4 branch.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: This is a pathway interpretation of uncorrected p values; all named Smad6-pathway rows had FDR=1.0.

summary: 054 CNU-MGE GABA was the most plausible but still exploratory site of a Smad6-linked response.
why_it_matters: It combined the largest nominal Smad6 gene count, nominal Skil down-regulation, and the strongest within-cell-type correlations to Ski, Smad2, Acvr2b, and Smad3 signatures.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: No CNU-MGE gene passed FDR<0.05 and the related-perturbation correlations were small.

summary: Brain Smad6 nonresponse should not be used to dismiss organismal SMAD6 loss-of-function liabilities in BMP-dosage-sensitive skeletal and cardiovascular tissues.
why_it_matters: Human genetics ties SMAD6 loss of function to craniosynostosis and bicuspid-aortic-valve/aortopathy phenotypes, whereas this neuronal dataset lacked target engagement and corrected neuronal biomarkers.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment sampled brain cell classes, not osteoblast, cranial suture, valvular, or aortic lineages; ChEMBL target-search absence is not proof of undruggability.

summary: Pvalb Gaba cells did not show a corrected Smad6 response despite an external mouse-cortex literature precedent for BMP-SMAD1 signaling in parvalbumin interneurons.
why_it_matters: This refines the neuronal BMP-SMAD1 literature to say that Smad6 knockdown in this dataset is not sufficient evidence for perturbing that PV-interneuron program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The comparison is indirect because the literature manipulated BMP-SMAD1 signaling in cortex, whereas the dataset measured Smad6 perturbation without observed target knockdown.

summary: Reln perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional program in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: RELN is an essential extracellular signaling ligand, so the absence of any stored FDR<0.05 gene is itself informative: this Perturb-seq readout did not recover a robust acute cell-autonomous RNA program for the ligand.
main_caveats: Target-transcript depletion was also not significant after FDR correction, so the negative downstream result cannot be separated from weak target engagement.

summary: The clearest but still sub-FDR Reln self-depletion localized to GABAergic populations, especially 053 Sst Gaba and then 046 CTX-CGE GABA.
why_it_matters: Adult Reelin is supplied prominently by GABAergic interneurons; the dataset therefore points to the expected source-lineage context but does not convert it into a statistically validated downstream signature.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: The strongest source-like class had only 27 perturbed cells and Reln itself had FDR=0.7368; individual nominal response genes should be treated as candidates only.

summary: Reln signatures were essentially orthogonal to perturbations of assayed Reelin receptor, adaptor, kinase, integrin, and SH3KBP1 pathway genes.
why_it_matters: DAB1, VLDLR, LRP8 and FYN are close biochemical neighbors of RELN; their failure to phenocopy Reln indicates that the measured RNA signatures should not be interpreted as a canonical Reelin cascade activity score.
main_caveats: Weak Reln target engagement can erase a true ligand phenotype; these are transcriptome-wide correlations, not biochemical phospho-DAB1 or receptor-occupancy assays.

summary: Even in 053 Sst Gaba, Reln had no high-correlation positive or negative signature neighbor in the whole perturbation library.
why_it_matters: The weak Reln/Sst signature was not merely mislabeled as another target; the largest positive and negative correlations across 1,931 alternatives were only 0.072 and -0.051.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: This is a restricted Sst-only signature-neighbor scan; the Reln signature itself is weak and low count.

summary: Reln did not phenocopy Grin1 or Grin2b even though Grin perturbations generated measurable transcriptional programs.
why_it_matters: Reelin can modulate NMDA-receptor physiology, but the dataset separates ligand loss from core NMDA-receptor-subunit loss at the RNA-program level.
main_caveats: The literature concerns receptor phosphorylation, calcium influx and LTP, whereas the dataset measures single-cell RNA after genetic perturbation.

summary: RELN genetic-disease relevance does not translate here into an acute transcriptomic target-engagement biomarker.
why_it_matters: RELN loss causes human cortical malformation and some familial epilepsies; in this dataset, however, neither Reln mRNA depletion nor any downstream disease-proximal marker passed FDR, arguing against using this signature as a pharmacodynamic assay without orthogonal validation.
main_caveats: Human RELN disorders are germline and often developmental or secretion-related; the perturbation dataset is mouse, cell-type-resolved, and transcriptional.

summary: Tgfbr3 was measured in all available contrasts but no neuronal class showed significant on-target Tgfbr3 transcript depletion or any FDR-significant downstream gene.
why_it_matters: Without verified target engagement, the Tgfbr3 perturbation cannot be interpreted as a clean loss-of-function test in these cell types.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: A true protein-level perturbation could still occur without a strong mRNA change, but the RNA target row gives no support for that in this output.

summary: Tgfbr3 perturbation did not elicit a coherent TGF-beta, BMP, FGF2, or NF-kappaB transcriptional response in the measured neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: TGFBR3 is annotated as a multi-ligand co-receptor, so absence of Smad/Id/Nfkbia or FGF2-axis transcriptional changes argues that the assayed edits did not recruit the expected pathways.
main_caveats: This is mainly a negative pathway readout; weak on-target knockdown prevents distinguishing biological buffering from ineffective editing.

summary: Tgfbr3 signatures were near-orthogonal to Tgfbr1, Tgfbr2, Bmpr2, activin/BMP receptor, and Smad perturbations, despite those targets belonging to adjacent TGF-beta-superfamily signaling modules.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating Tgfbr3 as an interchangeable proxy for catalytic TGF-beta/BMP receptors in this neuronal Perturb-seq setting.
main_caveats: Several related perturbations also have weak on-target rows, so the contrast is strongest for Bmpr2 and for the absence of any family-wide convergence, not for every individual comparator.

summary: The neuronal Tgfbr3 negative result does not evaluate the AD-associated soluble-TGFBR3 microglial mechanism targeted by emerging antagonists.
why_it_matters: Recent sTGFBR3 therapeutic work is framed around microglial TGF-beta/NF-kappaB balance, whereas the available Tgfbr3 cell types were Glut/GABA neuronal classes with no Nfkbia or Smad response.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The dataset contains no direct protein, soluble ectodomain, APP/PS1, STZ, or microglial perturbation readout.

summary: A restricted Tgfbr3 signature-neighbor scan yielded no recurrent positive or negative perturbation neighbor suitable for mechanism assignment.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpreting single noisy per-cell-type correlations as pathway evidence.
main_caveats: The scan used only the top 50 Tgfbr3-scored genes in each cell type and was intentionally restricted-signature based.

summary: Pi4ka mRNA depletion was directionally consistent but produced a strikingly sparse FDR-level transcriptional response.
why_it_matters: PI4KA is an enzymatic source of PI4P, yet most neuronal classes showed partial Pi4ka mRNA loss without activating broad mRNA readouts, so immediate transcriptomes are likely a poor surrogate for PI4P or PI(4,5)P2 depletion.
main_caveats: The dataset measures RNA rather than PI4P, PI(4,5)P2, membrane traffic, or evoked activity; many cell types had only nominal on-target depletion after FDR correction.

summary: Slc12a5/Kcc2 was the sole robust downstream transcript in Pi4ka-perturbed 191 MB P MY GABA cells.
why_it_matters: KCC2 controls neuronal chloride extrusion; selective Slc12a5 loss nominates a functional inhibitory-neuron marker to monitor in caudal GABAergic cells after PI4KA reduction.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Single-cell-type and single-gene FDR hit; Pi4ka itself was only nominal in this cell type and the Jun/Stmn4/Grin2d components were not FDR-significant.

summary: The low-n pineal glutamatergic contrast exposed an Abca2/Dgkd/Rap1gap lipid-homeostatic lead set that did not recur at FDR level elsewhere.
why_it_matters: The Abca2 hit connects the strongest rare-cell response to brain lipid handling, and the Dgkd signal suggests a candidate phospholipid-remodeling compensation after Pi4ka perturbation.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only 26 perturbed cells; Pi4ka transcript depletion was weak in this stratum; all genes except Abca2 were FDR 0.088-0.175 rather than FDR<0.05.

summary: Pi4ka signatures were almost orthogonal to Pi4kb and to several assayed phosphoinositide-pathway perturbations.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating PI4KA loss as interchangeable with PI4KB, PI3K, PTEN, synaptojanin, or inositol-phosphatase knockdowns in this neuronal Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: Pi4kb target engagement was weak, and the comparison uses whole-transcriptome signed scores rather than lipid measurements or matched perturbation efficiencies.

summary: Pi4ka had context-restricted positive signature neighbors in pineal and brainstem/medullary cells rather than a universal phosphoinositide-gene neighbor.
why_it_matters: The top Pitpna neighbor in pineal glutamatergic cells is biologically plausible for PI substrate transfer, whereas the MB P MY GABA neighbors point to a more general endomembrane stress/proteostasis axis that may be secondary to membrane lipid imbalance.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: All signature-neighbor correlations were modest, the pineal comparison had fewer than 30 cells per perturbation, and most neighbors are not direct PI4KA complex members.

summary: The acute mature-neuron RNA phenotype is much weaker than expected from human PI4KA developmental brain disease.
why_it_matters: Because biallelic PI4KA variants cause cortical malformation and hypomyelinating leukodystrophy, the muted RNA response suggests that disease mechanisms may depend on developmental timing, oligodendrocytes, structural membrane trafficking, or activity-dependent synaptic physiology not captured by this assay.
main_caveats: Species, developmental stage, perturbation strength, disease chronicity, and assayed cell types differ from patients.

summary: Setd5 produced a sharply selective FDR-resolved response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells rather than a pan-neuronal chromatin-regulator signature.
why_it_matters: The data point to a thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic vulnerability for an NDD chromatin regulator, refining broad expectations from Setd5 developmental literature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The cell-type contrast is confounded by weak measured Setd5 mRNA knockdown and modest perturbed-cell counts in many classes.

summary: The strongest Setd5 signature upregulated a postsynaptic/synaptic-membrane module that included Lrrc7, Ntng1, Cacna1g, Grm1, Rgs8, Camk2a, Cacng5, and Dagla.
why_it_matters: A chromatin perturbation converged on neuronal signaling transcripts, offering a compact downstream readout of Setd5 disruption in the 151 TH class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Some genes are supported at FDR 0.1-0.25 rather than FDR<0.05, and the pathway label comes from enrichment of an 18-gene set.

summary: Slc6a1 was the only near-FDR Setd5 response in 052 Pvalb Gaba cells.
why_it_matters: The solitary increase of a GABA-transporter transcript suggests a possible interneuron-specific sentinel of Setd5 perturbation even when a broad Pvalb transcriptome response is absent.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Single-gene signal just above FDR 0.05; no direct Setd5-Slc6a1 mechanism is established here.

summary: In 151 TH cells, Ankrd11 was Setd5's top positive all-gene neighbor while Med15, Rora, and Cic were the top negative neighbors; the contrast was concentrated on Prkcd/Lrrc7/Plekhg1/Ntng1/Grm1 rather than being a strong global correlation.
why_it_matters: This separates a restricted synaptic/cell-state module from generic chromatin perturbation effects and prevents over-grouping Setd5 with all STRING- or SET-domain neighbors.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: All-gene correlations were weak in absolute value; the mechanistic status of Med15, Rora, and Cic as Setd5 antagonists is only signature-based.

summary: Measured Setd5 mRNA was not a robust on-target knockdown marker in any tested cell type, including the 151 TH class with the strongest downstream program.
why_it_matters: Downstream signatures should not be interpreted as proportional to measured Setd5 RNA depletion, and null cell-type results may reflect insufficient target engagement rather than true biological buffering.
main_caveats: The parquet contains differential mRNA statistics only; guide identity, cut site, baseline target abundance, and protein depletion were not measured in this file.

summary: The thalamic Setd5 program increased synaptic genes even though Setd5 haploinsufficiency studies report impaired synaptic wiring and reduced cultured-neuron synaptic density/activity.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a simple 'SETD5 loss always lowers synaptic gene expression' model and is compatible with cell-type, timing, or compensatory transcriptional directionality.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The literature assayed Setd5 haploinsufficiency during development or in cortical cultures, not the same thalamic single-cell perturbation context.

summary: Yeats2 perturbation produced no FDR-resolved target-transcript or downstream differential-expression hit in any of 21 profiled neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: The dataset is best interpreted as a broad but weakly engaged screen for Yeats2, rather than as a validated loss-of-function transcriptomic atlas.
cell_types: all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types
main_caveats: A coding perturbation can act without lowering mRNA, and the per-cell-type perturbed-cell counts were small.

summary: The largest nominal downstream response was decoupled from the only nominal Yeats2 mRNA decreases.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-interpreting 046 CTX-CGE GABA as a selectively Yeats2-sensitive class and makes the 145 MH-LH TH Glut and 155 MB Glut signals more relevant for any target-engagement follow-up.
cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: All downstream genes in these cell types failed adjusted p<0.05; the observation is about mismatch between scalar signals, not a validated cell-type mechanism.

summary: Yeats2 perturbation did not induce coordinated mRNA feedback among measured ATAC-complex subunits.
why_it_matters: YEATS2 is an ATAC chromatin reader, so absence of Kat2/Tada/Zzz3/Mbip/Wdr5/Sgf29/Dr1/Drap1 transcript feedback argues that the weak Perturb-seq response did not obviously engage the canonical complex at the mRNA level.
cell_types: all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types
main_caveats: Only transcript feedback was tested; complex occupancy and histone-acylation marks were not measured.

summary: Nominal Yeats2 responses were cell-type-private and did not form a reproducible pan-neuronal module.
why_it_matters: The weak p-value hits are unlikely to be interchangeable cell-type samplings of one common Yeats2 pathway.
cell_types: all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types
main_caveats: The recurrence analysis uses nominal p<0.01 rows because no row was FDR significant.

summary: Yeats2 was isolated from both unbiased signature neighbors and available related chromatin perturbations.
why_it_matters: The dataset does not support treating the Yeats2 signature as a surrogate for broader acetyl-lysine reader, SAGA, or MSL/KANSL perturbation programs.
cell_types: all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types
main_caveats: The canonical ATAC complex members were not available as perturbation comparators; all correlations are dominated by weak Yeats2 signatures.

summary: FAME4 genetics nominate YEATS2 in humans, but acute Yeats2 perturbation in this mouse-brain screen did not elicit a robust basal neuronal transcriptome.
why_it_matters: The disease association should be modeled with the repeat-expansion allele or better target engagement instead of assuming that simple weak Yeats2 knockdown will reproduce FAME4 biology.
cell_types: all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types
main_caveats: Human intronic repeat insertions are not the same perturbation as mouse Yeats2 guide targeting; no seizure physiology was measured.

summary: The FDR-negative mouse-brain signatures should not be used as neuronal safety evidence for YEATS2 inhibition.
why_it_matters: YEATS2 has an oncogenic ATAC/H3K27ac reader role in NSCLC, but the present dataset lacks the engagement and signature strength needed to infer benefit or safety of target inhibition in brain.
cell_types: all 21 Yeats2-profiled cell types
main_caveats: Cancer cells and adult mouse neuronal classes differ in species, state, proliferation, and perturbation modality.

summary: Tnrc6a perturbation showed weak on-target transcript engagement and no FDR 0.05 downstream differential-expression hits in any measured cell type.
why_it_matters: TNRC6A is a core GW182 miRISC scaffold, so absence of a robust signature prevents confident loss-of-function interpretation of this perturbation.
main_caveats: The target mRNA self-row may underestimate protein depletion; no protein or guide-level validation is available in the supplied table.

summary: Atp1a3 and Ptges2 up-regulation in 155 MB Glut formed the only sub-10% FDR Tnrc6a response.
why_it_matters: This restricted pair nominates candidate readouts for a future stronger Tnrc6a perturbation in midbrain glutamatergic neurons while keeping the signal separate from pathway-level claims.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only FDR<0.10, not FDR<0.05; the Tnrc6a self-row in 155 MB Glut was very weak.

summary: Tnrc6a did not converge with its paralog Tnrc6b or with Ago1, Ago2, Dicer1, and Cnot1 perturbations.
why_it_matters: These genes are expected to occupy the same miRNA-silencing network, so near-zero correlations argue that the Tnrc6a rows are not reporting a clean canonical miRISC phenotype.
main_caveats: Whole-transcriptome correlations can miss small sets of direct miRNA targets; weak Tnrc6a engagement is the leading alternative explanation.

summary: The top positive and negative whole-library signature neighbors of Tnrc6a were weak and not miRISC components.
why_it_matters: Nearest-neighbor analysis often reveals hidden pathway structure; here it instead reinforced that the Tnrc6a signature is low-amplitude and off-pathway.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and was not a direct interaction assay.

summary: The Perturb-seq result does not model the TNRC6A familial adult myoclonic epilepsy mechanism.
why_it_matters: The disease association reflects noncoding pentanucleotide-repeat expansion, whereas the local dataset assayed weak transcript perturbation and showed no robust downstream module; this warns against treating partial TNRC6A inhibition as disease-reversal evidence.
main_caveats: The assay did not introduce repeat expansions and was not an epilepsy physiology assay.

summary: Hippocampal CA/MEA glutamatergic classes were not preferentially sensitive to Tnrc6a perturbation.
why_it_matters: A published developmental hippocampal dendrite phenotype made these classes biologically plausible, but the dataset did not produce a matching robust transcriptional response.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The literature used timed rat postnatal/cultured hippocampal perturbations, whereas the dataset cell states and perturbation strength differ.

summary: Trappc6b knockdown was detectable across cell types but produced no FDR-significant cell-type transcriptome in this screen.
why_it_matters: TRAPPC6B is a conserved ER/Golgi TRAPP subunit and a recessive neurodevelopmental-disease gene; the Perturb-seq result therefore argues that partial acute mRNA depletion is either buffered in these neuronal populations or underpowered, rather than producing a large canonical loss-of-function transcriptional state.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|053 Sst Gaba|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The on-target transcript did not pass per-cell-type FDR and the experiment measures mRNA abundance rather than TRAPP protein, Golgi trafficking, or secretory flux.

summary: A weak cross-cell positive response converged on sterol/SREBP-associated genes rather than on canonical vesicle-tethering genes.
why_it_matters: Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Fdft1, and Srebf2 form the clearest recurrent pathway-like signal in the otherwise buffered Trappc6b signatures, making cholesterol homeostasis an exploratory readout for follow-up after TRAPP perturbation.
main_caveats: The pathway score is driven by nominal cross-cell recurrence; most member genes did not survive meta-analysis FDR and no single cell type showed a corrected sterol response.

summary: Jun and Stmn4 were recurrently upregulated single-gene readouts of Trappc6b perturbation.
why_it_matters: Because no individual cell type generated an FDR-significant program, these directionally recurrent genes are practical but exploratory qPCR or imaging-validation markers for a subtle Trappc6b state.
main_caveats: They are not specific to TRAPP biology and should be treated as empirical readouts, not mechanistic drivers.

summary: Trappc6b did not phenocopy the measured TRAPP II subunits Trappc9 or Trappc10 at the transcriptome level.
why_it_matters: Physical TRAPP-complex membership and patient-cell TRAPP II disruption would predict some shared biology, but the three TRAPP-targeting perturbations were all transcriptionally weak and their top ranked genes barely overlapped.
main_caveats: Trappc1, Trappc3, Trappc6a, Trappc11, and Trappc12 were not available as perturbations, and Trappc9/10 target knockdown was only nominal.

summary: The lack of Trappc6b FDR hits was selective relative to several other vesicle-trafficking perturbations in the same data matrix.
why_it_matters: Corrected signatures from Vps37a, Sec31a, Vps54, and Vps35 show that the assay can detect strong transcriptional consequences of trafficking-gene perturbation, so the Trappc6b result should be interpreted as TRAPP-specific buffering or weak engagement rather than a universal failure of vesicle-transport targets.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparator genes act in distinct trafficking complexes, so their FDR-positive signatures are assay controls rather than mechanistic phenocopies.

summary: Nup93 perturbation was FDR-null across the brain Perturb-seq atlas despite nominal on-target Nup93 mRNA decreases in several cell classes.
why_it_matters: Nup93 is an NPC assembly factor and acute NUP93 depletion can have strong cellular effects, so the mouse-brain CRISPRi result is best read as weak or buffered perturbation rather than evidence that Nup93 is biologically inert.
main_caveats: Target engagement was assessed only from the Nup93 transcript and never reached FDR significance; protein depletion and single-guide performance were not measured here.

direction: nominal target down without distal response
summary: The apparent Nup93 cell-type pattern was a target-engagement gradient, with 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut showing the clearest high-cell-count knockdown but no detected downstream program.
why_it_matters: This prevents overinterpreting either the 217 P MY Pineal Glut maximum logFC, which used only 20 perturbed cells, or the nominal thalamic/midbrain self rows as cell-type-selective biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: No protein readout was available, and the largest scalar Nup93 logFC came from the lowest perturbed-cell stratum.

summary: Nup93 did not phenocopy the other assayed nucleoporins Tpr and Ranbp2: Tpr and Ranbp2 yielded FDR-supported signatures, whereas Nup93 had zero FDR hits and near-zero whole-transcriptome correlations with both.
why_it_matters: The result separates the weak inner-scaffold Nup93 CRISPRi readout from stronger peripheral-nucleoporin perturbations and argues against a generic shared NPC-stress signature in this dataset.
main_caveats: Direct Nup93 inner-ring partners such as Nup155, Nup205, Nup188, Nup35, Ndc1, and Pom121 were not perturbed, so the contrast is to related nucleoporins rather than one-for-one complex subunits.

summary: The podocyte NUP93-SMAD disease axis was not transcriptionally engaged by Nup93 in mouse brain; BMP/TGF-SMAD genes stayed FDR-null, and Smad4 perturbation itself was also FDR-null and uncorrelated with Nup93.
why_it_matters: SRNS literature nominates BMP7-SMAD4 as a NUP93-dependent disease pathway, but this brain dataset provides no mRNA-level support for that mechanism under the assayed developmental conditions.
main_caveats: BMP/SMAD activity can be post-translational and podocyte-specific; absence of mRNA changes in brain cells does not falsify the kidney mechanism.

summary: Loss-of-NUP93 biology should be treated as a structural-NPC and renal-risk mechanism, not as a supported brain transcriptional intervention in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Directly reducing Nup93 has established NPC-assembly and nephrotic-syndrome relevance, while the Perturb-seq profile lacks a robust beneficial or mechanistically coherent brain response.
main_caveats: This is a directionality warning rather than a druggability assessment; no small-molecule NUP93 perturbation was measured.

summary: Smarcad1 perturbation failed to produce either FDR-significant target-transcript knockdown or any FDR-significant downstream gene in the 20 measured brain cell types.
why_it_matters: The dataset should be interpreted primarily as a weak-engagement null result, not as evidence that mature brain cells tolerate complete SMARCAD1 loss.
main_caveats: Target mRNA was not convincingly depleted; most groups had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: Known SMARCAD1 heterochromatin and double-strand-break repair biology did not appear as a assayed brain-cell transcriptional program after Smarcad1 targeting.
why_it_matters: SMARCAD1 acts in chromatin maintenance and DNA end resection in biochemical and proliferative contexts, so the absence of a corrected signature implies that this Perturb-seq assay did not engage the canonical stress or replication states needed to expose those functions.
main_caveats: A gene-set test was not significant because there were no corrected DE genes; pathway absence follows from global lack of FDR-significant expression changes.

summary: Smarcad1 was transcriptionally inert compared with several chromatin regulators assayed in the same cell-type panels.
why_it_matters: The null Smarcad1 profile is unlikely to reflect a universal inability of the assay to detect chromatin-regulator perturbations: Brd4, Smarcb1, Smarcc2, Chd4, Chd8, Arid2, Setdb1, and Arid1a generated corrected signatures, whereas Smarcad1 did not and correlated poorly with related perturbations.
main_caveats: Each comparator has its own guide efficiency and cell-count distribution; the contrast does not prove that SMARCAD1 protein was depleted.

summary: The Smarcad1 signature had no stable positive or negative perturbation neighbor.
why_it_matters: No recurrent neighbor rescued a pathway hypothesis from the weak single-gene results; even the largest correlations were cell-type-local and involved targets without an obvious SMARCAD1 mechanistic connection.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor correlations were computed from weak Smarcad1 score vectors and are therefore a diagnostic for instability rather than positive mechanism evidence.

summary: The brain Perturb-seq data do not support a neuronal SMARCAD1 disease-transcriptome biomarker despite established skin-isoform disease genetics and broad human SMARCAD1 expression.
why_it_matters: Human causal evidence is strongest for keratinocyte/skin phenotypes, and public small-molecule pharmacology is sparse; the mouse-brain null result argues against using this dataset to nominate a direct neuronal therapeutic direction for SMARCAD1.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain and does not test skin isoforms, keratinocytes, intestinal epithelium, DNA damage, replication stress, or pharmacologic inhibition.

summary: Vps54 produced an FDR-level transcriptional phenotype only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut despite being profiled in 21 neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: This localizes the robust acute response of this guide-defined Vps54 perturbation to one thalamic glutamatergic subtype rather than to all neurons exposed to the perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cell groups outside 151 generally had fewer perturbed cells, and target-transcript knockdown was not FDR-significant in any group.

summary: The responsive Vps54 state was dominated by lower neuronal structural, vesicle-release, and peptide-processing transcripts together with Jun induction.
why_it_matters: Mouse wobbler genetics connect Vps54 partial loss of function to motor-neuron degeneration; these data suggest that a neuronal process/cytoskeletal stress program can appear rapidly in a discrete non-motor glutamatergic population after Vps54 perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The profiled cells are thalamic glutamatergic neurons rather than spinal motor neurons; the assay measures RNA after perturbation, not axonal morphology or protein trafficking directly.

summary: The Vps54 response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut converged most strongly with Atp6v0c and other endolysosomal or trafficking perturbations, but with only modest scalar correlations.
why_it_matters: GARP perturbation is expected to influence lysosomal enzyme sorting through retrograde TGN traffic; the Atp6v0c convergence links the Vps54 signature to a proton-pump/lysosomal axis rather than to a generic transcriptional artifact.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The top correlation was r=0.361, so the convergence is partial; Atp6v0c had a far stronger direct-transcript knockdown and much larger DE burden than Vps54.

summary: Vps53, the assayed GARP-complex partner of Vps54, did not phenocopy Vps54 in the thalamic responsive cell type.
why_it_matters: Human-cell RNAi studies predicted that VPS52, VPS53, and VPS54 depletions can be functionally similar for mannose-6-phosphate receptor-dependent lysosomal sorting; the dataset instead separates Vps54 from Vps53 at the transcriptome level.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Vps53 guide set did not show significant Vps53 mRNA depletion, so failure to phenocopy may reflect insufficient Vps53 engagement rather than a true difference between GARP subunits.

summary: A well-engaged Vps35 perturbation was active in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but was nearly uncorrelated with Vps54.
why_it_matters: The Vps54 phenotype is therefore not simply the default output of perturbing any endosome-to-Golgi trafficking gene in the same cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a restricted signature comparison between two targets; it does not measure trafficking cargo or retromer/GARP protein complexes directly.

summary: Measured Vps54 mRNA depletion was weak and did not scale with downstream response strength.
why_it_matters: The main phenotype should be interpreted as guide-associated Vps54 biology with uncertain target engagement, and non-responsive cell types cannot be assumed biologically buffered without better knockdown measurements.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The target transcript may be sparse or incompletely assayed, and transcript abundance is only a proxy for protein loss or editing efficiency.

summary: Rb1cc1 perturbation produced a statistically resolved transcriptional phenotype in only three of twenty-one assayed cell classes, with significant target-transcript depletion in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA and a downstream but only nominally engaged response in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: FIP200 is a core autophagy-initiation factor, so a broad response might have been expected; the dataset instead localizes interpretable acute Rb1cc1 responses to thalamic and midbrain/hindbrain neuronal contexts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The strongest cell class, 155 MB Glut, had Rb1cc1 mRNA depletion only at nominal p<0.001 but FDR 0.341; absence of response in other classes often coincided with weak or non-FDR target engagement.

summary: The recurrent Rb1cc1 output was a downregulated proteostasis module centered on Calr, Hspa5, Pdia6, and Psap rather than induction of a broad autophagy-gene transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: It connects an autophagy-initiation scaffold to ER-lumen chaperone and lysosomal transcripts in specific neurons, but it argues that the single-cell readout is not measuring a canonical compensatory upregulation of autophagy genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The ER signature is compact, several ER-stress genes were only nominal, and there is no protein-level autophagy-flux or UPR assay.

summary: Atp1a3 was the most reproducible neuronal membrane response, falling in both midbrain Rb1cc1 signatures, whereas Nrxn1 marked the 191 MB P MY GABA response.
why_it_matters: ATPase and synaptic-adhesion transcripts may be sensitive readouts of neuronal Rb1cc1 loss in midbrain glutamatergic and hindbrain GABAergic cells, even when the total FDR signature is sparse.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: This is a transcript biomarker hypothesis from two cell classes; Nrxn1 was FDR-significant in only one class.

summary: Other autophagy genes sampled by this screen were not interchangeable with Rb1cc1: Map1lc3a perturbation was self-knockdown-dominated, Atg5 was weak, and Becn1 partially converged with Rb1cc1 only in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: Because FIP200, LC3, ATG5, and BECN1 all sit in macroautophagy, treating all autophagy loss-of-function signatures as equivalent would erase a clear stage- and cell-context distinction in the dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Atg5 itself was not FDR-depleted, so weak target engagement may explain part of its divergence; correlations used a restricted Rb1cc1 signature rather than an independent pathway assay.

summary: Tsc1 and Tsc2 perturbations, although much stronger globally, aligned with the Rb1cc1 restricted signatures in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: This recovers a TSC/mTOR/FIP200 axis in the same cell classes where Rb1cc1 changes ER and neuronal membrane transcripts, supporting a pathway-neighbor relationship rather than an isolated off-pathway signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The Tsc signatures were far larger than the Rb1cc1 signatures, and the correlation was calculated on the top 200 Rb1cc1-ranked genes; several top neighbors lack a direct FIP200 prior and remain exploratory.

summary: Most assayed Rb1cc1 perturbation contexts were silent at FDR<0.05, including inhibitory classes with nominal Rb1cc1 mRNA decreases but low cell count or q=1 target rows.
why_it_matters: Negative cell classes should be interpreted as weak-engagement or buffered contexts in this Perturb-seq assay, not as evidence that FIP200 is dispensable in those neuronal types.
main_caveats: No raw guide efficiencies or protein measurements were available, and several silent classes had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: The dataset and genetic literature together argue against viewing direct RB1CC1/FIP200 inhibition as a benign autophagy-tuning strategy in brain: acute Rb1cc1 loss lowered ER-chaperone, ATPase, and synaptic transcripts in selected neurons, while mouse FIP200 or Atg5 loss impairs neural maintenance.
why_it_matters: The warning is directional for target selection: even partial neuronal RB1CC1 suppression produced cell-type-restricted stress on proteostasis and excitability markers in a pathway already known to protect neural cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Transcriptomic perturbations do not establish long-term degeneration or flux defects, and there is no direct pharmacologic RB1CC1 inhibitor experiment in this dataset.

summary: Supt16 perturbation most strongly affected 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where a predominantly down-regulated synaptic and ion-homeostasis program emerged.
why_it_matters: FACT is a chromatin-elongation and nucleosome chaperone complex; the largest downstream output in this brain Perturb-seq slice was not a generic RNA polymerase or cell-cycle module but loss of mature neuronal membrane and neurotransmission transcripts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The target Supt16 transcript itself was not significantly reduced in this cell type, so the biological response is strong but target engagement is not directly validated at mRNA or protein level.

summary: Snhg11 is a recurrent rank-1 negative transcript across the active Supt16 signatures.
why_it_matters: A single transcript ranking first in three FDR-active cell classes provides a compact candidate readout of Supt16-sensitive neuronal state, even where each individual class contains only tens of perturbed cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: This is a biomarker hypothesis from recurrence and rank only; Snhg11 was not FDR-significant in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and its mechanistic relationship to FACT was not established here.

summary: The significant response is extracortical and sparse: only four of 21 cell types had any FDR<0.05 genes.
why_it_matters: The Supt16 phenotype should not be treated as pan-neuronal in this dataset; after the dominant 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature, the remaining FDR signals were small sets in 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA.
main_caveats: Cell counts were modest, and the absence of FDR hits elsewhere may reflect weak guide activity rather than true biological resistance.

summary: Proteasome perturbations, not annotated FACT partners, are the strongest positive Supt16 signature neighbors across the active cell classes.
why_it_matters: Psmc1, Psmc5, Psmb4, and Pomp repeatedly ranked at or near the top of the genome-scale perturbation-similarity list, suggesting that Supt16 loss and impairment of proteasome assembly or 26S subunits converge on a shared neuronal stress state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The correlations are modest and purely transcriptomic; Ssrp1, Polr2a, and core PAF1 elongation components were not perturbations in this library, so direct complex-member comparisons were unavailable.

summary: No strong opposite perturbation was detectable for Supt16 within the screened target set.
why_it_matters: The lack of robust anti-correlated neighbors means the dataset points to a convergent essential-gene/proteasome-like state rather than a simple antagonistic target whose perturbation reverses the Supt16 signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Only targets present in the Perturb-seq library could be evaluated, and the analysis used whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon-score correlations rather than perturbation rescue experiments.

summary: The neuronal loss-of-function signature suggests that brain-penetrant FACT inhibition should be evaluated for synaptic-transcript liabilities.
why_it_matters: SUPT16H is linked to human neurodevelopmental disease, and the FACT inhibitor CBL0137 is being explored for cancers including CNS tumors; the mouse Perturb-seq response raises a directional warning that FACT suppression can depress neuronal membrane and neurotransmission genes outside tumor cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The clinical compound traps chromatin FACT rather than genetically lowering Supt16; the dataset is mouse and single-cell transcriptomic, not a toxicity or behavioral assay.

summary: Ppargc1a produced no FDR-significant differentially expressed genes in any of its 21 assayed brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: This establishes that downstream interpretation must start from a negative or weak-engagement perturbation rather than from a canonical PGC-1alpha loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: Ppargc1a mRNA was not measurably reduced, so the negative result may reflect weak editing, mRNA readout limitations, or insufficient protein loss rather than true buffering.

summary: Ppargc1a perturbation in 052 Pvalb Gaba failed to reproduce the published PGC-1alpha/PV-interneuron transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: PV interneurons are one of the clearest mouse-brain contexts in which PGC-1alpha loss has an expected direction; the dataset instead shows no Pvalb or PV-program FDR response in the corresponding class.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The Ppargc1a transcript was not knocked down in Pvalb cells; the result does not invalidate genetic PGC-1alpha loss studies.

summary: Esrra and Nrf1 perturbations revealed robust pathway-neighbor signatures that were absent from Ppargc1a, Ppargc1b, and PPAR/RXR perturbations.
why_it_matters: The mitochondrial-biogenesis transcriptional neighborhood was reachable in the assay, but the measured Ppargc1a perturbation did not access it, separating upstream coactivator targeting from downstream DNA-binding factor perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The Nrf1 and Esrra signatures were not identical to Ppargc1a and Nrf1 also lacked transcript-level knockdown, so this is a pathway-neighborhood contrast, not a proof of a single linear cascade.

summary: Ppargc1a and Ppargc1b signatures were nearly uncorrelated, and the single Ppargc1b Atp5b hit was not reproduced by Ppargc1a.
why_it_matters: PGC-1 coactivator paralogs should be considered separately in this dataset; the Ppargc1b result does not rescue or proxy for the failed Ppargc1a perturbation.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Both coactivator perturbations showed weak measured on-target mRNA effects, so divergence could reflect perturbation quality rather than true paralog-specific biology.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut contained a weak, nominal Ppargc1a trend overlapping the stronger Esrra response.
why_it_matters: Bcan plus nominal decreases in Atp5b, Idh3a, Atp1b1, Got1, and Mdh1 are the only dataset-grounded clues to a Ppargc1a-responsive neuronal state and nominate thalamic follow-up biomarkers.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: No Ppargc1a row in this class survived FDR; the Ppargc1a-Esrra relationship is based on a restricted significant-gene subset and small all-gene correlation.

summary: The Perturb-seq negative should not be used as a PPARGC1A pharmacology go/no-go result.
why_it_matters: Human resources currently provide no approved or clinical PPARGC1A-directed modality and no ChEMBL mechanism or IC50 support for CHEMBL6116, while the dataset itself lacks target-transcript engagement; downstream pathway biomarkers are a safer translational readout than Ppargc1a DE absence.
main_caveats: Disease and tractability annotations are human-centric, and the dataset is a mouse CRISPR transcriptomic assay without protein or edit-rate measurements.

summary: Sil1 perturbation was globally buffered or technically under-engaged: the target transcript itself was not significantly depleted and only one differential-expression row passed FDR<0.05 across 22 cell types.
why_it_matters: Complete SIL1 loss causes an ER-chaperone disease, so the near-null acute transcriptional phenotype argues that this dataset should be interpreted as weak partial perturbation or strong buffering rather than as a matched Sil1-loss disease model.
main_caveats: The negative result is strong for measured RNA but weak for loss-of-function biology because Sil1 RNA knockdown was not significant in any tested cell type.

summary: Sil1 guide cells did not activate a canonical HSPA5/BiP unfolded-protein-response transcript module, including Hspa5, Hyou1, Xbp1, Atf4, Ddit3, Atf6, Ern1, Eif2ak3, and Manf.
why_it_matters: Sil1 is a HSPA5 nucleotide-exchange factor in the ER lumen; absence of the expected BiP/UPR readout shows that the scRNA response is uncoupled from the stress program implicated by complete Sil1 deficiency.
main_caveats: scRNA readout cannot detect BiP ATPase cycling, Xbp1 splicing, or ER stress at the protein level; the RNA perturbation was weak.

summary: The only FDR-significant Sil1 DE call was a small Rsrp1 increase in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: This makes L5 ET CTX Glut the sole nominally selective cell type, but the hit is isolated and does not establish a coherent ER-stress pathway.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: One small-effect gene survived FDR; adjacent genes in the same cell type had FDR>=0.259, and the target transcript was not depleted.

summary: Sil1 signatures were essentially orthogonal to available ER-chaperone and stress-pathway-neighbor perturbations.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues against a shared acute transcriptomic state among partial Sil1 perturbation and stronger ER-chaperone perturbations rather than revealing a hidden BiP/UPR module.
main_caveats: Some comparators, especially Hspa5 and Atf6, also showed weak or inconsistent on-target RNA depletion; correlations are transcriptomic and do not assess chaperone activity.

summary: The Hyou1 compensation axis that can rescue Sil1-null Purkinje degeneration was not transcriptionally induced by Sil1 perturbation in this dataset.
why_it_matters: HYOU1 is a genetic modifier of Sil1 loss in vivo; its silence here narrows the perturbation to an acute, buffered state rather than a disease-like compensatory UPR state.
main_caveats: The dataset measures Hyou1 mRNA only, Hyou1 was not itself perturbed, and the assayed cell classes are coarse relative to Purkinje cells.

summary: The data do not justify treating SIL1 reduction as a safe or productive inhibitory direction: measured knockdown was weak, the disease genetics are loss-of-function, and no direct ChEMBL target entry was found for SIL1.
why_it_matters: For SIL1-associated disease, therapeutic logic is more consistent with restoring ER chaperone capacity, such as via HYOU1/GRP170, than with additional SIL1 inhibition.
main_caveats: This is a directionality warning, not a preclinical efficacy claim; the Perturb-seq dataset did not achieve a strong Sil1 loss-of-function state.

summary: Ubp1 perturbation generated one multiple-testing-significant dataset signal: depletion of its own transcript in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: A nuclear DNA-binding transcription factor might be expected to create target-gene cascades, but the measured mature-neuron response was buffered to the point that no downstream gene survived FDR correction.
main_caveats: DE results are transcript-level Wilcoxon outputs; absence of downstream FDR hits could reflect guide inefficiency, low UBP1 protein depletion, redundancy, or low activity in adult neurons.

summary: Detectable Ubp1 self-knockdown was restricted to a subset of neuronal classes and was far strongest in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: The target transcript was measured in all 23 cell types, so this pattern argues against treating Ubp1 as uniformly engaged across the brain screen.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|215 MB Dopa
main_caveats: Most engaged cell types were only nominal after multiple testing; 215 MB Dopa had only 20 perturbed cells.

summary: The only engaged cell type showed Ubp1 self-depletion without a coherent non-self transcriptional module.
why_it_matters: This uncouples an on-target transcription-factor perturbation from a detectable RNA-polymerase-II target-gene program in these mature neurons.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The nominal non-self genes are not validated UBP1 targets here and all had FDR=1.0.

summary: Assayed CP2/Grainyhead-family perturbations did not phenocopy Ubp1.
why_it_matters: Prior work and interaction databases group UBP1 with Tfcp2-family factors, but the available Tfcp2 and Grhl2 perturbations were themselves weak and had near-zero correlations with Ubp1, preventing any claim of functional interchangeability in this screen.
main_caveats: The contrast is limited because Tfcp2 and Grhl2 did not show robust self-knockdown or FDR-positive downstream signatures.

summary: No other 155 MB Glut perturbation was a strong positive or negative Ubp1 signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: A pathway or protein-complex neighbor might have revealed the hidden buffered program, but the top correlations were below 0.10 in absolute value.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed only within 155 MB Glut and on transcriptomic score vectors, not on protein or chromatin phenotypes.

summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq result does not nominate a therapeutic direction for UBP1 inhibition or activation.
why_it_matters: UBP1 has medically framed literature in the TFCP2 family and blood-pressure genetics, yet public target databases show no mature ligand track; the brain dataset adds only self-knockdown without a disease-rescuing downstream program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Database tractability is incomplete, and this screen tested loss of transcript in mouse brain cells rather than steroidogenic, vascular, cancer, or Alzheimer model systems.

summary: Slc25a4 perturbation produced robust target-mRNA depletion in several neuronal classes but did not produce a matched multi-gene transcriptomic state.
why_it_matters: ANT1 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane ADP/ATP carrier with proton-leak and mitophagy roles; the dataset therefore argues that loss of the Slc25a4 transcript is either buffered in these cells or expressed primarily as physiology that a single-cell mRNA DE assay does not capture.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measures RNA and not ATP/ADP exchange, membrane potential, mtDNA copy number, or mitophagy flux; protein depletion was not measured.

direction: strongest in 052/054/066/151/155/191; weak in 059/215/007/017/022 and other groups
summary: Measured Slc25a4 engagement was strongly cell-type dependent despite being negative in every group.
why_it_matters: The strong-buffering conclusion is most reliable in the six FDR-supported groups; weak or underpowered groups such as 215 MB Dopa, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and several cortical/hippocampal glutamatergic classes cannot be used as confident biological negatives.
main_caveats: The DE table does not separate baseline Slc25a4 expression, guide cutting, and sampling depth, so the selectivity could be technical or expression dependent.

direction: Slc25a4 target-only contrasted with broad Opa1/Dnm1l programs
summary: The same neuronal classes were capable of broad mitochondrial-stress transcriptional responses to Opa1 or Dnm1l, whereas Slc25a4 remained target-only.
why_it_matters: This contrast makes the quiet Slc25a4 profile less likely to be a universal inability of the assayed cell classes to respond to mitochondrial perturbation.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Opa1 and Dnm1l regulate mitochondrial fusion/fission rather than ADP/ATP exchange, so they are positive mitochondrial comparators, not complex members of ANT1.

summary: Slc25a4 knockdown did not transcriptionally induce the ANT paralog Slc25a5 or other measured SLC25 carriers.
why_it_matters: If ubiquitous Ant2/Slc25a5 or related carriers buffer Slc25a4 loss in neurons, the buffering is not visible as paralog mRNA up-regulation in this assay.
main_caveats: Only transcript-level carrier compensation was tested; transporter activity, ANT protein isoforms, and carriers absent from the measured gene set or perturbation library could still contribute.

direction: loss-of-transcript quiet in brain versus pathogenic dominant or recessive disease alleles in oxidative tissues
summary: The brain Perturb-seq phenotype is a partial loss-of-transcript model and should not be equated with dominant SLC25A4 mitochondrial disease mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Human dominant ANT1 missense alleles alter carrier function and mtDNA maintenance in muscle; a target-only brain RNA response therefore refines the disease interpretation toward tissue and allele specificity rather than contradicting SLC25A4 pathogenicity.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The disease tissues in the cited studies are predominantly skeletal muscle and heart, not the mouse neuronal classes in this dataset.

direction: brain buffering contrasted with heart/muscle liability
summary: The absence of a neuronal transcriptional injury signature does not make ANT1 pharmacologic inhibition an obviously safe neuroprotective strategy.
why_it_matters: Mouse Ant1 deficiency can be tolerated or protective in brain excitotoxicity models, but germline Ant1 loss causes myopathy/cardiomyopathy in mice and SLC25A4 human genetic evidence is enriched for mitochondrial cardiomyopathy and ophthalmoplegia; any therapeutic attempt to lower ANT1 activity would need tissue-selective exposure and non-transcriptomic mitochondrial safety assays.
main_caveats: This is a genetics-based warning; the dataset contains no drug treatment, no organismal heart or muscle readout, and no direct ADP/ATP transport measurements.

summary: Shoc2 perturbation yielded a very sparse steady-state RNA phenotype across 21 profiled neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: This keeps the strongest dataset result from being overgeneralized: most cell types showed no FDR-confirmed Shoc2 response, and the direct Shoc2 transcript was not FDR-depleted even where a downstream Vgf hit appeared.
main_caveats: Sparse RNA output cannot separate true signaling buffering from CRISPR edits that do not reduce Shoc2 mRNA; no protein-level engagement was measured.

summary: Vgf is the only FDR-significant Shoc2 downstream gene and is downregulated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Vgf converts a broad weak perturbation into a specific neuronal output candidate for SHOC2/MAPK signaling, because prior neuronal work placed VGF downstream of BDNF- and MAPK-dependent transcription.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Vgf passed FDR; the surrounding module is nominal and the literature is hippocampal BDNF stimulation, not mouse thalamic CRISPR.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Shoc2 follows the expected positive RAF/MEK direction: it resembles Braf and Map2k1 loss and opposes Nf1 loss.
why_it_matters: The Braf/Map2k1/Nf1 polarity argues that the Shoc2 Vgf phenotype is on the Ras-RAF-MAPK axis rather than a single isolated off-pathway RNA change.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Full-vector correlations are small in absolute value and the strongest convergence is restricted to one cell class.

summary: The thalamic Shoc2 RNA output is Braf/Map2k1-weighted and is not reproduced by Raf1 or Map2k2.
why_it_matters: SHOC2 is capable of controlling RAF-family phosphoserines, but these data show that individual RAF and MEK paralogs are not interchangeable at the level of steady-state neuronal RNA output.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is based on one cell type and on RNA signatures rather than direct RAF isoform activity measurements.

summary: Shoc2 loss downregulates a MAPK-inducible neuropeptide in one neuronal class, nominating Vgf as an exploratory CNS marker to monitor during SHOC2 blockade.
why_it_matters: Therapeutic SHOC2 inhibition is being explored to potentiate MEK inhibition in RAS-driven cancers, whereas pathogenic SHOC2 RASopathy alleles alter localization and signaling; the Perturb-seq loss-of-function signature highlights a neuronal on-target output rather than modeling the human gain-of-function syndrome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a mouse neuronal RNA hypothesis; it does not establish secreted VGF peptide loss, behavioral toxicity, or whether pharmacologic complex inhibitors will match CRISPR Shoc2 perturbation.

direction: target transcript not significantly reduced; downstream response sparse
summary: Usf1 perturbation was globally weak or transcriptionally buffered across the neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: USF1 is a nuclear E-box transcription factor, so the near absence of FDR-level response warns that most Usf1 guide-cell contrasts should not be interpreted as a clean loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: Target mRNA is only a proxy for perturbation efficiency; CRISPR effects that alter USF1 protein or chromatin occupancy without lowering Usf1 RNA would be missed by this readout.

summary: The only FDR-significant downstream Usf1 response was repression of Gaa in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, accompanied by nominal repression of Tpp1 and Ctsa.
why_it_matters: Gaa, Tpp1, and Ctsa encode lysosomal hydrolases; the result nominates a thalamic glutamatergic lysosomal module rather than a broad pan-neuronal Usf1 program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only Gaa passes FDR<0.05; Tpp1, Ctsa, and Ogdhl are nominal and should be treated as module-level context, not validated targets.

summary: The Usf1 thalamic lysosomal-hydrolase decrease runs counter to a simple model in which loss of a USF-family repressor derepresses TFEB-like lysosomal genes.
why_it_matters: USF2 has been reported to compete with TFEB and repress lysosomal/autophagy genes; the mouse-brain Usf1 data instead show decreased Gaa and nominally decreased Tpp1/Ctsa, arguing that USF1 and USF2 cannot be assumed interchangeable for neuronal lysosomal regulation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset perturbed Usf1, not Usf2 or Tfeb; the direct Usf2 comparator was absent, and the literature uses non-neuronal or engineered systems.

summary: Usf1 did not behave like a neuronal cholesterol-biosynthesis regulator despite USF1 lipid-metabolic genetics.
why_it_matters: In the same thalamic class, Srebf2 knockdown strongly repressed Dhcr24, Insig1, Hmgcs1, Msmo1, Cyp51, and Sqle, whereas Usf1 left this program neutral and was uncorrelated with Srebf2/Srebf1 signatures. This refines USF1 lipid-disease biology toward non-neuronal or context-specific mechanisms.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is restricted to one neuronal class and transcriptomic signatures; Usf1 target engagement was weak.

direction: Nfix transcript down in a subset; absent in most cell types
summary: Nfix self-transcript knockdown was measurable but concentrated in forebrain neuronal strata, with the strongest effect in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut.
why_it_matters: The only reproducible molecular sign that the perturbation engaged its target was reduction of Nfix itself, and that signal appeared in cortical or hippocampal/forebrain-associated classes rather than across all sampled neurons.

summary: Nominal Krit1 hits did not recur across cell types and top whole-signature neighbors were very weak.

summary: The dataset should not be used as neuronal support for a KRIT1-dependent CCM pharmacodynamic biomarker or therapeutic direction.

summary: Scamp5 knockdown was transcriptionally buffered across most neuronal classes despite measurable loss of the target transcript.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut was the selectively responsive Scamp5 class, adding Fyttd1 up-regulation and Gabra1 down-regulation to the target knockdown.

main_caveats: Only two downstream genes reached FDR<0.05 in this class; Fyttd1 is retained as a marker rather than mechanistically interpreted.

cell_types: all 23 measured cell types
main_caveats: Single-cell neuronal DE cannot test embryonic neural crest, dermal fibroblast, osteogenic, or epithelial cancer settings where TWIST2 biology has been defined.

summary: For STMN2-restoration therapeutic discovery, the dataset argues for humanized STMN2-splicing and axonal assays rather than native mouse soma transcriptomics as primary pharmacodynamic readouts.
why_it_matters: ASO strategies aim to restore functional STMN2 when TDP-43 is lost, but the native mouse Tardbp perturbation did not lower Stmn2 and direct Stmn2 loss was transcriptionally sparse.
main_caveats: This is an inference from perturbation transcriptomics plus published mechanism; the experiment did not test ASOs, humanized alleles, motor neurons, or axon regeneration.

summary: Assigned Washc4 perturbation was weakly engaged at the RNA level and produced no FDR-level transcriptomic response in any of 19 cell types.
why_it_matters: The null prevents a loss-of-function interpretation of WASHC4 biology and should be treated as an underpowered or under-engaged perturbation result.
main_caveats: Target mRNA is an imperfect guide-activity measure for some CRISPR modalities; perturbed-cell counts were low and no protein readout was available.

summary: Vesicle-trafficking comparators generated FDR responses, especially in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while Washc4 remained silent in the same cell class.

summary: A global signature-neighbor search found no robust positive or negative Washc4 module; all top score-vector correlations were weak.

summary: Washc4 did not yield a usable transcriptomic pharmacodynamic marker, and external evidence favors caution for WASHC4 perturbation as a therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: WASHC4 loss is linked to neuronal endolysosomal disease biology, while database evidence contains only preliminary binding data and no curated mechanism of action, so a weak null signature should not be used for target prosecution.
main_caveats: This is a direction-of-evidence warning, not a direct safety experiment or drug-response assay.

summary: Rara guide cells produced an extremely sparse DE phenotype and no measurable FDR-level knockdown of Rara mRNA.

main_caveats: Only transcript-level sentinel genes were tested; many RARA outputs are ligand-, enhancer-, and state-dependent.

why_it_matters: The closest receptor-family perturbations gave zero FDR-level genes and near-zero whole-signature correlations, so RARA-family biochemical relatedness did not translate into a shared Perturb-seq state under basal mouse-brain conditions.

summary: The lack of FDR-level cortical and hippocampal mRNA responses does not rule out RARα biology mediated by local dendritic translation or electrophysiological plasticity.

summary: RARA is pharmacologically tractable, but this dataset provides little direction for agonist or antagonist therapy in brain cell types.

summary: Zfp292 perturbation was not an interpretable RNA-loss experiment in the tested cells: the measured target transcript was not significantly reduced and no downstream gene reached FDR<0.20.

summary: The null was not confined to the lowest-cell-count strata; the three largest Zfp292 strata also had no target knockdown and no corrected hits.
why_it_matters: Low n_pert_matched values explain part of the weak screen, but 148, 114, and 98 perturbed cells were still insufficient to reveal any high-confidence Zfp292 response.

main_caveats: These cell types still may not be developmentally or molecularly competent for Zfp292 biology, and target engagement remained weak.

summary: The nominal Zfp292 outliers did not form a reproducible module or a strong positive/negative signature neighborhood.
why_it_matters: This argues against interpreting genes such as Glis2, Kctd6, or the highest correlation neighbors as a biological pathway; they are singleton or very weak observations.
main_caveats: Restricted to nominal p-value recurrence and Pearson comparisons in three inspected cell types; no corrected Zfp292 hits were available for pathway enrichment.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, STRING-listed Zfp292 network neighbors Ctcf, Arid2, and Kdm6a produced corrected signatures while Zfp292 produced none.

main_caveats: STRING edges are functional predictions, not proof of a single obligatory Zfp292 complex; downstream gene overlap was not required for this contrast.

summary: The top STRING partner Zfp644 and the predicted partner Tcf20 also lacked strong signatures and did not converge with Zfp292.

main_caveats: Zfp644 and Tcf20 target transcripts were not significantly reduced; the comparison is therefore an absence of detectable convergence, not a mechanistic disproof.

summary: The mouse-brain Perturb-seq null does not contradict ZNF292 neurodevelopmental-disease literature; it mostly shows that this perturbation did not reproduce a ZNF292 haploinsufficiency-like developmental transcriptional state.
why_it_matters: Human studies implicate ZNF292 loss in intellectual-disability/autism phenotypes and in cortical inhibitory-neuron development, so a weakly engaged Perturb-seq null should not be read as evidence that ZNF292 loss is benign or buffered in disease-relevant progenitors.
main_caveats: Species, developmental stage, perturbation efficacy, and the assayed neuronal states differ from the human stem-cell cortical interneuron loss-of-function models.

direction: no robust knockdown; no FDR-significant response

summary: The weak Zfp451 response showed an exploratory nominal skew toward 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, not a robust cell-type-specific program.

main_caveats: All constituent effects are nominal; no Zfp451 cell class contained an FDR<0.05 gene.

direction: no robust pathway activation or repression
summary: Known SUMO2/3-PML, SMAD, and SATB2 axes of ZNF451 were not recovered as a transcriptional module after Zfp451 perturbation.

summary: RANBP2, not Zfp451 or Nsmce2, produced the clearest SUMO-associated E3-ligase phenotype in this atlas.

main_caveats: The divergence could reflect poor Zfp451 knockdown rather than true dispensability or substrate specificity.

summary: Signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a hidden Zfp451 convergence or anti-convergence module.
why_it_matters: The largest positive and negative score correlations were small and a safe-target control appeared among the top positive neighbors, so there is no strong related-target or unrelated-target signature suggesting a missed biology axis.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed from very weak Zfp451 score vectors and should be read only as a restricted negative screen.

direction: no therapeutic direction from this dataset
summary: This Perturb-seq profile should not be used to prioritize or deprioritize Zfp451 inhibition in brain cells.
why_it_matters: The absence of a robust RNA signature is dominated by failed target engagement, while curated biology points to nuclear SUMO and chromatin functions that may require protein-level or stimulus-coupled assays; ChEMBL also lacks an annotated direct ZNF451 target record.
main_caveats: Absence from a ChEMBL search is not proof of intrinsic undruggability, and this dataset does not measure Zfp451 protein or enzymatic inhibition.

summary: Pik3r2 loss-direction perturbation was broadly transcriptionally buffered across the assayed mouse-brain classes.

main_caveats: The target mRNA itself never passed FDR correction, so biological buffering and weak perturbation strength cannot be separated.

summary: Hacd1 was the only recurrent nominal Pik3r2-up gene in three glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: This preserves a possible weak marker of Pik3r2 response without treating it as a pathway call; its recurrence may guide follow-up only if stronger target knockdown or protein-level PI3K readouts reproduce it.

main_caveats: All three Hacd1 rows were nominal only; the best Hacd1 FDR was 0.5949 and no Pik3r2 result passed FDR.

summary: The PI3K-AKT-mTOR disease network was responsive downstream at Pten/Tsc/Ntrk2 but muted at the proximal class-IA p85/p110 and receptor-entry nodes.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the dataset can detect perturbations in this disease family, but Pik3r2, Pik3r1, Pik3ca, and Pik3cb are not interchangeable with PTEN or TSC perturbation at the transcriptional level.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Cross-perturbation comparisons use RNA signatures, and some proximal perturbations also had weak self-transcript knockdown.

summary: Pik3r2 did not enter a strong positive or negative whole-transcriptome signature neighborhood.
why_it_matters: The scattered nominal genes should not be over-read as a coherent module; the strongest same-cell non-self correlation with any biological perturbation was only r=0.1815.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations over all measured genes are conservative for very sparse signatures and can miss small shared leading-edge effects.

summary: The dataset is loss-direction and therefore should not be interpreted as a failed model of gain-of-function PIK3R2 overgrowth disease.
why_it_matters: Human PIK3R2 neurodevelopmental disease is driven by activating alleles that enhance PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling, whereas these guides modestly reduced Pik3r2 RNA and produced no robust downstream signature; a null result therefore neither contradicts the gain-of-function disease mechanism nor validates p85β or PI3K inhibition as innocuous in developing brain.
main_caveats: The screen did not overactivate PIK3R2, did not assay embryonic growth phenotypes, and measured RNA rather than PI3K lipid products or AKT/mTOR phosphorylation.

direction: target transcript down; downstream genes not FDR-significant
summary: The best-engaged Yme1l1 contrast was transcriptionally buffered: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut showed Yme1l1 as the strongest nominally depleted gene but no FDR-supported secondary response.

cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Only 29 perturbed cells were in this contrast, Yme1l1 itself did not pass FDR, and protein loss was not measured.

summary: Yme1l1 transcript engagement was heterogeneous across the 19 measured cell-type contrasts and never reached FDR significance.
why_it_matters: The global absence of FDR hits should be read together with uneven target knockdown: thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic classes had clear nominal depletion, whereas some cortical and cerebellar classes had almost no target-transcript shift.
main_caveats: The dataset is differential-expression output only; guide-level and protein-level engagement cannot be checked from this file.

summary: Mitochondrial protease neighbors and the Opa1 axis were not positive Yme1l1 signature neighbors in the best-engaged cell type.

main_caveats: Correlation is restricted to one cell type and to RNA signatures; Yme1l1 itself had a weak downstream signature, making similarity estimates conservative but also noisy.

summary: Yme1l1 lacked a robust positive or negative signature-neighbor module among all other perturbations in its three most engaged contexts.
why_it_matters: The largest absolute correlations with any other perturbation were below 0.075, so the null Yme1l1 result is not hiding a clear alternate pathway match detectable by transcriptome-wide score correlation.
