main_caveats: This is a restricted signature-neighbor analysis in three cell types and uses scalar score correlation, not pathway-aware or guide-level modeling.

direction: disease severe in prior loss-of-function settings; acute RNA response absent here
summary: The Perturb-seq null refines YME1L1 neurological disease models toward chronic, developmental, and protein-level vulnerability rather than an acute broad mature-neuron RNA program.
why_it_matters: Human YME1L1 mutation, nervous-system Yme1l loss, and adult neural stem-cell Yme1l deletion are deleterious in the literature, but the measured mature brain classes showed at most nominal Yme1l1 mRNA depletion without FDR-supported mitochondrial stress outputs.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay optic-nerve, spinal-axon, neural-stem-cell phenotypes, mitochondrial morphology, or protein turnover.

direction: no RNA alarm despite known loss-of-function liability
summary: The transcriptional silence of Yme1l1-targeted neurons is a poor safety readout for YME1L1 inhibition.
why_it_matters: Because YME1L1 loss is linked to mitochondriopathy and selective nervous-system degeneration, absence of FDR DE after partial targeting should not be taken as evidence that reducing this protease is tolerated in post-mitotic neurons.
main_caveats: No drug perturbation was tested, human disease involves different alleles and timescales, and the Perturb-seq assay lacked morphology and survival endpoints.

summary: Tubb4a transcript depletion was strongly cell-type-selective across neuronal classes.

summary: The knockdown signatures did not show FDR-significant transcriptional replacement by other alpha- or beta-tubulin isotypes.

summary: Target-only buffering was shared by related tubulin-isotype and microtubule-associated perturbations.
why_it_matters: The Tubb4a phenotype is therefore not an isolated failure of its guides; multiple single tubulin or MAP knockdowns converged on self-transcript depletion with little common downstream DE.
main_caveats: This is an aggregate FDR-count comparison, not a full correlation or morphology analysis; the alpha-tubulin Tuba1a perturbation had somewhat more non-self hits in two cell types.

direction: knockdown buffered rather than broad mutant-toxicity response
summary: The neuronal knockdown response does not resemble a dominant TUBB4A disease allele response.
why_it_matters: Human H-ABC and DYT4 are driven by dominant missense alleles that alter tubulin biology, so simple partial depletion in the assayed neurons should not be interpreted as a full model of H-ABC leukodystrophy or DYT4 dystonia.
main_caveats: The dataset lacks the disease-causing missense variants and does not measure oligodendrocytes or microtubule dynamics.

direction: no effective target depletion in 308 CB GABA
summary: The dataset cannot rule out a cerebellar Tubb4a requirement.
why_it_matters: TUBB4A disease models and H-ABC pathology implicate cerebellar and myelinating compartments, but the only cerebellar-labelled class here, 308 CB GABA, had no detectable target knockdown.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: A negative result in CB GABA is uninterpretable for target biology; the assayed groups were neuronal Glut/GABA labels rather than oligodendrocyte lineage cells.

direction: Por down only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
summary: Por is an exploratory, cell-type-restricted marker of the strongest non-target response.
why_it_matters: Por should be retained as the sole FDR-significant downstream measurement, but its singleton behavior argues against elevating it into a recurrent Tubb4a pathway.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only one cell class reached FDR<0.05 for Por, and the dataset does not provide mechanistic evidence connecting Por to tubulin biology.

direction: 151 selective response; no FDR-significant genes in 21 other Rora tests
summary: Rora perturbation produced a strong FDR-significant program only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, while 21 other assayed cell classes were transcriptionally quiet at FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: RORA is broadly expressed in neurons, but the dataset points to a sharply restricted thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic dependency that extends prior RORalpha thalamic-development biology into a perturbational thalamic single-cell context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Direct Rora mRNA reduction was nominal rather than FDR-significant, and some silent classes had small n_pert counts.

direction: mixed; many subtype and ion-channel genes down with Agrn/Timp3/Uchl1/Kcnk9/Rims2 up
summary: The 151 response couples loss of Prkcd/Grin2c-subtype and postsynaptic ion-channel transcripts with a smaller upregulated remodeling module.
why_it_matters: The direction of genes such as Prkcg, Grin2c, Kcnc2, Gabra4, Gabrd, Gria2, Sema7a, Agrn, and Timp3 suggests that thalamic RORA controls synaptic and excitability programs, refining neurodevelopmental RORA phenotypes beyond generic nuclear-receptor or cerebellar effects.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The perturbation reports mRNA changes, not electrophysiology or axon morphology.

summary: Rora loss engaged only a narrow slice of the curated circadian circuit in 151 cells: Nr1d1 and Cry2 fell, but Arntl/Bmal1, Dbp, Clock, Nr1d2, Tef, Cry1, Per2, and Per3 did not pass FDR.
why_it_matters: Canonical RORA biology predicts RORE-mediated clock regulation, including BMAL1 activation; the thalamic Perturb-seq result shows that the clock edge most visible after Rora perturbation is Nr1d1/Cry2 loss rather than wholesale BMAL1-CLOCK oscillator collapse.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The experiment is not a circadian time course, and absence of FDR signal for Arntl or Dbp at one sampling context does not exclude rhythmic regulation.

summary: Rora was not interchangeable with its ROR-family paralogs Rorb or Rorc in the responsive thalamic class.
why_it_matters: RORA, RORB, and RORC share RORE DNA-recognition logic, yet only Rora created a broad 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut signature; this argues that the hit is a RORA-specific dependency rather than a generic consequence of perturbing any ROR nuclear receptor.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Rorb target engagement was only nominal and Rorc target engagement was not detected, so lack of response could partly reflect ineffective or low-expression perturbation.

summary: Clock-neighbor perturbations did not phenocopy Rora; Bmal1 and Nr1d1 signatures were weakly anti-correlated with the Rora signature even though Rora, Bmal1, Cry2, and Nr1d1 regulate each other in the canonical clock.
why_it_matters: The 151 Rora phenotype cannot be modeled as simple loss of downstream BMAL1 or CRY2 activity: a direct Bmal1 perturbation shared some downregulated clock transcripts with Rora but reversed many Rora synaptic genes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Score correlations were modest in magnitude and are restricted to one thalamic class; the direction mismatch should be read as network-level divergence, not as disproving direct RORE edges.

summary: A loss-of-Rora thalamic synaptic program flags a possible CNS liability axis for RORA inverse agonism or other systemic RORA down-modulation.
why_it_matters: RORA is a ligand-responsive nuclear receptor with experimental inverse agonists, and human RORA disruption causes syndromic neurodevelopmental disease; therefore thalamic synaptic genes should be watched if RORA-lowering chemistry is pursued outside the brain.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: CRISPR perturbation of Rora mRNA is not equivalent to partial small-molecule inverse agonism, and the dataset contains no drug exposure or behavior.

summary: Tnfrsf13c perturbation produced no measurable on-target transcript knockdown and a very small differential-expression burden across the profiled mouse brain classes.
why_it_matters: The primary signature is weak before pathway interpretation: most apparent downstream effects are isolated rather than a receptor-driven program.
cell_types: 23 profiled brain neuronal classes
main_caveats: This is transcript-level evidence only; raw counts, guide identities, genome editing, and BAFF-R protein were unavailable, and a transcript absent from neurons can produce unstable logFC estimates without a Wilcoxon shift.

summary: The neuronal signatures were uncoupled from the curated BAFF-R to TRAF/NF-κB/B-cell-survival pathway.
why_it_matters: A receptor whose canonical biology is B-cell survival via TNFSF13B, TRAF3, and NF-κB2 did not drive an NF-κB or survival-gene module in these brain cell classes.
cell_types: 23 profiled brain neuronal classes
main_caveats: Absence of transcript changes in neurons should not be read as pathway absence in B cells or CNS macrophages; the target itself was not detectably engaged.

summary: Nav2 induction in Sst GABA was the only genome-wide significant single-gene response to Tnfrsf13c targeting.
why_it_matters: The strongest positive result is a cell-class-restricted neuronal gene, suggesting that the few significant hits are not a broad BAFF-R immune program.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Only 62 matched perturbed cells supported the Sst test, the target transcript was not knocked down, and Nav2 was the lone Sst gene at FDR<0.10.

summary: Midbrain glutamatergic and hindbrain GABAergic cells carried exploratory neuronal/synaptic candidate responses, with mixed directions in Smap2, Sez6l, Nefl, and Stxbp5.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The highlighted genes did not form a known BAFF-R module and only Smap2, Sez6l, and Stxbp5 were below FDR 0.10.

summary: Tnfrsf13c did not converge with accessible BAFF/TNFR/NF-κB neighbor perturbations in the same cell classes.
why_it_matters: Even though TRAF3, NF-κB, CD40, and related TNFR genes are pathway neighbors in immune cells, their neuronal Perturb-seq signatures were weak and nearly uncorrelated with Tnfrsf13c.
cell_types: 23 profiled brain neuronal classes
main_caveats: The contrast uses transcriptomic correlations with weak signatures and omits BAFF/APRIL receptors or ligands that were not available as perturbation targets in this file.

summary: The brain-neuron Tnfrsf13c result is not a disease-direction model for BAFF-axis immunodeficiency, lupus, or BAFF-ligand blockade.
why_it_matters: TNFRSF13C has human immune-disease genetics and the BAFF ligand is pharmacologically inhibited, but this dataset points to a profiled-cell-type mismatch rather than a neuronal therapeutic mechanism.
cell_types: 23 profiled brain neuronal classes
main_caveats: ChEMBL and Open Targets are human immune-disease resources, while the measured dataset is mouse neuronal Perturb-seq with no B-cell or macrophage profiled class.

summary: Zbtb24 perturbation was transcriptomically buffered across the assayed mouse-brain classes rather than producing a broad loss-of-function program.
why_it_matters: ZBTB24 is a transcription-factor gene with severe developmental and immune disease genetics, so a near-absence of FDR-level acute neuronal RNA responses narrows the interpretation toward weak engagement, chromatin states not captured by scRNA-seq, or non-neuronal/developmental requirements.
main_caveats: The target-transcript knockdown was itself not FDR significant in any cell class, so buffering cannot be separated from incomplete perturbation.

summary: The only adjusted differential-expression hit was Taf6 down-regulation in 155 MB Glut.
why_it_matters: This confines the robust dataset signal to a midbrain glutamatergic class rather than to cortical or inhibitory classes, but the conclusion is deliberately narrow because it rests on one FDR-significant gene.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene FDR hit with no supporting pathway-level enrichment; this is not evidence for a full cell-state conversion.

summary: The canonical ZBTB24-CDCA7-HELLS ICF axis was not transcriptionally engaged by acute Zbtb24 perturbation in the brain dataset.
why_it_matters: Prior stem-cell and ICF work places CDCA7 and HELLS downstream of or functionally linked to ZBTB24, so the absence of Cdca7 or Hells mRNA changes argues that any neuronal effect in this assay was not mediated through a large acute drop in those transcripts.
main_caveats: Cdca7 and Hells were not themselves perturbed in this library, DNA methylation and satellite-repeat outputs were not measured, and weak Zbtb24 knockdown could mask downstream effects.

summary: Zbtb24 did not phenocopy available Dnmt3a, Mecp2, or other ZBTB-family perturbation signatures.
why_it_matters: This argues against interpreting the weak Zbtb24 signature as a generic DNA-methylation-reader/writer response or a generic ZBTB transcription-factor response in the assayed neurons.
main_caveats: Comparator genes are related by methylation biology or BTB/zinc-finger domains but are not one-to-one ICF paralogs; different guide efficacies and perturbed-cell counts can contribute to effect-size differences.

summary: Restricted signature-neighbor scans failed to reveal a strong positive or inverse Zbtb24-like perturbation.
why_it_matters: Even the best-matching perturbations in the two scanned classes had |r|<=0.136, so the dataset does not nominate an obvious pathway substitute, suppressor, or antagonist from correlation alone.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Neighbor analysis was limited to two cell classes and used Wilcoxon score-vector correlations rather than a full multi-cell-type latent model.

summary: Taf6 is an exploratory recurrent marker of the Zbtb24 response rather than a proven effector.
why_it_matters: The gene was the only FDR-significant hit and was nominally down in ten classes; because TAF6 encodes a TFIID basal transcription-factor subunit, its recurrence is a compact biomarker hypothesis for testing whether Zbtb24 loss perturbs general Pol II initiation machinery in sensitive neurons.

summary: Vsx2 perturbation lacked measurable on-target transcript change and was globally quiet across 22 assayed mouse-brain cell classes.

summary: The screen does not reproduce canonical VSX2 eye-development disease biology in the assayed brain neurons.

summary: Xylt1 lacks a strong neuronal pharmacodynamic signature or obvious direct ChEMBL druggability signal in this analysis.

main_caveats: Biomarker status is inferred from one Perturb-seq contrast and has not been validated at protein level, over time, or after independent Trps1 depletion.

direction: maximal non-self score correlation was weakly positive and the strongest inverse was weakly negative

main_caveats: Correlations used Wilcoxon-score vectors from one cell class; very weak correlations should be interpreted as absence of a close neighbor rather than as mechanistic opposition.

summary: Trim37 knockdown was FDR-significant in six mouse-brain cell types, but five of those six had Trim37 as the only FDR<0.05 transcript.
why_it_matters: The result separates target engagement from broad mRNA remodeling and suggests that acute Trim37 loss is transcriptionally buffered in most assayed neuronal contexts.

summary: FDR-resolved Trim37 target knockdown was restricted within the assayed brain atlas rather than being universal.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse tissue data show Trim37 expression in adult nervous system, but the Perturb-seq readout resolves responsive and subthreshold cell classes within brain.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|046 CTX-CGE GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Some subthreshold classes had only 44-69 perturbed cells, so absence of FDR significance is not absence of expression or sgRNA activity.

summary: Trim37 perturbation did not induce a detectable peroxisome/PEX mRNA module or converge with the available Pex1 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The known TRIM37-PEX5 mechanism is protein-stabilizing; the mouse-brain signatures warn that PEX5-dependent peroxisome biology may be invisible to whole-transcriptome FDR even when Trim37 RNA is depleted.

summary: The acute mouse-brain signatures lacked the upregulated Polycomb/H2AK119Ub derepression pattern reported after TRIM37 RNAi in amplified breast-cancer cells.
why_it_matters: TRIM37 chromatin biology is not necessarily cell-line portable; a cancer overexpression model should not be assumed to predict a large neuronal mRNA response.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|308 CB GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Mouse neuronal signatures were not assayed for H2AK119Ub or for the exact breast-cancer TRIM37 promoter targets.

summary: Sptan1 guide perturbation reduced its own transcript in all 23 assayed cell classes, but FDR-level on-target detection was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 155 MB Glut, with 191 MB P MY GABA near FDR 0.05.
why_it_matters: These cell types define where downstream interpretation is best powered; weaker classes cannot be treated as clean biological negatives.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: FDR-level target detection depends on perturbed-cell count and per-cell-type variance, so it is an engagement map rather than proof of true expression specificity.

summary: Sptan1 perturbation produced very few FDR-significant downstream mRNA changes; Sptan1 itself accounted for three of four FDR hits and Gnpat was the only non-target hit.
why_it_matters: The dominant phenotype is buffered at the transcriptome level, consistent with a structural cytoskeletal protein whose proximal defects may be in protein localization, axons, or synapses rather than RNA abundance.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: A later structural or electrophysiological phenotype could occur without a contemporaneous single-cell RNA signature.

summary: In 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, Ank3 elicited a large 121-gene differential-expression program whereas Sptan1 showed only its on-target hit, and the two signatures had only weak correlation.
why_it_matters: It separates αII-spectrin depletion from ankyrin-G perturbation at the immediate transcriptome level despite their shared neuronal membrane-skeleton and axon-initial-segment context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptomic only; it does not prove that Sptan1 and Ank3 have different effects on AIS assembly or electrophysiology.

summary: Neither unbiased signature neighbors nor available membrane-skeleton-related perturbations revealed a strong Sptan1-like or Sptan1-opposing program.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting weak nominal overlaps as a cytoskeletal module and indicates that Sptan1 is relatively isolated in the mRNA response space of this dataset.
main_caveats: Correlation ranks were calculated from differential-expression score vectors, so non-transcriptional convergence would be missed.

summary: Partial reduction of endogenous Sptan1 RNA in mouse brain cells did not reproduce the broad cellular stress expected from severe dominant-negative SPTAN1 spectrin-aggregation disorders.
why_it_matters: SPTAN1 developmental epileptic encephalopathy often involves mutant αII-spectrin proteins at the α/β heterodimerization site; a knockdown-biased Perturb-seq assay is therefore an incomplete model of the human disease mechanism.
main_caveats: The inference compares mouse guide perturbation and RNA output with human protein-altering variants; allele-specific mutant proteins were not assayed.

summary: A non-allele-selective strategy that simply lowers SPTAN1 activity is not supported as a direct rescue direction by these data.
why_it_matters: The perturbed cells showed little transcriptional compensation after Sptan1 loss, CNS αII-spectrin is required for neuronal organization and survival in mice, and current ChEMBL entries do not establish a disease-directed SPTAN1 mechanism of action.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: No allele-specific therapy, human neuron rescue assay, or drug perturbation was tested in the dataset.

summary: Nav3 loss did not generate a broad FDR-stable RNA program in this mouse-brain Perturb-seq readout.
why_it_matters: NAV3 is a neuronal cytoskeleton protein, so a pan-neuronal loss-of-function response might have been expected; the direct data instead show that the acute transcriptomic assay was dominated by weak target engagement and sparse hits.
main_caveats: Absence of an RNA module cannot distinguish biological buffering from incomplete editing, low Nav3 capture, or a primarily morphological phenotype.

summary: The only multiple-testing-stable Nav3-associated gene was a singleton Cars decrease in 053 Sst Gaba.
why_it_matters: This prevents overcalling a general Nav3 pathway: the strongest corrected signal was cell-type-restricted and not accompanied by a second Sst Gaba FDR hit.
cell_types: 053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: Only 41 perturbed Sst Gaba cells were available; Vps37a and all other Sst genes failed FDR<0.1, so Cars should be treated as a candidate readout rather than a pathway.

summary: The subclasses with the best nominal Nav3 transcript depletion still had no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: Pvalb, L2/3 IT, and NP-CT-L6b-OB cells are the best internal test of whether measured Nav3 lowering was sufficient for a transcriptional phenotype; it was not sufficient at FDR<0.05.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: The on-target p values were nominal and all target-transcript FDR values were 1.0, so the result is compatible with weak perturbation rather than true molecular buffering.

summary: Nav3 did not phenocopy canonical axon-guidance or neuronal-adhesion perturbations assayed in the same dataset.
why_it_matters: Related receptors and adhesion genes such as Cntn1, Ncam1, Robo2, L1cam, Robo1, Unc5c, and Plxna2 achieved strong self-knockdown in several subclasses, yet their all-gene signatures were almost orthogonal to Nav3; the Nav3 readout therefore should not be interpreted as a generic guidance-receptor transcriptome.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on weak Nav3 signatures; Nav1 and Nav2 paralogs were absent, and not every related comparator had strong guide engagement.

summary: The Perturb-seq result is more consistent with NAV3 disease acting through developmental cytoskeletal and neuronal-morphology mechanisms than through a large acute RNA cascade.
why_it_matters: Human NAV3 variants cause neurodevelopmental disease and model knockdown disrupts neuronal growth; the lack of a conserved adult neuronal DE program suggests that morphology, timing, or protein localization may be better phenotypic endpoints for NAV3 than bulk RNA target genes.
main_caveats: The assay did not measure neurite geometry, axon pathfinding, microtubule plus-end dynamics, or embryonic stages where NAV3 may be most important.

summary: NAV3 inhibition is not supported as a simple therapeutic direction by this dataset or by current druggability databases.
why_it_matters: Disease evidence is dominated by damaging NAV3 alleles, while Open Targets and ChEMBL did not show conventional small-molecule or antibody support; the weak CRISPR RNA signature also offers no robust reversal biomarker for down-modulation screens.
main_caveats: Database absence is not proof of undruggability, and the experiment did not test rescue or NAV3 gain-of-function strategies.

summary: Tmco1 knockdown was buffered at the RNA-program level: even the contexts with nominal target-transcript depletion produced no FDR-significant downstream genes.
why_it_matters: TMCO1 is an ER calcium leak channel and multipass-translocon component, so a large ER-stress or membrane-biogenesis RNA program was plausible; its absence means the dataset should be interpreted primarily as a partial-loss, transcriptomically silent perturbation rather than a strong TMCO1-loss phenotype.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: All Tmco1 self-tests had FDR=1.0, no protein or ER Ca2+ flux was measured, and most cell types had fewer than 50 perturbed cells.

summary: Apparent Tmco1 target engagement was selective, with the clearest nominal self-depletion in Pvalb, hypothalamic GABA, thalamic glutamatergic, and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon GABA populations, while several cortical and CNU-MGE contexts had essentially no self-depletion.
why_it_matters: The variable self-row separates true biological buffering from failed or very weak target engagement; downstream negative calls in the weakest contexts should not be over-interpreted.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Self-transcript readout can reflect basal expression, guide sampling, or RNA detection as well as true cell-type biology; no Tmco1 self-row survived FDR correction.

summary: The ER unfolded-protein-response module was inducible in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells after Atp2a2 loss but not after Tmco1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: Within the same ER calcium-homeostasis neighborhood, the dataset distinguishes SERCA2 depletion, which robustly up-regulated Ddit3, Chac1, Xbp1, Herpud1, and Hspa5, from partial Tmco1 depletion, which did not; the negative Tmco1 result is therefore not explained by an intrinsically UPR-incompetent assay or cell type.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Atp2a2 and Tmco1 perturb opposite ER Ca2+ fluxes and need not be phenocopies; the contrast establishes assay capacity for an ER-stress response, not mechanistic epistasis.

summary: No robust positive or negative signature neighbor was detected for Tmco1 in the three most engaged contexts scanned, and the queried TMCO1 paralog and multipass-translocon components were unavailable as direct perturbation comparators.
why_it_matters: Top correlations of the Tmco1 score vector with thousands of same-cell perturbations were near zero, and known MPT partners were not assayed as gene targets, arguing against a hidden convergent module or direct complex-member contrast in the screened library.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The scan used score-vector Pearson correlations and can miss nonlinear, protein-level, or very small gene-set effects.

summary: The Perturb-seq result refines human TMCO1 disease interpretation by showing that acute partial Tmco1 transcript reduction in sampled brain cell types is not sufficient to trigger a broad neuronal ER-stress program.
why_it_matters: Human biallelic TMCO1 loss causes a developmental craniofacial-skeletal-intellectual-disability syndrome and TMCO1 variants are linked to open-angle glaucoma; the mouse-brain RNA phenotype suggests those disease mechanisms may require complete loss, long developmental exposure, non-neuronal tissues, ocular contexts, calcium flux changes, or protein-level translocon defects rather than a large acute neuronal UPR.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is an inference from an acute transcriptomic negative result; the experiment did not model human biallelic null genotypes, eye tissue, skeletal development, or ER calcium physiology directly.

summary: Zfp341 knockdown did not generate an FDR-controlled transcriptomic phenotype in any profiled brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This makes weak target engagement, low expression, or strong buffering the dominant interpretation rather than a specific neuronal pathway response.
main_caveats: High confidence for this Wilcoxon readout, but the dataset alone cannot separate failed CRISPRi repression from true biological buffering.

summary: The expected ZNF341-to-STAT axis appears only as an exploratory, directionally consistent STAT1/STAT3 decrease after Zfp341 perturbation, not as corrected per-cell-type hits.
why_it_matters: The sign pattern is the one expected for loss of a STAT transcriptional activator, but its FDR-weak magnitude argues that the lymphocyte HIES mechanism is not reproduced as a robust acute neuronal transcriptome state.
main_caveats: The STAT1/STAT3 trend uses nominal single-gene rows and sign consistency; every individual adjusted p value under Zfp341 is non-significant.

summary: The same atlas is buffered to STAT-family perturbations: Stat1 can be knocked down in midbrain/thalamic classes without a broad downstream DE program, and Stat3/Il6st perturbations are weaker still.
why_it_matters: This cross-perturbation context suggests that the missing Zfp341 phenotype could reflect muted cytokine/STAT transcriptional coupling in the profiled neuronal populations rather than only a Zfp341-specific artifact.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Stat1, not Zfp341, provides the clearest on-target comparator; Stat3 and Il6st also had weak target-transcript engagement.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor scan found no meaningful positive or negative Zfp341 neighbor, including no convergence with Stat1, Stat3, or Il6st.
why_it_matters: The Zfp341 vector behaves like a near-null signature; unexpected related-target divergence or convergence should therefore not be inferred from this perturbation.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations summarize Wilcoxon score profiles and will miss effects confined to unmeasured genes or non-transcriptional phenotypes.

summary: Rab3gap1 knockdown was largely transcriptionally buffered: even the best target-transcript depletion produced no non-target FDR-significant gene expression response.
why_it_matters: RAB3GAP1 is a vesicle-traffic Rab regulator, so a weak single-cell RNA response can coexist with substantial post-translational, morphological, or synaptic biology.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The strongest target row had FDR 0.065 rather than <0.05, and most cell types contained fewer than 70 perturbed cells.

summary: Measurable Rab3gap1 target engagement was uneven across neuronal classes, peaking in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA while several cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic signatures showed almost no target-transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: Cell types with no target mRNA reduction cannot be used as strong negative biological tests of Rab3gap1 function, whereas 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA is the cleanest place to judge the lack of downstream RNA response.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Target transcript abundance and guide efficiency are not separated; weak target rows could mean low expression or failed depletion rather than true cell-type resistance.

summary: The RAB3GAP1-RAB3GAP2-RAB18 biochemical axis was not recovered as a shared transcriptomic module.
why_it_matters: Reactome, UniProt, STRING, and primary literature place the three proteins in a physical RAB18-activation module, but in this dataset Rab3gap1 perturbation did not transcriptionally regulate Rab3gap2, Rab18, or Rab3-family substrate genes, and Rab3gap1 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Rab3gap2 or Rab18 perturbations.
main_caveats: Only Rab3gap2 and Rab18 were available as perturbations; Rab3-family GTPases and Tbc1d20 were measured as transcripts but not guide targets.

summary: The near-absence of DE genes should not be read as evidence that partial RAB3GAP1 loss is biologically safe or therapeutically inert.
why_it_matters: Human RAB3GAP1 loss-of-function alleles cause Warburg Micro/Martsolf-spectrum disease, and mouse or human neuronal models show synaptic and neurite phenotypes; the dataset therefore argues that RNA biomarkers are insensitive, not that the target is dispensable.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq dataset measures steady-state RNA after partial perturbation and not developmental eye/brain anatomy, protein abundance, vesicle cycling, Rab-GTP loading, or electrophysiology.

summary: No robust Rab3gap1 RNA biomarker candidate emerged.
why_it_matters: The strongest non-target rows were isolated nominal effects with adjusted p values at least 0.493, and known Rab-pathway transcripts were not corrected hits, so follow-up biomarkers should come from protein trafficking, Rab18 localization, or synaptic assays rather than this DE table alone.
main_caveats: There may be subtle or combinatorial expression shifts below the Wilcoxon/FDR detection limit; this finding only rejects single-gene DE biomarkers from the supplied results.

direction: Rhot1 mostly down; downstream response absent at FDR<0.05
summary: Rhot1 knockdown was directionally visible but never FDR-significant and produced no FDR-significant transcriptome in any assayed cell class.
why_it_matters: Rhot1 is a mitochondrial outer-membrane Miro GTPase associated with mitochondrial positioning, so the dataset primarily reports a weak or buffered transcriptional phenotype rather than a conventional downstream DE program.
main_caveats: The absence of FDR-significant DE is secure, but target engagement itself was partial and not FDR-significant.

direction: nominal Rhot1 down with mixed nominal non-target genes
summary: The two cell classes with the strongest nominal Rhot1 self-depletion, L5 extratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons, still had zero FDR-significant genes.
why_it_matters: These were the best internal opportunities to see a Rhot1 transcriptional response, so their quiet profiles argue that organelle trafficking defects, if present, did not propagate to a strong acute bulk mRNA state in this assay.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The strongest Rhot1 p values were nominal only; the finding cannot separate true transcriptional buffering from insufficient CRISPRi knockdown.

direction: recurrent target down, no recurrent non-target module
summary: Rhot1 itself was the only recurrent nominal p<0.001 hit, so the screen did not reveal a reproducible non-target gene module downstream of Rhot1.
why_it_matters: The most repeatable signature feature is the reagent's self-knockdown rather than a compensatory stress, mitochondrial, or synaptic transcript set, limiting downstream-biomarker hypotheses.
main_caveats: Defined with nominal p-value recurrence because no downstream gene passed FDR correction.

summary: In the L5 ET context, Rhot1's restricted signature was only weakly related to both its best positive and negative neighbors and to perturbations of present mitochondrial transport partners plus quality-control/dynamics neighbors.
why_it_matters: Despite known Miro1 connections to TRAK/kinesin transport and PINK1/Parkin quality control, the Rhot1 Perturb-seq vector did not align with a canonical partner perturbation, arguing against treating these weak transcriptional effects as a pathway-level Miro1 transport signature.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: Signature-neighbor analysis was restricted to the top 500 Rhot1-scored genes and the Rhot1 response itself was weak.

direction: Rhot1 silent versus comparator on-target depletion
summary: Other mitochondrial dynamics and quality-control perturbations were detectable in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut while Rhot1 remained FDR-silent.
why_it_matters: The negative Rhot1 result is not simply because this dataset cannot detect mitochondrial biology; Dnm1l, Opa1, Vps35, Kif5a, and Kif5c all produced FDR-significant on-target loss or broader effects in the same cell class.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparators sample adjacent mitochondrial processes rather than an obligate RHOT1-containing complex, and guide efficacy differed by gene.

summary: The dataset should not be read as a direct dopaminergic Parkinson model because Rhot1 was not represented in the 215 MB Dopa class and the assayed classes did not align transcriptionally with Prkn-linked quality control.
why_it_matters: Human RHOT1/Miro1 disease literature is centered on Miro1 retention, PINK1/Parkin mitophagy, and Parkinson-relevant neuronal vulnerability; those mechanisms require dopaminergic or mitophagy-focused validation rather than inference from the quiet non-dopaminergic Rhot1 signatures here.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa|022 L5 ET CTX Glut
main_caveats: The absence of a 215 MB Dopa Rhot1 block may reflect guide/cell-count filtering rather than selective biological tolerance; Pink1 was not assayed as a target.

summary: Tgif1 targeting produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response and no significant target-transcript depletion in any of 23 assayed mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: TGIF1 is a transcriptional corepressor, so the absence of a DE program primarily argues that Tgif1 was unengaged, redundant, or not rate-limiting in these assays rather than revealing a strong TGIF1-regulated state.
main_caveats: The DE table cannot distinguish true biological buffering from poor guide activity or sparse target expression; protein-level perturbation was not measured.

summary: Known TGIF1 TGFβ/SMAD, CtBP/HDAC, and retinoid-associated transcripts were not significantly shifted after Tgif1 perturbation, and receptor/SMAD pathway-neighbor perturbations were also mostly weak.
why_it_matters: The result argues against a robust canonical SMAD or retinoid transcriptional cascade downstream of Tgif1 loss in the assayed brain cell classes.
main_caveats: A pathway can be silent because the target was not engaged, because ligand/receptor signaling was minimal, or because the correct developmental state was absent.

summary: Ski and Ctbp1 perturbations produced stronger cell-restricted signatures than Tgif1 and were not Tgif1 phenocopies.
why_it_matters: TGIF1 should not be treated as interchangeable with all SMAD-corepressor machinery in this dataset; the strongest related outputs were target- and cell-type-specific.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Ski and CtBP1 have TGIF-independent roles; the comparison is expression-signature based and Tgif1 engagement was weak.

summary: Tgif1 did not converge with Six3, Zic2, or Zic3 holoprosencephaly-family perturbations in the assayed mouse-brain signatures.
why_it_matters: Human TGIF1 disease biology is likely concentrated in embryonic forebrain-patterning and paralog-sensitive contexts rather than in a broad differentiated neuronal response captured here.
main_caveats: The assay context does not match early ventral forebrain development; Shh itself was not part of the related perturbation set analyzed.

summary: Tgif2 was not transcriptionally induced after Tgif1 targeting.
why_it_matters: Tgif1 and Tgif2 overlap in mouse development, but this dataset provides no evidence for acute Tgif2 mRNA upregulation as the buffering mechanism in the assayed cells.
main_caveats: No Tgif2 perturbation was available, Tgif1 knockdown was not verified, and compensation could occur at protein, chromatin, or developmental-selection levels.

summary: Direct TGIF1 perturbation was transcriptionally inert in the dataset and TGIF1 lacks an established direct small-molecule target record.
why_it_matters: These data do not support direct TGIF1 modulation as a practical way to tune TGFβ/retinoid transcription in the profiled brain cell classes.
main_caveats: Open Targets and ChEMBL are target-centric resources; absence of direct ligand tractability does not rule out indirect modulation of upstream TGFβ receptors or chromatin cofactors.

summary: Vps13a perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream mRNA response across 21 analyzed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A negative mRNA response is biologically informative for a membrane-contact lipid-transfer disease gene: the acute perturbation is either buffered, incompletely engaged at protein level, or acting through organelle phenotypes that are not captured by this DE endpoint.
main_caveats: No protein, lipidomic, or organelle morphology readout was measured; all target-gene depletion was nominal after FDR correction.

summary: Only 155 MB Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA showed Vps13a as the top negative transcript, and both remained FDR-silent downstream.
why_it_matters: These two classes define the best internal contexts for follow-up of Vps13a loss, but also demonstrate that target engagement alone was not sufficient to trigger a robust gene-expression program.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: The supporting genes are nominal only and the cell classes are broad developmental classes.

summary: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA showed only nominal Vps13a mRNA depletion and no FDR-significant downstream response despite VPS13A being a causal chorea-acanthocytosis gene.
why_it_matters: The disease-relevant direction of perturbation did not generate an acute transcriptional disease-like state in the broad LGE/CNU GABA class, refining follow-up toward protein loss, membrane-contact, lipid, or maturation-dependent endpoints.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: The label is only a broad proxy for basal-ganglia lineages, and the signature used 35 perturbed cells.

summary: Vps13a signatures were near-orthogonal to Vps13b, Vps13c, and Vps13d signatures throughout shared cell classes.
why_it_matters: Shared VPS13-family membership did not translate into transcriptomic interchangeability, consistent with contact-site specialization among VPS13 lipid-transfer proteins.
main_caveats: The conclusion is based on weak whole-transcriptome signatures rather than strong FDR-level response modules.

summary: The dataset’s transcriptional silence should not be interpreted as evidence that VPS13A inhibition is safe.
why_it_matters: Human VPS13A loss causes a recessive neurodegenerative disease, so a target-lowering intervention would emulate the pathogenic direction even when this acute mRNA assay has no FDR-level alarm.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: This is a directionality warning, not an assessment of any specific drug program or dose.

summary: The strongest positive and negative signature neighbors of Vps13a were too weak to define a convergent module.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-interpretation of top-ranked correlated perturbations as VPS13A pathway members in a setting where the Vps13a signature itself is weak.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Only the two most engaged Vps13a cell classes were used for the neighbor calculation summarized here.

summary: Zfp950 perturbation did not produce a multiple-testing-significant gene-level response in any assayed brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This is the primary dataset result: apparent Zfp950 effects should be interpreted as weak, hypothesis-generating nominal fluctuations rather than a reproducible cell-type-specific program.
main_caveats: The absence of FDR-significant genes is downstream of weak target-transcript engagement and does not prove absence of Zfp950 function under stronger knockout or in unmeasured transposable-element features.

summary: Direct Zfp950 transcript knockdown was weak: all 21 measured target-transcript rows had FDR 1.0 despite a bias toward negative log fold changes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation cannot be read as a clean loss-of-function experiment; negative downstream results are more consistent with low guide efficacy, low baseline expression, or technical power limits than with definitive buffering.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|054 CNU-MGE GABA|046 CTX-CGE GABA
main_caveats: Target mRNA logFCs are negative in most cell types but small and not FDR-significant.

summary: Zfp950 behaved very differently from the KRAB-associated chromatin effector Setdb1: Setdb1 had FDR-significant responses in the same dataset, whereas Zfp950 had none and its matched score signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Setdb1.
why_it_matters: The result argues against treating an individual, poorly engaged KRAB-ZFP perturbation as equivalent to disabling the shared KAP1/SETDB1 heterochromatin machinery in brain cells.
main_caveats: Setdb1 is a broad chromatin effector rather than a Zfp950 complex member; the contrast is pathway-proximal but not paralogous.

summary: A cell-type-matched, whole-signature neighbor search found no strong positive or negative transcriptomic analog of Zfp950.
why_it_matters: This reduces support for a hidden convergence with another assayed neuronal, disease-related, or chromatin perturbation that would have been missed by single-gene FDR thresholds.
main_caveats: The scan used Wilcoxon score vectors from the available Perturb-seq library only; a weak maximum correlation in 308 CB GABA should not be treated as a mechanistic link to Wdr26.

summary: Developmental Zfp950 phenotypes curated from mouse gene-trap work did not translate into an acute, gene-level brain Perturb-seq signature under the engagement achieved here.
why_it_matters: Zfp950 has whole-animal developmental annotations, but this dataset gives no robust evidence that partial acute perturbation in the tested brain cell classes engages the same programs, cautioning against direct extrapolation of developmental phenotypes to mature neuronal transcriptional state.
main_caveats: Context matching is poor: the references involve curated whole-animal development or PDGF-responsive gene-trap biology, not CRISPRi/perturbation in the same brain cell classes.

summary: Sec31a perturbation is concentrated in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 155 MB Glut, where both signatures repress axon/synapse-associated transcripts including Atp1a3, Atp1b1, Stmn3, Sparcl1, Nefl, and Vamp1.
why_it_matters: A core COPII perturbation was not pan-neuronally equivalent; the recurrent module highlights two brain cell classes and neuronal process genes that could connect SEC31A loss to neurological vulnerability.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Single-cell RNA signatures cannot distinguish direct COPII cargo failure from secondary loss of neuronal-state transcripts.

summary: The 155 MB Glut Sec31a response pairs neuronal-transcript loss with increased early secretory trafficking transcripts, most notably Sec23a, Copa, Copb1, Srpr, Arfgap1, and Golgb1.
why_it_matters: The up-regulated secretory genes are consistent with a compensatory ER-to-Golgi trafficking program after outer COPII-coat disruption, rather than only generic transcriptional collapse.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only a subset of COPII/ERGIC transcripts were induced; the dataset measures mRNA, not vesicle budding or cargo export.

summary: Sec31a does not phenocopy assayed COPII and early-secretory neighbors: Sec23a perturbation knocked down Sec23a mRNA in 155 MB Glut but was transcriptionally buffered, and Sec23a/Sar1b/Copa/Stx5a/Ssr4 signatures were weak or uncorrelated with Sec31a in the two dominant Sec31a contexts.
why_it_matters: SEC31A is a physical COPII coat partner of SEC13/SEC23/SEC24/SAR1, so the dataset argues that the outer-coat Sec31a node is more transcriptionally limiting than the assayed inner-coat or trafficking neighbors in these neurons, or that paralog buffering differs across COPII components.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Restricted to targets present in the screen; Sec13, Sec31b, and several Sec24 paralogs were not assayed as perturbations, and the divergent response could reflect paralog compensation or protein stability after guide targeting.

summary: Sec31a perturbation did not produce FDR-level induction of canonical ER-stress transcripts in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, even though Hspa5 perturbation in that same cell type induced Hsp90b1, Nfe2l1, Pdia4, and Derl3.
why_it_matters: Human SEC31A-null cells were reported to increase ER-stress pathways; the Perturb-seq response instead separates Sec31a's neuronal signature from a broad detectable unfolded-protein response in at least this thalamic context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: This is a transcript-level negative result from one matched cell type; weak ER stress below FDR, post-transcriptional stress signaling, or stronger responses under complete SEC31A loss remain possible.

summary: Most Sec31a signatures were buffered or very sparse: the Sec31a transcript was never significantly depleted, 14 of 20 cell types had no FDR-significant downstream genes, and four more had only one to four hits.
why_it_matters: The negative space prevents over-generalizing the two dominant signatures to all brain cell classes and makes direct target-mRNA engagement a major interpretive caveat for this perturbation.
main_caveats: An unchanged or increased Sec31a transcript does not exclude coding disruption by CRISPR editing; low perturbed-cell counts also reduce power in some contexts.

summary: Tmem63a perturbation produced no FDR-significant neuronal transcriptomic response and no measurable self-transcript depletion across the 22 assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: It sets a strong negative boundary on acute neuronal mRNA programs downstream of this target, while also showing that the perturbation cannot be interpreted as a fully engaged Tmem63a loss-of-function experiment.
cell_types: all 22 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: Self-transcript engagement was weak; channel activity, protein abundance, and raw expression were not measured.

summary: A Riok1-up nominal signal in 001 L5-6 IT Glut was the strongest Tmem63a-associated gene-level trend but did not reach conventional significance.
why_it_matters: The L5/6 trend is the only place in the dataset where the Tmem63a signature rose above fully adjusted p=1.0, making it a useful but very weak lead if future experiments achieve better target engagement.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: Riok1 had FDR 0.314 and the next strongest genes had FDR 1.0; this should not be treated as a validated biomarker.

summary: Tmem63a did not phenocopy the assayed TMEM63 paralogs or related cation-channel perturbations; Tmem63b, but not Tmem63a or Tmem63c, showed strong self-transcript depletion, and Tmem63a:Tmem63b/Tmem63c whole-signature correlations were near zero.
why_it_matters: The result argues against assuming paralog interchangeability from channel-family membership alone in this mouse-brain transcriptomic context.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA

summary: The negative neuronal signatures do not rule out TMEM63A disease biology because transient hypomyelination points to oligodendrocyte/myelin mechanisms that were not in the assayed neuronal panel.
why_it_matters: This prevents over-interpreting a neuronal Perturb-seq null as contradicting human TMEM63A leukodystrophy genetics.
cell_types: all 22 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: The dataset lacks OPCs/oligodendrocytes and did not establish efficient Tmem63a depletion in the neuronal cells.

summary: A dataset-wide signature-neighbor scan found no robust convergent positive or negative perturbation for Tmem63a.
why_it_matters: Without a correlated neighbor, the isolated nominal top genes should not be collapsed into a known perturbation module.
cell_types: all 22 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors and can only detect transcriptional similarity within the measured cell types.

summary: Sigmar1 CRISPRi is transcriptionally buffered: the target transcript falls nominally in several neuronal classes, but no downstream gene reaches FDR significance anywhere.
why_it_matters: SIGMAR1 biology is anchored in ER/MAM chaperoning and calcium handling, so the dataset argues that acute partial mRNA depletion in these brain neurons does not automatically expand into a broad steady-state RNA program.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant RNA changes is a negative transcriptomic result; it does not exclude protein-level, calcium-flux, lipid, or stress-conditioned phenotypes.

summary: Apparent Sigmar1 engagement is uneven across cell types, with L4/5 IT, Pvalb, midbrain glutamatergic, pineal-projecting glutamatergic, and cerebellar GABA cells carrying the clearest nominal target depletion, whereas several high-count classes show weak knockdown.
why_it_matters: Cell-type comparisons must separate biology from guide efficacy: a muted 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut response and the null 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut response are uninterpretable as true Sigmar1 resistance without stronger target engagement.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Target depletion was inferred from target mRNA ranks, not from Sigma-1 receptor protein abundance or functional occupancy.

summary: The expected ER-stress/MAM neighborhood is not recruited detectably by Sigmar1 knockdown.
why_it_matters: HSPA5/BiP and IP3-receptor coupling are central to the canonical Sigma-1 receptor model, yet ER-stress transcripts were not FDR-positive and Hspa5, Atf6, Itpr1 and glutamate-receptor perturbations were nearly orthogonal to the Sigmar1 signatures.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The test is restricted to steady-state RNA after CRISPRi; ITPR3 and TMEM97 were not perturbed in the dataset.

summary: Neurodegeneration-associated RNA-binding perturbations are much stronger than Sigmar1 in the same neuronal class, so Sigmar1 disease biology is not reproduced by the broad Fus/Tardbp-like transcriptional programs present in this dataset.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse studies implicate SIGMAR1 loss in motor-neuron disease through ER-mitochondria failure; the Perturb-seq contrast suggests that this mechanism is cell-state or assay dependent rather than a generic ALS-gene expression signature in every brain neuron.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The assayed classes are mouse brain neurons, not lower motor neurons; some comparator perturbations also differ in target engagement.

summary: CRISPRi loss of Sigmar1 provides little support for RNA biomarkers of Sigma-1 receptor ligand action.
why_it_matters: ChEMBL and Reactome show that SIGMAR1 is pharmacologically tractable through direct ligands, but the dataset found no reproducible FDR-significant downstream RNA response after genetic depletion; ligand studies should therefore prioritize proximal calcium, ER-mitochondria, survival, or stress-challenge readouts rather than expecting a large basal gene-expression signature.
main_caveats: CRISPRi knockdown is not equivalent to an agonist, antagonist, or allosteric modulator; no drug was applied in the Perturb-seq assay.

summary: A data-driven signature-neighbor search did not expose a hidden Sigmar1-like perturbation module.
why_it_matters: Even the nearest positive and negative full-vector neighbors in the five clearest target-engagement cell types had modest correlations, so the weak Sigmar1 phenotype is not simply a mislabeled member of a larger transcriptional module.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The correlation search covered five cell types, used whole-transcriptome score vectors, and the best cerebellar neighbor remained only r=0.141.

summary: Rax perturbation was globally buffered in the assayed neuronal panel: the target transcript was rarely testable, never significantly depleted, and only three downstream genes reached FDR<0.1 across 22 Rax-tested cell classes.
why_it_matters: The result argues that most assayed brain neuron classes are Rax-off contexts rather than cells in which an eye- or hypothalamus-developmental Rax program is actively maintained.
main_caveats: The absence of a target-row depletion signal means buffering and target non-expression cannot be separated from weak CRISPRi engagement in Rax-low cells.

summary: The corrected Rax hits were isolated, down-regulated singletons: Gosr2 in 001 L5-6 IT Glut, Myl12b in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, and Mapre2 in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut.
why_it_matters: Each surviving gene occurred in a different cell class with no recurrent effector, so the corrected signal should be interpreted as cell-type-restricted singletons rather than a shared Rax pathway.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Myl12b and Mapre2 pass only an exploratory FDR<0.1 threshold, and none of the three hits is backed by a significant Rax target-transcript knockdown in the same class.

summary: Rax did not recapitulate the canonical ocular RAX/Otx2/Pax6/Six3/Six6 transcription-factor network in the profiled-brain signatures.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse optic-vesicle work places Rx upstream of Otx2, Six3, and Pax6 during retinal progenitor formation; the Perturb-seq signatures were instead nearly orthogonal to eye-field and photoreceptor TF perturbations.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: The comparator perturbations were also mostly weak in this profiled-brain dataset, so the conclusion is restricted to absence of a detectable mature-neuron module.

summary: 308 CB GABA contained an exploratory Rax signature-neighbor axis that aligned Rax with Msx2, Dstyk, Cckar, Plxnd1, Wdr26, and Zic-family perturbations and opposed Ranbp2/Fbxo11-like signatures.
why_it_matters: This coordinate pattern prevents a purely one-gene view of Rax, but the lack of Rax FDR genes and the presence of Safe_target controls among negative neighbors make it a validation hypothesis, not a mechanistic claim.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Restricted to one cell class, no Rax gene reached FDR<0.1 in that class, and two Safe_target controls were among the negative neighbors.

summary: The Perturb-seq result is a poor proxy for congenital RAX disease mechanisms and offers no supported brain-cell therapeutic direction.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse evidence links RAX loss to developmental eye, forebrain, and hypothalamic phenotypes, whereas the dataset mainly samples brain neuron classes with Rax below reliable detection and no recurrent downstream program.
main_caveats: This warning does not test embryonic retina, embryonic ventral forebrain, or Rax-high retinal progenitors; it applies only to the profiled brain cell classes.

summary: Safe_target_44 produced no FDR-supported differential-expression response in any tested mouse-brain cell class and has no measured on-target transcript row.
why_it_matters: The perturbation should be interpreted as a safe-targeting negative control rather than a gene knockdown with a disease, pathway, or druggable target axis.
main_caveats: The table contains aggregate DE rows only; it cannot quantify indel formation or off-target edits for the guide.

summary: The largest nominal Safe_target_44 rows are isolated weak tails in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 308 CB GABA, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut rather than a recurrent module.
why_it_matters: Plausible-looking genes such as Coa3, Zdhhc17, Ube2o, and Bap1 do not survive adjustment, so they should not be converted into mitochondrial, palmitoylation, ubiquitin, or chromatin pathway calls.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: The finding is a negative interpretation of nominal DE rows; no per-cell expression matrix was available to test whether the same cells carried a shared state.

summary: Safe_target_44 belongs to a 100-member Safe_target control family, making other Safe_target controls the meaningful comparator set rather than paralogs, complexes, receptors, or disease-family genes.
why_it_matters: The comparison prevents a category error: Safe_target_44 has no encoded gene function, so any apparent response should be audited as guide-specific or control-family behavior.
main_caveats: Only coverage of the Safe_target family was computed here; adjusted-response distributions for every other Safe_target guide were not needed to call the Safe_target_44 FDR-null result.

summary: The top nominal genes under Safe_target_44 are not biomarkers or therapeutic directions.
why_it_matters: Mixed-direction nominal hits from a safe-targeting control can reflect sampling, off-target, or guide-assignment effects; treating them as target biology would create false pathway hypotheses.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|308 CB GABA|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: The DE table does not identify which technical mechanism, if any, generated the nominal tail.

summary: P2ry14 perturbation produced no FDR-significant differential-expression program in the assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: A receptor with strong glial and immune precedent did not show a broad autonomous transcriptional requirement in this mouse-brain neuronal Perturb-seq readout.
main_caveats: P2ry14 transcript was not measured as a DE row, many contrasts had fewer than 50 edited cells, and the assayed populations were neuron-rich rather than glial or immune.

summary: 308 CB GABA was the largest but only nominal P2ry14 outlier, with weak FDR support and a signature-neighbor pattern that included Safe_target-labeled perturbations.
why_it_matters: This prevents the cerebellar nominal genes from being overcalled as a P2ry14 signaling module while still preserving the only cell-restricted scalar signal.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: All 308 CB GABA genes had FDR at least 0.533; Safe_target-labeled neighbors make the module potentially nonspecific.

summary: The highest-count thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic P2ry14 contrasts were still transcriptionally buffered.
why_it_matters: The near-null phenotype is not confined to the very smallest guide bins, reducing the chance that every negative result is a simple power failure.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Even 94 and 136 cells are modest for small transcriptomic effects, and no target mRNA row was available to verify editing.

summary: P2ry14 signatures did not converge with P2ry12, P2rx2, or GPCR/G-protein pathway comparators in the same cell types.
why_it_matters: The data give no support for treating purinergic receptors or Gi/o-coupled GPCRs as interchangeable perturbations in this neuronal assay.
main_caveats: Whole-score correlations are restricted-signature comparisons; P2ry14 target engagement itself was unquantified.

summary: P2Y14 druggability and immune chemotaxis biology do not translate into a detectable neuron-only P2ry14 transcriptomic response here.
why_it_matters: P2Y14 antagonism may still be relevant in inflammatory, hematopoietic, glial, pericyte, or choroid-plexus compartments, but this dataset cautions against using mature neuronal signatures as the primary on-target efficacy biomarker.
main_caveats: The dataset did not directly assay neutrophils, microglia, astrocytes, pericytes, choroid-plexus epithelium, ligand stimulation, or cAMP and chemotaxis endpoints.

summary: Taar1 knockdown produced a globally weak, low-engagement transcriptional phenotype, and the on-target Taar1 transcript itself never showed detectable depletion.
why_it_matters: TAAR1 is a bona fide GPCR with potent signaling biology, so the Perturb-seq readout is more consistent with poor target engagement, sparse target RNA, or non-transcriptional buffering than with a confident loss-of-function program.
main_caveats: The screen reports transcript abundance, not ligand-evoked GPCR signaling; zero-inflated target RNA makes the Taar1 logFC values uninformative even where a Taar1 row is present.

summary: The only transcriptome-wide hits were an isolated U2af1 decrease in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and a weaker Tmem9 increase in 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut.
why_it_matters: The small number and restricted location of hits argue against a pan-neuronal Taar1 knockdown module and identify U2af1 and Tmem9 only as exploratory cell-type-specific biomarkers.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
main_caveats: Tmem9 is only FDR<0.10, the two genes do not recur across cell types, and neither is a known canonical TAAR1 effector.

summary: Taar1 signatures did not converge with monoamine GPCR or cAMP/G-protein pathway perturbations, even though TAAR1 is annotated as an amine GPCR capable of G-protein signaling.
why_it_matters: This separates the measured CRISPRi transcriptome from expected acute Gs/Gi/Gq signaling and discourages reading the weak Taar1 DE profile as a direct cAMP or dopamine-receptor state.
main_caveats: The correlations used whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon scores and are not pathway-activity assays; acute agonism and chronic CRISPRi can have different outputs.

summary: The dataset gives little leverage on dopaminergic or antipsychotic TAAR1 biology because 215 MB Dopa was not scored for Taar1 and other high-cell-count Taar1 strata remained transcriptionally quiet.
why_it_matters: TAAR1 agonism is clinically pursued in schizophrenia, but absence of a robust knockdown signature here should not be interpreted as evidence against TAAR1 as a drug target or as an agonist-response biomarker.
cell_types: 215 MB Dopa|052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The clinical agents are agonists whereas the screen attempted genetic loss of function; mouse postnatal cell classes only partially match adult human disease circuitry.

summary: No other mouse Taar paralog was targeted, so the screen cannot test TAAR-family redundancy, divergence, or interchangeability.
why_it_matters: TAAR1 belongs to a larger species-divergent amine-receptor family, but all within-family comparisons are absent from this matrix and should not be inferred from the Taar1-only profile.
main_caveats: This is an absence-of-comparator finding, not a claim that paralogs lack function.

direction: isolated positive downstream hits amid broad nonresponse
summary: Zfhx4 perturbation produced a globally sparse FDR-resolved response, with only Sccpdh in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut at FDR < 0.05 and Man2c1 in 191 MB P MY GABA at FDR < 0.10 across the 22 reported signatures.
why_it_matters: A large nuclear transcription factor with developmental neural annotations was expected to give a multi-gene program somewhere; instead the adult-like mouse brain signatures were mostly buffered or weak.
main_caveats: The target transcript did not reach FDR significance in any cell type, and the assay reports mRNA rather than protein depletion.

summary: The lowest-FDR Zfhx4 responses were restricted to hypothalamic and midbrain/pons/myelencephalon broad classes, with no comparable cortical response.
why_it_matters: This weakly aligns the Perturb-seq data with human single-nucleus evidence for ZFHX4 enrichment in a midbrain-derived inhibitory population, but the match is hypothesis-generating because each signature contains only isolated genes.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Only one row reached FDR < 0.05; the 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA signal had FDR = 0.218 and should not be treated as significant.

direction: target transcript down; downstream response buffered
summary: 155 MB Glut showed the clearest nominal depletion of the Zfhx4 transcript but no significant downstream response.
why_it_matters: The strongest measured on-target mRNA effect being uncoupled from downstream FDR implicates buffering, insufficient knockdown, or stage mismatch rather than a simple lack of guide assignment.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Zfhx4 depletion in 155 MB Glut was nominal only after multiple testing; no protein-level perturbation is available.

summary: Zfhx3 and Zfhx2 did not phenocopy Zfhx4; most strikingly, Zfhx3 generated a significant thalamic program that included Zfhx4 as a positive hit while Zfhx4 generated no FDR-resolved program in the same cells.
why_it_matters: The ZFHX zinc-finger homeobox paralogs are homologous, but the dataset argues against treating Zfhx3 as an interchangeable transcriptional proxy for Zfhx4 in the tested postmitotic brain classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison uses mRNA DE correlations, not direct binding or redundancy assays; Zfhx2 and Zfhx3 perturbation efficiency was not independently assessed here.

summary: Zfhx4 loss did not recapitulate Chd4 loss in brain cells despite literature linking ZFHX4 to the CHD4/NuRD complex in glioblastoma tumor-initiating cells.
why_it_matters: This is a therapeutic and mechanistic caution: the GBM TIC ZFHX4-CHD4 axis is context dependent and Chd4 perturbation is a poor neuronal proxy for Zfhx4 in this dataset.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: GBM tumor-initiating cells and normal human neural precursors are not matched to broad mouse postmitotic brain classes.

summary: Nearest-neighbor searches around the principal Zfhx4 signatures did not discover a robust convergent or opposing perturbation module.
why_it_matters: Very small correlations, plus Safe_target entries among top neighbors, argue that the Zfhx4 phenotypes are too weak/noisy for reliable module inference from the current signatures.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The neighbor audit was concentrated on the three most discussed Zfhx4 cell types and used Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors.

direction: disease literature positive; dataset mostly negative
summary: Acute Zfhx4 loss in broad mouse brain classes does not reproduce the broad developmental impact implied by 8q21.11 human deletion genetics.
why_it_matters: The negative result narrows where disease-relevant ZFHX4 biology is likely to appear: developmental precursors, untested dopaminergic midbrain, ocular/craniofacial lineages, or other contexts may be more sensitive than the assayed adult-like classes.

main_caveats: Human copy-number loss is lifelong and often multi-gene, whereas the Perturb-seq assay is acute and mouse; the dataset also lacks Zfhx4 in 215 MB Dopa.

summary: Sp110 produced no measurable on-target knockdown in the profiled neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The canonical Sp110/Ipr1 literature is driven by immune and infected macrophage contexts, so the dataset most likely samples a cell compartment in which the perturbation has little basal substrate rather than demonstrating that Sp110 is dispensable everywhere.
main_caveats: The target transcript readout cannot distinguish failed CRISPR perturbation from very low basal Sp110 expression; microglia and macrophages were not among the profiled cell labels.

summary: Sp110 perturbation did not move an interferon or antigen-presentation effector panel.
why_it_matters: SP110 sits in interferon-induced PML nuclear-body and SP-family biology, but the perturbation did not produce detectable Stat, Irf, Ifit, Oas, Psmb, Tap, B2m, or H2 transcriptional remodeling in basal brain neuronal classes.
main_caveats: This is a negative observation under unchallenged conditions with weak Sp110 engagement, not a test of IFN- or pathogen-stimulated macrophages.

summary: The only cell-type tail was a non-significant, mixed-direction 308 CB GABA nominal signal.
why_it_matters: The lowest FDR values were concentrated in 308 CB GABA, but the genes were not significant and did not recur across neighboring GABA or glutamatergic classes, preventing a robust cerebellar interpretation.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA|001 L5-6 IT Glut
main_caveats: All genes in this tail had FDR>=0.115; this row records an audit result, not a validated pathway.

summary: Sp110 lacked meaningful convergence with related IFN-pathway perturbations or with any data-driven signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: If the Sp110 signature were a genuine IFN/PML-body program, PML/SP perturbations or IRF, IFN-receptor, or STAT perturbations would be plausible neighbors; instead the closest complex-family perturbations were absent and every available cosine was near zero.
main_caveats: Similarity was computed from a weak Sp110 signature; absence of convergence is more reliable than the biological identity of any weak positive or negative neighbor.

summary: A neuronal negative result should not be read as evidence that systemic SP110 inhibition is safe.
why_it_matters: Mouse and human studies link Sp110/SP110 loss to tuberculosis susceptibility and immunodeficiency, while ChEMBL does not show a mature clinical SP110 mechanism; the Perturb-seq result is therefore best used to deprioritize basal neuronal follow-up, not immune safety concerns.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay macrophage infection, humoral immunity, liver endothelium, or drug exposure.

summary: Tm2d1 produced an adjusted response in only two glutamatergic classes, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The phenotype is not a broad pan-neuronal stress or amyloid-like program; downstream interpretation should be anchored to sparse cell-type-restricted hits.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The finding is based on very few adjusted genes and partial target engagement.

summary: The measured Tm2d1 transcript was directionally reduced but never FDR-significant, while 19 of 21 tested cell types had no downstream row even at FDR<0.20.
why_it_matters: Most null cell-type contrasts cannot be read as complete Tm2d1 loss-of-function; they could reflect low mRNA abundance, partial guide activity, or buffering.
main_caveats: Transcript knockdown is measured at the RNA level only; the dataset does not measure TM2D1 protein or Aβ challenge responses.

summary: Tm2d1 did not phenocopy APP-processing or Notch-axis perturbations in its two responsive cell types.
why_it_matters: TM2D1/BBP is linked to APP/Aβ biology and the TM2D family affects γ-secretase-step Notch signaling, but acute mouse Tm2d1 knockdown here did not collapse onto App, Psen1, Adam10, or Notch1-4 transcriptional programs.
