main_caveats: Correlation analysis used RNA signatures; absent or weakly engaged paralogs prevent a definitive functional redundancy test.

summary: Ufc1 perturbation produced a sharply cell-type-skewed response, with the only FDR-supported target-transcript depletion and the largest downstream signature in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, smaller signatures in 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA, and no broad FDR response in most assayed cell types.
why_it_matters: The neuronal consequence of impaired UFMylation in this dataset is not uniform; the thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c population is the clearest readout, whereas many apparent absences cannot be separated from weak engagement.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Cell types outside 151 usually lacked FDR-level Ufc1 transcript depletion; low cell counts in some groups mean lack of DE is not proof of biological buffering.

summary: The strongest Ufc1 signatures induced a proteostasis and integrated-stress module centered on Ddit3, with Ddit3 up at FDR in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA and nominally up in several additional groups.
why_it_matters: Ddit3 up-regulation is the transcriptomic feature that most directly connects Ufc1 loss to the known ER/UPR role of UFMylation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Ddit3 alone is a marker rather than a full unfolded-protein-response branch assay; several recurrent appearances were nominal rather than FDR-significant.

summary: Ufc1 most closely phenocopied Uba5, but not Ufsp2, among directly assayed UFMylation neighbors.
why_it_matters: The data recover the expected E1-to-E2 ordering of Ufm1 activation and transfer: Uba5 and Ufc1 loss should reduce UFM1 conjugation in the same direction, whereas Ufsp2 has distinct processing and deconjugating functions.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The signature comparison was transcriptome-only, and ligand/E3 components Ufm1, Ufl1, Ddrgk1, and Cdk5rap3 were not present as perturbation targets in the queried dataset.

summary: In the most engaged thalamic glutamatergic class, Ufc1 loss coupled stress activation to repression of synaptic and synaptic-membrane transcripts.
why_it_matters: Human UFC1, UFM1, and UBA5 variants cause severe neurodevelopmental disease; the dataset suggests that a UFMylation deficit can translate into neuronal circuit-gene suppression, not merely generic ER-stress transcription.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The synaptic module is a transcript-level association in one cell class; no electrophysiology or protein localization was measured.

summary: Loss-of-function signatures argue that systemic UFC1 or upstream UFMylation inhibition could be neurotoxic unless strongly context-limited.
why_it_matters: A structural study explicitly frames the UBA5-UFC1 interface as a possible basis for ufmylation inhibitors, but this mouse-brain screen and human genetics both point to neuronal stress when the cascade is weakened.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset is a knockdown/perturbation screen, not a drug exposure study; ChEMBL target search did not identify a clinical UFC1 inhibitor, so the warning is directional rather than compound-specific.

summary: Ufc1 loss aligned with the UFM1 E1 enzyme much more than with Atf6, Hspa5, or Vcp perturbations, arguing that the signature is not a generic copy of ER-stress or proteostasis-gene knockdown.
why_it_matters: This helps interpret Ddit3 induction as a UFMylation-defect output rather than a nonspecific match to any ER-homeostasis perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Atf6, Hspa5, and Vcp do not span every UPR branch, and some comparator perturbations had lower matched-cell counts.

summary: Tlr7 guide targeting produced no FDR-supported on-target transcript decrease or downstream transcriptional program in the assayed neuronal cell classes.
why_it_matters: The dominant quantitative result is a strong negative: basal Tlr7 perturbation did not activate the canonical innate-immune axis in these cells, so nominal genes should not be overinterpreted as TLR7 biology.
cell_types: 19 Tlr7-tested neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell counts were low and target-transcript depletion is only an mRNA proxy for target engagement.

summary: The absence of a Tlr7 response is most consistent with the dataset sampling neuronal classes rather than the pDC, macrophage, or CNS-macrophage contexts where TLR7 is expected to be enriched.
why_it_matters: It prevents a false claim that TLR7 lacks CNS relevance while explaining why a mouse-brain neuronal Perturb-seq matrix did not show a TLR7 innate signature.
cell_types: 19 Tlr7-tested neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: No microglia or CNS macrophage perturbation was present; ligand-induced neuronal TLR7 signaling remains possible under extracellular RNA stress.

summary: Basal Tlr7 signatures did not converge with perturbed Tlr8, Tlr9, Irf7, Nfkb1, or other measured innate pathway neighbors despite their annotated pathway proximity.
why_it_matters: A shared Reactome or STRING neighborhood was not sufficient to impose a common transcriptional phenotype in these neuronal states.
cell_types: Tlr7-overlapping neuronal classes|054 CNU-MGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Myd88, Unc93b1, Irak1, and Irak4 were top literature partners but were absent from the compared perturbation table; correlations are transcriptomic and basal-state only.

summary: The closest nominal genes and global signature neighbors do not form a reproducible Tlr7 biomarker module.
why_it_matters: Fnbp4, Lgi2, Nrsn1, Cpne8, and CA3-local neighbors such as Zbtb21 or Nr2c2 are hypothesis-generating at best and should not be treated as validated readouts.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: This is a negative biomarker assessment; it does not assign function to the nominal genes.

summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq result should not be used to infer TLR7 therapeutic efficacy or safety in immune or microglial compartments.
why_it_matters: TLR7 has causal lupus and druggability evidence, but the assayed basal neuronal classes lacked the expression and engagement needed to evaluate agonism or antagonism.
cell_types: 19 Tlr7-tested neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: No TLR7 ligand, clinical antagonist, agonist, immune cell, or microglial state was assayed.

summary: Trem2 perturbation was transcriptomically inert across the 22 assayed neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The experiment does not supply a significant Trem2 loss-of-function program to interpret; downstream genes should not be promoted simply because they appear at the top of nominal Wilcoxon lists.
main_caveats: The null is in the screened neuronal classes and is confounded by lack of measurable target-transcript knockdown.

summary: The Trem2 null refines, rather than negates, TREM2 biology because the screen sampled glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes rather than the TREM2-high microglia/CNS-macrophage context.
why_it_matters: TREM2 is a myeloid receptor in the TYROBP/DAP12-SYK axis; a neuronal Perturb-seq null should be read primarily as a cell-context and engagement limitation, not as evidence that TREM2 is irrelevant to Alzheimer-associated microglial states.
main_caveats: The dataset does not include annotated microglia, macrophages, osteoclasts, or dendritic cells, so it cannot test the expected TREM2-positive compartment.

summary: Plxna1 was perturbable in neurons but did not converge with Trem2, uncoupling neuronal PLXNA1 phenotypes from the immune SEMA6D-PLXNA1:TREM2:DAP12 complex.
why_it_matters: PLXNA1 is the only assayed member of one Reactome TREM2 complex; its significant neuronal signature should not be interpreted as evidence for active neuronal TREM2-DAP12 signaling, because Trem2 itself remained silent and uncorrelated.
cell_types: 191 MB P MY GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and cell-type-restricted; principal immune adapters such as Tyrobp and Syk were not directly perturbed.

summary: Other lysosomal or inflammatory disease-neighbor genes could be engaged in the same workflow, contrasting with the silent Trem2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The robust Ctsb and narrower Grn on-target effects show that the lack of Trem2 signal is not a universal failure of the Wilcoxon pipeline or of perturbing neurodegeneration-relevant genes in these cells.
main_caveats: Ctsb and Grn are not TREM2 complex members; this contrast tests detectability in the dataset, not shared mechanism.

summary: No reliable Trem2 signature neighbor, pathway seed, or biomarker candidate emerged from the nominal Trem2 ranks.
why_it_matters: The top nominal genes were isolated and FDR negative, and the full perturbation-neighbor search was dominated by weak correlations, so the safest interpretation is absence of a coherent Trem2 program in the measured cell types.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: Correlation-based neighbor calls are especially unstable when the anchor perturbation has no FDR-significant genes.

summary: This dataset cannot adjudicate TREM2 activation or inhibition as a therapeutic direction for Alzheimer disease.
why_it_matters: TREM2 drug discovery is centered on agonizing a myeloid DAP12/SYK receptor, whereas the neuronal Trem2 perturbation here has no engagement or coherent DAP12/SYK-like output; the null should not be treated as a counter-screen for TREM2 agonists.
main_caveats: The screen perturbs Trem2 rather than agonizing TREM2 protein, lacks the core adapters as guide targets, and does not assay phagocytosis, plaque engagement, or clinical endpoints.

summary: Zbtb10 perturbation produced no FDR-supported transcriptional response in any assayed brain cell type.
why_it_matters: A nuclear transcriptional repressor might be expected to create a measurable target-gene program, but in this dataset the dominant interpretable result is absence of robust differential expression rather than a positive pathway call.
main_caveats: The target transcript is an imperfect proxy for genome editing or protein loss; most cell types had only 33-91 perturbed cells, and the result does not exclude protein-level or lowly expressed direct targets.

summary: The largest nominal Zbtb10 signal was restricted to 145 MH-LH TH Glut, with mixed up- and down-regulated genes but no FDR-significant hits.
why_it_matters: This preserves the only clear cell-type skew in the scalar DE output while preventing it from being treated as a definitive pathway response.
cell_types: 145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: Only 55 perturbed cells supported this class; all listed genes had FDR >=0.8246 or 1.0, and no same-direction gene recurred broadly across cell types.

summary: The canonical cancer miR-27a-ZBTB10-Sp1/Sp3/Sp4 axis was not broadly derepressed after Zbtb10 perturbation in mouse brain neurons.
why_it_matters: Cancer studies position ZBTB10 as an upstream repressor of Sp transcription factors and angiogenic or survival effectors; the Perturb-seq data show that this axis cannot be assumed to operate as a large, shared neuronal module.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The literature perturbation is ZBTB10 gain of function or miR-27a inhibition in human breast cancer, whereas the dataset tests Zbtb10 perturbation in mouse brain cells and measures RNA only.

summary: Available Sp4, Myc, and ZBTB-family perturbations did not phenocopy the Zbtb10 restricted signatures.
why_it_matters: The weak cross-perturbation correlations argue against treating ZBTB10 as interchangeable with Sp4 or with other captured ZBTB factors in these neuronal populations.
main_caveats: All comparisons are transcriptomic correlations from weak signatures; some related perturbations may also have limited on-target activity, and restricted-signature neighbors included Safe_target controls.

summary: Zbtb10 signatures lacked a telomere, cell-cycle, or survival-effector program despite literature connecting human ZBTB10 to ALT telomere binding and cancer-cell Sp effectors.
why_it_matters: It separates two dividing-cell mechanisms of ZBTB10 from the postmitotic neuronal Perturb-seq context and discourages inferring ALT-telomere or VEGF/survivin biology from the brain signatures.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay telomere architecture or ZBTB10 chromatin occupancy; absence is inferred only from mRNA differential expression of measured genes.

summary: Zfp398 guide targeting produced a globally weak or buffered transcriptomic phenotype across the assayed adult mouse brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: A predicted nuclear transcription factor did not yield an FDR-significant acute RNA response in this dataset, so scattered nominal genes should be interpreted as hypotheses rather than pathway activation.
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant hits may reflect weak guide activity, low power in some cell classes, or biology; transcriptomics alone cannot distinguish those explanations.

summary: The perturbation showed no consistent measurable depletion of the Zfp398 transcript itself.
why_it_matters: Because the on-target mRNA row was FDR = 1.0 in every profiled cell type and changed sign across groups, all downstream negative and nominal results are conditional on weak measured target engagement.
main_caveats: CRISPR perturbations can disrupt function without reducing mature mRNA, but this table provides no protein- or allele-level validation.

summary: Zfp398 did not converge with TGF/BMP-SMAD or EP300/CBP perturbations in the adult mouse brain signatures.
why_it_matters: The hPSC literature places ZNF398 at SMAD3/EP300-bound TGF-beta targets; the near-zero correlations here argue that this module was absent, inactive, or not captured by weak Zfp398 perturbation in mature brain cell types.
main_caveats: Correlation was computed on weak Zfp398 signatures; several comparator target transcripts were themselves not strongly depleted in every cell type.

summary: The neuronal p52-ZER6 to MT3 repression axis was not reproduced as Mt3 derepression after Zfp398 targeting.
why_it_matters: MT3 is a reported antioxidant target suppressed by p52-ZER6 in neuronal models; its lack of robust induction suggests that an Alzheimer-associated p52-ZER6/MT3 mechanism should not be assumed to operate after Zfp398 perturbation in all brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The table does not distinguish p52 and p71 isoforms or overexpression from loss-of-function; Zfp398 target engagement was weak.

summary: 054 CNU-MGE GABA showed an exploratory nominal Zdhhc8/Zdhhc4 co-upregulation module.
why_it_matters: The top two positive transcripts in this cell class encode DHHC palmitoyltransferases, making protein S-palmitoylation a plausible follow-up biomarker axis if the MGE signal is reproduced.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Both rows were only nominal with FDR = 1.0, n_pert_matched was 51, and no direct Zfp398-to-DHHC regulation was established.

summary: An all-perturbation signature-neighbor search did not identify a robust phenocopy or inverse phenocopy of Zfp398.
why_it_matters: The largest absolute correlation to any other perturbation was only 0.155 and Safe_target controls appeared in top-neighbor slots, arguing against a hidden high-confidence pathway neighbor in these signatures.
main_caveats: Correlation was based on whole-transcriptome Wilcoxon score vectors; weak common technical structure can dominate when the query signature is weak.

direction: down in the three FDR-positive cell types
summary: Slc25a46 target-transcript depletion was statistically secure only in three subcortical neuronal classes: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA.
why_it_matters: These three classes define the interpretable core of this perturbation; the other 19 assayed Slc25a46 contrasts should be treated mainly as weak-engagement or low-power negatives.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type restriction is statistical restriction of the target transcript, not proof that these are the only Slc25a46-dependent brain cell types.

summary: Even where Slc25a46 mRNA was depleted at FDR<0.05, the perturbation produced no FDR-significant non-target genes.
why_it_matters: SLC25A46 is a mitochondrial outer-membrane organizer, so the absence of a broad acute mRNA response separates target engagement from detectable stress transcription in this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay measures RNA only; residual SLC25A46 protein, later mitochondrial-architecture phenotypes, or small subcellular effects could be missed.

direction: stress genes induced by Opa1/Dnm1l but absent after Slc25a46
summary: Slc25a46 knockdown did not activate the Asns/Chac1/Ddit3/Cars/Slc7a5 stress module that was recurrently induced by Opa1 and Dnm1l perturbation in the same cell classes.
why_it_matters: Although SLC25A46 is networked with mitochondrial fusion/fission and MICOS biology, partial Slc25a46 loss was transcriptionally uncoupled from the amino-acid/integrated-stress-like response triggered by inner-membrane fusion and fission perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The Opa1/Dnm1l comparison is by target-neighbor logic, not a matched biochemical epistasis experiment; Slc25a46 engagement was partial.

direction: carrier target-only versus dynamics-GTPase stress response
summary: Within the SLC25 carrier family, Slc25a46 more closely resembled Slc25a4 and Slc25a12 target-only contrasts than Opa1/Dnm1l stress-inducing contrasts.
why_it_matters: The atypical outer-membrane SLC25A46 should not be assumed to phenocopy every mitochondrial-dynamics hit at the mRNA level; carrier-family knockdown can be visible at the target transcript while remaining almost silent downstream.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Family membership does not imply identical localization or substrate; Slc25a46 is functionally atypical and outer-membrane associated.

direction: disease loss-of-function versus buffered acute transcriptome
summary: The mouse-brain response refines severe SLC25A46 disease genetics by showing that partial Slc25a46 transcript loss is not automatically coupled to a broad acute neuronal stress transcriptome.
why_it_matters: Optic atrophy, peripheral neuropathy and pontocerebellar hypoplasia may depend on mitochondrial architecture, lipid/cristae defects, protein-level loss, developmental timing or chronically vulnerable neurons rather than on an immediate pan-cellular RNA stress program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The dataset does not assay optic nerve, peripheral axons, cerebellar development, respiration or mitochondrial ultrastructure.

direction: target transcript down; candidate stress markers not induced
summary: Slc25a46 mRNA, not Ddit3/Asns/Chac1/Slc7a5-like stress genes, was the only robust acute biomarker of Slc25a46 perturbation in this readout.
why_it_matters: A rescue or drug screen that only monitors canonical mitochondrial-stress transcripts could falsely score these Slc25a46-perturbed neuronal populations as unperturbed.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Biomarker inference is based on transcriptomics only and on three cell types with partial target depletion.

summary: The lack of Slc25a46 downstream DE is compatible with compensation or buffering of SLC25A46 loss, but this remains an exploratory interpretation.
why_it_matters: Slc25a46 biology is known to permit in-vivo buffering in stable zebrafish mutants, so a quiet Perturb-seq response should not immediately be dismissed as an off-target or null observation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: No longitudinal data, mutant-mRNA decay assay, protein measurement, or rescue experiment was performed in this dataset.

main_caveats: Absence is specific to the perturbation target labels in this parquet and does not say whether those genes were expressed as measured transcripts.

summary: The human ANE ribosomopathy mechanism was not reproduced as a strong acute mRNA differential-expression state after partial Rbm28 perturbation in mouse brain cells.
why_it_matters: ANE involves chronic recessive RBM28 deficiency with neurological and endocrine disease; the Perturb-seq data suggest that rRNA processing, translation, development, or stronger knockdown must be measured before concluding which brain cell populations are vulnerable.
main_caveats: The comparison crosses human disease to mouse CRISPRi, inherited chronic partial loss to acute perturbation, and ribosome/nucleolar biology to a polyadenylated mRNA readout.

summary: Chrne perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response in any of 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The result prevents a pathway-level claim from the Chrne signatures and marks Chrne as an off-context or non-engaged target in this brain atlas.

summary: Agrn, Pak1, Cdc42, and Chrnb2 produced clear self-transcript knockdown in selected cell types, whereas Chrne and the muscle AChR subunits did not.

summary: Nominal Xbp1 and Erp29 induction marks a very weak stress/ER candidate signal in CNU-MGE GABA cells.

summary: Zfp236 guides did not measurably deplete the Zfp236 transcript in any assayed cell type.
why_it_matters: Downstream signatures must be interpreted as guide-assigned transcriptional effects rather than as a transcript-validated Zfp236 loss state; a coding or protein perturbation could still have occurred, but the mRNA readout gives no corrected on-target confirmation.
main_caveats: Target mRNA abundance is an imperfect proxy for Zfp236 protein activity, and guide-level editing or protein measurements were not available.

summary: Nominally all Zfp236 cell types and FDR-positive signatures in 11 cell types converged on Ogt down-regulation, accompanied by recurrent Eif4a2 down-regulation.
why_it_matters: Ogt and Eif4a2 encode broadly required O-GlcNAcylation and translation-initiation machinery with human neurodevelopmental disease links, so these two transcripts are plausible high-value biomarkers of the Zfp236-assigned response even where the rest of the FDR-corrected signature is small.
main_caveats: mRNA changes do not demonstrate lower OGT or EIF4A2 protein; the response is interpreted downstream of Zfp236 even though Zfp236 target-transcript depletion was not observed.

summary: The strongest corrected Zfp236 response was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, with compact Ogt/Eif4a2-centered signatures in midbrain, hindbrain, hypothalamic, Pvalb, and cerebellar classes.
why_it_matters: Human ZNF236 is broadly expressed rather than brain-region selective, so the differential recovery of corrected transcriptomic effects points either to cell-state-specific vulnerability or to differential power rather than to a simple expression map.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Perturbed-cell number was strongly correlated with apparent signature strength, so cell-type selectivity cannot be separated cleanly from statistical power.

summary: Cpt1c and Kmt5b were selectively down-regulated within the strongest TH/MB/P-MY signatures, marking a smaller submodule nested inside the Ogt/Eif4a2 core.
why_it_matters: Cpt1c is a brain-enriched energy-homeostasis gene, so its FDR-positive loss in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 155 MB Glut, and 191 MB P MY GABA nominates these cell classes for follow-up of neuronal metabolic and ER-associated consequences.
cell_types: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The Cpt1c/Kmt5b pattern involved only four to five cell-type tests and should be viewed as a biomarker hypothesis, not a proven mechanism.

summary: Restricted-signature comparison placed Gfpt1 and Ogt among the closest positive Zfp236 neighbors but only with weak correlations, and direct Ogt knockdown did not reproduce the full Zfp236 Ogt/Eif4a2/Cpt1c pattern.

summary: Rubcn perturbation produced weak, directionally negative target-transcript engagement but no FDR-significant downstream response in any of 23 assayed cell types.

main_caveats: Rubcn mRNA itself was not FDR-significantly knocked down; the assay does not measure Rubicon protein, lipid kinase activity, Rab7 activation, or autophagic flux.

summary: Rubcn perturbation did not transcriptionally activate or repress a canonical autophagy, PI3KC3, Rab7/HOPS, Rag, TSC, or MTOR marker set.
why_it_matters: The result argues against using mRNA levels of neighboring autophagy genes as a Rubcn pharmacodynamic readout in these neuronal classes and is consistent with prior work in which Rubicon controls vesicle maturation through protein complexes.
main_caveats: Only transcript levels were tested; pathway flux could change without differential expression of the pathway genes themselves.

summary: Rubcn failed to phenocopy strongly active autophagy/endolysosomal and mTOR-neighbor perturbations in the same TH and midbrain glutamatergic cell types.
why_it_matters: The same cell types and analysis detected hundreds of FDR-significant genes after Rab7, Tsc1, and Tsc2 perturbation, so the Rubcn null result is not explained simply by an insensitive cell type or by lack of autophagy-neighbor biology in the screen.

main_caveats: The comparators are pathway neighbors rather than interchangeable Rubicon-complex subunits; different guide efficiencies may contribute.

summary: The only Rubcn cell-type peaks were exploratory near-misses in Pvalb, pineal glutamatergic, and superficial cortical glutamatergic classes.

summary: The dataset does not provide a neuronal transcriptional biomarker for the pro-autophagy Rubicon-inhibition strategy suggested by aging work.

main_caveats: The screen does not assay aged animals, chronic Rubicon loss, alpha-synuclein burden, or autophagic flux.

summary: A genome-wide signature-neighbor search found no strong positive or negative phenocopy of the Rubcn signatures.

summary: The weak neuronal signature should not be read as evidence that STAT3 is broadly dispensable in clinically relevant cytokine, injury, leptin, or immune settings.

summary: A whole-signature neighbor scan found no strong Xpr1-like or Xpr1-opposing perturbation among approximately two thousand programs per cell type.

summary: The weak neuronal Perturb-seq phenotype does not de-risk the XPR1 phosphate-export axis for brain calcification or for systemic XPR1 inhibition strategies.

summary: Acute single-gene Snrpn targeting did not converge with assayed PWS-region genes, other imprinted genes, or the SmN paralog Snrpb.

summary: Nr4a1 was not a robust Snrpn-induced transcript in this dataset, despite prior cortical-neuron work placing Nr4a1 downstream of SNRPN knockdown.
why_it_matters: NR4A1 antagonism has been proposed from embryonic cortical culture phenotypes; these mouse-brain Perturb-seq cell classes do not support Nr4a1 mRNA as a universal pharmacodynamic marker of partial Snrpn loss.

summary: Pja1 up-regulation in L4/5 IT cortical neurons was the only downstream gene-level FDR hit after Snrpn perturbation.

summary: Trp53 perturbation was buffered across all 23 assayed mouse-brain cell classes, with no FDR-significant downstream genes despite measuring the Trp53 transcript in every class.
why_it_matters: The primary dataset result is not a p53-like stress program but rather a near-null basal signature, consistent with p53 being mainly stress activated and context dependent.
main_caveats: On-target mRNA reduction was only nominal and never FDR-significant; buffering could reflect weak guide activity, low basal Trp53 expression, protein persistence, or the absence of DNA-damage stress.

summary: Canonical p53 effector transcripts for cell-cycle arrest, feedback, DNA damage, and apoptosis were not engaged by Trp53 perturbation.
why_it_matters: The few nominal top genes in the screen should not be interpreted as an active p53 transcriptional program without Cdkn1a, Mdm2, Bax/Bbc3/Pmaip1, Gadd45a, or related effectors moving.
main_caveats: Only transcript abundance was tested; p53 can also act through protein stabilization, post-translational regulation, and stimulus-dependent enhancers.

summary: The best Trp53-associated signals were weak and localized to 217 P MY Pineal Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than recurring across many cell types.

summary: Trp53, Trp63, and Trp73 did not form a convergent p53-family module in unstressed brain cells.
why_it_matters: The p53 paralogs are homologous transcription factors, so the lack of common signatures indicates that they were either weakly expressed or functionally inactive under these basal conditions rather than interchangeable in this assay.
main_caveats: Trp63 and Trp73 also lacked target-transcript engagement, and Mdm2/Mdm4 perturbations were not available for a more canonical p53-axis comparison.

summary: The null Trp53 result is not a global failure of this cell-type-resolved screen: Pten and E2f4 produced FDR-significant programs in the same broad brain dataset.
why_it_matters: Comparator activity makes the Trp53 silence more target-specific, particularly in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut where Pten and E2f4 both produced strong signatures with fewer or comparable perturbed cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Pten and E2f4 are not linear Trp53 complex members; they serve as same-dataset tumor-suppressor/cell-cycle comparators rather than as proof of a p53-specific neighbor response.

summary: Basal neuronal silence after Trp53 targeting should not be interpreted as evidence that p53 loss is biologically safe or therapeutically desirable.
why_it_matters: Cancer genetics and p53-directed clinical chemistry emphasize restoring or stabilizing p53, while the Perturb-seq assay lacks the genotoxic stress and long latency required to expose p53-dependent tumor suppression or DNA-damage apoptosis.
main_caveats: This is a short-term transcriptomic inference from normal mouse brain cells, not a cancer, stress, survival, or tumorigenesis experiment.

summary: Robo4 is effectively inert across the assayed neuronal brain classes rather than forming a neuronal response program.
why_it_matters: The absence of both target-transcript displacement and FDR-significant downstream genes is biologically coherent with Robo4 being a vascular-endothelial receptor, so this contrast primarily tests off-context neuronal cells.
main_caveats: A silent target row cannot distinguish lack of Robo4 expression from ineffective editing when the transcript is essentially absent.

summary: Robo4 does not phenocopy Robo1, Robo2, Slit2, or adjacent guidance-receptor perturbations.

summary: The nominal Robo4 tail is composed of isolated, nonrecurrent genes rather than a reproducible cell-type module.

summary: The neuronal null result should not be read as evidence that Robo4 biology is irrelevant or safe to perturb in brain disease settings.
why_it_matters: ROBO4 is tied to vascular integrity and aortic-valve/aortic-aneurysm genetics; the present neuronal dataset lacks a measurable endothelial response, so it cannot forecast vascular barrier consequences of inhibiting or activating Robo4.
main_caveats: No endothelial cell perturbations, vascular permeability readouts, or organismal cardiovascular phenotypes were measured in the dataset.

summary: Tcf7l2 perturbation produced an almost all-or-none response concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

summary: High-cell-count non-thalamic tests, especially 155 MB Glut, showed little downstream response despite adequate matched cell numbers and nominal Tcf7l2 transcript reduction in 155 MB Glut.

summary: The same beta-catenin/TCF7L2 node that carries human metabolic, cancer, and neurodevelopmental evidence controls a thalamic synaptic transcriptional program in mouse neurons.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

main_caveats: This is a perturbation-derived safety hypothesis, not a clinical toxicity measurement; approved proteasome inhibitors primarily bind beta subunits rather than PSMC1 itself.

summary: Smchd1 perturbation was an FDR-level transcriptomic null across the assayed mouse brain cell types.
why_it_matters: SMCHD1 is a major chromatin silencer in established biology, so the absence of corrected coding-gene DE means this Perturb-seq experiment should not be interpreted as revealing a strong acute neuronal SMCHD1-regulated program.
main_caveats: The null is limited by weak target-transcript depletion; it does not rule out protein-level, repeat-element, long-timescale, or non-neuronal SMCHD1 functions.

main_caveats: The on-target rows themselves had pvals_adj = 1.0, so this is only a nominal self-knockdown/buffering hypothesis.

summary: Nominal Smchd1 hits and nearest perturbation neighbors did not form a reproducible biomarker or pathway module.
why_it_matters: A weak-looking scalar response is not hiding a coherent restricted signature: top nominal genes were mostly singletons, maximum same-cell-type neighbor correlations were only about 0.05-0.07, and safe-target controls appeared among top positive neighbors.
main_caveats: Correlation calculations were performed in three representative cell types, not exhaustively reported for all 22 Smchd1 groups.

direction: orthogonal to Lrif1; weaker than Smc1a positive contexts
summary: Smchd1 did not converge with Lrif1, its main assayed literature-grounded partner, and the dataset could detect a separate SMC-family perturbation, Smc1a.
why_it_matters: LRIF1-SMCHD1 proximity at heterochromatin would make concordance plausible, but near-zero Smchd1-Lrif1 score correlations and a null Lrif1 response argue that this neuronal screen did not activate that module; Smc1a positives show that the result was not a universal failure of all SMC-family perturbations.
main_caveats: Lrif1 itself showed no corrected hits, so the contrast is also compatible with poor Lrif1 engagement or lack of SMCHD1-LRIF1 activity in these brain cells.

direction: caution against interpreting null neuronal coding-gene data as therapeutic safety for inhibition
summary: The mouse brain negative result should not de-risk SMCHD1 loss-of-function or inhibitor strategies for FSHD-relevant biology.
why_it_matters: Human FSHD2 is linked to SMCHD1-dependent repression of D4Z4/DUX4, Open Targets prioritizes FSHD2 for SMCHD1, and ChEMBL already contains early SMCHD1 inhibitor-like biochemical activities; the dataset neither assayed DUX4 nor produced a loss-of-function signature that could define a safe inhibition window.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay used mouse brain cells and did not directly measure human D4Z4 repeats, DUX4, or muscle differentiation phenotypes.

summary: Wnk1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered at the multiple-testing level across all tested mouse-brain cell types.

summary: The strongest nominal on-target Wnk1 decreases were restricted to 155 MB Glut and 308 CB GABA, whereas other Wnk1-tested classes showed weaker or absent direct transcript depletion.

summary: Wnk1 perturbation did not transcriptionally propagate to Stk39/Oxsr1 or Slc12 cotransporter genes even though WNK1 is known to act through SPAK/OSR1 phosphorylation of cation-chloride cotransporters.

main_caveats: Absence of mRNA changes cannot rule out acute phosphorylation changes within the same pathway.

summary: Wnk1 and Wnk3 were not interchangeable at the transcriptomic-signature level.
why_it_matters: WNK1 and WNK3 both regulate cation-chloride cotransporter biology in the literature, yet their Perturb-seq score vectors were essentially uncorrelated; the most conservative interpretation is that these kinases did not drive a shared steady-state mRNA program in this screen.
main_caveats: Wnk3 target engagement was weak in this dataset, so this is a failure to observe interchangeability rather than proof that engaged WNK3 loss would diverge mechanistically from WNK1 loss.

summary: Wnk1 had no recurrent positive or negative signature neighbor across the all-target screen.

main_caveats: Only Pearson correlations of Wilcoxon score vectors were used; non-linear or phospho-proteomic convergence would be missed.

summary: For WNK1-directed therapy, this Perturb-seq experiment supports a warning against using these weak brain mRNA signatures as pharmacodynamic biomarkers.
why_it_matters: WNK1 is disease-linked and chemically tractable, but the Wnk1 perturbation did not yield a robust transcriptional signature or a cotransporter-axis mRNA readout; WNK inhibitor programs should prioritize pathway phosphorylation, chloride handling, and renal electrolyte physiology over the nominal RNA hits reported here.
main_caveats: The dataset used genetic perturbations in mouse brain cell classes, not acute pharmacologic pan-WNK inhibition in kidney, sensory neurons, or disease models.

summary: Measured Polr3b perturbations did not produce detectable self-transcript depletion in any of the 21 cell types.

summary: Nr2f2 perturbation was not a significant transcriptomic perturbation in the profiled mouse-brain classes.

cell_types: 046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba

summary: Tbx4 is transcriptionally silent or unengaged across the assayed mouse-brain classes rather than producing a corrected downstream program.

summary: Tbx4 did not converge with Tbx3/Tbx5 paralog-family signatures or with the cortical T-box factor Tbr1; Tbr1 itself was active in the same dataset.

main_caveats: Correlations were computed over restricted same-cell signed Wilcoxon-score vectors from this dataset only; poor Tbx4 engagement limits mechanistic interpretation.

summary: Neuronal Tbx4 perturbation did not phenocopy assayed pulmonary-arterial-hypertension or BMP/TGF-beta disease neighbors.
why_it_matters: Human TBX4, BMPR2, ACVRL1, ENG, SMAD9, and SOX17 all connect genetically to PAH, but the Tbx4 brain signature was uncorrelated with these perturbations, implying that this neuronal assay is not a useful reconstruction of the pulmonary vascular TBX4 disease module.

summary: TBX4 loss-of-function disease genetics should not be directionally interpreted from the weak Tbx4 neuronal Perturb-seq signature.
why_it_matters: TBX4 deficiency is causal in limb-pelvis-lung developmental syndromes and is associated with childhood PAH; in contrast, this assay lacks target engagement and corrected downstream hits, so the dataset provides little evidence about whether increasing or decreasing TBX4 would be therapeutic in pulmonary disease.
main_caveats: This is a warning from a mismatch between a developmental pulmonary/limb disease gene and a neuronal perturbation assay, not a direct test of TBX4 in pulmonary arterial cells.

direction: Vamp1 down; downstream differential expression buffered

summary: No Vps13b contrast contained an FDR-supported downstream transcript, even though VPS13B is a Golgi/endosomal lipid-transfer factor in prior work.

summary: Nominal Vps13b peaks were idiosyncratic rather than a reproducible cell-type-selective program.

summary: A search over all same-cell-type perturbation signatures found no strong positive or negative Vps13b neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak maximum absolute correlations argue that the Vps13b rows supply no robust convergent module from which to infer a hidden pathway, complex member, or disease-family phenocopy.

summary: The weak Perturb-seq response should not be read as evidence that inhibiting VPS13B is safe.
why_it_matters: Human loss-of-function VPS13B causes Cohen syndrome, Open Targets returned no approved or clinical modality for VPS13B, and the present assay lacks strong knockdown; therapeutic reasoning should therefore favor understanding or restoring VPS13B function rather than extrapolating benefit from an apparently silent acute knockdown.

summary: Tshz2 showed no measurable target-mRNA depletion in any assayed brain cell class.

summary: The Tshz2 transcriptome response was FDR-null in every covered cell class.
why_it_matters: A broad adult-brain response would be expected for a strongly engaged developmental DNA-binding factor with ongoing expression; instead the screen saw no FDR-controlled downstream gene, so nominal genes should be treated as unvalidated leads.
main_caveats: FDR-null does not separate true buffering from weak editing, low target expression, or an embryonic function absent from the assayed adult-like cell classes.

summary: The assayed Tshz3 paralog converged with Tshz2 on a null FDR phenotype and did not share even a nominal signature.
why_it_matters: Tshz2 and Tshz3 are paralogous teashirt zinc-finger factors, and Tshz3 has established cortical projection-neuron roles; the dataset therefore argues against an interchangeable Tshz2/Tshz3 adult-brain module in this assay.
main_caveats: The contrast is dominated by two weakly engaged perturbations; it should not be read as evidence against Tshz3 biology in validated developmental or postnatal knockout models.

summary: The strongest Tshz2 signature neighbors were weak and did not reveal a hidden convergent module.
why_it_matters: If the zero-FDR result reflected a smooth but coherent pathway shift, another perturbation might align with the full Tshz2 vector; the best correlations in two nominally strongest classes were small.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Only two cell classes were profiled for full-vector neighbors; all correlations were computed from nominal genome-wide score vectors with no FDR-supported Tshz2 index genes.

summary: A mammary TSHZ2-GLI1/CtBP target module was not detectably reactivated by Tshz2 perturbation in brain cells.
why_it_matters: Prior tumor work predicts that TSHZ2 loss can increase GLI1 targets such as AEBP1 and CXCR4; the absence of movement of Gli1, Aebp1, Cxcr4, and Ctbp2 cautions against projecting that cancer mechanism onto these brain cell classes.
main_caveats: The reference mechanism was derived from mammary epithelial cancer models, not mouse neurons, and several GLI-axis genes appear very lowly expressed in the Perturb-seq output.

summary: The same DE pipeline could detect a cortical transcription-factor response for Tbr1 while Tshz2 stayed silent.
why_it_matters: Tbr1 is a known postmitotic cortical identity regulator; its FDR-significant response in cortical glutamatergic classes means the Tshz2 null is not simply a universal failure of the Wilcoxon pipeline or of these cell classes to respond to transcription-factor perturbation.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut
main_caveats: Tbr1 is a positive comparator, not a pathway neighbor of Tshz2; different guide efficiencies and target expression still remain possible.

summary: Ptch2 guides produced no FDR-significant target-transcript or downstream transcriptional response in any of the 23 profiled mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The primary interpretation of this perturbation is a null or failed-engagement phenotype rather than a clean Ptch2 loss-of-function state.
main_caveats: mRNA abundance is an imperfect measure of CRISPR editing; the guide could disrupt protein without lowering the transcript, but no robust downstream rescue signal was detected.

summary: 155 MB Glut carried the only exploratory Ptch2 hit, Ptpn5 up-regulation, with nearby nominal increases in Cep70, Cdkal1, Golgb1, and Fzd3.
why_it_matters: If the Ptch2 signature is real anywhere in this screen, the midbrain glutamatergic class is the best follow-up context and Ptpn5 is the best single-gene readout.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Ptpn5 did not pass FDR<0.05 and all other named genes had FDR>=0.879.

summary: Ptch2 perturbation failed to move canonical GLI/PTCH/SMO feedback transcripts even though PTCH2 is a Hedgehog receptor and GLI-responsive gene.
why_it_matters: A transcriptional Hedgehog activation model predicts altered pathway readouts after effective PTCH2 loss, so the dataset indicates either pathway buffering, absent ligand tone, or insufficient Ptch2 perturbation in these neuronal classes.
main_caveats: The literature expectation applies to effective Hedgehog-pathway modulation, whereas the Ptch2 transcript itself was not significantly perturbed.

summary: Ptch2 was not merely isolated from a responsive receptor module; an eight-gene related Hedgehog panel was itself very weak and Ptch2 signatures were orthogonal to Ptch1, Smo, Gli1/2/3, Gpr161, Cdon, and Ptchd1.
why_it_matters: The paralog and pathway-neighbor contrast shifts the interpretation from a Ptch2-only anomaly toward a broader lack of CRISPR-coupled canonical Hedgehog transcriptional output in the assayed mouse-brain cell classes.
main_caveats: Most related perturbations also lacked direct target-transcript validation; correlation values summarize transcriptome-wide ranks, not a pathway activity assay.

summary: The 308 CB GABA Ptch2 signature had a modest inverse relationship to B9d1, a ciliary transition-zone Hedgehog regulator, even though Ptch2 itself had no significant CB GABA DE genes.
why_it_matters: This preserves a biologically suggestive top negative signature neighbor that would be missed by FDR-only review, but treats it as a hypothesis about ciliary/Hedgehog coupling rather than a confirmed module.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: The largest absolute correlation was only 0.254, was confined to one cell type, and the Ptch2 CB GABA DE table had zero FDR<0.25 genes.

summary: The dataset gives no support for using Ptch2 suppression alone to drive a broad brain GLI program despite PTCH2 disease links in Hedgehog-driven cancers.
why_it_matters: PTCH2 has cancer and basal-cell-carcinoma genetic associations, but these neuronal Perturb-seq data argue against extrapolating those contexts to a robust mouse-brain transcriptional effect.
main_caveats: The screen measures RNA in selected mouse-brain classes, not skin, tumor, medulloblastoma, or protein-level Hedgehog signaling.

summary: Ube2e2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered across the mouse-brain survey.
why_it_matters: UBE2E2 is an enzymatic ubiquitin-transfer factor, so an acute partial perturbation could change ubiquitin chemistry without producing a large steady-state mRNA signature; the dataset therefore argues against a robust transcriptional cascade, not against ubiquitin-level biology.
main_caveats: The target transcript itself was only nominally reduced, never FDR-significant, and RNA sequencing does not measure ubiquitin-chain topology or substrate ubiquitylation.

summary: Nominal on-target RNA depletion was concentrated in a few posterior and midbrain classes rather than being uniform across all neurons.
why_it_matters: The pattern nominates 217 P MY Pineal Glut, 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and one cortical L2/3 IT class as the only places where the Ube2e2 guide produced even nominal transcript reduction.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: All target-transcript FDR values were 1.0; the strongest fold change occurred in the lowest-count cell type.

summary: No strong convergent or inverse perturbation neighbor emerged for Ube2e2, including the other ubiquitin-system target Ube3a.
why_it_matters: This prevents assigning Ube2e2 to a neighboring CRISPR signature or paralog module from this dataset; the best score-vector correlation was only |r|=0.120 and Ube3a correlations were essentially zero.
main_caveats: UBE2E1 and UBE2E3 were not in the perturbation panel, so true same-family redundancy could not be measured directly.

summary: Brain Ube2e2 perturbation did not reproduce the diabetes-linked gain-of-UBE2E2 biology reported in pancreatic beta cells.
why_it_matters: The diabetes literature points to UBE2E2 dosage and Nedd4-dependent ubiquitin-chain elongation in beta-cell mass control, whereas the mouse-brain perturbation produced no FDR-supported neuronal response; disease interpretation should therefore keep tissue and direction of perturbation separate.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq experiment assayed brain neurons, not pancreatic beta cells, and perturbed Ube2e2 downward rather than modeling overexpression or the noncoding human diabetes allele.

summary: The weak brain transcriptomic readout should not be interpreted as a clean CNS-safety result for future UBE2E2 modulators.
why_it_matters: Open Targets did not report an approved or clinical UBE2E2-directed modality, so any therapeutic strategy is early; the Perturb-seq data provide a useful negative brain-transcription screen but were under-engaged for the target transcript.
main_caveats: No proteomic ubiquitination endpoint, weak target-transcript reduction, and no drug-like exposure were measured.

direction: Spast mRNA down; downstream response weak
summary: Spast perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: even the best target-transcript decrease produced no FDR-significant downstream response.
why_it_matters: Spastin is a catalytic microtubule-severing HSP protein, so a nearly silent acute single-cell RNA response argues that the disease-relevant deficit is not captured well by broad steady-state mRNA changes in these brain cell classes.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: On-target depletion is measured at RNA level only and never reaches target-transcript FDR<0.05; Pvalb still has only 104 perturbed cells.

summary: The largest nominal Spast signatures were cell-type-private and did not scale with Spast mRNA depletion.
why_it_matters: The response pattern argues against a uniform pan-neuronal transcriptional stress program after Spast perturbation, despite broad SPAST brain expression annotations.
cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: All genes in the cell-type-private signatures are nominal only; differences may reflect cell number, cell state, or incomplete target engagement.

summary: Spast signatures did not resemble Atl1, Reep1, Reep2, or Atl3 signatures even though these proteins are linked to the same tubular-ER HSP module.
why_it_matters: Physical and disease-module proximity did not translate into transcriptomic interchangeability; ER-shaping perturbations should not be assumed to be equivalent in this assay.
main_caveats: The contrast uses whole-transcriptome score correlations dominated by weak Spast signatures; Atl3 was co-measured in only 15 of the 22 Spast cell types.

summary: A weak pooled organelle-membrane signal is detectable, but it is scattered across cell types rather than a coherent per-cell ESCRT/ER program.
why_it_matters: The nominal genes point in the broad direction of spastin endosome, ER, and ESCRT biology, preserving a hypothesis for follow-up without overstating FDR-negative evidence.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|053 Sst Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The module appears only after pooling nominal P<0.001 genes across cell types; pathway enrichment used an exploratory input list with no FDR-significant individual genes.

summary: The absence of a robust RNA signature after Spast perturbation should not be read as safety of lowering spastin.
why_it_matters: SPAST is the SPG4 disease gene and emerging therapeutic logic aims to restore, not inhibit, spastin; this dataset shows that disease-relevant loss of spastin can be nearly invisible to short-timescale transcriptional readouts.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not measure axonal transport, ER morphology, microtubules, motor function, or long-term neurodegeneration.

direction: strongest in subcortical and midbrain/hypothalamic classes; weak or absent in many cortical/hippocampal classes
summary: Detectable Xpo1 gain produced a strongly subcortical response; most cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic classes were buffered or had weak target engagement.
why_it_matters: A core nuclear export receptor would be expected to be broadly consequential, but the measured response concentrated in thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, and hindbrain-associated classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Cell-type differences combine biology with guide activity, target accessibility, and cell-count effects; two dataset cell classes lacked an Xpo1 signature altogether.

summary: Responsive Xpo1 targeting repeatedly induced Arrdc3/Slc16a6/Vamp2/Sun2-like transcripts while repressing an RNA-processing module headed by Snrnp70, Pabpn1, Arglu1, and Srsf-family genes.
why_it_matters: The endogenous transcriptional consequence of excess Xpo1 in neurons was not a single canonical cargo pathway; it was an RNP/RNA-processing state coupled to a stereotyped compensatory induced module.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The assay measures steady-state transcripts, not XPO1 protein level, NES-cargo localization, or direct cargo export.

direction: Tpr convergent; other nuclear-transport comparators heterogeneous
summary: Tpr activation was the recurrent Xpo1-like nuclear-pore perturbation, whereas Xpo7, Ranbp2, Nup93, and Kpna3 were not broadly interchangeable with Xpo1.
why_it_matters: A topological neighbor at the nuclear pore basket phenocopied Xpo1 more reproducibly than exportin/importin paralogs, focusing the phenotype on the CRM1-nuclear-pore interface rather than generic karyopherin abundance.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were calculated only on the top 250 Xpo1 response genes per cell type and are transcriptomic similarity scores, not proof of molecular interaction inside these cells.

direction: endogenous Snrnp70/Srsf transcripts down under Xpo1, but Snrnp70/Srsf1 perturbation signatures positively correlated with Xpo1
summary: Snrnp70 and Srsf1 perturbations aligned positively with Xpo1 signatures even though endogenous Snrnp70 and Srsf-family transcripts were repressed by Xpo1 targeting.
why_it_matters: The negative RBP transcripts are unlikely to be a simple linear loss-of-Snrnp70 driver; both gain of Xpo1 and gain of selected splicing-factor targets can lead cells toward a shared RNA-processing stress state.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The comparison used restricted signatures and target activation, so it identifies network convergence rather than the sign of a direct regulatory edge.

direction: target transcript up; inhibitor pharmacology would block XPO1
summary: The dataset is a gain-of-Xpo1 transcript model and did not show FDR-level transcriptional activation of a small WNT/TGF-beta/p53 cargo sentinel panel, so it should not be interpreted as a selinexor-like XPO1-inhibition signature.
why_it_matters: XPO1 is clinically inhibited in oncology; the Perturb-seq response is directionally opposite at the target and mainly highlights neuronal modules to monitor under altered export flux.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Absence of sentinel transcript changes cannot exclude protein relocalization, post-translational signaling, or drug-specific effects.

summary: Arrdc3 is a sensitive positive marker of cellular perturbation after Xpo1 targeting but is not specific for complete Xpo1 engagement.
why_it_matters: Arrdc3 was the most recurrently induced transcript, yet it occurred as the only significant gene in Pvalb and CNU-MGE GABA classes where Xpo1 itself was not significantly increased; it should be paired with Slc16a6 and Snrnp70/Pabpn1 repression to score the full response.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: Specificity was assessed only within the Xpo1-targeted rows summarized here; other perturbations may also induce Arrdc3.

summary: Sp4 perturbation produced a multiple-testing-corrected transcriptomic response almost exclusively in thalamic and midbrain glutamatergic neurons.
why_it_matters: SP4 is a broadly expressed nuclear transcription factor, so the dataset argues that its measured transcriptional liability is highly state- or cell-class-limited rather than pan-neuronal.
comparators: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The two responsive classes also had the largest Sp4 perturbed-cell counts, so weaker responses in lower-powered classes could be missed.

summary: The two active Sp4 signatures converged on an upregulated Tsga10/Abhd11-centered module, with Dnajc4, Svip, and Strada recurring at FDR or strong nominal support.
why_it_matters: The recurrence makes these genes better Sp4-response biomarkers than any one cell-type-specific hit and suggests that the active TH and MB glutamatergic responses share a noncanonical core.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Only Tsga10 and Abhd11 were FDR<0.05 in both cell classes; Dnajc4, Svip, and Strada rely on one FDR call plus nominal replication.

summary: Most Sp4-assigned neuronal classes were buffered or below detection at the transcriptome-wide level.
why_it_matters: Nominal Sp4 mRNA movement without FDR-corrected downstream genes, especially outside 151 and 155, argues against propagating the TH/MB gene program to all Sp4-expressing neurons.
comparators: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut|012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Zero FDR hits can reflect low power, weaker editing, or true biological buffering; the parquet does not contain gRNA indel or SP4 protein measurements.

summary: The active whole-brain Sp4 signatures did not recapitulate the canonical cerebellar Sp4--NMDAR1/NT3/Nwk2 mRNA axis.
why_it_matters: SP4 disease literature emphasizes dendrite pruning and NMDAR regulation, but Grin1, Ntf3, and Fchsd1/Nwk2 were not FDR-altered in the responsive TH/MB glutamatergic classes, refining that pathway to a developmental and cell-context-specific mechanism.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The prior studies assayed developing cerebellar granule neurons or hypomorphic mouse tissue and often measured NR1 protein rather than Grin1 mRNA.

summary: Sp4's responsive signatures were not shared by assayed SP/KLF-family perturbations or by any close atlas-wide signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The weak correlations with Sp7 and Klf perturbations argue that the Sp4 output is factor-specific, not a generic GC-box zinc-finger transcription-factor stress response.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The neighbor analysis used the top 500 absolute Sp4 genes rather than full-transcriptome correlations; Sp1 and Sp3 were not assayed as perturbations.

summary: The Sp4 transcript itself increased in Sp4-assigned cells instead of showing transcript depletion.
why_it_matters: Sp4 mRNA is therefore an inducible readout or retained mutant transcript in this dataset, not a direct proxy for SP4 protein loss.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
main_caveats: The dataset tests RNA abundance; nuclease-induced coding edits can leave stable transcripts, and SP4 protein was not measured.

summary: Direct SP4 inhibition is a risky therapeutic direction for neuropsychiatric disease models.
why_it_matters: Human SP4 is linked to schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, no conventional SP4 small-molecule mechanism was found in ChEMBL, and the mouse Perturb-seq response shows that altering Sp4 can perturb selected glutamatergic neuron programs; restoration or circuit-specific strategies would be safer hypotheses than untargeted inhibition.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Disease associations and the mouse Perturb-seq signatures do not establish a cell-autonomous therapeutic direction or show that increasing SP4 would rescue disease.

summary: Sv2a perturbation depleted its own transcript across many neuronal classes but produced no FDR-significant non-target transcriptome.
why_it_matters: This is a strong negative result: the primary cell-autonomous consequence in this assay is Sv2a mRNA loss, consistent with SV2A acting through presynaptic vesicle physiology rather than through a broad transcriptional program.
main_caveats: Perturb-seq measures steady-state mRNA, not vesicle release, protein abundance, or network excitability.

summary: The Pvalb and Sst interneuron classes that are seizure-relevant in conditional Sv2a knockout studies were transcriptomically buffered after Sv2a mRNA knockdown.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates target engagement from downstream mRNA remodeling in the same inhibitory subclasses that literature nominates as critical for SV2A-dependent seizure control.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: The Sst arm has only 39 perturbed cells and the assay does not measure firing or secretion, so functional interneuron vulnerability could be present without an mRNA signature.

summary: Sv2a loss did not transcriptionally induce or repress a curated synaptic-vesicle/SNARE-neighbor panel.
why_it_matters: Lack of coordinated changes in Syp, Snap25, Syt2, Synapsins, Complexins, and Stxbp1 argues against a simple compensatory mRNA response of the vesicle-release apparatus under the sampled conditions.
main_caveats: The gene panel is transcript-level and does not test SV2B or SV2C directly because those paralogs were absent from the perturbation target list.

summary: The Sv2a signature is not interchangeable with all presynaptic perturbations: Stxbp1 produced many non-target DE genes in matched cells whereas Syp, Cplx1, Gad1, and Sv2a were target-dominant.
why_it_matters: Presynaptic genes can be functionally related yet differ sharply in whether their perturbation is coupled to detectable cell-autonomous transcriptional remodeling.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Comparison uses gene-level perturbation summaries and does not prove that the transcriptional response is a direct vesicle-fusion consequence.

summary: A transcript-lowering Sv2a perturbation should not be interpreted as mimicking levetiracetam or brivaracetam, which are SV2A modulators rather than expression knockdowns.
why_it_matters: The flat mRNA response after Sv2a loss is compatible with strong human and mouse disease relevance and with SV2A druggability; it warns against screening SV2A ligands by expecting a large cell-autonomous knockdown signature.
main_caveats: The dataset contains genetic downregulation only, not exposure to SV2A-binding antiseizure compounds.

summary: A whole-signature neighbor scan found no robust positive or negative perturbation neighbor for Sv2a.
why_it_matters: The largest correlations were small and occurred among unrelated targets, so apparent nearest neighbors should be treated as noise-level exploratory hits rather than pathway convergence.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed over mostly flat one-vs-control signatures; they are useful for ruling out large convergence but not for ranking subtle mechanisms.

summary: Rgma knockdown did not create a defensible loss-of-Rgma transcriptional state in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: Known RGMA biology is strong, but this Perturb-seq target should be interpreted primarily as a weak-engagement negative because the target transcript itself and all downstream genes failed FDR correction.
main_caveats: The conclusion is limited to scRNA transcript readout and does not prove absence of RGMA protein perturbation or absence of extracellular RGMA signaling.

summary: The only coherent Rgma nominal footprint was concentrated in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA cells.
why_it_matters: Pde1b, Scn4b, Ano3, Rasd2, Tbc1d8, and Rgs9 formed the top nominal up arm in a basal-ganglia GABA class; this is the best biomarker hypothesis in the run, but every member remained FDR-nonsignificant.
cell_types: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA
main_caveats: This cell type still lacked significant Rgma target-transcript depletion and its best genes had FDR values of 0.391 to 0.437.

summary: Rgma was not transcriptionally interchangeable with Neogenin, Hjv, or BMP-receptor perturbations.
why_it_matters: Because RGMA is a NEO1 ligand and BMP coreceptor, convergence with Neo1 or BMPR-family knockdowns was expected if the screen captured the canonical cell-autonomous pathway; correlations stayed near zero even where Bmpr2 itself was knocked down effectively.
main_caveats: Correlation is a restricted transcriptomic comparison; weak Rgma target engagement can erase real pathway similarity.

summary: The screen does not model the extracellular anti-RGMA therapeutic mechanism closely enough to nominate a neuronal disease-reversal signature.
why_it_matters: RGMA-neutralizing therapy is being pursued with an antibody against a cell-surface/extracellular cue in injured or inflammatory CNS settings, whereas this dataset perturbs Rgma transcripts in mostly glutamatergic and GABAergic neuronal classes and shows no FDR-significant response.
main_caveats: This is a model-match warning, not evidence against RGMA neutralization in demyelination, stroke, or spinal-cord injury.

summary: Large nominal effects in 217 P MY Pineal Glut should be treated as a low-cell-count artifact candidate rather than a biological Rgma program.
why_it_matters: The rarest tested Rgma class produced fold-changes above one log unit in both directions, but only 22 perturbed cells and FDR=1 make these genes unsuitable as biomarkers.
cell_types: 217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Low power and no correction support; not interpreted mechanistically.

summary: Genome-wide signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a strong hidden perturbation state for Rgma.
why_it_matters: The largest non-self neighbors were modest and idiosyncratic, so neither top positive nor top negative neighbors rescue a canonical RGM/BMP/neogenin interpretation.
main_caveats: Pearson correlations used whole measured score vectors and do not exclude a local effect on a small subset of genes.

summary: Snrpb perturbation did not achieve robust measured depletion of the Snrpb transcript in any assayed mouse-brain cell class.
why_it_matters: This makes the main Snrpb result a target-engagement caution: weak downstream expression changes cannot be read as evidence that SmB/B' is dispensable.
main_caveats: The evidence is based on total Snrpb mRNA; protein depletion or isoform-specific effects were not measured.

summary: Foxp1 up-regulation in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut was the sole FDR-significant Snrpb-associated response.
why_it_matters: FOXP1 is a high-value cortical neurodevelopmental regulator, so its isolated induction is worth tracking as a neuronal-state marker even though it should not yet be interpreted as a direct SNRPB mechanism.
cell_types: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Single-gene finding in one cell type; Snrpb itself was not significantly depleted; related splicing perturbations did not reproduce Foxp1 induction.

summary: Several measured spliceosome-associated perturbations triggered large expression programs, whereas Snrpb remained nearly silent even in cell types with comparable or larger Snrpb cell counts.
why_it_matters: The contrast argues that the Snrpb null signal is not merely a generic limitation of perturbing RNA-processing genes in this dataset; it is specific to Snrpb engagement or to the SmB/SmN branch captured here.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The strongest canonical Sm-core interactors were mostly absent as perturbation targets, and Snrpb target mRNA engagement was weak.

summary: The brain/heart SmB paralog Snrpn also produced very few downstream total-expression hits despite clearer self-knockdown, converging with Snrpb as a muted SmB/SmN module.
why_it_matters: Because SmN can substitute for SmB in brain snRNPs, the parallel absence of broad gene-level responses suggests buffering or a response that is better seen at the splicing-isoform level rather than in total mRNA abundance.
main_caveats: Snrpb itself did not meet target-engagement criteria; the dataset does not directly measure snRNP composition or alternative splicing.

summary: The mouse-brain Snrpb perturbation did not reproduce the strong developmental splicing phenotypes reported for SNRPB loss in cerebro-costo-mandibular syndrome models.
why_it_matters: Human CCMS genetics and mouse neural-crest data implicate reduced SNRPB in development; the Perturb-seq profile indicates that this dataset assayed a different, weakly depleted neuronal context and should not be used to dismiss embryonic or craniofacial sensitivity.
main_caveats: Disease studies used human genetics and embryonic mouse neural crest/developing brain, whereas the dataset measured gene-level expression after perturbation in brain cell classes.

summary: The data do not support a cell-type-selective SNRPB therapeutic window from this perturbation alone.
why_it_matters: SNRPB is a broadly expressed core spliceosomal protein with only limited chemoproteomic activity evidence in ChEMBL; an apparently benign Snrpb signature here is more parsimoniously explained by weak engagement and missing splicing readouts than by selective tolerability.
main_caveats: The dataset is not a viability, dose-response, or pharmacology assay; low-count signatures further limit safety inference.

summary: Tubb3 target engagement was strong but confined to a subset of neuronal classes.
why_it_matters: The perturbation should be interpreted primarily in the ten cell types with FDR-significant Tubb3 depletion; CA/MEA, CA3/CA2-FC/DG, and several cortical or GABAergic classes are weak-engagement contexts rather than clean null phenotypes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut|022 L5 ET CTX Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Engagement can reflect baseline expression, guide capture, and sample size; low or null target knockdown cell types cannot establish absence of biological Tubb3 function.

summary: Acute Tubb3 depletion produced an almost self-only transcriptional phenotype.
why_it_matters: TUBB3 is a core microtubule subunit, yet partial transcript depletion did not create a broad immediate stress, cytoskeletal, or axon-guidance mRNA program in the measured cell bodies.

summary: Syn2 knockdown was detectable across many neuronal classes but FDR-significant on-target suppression was concentrated in three non-cortical classes: 155 MB Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 191 MB P MY GABA.

summary: Acute Syn2 perturbation produced an almost exclusively on-target mRNA phenotype with no non-Syn2 transcript reaching FDR<0.05 in any cell class.

summary: The Perturb-seq phenotype is much narrower than the seizure, ASD-like and synaptic-vesicle phenotypes reported after Syn2 loss, implying that expression alone is a poor proxy for the electrophysiologic disease mechanism.

cell_types: 155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA

summary: Syn2 mRNA itself was the only robust biomarker of successful Syn2 perturbation; the leading non-target candidates such as Alg10b, Kat14 and Fam91a1 were nominal and cell-class restricted.

cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut

direction: loss-of-function with no genome-wide FDR response

direction: loss-of-function risk despite weak acute RNA signal

summary: Zfhx2 perturbation produced no FDR-significant downstream transcriptional response in any assayed brain group.

summary: The dataset did not recapitulate the ZFHX2 nociceptor-pain program that dominates Marsili-syndrome biology.

main_caveats: The assayed cells are annotated brain classes rather than dorsal-root-ganglion nociceptors, and many nociceptor markers are probably lowly expressed in this dataset.

direction: warning against extrapolating the null brain signature to analgesic efficacy
summary: The analgesic interest in lowering ZFHX2 activity lacks a robust brain-cell transcriptomic response or curated small-molecule/pathway handle in these datasets and databases.
why_it_matters: Habib et al. proposed ZFHX2-regulated genes as potential analgesic targets, but the Perturb-seq data provide no reliable brain biomarker for monitoring Zfhx2 inhibition and database searches did not reveal a ChEMBL target record or Reactome pathway placement for the transcription factor.
main_caveats: A brain Perturb-seq assay is indirect for peripheral pain biology and absence of a ChEMBL record is not proof that ZFHX2 or downstream effectors are undruggable.

summary: Acute Slc1a2 knockdown in the three FDR-engaged neuronal classes stopped almost entirely at the target transcript.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|046 CTX-CGE GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: These genes may be low or dropout-prone in neuronal clusters, so absence of induction is most informative within the assay and not proof that astrocytes would fail to compensate.

direction: Slc1a2 buffered; Grin perturbations active; correlations near zero
summary: Slc1a2 knockdown was transcriptionally uncoupled from NMDA-receptor subunit perturbations in matched excitatory neurons.

cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut

summary: The neuronal Perturb-seq result should not be read as refuting astrocytic GLT-1 disease biology or as validating neuron-autonomous GLT-1 up-regulation.
why_it_matters: Disease and therapeutic literature centers on extracellular glutamate clearance, astrocytes, seizures, and transporter function; this dataset largely samples neuronal subclasses and shows only on-target transcript depletion, so it narrows the usable biomarker window to target knockdown rather than disease-relevant protection or toxicity.
main_caveats: Different developmental stage, species-to-human translation, perturbation direction, and absence of astrocytes all limit clinical extrapolation.

summary: Sar1b target engagement was concentrated in five neuronal classes rather than evenly distributed across all tested brain cell types.
