main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity was inferred from target mRNA depletion in aggregate guide groups; guide identities and protein depletion were not available.

summary: Even the target-engaged Sar1b perturbations produced a buffered transcriptional phenotype with no FDR-significant non-target genes and no repeated nominal downstream module.
why_it_matters: SAR1B is a core vesicle-biogenesis GTPase, so the absence of a broad RNA response argues that acute or partial perturbation in these neurons is either functionally buffered or manifested mainly through post-transcriptional trafficking phenotypes.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: All downstream genes were below FDR significance; transcriptome buffering does not exclude ER-exit, cargo secretion, or proteostasis defects.

summary: The dataset did not show transcriptional induction of the Sar1a paralog or a recurrent COPII-compensation program after Sar1b repression.
why_it_matters: SAR1A/SAR1B overlap is a plausible buffer, but this experiment suggests that any compensation in neurons is not achieved by recurrent Sar1a mRNA up-regulation or by a uniform increase in core COPII transcripts.
main_caveats: Only mRNA compensation was tested; Sar1a was not itself a perturbation target in this dataset, and several COPII-related genes were nominal single-cell-type hits.

summary: Sar1b did not phenocopy Sec23a or Sec31a transcriptomically, despite all three encoding COPII coat-cycle components.
why_it_matters: The contrast warns against using annotated complex membership alone to impute Perturb-seq similarity; different COPII nodes, partial engagement, and outer-coat guide efficacy can yield non-equivalent neuronal signatures.
main_caveats: Sec31a target engagement was weak or directionally inconsistent, and Sar1b downstream signals were weak; the finding is based on whole-signature correlations rather than FDR-significant shared genes.

summary: The mouse-brain Sar1b signatures did not recapitulate the lipoprotein-export or mTORC1/leucine transcriptional contexts that dominate SAR1B literature.
why_it_matters: Known SAR1B disease biology is driven by cargo-selective lipoprotein transport in intestine and liver and by a nutrient-sensing interaction; this neuronal dataset instead shows target knockdown without recurrent Surf4/APO or mTOR-pathway transcript changes.
main_caveats: APOB was largely not expressed/measured in the brain dataset; mTORC1 activity is usually regulated post-translationally, so phospho-signaling could be missed by RNA-seq.

direction: Tardbp down with downstream response strongest in discrete thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and GABAergic groups
summary: Tardbp knockdown produced a strongly cell-type-restricted transcriptomic response: the target transcript fell in every measured cell class, but broad non-target programs concentrated in thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and selected GABAergic classes rather than all cortical classes.
why_it_matters: The response is not just a uniform housekeeping consequence of lowering a ubiquitous RNA-binding protein; neuronal subtype context dictates how much of the TDP-43 loss-of-function program becomes visible as 3' gene-expression change.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut
main_caveats: The trend is based on FDR-level 3' expression summaries and is partly affected by per-cell-type perturbation counts and target engagement.

summary: A recurrent noncanonical Tardbp response module was directionally coherent across sensitive cell types: Ppp6c, Fam219a, Usp15, Brms1l, Uggt2, Gabpa, Abcc5, Fam135a, and Sec24b repeatedly increased, whereas Snrnp70 repeatedly decreased.
why_it_matters: These genes provide scalar biomarkers of TDP-43 depletion in this dataset even though most are not the famous STMN2/UNC13A cryptic-exon markers emphasized in human motor-neuron studies.
main_caveats: The module is defined by gene-level abundance changes, not by direct TDP-43 binding or isoform measurements; pathway enrichment of these recurrent genes was not established.

direction: target down with minimal non-target DE
summary: Several cell classes with significant Tardbp transcript reduction had almost no FDR-level secondary response, most clearly 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, and 053 Sst Gaba.

summary: Slc9a9 guide-labeled cells did not achieve a validated RNA-level Slc9a9 loss-of-function and produced no FDR-significant transcriptomic response in any assayed neuronal class.

summary: The few nominal Slc9a9 hits did not assemble into the expected endosomal pH, V-ATPase, transferrin, GLAST, or glutamate-receptor trafficking program.

summary: Slc9a7, another intracellular CPA1-family Na+/H+ exchanger, was measurably knocked down in the same dataset whereas Slc9a9 was not, and Slc9a7 and Slc9a9 score vectors were essentially uncorrelated.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The two transporters act in overlapping but distinct organelles; the comparison is paralogous rather than a direct protein-complex comparison.

summary: Perturbing the V-ATPase accessory gene Atp6ap1 generated strong on-target knockdown and Atp6v0a1 RNA changes, yet its signatures did not resemble the weak Slc9a9 signatures.

summary: A panel-wide nearest-neighbor scan found no strong positive or negative Slc9a9 transcriptomic neighbor.

summary: The neuronal RNA null result refines, rather than falsifies, SLC9A9 ASD/ADHD biology because established NHE9 phenotypes center on endosomal pH, surface trafficking, astrocytes, blood-brain-barrier cells, and synaptic physiology.

main_caveats: The perturbation did not deplete Slc9a9 RNA, and the dataset lacks direct pH, surface-protein, behavior, astrocyte, and endothelial readouts.

summary: The lack of Slc9a9 DE should not be read as evidence that SLC9A9 inhibition is benign or disease-corrective.
why_it_matters: Autism-associated NHE9 variants and mouse Slc9a9 inactivation are consistent with loss of function, whereas the perturbation data are dominated by absent target engagement and SLC9A9 has no established ChEMBL target pharmacology in the queried database.
main_caveats: This finding is a decision warning, not an efficacy claim for activation or gene restoration.

summary: The assay does not support a therapeutic hypothesis of lowering NKX2-1 activity in brain cells.

summary: Tlr2 perturbation was a pan-neuronal blank rather than a TLR2-response program.

summary: The weak nominal Tlr2 ranks are cell-type-private noise-like tails, not a hidden shared downstream module.
why_it_matters: A true low-amplitude TLR2 program would be expected to recur across related cell types or in score-vector correlations, but the top nominal genes had high FDR values and almost never recurred.
cell_types: all 22 Tlr2-tested neuronal classes
main_caveats: The claim is about recurrence of rank signatures, not about the biological functions of the individual nominal genes.

summary: Available TLR/PRR/NF-kB pathway-neighbor perturbations converged with Tlr2 on silence rather than revealing an interchangeable inflammatory signature.

main_caveats: The most proximal Tlr1, Tlr6, Myd88 and Tirap perturbations were absent as assayed targets, so silence cannot be tested for every complex member.

summary: DG-containing glutamatergic classes did not reproduce reported TLR2-dependent adult neurogenesis phenotypes at the acute mature-neuronal RNA level.
why_it_matters: TLR2 has been implicated in adult hippocampal progenitor biology, but the 012 and 017 DG/hippocampal classes were as silent as the rest of the neuronal panel, separating an NPC or niche-level role from direct acute transcriptional dependence in these captured neurons.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: The dataset does not isolate adult neural progenitor cells or directly measure neurogenesis, so this is a context refinement rather than a disproof of the in vivo finding.

summary: For neuroinflammatory disease, this dataset points away from broad direct neuronal transcriptomic effects as the main expected consequence of TLR2 blockade.
why_it_matters: TLR2 has glial neuroinflammation and Alzheimer-model literature and curated drug-discovery/clinical entries, yet Tlr2 and related PRR perturbations were silent in basal neuronal classes; target effects of TLR2 antagonism in the brain are therefore more plausibly ligand-, glia-, or disease-state-dependent than pan-neuronal.
cell_types: all 22 Tlr2-tested neuronal classes
main_caveats: No disease challenge, microglia, astrocytes, peripheral immune cells, protein readout, or antibody pharmacology was measured.

summary: Tenm4 perturbation produced no FDR-significant transcriptional response across 22 neuronal cell types.
why_it_matters: This prevents strong pathway calls from being made from nominal single-gene changes and indicates that the Perturb-seq transcriptome largely buffered or failed to detect Tenm4 loss.
main_caveats: FDR was computed over many genes; weak or sparse Tenm4 mRNA detection could obscure protein perturbation.

summary: Nominal Tenm4 self-depletion was concentrated in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut rather than being pan-neuronal.
why_it_matters: The best support for on-target perturbation comes from two glutamatergic classes; most other classes should not be interpreted for Tenm4 downstream biology.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The two best self rows still did not reach FDR<0.05, so the selectivity is based on relative nominal target engagement.

summary: Tenm4 did not share a coherent score-vector signature with Tenm3, Adgrl1, Adgrl2, Adgrl3, or Flrt3 despite their known adhesion relationships.
why_it_matters: A structural teneurin-latrophilin relationship should not be treated as evidence that these perturbations are transcriptomically interchangeable in this neuronal assay.
main_caveats: Signature correlations are restricted-signature summaries and all non-self transcriptional responses were weak.

summary: Cntn2 down and Neo1 up in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut are an exploratory adhesion and axon-guidance marker hypothesis for Tenm4 depletion.
why_it_matters: These genes provide the only nominal link between the best target-engaged neuronal class and the cell-adhesion biology expected for a teneurin.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Both genes were nominal only; Cntn2 FDR was 0.732565 and Neo1 FDR was 1.0.

summary: The negative neuronal Perturb-seq result is best read as a context mismatch with TENM4 disease mechanisms centered on myelination, axon guidance, and dominant missense effects.
why_it_matters: It avoids overclaiming that lack of DE falsifies TENM4 involvement in tremor or psychiatric disease and redirects follow-up toward oligodendrocyte, synapse, morphology, or variant-specific models.
main_caveats: The dataset did not assay oligodendrocytes and used knockdown rather than the pathogenic human missense alleles.

summary: Upf3b perturbation produced a focused Inpp5f induction concentrated in six subcortical, thalamic, midbrain, or hindbrain neuronal classes, with Inpp5f positive in every measured Upf3b cell type.
why_it_matters: The only FDR-significant output of Upf3b perturbation is a phosphoinositide/endocytic regulator, nominating Inpp5f as a cell-type-skewed biomarker of the perturbation rather than a broad canonical NMD target set.
cell_types: 054 CNU-MGE GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Single-gene gene-level signal; the dataset does not show that Inpp5f is a direct NMD substrate, and Upf3b mRNA engagement was weak.

summary: The Upf3b gene-level response is much narrower than a broad NMD/EJC transcriptional program: only Inpp5f cleared FDR and core NMD-factor mRNAs were not significantly regulated.
why_it_matters: UPF3B is an EJC-linked NMD factor, so a widespread increase in NMD-sensitive mRNAs would have been expected under strong loss of function; the dataset instead supports either weak engagement, branch-selective NMD inhibition, or buffering.
main_caveats: The target transcript was not significantly depleted, and gene-level DE cannot detect isoform-specific NMD effects.

summary: Across the full perturbation panel, Upf3b was the most recurrent nominal positive regulator of Inpp5f, ahead of Hnrnpc, Srsf1, and Xrn1.
why_it_matters: This makes the Inpp5f response an Upf3b-skewed cross-perturbation feature rather than a random isolated hit, while also identifying RNA-processing or decay neighbors that partially converge on the same gene.
main_caveats: Defined by nominal recurrence for one measured gene; direct UPF3B paralogs and core NMD/EJC factors were not perturbation targets.

summary: The many zero-FDR Upf3b cell types fit a buffered UPF3B branch model, but the Perturb-seq data do not show Upf3a or SMG transcriptional compensation.

summary: The few downstream hits were isolated and cell-type restricted rather than a recurrent Trmt1 pathway.

main_caveats: Species, developmental stage, perturbation completeness, and assay readout differ from human germline disease and fibroblast/cell-line studies.

summary: The sparse mRNA signature should not be interpreted as evidence that pharmacologic TRMT1 inhibition would be safe.
why_it_matters: TRMT1 is linked to recessive neurodevelopmental disease, and the measured knockdown was partial; no broad mRNA injury in this assay is therefore a poor de-risking endpoint for a tRNA-modifying enzyme.

summary: Genome-wide Trmt1 signature-neighbor correlations were weak in every cell type.
why_it_matters: The perturbation lacks a strong correlated positive or anti-correlated neighbor that would justify assigning an additional pathway solely from signature geometry.

main_caveats: Pearson correlations over all measured genes can miss convergence confined to a small gene set.

summary: Nt5c2 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered in mouse brain neuronal classes: the target mRNA usually trended downward, but no Nt5c2 target-transcript row was FDR-significant and only one of 371,818 rows passed FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: NT5C2 is a conserved purine-catabolic enzyme, so a weak mRNA program argues that partial loss in mature neurons is not sensed as a broad cell-stress or nucleotide-metabolism transcriptional state in this assay.
main_caveats: The target transcript was only nominally reduced in 6 of 22 classes and the assay measures RNA rather than IMP/GMP, inosine/guanosine, or enzymatic flux.

summary: Nominal on-target Nt5c2 mRNA reduction was concentrated in six classes: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 155 MB Glut, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, while most cortical and hippocampal classes showed weak target-transcript shifts.
why_it_matters: Because Human Protein Atlas annotates NT5C2 as broadly detected across brain regions, this selectivity is more likely to reflect perturbation delivery, guide efficacy, or cell-state buffering than a simple absence of the gene from other brain regions.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|155 MB Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: None of the target-transcript reductions survived within-signature FDR correction; apparent selectivity could be technical.

summary: Assayed purine or adenosine neighbors did not phenocopy Nt5c2: Nt5c2 signatures were essentially uncorrelated with Adk, Adora2a, Guk1, and Nme7 perturbations across matched cell classes.
why_it_matters: Reactome places NT5C2 in IMP/GMP catabolism, but pathway adjacency did not translate into an interchangeable cell-state signature, consistent with metabolite-level regulation being insulated from steady-state RNA output.
main_caveats: The comparison is transcriptomic and full-signature correlations can miss metabolite changes or sparse effects on a few enzymatic genes.

summary: The mouse-brain in vivo dataset did not recapitulate the strong NT5C2-knockdown AMPK/protein-translation program reported in human neural progenitor cells.
why_it_matters: Schizophrenia-associated reduced NT5C2 expression may act in a developmental, species-specific, or post-transcriptional metabolic context rather than by launching a large transcriptional AMPK module in every mature neuron.
main_caveats: The perturbation was partial and nominal; AMPK activity and RPS6 phosphorylation were not measured directly.

summary: Nt5c2 was not transcriptionally interchangeable with the available chromosome 10q24 neighboring perturbations Cnnm2 and Arl3.
why_it_matters: Human schizophrenia GWAS variation at 10q24 can cis-regulate several nearby genes, and the mouse perturbation data argue against collapsing that locus into a single shared neuron-autonomous transcriptome in the assayed brain classes.
main_caveats: Borcs7 and As3mt, two key 10q24 cis-regulated genes, were not present as perturbations in the dataset.

summary: The only adjusted hit, Ddx50 down-regulation in 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut, was isolated and occurred in a cell class where Nt5c2 itself was not detectably reduced.
why_it_matters: This keeps a nominal-looking FDR result from being overinterpreted as a recurrent DDX50 or ribosome-biogenesis axis downstream of Nt5c2.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: A true L4/5-specific Ddx50 effect cannot be excluded, but it lacked both target-transcript support and recurrence.

summary: Brain-cell transcriptomic readouts are likely to be insensitive pharmacodynamic markers for NT5C2 inhibition compared with direct metabolite or thiopurine-toxicity assays.
why_it_matters: In leukemia, activating NT5C2 mutations confer resistance by increasing nucleoside-analog turnover; the weak neuronal RNA response here warns that target engagement in non-dividing brain cells may have to be monitored biochemically rather than by a robust mRNA signature.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay modeled partial genetic loss, not acute allosteric inhibition or thiopurine challenge.

summary: Safe_target_21 is transcriptomically inert at FDR level across the tested mouse-brain cell types.
why_it_matters: This makes Safe_target_21 suitable as an RNA-level null guide for this run and argues against interpreting its nominal hits as a target-driven biology module.
main_caveats: RNA-seq cannot verify editing at the safe locus or rule out rare genomic off-target cuts; 215 MB Dopa was not tested for this perturbation.

summary: The strongest Safe_target_21 nominal hits are single-cell-type events rather than a repeated pathway or gene module.
why_it_matters: It prevents over-calling Tet2, Ablim2, Syne1, or other small-p genes as downstream Safe_target_21 biology when their FDR values remain non-significant and recurrence is absent.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: This is a negative pathway conclusion from nominal DE summaries, not a formal enrichment test.

summary: Safe_target_21 is not an outlier among safe-target controls, whereas a few other Safe_target labels show isolated FDR-significant rows.
why_it_matters: The control family itself has to be empirically screened; Safe_target_21 is among the controls that remained null in this table.
main_caveats: The comparison uses only safe-target labels present in the DE table and does not use guide-sequence off-target models.

summary: No gene perturbation or safe-target perturbation forms a strong positive or negative signature-neighbor relationship with Safe_target_21.
why_it_matters: Top-neighbor analysis did not uncover a hidden target-like Safe_target_21 phenotype that would warrant pathway assignment or disease-target interpretation.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA
main_caveats: Correlations were computed from Wilcoxon score vectors, not from raw expression or replicate-level pseudobulk.

direction: Smarcb1 down; 149 genes down and 137 genes up at FDR<0.05 in the selective 151 response
summary: Smarcb1 loss produced a broad, FDR-resolved transcriptional response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: A ubiquitous chromatin-remodeling subunit did not yield a uniform pan-neuronal phenotype; the main interpretable effect is a specific state in one TH/Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class.
comparators: 155 MB Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|other Smarcb1 cell-type contrasts
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The Smarcb1 transcript itself was only FDR 0.0936 in 151 and protein depletion was not measured.

why_it_matters: Finding the closest transcriptomic phenocopies among physical SWI/SNF subunits argues that the 151 phenotype is BAF-complex biology rather than a guide-specific orphan effect.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The strongest correlations were computed on the 500 genes with the largest absolute Smarcb1 scores; whole-transcriptome correlations were lower but preserved the same BAF ordering.

direction: Smarcb1/Smarcc2 broad response contrasted with weak or absent ATPase/common-subunit responses
summary: Smarcb1 was not interchangeable with all SWI/SNF perturbations: Smarca2 knockdown and several common-subunit perturbations failed to phenocopy the Smarcb1/Smarcc2 response in 151.
why_it_matters: The dataset separates a SMARCB1-SMARCC2-SMARCE1/ARID axis from ATPase or weakly engaged common-subunit perturbations, warning against interpreting every BAF subunit as an equivalent node.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Some negative comparators, especially Smarcc1 and Smarca4, also had weak target-transcript depletion; only the Smarca2 contrast combines strong target-mRNA reduction with little downstream response.

direction: mixed: NMDA/postsynaptic effector genes down; Calsyntenin/Grm5/Syt4-associated genes up

why_it_matters: Downregulation of Grin1/Grin2b/Grin2c/Camk2a/Shank1 occurred alongside upregulation of Calsyntenins, Syt4, Grm5, Dagla, and Rims3, suggesting a rewired synaptic state instead of a generic loss of neuronal transcripts.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The pathway label comes from known gene annotations and enrichment of the DE gene set; the assay measured mRNA rather than receptor abundance or synaptic physiology.

direction: buffered or underpowered relative to the 151 response
summary: Several cell types with nominal Smarcb1 target reduction showed little or no FDR-resolved downstream response.
why_it_matters: The absence of broad DE in 022 L5 ET, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM, 145 MH-LH TH, and 191 MB P MY GABA makes the 151 response a selective vulnerability rather than a universal consequence of any measurable Smarcb1 mRNA decrease.
cell_types: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: Nominal target-transcript reduction was not FDR-significant in these classes, so buffering cannot be cleanly separated from weaker editing, transcript detection, or power.

summary: The neuronal loss-of-function signature and SMARCB1 tumor-suppressor genetics jointly argue against treating SMARCB1 inhibition as a benign way to tune BAF output in SMARCB1-intact brain cells.
why_it_matters: SMARCB1 is a disease gene whose deficiency defines tumor and neurodevelopmental contexts; the Perturb-seq response shows that partial loss can perturb synaptic gene programs in a susceptible glutamatergic class, whereas oncology trials target EZH2-related dependencies of SMARCB1-deficient tumors rather than SMARCB1 itself.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset is a mouse-brain mRNA perturbation assay and does not test tumor fitness, EZH2 inhibition, or rescue of SMARCB1-mutant cells.

summary: Slc4a7 produced no conventionally significant RNA-seq differential-expression response in any assayed neuronal class.
why_it_matters: SLC4A7 is a plasma-membrane bicarbonate transporter, so this genome-wide null means that this Perturb-seq contrast should not be interpreted as a captured loss-of-function pH phenotype.
main_caveats: RNA knockdown was itself weak; the assay may miss acute transporter physiology or protein-level loss.

summary: The only nominal self-knockdown signal appeared in 052 Pvalb Gaba and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, but both cell types had only isolated near-FDR downstream rows rather than a coherent response.

cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Nominal seed only; all Slc4a7 self rows had FDR=1.0 and all downstream rows had FDR>=0.143.

summary: Slc4a7 signatures were essentially orthogonal to perturbations of other assayed pH and ion-transport genes.
why_it_matters: Within the limits of the target set, the weak Slc4a7 signature is not a reusable bicarbonate-transport or acid-base module.
main_caveats: The dataset did not contain SLC4 paralog perturbations and the correlation test used weak Slc4a7 score vectors.

summary: A genome-wide same-cell signature-neighbor search did not identify a convincing biological Slc4a7 neighbor.
why_it_matters: The strongest neighbors had |r|<0.18 and multiple safe-target controls ranked among top neighbors, arguing that the Slc4a7 profile is near the null rather than converging on a latent neuronal program.
main_caveats: Correlation of whole-transcriptome scores cannot distinguish a slight true response from residual noise when the seed perturbation is weak.

summary: The Perturb-seq null refines rather than overturns neuronal Slc4a7 biology: published knockout studies link NBCn1 to neuronal pH, NMDA injury, locomotor behavior, hearing, and alcohol phenotypes, but those phenotypes were not recapitulated as broad steady-state RNA programs here.
why_it_matters: SLC4A7 should be followed with protein, pH-imaging, and electrophysiology assays before drawing CNS therapeutic direction from this screen; transcriptome absence is not evidence that the transporter is physiologically inert.
main_caveats: Literature phenotypes come from organismal or hippocampal knockout contexts, whereas the screen measured short-term cell-class RNA changes with weak target-transcript suppression.

summary: Partial Tspoap1 perturbation was transcriptionally buffered: the target transcript trended down in most cell types, but no Tspoap1 row or downstream row reached FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: TSPOAP1/RIM-BP1 is an active-zone scaffold; the dataset indicates that modest mRNA loss in unstimulated neurons is not converted into a broad basal transcriptional state.
cell_types: all 23 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: The inference is about basal mRNA signatures only; target knockdown was modest, cell counts were 33-223 per class, and protein/function were not measured.

summary: The only FDR-near responses were two different GABAergic classes and neither gave a clean on-target RIM-BP1 program.
why_it_matters: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA contained the lowest adjusted p value but no recognizable RIM-BP effector, whereas 054 CNU-MGE GABA contained Rimbp2 and other nominal synaptic genes but lacked Tspoap1 mRNA depletion; this prevents over-calling a true paralog-compensation module.

main_caveats: Both leading rows were FDR>0.05, and the more synaptic-looking 054 CNU-MGE signature had positive rather than negative measured Tspoap1 logFC.

summary: Tspoap1 did not transcriptionally converge with available presynaptic calcium-channel or vesicle-release perturbations.
why_it_matters: RIM-BP proteins physically organize Ca2+ channels at presynaptic active zones, but Tspoap1 full-gene signatures were essentially orthogonal to Cacna, Kcnma1, Unc13, Stxbp1, Syn, and Cplx perturbations in the same cell types.
cell_types: all 23 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: Direct partners Tspo, Rims1, Rims2, Acbd3, and Rimbp2 were not perturbation targets, and weak Tspoap1 target engagement decreases sensitivity to detect convergence.

summary: The experiment is a weak partial-loss mRNA model and did not reproduce a cerebellar TSPOAP1 dystonia-like transcriptional state.
why_it_matters: Human TSPOAP1 disease involves both loss-of-function and missense alleles with opposite effects on spike-evoked release; the absent 308 CB GABA response argues that this screen should not be used alone to assign therapeutic direction or disease biomarkers.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|all 23 assayed neuronal cell classes
main_caveats: The assayed cerebellar class is bulk CB GABA, not purified Purkinje cells with electrophysiology; lack of mRNA response is not evidence of absent synaptic dysfunction.

summary: An unbiased same-cell signature-neighbor search found no strong Tspoap1-like or Tspoap1-opposing perturbation among approximately 44,110 comparisons.
why_it_matters: No high-correlation neighbor rescued a hidden pathway module; the strongest positive and negative correlations were small and arose in 308 CB GABA where Tspoap1 itself was not depleted.
cell_types: 308 CB GABA|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Correlation used Wilcoxon score vectors and can miss sparse gene-set overlap, nonlinear relationships, or effects hidden by poor on-target perturbation.

summary: Thap1 generated FDR-level expression changes in only 5 of 23 assayed neuronal cell classes, with the strongest response in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and smaller responses in 155 MB Glut, 191 MB P MY GABA, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA.
why_it_matters: The screen localizes the detectable Thap1 response to a small subset of neuronal states rather than supporting a uniform pan-neuronal THAP1 program.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: Most active cell classes had only one to three FDR genes; the assayed cell taxonomy does not map exactly onto the mouse-model or human patient contexts in the literature.

summary: Thap1 targeting did not deplete measured Thap1 RNA; the target transcript was increased in 22 of 23 cell classes and FDR-significantly increased in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Loss-of-function interpretations are unsafe without protein or editing validation because the measured transcript went in the opposite direction from knockdown.
main_caveats: Transcript abundance is an imperfect proxy for DNA editing, protein level, and THAP1 activity.

summary: Prepl down-regulation recurred in four FDR-level Thap1 signatures, and the Prepl-down, Cuedc2-down, Fam117a-up triad recurred in the three strongest Thap1 contexts.
why_it_matters: This compact module is the best reproducible downstream marker set for the Thap1 response even though it is not yet a defined canonical pathway.

main_caveats: The module is only three recurrent genes; direct Prepl perturbation did not reproduce the genome-wide Thap1 signature.

summary: Thap11, Ogt, and E2f1 did not phenocopy Thap1 in shared neuronal cell types despite representing the available THAP-family, HCF-1/OGT, and pRB/E2F-related comparators.
why_it_matters: The neuronal Thap1 response is not explained by a generic THAP-domain program, by individual Ogt perturbation, or by an E2f1-like cell-cycle signature.
main_caveats: Hcfc1 and Thap3 were not available as direct perturbation comparators; correlations are transcriptomic and same-cell within this mouse-brain screen.

summary: A restricted scan of all perturbations on high-absolute-score Thap1 genes found no strong positive or negative signature neighbor.
why_it_matters: The lack of a close look-alike argues against a single obvious upstream or downstream perturbation explaining the Thap1 state.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|052 Pvalb Gaba|054 CNU-MGE GABA
main_caveats: The scan used a 560-gene restricted Thap1 feature set and top correlations were modest, especially outside 054 CNU-MGE GABA.

summary: The DYT6-associated Thap1 transcriptional response in this dataset was selective for thalamic, midbrain, and hindbrain neuronal classes and absent at FDR level from most cortical, hippocampal, dopaminergic, and pineal glutamatergic signatures.
why_it_matters: This supports a selective-vulnerability view of THAP1 dystonia biology and cautions against treating cortical or dopaminergic neurons as uniformly responsive to Thap1 perturbation.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|215 MB Dopa|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq cell types, developmental state, and perturbation modality differ from patient cortex, iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons, and rodent disease models; 215 MB Dopa had only 22 perturbed cells.

summary: Unc5c knockdown reached transcript-level FDR only in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The dataset provides one high-confidence on-target cellular context rather than broad interpretable Unc5c loss across mouse brain cell classes.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Cell-type selectivity is measured as target mRNA knockdown in this Perturb-seq assay; it may reflect guide delivery, expression, and power rather than endogenous biological specificity alone.

summary: The engaged thalamic Unc5c knockdown was transcriptionally buffered: Pcdh9, Socs5, Kcnn2, and other top genes remained nominal while only Unc5c survived FDR.
why_it_matters: Known UNC5C signaling is receptor phosphorylation, SHP2/Src/FAK-PAK1 recruitment, and microtubule remodeling; the sparse mRNA signature implies that acute Unc5c loss did not propagate into a large steady-state transcriptional program in this cell type.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Absence of FDR-significant mRNA changes does not test rapid phosphorylation, growth-cone collapse, apoptosis, morphology, or neurite guidance phenotypes.

summary: Unc5c perturbations outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut were weak or unengaged, including nominal target reductions with FDR=1.0 and a 308 CB GABA nominal signature lacking target knockdown.

why_it_matters: UNC5C is curated and experimentally connected to DCC, DSCAM, NTN1, SRC/PTK2/PTPN11, and neogenin-family signaling, so a shared perturbation module was plausible but not observed at the transcriptome level.

main_caveats: Restricted to mRNA score-vector correlations in one cell type. Several receptor-neighbor perturbations did not have FDR-level self knockdown, so lack of convergence is not a clean epistasis result.

summary: Acute Unc5c mRNA loss did not recapitulate the AD-linked T835M death-signaling model in the engaged thalamic cells.
why_it_matters: Late-onset Alzheimer studies implicate T835M as a potentiating/gain-of-death mutation, whereas this dataset is a knockdown experiment; APP and DAPK1/PKD/ASK1/JNK transcripts stayed unchanged, supporting a mechanistic separation between loss of mRNA and T835M apoptotic stress signaling.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The AD literature used T835M overexpression or disease-variant models and neuronal death assays, not CRISPR knockdown in mature thalamic excitatory neurons; mRNA was measured instead of kinase activity or caspase activation.

summary: The dataset supports caution against using simple UNC5C inhibition as a pan-neuronal proxy for Alzheimer biology.
why_it_matters: UNC5C is a cell-surface receptor but Open Targets did not flag small-molecule tractability, and the only clean knockdown response in this screen was a buffered thalamic loss signature; a therapy aimed at AD-linked UNC5C death signaling would need to target ligand/dependence-receptor or T835M-specific mechanisms rather than assume that lowering Unc5c broadly rewires neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Therapeutic tractability is inferred from public target annotations, and the Perturb-seq dataset contains transcriptomic knockdown rather than pharmacology, apoptosis, or aging readouts.

summary: Ppt1 CRISPRi measurably depleted the target transcript in many, but not all, neuronal classes.

why_it_matters: The lack of signature convergence argues that the Lrp2 null is not a generic failure to detect LDL receptor or BMP-family perturbations, and that LRP2 is not interchangeable with paralogous receptors in the assayed neuronal transcriptomes.
main_caveats: The comparison uses score-vector correlations of weak Lrp2 signatures; several physical LRP2 partners such as Cubn and Dab2 were not targeted in this guide set.

summary: The neuronal null response is more consistent with Donnai-Barrow biology arising from early neuroepithelium, ependyma/choroid plexus, and epithelial cargo uptake than from a broad postmitotic-neuron transcriptional program.
why_it_matters: LRP2 is a Mendelian disease gene with neurodevelopmental, ocular, hearing, and renal phenotypes, so a negative result in these neuronal populations should not be used to deprioritize LRP2 loss-of-function disease mechanisms or to assume that LRP2 inhibition would be CNS-neutral.
main_caveats: The dataset does not assay the early cranial neuroepithelium, human kidney, retina, inner ear, or ependymal niche in which strong LRP2 functions are documented.

summary: Twist1 perturbation was transcriptomically silent at FDR thresholds across the neuronal panel.

summary: Zeb1 and Zeb2 had selective FDR-significant signatures while Twist1, Twist2, Snai2 and most E-protein-adjacent perturbations were largely inactive.

summary: The null adult neuronal response narrows, rather than negates, TWIST1 developmental and cancer mechanisms.
why_it_matters: Human TWIST1 disease and EMT literature point to cranial mesenchyme, calvarial osteoblasts, epithelial cancer cells and non-neuronal adult brain expression; a silent mature-neuron signature is therefore best interpreted as strong context restriction.
main_caveats: The dataset does not assay calvarial osteoblasts, cranial neural crest, epithelial tumor cells, or brain endothelial/fibroblast populations where TWIST1 biology is more directly expected.

direction: Rnpc3 down; downstream response strongest in selected thalamic, midbrain, hypothalamic, and Pvalb classes
summary: Rnpc3 knockdown produced a strongly cell-type-skewed transcriptomic phenotype despite on-target depletion in most assayed classes.
why_it_matters: RNPC3 is a core U12-dependent splicing factor, but the downstream mRNA response was not uniform; thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic, midbrain glutamatergic, hypothalamic GABA, and Pvalb GABA populations were the most responsive.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|191 MB P MY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut
main_caveats: Single-cell mRNA output was measured, not U12 intron retention; smaller cell classes have lower power.

direction: Amy1 and Tcea2 down; Pcyt2, Mapk8, Ap2a1, Wdfy1, Rab6b, Smyd2, Srp72, and Trit1 up
summary: A same-direction Rnpc3 marker module recurred across responsive classes: Amy1 was repeatedly down, while Pcyt2, Mapk8, Ap2a1, Wdfy1, Rab6b, Smyd2, Srp72, and Trit1 were repeatedly up.
why_it_matters: The recurring genes give a compact transcriptional readout of effective Rnpc3 perturbation and highlight a JNK-containing response signature whose connection to minor-spliceosome failure is dataset-derived rather than established.
main_caveats: Marker status is based on scRNA expression and a 21-cell restricted all-target panel; these are not proven direct minor-intron substrates.

direction: positive for Prpf6, Ddx23, Snrnp70, and U2af2; near-neutral for Snrpb and Snrpn
summary: On the Rnpc3 response panel, Prpf6 was the closest positive perturbation neighbor and broader spliceosome/RNA-processing factors Ddx23, Snrnp70, and U2af2 were also positively correlated, whereas Snrpb and Snrpn were nearly uncorrelated.
why_it_matters: The screen supports partial convergence with a spliceosome-centered neighborhood, but it also argues against treating every snRNP-associated perturbation as interchangeable with Rnpc3.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only on a 209-gene Rnpc3 response panel, so they are signature-neighbor metrics rather than transcriptome-wide similarities.

summary: Rnpc3 knockdown did not induce mRNA-level compensation of measured minor-spliceosome-associated factors Pdcd7, Snrnp25, Snrnp35, Snrnp48, Zcrb1, or Zrsr2.
why_it_matters: A failed U11/U12 65K component could in principle alter expression of other U11/U12 factors, but the dataset instead points to downstream cellular responses without a detectable compensatory rise in these complex genes.
main_caveats: The assay quantifies steady-state mRNA; it does not test U11/U12 snRNP protein abundance, snRNA abundance, or post-transcriptional feedback.

summary: The classes with no FDR-level response also had weak Rnpc3 transcript engagement, so they should be treated as under-engaged negative results rather than as evidence of true resistance.
why_it_matters: This prevents overcalling apparent buffering in L5-6 IT, Sst GABA, and CA3/CA2-FC/DG glutamatergic cells when the perturbation itself was not significant after correction.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|053 Sst Gaba|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Low perturbed-cell counts and nonsignificant Rnpc3 depletion confound any biological conclusion about buffering.

summary: The strong mature-neuron response in hypothalamic and other subcortical classes is directionally consistent with RNPC3 endocrine genetics but extends the affected context beyond the developing pituitary axis.
why_it_matters: Human RNPC3 disease is centered on hypopituitarism and growth-hormone deficiency, while this mouse-brain Perturb-seq dataset shows RNPC3-sensitive transcriptomes in mature hypothalamic, thalamic, and midbrain neuronal populations.
cell_types: 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut|145 MH-LH TH Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The dataset samples mouse brain cell classes rather than pituitary or ovary and measures acute transcript abundance rather than organismal endocrine phenotypes.

summary: Trhr perturbation produced neither target-transcript depletion nor any FDR-significant downstream gene in the 21 reported brain cell types.
why_it_matters: A GPCR with a defined TRH-to-phosphoinositide signaling route should be interpretable only if engaged; this dataset reads as unengaged or strongly buffered rather than as a clean TRHR loss-of-function map.

summary: The absence of a robust Trhr response in brain neuronal classes refines known TRHR loss-of-function disease genetics toward pituitary and physiological signaling contexts rather than broad steady-state neuronal RNA dependence.
why_it_matters: Mouse receptor knockout and human TRHR mutations cause central hypothyroidism, yet this screen provides no FDR-level disease-like signature in the assayed brain classes.
main_caveats: The perturb-seq dataset did not test anterior pituitary thyrotrophs or acute hormone secretion.

summary: High-cell Trhr classes remained null even though Thra, Adcy3, and Camk2b showed measurable target depletion in overlapping broad classes.
why_it_matters: The comparison argues that the null Trhr output is target-specific or engagement-specific, not simply an invariant property of all perturbations in these neuronal classes.

main_caveats: Comparator perturbations had larger perturbed-cell counts and are not one-to-one TRHR pathway members.

summary: Restricted top-gene signature matching found only weak, non-recurrent Trhr neighbors and no compelling anti-Trhr neighbor.
why_it_matters: This closes a common false-negative loophole: a subtle Trhr module is not obviously hidden among related or opposing perturbation signatures.
main_caveats: Correlations were computed only on each cell type's top 200 Trhr genes and are dominated by nominal Trhr features.

summary: Zbtb11 loss produced a sharply restricted downstream signature, dominated by 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and two midbrain classes rather than all assayed brain classes.
why_it_matters: A broadly expressed transcription factor can still expose cell-state-specific mitochondrial/RNA-processing vulnerability; the dataset therefore refines Zbtb11 biology from a ubiquitous essential regulator to a program that is detectably engaged in only selected neuronal contexts under this assay.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: FDR-gene counts covaried with perturbed-cell number, so silent classes with 22-48 perturbed cells may be underpowered; nevertheless, several similarly sized classes diverged strongly.

summary: Responding Zbtb11-perturbed neurons converged on a down-regulated mitochondrial, nucleolar/RNA-processing, and endomembrane/glycan module rather than on a single target transcript.
why_it_matters: The repeated reduction of Ndufc2, Ndufaf1, Gtpbp3, Acsf3, Rbm28, Taf1b, Stx16, Pigq, and Man2c1 connects the mouse-brain Perturb-seq signature to known ZBTB11 control of mitochondrial and RNA-processing genes while extending it to a recurring Golgi/GPI/glycan arm.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The Golgi, GPI-anchor, and glycan genes are transcriptomic co-responses; the dataset does not prove direct Zbtb11 promoter binding in the assayed neurons.

summary: Acsf3 down-regulation links the neuronal Zbtb11 signature to the biochemical branch reported in ZBTB11 patients.
why_it_matters: Patient fibroblasts with mutant ZBTB11 show reduced ZBTB11 binding at ACSF3 and decreased ACSF3 transcript; seeing Acsf3 as a recurrently decreased neuronal transcript suggests that the malonate/methylmalonate arm is not fibroblast-restricted and may be a useful readout of Zbtb11 loss in vulnerable brain cells.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The sequencing data measure Acsf3 RNA only; no malonic or methylmalonic acid metabolites were measured.

summary: Zbtb11 did not phenocopy direct complex-I knockdown: individual Nduf and Ndufaf perturbations were transcriptionally buffered in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: Because ZBTB11 is upstream of nuclear complex-I gene expression, a broad Zbtb11 signature could have been a generic response to complex-I impairment. The lack of a broad response after direct Nduf/Ndufaf perturbation argues instead for a Zbtb11-specific regulatory collapse or multi-gene threshold effect.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The comparison is one cell class and uses transcriptomic outcomes; the direct Nduf perturbations may differ in protein depletion efficiency.

summary: Endogenous Zbtb11 RNA did not decrease detectably after Zbtb11 assignment, even in cell types with strong downstream programs.
why_it_matters: This decoupling warns that Zbtb11 guide activity cannot be judged by the measured target transcript. Strong downstream signatures are interpretable, but null cell types could reflect true buffering, weak CRISPRi at the locus, or insufficient power.
main_caveats: The dataset assayed RNA, not nascent transcription, chromatin binding, or Zbtb11 protein.

summary: A small induced branch, including Dhx16, Mtg1, and Ppargc1a, was superimposed on the otherwise down-biased Zbtb11 loss signature.
why_it_matters: Selective induction of a mitochondrial ribosome assembly factor and Ppargc1a/PGC-1alpha suggests candidate homeostatic attempts to restore RNA or mitochondrial output in only some vulnerable neurons.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The induced genes are few and not all recur across cell types; the compensatory interpretation is transcript-only and hypothesis-generating.

summary: Assayed ZBTB-family perturbations did not substitute for Zbtb11 in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The contrast keeps the recurrent Zbtb11 program from being misread as a nonspecific signature of any BTB-zinc-finger transcription factor knockdown.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Known NRF-2/GABP partners and Zfp131 were absent from the panel, so the most mechanistically relevant related-target tests could not be performed.

summary: The loss-of-function direction points to a neuronal liability for any strategy that chronically reduces ZBTB11 activity.
why_it_matters: Human ZBTB11 deficiency causes a neurodevelopmental syndrome, and the Perturb-seq data show that Zbtb11 perturbation can repress complex-I, mitochondrial-metabolic, and nucleolar transcripts in defined neuronal classes; a therapeutically induced loss of ZBTB11 would therefore need stringent brain and cell-state selectivity.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|145 MH-LH TH Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: No therapeutic ZBTB11 perturbation was tested here; this is a direction-of-effect warning from CRISPRi-like knockdown signatures and human loss-of-function genetics.

summary: Slc12a2 knockdown produced a broadly buffered mouse-brain transcriptional phenotype rather than a robust DE program.
why_it_matters: The target is an ion cotransporter whose primary biology is chloride and volume transport; the dataset indicates that reducing its transcript did not, by itself, trigger a large steady-state mRNA remodeling response in any assayed neuronal class.
main_caveats: On-target Slc12a2 RNA was never significant after gene-wise FDR correction, so the negative downstream result may combine biology with incomplete target engagement or low transcript detection.

summary: No convincing Slc12a2 cell-type-selective module emerged; the apparent 001 L5-6 IT Glut and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA signals were weak q≈0.46-0.49 hypotheses.
why_it_matters: These two classes are the only places where any Slc12a2 row reached FDR<0.5, so they should be treated as prioritization hints rather than pathway calls.
cell_types: 001 L5-6 IT Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA
main_caveats: All adjusted p values were far above 0.05; individual weak genes may be false positives and should not be interpreted as an NKCC1 pathway.

summary: The neuronal chloride exporter Slc12a5/KCC2 was much more responsive than Slc12a2/NKCC1 and did not share a correlated signature with Slc12a2.
why_it_matters: NKCC1 and KCC2 are functionally coupled in chloride homeostasis, but the screen separates them: KCC2 knockdown gave FDR-significant target loss and a 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut Nr4a1/Dusp1/Fos response, whereas NKCC1 knockdown remained flat.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA
main_caveats: The contrast is transcriptional, not an ion-flux measurement; weaker Slc12a2 guide efficacy could contribute.

summary: WNK1/WNK3/STK39 pathway-neighbor perturbations did not recapitulate Slc12a2 at the mRNA-signature level.
why_it_matters: The negligible correlations are consistent with a CCC pathway whose acute regulation is largely by transporter phosphorylation and activity rather than transcription of the same downstream genes.
main_caveats: Own-transcript engagement for Wnk1, Wnk3, and Stk39 was also weak, so this is a pathway-level negative result rather than proof that kinase activity is irrelevant.

summary: The mouse-brain dataset is quiet despite strong human SLC12A2 disease genetics, pointing away from a broad DE mechanism for Delpire-McNeill/Kilquist-type biology in the assayed cells.
why_it_matters: Human SLC12A2 disorders involve neurodevelopmental and cochleovestibular phenotypes; the mouse Perturb-seq result suggests that disease-relevant readouts may sit in development, cochlea/choroid/epithelia, protein activity, or cell physiology rather than steady-state RNA in these brain classes.
main_caveats: The perturbation was in mouse brain cell classes, not human development, cochlea, choroid plexus, or secretory epithelia.

summary: The screen yields no robust Slc12a2 mRNA biomarker or signature neighbor for NKCC1 pharmacology, so chloride-flux or phospho-CCC assays are likely better pharmacodynamic readouts.
why_it_matters: NKCC1 is inhibited by loop diuretics such as bumetanide, but this dataset warns that efficacy of CNS-directed SLC12A2 modulation may be missed by whole-transcriptome DE alone.
main_caveats: Genetic knockdown and acute pharmacologic blockade are not equivalent; the dataset has no NKCC1 protein, phosphorylation, chloride, or electrophysiology measurement.

direction: measured Zfat transcript increased; downstream response narrowly positive for Setd1a in 151 and negative for D6Wsu163e in 155
summary: Zfat perturbation produced FDR-level target-transcript engagement only in two glutamatergic classes and was otherwise transcriptionally buffered.
why_it_matters: A transcription factor expected to regulate gene expression generated an unusually narrow response in this mouse-brain assay: even the two best-engaged cell types had only one FDR-level downstream gene each.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: The DE table shows higher Zfat RNA in targeted cells but does not prove increased functional ZFAT protein, and the number of perturbed cells was low in several classes.

direction: Setd1a up without coordinated partner up-regulation
summary: Setd1a is the dominant recurrent positive Zfat-responsive transcript, but the rest of the measured SET1A/COMPASS module is not co-induced.
why_it_matters: The dataset points to a chromatin-regulatory transcript, Setd1a, while arguing against simple stoichiometric up-regulation of the whole H3K4 methyltransferase complex.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Most Setd1a recurrences were nominal rather than FDR-level, and mRNA measurements cannot establish SET1A complex abundance or H3K4 methylation activity.

summary: D6Wsu163e, now annotated as Ferry3, is a recurrent negative marker of Zfat perturbation and is shared with Setd1a perturbation in the two engaged glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: This nominates an endosomal RNA-transport complex subunit transcript as a compact readout that may be more reproducible than any broad Zfat signature.
cell_types: 155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Only the midbrain glutamatergic Zfat effect survived FDR, FERRY3 function is inferred largely by homology in UniProt, and the Setd1a comparison does not imply a direct ZFAT-SETD1A-FERRY3 pathway.

summary: Zfat has no strong whole-transcriptome neighbor in the perturbation library, and the SETD1A perturbation is nearly uncorrelated with it.
why_it_matters: The Setd1a RNA increase is a local shared feature, not a global switch into a SETD1A-like perturbation state; this prevents over-interpreting one recurrent chromatin transcript as a pathway-level signature.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlation was computed from Wilcoxon score vectors for only the two Zfat-engaged cell types; sparse signatures can make all genome-wide correlations small.

direction: canonical targets unchanged at FDR level
summary: Mouse-brain Zfat perturbation does not reactivate the canonical immune and hematopoietic Zfat program.
why_it_matters: Prior mouse Zfat biology emphasizes Tal1, Lmo2, Gata1, thymocyte, and Brpf1-centered regulation; their absence as FDR hits here indicates that the neuronal response is context-restricted rather than interchangeable with the established blood and T-cell programs.
main_caveats: Genes outside the canonical set could be direct Zfat targets in brain, and the Perturb-seq table alone does not distinguish direct from indirect regulation.

summary: Otulin produced one genome-wide hit, Gpm6a induction, restricted to 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest measured Otulin consequence is a limbic glutamatergic neuronal membrane/synapse marker rather than the expected inflammatory effector program, making Gpm6a an exploratory biomarker of the responsive state.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Only 41 perturbed cells supported the 012 contrast, only Gpm6a passed FDR, and Otulin mRNA knockdown itself was not FDR-significant.

summary: The Otulin limbic transcriptome did not show canonical TNF/NF-kappaB or cytokine activation.
why_it_matters: Loss of OTULIN is expected to dysregulate Met1 ubiquitin and can activate inflammatory NF-kappaB/TNF biology in immune settings; its absence here reframes the brain response as a neuronal, non-inflammatory output in this assay.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Sentinel genes were selected a priori rather than tested with raw pathway enrichment, and weak target engagement could mask inflammatory activity.

summary: Most Otulin brain cell types were transcriptionally quiet despite measurable contrasts, and even the strongest nominal target-knockdown context lacked a downstream FDR hit.
why_it_matters: This prevents overgeneralizing the single Gpm6a response and suggests either biological buffering of partial Otulin loss or inadequate guide-mediated target engagement across many neuronal and GABAergic classes.
cell_types: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Because no cell type had FDR-significant Otulin transcript depletion, the quiet signatures cannot be cleanly assigned to true pathway buffering.

summary: Otulin did not converge with available CYLD, NF-kappaB, NOD, TLR, TNF, or MAP3K7 perturbations in the responsive 012 cell type.
why_it_matters: OTULIN sits in a LUBAC/linear-ubiquitin network, but the Perturb-seq signature was neither a shared innate-receptor output nor a CYLD-like deubiquitinase output; the result argues for pathway uncoupling in these neurons.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: Core LUBAC perturbations Rnf31, Rbck1, and Sharpin were absent, and score-vector correlations summarize transcriptional similarity rather than biochemical epistasis.

summary: The neuronal Gpm6a response should not be interpreted as an ORAS-like or anti-inflammatory OTULIN-loss program.
why_it_matters: Human and mouse OTULIN loss of function is linked to TNF-associated autoinflammation; this dataset instead shows sparse neuronal output without TNF/NF-kappaB induction, so therapeutically reducing OTULIN activity would require caution rather than being inferred as beneficial from the brain signature.
cell_types: 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut
main_caveats: The experiment was in mouse brain cell classes with weak mRNA-level target engagement and did not assay protein, linear ubiquitination, TNF secretion, or cell death.

summary: Zmynd11 showed directional but weakly FDR-supported on-target transcript depletion across mouse-brain neuronal classes, with the clearest RNA engagement in Pvalb GABA, MB Glut, and TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than a uniform cell-type response.
why_it_matters: ZMYND11 is an H3.3K36me3 reader and transcriptional corepressor; the observed signatures are therefore limited first by target engagement, not by an obviously broad Pol II elongation program.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|001 L5-6 IT Glut|217 P MY Pineal Glut
main_caveats: Only one cell type reached target-transcript FDR<0.1 and none reached FDR<0.05; cell-type differences may reflect guide capture, expression, or sampling rather than biology alone.

summary: The best-engaged Pvalb GABA and MB Glut responses were target-proximal: Zmynd11 itself was the top-ranked nominal gene, yet no other gene survived 5% FDR.
why_it_matters: A chromatin reader can in principle create broad transcriptional changes, but these data argue that the assayed neurons buffer acute Zmynd11 transcript depletion or that protein-level depletion was incomplete.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|155 MB Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: The on-target RNA FDR values were 0.0685 and 0.173 in the two rank-1 classes; a stronger knockdown or protein assay could reveal latent responses.

summary: The embryonic Zmynd11-Epha2-PI3K axis was not recapitulated as a mouse-brain neuronal RNA module: Epha2 and core PI3K/AKT/mTOR transcripts were not FDR-significant after Zmynd11 perturbation.
why_it_matters: This separates a developmental neurogenesis mechanism from the weak Perturb-seq phenotype and warns against assuming that Epha2 is an acute biomarker of Zmynd11 perturbation in these cells.
main_caveats: The comparison is indirect because the published mechanism is embryonic and Epha2 was sparsely expressed in many cell types; PI3K signaling need not be visible at the mRNA level.

summary: Zmynd11 was much weaker than several chromatin-regulator perturbations in the same TH and MB Glut strata: Chd8, Zmynd8, Adnp, Kdm5c, Deaf1, and Mga produced FDR-significant signatures where Zmynd11 did not.
why_it_matters: The null Zmynd11 downstream response is not explained by a global inability of these neuronal classes to report chromatin perturbations, and related regulatory genes should not be treated as interchangeable perturbations.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: Comparator perturbations had different guide sets and cell counts; stronger comparator signatures do not prove equal target engagement.

summary: Neither mechanism-guided nor unbiased neighbors yielded a convergent Zmynd11 surrogate: H3f3a and Setd2 were mostly null, and the closest positive or negative whole-signature neighbors in Pvalb, TH, and MB Glut had |r| below 0.09.
why_it_matters: The Zmynd11 perturbation should not be rescued analytically by borrowing a strong signature from a pathway neighbor or a top correlated target, because no such neighbor was present in this dataset.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut
main_caveats: Correlations were computed on precomputed Wilcoxon score vectors and are meaningful only for perturbations represented in the same cell type.

summary: A ZMYND11 inhibitor is not an obvious therapeutic direction for neurodevelopmental disease: human genetics points to pathogenic loss of function, drug databases show no active clinical-quality ZMYND11 mechanism, and the mouse dataset did not expose a robust rescue pathway.
why_it_matters: If intervention were contemplated, the available evidence points toward restoring ZMYND11 function in defined developmental contexts rather than inhibiting its reader activity in the assayed neurons.
main_caveats: The Perturb-seq assay is a loss-of-function-like transcriptomic screen and does not test gain-of-function rescue, protein abundance, or developmental phenotypes.

summary: Tpm1 perturbation was globally FDR-null in mouse-brain cell classes.
why_it_matters: The screen could detect strong cytoskeletal responses for core actins, but Tpm1 loss did not trigger a reproducible Tpm or sarcomeric program; interpretation should start from a buffered or weakly engaged brain phenotype rather than from isolated nominal hits.
main_caveats: The null is at the transcriptional FDR level; weak target mRNA suppression makes it impossible to distinguish biological buffering from incomplete perturbation in many cell types.

summary: Measurable target-transcript depletion was restricted, with the clearest Tpm1 mRNA decreases in 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The strongest overall scalar hits occurred in other cell types that did not repress Tpm1, so cell-type interpretation should prioritize target-engaged CA3 and TH contexts and down-weight unengaged Dopa, 008 L2/3, and Sst signatures.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|215 MB Dopa|008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut|053 Sst Gaba
main_caveats: The Tpm1 rows are nominal rather than FDR-significant, and the 215 MB Dopa signal has only 21 Tpm1-perturbed cells.

summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut buffered Tpm1 depletion despite high perturbed-cell support.
why_it_matters: This cell class had the largest Tpm1 perturbed-cell count and nominal target repression but only Mafg plus Tpm1 at p<0.001, making it the clearest example of target engagement without a broad downstream transcriptome.
cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut
main_caveats: Target repression was modest, with pvals_adj=1.0, and buffering was inferred from RNA output only.

summary: Tpm1 did not phenocopy Tpm3 or actin-regulatory perturbations and did not transcriptionally induce the measured Tpm2/Tpm4 paralogs.
why_it_matters: A simple model in which tropomyosin genes are interchangeable neuronal actin-filament regulators is not supported by these signatures; any effect of Tpm1 appears isoform- and cell-context-specific.
main_caveats: Tpm3 and Actb target transcripts were not present as response rows, and Tpm1 itself produced weak signatures, so absence of convergence should not be read as definitive absence of shared protein-level function.

summary: Mouse-brain Tpm1 loss-of-function did not recapitulate the dominant sarcomeric cardiomyopathy biology linked to human TPM1.
why_it_matters: Human TPM1 disease evidence is concentrated in cardiac thin-filament disorders, and TPM1 has no recorded Open Targets clinical candidates; these brain Perturb-seq data therefore argue for a cardiac contractility assay, not a neuronal transcriptional screen, to evaluate therapeutic direction or variant pathogenicity.
main_caveats: The dataset is mouse brain and mRNA knockdown, whereas cardiomyopathy is usually assayed in cardiomyocytes and often involves missense, dominant thin-filament mechanisms.

summary: Mrtfa is an exploratory CA3 marker coupled to the only clearly target-engaged Tpm1 nominal module.
why_it_matters: MRTF/SRF is an actin-sensitive transcriptional axis, so nominal Mrtfa down-regulation beside Tpm1 down-regulation in CA3 is a biologically plausible but unvalidated readout of tropomyosin-actin perturbation.
cell_types: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut
main_caveats: Mrtfa was nominal only, not FDR-significant, and the literature link concerns actin-dependent MRTF/SRF activity rather than Tpm1-dependent Mrtfa mRNA abundance.

summary: Srsf1 knockdown was directionally consistent but the downstream gene-expression burden was highly cell-type selective.

cell_types: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut|155 MB Glut|191 MB P MY GABA|217 P MY Pineal Glut|066 CNU-HYa HY GABA|017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut|059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA

summary: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA were buffered at the gene-abundance level despite significant Srsf1 transcript reduction.

summary: Small-molecule SYNCRIP binding is chemically precedented, but the weak adult neuronal transcriptomic response should not be interpreted as evidence that SYNCRIP inhibition is safe.

summary: This brain null is not a TBX5 disease or neurological-safety surrogate.
why_it_matters: TBX5 disease evidence is cardiolimb/conduction dominant, while this atlas lacks engaged Tbx5 biology and TBX5 has little drug pharmacology.
main_caveats: No cardiac, limb, lung, retina, or human perturbation was assayed.

summary: The validated 052 Pvalb Gaba response is target-RNA autonomous: Rab3gap2 itself is depleted, but no second gene reaches FDR<0.05.
why_it_matters: The best-engaged neuronal class does not expose a transcriptional effector module, making organelle, Rab18-localization, autophagy, or synaptic-release assays more appropriate than a bulk mRNA marker panel for acute Rab3gap2 loss.
cell_types: 052 Pvalb Gaba
main_caveats: The dataset confirms RNA depletion only; protein persistence or post-transcriptional trafficking phenotypes could remain invisible in the Wilcoxon mRNA readout.

summary: Rab3gap2 perturbation is transcriptionally weak across the assayed neuronal atlas.
why_it_matters: A severe neurodevelopmental disease gene produced only two FDR-supported rows among 371,818 tests, so most cell classes cannot be interpreted as having a resolved Rab3gap2 downstream program.
main_caveats: Many cell types have fewer than 75 perturbed cells, and only 1/22 target-transcript rows passes FDR<0.05.

summary: The RAB3GAP/RAB18 disease-axis genes do not form a correlated Rab3gap2 Perturb-seq signature.
why_it_matters: RAB3GAP1, RAB3GAP2, and RAB18 act in one curated trafficking axis, so convergence would have been expected if the mRNA screen captured that biology; the observed near-zero correlations argue that the axis is silent, buffered, or under-engaged at the transcriptome level.
main_caveats: Rab3gap1 and Rab18 perturbations themselves had no FDR-level own-transcript knockdown, so absence of correlation is a restricted signature result rather than proof that the proteins have divergent biology.

summary: Rab3gap2 does not phenocopy robust synaptic-vesicle exocytosis perturbations at the mRNA-signature level.
why_it_matters: The original Rab3GAP biochemical context was Rab3-linked regulated exocytosis, yet Snap25 and Stxbp1 knockdowns that are readily detected in this dataset are not Rab3gap2-like; this favors a post-translational or developmental Rab3gap2 role over a shared steady-state exocytosis transcriptome.
main_caveats: Snap25 and Stxbp1 are pathway neighbors rather than Rab3gap complex members; the comparison tests transcriptomic similarity, not vesicle release itself.

summary: The screen refines RAB3GAP2 disease genetics by showing little acute steady-state mRNA consequence in differentiated mouse neurons.
why_it_matters: Warburg Micro and Martsolf syndromes arise from congenital biallelic disruption of the RAB3GAP/RAB18 pathway; the Perturb-seq result suggests that early developmental stages, ocular/endocrine compartments, or morphology-first membrane-trafficking phenotypes may be more disease-relevant than broad mature-neuron transcriptional rewiring.
main_caveats: The dataset samples mouse neuronal subclasses and lacks developing eye, endocrine, fibroblast ER-structure, and organismal developmental readouts used in the literature.

summary: The near-null Perturb-seq profile should not be taken as evidence that RAB3GAP2 inhibition is safe.
why_it_matters: Human genetics points to loss of RAB3GAP2 function as an ocular and neurodevelopmental disease mechanism, while the screen was too weakly engaged to reveal most transcriptomic consequences and target-disease databases show no established clinical-modality tractability for RAB3GAP2.
main_caveats: This is a genetic-direction warning, not evidence from pharmacologic RAB3GAP2 inhibitors.

why_it_matters: PTPRO is not a generic high-amplitude transcriptomic switch in this mouse-brain screen; the result points either to post-transcriptional phosphotyrosine biology, incomplete mRNA knockdown, or compensation rather than a broad cell-state transition.

summary: L4/5 intratelencephalic cortical glutamatergic neurons were the only Ptpro context with a corrected single-gene response, a selective decrease of Grik5.
why_it_matters: A single kainate-receptor subunit rather than a pan-neuronal program was the most robust Ptpro-associated readout, making Grik5 a candidate cell-type-specific marker of Ptpro sensitivity rather than a universal target transcript.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: The same L4/5 signature did not show measurable Ptpro mRNA knockdown, so the Grik5 link could reflect protein-level editing, an unmeasured isoform, or an off-target/guide-composition effect.

summary: The L4/5 Grik5 hit was accompanied only by nominal decreases in synaptic and Eph/Src/FAK-adjacent genes, including Nptx1, Epha5, Ptk2, Srcin1, and Rasal1.
why_it_matters: These genes make the corrected Grik5 hit biologically plausible against prior PTPRO synapse/Eph biology, but they argue for a weak synaptic-adhesion hypothesis rather than a statistically proven pathway-level response.

main_caveats: All module genes except Grik5 had FDR=1.0 and should be treated as rank-level support only.

summary: Ptpro signatures did not transcriptionally phenocopy Eph receptors, Ntrk3, Plxna4, or receptor-like PTP relatives in matched cell types.
why_it_matters: Prior work places PTPRO near Eph and neurotrophin receptor tyrosine kinase signaling, but the screen does not support a simple model in which knocking down a substrate receptor, axon-guidance neighbor, or paralog is interchangeable with Ptpro perturbation.
main_caveats: The contrast is limited by weak Ptpro response amplitudes and by mixed target engagement of several comparators; correlations of restricted top-score signatures were modest and non-specific.

summary: Genetic Ptpro loss in brain raises an exploratory synaptic-liability warning for PTPRO inhibition.
why_it_matters: PTPRO loss-of-function reduced excitatory synapse measures in cultured neurons and hippocampal Ptpro loss sensitized mice to cognitive injury in prior work; the Perturb-seq decrease of Grik5 and nominal synaptic genes is directionally consistent with caution for CNS-directed inhibition, although it is not a drug experiment.
cell_types: 005 L4-5 IT CTX Glut
main_caveats: Only one transcript passed FDR in the dataset, the perturbation was genetic rather than pharmacologic, and available ChEMBL activity records are biochemical rather than validated CNS inhibitors.
